3716.description: The University of Florida will leverage its institutional investment in artificial intelligence and world class facilities to bring to Florida the best medical researchers at the intersection of brain health and machine learning to build the next generation of medicine. In addition to cutting edge research, the program will develop new strategies to treat brain afflictions and diseases using the latest advancements in AI. The University of Florida will incorporate the many resources on hand, including students, faculty, and partnerships with other state institutions. The funds will be used to enhance existing facilities, making the absolute most of the state's existing investments.
3716.purpose: To establish a state of the art and world-class research program at the cutting edge of biology and artificial intelligence at the University of Florida.
3716.activities: Scientists will be researching improvement in the understanding of the brain and its related afflictions and diseases. Multiple clinical trials in the areas will establish strategies and treatments to cure and prevent maladies of the brain and its functions.
3716.direct_services: Such a program and its facilities will not only benefit patients with afflictions of the brain, however it will also benefit all citizens in its research of treatments that prevent illnesses and enhance the cerebral health of all. Further, it will benefit the education of students from across the broad section of disciplines whose study involves the brain by granting them access to the highest lev
3716.population: As stated, the target population is limitless as the objective is to bring together the best experts in the field of brain research to research, learn, and promulgate strategies and treatments across the spectrum of brain-related health.
3716.outcome: Each project will address specific research questions that are highly relevant to an important scientific problem using established technologies and experimental protocols. During the funding period, progress will be evaluated by written progress reports including qualitative and quantitative data related to the proposed specific aims. These findings will then be submitted to scientific journals.

3711.organization: North Miami Foundation for Senior Citizens
3711.description: Improved nutrition, social engagement, transportation, improved mental health, and overall improved health through access to home delivered meals, transportation, assessment and other services thereby stabilizing elder's risk; providing adequate nutrition and other in-home services are vital to the wellbeing of seniors; improved mental health functioning due to improved services and social interaction which are critical for elders facing isolation, depression - while improving quality of life.
3711.purpose: Improved nutrition, social interaction, transportation, improved mental health, and overall health through access to home delivered meals, groceries, transportation, assessments and other services thereby stabilizing risk; adequate nutrition and other in-home services are vital to the health and wellbeing of seniors; improved / stabilized mental health functioning due to improved services and social interaction which are critical for elders facing isolation and depression due to loneliness.
3711.activities: Home delivered meals, transportation, screening and assessments, telephone reassurance and other services to elderly residents who are at risk, and homebound.
3711.direct_services: Home delivered meals, seven days per week, to elderly residents at risk of hunger and malnutrition. Transportation, screening and assessments, social interaction, telephone reassurance and other services provided to at-risk and homebound elders.
3711.population: Elder persons at risk of malnutrition and food insecurity.
3711.outcome: Improved / stabilized mental health functioning due to improved nutrition, transportation, assessments, social interaction, telephone reassurance and other services for isolated elders at risk and elders facing isolation and depression due to loneliness.

3787.description: This project will improve public safety and provide law enforcement with tools to enable swift incident response, stronger protection, better crowd control, and heightened security along SR811 with significant tourist activity and regional traffic flow. This project would install barriers to protect pedestrials along the sidewalk from vehicle inspired attacls. Also includes purchase and installation of an integrated camera and survelliance system.
3787.purpose: Installation of barriers will help reduce the threat of and protect citizens from terrorist attacks involving motor vehicles inspired by recent attacks in New Orleans, Vancouver, Germany, et al.
3787.activities: Reduced threat level and enhanced protection allowing citizens to continue to attend popular events and continue to benefit from strong tourism.
3787.direct_services: Incident response, crowd control, heightened security, ensuring the safety of residents and visitors.
3787.population: City residents and visitors. 12,000 residents and 50,000+ visitors for various events.
3787.outcome: Installing bollards will improve safety by preventing vehicles from entering pedestrian areas. This is critical for protecting attendees at popular events from potential vehicle attacks, a concern heightened by recent events. Surveillance will improve incident response and heighten security in a main transportation corridor (SR811). Methodology involves attendance at events throughout the year. Incident response times, incident resolutions, threat detection and prevention, number of car plates detected, and number of infractions recorded.

3724.description: This program involves the replacement of outdated 9-1-1 dispatch consoles with modern, space-efficient units to improve operational effectiveness and support future growth. The project aims to reduce the physical footprint of console infrastructure within the communications center, while also expanding capacity from current levels to support up to 15 dispatch positions. This will enhance emergency response capabilities, provide greater flexibility for staffing during peak demand or special events, and ensure the system meets current ergonomic, technical, and public safety standards.
3724.purpose: To provide a modernized and efficient facility for processing 9-1-1 calls and dispatching Fire and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) services, ensuring improved reliability, functionality, and support for current and future operational needs.
3724.activities: Enhanced E9-1-1 call-taking and dispatching of EMS and Fire resources to ensure rapid, coordinated emergency response.
3724.direct_services: Enhanced E9-1-1 call-taking and dispatching of EMS and Fire resources to ensure rapid, coordinated emergency response.
3724.population: Citizens and visitors to Escambia County Florida. >350K
3724.outcome: The modernization of 9-1-1 facilities will enhance the speed and efficiency of emergency call processing, resulting in faster response times and improved public safety outcomes. Escambia County Administration ensures accountability and continuous improvement by monitoring 9-1-1 service performance through regular internal and external audits.

3745.description: This program is designed to strengthen the City’s capacity to address food insecurity by ensuring seniors have consistent access to nutritious meals.
3745.purpose: This program is intended to increase the City's ability to combat food insecurity among its most vulnerable population by providing the City's senior population with a stable source of meals.
3745.activities: Funding for this program will enable the City to provide a source of meals for its most vulnerable and food insecure seniors. For the seniors who will receive meals through this program, they will be able to experience more stability and security.
3745.direct_services: Increased access to food security for vulnerable seniors through the increased delivery of meals to the seniors in need in our community.
3745.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is reduced food insecurity and increased stability for vulnerable senior residents by providing consistent access to nutritious meals, thereby improving their overall health, well-being, and quality of life. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of seniors served, the number of meals distributed, program participation rates, and ongoing eligibility records. Additional evaluation may include participant feedback and periodic assessments of service consistency and delivery.

3765.description: The new community aquatic facility improvements will include a children’s interactive water feature element with a zero entry kiddie pool and water playground structure, new resort style pool with a lazy river and small water slide. Also due to the age of the current facility, a new expanded lap swim pool will be construction. The new facility will also include new locker rooms, office, storage area and family restrooms.
3765.purpose: Constructed more than thirty plus (30+) years ago, the pool has reached its ‘end of life’ and has reached its maximum capacity. The City fields daily requests for usage that go unfulfilled. Local swim clubs, neighborhood schools and local non-profits have lined up to request availability of the existing facility. The needs and requests are greater than the existing capacity can fulfill. Swim times are limited in order to accommodate as many residents as possible.
3765.activities: Constructed more than thirty plus (30+) years ago, the pool has reached its ‘end of life’ and has reached its maximum capacity. The City fields daily requests for usage that go unfulfilled. Local swim clubs, neighborhood schools and local non-profits have lined up to request availability of the existing facility. The needs and requests are greater than the existing capacity can fulfill. Swim times are limited in order to accommodate as many residents as possible.
3765.direct_services: Expanded swim classes/lessons for children and adults, extended free swim times, more recreational facilities (lazy river, kiddie pool, recreational play equipment), pool safety programs, lap swimming for leisure and competition, etc.
3765.population: Bonita Springs residents, both children and adults as well as residents from neighboring communities such as Estero, Fort Myers Beach and North Naples/Collier County. With the expansion of the aquatic facilities the City expects to serve well over 10,000 people per year.
3765.outcome: Swimming is a low-impact exercise that benefits cardiovascular health, muscular strength and endurance. Swimming also can help reduce stress, improve mental health and promote relaxation. Increased number of individual residents, swim clubs, swim classes, etc., utilizing the new facility.

3778.description: The Duval Street project would feature a new pump station to support increased performance of the stormwater system throughout the entire Lower Duval corridor and provide comprehensive flooding mitigation. The existing pump station serving the corridor would be replaced and this new pump station would manage expected increases in stormwater runoff to prevent Duval Street flooding. The project would also include a series of pipe upgrades within the Duval Street corridor itself and connecting it to the pump station to move water away from areas prone to flooding on Duval Street.
3778.purpose: The Duval Street and Mallory Square Area Stormwater Pump Station and Resilience Project is a comprehensive flood mitigation project designed to improve stormwater management, enhance infrastructure resilience, and reduce chronic flooding in Key West's critical economic and cultural corridor.
3778.activities: Funds will be allocated and awarded for construction and redevelopment of existing stormwater systems by structural hardening, resilience upgrades, stormwater wells to redirect runoff underground, water quality treatment features and storm drain inlets and pump station, tide valves to prevent stormwater intrusion, and upgrades to the underground stormwater infrastructure to increase drainage capacity.
3778.direct_services: Flood mitigation will protect public and private property, utility infrastructure, Key West's commercial economic core district from flood events, storm surges, and unusually high tidal events.
3778.population: A large portion of Key West's 17,000-member workforce relies on the project area for employment, including over 5,100 workers directly employed within the project footprint. Additionally, the area supports over 2.7 million annual visitors, who rely on transportation networks, accommodations, and commercial activity within the corridor.
3778.outcome: Capturing and treating stormwater will improve near shore water quality while mitigating flooding impacts and hazards. Methodology utilized to confirm this outcome will be the tax revenue generated by keeping Key West's critical commercial corridor accessible and resilient in storm and tidal events.

3801.description: The remaining funds from Fiscal Year 2023-2024 OCEARCH Mayport Research and Operations Center (Jacksonville University) (SF 2756) should revert from Jacksonville University and be reappropriated to the City of Jacksonville for capital improvements to the City of Jacksonville property being utilized for the OCEARCH Mayport Research and Operations Center.
3801.purpose: Funds will support the construction of a purpose-built facility (OCEARCH’s Global Headquarters). This facility will consolidate all OCEARCH operations and research activities, greatly expanding public access and providing colleges, universities, K–12 schools, and research entities with unprecedented opportunities to engage in ocean science, conservation, and applied research. The facility will also serve as a new workforce development hub for maritime operations.
3801.activities: This complex will include building(s) for public education and displays, public meetings, workforce development partnerships and OCEARCH ship operations. The facility will host public education opportunities (K-12, undergraduate, graduate, and life-long learning) centered around sharks and other marine life in Florida as well as partnerships with local industry partners in the maritime realm.
3801.direct_services: Education and career development will play a critical role in the facility. We will work with local school districts and state college to host experiential education opportunities, both locally and virtually. Further, we will work with local industry partners that focus on maritime career development. Outcomes will be measured by number of students served.
3801.population: The target population includes over 1M residents in Duval County and the 22M overnight and day trippers who visit Duval County annually. Nearly 28,000 people visit Jacksonville every night and another 30,000 day-time visitors. As an international leader in shark and ocean research, the facility will also attract visitors from around the state of Florida and other other states and countries. With Mayport's rich maritime history, our target audience includes residents and visitors of Duval County,
3801.outcome: The OCEARCH Headquarters and marine science research facility will provide economic benefits to Mayport, Jacksonville, and Florida at large through generated tourism, with outcomes measured by annual visitors, and overall economic impact. Expanding scientific knowledge of sharks will play a key role in the facility's overall mission. Outcomes will be measured by number of research efforts hosted, papers published, and overall impact in driving datacentric maritime policy efforts. Local education outreach will be measured by number of students served and career development will play a critical role in the facility. Additionally, the general public will develop a better understanding of public

2311.description: Polk State College seeks $25,389,752 to renovate Building #3 (LLC) on the Lakeland Campus, a central hub for student learning and support. LLC houses classrooms, laboratories, faculty and staff offices, the campus library, and the testing center—facilities that serve thousands of students each year. The project will replace the aging roof, upgrade HVAC and technology systems, and modernize classrooms, labs, and offices to meet current instructional and safety standards. Expansion of the library and testing center will increase access to academic resources and improve service capacity for a growing student population.
2311.purpose: The funds will be used to renovate and modernize Building #3 (LLC) on the Lakeland Campus, replacing failing infrastructure and upgrading instructional and student support spaces. This project will extend the facility’s useful life, improve energy efficiency, and expand access to library and testing services, directly enhancing student learning and success.
2311.activities: Project activities include replacing the existing roof; upgrading HVAC, electrical, and technology systems; modernizing classrooms, laboratories, and offices; and expanding the library and testing facilities within Building #3 on the Lakeland Campus. These improvements will provide modern instructional spaces, expanded student study and testing areas, and upgraded technology infrastructure to support high-quality teaching and learning.
2311.direct_services: Polk State's mission is to provide accessible, affordable, quality higher education and training to the Polk County community. With 92% of Associate in Science graduates and 85% of baccalaureate degree graduates employed or continuing their education, some of the highest percentages in the state, Polk State consistently produces graduates who are well-prepared for the workforce. Projects such as t
2311.population: The target population includes the more than 9,300 students served annually on Polk State College’s Lakeland Campus, who will directly benefit from enhanced classrooms, laboratories, and academic support spaces. Building #3 also houses the campus library, testing center, and tutoring services, which serve both enrolled students and members of the public pursuing workforce certification or continuing education.
2311.outcome: While this project is not expected to immediately increase the total number of degrees or certificates awarded, it will enhance student retention, completion, and academic performance by improving access to library, tutoring, and testing services. Renovation and expansion of these areas in Building #3 will provide modern, technology-enabled study spaces and flexible learning environments that better support students’ academic needs. Success will be measured by tracking student usage of library and tutoring services, monitoring testing center capacity and throughput, and analyzing retention and course completion rates.

1926.description: Funds will support design and permitting for Phase 3 of Lady Lake’s Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) expansion. The project will increase capacity to 3.0 MGD, implement advanced wastewater treatment (AWT), and expand reclaimed water capabilities. These upgrades address rapid growth and capacity constraints, enhance nutrient removal, and ensure compliance with the Silver Springs (SILV) and Upper Ocklawaha (OKLA) BMAPs, protecting regional water quality and supporting sustainable development.
1926.purpose: The funds will support design and permitting for Phase 3 of the Town’s Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) expansion, which will increase capacity to 3.0 MGD, implement advanced wastewater treatment (AWT), and expand reclaimed water capabilities. The improvements are needed to address rapid population growth, meet regulatory nutrient limits, and ensure long-term compliance with the Silver Springs (SILV) and Upper Ocklawaha (OKLA) BMAPs.
1926.activities: Activities will include engineering design, environmental and regulatory permitting, process and hydraulic modeling, site investigations, development of construction plans and technical specifications, cost estimating, and preparation of bid documents. These services will advance the project to construction readiness and ensure all regulatory requirements are addressed.
1926.direct_services: The project will provide the community with a fully designed and permitted expansion of the WRF, enabling the Town to move forward with construction of additional treatment capacity, AWT processes, and reclaimed water improvements. This will support reliable wastewater service, protect groundwater and springs, and ensure adequate capacity for existing and future customers.
1926.population: The project will serve the Town of Lady Lake’s approximately 17,000 residents, as well as future residential and commercial developments in the Town’s rapidly growing utility service area. Beneficiaries also include surrounding communities and users of the regional springs and surface waters protected by improved wastewater treatment.
1926.outcome: Expected Outcomes: Improved wastewater treatment performance, increased capacity to 3.0 MGD, enhanced nutrient removal to support BMAP compliance, and expanded reclaimed water capabilities to reduce potable water demand. Method of Measurement: Evaluation of projected treatment capacity, modeled AWT effluent concentrations, BMAP compliance tracking, and updated reclaimed water utilization and potable-offset estimates.

1675.description: This project will retrofit, harden, increase the capacity of the existing pump station, and enable the optimization of its operation. It will improve storage and conveyance capabilities by mitigating flooding and reducing nutrient loading in the drainage basin, thereby improving the flood quantity and water quantity level of service. Project location: NE 26 Avenue between NE 204 Terr to NE 205 Street.
1675.purpose: The goal is to mitigate flooding by increasing and enhance the capacity of the existing stormwater pump station (NE 26 Avenue Stormwater Pump Station), by optimizing its operation, prevent pollutants from entering the stormwater systems, and impact the water quantity and quality in the nearby C-9 watershed basin in Miami-Dade County. Project location: NE 26 Avenue between NE 204 Terr to NE 205 Street.
1675.activities: Addition of an emergency generator at the pump station; and upgrade, hardening, and elevation of pump station's electrical and mechanical components.
1675.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
1675.outcome: Mitigate flooding by increasing and enhancing the capacity of the existing stormwater pump station (NE 26 Avenue Stormwater Pump Station)——measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

3370.description: Design design (planning/engineering) for improvements necessary for the rehabilitation/replacement of the Cove Stormwater Pump Station and critical infrastructure to reduce flooding and harden utilities.
3370.purpose: Design for the rehabilitation/replacement of the City's Cove Stormwater Pump Station that corresponds to the Mutli- Basin Assessment.
3370.activities: Planning and Engineering services to replace the Cove Stormwater Pump Station.
3370.direct_services: Design for future stormwater and other critical infrastructure improvements to enhance resiliency of the neighborhood.
3370.population: Directly impacts approximately 1,500 residents residing within the neighborhoods of Basin III (477 acres) as well as community establishments.
3370.outcome: Reduce infrastructure failures and minimize risk of flooding, and maintain emergency access within areas (Basin III) serviced by the Cove Stormwater Pump Station. Visual observations, loss of property reports associated with flooding within the Basin III area; includes road closure logs and incident response times.

1804.description: The construction of Fire Station 17 will enhance public safety and emergency response in an underserved, economically disadvantaged community by reducing response times, improving fire suppression, and expanding emergency medical services. It will also serve as a community resource, offering fire prevention education, emergency preparedness programs, and a 160-person community room, maximizing resources while strengthening public safety and economic growth.
1804.purpose: The requested funds will be used to construct a new fire station in an underserved community that experiences over 5,000 emergency calls annually. This investment will improve response times, enhance fire suppression and medical services, and provide fire prevention education and community engagement opportunities, ensuring greater public safety and support for residents and businesses.
1804.activities: The funds will support the construction of a new fire station that will provide fire suppression, emergency medical response, fire prevention education, and community engagement services. This facility will house fire responders, prevention teams, and a 160-person community room, ensuring faster response times, improved public safety, and enhanced emergency preparedness for an underserved area.
1804.direct_services: The funding will provide critical fire suppression, emergency medical response, and fire prevention education to residents in an underserved area with over 5,000 emergency calls annually. The new fire station will ensure faster response times, improved life-saving capabilities, and enhanced public safety programs while serving as a community resource for education and engagement.
1804.population: The target population includes underserved and economically disadvantaged residents and the general population in Tallahassee’s Southside, ensuring equitable access to fire suppression, emergency medical response, and public safety resources. The new fire station will serve thousands of residents, businesses, and visitors, addressing over 5,000 emergency calls annually and enhancing community-wide safety and resilience.
1804.outcome: The new fire station will improve response times, fire suppression, and medical services in an underserved area with over 5,000 emergency calls annually, while also lowering insurance costs, attracting businesses, and supporting fire prevention education. Success will be measured through response time data, emergency call volumes, fire damage reduction, and community engagement metrics.

3487.description: State support for care at the Steven A. Cohen Military Family Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners will continue to provide critical expansion of behavioral health services for Military Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and military connected families of all ages. Too often our countries military and their families struggle to cope with mental health concerns related to a life of military service and experience barriers to care such as ability to pay, access to childcare during therapy or transportation to and from appointments. Our Cohen Clinics will continue to provide evidence based, culturally competent, targeted therapy for all mental health concerns, couples & family relationship issues, transition challenges and children's behavioral concerns. Services will include assessment, diagnosis, outpatient treatment both in-person or via tele video as well as case manageme
3487.purpose: Cohen Military Family Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners will provide critical ongoing expansion of behavioral health services for Veterans, National Guard and Reservists and military family members of all ages across the state. This population struggles with the side-effects of a life of service to our country; moves, deployments, relationship and parenting stressors, trauma, other mental health concerns. Aspire and Centerstone provide evidenced based, culturally competent, perso
3487.activities: Veterans and military families of all ages will be provided initial assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning and outpatient mental health therapy tailored to the identified needs of the individual, couple and/or family to both target the concerns and improve quality of life for our military-connected families. These clinics also offer whole-person support via case management. All care is available across the state of Florida, either in-person or via telehealth as described in Ch. 65D-30 and in
3487.direct_services: Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and their families of all ages will be provided services to include initial assessment, treatment planning, suicide screening and intervention (as appropriate), crisis intervention, case management (to provide wrap-around community resources and referrals), individual, couples, family and/or group outpatient therapy both in-person and via televideo across Flori
3487.population: Military Veterans, National Guard and Reserve and their family members of all ages. We expect to serve between 401-800 individuals yearly across both Cohen Clinics at Centerstone and Aspire Health Partners.
3487.outcome: We will improve the mental health of those served by the reduction of depressive and anxiety symptoms by 25%, reduction of PTSD by 25%, improved quality of life by 10%, reduction in suicidal ideation by 20%. Outcome measures will be collected for each client served at initial assessment and monthly throughout each client's episode of treatment. Outcome measures include: PHQ-9 (for Depression), GAD-7 (for Anxiety), C-SSRS (for suicide risk), PCL-5 (for PTSD) and QLES (quality of life rating scale) at baseline and discharge.

3389.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3389.description: The purpose of this program is to reimburse the school for the additional cost of providing Kosher meals over what the Federal Government is reimbursing under the National School Lunch Program.
3389.purpose: These funds will enable the school to continue to serve our students Kosher meals and snacks during school. These funds specifically make up the difference between what the Federal Government is paying and what the meals actually cost.
3389.activities: Breakfast, Lunch and snacks will be served daily to the student of Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3389.direct_services: Breakfast, Lunch and snacks will be served daily to the student of Chabad Hebrew Academy.
3389.population: School Aged children are the target population, over 800 individuals are expected to be served.
3389.outcome: The expected benefits are that when students receive healthy and nutritious meals following the USDA guidelines, they are statistically more likely to be successful academically. The methodology we use to measure the outcome is both attendance and standardized testing scores.

1885.description: The funds will be used to de-commission two wells according to DEP Requirements and Standards in order for us to use the property to build a 2-3 story parking garage.
1885.purpose: Two (2) potable wells will be abandoned so a parking garage can be constructed to facilitate parking for downtown Tavares.
1885.activities: The two wells will be closed down. A 2-3 story parking garage will be built in order to provide parking for the citizens and visitors to the City of Tavares.
1885.direct_services: The two wells will be closed down. A 2-3 story parking garage will be built in order to provide parking for the citizens and visitors to the City of Tavares.
1885.population: General population - 20,000. Plus, visitors who come through the area.
1885.outcome: By abandoning the two wells, a parking garage will be constructed to help provide parking for the downtown area for events, parks, and local businesses.

The apparatus will provide first response to structural and wild land fires in unincorporated northeast Leon County not serviced by fire hydrants. The BVFRD serves a 110 square mile area of mixed use (urban, suburban, and rural) containing over 12,500 residential structures. This number does not include commercial, government, educational, and agricultural buildings. This unit will also respond to mutual aid requests within and outside Leon County.
1425.purpose: The BVFRD will acquire a 2,500-gallon pumper tanker for the purposes of maintaining a mobile strategic water reserve in rural northeastern Leon County where there are no fire hydrants. The funds will be allocated directly to the firefighting apparatus to replace a 20-year-old firefighting tanker that has become expensive to maintain for reliable in daily operation. The frequency and duration the current unit is out of service has put local residents at risk. When in service the safety of unit's
1425.activities: The BVFRD will purchase a 2,500-gallon firefighting pumper tanker/tender to provide emergency structural and wild land fire suppression services to the residents of unincorporated Leon County. Additionally, this apparatus will be utilized to train the responders of the Bradfordville Volunteer Fire and Rescue department as well as new recruits to the fire service. The unit may be dispatched as part of mutual aid to territories within and outside of Leon County.
1425.direct_services: The BVFRD provides first response emergency medical and fire suppression services in northeast Leon County that is mixed urban, suburban, and rural. This firefighting unit (pumper tanker/tender will primarily serve a rural area of the county where residents are not serviced by a manned fire station or operational fire hydrants. This pumper tanker/tender will primarily serve a rural area of the county where residents are not serviced by a manned fire station or operational fire hydrants. This tanker will prove valuable as immediate target population is unincorporated northeast Leon County consisting of approximately 12,500 residential structures. This number does no
1425.outcome: The planned expected outcome will be the BVRFD receives a 2,500-gallon tanker capable of pumping 1,250gpms to provide fire suppression and support to the residents of Leon County. The benefit of this apparatus will be immeasurable due to the nature of structural and wildland fire incidents. Its value will be determined in two ways: (1) during fire suppression efforts, water will be readily available through this capable apparatus in areas not serviced by fire hydrants; and (2) insurance ratings may drop for residents due to the type of apparatus stationed near their personal residences. The matrices for which success will be measured is a decrease in the frequency and duration the unit is ou

1426.description: Both the design (DAG) and construction (Allstate) companies selected to build the new Quincy K-8 School have determined the minimum cost to build the new K-8 School in today’s economy to be $108,470,014.00. To date, Gadsden County School Board has been approved for $81,703,933.00 nonrecurring State Special Facility funding. The Board is requesting the remaining $26,766,081 of the $108,470,014.00 to cover the total cost of completing the construction of the school.
1426.purpose: The purpose of this project is to improve public education in a small rural community. Gadsden County School Board will have all the required funding to complete the construction of the new K-8 school in a timely manner meeting all construction requirements.
1426.activities: 1) Relocation of power poles, fiber optic cabling and other utility lines 2) Installation of a sewage lift station 3) Extensive earthwork operations due to significant grade changes at new school location 4) Asbestos abatement 5) Fund additional cost due to construction on an occupied site
1426.direct_services: The new Gadsden K-8 will provide a safe, secure and state-of-the-art school to approximately 1500 students and fill the County’s 649 special needs emergency evacuation space deficit.
1426.population: The 1500 K-8 students zoned to attend Stewart Street Elementary, George Munroe Elementary, James A. Shanks Middle School, and Gadsden Elementary Magnet is the primary target population served by this project.
1426.outcome: Gadsden County School Board will be able to complete the construction of the new K-8 school in a timely manner meeting all construction requirements. This will improve the public education of our small rural community.

1045.organization: Jewish Adoption and Family Care Options
1045.description: Eagles' Haven community wellness center offers wellness services, case management, trauma education and crisis intervention/counseling 7 days a week, free of charge. Funding is requested to support the programs at the Wellness Center that offer support services, wellness classes and crisis support to the continuously grieving Parkland/Coral Springs community in the aftermath of the mass shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School and to others impacted by mass violence in an effort to help them regain a sense of wellness and assist in their recovery.
1045.purpose: Funding will support programs at Eagles' Haven Wellness Center, which offers support services, wellness classes and crisis support to the continuously grieving Parkland community and others impacted by mass violence. The goal is for those impacted by mass violence to regain a sense of wellness and to be connected to support services to assist in their recovery.
1045.activities: Eagles' Haven offers wellness activities, case management, trauma education and crisis intervention. The center is open to the community 7 days a week. The Eagles’ Haven Navigators provide clinical assessment and crisis support while also linking families to needed social or therapeutic services in the community.
1045.direct_services: Wellness Experiences including but not limited to: Pet Therapy, Kickboxing, Exercise classes, Yoga, Tai Chi, Meditation & Mindfulness, Blender Bike Smoothie Making, Drumming Circle, Zumba, Chi Gong, Acupuncture, Aromatherapy, Relaxing with Art, Improv, Open Mic Poetry, Singing, Stretching Classes, Chair Massage, Boot Camp, and Cooking. Navigating Services/Case Management: Our clinicians provide in
1045.population: This program targets anyone impacted by the shooting in Parkland, Florida in 2018 or other incidents of mass violence. While initially aimed at students, parents and teachers in the Parkland/Coral Springs community, the center has expanded to serve anyone suffering from trauma related to mass violence incidents.
1045.outcome: The goal of the project is to improve wellness and restore hope to the Parkland community through the provision of wellness activities and support services. Objectives are as follows and are measured by care plan reviews and satisfaction surveys: 1. 90% of clients will be linked to the appropriate services as determined during assessment and listed on their care plan 2. 85% of clients will meet the wellness goals listed on their care plan

2461.organization: PARC Housing Inc dba Parc Center for
2461.description: Parc Center for Disabilities' Bert Muller Home, built in 1979, has provided care and housing for 48 individuals with developmental disabilities for over 4 decades. For 46 years, this vital home has remained largely unchanged, with no major renovations to its living or community spaces. While the building has served faithfully, the environment now reflects an outdated and institutional style that does not meet the current standards of dignity and comfort that our residents deserve. Through this renovation initiative, we will transform the common and living areas of the Bert Muller Home into a welcoming, modern, and home-like environment. These improvements will elevate daily life for the individuals who live here by fostering a sense of belonging, comfort, and pride in their surrounding. This is more than a renovation. It is an investment in quality of life.

1162.description: The project will accomplish the realignment of the SR 72 (Clark Rd) McIntosh Rd. intersection. The intersection is currently offset and bifurcated by the Legacy Trail. Completing the realignment will resolve the issue of errant vehicles turning down the trail entrance improving the safety of the intersection for all users, motorized and ped/bike, and will mitigate/reduce crashes, aligning with Target Zero goals. FDOT is currently completing the state environmental document for this project. Funding is requested for design, right of way and construction activities.

3080.description: Hurricanes Irene, Milton and Helene substantially damaged the City of Cedar Key and Otter Creek's drinking water supply. This appropriations funding request relocates the drinking water facility off of the island and provides a water transmission system to address potable water quality needs, providing relief to residents a more reliable safe drinking water supply.
3080.purpose: The purpose of this appropriations funding is to design a drinking water plant and potable water distribution system to provide reliably safe drinking water to Cedar Key, Bronson, and Otter Creek.
3080.activities: Geotechnical borings, environmental documentation, professional survey, civil engineering plans for drinking water facility and 32 miles of water transmission line.
3080.direct_services: The direct service being provided to citizens of Cedar Key, Town of Otter Creek and Bronson and surrounding areas is reliable safe drinking water.
3080.population: Target population served by this project include Rosewood/Summer and University Oaks as well as Bronson, Otter Creek, and Cedar Key including a estimated, normalized Cedar Key tourist population (assuming Friday to Sunday occupancy at twice permanent population, normalized on an annual basis) for the planning period 2025-2070. There is an expected 4,241 individuals that will be served by this potable water project.
3080.outcome: The benefit of this project will be safe reliable drinking water for over 4,000 people within the W3C service in Levy County. The outcome will be measured by the volume of water delivered annually to the members of the W3C.

1046.description: There are several sensitive locations throughout the City of Coral Springs. These range from water treatment facilities, City Hall where local, State of Florida, and US Congressmen have offices and utilize community space for meetings, and a public safety building. The city has an initiative to add ballistic film to specific areas at these locations that will allow for greater protection of visitors, employees, and dignitaries – enhancing the overall safety and preventing threats from causing serious injury or death.
1046.purpose: The City of Coral Springs has several sensitive sites, including water treatment facilities, City Hall with offices for state and federal officials, and a public safety building. To enhance safety, the City plans to install ballistic film in key areas, providing greater protection for visitors, employees, and dignitaries while reducing risks of serious injury or death from potential threats.
1046.activities: The city will add ballistic film to specific areas at sensitive locations that will allow for greater protection of visitors, employees, and dignitaries – enhancing the overall safety and preventing threats from causing serious injury or death.
1046.direct_services: Citizens will have increased protection when visiting city buildings. Enhanced security at the water treatment plant will ensure potable water for citizens is protected from contamination.

1046.outcome: The expected benefit is to improve overall safety and prevent threats from causing serious injury or death to the general public. Outcome will be measured by conducting vulnerability/risk assessments before and after installation to quantify reduced exposure.

1209.description: This project will replace the outdated SCADA radio telemetry system used at the City of Coral Springs's (City’s) water treatment plant. The current system has reached an end-of-life and does not support encryption, leaving critical infrastructure vulnerable to potential cyberattacks. A modern, encrypted telemetry system is necessary to secure communication between remote water facilities, treatment processes, and monitoring systems.
1209.purpose: This project will replace the outdated SCADA radio telemetry system used at the City’s water treatment plant. The current system has reached an end-of-life and does not support encryption, leaving critical infrastructure vulnerable to potential cyberattacks. A modern, encrypted telemetry system is necessary to secure communication between remote water facilities, treatment processes, and monitoring systems.
1209.activities: Funds will support purchasing and installing a modern, encrypted SCADA telemetry system at the water treatment plant. Activities include replacing outdated equipment, integrating secure communication between remote facilities and treatment systems, configuring and testing the system, and training staff to operate and maintain it, ensuring protection against cyber threats.

The upgraded SCADA system will prevent cybe-rattacks, ensure continuous monitoring and operation of water treatment processes, and protect public health and the City’s water supply.
1209.population: The target population is the general public. Over 135,000 individuals will be served.
1209.outcome: The expected benefit is to improve security at the water treatment plant and allow for a reduction in system vulnerabilities ensuring resilient water treatment operations. Outcomes will be measured by comparing system logs before and after installation of the SCADA system to ensure secure, continuous communication and prevention of unauthorized access or cyber incidents.

1888.description: The "Central FL Responsible Fatherhood" initiative aims to empower fathers in building nurturing, responsible, and enduring relationships with their children. Through a series of workshops, mentorship programs, and community outreach, we equip dads with the tools to excel in positive parenting, financial literacy, and emotional well-being. Our curriculum emphasizes the vital role that fathers play in child development and family dynamics, stressing the importance of active engagement and open communication. By fostering a network of support among fathers, we work to create more stable and enriching home environments for children. Strong dads are the cornerstone of happy, successful families.
1888.purpose: The Responsible Fatherhood program aims to enhance fathers' participation in their children's lives through workshops, mentorship, and support groups. The aims to decrease delinquency and lower the risk of children entering the criminal justice system & enhance education. Research has shown that children from single-parent households are more likely to be involved in the criminal justice system, as per "Fragile Families and Child Wellbeing Study" (FFCWS) by Princeton and Columbia University.

Financial Management, Employment Assistance, Health & Wellness, Social & Emotional Support services, to provide fathers with the support needed to be successful.
1888.population: The targeted population is single parent families, young fathers, single parent fathers, nuclear families, economically disadvantage families & fathers, at-risk youth and young adults, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, military veterans and divorcees. The total # of individuals to be served is approximately 175.

2023.organization: Palm Beach County Board of County
2023.description: The CR 880 Bridge Replacements Project will construct a new bridge to replace the existing 80+ year old CR 880 Bridge over the SFWMD C-51 Canal, a narrow 2-lane truss bridge that has been classified as structurally deficient and functionally obsolete. The Sam Senter Road Bridge at CR 880 has been classified as structurally deficient and functionally obsolete. This project will replace that bridge with a new concrete bridge and will reconstruct a small portion of CR 880 to mitigate impacts of muck/organic materials.
2023.purpose: This funds requested will be utilized to construct new concrete bridges to replace 2 functionally obsolete and structurally deficient bridges in rural western Palm Beach County.
2023.activities: The funds will be used for construction of two (2) new bridges and improvement of CR 880 adjacent to the bridge. Work will include maintenance of traffic, clearing and grubbing, existing bridge removal, limited canal reshaping, new bridge construction, installation of drainage structures and pipe as needed, and construction of new roadway utilizing the rigid inclusion methodology to stabilize the muck/organic materials located beneath CR 880 at Sam Senter Road.
2023.direct_services: The bridges that will be replaced are important links to both CR 880 and surrounding roads in the Glades area that are heavily utilized by the agricultural farms to transport crops from farms to processing facilities, packing facilities and ultimately to market for purchase and consumption by both local citizens and larger markets.
2023.population: Replacement of the bridges serves the overall travelling public both in and through the Glades, with heaviest population use expected by the agricultural community and businesses.
2023.outcome: The expected benefit of the bridge replacements assures safe travel and passage by the traveling public. Replacing both functionally obsolete and structurally deficient existing bridges with new larger, wider bridges allows for safe passage of both passenger vehicles and large agricultural trucks, which should result in reduced accidents in the area. This will be monitored through the collection and analysis of accident reports and traffic data that includes traffic volumes, capacity analysis, and turning movements (where applicable).

1080.description: The proposed project will upgrade an existing stormwater pump station that is a critical component to providing flood protection for a large portion of the community that makes up the project impact area. The effort will include both the hardening of the facility against the increasing threats of flooding, high winds, and power loss, as well as enhancements to the operating capacity of the station to meet the growing impacts of severe weather. The Village is requesting financial assistance to replace and upgrade unreliable, inefficient, and aging equipment and technology at Pump Station 3. In addition to the hardening of the facility's building, the replacement and upgrade of critical systems, including emergency power, control devices, and trash rakes, will ensure that the Village is able to provide effective flood protection for tens of thousands of residents and many critical assets a
1080.purpose: The project will upgrade an existing stormwater pump station that is a critical component to providing flood protection for hundreds of structures within the community. The effort will improve the infrastructure against the increasing threats of flooding, high winds, and power loss and enhance the operating capacity of the stations to provide effective stormwater management for tens of thousands of people.
1080.activities: The requested funding will be used to improve and harden Pump Station #3. Funding will assist with the construction, including replacement of the emergency generator, trash rake system, and doors at the facility. In addition, electric upgrades will further harden the critical infrastructure and provide long-term flood protection.
1080.direct_services: The project will provide stormwater management and flood protection for a large portion of the community. The project will result in more effective drainage and protect the health, property, and emergency response for tens of thousands of people and hundreds of businesses.
1080.population: The project will benefit a large portion of the Village of Wellington. It is anticipated that over 10,000 people will be impacted by the project.
1080.outcome: The project will provide protection and increase the capability of critical drainage facilities from increasing threats of severe weather, such as a hurricane. Through mitigation efforts, the pump station will be more reliable and effective as the frequency of high-intensity rainfall increases. This effort will allow the facility to operate at full capacity during and after a storm, protecting the project impact area from flooding. The outcome can be measured by the reduction of the impacts of significant rain events, including property damage and disruption of emergency services.

1893.purpose: The project will construct a 1.6-mile multi-use trail and 0.24-mile sidewalk segment along Binion Road, providing safe and continuous pedestrian and bicycle connectivity between Camp Wewa, Lust Road Trailhead, and Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive. The goal is to improve multimodal safety, expand recreational access, and enhance stormwater quality through sustainable design.
1893.activities: Activities include final permitting, construction of trail and sidewalk facilities, installation of pedestrian railings and signage, stormwater improvements using an exfiltration trench, and site restoration. Services include construction administration, quality assurance testing, and compliance documentation under FDOT Local Agency Program procedures.
1893.direct_services: The project will directly provide a safe, ADA-compliant corridor for walking, biking, and recreation. It will improve access to parks, schools, and natural areas while promoting health, safety, and connectivity for residents and visitors. The improvements will reduce pedestrian and bicycle conflicts with vehicular traffic along Binion Road.
1893.population: The project serves residents, students, seniors, visitors, and recreational users throughout northwest Apopka. It is expected to benefit approximately 10,000 to 15,000 people annually, including local trail users, school groups, and Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive visitors. Over 100,000 people visit the SJRWMD's Wildlife Drive and this project will connect those visitors to a network of trails thereby increasing eco-tourism opportunities.
1893.outcome: The project will result in safer, continuous, and ADA-compliant pedestrian and bicycle access along Binion Road, connecting residents to parks, trailheads, and Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive. Outcomes will be measured by completion of 1.6 miles of new multi-use trail and 0.24 miles of sidewalk meeting FDOT and ADA standards; reduction in pedestrian and bicycle conflicts along Binion Road (measured through crash data comparison from before and after construction); increased public use and connectivity, tracked through trail counters and City Parks visitation records and; improved stormwater quality, verified through post-construction inspection and exfiltration trench performance reports.

Each month, CPP publishes and distributes free of charge an 8 page, 4 color newsprint paper full of 300–500 word stories, at a 6th grade level. The articles feature narratives about paintings, photography, landmarks, celebrities, political figures, literature, historical events, documents and monuments, cultural folktales, finance, and science. CPP capitalizes upon the power of story to enable those who experience incarceration to rewrite the script of their lives that results in desistance from crime and physical, psychological, and social flourishing. CPP interrupts the destiny of doom that governs the aftermath of poor decisions, failure, abuse, trauma, deprivation, and isolation. CPP’s programmatic intervention fosters hope, self-confidence, agency, and cultur

2810.activities: CPP will compose, edit, curate, publish, translate into Spanish, and distribute English and Spanish editions of CPP to each of FDOC’s facilities. CPP will continue to form community partnerships with other nonprofits, educational institutions, and others to strengthen the paper, its reach, and the overall work. CPP will make its research findings available to FDOC and other partner organizations.
2810.direct_services: CPP will provide copies of its paper to those incarcerated and formerly incarcerated. CPP will keep regular contact with the chaplains/librarians to gather data, offer support, and meet specific needs. CPP will conduct research regarding the efficacy of the paper (including prison visits and analyzing letters as qualitative feedback) and use the findings to improve effectiveness. But CPP also serv
2810.population: Currently and formerly incarcerated people constitute the primary population. At a minimum, CPP will impact 23,100 each month housed in FDOC prisons. Over the course of the year CPP will distribute a minimum of 277,200 papers. But that is but the beginning. CPP will also impact other populations—those in forensic hospital suffering mental illness, at-risk youth in the juvenile justice detention, those in participating in parole and probation, prison camps, reentry, and those housed in county jai
2810.outcome: 1) CPP fosters hope and confidence among the incarcerated. Hope and confidence bring light into otherwise dismal futures. Hope and confidence are empirically proven components of a self-efficacy that leads to post incarceration resistance from crime. Hope and confidence break the vicious cycle that leads from prison right back to prison. 2) CPP enables those incarcerated to imagine a new script for their lives, reject a destiny of doom and embrace a narrative of redemption. 3) Because CPP provisions a cultural literacy, CPP enables a cultural confidence and competency that leads to social flourishing. 2676.description: Walkabouts are on-demand adventures that transform math, language arts, and reading content into short, movement- rich activities for PreK to 5th grade students. This evidence based online tool makes it easy for teachers and parents to create lessons that bring key concepts to life through physical activity. Walkabouts correlate to FL state standards teachers already use to develop lessons.~400 Florida schools (400,000 students) will receive a 12 month license to use Walkabouts.
2676.purpose: The kinesthetic learning preference is often overlooked in the classroom setting. All children benefit from movement and physical activity; however, many children need to move as they learn. Walkabouts provides those students a resource to do just that. Research on Walkabouts demonstrates that the more kids move, there are fewer behavior problems, less hyperactivity and more academic engagement.
2676.activities: Each school will receive an unlimited 12 month license for Walkabouts at school and unlimited access to the program for each student at home. With the funding requested and the match over 400,000 prek-5th grade students will be served (approximately 400 Florida Elementary Schools). Funds include professional development for all teachers and full on-boarding and technical implementation training.
2676.direct_services: Approximately 400 elementary schools (400,000 students) will each receive a 12 month license. Each student will also have unlimited access to the Walkabouts platform at home.
2676.population: Walkabouts is an on-line platform housed in the cloud; there is no software to download. The platform provides lessons for PreK-5th gr. students in English Language Arts, Math, Social Studies and Science that specifically correlate to FL standards. The platform provides an alternative movement guide for students with physical limitations to ensure all can participate. Home access is included too.
2676.outcome: Evidenced from Iowa State University and UC Irvine validate that students using Walkabouts can expect to increase focus, decrease hyperactivity and increase academic engagement. These specific educational outcomes/benefits are significant predictors of academic performance. Academic progress and individual grades are examined. The independent evaluation team that has already validated the platform surveys teachers each quarter to evaluate learning effectiveness. Additionally, the evaluators develop teacher case studies and administer focus groups to measure the impact of the platform on student learning.

1006.description: DAV, Chapter 32 is the oldest and most active chapter in Brevard County ranking 6th largest among Florida's 67 counties. Our Chapter has been supporting veterans and families since 1947. With over 2,100 current members and growing a service catchment of 65,900 veterans including spouses & dependents approx.150,000, yet our building built in 1961 accommodates only 25 people safely. We seek funds to construct an accessible, modern facility at 2265 N Harbor City Blvd, Melbourne, FL, including new offices, a commercial kitchen, meeting spaces, and monument area upgrades. Services supported: all core DAV programs, medical transportation, job fairs, legislative resolutions, special event dinners, bingo, community volunteer programs, outreach, and local meeting, event's, rentals to other veteran organizations.
1006.purpose: Build a modern, fully accessible DAV facility to double service capacity, reduce waiting times, host all core programs (claims, counseling, volunteer, job fair, transport, resolutions), and provide space for community events and allied veteran group use.
1006.activities: VA claims assistance, medical transportation, outreach, counseling, job fairs, legislative resolution work, volunteer programs, special events, bingo, meeting/event rental to VFW/American Legion/etc.
1006.direct_services: Claims counseling, medical transport, job search, transition support, legislative advocacy, referrals, social events.
1006.population: 65,900 veterans, including 150,000 spouses and dependents just in Brevard County; expected to serve over 2,100 members a year directly and reach thousands more through outreach.
1006.outcome: Track increase in people assisted, reduced waitlists, event attendance, annual survey data, resolution output, and program statistics pre- vs. post-construction.

1005.description: Replacement of the current Pathology Clinic and Tissue Lab housed in a building constructed in 1940, located in the Tropical Research Center at the University of Florida Institute of Food and Agriculture in Homestead, FL. The Clinic/Lab is the only facility in the State of Florida solely dedicated to identification of plant pests and pathogens of tropical fruits, tropical vegetables and tropical ornamental plants. It offers growers immediate on-site diagnostics and solutions of samples they bring in, the equivalent of a highly specialized emergency room. The present building cannot support additional bio-safe cabinets due to lack of space, electrical capacity and HVAC limitations. These cabinets are needed to isolate plant pathogens and tissue samples for analysis. Vital diagnostic work is being constrained due to this limitation. Renovation is not possible due to the age and dilapidated
1005.purpose: Build a plant pathology clinic and tissue lab at the UF/IFAS Tropical Research and Education Center in Homestead.
1005.activities: Develop and disseminate science-based information about tropical horticulture and natural resource sciences through basic and applied research, extension, and teaching; provide pest and disease detection for ornamentals, tropical fruits, and vegetables; and conduct essential research into water, soil, and marine ecosystems for the Biscayne Aquifer and the Everglades.
1005.direct_services: Protect and improve the regional agricultural and local economy; protect and enhance natural resources; and manage invasive species at the gateway of exotics into the U.S.

3664.description: The historic downtown Arcadia area suffers from frequent flooding and standing water due to inadequate stormwater drainage, a longstanding issue across much of the city. The City is undertaking a green infrastructure project covering approximately 2,000 linear feet, including portions of Oak Street and segments of Monroe and Polk Avenues. The project includes the installation of rain gardens to capture runoff, permeable paving drains to allow water infiltration, and bioswales to slow and filter stormwater. The requested fund will be used for design and construction.
3664.purpose: The requested funds will be used to design and construct a green infrastructure project in historic downtown Arcadia. The goal of the project is to address frequent flooding and standing water caused by inadequate stormwater drainage. Specifically, the project will install permeable paving drains, and bioswales to manage and filter stormwater runoff.
3664.activities: Engineering and Design Services: Development of detailed plans and specifications for the green infrastructure elements, including rain gardens, permeable paving systems, bioswales, and street tree placement. Construction Activities: Installation of approximately 2,000 linear feet of green infrastructure improvements along Oak Street and parts of Monroe and Polk Avenues
3664.direct_services: Flood Mitigation and Drainage Improvement: Residents and businesses in the historic downtown area will benefit from reduced flooding and standing water, improving property protection and reducing storm-related disruptions. Improved Public Safety and Accessibility: By eliminating pooling water and enhancing drainage, sidewalks and streets will become safer and more accessible for pedestrians, cycli
3664.population: Residents and businesses in the historic downtown area.
3664.outcome: Reduced flooding and standing water Improved stromwater quality Enhanced public safety and accessibility More liveable downtown

2680.description: Builders Care will be reroofing homes for low-income, elderly, veterans, and disabled individuals who are otherwise unable to afford repairs and eventually have to leave their homes due to condemnation. We will also be building home- access ramps for low-income, elderly, veterans, and disabled individuals who are otherwise isolated and unable to leave their homes. Many of Builders Care's disabled clients haven't been outside of their homes in one to two years due to their inability to safely leave their home since they have no home-access ramp. Builders Care currently has 200 people on their reroof waitlist, and the waitlist for home-access ramps has 141 people on it, which show the massive need in our community for these services.
2680.purpose: Reroofing homes for low-income, elderly, veterans, and disabled individuals who are otherwise unable to afford repairs and eventually have to leave their homes due to condemnation. We will also be building home-access ramps for low- income, elderly, veterans, and disabled individuals who are otherwise isolated and unable to leave their homes.
2680.activities: Builders Care will repair/replace approximately 20 roofs for individuals in need. Builders Care will also build approximately 20 home-access ramps for those in need with these funds.
2680.direct_services: Citizens who have demonstrated their financial need through three months of bank statements will receive roof repairs or replacements free of charge since they'll otherwise be unable to afford the work. Home-access ramps will be provided to those who can prove their financial need and who have documentation of a permanent disability.
2680.population: Target populations are: Elderly persons, economically disadvantaged persons, developmentally disabled, and physically disabled. About 40 individuals will be served.
2680.outcome: The roof will be fully repaired (weather-tight). This will benefit residents by allowing them to stay in their homes, stopping leaks which cause mold and mildew, as well as preventing ceiling collapses. An ADA-compliant home-access ramp will be fully constructed allowing safe entry and exit of their home. This will improve physical and mental health by allowing once-isolated individuals to have independence. Also, the lifting of these massive cost burdens from these individuals will allow them to both stay in their homes longer and to be able to focus all money on their self-sufficiency. It will also allow them the option to begin working again if they want (especially for home-access ramps)

1033.description: The BayCare Hospital Manatee Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) Level II has 8 beds, doubling the number of neonatal intensive care beds in Manatee County. The goal is to provide advanced and expert care for sick neonates, premature babies born at 30 weeks, and those recovering from other serious conditions.

This NICU doubles the amount of neonatal intensive care beds in Manatee County. NICUs have a compounding positive health care effect that enhances care in the county for women and children as well as neonates. Placing a NICU in a hospital stimulates access to preconceptions services, maternal fetal medicine, developmental care services, and many other pediatric subspecialties. Additionally, as part of a large health care system,
1033.population: The NICU will serve an estimated 134 patients and their families per years after a 5-year ramping up. Additionally, the NICU will enhance services for the nearly 1300 newborn patients expected annually after 5 years.

TGhis will be measured by the number of NICU discharges in Manatee County annually. Secondary benefits include the number of high-risk pregnancies that are cared for in Manatee County due to the presence of beds that can support that care.
