1010.organization: Cuban American Bar Association Pro Bono
1010.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
1010.description: CABA Pro Bono’s Special Needs Legal Assistance Program provides free legal services to neurodivergent individuals with developmental and intellectual disabilities and their families regarding the legal mechanisms necessary for a parent or caregiver to continue to support their child’s decision-making in key areas such as medical, financial, and education after the child’s eighteenth birthday. The Program provides alternatives to traditional legal guardianships for individuals that require decision-making support but are still able to make some decisions over their daily lives. The Program assists a vulnerable population of our community with the necessary legal documentation, court proceedings, and support required to exercise the fundamental right to seek and retain employment, access medical care, and pursue education.
1010.purpose: This amount will be used to help cover court fees and other litigation costs including Court reporters, translators, and process servers. This amount will also be used to help cover parking, telephone/internet, and office supplies.
1010.activities: Attorneys and paralegals employed by CABA Pro Bono for this Program, will conduct outreach, legal educations presentations on the relevant legal topics, legal Counsel and Advice, legal document/form preparation and direct legal representation to neurodiverse individuals and their families.
1010.direct_services: CABA Pro Bono’s legal services include not only guardian advocate petitions and proceedings but also the preparation of power of attorney forms, designation of healthcare surrogate forms, privacy waivers for healthcare and education as well as supported decision making agreements.
1010.population: This project serves: economically disadvantageous persons, at-risk youth, developmentally disabled persons. With the expectation to serve between 200-400 citizens.
1010.outcome: This project will help to cover court costs and litigation fees for disadvantaged citizens to provide quality representation.

1180.description: Modeling efforts completed for the IRL National Estuary Program and Canaveral Port Authority indicate that natural circulatory flow in the Banana River is disrupted by earthen causeways and contributes to poor water quality and algae blooms. A US Army Corps of Engineers Feasibility Study will analyze how much the 528 causeway contributes to degraded water quality, habitat, flora and fauna. If found "feasible," federal legislation in WRDA Section 206 provides 65% federal cost share up to $15 million to construct ecosystem restoration projects that improve circulation to reestablish habitat and passage for fish and wildlife. FDOT agreed to convert the road to low span bridges allowing for causeway removal, where found to be feasible.
1180.purpose: The goal is to improve understanding of the relationship between circulatory flow, water quality, algae blooms, seagrass cover and marine life in the northern Banana River, the most impaired section of the Indian River Lagoon ecosystem. This knowledge will be applied to federally funded solutions - removing sections of man-made causeway to improve circulation and foster natural recovery of ecosystem services.
1180.activities: Alternatives will be fully developed in the Integrated Feasibility Report and National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) assessment. Management measures will be refined and combined to form conceptual alternatives. Alternatives will be screened by evaluation criteria to demonstrate each alternative’s effectiveness in meeting project objectives. Additionally, the feasibility study will analyze sea level change (SLC) and qualitatively assess how the SLC rates impact project benefits for all applicab
1180.direct_services: The implementation of the selected alternative will allow for the reestablishment and self-generation of seagrass beds and the water flow within the Banana River creating a healthier ecosystem for fish, foraging manatees, other marine life and human use.
1180.population: The Brevard population is 660,000 however many tourists also enjoy using the Indian River Lagoon.
1180.outcome: The feasibility study will determine the best alternative for improving lagoon health by modifying the 528 causeway. Implementation of the selected alternative will allow for the reestablishment and self-generation of seagrass beds and water flow within the Banana River, creating a healthier ecosystem.

1181.description: This project will upgrade at least 300 septic systems posing the highest threat to Indian River Lagoon water quality in terms of nutrient and pathogen loading. Grants will be offered to homeowners who upgrade to nitrogen-reducing NSF- certified aerobic treatment units or In-ground Nitrogen Reducing drainfields. State grant funding will be used to fund up to $10,000 for each septic upgrade. The Save Our Indian River Lagoon program will provide up to $10,000, for maximum homeowner eligibility of $20,000/property.
1181.purpose: The ultimate goal of this project is to improve water quality of the Indian River Lagoon by reducing the amount of nitrogen and phosphorus pollution from household wastewater that enters groundwater through septic drainfields. By reducing this nutrient pollution, groundwater which makes its way to the Indian River Lagoon will not fuel new algae blooms or exacerbate ongoing blooms. Bloom conditions reduce water clarity and decrease dissolved oxygen, contributing to seagrass loss and fish kills.
1181.activities: Septic contractors will replace existing conventional septic systems with advanced septic systems that meet NSF 245 wastewater standards for nitrogen reduction. Septic upgrades and site restoration will take place on private properties with the consent of owners who volunteer to participate in the program. The first 300 applicants who are located outside of current or planned sewer service areas will be offered funding. Over 60,000 septic systems remain within the watershed of the Indian River L
1181.direct_services: Brevard County will provide funds for qualified septic contractors to upgrade conventional septic system to advanced treatment septic systems on private property. Funds will cover the costs associated with abandonment of deactivated septic systems and planning, permitting, and installation of the new system. Individual funding amounts will be based on each particular septic parcel's modeled nitrog
1181.population: At least 300 owners of conventional septic systems in Brevard County will be served. The highest priority sites within the Indian River Lagoon watershed in Brevard County are older, waterfront properties where sewer service is not available, septic systems installed in close proximity to surface waters, and in sandy high-conductance soils with shallow depth to groundwater. Targeted priorities include high-density, 1950s to 1960s single family homes, mobile home parks and recreational vehicle lot
1181.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is a reduction of up to 1,125 pounds of nitrogen, though total nitrogen reductions could be as high as 7,000 pounds depending on specific properties that apply. The success of the program may be measured by the number of participants, the estimated reduction in nitrogen loading, and performance data from measuring the groundwater at a subsample of participating sites.

1021.description: The City of Cocoa Beach (City) is seeking funding to relocate and rebuild Fire Station #50 in North Cocoa Beach. The proposed project involves constructing a resilient, minimalistic two-story facility. The ground floor will house three engine bays to accommodate modern firefighting apparatus, while the second floor will include administrative offices, living quarters, and essential support spaces for on-duty personnel. Funding is critical to replace the aging and undersized existing station, which no longer meets current safety standards or operational needs. This investment will significantly improve emergency response times, enhance firefighter safety, and ensure reliable service to the growing North Cocoa Beach community.
1021.purpose: Cocoa Beach Fire Station 50 is 63 years old and only 2,600 sq ft, it is significantly undersized for modern fire service operations. Its outdated infrastructure compromises firefighter safety and operational readiness. Living quarters are exposed to engine exhaust, facility lacks a decontamination area and gender-specific rooms. Relocating the station would provide a larger more resilient facility—improve response times—especially for water rescues ensuring it meets today’s public safety standar
1021.activities: Relocating and rebuilding the Fire Station will create a more resilient, strategically positioned and operationally efficient facility. The new station will be constructed to modern building standards ensuring it can withstand severe weather events and continue to operate during any natural disasters, an essential capability in a coastal community ultimately saving lives and reducing property damage.
1021.direct_services: It will enable faster emergency medical response, improved fire suppression and rescue operations, and quicker access to the beach for water rescues. The station will also serve as a critical operations center during hurricanes and natural disasters, ensuring uninterrupted service when it’s needed most. The station will offer multiple services strengthening public safety and community engagement.
1021.population: This project will serve the more than 11,000 residents of Cocoa Beach, as well as the approximately 2.5 million tourists who visit annually. Additionally, through an automatic aid agreement, the City of Cocoa Beach (City) provides mutual support to neighboring communities, including Cape Canaveral and Merritt Island, further extending the regional impact of this critical infrastructure investment.
1021.outcome: The success of the new fire station will be measured through improved emergency response times—projected to decrease by up to two minutes. Emergency Response Time Reduction: Response times will be tracked and compared to current benchmarks, with a projected improvement of up to two minutes, as identified by the International City/County Management Association (ICMA) Center for Public Safety Management.

1009.description: The goal of this project is to replace the community's 58-year-old fire station and upgrade the City of Indian Harbour Beach's (City) capability to respond to emergencies within their jurisdiction and support responses to that of the surrounding barrier island communities. The new annex would allow for the City to shift from its current fire station that is housed in facility previously used as a recreation center. The new annex would allow for sleeping quarters to support 24- hour services, as well as accommodations for laundry and decontamination. The new annex would include upgrades for storm-hardening to reduce the likelihood of damage from natural disasters.
1009.purpose: The goal of this project is to replace the community's 58-year-old fire station and upgrade the City's capability to respond to emergencies within their jurisdiction and support responses to that of the surrounding barrier island communities. The new annex would allow for the City to shift from its current fire station that is in facility previously used as a recreation center. The project would include upgrades for storm-hardening to reduce the likelihood of damage from natural disasters.
1009.activities: The current station is not capable of providing overnight accommodation or necessary health and safety amenities for our emergency responders. This has been identified as a critical need to support recruitment and retention of our volunteer firefighting personnel. This will markedly improve our response time to emergencies by allowing first responders to remain at the fire station overnight.
1009.direct_services: A modern facility provides the base of operations for functional living and community spaces to recruit younger generations, accommodate volunteers during all shifts, provide for community engagement and adequate training areas to foster continual education and skill development, all of which directly support improved response and mitigation of emergency incidents and citizen requests for service.
1009.population: The approximately 8,900 residents of the City and visitors to the community.
1009.outcome: Increased response time to calls for service and increased safety for fire department personnel who are required to shelter in place during hurricanes.

2820.organization: DBWP, Inc. d/b/a Delores Barr Weaver Policy
2820.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General

CCM reduces suspension rates for girl in elementary school, stops the revolving door of girls cycling in and out of the justice system and serves survivor/victims of commercial sexual exploitation. CCM has proven, the right services result in girls receiving needed support in their community, saving the state significant dollars by preventing girls who do not pose a public safety risk from being committed to costly residential commitment programs. An investment of $700,000 supports direct services, support and the signature Girl-Centered Practice stakeholder training. This provides intensive services for 70 girls; skills building groups for 90 girls and intensive training for 30 system stakeholders. Since the programs inception, girls incarceration has redu
2820.purpose: The purpose is too (1) increase public safety by reducing risk factors leading to school suspension, and deeper involvement in the juvenile justice system (2) ensuring there are appropriate services for trafficked youth, (3) providing interventions at multiple points to interrupt the pathway for girls justice system involvement (suspension, arrest, detention, probation, court, commitment and re-entry), (4) interrupting pathways to abuse/trauma that leads to girls internalizing (suicide ideation,
2820.activities: 1. Individual/Family Counseling/Intensive Services with focus on root causes of behaviors. 2. Mobile Care Management/Crisis Intervention Staff available 24/7/365 providing real-time services. 3. School Intervention Services including skills building, mentoring, and academic advocacy. 4. Skills Building Groups as a form of community based diversion, support in the juvenile detention center and pre-trial and providing alternatives to school suspension. 5. Transitional Services Assistance with educ
2820.direct_services: Services are designed to improve public safety by addressing the root causes of justice system involvement, school suspension and commercial sexual exploitation. Direct services include, intensive interventions for under served, high need girls/families living in high risk/under-resourced communities. We collaborate with school administration, judges, law enforcement, state attorney, public defend
2820.population: Girls ages 5 to 24 who are at risk of entering the justice system, facing school suspension, or identified as victims of commercial sexual exploitation, and their families, will be served in Duval, Baker, St. Johns, Clay, and Nassau Counties. Intensive, individualized services will be provided to 70 girls, while an additional 90 girls will benefit from group services offered at detention centers, teen court, pre-trial services, in schools or high-need after-school programs. Additionally, 30 stak
2820.outcome: 1. Reduced rates of school suspension and expulsion: 85% will not be suspended or expelled from school once they receive services. 2. Reduce Recidivism: 95% of girls served will avoid arrests for new criminal activity after receiving services as evidenced by DBWPC Ongoing Assessment Tool. 3. Access to Resources: 95% of girls will have access and opportunities for needed resources (including education, employment, basic needs, counseling, medical treatment, etc.) as documented in DBWPC Ongoing Assessment Tool. 4. Increased Knowledge and Skills: 95% of stakeholder training participants will report increase in knowledge and skills as a result of participating in Girl-Centered Practice Training.

2937.description: United Ways and their partners will secure donated and/or discounted office space in facilities owned by non-profit, for- profit and governmental partners at which IRS-certified volunteers will help low and moderate income workers complete their federal income tax returns. Site coordinators will be hired to identify, secure and set up the sites, and recruit and help certify volunteer tax preparers. Sites will be offered throughout the state.
2937.purpose: More than 30,000 low-to-moderate income working Floridians will be assisted by the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program, saving these working families and individuals up to $2.7 million in tax preparation fees and generating more than $48 million in total tax returns, $13 million in Earned Income Tax Credits, and an estimated $2.75 million in state and local sales taxes.
2937.activities: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and financial coaching services will be provided to working families and individuals throughout the state. To prepare and offer this service, training is provided to volunteers to achieve IRS certification. Site coordinators identify, secure and set up the sites; and recruit and assist in the training of preparers. United Ways and their partners secure donated office space in facilities owned by their non-profit, for-profit and governmental partners to offe
2937.direct_services: IRS-certified and trained volunteers will provide reliable tax preparation assistance to Florida’s ALICE families, who are low and moderate income workers including veterans, the elderly and the disabled, enabling them to meet tax obligations and receive the highest refund for which they are eligible. Financial coaching services are also made possible.
2937.population: Low-to-moderate income workers - Florida's ALICE population. 34% of Florida’s households are ALICE: Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed — with income above the FPL, but not enough to afford basic expenses in the county where they live.
2937.outcome: $48 million in federal income tax returns for low-to-moderate income working Floridians. This is validated by IRS reports and documentation provided by local United Ways. Outcomes will be quantified primarily through official IRS reports and supplemented with data provided by UW.

1183.description: The funding request is for a multi-basin study of the Maemir/Martin/Fiske Area drainage improvements to study stormwater management options for the area. The project area is currently experiencing issues with localized flooding and inadequate drainage infrastructure. The study will be done in coordination with FDOT and the City of Rockledge.
1183.purpose: The specific goal of the multi-basin study is to evaluate stormwater management options to alleviate flooding issues in the area that occurs during large storm events.
1183.activities: The multi-basin study will include the following: 1. Conducting a field investigation to collect information on the drainage network for the different outfall paths within the designated multi-basin service area. 2. Creation of an existing conditions model to understand current flooding issues, an analysis of the results will show bottlenecks and other issues in the existing drainage system. 3. An efficiency analysis will identify potential solutions to the drainage system and/or provide recomme
1183.direct_services: By completing the multi-basin study, Brevard, FDOT, and the City of Rockledge will better understand the costs associated with the design and construction of the improvements to mitigate flooding occurring after large storm events. The flooding currently occurs over roadways and within private residential properties in the region.
1183.population: The target population to be served by this project will be the residents of the immediate area. Approximately 1000 individuals are expected to be served by the improvements.
1183.outcome: The multi-basin study will aid the County, FDOT and the City of Rockledge in determining costs to alleviate flooding across roadways and residential properties therefore improving the water quality flowing through to the different outfall paths within the designated multi-basin service area

1184.description: The purpose of the project is to improve storm water runoff between Newfound Harbor Drive (NFHD) and Banana River Drive, including up-sizing 11 existing cross drains to triple barrel 36-inch culverts to provide immediate benefits to adjacent areas and collection systems that discharge directly into Pelican Creek. Improvements to NFHD and Fowler Dr include modifying the drainage system and maintaining existing systems. Also proposed is the replacement of the existing pipe trunkline and inlets.
1184.purpose: The purpose of the project is to improve storm water runoff between Newfound Harbor Drive (NFHD) and Banana River Drive. Drainage improvement concepts are based on strategies involving introducing/enhancing pipe collection systems to improve surface drainage.
1184.activities: Activities and services include up-sizing 11 existing cross drains to triple barrel 36-inch culverts to provide immediate benefits to adjacent areas and collection systems that discharge directly into Pelican Creek. Improvements to NFHD and Fowler Dr include modifying the drainage system and maintaining existing systems. Also proposed is the replacement of the existing pipe trunk line and inlets.
1184.direct_services: Residents in the area experience flooding across driveways, by improving storm water runoff in the area, this nuisance flooding may be mitigated.
1184.population: The replacement project targets the general population in the area and will serve approximately 5000 residents and local businesses
1184.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of the project is the replacement and/or upgrades the drainage systems to reach an acceptable level of service for flood control throughout the project area. The outcome will be measured during rainy conditions in the area to determine whether the improvements alleviated flooding by allowing the runoff to flow to existing outfalls.

1284.description: This project is a continuation of an existing FDEP grant to upgrade the 6.0 MGD wastewater treatment train at the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility to Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) in compliance with F.S. 403.086 requiring reclaimed water to be AWT quality. The South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility is located in the Indian River Lagoon Basin Management Action Plan area.
1284.purpose: Reduction in the total nitrogen and total phosphorus loadings within the Indian River Lagoon Basin Management Action Plan area and to bring the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility in compliance with Section 403.086, Florida Statutes.
1284.activities: Conversion of the 6.0 MGD wastewater treatment train at the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility to Advanced Wastewater Treatment.
1284.direct_services: This project will bring this facility to compliance with Section 403.086, Florida Statutes - Provide higher quality reclaim water, reduce the nutrient loading to the Indian River Lagoon Basin Management Action Plan area, and make reuse supply readily available for potential future expansions.
1284.population: Approximately 70,000 residents that are serviced by the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility and approximately 644,000 individuals that live in Brevard County adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon.
1284.outcome: Reduced nutrient loading to the Indian River Lagoon Basin Management Action Plan area will reduce algal blooms and provide a healthier local environment for valuable native species to thrive, improving economic and cultural features of Brevard County. Effluent analysis of the treated wastewater will allow for quantification of the water quality improvement following the upgrade to Advanced Wastewater Treatment.

1285.description: Brevard County operates the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility (SBWWTF) which currently disposes of treated effluent via deep injection well with a backup surface water discharge to the Indian River Lagoon. Recent legislation (2021 FL SB 64; updates to F.S. 403.064) to eliminate surface water discharges to environmentally sensitive waterways require the Grantee to provide for plant redundancy in the event of failure of the existing injection well system.
1285.purpose: Reduce nutrient loading to the Indian River Lagoon by eliminating the need for discharges to the Indian River Lagoon, provide system redundancy, and bring the facility in compliance with 403.064.
1285.activities: Installation of a second deep injection well at the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility.
1285.direct_services: This project will bring this facility in compliance with 403.064, reducing the potential for surface water discharges and nutrient loading to the Indian River Lagoon.
1285.population: Approximately 70,000 residents that are serviced by the South Beaches Wastewater Treatment Facility and approximately 644,000 individuals that live in Brevard County adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon.
1285.outcome: Reduce nutrient loading to the Indian River Lagoon by eliminating the need for surface water discharges to the Indian River Lagoon. Quantification of the reduction in total nitrogen and phosphorus will be based on historical discharges to the Indian River Lagoon during storm events.

1186.description: The funding will be used to fully design the improvements for all phases consisting of upgrading and replacing drainage systems to achieve effective flood control in the Scottsmoor region (Basin IX). The five areas of flooding concern include Aurantia Road, Burkholm Canal, Lawrence, Ravencrest and Shamrock-Bouganvilla. The planning study recommends replacing or adding structures such as culverts, inlets, and weirs, clearing or dredging channels and implementing detention measures where feasible. There is a total of 7 phases projected at $9.3M in construction costs.
1186.purpose: The planning effort completed for the Scottsmoor/Mims North region (Basin IX) in December 2024 indicates that upgrading and replacing drainage systems may mitigate flooding in the area. Designing the improvements in phases will ensure a logical progression for flood mitigation and cost effectiveness.
1186.activities: The funding will be used to fully design the improvements for all phases consisting of upgrading and replacing drainage systems to achieve effective flood control in the Scottsmoor region (Basin IX). The plan includes replacing or adding structures such as culverts, inlets, and weirs, clearing or dredging channels and implementing detention measures where feasible.
1186.direct_services: By completing the design project, Brevard will improve on its study to have shovel ready projects while better understanding the costs associated with the construction of the improvements and refine the logical progression of phases to mitigate flooding occurring after large storm events. The flooding currently occurs over roadways and within private residential properties in the region.
1186.population: The general public residing in the Scottsmoor/Mims North area is the target population to be served by this project.
1186.outcome: The completion of design for the stormwater improvements will aid the County in determining costs to alleviate flooding across roadways and residential properties therefore improving the water quality flowing into the Indian River and will increase resiliency during large storm events. The Indian River is home to over 4000 aquatic species of plants and wildlife.

1049.description: This intersection has experienced vehicular crashes as well as near-miss incidents exacerbated by the growing student loading at the five-year-old Viera Elementary School. Construction will alleviate the traffic concerns at this current emergency temp. all way stop intersection. The project is currently at 100% design and is moving forward without the appropriations by leveraging other project funds. The County is working with the Brevard County School district to complete the signal project this fiscal year.
1049.purpose: This intersection has experienced vehicular crashes as well as near-miss incidents exacerbated by the growing student loading at the five-year-old Viera Elementary School. Construction of the intersection improvements will alleviate the traffic concerns at this current all way stop intersection. The project is currently at 100% design and the project is ready to move forward. The County is working with the Brevard County School district to complete the signal project this fiscal year.
1049.activities: Improvements to the intersection will include a fully signalized intersection at Stadium and Cuddington and will include the addition of ADA compliant sidewalks at the intersection crossings.
1049.direct_services: By constructing the intersection improvements, roadway users will find the intersection to be a safe mode of transportation for those using motor vehicles, buses, and other modes of transportation such as grade school walkers and bikers as well as parents driving a golf carts.
1049.population: The target population are those students and general public that are using the intersection to get to school or traverse the roadway at the intersection.
1049.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is a safe intersection for both pedestrians, active transportation users, and roadway users. This will be measured by a decrease in traffic incidents at the intersection

1086.organization: Space Coast Health Foundation dba Lifetime
1086.description: This project is an expansion of the Thrive Within Program throughout Brevard County and surrounding counties. It is designed to help ensure individuals in our community have timely access to mental health support, while also helping to ameliorate the overload on the mental health system of care. This project will continue to provide prevention and early intervention services to children, adolescents, and adults across the community. We will also continue to provide outpatient mental health and substance abuse counseling for uninsured individuals, who currently have the most difficulty accessing services. By expanding access to prevention and early intervention services and education, as well as outpatient treatment services, we will continue to reduce the need for more expensive higher levels of care such as crisis intervention, inpatient stabilization, and residential treatment.
1086.purpose: The goal of this project is to expand the Thrive Within program throughout Brevard County and to surrounding counties. This program provides prevention and early intervention services, as well as outpatient mental health and substance abuse counseling for uninsured individuals without financial means to pay for services. Continuing to expand the reach of these services will further reduce the need for much more expensive higher levels of care such as crisis intervention, inpatient stabilization,
1086.activities: We will continue to expand prevention and early intervention services throughout Brevard and beyond, as well as providing treatment for uninsured individuals without financial means to pay for services, totaling 4000 hours of service. Activities include mental health/wellness training, psychoeducational groups, monthly lunch-n-learn support, monthly informational newsletter, and expansion of our Thriving Community training program.
1086.direct_services: Direct services include mental health and/or substance abuse treatment, as well as customized mental health/wellness training for the general public and for other professionals, psychoeducational groups, a specialized Thriving Community training/support program for the general public, monthly virtual lunch-n-learn sessions, monthly informational newsletters, and a variety of electronic resources.
1086.population: The target population is the Brevard County community as a whole (all ages), as well as surrounding counties. Total reach will be at least 500,000 people, which includes outpatient counseling services to the uninsured in Brevard County, education/early intervention for Brevard and surrounding counties through multiple communication platforms, including social media, in-person and virtual training, in-person psychoeducational groups, and community partnerships.
1086.outcome: We expect to improve mental health/wellbeing and reduce substance abuse in our community by: 1. Improving community awareness/understanding of mental wellness strategies 2. Improving community awareness/understanding of substance misuse and the connection between substance misuse and mental health challenges 3. Addressing early signs of mental health difficulties/distress 4. Improving healthy coping skills and resiliency 5. Improving the ability of individuals to help one another 6, Reducing the need for referral to higher levels of care We will measure these outcomes by: 1. Tracking the number of participants in community education/training events 2. Completion of pre- and post-tests by tho

1190.description: Recent legislation including Senate Bill 712 mandated the elimination of all surface water discharge of secondary effluent in a Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP). The City of Melbourne is constructing a second deep injection well as an alternative means of secondary effluent disposal for both of Melbourne's water reclamation facilities thus eliminating the need to discharge secondary effluent to the Indian River Lagoon during the required 5-year Mechanical Integrity test of the original well. Also complying with 403.064(17), F.S.
1190.purpose: Senate Bill 712 eliminated the City's permitted surface water discharge of secondary effluent from both of the City's water reclamation facilities during the required 5-year Mechanical Integrity testing on the original injection well. Therefore, a second redundant deep injection well is required to allow for mechanical integrity testing every 5 years.
1190.activities: Activities will include the actual construction of the deep injection well including the well piping and associated pumps, process piping connections and control systems.
1190.direct_services: The citizens are served indirectly through the effective management and disposal of wastewater generated by the community and by the protection of Crane Creek and the Indian River Lagoon.
1190.population: The target population is the community at large.
1190.outcome: The expected outcome is the elimination of potential secondary effluent discharge to the Indian River Lagoon from both of the City's water reclamation facilities and compliance with Senate Bill 712 and 403.064(17), F.S. Elimination of potential discharge will prevent additional nutrient loading that contributes to the deterioration of water quality and negatively impacts aquatic systems in a Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) area. Various government and non- profit agencies monitor the water quality and overall health of the Indian River Lagoon.

1040.description: The goal of this project is to provide a community space for the public to gather in the heart of downtown Melbourne's Historic District. Downtown Melbourne lacks a community gathering place to hold festivals and farmers markets. The re- purposing of this park will include a terraced amphitheater overlooking beautiful Crane Creek, a family play zone including nature inspired materials with shaded seating, a public restroom, and a multi-purpose open plaza area to accommodate up 75 tents for vendors to use for downtown events.
1040.purpose: The project is to provide a community space for the public to gather in the heart of downtown Melbourne's Historic District. Downtown Melbourne lacks a community gathering place to hold festivals and farmers markets. The re- purposing of this park will include a terraced amphitheater overlooking beautiful Crane Creek, a family play zone including nature inspired materials with shaded seating, a public restroom, and a multi-purpose open plaza area to accommodate up 75 tents for vendors to use for
1040.activities: The upgraded park will serve to provide the public with an opportunity with a place to gather passively to enjoy the downtown area or during special events such as the City's Friday Fest music and vendors, food trucks and movie night, farmers markets, family day-long festivals for kids with games, small weddings and photo backdrop opportunities for a multitude of special moments.
1040.direct_services: There are no direct services anticipated to be provided with the appropriation project.
1040.population: The target population is all the citizens of Melbourne of all demographics including neighboring cities and Brevard County, visitors to the downtown and everyone who calls the Space Coast home. The target population is the 30- something home school mom, the retired U.S. Air Force colonel turned storyteller, the school teacher who serves on the City Council, the Late 20's young professionals who are starting out their careers and seek a respite during lunch breaks, or the 80 something retirees wh
1040.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is anticipated to be exponential. The enlarge gathering space will provide a place where residents and tourists can improve mental and physical health, enrich the cultural experience and incentivize tourism in the downtown. Patrons can walk from the park to the adjacent downtown which offers over 230 business activities, including restaurants, theatre, retail shopping. They can relax in with the panoramic views of Crane Creek while enjoying a live show in the small amphitheater. All these benefits can be measured by tracking engagement by counting visitors and participations in the various activities, surveys, feedback sessions, and observatio

1041.description: The Melbourne Fire Department's existing training center has exceeded its useful life and no longer meets the standards for firefighter training. This project will replace the facility with a modern, multi-use training complex that includes a modern burn building with live fire training capabilities, technical rescue and confined space training props, classrooms equipped with modern instructional technology, a command training simulator for officer development, and support facilities (restrooms, storage, SCBA refill stations). The training center will be a regional training center that can be used by other agencies. The request is for the land acquisition and design.
1041.purpose: The Melbourne Fire Department seeks to replace its outdated training center with a modern, multi-functional, regional facility that will meet the needs of today’s fire service and future growth. The current training center is over 30 years old and no longer meets safety, instructional, or operational standards. A new facility will provide a state-of-the-art training environment for over 150 sworn personnel; ensure compliance with NFPA standards and ISO requirements for firefighter training; enha
1041.activities: This facility will provide an area for firefighter recruit training as well as continuing education and skills maintenance for firefighters and officers. Firefighters will have the ability to participate in live fire, technical rescue, and EMS skills training. The space will also be used by law enforcement partners and may have the potential for community safety programs.
1041.direct_services: With the construction of a new fire training facility firefighters have the ability to become better trained and able to provide a quicker and safer response to fires, accidents, and natural disasters thus reducing loss of life, injury, and property damage. Effective training and training spaces provide the department to maintain NFPA standards as well as current a current ISO Rating of 1 that can
1041.population: Primary beneficiaries are the over 150 sworn personnel of the Melbourne Fire Department. The total public impact can span the approximate 87,000 Melbourne residents and over 600,000 residents of Brevard County who will benefit from better prepared emergency responders.
1041.outcome: Over 150 firefighters trained annually to maintain current standards and additional certifications. Documented live fire training will increase at least 40% over current baseline. Anticipated reduction in training related injuries that is measured through safety reports. Maintaining current ISO rating (1) compliant training as well as continued recognition of a State of Florida Light Technical Rescue Team.

1042.description: The City of Melbourne (City) requests funding for a new station alerting system for eight fire stations. The Fire Station Alerting System Upgrade will replace outdated station alerting equipment with a modern, network-based solution that reduces emergency response times, increases reliability, and enhances firefighter safety. The new system will provide redundant communication pathways, integrate with regional Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD), and deliver both audible and visual alerts for improved situational awareness. The new system will include upgraded speakers, visual strobes, message boards, and station automation for eight fire stations.
1042.purpose: The Fire Station Alerting System Upgrade will replace outdated alerting infrastructure with a modern, network-based solution to improve emergency response times, enhance firefighter safety, and increase reliability of dispatch notifications. The project will install redundant systems, visual and auditory alerting, and station automation to ensure rapid turnout.
1042.activities: The requested funds will be used to purchase, install, and implement a modern fire station alerting system that integrates with regional dispatch. This project will provide faster and more reliable emergency notifications through upgraded speakers, visual strobes, message boards, and station automation. The system will be configured, tested, and maintained to ensure 99.9% uptime, while firefighters and dispatchers will receive full training to ensure effective use. These activities will reduce e
1042.direct_services: This project directly benefits the community by reducing emergency response times, which can make a life-saving difference during fires, medical emergencies, and other critical incidents. Faster and more reliable alerting improves the safety of firefighters, ensuring they are better prepared to serve residents. The upgraded system will enhance protection within the department's jurisdiction, while
1042.population: The population of Melbourne is approximately 87,000 with over 150,000 during the day. The Fire Department has experienced an increase in call volume and has exercising as many options as it can to reduce response times to emergencies. Fire Station alerting and traffic preemption are the only remaining efforts that can be made in assisting to keep emergency response times down, outside of placing new apparatus on the streets. 2035.purpose: Place of Hope, Inc. is requesting funding to continue to meet the operational functioning of regional placement needs for Florida's abused and neglected children, victims of human trafficking and otherwise homeless young adults, and child abuse prevention services and support.
2035.activities: The request includes funding for operational functioning expenses associated with our "seamless" provision of programming, housing and therapeutic support for abused and neglected children, sexually exploited adolescent youth, and other victims of human trafficking throughout Florida. The funding request will also help to continue our highly sought Human Trafficking Prevention and Education for at-risk youth and community members.

Place of Hope also provides human trafficking prevention and education for at- risk youth (to recognize potential situations of human t
2035.population: Abused and neglected children are provided necessities, care, and love. Our Child Welfare, Foster Care and Human Services Trafficking Prevention and Education Support Services, child abuse prevention services and support initiative impact victims of human trafficking, children in foster care, at-risk youth and the community at large. Place of Hope will be able to provide for abused and neglected children, homeless youth, and victims of human trafficking. 1109.description: WTP 8 currently does not have an effective treatment process for the removal of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) chemical compounds, which is required by federal law by 2031. Funds secured for this project will: 1. construct a new water treatment plant designed using nanofiltration to reduce emerging contaminants; 2. upgrade aging plant infrastructure; 3. new membrane & electrical room, hurricane hardening, & a new generator for expansion and redundancy to prevent plant disruptions or failures. This project provides process improvements to improve water treatment, reliability, and efficiency to maintain treatment quality and quantity through the next decades. To meet the required timeline of 2031, design needs to occur in 2026. Construction of water plants can take up to 5 years to complete.
1109.purpose: Funding for this project will upgrade WTP 8, a critical infrastructure, to improve water treatment quality, quantity, & reliability for all residents. Clean & safe drinking water is vital to our health, communities, & economy. As the population increases, so does the need for clean water. This project will result in an increase in clean drinking water that meets strict regulatory standards. The requested funds will go towards the design of the facility.
1109.activities: Activities include, but is not limited to: 1. A new water treatment plant will be designed using nanofiltration to comply with drinking water standards; 2. The project includes plant expansion, hurricane hardening, and a new generator for redundancy; and 3. A new membrane and electrical room are required for expansion and redundancy to circumvent disruptions or failures; and 4. Pre-treatment and post-treatment processes, production wells, and pumping systems
1109.direct_services: Safe, reliable and clean drinking water is a direct service and outcome of this project to PBC residents, businesses and visitors. Improvements to WTP 8 will ensure that every household and business has access to quality water that meets required water quality treatment standards.
1109.population: Palm Beach County Water Utilities Department, through its interconnected water treatment plants serve over 641,000 residents. WTP 8 serves 170,000 residents in the following communities who will continue to enjoy access to clean drinking water: Boynton Beach, Greenacres, Town of Hypoluxo, Village of Palm Springs, Royal Palm Beach, West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Loxahatchee Groves and Wellington. As paying customers, the residents expect that the utility provides clean water that meets drin
1109.outcome: Increase in clean drinking water that meets strict regulatory standards. PFAS or "forever chemicals" are classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the the International Agency for Research on Cancer and have been widely found in US drinking water systems. EPA adopted drinking water quality standards for PFAS that water utilities must meet by 2031. Improvements to WTP 8 will comply with federal regulations, which reduces levels of PFAS. Nanofiltration, one of the most effective approaches for PFAS treatment, will be utilized. Water quality data will be measured, monitored and publicly made available.

1048.description: EFSC is requesting $3.3 million from the state to match the $3.3 million dollar request to Congress (via Congressman Mike Haridopolos) to provide the $6.6 million needed to relocate and expand the educational opportunities in preventative dental care. Currently, the existing 7,000' dental area is inadequate to produce the number of dental hygienists and dental assistants needed on Florida's Space Coast. The relocation of the program into a larger available space (13,000') in another building on the same campus will allow EFSC to double if not triple the number of graduates being introduced to the workforce.
1048.purpose: Eastern Florida State College will be better able to provide the necessary number of graduates in the dental hygiene and dental assisting programs to help meet the critical workforce needs in dental care on Florida's Space Coast.
1048.activities: The current small size of the existing dental education programs only affords the opportunity of producing a fraction of the student graduates needed to meet the workforce needs required by the dental profession. By moving the program into a larger area in another building will allow EFSC to increase the number of students being simultaneously served resulting in doubling if not tripling the number of formally trained dental hygienists and dental assistance available to meet current workforce ne
1048.direct_services: One of the excellent benefits to the community in addition to ensuring the dental profession has the trained human resources they need, is the direct dental care services this program provides to the community. The EFSC dental programs offers exceptional low and no-cost services (teeth cleanings, sealants, etc.) to the citizens, especially seniors and children who cannot afford professional dental
1048.population: The entire Space Coast of Florida will greatly benefit by ensuring our many dental offices have the trained and certified human resources they need to serve their clients. Florida's Space Coast has been enjoying great success with new and expanding companies as a result of the growth our aerospace and high tech industries. Unfortunately, that growth is being impeded by not having an adequate number of dental health care professionals available to serve them.
1048.outcome: There will be two objective measures which can be employed to track the success of this request. First, the number of program graduates entering the workforce is expecting to double. Second, the citizens being served by this program directly are also expected to double.

1187.description: The City of Cocoa is seeking funding to replace septic systems with a modern gravity sewer system for 88 single-family homes along Indian River Drive, aiming to protect the Indian River Lagoon. This initiative will connect these homes to the City’s existing sewer network, reducing pollution and improving water quality in the lagoon, which supports five state parks, four federal wildlife refuges, and the national seashore. Aging septic systems contribute to nutrient pollution for the lagoon.
1187.purpose: The City of Cocoa is seeking funding to replace septic systems with a modern gravity sewer system for 88 single- family homes along Indian River Drive, aiming to protect the Indian River Lagoon. This initiative will connect these homes to the City’s existing sewer network, reducing pollution and improving water quality in the lagoon, which supports five state parks, four federal wildlife refuges, and the national seashore. Aging septic systems contribute to nutrient pollution for the lagoon.
1187.activities: The funding will cover expenses associated with extending the existing sewer pipe connection and then connecting the homes in the project area to the new sewer pipe to remove the reliance to the aging septic tanks. This will be a direct benefit to those residents within the service area but also to the entire region when the nutrient load to the lagoon is reduced.
1187.direct_services: Removal of reliance on aging septic tanks that leech harmful nutrients to the Indian River Lagoon.
1187.population: The general public to include residents and business owners along the roadway and tourists to the area. This project will directly impact hundreds of thousands of individuals that will utilize the Indian River Lagoon.
1187.outcome: Improve environmental quality by reducing nutrient loads to the lagoon and preventing harmful algal blooms which can be measured through water quality testing. This will also increase economic activity, tourism and create specific immediate job opportunities.

1575.description: This critical infrastructure improvement project is a critical infrastructure project that will link State Road 501 (Clearlake Road) to the future Cocoa Brightline Multi-modal Station. It is essential to integrate the station with our existing roadway network, ensuring efficient commuter access, economic development, and regional mobility, setting the foundation for future transit-oriented development, and ensuring the long-term success of the Cocoa Multi-modal Station.
1575.purpose: This is a critical infrastructure project that will link State Road 501 (Clearlake Road) to the future Cocoa Brightline Multi-modal Station. It is essential to integrate the station with our existing roadway network, ensuring efficient commuter access, economic development, and regional mobility, setting the foundation for future transit-oriented development, and ensuring the long-term success of the Cocoa Multi-modal Station.
1575.activities: Create a functional and efficient transportation link between Clearlake Road (SR 501) and the future Cocoa Brightline Multimodal Station. The investment will establish a critical connector, reduce local congestion, increase station accessibility, and support broader multimodal infrastructure goals.
1575.direct_services: Funding this project will provide direct access to high-speed rail services for Cocoa residents by connecting Clearlake Road to the future Cocoa Brightline Multimodal Station, enabling easier travel to Orlando and South Florida. It will also improve local mobility, traffic flow, and safety through the addition of a modern roadway, sidewalks, and multimodal access.
1575.population: The general public to include residents and business owners along the corridor and tourists riding the Brightline Train. This expansion will directly impact hundreds of thousands of individuals that will utilize this corridor.
1575.outcome: This project will improve transportation to the future multi-modal station, it will increase economic activity, increase tourism and create immediate job opportunities. These benefits can be measured through traffic counts, economic activity, visitor counts and job data.

1188.description: The purpose of this project is to connect Stradley Park to the City of Cocoa’s sewer system to replace the existing septic system, which often cannot handle the high demand during community sporting events. This improvement will enhance public health, safety, and environmental protection by eliminating septic overflows. Additionally, extending the sewer connection will support the park’s continued growth and ensure reliable infrastructure for future recreational use.
1188.purpose: The purpose of this project is to connect Stradley Park to the City of Cocoa’s sewer system to replace the existing septic system, which often cannot handle the high demand during community sporting events. This improvement will enhance public health, safety, and environmental protection by eliminating septic overflows. Additionally, extending the sewer connection will support the park’s continued growth and ensure reliable infrastructure for future recreational use.
1188.activities: The project will include engineering design, permitting, and construction activities. Services will include installation of new sewer pipelines, potential lift stations, and proper abandonment of the existing septic systems. These improvements will ensure reliable wastewater service for park users and support ongoing recreational activities without interruption.
1188.direct_services: Funding this project will provide citizens with improved sanitation and reliable wastewater services. It will eliminate septic system failures that can disrupt events, ensuring a cleaner and safer environment for players, families, and visitors. This upgrade will enhance the overall experience at the park by supporting uninterrupted recreational activities and promoting public health.
1188.population: The general public to include residents in the surrounding communities and throughout Brevard County that utilize that park.
1188.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, protect the general public from harm, improve environmental quality, and improve wastewater management and groundwater quality. All of which can be measured through water quality testing.

1189.description: The goal of the proposed project is to improve water quality in the Indian River Lagoon by installing baffle boxes with filter media along stormwater basin outfalls in the City of Cocoa. These structures will capture and treat stormwater runoff, significantly reducing nitrogen, phosphorus, and suspended solids before discharge into the lagoon. Overall, the project aims to enhance the lagoon’s health by retrofitting existing drainage systems to remove pollutants efficiently and sustainably.
1189.purpose: The goal of the proposed project is to improve water quality in the Indian River Lagoon by installing baffle boxes with filter media along stormwater basin outfalls in the City of Cocoa. Activities include site preparation, installation of stormwater structures and piping, roadway and right-of-way restoration, and construction management. These efforts will ensure effective treatment of stormwater runoff.
1189.direct_services: By funding this project, citizens will directly benefit from cleaner waterways and improved environmental health in the Indian River Lagoon. The baffle boxes will reduce pollutants, sediments, and nutrients entering the lagoon, helping to restore water clarity and support local wildlife.
1189.population: The general public to include the surrounding community and the population at large that utilizes the lagoon.
1189.outcome: Improve the environmental quality, protect the general public from harm, increase economic activity, increase tourism, create specific immediate job opportunities, and improve surface water quality. All can be measured through water quality testing and economic activity.

1429.description: Sustaining the current capacity of Residential Level II & IV licensed beds for the treatment of severe Opioid Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder for individuals residing in Circuit 2.
1429.purpose: Provide treatment in the current capacity of Residential Level II & IV licensed beds for the treatment of severe Opioid Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder for individuals residing in, but not limited to, the Second Judicial Circuit.

Count number of total available beds, by licensed level of care, prior to the project and after the project completes and measure the number increased.

2713.description: The mission is to establish and construct the National POW/MIA Memorial and Museum to honor all former Prisoners of War, 140,000+ U.S. service members, and to remember those service members still Missing in Action and unaccounted for, 80,900 U.S. service members, from WWII to present. The site is located at the former NAS Cecil Field, in Jacksonville and will be the first of its kind. In August 2017, the city provided the rights to develop, expand, and maintain 26 acres for the National POW/MIA Memorial. The Memorial site will serve as a national destination to provide awareness and to educate through special events, youth activities, and STEAM+H outreach, ultimately connecting generations through educational and informative exhibits.
2713.purpose: The National POW/MIA Memorial and Museum is planned as a historic site and national destination. In addition to supporting families and friends of service members who are Missing in Action, the Memorial will provide educational opportunities and host community events, youth programs, and STEAM+H outreach. The facility will offer exhibits designed to inform and connect different generations.
2713.activities: Appropriated funds will go directly to supporting the construction of the National Memorial. Work will include the Phase 2 architectural planning, permitting, contracting, clearing, general conditions, earthwork, leveling, sitework, foundation, initial utilities, electrical fixture purchases. All this to provide for the future a unique, historic and national treasure.
2713.direct_services: National POW/MIA Memorial and Museum is to be established as a historic site and national destination. Along with the important mission of providing solace for those families and friends of the service members Missing in Action, the Memorial site will serve and educate the community through special events, youth activities and STEAM+H outreach, ultimately connecting generations through educational

Exhibits and interactive displays will be incorporated to educate the public and foster ongoing remembrance. Upon completion of Phase 1, subsequent construction phases will begin without delay. Phase 2 focuses on environmental dredging of the highest-fluxing sections in the remaining project area & is estimated to reduce the annual nitrogen flux by roughly 29,000 pounds & phosphorus flux by approximately 1,500 pounds. These funds would be used to remove up to roughly 50,000 cubic yards of organic muck from Sykes Creek in the Banana River through environmental dredging. The entire project area has over 400,000 cubic yards of decaying muck, and Phase 2 targets a project area of approximately 90 acres of submerged land along Sykes Creek, adjacent to the Ulumay Wildlife Sanctuary. 2020.description: The Statewide Interagency Communications and Regional Coordination Platform will strengthen Florida's emergency management system by connecting FDEM, its regional coordinators, and partner agencies through a secure, centralized hub, powered by Civic Roundtable. Designed to replace fragmented tools and one-way updates, the platform will enable real-time coordination across FDEM, DOH, FDC, FDOT, FDOE, DEP, and county emergency managers. By streamlining communication, preserving institutional knowledge, and accelerating recovery operations, the project will enhance Florida's readiness and resilience—ensuring faster, clearer, and more effective support to communities before, during, and after disasters.
2020.purpose: To establish a statewide platform for FDEMs Communications and Regional Field Team, the first line of support to counties before, during, and after disasters. The platform will streamline communications across state, regional, and county partners; enhance coordination with other state agencies during response operations; centralize recovery resources; support after-action learning; and reduce administrative burden so coordinators can focus on technical support and county guidance.
2020.activities: Activities: Platform deployment across all seven FDEM regions; training for coordinators; creation of county-specific workspaces; integration with recovery grant tracking. Objectives: Streamline communications by replacing fragmented reporting with real-time engagement; centralize grants, templates, and recovery resources to support FEMA, CDBG, and HMGP; provide a persistent hub for training, exercises, and plans to preserve institutional knowledge; and capture lessons learned to strengthen stat
2020.direct_services: Direct Services: Faster and more accurate state support for counties during disasters; better coordination of resources for affected residents; and more effective, timely assistance to citizens before, during, and after emergencies.
2020.population: Target Population: All Floridians impacted by disasters; FDEM agency staff and partners.
2020.outcome: Statewide adoption with all FDEM regions using the platform; reduced duplication of reporting across email, Excel, and portals; consistent use by coordinators to store plans, exercises, and lessons learned, preserving institutional memory; and integration into recovery operations to track resources, grants, and milestones, feeding directly into After Action Reports and mitigation planning.

1165.description: Due to storms and historic rainfall in 2024, the County Stormwater Department is addressing Phillippi Creek maintenance by removing sediment and debris. Sediment removal will restore flood drainage capacity and reduce flooding risks in the basin. The project includes a two-phase dredging, 50’ wide by 4’ deep (below Mean Low Water): Phase 1 will dredge 1.53 miles of creek (Tuttle Ave. to Beneva Rd.) and Phase 2 will dredge 0.46 miles (Bee Ridge Rd to Tuttle Ave.)
1165.purpose: To remove sedimentation and debris build up, from 2024 storm season, mitigating potential flooding of residential and commercial structures and evacuation routes. Flood prediction modeling suggests sedimentation, caused by previous storm events, could cause an impact to flood service levels for the 1% design (100Y, 24H) storm.
1165.activities: Dredge (phase 1 and 2), along the center line of Phillippi Creek from Bee Ridge Rd to Beneva Road. To match historic excavation profile grades as defined in the original dredge conducted for the Sarasota-Fruitville Drainage District construction.
1165.direct_services: Significant reduction in potential of residential and commercial structure flooding and evacuation route flooding.
1165.population: Over 1,100 residential properties in the Phillippi Creek Basin impacting several thousand Sarasota County residents. The greater general Sarasota general population will benefit from the reduction in potential flooding and flood related disruption to businesses and commercial properties in the Phillippi Creek area.
1165.outcome: Reduced potential residential and commercial flooding using existing, engineered stormwater model to more accurately predict the area floodplain. Specifically, updating the existing Phillippi Creek Watershed Model with post construction survey to predict design storm floodplain (1% storm design). A comparison of the post construction dredge survey to the as-built, historic excavation profile of Phillippi Creek, defined by the Sarasota-Fruitville Drainage District construction, will also be considered as part of the modeling.

2031.description: The requested funds will support a Specialized Workforce Training Program that prepares adults with autism spectrum disorder for meaningful employment through individualized, evidence-based vocational training. The program aims to reduce barriers to employment, promote long-term economic independence, and foster partnerships with local employers to create inclusive pathways tailored to the strengths and needs of individuals with autism. Training options will be offered both on The Els Center of Excellence Campus and in the community with employer partners.
2031.purpose: The requested funds will support a Specialized Workforce Training Program that prepares adults with autism spectrum disorder for meaningful employment through individualized, evidence-based vocational training. The program aims to reduce barriers to employment, promote long-term economic independence, and foster partnerships with local employers to create inclusive pathways tailored to the strengths and needs of individuals with autism.
2031.activities: The project will provide individualized vocational training, hands on community-based learning, job coaching, ongoing evaluation, and employer education. These services will prepare adults with autism for meaningful employment, reduce barriers to economic stability, and build inclusive workforce partnerships. Participants will also receive Care Coordination and peer group engagement opportunities.
2031.direct_services: Participants will learn industry-specific skills through visually engineered vocational labs and community-based settings, complete monthly surveys, receive progress assessments, and engage in programs to enhance employability and readiness for meaningful employment. All graduates will develop an employment portfolio to support future job placement.
2031.population: Individuals with autism spectrum disorder and related disabilities 18 years and older. A total of 65 individuals will be served with approximately 40 completing an on-campus workforce training and 25 completing a community-based workforce training.
2031.outcome: Participants will be trained in preemployment skills and industry specific job skills to be better equipped to find and secure meaningful paid employment upon completion of the program. Specialized training using evidence-based practices will be provided by experienced instructors and job coaches. Outcomes will be measured through pre/post assessments, completion of employment portfolio, satisfaction surveys, number of participants enrolling in Vocational Rehabilitation, Situational assessment completion during intake process for baseline measure of key job readiness skills, monthly participant feedback through surveys measuring confidence in job readiness, and monthly job coach assessments

The SOV will serve as a mobile command and rehab unit equipped with communications, surveillance, and weather monitoring systems, ensuring faster, more effective response to large-scale incidents, special events, and critical emergencies.

The SOV is a type of apparatus that will enhance the response and mitigation capabilities of the Fire-Rescue Department in its committed duty to safeguard the lives of the residents and visitors to the City of Miramar (City) and effectively protect the properties and structures within its boundaries. The SOV can be deployed at any time an emergency may dictate the use of a vehicle speci
1050.activities: Vehicle will be outfitted with computers, communications, surveillance and weather station equipment to assist in effective incident command operations. The convertibility of the vehicle will allow for risk reduction and response to emergencies. This vehicle may be utilized as an Arson command center during structure fires and investigations. The use of the SOV during extreme emergencies as a Critical Response Vehicle would be invaluable to our citizens, as it would facilitate the recovery and m
1050.direct_services: The SOV is a type of apparatus that will enhance the response and mitigation capabilities of the Fire-Rescue Department in its committed duty to safeguard the lives of the residents and visitors to the City of Miramar and effectively protect the properties and structures within its boundaries and wherever needed from a state regional aspect.
1050.population: The City of Miramar and its surrounding cities for example, City of Pembroke Pines, City of Hollywood, City of West Park and City of Miami Gardens.
1050.outcome: The use of the SOV during extreme emergencies as a Critical Response Vehicle would be invaluable to our citizens, as it would facilitate the recovery and mitigation of any incident by having on scene support and direction as needed.
