1649.description: The project will modernize the Galt Ocean Mile by upgrading aging infrastructure and enhancing public safety through milling and resurfacing worn pavement, constructing wider sidewalks, installing bike lanes, enhancing pedestrian lighting, and adding stamped asphalt raised intersections with updated markings and signage. These enhancements will revitalize a corridor that has not been renovated since 1996, creating a safer, more accessible environment for residents and visitors while strengthening multimodal transportation, reducing vehicle and pedestrian conflicts, and supporting the area’s economic and cultural vitality.
1649.purpose: To revitalize the Galt Ocean Mile by milling and resurfacing worn pavement, constructing wider sidewalks, upgrading streetscape, adding bike lanes, improving pedestrian lighting, and installing raised intersections with updated pavement markings and signage. This will modernize a corridor, creating a safer, more accessible environment for residents, visitors, and tourists.
1649.activities: The project will provide activities and services including milling and resurfacing existing pavement, constructing wider sidewalks, installing pedestrian lighting, creating stamped asphalt raised intersections, improving pavement markings and regulatory signage, and adding bike lanes to enhance safety and mobility.
1649.direct_services: Citizens will directly benefit from safer and more mobile streets through wider sidewalks, raised crosswalks, improved lighting, enhanced and upgraded bike lanes and walkways. These services will promote walkability, encourage active transportation, reduce safety risks, and improve the overall quality of life for residents, businesses, and visitors.
1649.population: Residents, businesses, and visitors frequenting the beaches, businesses, and surrounding amenities. The improvements span from NE 32nd Street to NE 41st Street, covering seven intersections and serving over 10,000 residents and visitors annually.
1649.outcome: The project will enhance transportation safety and accessibility. Residents and visitors will benefit from wider sidewalks, improved lighting, safer intersections, and bike lanes, resulting in improved mobility, reduced pedestrian/vehicle conflicts, stronger economic activity, and an enhanced quality of life; all measured using pre- and post-project data, traffic counts; accident and crime statistics; business and tourism activity levels; and community satisfaction surveys.

1714.description: Tampa Bay Watch's principle mission for over 32 years has been the restoration and preservation of shorelines and improving water quality in and around greater Tampa Bay. Damages to coastal shorelines in Pinellas and Hillsborough counties caused by hurricanes in 2024 further demonstrate a need to proactively protect the coast from surge and rising sea levels. Tampa Bay Watch has proven highly effective in mobilizing the local community to participate in habitat restoration projects, including Living Shorelines, that preserve and protect the coast. Our initiatives simultaneously create habitat for the eastern oyster, which provide a nature-based solution by filtering and improving waters that are both cost- effective and timely.
1714.purpose: Sea rise imposes an existential threat to low-lying coastal communities like Tampa Bay. Living shoreline solutions provide a value-driven and nature-based approach toward long-term resiliency building that preserves the increasingly delicate balance between natural and human systems. These projects will address ecosystem concerns, including the stabilization of the shoreline that helps protect local residents and species. Methods used (including community participation in implementation) will he
1714.activities: Tampa Bay Watch will engage the community to create living shoreline projects throughout the bay, including oyster reefs, sea grass support and marsh grass plantings. Additionally, TBW will expand an already successful oyster shell recycling program, working with local restaurants to collect the shells before being discarded that can be used in our living shoreline creation projects that reduce land-fill and accelerate oyster volume, resulting in better water filtration.
1714.direct_services: These projects generally have multiple goals and objectives including the creation and restoration of aquatic habitat, creation of foraging area and food sources for local wildlife, filtering nutrients, improving water quality, stabilizing sediments to reduce erosion and engagement of the community in environmental stewardship and hands-on restoration efforts.
1714.population: The target population by the project is the entire Tampa Bay community. Indirectly, all of the residents of Tampa Bay area will benefit from the better shoreline protection and recovery, as well as increases in estuarine habitat and water quality improvements provided by the projects completed.
1714.outcome: The efforts of Tampa Bay Watch to restore and protect the bay's habitat through stewardship provide effective long- term improvements to the bay and empower our community to counteract local environmental problems. Desired outcomes of successful living shorelines projects include: reduced coastal erosion, wildlife habitat creation, reduced flooding, improved water quality, and in some cases, recovered shoreline. In addition, a healthy Bay provides increased opportunities for outdoor recreation and supports regional tourism and commerce. This program also allows us to gain invaluable information about the long-term trends of living shoreline projects. This will be measured by the number of li

1034.description: Lakewood Ranch Medical Center proposes construction of a 14-bed dedicated Geriatric Behavioral Health Unit within the existing hospital. The goal of the unit is to address a critical gap in services and ensure seniors can receive compassionate, safe, and evidence-based behavioral health treatment close to home. With the growing aging population in the Sarasota Manatee Counties comes increased prevalence of behavioral health challenges including dementia, Alzheimer's disease, depression, anxiety, delirium, and late-life psychiatric disorders. Currently, access to specialized inpatient geriatric behavioral health care in the region is limited, often forcing seniors and families to travel outside of the area or rely on general adult psychiatric units not tailored to their unique needs.
1034.purpose: Florida's senior population is among the fastest growing in the nation, with Manatee and Sarasota Counties ranking as two of the state's most concentrated areas for older adults. These funds will be allocated for new construction of a 14- bed dedicated Geriatric Behavioral Health Unit within the Lakewood Ranch Medical Center.
1034.activities: Lakewood Ranch Medical Center will provide specialty care and elderly services to include: - Provide a specialized inpatient environment designed specifically for the physical, cognitive, and emotional needs of seniors. - Reduce unnecessary transfers to distant facilities by offering local, accessible care. - Support families and caregivers with resources, education, and discharge planning. - Improve coordination between primary care, psychiatry, neurology, and social services
1034.direct_services: - Crisis stabilization for seniors experiencing acute behavioral health issues. - Medication management and monitoring tailored to complex geriatric needs. - Therapeutic interventions such as group therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, activity therapy, and occupational support. - Specialized dementia and Alzheimer's behavioral management. - Integrated medical and psychiatric care to address
1034.population: Adults age 65 and older in Manatee, Sarasota, and surrounding counties. Seniors experiencing dementia or Alzheimer's-related behavioral issues, depression, anxiety, or late-life psychosis, behavioral disturbances linked to medical illness and/or acute mental health crises requiring stabilization. We anticipate seeing over 1,200 pateints per year.
1034.outcome: - Improved Access: Local seniors will have timely, appropriate care without needing to leave the community. - Enhanced Quality of Life: Patients receive care in a safe, age-appropriate environment that promotes dignity and recovery. - Reduced Strain on Emergency Departments: Seniors in behavioral health crisis will have a dedicated care setting, alleviating overcrowding and improving ED efficiency. - Support for Caregivers and Families: Education and coordinated discharge planning reduce caregiver burden and prevent readmissions. •Economic and Community Impact: Investment in local behavioral health resources keeps healthcare dollars in the region and strengthens the overall continuum of care

1106.description: The funds will be used to reconstruct the wharf at Nova Southeastern University's (NSU) Oceanographic campus. The reconstruction is necessitated by an Army Corps dredging project at Port Everglades which would destabilize NSU's existing wharf. The reconstruction will harden the sea wall abutting the wharf, to allow berthing for large research vessels, and relocate seagrass habitats that could be irreversibly damaged by the Army Corps dredging project.
1106.purpose: The funds will be used to reconstruct the wharf at Nova Southeastern University's (NSU) Oceanographic campus. The reconstruction is necessitated by an Army Corps dredging project at Port Everglades which would destabilize NSU's existing wharf. The reconstruction will harden the sea wall abutting the wharf, to allow berthing for large research vessels, and relocate seagrass habitats that could be irreversibly damaged by the Army Corps dredging project.
1106.activities: Planning, design, permitting and construction costs associated with hardening NSU's existing marina breakwater, over-water wharf, and alongshore seawall at the widener portion of the Port Everglades project.
1106.direct_services: Wharf renewal and seagrass mitigation proximate to the proposed Port Everglades navigational improvements will expand oceanographic research capabilities, promote resilient coastal infrastructure, and enhance educational opportunities while contributing to the blue economy that drives area tourism.
1106.population: The project will serve university/college students and well as the general population. University/College students will benefit from additional educational opportunities generated by the berthing of a larger research vessel, and the expansion of the coral restoration effort at NSU. The general population will benefit from the environmental research and the seagrass mitigation which will bolster the blue economy.
1106.outcome: Wharf renewal and seagrass mitigation proximate to the proposed Port Everglades navigational improvements will expand oceanographic research capabilities, promote resilient coastal infrastructure, and enhance educational opportunities while contributing to the blue economy that drives area tourism. The project will mitigate seagrass habitats which are already at risk due to Port Everglades improvements, increase the capacity for coral restoration and repopulation projects, and promote resiliency in coastal infrastructure and ecosystems. These benefits could be measured upon completion of the project.

2465.description: SPC serves as the regional training center for 13 local law enforcement agencies and numerous state, federal and military organizations. New equipment will provide immersive, scenario-based training in de-escalation, crisis response and mental health awareness. The Field Training Equipment and Support initiative will deploy advanced ballistic robots, simulation technology and combat robots. These innovations will enhance officer safety, improve efficiency, and strengthen community trust through transparent, ethical policing, benefiting more than 4,400 public safety students annually and supporting safer, more effective law enforcement across Florida.
2465.purpose: St. Petersburg college has always been a leader in providing top tier training to our first responders, AI driven ballistic robots, coupled with AI driven simulators, and medical robots open an entire new world of scenario-based training, providing critical de-escalation scenarios, lethal force training, and essential first aid and self-care training.
2465.activities: St. Petersburg College provides year-round training to thousands of our constituents. These tools will enable us to offer courses in an immersive light as never before seen.
2465.direct_services: Enhanced Public Safety • Better-trained officers can de-escalate volatile situations, reducing the likelihood of violence. • Specialized training in crisis response, mental health awareness, and cultural sensitivity ensures safer interactions with diverse communities. 2. Stronger Community Trust • Citizens benefit from transparent, professional, and consistent policing practices. • Advanced traini
2465.population: Florida students and their families who are either interested in public safety careers or who are currently serving in an agency. In FY 24-25 there were 4400 students enrolled at Saint Petersburg college public safety center last year and there are approximately 45,000 students served by the College.
2465.outcome: Public safety professionals learn safe and proper responses to incidents and proper use of force escalation and de- escalation techniques within diverse populations. This will result in less incidents and civil unrest as well as measured reductions of injuries to 1st responders and the public.

1072.organization: Align To Meet A Need DBA Align Benefit Corp
1072.description: Growing OAKS is an Initiative for Circuit 12. The Connection Coordinator Program will prevent children from entering the state-run, state-funded Foster Care System by providing 4 Connection Coordinators who will work collaboratively with Community Action Treatment (CAT) Teams and the Youth At-Risk (YAR) Teams to connect more families in crisis with the needed resources to keep a higher percentage of these families together. This Intervention and Prevention Project is supported by the Family Safety Alliance of Circuit 12 studies as well. Net estimated savings to the State of Florida based on past success rates of keeping children out of foster care will be at least $4 million which can then be reallocated to other areas of need within the system.
1072.purpose: Families currently in crisis with little to no connection to resources and support will have guidance to resources in Manatee County and Sarasota County through the Connection Coordinator Project. This provides support and prevention, provides follow up for those families who complete Community Action Treatment (CAT) Teams or who do not qualify for CAT Teams and provides follow up to Youth At-Risk (YAR) referrals.
1072.activities: One-to-One connection, peer support, resource connector, empowering each family through advocacy and alleviating system barriers, provide skill building, advocacy mentorship, recovery support, problem solving, goal setting and tools to navigate through education.
1072.direct_services: Direct Connections to the various needs of the citizens for example, Individual and Supportive Services, Food Assistance, Mental Health Services, Medical Services, Educational Services, Vocational Services, in addition to Government Services they qualify for.
1072.population: Families and child/youth on the waitlist for CAT Teams, who complete services with Community Action Treatment (CAT) Teams of families and child/youth who do not qualify for CAT Team wrap around care. Families and Youth with the Youth At Risk (YAR) Teams. Each Connection Coordinator would manage 12-15 families per month.
1072.outcome: The measured outcome will be to reduce the gap for families in crisis with anticipated prevention and intervention for child/youth entering the child welfare system. The anticipated prevention and intervention will potentionally benefit the state funding by saving, at a minimum, 4 million dollars which can then be reallocated to other areas of need. The digital platform Unite us will be utilized to track data and measure outcomes.

1013.description: The cornerstone of public safety is public trust. Legislative funding will bolster police operations against public corruption and criminal conspiracy in Miami-Dade County through investigating acts of criminal misconduct involving public officials, County employees, police officers, lobbyists, and private vendors conducting business with Miami-Dade County. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office strives to effectively investigate allegations of misconduct, corruption, and other criminal activity which could directly or indirectly impact the ability to serve the community in a manner free of corruption.
1013.purpose: Reduction in public corruption incidents in Miami-Dade County
1013.activities: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations
1013.direct_services: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations
1013.population: All residents and visitors in Miami-Dade County; over 5 million persons
1013.outcome: Reduction in public corruption incidents, increased public trust in Miami-Dade County, and increased law enforcement and public safety operations as measured by MDSO tracking data

1014.description: The legislative funding will allow the new Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office (MDSO) to rebrand and establish itself as a distinct entity from the former Miami-Dade Police Department (MDSO). Rebranding will replace MDPD with MDSO signage on district stations and government facilities, patrol vehicles, boats, motorcycles, aircraft, uniforms, printed materials, etc. Current outdated MDPD brand confuses residents and visitors and decreases public safety. This project is critical for strengthening community trust and ensuring the sheriff’s office is seen as relevant, professional, and approachable.
1014.purpose: Improved law enforcement and public safety operations
1014.activities: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations
1014.direct_services: MDSO rebranding will improve trust because it is paired with authentic change. If the community sees both a new look and new actions (transparency, fairness, engagement), the rebrand will reinforce the transformation.
1014.population: All residents and visitors in Miami-Dade County; over 5 million persons
1014.outcome: Improved community trust and visibility, and increased law enforcement and public safety operations as measured by MDSO tracking data

1390.description: The Town of Bronson seeks funding to complete engineering design, topographic surveying, permitting, and geotechnical work necessary to make its Septic Tank Phase Out, Phase 3 project shovel-ready. This project will prepare for construction to connect approximately 270 properties currently on septic systems to the Town’s central wastewater system, reducing nitrogen loading and protecting groundwater and springs within the Silver River and Rainbow Springs BMAP area. As a financially disadvantaged community, this investment will strengthen Bronson’s long-term sustainability by expanding its limited ratepayer base and supporting economic and environmental resilience.
1390.purpose: The purpose of this project is to complete design, surveying, permitting, and geotechnical work necessary to make the Town’s Septic Tank Phase Out, Phase 3 project shovel-ready. The long-term goal is to eliminate approximately 270 aging septic systems by connecting those properties to the Town’s central wastewater system, thereby reducing nutrient loading, protecting groundwater and springs within the Silver River and Rainbow Springs BMAP area, and strengthening the Town’s financial sustainabili
1390.activities: Funds will be used for engineering design, topographic surveying, environmental permitting, and geotechnical investigations. These activities will produce complete, biddable construction plans and specifications that position the project to advance into the construction phase.
1390.direct_services: This project will directly benefit residents and businesses by laying the groundwork for expanded access to safe, reliable wastewater service. Once constructed, the improvements will eliminate the need for costly septic system repairs or replacements, protecting household finances while reducing health and environmental risks. These upgrades will enhance quality of life, safeguard groundwater, and
1390.population: The project serves all citizens and businesses within the Town of Bronson, a financially disadvantaged community with an estimated population of approximately 1,400 residents. The Phase 3 expansion will directly benefit about 270 households and indirectly benefit the entire community by improving environmental quality and utility system reliability.
1390.outcome: The expected outcome is a shovel-ready design package for Phase 3 of the septic-to-sewer expansion, positioning the Town to pursue construction funding and implement nitrogen-reduction improvements. Success will be measured through completion of design milestones, issuance of environmental permits, and submission of a final construction- ready bid package. Long-term environmental benefits will be tracked through nitrogen-reduction estimates and reductions in the number of active septic systems.

1128.description: Young Musicians Unite (YMU) will provide in-school music education to more than 19,500 students across 88 Miami- Dade County Public Schools. The program has restored music programs, increased student engagement, and reduced absenteeism. In support of Florida’s classical education model, YMU integrates music with academics to create a values- based learning experience. This request will fund additional music teachers for 11 schools, reaching 2,242 more students and completing full feeder-pattern continuity. This proven, community-driven model improves attendance, fosters collaboration, and celebrates American culture while maximizing Florida’s investment in education.
1128.purpose: This $600,000 request will fund additional music teachers in 11 schools, serving 2,242 students within YMU's broader network of 19,500 students across 88 campuses. The funds will expand access to music education that improves attendance, engagement, and academic achievement across Miami-Dade County Public Schools. Through in-school and after-school programs, YMU fosters purpose, belonging, and pride while advancing Florida's classical education priorities. Music transforms school culture by moti
1128.activities: The project provides music programs that keep students engaged, inspired, and connected to their schools. Through YMU's model, music becomes a central part of school culture. Programs run during and after school, offering a safe, structured environment that builds discipline, creativity, and pride. One principal even rescheduled an English class to follow music because attendance was higher on those days, leading to improved reading scores and grades. Program Activities and Services: • Music Ins
1128.direct_services: This initiative provides a direct public service by expanding access to music education that improves attendance and reduces absenteeism. Through this appropriation, 2,242 students across 11 Miami-Dade County Public Schools will receive free, high-quality instruction rooted in America's musical heritage. Students perform at parades, festivals, and community celebrations that promote pride, belongi
1128.population: The project will serve 2,242 students across 11 Miami-Dade County Public Schools, representing one full feeder pattern, spanning grades K-12. These campuses have historically faced high absenteeism and limited access to arts education. Through YMU's in-school and after-school programs, students gain daily opportunities for creativity, teamwork, and leadership in a safe, structured environment that fosters discipline and civic engagement. Beyond the classroom, performances and community events un
1128.outcome: The project increases student attendance, engagement, and academic achievement through daily participation in high- quality music programs. By making music central to school culture, students develop confidence, teamwork, and leadership while improving their commitment to learning. Expected Benefits and Outcomes: • Improved Attendance: Students in YMU programs attend school more consistently with fewer absences and tardies. • Academic Growth: Participants maintain higher GPAs, take more advanced courses, and show stronger long-term performance. • Civic and Cultural Impact: Public performances build pride, belonging, and community connection. Methodology for Measuring Outcomes: Miami-Dade Cou

1696.description: The Australian Avenue Drainage Improvement project will construct a new underground stormwater drainage collection and treatment system in this 3 mile corridor, to alleviate flooding that occurs during storm events. Construction of the new system will require reconstruction of the existing 4-lane median divided roadway, and includes the addition of 4' shoulders, new curb and gutter, sidewalks that vary from 6'-8' in width, mast arm traffic signal upgrades at 7 intersections, and replacement of 4 functionally obsolete bridges. The City of West Palm Beach will also replace 2 lift stations, line significant portions of its force mains, and replace significant portions of its water mains within the project limits.
1696.purpose: This project will construct a new stormwater drainage system to alleviate flooding throughout the 3 mile corridor that occurs during regular and significant rainfall and/or storm events. The nature of this work requires significant underground work that will necessitate reconstruction of the roadway as a whole, which allows the opportunity to provide roadway shoulders/bike lanes, to expand sidewalks, and to replace the 4 functionally obsolete bridges in this corridor to bring them up to current
1696.activities: A new stormwater drainage system will be constructed that is comprised of more than 150 new stormwater drainage inlets, over 13,000 linear feet of underground pipes, and roughly 4 acres of land adjacent to the Carver Canal will be excavated and shaped into a new pond to expand stormwater drainage capacity. The roadway will be completely reconstructed and widened to include shoulders and wider sidewalks, and 4 functionally obsolete bridges will be raised to the extent possible and replaced.
1696.direct_services: Many of the adjacent properties and older developments drain to the Australian Avenue right-of-way today, overwhelming the existing open-swale drainage system, causing flooding both in the road and properties adjacent to it. Construction of the new stormwater drainage system will alleviate both road flooding and offsite flooding that occurs by expanding the capacity of the drainage system as a who
1696.population: This roadway serves the travelling public as a regionally significant north/south roadway, carrying over 28,000 vehicles per day. The population directly served by this 3-mile long project includes over 120 single family homes, 20+ commercial businesses, non-profits and churches, 3 apartment complexes, residents of the Twin Lakes West Palm Beach Housing Authority community, 2 schools, and 3 Palm Tran bus routes, all of whom experience the effects of Australian Avenue flooding during rain and sig
1696.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to eliminate flooding on Australian Avenue and along the adjacent properties and neighborhoods. This will be measured by documenting the reduction in maintenance repairs and costs, reduction in emergency calls related to flood and/or infrastructure failure, evaluation of the improved/increased life of the pavement and all road and bridge infrastructure within the project limits.

1684.organization: Exchange Club Dick Weber Center DBA: The
1684.description: The Children’s Healing Institute requests funding to deliver evidence-based Parent Aide Program services to 100 at-risk families (250+ children) in Palm Beach and Broward Counties. Parent Aide keeps families intact, ensures children’s safety, and equips parents with skills, tools, and resources for a safe, stable home. Services include needs assessments, parenting education, stress reduction, safety planning, and access to essential items and community resources. Families face challenges like financial instability, housing insecurity, domestic violence, and unemployment. The program serves families with children under 18, offering free weekly sessions for 6–18 months. Parent Aide costs $3,000 per child annually versus $105,000 for foster care, significantly reducing out-of-home placements while fostering family resilience.
1684.purpose: Delivery of intensive in-home child abuse prevention services via evidence-based Parent Aide program for at-risk families in Palm Beach & Broward Counties. Goal: enhance family protective factors, reduce child maltreatment risk, DCF involvement, and child removal, & lessen the state's financial burden (close to 2,100 children were in foster care in PB/Broward in 2024). Parents completing 6+ months will improve their capacity for positive relationships, healthy attachment, and parenting knowledge
1684.activities: Referred families undergo eligibility screening, including an Initial Needs Assessment, and pre/post evaluations (AAPI- 2.5 and Protective Factors Survey). A Family Plan with service goals is created. Weekly in-home support for 6+ months includes Nurturing Parenting curriculum as needed. Community collaborations offer additional support. Data is collected for program assessment .
1684.direct_services: We offer free services to at-risk families, aiming to prevent child removal. Program provides weekly in-home support with needs assessments, goalsetting, parenting education, mentoring, and case management for resource connections. Services last 6-18 months based on the Parent Aide model. The goal is to address root issues, enhance family well-being, stability, & reduce the risk of child removal.
1684.population: The project will serve families with and without DCF involvement in PB & Broward counties, focusing on high-risk households with at least one child under 18. Target populations include families in reunification, families assessed by DCF whose children remain at home, and those referred by community partners or self referred. These groups face critical needs identified by Community-Based Care (CBC), DCF, and the community. Project will serve up to 100 families (+/- 250 children), addressing servi
1684.outcome: This project aims to prevent child maltreatment and reduce the need for foster care or DCF intervention among high- risk families in PB/Broward counties by increasing protective factors/decreasing risk factors within the families for abuse and negelct. Methodology used will be pre and post evaluations using the Protective Factors Survey; AAPI; monthly progress notes; Family Plan goals; parent self report; and Program Outcome Survey.

1698.description: WTP 2 currently does not have an effective treatment process for the removal of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances(PFAS) chemical compounds, which is required by federal law by 2031. Funds secured for this project will: 1. construct a new water treatment plant designed using nanofiltration to reduce emerging contaminants; 2. upgrade aging plant infrastructure; 3. new membrane & electrical room, hurricane hardening, & a new generator for expansion and redundancy to prevent plant disruptions or failures. This project provides process improvements to improve water treatment, reliability, and efficiency to maintain treatment quality and quantity through the next decades. To meet the required timeline of 2031, design needs to occur in 2026. Construction of water plants can take up to 5 years to complete.
1698.purpose: Funding for this project will upgrade WTP 2, a critical infrastructure, to improve water treatment quality, quantity, & reliability for all residents. Clean & safe drinking water is vital to our health, communities, & economy. As the population increases, so does the need for clean water. This project will result in an increase in clean drinking water that meets the required strict regulatory standards. The requested funds will go towards the design of the facility. To meet the required timeline
1698.activities: Activities include, but is not limited to: 1. A new water treatment plant will be designed using nanofiltration to comply with drinking water standards; 2. The project includes plant expansion, hurricane hardening, and a new generator for redundancy; and 3. A new membrane and electrical room are required for expansion and redundancy to circumvent disruptions or failures; and 4. Pre-treatment and post-treatment processes, production wells, and pumping systems
1698.direct_services: Safe, reliable and clean drinking water is a direct service and outcome of this project to PBC residents, businesses and visitors. Improvements to WTP 2 will ensure that every household and business has access to quality drinking water that meets the required federal standards.
1698.population: Palm Beach County Water Utilities Department, through its interconnected water treatment plants, serves over 641,000 residents. WTP 2 serves 140,000 residents in the following communities who will continue to enjoy access to clean drinking water: Boynton Beach, Greenacres, Town of Hypoluxo, Village of Palm Springs, Royal Palm Beach, West Palm Beach, and Wellington. As paying customers, the residents expect that the utility provide clean water that meets drinking water quality standards.
1698.outcome: Increase in clean drinking water that meets strict regulatory standards. PFAS or "forever chemicals" are classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer and have been widely found in US drinking water systems. EPA adopted drinking water quality standards for PFAS that water utilities must meet by 2031. Improvements to WTP 2 will comply with federal regulations, which reduces levels of PFAS. Nanofiltration, one of the most effective approaches for PFAS treatment, will be utilized. Water quality data will be measured, monitored and made publicly available.

1330.organization: ADE-Association for the Development of the
1330.description: $ 550,000 will convert two Branches of ADE, Inc., serving adults with Autism and Disabilities since 1976, to a fully ADA Accessible building, by installing an elevator per branch. Consumers/Staff/Visitors with physical disabilities will be able to access the second floor of our ADE Central, and ADE Homestead Facilities, which is only accessible through stairs. The funding will cover the cost of plans, engineering, construction of elevator shaft, elevator cab, motor controls, installation, ventilation, heating/cooling, and Building Permits, City License & Fees. This will allow additional consumers with disabilities of APD, and the manage care Pilot Program to access our facilities.
1330.purpose: The goal is to construct infrastructure and install elevators at two of our agencies buildings, serving adults with Autism and Disabilities since 1976. This will allow additional physically challenged consumers to receive Life Skills and Vocational Training in the second stories at our Doral and Homestead Facilities in Miami-Dade County. It will allow additional consumer enrollment and additional job creation. It will satisfy Adults with Disabilities Act requirements.
1330.activities: Physically Challenged consumers will access the 2nd floor of our existing facilities to receive Training in Life Skills, Vocational Skills, Companion Skills, Employability Seeking Skills, Employment on the Job-training, Community Inclusion, and Transportation will be offered in the newly accessible space with the funds from this appropriation to APD consumers and those participating in the Manage Care Pilot Program in Miami Dade County.
1330.direct_services: We will be able to provide programs and services to approximately 50-100 additional consumers. Some may be referred through Support Coordination Services from the wait list of The Agency for Persons with Disabilities or from Florida Community Care-Manage Care Pilot Program.
1330.population: The targeted population are adults 21 and older, with Autism, Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities, and or secondary physical/behavioral challenges.
1330.outcome: To expand the accessibility capacity at "ADE's Miami-Dade County Central Branch & Doral Branch", which provides Life Skills and Work Development Skills to persons with Developmental Disabilities", located at 7330 NW 12 Street, Miami, and 200 NE 2nd Drive, Homestead. These two facilities do not have elevator services, and thus the second floor of either buildings cannot be accessed by consumers with physical handicaps. To convert these two locations fully accessible ADA compliant buildings will allow our existing curriculum and services to opened up to a broader number consumers within our unique population. Marketing independence and a path to workforce development.

1054.organization: Ruth & Norman Rales Jewish Family Services
1054.description: Serving approx. 4,500 households annually, the Immediate Need Triage Line for Individuals and Families, by Rales Jewish Family Services is a centralized intake and referral program that provides a free initial psycho-social assessment to identify needs and quickly connect callers with recommendations for services at Rales JFS and/or other community resources. Licensed and/or experienced Geriatric Care professionals provide customized referrals within 48 business hours for mental health counseling, psychiatry, financial assistance, food assistance, Pediatric Occupational, Physical and/or Speech therapies, specialized care for vulnerable populations and emergency situations.
1054.purpose: Funds will support a single point of entry for residents in immediate need, ensuring they receive timely, coordinated access to behavioral health care and wrap-around supports. The goal is to stabilize individuals and families, reduce the impact of urgent crises, and improve household well-being.
1054.activities: INTL will operate as a centralized intake and referral program staffed by licensed and experienced professionals. Each caller will receive a no-cost psycho-social assessment by phone to identify and triage immediate needs. Based on the assessment, individuals will be connected with appropriate Rales JFS services—including mental health counseling and psychiatry, pediatric therapies (OT, PT, Speech), summer camp scholarships, financial assistance, food pantry, Meals on Wheels, and senior services
1054.direct_services: Through INTL individuals gain direct access to a system of triage of needs including an initial psycho-social assessment, followed by tailored connections to services that address their immediate needs. Direct supports include access to counseling and psychiatry, food assistance, emergency financial aid, summer camp scholarships for children, and specialized care for seniors, veterans, and individ
1054.population: INTL serves all demographics, including but not limited to all socio-economic populations: children, adults, seniors, Holocaust survivors, all religious affiliations, persons with disabilities, and, in many cases, working families with constraints of limited household income and personal assets. Anticipated impact is 9,000 individuals.
1054.outcome: INTL provides swift connections for individuals facing urgent situations, linking them to Rales JFS' services and/or essential community supports. Nearly 90% of callers will receive follow-up and referral information within 24–48 hours. Additionally, at least 85% of callers connected to the INTL financial assistance/ counseling will report increased ability to pay household expenses as well as reduced symptoms of anxiety and depression evidenced by client report and PHQ9/GAD assessments. By promptly addressing immediate needs, the service helps ease anxiety, and related challenges while equipping callers with a clear, solution-focused plan of action. Access to Rales JFS’ broad network of ser

1022.organization: Ruth & Norman Rales Jewish Family Services
1022.description: Aging in Place with Grace, is a comprehensive senior services program designed to enable older adults to age in place by providing a broad safety net of essential services including home delivered meals, transportation, socialization, case management, home care, and connection to services provided by Rales JFS and the broader community.
1022.purpose: Approximately 440 senior citizens will be provided with a safety net of services that allow them to age in place and avoid nursing home placement. Services will include any or all of the following: dynamic and varied socialization activities, transportation, financial assistance, home care, and home-delivered meals, as well as wrap-around support.
1022.activities: Socialization activities, case management, home care, transportation, home-delivered meals, and wrap around services such as financial assistance and behavioral healthcare will be provided to approximately 440 senior citizens in Palm Beach County by Rales Jewish Family Services, in order to enable seniors to age in place independently and to their highest quality of life potential.
1022.direct_services: Comprehensive direct services and wrap-around services will include socialization activities, case management, home care, financial assistance, transportation, home-delivered meals, and/or behavioral health care. Rales JFS has over 40 years of experience providing these direct services to senior citizens. We have been recognized as the premier provider of aging services in Palm Beach County.
1022.population: The target population of this project are approximately 440 senior citizens of Palm Beach County.
1022.outcome: Approximately 440 senior citizens will age in place and avoid nursing home placement. We expect 85% will avoid being placed in nursing home care. Methodology: Data will be tracked and records kept on how many seniors from our program enter state-funded nursing home care. Surveys and evaluations will measure senior satisfaction with home- delivered meals, transportation, home care, socialization opportunities and more.

1023.description: State funds will be dedicated to enhancing the existing senior center through infrastructure and facility improvements. These will include upgrading community spaces, modernizing electrical and HVAC systems, replacing doors and windows, integrating new technology, and installing safety devices.
1023.purpose: State funds will be used to enhance the existing senior center through a series of infrastructure and facility improvements including upgrades to community spaces, modernization electrical and HVAC systems, replacement of door and windows, integration of new technology and installation of safety features.
1023.activities: The senior center will offer social and recreational activities, health and wellness programs, educational and enrichment opportunities, and essential support services.
1023.direct_services: The senior center will offer a variety of direct services to support the health, independence, and well-being of older adults. These services will include nutrition education, wellness screenings and health education programs, and transportation assistance to help seniors access medical appointments and essential destinations. The center will also offer information and referral services to connect
1023.outcome: Modernizing the senior center will attract more seniors to utilize the facility, helping to reduce isolation and loneliness while fostering a greater sense of community and belonging. The project will also support the local economy by increasing engagement and benefiting nearby businesses. Outcomes will be measured through participant surveys, comments, and suggestions, which will be used to guide improvements to programming and activities. Economic benefits would be obtain through the local Chamber of commerce and other economic related organizations.

1015.description: Palm Beach County (PBC) in collaboration with the Florida Department of Corrections (FDC) and community-based reentry partners facilitate the successful reintegration of reentry participants returning to PBC. The Regional and State Transitional Offender Reentry (RESTORE) Initiative, established in 2011, is a comprehensive model for reentry designed to reduce recidivism by identifying needs, providing targeted evidence-based programs, and coordinating pre- and post- release services to assist individuals transitioning from incarceration to the community. The project will focus on 1)pre- release case management and skill building for people housed at the Sago Palm Reentry Center in Pahokee, FL; 2)post- release case management currently provided by two contracted community service providers: 3) supportive services (job placement, access to drug-free housing, transitional jobs, work boots/su
1015.purpose: Palm Beach County (PBC) in collaboration with the Florida Department of Corrections (FDC) and community-based reentry partners facilitate the successful reintegration of reentry participants returning to PBC. The Regional and State Transitional Offender Reentry (RESTORE) Initiative, established in 2011, is a comprehensive model for reentry designed to reduce recidivism by identifying needs, providing targeted evidence-based programs, and coordinating pre- and post-release services to assist indi
1015.activities: In order to meet our intended purpose, all re-entry staff will be sufficiently trained in the following areas: motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral interventions, LS/CMI assessment, amongst others. In addition, staff will meet monthly with County staff to discuss relevant data, progress, resources, and barriers as well as provide any additional trainings.
1015.direct_services: Individuals housed or released from FDC facilities will receive case management and support services. Prior to any services being delivered, coordinators will administer the LS/CMI assessment to determine their risk, needs, and protective factors which will guide their plan of care which may include transitional jobs, housing assistance, basic needs, employment, identification and more.
1015.population: The target population for this Program will be active inmates housed at Sago Palm Reentry Center and recently released inmates from the Florida Department of Corrections institution/facility convicted in and returning to Palm Beach County, Florida. The RESTORE will target 400+ medium to high-risk people, as determined by the Level of Service Case Management Inventory (LS/CMI) Scores from completed risk assessments to provide re-entry services which support successful reintegration into the commu
1015.outcome: The expected benefit is an increase in public safety, a safer community, cost savings on a local and state level, continued reduction in recidivism and an overall improvement in the quality of life for those returning to our community. Outcomes will be measured by capturing data regarding rearrests, reconviction and return to FDC rates. Data collection and analysis will be evaluated on a regular basis to ensure adequate oversight and compliance. Programming will also be monitored in person as well as through regular review of case notes and data entered into our shared database system.

1051.description: The Palm Beach County Fire Rescue (PBCFR) seeks funding for water vessels and trailers in order to increase the readiness/ability to respond to water related incidents. PBC is specifically mentioned in the County's Hazard Specific Plans for Dike Failure of the Herbert Hoover Dike as well as for flooding. Our most vulnerable populations are at risk. There are over 33,000 flights over Lake Okeechobee each month, numerous boaters and fishing tournaments, as well as other activities that occur monthly. These boats will allow the PBCFR the ability to respond to any emergency on the water.
1051.purpose: To increase the readiness/ability to respond to water related incidents. PBC is specifically mentioned in the County's Hazard Specific Plans for Dike Failure of the Herbert Hoover Dike as well as for flooding. Our most vulnerable populations are at risk. There are over 33,000 flights over Lake Okeechobee each month, numerous boaters and fishing tournaments, as well as other activities that occur monthly. These boats will allow the Palm Beach County Fire Rescue (PBCFR) the ability to respond to a
1051.activities: Emergency response by boat to incidents in areas that cannot be serviced quickly in emergencies with current equipment. For example, the Rib Boat/Hard bottom boat is capable of traversing the deeper locations on Lake Okeechobee. The airboat(s) is capable of crossing the swamp and shallow parts of lake but is not capable of covering the larger open water areas of the lake in adverse conditions.
1051.direct_services: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue will be able to drastically improve the available resources, provide for the safety of our personnel as well as the timeliness of responding to emergency calls on Lake Okeechobee. The PBCFR will also be able to provide a valuable resource to the Ag Reserve area which is currently not available.
1051.population: The 1.5 million residents of Palm Beach County, the millions of visitors to the county each year, and potentially the residents and visitors of other jurisdictions located around Lake Okeechobee and the Arthur Marshall Wildlife Reserve.
1051.outcome: The PBCFR will be able to drastically reduce response times and patient contact times to areas with limited access. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue will be able to drastically improve the available resources, provide for the safety of our personnel as well as the timeliness of responding to emergency calls on Lake Okeechobee. The PBCFR will also be able to provide a valuable resource to the Ag Reserve area which is currently not available.

1898.description: Replace the 1956 Cherry Lake Dam, classified as a significant hazard potential structure by the National Inventory of Dams, with a modern structure that will ensure on-going protection and safety of residents and properties downstream of the existing dam from major storm events and maintain water levels and flow rates throughout the upper Ocklawaha River basin.
1898.purpose: The requested funds will support the replacement of the aging Cherry Lake Dam Structure to ensure continued optimal water-level management and flood protection for the watershed. The project's goal is to restore the dam's full functionality, improve public safety, and maintain downstream ecological balance by providing reliable water control infrastructure.
1898.activities: Activities will include engineering design, permitting, and demolition of the existing deteriorating structure, and construction of a new reinforced concrete dam with updated gates and control systems. Services will also include geotechnical analysis, environmental protection measures during construction, and installation of new instrumentation to monitor flow and water levels in coordination with the U.S. Geological Survey Network
1898.direct_services: The project will directly protect nearby residents, agricultural areas, and public lands from flooding, while preserving recreational opportunities such as boating and fishing on Cherry Lake. Citizens benefit through improved water management reliability, protection of property, and enhanced ecosystem stability supporting water quality and wildlife habitat.
1898.population: The project serves approximately 20,000 to 25,000 thousand residents located within the Cherry Lake and Palatlakaha River watershed in Lake County, Florida. It also benefits visitors who use the Clermont Chain of Lakes for recreation and supports the broader downstream population of more than 100,000 residents by maintaining proper water flow and flood protection for connected waterways.
1898.outcome: Replacement of the dam with a higher conveyance capacity modern structure. Reduced flood risk and improved water-level & flood control. Provide measurable improvements in water conveyance and safety inspections. Improve ecosystem health. Success will be measured through compliance with State & Federal dam safety standards, and post-construction monitoring data, in combination with U.S. Geological Survey.

1171.description: Lakewood Ranch Medical Center (LWRMC) is experiencing significant growth in obstetric deliveries, reflecting the rapid expansion of the Manatee and Sarasota County region. To meet the increasing demand for advanced neonatal services, LWRMC seeks state support to establish a Level II, 6-bed Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).
1171.purpose: The goal is to provide expert neonatal services to the local community and Sarasota and Manatee Counties. Establishment of a Level II, 6-bed Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) to meet the increasing demand for advanced neonatal services. The new NICU will double the number of neonatal intensive care beds in the County. The new NICU will allow families to remain intact, closer to home, by not having to seek care or be transferred outside of the area for maternal care.
1171.activities: Lakewood Ranch Medical Center and The Women's Center will provide specialty care and services for: - Women with high-risk pregnacies - Intensive care services to premature babies or critical newborns - Care for neonates requiring close monitoring and specialized support - Specialty care for infants recovering from serious health conditions
1171.direct_services: Neonatal Intensive Care Units offer and provide life-saving care for infants and premature babies. The specialized unit will provide: - Advanced monitoring and treatment for premature and high-risk infants - Immediate access to neonatal specialists for emergency and ongoing care - Support for high-risk pregnancies and complex deliveries - Family-centered care, minimizing separation between parents
1171.population: The target population are high-risk mothers and their families. This is an extremely vulnerable population in the growing community of Lakewood Ranch and the surrounding region. It is estimated the new NICU will care for approximately 120 NICU patients and their families annually for the initial 2 years and increase to over 135 each year thereafter. We project the specialty service will increase the growing number of births being delivered at Lakewood Ranch by over 500 per year.
1171.outcome: We expect the primary and overall benefit to the community in the increase in high-risk, specialized care for the neonatal population. These benefits include, but are not limited, to: - Improved neonatal outcomes: Timely, advanced care provided in a safe and specialized setting - Family impact: Keeping families together, reducing travel and financial burdens - Community health: Expanding access to critical neonatal services within a growing population center - Regional benefit: Positioning Lakewood Ranch and surrounding counties with the infrastructure to support continued growth and healthcare needs

1899.description: To meet the increasing demand for programs and activities, Trout Lake Nature Camp (TLNC) began to improve its infrastructure and education facilities in 3 phases. Phase 1 was completed. Phase 2 will be fully completed in the next month and was partially funded by the State of Florida. Phase 3 is building an ADA accessible, environmentally sustainable, building to house a museum, meeting spaces, community space, gift shop, and offices along with a screened education area to connect new and existing buildings. For FY 2025-26, a $1,000,000 funding request was submitted. TLNC received $500,000 to construct and furnish a new building. Due to this partial funding, additional funds are needed to complete the interior of the building, develop and install museum exhibits, and potentially renovate portions of the existing education building.
1899.purpose: Provide nature-based education for the region, visitors, and students. To expand programs and increase our capacity to meet demands for programs and services, we need to build additional classrooms (indoors and outdoors), replace our aging natural history museum trailer, provide ADA accessible bathrooms and add meeting rooms. Construction will allow for a nature play area for smaller children and provide additional space to offer overlapping programs.
1899.activities: Contractor has been selected and first pre-construction meeting to build a 10,000 SF building. Preliminary design has been started with contractor and TLNC. Completion of needed construction drawings and plans to be able to apply for needed permits and begin the construction bid process.
1899.direct_services: Serving as the only nature center in Lake County, TLNC will be able to expand education programs and events and add new programs. Having an updated and improved interpretive natural history museum will benefit visitor's learning. Concurrent programs will be possible and business retreats, professional development training and eco-therapy programs can be expanded.
1899.population: In the past 9 years, TLNC has provided 600 student field trips to students within and without Lake County reaching about 232,000 students with these learning experiences. In addition, TLNC programs, activities and trails have been used by an additional 295,000 people allowing us to educate a little bit more than half a million people. Annually, we service about 30,000 people with a variety of programs and trail and exhibit visitations.
1899.outcome: Programs are evaluated using quantitative and qualitative methods, visitation is tracked, participant numbers recorded and online reviews are used.

1432.description: The purpose of this funding request is to repair/replace the Dogwood Ave lift station in Havana. These repairs were highly recommended by the Florida Rural Water Association. Havana is working with Florida Department of Environmental Protection State Revolving Fund for project funding however, cannot afford the agreement amount.
1432.purpose: Provide functional and efficient waste water system for the community. FRWA has provide a review of the 5th Ave lift station and has confirmed that they are in critical condition.
1432.activities: Provide functional and efficient waster water system for the community.
1432.direct_services: Clean, safe, and modernized waste water system.
1432.outcome: The level of benefit can be measured by the efficiency in delivery of waste to the treatment plant, the total reduction in alarm calls for pump stoppages, a reduction in service calls, and total reduction in waste spills.

1433.description: The purpose of this funding request is to repair/replace the 5th Ave lift station in Havana. These repairs were highly recommended by the Florida Rural Water Association. Havana is working with Florida Department of Environmental Protection State Revolving Fund for project funding however, cannot afford the agreement amount.
1433.purpose: Provide functional and efficient waste water system for the community. FRWA has provide a review of the 5th Ave lift station and has confirmed that they are in critical condition.

1433.outcome: The level of benefit can be measured by the efficiency in delivery of waste to the treatment plant, the total reduction in alarm calls for pump stoppages, a reduction in service calls, and total reduction in waste spills.

1434.description: This funding will be to finish building a new high school in Wakulla County. Special facilities funding was committed to this project at an original cost of $65,848,580 in 2023. This funding was to be distributed over a three year period. Due to substantial construction costs increases and the way the school cost was originally calculated using the per student station formula additional funds are needed to finish the school. This request includes the original third year funding and an additional $32,407,046 to finish the school.
1434.purpose: The purpose of the funding will be to finish the construction of the new high school. This will be the only public high school in the county. The design of the school has remained exactly the same since the beginning of the special facilities process. The only thing that has changed is the cost of construction and the fact that the funding model used to fund this project is no longer being used due to the shortfalls that were re-occurring.
1434.activities: A new school will be provided for the students of Wakulla County ensuring that they are able to keep up with the education requirements of the state and the nation, allowing them to be able to transition into the trades or post secondary education path.
1434.direct_services: Currently the high school is in many ways the hub of the community. Numerous events, programs, and services take place there. On almost any weekday there are more people at the high school that any other facility in the county. This new school will allow this to continue as the county population grows.
1434.population: The approximately 4600 students are the target population that will be served, but the entire population of the county, <30,000 will benefit in some way from the project.
1434.outcome: There are many benefits and outcomes associated with this project; some of the most important ones will be a better learning environment, updated technology and classrooms, better school safety measures, higher graduation rates and student achievement scores, and increased student confidence.

1435.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1435.description: The project is designed to provide high risk lightning data access into existing platforms through strategically located, edge computing sensors with real-time alert capabilities. Detectors will be immediately deployed to high hazard risk areas where severe events are likely, based on existing fuel and environmental factors.
1435.purpose: The requested funding will significantly expand the state's network of high-risk lightning sensors. The sensors offer real-time data of high-risk lightning events to instantly detect fires. The state can operationalize the data to improve responsiveness and resource allocation to lightning-caused wildfires.
1435.activities: High-risk lightning data accessibility into existing platforms through strategically located, edge computing sensors with real-time alert capabilities. Detectors will be immediately deployed to high hazard risk areas where high-risk lightning events are likely based on existing fuel and environmental factors. Additional sensors deployed will enhance statewide coverage to high-risk lightning data.
1435.direct_services: Citizens and communities will benefit from an increased awareness and preparedness to high-risk lightning ignited fires. Currently, working with FiResponse and Foreflight has allowed for firefighters and emergency response leaders to leverage actionable intelligence to reduce response time by 10x, saving cost and lives.
1435.population: The targeted population for this project will look to focus on the communities with the largest impact to risk of wildfire within Florida. The deployment of the real time sensors will seek to enhance the overall coverage in the region where fuels and risk of wildfire continue to be a threat.
1435.outcome: Provides Florida Forestry Services and local communities access to real-time data to prevent potential catastrophic wildfire events. The speed, resilience and accuracy will help improve situational awareness and enhance workforce optimization for FFS. The enhancement of workforce optimization will efficiently place FFS crew in strategically focused areas to reduce impact of wildfire to communities. Success will be defined by how real time data from the newly deployed areas assists with early, real-time detection of potential wildfires caused by high-risk lightning. The goal is to streamline workforce by optimizing flight patterns, reducing acreage burned from Lightning-ignited fires and redu

1130.description: The proposed project aims to develop the Town's first Emergency Operations Command Center, eliminating existing operational gaps in the Town's emergency response plan. The new EOC will improve multi-agency coordination, enabling law enforcement to share intelligence, operational updates, and coordinate emergency responses. The project protects public health and enhances the Town's capacity to restore community lifelines following a disaster. The primary critical lifelines associated with this project include safety and security, energy, and communications.
1130.purpose: The Town of Cutler Bay aims to construct its first Emergency Operations Center (EOC) for residents and to house the Sheriff's Department. Currently, emergency operations are relocated to a corporate partner's building, which is unsustainable. Designed to withstand Category 5 storms, the EOC will enhance emergency preparedness, management, and response. It will also support technological needs and include a secondary power source, ensuring best practices in emergency operations.
1130.activities: The Town proposes constructing an approximately 7,000 square foot emergency operations command center. The building will be constructed to meet LEED Gold-Level Certification and withstand a Category 5 Hurricane.
1130.direct_services: The Town's project will protect public health and improve the Town's ability to re-establish community lifelines after a disaster. The primary critical lifelines associated with this project include safety and security, energy, and communications.
1130.population: The project is part of the Town of Cutler Bay's comprehensive approach to emergency management. The Town's population is 43,958 (Census 2022).
1130.outcome: The expected benefit/outcome is a fully constructed and operational Sheriff Emergency Operation Command Center that fosters public trust. The community will have a dedicated center which will improve the Town's resilience and sustainability. The project's success will be measured using monthly construction schedules and reports from the Contractors, to the Town Council during the building phase. Following construction, all data collected post disaster or crisis events will be utilized to improve upon re-establishing community life lines.

1152.description: The Town requests $300,000 in matching funds to support the restoration of the Bel-Aire Park Community Center. This Park is the only active public park within walking distance for residents living in the northwest quadrant. The building supports sporting leagues & academic programming; however, it was closed on July 11, 2022, due to the potential risk of structural collapse. Funds will be used to demolish the existing 1,375 sq ft building and construct a 2,500 sq ft universally accessible LEED-certified community ctr. & concession stand. The project enhances disaster response as the park may be activated as an emergency distribution site.
1152.purpose: The proposed project aims to demolish an unsafe community center facility and construct a new, larger facility that will support team sporting events, youth academic support programs, indoor recreation, and community gatherings (e.g., workshops for older adults, or outreach activities). The new building will meet current ADA and FEMA elevation and disaster mitigation requirements.
1152.activities: The project has two components: (1) Gain public input on the design plans and potential park activities, and (2) Construct an approximately 2,500 square-foot facility to support public recreation that meets LEED Gold Certification Standards.
1152.direct_services: The proposed project expands the availability of safe and accessible recreational spaces for citizens. Citizens in this community currently do not have a park within walking distance from their homes, and the existing youth and adult programs have been displaced due to the unsafe structure.
1152.population: The Town of Cutler Bay's population is 43,958 (Census 2022). The facility supports more than 800-grade school students and the general public each year.
1152.outcome: The Project promotes an active lifestyle by restoring a safe and accessible Park building within walking distance from homes, w/ the ability to provide tutoring, academic support, and mentoring for grade school youth which also improves the quality of education. The measure of success for this project is the re-opening of the Community Center. Methodology includes monthly planning/design/construction schedules/progress reports made to the Town Council by the Designers/Contractors.

1132.description: The Town of Cutler Bay is requesting $100,000 to develop a comprehensive Economic Development Plan that reviews the current Land Development Regulations, identifies gaps in workforce training, and lays out a marketing plan to attract new business that leads to gainful employment for South Dade’s residents. The Plan will consider existing conditions and future trends for economic development within the Town limits along the US-1 Corridor, Town Center District, and Federally Qualified Opportunity Zones.
1132.purpose: Cutler Bay is located in South Miami-Dade County (Commission District 8), an area that is experiencing great population growth. The Town has established itself as a great place to live and play. The Economic Development Plan will help the Town reach its goal of becoming a great place to work. The goal is to identify gaps in workforce training and create a marketing plan to attract new business that leads to gainful employment for South Dade’s residents. The Town also values entrepreneurship and
1132.activities: The project has two components: (1) Assess existing conditions and conduct a needs assessment to support economic growth within the Town. Identify ways to promote and capitalize on benefits offered in opportunity zones, and (2) Identify strategies to promote the growth of small businesses and foster entrepreneurship.
1132.direct_services: The Town shall conduct a needs assessment and a series of public involvement meetings to gain citizens’ input on the future growth and development of the community. This includes directly engaging the business community.
1132.population: Small Businesses, General Public, Large Employers
1132.outcome: The outcome of this project will be the adoption of an economic development plan that will lay out specific policy changes and projects to stimulate economic development, facilitate the use and reuse of existing infrastructure, protect green spaces and natural resources, and promote sustainable and equitable development. The methodology for measurement includes data collection of the no. of new businesses, business expansions, new jobs, recreational venues, night life businesses, and business sponsorship/participation in Town cultural events.

1133.description: The Town is requesting $1,000,000 for Capital Improvements to improve the stormwater management system and treat runoff pollutants in the SW 207 Street and SW 85 Avenue corridors. The shovel-ready project aims to improve the existing drainage system by installing an additional 3,600 linear feet of exfiltration trench underneath the roadway, adding supplementary catch basins; replacing some existing catch basins, and installing additional supplementary exfiltration trenches and pipes.
1133.purpose: The project aims to improve water quality and mitigate flooding in a hazard area.
1133.activities: The shovel-ready project aims to improve the existing drainage system by installing an additional 3,600 linear feet of exfiltration trench underneath the roadway, adding supplementary catch basins; replacing some existing catch basins, and installing additional supplementary exfiltration trenches and pipes. The existing catch basins will be modified to provide sediment traps and pollution retardant baffles to protect the French drains. Additional French drains, catch basins, and/or manholes will
1133.direct_services: The proposed project reduces the flood risk for the residents of Cutler Bay and protects the Town's evacuation routes. Since incorporation, the Town has adopted higher regulatory standards and, currently, adheres to the base flood elevation standard, plus 1ft. above. Due to the efforts of the Public Works Department, the Town is currently rated by FEMA as a Community Rating System 3 which provides
1133.population: The Town of Cutler Bay's population is 43,958 (Census 2022), this project supports the entire community.
1133.outcome: The benefit of this Project is the decreased amounts of pollutants into Biscayne Bay & surrounding communities such as SW 207St. & SW 85 Ave., coming from the Town's outfalls which empty directly into the Bay. Methodology for measurement includes the implementation of water quality treatment data collection, which measures and quantifies the reduction load of pollutants to the bay. Proposed reductions are: 92.7% reduction in Total Phosphorus, 89.5% reduction in Total Nitrogen, and 90.6% reduction in Total Suspended Solids.

1228.description: The Mental Health Clubhouse Supported Employment program increases the financial independence of adults living with Severe and Persistent Mental Illness by equipping them with the skills and industry certifications needed to fill the staffing needs of area employers. Combined earnings of Clubhouse members statewide were $4,719,943 in FY 2024-25 and $11,456,672 over the last three years. Recurring state funding allocates $1.8 million to DCF to support 14 of Florida's Mental Health Clubhouse programs at approximately $129K each. The Legislature provided equivalent non- recurring state support for four new Clubhouse programs in 2023, re-appropriated in 2024. Since then, two additional clubhouses have opened. State funding would allocate proportionate funding for the six new Clubhouse programs and provide support to all 20 Florida Clubhouse programs to help more adults with SPMI transition f
1228.purpose: Expand workforce training for adults with SPMI at 6 new Mental Health Clubhouses and a full-time Coalition Coordinator under contract for one year to provide expert training and assistance for new Clubhouses to prepare for and meet the 37 Clubhouse International standards for accreditation, ensure that accredited Clubhouses maintain their accreditation, and provide more vocational training and job placement opportunities for Clubhouse members through employer outreach and recruitment.
1228.activities: Provide proportionate funding for six new Mental Health Clubhouse programs -- MHA Belle Glades Clubhouse (Palm Beach); Academy at Bradenton (Manatee); Club Success Haines City (Polk); ACTS Tampa Clubhouse (Hillsborough); Key Clubhouse (Miami-Dade); and Chobee Clubhouse (Okeechobee) -- to help adults with SMI transition from being a tax burden to becoming taxpayers.
1228.direct_services: All 20 Florida Mental Health Clubhouse programs will receive essential financial and technical support to ensure their programs are fulfilling the staffing needs for area employers while equipping more than 2,500 Clubhouse members with the skills needed to fill jobs, increasing member independence and recovery while reducing their dependency on state benefits. On-site visits to all 20 Clubhouses w
1228.population: 2500 Florida residents living with SPMI. Combined earnings of Clubhouse members statewide were $4,719,943 in FY 2024-25.
1228.outcome: This request would ensure that the six new Clubhouse programs in Manatee, Hillsborough, Polk, Miami-Dade, Okeechobee and Palm Beach counties receive the same level of state support to help their members secure and sustain employment in the competitive marketplace. Independent studies have found that one year of holistic recovery services are delivered to Clubhouse members for the same cost as a 2-week stay at a psychiatric hospital. Clubhouse members experience a significant decrease in hospitalizations, reduced incarcerations & reduced criminal justice system involvement. Clubhouses are active participants in the recovery-oriented system of care, a core DCF strategy. The Clubhouse model is

Last year, CFCC served over 7500 disadvantaged children and families in Palm Beach County alone, partnering with public and private local stakeholders, yet referrals to CFCC have continued to increase. In 2023, CFCC received a state appropriation to expand its own capacity and eliminate the wait-list of 500-1000 families waiting for services from CFCC. 2040.activities: New bachelor level and masters level behavioral health professionals will participate in the in-person and web-based training programs, curriculum, and supervision. CFCC utilizes an innovative training approach, which provides a combination of site based and web-based training to CFCC student interns and new clinical staff. Phase 1 of the curriculum promotes the integration of theory and practice among staff and situates their perspective within the context of CFCC’s client populations. Phase 2
2040.direct_services: Ultimately, CFCC expects the program to contribute to the statewide pipeline of available and well-trained bachelor and master's level youth mental health professionals, who are then able to serve thousands of children in need across Florida, many of whom have been victimized by adverse childhood experiences like trauma, abuse, and violence. CFCC has a long history working in the community (since 1999) and is well supported, with numerous letters of recommendation from local elected officials and community organizations/partners on both sides of the partisan divide. CFCC's public health framework has, for years, been focused on building caregiver and community capacity to support children's mental health.
