The funds will be used toward the project's planning and design.
2528.purpose: As statutorily required, the Florida Museum of Black History Task Force selected St. Johns County as the location for the statewide Museum of Black History. The funds received will be used toward project planning, design, engineering, and administration of the project.
2528.activities: This multi-stage project will design and construct the Florida Museum of Black History campus, which will serve as a nationally significant museum and performing arts center to enhance the public's access to African American History, provide new opportunities for education and research, and further the cultural enrichment of Floridians and the many national and international patrons that will visit the museum.
2528.direct_services: Museum exhibits will provide the opportunity for citizens to learn about Florida's rich history as it relates to African Americans. The performing arts center is expected to attract renown concerts and theatrical events. In partnership with Historically Black Colleges and Universities, the museum campus will serve as a center for African American historical research.
2528.population: This project will serve the general population to include all Floridians, as well as national and international visitors. The campus will host exhibits and events relevant to all age groups. Thousands of patrons are expected to utilize the facilities on the campus annually.
2528.outcome: Enhanced economic activity, increased tourism, creation of new job opportunities, increased access to African- American history and education, and improved quality of education. The outcomes will be measured by utilizing data collected by the museum and the appropriate local and state agencies.

2530.organization: St. Johns County Board of County
2530.description: Phase I of this multi-stage project entails the design of core regional park components, including recreation amenities, marine basin, boat ramps, a Unified Emergency Water Rescue Substation, parking, and access points to the transportation network. Adjacent to the San Sebastian River, the project site connects to the Florida Greenways and Trails System (Priority Paddling Trail). The project also aligns with the goals of Florida's Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan, which encourages healthy and active lifestyles choices.
2530.purpose: The project goals include the promotion of healthy and active lifestyles through outdoor activity, fostering opportunity for economic growth and meeting the stated priorities of Florida's Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP). Specifically, the project fulfills all four priorities of the 2019 SCORP: 1) health and wellbeing; 2) public access, accessibility and connectivity; 3) economic opportunities and ecotourism; and 4) resource management and stewardship.
2530.activities: The project will result in the final design of a waterfront park that meets Florida's Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan and provides increased recreational opportunities for both visitors and residents. The design will support a connection to the Florida Greenways and Trails System Designated Paddling Trail. Per a 2017 statewide study commissioned by the Department of Environmental Protection, boating and other saltwater activities are ranked in the top 5 of all outdoor activities
2530.direct_services: The unified emergency water rescue substation will be used to stage and deploy watercraft, enabling rapid response and rescue operations across the numerous recreational inland waterways accessible from this facility. This project will significantly reduce response times, allowing for quicker patient contact and ultimately saving lives.
2530.population: This project will benefit not only the residents of St. Johns County (population 306,841), residents from surrounding counties, and the 7 million tourists who visit St. Augustine each year.
2530.outcome: The project provides an additional outdoor recreational opportunity for residents and visitors to St. Johns County which encourages physical activity and is measured by numbers of patrons utilizing the facility and attending recreation programming at the park. The waterfront park will provide an opportunity for boating access to the many waterfront historical sites in St. Augustine, including Fort Matanzas, Castillo de San Marcos National Monument, and Fort Mose. The increased economic activity is measurable through TDC statistics.

2561.organization: St. Johns County Board of County
2561.description: Design, permitting, construction, post-design services and CEI of State Road 16 widening to 4 lanes from International Golf Parkway to Interstate 95. The project features bike lanes, medians to prevent illegal passing, sidewalks, and/or a multi-use path linking pedestrians and bicyclists to a regional park. The project improves traffic and pedestrian safety, enhances transportation network connectivity, and provides traffic flow resiliency with direct connections to CR 2209 and Interstate 95, a SIS facility.
2561.purpose: Design, permitting, construction, post-design services and CEI of State Road 16 widening to 4 lanes from International Golf Parkway to I-95 . The project will feature access management, medians to prevent illegal passing, and may include bike lanes, sidewalks, or multi-use paths that will link pedestrians and bicyclists to a regional park. The project improves traffic and pedestrian safety, enhances transportation network connectivity, and provides traffic flow resiliency with direct connections
2561.activities: Contracted services will be procured to design, permit, engineer and construct the widening of State Road 16 from two lanes to four lanes from International Golf Parkway to I-95 including intersection improvements at International Golf Parkway and County Road 2209.
2561.direct_services: The project constructs a 4-lane divided highway which increases the efficiency and level of service of a primary evacuation route. Per FDOT's summary analysis, this project reduces the potential for head on vehicular collisions on a high speed roadway.
2561.population: This project will benefit not only the residents of St. Johns County (population 320,110), residents from surrounding counties, and the 10 million tourists who visit St. Augustine each year.
2561.outcome: Per FDOT's summary analysis, this project reduces the potential for head on vehicular collisions on a high speed roadway. The project increases the efficiency and level of service of a primary evacuation route by decreasing existing traffic congestion and removing single-lane bottlenecks. This will mitigate existing traffic obstruction, which routinely delays emergency response times.

2562.description: The project will be for an Education Building that will also function as a residential hurricane shelter on the new transitional housing campus in St Johns County for 180 women and children. The education building will house all of our support services for both our two-year transitional housing and permanent, affordable housing residents to access vital resources such as counseling, education, job training, medical services, financial literacy classes, a daycare and after school program, a full service kitchen and dining hall with administrative offices. In addition to the building being used for our resident services it will also be used by community members who access essential needs such as diapers, baby needs, formula, and clothing vouchers. This community building will also be open to the public during hurricane moths for emergency shelter.
2562.purpose: The purpose of this education center is to provide a residential emergency shelter during natural disaster, and ongoing daily support services to women and children whom reside in our transitional and permanent housing.
2562.activities: This education building will be located on the campus of multi-site housing that will encompass case management for residents, a daycare, a full service kitchen and dining hall for residential community meals, job training, continuing education classes for obtaining higher education opportunities and career path development, medical clinic, library, individual and group counseling with life-skill community taught workshops, technology lab, before and after school care, and administrative offices
2562.direct_services: Residential shelter will be provided during a hurricane or natural disaster, and ongoing community closet that distributes free diapers, baby essentials, formula, clothing vouchers, hygenic items and a resource desk with personal help to find additional resources for crisis and long term solution support contacts.
2562.population: Transitional and Affordable/Permanent housing. Transitional two-year program housing demographic: young mothers between the ages of 18-28 yr, children age 0-10 yr, senior women between the ages of 60 and up. Permanent housing demographic: 18 years-60 plus. All ages: Community Hurricane Shelter and Community Resources
2562.outcome: Provide a place that will give vital resources to strengthen young mothers, their children, and senior women who are experiencing housing and food insecurity due to a lack of stable housing, education, mental instability and job insecurity. Our education building will be a place for women and children to break the cycle of poverty to become self sustaining, and live in financial independence all within a loving and supportive community. The education building will be easy to access. Seniors have on campus access to medical services, activities, and meals. Mothers will be on campus as safe care is provided for their children as they receive their education. Transportation will no longer be a

2565.description: The programs - Community Action Teams (CAT) and Coaches - provide intensive, comprehensive in-home community- based services with a multi-disciplinary team using a High-Fidelity Wraparound model for St. Johns, Flagler and Putman County children and youth, ages 6-21, with a history of mental illness, substance abuse, and multiple treatment failures. These children are at risk of out-of-home placement such as child welfare, DJJ, or hospitalization. Most children served are from low-income, underserved and under-insured homes.
2565.purpose: The programs offer intensive, comprehensive in-home community-based behavioral health services through a multidisciplinary team using a High-Fidelity Wraparound model for children and youth ages 6-21 in St. Johns, Flagler, and Putnam counties. The programs serve those with a history of mental illness, substance abuse, and multiple treatment failures at risk of out-of-home placement in settings such as child welfare, DJJ, or hospitals. Most children served come from low-income, under-insured, and
2565.activities: Activities include individual and family counseling, assistance with navigating systems to access resources like housing, care benefits, additional diagnostic testing, and services as needed. It also involves coordination with school staff to address academic needs, crisis support, youth mentoring, and life skills training to promote stability, safety, and overall well-being.
2565.direct_services: Services include in-home professional counseling using evidence-based interventions provided weekly, at a minimum. The services also offer high-fidelity wraparound certified case management to foster collaboration between providers and youth support systems, helping maintain in-home stability, and youth mentoring to develop an ongoing individualized wellness recovery plan for youth.
2565.population: Youth age 6-21 with a history of mental illness, substance abuse, and multiple treatment failures, who are at risk of out-of-home placement in St. Johns, Flagler and Putnam counties. The funding is expected to provide services to between 101-200 youth.
2565.outcome: To improve youth functioning in the community and reduce out of home placement. 80% of referred youth remain in the community and do not require intensive placement, which will be documented through discharge and aftercare planning. Ninety percent of youth who successfully complete the program will show improved functioning on the CFARS scale, as measured by completing the CFARS at admission and discharge.

1365.description: With the highest number of pedestrian crashes in Miami-Dade County, Little Havana has seen a 160% increase in crashes over 5 years—from 145 crashes in 2020 to 386 in 2025, resulting in 284 injuries and 18 deaths. In response, Miami-Dade County has partnered with the City of Miami to transform pedestrian safety around one at-risk Little Havana school, Citrus Grove K-8 Center at 2121 NW 5th St, Miami, FL 33125. Thanks to State and local funding, Phase 1 improvements are delivering critical safety improvements along NW 22nd Ave., NW 6th St., and NW 3rd St. Phase 2 funding will complete this life-saving initiative by converting NW 3rd Street and NW 19th Avenue into a safe corridor, creating protected pathways that allow children to walk to school without fear in this working-class neighborhood. The project includes safer intersections, enhanced lighting, improved sidewalks, high-emphasis cro
1365.purpose: The funds will be used to design and construct pedestrian safety projects and essential stormwater improvements around Citrus Grove K-8 Center to make it safer for the children who attend the school, many of whom walk to school, and to reduce the number of pedestrian crashes, injuries, and fatalities.
1365.activities: Sidewalks will be constructed where none exist across the street from the school entrance. Crossing distances will be shortened with curb extensions. High-emphasis crosswalks and stop signs will increase pedestrian visibility for drivers. Trees will be planted every 30 feet, and sidewalks will be level (instead of sloped as is the current condition), to make it more comfortable for children to walk. Underground drainage will be upgraded. Street lighting will be upgraded.
1365.direct_services: Primary services include roadway safety for children walking to and from school, as well as stormwater upgrades. Citizens will have fewer collisions with cars, fewer injuries and fatalities, and a reduction in roadway flooding. Crash data from 2015-2019 compared to 2020-2025 showed a decrease in crashes at two Little Havana locations where similar safety improvements were implemented near Miami Se
1365.population: The target population served are children and families attending Citrus Grove K-8. 1,337 students attend the school.
1365.outcome: The expected outcome is fewer pedestrian collisions, injuries and deaths, and reduced flooding on roadways. There were 18 fatalities between 2020 and 2025, and 284 injuries according to Signal 4 crash data. Signal 4 collects crash data monthly, and this data will be used to measure outcomes.

1462.description: The Liberty County School District is requesting state dollars to enhance classroom safety and security at our three schools: WR Tolar K-8, Hosford K-8, and Liberty County High. Specifically, funds are needed to retrofit classroom door sidelights and install bullet proof film on the classroom windows that are vulnerable to outside threats.
1462.purpose: The Liberty County School District is requesting state dollars to enhance classroom safety and security at our three schools; WR Tolar K-8, Hosford K-8, and Liberty County High. Specifically, funds are needed to retrofit classroom door sidelights and install bullet proof film on the classroom windows that are vulnerable to outside threats. Due to the existing sidelight windows and exterior windows, an intruder can break the glass and enter the safe space. This means increased SAFETY for our stud
1462.activities: The Liberty County School Board, District/School administration, and the community have some grave concerns about the safety of our schools with existing sidelights (windows) in the classrooms and on the exterior of the school. Parents are also concerned if our schools are indeed safe from outside threats in our buildings. The purchase and installation of the new windows will help keep us safer!
1462.direct_services: The added safety retrofitting will also be an added bonus for citizens in the community who come to any and all school events.
1462.population: Primarily the target population are the students and staff at all 3 of our schools in Liberty County. This is about 1400 people on a daily basis. It will also provide added safety during public events such as graduation services, ball games, and parental participation events throughout the school year.
1462.outcome: The knowledge of having extra safety measures in place should make students and parents confident to send their children to school knowing it is a very safe environment. Hopefully we will never have an active shooter situation, but if we did, we know these safety window upgrades should drastically reduce loss of life.

1198.description: The Town of Bay Harbor Islands seeks funding to improve its stormwater system. The Town is on a major evacuation state road and surrounded by Biscayne Bay, deemed by the state as an impaired body of water. Significant and disruptive flooding continues to impact the Bay, contributing to groundwater pollution and repetitive losses to residents and businesses. Funds will specifically be used to enhance pump stations, increase outfall pipe sizes, tidal check valves and address other stormwater risks that ultimately improve environmental resilience and the Town's capacity to mitigate flooding.
1198.purpose: The Town of Bay Harbor Islands seeks funding to improve the resiliency of its stormwater system. Significant and disruptive flooding continues to impact Biscayne Bay contributing to goundwater pollution and repetitive losses to residents and businesses. Funds will specifically be used to enhance pump stations, increase outfall pipe sizes, tidal check valves and address other stormwater risks.
1198.activities: The improvements to the stormwater system include upgrading existing pump stations, and adding new injection wells, increasing outfall pipe sizes to enhance system capacity, and installing tidal check valves to prevent saltwater intrusion during high tides and storm events. Additional drainage improvements will be implemented to improve flow efficiency and reduce flooding risks throughout the Town which has state-wide impact by preserving Biscayne Bay waters from pollution and contaminants that
1198.direct_services: The project will provide residents and businesses with improved flood protection and drainage services during heavy rain and high-tide events. It will reduce roadway and property flooding, improve public safety and accessibility, and enhance water quality within Biscayne Bay. These improvements directly benefit citizens by protecting homes and infrastructure, minimizing disruptions to daily life,
1198.population: The project will serve residents from the Town of Bay Harbor Islands and multiple Miami Dade County municipalities that share access to the surrounding bay waters. According to the US Census Bureau estimates, the Town's population and neighboring municipalities total approximately 35,000 residents.
1198.outcome: The state deemed Biscayne Bay as impaired due to the level of pollutants in the water. The project will significantly reduce flooding frequency and duration within the Town, improve stormwater drainage capacity, and protect public and private property from flood-related damages. Enhancements to the stormwater system will also improve water quality entering Biscayne Bay by reducing pollutant and sediment discharge during rain events. Project success will be measured by comparing pre- and post-construction data, including reductions in flood-related service calls/complaints, observed standing-water occurrences, and water quality sampling results at discharge locations. Performance will also be

1464.description: Our goal is to restore , as much as possible, the natural hydrology of our part of the Panhandle, specifically the natural, historic watershed boundary that separated the St. Andrew/St. Joe Bay Watershed from the Apalachicola Bay Watershed and Apalachicola River Floodplain until it was breached by the USACE in the early 1900s with the Gulf Intracoastal Canal (GIWW). This breach has reversed the flow of the Jackson River, diverting over 10% of the total Apalachicola River Flow AWAY from Apalachicola Bay and harmfully discharging this river water and sediment into St. Joe Bay and St. Andrew Bay. This breach also eliminated the natural function of Lake Wimico and its surrounding marsh and drainage basin, which was to collect, store and filter local rainfall and send it down the Jackson River into Apalachicola Bay. The first step in this effort is a collaborative feasibility study between FD
1464.purpose: The first step toward restoring the the natural hydrology of the Panhandle and the historic watershed boundary that separated the St. Andrew/St. Joe Bay Watershed from the Apalachicola Bay Watershed and Apalachicola River Floodplain is a collaborative feasibility study between FDEP and USACE. Since the GIWW is the cause of this breach, and the only entity with jurisdiction on the GIWW is the USACE, by federal statute this study must involve both parties in an equal, cost sharing partnership.
1464.activities: The Collaborative feasibility study, these funds will pay for FDEP's share. The study, under federal guidelines, must provide potential solutions for any problems discovered. Executing any solution is a separate political act.
1464.direct_services: The entire economies of Gulf and Franklin Counties, and a good portion of Bay County, depend on the restoration of Apalachicola Bay, St. Joe Bay, St. Andrew Bay and Lake Wimico. Without the restoration of these ecosystems our tourism based economies will fail; with them they will flourish. Our tourism economies are multi billion dollar industries that depend solely on the environmental health of t
1464.population: Gulf and Franklin Counties Mostly, with a large contingent of Bay County as well. All citizens in all three counties will be served. The estuaries of these three bays serves as a nursery for ALL the reef fish in the eastern Gulf, so All of Florida will be served!
1464.outcome: The restoration of our natural hydrology, specifically the restoration of the natural, historic watershed boundary, will allow the economies of these three counties to flourish. We will measure our success with tourism numbers, economic data, bed tax revenues, property tax revenues, real estate sales and rentals, as well as water quality assessments, fish, oyster and shrimp catches, sea grass die off or proliferation, and decreased bay closures.

1241.description: This program expands Florida's maritime education pipeline by delivering interactive, STEAM-based learning experiences to K-12 students. Through hands-on activities such as ship building and ship exploration, the program introduces students, particularly those who are non-college bound to a wide range of marine-related careers. It incorporates soft skills training, digital engagement, and educator outreach to prepare youth for both land-based and at- sea opportunities. The initiative fosters industry partnerships and environmental stewardship, aiming to increase student proficiency in STEAM subjects, career awareness, and employability across Florida's maritime and marine science sectors.
1241.purpose: The goal is to continue expanding maritime career education in Florida through interactive STEAM-based learning for Grades K–12, offering hands-on opportunities that introduce students to a variety of marine-based jobs. The initiative will begin developing post-secondary pathways through strategic partnerships to extend maritime instruction and workforce readiness expanding to create a seamless educational pipeline that supports lifelong career development in the maritime and marine science sect
1241.activities: Students will explore a variety of fun lessons and activities focused marine career exploration, marine ecosystem protection. Through STEAM and SEL materials, they'll learn about ships, build their own boat, and discover the importance of protecting our planet's waters and ecosystem health, all while demonstrating how STEAM translates into real world job opportunities.
1241.direct_services: The funding provides Florida students with hands-on learning focused on maritime job exploration. Through engaging STEAM and SEL activities, students will explore ships, build boats, and connect classroom concepts to real-world maritime careers. These experiences promote teamwork, problem-solving, and environmental stewardship, equipping students with valuable life and workforce skills. In additio
1241.population: The program serves Florida students in Grades K–12, with a focus on non-college bound youth. and engaging post- secondary students through emerging partnerships with Florida colleges. In the 2024-2025 school year, the initiative reached over 2.5 million teachers, students, and families statewide through classroom instruction, digital platforms, and educator networks. Tens of thousands of students are expected to be directly served annually, with continued growth as curriculum and partnerships ex
1241.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a stronger maritime education pipeline in Florida, preparing students for future careers in the maritime, marine science, and related STEAM industries. Specific benefits include: Increased student engagement and proficiency in STEAM subjects through real-world maritime applications. Enhanced awareness of maritime and ocean-related career opportunities among K–12 students. Development of employability and soft skills, such as teamwork, communication, and problem-solving.Strengthened partnerships between schools, industry professionals, and maritime organizations, fostering long-term educational and career pathways. Ultimately, the project aims to build

2569.description: The City of St. Augustine is requesting state funding assistance to support the design and planning phase of infrastructure improvements required under Florida Senate Bill 64 (2021). This legislation mandates the elimination of non-beneficial surface water discharges of treated wastewater by January 1, 2032. The proposed project will fund preliminary engineering, environmental review, and design necessary to evaluate alternatives to ensure regulatory compliance and environmental protection.
2569.purpose: This planning effort represents a critical step toward long-term sustainability of the City's wastewater system, reduction of nutrient loading to local waterways and alignment with the State's goals for water resource management and reuse.
2569.activities: A professional engineering consultant will be hired to create alternatives for the City to consider that will eliminate the surface water discharge. The City will select an alternative or combination of alternatives and have the consultant begin the design and permitting of the system.
2569.direct_services: This planning effort represents a critical step toward long-term sustainability of the City's wastewater system, reduction of nutrient loading to local waterways and alignment with the State's goals for water resource management and reuse. It will serve all of the utility costumers in the City's service area.
2569.population: The City's utility service area which encompasses approximately 50,000 users.
2569.outcome: The expected outcome is to have designed and permitted construction plans ready to move into construction that will meet the requirements of SB64 (2021) and the statutes deadlines.

2727.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2727.description: Founded in 2021, Guardians of Florida Animal Rescue (“GOFAR”) provides a critical service to the community by providing a no-kill option, as well as medical and general care and temporary shelter, for animals being surrendered by owners, either voluntarily due to unsustainable situations (such as housing, financial or domestic issues), or involuntarily due to circumstances such as neglect, hoarding or cruelty cases. The current kennel buildings on leased property are in chronic disrepair. Cinder blocks are crumbling, external doors are rusting and allowing insects and rodents into the kennels, kennel gate doors are falling apart, and the HVAC design is not adequate to keep the AC on consistently. State funding would support $1.9M in private investment to build a new shelter, including 5 kennels/office space, 3 fenced enclosures and expand septic and well capacity to sustain its ability t
2727.purpose: Since its launch in 2021, GOFAR has transformed the lives of over 2,700 homeless, unwanted, neglected, stray and/or injured animals in its no-kill shelter. State funding would support $1.9M in private investment to build a new shelter, including 5 kennels/office space buildings, 3 fenced enclosures and expand septic and well capacity to sustain its ability to protect 200 unwanted and stray animals each day from being endangered or endangering communities.
2727.activities: The current kennel buildings on GOFAR's leased property are in chronic disrepair. This one-time state appropriation would support a new facility on recently purchased property. Without the new structures in place, GOFAR will soon be forced to reduce its operations by approximately 85% (with approximately 900 animals saved annually, 765 animals would be put at risk every year).
2727.direct_services: Removal of animals from situations that are abusive, endangering and/or neglectful, which include, but are not limited to: kill shelters, stray animals, owner surrenders and puppy mills; Temporary homes and appropriate care for rescued animals; Placement of rescued animals into responsible, permanent adoptive homes or providing sanctuary for rescued animals for which adoption is not feasible.
2727.population: GOFAR provides a critical service to pet owners in need of surrendering their animals by providing a no-kill option and takes in animals from county shelters across Central and South Florida lessening the burden for the facilities and reducing euthanasia rates for animals in those facilities. GOFAR also provides the community with companion animals through its adoption program. GOFAR positively impacts over 1000 community members annually through its intake and adoption programs.
2727.outcome: On average 200 animals each day will be protected from harm, nurtured and made available for adoption. Outcomes will be measured by the number of animals sheltered, placed and/or adopted, as well as the number of public community events and students participating in volunteer and hands on animal care to educate community members on the importance of spaying/neutering and responsible animal ownership.

1472.description: The specific focus is community revitalization and workforce empowerment initiative as follows: -Creating permanent and part-time jobs in STEM, Healthcare and cultural arts. -Supporting small business incubation through the HCDC's facility. -Boosting tourism via cultural and agri-business programs such as museum, dance program, and aquaponics farm. -Expanding skills training for those with limited education via STEM Gym and Farm-to-Table program. -Strengthening the local economic base and vendor participation.
1472.purpose: The program will provide a means for being proactive in the reduction of health issues via primary healthcare, access to healthy meals and physical exercises; indirect impact on the reduction of crime by providing especially youth a place to go and conduct constructive activities; reduction of healthy food desert; increased access to cultural events and activities; and enhanced ability for the community to get to events and healthcare.
1472.activities: Health and Wellness program; Recreation programs for all age groups; Farm-to-Table program; transportation; STEM Gym for science, technology, engineering and math activities; museum; African/Carribean dance program, reading program; and a transportation program.
1472.direct_services: Access to a gymnasium and recreational programs, access to fitness center, access to commercial kitchen for training how to cook healthy foods; access to community garden; increase access to healthy foods and training how to grow healthy foods; access to STEM activities that address standards being taught in the classrooms; access to cultural events via dance programs and museum; access to reading
1472.population: Citizens of Havana, Midway, Richbay, Hinson, Jamison, Gibson, Coon Bottom, Quincy and Tallahassee.
1472.outcome: Footprint to the facility will be greater than 5000. Records will be maintain, analyzed and concluded via the number of participants and comparison of county data to determine the effectiveness and success of the programs offered especially with the healthcare and recreational programs.

2735.description: Big Bend Hospice requests $990,000 of funding to remodel and modernize the Dozier House Inpatient Unit, which currently provides critical end-of-life care for patients and their families. This renovation will enhance comfort, safety, and dignity for patients, while also improving facilities for families and staff. The requested funding will cover: • Complete remodeling of 12 patient rooms (paint, new flooring, new furniture). • Furniture replacement throughout the unit, ensuring accessibility, comfort, and homelike design. • Kitchen renovation, allowing families and staff access to nutritious meals and supportive amenities. • New roof and outdoor exterior maintenance.
2735.purpose: The requested funds will be used to remodel and modernize the Dozier House Inpatient Unit, enhancing the quality, safety, and comfort of hospice care for patients and families. The renovation will create a more home-like, therapeutic environment that supports dignity at end of life, improves staff efficiency, and aligns the facility with current healthcare design standards and infection control guidelines.
2735.activities: These shortcomings not only impact the quality of care experience but also the healing environment that hospice care strives to provide. Modernizing this unit will elevate the patient and family experience and ensure our facility continues to meet high standards of comfort and compassion.
2735.direct_services: Activities include: Renovation of 12 patient rooms with new flooring, paint, lighting, and accessible furniture. Kitchen modernization to support family meals and nutritional needs. Exterior maintenance for safety and facility longevity. Upgraded family lounge and bereavement support areas to enhance the healing environment. Replacement of aging medical furniture and patient equipment to meet ADA
2735.population: The project directly supports inpatient hospice care for citizens facing advanced illness who require 24-hour skilled nursing and symptom management in a compassionate, home-like setting. The Dozier House serves as a critical safety-net facility for individuals who cannot be safely cared for at home due to medical or social needs. Services provided include pain and symptom management, psychosocial and spiritual support, and respite care for family caregivers.
2735.outcome: The target population includes terminally ill adults and children, as well as their families and caregivers, within Florida’s Area 2A counties. The Dozier House serves individuals regardless of ability to pay, including Medicaid, Medicare, and uninsured patients. Estimated 400–500 patients will receive direct inpatient care annually. Approximately 1,200–1,500 family members will benefit from supportive services such as grief counseling, family lodging, and respite care.

2967.description: Purpose: To expand access to community-based palliative care in rural counties of the Big Bend region through mobile health units, telehealth, and community outreach. Description: Funding will support three key staff positions: a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (Navigator), a Nurse Practitioner, and an Outreach/Mobile Unit Coordinator, to bring palliative care to underserved, rural counties. The project will enhance access to symptom management, advance care planning, and caregiver support through both in-person and telehealth services.
2967.purpose: To expand access to community-based palliative care in Florida’s rural Big Bend counties through mobile health, telehealth, and outreach services for adults with serious illness and their caregivers.
2967.activities: Mobile and telehealth palliative care visits Care navigation and advance care planning Community outreach events and education
2967.direct_services: Medical visits and symptom management Psychosocial assessment and navigation Counseling and caregiver support
2967.population: Adults with advanced illness and their caregivers in Leon, Jefferson, Madison, Taylor, Franklin, Liberty, Gadsden, Wakulla, Calhoun, Bay, and Jackson counties.
2967.outcome: Improved access to care: Number of visits and counties reached Improved patient/caregiver outcomes: Surveys and case reviews Community engagement: Number of outreach events, attendees, and partnerships formed

2982.description: Baker Senior Center Naples provides the only Dementia Respire Support Program in Collier and southern Lee counties for seniors who have a medical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and/or related dementias (ADRD) residing at home. The program is recognized as evidence-based, innovative, and most importantly, providing the highest standard of care to clients with dementia. The program provides socialization and wellness with a holistic approach to everyday living and challenges using activities that focus on connection when primary verbal communication and interaction abilities are altered.
2982.purpose: The goals of the program are: to offer opportunities for persons with Alzheimer's disease and/or related dementias (ADRD) to engage in a program of meaningful social and recreational activities in a secure and supportive setting, in order to maximize their cognitive and social abilities; and to provide relief and support to family members and other primary caregivers of individuals with ADRD.
2982.activities: Activities are designed to enhance communication skills, improve mood, help access long term memory, and increase socialization. The 4-hour groups include focus, concentration, and memory activities, such as "icebreakers," to help participants enhance social skills and assist in recall and language skills. Music therapy is provided by a credentialed music therapist for the last 30 minutes.
2982.direct_services: Language skills, memory techniques, relaxation techniques, socialization, and building self-esteem are concentrated on during each group's activities with the focus on what strengths the participants possess. Participants are offered an opportunity for socialization and cognitive stimulation in a non-judgmental, friendly environment. Participants are encouraged to participate in activities that en
2982.population: The targeted population are seniors age 60 and older with a medical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or related dementias (ADRD), which is 14.1% of Collier County. In 2017, 22,000 cases of ADRD were counted in Collier County. Of those 22,000, 13% live alone. Each year, this increases by an estimated 20%. Our community's limited existing resources are overwhelmed by demand. Thirty-six percent (36%) of Collier and southern Lee counties' populations are over age 60. Of those, 8% are 85 or older. It
2982.outcome: The Dementia Respite Support Program provides tools, support, and coping skills to assist these individuals and their families. Clients who attend the program may achieve the following goals and outcomes: be less agitated, more engaged in their surroundings, experience fewer incidents of "sundowning," particularly on the days when clients have music therapy, and caregivers report that the program has had a positive impact on both the client and caregiver's lives. The Memory and Problem Behavior Checklist is used for the clinical and empirical assessment measuring outcomes. For this population, outcomes are measured in relationship to a limited time period, such as during and after the progra

2985.organization: David Lawrence Mental Health Center, Inc.
2985.description: David Lawrence Centers (DLC) is requesting funding to support the implementation of the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) model at in Collier County. The CCBHC model is a nationally recognized framework designed to expand access to comprehensive, coordinated behavioral health services. Funding will enable DLC to meet certification criteria, enhance crisis response capabilities, integrate physical and behavioral health care, and improve outcomes for underserved populations.
2985.purpose: DLC will utilize the funds to bridge gaps in service areas and data collection/reporting required for CCBHC implementation, to include: same-day behavioral health service access, coordination of integrated care between behavioral health and primary care (through Federally Qualified Health Center), specialized services for veterans, and the development of a psychosocial rehabilitation program.
2985.activities: DLC will utilize the funds to bridge gaps in service areas and data collection/reporting required for CCBHC implementation, to include: same-day behavioral health service access, coordination of integrated care between behavioral health and primary care (through Federally Qualified Health Center), specialized services for veterans, and the development of a psychosocial rehabilitation program.
2985.direct_services: Behavioral health services to include: crisis support/emergency services, assessment, outpatient therapy and medication management, care coordination, case management.
2985.population: Adults and children with mental health and substance use disorder challenges. Adults and children needing access to primary health care. Individuals with serious mental illness. Veterans. Estimated numbers to be served > 800.
2985.outcome: DLC will improve readiness for certification as a community behavioral health clinic. CCBHC readiness ensures 24/7 access to crisis services same-day access, and access to care regardless of ability to pay or insurance status. Access to CCBHCs significantly reduces wait times and improves access to behavioral health services in underserved areas. CCBHCs improve access to primary health care.

2986.organization: David Lawrence Mental Health Center, Inc.
2986.description: As the demand for mental health services continues to increase, traditional inpatient care models often fail to meet the needs of individuals with chronic conditions who do not require 24-hour hospitalization but still need intensive care and support. David Lawrence Mental Health Center (DLC) Pathways to Healing Day Treatment/Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP) is a critical component of mental health care for adults with serious mental health challenges, offering a structured, intensive therapeutic environment that balances clinical support with the opportunity for community engagement and recovery.
2986.purpose: Funds will be used to support the Pathways to Healing Program (PHP), an adult partial hospitalization program (outpatient day treatment program) for individuals with behavioral health disorders requiring intensive day treatment as a bridge for the gap between inpatient hospitalization and traditional outpatient services. PHP provides clinical services for a minimum of 20 hours per week, five days per week. Services will be provided by a multidisciplinary behavioral health treatment team.
2986.activities: Partial hospitalization/day treatment structured behavioral health services, including: group therapy, individual psychotherapy, medication management, psychoeducation, psychiatric rehabilitation services, recreational and wellness therapies.

A new Customer Relationship Management (CRM)/Electronic Health Record (EHR) system will improve referral accuracy, follow-up, and client records. Phone-based peers will use our 200+ resource database to assist callers in crisis, schedule stabilized individuals for in-person support, develop recovery plans, and connect them to wraparound services. We plan to establish a dedicated Call Center, separating Helpline calls from participant calls. We plan to purchase furniture, equipment, and an EHR system for this center. This will strengthen our 24/7 services across our existing service area as well as allow for expansion in the future.
1244.activities: Funds will support the creation of a dedicated Call Center, including equipment, workspace, and a CRM/EHR system to improve Helpline operations. Activities include triaging callers, scheduling in-person support, providing recovery planning, and connecting individuals to treatment and essential wraparound services.
1244.direct_services: Phone-based peers will use our 200+ resource database to support individuals in crisis and schedule stabilized callers for in-person visits where they can create Recovery Management Plans and access wraparound services. Strengthening call-in operations eases pressure on in-person staff and streamlines RCCF’s ability to support all stages of recovery.

1247.description: The City of Oviedo (City) seeks funding for a public safety training center. This project aims to reduce preventable hospital visits, improve chronic disease outcomes, and strengthen the local workforce through job creation and integrated, patient-centered care.
1700.purpose: The East Marion / Ocala National Forest Health Access Project will establish a new community health center to expand access to primary, dental, and behavioral health services for rural residents. This investment not only addresses an urgent infrastructure need but also aligns with the city’s long-term goals for system expansion and modernization.

2318.description: The City of Lakeland (City) urgently needs to replace its aging Motorola P25 radios used by its public safety personnel and first responders. These radios, now 13 years old, have been unsupported by Motorola since 2023, and replacement parts are increasingly difficult to locate, making repairs unreliable, costly and time-consuming. This project will replace the existing radios with new Motorola APX N70 7/800 Model 4.5 Radios for the Lakeland Police Department and Lakeland Fire Department.
2318.purpose: The City's public safety radios are no longer supported by the manufacturer, creating a risk to dependable emergency communications. State funding will enable the replacement of outdated radios with modern, manufacturer-supported models to maintain reliable, interoperable voice communications, which are essential to officer safety, firefighter coordination, and public trust in emergency responses.
2318.activities: New Motorola APX N70 7/800 Model 4.5 radios will be provided to the Lakeland police department and Lakeland Fire Department.

2318.outcome: Replacing the existing radios will deliver several key benefits: - Improved speech clarity in high-noise environments; - Long-Term Evolution (LTE) network roaming capability when outside traditional radio coverage areas; - Enhanced encryption to safeguard sensitive communication; - Reliable connectivity with dispatch centers for seamless coordination during emergencies; and - Measuring can be performed by utilizing radio performance logs, and by monitoring radio system uptime and radio system coverage.

1916.population: Beacon's Florida students -- all, of which, have learning and attention issues (ADHD, Dyslexia, ASD, etc.) -- with high financial need will be eligible to be served and supported. There are approximately 70-100 students

1339.description: One Rake At A Time aims to continue restoration efforts in the lower Rainbow River. This project will utilize the same methodology that has been extremely successful in Kings Bay, Crystal River. One Rake At A Time has spent over 10 years hand raking and cleaning Florida's rivers but now it is clear hand raking alone will not be enough to restore the river. This project will utilize vacuum dredging to remove decades of muck and invasive plants from the river bottom followed by the replanting of native submerged and emergent plants.
1339.purpose: Funds will be provided to restore the impaired lower Rainbow River. Designated as an aquatic preserve in 1986 and an Outstanding Florida Water (OFW) in 1987, it was then deemed in 1989 to be a SWIM priority water body. The river has been declining for decades, and the lower river is especially impaired from historic phosphate mining. It is a world famous tourist attraction and critical habitat that will be restored. Educational opportunities for school children, visitors, and residents are plann
1339.activities: This project will remove millions of pounds of muck and legacy nutrients as well as invasive plants from the river bottom through selective diver held vacuums. Once removed, native plants will be installed and eventually these native plants will out compete the invasive plants to restore the river. As part of the agreement with DEP monitoring will continue for 3 years.
1339.direct_services: Rainbow Springs State Park is a hugely popular attraction drawing visitors from around the world. While the head spring is still full of native eelgrass, algae has begun moving in and threatening the health of the river. Cleaning the river will ensure all the businesses that rely on tourism such as boat and tube rentals, restaurants,and lodging, will continue to thrive and the natural beauty of th
1339.population: Anyone that lives on or enjoys the river will see increased water quality, a healthier river, and a decrease in toxic/harmful algae and invasive species. Businesses in the local community will benefit by increased tourism. Over 400,000 visitors are estimated to use the river annually.
1339.outcome: Increased tourism can be measured in numbers of state park visitors, the increased revenue from tourism in the local area, number of hotel rooms rented, number of boat rentals, etc. Increased beneficial/native plants are measured as part of the required annual survey that is conducted for 3 years post restoration. Reduction in nutrients such as phosphate and nitrogen can be measured by the thousands of pounds of organic muck and hydrilla that is removed from the river and by an independent third party biological assessment.

ZeroEyes will partner with Florida schools to deploy gun detection software on existing camera infrastructure across the State of Florida to mitigate gun violence.

2871.description: 211 GOLD (Guidance for Older Adults with Linkage and Direction) is a statewide initiative to strengthen Florida’s 211 network and better meet the needs of older adults. Reports show that 58% of Florida seniors live with multiple chronic conditions and are highly vulnerable during disasters. 211 data also shows seniors account for 27% of all calls, underscoring their reliance on 211 as a trusted lifeline. This program expands 211’s capacity to provide live support, wellness check-ins, and care coordination to ensure timely access to food, shelter, health, and disaster resources—reducing isolation, preventing crises, and helping seniors remain safe and independent.
2871.purpose: The funds will strengthen Florida’s 211 network to better serve the state’s 5.5 million seniors, 58% of whom live with multiple chronic conditions and account for 27% of all 211 calls. Staff will connect seniors to food, shelter, healthcare, and disaster resources, monitor follow-ups, and ensure services are effectively delivered year-round and during emergencies.
2871.direct_services: Seniors contacting 211 will receive live support from trained specialists who assess needs, provide tailored referrals, and conduct follow-up as needed. They will be connected to essential resources, reassurance calls, and care coordination that reduce isolation, prevent crises, and help them remain safe, connected, and independent year-round and during emergencies.

2142.population: Direct target population will be the Westlake community and three neighboring municipal communities with audiences to include children, teens and students, older adults and seniors, health/wellness and nature/environment enthusiasts.
2142.outcome: Benefits that enhance the quality of life, recreation and leisure opportunities that promote active lifestyles. Benefits also include health and wellness providing safe, accessible spaces for exercise, relaxation, and mental well-being. Other expected benefits include environmental with the preservation of green space, improved air quality and the strengthening of community and social connections. The outcome will be measured by the utilization of the park.

2043.description: This is part of the overall stormwater improvement project for the 640-acre impoundment expansion. This particular project allows ITID to move water to the west of the impoundment unhindered while also allowing the Florida Fish & Wildlife Commission to hold water levels much higher to the north of the M-O Canal in the J.W. Corbett Wildlife Management Area while keeping the area drier to the south of the M-O Canal for better wildlife management and the original ecosystem. This improves our ability to move stormwater during major rain events or hurricanes for ITID, Palm Beach Gardens, Royal Palm Beach, Palm Beach County, and FWC. This also can provide future water to the C-18 Reservoir that will replenish the Loxahatchee River Restoration Project for the SFWMD.
2043.purpose: Improved stormwater flow during heavy rainfall. Allows FWC to maintain higher water levels in the northern section of J.W. Corbett Wildlife Management Area (CWMA) while allowing lower water levels for the southern section of the CWMA. Potential future use of moving from the L-8 Canal and other STA's for SFWMD to the Loxahatchee River Restoration Project.
2043.activities: Vegetative removal and canal bank/levee re-enforcement.
2043.direct_services: Better stormwater removal to protect properties and life.
2043.outcome: This improves ITID's ability to move stormwater during major rain events or hurricanes for ITID, Palm Beach Gardens, Royal Palm Beach, Palm Beach County, and FWC. Allowing FWC to hold higher water levels north of the M-0 Canal. This also can provide future water to the C-18 Reservoir that will replenish the Loxahatchee River Restoration Project for the SFWMD. Measure levels of stormwater discharge, and in conjunction with FWC, monitor levels within the CWMA.

2045.description: This project seeks $750,000 in legislative funding to preserve and revitalize Camp Welaka, a historic 640-acre Girl Scout camp, which has been in existence over 70 years, along the Loxahatchee River. The investment will address critical infrastructure needs through bathroom facility reconstruction and ADA compliance upgrades, while implementing vital environmental restoration measures including erosion control and reforestation of the protective tree canopy.
2045.purpose: To preserve and revitalize Camp Welaka, a historic 640-acre Girl Scout camp along the Loxahatchee River that serves 10,000 Girl Scouts annually from six Florida counties (Martin, St. Lucie, Broward, Palm Beach, Okeechobee, and Indian River). This strategic investment will address critical infrastructure needs through bathroom facility reconstruction and ADA compliance upgrades, while implementing vital environmental restoration measures. These improvements will ensure continued access to outdoor
2045.activities: Activities include modernizing bathroom facilities to meet ADA compliance standards, upgrading program spaces for safe, accessible activities, and stabilizing waterfront areas for water safety education. Environmental protection measures will implement comprehensive erosion control, conduct strategic reforestation of the protective tree canopy, and stabilize grounds around existing facilities. Program enhancements will expand outdoor education opportunities, develop new leadership training space
2045.direct_services: The funding will support critical infrastructure and environmental improvements at Camp Welaka, enabling us to provide essential outdoor educational services to Florida's youth. Specific activities include modernizing bathroom facilities to meet ADA compliance standards, implementing comprehensive erosion control measures along our historic riverfront, stabilizing grounds to protect existing facil
2045.population: Camp Welaka serves Girl Scouts ages 5-17 from six Florida counties: Martin, St. Lucie, Broward, Palm Beach, Okeechobee, and Indian River. The camp directly serves 10,000 girls and their family members annually through outdoor education, leadership development, and environmental programs.
2045.outcome: The primary benefit of this project is to provide safe, modernized facilities at Camp Welaka that will serve 10,000 Girl Scouts annually from six Florida counties through essential outdoor educational programming and leadership development. Success will be measured through comprehensive facility usage metrics including program participation rates, ADA compliance, and quarterly occupancy data. Environmental impact will be tracked through regular assessments of erosion control effectiveness, tree canopy coverage, and waterfront preservation, ensuring the investment achieves its intended impact of providing a sustainable outdoor educational resource for generations to come.

2181.description: The Fire Watch is Florida's fight to end Veteran suicide. We've built an early intervention network of 10,000+ Florida community members trained to direct at-risk Veterans to resources they need. Where our network exists, suicides are down 12% since 2019. Where we're not, they're down only 2%. These funds will build an AI-driven Veteran suicide predictive model, expand the Watch Stander program, and reduce suicides, all in partnership with FDVA.
2181.purpose: The Fire Watch is Florida's fight to end Veteran suicide. We've built an early intervention network of 10,000+ Florida community members trained to direct at-risk Veterans to resources they need. Where our network exists, suicides are down 12% since 2019. Where we're not, they're down only 2%. These funds will build an AI-driven Veteran suicide predictive model, expand the Watch Stander program, and reduce suicides, all in partnership with FDVA.
2181.activities: These funds will build an AI-driven Veteran suicide predictive model, expand the Watch Stander program, and reduce suicides, all in partnership with FDVA.
2181.direct_services: Direct services are a network of community volunteers to identify risk signs of Veterans in crisis and direct those veterans to the resources they need and more insightful data. We have trained over 10,000 Watch Standers who will refer more than 12,000 Veterans to help over the next 12 months. Due to this, Veteran suicides are dropping. This funding will train 3,500 new Watch Standers.
2181.population: Veterans who are: elderly, have poor mental/physical health, jobless, economically disadvantaged, homeless, physically disabled, university/college students, currently/formerly incarcerated.
2181.outcome: Our program creates protective factors around at-risk Veterans to get them to the crisis or upstream help that they need, most often mental health services. We will increase Watch Standers by 3,500 (to a total of 13,500) during program year, achieve 70% Veteran Engagement and 30% Veteran Referral rates, and reduce veteran suicides in Florida by 25% over baseline 2022 year. We measure new trainees weekly and currently have 10,180 Watch Standers with a goal to reach 13,500 by end of FY 2026. We measure engagement and referral rates by a quarterly survey of Watch Standers. Veteran suicide data for each preceding full year is collected from FDOH by NLP Logix, with Florida's baseline year being 2

2048.description: Provides faculty and staff, including computer scientists, mechanical engineers, electrical engineers, data management specialists, graduate students and support staff at the Gulf Coast Research & Education Center. The Center will provide the structure and support for scientists to focus on the design, construction, evaluation, and demonstration of novel advances in technology for agriculture with an emphasis on rapidly moving technology from concept to prototype.
2048.purpose: Support applied research that leads to market-readiness; forge private-public partnerships with technology firms and start-ups; provide advanced education and vocational training and curriculum to create a highly skilled workforce.
2048.activities: Work on the design, construction, evaluation, and demonstration of novel, advanced technologies for agriculture with an emphasis on moving technology from concept to prototype. Provide a training ground for graduate students and Post-Doctoral Associates on practical applications of AgTech..
2048.direct_services: Increase opportunities for commercialization of AgTech; Support applied research that leads to market-readiness; and develop a highly skilled and experienced workforce to serve the needs of the industry and bolster the economy with employees qualified for higher paying jobs.
2048.population: Potential entrepreneurs, industry, agriculture producers, and UF students.
2048.outcome: The outcome will be measured by student employment, research outcomes, interest in public private partnership and attraction for technology firms to locate in Florida.

2322.description: Known as the Commissioner’s Academic Challenge, funding for the state academic tournament is used to provide a statewide, academic tournament for high-achieving students in grades 9 to 12 that is aligned with Florida's curricular benchmarks. Funding provided is used to set up and operate the tournament, offset registration and travel costs for student participants, and provide high-achieving students with the recognition they deserve.
2322.purpose: Known as the Commissioner’s Academic Challenge, state funding of the state academic tournament grant provides a statewide, curricular-based academic tournament for high-achieving students in grades 9 to 12. Funding provided is used to set up and operate the tournament, defray registration and travel costs for student participants, and provide high-achieving students with the recognition they deserve.
2322.activities: Training & materials provided to educators who then provide student with rigorous, academically-focused extra- curricular activities. Training for teachers with subject area expertise to write & review tournament questions directly related to state curricular benchmarks. Production of electronic displays, graphic displays, & audio components to aid in presentation of questions during competition.
2322.direct_services: Offset costs for student travel and participation. Local teams use material developed to prepare and conduct local and regional competitions prior to the statewide final tournament.
2322.population: Over 200 high performing high schools from about 45 of Florida's school districts, as well as charter and private school students.
2322.outcome: To provide rigorous academic high school competition to our most accomplished students. 1. The tournament will recruit at least 50% of Florida's school districts to participate and include charter and private schools. Outcomes will be measured by providing team participation logs, listings on event website, and participation by FDOE.

2050.organization: City of Palm Beach Gardens Engineering
2050.description: The City of Palm Beach Gardens Economic Development Infrastructure project will provide utility infrastructure to a 60- acre city-owned economic development parcel to create a shovel-ready site to attract primary job creation from targeted industries to serve as a job center for western Palm Beach Gardens.
2050.purpose: This project will create a shovel-ready site to attract primary job creation from targeted industries to serve as a job center for western Palm Beach Gardens.
2050.activities: Infrastructure installation on the economic development site, including providing water, sewer, and electric utilities will create a shovel-ready site to attract primary job creation from targeted industries.
2050.direct_services: Enhanced employment opportunities and economic impact of substantial primary job creation.
2050.population: This project will serve the general public by enhancing employment opportunities and the economic impact of substantial primary job creation.
2050.outcome: Primary job creation. Outcomes will be measured through various job creation reporting.

2051.description: The Regional Center Stormwater Improvements project consists of cleaning, inspection, repair, televising, and pipe replacement of the stormwater facilities in this major drainage artery of the city’s stormwater system. This work includes removing cubic yards of sediment and repairing or replacing stormwater pipes in the Regional Center. These improvements will help protect property, prevent flooding, and improve water quality that discharge into State drainage basins.
2051.purpose: This project will increase stormwater system capacity and conveyance and improve water quality, which will help to protect property, prevent flooding, and improve water quality that discharge into State drainage basins.
2051.activities: This project consists of cleaning, inspection, repair, televising, and pipe replacement of the stormwater facilities in this major drainage artery of the city’s stormwater system to increase stormwater system capacity, conveyance, and improve water quality.
2051.direct_services: Prevention of future environmental hazards, such as possible localized flooding of commercial and residential properties in downtown Palm Beach Gardens.
2051.population: Commercial and residential properties in downtown Palm Beach Gardens in addition to the general population who benefit from stormwater system improvements.
2051.outcome: Cleaning, televising, repair, and/or replacement of storm-water system will create additional storm-water capacity, conveyance, and improve water quality. Outcomes will be measured by cubic yards of sedimentation removed and linear feet of pipes repaired and/or replaced. Reduction of pollution into the groundwater and surface water quality by improvements of storm-water pipes, retention, and detention areas. Outcomes will be measured by the number of repairs to storm-water pipes, retention, detention areas, and linear feet of storm-water pipes repaired and/or replaced.

2183.description: This project will mitigate and reduce localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhance protection of residential homes from flood events, increase drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods. This is through design, permitting, and construction of new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2183.purpose: The specific goal is to construct the project for the purpose of mitigating and reducing localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhancing protection of residential homes from flood events, increasing drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods
2183.activities: Design, permit and construction of a new drainage system including new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2183.direct_services: The direct service will be increased drainage capacity and reduced street flooding in the drainage basin which will lessen impact to property of over 800 residential homes as well as maintaining the safety of an evacuation route and major North South connecting road in the Town.
2183.population: 82nd avenue provides connections to several residential communities as well as the business district on NW 154th Street. The target population is the surrounding residential community as well as the general population of road users that utilize this facility. Increased drainage capacity in this area would directly impact over 800 properties.
2183.outcome: Expected benefits include improved drainage, reduced localized flooding, increased drainage capacity, improved stormwater management, eliminated standing rainwater, reduced probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, reduced impact to property and life, enhanced environmental protection to the general public, improved transportation conditions, and improved groundwater and surface water quality. Outcome will be measured by field inspection and documentation of rainfall events. Project will create specific contractor, engineer, environmental, and consultant immediate job opportunities in stormwater and construction management measured by contractual agreements.

1098.description: This multi-trophic project aims to repair hurricane damage and address the ongoing challenges of sea level rise, shoreline erosion, flooding, and wind/water damage. These issues threaten lives, infrastructure, and the habitat at Pigeon Key, a National Historic District in Marathon, FL which serves as a popular marine education center welcoming thousands of students, visitors, and residents annually. To protect this vital site, innovative wave attenuation devices will be installed to reduce wave energy by 90%, helping to naturally rebuild sand around the island and eliminate the need for expensive beach renourishment. The project will also include the installation of tree windbreaks to reduce wind erosion, seagrass recruitment to slow waves through increased drag, and a living shoreline with mangrove planters to guard against flooding and further erosion.
1098.purpose: This multi-trophic project aims to repair hurricane damage and address the ongoing challenges of sea level rise, shoreline erosion, flooding, and wind/water damage. These issues threaten lives, infrastructure, and the habitat at Pigeon Key, a National Historic District in Marathon, FL which serves as a popular marine education center welcoming thousands of students, visitors, and residents annually. To protect this vital site, innovative wave attenuation devices will be installed to reduce wave
1098.activities: Activities will include manufacturing Wave Attenuation Devices that will be used to stop wave energy and erosion.

Protect lives, infrastructure, and habitat from severe weather events 3. Reduce the risk of storm and wind damage, and flooding of the Key's buildings 4. Improve essential fish habitat which will provide enhanced fishing opportunities 5. Improve
1098.population: The target population includes the residents and visitors of the City of Marathon and Monroe County. Population counts fluctuate due to the seasonal nature of the Keys with the population growing during peak season and decreasing during the off season. Marathon serves as one of the largest communities in the Keys and is often considered the "Heart of the Keys" due to its central location.
1098.outcome: Project will: 1. Restore and protect this vital marine education center for thousands of students and visitors 2. Attenuate 90% of wave energy, ending shoreline erosion 3. Rebuild/renourish and expand the shoreline naturally through sand accretion shoreward of the Wave Attenuation Devices eliminating the need for future costly beach renourishment projects 5.
