1200.description: Corrective actions in engineering and construction for the FDEP funded and permitted replacement of the existing North Plantation Key Transfer Pump Station (that has experienced several sanitary sewer overflows) with an in-line booster pump station in compliance with all necessary parties and in a time frame compliant with the FDEP issued consent order (OGC FILE NO. 25-0038) and Village response plan.
1200.purpose: The construction and commissioning of the in-line booster pump station in compliance with all necessary parties and in a time frame compliant with the FDEP issued consent order (OGC FILE NO. 25-0038) and Village response plan.
1200.activities: 100% of these funds will be utilized for construction.
1200.direct_services: Reduction in sanitary sewer overflows and elimination of odor by replacing the open tank with a closed system.
1200.population: Individuals expected to benefit from this project include all Village of Islamorada residents (population of 7,076 as of 2021 census) and the millions of visitors annually to the Florida Keys.
1200.outcome: The outcome of the project is to solve the effluent transient surge within the conveyance force main to Key Largo Wastewater Treatment District. Benefits will be measured by reduction in volume (gallons) of effluent overflows and breaks within the system, as well as residential complaint factor to measure odor reduction.

3565.description: Improvement or replacement of the public restroom facility at Oak Street Park. The existing building has exceeded its useful life and requires significant upgrades to meet current standards for accessibility, hygiene, and community use. Planned improvements include remodeling or reconstruction of the structure, updated restroom facilities, and replacement of all plumbing and electrical fixtures.
3565.purpose: Goal is to provide safe, modern and ADA-compliant public restrooms at Oak Street Park, improving accessibility, hygiene, and community usability for residents and visitors at this popular outdoor recreational facility that includes tennis courts, walking trail, playground area and picnic facilities. Restrooms are old and have exceeded their useful life. City is financially disadvantaged municipality that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO). To meet modern standards for accessibility,
3565.activities: To seek contractual services through the City's procurement policies and procedures for engineering, design, permitting, construction, and project management for the restroom renovation improvements, reconstruction, new plumbing, electrical systems, and ADA-compliant fixtures.
3565.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from safe, clean, and fully accessible public restroom & storage area facilities at Oak Street Park, enhancing the usability of the park for recreation, events, and daily community activities. Improving the quality of life and health in this financially disadvantaged municipality that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO).
3565.population: The target population in this financially disadvantaged municipality that is located in Hardee County, which is designated as a rural area of opportunity includes residents, visitors, elderly persons, the general public, and the surrounding areas. Population expected to be served exceeds 25,000 people.
3565.outcome: Expected outcomes include renovated restrooms resulting in improved public health, enhanced accessibility, and safer recreational experiences. Outcomes will be measured through ADA compliance, facility usage rates, community satisfaction surveys, and reduced maintenance issues. Completion and certification of the project.

2185.description: The Miami Lakes NW 155th Street Roadway Improvements Project includes the design, permitting, and construction relocation of the existing median parking to areas along the north and south curbs, adding a left turn lane at the intersections of NW 79th Avenue and NW 82nd Avenue, milling and resurfacing, new stripping, and signage. The project's proposed goal is to reduce traffic congestion on NW 154th Street, thereby decreasing congestion on the SHS SR826 off ramps, as well as improve public safety access for emergency vehicles at the nearby MDFR Miami Lakes West Station 64.
2185.purpose: Funds requested will achieve the purpose of reducing traffic congestion on NW 154th Street, thereby decreasing congestion on the SHS SR826 off ramps, as well as improve public safety access for emergency vehicles at the nearby MDFR Miami Lakes West Station 64.
2185.activities: Activities and Services provided are the relocation of the existing median parking to areas along the north and south curbs, adding a left turn lane at the intersections of NW 79th Avenue and NW 82nd Avenue, milling and resurfacing, new stripping, and signage.
2185.direct_services: Direct services to be provided to the citizens and general public of road users include reduced traffic congestion, improved transportation infrastructure and access, improved transportation conditions, and increased traffic flow.
2185.population: Target population served by this project are over 31,000 Miami Lakes' citizens, the general public of road users, and emergency vehicles traveling on NW 155th Street, NW 154th Street/Miami Lakes Drive, and SHS SR826 on ramps.
2185.outcome: Expected benefits include reduced traffic congestion, improved transportation infrastructure and access, improved transportation conditions, and increased traffic flow. Outcome will be measured by field observations. The project will create specific contractor, engineer, environmental, and consultant immediate job opportunities measured by contractual agreements.

1308.description: We will modernize and expand Florida International University's Aquarius Reef Base, (ARB) the only underwater saturation research laboratory and habitat available globally to scientists, private industry, environmental educators and federal civilian agencies.
1308.purpose: We will modernize and expand Florida International University's Aquarius Reef Base, (ARB) the only underwater saturation research laboratory and habitat available globally to scientists, private industry, environmental educators and federal civilian agencies. Funds will be used to upgrade the underwater components of the ARB, upgrade the support vessels, add a research laboratory and support spaces on land and implement a web portal for real-time water quality data visualization.
1308.activities: Scientific research (both pure and applied); human performance training from NASA and DoD; serving as an underwater test bed for marine technologies, water quality data collection, publication and visualization; K-12, university and postgraduate education.
1308.direct_services: Better environmental management of outstanding Florida Waters; more efficient management of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary; real-time information on water quality, boating and diving conditions in support of Florida's water-based economy; and environmental health; class room and experiential learning opportunities, cutting edge science support.
1308.population: Operators of water-based businesses in the Keys, fishers, scuba divers, environmental managers.
1308.outcome: Better understanding of the links between human modification of the water cycle and degradation of the water quality of the nearshore marine habitat of the Florida Keys. Fewer and less intense harmful algae blooms and increases in seagrass and coral cover.

1340.description: The Alachua County Sports Center Venue Versatility and Event Capacity Upgrade is a $500,000 capital investment designed to maximize the economic return of this fully County-owned and operated public asset. Funding will secure a portable collegiate level flooring system, an integrated sound system, and portable bleacher seating. These targeted upgrades are essential for expanding the facility's utility beyond track events, immediately allowing the County to attract collegiate and professional level court-based events. This infrastructure enhancement sustains momentum from major events like World Masters Indoor Track event in 2025, and is critical for helping the facility better compete with out-of- state rivals, generating a significant increase in sports tourism, event bookings, and hotel night stays for the region.
1340.purpose: The specific purpose is to transform the County-operated Sports Events Center into a versatile, multi-sport championship facility, maximizing its economic utility and tourist draw. The funds will achieve this by procuring a portable wood floor, integrated sound system, and bleacher seating, immediately enabling the facility to attract collegiate level and court sports. Hosting these cornerstone multi-sport events will significantly increase sports tourism traffic, maximizing hotel occupancy, and
1340.activities: County staff will provide professional management services and marketing of the facility. The team will coordinate the scheduling and rental of the facility for collegiate and professional level events made possible by the new court-based assets. These services fully integrate the Sports Events Center into the wider tourism and hospitality offerings of Alachua County.
1340.direct_services: The appropriation will support services related to year-round sports tourism and event hosting in a facility capable of providing multiple court sports alongside track and field. The facility also serves as an ideal venue for local events, trade shows, conventions, and concerts. This ensures a world-class, multi-functional venue, built to Class A institutional quality, remains available for local
1340.population: The target population is two-fold: out-of-county sports tourists (athletes, coaches, and spectators) attending high- profile weekend events, and local residents utilizing the facility for weekday practices and community events. Based on established economic modeling, the fully functional, versatile facility is expected to see an annual attendance of approximately 752,000 visits, with out-of-county visitors accounting for at least 54% of annual attendance, resulting in over 116,000 new annual hot
1340.outcome: The expected outcome is a significant and measurable increase in sports tourism revenue, achieved by allowing the Sports Events Center (SEC) to better compete with out-of-state rivals in markets like Birmingham, Alabama, and Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. The $500,000 investment in a portable collegiate level court system, sound system, and bleachers is critical to achieving competitive parity, enabling the SEC to successfully attract collegiate and professional level court-based events that it cannot currently host. The primary mechanism to judge success will be the impact on the hotel, tourism, and overall occupancy of the facility. This project is estimated to help generate over $77 millio

2920.organization: Alachua County Board of County Commission
2920.description: Alachua County Fire Rescue requests funds for the purchase of an Emergency Evacuation Vehicle (Bus) for the transport of medically compromised patients during a mass casualty incident, or during declared emergencies as a deployable state resource to evacuate patients or respond to post incident mass event. This vehicle will replace the current emergency evacuation vehicle provided by a 2012 UASI grant. As the bus has aged, maintenance costs (born by the County) are increasing. Alachua County's MSU Bus is one of the first requested assets by the Department of Health to assist in pre landfall evacuations and post landfall response. It has been deployed to South Florida and the Panhandle in almost every Hurricane landfall since being placed in service.
2920.purpose: Replacing the current MSU bus that is fourteen years old with a new, more reliable bus in order to continue deployments during declared states of emergencies.
2920.activities: The Emergency Support Unit Bus will be a state deployable asset responding at the request of Mutual Aid, Department of Health, or Emergency Management. The Mass Casualty Emergency Evacuation Vehicle provides rapid on-scene triage, advanced life support, and stabilization for multiple patients during large-scale emergencies. It coordinates patient transport, integrates with incident command and other responders, and ensures efficient deployment of medical resources to enhance emergency response c
2920.direct_services: The Mass Casualty Emergency Support Unit provides rapid on-scene triage, advanced life support, and stabilization for multiple patients during large-scale emergencies. It coordinates patient transport, integrates with incident command and other responders, and ensures efficient deployment of medical resources to enhance emergency response capacity and improve patient outcomes.
2920.population: The Mass Casualty Emergency Support Unit is a regional asset that can be deployed within the State of Florida.
2920.outcome: Mass transportation during critical public safety events and or declared emergencies. A new unit will ensure a reliable response. The measurable outcome is the total number of mass casualty incidents in which the mass casualty medical support unit is deployed and provides medical support each year. The Department will maintain a log documenting each incident including date, location, type of incident, and number of patients treated.

1974.description: Implementation of proposed improvements will reduce nutrient loading and help improve water quality in Newnans Lake, which is on the verified list of impaired waters in the Basin Management Action Plan for the Orange Creek Basin. Restoration of stream function and floodplain connectivity will provide hydrologic and habitat improvements, flood resiliency, and pollutant load reductions through stream restoration techniques, increased floodplain wetland area and contact time. Grant funds for the design phase of the project have been granted by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and additional funds are needed for the construction phase of the project.
1974.purpose: Newnans Lake has been determined by FDEP to be impaired for nutrients. A TMDL has been developed and BMAP implemented. This project will address the nutrient loads allocated to Alachua County in the OCB BMAP.
1974.activities: These funds will be utilized to construct the proposed restoration project, which includes a combination of stream, floodplain and wetland restoration. This will address the nutrient load from Hatchet Creek, which is the highest flow and nutrient contributor within Newnans Lake Watershed.
1974.direct_services: Citizens in the area will be positively impacted by the increased flood storage and flood resiliency that the project will provide. Additionally, they will benefit from the hydrologic restoration and improved water quality through improved quality of life and improved hunting, fishing and recreational opportunities.
1974.population: Population served includes citizens and visitors to Alachua County, over 270,000 persons annually. The area is already a popular eco-tourism destination. Newnans Lake is in the headwaters of the Orange Creek Basin, which includes Lochloosa and Orange Lakes. Newnans Lake is a popular lake for fishing, hunting, and boating with two County boat ramps and additional public access recreational areas managed by various state and local entities.
1974.outcome: This project will restore historic wetlands and restore the Hatchet Creek System, providing flood resiliency in an area prone to flooding as well as water quality improvement in one of Florida's verified impaired water bodies, Newnans Lake. Monitoring will be performed to measure project nutrient load reductions and overall project performance.

1923.description: To upgrade the existing culvert piping located under St. Clair Abrams that has failed with adequate size piping for current storm water flow to mitigate flooding in the Lake Frances community region.
1923.purpose: To reduce stormwater flooding. Eliminating emergency response issues, egress and ingress, possible structural and collateral damage to resident homes.
1923.activities: Drainage services will be provided for the general public to help with the flooding of this area
1923.direct_services: Reduce flooding to this area, eliminating emergency response issues, egress and ingress, possible structural and collateral damage to residents' homes.
1923.outcome: Reduce flooding to this area. This will be measured and monitored after each rain event.

1593.description: Casa Valentina bridges the gap in external support for youth transitioning from foster care to independent living. We offer safe, affordable housing paired with comprehensive wrap-around services to help young people navigate this critical life stage. Our goal is to expand our life-skills programming, providing tailored support to individuals aged 13-23 who are preparing to exit foster care or are at risk of instability.
1593.purpose: Casa Valentina addresses the abrupt transition from foster care to independent living, by filling in the gaps in external support. We provide safe & affordable housing, and intensive wrap-around services. We want to extend the life-skills based programming. Staff provides support services to 13-23 year olds on the cusp of transitioning out of foster care and/or who are otherwise at-risk.
1593.activities: Whether in a classroom, at one of our non-profit partners, or a DCF-approved placement facility, Casa Valentina delivers life skills services to any youth in the child welfare system of care. They participate in life skills group meetings lasting one to two hours.
1593.direct_services: The participants engage in life skills group meetings regularly. All sessions focus on the five pillars of success for youth transitioning into independence: 1) Education, 2) Employment, 3) Money Management, 4) Self-Care and 5) Household Maintenance. Activities are tailored to the participants' individual needs with the ultimate goal of making youth more resilient and self-sufficient.
1593.population: We will be working with economically disadvantaged youth who are considered at-risk of homelessness and/or involved in the foster care system, as well as youth in high school. We anticipate serving between 500-800 youth.
1593.outcome: We anticipate that youth will improve the quality of education; enhance their specific economic self-sufficiency; and improve in other key areas of general life skills in order to support them as they grow. Outcomes are measured through evidence-based methodologies such as the Ansell Casey Life Skills Assessment.

1302.description: In Broward County, ChildNet operates a short-term licensed emergency shelter called Safe Place. It is designed to ease the transition of children entering foster care through an evidenced-based, trauma-focused approach that provides children with a safe, nurturing, and therapeutic environment. Children entering foster care often experience confusion, grief and loss. Safe Place provides supervision and support with a trauma-informed focus on the child’s adjustment to removal from their home. During their stay at Safe Place, the needs of each child are assessed to ensure their immediate needs related to food, clothing, and medical/behavioral health services are met expeditiously. Due to the growing entry of high acuity teens with complex needs, it is essential that these youth have a safe, private, and comfortable area that is separate from younger or more vulnerable children. 1302.purpose: The purpose will be to provide a safe, nurturing, and comfortable teen-friendly environment for older youth spending time temporarily at Safe Place in Broward County. In this nurturing setting, the immediate basic needs of youth will be met including shelter, food, clothing, and medical/behavioral health care needs while focusing on reduction of trauma. Along with those critical reasons, the ultimate goal is to maintain the youth in a safe and comfortable setting, that is welcoming and age appro
1302.activities: ChildNet will provide supervision and trauma-focused care 24 hours a day, 7 days per week for the youth at SafePlace. This includes assessment of needs and coordination of basic needs that includes provision of food, clothing, short-term safe housing, and connection to medical and behavioral health care. ChildNet will coordinate and oversee all construction in order to renovate the space to enhance safety, privacy, and comfort for the youth.
1302.direct_services: Direct services to the citizens will include 24/7 shelter, supervision and trauma-informed care, as well as providing basic needs of food, clothing, short-term safe housing, and connection to medical and behavioral health care.
1302.population: Target population includes children ages birth to 18 who enter the foster care system in Broward County due to abuse, neglect, and/or abandonment. Ages of the children may range from 0-18, but focus of this project will be on teens ages 13-17. ChildNet's Broward Place programs will serve at least 150 children annually.
1302.outcome: The ultimate outcome is to increase placement stability for children in out of home foster care in Broward county. This will be measured applying the metric: Placement moves per 1000 days in foster care will be not exceed 4.5%. Methodology: This measure is the rate at which children change placements while in Out of Home Care (OHC) during the report period. Denominator: The total number of days in OHC during the report period Numerator: The total number of placements moves during the report period for all children in the denominator Method: Total # of children entering care in the SFY divided by the total pop of children x 1000

2576.description: Independence Landing is seeking capital funds to build an additional 30 units for our independent, affordable supportive living community. We currently have a waitlist of over 50 individuals, and adding these units will provide critically needed permanent housing, as there are no other supported independent living options in our region. Our residents love living here, reflected in a positive lease renewal rate to date, and expanding the community will allow more adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities to live safely, independently, and with dignity.
2576.purpose: Expanding Independence Landing allows adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities to live independently in a supportive environment, reducing reliance on costly state institutionalization and lowering the risk of homelessness. By providing stable housing, families experience less financial strain, and the state realizes long-term savings through decreased demand for institutional care and emergency housing services, while residents gain the opportunity to contribute economically and
2576.activities: The project will provide affordable supportive housing with programs that teach independent living skills and workforce development, promoting independence and community inclusion. It will ease burdens on families and deliver economic benefits through job creation, local investment, and reduced reliance on institutional care.
2576.direct_services: The funding will provide permanent supportive housing for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, along with direct services that include self-help and daily living skills training, independent living support, and transportation access, enabling residents to live autonomously while fully participating in the community.
2576.population: Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities
2576.outcome: The project will provide 30 additional units of independent supportive living, allowing adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities to live safely, independently, and with dignity. Expected outcomes include reduced reliance on state institutionalization, lower risk of homelessness, increased housing stability, and improved quality of life for residents. Families will experience reduced financial and caregiving burdens, and the community will benefit from residents’ greater economic and social participation. Outcomes will be measured by tracking occupancy and waitlist numbers to assess demand and access, monitoring lease renewal rates and housing stability to evaluate resident sat

2577.organization: Ounce of Prevention Fund of Florida
2577.description: This project will support continued successful implementation of the Period of PURPLE Crying evidence-based prevention program to reduce incidence of shaken baby syndrome, known as abusive head trauma (AHT), and expand services to additional areas of the state. PURPLE Crying includes a statewide public education campaign, targeted support services to parents of newborns, ongoing education & training for healthcare professionals, and evaluation. This project is supported by Prevent Child Abuse Florida, Florida Child Abuse Death Review Committee, Florida Chapter of American Academy of Pediatrics, and Florida Dept. of Health.
2577.purpose: The specific goal is to prevent abusive head trauma (AHT) to infants (shaken baby syndrome) through evidence-based parent education and support about coping with infant crying. Research on Period of PURPLE Crying has shown that use of the materials appears to lead to increased knowledge about early infant crying and the dangers of shaking a baby. Research on Period of PURPLE Crying also shows that implementing the program may reduce emergency room visits for complaints of infant crying and AHT h
2577.activities: Period of PURPLE Crying evidence-based AHT prevention program will be offered statewide through participating hospitals, pediatricians, health departments, home visiting programs, and other health providers. Parent education services will be provided by local hospitals, pediatricians, home visitors, and other partners. Training, technical assistance, quality assurance, evaluation, and a statewide multi-media public education campaign on AHT prevention will be administered by Prevent Child Abuse
2577.direct_services: Parents and caregivers of newborns will receive education on normal early infant crying, safe sleep, choosing safe caregivers, and action steps to prevent shaking a baby. Families receive an app, booklet, and father-specific booklet, along with in-person coaching prenatally or at birth. A second coaching session during the first three months reinforces prevention and provides ongoing support durin
2577.population: The program will directly serve all parents and caregivers of newborns in participating hospitals and birthing centers across Florida, ensuring they receive life-saving education on normal infant crying, safe sleep, choosing safe caregivers, and preventing abusive head trauma (AHT). Healthcare and family support professionals statewide including pediatricians, nurses, midwives, doulas, home visitors, and obstetricians will receive and provide ongoing specialized training to provide consistent, e
2577.outcome: Parents of newborn babies will gain appropriate knowledge and skills for coping with infant crying without shaking a baby, reducing cases of AHT in Florida. Evaluation will include surveys that measure participating parents' knowledge about early infant crying and the dangers of shaking a baby. Focus groups with participating parents will collect opinions and feedback on parent behaviors when their infant cries.

2581.description: North Florida Goodwill, has launched the “GoodTrades” initiative to significantly expand skilled trade education for local residents. This program directly addresses a critical shortage of skilled workers in booming Florida construction trades—such as carpentry, plumbing, HVAC, and welding—which are struggling to fill positions. Simultaneously, the program targets North Florida areas with high unemployment rates, aiming to connect motivated learners with sustainable career pathways. By providing advanced training skills, this partnership seeks not only to empower individuals and strengthen families through career readiness but also to revitalize entire communities by cultivating a thriving, educated workforce that can fill the crucial labor gap in the region's rapidly growing construction sector. Focus programs include NCCER Basic Construction, Plumbing and Carpentry Pre Apprentice track
2581.purpose: The overarching goal of a collaborative program like GoodTrades is to create a powerful, self-sustaining loop of economic opportunity and community revitalization by addressing key deficits in the local workforce and education systems. We will bridge the skilled labor gap and meet industry demands. We will create pathways to sustainable employment and economic mobility.
2581.activities: The funding will be used to support a comprehensive set of activities and services that cover the entire participant journey—from initial outreach and essential skills development to advanced trade training and guaranteed job placement support. Activities include, credentialing and certification programs, career readiness and employer engagement; providing dedicated careers services staff to help with career placement and post placement retention. In addition, critical emergency wrap around supp
2581.direct_services: Hands on trades training in residential carpentry, plumbing, core construction and other trades identified as needed.
2581.population: 200 plus individuals will be served. Target population is high school graduates not attending college, unemployed or those who are looking to change careers and upskill.
2581.outcome: The primary benefit is a direct pipeline of qualified, work-ready candidates to fill the numerous open positions (carpentry, plumbing, HVAC, electrical, welding, masonry, solar installation, etc.). This helps employers reduce recruiting costs and time-to-hire by accessing a pre-vetted pool of local talent. In addition, alleviate production bottlenecks caused by labor shortages, allowing companies to accept and complete more projects. This program addresses the long-term need for skilled workers, ensuring the industry has a strong foundation for future growth and succession planning.

1475.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1475.description: To provide Spay/Neuter Clinics and Vouchers for Gulf County
1475.purpose: To address the overpopulation crisis in Gulf County’s rural communities with limited access to veterinary care by setting up spay/neuter clinics.
1475.activities: Spay and Neuter Clinics and Vouchers
1475.outcome: Increased Spay and Neuter of the cat and dog population will lead to less stray cats and dogs on the streets of Gulf County. Stray cat and dog pick up calls to Animal Control decrease year after implementation of increased spay and neuter program.

2187.description: Goodwill South Florida offers vocational education & training programs where participants are taught job skills and gain work experience. The appropriation will provide vocational education & training where participants are taught job skills and gain work experience in positions in the sewing trade. 90% of program participants will have a disability or barriers to work. The program will provide training opportunities for 450 individuals (new participants or retraining of current participants) who have the capabilities and interests to perform in a job but are in need of additional training (classroom and/or on-the-job training) and supportive counseling due to a specific condition that impairs their productivity or precludes them from achieving standard productivity levels.
2187.purpose: Provide training opportunities for 450 individuals (new participants or retraining of current participants) who have the capabilities and interests to perform in a job but are in need of additional training (classroom and/or on-the-job training) and supportive counseling due to a specific condition that impairs their productivity or precludes them from achieving standard productivity levels.
2187.activities: The appropriation will allow us to invest in programs that help transition someone seeking our services from dependency to independence. Rather than using tax dollars to receive state services, our successful job placements can help convert tax users to become taxpayers by now being able to find a job and contribute to the community rather than depending on it.
2187.direct_services: Individualized supervision, supportive counseling, on-the-job training, and transitional employment services for individuals to develop their maximum potential for employment. Some general skills taught are communicating effectively with supervisors, co-workers, and customers, understanding and following workplace behaviors, following directions, and paying attention to tasks.
2187.population: Goodwill South Florida will identify adults with disabilities from the following: Current participants that work in the Apparel Division and have a disability who a.) could benefit from supplemental training to enhance their skills or b.) are performing at a lower efficient/productivity rate. General recruitment activities that will focus on seniors, individuals who are economically disadvantage, and individuals who have been trained while in a jail reentry program.
2187.outcome: Providing individuals an income while receiving training for an employable skill by measuring the number of participants who complete the program. Trainees will be measured by their performance prior to the training. Pre- testing and post-testing will be conducted against key performance indicators identified to assess comprehension and progress.

1478.description: After Hurricane Idalia hit in August 2023, new leakage points appeared in the historic Jefferson County courthouse roof that in turn affected the building interior. The County was awarded $375,000 last year from the State to work on this project. Our Commissioners also dedicated an additional $505,000 to the project to get most of the work done. This additional $500,000 request should see the project through to completion. A comprehensive repair project will address cosmetic, structural and safety deficiencies. Courts still function daily; the Clerk of the Court, staff offices and judges' chambers are housed there. The building is a contributing property in the Monticello Historic District listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is part of the historic downtown walking tour. Water damage, cracked plaster and safely sealed electrical boxes are just a few repairs detailed in
1478.purpose: A comprehensive repair project will address cosmetic, structural and safety deficiencies. Courts still function daily; the Clerk of the Court, staff offices and judges' chambers are housed there. The building is a contributing property in the Monticello Historic District listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is part of the historic downtown walking tour. Water damage, cracked plaster and safely sealed electrical boxes are just a few repairs detailed in the scope attachment.
1478.activities: The courthouse serves Florida's Second Judicial Circuit and the citizens of Jefferson County. Courts function daily; the Clerk of the Court, staff and judges' chambers are housed there. Individuals doing business in the courthouse should feel safe in a secure structure fit to house the various services provided, from child support to probate, evictions to family law, misdemeanor to felony.
1478.direct_services: Citizens/employees will experience the continuation of all court services in a cleaner and visibly enhanced environment. Interior work and public spaces will have improved climate control, safer high traffic area flooring and stairs, operable windows, and more. Exterior pedestrian areas will be made safer by rainwater diversion and increased visibility in treed areas.
1478.population: The general population will be served by this project; there are no targeted special populations. Courthouse staff, visitors and those engaging in the judicial system services, both as legal staff and clients, able-bodied and those with physical challenges, will all benefit from a safe, clean and updated public building. An estimated 35,000-40,000 people utilize the Jefferson County Courthouse each year for various services provided.
1478.outcome: Please see the EXPECTED BENEFITS attachment with details about the benefits of this project, including outcomes and methods of measurement.

1574.organization: Area Agency on Aging for North Florida, Inc.
1574.description: This project expands access to innovative, AI-driven infrared fall detection technology designed to protect at-risk seniors. The aesthetically refined ceiling-mounted light integrates seamlessly with a 24-hour, professionally staffed wellness center, enabling seniors to live safely and independently while reducing hospitalizations, long-term care placements, social isolation, and the burden on unpaid caregivers. The system delivers real-time alerts in the event of a fall or safety incident, ensuring rapid response and supporting Florida’s strategic objective of helping seniors age safely in place. Its advanced 13-point dynamic skeletal imaging technology minimizes false alarms, thereby preventing unnecessary 911 activations and optimizing emergency response resources.
1574.purpose: At-risk individuals utilizing the fall detection technology will be able to remain safely in their homes while maintaining greater independence and peace of mind. The system provides 24/7 monitoring that immediately detects when a fall occurs ensuring that help is dispatched even when the person is unable to call for assistance. By automatically notifying caregivers, family members, or emergency responders, the technology significantly reduces the time between a fall and intervention.
1574.activities: This project expands access to innovative, AI-driven, functional ceiling mounted light, infrared fall detection and 24 hour live wellness monitoring technology for at-risk seniors, helping them live safely and independently while reducing hospitalizations and long-term care placements. The project provides real-time alerts when a fall or safety event occurs, enabling rapid response and supporting Florida’s goal of helping seniors age in place.
1574.direct_services: • Installation of ceiling-mounted fall detection devices in participating homes or senior living environments. • 24-hour live wellness monitoring by trained operators who respond immediately to safety events or abnormal activity. • Concierge support services that provide personalized assistance, coordination of care, and access to community- based programs that promote social connection and well-b
1574.population: The project will serve seniors at high risk for falls, fully embracing any senior on the memory care spectrum, sight or hearing impaired reaching an estimated 100–140 participants. Total costs will vary based on each home’s infrastructure needs, such as the availability of reliable Wi-Fi or other necessary connectivity to support system installation and operation.
1574.outcome: Reduction in fall-related injuries and significantly faster emergency response times following a detected fall, ensuring assistance is provided within the critical “golden hour” when timely intervention can prevent serious complications and improve recovery outcomes. This will be measured by tracking and comparing average response times between fall occurrence and contact with caregivers or EMS before and after installation. Data will be collected directly from system analytics, which measure each event in real time.

1479.description: This program will support DSR Public Health Foundation in expanding it's reach, effectiveness, and efficiency of efforts to increase the awareness, access, and increase utilization of critical resources that support positive health outcomes and wellbeing in rural communities in Madison County and the Big Bend Region. Funds will be used to enhance our existing multi-sector network of partners implementing evidence-based efforts to address persistent social and economic factors contributing to poor health outcomes in rural communities.
1479.purpose: The funds will leverage a multi-sector network of partners to address and sustain evidence-based efforts to address persistent social and economic factors contributing to poor health outcomes in rural communities. Community Health Workers and other professionals will work with individuals and families to increase awareness, access, and increase utilization of critical resources that support positive health outcomes and wellbeing using a data-driven approach.
1479.activities: DSR will implement a multi-sector partnership network to coordinate services, reduce duplication, and address community needs. Community Health Workers and program staff will facilitate outreach, conduct screenings, make referrals, and connect individuals and families to critical health and social resources that support improved outcomes in rural communities.
1479.direct_services: DSR will work collaboratively with partners to increase availability of services, including but not limited to, health and nutrition education, tutoring, and screenings, and develop regularly updated resource repositories for organizations serving rural Big Bend counties. CHWs and other professionals will connect individuals and families to resources needed to improve health and wellbeing.
1479.population: Elderly persons; Persons with poor mental health; Persons with poor physical health; Jobless persons; Economically disadvantaged persons; At-risk youth; Homeless; Developmentally disabled; Physically disabled; Preschool students; Grade school students; High school students; University/College students; Currently or formerly incarcerated persons
1479.outcome: Improved physical health measured by the number of youth and adults receiving health and nutrition education and/or showing improvement in health behaviors. Improved mental heath measured by the number of youth, caregivers, and community members completing screenings and receiving referrals. Improved quality of education measured by the percent change of student reading and math scores. Improved economic activity measured by the number of participants completing college/career readiness workshops.

1481.description: Forensic step-down diversion beds for individuals w/ serious mental illness who are involved in the criminal justice system are needed to maximize state and law enforcement resources in the community and the State psychiatric system. This program provides a residential resource for the diversion of seriously mentally ill individuals from less appropriate and/or more expensive venues in the community mental health system. The beds would be $327 per day, a 14% savings over the daily rate at the State-operated Mental Health Treatment Facilities. This is included in DCF's LBR.
1481.purpose: Step-down & diversion services for individuals w/ serious mental illness who are involved in the CJ system are needed to maximize State & law enforcement resources in the community & the State psychiatric system. This program provides a residential resource for the diversion of seriously mentally ill individuals from less appropriate cost and/or more expensive venues into the community mental health system. The beds would be priced at $327 per day, a 14% savings & this is included in DCF's LBR.
1481.activities: The provision of Level 1 Community Residential Facility housing and associated competency restoration, psychiatric, case management, court liaison, discharge planning, group and individual counseling, psychiatric assessment and psychiatric rehabilitation services for individuals diverted from the criminal justice system and stepped down from State secure forensic facilities.
1481.direct_services: Level 1 Community Residential Facility housing and associated competency restoration, psychiatric, case management, court liaison, discharge planning, group and individual counseling, psychiatric assessment and psychiatric rehabilitation services for individuals diverted from the criminal justice system and stepped down from State secure forensic facilities.
1481.population: High-risk seriously mentally ill forensic residential populations.
1481.outcome: This program provides a residential resource for the diversion of seriously mentally ill individuals from less appropriate cost and/or more expensive venues into the community mental health system. The beds would be priced at $327 per day, a 14% savings.

2189.description: The primary purpose of this project is to improve the safety for all road users, reduce pedestrian/bicyclist conflicts, provide accessible marked ADA walkways, and improve the quality of life for the residents. The project scope includes milling and overlaying roadways on the west side of the Village - including 41st Street - which is a shared roadway between the Village of Virginia Gardens and City of Miami Springs. Improvements also include removal/replacement of deficient sidewalks and ADA compliant crosswalks, and speeding signage installation.
2189.purpose: Improved roadway accessibility and safety for vehicular traffic, bicyclists and pedestrians.
2189.direct_services: Improved transportation conditions for the general public including the residents, business owners, and cut through traffic from the City of Miami Springs, as well as traffic flow from NW 36th Street- a main thoroughfare.
2189.population: The target population are the 2,400 residents of the Village of Virginia Gardens, as well as non-residents who traverse the Village. More than 5,000 individuals are expected to be served.
2189.outcome: Improved transportation conditions for the general public, measured by local traffic incident reports.

2190.description: Rebuild/Rehabilitation of the current pump station. This will include the rehabilitation of 2-70HP FLYT pumps, 120K emergency generator and replacing the control panel. Install covering over the control panel. This will also include filming/cleaning/updating and GIS mapping the of the Storm Water Master Plan and drains as required by the state.
2190.purpose: Allow homeowners to access their property during heavy rains.
2190.activities: The rehabilitation will extend the life of the storm water pump station and will allow the Village to GIS map the storm water master plan and drainage.
2190.population: Village of Virginia Gardens residents and surrounding communities and commuters. 10,000

2191.description: Requested funds will replace and upgrade approximately 5000 feet of undersized water mains/meters, ensuring reliable service and improved water quality for customers. Leak detection will identify aging mains for replacement, with the project phased by district, completing one district per year. These upgrades will enhance water conservation, reduce water loss, improve utility resiliency, ensure compliance with Florida’s Lead & Copper Rule Revision, and provide efficient water flow.
2191.purpose: The project will enhance environmental quality by reducing water loss, improving system efficiency, and promoting water.
2191.activities: The rehabilitation will extend the life of the storm water pump station and will allow the Village to GIS map the storm water master plan and drainage.
2191.direct_services: The project will protect public health by ensuring compliance with the State's Lead & Copper Rule, reducing exposure to lead and other harmful contaminants in drinking water.
2191.population: Village of Virginia Gardens residents and surrounding communities and commuters. 10,000
2191.outcome: The benefit will be measured by conducting routine water quality testing, tracking lead and copper levels, and ensuring adherence to regulatory standards for safe drinking water.

2877.description: Prodigy Cultural Arts Program is a 25 year old juvenile delinquency prevention research-based program that utilizes the arts to teach life skills to 1,125 at risk youth ages 5-17 across 7 counties in West Central Florida yearly. According to the Florida Department of Juvenile Justice's statistics (2024-25), 100% of youth enrolled in the Prodigy do not get into trouble with law enforcement thus lessening the burden on the state juvenile system, increasing public safety and saving the state millions of dollars. Prodigy classes are taught in person by professional artists where youth learn problem solving, anger management, communication, leadership and other life skills through various art disciplines. One year of Prodigy services costs below $2,000 per youth enrolled, making it one of the most cost effective youth development programs.
2877.purpose: The funds will be used to support the implementation of the Prodigy Cultural Arts program across West Central Florida for 1,125 high risk youth. For 25 years, Prodigy has been providing life skills infused cultural arts programs to keep youth out of the juvenile justice system. The funds will support program development, classroom materials, professional instructors, art, music and dance supplies, data collection and reporting, field trips, and other program management tasks.
2877.activities: Prodigy Cultural Arts implements classes which are taught by professional artists. Classes consist of a variety of art disciplines which are infused with life skill activities. These activities include: anger management, leadership, problem solving, and communication skills. Activities such as field trips, educational workshops, mentoring sessions, community events and showcases are also included. Showcases consist of performances from Prodigy youths participating on stage while utilizing music
2877.direct_services: Participants enrolled in Prodigy receive a life skills and risk assessment to gauge what type of services they need. This may include other services such as mentoring and tutoring. They also receive their choice of art classes or music, dance, photography, performance, among many others. Participants (and their parents) also receive workshops on parent/child communication, stress management techni
2877.population: Prodigy is expected to serve an average of 1,125 youths ages 5-17 through west central Florida counties in a year. Prodigy targets communities in which law enforcement has deemed at risk for high levels of crime, truancy, and delinquency. Some youth enrolled in the program are often considered school drop outs and/or display delinquent behavior. Prodigy serves participants in communities from Pinellas to Hillsborough, Polk, Osceola, and Orange Counties. Prodigy also serves rural communities such
2877.outcome: The expectation of the Prodigy program is to keep youths out of the juvenile system by providing them with an safe arena to express themselves through various art disciplines. Prodigy participants receive risk assessments to determine need for services. They attend a minimum of 6 hours per week for a minimum of 8 weeks to learn new skills and establish mentoring relationships with professional art instructors. The lessons taught are infused with life skills to enable youths to use their creative thinking through visual and performing art forms. Prodigy is monitored by the Florida Department of Juvenile Justice by undergoing annual reviews of monthly programming where participants data is col

2192.description: The primary objective of this initiative is to upgrade the City of Miami Springs’ technology infrastructure, with particular emphasis on strengthening our public safety communication systems. The department’s current radios have reached end-of-life, are no longer manufactured, and lack ongoing support, creating significant risks to reliable communication and posing a direct safety risk to officers in the field. This project entails the acquisition of upgraded radios designed to significantly enhance real-time communication and coordination among first responders. The necessity for this investment is rooted in the critical need for reliable, uninterrupted, and efficient communication, especially during emergencies where the rapid and accurate dissemination of information is paramount.
2192.purpose: The funds will be used to replace the City of Miami Springs Police Department’s current radios, which are at end-of-life and are no longer being manufactured or supported. Upgrading to modern, reliable communication equipment will ensure seamless connectivity during emergencies, strengthen coordination among first responders, and enhance the City's overall emergency preparedness and public safety operations.
2192.activities: The project will include the procurement, installation, and maintenance of new radio systems and related equipment for the City’s police department fleet and personnel. This will involve outfitting patrol vehicles, assigning portable radios to officers, and ensuring that all equipment is properly installed, programmed, and maintained for long-term functionality.
2192.direct_services: Citizens will directly benefit from faster emergency response times, improved officer coordination, and enhanced public safety services. The upgraded communication system will enable first responders to share real-time information, respond more effectively to critical incidents, and maintain a higher level of safety and security for the community.
2192.population: The primary target population served by this project is the residents, visitors, and businesses of the City of Miami Springs. By improving communication and coordination among police officers, the project will enhance public safety and emergency response for the entire community. The project is expected to directly impact all citizens within the city’s jurisdiction, serving an estimated population of approximately 14,500 individuals, while also benefiting approximately 60 Miami Springs first res
2192.outcome: This project will enhance officer safety and public protection by providing reliable radios, which are critical for daily operations and emergency response. Without functional radios, officers cannot safely or effectively perform their duties. Success will be measured through system reliability, response-time records, and officer feedback on communication performance during critical incidents.

2878.organization: The Caring About Living Individuals Project
2878.description: The C.A.L.I. Cares Community Health Clinic is a community based initiative dedicated to providing accessible, evidence-based behavioral health services to vulnerable populations. The clinic integrates individual and group counseling, crisis intervention, peer mentoring, care coordination and transportation support to remove barriers to care and ensure consistent engagement.
2878.purpose: Funds will be used to establish an evidence-based community health and mental wellness clinic designed to strengthen Pinellas County's behavioral health infrastructure, expand equitable access to quality care, and eliminate transportation barriers that often prevent residents from receiving consistent services. By integrating counseling, case management, mentoring, and reliable transportation, the program promotes recovery, stability, and long-term self- sufficiency for individuals
2878.activities: Individual and group counseling, crisis intervention, peer mentoring, care coordination, and transportation to connect residents with medical, mental health, and mentorship resources.
2878.direct_services: Services include health education, wellness planning, and follow-up support that help individuals achieve stability, independence, and sustained participation in community life.
2878.population: 50-100 individuals are expected to be served Target population: Elderly persons Persons with poor mental health Persons with poor physical health Jobless persons Economically disadvantaged persons At-risk youth Homeless Developmentally disabled Physically disabled Drug users (in health services) Grade school students High school students University/College students Currently or formerly incarcerated persons Drug offenders (in criminal Justice) Victims of crime
2878.outcome: The expected outcome is the overall improvement in community health, stability, and public safety through coordinated behavioral health, mentoring, and transportation services that reduce system costs and enhance quality of life. This will be measured by quarterly outcome reports, partner agency data, and cost-avoidance analysis will confirm long-term benefits including reduced crisis utilization, stronger families, and sustained community wellbeing

2879.description: The CALI Career Builders Workforce Development Program is a comprehensive career readiness and job placement initiative designed to equip underrepresented and transitional young adults with the skills, experience, and support needed to enter high-demand industries and achieve long-term self-sufficiency. Through a structured hands on cohort model, participants receive industry-specific training, financial literacy education, and personalized career coaching, while also engaging with employer partners who provide mentorship, site visits, and job placement opportunities.
2879.purpose: The requested appropriations funds will be used to expand and sustain the CALI Career Builders Workforce Development Program, enabling The C.A.L.I. Project to train and support up to 100 youth and young adults annually in career pathways that lead to livable-wage employment.
2879.activities: Instructional delivery, Participant stipends to encourage completion and engagement; certification costs needed for hands-on learning.
2879.direct_services: Career coaching and case management to address barriers to employment; Employer engagement activities such as site visits, mock interviews, and job placement support
2879.population: The CALI Career Builders Workforce Development Program serves youth and young adults who face barriers to employment and economic stability, including those who are aging out of foster care, experiencing homelessness, justice-involved, or from low-income and underserved communities. We expect to serve 100 individuals
2879.outcome: Expected outcome: 100 participants will complete industry-specific workforce training annually. 80% of participants will demonstrate increased job readiness skills (resume development, interviewing, communication, professionalism). 70% will achieve job placement, internship, or apprenticeship within 90 days of program completion. 90% will report improved financial literacy and budgeting confidence. 85% will engage in continued career development or education within six months post-program Methodology by which this outcome will be measured - Pre- and post-assessments, Case management tracking, Employer feedback

2193.description: This project consists of the roadway improvements on the Westward Drive corridor from Miami Springs Circle. to Hammond Drive, to accommodate pedestrian, bicycle and vehicular activity and to address public safety. Construction to provide roadway resurfacing, re-striping to ensure safer roads, optimize traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve overall safety and transportation efficiency. As well as implement safety measures, including the installation of improved signage, benches and expand pedestrian safety with crosswalks/sidewalks. Project to include the cost of engineering, CEI Services, architectural design, permitting, construction management and cost estimating.
2193.purpose: To ensure safe and secure protections for pedestrians and optimize traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve overall transportation safety and efficiency. Implement safety measures, including the installation of improved signage, benches and expand pedestrian safety with crosswalks/sidewalks with Vision Zero objectives.
2193.activities: Project to include the cost of engineering, CEI Services, architectural design, permitting, construction management, cost estimating and construction (roadway milling and repaving, and re-striping).
2193.direct_services: Enhance public safety by constructing roadway improvements to Westward Drive spanning from Miami Springs Circle to Hammond Drive.
2193.population: This project holds significant importance as it falls within a service area that the city has identified as a top priority due to its proximity to multiple elementary schools, senior centers and recreation center and will safeguard pedestrians of all age groups.
2193.outcome: Improve overall transportation efficiency and implement safety measures, including the installation of improved signage, benches and expand pedestrian safety with crosswalks/sidewalks with Vision Zero objectives.

1342.description: The Persaud Legacy Farm is located on over 1,000 acres in Marion County Florida. The Persaud's vision is not just to offer world-class sport horse facilities, but to also provide sustainable, equine therapy on a large scale. This project assists with the development of the Persaud Legacy Equine Therapy Center to provide services to children with disabilities and military veterans suffering from PTSD. Funds for this project will be used in build out of the Equine Therapy Center, including therapy areas and equipment, as well as auxiliary spaces for families that have traveled for therapy.
1342.purpose: Equine Therapy Programs improve quality of life, and the physical, social and emotional well-being. 1484.description: This request seeks funding for the purchase of a new pumper-engine fire truck, along with a complete suite of modern firefighting equipment for Liberty County. This investment is critically needed due to the advanced age and deteriorating condition of the county's current fire apparatus. The fire department serves a large and geographically diverse area, where timely response is vital to protecting lives and property. However, declining volunteer numbers have placed additional strain on operational capacity, making dependable equipment even more essential. A new, fully equipped pumper-engine fire truck will significantly enhance emergency response capabilities, improve firefighter safety, and ensure the community receives the reliable protection it deserves. This investment represents not only an upgrade in equipment but also a commitment to maintaining
1484.purpose: All expenditures directly support enhancing emergency response and firefighter safety across Lafayette County and surrounding communities
1484.activities: Purchase of a new pumper truck and equipment.
1484.direct_services: Faster response times in emergency situations and possibly reduced homeowners insurance rates due to lower rating.
1484.outcome: All expenditures directly support enhancing emergency response and firefighter safety. This will be measured by response times, structures saved, and lower personnel accidents.

1215.description: The Project is for the expansion of the Authority's regional transmission system through the construction of two (2) large diameter regional drinking water transmission pipelines (20.3 miles total). The two segments include the extension of the regional drinking water transmission system that conveys wholesale drinking water to Charlotte, and City of North Port (Phase 2B) and the extension of the regional drinking water transmission system that conveys wholesale drinking water to Sarasota County (Phase 3C), which includes 5 Million Gallons in finished water storage and increased pumping capacity.
1215.purpose: Construction of the 20.3 miles of regional drinking water transmission lines will extend the regional drinking water transmission system that conveys drinking water from alternative water supplies to Charlotte, DeSoto, and Sarasota Counties. One segment, the Phase 2B pipeline, will improve regional drinking water system reliability, meet growing water needs in northern and western Charlotte County and facilitate future regional interconnects. The second segment, Phase 3C Pipeline, will improve r
1215.activities: Construction of 13 miles of 42" diameter water transmission pipeline to improve water system reliability and support growing water demands in Charlotte County (Phase 2B), and construction of 7.5 miles of 42" diameter potable water transmission pipeline and pumping and storage facilities to improve water system reliability and support growing water demands in Sarasota County (Phase 3C).
1215.direct_services: This Project delivers a reliable and safe drinking water supply for public health, safety and welfare of the residents and economic growth of the region consisting of Charlotte and Sarasota Counties.
1215.population: The four-county region comprising the Authority's service area has a population of approximately 1,100,000 residents. The Authority's regional water supply system interconnects utilities serving the majority of that population. In 2024 approximately 31 million gallons per day of drinking water was supplied to the region from Authority facilities to meet growing drinking water supply needs and support public health and economic growth.
1215.outcome: This Project provides reliable water supply infrastructure to the region for economic development and public health and safety. The project enhances regional water supply resiliency to disasters such as drought, floods, hurricanes, and climate change. The outcome will be measured through improving water supply availability, resiliency of the system during emergencies, and maintaining the current high standards for drinking water quality.

This is for in person mental health support as well as monitoring the peer support hotline.

1492.description: The specific purpose of this project is to enhance the recreation opportunity for the citizens of Liberty County and visitors who utilize the Bristol Boat Ramp. If funds are secured, the improvements would include resurfacing and widening the existing boat ramp to accommodate higher volumes of traffic, install a floating dock to provide convenient and safe boat launching, mitigation for erosion by installing sheet - piles and rip-rap, upgrading the lighting system, and improving the parking lot.
1492.purpose: The purpose of this funding request is to provide long over due improvements to the Bristol Boat Ramp. The County has diligently pursued available funding to make the improvements but has not been successful. These improvements are necessary for the safety of citizens using the facility and will ensure modern materials are used for sustainability of the boat ramp.
1492.activities: The improvements that will be made if funded include resurfacing and widening the existing boat ramp to accommodate higher volumes of traffic, install a floating dock to provide convenient and safe boat launching, mitigation for erosion by installing sheet - piles and rip-rap, upgrading the lighting system, and improving the parking lot.

2324.description: At the headwaters of the Peace River along Peace Creek Canal, this floodplain project provides flood water storage and water quality enhancements to the Peace River Watershed. The project, located in Polk County East of US Hwy 17 and North of SR60, can capture an average annual volume of 2,000 acre-feet of water. Protection and restoration of wetlands will mimic the movement of the historical reaches as identified by historic aerials. The project will expand and secure floodplain storage with the restoration of 360 acres of floodplain at the Headwaters of the Peace River, and allow for much needed reduction in the stage elevation and velocity of flood waters near the site, as experienced during Hurricanes Ian and Milton.
2324.purpose: 1. Provide Water Quantity and Flood Resiliency Benefits: The reconnection and protection of floodplain wetlands allow the project to capture an annual average volume of approximately 2,000 ac-ft of water when conditions in the Peace Creek exceed 94 ft NAVD88 flood stage. 2. Provide Water Quality Benefit: The improved stream corridor and wetland restoration will include a pathway for water to regularly and continuously come in contact with wetlands, improving water quality through natural process
2324.activities: Floodplain and stream restoration construction activities will include land clearing, grading, planting, berm removal, bank stabilization, and installation of best management practices. Contractor over site of implementation of a Quality Control/Quality Assurance plan is included as well. considered a valid response.
2324.direct_services: Creation and protection of flood storage which will help reduce flooding threats on private lands in Polk County. The public will have access to the property after the project is complete.
2324.population: The population served by this Project will be nearby landowners experiencing a reduction of flood depths and velocities during high water events and downstream constituents experiencing improved water quality downstream of the project location. The public will have access to the property after the project is complete.
2324.outcome: 1. Provide Water Quantity and Flood Resiliency Benefits: The protection and reconnection of floodplain wetlands allow the project to capture an annual average volume of approximately 2,000 ac-ft of water when conditions in the Peace Creek exceed 94 ft NAVD88 flood stage. Level meters will be installed to evaluate the amount average amount of water stored at the completion of the project.

1107.description: The requested funds will allow Florida Keys Children Shelter (FKCS) to establish a new Transitional Living Program in the Upper Keys, expanding housing and supportive services for older youth transitioning to independence. This program will provide safe housing, life skills training, education, and employment support, strengthening statewide capacity to serve at-risk youth referred from Monroe, Miami-Dade, and across Florida. This program will provide the necessary skills for individuals to acquire independent living. Since 2021 Monroe County has secured $1.6 million to fund the transitional living program. This funding will expand those critical services to the Upper Keys, maximizing the available federal funding.
1107.purpose: The requested funds will allow FKCS to purchase an existing home in the Upper Keys to establish a new Transitional Living Program for older youth experiencing homelessness or family instability. This program will provide safe housing, life skills training, education, employment support, and counseling to help youth achieve stability, independence, and long-term self-sufficiency.
1107.activities: The project will provide safe, supervised housing, life skills training, educational support, employment readiness, and case management to help youth ages 16–22 achieve stability, self-sufficiency, and long-term success through FKCS’s proven Transitional Living Program model.
1107.direct_services: The funding will enable FKCS to offer transitional housing and individualized support services to youth experiencing homelessness or family instability. Residents will receive guidance in education, employment, budgeting, and daily living skills, fostering independence and reducing long-term reliance on public systems.
1107.population: The target population is youth ages 16–22 experiencing homelessness, family conflict, or housing instability. The program will primarily serve youth from Monroe and Miami-Dade Counties but will also screen and accept referrals from across the State of Florida. FKCS expects to provide outreach and screening services to over 50 youth each year and offer housing and case management to 10 residents annually through the Transitional Living Program, supported by guaranteed federal funding.
1107.outcome: The project will increase safe and stable housing for youth ages 16–22 while improving education, employment, and life skills outcomes. Success will be measured by the percentage of youth who secure stable housing (target 75%), enroll in school or job training (75%), and gain employment or income (75%) as tracked through case records, verification documents, and follow-up assessments.

3002.description: This project will serve the Economic Development Zone of Golden Gate City and is the first phase to provide the foundation for septic to sewer conversions for a population of approximately 25,000. This would represent 80% of septic parcels in the Collier County Sewer District on lots that are less than one acre. Golden Gate City is the major source of freshwater to Naples Bay but also delivers significant loadings of potential pollutants.
