2550.organization: Ohel Children's Home and Family Services
2550.description: To address the mental health needs of youth, and to foster resilience and well-being, Ohel will expand trainings to educators and professional implementing our social-emotional learning curricula and resources as well as substance use prevention programming. Ohel has a dedicated Trauma Team, across South Florida, that specializes in crisis response, and resilience and support services for acute traumas, such as drownings, suicides, sudden deaths, fatal diagnoses, natural disasters, and community tragedies.
2550.purpose: Ohel will continue to mobilize a dedicated Trauma Team across South Florida to provide services that address acute trauma, such as suicide, drownings, sudden deaths, fatal diagnoses, natural disasters, and community tragedies. Using Ohel's social-emotional curriculum and resources, Ohel seeks to foster resilience and well-being in children and youth by building educators' capacity to address mental health needs. In addition, schools will be offered our substance use prevention programming.
2550.activities: Activities and service include crisis intervention for children, schools, families, and communities following unanticipated tragedies; parent, teacher, and student education to promote resilience toward improved mental health; and substance use prevention program for children and youth, grades 5-12.
2550.direct_services: Direct services to educators include resilience education to build and strengthen emotional well-being among students and families; crisis response and support following unanticipated tragedies; and substance use prevention programming, currently provided in 13 Florida Day, Middle, and High Schools.
2550.population: Elderly persons, persons, with poor mental health, preschool children, grade-school students, high school students, university/college students, victims of crime, and youth at risk.
2550.outcome: Outcomes: Enhance educators' and students' resilience and well-being, trauma Team ensures access to mental health interventions as well as grief and bereavement services, enhance individuals' coping skills and increase their connections to resources in the aftermath of traumatic events, build community resilience, build community resilience, Ohel's substance use prevention programming for students, educators, parents and communities provides education regarding substance use prevention, with the goal of enhancing students’ refusal skills and understanding of the harm/dangers of substance abuse. Measure: Pre/post-surveys will track efficacy and impact of teacher trainings and school programmi

1207.organization: The Bay of Pigs Museum and Library
1207.description: The Bay of Pigs Museum is seeking enhanced operational support to strengthen its mission of preserving the legacy of Brigade 2506 and safeguarding the invaluable artifacts of the Bay of Pigs Invasion. Expanded resources will improve daily programming, increase staffing capacity, and elevate security, conservation, and public engagement. This support will allow the museum to better serve teachers, students, researchers, and visitors while maintaining its role as a vital cultural institution in Historic Little Havana—honoring the veterans’ sacrifices and contributing to the neighborhood’s continued vibrancy and growth.
1207.purpose: This funding ensures the museum operates safely, sustainably, and at a high standard of public service. Support is needed for maintaining essential systems—including air conditioning, security, and preservation—to protect historical materials and provide a safe, welcoming environment for visitors, staff, and archives. Funding allows for the hiring of a Development Officer and Guest Services staff member, strengthening operations, improving the visitor experience, and securing long-term support f
1207.activities: The funds will support professional maintenance of critical systems—including air conditioning, security, and preservation—to protect historical materials and ensure a safe, welcoming environment for visitors, staff, and archival collections. A Development Officer to secure long-term financial support and a Guest Services staff member to improve operations, enhance the visitor experience, and expand educational programs and community engagement. The Cultural Passport program alone has 200 studen
1207.direct_services: Direct services to citizens will be an open museum where teachers and students in our community engage with civic and primary source programming, the elderly can use our space to support programs for mental health through activity (Assisted Living facilities visit us and the OLLI (Osher Lifelong learning Institute). Researchers and university students use our books and speak to our historian and v
1207.population: This project will serve a broad and diverse audience. While we place a strong focus on engaging young people through our educational programs, the museum welcomes visitors of all ages, including children, adults, and seniors. Our programs and resources also serve teachers, students, university professors, and researchers, as well as a wide range of community members and tourists, ensuring that people from every segment of our community can learn, explore, and engage with the museum's history and
1207.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is that the museum will contribute to the economic vitality of Little Havana by serving as a popular cultural and historical attraction. Our primary goal is to become the leading institution for Victims of Communism curriculum and education in partnership with Miami-Dade Public Schools and civic education programs. Success will be measured by the number of visits from public and private schools, special community groups, and tourists, tracked through surveys and our ticketing system.

3058.description: The Historic Bank of Everglades Building, completed in 1927, is an iconic structure built by Barron Gift Collier and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Over the years it has survived hurricanes, including Irma and Ian, and is now in disrepair. The Everglades Society for Historic Preservation (ESHP) has received $3 million from the federal government (Community Project Funding) to stabilize the structure and its foundation. Also, monies were raised via local fundraising events and donations from individuals/businesses. A capital campaign is planned to raise the remaining amount via a combination of private donors and grant funding. State funds are being requested to assist with the Bank's rehabilitation and adaptive reuse as the Everglades Welcome Center, Trail Town Headquarters, Florida Wildlife Corridor resource, and a community center providing humanities-based prog
3058.purpose: The requested funds will provide an HVAC system for the entire two-floor building and the electrical will service the interior, exterior, and elevator of the building.
3058.activities: Everglades City was designated a Florida State Trail Town in 2019 and is at the southernmost terminus of the Florida Wildlife Corridor, attracting visitors from around the world. Currently, in its temporary facility, ESHP welcomes thousands of visitors each year and expects to attract many more tourists and visitors when the Bank Building is completed. Additionally, ESHP will offer humanities programs to the public in the form of art and history exhibitions, establish a research library, and hos
3058.direct_services: The Visitor Center refers tourists to local businesses which stimulates the local economy in rural southeast Collier County. The Bank Building will restore pride in the community recognizing Barron Collier's vision and be the focal point in town. In addition to providing information and brochures to tourists, the Everglades Area Visitor Center will also be a central gathering place for locals, res
3058.population: The target population includes eco-tourists who visit this area's seven national and state parks and preserves, as well as the elderly, persons with disabilities, students of all ages, tourists from around the world, residents of Collier County and nearby counties of Miami-Dade, Monroe, Broward, Lee, and Hendry. There are over one million visitors to the greater Everglades area each year, and it is anticipated that approximately 40,000 people annually will benefit from the services provided in t
3058.outcome: Enrichment of cultural experiences, improve quality of local educational opportunities, enhance and preserve old Florida, increase economic activity, increase tourism, and the creation of specific immediate jobs. Methodology includes the maintenance of daily visitor logs, participant logs, tracking the number of tourists and sharing this information with the Collier Convention & Visitor Bureau, and hiring local professionals for construction needs now and operational needs once completed.

3188.description: This project, which received partial funding last session, represents the final funding to complete the renovation of FSW's Health Professions building in Charlotte. The nursing profession faces a critical shortage with job openings projected to reach 12.2% statewide by 2030, with a specific increase of 8.9% in Southwest Florida alone. Moreover, nursing programs are often challenged to graduate students who are proficient in critical thinking, clinical situations and judgement, and sophisticated healthcare technology. The 16,448 gross square foot project will align the vocational program, facilities, and technology to create high-fidelity patient simulations and skills labs necessary to decrease training variability and increase standardization without exposing people and patients to unnecessary risks.
3188.purpose: The Charlotte Campus - Building E Health Professions Remodel will enhance nursing education by creating state-of- the art simulation labs and increasing enrollment capacity from 84 to 192 students within three years. The project ensures consistent, high-quality training across campuses, meets Florida's standards for simulation-based clinical education, and includes vital upgrades to support advanced technology. It will also benefit the community by providing specialized training for healthcare p
3188.activities: The renovation of Building E at the Charlotte campus will transform nursing education by providing high-fidelity simulation labs and expanded skills labs, enabling students to complete up to 50% of their clinical training in advanced, realistic settings. The project will increase lab capacity to support higher enrollment and create modern classrooms, debriefing rooms, and hospital-like environments equipped with state-of-the-art technology and furnishings. Faculty and staff will benefit from imp
3188.direct_services: The renovation of Building E will directly benefit citizens by addressing the regional nursing shortage, producing more highly trained Registered Nurses to meet healthcare demands. The upgraded simulation and skills labs will also support community healthcare partners by providing spaces for specialized training and skills development. These improvements will enhance healthcare outcomes and workfo
3188.population: The renovation of Building E will serve nursing students by expanding program capacity and providing advanced training environments. It will also benefit local healthcare providers through access to state-of-the-art training spaces and ultimately support Southwest Florida residents by addressing the regional nursing shortage and improving access to skilled healthcare professionals.
3188.outcome: This project will increase program enrollment from 84 to over 192 students, addressing the regional nursing shortage by producing more qualified Registered Nurses. Enhanced training quality will be achieved through the creation of high-fidelity simulation labs and modernized facilities, preparing students for real-world clinical environments. Additionally, the facility will support community healthcare partners with specialized training spaces, strengthening the local workforce. Outcomes will be measured by tracking enrollment growth, graduation rates, and the number of program completers entering the local healthcare workforce.

1113.organization: Community Child Care of Delray Beach , Inc.
1113.description: This project will upgrade and modernize safety, security, and technology systems across Achievement Centers for Children & Families’ two licensed child care centers and administrative buildings in Delray Beach. Improvements include new door and gate locks, surveillance cameras, emergency alert systems, LED lighting, electrical upgrades, and cybersecurity enhancements. These updates will create safer learning environments, strengthen emergency preparedness, and ensure secure, uninterrupted operations that protect over 800 children, families, and staff.
1113.purpose: The goal of this funding request is to replace and upgrade critical infrastructure, safety, security, and technology systems across Achievement Centers' two licensed child care centers and two administrative buildings in Delray Beach. These facilities serve more than 1,000 children (ages 1–12) on weekdays, teens during weekend programming, and families year-round. The proposed upgrades will ensure ACCF’s campuses remain safe, secure, and technologically reliable for all.
1113.activities: Activities include upgrading security, technology, and electrical systems by installing new door and gate locks, CCTV cameras, LED lighting, emergency alert systems, network and cybersecurity enhancements, blinds, lockdown shades, and safety signage across ACCF campuses.
1113.direct_services: The funding will provide direct services to children, families, and staff by ensuring safe, secure, and well-equipped learning environments with reliable technology and rapid emergency communication.
1113.population: The target population to be served by the requested funds are over 800 youth, families, and staff served by Achievement Centers for Children & Families' programs. The target population includes economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, preschool students, grade school students, middle school and high school students, and their families.
1113.outcome: Improved quality of education for children served at ACCF’s campuses through enhanced safety, security, and technology systems that support consistent learning environments. Increased student engagement, attendance, and academic performance supported by reliable technology and uninterrupted program operations. Reduction in safety and security incidents within and around ACCF facilities, and improved response times during emergencies. Outcomes will be measured through security incident logs, law-enforcement reports, attendance and academic data from ACCF’s ProCare system and the School District data-sharing agreement, and staff and parent satisfaction surveys assessing safety and learning-env

1114.organization: Community Child Care of Delray Beach , Inc.
1114.description: Achievement Centers for Children & Families (ACCF) provides early learning and out-of-school programs to over 800 children from under-resourced families in Delray and Boynton Beach areas. To ensure safe, high-quality learning environments, ACCF seeks funding for critical infrastructure upgrades at two licensed campuses. The project includes water system modernization, roof and gutter repairs, bathroom and flooring renovations, generator installation for emergency continuity, storage conversion, and technology enhancements. These improvements will promote health, safety, and educational resilience for precious young children and their families.
1114.purpose: Funds will be used to repair and modernize infrastructure across multiple Achievement Centers buildings. Improvements include filtered water systems to enhance quality and safety, renovations to gutters, bathrooms, flooring, exterior building painting, and installation of a generator for emergency continuity. These upgrades will strengthen health, safety, and learning environments while supporting long-term resilience.
1114.activities: Activities include replacing and installing water fountains and filtration systems; completing roof, gutter, stucco, and exterior painting repairs; upgrading doors, flooring, and bathrooms; adding a generator and converting patio space to storage; and enhancing technology infrastructure with laptops, tablets, and interactive learning tools. These improvements will ensure clean, filtered drinking water, safe and sanitary facilities, reliable power, and modernized learning environments that suppor
1114.direct_services: The funding will provide direct services by ensuring safe, sanitary, and energy-efficient facilities with clean drinking water, reliable power, improved learning environments, and enhanced technology access for children, teens, families, and staff served daily at ACCF’s licensed education and community center in Delray Beach.
1114.population: The funds requested will serve the over 800 youth and families ACCF serves. This population includes; economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, preschool students, grade school students, middle school students, and high school students.
1114.outcome: Increased access to clean, filtered drinking water and reduction in maintenance or water-quality concerns across campus. Enhanced learning environments and increased student engagement through upgraded classrooms, technology, and facility conditions. Improvements will protect health and safety, ensure compliance with Department of Health standards, and support long-term operational resilience. Outcomes will be measured by tracking installation and maintenance of water filtration systems and fountains, completing annual water-quality tests, reviewing facility maintenance logs, and monitoring attendance, program participation, and satisfaction surveys on learning-space quality.

1261.description: The goal is to purchase two critical pieces of equipment vital to comprehensive patient care for the low-income, uninsured patients enrolled at Grace. The first is a Cone Beam CT for our dental services that serve Orange, Osceola and Seminole counties and the second is a digital x-ray machine for the medical services primarily in Orange County. Our existing equipment for these images is antiquated and the technology advances in new equipment will greatly improve efficiency and patient care. Student interns from UCF will be exposed to this new equipment which will give them an advantage when applying to advanced learning programs in health care.
1261.purpose: The specific purpose achieved by the funds requested is to replace outdated equipment that is no longer supported by software and is not HIPAA compliant. We have volunteer radiologists, orthopedists, oral surgeons, and otolaryngologists who all volunteer at Grace Medical Home or the Dental Center, but they need updated and current equipment to provide accurate diagnostic imaging. We also have a lot of UCF students who intern at Grace Medical Home and would be exposed to new equipment that would
1261.activities: Grace Medical Home serves uninsured residents of Central Florida who reside at or below 225 percent of the federal poverty level. We serve roughly 1,300 unduplicated patients annually, and 5,037 people since inception. The activities and services provided will be free Cone Beam CTs and digital x-rays to give much more accurate diagnostic images for our volunteer physicians and dentists to have more accurate and efficient treatment plans.
1261.direct_services: Free Cone Beam CTs and digital x-rays to Grace Medical Home's low-income, uninsured patients who have no other place to go and cannot afford these images. The digital x-rays provides direct imaging to help identify a range of medical conditions including pneumonia, bone fractures, joint issues, arthritis, osteoporosis and spinal problems. The Cone Beam CT provides accurate 3D imaging of the anatom
1261.population: Grace Medical Home serves uninsured residents of Central Florida who reside at or below 225 percent of the federal poverty level. We serve approximately 1,300 unduplicated patients every year and all would be eligible to receive tests with this new equipment. However, this equipment will last at least a decade, well-past the completion of this funding year so that tens of thousands of uninsured, low-income Central Floridians will be served in the future.
1261.outcome: We will improve physical health by providing at least 25 x-rays or CBCTs each month for optimum patient care. We will measure this by the number of imaging studies that are performed each month. We will enhance our patients' economic self sufficiency by having these two pieces of diagnostic equipment available to our staff or volunteer medical or dental clinicians who can more readily alleviate pain or discomfort so that our patients can go back to work. We will measure the number of patients seen each month for medical and dental services at Grace. They all have access to this new equipment if ordered by the clinician.

1157.description: The Public Safety Dock Rehabilitation Project is a strategic, multi-agency public safety asset on the Intracoastal Waterway, serving as a maritime operations hub for the Boca Raton Police Department and Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC). The proposed project is to rehabilitate the dock and revetment to restore full operational capacity, secure local and state law enforcement assets, and enhance the safety of Florida's waterways. Additionally, this area houses two floating docks, several picnic tables, and a nearby kayak launch. These are all accessible to the public and may be revitalized during this project.
1157.purpose: Enhance the operational capability of the Boca Raton Police Department and the Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission along the Intracoastal Waterway.
1157.activities: Replacement of aging infrastructure to better serve the community.
1157.population: >100,000 residents. The South Palm Beach County area.
1157.outcome: The new design configuration allows for faster deployment and mitigates wake impacts from vessels entering and exiting the slips.

1158.description: The Infrastructure Sustainability Improvement Program, or iSIP, is a crucial long-term initiative of the City’s overall robust and comprehensive asset management program. The City uses technology and data to evaluate, prioritize, and improve critical infrastructure throughout the City’s water distribution and wastewater collection systems. Water and wastewater infrastructure failures can potentially cause significant disruption to residents and commercial customers, impacting health, safety and material damage. With aging infrastructure, proactive end-of-useful life replacement and improvements to drinking water transmission and distribution as well as wastewater infrastructure systems ensure that the City can continuously provide reliable, sustainable, and resilient drinking water and wastewater services to current and future residents and businesses in the City of Boca Raton as well as
1158.purpose: Provide a better water quality to the citizens of Boca Raton
1158.activities: Replacement of aging water mains to serve the community
1158.direct_services: Water quality to the homes will be better and more consistent
1158.outcome: Completion of the project on time and within the budget. Reliable clean drinking water on a daily basis

1262.description: Volusia Volunteers In Medicine is a medical clinic providing free health care to the uninsured citizens of Volusia County who fall under 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. Patients are required to be between the ages of 19 and 65 and show proof of residency within the past year. The "Clinic" has a 501(c)(3) designation and is operated by one paid part- time office manager. Local physicians, nurses and office personnel are volunteers. An all-volunteer Board oversees the operations of the clinic.
1262.purpose: To provide free health care to the growing numbers of uninsured adult citizens living in Volusia County who fall at or below 300% of the federal income poverty level.
1262.activities: Funds will allow the clinic to increase hours of operation in the Daytona Beach location and the New Smyrna Beach location and potentially see more patients who live in Volusia County. Free primary health care can be provided to reduce numbers of visits to the local hospital emergency rooms.
1262.direct_services: Patients will be seen at no charge by resident physicians, nurses, specialists and medical professionals. Funds will help with costs of physical examinations, laboratory tests, imaging, X-rays, MRIs and CT scans that are not provided with discounted rates by local hospitals, imaging centers, lab facilities and physicians.
1262.population: In Volusia County, one of every five adults age 19-65 has no health insurance - that is more than 100,000 residents. US Census Bureau reported that Daytona Beach alone has 13.3% of its population without any medical insurance.
1262.outcome: The more citizens who can be seen by the clinic should result in fewer visits to our taxpayer supported hospital emergency rooms, reduce work absenteeism, and provide early detection of debilitating diseases resulting in a reduced burden on our public healthcare system. Data can be reviewed based on patient visits and records.

1661.description: Continue the supervised training and mentoring, and improving a strong training module for new guardians that assist with alleviating the wait-lists the state Public Guardians maintain in accepting court appointments to new cases. The training program will prioritize undertaking these cases on the wait-lists, which saves the state. Work performed will be Pro-bono in each of the 20 Judicial Circuits. Program fosters a mechanism to improve best practices and ethics related to guardianship.
1661.purpose: Project can be traced to the Florida's Dept. of Elder Affairs and its previously called Statewide Public Guardianship Office SPGO (now OPPG) since 2010. The special training and mentoring program which has not been available was still referenced in the State's official training manual up front in its first chapter. Continues to be strongly supported by Elder Affairs and the Courts. A strong hands-on training and mentoring program is now being implemented, and will provide cost-savings to the Sta
1661.activities: Continue implementation and developing a strong education and mentoring training program targeting newly registered practitioners in guardianship from the outset. Qualified instructors/supervisors in good standing will be enlisted. And will partner with various related organizations and interested parties such as licensed social workers, disability advocacy groups, the Alzheimer's Association, mental health groups, and judges.
1661.direct_services: Though seemingly indirectly for the intended beneficiary, those most vulnerable, these individuals will assuredly gain in general nonetheless. Practitioners will be better prepared and qualified to assist having had additional training and critical individual supervision. The added responsiveness to the individual situation contributes directly to better person- centered care and attention.
1661.population: Those that are among the most vulnerable, range from frail elderly to younger mentally ill adults. (200-300) - Elderly - Persons with poor mental health - Persons with poor physical health - Developmentally disabled - Physically disabled
1661.outcome: The special and enhanced training program will provide precisely the on-point training recommended by the Florida Clerk's Guardianship Improvement Task Force led by Pinellas Clerk Ken Burke. Enhanced Education of Professionals and Parties in Guardianship was one of the top 9 areas recommended for needed focus as outlined in its 2022 report. Provide reports of all those receiving the enhanced education and training, and by professional categories as well to in order at a minimum indicate the level of participation.

1730.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
1730.description: Goodwill Industries-Suncoast has a long standing reputation of providing best in class services to at risk individuals in the Tampa Bay community. The organization currently operates a Pathways program serving victims of human trafficking in our Clearwater, FL location. This project proposes to provide services to 60 - 75 more people in the Tampa Bay Area during FY 2026-2027. Services include intensive assessment, mental health counseling, substance abuse counseling, and career planning and development to victims of human trafficking once stabilization has occurred. Services are offered in this project in an outpatient setting.
1730.purpose: The Goodwill Pathways program assists survivors of human trafficking, helping them plan for their futures once initial stabilization services have taken place. Our goal is to meet the individualized needs of survivors by offering life skills and career development opportunities. Job Placement is the measured goal.
1730.activities: Intake, assessment, substance abuse and mental heath counseling, life skills coaching, parenting, financial literacy, educational skills development and referral and job placement activities.
1730.direct_services: In our second year, we’ll continue walking alongside survivors of human trafficking, providing the comprehensive, trauma-informed support they need to heal, rebuild, and thrive. Specific services include: Assessment of skills and abilities Development of personal, educational and career goals with an eye toward achieving family-sustaining employment. This will include facilitated work experience a
1730.population: The program will serve individuals who are victims of human trafficking who have reached stabilization (i.e. are no longer under the human trafficker's control). We anticipate serving 60-75 additional individuals in Year 2. This is based on the current wait list from year 1.
1730.outcome: Goodwill's previous capacity building and operations in this sector have substantiated that life skills and career development are critical for the successful transition of victims of human trafficking. Victims receive intensive assessments and life coaching and career development, emphasizing up skilling and re-skilling. Goodwill will supplement these services with substance abuse, mental health counseling, and parenting with family reunification. All services are offered using motivational interviewing and active listening techniques. and by applying a variety of modalities through a trauma-informed, victim- centered, and survivor-informed lens. Goodwill will analyze strategies and track o

1344.description: Requested funds for upgrades to meet baseball league standards for the Parks 16 baseball fields include: replace/repair fencing, sidewalks, posts, and gates. The park attracted 494,000 visitors in 2024 and Six Months within 2025 the Park has already attracted 308,000 visitors -- a 25% increase from 2024. This important venue in Florida also provides immediate regional economic benefit gains for 278,468 Alachua County residents and 6,630 business establishments.
1344.purpose: Champions Park is an economic driver for our region as it attracts in-state and out-of-state visitors through the various league competitions and tournaments. Our immediate goal is to replace outfield fencing for the safety of the players and be in compliance with league standards. Our long-term goal is to completely renovate all 16 baseball fields to continue to grow higher-tier USSSA, USA, NFHS and NAFA League competitions and make this park the premiere venue for baseball and fast-pitch softb
1344.activities: Champions Park 16 baseball fields book competitions and tournaments a year in advance due to high-demand for this venue in our region. The funds for outfield fence replacement will provide safety features mandatory by league standards that minimize risks of injuries for players and spectators and allow an uninterrupted game flow for the best possible performance.
1344.direct_services: Direct services include economic benefits for residents, increased tourism, health benefits from competitive outdoor sports, foster social connections, and play a vital role in increasing available sports and community-based programming for all ages.
1344.population: The targeted population served includes grade school, high school and college age youth. Economically disadvantaged populations are serviced through economic gains from tourism that increase job opportunities.
1344.outcome: The project's outcome is to (1) meet mandatory league standards, and (2) increase tourism through the various baseball leagues competitions and tournaments. City staff's methodology of measurement is to document reduced incidences of play/spectator injuries and provide summary of visitors lodging accommodations, attendees location of origin (city, county, Florida, and other states), total sales tax collected, and total direct sales.

2689.description: Matthews Computer Science Bldg. 15 includes departmental and general classrooms, class labs, and faculty offices. The building is showing its age due to the high use and minimal improvements over the years. Most classrooms need to be upgraded to reflect the technology current Computer Science teaching environments employ. The project will remodel all three floors and provide a more inviting and collaborative environment by enclosing the circulation space to create internal corridors and lobbies for enhanced security and more appropriate surroundings. There is an increased interest in cyber security and the project will include new technology and infrastructure improvements to facilitate growth for the cyber security curriculum and programs.
2689.purpose: Improvements in student academic services, as well as the opportunity to increase program offerings in computing and STEM degrees as the university grows.
2689.activities: A remodel/renovation of three floors of the building, creating expanded curriculum, updated classrooms, and study area with collaborative space for students. Project includes installation of new ceilings and lighting, update existing HVAC and electrical systems throughout the building, including better control systems and power distribution.
2689.direct_services: Students, over 90% of whom are from Florida and especially northeast Florida, will have access to additional classroom, study space and updated systems needed for proper building function.
2689.population: Students. The entire UNF student body.
2689.outcome: Number of graduates in STEM areas are evaluated by the Board of Governors. We report them at least annually through our Accountability Plan, and they are part of the Performance Funding Metrics by which all of the SUS is measured.

1702.description: The Marion Oaks Manor Extension project involves extending the road from SW 49th Avenue to CR 475, which includes the construction of a flyover bridge over Interstate 75 (I-75). This flyover will provide a critical new route for residents south of Highway 484, offering a safe and efficient way to cross I-75. The extension of Marion Oaks Manor will also include widening the road to four lanes, addressing future traffic congestion based on projected growth in the area. The widened roadway will improve traffic flow, reduce bottlenecks, and enhance overall safety. The project will implement a stormwater management system that meets environmental standards, ensuring proper drainage and preventing flooding.
1702.purpose: Marion County is requesting $2,000,000 for planning, design, and right-of-way acquisition costs associated with the project.
1702.activities: Environmental assessments will be conducted to comply with all regulations, and any required mitigation measures will be put in place. Right-of-way acquisition and utility relocations will be necessary along the project corridor to accommodate the road extension and bridge construction.
1702.direct_services: This project involves extending the road from SW 49th Avenue to CR 475, which includes the construction of a flyover bridge over Interstate 75 (I-75). This flyover will provide a critical new route for residents south of Highway 484, offering a safe and efficient way to cross I-75.
1702.population: This project will target residents and visitors traveling south of Highway 484, offering a safe and efficient way to cross I-75. The Marion Oaks subdivision houses roughly 25,300 residents. This project offers those traveling east and southeast an alternative to the existing routes. Additionally, secondary connection point from the west side of Marion County to the villages. Overall, the target population served by this project would include travelers and residents as well, which numbers in hund
1702.outcome: The project involves extending the road from SW 49th Avenue to CR 475, which includes the construction of a flyover bridge over Interstate 75 (I-75). This flyover will provide a critical new route for residents south of Highway 484, offering a safe and efficient way to cross I-75. This will be measured by traffic congestion, traffic count, and intersection performance at locations impacted by the project. Additionally, the project will implement a stormwater management system that meets environmental standards, ensuring proper drainage and preventing flooding.

2692.description: Global Leadership Academy, a Title I public charter network serving 3,000 K-12 students in Duval County, requests state support to complete enhancements to its athletic facility at 8985 Lone Star Road, Jacksonville, FL 32211, including synthetic turf installation, new field lighting, restroom upgrades, and expanded bleacher seating. The 285×165-foot field is fully graded and permitted, with $1.6 million invested by the school. Once complete, the facility will provide Title I students and surrounding economically disadvantaged communities access to a premier athletic complex offering year- round use for physical education, competitions, and community events. GLA High School, an FLDOE High-Performing School, will be the primary user, promoting student achievement, teamwork, and leadership through sports. Most charter high schools in Jacksonville lack lighted soccer fields, therefore limit
2692.activities: The completed facility will support a full calendar of athletic and community programming, including high school soccer matches, physical education classes, after-school training, and regional tournaments. Global Leadership Academy will coordinate league play and mentorship events that link athletic participation with leadership and academic growth. The improved restrooms and seating will allow the campus to host family-oriented activities and community celebrations, expanding use beyond school
2692.direct_services: The project will directly provide citizens with access to a modern athletic and recreation facility designed for broad public use. The addition of lighting will extend evening hours and allow several Jacksonville charter high school teams to host practices and games locally, giving students and families greater opportunities to participate. The synthetic turf will enable frequent, year-round use w

The primary beneficiaries are high school students who currently lack access to lighted, well-maintained athletic facilities for safe evening and winter play. Expected outcomes include increased athletic participation, improved student health, and greater family engagement through extended evening and weekend events. The addition of lighting and synthetic turf will reduce cancellations, extend play hours, and create fair access for charter teams that currently lack lighted fields. Success will be measured through participation data, maintenance cost comparisons, and event attendance records. CAP empowers families to pursue the best educational path while driving academic excellence, career readiness and civic pride. Proven CAP outcomes include 80%+ gains in academic performance, focus and classroom engagement, equipping students for long- term economic self-sufficiency and active citizenship through college and career success. Building on this year’s success, CAP will expand services to early childhood learning centers on military bases, providing specialized teacher training and student programming. Military children thrive in group arts education that strengthens communication, confidence and leadership, while teachers adopt strategies that embed civic and patriot
2691.purpose: CAP empowers parental choice by delivering high-quality arts education and career-focused field trips that prepare students for lifelong success: 1.Serve 500 students from military families, charter schools, homeschools, and residential crisis care with high-quality arts education. 2.At the request of MWR Mayport, CAP is expanding military initiatives with on-base programs for children through teens. Tailored teacher training and age-appropriate student programming strengthen academic foundation
2691.activities: CAP programs build academic achievement, character, and civic responsibility that prepare students for success in school, higher education, the workforce, and life. CAP students score 20 points higher on state tests and demonstrate 80%+ improvement in problem-solving, task completion and communication skills. Military Students and Teachers: On base, tailored student instruction and teacher training enhance academics while integrating civics, patriotic values, and leadership. Students gain commun
2691.direct_services: Military Students: Group arts classes focus on communication and community building to reduce isolation caused by trauma from family deployment while fostering civic awareness. Military Teachers: Tailored on-base training equips teachers to help students manage deployment-related stress through the arts and civics education. Homeschool Students: Home-education-specific curricula offer low student-
2691.population: 500 students from charter schools, homeschool families, military families, and residential crisis care residing in Duval, St. Johns, Nassau and Clay counties will receive a variety of high-quality, yearlong arts education programs. CAP’s yearlong programs create opportunities for students to explore career paths and cultivate civic knowledge and patriotic pride, preparing students for greater economic self-sufficiency and engaged citizenship.
2691.outcome: Using rubric, pre and post program student evaluations will demonstrate the following: • Improved mental focus: 85% will report improved ability to set goals and work on a task from beginning to end. • Improved social engagement: 85% will report improvement in participation in class sessions. • Improved ability to solve problems: 80% will report improved reasoning and problem solving skills. • Improved communication skills with peers and adults: 80% will report improved communication skills. • Skill based learning: 90% will report improvement in their arts discipline specific skills. • Academic achievement: 80% will report improved academic engagement.

2693.description: The goal of this project is to provide safe, accessible, and supportive housing for aging individuals with developmental disabilities by constructing a specialized group home designed to meet their evolving physical, medical, and social needs and avoid costly placement in a nursing home or institution. The home will feature barrier-free design, private bedrooms, accessible bathrooms, widened doorways, non-slip flooring, adaptive equipment to support mobility and independence, fire suppression systems, and generator. Enhanced safety systems, such as emergency call technology and accessible kitchen and bathing areas, will promote dignity and care. This environment will ensure continuity of care, reduce hospitalizations, and allow residents to age in place within a compassionate community-based setting.
2693.purpose: Pine Castle has provided quality care to many individuals in residential homes for several decades. Many residents are now aging and require of higher level of care and services which are specialized. The construction of a new home will be designed to accommodate their evolving physical, medical, and social needs, allowing each resident to age in place with the proper supports and special accessibility and safety features.
2693.activities: Upon completion of construction, residents will receive 24-hour support, personal care, health monitoring, nutritious meals, and life skills training all in the comfort of a home that was designed to meet their medical and aging in place needs.
2693.direct_services: Direct services will include personal care assistance, medication management, assistance and transportation to health care providers, meal preparation, assistance with bathing and grooming, self-help training, participation in activities in the home and broader community. Family involvement will be encouraged and input into the individualized care planning.
2693.population: The home will be designed to meet the needs of individuals who are aging who have a developmental disability. A total of six residents will be served with single bedroom occupancy, accessible bathrooms and kitchen, wide hallways and doors for easy wheelchair access. Special safety features, such as fire suppression systems and emergency call systems will further enhance each person ability to age in place.
2693.outcome: Resident outcomes will be measured through regular health assessments, medications reviews, and progress reports on mobility, nutrition and daily living skills. Data from medical visits, incident reports and caregiver evaluations will track improvements in health, independence and quality of life. Progress in social participation, emotional stability and reduction in anxiety or depression will be documented. Cultural enrichment will be measured through participation records, resident feedback and staff observations.

This request represents a critical continuation and expansion of the work ReUp started last year. ReUp currently serves multiple Florida institutions, including: Florida International University, Florida Gulf Coast University, State College of Florida Manatee-Sarasota, Miami Dade College and St. Pete College. ReUp is 3 times more effective at finding, engaging, & enrolling the SCNC population than when colleges and universities attempt this work alone. The initiative began with Florida International University, Florida Gulf Coast University, State College of Florida Manatee-Sarasota, and St. Petersburg College, and has since expanded to include Miami Dade College. This continued investment will ensure statewide support for returning students and adult learners. ReUp leverages postsecond

Data Analytics: ReUp has analyzed over a million interactions with SCNC individuals, which gives us unique perspectives and insight. Learners often tell us that we have a deeper understanding of their circumstances and options than they have themselves. 2694.outcome: The expected benefits are (a) ROI for the state in regards to educational dollars invested in citizens who began a credential but did not complete, (b) driving scale and utilization of existing state programs like Florida Work Experience Program and Florida Public Postsecondary Career Education Student Assistance Grant Program, and (c) providing skilled and employable citizens aligned with the existing workforce gaps in the state. ReUp provides reporting at both the state level and at the institutional levels. ReUp provides an aggregate summary report for the state of Florida and detailed summary reports for participating institutions on student outreach and subsequent pipeline, with context

2695.description: The READ USA literacy tutoring program equips teen tutors—many from under-resourced communities—with professional skills while improving literacy outcomes for elementary students. The requested funds will support tutor recruitment, training, and mentorship, providing hands-on experience in instruction, assessment, leadership, and communication—skills that enhance employability. Through structured one-to-one tutoring, tutors gain workforce experience while students receive targeted reading support. The program expects to train hundreds of tutors while serving up to 1,000 students, creating a pipeline of skilled workers and educators. Measurable outcomes include improved literacy and attendance for students and increased workforce readiness for tutors, evaluated through assessments, attendance tracking, and independent validation by The Ohio State University.
2695.purpose: The funds requested will support the READ USA literacy tutoring program, which serves a dual purpose: improving reading proficiency among elementary students while providing workforce development opportunities for teen tutors, many of whom come from under-resourced communities. The program equips these teen tutors with critical workforce skills, including leadership, communication, instructional techniques, and data analysis, all of which are transferable to future careers. By investing in their
2695.activities: The program provides structured workforce development training for teen tutors, preparing them for future employment while delivering literacy support to young students. Tutors receive specialized training in instructional strategies, assessment administration, and lesson planning, along with hands-on experience in managing structured literacy interventions and adapting lessons based on individual needs. Tutors develop essential soft skills, including leadership, teamwork, and problem-solving, w
2695.direct_services: This project will directly benefit two groups: elementary students who receive literacy tutoring and teen tutors who gain workforce development experience. The elementary students will participate in structured, one-to-one reading interventions tailored to their specific learning needs, focusing on foundational literacy skills such as phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing. By pa
2695.population: The primary beneficiaries are teen tutors and elementary students from under-resourced communities. The program is expected to serve up to 1,020 elementary students who require literacy intervention, primarily from Title I schools where data indicates a significant need for additional reading support. The program ensures that they receive consistent, structured literacy tutoring to help them achieve grade-level proficiency. The program targets teen tutors who are seeking professional development

The program aims to increase reading proficiency on standardized assessments such as the Gates-MacGinitie Reading Test or the Florida Assessment of Student Thinking. 2583.description: This appropriation is to create an Engineering Pathways Academy and Aviation Maintenance Academy at Interlachen Jr.-Sr. High School. These additional secondary workforce programs will support meeting the demands of high skill high wage workforce needs in Region 8 and throughout the state. This funding would allow the district to purchase equipment and complete necessary enhancements to the classrooms/labs for year 1 and 2 of these programs.
2583.purpose: The goal of this appropriation is to create an Engineering Pathways Academy and Aviation Maintenance Academy at Interlachen Jr.-Sr. High School. These additional secondary workforce programs will support meeting the demands of high skill high wage workforce needs in Region 8 and throughout the state. This funding would allow the district to purchase equipment and complete necessary enhancements to the classrooms/labs for year 1 and 2 of these programs.
2583.activities: Workforce programs to be added are Aviation Maintenance General (SOC Code 49-3011- Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians) and Engineering Pathways (Industry certification RECFN001 RECF Pre-Engineering Certification given by the Robotics Education and Competition Foundation).
2583.direct_services: Additional opportunities for future employment or post secondary education for students.
2583.population: Interlachen Jr.-Sr. High School is located in an rural area of opportunity. This project would serve 150-300 students each year,
2583.outcome: Students who participate in the workforce programs may receive industry certification to support their opportunities for future employment. We expect 70% of the students enrolled to receive industry certification in the next 6 years.

2584.description: The project upgrades the East Putnam Regional Wastewater Treatment Plant by adding one 150,000-gallon treatment trains, effluent sprayfields, and connecting piping, increasing capacity by 450,000 gallons per day. The expansion will serve SR 207 and San Mateo residents, allowing those near the St. Johns River to switch from sewer to septic. Work will occur in three phases: engineering and tank construction, plant fit-out, and sprayfield development.
2584.purpose: The project upgrades the East Putnam Regional Wastewater Treatment Plant by adding one 150,000-gallon treatment trains, effluent sprayfields, and connecting piping, increasing capacity by 450,000 gallons per day. The expansion will serve SR 207 and San Mateo residents, allowing those near the St. Johns River to switch from sewer to septic. Work will occur in three phases: engineering and tank construction, plant fit-out, and sprayfield development.
2584.activities: Expansion of water treatment/sewer service in East Palatka area, notably in residential neighborhoods adjacent to the St Johns River where FDEP has identified concerns with continued use of septic systems. This expansion will allow the waste water treatment plant to service 2,700 households compared to the current 1,200 capacity.
2584.direct_services: Residents will be able to switch their waste water services from septic to sewer. The expansion will allow the plant to service as many as 2,700 households compared to the current 1,200 capacity
2584.population: Residents located in the waste water district
2584.outcome: Residents will be able to switch from septic to sewer which will result in less possibility of contamination of ground water, aquifer and the environment.

2589.organization: Central Florida Auto Dealers Association, Inc.
2589.description: This project will expand a successful apprenticeship program for automotive, diesel and collision technicians in 15 counties throughout Central Florida. With over 500 franchised new car dealers in Central Florida, the need for technicians is growing exponentially. This program allows individuals to get on-the-job training under the guidance of experienced mentors and trainers where they learn the skills to immediately join the work force once their program is complete.
2589.purpose: Our vision is to provide underemployed and underserved communities opportunities for gainful careers in vehicle repair by developing, piloting, and launching a training ecosystem. The workforce ecosystem will be designed for training, on-the-job support, reference, and micro-learning. It will support up-skilling the current and new workforce. At the end of the training, students receive a credential that certifies successful program completion and workforce readiness.
2589.activities: A platform will be developed to provide training on how to safely maintain and repair vehicles. The theoretical learning will be followed by hands-on practice at a business. Students will complete on-the-job training before becoming certified as an automotive technician. The Automotive Service Excellence organization will provide a credential.
2589.direct_services: Young adults, veterans, and individuals seeking a career in gas, hybrid, electric vehicle technology can receive training and certification to pursue a career as an auto tech. Funding is necessary to meet the unique and immediate need for effective and affordable training that allows individuals to enter a long-term lucrative career in transportation.
2589.population: Unemployed and underemployed parents, jobless youths, veterans, economically disadvantaged persons, high risk youth, high school students.
2589.outcome: An auto tech will perform a variety of mental, diagnostic, and physical tasks. The key outcome and metric is a tax paying citizen with consistent employment with career growth enjoying a middle class lifestyle. The outcome is a gainful career that allows individuals to meet their needs as posited by Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs (physiological, security and safety, love/belonging, esteem, and self-actualization needs) means that individuals do not need to consider alternative methods for subsistence and self-actualization.

1651.description: State funds will provide for production and installation of interactive educational environments at a new 10,000 sq. ft. Marine Science Center that supports the evolution of the Ocean Economy, encouraging the sustainable use of ocean resources to protect marine diversity, generating economic growth, fostering new technologies and promoting responsible ecotourism. 10 paid jobs at the Marine Science Center will be filled by high school Lead Interns interested in pursuing high demand careers in environmental fields. Lead Interns will activate programs and use the Center as a platform to empower citizens to advocate for a sustainable future.
1651.purpose: State funds will provide for production and installation of interactive environments at the Marine Science Center that raise public awareness regarding the sustainable use of marine resources, promote the work of ocean-based industries and university research, establish a family venue for ecotourism, strengthens workforce readiness for youth to pursue high demand careers and supports the overarching goal of Florida's Office of Ocean Economy at Florida Atlantic University to ensure the economic p
1651.activities: MODS will produce and install 5,000 sq. ft. of immersive, interactive marine environments that reflect a diversity of Florida habitats and wildlife; the importance of protecting the Intracoastal Waterway - a living example of the Ocean Economy - where commerce, recreation and conservation intersect; installation of the Florida Ecosystems Theater and an AI-powered interactive experience to elevate exploration of Florida's ecosystems for guests; and establishment of paid workforce positions leadin
1651.direct_services: The project, supported by a grant from the Florida Inland Navigation District, raises public awareness to support and grow the ocean- and coastal-based industries that drive jobs, investment and innovation across our state, as well as the need to conserve and protect healthy ecosystems for future generations. The project also provides paid employment at a competitive wage for high school students
1651.population: The funds requested will impact a minimum of 26,000 visitors annually to the Marine Science Center, reflecting MODS' audience which is drawn from all 50 U.S. states, 47 Florida counties (70% of the state), 27 foreign countries, as well as students and teachers from Broward and Palm Beach school districts. The target population for workforce internship positions are high school students - 84% of whom reside in ALICE (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) households.
1651.outcome: State funds will educate a minimum of 26,000 citizens annually from at least 70% of Florida counties, increasing their awareness and understanding of the Ocean Economy, its importance to Florida's prosperity and the need to balance the relationship between human activity and environmental health. Funds will also provide workforce and life skills readiness, paid employment, uniforms, educational materials and transportation for 10 high school Lead Interns who will educate the public through activation of programs at the Marine Science Center.

1652.description: Funding would provide for the Construction of ADA-compliant sidewalks and crossings, upgraded pedestrian facilities, traffic calming measures, landscaping and streetscape enhancements, lighting upgrades, and multimodal infrastructure. This will greatly enhance safety at the City's most economically powerful corridor, Las Olas Boulevard, by transforming it into a complete street that will support safe, accessible, and vibrant movement for residents, commuters, and visitors alike. As the centerpiece of a downtown district that generates over $30 billion in annual economic impact, the project will strengthen that role by advancing the City’s Vision Zero goals, improving ADA accessibility, and creating a world-class “Main Street” experience that will drive tourism, investment, and sustained economic growth.
1652.purpose: To create a complete street that enhances pedestrian safety, upgrades ADA facilities, and promotes a vibrant, accessible, and economically thriving corridor. This project improves multi modal mobility, and strengthens Las Olas Boulevard as a world-class destination for residents, visitors, and businesses.
1652.activities: The funds will be used to implement streetscape improvements along Las Olas Boulevard, including ADA upgrades, enhanced pedestrian crossings, sidewalk and streetscape enhancements, traffic calming measures, and other safety features.
1652.direct_services: The project will provide safer, more accessible streets and pedestrian pathways, upgraded ADA facilities, and enhanced streetscape amenities
1652.population: The project serves all users of Las Olas Boulevard, including residents, visitors, commuters, and business patrons. This encompasses pedestrians, cyclists, transit riders, and motorists. The corridor impacts tens of thousands of people daily, with the broader downtown area hosting over 65,000 employees and attracting millions of visitors annually.
1652.outcome: The project will create a safer streetscape that supports pedestrian mobility, ADA compliance, multi modal transportation, and economic vitality. Outcomes will be measured by tracking pedestrian and vehicular safety metrics, ADA compliance improvements, completion of streetscape enhancements, and economic indicators such as increased foot traffic, business occupancy rates, and visitor engagement along the corridor.

1653.description: The project will repair streets with a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 55 or below using asphalt overlay or milling and resurfacing. It was also install FDOT S-3 asphalt, ADA access ramps, thermoplastic pavement markings, milling and leveling of existing asphalt pavement and other items. With 564 miles of city-managed roads, many have deteriorated from age, weather, traffic, and utility work, causing potholes and uneven surfaces. The project will improve road safety, extend pavement lifespan, and enhance travel reliability throughout the City’s right of way.
1653.purpose: The specific purpose of the funds requested is to resurface and restore Fort Lauderdale’s roadways with a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 55 or below. The project will address deteriorated streets by performing asphalt overlay and/or milling and resurfacing, improving roadway safety, ride quality, and overall infrastructure conditions. This investment will ensure safer, smoother, and more reliable streets, reduce hazards from potholes and uneven pavement.
1653.activities: The project will provide roadway improvements through milling and resurfacing of streets with a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) of 55 or below. Activities include applying asphalt overlays, repairing pavement damaged by utility work, and restoring streets affected by ruts, potholes, and other surface irregularities.
1653.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with safer, smoother, and more reliable roadways by repairing damaged pavement, eliminating potholes, ruts, and uneven surfaces, and restoring streets affected by utility work. Residents, commuters, and visitors will benefit from improved travel conditions, reduced vehicle wear and tear, enhanced traffic safety, and more efficient transportation throughout the Cit
1653.population: The target population served by this project includes a target population of approximately 180,000, which include residents, businesses, and visitors using Fort Lauderdale’s roadways.
1653.outcome: Improve roadway conditions, resulting in safer streets, reducing vehicle damage and accidents, extending the lifespan of pavement, enhancing traffic flow, and supporting economic activity by improving access to businesses and public spaces. Outcomes will be measured by tracking improvements in areas experiencing resurfacing, monitoring traffic safety reports, analyzing citizen service requests, and evaluating roadway performance.

1924.description: This project will create an advanced, scalable and effective AI-based monitoring tool for law enforcement to combat the demand for human trafficking activity by monitoring and analyzing buyers’ on-line search behaviors. Additionally, the Center will establish a Joint Law Enforcement Training Program to provide ongoing training opportunities for law enforcement in newly developed technology and detection tools.
1924.purpose: This project will create an advanced, scalable and effective AI-based monitoring tool for law enforcement to combat the demand for human trafficking activity by monitoring and analyzing buyers’ on-line search behaviors. Additionally, the Center will establish a Joint Law Enforcement Training Program to provide ongoing training opportunities for law enforcement in newly developed technology and detection tools.
1924.activities: The outcome objectives for this initiative include (1) developing a monitoring tool, (2) providing actionable intelligence to law enforcement and NGOs, (3) raising awareness and educating among potential buyers to mitigate and stop before it happens, and (4) ensuring the tool can be adapted for use across different disciplines and on-line platforms.
1924.direct_services: Same as (a) above: (1) developing a monitoring tool, (2) providing actionable intelligence to law enforcement and NGOs, (3) raising awareness and educating among potential buyers to mitigate and stop before it happens, and (4) ensuring the tool can be adapted for use across different disciplines and on-line platforms.
1924.population: At-risk youth, crime victims, vulnerable women and children, and tools and training for state and local law enforcement.
1924.outcome: Combating human trafficking activities; developing and implementing an advanced AI-driven solution for Law enforcement; providing actionable intelligence to help identify and prosecute buyers and support victims; educating potential buyers to mitigate and stop the purchase before it happens and promoting safe on-line behaviors. Measurements: reduction in victims and arrests; increased protection for women and girls (78% of victims).

2474.description: Best Buddies is a non-profit organization that creates opportunities for one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, leadership development, inclusive living, and family support for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). This project will provide services to place 50 adults with IDD in jobs, deliver 20 trainings on hiring people with disabilities to potential employers, develop 28 new employer partners across Florida, deliver four presentations to vocational rehabilitation offices, and continue expansion of our Project SEARCH program in Tampa. Best Buddies prioritizes matching a job seeker's interests and abilities with a job of their choosing that pays at or above minimum wage.
2474.purpose: This funding will prepare students and young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities for competitive integrated employment. The funds will be used to educate employers on the benefits of employing people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and place individuals with disabilities in jobs that match their interests and abilities and pay at or above minimum wage.
2474.activities: Best Buddies will provide services to place 50 adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities in jobs, deliver 20 trainings on hiring people with disabilities to potential employers, and develop 28 new employer partners across the state, present to four local vocational rehabilitative offices, and continue expansion of the Project SEARCH program in Tampa.
2474.direct_services: The direct services provided are characterized by individualized support to prepare participants for employment, job coaching after placement, and follow along services to ensure long-term success in the workplace.
2474.population: The target population for this project is individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities seeking employment. This project will serve 50 individuals with disabilities, age 18 and over.
2474.outcome: This project will prepare individuals with disabilities for work, and will place them in jobs that pay at least minimum wage. Participants in the following counties will be served: Broward, Clay, Duval, Hernando, Hillsborough, Lake, Miami- Dade, Orange, Osceola, Palm Beach, Pasco, Seminole, and St. Johns. Project outcomes will be measured using data and progress reports from Set-Works, a case management system, and an annual survey of participants, caregivers, and employers.

1307.organization: the John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art
1307.description: The destructive impact of Hurricanes Helene and Milton has underscored the urgent need to safeguard Florida’s vulnerable coastal environments and the historic buildings on coastal waters. The Ringling Museum’s bayfront campus in Sarasota sustained significant damage from wind action and storm surge, compromising critical infrastructure, including the seawall, pedestrian walkway, balusters, royal pal trees, and the terrace at Ca’ d’Zan.
1307.purpose: The funding request is critical to repairing and replacing critical infrastructure designed to protect coastal erosion along The Ringling Museum’s campus along Sarasota Bay, and to preserve cultural and historic resources, such as the Ca’ d’Zan’ s terrace, vital to the State of Florida
1307.activities: Visitors to The Ringling Museum will have full access to the walkway along Sarasota Bay, including the terrace at Ca’ d’Zan.
1307.direct_services: Access to the pedestrian walkway leading to Ca’ d’Zan along Sarasota Bay, enhancing The Ringling Museum visitor experience A close-up view of a vibrant and healthy Sarasota Bay along The Ringling Museum’s campus.
1307.population: This Project serves the general population of the State of Florida. The Ringling Museum welcomes over 300,000 visitors annually.
1307.outcome: The Project is expected to deliver a wide range of benefits, including the preservation of environmental quality, protection from coastal flooding, increased tourism and economic activity, improved physical and mental health, enriched cultural experiences, and enhanced educational outcomes. Methodologies to measure these benefits include 1) ticket sales, 2 )customer surveys, 3)partner feedback, etc.

1121.description: Currently, senior programming offered at Boulevard Heights Community Center is offered as a partnership with Memorial Regional Hospital with an intent to improve the mental and physical health of Broward County senior citizens. Sample programs include physical exercise and cognitive classes, Medicare and healthy lifestyle classes, and arts & crafts programming. These funds will serve to match existing programming and expand those in order to promote healthy living among a greater population.
1121.purpose: With a growing senior population and with that, greater demand for services, the expansion of senior programming and activities at the Boulevard Heights Community Center (strategically located in the western part of the City) would offer opportunities to positively address seniors' physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual well being.
1121.activities: The Boulevard Heights Community Center is a hub for the community, especially the City's senior population. The intent is to expand programs and activities that address seniors' physical, mental, emotional, social and spiritual well being. The funding will provide enhanced recreational and social programs ranging between educational, cultural enrichment, leisure activities, trips and tours.
1121.direct_services: 1. Programs: Bingo, Painting with a Senior, Table Tennis, Yoga, Arts & Crafts, Stamp Club, Bridge lessons, Movie nights, ESOL, Garden Club, Technology Classes 2. Field trips: Aladdin, Cirque du Soleil, Wicked, Universal Soul Circus, Health Fairs, Luminousa Chinese Lantern Festival 3. Special Events: Fall Festival, Halloween Breakfast, Holiday Luncheon, Valentine's Day Dance, Senior Prom
1121.population: Elderly individuals and those experiencing poor mental/physical health. The expectation is that this service will be available to up to 300 persons from the surrounding area.
1121.outcome: Greater participation in social and cognitive activities, physical activities, events, and field trips. This outcome will be measured by attendance, participation, data, and surveys.

1202.description: The City of Marathon Deep Injection Well Project consists of five phases that consolidate treated effluent from the City’s five wastewater treatment plants into a single Class I Deep Injection Well at the Area 6 Wastewater Treatment Plant. The project includes installation of HDPE transmission mains, new pump stations, and effluent storage improvements. Once complete, the system will eliminate shallow-well effluent disposal, protecting nearshore and groundwater quality, seagrass and coral habitats, and public health. The project fulfills commitments made under the 2023 FOLKS settlement and ensures long-term regulatory compliance, flood resilience, and environmental sustainability for the City’s centralized wastewater infrastructure.
1202.purpose: The requested funds will contribute to the five phases of the City of Marathon Deep Injection Well Project, which consolidates effluent from five wastewater treatment plants into a single Class I deep injection well at the Area 6 WWTP. This will eliminate shallow-well effluent disposal, protect nearshore water quality, and ensure long-term regulatory compliance, flood resilience, and environmental sustainability for the City’s wastewater system.
1202.activities: Funds will be used for design, permitting, construction, and inspection of wastewater conveyance and disposal infrastructure, including effluent transmission mains, pump stations, storage improvements, and a Class I Deep Injection Well. These activities will eliminate shallow-well effluent disposal, protect water quality, and ensure regulatory compliance and long-term system resilience.
1202.direct_services: The project will provide reliable and uninterrupted wastewater service to residents, businesses, and visitors throughout the City of Marathon. By replacing the City's shallow injection wells with a centralized deep injection well disposal system, it directly protects public health, drinking and surface water quality, and the marine environment that supports the local economy and quality of life fo
1202.population: The target population includes all residents, businesses, and institutions served by the City of Marathon’s wastewater system. The project will serve approximately 9,857 permanent residents and over 5,000 service connections across the City’s five wastewater service areas. During peak tourism seasons, the system supports an additional 10,000 to 12,000 visitors and seasonal workers who rely on essential wastewater services.
1202.outcome: The project will eliminate shallow-well effluent disposal and redirect treated wastewater to a centralized Class I Deep Injection Well, protecting nearshore, groundwater, and drinking-water quality while improving public health and environmental resilience. It prevents discharge of approximately 13,698 lbs of nitrogen and 4,566 lbs of phosphorus annually, supporting seagrass, coral, and fisheries recovery. Benefits also include enhanced flood protection, regulatory compliance, and economic stability for approximately 9,857 residents, plus additional seasonal visitors. 1264.purpose: To continue and expand the American Legion Mission of promotion of veteran's welfare, growth of children and youth, Americanism and National Defense.

This will include a private space for counseling and learning of veterans benefits and opportunities. Additionally, this space will include a larger resource library as well as an expanded area to serve the five Boy Scout and Girl Scout troops, the ten high schools and elementary schools and the six
1264.direct_services: The direct services will include but not limited to improved physical and mental counseling to include PTSD, suicide prevention and substance abuse. Counseling and awareness of veterans employment and education opportunities.
1264.population: The target population in addition to the 300 members and families the facility will serve the students, faculty and parents of the ten high schools and elementary schools, the five boy scout and girl scout troops, and the six retirement homes associated with the Post. The number is in excess of 1000 people annually.
1264.outcome: The Department of Florida has a requirement for a detailed annual report which requires the documentation for all activities including attendance at all meetings, all service officer duties to include counseling and referrals, all community service events and support activities.
