2536.description: Pinellas and Pasco counties saw tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged by the combined devastation wrought by Hurricanes Helene and Milton. With funding in the amount of $1M, Rebuilding Together Greater Florida would be able to return at least 80 of these damaged homes to habitability for low-income Pinellas and Pasco County residents over a 12-month period.
2536.purpose: Pinellas and Pasco counties saw tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged by the combined devastation wrought by Hurricanes Helene and Milton. With funding in the amount of $1M, Rebuilding Together Greater Florida would be able to return at least 80 of these damaged homes to habitability for low-income Pinellas and Pasco County residents over a 12-month period.
2536.activities: Funding will be used to return our most vulnerable to safe, healthy, habitable, and resilient housing.
2536.direct_services: This will be accomplished by providing critical home repairs to low-income Pinellas and Pasco residents, free of charge.
2536.population: The population to be served includes low-income individuals in Pinellas and Pasco counties, elderly residents, and others on fixed incomes. It is anticipated that at least 80 homes can be served with the requested funding.
2536.outcome: It is expected that, through facilitating critical repairs, homeowners' long-term financial stability will be improved, as will their health and safety. In additional to recording the number of homes served, outcomes can also be measured via program participants' self reporting.

1547.description: A statewide initiative that provides families, young adults, and 9th–12th grade students with financial-empowerment, college, and career-readiness training. The program focuses on rural and economically disadvantaged communities and strengthens Florida’s workforce pipeline through financial literacy, employment skills, and entrepreneurship education.
1547.purpose: To strengthen Florida’s workforce pipeline by equipping families, young adults, and 9th–12th grade students with financial literacy, college and career-readiness skills, and entrepreneurial knowledge that improve economic self- sufficiency and employment outcomes in rural and economically disadvantaged communities.
1547.activities: Financial literacy workshops for families and young adults. High-school sessions on college planning, FAFSA awareness, and career pathways. Job-readiness training (resumes, interviews, workplace skills). Entrepreneurship and small-business simulations. One-on-one and small-group financial coaching. Regional events connecting participants with employers, colleges, and resource partners.
1547.direct_services: Direct services include in-person workshops, individualized coaching, mentoring, college and career guidance, and structured entrepreneurship training delivered to participants in their communities.
1547.population: High school students (9th–12th grade) Young adults Economically disadvantaged persons Jobless persons At-risk youth Rural families Estimated number to be served:Approximately 1,000 participants statewide during FY 2026–2027.
1547.outcome: Benefits/Outcomes: 80% of participants improve savings, budgeting, or credit behaviors. 65% report new or improved employment, income, or entrepreneurial activity within six months. 85% of participating students show increased college and career-readiness. Methodology: Pre/post financial wellness and college/career-readiness assessments. Follow-up surveys 3–6 months post-program. Verification through partner organizations where appropriate. Annual impact report submitted to the Department of Commerce.

1502.description: Lively Technical College seeks to modernize welding and pipefitting infrastructure to address critical workforce needs. Upgraded labs and facilities will train students in advanced welding techniques and pipe fabrication skills essential for Florida's manufacturing sectors. The funding supports hands-on training, industry certifications, and partnerships that prepare students for high-demand manufacturing jobs, aligning with Florida's economic growth and workforce.
1502.purpose: Building a workforce equipped to meet the demands of advanced manufacturing sectors, including aerospace, industrial fabrication, and infrastructure construction, fueling local talent pipelines with skilled welders and pipefitters prepared for evolving technology and industry standards is the specific purpose of special appropriations request.
1502.activities: By establishing state-of-the-art welding and pipefitting labs, we aim to enhance student preparedness for high-wage manufacturing jobs through rigorous technical skill proficiency and real-world practice; support accelerated workforce credentialing by providing pathways to nationally recognized certifications such as AWS Certified Welder in multiple welding processes and pipe welding.
1502.direct_services: Expand access to hands-on training for diverse populations including veterans, underemployed workers, and high school dual enrollment students, addressing Florida’s critical labor shortages in manufacturing trades. Foster strategic industry partnerships facilitating apprenticeships, internships, and direct employment pipelines within Florida's growing manufacturing economy.
1502.population: Jobless person, economically disadvantages persons, at-risk youth, homeless, high school students, college students, formerly incarcerated persons will be served by this project. 50-100 persons are expected to be served each year.
1502.outcome: The appropriation request is critical for preparing a highly skilled manufacturing workforce in Florida. Modernizing our welding labs with industry-standard equipment and expanding pipefitting fabrication facilities will provide students hands-on training in high-demand skills such as SMAW, GTAW, and advanced pipe welding techniques essential for the manufacturing and construction industries.

1503.description: Study will evaluate the technical, environmental, and financial feasibility of consolidating multiple small wastewater systems (Ft. White, Branford, Ellisville) and replacing aging or failing septic systems (estimating 4,000-6,000) with modernized regional facilities with advanced treatment capabilities, alternative water reuse, and aquifer recharge. Additionally the study will identify and prioritize projects aligning with FDEP and SRWMD strategic water quality and sustainability objectives.
1503.purpose: The study will evaluate the technical, environmental, and financial feasibility of consolidating multiple small wastewater systems and replacing aging or failing septic systems with a modern regional facility. The project aligns with Florida’s strategic water quality and sustainability objectives under the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and the Suwannee River Water Management District (SRWMD).
1503.activities: The funds will drive the assessment of existing and future wastewater system needs, identify deficiencies and opportunities, and develop a list of implementable, fundable projects to improve service reliability, sustainability, and growth capacity for Suwannee and Columbia Counties.
1503.direct_services: Study will evaluate the technical, environmental, and financial feasibility of consolidating multiple small wastewater systems (Ft. White, Branford, Ellisville) and replacing aging or failing septic systems (estimating 4,000-6,000) with modernized regional facilities with advanced treatment capabilities, alternative water reuse, and aquifer recharge.
1503.population: The funds will serve all citizens and groups in Suwannee and Columbia Counties.
1503.outcome: Improved physical health, protection of the general public from environmental harm, increase or improve economic activity, improve regional wastewater management, and improve groundwater quality. Measurement: Formulate a prioritized list of regionally based implementable projects aligning with Florida’s strategic water quality and sustainability objectives under the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and the Suwannee River Water Management District (SRWMD).

2481.organization: Gulf Coast Jewish Family and Community
2481.description: This project is part of the agency's overall improvements at the Gulf Coast JFCS Administration campus in Clearwater, Florida. Phase II of the Gulf Coast JFCS Renovation project includes infrastructure improvements that will update the built work environment and strengthen the facility safety and security. The proposed improvements will harden the facility against external threats and mitigate acts of violence including gunfire, forced entry, vehicular assault and potential bomb threats. Improvements may include bollards, ballistic shielding, additional exterior lighting, additional security cameras, hardening of entryways and installation of a security vestibule in the main lobby.
2481.purpose: Improved safety and security of the Gulf Coast JFCS Administration facility which as serves as the primary hub for the agency's statewide social service activities.
2481.activities: Construction of infrastructure and security Improvements that may include: bollards, ballistic shielding, additional exterior lighting, additional security cameras, hardening of entryways and installation of a security vestibule in the main lobby.
2481.direct_services: All current clients and visitors to Gulf Coast JFCS will be better protected and feel more secure from potential threats.
2481.population: Approximately 18,000 clients are served by 200 staff through this Clearwater, Florida, Pinellas County facility each year.
2481.outcome: The agency will have a hardened, safer environment for client service delivery. an updated security assessment will be requested from the the Secure Community Network to assess improvements. This will document improvements as outlined in a 2017 Homeland Security assessment and a 2024 Secure Community Network assessment (an non profit designated as the official safety and security organization for) the Jewish Community in North America.

3570.description: The City of Bowling Green is requesting funds to acquire a Utilitly and Stormwater Maintenance Vacuum (VAC) Truck. The City of Bowling Green is a rural community with aging infrastructure. This essential equipment will enhance the city's ability to maintain and improve it's utility and stormwater systems, ensuring efficient operation, reducing environmental risks, and supporting the community's infrastructure needs.
3570.purpose: The requested funds will be used to acquire a Utility and Stormwater Maintenance Vacuum (VAC) truck for the City of Bowling Green, a rural community with aging infrastructure. This essential equipment will enhance the city's ability to maintain and improve it's utility and stormwater systems, ensuring efficient operation, reducing environmental risks, and supporting the community's infrastructure needs.
3570.activities: The VAC truck will provide essential services such as cleaning and maintaining stormwater drains, sewer lines, and utility systems. It will help prevent sanitary swewer overflows, pipe blockages, reduce flooding risks, and ensure proper wastewater management.
3570.direct_services: The VAC truck will provide essential services such as cleaning and maintaining stormwater drains, sewer lines, and utility systems. It will help prevent sanitary sewer overflows, pipe blockage, reduce flooding risks, and ensure proper wastewater management. These activities will improve infrastructure reliability, protect public health, and enhance environmental safety for the citizens of Bowling
3570.population: The project serves all residents, businesses, and visitors within the City of Bowling Green. Approximately 3,000 or more individuals will benefit from improved sewer and stormwater reliability, reduced flooding risks, and faster emergency response provided by the VAC truck.
3570.outcome: The project will improve the reliability of the City's sewer and stormwater systems, reduce blockages and overflow incidents, and strengthen emergency response. Outcomes will be measured by tracking completed line cleanings, reductions in service interruptions, faster response times to problems, and fewer citizen reports of sewer or drainage issues.

1507.description: The Gulf County Sheriff's Office is seeking $1,500,000 in state appropriations funding to construct an extension of our administrative offices to house a new dispatch center and training facility. Currently, the dispatchers operate out of a room that is less than 400 square feet. The dispatchers do not have an adjoining restroom or kitchenette and have to utilize the public restrooms facilities in our main lobby and use the kitchen that is located on the second floor. Our current training room is also less than 400 square feet and is too small to conduct effective training, especially defensive tactics. This expansion project will provide an adequate dispatch center and training room. The old facilities will be converted into much needed office spaces.
1507.purpose: The building addition will achieve multiple goals. Increased Public Safety: A modern, well-equipped dispatch center will enhance the ability to dispatch first responders to emergencies and maintain public safety. Enhance Law Enforcement Training: A spacious training facility will allow us to host quality training classes for GCSO and surrounding agencies. Community Outreach: the training facility will also be used for community outreach programs. Cost Savings: The renovation of the existing disp
1507.activities: Dispatch services: The building addition will improve our ability to properly dispatch law enforcement services in Gulf County. Training services: The new training facility will provide the opportunity to train more efficiently with larger classes and allow on site training for new curriculum. Community Engagement: The training facility will also be used for community outreach programs, meetings, and events to foster better community relationships.
1507.direct_services: Enhanced dispatch services: Improve response times for law enforcement, ensuring the safety and security of the county. Better Trained Law Enforcement Officers: Law enforcement will be better trained and able to serve the community better. Community Outreach Programs: community meetings, workshops, and events aimed at building relationships & trust between law enforcement and citizens.
1507.population: The target population served by this project include all residents and visitors of Gulf County. This population encompasses a diverse demographic including families, business,and tourists seeking various services from the Gulf County Sheriff's Office. This project will serve all the residents, businesses, and tourists seeking law enforcement services from the Gulf County Sheriff's Office.
1507.outcome: Benefit: Enhanced dispatch services: Improve dispatch environment and response times for law enforcement, ensuring the safety and security of the county. Measuring Benefits: Monitor response times and dispatcher retention. Benefit: Better Trained Law Enforcement Officers: Law enforcement will be better trained and able to serve the community better. Measuring Benefit: Monitor hours of training and citizen complaints. Benefit: Community Outreach Programs: community meetings, workshops, and events aimed at building relationships & trust between law enforcement and citizens. Measuring benefit: Number of meeting and community contacts.

2482.description: Neighborly Care Network is a senior service non-profit serving Pinellas County for over 50 years. We have three services for seniors: Adult Day Care, Transportation, and Nutrition. We are best known as Meals on Wheels Pinellas County. Neighborly requests state funding for nutritious meals to at-risk seniors in our community. Neighborly serves over 2000 seniors yearly, but over 650 people wait for meals. The nutrition program ensures that seniors who cannot prepare meals for themselves due to physical, financial, or social limitations receive the proper nutrition they need to maintain their health and independence. With your support, we can ensure that 500 seniors stay off of the Meals on Wheels waitlist and receive nutritious meals, social connections, and other resources to help them thrive independently.
2482.purpose: Help prevent malnutrition and isolation among seniors in Pinellas County by supporting Meals on Wheels. With one in two seniors at risk of malnutrition, providing meals and connection to at least 500 seniors is crucial. Your support can make a difference and ensure seniors can thrive, and live independently at home, avoiding costly institutional care. Help prevent the waiting list from growing each month.
2482.activities: We provide seniors meals (dine-in or delivery) and wellness checks by volunteers or staff to support seniors to live independently and improve their quality of life. Our service is a lifeline, and drivers have even prevented suicide. Drivers and staff may call family if they notice a change in the client, make an Elder Abuse report if they are concerned for their safety, or call 911.
2482.direct_services: In-person meals and social connection with a caring volunteer or Neighborly employee. All meals are planned by a registered dietitian to ensure they are balanced and meet the needs of older adults. Recipients will receive a daily lunch whether they dine in or need delivery. They can get hot, frozen, or hurricane meals. They also have access to nutrition counseling and education.
2482.population: We will serve older adults age 60 and over. We expect to serve at least 500 people. Targeted populations include clients who are low-income, minority, live alone, veterans, and at-risk for institutional care. Pinellas County is reported to be 35% age 60+, 13% minority, 30% living alone, and 14% low-income.
2482.outcome: Food security and reduced isolation and malnutrition for seniors. We track this through evidence-based assessments and client survey data. Meal data and client welfare notes are tracked daily. Preliminary findings in an ongoing study on Pinellas County meals on wheels recipients suggest that in-person meal delivery improves health outcomes, reduces loneliness, and decreases food insecurity. Community-based Meals on Wheels programs are evidence-based, cost- effective solutions to reducing healthcare costs. institutional care, healthcare utilization, improving nutrition status, and safety.

1272.description: The request involves the purchase and deployment of mobile vehicle threat mitigation barriers to enhance security at numerous pedestrian-focused events. These barriers would establish a hard perimeter to prevent or reduce the risk of vehicular attacks and related incidents. The primary goal is to strengthen public safety by deterring and limiting the use of vehicles in potential mass casualty attacks. The City of Winter Park hosts a significant number of public events annually, drawing more than 100,000 attendees. Once acquired, the barriers would serve as a regional asset and could be made available—upon request—to other law enforcement agencies for similar high-attendance public gatherings.
1272.purpose: The purpose/goal of the funds is to enhance public safety through deterrence and mitigation of vehicular threats on public gatherings.
1272.activities: The trailers, barriers and accessories will be stored at the Winter Park Public safety complex and deployed according to operational plans at events. The deployment of barriers will allow for roadways and walkways to be safely protected against vehicle threats and incidents.
1272.direct_services: The citizens will have enhanced safety while attending public events. The enhanced safety is provided by blocking vehicle access, on roadways and walkways, to public gatherings. The barrier systems are specifically designed for this purpose and tested to ensure proper function against vehicle incidents. The barrier systems will also help achieve on overall sense of calm and safety at public events
1272.population: The City of Winter Park host approximately seventy-five (75) events each calendar year. The attendance for all of the events combined is estimated at over one hundred thousand people (100,000). In addition to events with the City limits of Winter Park, the barrier systems would be a regional asset and available for use by other law enforcement agencies within Central Florida.
1272.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome for this project is to provide a safe environment for public events where the risk of vehicular attacks or incidents are significantly reduced due to the requested equipment. The outcomes for the success of the project will be measured by the public sense of safety at events as well as the absence of any incidents or the effective prevention of an attempted incident.

3572.description: SMM’s Disaster Volunteer Village will host up to 100 volunteers through a Volunteer Reception Center, bunkhouse, and 10 RV campsites with hookups. Located beside the SMM Disaster Volunteer Headquarters, home to the Disaster Warehouse (100% funded, 90% constructed) and Disaster Office (100% funded, pending construction). The Village will provide essential support for disaster response in Hardee County and surrounding areas.
3572.purpose: SMM’s Disaster Volunteer Village will host up to 100 volunteers through a Volunteer Reception Center, bunkhouse, and 10 RV campsites with hookups. Located beside the SMM Disaster Volunteer Headquarters, home to the Disaster Warehouse (100% funded, 90% constructed) and Disaster Office (100% funded, pending construction), The Village will provide essential support for disaster response in Hardee County and surrounding areas.
3572.activities: Primary: Increase resiliency and respond quickly after a natural disaster by providing housing and hookups for volunteers Secondary: Provide space for a No Notice shelter & temporary housing after a storm, fire, or other local emergency
3572.direct_services: As a Volunteer Organization Active in Disaster (VOAD) in Hardee County, SMM manages the Volunteer Reception Center (VRC) and houses volunteers, assists in immediate response, short-term relief, and long-term recovery, repairing and replacing damaged homes, providing temporary housing, assisting with FEMA applications, and other support services, including Disaster Case Management.
3572.population: Target populations in Hardee County include: elderly, persons with poor physical/mental health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged, at-risk youth, homeless, developmentally/physically disabled, students (pre-school, grade school, high school, university/college).
3572.outcome: The primary outcome of this project is to have one centralized location for Hardee County to receive and house disaster relief volunteers. The secondary outcome of this project is to provide space for No Notice Shelter and temporary housing after a storm, fire, or other local emergency. Methodology by which the outcome will be measured will be a construction timeline with anticipated completion date of 6/30/2027 prior to the 2027 hurricane season.

3441.organization: Lighthouse of Broward for the Blind & Visually
3441.description: LHOB’s targeted, community-based programs enable seniors to remain safe, independent, and in their own homes—avoiding premature and expensive placement in state-subsidized facilities, reduce reliance on in-home support or social services, and improve physical and mental health outcomes. We endeavor to increase the number of seniors served by 100%. In FY 2024–25, we served 338 seniors; with additional support, we can expand access to hundreds more. All education and training is delivered by master’s-level and nationally certified professionals in Independent Living Skills, Orientation & Mobility, Assistive Technology, and Social and Therapeutic Groups.
3441.purpose: LHOB intends to increase services to seniors by 50%. In FY 2021-22, LHOB served 338 seniors vs. est. 177,000 seniors who need vision rehab services (2020 U.S. Census), which will double by 2050. As a result of failing eyesight, they are vulnerable to losing their independence to a senior residential facility. LHOB services will allow them to remain living independently and safely in their homes through instruction in the areas of Living Skills, Orientation & Mobility, and Assistive Technology.
3441.activities: Services will include Vision Rehabilitation Therapy, Orientation & Mobility, Rehabilitation Counseling, Vocational Evaluation, Geriatric Case Management, Daily Skill Training, Adjustment to Blindness Counseling, Medication Management, Safe Travel Skills, Assistive Computer/Technology, Health and Wellness Education, Socialization, Education/Support, and Low Vision Comprehensive Eye Exams.
3441.direct_services: The full compliment of rehabilitation services including Vision Rehabilitation Therapy, Orientation & Mobility, Rehabilitation Counseling, Vocational Evaluation, Geriatric Case Management, Daily Skill Training, Adjustment to Blindness Counseling, Medication Management, Safe Travel Skills, Assistive Computer/Technology, Health and Wellness Education, Socialization, Education/Support, and Low Vision
3441.population: At least 100 senior adults age 65 and over who reside in Broward County will be served. Broward County is home to more than 340,000 adults aged 65 and older, living across 31 municipalities. Among the seniors we serve: 43% are male, 57% female, 33% Black, 62% Caucasian, 15% Hispanic, and 7% Haitian. 63% live below the federal poverty level.
3441.outcome: The following performance metrics will be used to assess the success of the program. Goal 1 = 100% of Seniors will remain independent; Goal 2 = 75% of clients completing the program or ongoing clients with the progress made can perform one or more daily living activities (safe indoor/outdoor travel, medication management, meal preparation, money identification/bill paying); Goal 3: 75% of clients improve communication skills demonstrated by proper use of assistive devices.

2483.description: This project will enhance youth mental health services, ensuring youth have access to vital mental health resources, support, and education, ultimately fostering improved mental wellness and resiliency among young individuals in the community. This includes mental health education, counseling, crisis intervention, and resource coordination for youth, parents, and educators. Other direct services include youth crisis support; access to counseling, educational programs, resilience training, and emotional support; and providing referrals for mental health resources to gain immediate and long-term wellbeing.
2483.purpose: The primary goal of this project is to strengthen the resilience of young people by engaging them in developing solutions that meet their needs with events, spaces, and content that supports youth mental health. We will consider the project a success if we have partnered with multiple schools to develop in-school Wellness Rooms and accessible youth mental health programming. We intend for the success of this project to also have a positive impact and encourage meaningful engagement with families
2483.activities: In-school technical assistance to support the development of a fully planned location for mental wellness. This includes design services for each room, planning and technical support for creating the program and evaluating outcomes, and ongoing tracking of progress for behavior across the school population. In addition, all sites will be part of an evaluation by University of South Florida, and partake in a facilitated learning cohort to increase outcomes and speed to scale.
2483.direct_services: The Wellness Rooms will deliver support and coordinated access to mental health services within the school. Students will have access to therapeutic services such as art therapy, music therapy, support groups, mentorship (and peer mentorship), yoga, breathwork, and other prevention focused activities to learn core elements of resilience and emotional regulation. Parents/caretakers will have access
2483.population: Students and families/caregivers in identified Title 1 schools in Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, and Polk Counties.
2483.outcome: The proposed short-term outcomes from this project will include: • Increase in personal wellbeing among students who visit the Wellness Room as measured by pre- & post- student surveys based on the PWI-SC • Increase in personal wellbeing among students who connect with a Youth Mental Health Peer Ambassador as measured by pre & post student surveys based on the PWI-SC • Increase in personal wellbeing among individuals who participate in a Mental Health program or service through this initiative as measured by pre & post student surveys based on the PWI-SC • Increase in awareness of strategies and tools that support youth mental health and wellbeing as measured by post- program survey question

1732.description: Miracle Place Pasco provides housing and support services to 100 families annually experiencing homelessness in Pasco County. Services are designed to strengthen families using a two generation approach, providing a pathway towards self-sufficiency for both adults and children. Families have access to housing, 3 nutritious meals a day, and an array of support services which help adults increase income and sustain housing, including case management, adult education/training, childcare/out-of-school time and tutoring (0-18), employment, housing placement, health/wellness, and counseling. 18 months after exiting, 92% of families remain housed.
1732.purpose: The requested funding will allow 100 homeless families access to safe shelter and wrap-around support services. Miracle Place Pasco participants have access to a "one-stop shop", which includes 48 Shelter units, food, a 10,000 square foot Childcare Center (ages 0-18) and support services, which include Case Management, Employment, Adult Education, Housing Placement, Counseling, and Health Access. 80% of families will exit to permanent housing and 75% will increase income.
1732.activities: Families living in Miracle Place Pasco receive housing (on average 3-6 months), access to 3 meals a day, daily living resources (hygiene or cleaning supplies), and an array of support services, including case management, adult education/training, employment, housing placement, budgeting, health/wellness, counseling, and childcare or out-of- school time care.
1732.direct_services: Services are designed to provide citizens experiencing homelessness a pathway to self-sufficiency and housing stability. Each household develops an individualized case management plan designed to address barriers towards self- sufficiency. Adult education and employment resources assist adults in increasing income and maintain employment, supported by resources such as counseling and childcare.
1732.population: The target population for this project is homeless and at-risk of homeless households living in Pasco County. Approximately 100 families are expected to be served annually consisting of 110 adults and 250 children.
1732.outcome: 100 households experiencing homelessness will have access to shelter with case management and wrap-around support services. 80% of households will exit to permanent housing. 75% of households will exit with increased income. Pre and post assessment will be completed for housing and income and documented in the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS).

1156.description: This project will involve the modification of 2 sluice gates at the S-2 and S-7 pump stations within SBDD to double their discharge capacity via gravity flow. The project also calls for a brand new 60" RCP culvert with emergency sluice gate to be installed within SBDD's S-3 basin. This also includes installation of telemetry system for 24/7 monitoring and operation by SBDD staff to be used in emergency cases for additional pre- and post-storm draw down to increase storage capacity within lakes and canals within SBDD. This improvement will provide tremendous benefit to the residents and businesses by allowing SBDD to more effectively provide drainage and flood protection to the residents within the effected areas. These gates were part of a larger FEMA BRIC Grant project where SBDD was a project partner with SFWMD. The BRIC program was ended in 2025 before the construction phase commenced
1156.purpose: The purpose of the funds would be the modification of 2 sluice gates located at the S-2 and S-7 pump station to increase their size and flow capacity as well as the installation of a new emergency sluice gate within a neighborhood in SBDD's basin S3 to be used for emergency discharge in the event of a large scale incoming storm. The new gate will also allow for a built in discharge point for SBDD's mobile stormwater pump to use in emergency pre- and post- storm operations.
1156.activities: The project will provide 2 modified sluice gates to be controlled automatically through SBDD's telemetry system within the pump stations and a new culvert and sluice gate with telemetry to allow for automatic control of the emergency gate as well. These improvements will allow for a better level of service within SBDD Basins S-2, S-3, S7, and S-13 through increased ability to draw down levels pre-storm to create more capacity in the lake and canal system. This will allow for flood levels to be l
1156.direct_services: SBDD will be provided real-time water level monitoring with an increased ability to provide pre-storm and post-storm drawdowns which will enhance the level of service of flood protection (both stages and duration) for the citizens and businesses within the region.
1156.population: According to 2020 Census data the total population effected by this project is 129,966 people.
1156.outcome: This project will provide added flood protection within the region. By lowering surface water levels within the interconnected lakes and canal system, SBDD will have the ability to perform a faster more effective pre-storm draw down via gravity within the SBDD Basins 2, 3, and 7. The residents and businesses will benefit from the pre-storm draw down which will lower the lake levels and provide additional, critical, storm-water storage within the community faster than what was previously possible to ensure there is optimum storage even with shorter notice for storm warnings. The extra storage capacity will allow for businesses to remain open longer, for residents to return to work sooner and

1210.description: The half-size replica of the Vietnam Wall in Washington, DC, to be built at the Miami-Dade Military Museum is one of the most important projects that will come before the Florida legislature. The $2.9M total cost will be shared with federal, local, and philanthropic support. Florida's largest constituency are its 1.5 million military Veterans, and the overwhelming majority are Vietnam Veterans. They served; they fought; 58,000 gave their lives. Yet their welcome was a cold one. The 1/2-size Wall will stand as the rightful thank you to those who gave everything for our freedom. It will solace the older and inspire the younger. The true message, which our legislators should never forget is this: Freedom is not Free.
1210.purpose: To reflect credit on the military service of our Veterans, especially our Vietnam Veterans, who served honorably but received uncertain welcome on their return from the Vietnam War. Rather, they were all too often overlooked by society only now seeing the importance of their service and that over 58,000 gave their lives, the ultimate sacrifice. Our Vietnam Wall will have engraved in its granite the names of every one of those heroes who fought and died for America.
1210.activities: An overwhelming part of our national military heritage is the Vietnam experience. The Vietnam Wall stands in somber reflection of all our struggles and triumphs as a people. The Wall is a quiet remembrance of the unspoken unity of all Americans. The full-size Wall in Washington, DC, is the most-visited shrine in America. Our half-size replica will be among the most visited destinations in Florida.
1210.direct_services: There has been an alarming epidemic of Veterans committing suicide. The Wall will be highly therapeutic in preventing this. The Honor Flight program hosts airplane trips to Washington, DC, filled primarily with Vietnam Veterans. More than any other Washington monument they are drawn to the Vietnam Wall. Its solemn recognition of their service resonates tremendously with all Vietnam Veterans.
1210.population: Florida has 1.5 million Veterans, the third-largest number of any State in the US. The Wall project will put Florida on the map to welcome Veterans and show appreciation for their service. National and International Tourism will benefit greatly from this solemn patriotic reflection of America's best virtues. South Florida has over 40 high school JROTC units, literally thousands of cadets who are the future of America. The Wall is for them, as much if not more, than the Veterans who are finally r
1210.outcome: The Vietnam Wall will be open to all visitors and provide a meaningful experience for everyone. We are located on the grounds of Zoo Miami, the largest in the Southeast US, and The Wall will complement and enhance the appeal and attraction of both the Military Museum, the adjacent Railroad Museum and the Zoo Miami itself. The patriotic nature of the Wall will serve as inspiration to all future Americans.

2697.description: Recladding of existing cupola and clock replacement
2697.purpose: The historic courthouse is an operating courthouse and a historic landmark for Fernandina Beach. The funding will allow for the continuing function of the building and historical structure for tourism purposes.
2697.activities: Recladding of existing cupola and clock replacement
2697.direct_services: The historic courthouse is an operating courthouse and a historic landmark for Fernandina Beach. The funding will allow for the continuing function of the building and historical structure for tourism purposes. Tourism helps to provide economic impacts to the local businesses and community.
2697.population: The target populations are court visitors and tourist. The County has approx. one million visitors a year. The Court operations vary annually depending on case loads.
2697.outcome: Maintaining the historic courthouse, which is a focal point for tourist visiting the island, will help support tourism on the island. The measurement can be maintaining or increasing tourist visits. This can be measured through tourist visits, and economic impacts from the tourism to the community, businesses, etc.

2698.description: Courthouse redesign for the addition of new courtrooms and judicial offices
2698.purpose: The funding will allow for the addition of courtrooms and judicial offices.
2698.activities: This will provide for the initial architectural and engineering design work.
2698.direct_services: The courthouse is an operating courthouse. The funding will allow for the continuing function of the courthouse.
2698.population: The target populations are court visitors. The Court operations vary annually depending on caseloads. The increased courtrooms will allow for faster processing of cases.
2698.outcome: The County will need new courtrooms to support the increased number of County and Circuit Court Judges. These courtrooms will provide for better court operations. This can be measured by the number of increased cases utilizing the new courtrooms.

1510.description: These funds will allow the City of Jasper to complete the design and permitting phase for its New Water Treatment Plant (WTP) and 16-inch Potable Water Transmission Main project—critical upgrades needed to replace the City's failing WTP; resolve long-standing water quality, reliability, redundancy, and resiliency issues; improve system pressure and fire protection; expand the City's O&M capabilities; and support essential residential and economic growth. Advancing this work also ensures Jasper can meet regulatory standards, protect public health, and accommodate existing and future needs.
1510.purpose: The funds will complete the design and permitting of Jasper’s new Water Treatment Plant and 16-inch transmission main—critical upgrades needed to replace the failing WTP, resolve long-standing water quality and reliability issues, improve system pressure and fire protection, and support future residential and economic growth.
1510.activities: Activities include engineering design, permitting, technical evaluations, hydraulic modeling, topographic surveying, geotechnical investigation, preparation of construction documents, and development of project specifications for both the new WTP and the associated 16-inch transmission main.
1510.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with a fully designed, permitted, and shovel-ready WTP and transmission main, enabling the City to move into construction and ultimately deliver improved water quality, reliable system pressure, enhanced fire protection, and long-term system resiliency.
1510.population: The project will serve approximately 3,600 residents, along with the broader utility service area that includes local businesses, schools, commercial corridors, Hamilton County Correctional Institute, and critical facilities. The improved water treatment capacity and reliability will support future residential development and commercial investment, benefiting both current and projected populations.
1510.outcome: The project will result in completed design and permitting packages that position the City to begin construction of a modern, resilient WTP and transmission main. Success will be measured by obtaining regulatory approvals, completion of all design deliverables, and readiness to proceed to construction, which will ultimately support improved water quality, system reliability, pressure, and fire protection.

1297.description: CityHouse will provide long-term affordable housing and full wrap-around services to single mothers and their children experiencing homelessness in Palm Beach and Broward Counties.
1297.purpose: We envision a world where single mothers in need who are facing homelessness can be given the opportunity to learn how to competently provide a safe, healthy environment for their children. CityHouse is premised on the research that strengthening the family unit can prevent children from entering the child welfare system. While many local organizations provide care to families or children post foster-care placement, CityHouse offers a proactive response. We prevent it by providing front-end serv
1297.activities: CityHouse is a one-to-two-year program that offers safe and affordable housing, wrap-around services, daily mentoring, educational opportunities, mental health services, and skill-building opportunities. We focus on empowering our mothers to live healthier lives through education, community, and career development offering a holistic approach to each family's multifaceted needs. Our program is designed to instill life-changing skills, values, and character into the families we serve.
1297.direct_services: Affordable housing lays the foundation for mothers to gain steps towards autonomy and for children to achieve steps towards successful futures. Single-family apartments in a community setting are newly renovated, fully furnished, and stocked with necessities, such as toiletries. Residents are responsible for a small amount of rental expenses, equaling about 30 percent of a full-time, minimum wage
1297.population: Homeless mothers and children have extremely complex needs. Studies show a variety of factors that need to be addressed, including mental health, physical health, development, and safety. The "Homeless Children: America's New Outcasts" report indicates 92% of homeless mothers have experienced severe assaults (physical or sexual). Homeless mothers have an alarming rate of mental health and emotional problems, including depression. Homeless children are four times more likely to have developmental
1297.outcome: We utilize individual treatment plans and clinical evaluation tools to assess self-sufficiency, and each families’ readiness to sustain independence. Financial support is provided to help secure independent housing, and services are assessed and provided through the transition and stabilization process. We challenge our mothers to learn and become empowered to successfully live beyond their time at CityHouse. Due to our overarching goal to have long standing changes, we conduct follow-up evaluations with program graduates through the structure of our Alumni Care Program. The Alumni Care Program offers continued access to services and support over a five-year, step-down program to ensure grad

1514.description: The Town of Horseshoe Beach, Florida, suffered severe damage from Hurricane Helene, including the complete destruction of its Town Hall, the central facility for local government operations. Without this critical infrastructure, municipal functions such as administrative services, public meetings, and emergency coordination have been significantly disrupted, impacting both residents and town officials. This project seeks funding to rebuild the Town Hall including the post office to modern, hurricane-resilient standards.
1514.purpose: Securing necessary permits and regulatory approvals and construction of phase one of the new town hall facility. The new hurricane-resilient facility will house administrative offices, public meeting spaces, a protected post office, and emergency operations capabilities, ensuring the town government can function efficiently.
1514.activities: This is a fixed capital outlay project. All funds will be used for the construction of the new Town Hall facility which will provide the Town of Horseshoe Beach with government operations, a protected post office, emergency operations capabilities in the new location that would mitigate further risk.
1514.direct_services: The citizens of Horseshoe Beach will regain a functional Town Hall, a protected post office, a location for their water and utilities offices, enhance community engagement with a functional public meeting place, and improve disaster preparedness and response capabilities, ultimately benefiting all residents.
1514.population: All citizens and businesses of Horseshoe Beach and the surrounding zip code of the post office.
1514.outcome: This project will provide the Town of Horseshoe Beach with a storm-resilient Town Hall facility on a larger parcel of land outside of the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Areas to also include a post office. Please see the attached Opinion of Probable Cost for the methodology of this outcome.

1516.organization: Mt Pleasant Volunteer Fire Department, Inc
1516.description: This project is to purchase a new Type 6 Wildland Fire Apparatus to improve the capability of the Mount Pleasant Volunteer Fire Department to support our rural community and provide mutual aid to all surrounding fire departments and the Florida Forest Service for outdoor / wildland fire responses.
1516.purpose: Mt. Pleasant Volunteer Fire Department (Department) has an outdated Type 6 Wildland Fire Apparatus on loan from the Florida Forest Service to support our rural community and provide mutual aid to all surrounding fire departments. The Department seeks to add capability to provide our rural community with the needed equipment to combat outdoor and wildland type fires and other incidents, while being able to effectively provide mutual aid to our neighboring fire departments and the Florida Forest S
1516.activities: Providing fire and rescue services timely, efficiently, and adequately will have an improved impact on the level of protection provided to our residents and help our department maintain our ISO rating.
1516.direct_services: The direct purpose and goal is to provide improved Fire/Rescue Services to include Fire Suppression Operations, Medical Assists, Rescue Operations, Wildland Fire Responses within our rural community and Mutual Aid to all neighboring departments upon request.
1516.population: Gadsden County has approximately 50,000 residents. Our Department's first due ISO area covers approx. 65 Square Miles plus mutual aid areas. Our Department would provide services to the entire population of Gadsden County and areas we provide mutual aid to.
1516.outcome: Our Department believes Life & Property Protection is paramount and rapid response times are essential to rural areas of Gadsden County. Responding with the proper equipment is very important to be able to efficiently manage incidents. Monitoring of response times and community reactions based on event size by Department senior staff and information from the National Emergency Response Information System (NERIS).

2880.description: Baby CAT is an intensive familiy services program operating using a teaming model similar to CAT. Baby CAT is specifcally to prevent young and very young children 0-5 years of age from entering the child welfare system due to child abuse or neglect due to the substance misuse and mental health of the care giver(s) and to increase the children 0-5 stability and safety at home and community. Baby CAT teams are multi-disciplinary clinical teams that provide intensive in home and in community treatment to families with kids ages 0-5, who are at risk of out-of-home placement because of a substance misuse disorder or co-occuring mental health and SUD.
2880.purpose: To prevent young and very young children from being removed from their parent/caretaker due to abuse or negelct due to SUD or mental illness. Further to prevent injury or death to a children at the hands of the parent/caretaker due to abuse, neglect due to SUD or mental illness.
2880.activities: Intensive in-home services parenting skills training to address the protective capacity of the caregiver, in-home treatment to reduce or eliminate substance misuse, in home treatment to address untreated mental illness, past trauma's, and domestic violence. The top three reasons children are being abused or neglected and entering out of home care.
2880.direct_services: Intensive in-home counseling, case management to address SUD and or mental illenss of the care taker/parent. Parenting classes using Nurturing parenting an evidenced based practice, ensuring that young and very young children needs are met and they are connected to an early learning center daily.
2880.population: Families with a primary caretaker who has come to the attention of the child welfare system due to SUD and or mental health conditions and the abuse or neglect of a young or very young child 0-5- years of age. 50 families 100 individuals
2880.outcome: No future abuse, negelct or maltreatment of the children served in the program. FSFN will be used to verify that no new abuse or negelct of the children has been reported.

1222.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1222.description: The Mitzvah Kitchen operates the only community-run, industrial kosher kitchen in the greater Miami-Dade area. Volunteers and adults with disabilities prepare and distribute meals to individuals and families—both Jewish and non- Jewish—experiencing food insecurity or requiring kosher meals. The program also provides adults with special needs valuable training and certifications to support workforce entry. Demand for kosher food continues to grow across Miami, reflecting both adherence to Jewish tradition and an increased emphasis on food safety and community security.
1222.purpose: The Mitzvah Kitchen program provides individuals with special needs hands-on culinary training focused on kosher meal preparation, equipping them with practical skills, certifications, and workforce readiness. The program also promotes personal growth, community engagement, and long-term independence while fostering inclusivity within the local business community and building partnerships with organizations addressing food insecurity and the growing need for kosher meal access in Miami-Dade.
1222.activities: The Mitzvah Kitchen provides the only community-run, industrial kosher kitchen in Miami Dade area that engages individuals with special needs and volunteers from various businesses who prepare and distribute restaurant-quality meals to individuals and families (Jewish and non-Jewish) experiencing food insecurity as it relates to kosher restrictions.
1222.direct_services: The Mitzvah Kitchen provides citizens the opportunity to gain culinary experience through the only community-run, industrial kosher kitchen in Miami Dade area. Individuals with special needs will receive culinary certificates that will benefit them in job placement. Individuals and families (Jewish and non-Jewish) experiencing food insecurity as it relates to kosher restrictions will be provided m
1222.population: Elderly persons; persons with developmental and physical disabilities; persons with poor mental and physical health; persons who are economically disadvantaged, to include homeless, jobless; persons who are at-risk youth; persons who are high school and college/secondary level students.
1222.outcome: The program delivers valuable instruction for individuals with special needs, aimed at enhancing self-confidence, self- esteem, assisting with life-skills, and fostering financial independent by better preparing the individual to attain employment that fosters their economic self-sufficiency while serving those experiencing food insecurities. The program helps to establish stability and promotes improved mental health, enhancing culinary skills while encouraging cultural enrichment and promoting tolerance, inclusion, and diversity within the community for individuals with special needs. Outcomes will be assessed through data reports, behavioral observation by staff, feedback from participant

1520.description: The requested funds will bring Hamilton County Fire Rescue onto the SLERS network, replace outdated end-of-life equipment, and add two new 911 dispatch consoles. These enhancements will complete the county’s SLERS migration, expand dispatch capabilities, improve coverage, and deliver stronger regional interoperability with state and federal users. Collectively, they will create a resilient, fully integrated system that enables faster and more coordinated emergency response.
1520.purpose: Requested funding will connect Hamilton County Fire Rescue to the SLERS network, upgrade obsolete end-of-life equipment, and install two additional 911 dispatch consoles. These actions will complete the county’s transition to SLERS, increase dispatch capacity, enhance coverage, and improve interoperability across the region with state and federal partners. Together, these upgrades will build a robust, integrated system to ensure quicker, more coordinated emergency responses.
1520.activities: Services provided by the implementation of this project include enhanced, secure, reliable SLERS radio communication services to ensure first responders are able to quickly and accurately provide emergency response services to the county and to provide mutual aid to state and federal users.
1520.direct_services: Once completed, the upgraded systems will allow first responders in Hamilton County to provide accurate and timely response to requests for emergency services.
1520.population: The target populations that will benefit from this project are the residents of Hamilton County, local businesses, schools, and visiting tourists.
1520.outcome: The expected benefits provided by the implementation of this project include improved communication for fire, and emergency services with P25-compliant equipment, improving coverage and interoperability, and reduced response times. Outcomes will be measured by tracking response times and incident resolution.

1521.description: The requested funding will enable Liberty County Fire Rescue to operate on the same communication network as the Liberty County Sheriff's Office and 911 dispatch, fostering seamless coordination among all first responders. Upgrading Fire Rescue radio equipment to meet the requirements of the P25 compliant SLERS 2 system ensures compliance with statewide standards.
1521.purpose: Funds will be utilized to upgrade Liberty County’s Fire Rescue radio equipment to the P25-compliant SLERS Phase 2, ensuring statewide compliance and unifying communication for Fire, EMS, and the Sheriff’s Office. This enhances interoperability, improving coordination among local, state, and federal agencies for more effective response efforts. The upgrade also strengthens first responder safety and mutual aid support to neighboring areas.
1521.activities: Enhanced, secure, reliable Fire Rescue radio communication services to ensure first responders are able to quickly and accurately provide emergency response services to the county and to provide mutual aid to surrounding areas.
1521.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens are the improvement of communications for Fire Rescue providing greater interoperability and safety for first responders, as well as reducing emergency response times, injuries, fatalities, and property damage.
1521.population: The target population for this project are the citizens and visitors of Liberty County that would benefit from the improvement in Fire Rescue communications and increased efficiency between agencies that provide emergency response at the local level.
1521.outcome: The expected benefits of this project include improvements to public physical health through faster response times to emergencies, and an improvement of communication between local law enforcement and state agencies. Outcomes will be measured by tracking response times, and incident resolution.

1211.description: "Six Who Fought for Florida" presents our military heritage. 1. Bernardo de Galvez Revolutionary Founding Father was the Governor of Cuba who raised an army to defeat the British at Pensacola. 2. Marjory Stoneman Douglas, in World War One was a Navy volunteer stationed at Key West. Later she wrote River of Grass. 3. Chappie James, Floridian first African-American 4-Star Air Force General was in the Tuskegee Airmen, then fought in Vietnam. Under consideration for Lt. Governor when illness took him. 4.Lt. Sandy Nininger of Ft. Lauderdale, the very first World War II Medal of Honor recipient, for bravery in combat died fighting in the Philippines. 5.Madeleine Coleman Roach, Coconut Grove, a WWII volunteer in the Women's Army Corps, the 6888 Unit who deployed overseas for our victory. The Movie "Six Triple Eight" shows their greatness.6. PFC Bruce Carter, Miami Springs, Vietnam Medal of Hono
1211.purpose: To educate and inspire the young people of Florida about the wonderful heritage we all share in common. The stories of the "Six Who Fought for Florida" resonate with everyone. These are true stories of Black, Hispanic, and Anglo heroes, male and female, who helped create and defend Florida and the United States as a whole.
1211.activities: Research and development, assembly and construction, presentation and promotion of these outstanding examples of the very best citizens Florida has to offer. Each of these heroes and heroines represent the best that we are in terms of courage, service, sacrifice, and long-lasting accomplishments.
1211.direct_services: Our citizens will be impacted directly by these presentations of real-life heroism by fellow Floridians. Nothing can provide Floridians with better examples for America's 250th Anniversary than the timelss stories of "Six who fought for Florida."

Likewise our schools, public and charter equally, will be served by these display exhibits. All will be free and open to the public, providing inspiration and education to be enjoyed by great numbers of Americans.

Bernardo de Galvez, 2. Marjory Stoneman Douglas, 3. Lt Sandy Nininger, 4. General Chappie James, 5. Madeleine Coleman Roach, and 6. PFC Bruce Wayne Carter.

3718.organization: Feed and Instruct the Hungry, Inc. d/b/a The
3718.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3718.description: Because No One Should Go Hungry is our purpose. Funding will support a new 25,000 sq. ft. facility, housing the newest model in food pantry service and provide holistic services. We now serve more than 26,500 families each year and the need is growing. Our capacity is limited only by space. We expect an annual increase of 10% per year. This new facility will improve functionality and become a hub for expanded access to our more than 35 community partners on-site and increased upskill that foster self-sufficiency and independence. We will have 14,500 sq. ft. pantry and warehouse space; 3,500 sq. ft. of case management and classroom space; 3,500 of administrative offices and volunteer space.
3718.purpose: This fund request will support the pre-construction efforts including the Design, planning and preparation activities for the ultimate construction of a 25,000 square foot food pantry facility; the capacity of which, when complete, will serve more than 50,000 families in South Lake County.
3718.activities: Grocery Store style pantry providing nutritious groceries on a weekly basis; Holistic Case Management to include guidance and referrals, progress monitoring; Educational classes i.e., Nutrition, Gardening, Financial Literacy, up-skills; job search & more; Healthcare referrals and on-site access to other community agencies and programs such as SNAP, Housing, Legal Aid, Dept of Health; Job search and more.
3718.direct_services: As a licensed food pantry, we are dedicated to improving food security and overall health through a holistic, client- centered approach. Our Programs include: Family Stability Program focuses on self-sufficiency; Food Pantry-nutritious groceries; School Break Food; Nutrition Classes; Gardening Classes: Financial Literacy: SNAP benefits assistance: Legal Aid workshops: Healthcare referrals; more th

In 2025, this equates to an annual income of up to $64,300 for a family of four.In South Lake County, nearly 68% of the population falls within this income bracket: • 11% live below the federal poverty level • 57% fall within the 100–200% range, a group defined by United Way as A.L.I.C.E. (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed)—those who earn too much to qualify for government assistance, yet too little to meet basic needs without help

Pre/post client surveys capturing changes in client status as it relates to the above criteria. 3.Follow up Case Management interviews and client consistency of participation in programming

1925.organization: Second Harvest Food Bank of Central Florida,
1925.description: Second Harvest Food Bank of Central Florida’s School Partnerships program works with local schools across seven counties to provide nutritious food to children and families experiencing food insecurity. Through onsite school pantries and fresh markets, students and families receive fresh produce, healthy snacks, and shelf-pantry staples during the academic year. The program leverages school infrastructure to improve food security and support the health, wellbeing, and academic success of students. Additionally, schools with onsite pantries provide students the opportunity to manage the market, gaining hands-on experience in inventory management, budgeting, and building other workforce readiness skills. This project strengthens household stability, supports local agriculture, and promotes long-term community resilience by ensuring that children and families have reliable access to nutriti
1925.purpose: The funds will expand and strengthen Second Harvest Food Bank’s School Partnerships program, providing nutritious food to more children and families experiencing food insecurity in Central Florida. By leveraging partnerships with local schools, the program improves access to healthy food during the academic year, supporting household stability and fostering the development of essential workforce readiness skills for students.
1925.activities: Second Harvest’s School Partnerships program works with schools across 7 counties to ensure children and families have access to nutritious food during the academic year via onsite pantries. Second Harvest provides onboard training for school staff and enhances site capacity through essential supplies, materials, and equipment such as shelving, carts, and signage.
1925.direct_services: Second Harvest will provide direct distribution of nutritious food resources including snacks, shelf-stable pantry essentials, and fresh produce during the academic year. At schools with onsite pantries, students gain hands-on experience in managing food distribution while building essential life and workforce skills such as budgeting and communication.
1925.population: The project serves children and families experiencing economic hardship across Central Florida. Second Harvest anticipates reaching approximately 150,000 students through ongoing distributions during the academic year, with many individuals potentially being served more than once as part of ensuring continued access to nutritious food.
1925.outcome: The project will improve family and community wellbeing by increasing access to nutritious food, strengthening physical health and mental wellbeing, and reducing hunger-related barriers to education and self-sufficiency. Additionally, the program supports local agriculture, improved student engagement and attendance, and greater household stability which contributes to our community’s long-term prosperity. Outcomes will be measured through a combination of quantitative metrics tracked such as total pounds of food distributed, number of households served, number of student interactions, and number of schools reached and pre-/post-surveys to assess awareness of food security and changes in wel

3297.description: he STEMCAT Fieldhouse is a 20,000 sq. ft. workforce hub built to close the gap where 58% of jobs in Southwest Florida are non-degree technical roles. It will prepare the 32% of high school graduates and GED earners through micro and digital certifications leading to apprenticeships in healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, and technical fields. Featuring 20 vocational labs, the Fieldhouse will fill critical workforce needs retain talent, attract business, and serve as a hurricane- rated shelter.
3297.purpose: Construction funding of a 20,000 sq ft, multi-use STEMCAT Field House in Fort Myers, FL. We believe the Field House is a bold, transformative, and practical solution providing more than 20 vocational labs and training spaces in aviation, welding, robotics, agriculture, digital media, and healthcare technology. The intent is to create a resilient community hub that fills critical workforce gaps in high-demand industries while also serving as a shelter-in-place resource during natural disasters.
3297.activities: e STEMCAT Fieldhouse will house 20 labs in welding, robotics, aviation/drones, AI, renewable energy, healthcare tech, and certification programs, plus 5 telehealth suites for training. Funds will cover site prep, resilient construction, and equipment, creating a career pipeline and hurricane-rated safe haven for youth, families, and vulnerable residents.
3297.direct_services: In addition to the above financial aid assistance, job placement, academic support, and social services.
3297.population: skilled trades, healthcare technology, and emerging STEM fields. Participants will earn tiered certifications that allow them to enter the workforce quickly while continuing to advance their knowledge for higher-wage opportunities. The project is expected to serve over 500 individuals annually through more than 55 cohort-based training groups.
3297.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is that program completers will earn industry-recognized credentials that lead directly to employment in high-demand skilled trades, healthcare technology, and STEM-related fields. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of completers who secure employment in their credentialed field within three months of program completion, as well as comparing participants’ income levels before enrollment and after credential attainment.

3256.description: This is the final year of a three-year project to increase public safety coverage for the SLERS radio system in Hendry and southern Glades Counties. The shift in population and business to eastern Hendry County has resulted in a significant increase in the number of calls for services by public safety personnel. Engineering was completed in year one with the construction of the tower site in year two. The final phase (Phase 3) will provide all electronics and connectivity to the SLERS network.
3256.purpose: Improved communications for law enforcement and first responders in Hendry County and southern Glades County. Public safety communications were analyzed for Hendry and the adjacent counties by radio frequency engineers. The studies show significant coverage gaps in areas of growth and development in Hendry County.
3256.activities: Providing public safety communications to law enforcement, rescue, and fire personnel in areas of the county which currently do not have in building radio coverage.
3256.direct_services: Provide critical response services to assure protection of life and property of Hendry County residents and businesses.
3256.population: All residents, businesses, and visitors of Hendry County and southern portion of Glades County, including Moore Haven.
3256.outcome: Improved radio communications that can be measured by engineers and users.

1370.description: In 2025, the City of Sanibel completed its Surface Water Management Master Plan Update (stormwater). Based on the plan’s findings, two key improvements are recommended to mitigate saltwater intrusion during high tides: Modifying the existing flap gate at the Beach Road Weir, and Installing a new flap gate at the Tarpon Bay Weir. These improvements are essential to prevent the backflow of saltwater into Sanibel’s freshwater interior and to reduce the risk of storm surge and tidal flooding on private properties. The City has included $130,000 in its FY26 budget to design the flap gates at both weirs. The total estimated cost for fabrication and installation is $600,000. Sanibel is requesting a state appropriation of $600,000 to fully fund implementation once design is complete.
1370.purpose: Sanibel is requesting a state appropriation of $600,000 to fully fund implementation once design is complete. The City has included $130,000 in its FY26 budget to design the flap gates at the Beach Rd. Weir, and the Tarpon Bay Weir. This investment is critical to protecting developed property and the island’s sensitive freshwater wetland ecosystems in both the east and west drainage basins from salt water intrusion related to storm surge and high tide flooding.
1370.activities: State funds will be used to fabricate and install the flap gate for the Tarpon Bay Weir and fabricate and install a modified flap gate at the Beach Rd. Weir.
1370.direct_services: This project, if funded, serves to protect Sanibel's property values and local economy by mitigating the threat of saltwater flooding of developed property and the island’s sensitive freshwater wetland ecosystems in both the east and west drainage basins due to storm surge and high tide flooding.
1370.population: The general public will be served by the project. Approximately 2,000 structures will be served by this project.
1370.outcome: Protect economic losses from property damage, and preserve freshwater wetlands and wildlife habitat by mitigating impact from saltwater flooding. Outcome will be measured by the reduced frequency of property flooding from saltwater storm surge or high tide flooding.

The project will increase access for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) ages 18 and older, enhance vocational readiness, and improve social-emotional and independent-living outcomes. This expansion will double dail

1632.outcome: Completion of ADA-compliant renovation and facility expansion by December 2026. 50% increase in daily capacity (from 50 to 75+ participants). 80% of program participants achieve measurable progress on at least one independent-living or employment-related goal within six months. 90% caregiver satisfaction rating. Creation of at least 10 new community-based jobs (instructors, direct support, and program specialists).

1371.description: This funding will support the rebuilding of the Woman’s Club Clubhouse and Community Building, which was destroyed by Hurricane Ian. In the aftermath of the storm, fundraising efforts provided over $730,000 in direct assistance to residents. The Woman's Club remains dedicated to the mission of supporting nonprofit and charitable organizations throughout the Greater Fort Myers Beach area. Since Ian, the club has contributed more than $300,000 to local nonprofits and infused over $190,000 into the local economy.
1371.purpose: The rebuilding of the Woman’s Club Clubhouse and Community Building will restore a vital hub for local residents, nonprofits, and visitors. The Clubhouse will be available for local nonprofits to host events, meetings, and outreach programs, ensuring continued support for those in need. 1371.outcome: The Club will play a crucial role in boosting local economic activity by continuing to host and expand community-driven events that attract residents and visitors. 1733.description: The Department of Corrections (FDC) will provide a broad array of valuable, connected services that help FDC employees, their spouses, and their children (the “FDC Family") reach their educational goals and obtain career development growth. These offerings will help attract and retain employees in a competitive market, and provide opportunities for career enhancement within or even outside the Department. The offering includes: - One-on-One coaching for SOCE exam test preparation for FDC recruits, higher education academic advising & career advancement coaching for FDC employees and their immediate families. - Custom test preparation for the state-wide corrections examination, General Educational Development (GED) test preparation for employees and dependents, General Test Preparation for State Scholarship qualification and higher education access. - Learn-to-Learn webinars for all conti
1733.purpose: FDC has enduring challenges related to employee recruitment and retention. Of the FDC's ~24,000 employees, ~17,000 are correctional officers yet over 5,000 vacancies still exist statewide, with 23,375 positions overall. The vacancy rate of just over 25% is an improvement over November 2021's 38.5%. But gaps still exist despite recent reforms in what can often be a dangerous and undesirable place to work. Employees are leaving for higher paying jobs and FDC is limited in its ability to compete.
1733.activities: FDC will offer coaching and advising services at no out of pocket costs to FDC Employees and their family members. Through one-on-one sessions, coaches will help FDC Employees and their immediate family members define their education and career goals. Webinars will be provided to recruits to help drive success in the Academy. Exam preparation and coaching will be provided for the SOCE exam. The offering extends to those who wish to pursue higher education. In addition, coaches will help with ret
1733.direct_services: FDC will offer coaching and advising services at no out of pocket costs to FDC Employees and their family members. Through one-on-one sessions, coaches will help FDC Employees and their immediate family members define their education and career goals. Webinars will be provided to recruits to help drive success in the Academy. Exam preparation and coaching will be provided for the SOCE exam. The of
1733.population: Florida Department of Corrections 24,000 employees and their immediate families.
1733.outcome: The expected benefit or outcomes of this project are: 1) Increase the number of recruits becoming corrections officers by increasing SOCE pass rates and supporting Academy retention and graduation rates 2) Increase overall employee retention The measures that will be used are: 1) Utilization of services provided by Kaplan such as coaching, SOCE prep, employee webinars 2) Academy graduation rates, recycle rates, and timelines 3) Employee retention rates

2590.description: This facility is a joint initiative between UCF and Daytona State College. It will house UCF's Institute for Risk Management & Insurance Education and programs in business, nursing, entrepreneurship, and continuing education/professional development, directly addressing workforce needs in the region. The HUB will provide degrees, stackable credentials, executive education, and hands-on learning opportunities with industry collaboration.
2590.purpose: This facility is a joint initiative between UCF and Daytona State College. It will house programs in business, nursing, risk management & insurance, entrepreneurship, and continuing education/professional development, directly addressing workforce needs in the region. The HUB will provide stackable credentials, executive education, and hands-on learning opportunities with industry collaboration.
2590.activities: Teaching and research activities; industry innovation space to facilitate collaboration between businesses, researchers, and students and to drive applied and translational research in advanced manufacturing, healthcare, and entrepreneurship; modern office and co-working spaces to support start-ups and workforce training.
2590.direct_services: Teaching, research and professional development programs and activities; industry innovation space to facilitate collaboration between businesses, researchers, and students and to drive applied and translational research in advanced manufacturing, healthcare, and entrepreneurship; modern office and co-working spaces to support start-ups and workforce training.
2590.population: University and college students, faculty, industry leaders and workforce members; business startups & industries in the region in partnership with UCF and employing UCF graduates,
2590.outcome: Increasing classroom and lab availability; facilities to foster engagement in productive industry partnerships; co- locating academic programs, industry innovation and entrepreneurship resources to enhance the pipeline of talent for high demand careers; increasing enrollment and graduates in key industries present and growing in the regions being served; graduates in the fields being served by this facility are in high demand and will be immediately employed by Florida employers.

1527.description: Crossroad Academy, a Blue Ribbon K–12 charter school since 1998, seeks funds to build its first on-campus playground. Currently, students must cross the street to play, creating safety concerns. The Learning in Motion Project will provide a safe, accessible space promoting fitness, wellness, and balanced learning for 570 students and over 800 people. This is a non-recurring request that supports student health and community engagement in the Gadsden County community.
1527.purpose: At least 85% of students will demonstrate increased engagement, focus, and participation in classroom activities as a result of structured “learning in motion” breaks on the playground, measured through teacher observations, academic participation logs, surveys and student grades.
