1251.description: The requested funds will support Sarasota’s Juvenile Delinquency Citation programs growth, providing early intervention and prevention services that divert youth from formal prosecution. Expansion will increase capacity for restorative sanctions, case management, and family engagement. With a documented 90% success rate in reducing recidivism, this investment ensures taxpayer savings, stronger public safety, and second chances for youth.
1251.purpose: The requested funds will support Sarasota’s Juvenile Delinquency Citation programs growth, providing early intervention and prevention services that divert youth from formal prosecution. Expansion will increase capacity for restorative sanctions, case management, and family engagement. With a documented 90% success rate in reducing recidivism, this investment ensures taxpayer savings, stronger public safety, and second chances for youth.
1251.activities: Funds will support prevention programs in schools, expansion of delinquency citation services, youth leadership training, expanded court sessions, and volunteer coordination. Services include early intervention, mentoring, case management, technology upgrades, and evaluation to strengthen youth outcomes and community engagement across Sarasota County.
1251.direct_services: Funding will provide direct services including youth diversion and intervention, school-based prevention programs, parent workshops, leadership training, mentoring, and volunteer coordination. These services support positive youth development, reduce recidivism, and strengthen families across Sarasota County.
1251.population: Teen Court of Sarasota serves at-risk and high-risk youth referred by schools, families, law enforcement, or through a Juvenile Delinquency Citation. The program supports youth ages 8 to 18, providing early intervention and accountability services. In 2026, Teen Court anticipates serving more than 900 students and their families.
1251.outcome: The expected outcome is reduced youth recidivism through quality early intervention and prevention services. By addressing issues before they escalate, Teen Court helps youth avoid future involvement or incarceration. Success is measured by completion rates, pre/post surveys, and a 90% non-re-offense rate after program completion.

1306.description: Build and operate a Solid Waste Transfer Station in order to manage the City of North Port's solid waste more safely and efficiently. Land for the Station has been obtained. Design and engineering is underway. The Station will support ongoing efficient solid waste collection, more beneficial disposal options, and the ability to accommodate population growth. The station reduces the number of trips to the landfill, saving fuel, staff time, and vehicle wear and tear.
1306.purpose: More efficient solid waste collection and disposal providing significant cost savings to the City.
1306.activities: Once the Transfer Station is constructed, it will support ongoing efficient solid waste collection, more beneficial disposal options, and the ability to accommodate population growth. It will strengthen the City's resilience by creating a local facility that lessens dependence on distant landfills and improves service reliability during disruptions.
1306.direct_services: More efficient solid waste collection and disposal.
1306.population: This project will benefit the entire City (approximately 95,000 citizens).
1306.outcome: The Station will reduce the number of tips to the landfill, saving fuel, staff time, and vehicle wear and tear. The estimated cost savings over a five-year period is approximately $13,050,100. The methodology examine the total Tonnage of waste removed and then the cost savings to City and thus to the Citizenry.

1252.description: The City of North Port has committed over $13.8 million to build a new, state of the art Emergency Operations Center (EOC). The requested funds will be used to provide the furnishings, fixtures, and equipment (FFE) necessary to fully outfit the EOC, the final funding necessary to complete this project. The City of North Port is one of the fastest-growing communities in Florida and faces a range of natural hazards, including flooding, hurricanes, and wildfires. A fully functional EOC is essential to coordinating emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation operations that protect lives and property.
1252.purpose: Outfitting the Emergency Operations Center (EOC) with furnishings, fixtures, and equipment will ensure the facility is fully functional, resilient, and capable of supporting coordinated emergency management operations. The goal is to create an environment that enables efficient communication, decision-making, and resource coordination during disaster response and recovery activities. This will enhance operational readiness, improve situational awareness and coordination, and support continuity o
1252.activities: Outfitting the EOC with furniture, fixtures, and equipment will support a fully staffed emergency response during times of disaster. Having current equipment for use during emergencies is imperative in continuity of operations. Community outreach and education will be provided during blue skies, as well as collaboration with internal and external partners including North Port's Community Emergency Response Teams (CERTs).
1252.direct_services: The Situation Room, Emergency Call Center, Joint Information Center, and Backup Data Center will be located in this building. During times of emergency, citizens will receive emergency management and support services. During non- emergency times, Emergency Management will provide community outreach and preparedness services available to the citizens.
1252.population: This project does not have a specific target population as all citizens would benefit. Current population estimated to be served is 94,600.
1252.outcome: 1. Benefit: Faster response times due to coordinated resource deployment. Measure: reduced response times. 2. Benefit: Resource prioritization for most critical need. Measure: reduced request and resolution times. 3. Benefit: Continuity of operations for essential government and critical infrastructure during times of crisis. Measure: reduced resolution times for restoration of essential services.

1936.description: The Veterans Housing Initiative seeks to help veterans and their families find the housing assistance they need, whether that means a chance at home ownership or help with home repairs and accessibility modifications. Through the Veterans Housing Initiative, we are also able to provide our community’s veterans with access and referrals to additional wrap- around services like food security, health and wellness resources, and financial counseling. We successfully launched our Veterans Housing initiative with the completion of a 14-unit pocket neighborhood, The Umatilla Veterans Village, in 2018. Since then, our program has grown to include new construction, preservation, and critical home repairs for veterans throughout Lake and Sumter counties.
1936.purpose: Through Veteran’s Housing Initiative (VHI) we will serve 8-11 veterans in Lake/Sumter with critical home repairs, accessibility improvements, and homeownership opportunities through new construction. Many veterans live in aging homes that pose health and safety risks. Through our housing interventions we will offer safe, stable housing allowing Veterans to thrive with physical and mental well-being, economic security, and long-term quality of life.
1936.activities: Habitat will be the project manager/builder for all repairs and new builds to administer the scope of work as identified for each Veteran. Our staff will take a trauma informed approach to ensure trust is built with the veteran, allowing us to offer holistic care beyond just housing. Homeowners will participate in "sweat equity" or volunteerism in a way that fits their capability and schedule.
1936.direct_services: Access to critical home repair services offered to low-income veterans at no cost to them. Access to homeownership that comes with an affordable mortgage. Habitat will offer free access to educational courses during the program such as credit, budgeting, and home maintenance for future success.
1936.population: Veteran’s Housing Initiative (VHI) will serve 8-11 veterans in Lake/Sumter. Our target income population is 50% AMI, but we will consider veteran applications up to 120% AMI. The homeowners with lower income will be prioritized to be served first. Historically, 75% of our repair households served were at or below 50% AMI. Those seeking to become homeowners will hold an income range of 40%-80% AMI.
1936.outcome: Access to safe, accessible, and affordable housing for veterans. VHI will reduce physical hazards due to unsafe or overcrowded housing conditions, reduce stress, and will increase financial stability and flexibility. Pre and post surveys will be used to monitor outcomes. There is also an economic benefit to our work. A 2022 economic impact analysis conducted on our affiliate operations indicated $1.52 was injected into the local economy for every dollar we invested into the community. Thus the $465,000 invested into the VHI program for FY26-27 will produce $706,800 in economic activity. We used IMPLAN, an analysis software to model this.

1844.description: The requested funds will be used to install backflow prevention devices at key locations throughout the city to ensure tailwaters do not enter residential areas. These critical upgrades will provide lasting financial and environmental benefits by reducing flood risk, safeguarding property, and enhancing environmental quality for the city's residents and the State of Florida. The funding will be matched dollar-for-dollar by the city.
1844.purpose: The requested funds will be used to install backflow prevention devices throughout the City’s stormwater system to prevent tailwaters from entering neighborhoods. This project will reduce flooding, protect property, and enhance the resilience of critical infrastructure, ensuring safer and healthier living conditions for residents.
1844.activities: Activities will include identifying priority installation sites, procuring and installing backflow prevention devices, conducting excavation and construction work, restoring disturbed areas, and ensuring system integration with existing stormwater infrastructure. Services provided will include enhanced flood prevention and improved stormwater management citywide.
1844.direct_services: Residents will directly benefit from reduced neighborhood flooding, protection of homes and businesses from stormwater intrusion, improved road and property access during heavy rainfall events, and decreased health and safety risks related to standing water.
1844.population: The project will serve all residents and businesses within the City of South Daytona, particularly those in low-lying areas most vulnerable to stormwater backflow. Approximately 13,000 residents, along with hundreds of businesses and community facilities, are expected to benefit from the improved stormwater protections provided by this project.
1844.outcome: The project will significantly reduce neighborhood flooding by preventing stormwater tailwaters from backing into residential areas. Expected outcomes include improved public safety, protection of private and public property, enhanced reliability of the stormwater system, and greater community resilience to heavy rainfall events. In addition, the project will deliver long-term financial benefits by reducing flood damage costs, emergency response needs, and infrastructure repair expenses.

Each month, youth meet with a volunteer mentor at their job site, where they experience first-hand the world of work from the perspective of, and with encouragement from, someone who is already employed by our respective partner. Workplace partners facilitate workshops on topics, such as work-readiness, preparing for post- secondary education and/or employment, resume writing, business etiquette, and interview skills. BBBS staff provides support to workplace partners regarding the youth and mentoring strategies. Our mentoring services provide experiences that assist youth to immediately enter the workforce.
1738.purpose: The School-to-Work program goal is to ensure that students improve their chances of graduating and transitioning to the workplace. This allows them to meet with and shadow volunteer employee mentors at our workplace partners offices, sites, etc. each month during the school year. This exposure to the workplace and encouragement from volunteer mentors makes a world of difference as students improve their grades, gain in self-esteem, and graduate high school with plans for a career. The immediate
1738.activities: Our corporate partners open doors of hope and opportunity for students by welcoming them into the workplace to meet and shadow volunteer employee mentors each month during the school year. This firsthand exposure to professional environments—combined with the guidance and encouragement of caring mentors—makes a lasting difference. Students improve their grades, build self-confidence, and graduate high school prepared for success in college, careers, and life.
1738.direct_services: Facilitated through our statewide BBBS local agencies, BBBSAF will match approximately six hundred (600) students, identified as at-risk youth, with mentors who are employed in corporate workplace partners of Big Brothers Big Sisters local agencies. Each month, youth in STW meet with and shadow a volunteer mentor at his or her job, where youth experience first-hand the world of work from the persp

Unfortunately, this skills gap affects some of the state’s most vulnerable youth disproportionately: rates of college attendance, unemployment and underemployment tend to be higher for at risk and/or low-income youth. Big Brothers Big Sisters local agencies identify at-risk youth for participation in the STW program. Students and mentors are encouraged to commit to th
1738.outcome: In addition to the benefits of youth having a caring adult mentor who is a successful role model, the STW program offers opportunities for youth to learn valuable career skills. In the corporate environment, youth shadow the work of their mentor, and other workers, to provide an opportunity to be exposed to various types of jobs/careers. 1937.description: This project is designed to provide hands-on education in valuable technical skills – ultimately leading to an opportunity for gainful employment, while engaging students in the social aspect of building affordable housing and bettering their community one project at a time. The Youth Construction Academy (YCA) is a partnership with Eustis High, Leesburg High, South Lake High, Wildwood High, and Villages Charter High. Students will visit our home build sites scattered throughout Lake and Sumter counties 3-4 days a week as their class time throughout the school year, building a home from slab to CO. Collectively they will build 6 homes for qualified low-income families, providing homeownership opportunities to those that would otherwise not have access to purchase their own home. Families within the program participate in sweat equity and education during their time with Habitat.
1937.purpose: This project will increase affordable housing and workforce training through an education collaborative with Eustis High, Leesburg High, South Lake High, Wildwood Middle High, and Villages Charter. Students will build 6 homes, with state funds invested in hard cost of construction. Following our “sweat equity” model, home buyers will be fully engaged in their build through volunteerism as well as education. Each home will be sold to local low-income resident with an affordable mortgage, providin
1937.activities: Habitat will be the developer/builder, managing construction and educational oversight. Students will build homes, gaining experience from slab to CO, while producing an output of affordable housing. Home buyers will be income qualified and perform sweat equity, including educational courses such as budgeting, understanding credit, home maintenance, and estate planning. Students will gain technical and soft skills, ready to enter workforce.
1937.direct_services: Availability of 6 affordable housing units for qualified low-income home buyers to purchase. In addition, students will gain construction skills while building homes. Projects are located on infill lots or within pocket neighborhoods that are being developed within existing neighborhoods. These new units will uplift the existing neighborhood, eliminate current dumping/blight on vacant lots.
1937.population: Residents of Lake or Sumter County who have a household income at or below 80% of the Area Median Income. We anticipate these homes to serve approximately 20 individuals in the first generation of each home. In addition, 75-100 high school students will be served through the educational element across all five schools.
1937.outcome: 1) New Homebuyers: Studies show, positive outcomes of homeownership include increased graduation rates, better childhood health, and ability to build wealth. Decrease in children's behavioral problems and the need for government assistance. https://www.habitatbuilds.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Benefits-of-Homeownership-Research- Summary.pdf 2) Students: We expect increased skills based knowledge and will monitor this through pre and post surveys. We also anticipate deeper engagement in the curriculum and the ability to graduate ready to enter the workforce. We will request the ability to do a follow up with each student within the first 5 years of graduation to find out what they ended up

1283.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1283.description: The project involves demolishing the antiquated Brevard County animal shelter and constructing a new, state-of-the-art facility to address current and future animal care and welfare needs. The existing shelter is outdated, lacks sufficient space, is an open air design and does not meet modern animal care capabilities. The new facility will be a climate- controlled, sound-dampening environment built for current and future needs, immediately adjacent to the recently constructed and opened Animal Surgery Center.
1283.purpose: The primary goal of the new Animal Care Center is to provide a safe, temporary refuge for lost, abandoned, and mistreated animals while actively working to reunite them with their owners or find them permanent, loving homes. This mission extends beyond mere housing. Core objectives include animal medical care, welfare, relieving overcrowded accommodations, public safety and health, reunification and homing services, facilitating adoptions and rescues, enforcing animal control laws, and educating
1283.activities: Funds will provide for construction of a modern Animal Care Center that offers significant improvements in animal welfare, operational efficiencies, staff morale, and community engagement. The facility will deliver a modern infrastructure (zoned HVAC and LED lighting), improved safety, better housing of animals, reduced animal stress, expanded programs, and a welcoming environment to the public.
1283.direct_services: This new Animal Care Center will provide citizens with services focusing on animal control and public safety, animal welfare and care, and community outreach and education programs. These services include stray animal management, lost & found support, animal cruelty response, shelter and veterinarian care, spay & neuter education, adoption and foster programs, and volunteer opportunities.
1283.population: This new Animal Care Center will serve all residents of Brevard County and their animals in need.
1283.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of constructing a new, modern Animal Care Center in Brevard County are centered on significantly improving animal welfare, increasing operational efficiencies, and enhancing community engagement. The key benefits of this facility will be improved animal health and well-being, streamlined operational efficiencies, stronger community involvement and volunteerism, and expanded services and educational opportunities. The best measure of success will be the success rate of adoptions and an increase of employee morale and volunteers.

1412.description: The goal is to reduce flooding and protect properties on SW 117 Avenue from SW 114 Place to SW 114 Court by installing 650 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 19 drainage inlets. The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance.
1412.purpose: Reduction of flooding and protection of properties on SW 117 Avenue from SW 114 Place to SW 114 Court by installing 650 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 19 drainage inlets. The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance.
1412.activities: Installation of 650 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 19 drainage inlets.
1412.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
1412.outcome: Mitigate flooding by improving the stormwater drainage infrastructure—measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

3670.description: Full roadway reconstruction. Removal of current asphalt and road base. New sub-base with new pipeline infrastructure (water, storm water, reclaim) and electrical conduit for street lighting. Sidewalks and drainage will be installed with F type curbs, and streetlights will be installed at the end of this project.
3670.purpose: Full roadway reconstruction. Removal of current asphalt and road base. New sub-base with new pipeline infrastructure (water, storm water, reclaim) and electrical conduit for street lighting. Sidewalks and drainage will be installed with F type curbs, and streetlights will be installed at the end of this project.
3670.activities: The reconstructed road will provide a widened roadway and new asphalt, where there is beginning alligator cracks; sidewalks will be implemented. A professional engineer will inspect the roadway regularly and pedestrian counts will be measured frequently.
3670.direct_services: The road will have greater stormwater infrastructure, which will reduce the likelihood of flooding during storms. Inspections prior to the project measuring levels of flooding and puddling, then compared with data collected after the installation.
3670.outcome: Sidewalks are to be replaced in this project. Social media surveys post-project in include questions such as "how often were you walking in the neighborhood prior to this project" and "how often are you walking in the neighborhood post- project?"

1624.description: Improving senior's access to healthcare, health and wellness activities, individual and group counseling, nutrition, recreation and socialization by offering additional transportation during the week and weekends. Providing daily breakfast and a weekend take away meal to improve senior's overall physical health outcomes through nutrition.
1624.purpose: Funding will grant seniors increased access to medical care, socialization, congregate meal sites, and local outings by offering extended transportation options during the week and weekends. Senior's overall health outcomes will improve by providing a balanced daily breakfast and a weekend take away meal.
1624.activities: Transportation services to Congregate meals sites, to and from medical appointments (including dialysis appointments), prescription drug pickup/delivery, shopping, and community outings. Daily breakfast and a weekend take away meal will be provided in addition to health and wellness activities, individual and group counseling, nutrition education, recreation and socialization.
1624.direct_services: Transportation to access healthcare, health and wellness, individual and group counseling, nutrition, recreation and socialization. Daily breakfast and a weekend take away meal will be provided.
1624.population: Low-income, frail elders 60 years of age and older, persons with poor physical and mental health, and developmentally and physically disabled persons. Expect to serve 95 individuals daily, Monday through Friday (250 days/year) and 95 take away meals per week for 52 weeks.
1624.outcome: Expected benefits/outcomes include, but is not limited to, improved balance, strength, flexibility, mood, nutrition, access to healthcare, education and life enrichment through opportunities to socialize with peer group. Outcomes will be measured utilizing self-report surveys. Additionally, data regarding improvements in health, e.g., blood pressure, pain management will be compiled and tracked to assess improvement and/or need to modify plan. The actual number of passengers and trips will measure transportation outcomes.

1263.description: The Brain Bus: A Mobile Brain Health Initiative is able to educate the general population in Florida about Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. By focusing on community education of healthy habits and early detection, we are potentially able to reduce burden, improve health outcomes, and promote health and well-being among community members. The Brain Bus is focused on serving all communities statewide.
1263.purpose: The primary goal of the Brain Bus: A Mobile Brain Health Initiative is to educate all Floridians about how to reduce their risk of developing Alzheimer's and other dementias. We also provide outreach to support to individuals who need resources. Additionally, this is a proven program that completed 351 stops in FY24 and served over 20,000 people.
1263.activities: We will accomplish 400 stops with these funds. We will inform individuals about a variety of educational topics including risk reduction, early warning signs, the benefits of early detection, local resources, research and information about diagnostic centers.
1263.direct_services: The Brain Bus: A Mobile Brain Health Initiative will provide in-person "stops" and limited virtual "stops". The stops are primarily completed by Brain Bus drivers by utilizing the RV & van; however, if multiple events occur throughout the state at the same time, other Association staff such as Program Managers, will be utilized to ensure that needs are being met and all communities are served.
1263.population: The target population is Floridians 18 and older. The services of the Brain Bus are open to all Floridan's who need services, and always free of charge. Over the course of one year, 400 stops will be made across the State of Florida providing information and services to thousands of Floridians.
1263.outcome: Visitors will gain knowledge about the importance of brain health, the warning signs of Alzheimer's and the benefits of an early diagnosis. Visitors will also gain knowledge about local resources and Alzheimer's Association provided services. Individuals who visit the program will receive rack cards and have the ability to speak with knowledgeable Association team members.

1582.description: The project involves of enhancing stormwater management practices in the project area by implementing engineering strategies to mitigate flooding in the public right-of-way, thereby raising the area's stormwater drainage system, and improving the Level of Service protection for both water quantity and quality. Project location: SW 127 Ave to SW 132 Ave, from SW 42 Terr to SW 53 Street (Royal Green).
1582.purpose: The goal is to reduce flooding, protect properties and lives by raising the area's drainage system to provide a standard Level of Service by installing 6,750 linear feet of exfiltration trenches, 225 drainage inlets, and pollution control structures, which will prevent pollutants from entering the stormwater systems and discharging into the C-2 Snapper Creek watershed basin. Project seeks to improve the storage capacity and conveyance of the stormwater drainage infrastructure. Project location:

2604.description: The Mickler Boulevard outfall south treats and conveys stormwater runoff from approximately 50% of the city of St. Augustine Beach. Erosion and sedimentation resulting from rainfall events have compromised outfall resiliency and capacity. This funding initiative request is for design, permitting and construction of a durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground and overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes and 4) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2604.purpose: Provide durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground and overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes and 4) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2604.direct_services: Increased Level of Service (LOS) by providing durable bulwark to protect existing 1) underground & overhead utilities; 2) traffic evacuation & pedestrian mobility routes & 3) stabilize the outfall west bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent property. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2604.population: City of St. Augustine Beach residents and a portion of St. Johns County residents. Approximately 5,000 individuals are expected to be served.
2604.outcome: Mitigate stormwater runoff: 1) Roadway inundation by floodwater: City staff observations of road inundation and infrastructure performance, field data collection, resident interviews, and # of Public Works work orders related to roadway/flood damage. 2) Infrastructure damage mitigation: # of threats or safety hazards to the general public and emergency responders, # of related resident comments or complaints and routine vulnerability assessment updates.

Funds requested will help finalize the Teen Center construction, and build out our Stem Lab, Reading Lab, and Career Readiness Lab at the Center with the proper equipment, devices, and some furnishings.

Activities and skill development that keep teens productive and engaged are very different, and teens command a different type of support than do elementary Club members. These funds will help us to cater to teen development by building out the St. Augustine Teen Center with a Career Readiness Lab, Reading Lab, and STEM Lab. The Club will be large enough to comfortably accommodate approximately 75

The STEM Lab, Reading Lab, and Career Readiness Lab will all support social-emotional development and skills growth so our Teens have the knowledge and confidence to build a viable career and cultivate a successful future.

Expected benefits include: teens stay on grade level, and achieve academically; avoid risky behaviors; graduate high school; and have a plan for their future that will include secondary education such as college, vocational/trade school, or the mili

Apprentices receive tools, mentorship, and tuition-free classes to ensure they develop competency and practice safe work habits. Additionally, apprentices have the opportunity to earn an Associate of Science Degree in Leadership for Industry at Santa Fe College. The funds requested will be used directly to support these apprentices in their learning and career development.

2800.description: This project will increase stormwater capacity at the SR-442/I-95 Interchange to address flooding from events such as Hurricane Ian, ensuring continuous I-95 evacuation access and reliable movement of residents, freight, and emergency services. Construction will installs inlets/culverts, conveyance swales, and outfall improvements, utility enhancements, MOT, and restoration within existing ROW. The project de-risks over 11 million sq ft of planned industrial/commercial space in Deering Park and Parktowne Industrial Park to support the aerospace and advanced manufacturing industries and would be sequenced with the road widening project already in progress and the future Diverging Diamond Interchange (DDI). The adjacent landowner has agreed to take the stormwater flows from the interchange into their master stormwater system and construct those improvements.
2800.purpose: To address flood-related closures at the SR-442/I-95 interchange by designing, permitting, and constructing stormwater upgrades - upsized inlets/culverts, conveyance swales, and outfall improvements. This will ensure continuous, all-weather evacuation access, protect public safety, and de-risk adjacent industrial/commercial investment, accelerating job creation. The improvements would be coordinated with road widening construction and the future DDI.
2800.activities: Install/upsized inlets, RCP/culverts, headwalls and control structures; build conveyance swales and outfall stabilization; utility protection/adjustments; maintenance of traffic; erosion/turbidity control; final restoration and as- builts - within existing ROW and coordinated with current road widening project and future DDI.
2800.direct_services: Reliable, all-weather access to I-95 (including hurricane evacuation); fewer flood closures/detours; faster emergency response; safer travel during major rain events; reduced property and business disruption.
2800.population: 24,000 existing residents; 1,600 - 2,250 local manufacturing employees; regional commuters, freight operators, and emergency responders using the SR-442/I-95 interchange - serving tens of thousands annually during storm seasons.
2800.outcome: The project will support job creation, improve resilience, increase disaster preparedness, and reduce congestion. Success will be measured through a reduction in storm-related closure hours at SR-442/I-95 and documentation of new business and employment growth.

The new Rescue Vehicle will be equipped with vital accessories, including chassis, radio system, essential equipment, patient-specific customizations, and will undergo comprehensive final inspections. The Rescue Vehicle will be designed to possess a sturdy, custom-built interior patient compartment, enabling specialized care response. This feature will significantly aid the Fire-Rescue Department in delivering Critical Care Transport rescue services for Cooper City and Broward County citizens through mutual aid agreements.
1395.purpose: The specific purpose of the funds requested is to enhance public safety, improve emergency response capabilities and times, ensure compliance with national and local safety standards, and provide the community with critical, efficient, and dependable rescue services. The specific goal is to accomplish the purchase of a new Fire Rescue Critical Care Transport Vehicle to meet the unique needs and specialized care of the citizens, achieve National and County service life and safety standards, and p
1395.activities: Purchase of a new Fire Rescue Critical Care Transport Vehicle to meet the unique needs and specialized care of the citizens. The Project includes the purchase of a new Rescue Vehicle for the Fire-Rescue Department, improving public safety service delivery and enabling specialized care response. This Project will significantly aid the Fire-Rescue Department in delivering Critical Care Transport, effectively addressing the unique needs of our community, in Cooper City and Broward County.
1395.direct_services: The Project will provide citizens with more efficient and dependable critical care rescue services, critical equipment, faster response times, and improved protection of lives in our community. This Rescue Vehicle will be engineered and outfitted with a robust customized interior patient compartment that will allow specialized care response and assist the Fire-Rescue Department to deliver essentia
1395.population: All Cooper City residents - 34,400 plus Countywide mutual aid responses. The Project will not only serve Cooper City, but provides regional benefits through Countywide automatic aid agreements, and mutual aid agreements, either of which may be called upon to assist during disasters. This Fire Rescue Critical Care Transport Vehicle is not just a means of transport but a life-saving tool. The design and features will allow for rapid response times, immediate medical intervention, and a safe transf
1395.outcome: Expected benefits of this Project includes life-saving support for first responders in delivering critical care during medical emergencies, accidents, or disasters. This Project holds immense value in the community. The Project will serve as a mobile intensive care unit, equipped with state-of-the-art medical equipment that can handle severe injuries and life-threatening situations swiftly and efficiently. This Rescue Vehicle is designed to bring the highest level of medical care to the patient at the scene, minimizing the time between the onset of illness or injury and the initiation of definitive care. The Project will be measured for responsiveness, lifesaving capabilities, and operationa

Over time, around 17 miles of this system have deteriorated due to natural settling and age, leading to a multitude of issues. The compromised state of these pipes invites an influx of groundwater, necessitates superfluous treatment, triggers sanitary sewer overflows (SSO) from manholes and lift stations, and negatively affects surface water quality. The City has committed efforts to maintain compliance with the FDEP and other regulatory agencies. This Project will rehabilitate approximately 2.5 miles of ailing gravity sewer lines as a determined effort to rectify the City's existing aging sewer piping. This Project includes the installation of folded form liners, the repair of damaged pipe sections, and the removal of intrusions. This Project will improve wa
1315.purpose: In the year 2023, the City engaged an independent consultant to undertake an initial CCTV inspection of the gravity sewer mains citywide. This investigation was designed to pinpoint the areas of greatest concern within our sewer piping system. As a result of this examination, this project emerged as a site of critical importance. The specific goal to be achieved with State funds is the rehabilitation of approximately 2.5 miles of deteriorated gravity sewer lines. The successful completion of thi
1315.activities: Funds will be used to repair and rehabilitate existing sanitary sewer pipes via pipe lining (lining of existing sanitary sewer pipes). Activities to be provided to meet the intended purpose of these funds include the cleaning and video inspection of the gravity sewer collection system and constructing/rehabilitating of approximately 2.5 miles of degraded gravity sewer lines by installing folded form liners, repairing damaged sections of piping, and removing intrusions. The least disruptive and m
1315.direct_services: Improvements will mitigate volume of inflow and infiltration into the sanitary sewer system. Repairs will mitigate sanitary sewer overflows (SSO). The potential harm to the public if this Project is not funded includes the further degrading and deteriorating of the piping, which may lead to environmental harms such as contaminated ground water and ecosystems.
1315.population: All City residents - 34,400. Direct services to citizens include improved ground water quality and surface water quality, and enhanced protection of residential homes from sanitary sewer overflows (SSO). This Project will improve wastewater management, storm water management, and ground water quality.
1315.outcome: Expected benefits include, improved ground water quality and environment, extended life cycle of existing sewer piping, reduced excess rainfall/infiltration or inflow/ground water for treatment during heavy rains, reduced flows through manholes and lift stations, prevented sanitary sewer overflows (SSO) into sensitive water bodies of the State, improved wastewater management and ground/surface water quality, and the protection of residential property from other adverse environmental impacts.
