HUF seeks to complete this objective by: (1) Offering Career Technical Education (CTE) in keeping with market drivers in partnership with recognized educational institutions and (2) provide wrap around services to guarantee client success enrolled in CTE (3) guarantee job placement of clients post-graduation by strengthening partnerships with employers in relevant industries.
1320.purpose: The requested funds will expand HUF’s capacity to deliver short-term, high-demand career training programs by increasing staffing and removing financial and logistical barriers for clients. This investment will help working families access well-paying jobs and strengthen Florida’s workforce and economy.
1320.activities: -Initial assessment and identification of skill sets, experience, and expertise to advise clients on career pathway to guarantee success. -Access to education and trainings partners that cater to the unique: multiple modalities, flexible locations, student support etc. -Job placement for participants in high paying jobs. -Market research of job market in Florida to identify synergy with programs.
1320.direct_services: -Identify the transferable related occupations for clients with existing skills and experience. -Provide wrap around services: (i.e.: childcare, transportation) to address any potential challenges that might impact client successfully completing the education program. -Skills development for successful job placement (i.e.: interview skills, soft employment skills). -Financial education.
1320.population: Elderly persons, Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, High school students, General. Expected to serve: 150 individuals.
1320.outcome: -Number of clients completing career technical education programs. -Number of participants placed in high paying jobs. -Number of participants who show career progression one year after being placed in job. -Increase salary. -Percentage of increased household income. -Increased savings. -Increased credit score. -Reduction of debt. -Graduation rates. -Job placement with an hourly wage over $20. -Long term career progression once placed in a job. -Enrollment to completion rates. -Credential attainment. -More clients will access high-paying jobs and long-term careers. -10% increase in household income (measured through household budget comparison (pre and post).

1749.description: This request would support the Daily Healthy Meal & Activity Program for Seniors at the newly renovated Dr. Armando Badia Senior Center located in the City of Miami, ensuring that older adults receive nutritious meals and engage in physical, social, and mental wellness activities. The funding will be allocated to Nutritious Meal Provision, Physical & Recreational Activities, Cognitive & Social Engagement and Facility & Program Support.
1749.purpose: To support the Daily Healthy Meal & Activity Program for seniors, ensuring that older adults receive nutritious meals and engage in physical, social, and mental wellness activities.
1749.activities: This program provides seniors with balanced, dietitian-approved meals that meet their dietary needs while supporting overall health. In addition to nutritious food, the program includes a variety of physical, social, and recreational activities aimed at enhancing mobility, cognitive function, and social interaction. Activities may include light exercise, wellness workshops, arts and crafts, educational sessions, and community gatherings.
1749.direct_services: Daily meals and related supplemental services/programming.
1749.population: The target population for this project is senior citizens, it is expected that 200 senior citizens will be served on a daily basis.
1749.outcome: The outcome of the Daily Healthy Meal & Activity Program for Seniors is an overall improvement in participants' physical health, mental well-being, and social engagement.

1296.description: Manatee County Habitat for Humanity, Inc., requests funding for infrastructure (water, sewer, storm water management, underground electrical, roads, grading & more) in preparation for building 20 affordable townhomes for low-income Manatee County families in the 50 to 80% range of Area Median Income. The homes will be located in the Palmetto CRA. Once infrastructure has been installed, we will build 20 houses (hardened against natural disasters and both energy- and water-efficient) and sell them to prequalified low- to moderate-income families with a low or zero-percent mortgage.
1296.purpose: 20 low- to moderate-income Manatee County families will be able to purchase affordable, storm-hardened, water and energy efficient homes with mortgages not to exceed 30% of their income. Children who grow up in Habitat homes are TWICE as likely to go to college, family health and financial stability improves, and new homeowners will pay taxes.
1296.activities: We will install infrastructure - water and sewer, underground electric, storm water management, roads and more - needed by 20 future homeowners. Correct installation makes flooding from storms less likely and handles other issues that normally would impact community resources.
1296.direct_services: The availability of clean water, sewer installed to latest code, proper management of storm and flood waters, electricity, properly graded roads and common areas, and more.
1296.population: We will serve approximately 75 to 100 individuals from 20 families in the 50 to 80% range of Area Median Income (AMI) who live in unsustainable housing. This income range is classified as low and moderate income and includes educators, medical personnel, emergency personnel, and many other people who are critical to the smooth functioning of our economy and the community.
1296.outcome: 20 low to moderate income Manatee County families will be able to purchase a well-built, storm-hardened, water and energy efficient home with a low or zero-percent mortgage with payments of no more than 30% of family income. This will remove them from the trap of rental housing, giving the entire family new stability and improving their health. Other expected outcomes are improved educational outcomes including college attendance, building family wealth through accumulation of equity and lower housing costs (a home for families in this income range is approximately 81% of family wealth), a reduction of crime and teen pregnancy, and new tax revenues for the community. Families living in a fam

3433.description: Established in 1884, Daniel is the oldest child-serving agency in Florida. Our motto, "improving the odds for kids" captures the purpose of our mission to "improve the lives of children and families." To this end, we offer mental health treatment, foster care, and homeless services. We seek to ensure that the most vulnerable children and families are provided with the skills and supports necessary to become healthy, contributing citizens. The purpose of this project is to plan, design, and construct a new state-of-the-art treatment facility for children facing complex mental health disorders.
3433.purpose: The purpose of this request is to construct a state-of-the-art residential treatment cottage in which to provide a safe, homelike facility for the most vulnerable children in the State of Florida.
3433.activities: Funds will be used for the demolition of the existing structure, and planning, design and construction of a new, treatment home with an attached commercial kitchen that serves the entire campus (comprising four treatment cottages).
3433.direct_services: The Statewide In-Patient Psychiatric Program provides comprehensive child mental health services comprising psychiatric and therapeutic care, behavioral services, nursing/medical services, medication management, recreation, and on-site academic instruction.
3433.population: The target population are children, ages 7-18, facing mental health disorders that affect their respective abilities to thrive. The program serves approximately 110 children annually.
3433.outcome: The benefit for this project is to provide a safe, modern facility for psychiatric treatment of children facing significant, complex mental health disorders. The goal for these children is to develop the coping skills and resilience to thrive and return to their respective Florida communities. Positive outcomes are measured by incremental progress toward individual treatment plan goals as well as successful discharge.

2251.description: Recognizing the needs among our local Veterans, we provide groceries on a weekly basis in our community. Since we opened in July 2024, we have provided meat, produce, dry goods, and bread to over 8,000 veterans, offering those goods through a combination of private donation and fundraising efforts. Each week we see more veterans in need visit our location to receive aid from our volunteer staff. This funding will cover three years of our food costs at our current rate of spending, while also allowing some growth to provide assistance to more of our veteran community.
2251.purpose: In 2023, estimates showed 1 in 5 military or veteran families faced food insecurity. These funds will be used to purchase food for Veterans (meat, fresh produce, dry goods, and bread) that will be distributed during our weekly shopping opportunity. In just over 14 months of operation, we have fed more that 8,000 veteran families and continue to see a growing need.
2251.activities: Each week we offer a selection of meat, produce, dry goods, and bread to veterans. These funds will cover our current food expenses for the next three years (approximately $1,500 per week) while allowing us to service additional veteran families through our private donations and fundraising efforts.
2251.direct_services: We provide groceries (fresh produce, meat, bread, and dry goods) to veterans at zero charge to address the issue of food insecurity in that community. As part of our mission to assist the veteran community, we do require that recipients have completed a verification form demonstrating their military service.
2251.population: We offer goods to all veterans that come to our food distribution day. At this time, we are approaching nearly 200 veteran families served each week, with over 8,000 veterans receiving food assistance since we began operation in July 2024.
2251.outcome: Hunger among our veteran community is a serious concern. Our weekly provision of meat, fresh produce, bread, and dry goods to veterans helps to alleviate some of those issues locally. We maintain records of the number of veterans who are serviced and are seeing increased numbers each week. By tracking those numbers, we are able to determine the number of veterans that are receiving necessary nutritional assistance through our mission.

2346.description: Renovation of existing school facility to allow it to serve as a Vocational Trades High School.
2346.purpose: Renovation of Roosevelt High School to serve as vocation trades high school.
2346.activities: Renovations will include facility renovations (labs, ADA, MEP upgrades, fire suppression), as well as site utilities & power upgrades (3-phase, compressed air, ventilation)
2346.direct_services: Each Academy will house 3–6 high-demand pathways (e.g., Construction, Electrical, Welding, HVAC/R, Automotive/Diesel, Advanced Manufacturing, Health Sciences), aligned to CAPE industry certifications and local workforce needs and will service students in grades 9–12 with embedded academics, work-based learning, and dual enrollment opportunities provided.
2346.population: The renovated school will serve 900 high school students.
2346.outcome: Educational benefits: 1.85%+ students earning =1 industry certification 2. 0–15 percentage-point gains in on-time graduation for participating students 3. 25–40% reduction in behavior/attendance issues due to program engagement (historical pattern for high-interest CTE) Outcomes will be measured by Industry certifications earned and graduation rates which are all tracked by the State. Reduction in behavior and attendance goals will be tracked by the school district and provided upon request.

2252.description: This project will expand capacity for treatment at the Ibis outpatient center, creating greater continuity of care, integrating mental health, pharmacy, substance use, and primary care services. This will decrease emergency room visits by 74% and law enforcement encounters by 95%. It will also enhance direct care service to more than 3,000 patients through the provision of outpatient therapy and medication management, care coordination, substance use disorder services, and assertive community treatment.
2252.purpose: To expand capacity for treatment at the Ibis outpatient center, creating greater continuity of care, integrating mental health, pharmacy, substance use, and primary care services. This will decrease emergency room visits by 74% and law enforcement encounters by 95%. It will also enhance direct care service to more than 3,000 patients through the provision of outpatient therapy and medication management, care coordination, substance use disorder services, and assertive community treatment.
2252.activities: Provide space for care coordination to close/eliminate the gap between inpatient treatment and outpatient follow up/ongoing care. It will also expand much needed virtual health services as well as provide adequate group rooms to conduct afterctreatment including but not limited to, trauma informed care, domestic violence, postpartum depression, substance use, recidivism avoidance in Tampa Bay.
2252.direct_services: This project allows us to better serve clients through the provision of outpatient therapy and medication management, primary health care, pharmacy services, care coordination, substance use disorder services, assertive community treatment, as well as community education. Data indicates a 74% reduction in emergency rooms visits and 96% reduction with law enforcement encounters.
2252.population: 00+ forensic patients and 300+ trauma patients will recieve services annually. Populations include persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, Homeless, Developmentally disabled, Physically disabled, Victims of crime.
2252.outcome: The facility will include a multi -disciplinary team to address issues physical and mentals health issues. There will be an overall reduction in readmissions and better mental and physical health outcomes. Care Coordination has been shown to result in a 74% reduction in emergency room visits and a 95% reduction in law enforcement encounters. Advanced care coordination and diversion reduces costs to the state by more than 50%.

2253.organization: Living Above The Noise, DBA More Too Life
2253.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
2253.description: More Too Life (MTL) is an anti-human trafficking organization providing direct services to victims of human exploitation in Sarasota, Manatee, Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, and Miami-Dade counties. The organization was founded over 19 years ago and aims to offer effective services, programs, and resources that educate and empower victims of human exploitation/trafficking. The requested funding will increase service delivery to meet this growing demand and increase MTL’s ability for coordination throughout the state to meet the complex needs of this population.
2253.purpose: Expand services to children, youth, and young adult victims of sex trafficking. This request supports additional staff to meet critical unmet needs in the service area including coordination with law enforcement/judicial system, employment of survivors of human trafficking, mental/behavioral health, digital advocacy, human trafficking awareness, and training to community-based organizations on best practices to serve this population. The request also supports unmet needs of victims of human traf
2253.activities: MTL will provide victim advocacy, specific to criminal justice investigations of alleged traffickers, mentoring, and education for victims in the justice system. MTL will provide survivor-informed training to case managers and stakeholders who work with victims in trauma-informed settings. MTL will address victims' mental health needs resulting from sex trafficking & support victim identification.
2253.direct_services: Provides advocacy with law enforcement, mentoring and therapeutic services to victims of sex trafficking, along with support in victim identification. Training Program will provide educational and informative sessions on best-practices and trauma-informed approaches to case managers and other stakeholders who have direct interactions with children, youth and young adults who have been trafficked.
2253.population: The primary population served will be victims of Human Trafficking, youth serving organizations, persons with poor mental health and physical health, school aged students, jobless persons, at risk youth, homeless, economically disadvantaged persons, high school students, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders in criminal justice, victims of crime. 200-400 individuals are expected to be served.
2253.outcome: Using several proven processes for tracking, monitoring, measuring and reporting performance outcomes, More Too Life will report the number of exploited and trafficked victims identified and referred. MTL will track and report on the number of victims receiving services, the types of services received by victims, and the demographic information on those being served. Primary benefits of this project include improving victims' physical and mental health, improving victims' economic self-sufficiency, reducing recidivism, and preventing victims from entering criminal and juvenile justice systems. "

2256.description: Warrior Wellness Program will offer 22 Accelerated Wellness Programs (AWP). The AWP is a 5-day intensive program offering highly effective therapies such as Accelerated Resolution Therapy, adaptive yoga, Integrative Restoration, physical fitness and mindfulness techniques such as vision boarding and art therapy. Program outcomes for the AWP shows participants show an average reduction of 60% in PTSD, 68% in Depression and 65% in Anxiety.
2256.purpose: Warrior Wellness Program's goal is to provide veterans and active-duty military personnel an opportunity for healing. The men and women who served our country will attend the Accelerated Wellness Program providing them increased access to Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART) and other alternative therapies that effectively treat symptoms and issues related to trauma, post-traumatic stress, anxiety, depression and more, which will result in improved mental health and wellness.
2256.activities: Warrior Wellness Program will offer 22 Accelerated Wellness Programs (AWP). The AWP is a 5-day intensive program offering highly effective therapies such as Accelerated Resolution Therapy, adaptive yoga, Integrative Restoration, physical fitness and mindfulness techniques such as vision boarding and art therapy.
2256.direct_services: The organization will provide mental health and wellness services including Accelerated Resolution Therapy, a proven therapy that works in 1-5 sessions to provide healing for veterans and active-duty military members experiencing post- traumatic stress symptoms including depression and anxiety. Adaptive Yoga & iRest are provided together to increase body awareness and improve sleep outcomes. Mindf
2256.population: This project will deliver services to 125 veterans and/or active-duty service members and their spouses who suffer from issues related to post-traumatic stress, anxiety and depression due to the traumas of war. Services will be delivered through Warrior Wellness Program's Accelerated Wellness Program, a 5-day intensive program providing an array of effective mental health and wellness therapies.
2256.outcome: Participants will experience a reduction in PTSD, depression, anxiety and stress. In addition, they will experience an increase in resiliency and community engagement. Pre- and post- assessments are conducted and use valid and reliable measures of psychological and physical health including the Post-Traumatic Checklist and the Brief Symptom Inventory. An external evaluator uses the data collected to perform an extensive analysis to produce a comprehensive program evaluation on overall service impact.

2259.description: To expand Operation Healing Forces' ability to provide vital services to wounded, ill, injured, and fallen Special Operations Forces service members, veterans, their families, and caregivers. Funds will support Therapeutic Retreat Programs for SOF Couples and Caregivers and the Immediate Needs Program, which provides urgent financial assistance for hardship and crisis situations not covered by government means, including essential living expenses, mental health care, and medical-related needs.
2259.purpose: To expand Operation Healing Forces' ability to provide vital services to wounded, ill, injured, and fallen Special Operations Forces service members, veterans, their families, and caregivers. Funds will support Therapeutic Retreat Programs for SOF Couples and Caregivers and the Immediate Needs Program, which provides urgent financial assistance for hardship and crisis situations not covered by government means, including essential living expenses, mental health care, and medical-related needs.
2259.activities: Expanded opportunities for Floridians to participate in OHF's Therapeutic Retreats that promote the long-term mental, physical, and emotional wellbeing of OHF's targeted populations to enhance their resilience, empower their rehabilitation, embrace their reintegration, and lead fulfilling and productive lives. Increased financial grants to reduce hardships, such as med costs and food insecurity.
2259.direct_services: Provide valuable tools and life skills through the retreats designed to counteract the high suicide, domestic abuse, illness, and divorce rate found within the SOF community; resources to individuals in need of additional mental health support and treatment; and, financial assistance in times of hardship to reduce stress and trauma triggers during times of crisis.
2259.population: Up to 400 Special Operations Forces (SOF) service members, veterans, their families, and caregivers.
2259.outcome: Improve physical health: Recipients of Immediate Needs Program funds have increased physical wellness and gain access to medical devices and therapeutics and better nutrition. Participants are enrolled in virtual wellness coaching sessions that provide individuals and family units with customized wellness guidance in areas such as nutrition, physical activity, and guided movement classes. Improve mental health: OHF programs increase protective factors related to family bonding and healing and reduces risk factors related to isolation, anxiety, anger, depression, and stigma. SOF couples and family experience of feeling positive emotions, a sense of control over critical aspects of life to inc

2486.description: Hurricanes Helene/Milton caused flooding to the police and fire station which sustained substantial damage and is unable to be repaired due to FEMA regulations. A replacement facility is required in order to provide law enforcement, fire and EMS services to the community. This replacement public safety building will be hardened and elevated above the floodplain.
2486.purpose: Replace and elevate public safety building that was destroyed by Hurricanes Helene and Milton so that first responders can provide necessary services to the community and immediately respond to future storms. This facility will be elevated and hardened to comply with FEMA requirements for use by our police and fire departments.
2486.activities: Police administration, crime prevention and patrol operations will be conducted from this building. The building will house fire apparatus, firefighter quarters and administrative offices. New facility will meet FEMA requirements including elevation above floodplain for immediate use.
2486.direct_services: EMS/fire & police 911 response and administration. An elevated and hardened facility provides the ability for first responders to return to the barrier island to provide critical services immediately as flooding recedes. We currently have no public safety facility from which to conduct lifesaving operations immediately post storm/disaster.
2486.population: This public safety facility will serve the citizens and visitors to our barrier island community. Current population is 6,552 which triples on busy weekends and holidays. First respnder services are also provided to neighboring communities within Pinellas County through automatic aid agreements.
2486.outcome: To provide an elevated and hardened facility for first responders to return to the barrier island to provide critical services immediately as flooding recedes during natural disasters. We currently have no public safety facility from which to provide law enforcement, emergency medical services or fire protection. These services are using portable buildings that do not meet building code and would be uninhabitable during a tropical weather event. This project will provide a permanent facility for these necessary public safety functions.

2487.description: The City of Seminole Community Recreation Center opened in 2001 in a converted church building built in 1983. The facility has reached the end of its useful life. The City provides much needed quality-of-life programming/activities to a multi-generational community and has identified funding to assist in the construction of a new Center. This appropriations request will allow timely construction of a new Recreation Center to serve the greater Seminole Community for many generations.
2487.purpose: The funds will be used towards the construction of the Community Recreation Center. The Community Recreation Center will enhance the quality of life through recreation, athletics, the arts, fitness/wellness, veterans' programming, youth camps, and various other community interest opportunities for Seminole and surrounding areas.
2487.activities: Activities and programs will be offered to youth (e.g., athletic leagues, camps, homeschool programs, art programs, swim lessons) adults, seniors, and community programs for veterans and for persons with special needs. It will serve as a facility after natural disasters, with programs and day camps provided for families of first responders during recovery. It will also serve as a cooling and charging station, fully equipped with a generator, and will serve as a FEMA distribution site for ice and
2487.direct_services: Programs for all ages including group fitness, basketball/pickleball courts, weight/cardio room, swimming pool, splash pad, community meeting rooms, performing arts area, senior lounge, Esports programs, craft room, outdoor courts and athletic field space. Organized activities such as community events, youth and adult leagues, senior programs, socials, special events, youth camps, swimming lessons
2487.population: The new Community Recreation Center will serve all populations from infant to Seniors (55+). It is expected to serve a minimum of 45,000-50,000 Seminole and Pinellas County residents annually.
2487.outcome: The Community Recreation Center would improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural and art experiences, will provide a location for homeschool programs, and increase economic activity by hosting various large scale regional events. The Community Recreation Center would be be activated post natural disaster for a point of distribution for ice/water, cooling and charging station and provide childcare for families of first responders during recovery efforts. Outcomes will be measured using tracking and evaluation systems for program/activity attendance, number of citizens utilizing the facility, mobile analytics data to monitor where event attendees are going after they leave events/prog

2261.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2261.description: United Food Bank and Services, one of the largest food banks in Hillsborough County and in operation for 34 years, serves as a lifeline for families, seniors and students facing food insecurity across ten East Hillsborough County communities. This $1.5 million operational request will allow us to expand staffing, enhance service delivery, and grow programs, ensuring that more neighbors are fed, educated, and supported, creating measurable community impact and long- term stability across East Hillsborough County.
2261.purpose: United Food Bank and Services, one of the largest food banks in Hillsborough County, serves as a lifeline for families,seniors and students facing food insecurity across ten East Hillsborough County communities. This $1.5 million operational request will allow us to grow staffing and programs, support operational and programming costs, and ensure that more neighbors are fed, educated, and supported, creating measurable community impact and long-term stability across East Hillsborough County.
2261.activities: These funds will be used to expand staffing, strengthen operations, and reach more families, students, and seniors across East Hillsborough County. Funding will support new staff, strategic donor engagement, and Board training to ensure sustainable, high impact programs. These efforts will provide reliable access to nutritious food, education, and empower families to achieve long-term stability.
2261.direct_services: Funding will support supplemental food distribution, enhanced logistical procurement, individual assessment for community referrals, and direct services for families, students, seniors, and children with family focused- workshops on nutrition, financial literacy, and programs that advance health equity.
2261.population: Serving more than 15,000 community members each month, including very low-income individuals, seniors, children, and families facing food insecurity across ten East and South Hillsborough Communities such as Plant City, Seffner, Dover and Wimauma. With 31% of Hillsborough residents and 52% of Plant City residents classified as ALICE ( Assest Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) these areas are identified as Transportation Disadvantaged Target Areas due to high poverty, unemployment, and limite
2261.outcome: Funding will provide families, seniors, and children facing food insecurity with healthy, nutritious foods, including fresh fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins. Access to these foods improves physical health by supporting better diet quality, reducing risk for chronic disease and promoting overall wellness. Funding will also expand access in under served areas, reduce transportation barriers, and allow United Food Bank to serve a minimum of 40 new families each week, totaling approximately 2,080 new families over the 26-27 fiscal year.

2262.description: Funds will support PHSC as it advances into the implementation phase of its statewide initiative to address the nursing and allied health workforce shortage. Prior funding has supported PHSC through the establishment and launch of the School of Health Science and Nursing (formerly the Institute for Nursing and Allied Health Advancement). Leveraging existing facilities and infrastructure, PHSC will continue to formalize alliance agreements that strengthen the workforce pipeline, execute initiatives to recruit and retain qualified faculty in these high-demand fields, and establish sustainable partnership agreements with healthcare providers.
2262.purpose: Through active collaboration with key stakeholders, PHSC will develop and implement comprehensive strategies to recruit and retain highly qualified nursing and allied health faculty. These efforts will directly contribute to an increased number of graduates from these critical programs. Graduates will fill essential roles in healthcare institutions, thereby improving patient physical health and well-being by enhancing the quality and timeliness of care delivery.
2262.activities: This funding will expand enrollment capacity in nursing and allied health programs, resulting in a greater number of qualified graduates entering the workforce. Addressing current workforce shortages will lead to measurable improvements in patient care, including reduced response times, shortened emergency room wait times, and more timely attention to patient needs during admissions.
2262.direct_services: The School of Health Science and Nursing will alleviate the burden on overextended healthcare professionals by enabling more qualified graduates to fill open nursing and allied health positions. This reduction in workload is expected to improve both the physical and mental well-being of healthcare workers, while simultaneously enhancing patient care quality and outcomes.
2262.population: The program will serve a population including high school students, college/university students, elderly individuals, persons with physical or mental health challenges, unemployed and economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, developmentally and physically disabled individuals, individuals with substance use disorders engaged with health services, as well as current nursing and allied health faculty. It is anticipated that this initiative will positively impact more than 800 individuals
2262.outcome: Success will be measured by tracking the number of faculty positions filled and the number of students graduating from nursing and allied health programs who secure employment in healthcare institutions. Additionally, the economic impact will be assessed by the increased income flowing to faculty, graduates, and the broader community as a result of employment in these fields.

2264.description: The goal is to provide financial assistance to families whose children are battling cancer with medical co-pays, basic needs such as gas, food, and utilities, etc. Additionally, the funds will go towards providing financial support for memorial services for children whose battle with cancer has ended.
2264.purpose: To support Florida families who have been affected by childhood cancer by providing resources to alleviate the financial burdens incurred while undergoing treatment.
2264.activities: Live Like Bella works directly with licensed pediatric healthcare professionals and families to provide needed funds for basic necessities to alleviate everyday financial burdens. Families receive assistance with medical copays, basic needs such as gas, food, utilities, and everything in between.
2264.direct_services: Florida families whose children are battling cancer will receive direct services including, but not limited to, all aforementioned ancillary costs associated with their ongoing care.
2264.population: Children and families undergoing cancer treatment. Upwards of 400 families receive support throughout the State of Florida.
2264.outcome: Ease financial burdens incurred by families whose children are battling cancer measurable through assessment of family expenses

2265.description: The funding will support our Veterans Mental Health Initiative, Operation Resilience. This initiative offers mental health counseling, animal-assisted therapy, and service dog training to veterans diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, and /or MST. The goal is to restore independence by improving mental health, reducing suicide rates, sustaining recovery from substance abuse, and empowering veterans through enhanced emotional regulation and vocational integration, fostering self- sufficiency and success. The project will be tracked and monitored by researchers at the University of Central Florida, Dr. Christopher Stewart.
2265.purpose: The program aims to reduce veteran suicide risk by offering service dog support, trauma-informed counseling, and crisis intervention strategies. Success will be measured by a reduction in suicide risk, with improvements in suicidal ideation and mental health crises. UCF research with K9P4P participants shows a 22% decrease in depressive symptoms, supporting suicide risk reduction.
2265.activities: The activities provided include trauma-informed mental health counseling, animal-assisted therapy, service dog training, and data analysis of program outcomes, as monitored by UCF. Veterans will participate in weekly counseling and therapy sessions, service dog training that enhances emotional regulation and social mobility, and LCSW-led aftercare to support long-term symptom management.
2265.direct_services: The funding will provide veterans with PTSD, TBI, and MST access to mental health counseling, animal-assisted therapy, and service dog training. Services include individual and group therapy, telehealth access, veteran travel assistance, and aftercare programs, ensuring long-term stability, crisis prevention, and improved quality of life.
2265.population: Funds will be used to serve veterans diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, and/or MST, including rural and low income veterans. Veterans with poor mental and physical health. Veterans who are physically disabled as well as veterans who are jobless or economically disadvantaged.
2265.outcome: The program will reduce veteran suicide rates, crisis episodes, and emergency mental health interventions, easing the burden on public services. Veterans will experience a reduction in PTSD, anxiety, and depression symptoms, leading to fewer crises, increased resilience, and improved emotional stability. The program will reduce reliance on medications and emergency interventions, enhancing self-sufficiency. UCF research shows a 25% reduction in PTSD symptoms and improved emotional regulation among K9P4P participants.

3382.description: To ensure law enforcement officers have a consistent, compassionate resource to support children during emergency encounters by supplying fully stocked Hero Kits—featuring a Benny Bear, a custom coloring book, crayons, and comfort items. Funding will sustain and expand this program so every responding officer can offer a child reassurance, safety, and kindness right in the moment it’s needed. Each Hero Kit becomes a meaningful bridge between a uniform and a child, helping officers create comfort instead of fear. Your investment transforms a police interaction into a moment of hope.
3382.purpose: To give police officers in the city of Naples and Collier County this tool to de-escalate a crisis and build a relationship with our officers. We also want to build trust, respect for our law enforcement and the understanding law enforcement is a resource.
3382.activities: Immediate response to an interaction with a child in any situation where there is law enforcement intervention. Hero Kits are to create a safe space in trauma. A resource for every patrol officer.
3382.direct_services: Beverly’s Angels provides direct crisis support to children who encounter law enforcement by supplying officers with Hero Kits filled with brand-new comfort items. These kits help reduce fear, ease emotional distress, and create a positive connection between officers and children during emergencies. Officers can immediately offer something soothing to hold, something to focus on, and a tangible re
3382.population: The target population for the Hero Kits program is children who experience a law enforcement encounter during moments of crisis, including domestic disturbances, car accidents, welfare checks, emergency calls, or any situation where a child may feel fear, uncertainty, or emotional distress. These children often face sudden, overwhelming circumstances. 500-800 Children
3382.outcome: Children who experience a crisis will feel calmer, safer, and more supported during law enforcement interactions. Hero Kits help reduce fear, ease emotional distress, and create a more positive connection between officers and children. Officers will complete a brief usage log noting when a Hero Kit is distributed, the type of call, and observed child response. Program success will also be measured through quarterly reports from the City of Naples Police Department and replenishment rates of kits.

3043.description: Hendry County is seeking $2.5 million for the rehabilitation of gravity sewer mains in the Port LaBelle Utility System to reduce groundwater inflow and infiltration and to increase wastewater treatment plant capacity. The County previously received grant funding from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) in the amount of $800,000 for the rehabilitation of gravity sewer mains. The County used these funds to clean and survey the gravity sewer mains to determine which mains needed repair and the order of priority for those repairs, and to rehabilitate the gravity mains in the most severe conditions. Additional funding is needed to complete the rehabilitation of the remaining gravity sewer mains. This area is included in the FDEP Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) area in the Eastern Caloosahatchee Basin. By reducing inflow and infiltration, the wastewater treatment plan
3043.purpose: The funds will be used to perform rehabilitation of a wastewater collection system to reduce inflow and infiltration (I&I) which serves approximately 899 customers within Units 1, 4 & 5 of the Port LaBelle Utility System. This customer count includes Florida Southwestern State College, Country Oaks Elementary, and LaBelle High School. This area is included in the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Basin Management Plan (BMAP) area in the Eastern Caloosahatchee Basin.
3043.activities: Construction and construction engineering and inspection (CEI) services for the rehabilitation of a wastewater collection system
3043.direct_services: There are no direct services provided. However, the rehabilitation of the wastewater collection system will reduce inflow and infiltration providing increased wastewater plant (WWTP) capacity for septic to sewer conversions as the WWTP will be processing less ground water while processing wastewater. This also results less maintenance costs of equipment and reduces the changes of wastewater leakin
3043.population: Approximately 899 customers within Units 1, 4 & 5 of the Port LaBelle Utility System
3043.outcome: Increased volume of wastewater treatment plant capacity at the wastewater treatment plant due to less ground water intrusion. The outcome will be measured by the reduction of monthly wastewater flows to the wastewater treatment plant.

3044.description: Hendry County (County) is requesting funding to construct a new public safety facility to serve the western side of the County and to replace the current EMS station and administrative office building located in LaBelle. The current station was built in 1991 and is in need of extensive repairs. Due to the age and condition of the building, public safety crews cannot stage in the station during hurricanes and the cost to harden the current structure would exceed that of a new and improved station. The new station will have the capacity to house not only EMS, but also fire and Sheriff's personnel as needed and will allow for faster response times for our constituents during emergencies on blue sky days as well as hurricane events. As a rural community, Hendry County needs the ability to better facilitate response times in emergencies for life safety purposes.
3044.purpose: Construction of a new public safety station in western Hendry County to serve residents in the City of LaBelle and surrounding areas and facilitate faster response times
3044.activities: More efficient Fire, EMS, and Sheriff's deputy coverage while allowing emergency personnel to stage in their stations during a major storm event which is not possible at this time due to current facility not rated for storm events.
3044.direct_services: Construction of the station will provide faster emergency response times to residents and visitors in western Hendry County on blue sky days as well as during a major storm event.
3044.population: Hendry County has a population of approximately 40,000 residents
3044.outcome: Faster emergency response times. This will be measured by showing when a call is placed to 9-1-1 and the time it takes for responders to get to the scene of the incident.

2269.description: Operation Song will expand its evidence-based program across Florida to serve veterans, and their families. With this funding, we will write 50 original songs, hold three in-person retreats, host 35 virtual sessions, and co-host the Destin Songwriters Festival. These efforts will directly serve approximately 100 veterans and families, reach an additional 3,000-4,000 Floridians through events, and 25,000 online, uniting communities in honoring and supporting those who served.
2269.purpose: The goal is to reach more veterans and their families across Florida by providing accessible, non-clinical creative outlets that promote emotional healing and connection. Through songwriting, veterans will have the opportunity to process their experiences, reduce isolation, and rediscover purpose. At the same time, Operation Song will work to build a statewide network of VA facilities, veteran nonprofits, community groups, and corporate partners that collaborate to support these programs. This n
2269.activities: Operation Song will provide its evidence-based program across Florida to serve veterans, and their families. With this funding, we will write 50 original songs, hold three in-person retreats, host 35 virtual sessions, and co-host the Destin Songwriters Festival. These efforts will serve approximately100 veterans and families, reach 3,000-4,000 Floridians through events, and engage 25,000 online, uniting communities in honoring and supporting those who served.
2269.direct_services: Participants will work one-on-one with a professional songwriter to craft an original song that captures their personal story of service and sacrifice. Each participant retains 50% ownership of the song through Operation Song Music Publishing, registered with ASCAP. Upon completion, participants receive a professional MP3 recording of their song to share with family, friends, and their community.
2269.population: The target population includes Florida veterans, active-duty service members, first responders, and their families, with a focus on those coping with the effects of service-related stress, trauma, or transition. Through the proposed expansion, Operation Song will directly serve approximately 100 participants through in-person retreats and virtual songwriting sessions. In addition, 3,000–4,000 Floridians will be reached through live community events, with an estimated 25,000 more engaged online,
2269.outcome: The project will improve the mental health, emotional well-being, and social connection of Florida veterans, service members, first responders, and their families. Participants will experience reduced stress and isolation, along with a renewed sense of purpose through the songwriting process. Operation Song will measure outcomes through pre- and post-program surveys, feedback, and attendance data, tracking improvements in mood, connection, and overall well- being.

2276.description: Funding will be used to build a Security Operations Center and a cybersecurity forensics laboratory to train students in advanced digital defense, network monitoring, and forensics techniques. The project also includes hiring qualified faculty to teach in Saint Leo University's undergraduate and graduate cybersecurity programs. The Tampa Bay region is rapidly becoming a hub for technology companies, with a projected national shortfall of over 1 million cybersecurity professionals by 2027. This initiative directly supports Florida's workforce demand by producing trained cybersecurity specialists prepared for roles in both public and private sectors.
2276.purpose: Funding will be used to build a Security Operations Center and a cybersecurity forensics laboratory. In addition, funding will also be used to hire one qualified faculty to teach in our undergraduate and graduate cybersecurity programs. The Tampa Bay region is fast becoming a hub for tech companies. Recent projections indicate that there will be over 1 million open positions nationwide for cybersecurity roles in 2025-2027.
2276.activities: Funding will be used to build a Security Operations Center and a cybersecurity forensics laboratory, hire qualified faculty to teach in our undergraduate and graduate cybersecurity programs. The Tampa Bay region is fast becoming a hub for tech companies, and there is strong demand for cybersecurity professionals in the region.
2276.direct_services: To complete Associate, Bachelors and Masters degrees in Cybersecurity, students from across the state of Florida, as well as high school students, would have direct access to the services provided by the proposed program.
2276.population: Target populations for this project include those persons without a career/employment, the economically disadvantaged, high school students, and university/college students. This program is expected to benefit well over 800 persons.
2276.outcome: The proposed Cybersecurity and Cyberforensics Training and Education Center will significantly strengthen Florida's ability to prepare a highly skilled technology workforce. Through the establishment of a state-of-the-art Security Operations Center and Cyber Forensics Laboratory, Saint Leo University will provide students with practical, hands-on training in data protection, network defense, and digital investigations. This will be measured by enrollment and graduation rates.

3375.description: Design for installation of stormwater improvements and other critical infrastructure within the Gordon Dr. neighborhood.
3375.purpose: Design for stormwater and other critical infrastructure improvements corresponding to Mutli-Basin Assessment and Basin IV Project Implementation Plan.
3375.direct_services: Design for future stormwater and other critical infrastructure improvements to enhance resiliency of the neighborhood.
3375.population: Directly impacts approximately 1,800 residents of Aqualane Shores and Port Royal neighborhoods as well as community establishments. Broader community impact for improved recovery time and operations from major storm events.
3375.outcome: Reduce untreated discharges by =10% via conveyance and control upgrades. Methodology: Outfall monitoring and pollutant load estimates. Also, removal of 33 buildings from 25-year floodplain; removal of 2,494 LF of collector roadway from floodplain; removal of 5,339 LF of local roads from floodplain. Reduce roadway flood depth by =6 inches during 2–10 yr events; cut flooded hours by =50%. Methodology: Pre/post storm modeling; high-water mark surveys; SCADA/lake level logs.

2277.description: The Nursing Program Expansion project will enhance Saint Leo University's capacity to educate and train future nurses to meet Florida's growing healthcare needs. Funding will be used to reconfigure and equip existing campus space to include three additional classrooms, one nursing lab, and faculty and staff offices. The project also includes simulation and teaching equipment, professional development for faculty, and upgrades to classroom technology and instructional spaces. This expansion supports a critical statewide priority: addressing Florida's projected shortage of 60,000 nurses by 2035. By increasing enrollment capacity and improving learning facilities, Saint Leo University will help supply qualified nurses to serve hospitals and healthcare systems throughout the region and state.
2277.purpose: The purpose of the funds is to increase nursing program capacity through an increase in faculty and staff, resources for teaching and learning, and renovation of existing space for additional classrooms, lab, and faculty and staff space. The funding will allow for an increase in enrollment and will support nursing program completion.
2277.activities: Citizens of Florida will be educated and trained in nursing and will obtain a Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree. These citizens will use their skills to address the nursing shortage in Pasco County and throughout the State of Florida.
2277.direct_services: The funding requested will provide the physical space, teaching, and support resources to increase program enrollments in the nursing program. Saint Leo University's nursing program has grown rapidly in response to workforce demand, increasing from 77 incoming pre-nursing students in Fall 2024 to 124 in Fall 2025, with projections of 150+ students in Fall 2026. The proposed facility improvements a
2277.population: Target populations for this project include those university/college students seeking a degree in nursing. With full program implementation, up to 51-100 students may be trained and educated annually in the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program.
2277.outcome: The Nursing Program Expansion will directly increase the number of qualified nursing graduates entering Florida's healthcare workforce each year, helping to reduce the state's severe nursing shortage. With the addition of new classrooms, laboratories, and simulation spaces, the program will be able to educate and train up to 100 Bachelor of Science in Nursing students annually. Graduates of the program will provide critical healthcare services in hospitals, clinics, and community health centers throughout the region, improving access to care and patient outcomes.

2278.description: SOF Missions provides a four-pillar whole health program to at risk Veterans at no cost to them. Our goal is to build resiliency in Veterans that has a positive and lasting effect on their life, their families, their communities, and their interactions with others. We aim for each Veteran to show improvement in their overall psychological, physical, spiritual, and social health. Our objectives for 2025-2026 are to host more Veterans in our Monthly Be Resilient Clinics (10 Annually) and 2 Be Resilient Retreats, which will provide care to over 3,000 Veterans.
2278.purpose: SOF Missions exists to provide four-pillar whole heath care programs to at risk veterans. Our goal is to build resiliency in veterans that has a positive and lasting effect on their life, family, and community. We aim for each veteran to show an improvement in their overall psychological, physical, spiritual, and social health. Our objectives for 2023 are to host 10 Be Resilient clinics and 2 retreats, which will provide care to over 300 veterans.
2278.activities: SOF Missions offers a unique approach to combat veteran suicide and provide care through a whole health intradisciplinary model—The Resiliency Project is a four-pillar program that addresses the areas of psychological, physical, spiritual, and social wellness. Care plans are provided through three main delivery methods: Clinics, Coordinated Care, and Collaborative Care.
2278.direct_services: Services available for psychological care range from peer-based programs, mental health therapy, and creative therapy. Spiritual care includes education, mentorship, and support groups. Physical care includes physical therapy, alternative PTSD/TBI treatments, cognitive rehab therapy, and sleep therapy. Lastly, social care includes recreational therapy, service animals, and service projects.
2278.population: Persons with poor mental health Persons with poor physical health Physically disabled Veterans, active duty service members, and their families 300 people are expected to be served
2278.outcome: Improved mental, physical, social and spiritual health for veterans, active duty service members and their families. Methods used to measure the outcome will include: Physical Health -Lab marker changes at initial and follow up appointments. (ex: hormone, cholesterol, and vitamin levels) - Functional Movement Screening - Selective Functional Movement Assessment - Wearable sleep monitoring devices - Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) to assess pain Mental Health - Improved score on Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) Depression measure - Improved score on PCL-5 PTSD checklist Social and Spiritual Health - Increased participation in leisure activities - Greater ability to maintain positive friendshi

2345.description: To advance the Willowbrook Road project to 60% design and permit ready, positioning the project to better leverage dollars for construction costs from a federal appropriation. The road construction will alleviate congestion on State Road 544, improve connectivity for one of the fastest-growing areas in Polk County, and enhance mobility for pedestrians, cyclist, and motorists.
2345.purpose: Improve transportation network by adding a new connection, reducing congestion on SR 544, and supporting regional mobility.
2345.activities: Road construction, bridge development, and trail connectivity.
2345.direct_services: Improved roadway access for commuters, businesses, and emergency responders.
2345.outcome: Willowbrook Road will feature a multimodal trail, seamlessly expanding the city’s trail network and encouraging safe, active transportation for all users. The project also includes a bridge, ensuring vital connectivity while thoughtfully accommodating both natural and built environments. By addressing increasing pressure on existing roadways, this road will enhance regional mobility and support the area’s rapid growth.

2488.organization: Area Agency on Aging of Pasco-Pinellas, Inc.
2488.description: This project expands access to innovative, AI-driven infrared fall detection technology designed to protect at-risk seniors. The aesthetically refined ceiling-mounted light integrates seamlessly with a 24-hour, professionally staffed wellness center, enabling seniors to live safely and independently while reducing hospitalizations, long-term care placements, social isolation, and the burden on unpaid caregivers, if one exists. The system delivers real-time alerts in the event of a fall or safety incident, ensuring rapid response and supporting Florida’s strategic objective of helping seniors age safely in place. Its advanced 13-point dynamic skeletal imaging technology minimizes false alarms, thereby preventing unnecessary 911 activations and optimizing emergency response resources.
2488.purpose: At-risk individuals utilizing the fall detection technology will be able to remain safely in their homes while maintaining greater independence and peace of mind. The system provides 24/7 monitoring that immediately detects when a fall occurs ensuring that help is dispatched even when the person is unable to call for assistance. By automatically notifying caregivers, family members, or emergency responders, the technology significantly reduces the time between a fall and intervention.
2488.activities: This project expands access to innovative, AI-driven, functional ceiling mounted light, infrared fall detection and 24 hour live wellness monitoring technology for at-risk seniors, helping them live safely and independently while reducing hospitalizations and long-term care placements. The project provides real-time alerts when a fall or safety event occurs, enabling rapid response and supporting Florida’s goal of helping seniors age in place.
2488.direct_services: • Installation of ceiling-mounted fall detection devices in participating homes or senior living environments. • 24-hour live wellness monitoring by trained operators who respond immediately to safety events or abnormal activity. • Concierge support services that provide personalized assistance, coordination of care, and access to community- based programs that promote social connection and well-b
2488.population: The project will serve seniors at high risk for falls, which includes seniors who may be on the memory care spectrum, or who are experiencing sight or hearing impairment, reaching an estimated 100–140 participants. Total costs will vary based on each home’s infrastructure needs, such as the availability of reliable Wi-Fi or other necessary connectivity to support system installation and operation.
2488.outcome: Reduction in fall-related injuries and significantly faster emergency response times following a detected fall, ensuring assistance is provided within the critical “golden hour” when timely intervention can prevent serious complications and improve recovery outcomes. This will be measured by tracking average response times between fall occurrence and contact with caregivers, if available, or EMS after installation. Data will be collected directly from system analytics, which measure each event in real time. This data will be compared with available state and national average data of response times between a fall occurrence and emergency services.

1609.organization: The School District of Osceola County
1609.description: As part of the new school development and in coordination with the existing athletic complex at High School 'AAA', SDOC plans to construct a state-of-the-art aquatic facility. It will provide students and the community enhanced opportunities for competitive swimming, water safety education, physical fitness, and recreation. The district will ensure programming for water safety and drowning prevention, including dedicated areas for students with sensory differences or physical impairments. The facility will be open to the public when not used for school events and lessons.
1609.purpose: The district is requesting support to expand drowning prevention and water safety programs, including the development of accessible facilities and specialized programming designed to serve students and families with special needs.
1609.activities: The funds will support a new aquatic facility offering swimming, water safety, fitness, and adaptive programs for students and the public. It will provide inclusive education, supervised recreation, and community engagement while promoting health, safety, and lifelong learning.
1609.direct_services: Water safety and drowning prevention classes will be available to the citizens of Osceola County.
1609.population: All students and staff of Osceola County (65,000 students). Also residents of East Osceola County.
1609.outcome: The project will improve physical health, mental well-being, water safety knowledge, and community engagement, including programs for students with sensory or physical impairments. Outcomes will be measured through facility usage, program participation, surveys, and safety incident reports.

2610.description: The City of Palatka seeks state appropriations to design and construct a new master sanitary sewer lift station that will expand system capacity and improve overall wastewater management for the city. This new facility will serve as an additional regional lift station to accommodate future growth, reduce demand on existing stations, and enhance system redundancy and resilience.
2610.purpose: The City of Palatka seeks state appropriations to design and construct a new master sanitary sewer lift station that will expand system capacity and improve overall wastewater management for the city. This new facility will serve as an additional regional lift station to accommodate future growth, reduce demand on existing stations, and enhance system redundancy and resilience.
2610.activities: The lift station will move wastewater from lower to higher elevations and is a critical component of the sewer system, ensuring regulatory compliance.
2610.direct_services: The direct service provided will be the prevention of wastewater from backing up and contaminating water sources; thereby ensuring public health and safety and contributing to environmental protection.
2610.population: The majority of funds requested will serve the economically disadvantaged and the general population. Roughly 200- 400 citizens will be served.
2610.outcome: The benefit in protecting the general public is to enhance environmental protection by reducing the risk of overflows and ensuring compliance with FDEP standards. It will be measured by matrix and analysis performed by the environmental consultants. The new master sanitary lift station will improve waste water management by expanding the system capacity and improving overall wastewater management for the city. It will be measured by the results issued from regulatory agencies.

2612.description: The ROVETTA BUILDING A (RBA) and ROVETTA BUILDING B (RBB) are essential to FSU's academic operations, housing departments like Accounting, Finance, Marketing, and Economics, among others. However, both buildings are aging and in need of renovation. RBA, built in 1983, covers 67,518 square feet, while RBB, constructed in 1957, spans 74,705 square feet. These buildings are integral to the College of Business, which is being relocated to new construction. Given their deteriorating conditions, the requested appropriations aim to address the critical need for renovations to ensure these spaces remain functional and conducive to academic excellence for the departments still housed within them.
2612.purpose: The funds requested will be used to renovate Rovetta Building A and B, with the goal of improving the quality of education at FSU. The renovations will create modern, accessible classrooms, offices, and common areas that support teaching and learning. The improved facilities will enhance the academic experience for students and faculty, ensuring that the buildings remain functional and conducive to academic success.
2612.activities: The funds will be used to renovate Rovetta Building A and B, including upgrading classrooms, offices, restrooms, and common areas. These improvements will enhance the functionality, safety, and accessibility of the spaces, supporting the delivery of high-quality education. The renovations will ensure the buildings can continue to serve academic departments effectively, providing an environment conducive to learning, teaching, and administrative functions.
2612.direct_services: The direct services provided by the appropriation project will include improved learning environments for students through renovated classrooms, study areas, and common spaces. These upgrades will create safer, more accessible, and efficient facilities that support academic success. Students will benefit from enhanced spaces that foster better learning experiences, increased engagement, and improv
2612.population: The target population served by this project is Florida State University (FSU) students, including those in departments such as Accounting, Finance, Economics, and Marketing. The renovation of Rovetta Building A and B will directly benefit thousands of students who use these spaces for classes, study sessions, and academic activities. It is estimated that over 5,000 students will benefit from the improvements each semester.
2612.outcome: The expenditure of the requested funds will directly improve the quality of education by enhancing the learning environment in Rovetta Building A and B. Renovations will upgrade classrooms, offices, and common areas, creating modern, accessible spaces that foster better teaching and learning. A measurable outcome will be improved student engagement and academic performance. Key indicators will include improvements in student engagement, academic performance, and faculty effectiveness. Additionally, usage rates of the upgraded facilities and reductions in maintenance costs will be tracked to evaluate the impact on the quality of education provided.

3273.description: Home Base Florida is dedicated to delivering life-saving clinical care and support for Florida Veterans of all eras, Service Members, Military Families, and Families of the Fallen healing from invisible wounds, including post-traumatic stress, traumatic brain injury, anxiety, depression, co-occurring substance use disorder, family relationship challenges, and other issues associated with military service. Home Base is committed to eliminating barriers and filling gaps in care where they exist, offering services at no-cost and regardless of discharge status. 1 in 3 veterans return home with an invisible wound. If left unaddressed, it can lead to an increased risk of suicide. Home Base seeks funding to sustain and expand access to evidence-based, gold standard care, regardless of where you live in Florida.
3273.purpose: For FY26-27, Home Base will continue providing world-class services in the state, with the goal of increasing program offerings in Tampa and NW Florida alongside local partners. Increased state funding allows for greater patient access to poly-trauma and clinical care, wellness-based programs, and peer support at no-cost for Florida Veterans, service members, and military-connected families.
3273.activities: (1) In partnership with Tampa General Hospital (TGH), Lee Health and David Lawrence Centers for Behavioral Health Home Base will provide evidence-based treatment for the PTSD and other invisible wounds. (2) In partnership with Florida Gulf Coast University and TGH, will offer the wellness programs to improve physical health and well-being through supervised exercise prescription. (3) In partnership with TGH and Lee Health, will provide clinical services for traumatic brain injury (4) Provide on-
3273.direct_services: (1) Prolonged Exposure, Cognitive Processing Therapy, Cognitive Behavior Therapy, Pharmacotherapy, Addiction Medicine (2) exercise prescription, postural & mobility training, nutrition counseling, resiliency courses (3) physiatry, nurse case management, neuropsychology, psychology and physical therapy (4) training in military culture, PTSD, TBI, substance use disorder, complicated grief etc.
3273.population: Services are provided to Florida Veterans of all eras, Service Members, Military-Connected Families and Families of the Fallen at no cost to them. Number Served: (275) unique patients to receive evidence-based treatment for PTSD, anxiety, depression and other invisible wounds, (250) individuals will be served through our Warrior Health and Fitness Program, (50) Veterans will receive comprehensive outpatient services for traumatic brain injury, (500) clinicians, healthcare providers, first respon
3273.outcome: Funding will enable Home Base to sustain and expand the number of Florida Veterans, Service Members and their families that can receive live-saving clinical care and support. Outcome Measures: (1) Provide the number of Florida Veterans, Service Members and Military-Connected Families that receive clinical care. (2) Provide the number of Florida Veterans, Service Member and Families served through our Warrior Health & Fitness Program. (3) Provide the number of Veterans or Services served though TBI programs. (4) Provide the number of individuals trained though in- person and on-line training.

2894.description: The federal VA has found loneliness to be the highest factor correlated with depression and suicidal ideation, while frequent in-person socializing can lower odds for depression and PTSD symptoms by 50%. Tampa-based Krew Social produces the first enterprise belonging and loneliness solution designed to foster daily in-person gatherings. The project would create a white-labeled mobile app for the Florida Department of Veterans Affairs incorporating all features of the current mobile web app as well as Krew Social's belonging platform that users love. This technology would compliment the “Governor’s Challenge to Prevent Suicide among Service Members, Veterans, and their Families.”
2894.purpose: The federal VA has found loneliness to be the highest factor correlated with depression and suicidal ideation, and frequent in-person socializing can lower odds for depression and PTSD symptoms by 50%. Tampa-based Krew Social produces the first enterprise belonging and loneliness solution designed to foster daily in-person gatherings. Goals would be lower incidence of suicide, suicidal ideation, depression, loneliness, and drug and alcohol abuse amongst veterans. This technology would compliment
2894.activities: A white-labeled GovChallenge Krew mobile app capable of providing all services currently provided by the FDVA mobile web app, as well as Krew Social's revolutionary event and micro-event interface, including map interface, suggestion algorithm, and user-generated safe hangouts. Customer service will also be provided.
2894.direct_services: Florida's veterans will have one place to go for all FDVA services and events. Events will be significantly enhanced to show users which ones to go to, who to talk to at each one, and what to talk to them about based on the highest potential of forming a deep relationship. Veterans will also have the ability to create their own fun, safe hangouts doing healthy activities.
2894.population: It would be available to all of Florida's 1.3 million veterans.
2894.outcome: Improved physical health- Report percentage of hangouts that are physical activities. Improved mental health- Surveys can measure depression, suicidal ideation, and loneliness amongst veterans who are monthly active users compared to those who are not. Suicide rate amongst monthly active users can be compared to non-users. Reduced substance abuse- Surveys can measure substance abuse amongst veterans who are monthly active users compared to those who are not. Drug and alcohol-related offense rate of active users can be compared to non-users. Reduced recidivism- We can compare recidivism among former inmate veterans who actively use the platform compared to those who do not. Increased economic

2895.description: This project will replace outdated windows and upgrade 26Health’s existing residential-grade air conditioning units with a commercial HVAC system designed for healthcare facilities. The current systems are inefficient, unreliable, and unable to maintain consistent air quality or temperature control across patient care areas. Replacing the windows and installing a modern HVAC system will improve energy efficiency, indoor air quality, and patient comfort while ensuring compliance with healthcare facility standards. These upgrades will enhance safety, reduce maintenance costs, and support a healthier environment for patients and staff.
2895.purpose: The requested funds will allow 26Health to replace outdated windows and install a commercial-grade HVAC system to improve the facility’s safety, efficiency, and environmental quality. The upgrades will ensure proper ventilation, temperature control, and energy conservation, creating a healthier and more comfortable setting for patients and staff. This project will extend the building’s useful life, reduce operational costs, and help maintain continuity of care during Florida’s extreme heat and w
2895.activities: 26Health will engage licensed contractors to remove outdated windows, install energy-efficient replacements, and upgrade the existing residential air conditioning units to a commercial HVAC system. Work will include design, permitting, equipment installation, and post-installation testing to ensure compliance with building and healthcare standards. These improvements will enhance air quality, temperature regulation, and overall safety within patient care areas.
2895.direct_services: The project will provide patients and staff with a safer, more comfortable, and energy-efficient healthcare environment. Improved air quality and temperature control will reduce health risks related to heat and poor ventilation, supporting better overall wellness. By maintaining a stable indoor climate, 26Health can ensure uninterrupted delivery of primary care, behavioral health, and specialty se
2895.population: The project will serve the uninsured, underinsured, and medically underserved residents who receive care at 26Health’s primary facility in Orange County, including low-income individuals and families. By improving air quality and safety, the project will directly benefit all patients, staff, and visitors who use the building each year - approximately 5,000 individuals annually.
2895.outcome: The project will improve air quality, temperature regulation, and energy efficiency within 26Health’s facility, leading to a safer and healthier environment for patients and staff. These improvements will reduce maintenance issues, lower utility costs, and enhance patient satisfaction. Success will be measured through air quality testing, energy consumption reports, maintenance logs, and patient and staff satisfaction surveys conducted before and after project completion.

3045.description: The City of Labelle will construct a new Class I deep injection well to expand wastewater treatment and disposal capacity and support future economic growth. This activity will eliminate dependence on the existing spray field, providing long-term, environmentally sound effluent disposal capacity consistent with state and federal standards. The infrastructure will support current and future residential, commercial, and industrial users within LaBelle’s service area, ensuring adequate capacity to meet projected growth and regulatory requirements.
3045.purpose: Pre-Construction/Construction of a new Deep Injection Well to expand the City's wastewater disposal capacity to support current and future residential, commercial, and industrial users. The well will also allow for the decommissioning of the existing spray field, providing long-term, environmentally sound effluent disposal capacity consistent with state and federal standards.
3045.activities: Pre-Construction/Construction of a new Deep Injection Well to expand the City's wastewater disposal capacity.
3045.population: The target population served by this project is the entire City of LaBelle - population of 5,222.
3045.outcome: Installing a deep Injection well to replace the existing spray field will eliminate dependence on the existing spray field, providing long-term, environmentally sound effluent disposal capacity consistent with state and federal standards. This will be measured by amount of the change in mode of effluent disposal. Unlocking developable land now connected with the spray field, which, along with increased wastewater capacity, will meet documented barriers to growth. This will be measured by number of acres reaching certain levels of development, up to and including construction beginning on commercial and/or residential properties.

3039.description: This funding will be to finish building a new high school in Hendry County. Special facilities funding was committed to this project at an original amount of $90,630,801 in 2023. This funding was to be distributed over a three-year period. Due to substantial material and construction costs increases and the way the school cost was originally calculated using the per student station formula this request includes an additional $33,130,316 in funding needed to finish the school along with the original remaining 3rd year.
3039.purpose: The requested funds will allow the district to complete construction of a new high school.
3039.activities: Complete construction of new high school.
3039.direct_services: The new school will provide a safe and modernized high school for the students of Hendry County. It will also serve as a storm shelter for all citizens of the county.
3039.population: The target population for this project will be high school students located within Hendry County; however, there will also be adult education classes and FGCU classes at the school.
