1388.description: The high-water rescue vehicle (HRWV) is used during disasters in high-water flood zones and flooded conditions to assist with citizen evacuations, delivery of supplies, and providing emergency services such as transporting boats, temporary lighting, and communication equipment.
1388.purpose: The requested funds will be used to purchase a high-water rescue vehicle (HWRV) to be used by the Sarasota Police Department during disaster situations. The HWRV will enhance public safety throughout the City of Sarasota by providing evacuations services to vulnerable citizens, delivering supplies, emergency equipment, and performing disaster assessments.
1388.activities: The HWRV will provide services such as evacuating citizens during an extreme weather event and/or flooding incidents. It can also be used to deliver supplies to residents, business and city locations, along with delivering emergency equipment and assisting city staff with disaster assessments in areas that are not safe for traditional emergency vehicles.
1388.direct_services: While the purchase of the HWRV will not directly provide services to citizens, they can be used to assist citizens during a natural disaster for evacuations and providing needed supplies.
1388.population: It could be used for any of the 57,000 City residents, along with businesses. It could be used to assist surrounding communities such as Longboat Key, Sarasota County and Manatee County, as well, if needed.
1388.outcome: Benefits provided to the general public would include enhanced public safety by evacuating and transporting citizens from flooded areas, traversing flooded areas to delivery supplies and equipment during flooding and disasters in areas other vehicles cannot travel. Additionally, the HWRV can improve transportation conditions during floods by traveling on roadways other vehicles cannot travel to provided needed services and evacuation services. The measurements can be done through incident report and safety reports issued by the Sarasota Police Department along with police reports filed for each incident, safety reports, and disaster recovery reports. .

1954.organization: Heart of Florida United Way, Inc.
1954.description: Heart of Florida United Ways Digital Horizons Program equips residents of Orange, Osceola, and Seminole counties with the tools and training to succeed in a digital world. Participants receive digital literacy instruction through trained Navigators and access to personal computers, helping them build long-term skills for education, employment, and self- sufficiency.
1954.purpose: Through hands-on digital literacy training, the Digital Horizons Program empowers ALICE families in Orange, Osceola, and Seminole counties to confidently navigate the digital world. Participants learn essential online skills from Digital Navigators and receive devices to apply those skills, supporting education, employment, and long-term self-sufficiency.
1954.activities: The program will provide digital literacy trainings and community clinics led by Digital Navigators who teach residents how to use technology for work, education, and benefit services. Participants will also receive devices to apply these skills. Navigators will follow up with clients to ensure continued use, creating lasting self-sufficiency and measurable community impact.
1954.direct_services: Citizens will receive direct support through Digital Navigators who provide one-on-one and group digital literacy training, ongoing assistance, and troubleshooting by phone, virtually, or in person. The program will also include the distribution of devices to eligible participants, enabling them to apply these skills for education, employment, and essential online services.
1954.population: The program will serve ALICE households across Orange, Osceola, and Seminole counties, focusing on seniors, youth, veterans, and working-age adults who lack devices or digital skills. At least 2,000 individuals will benefit directly through device distribution and digital literacy training, with additional residents reached through ongoing Navigator support.
1954.outcome: The program aims to increase digital literacy, enabling participants to access education, job training, personal benefits, and economic opportunities, supporting long-term economic self-sufficiency. Progress will be monitored through intake surveys at clinics and follow-up contacts with participants at 3, 6, and 9 months to assess skill development and ongoing needs.

1706.description: The program aims to deflect citizens with chronic mental health, substance abuse related issues, chronic disease, and chronic falls from becoming system involved. In helping high service utilizers become self-sustainable, the overall outcomes being achieved are systemic and cost-effective solutions for those is mental and/or physical health crises.
1706.purpose: The program aims to deflect citizens with chronic mental health, substance abuse related issues, chronic disease, and chronic falls from becoming system involved. In helping high service utilizers become self-sustainable, the overall outcomes being achieved are systemic and cost effective solutions for those is mental and/or physical health crises.
1706.activities: Develop referral, dispatch and follow-up protocol for behavioral health response with Lutheran Services Florida; Crisis Intervention trained & behavioral health specialist to respond to health crisis; team to determine level of care; warm handoff for individuals who are stabilized in the community to the appropriate case manager; data collection and analysis; stakeholder high utilizer staffing.
1706.direct_services: Referral/identification from hospitals, DCF, law enforcement, paramedics of high utilizers; Onsite de-escalation, assessment, and identification of treatment needs; Crisis intervention and brief counseling; Linkage and referral. Follow up as needed to promote crisis resolution and increase quality of life. Evaluation and arrangement for inpatient hospitalization, respite, and ongoing supervision.
1706.population: Elderly persons with poor mental and physical health, economically disadvantaged, homeless, physically disabled. We currently serve an average of 300 seniors quarterly, so with this appropriation request, we plan to double those numbers serving 600 seniors quarterly.
1706.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, reduce recidivism and substance abuse and divert from criminal/justice system. Monthly data collection, analysis, reporting, program implementation and process evaluation and quality improvement.

1745.description: The City of Port Richey (City) requests to revert and reappropriate Senate Form 1275, Specific Appropriation 22445A, not be available during the current fiscal year. The project replaces an aging 2008 E ONE model engine that has exceeded its service life. The new engine will meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards and also achieve compliance with Insurance Services Office (ISO) requirements. Additionally, it will reduce annual maintenance costs in the department as well as increase in service time of the apparatus since it will require less unexpected servicing.
1745.purpose: REVERT AND REAPPROPRIATE. The specific purpose of the funds requested is to enhance public safety by purchasing a new fire engine to replace a 20-year-old vehicle that has become unreliable and costly to maintain. This new engine will improve emergency response capabilities, ensure compliance with modern safety standards, reduce maintenance downtime, and provide the community with more efficient and dependable firefighting and rescue services. By upgrading this critical equipment, the funds will
1745.activities: The funds allocated for purchasing a new fire engine will enhance emergency response capabilities and community safety. Key activities include fire suppression, rescue operations, and hazardous material mitigation, ensuring quicker and more effective responses to emergencies. The fire engine will also support medical first response and disaster preparedness, protecting lives and property during natural or man-made disasters.
1745.direct_services: The appropriation project for the new fire engine will provide the following direct services to citizens:Emergency Firefighting: (1) Rapid response to extinguish residential, commercial, and wildland fires, protecting lives and property. (2) Emergency Medical Assistance: Support for first responders in delivering life-saving care during medical emergencies and accidents. (3) Disaster Response: Enh
1745.population: The target population are the residents of the City of Port Richey (approximately 3200). Additionally, because of mutual aid agreements with Pasco County and the City of New Port Richey, the number of people served by this purchase would be in excess of 30,000.
1745.outcome: Increased fire protection, lower insurance premiums, protection of life and property. This will be measured by decrease in fire loss and increased public safety.

1955.description: This hub will serve as a vital resource for residents seeking opportunity, stability, and support in a rapidly changing world. It will host year-round programming in workforce development, small business growth, and environmental education. By bringing these programs under one roof, the Hub will strengthen the region’s social, economic and environmental capacity, providing a model of resilience for other communities across Florida. The facility will also serve as an emergency resource center during times of crisis, ensuring residents can access information and essential support. Funds will be used for property acquisition, renovation, and operational setup, creating a vibrant community center that encourages collaboration, innovation, and economic advancement.
1955.purpose: To establish the first Community Resilience Hub in Central Florida, a permanent center focused on: Economic advancement through workforce training, small business support, and job readiness programs. Social well-being is achieved by providing a space for families and individuals to access year-round resources, workshops, and emergency preparedness support. The funds will help create a sustainable hub that strengthens Central Florida’s capacity to thrive.
1955.activities: The Resilience Hub will provide year-round community resilience programming and serve as a critical operations center during emergencies. Activities will include preparedness education, workforce training, sustainability workshops, and community engagement events focused on energy efficiency, emergency response, and climate adaptation. During normal operations, the Hub will function as a community gathering space offering access to digital resources, cooling and heating centers, and public Wi-Fi
1955.direct_services: Emergency Support Services: Safe shelter, power access (solar + battery backup), charging stations, food, water, and medical assistance during disasters. Community Preparedness and Training: Workshops on emergency readiness, first aid, and disaster response. Resilience and Sustainability Programs: Education on energy conservation, climate adaptation, and household resilience. Social and Digital Se
1955.population: The primary target population includes residents in vulnerable and underserved communities who are disproportionately affected by extreme weather events, power outages, and public health emergencies. This includes low-income families, seniors, individuals with disabilities, and those lacking access to reliable energy or emergency resources. Depending on the hub’s capacity and service area, the project is expected to directly serve approximately 2,000–5,000 residents annually through regular prog
1955.outcome: The Resilience Hub will strengthen community preparedness, improve response capacity during emergencies, and enhance long-term sustainability for vulnerable populations. Expected outcomes include increased access to safe shelter and essential services during disasters, greater public awareness of emergency preparedness, and measurable reductions in community vulnerability.

1811.organization: Friends of Birch State Park, Inc.
1811.description: The project replaces approximately 3,250 linear feet of failing perimeter fencing along A1A and Sunrise Boulevard. It will remove aging, breachable chain-link fencing and replace it with an 8-foot fully welded aluminum fence that enhances public safety, reduces unauthorized access, protects sensitive wildlife habitat, and improves aesthetics along a key tourism gateway in Fort Lauderdale. The project also includes the replacement of park entrance/exit gates and installation of an app-based smart access control system to safely manage after-hours access for permitted youth groups using the Elks Youth Camp and park volunteers and staff.
1811.purpose: A modern perimeter fence will: • Enhance safety for nearly half a million annual visitors • Improve security for youth programs and after-hours camp rentals • Reduce environmental disturbance caused by unauthorized access • Protect rare habitats including coastal dune lake, mangrove forest, and maritime hammock • Improve the visual character of this iconic coastal state park and adjacent Fort Lauderdale beach
1811.activities: The funds will support removal of deteriorated fencing, clearing of vegetation along the park’s perimeter, installation of 3,250 feet of new 8-foot welded aluminum security fencing, replacement of entrance and exit gates, and implementation of an app-based access control system. These activities will enhance safety, prevent unauthorized access, protect sensitive habitat, and improve the overall visitor experience along the A1A and Sunrise Boulevard corridor.
1811.direct_services: The project will provide safer park access for visitors, improved security for youth groups and families, protection of sensitive wildlife areas, and a more attractive and welcoming A1A/Sunrise Boulevard corridor. Citizens will directly benefit from reduced unauthorized access, enhanced safety during recreation, and a cleaner, better-maintained environment for walking, biking, and enjoying the par
1811.outcome: The project is expected to improve visitor safety, reduce unauthorized access, and protect sensitive wildlife habitat along the A1A and Sunrise Boulevard perimeter of Hugh Taylor Birch State Park. The replacement of deteriorated fencing with secure, 8-foot welded aluminum fencing and upgraded gate systems will enhance the overall safety, environmental protection, and visitor experience. Outcomes will be measured through - Park Ranger and Law Enforcement Reports tracking reductions in trespassing, breaches, and homeless encampments; Environmental monitoring documenting decreases in habitat disturbance along the fence line; Visitor attendance and program participation data showing increased us

2617.description: Construct ADA compliant facilities as we continue to strive for excellence and access, ensuring that our buildings meets the standards established by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is both a legal requirement and a moral imperative. $500,000 to create ADA access for the two bathhouses and sixteen cabins and the lake swimming area at YMCA Camp Winona. $500,000 for ADA bathrooms, entrance ramps and noise reducing insulation for the new sports gym at the Lydecker Family YMCA to accommodate special needs population who are sensitive to noise and over stimulation. $1,000,000 for a new Olympic size pool in Palm Coast to add a zero entry section to accommodate easy access for the special needs population and for ADA compliant playground and locker rooms.
2617.purpose: To expand attendance capacity for programs and services that serve the special needs community. These facility improvements will provide fully accessible environments for people of all abilities/ages; safe, positive environments for more youth/teens to build character/values through afterschool/teen/sports programs; evidence-based programs/initiatives that address chronic disease caused by lifestyle choices; and flexible gathering spaces for community to connect.
2617.activities: Youth sports, aquatics, child care, camping for people with disabilities including veterans, chronic-disease prevention & support programs, sports practices & games, and multiple facilities that will provide a safe place for families and individuals to gather. In addition, locations can be used for food and meal distribution, emergency supplies and shelter for the community and surrounding service areas.
2617.direct_services: After school care, summer day camp, summer resident camp, swim lessons, youth sports, outdoor education, team building, wellness services for seniors and veterans.
2617.population: The special needs population is the target population but the facilities will be used by the entire population. On an annual basis, we anticipated 12,721 participants under 18 years of age, 10,081 participants from ages 18-60 and 6,112 over the age of 60 will benefit from this project for a total of 28,914 individuals. Over the 20 year facility life of this project over 578,280 people will be served.
2617.outcome: For the new YMCA in Flagler County we are partnering with the city of Palm Coast to build a 35,000 square foot facility with an Olympic size pool. We anticipate a membership base of 9,000 in addition to 19,000 individuals utilizing the facility through program use for aquatics, youth sports, child care, summer camp, community programs and event rentals. The facility and program usage are modeled after the current Ormond Beach Family YMCA. We anticipate similar usage patterns as many of the community needs we meet in the Ormond Beach community are similar to the needs identified in the Flagler County community. YMCA Camp Winona serves 924 kids each week and will be able to double that amount

1678.description: The Austin Hepburn Senior Mini-Center - City of Hallandale Beach will provide critically needed community-based services to persons aged 60 years plus. The program offers stimulating recreational activities and transportation services to minimize social isolation, depression, loneliness to avoid and/or delay nursing home placement. The program will require approximately $111,006 in funding for annual services to senior clients/family through the Department of Elder Affairs in a safe secure environment. A Social Worker is available to provide case management services, and will complete an initial face to face assessments to evaluate, address, coordinate client’s specific needs, complete annual reassessments to identify any change, evaluate the progress, and/or modify coordination of services, resources and referrals.
1678.purpose: Continue to provide critically needed community-based services to persons aged 60 years plus. The program offers stimulating recreational activities and transportation services to minimize social isolation, depression, loneliness to avoid and/or delay nursing home placement. The program will require approximately $111,006 in funding for annual services to senior clients/family through the Department of Elder Affairs in a safe secure environment.
1678.activities: The City, together with the DOEA seeks to offer a year-round Senior Center to people age 60 and older. Clients will have the opportunity to participate in a wide array of recreational activities to address loneliness, isolation, increased depression, anxiety, reduced nutrition, and community engagement. Elder friendly transportation will be provided with enhanced support amenities for older adults.
1678.direct_services: Direct Services will include-Recreation activities: classes, educational forums, games, music enrichment, fitness activities, arts and crafts, technology, birthday and holiday celebrations. Developing client enrichment activities. Transportation activities: field trips to museums, health fairs, botanic gardens, parks, movies, shopping, sightseeing, excursions, concerts, medical.
1678.population: The program will provide services to approximately 800 unduplicated people age 60 and older. Current diverse program demographics included 83.8% female, 16.2 % male, 64.3% Hispanic, 14.9% Caucasian, 17% African American, and .6% Asian American, 3.2% Other. Age ranges are as follows: Ages 60-64-9.1%, 65-69 14.9% 70-74 13%, 75-79-18.2%, 80-84 21.4%, Over 85 23.4%. 2% utilize assistive walking devices for mobility, 28.4% live alone and 44.8% serve as head of household.
1678.outcome: The Austin Hepburn Senior Mini-Center - City of Hallandale Beach will provide improved physical and mental health, provide enriched cultural programing, improve quality of education, transportation, enhance individual's economic self sufficiency, and provide linkages to resources through case management services. Methodologies used to measure program outcomes will included the number of program participants, participant surveys, improved levels of education in ESOL and technology, and data reports.

2619.description: The requested funds will be used to install a new force main to provide critical redundancy and ensure continued service in the event of a failure in the existing line. This upgrade is vital to maintain public health standards and protect the Halifax River from potential environmental impacts.
2619.purpose: The requested funds will be used to install a new force main to provide critical redundancy and ensure continued service in the event of a failure in the existing line. This upgrade is vital to maintain public health standards and protect the Halifax River from potential environmental impacts.
2619.activities: A firm will be hired to construct the system.
2619.population: The target population are the residents on the beach side - North and South peninsula within Ormond Beach city limits. The total population of Ormond Beach, according to U.S. Census data is 5,892, and all will benefit from the project.
2619.outcome: The installation of a new force main will provide critical redundancy and ensure continued service in the event of a failure in the existing line. This upgrade is vital for maintaining public health standards and protecting the Halifax River from potential environmental impacts. The City will install and monitor flow meters and pressure gages that will that service is being optimized to customers on the City's Peninsula and provide assurance that these pipes operate without failure in the crossing of the Halifax River.

2095.description: The purpose is to provide the necessary demucking and backfilling of two municipal park, MLK Park and Glades Citizen Villa Park in the city of Pahokee. The funds will cover costs associated with demucking, which involves the removal of excess mud, silt, and debris from both parks and backfilling with appropriate soil or materials. This process will reinforce the grounds and create a stable base for further development and ensure safe accessibility for park users.
2095.purpose: The purpose is to provide the necessary de-mucking and backfilling of two municipal park, MLK Park and Glades Citizen Villa Park in the city of Pahokee. The funds will cover costs associated with demucking, which involves the removal of excess mud, silt, and debris from both parks and backfilling with appropriate soil or materials. This process will reinforce the grounds and create a stable base for further development and ensure safe accessibility for park users.
2095.activities: The activities and services provided will be to de-muck and backfill two municipal parks to reinforce grounds for further development. New development will create opportunities for residents.
2095.direct_services: The direct services provided will create new development that will create opportunities for residents.
2095.population: The target population are all residents within the City of Pahokee.
2095.outcome: The expected benefit is to improve stormwater management by naturally enhancing stormwater management and increasing stormwater flow. The benefit will be measured by water quality monitoring and community feedback. The benefit will also improve landscape improvement which will create better connections between parks and new housing developments. This will be measured by community engagement and surveys on how well the landscape connects the Parks and housing developments.

1859.organization: Centro Mater Child Care Services, Inc.
1859.description: Centro Mater Foundation, Inc., established in 1968, is a nationally accredited educational and childcare organization that serves low-income working families. The initiative aims to educate parents and caregivers on vital topics such as family planning, child development, co-parenting, violence prevention, and mental health awareness. The program will offer weekly educational and intervention sessions, crisis support, and referrals for families in need, with a focus on the East Little Havana community.
1859.purpose: The primary goal is to strengthen the well-being and stability of low-income working families in Miami-Dade County by providing preventive mental health support, education, and intervention services to parents, guardians, and children, fostering stronger family relationships and improved mental wellness outcomes.
1859.activities: a. Mental health awareness and substance abuse prevention workshops. b. Co-parenting and positive discipline sessions to strengthen family relationships. c. On-site clinician support and crisis intervention services. d. Follow-up and referral to long-term mental health and family services. e Youth empowerment and emotional wellness activities. f. Community outreach and educational events promoting mental wellness.
1859.direct_services: a. Bilingual individual and family counseling sessions. b. Crisis intervention and short-term mental health support. c. Case management and referral to long-term services. d. Parent coaching and family mediation sessions. e. Youth mentoring and resilience-building activities.
1859.population: The program serves approximately 1,500 low-income working families in East Little Havana, Miami-Dade County, an area where a significant percentage of households live below the poverty line. The median household income is about $38,500, and many residents face barriers such as limited English proficiency, high stress, and single-parent household challenges. The community also experiences elevated rates of family instability and domestic violence. Centro Mater provides preventive mental health an
1859.outcome: The project will improve quality of life, mental health awareness, and family relationships among low-income working families in East Little Havana. Expected outcomes include reduced stress, stronger coping skills, and increased access to mental health resources. Progress will be measured through direct family engagement, referral tracking, consultations with mental health professionals, and follow-up evaluations, consistent with best practices in psychology and family support services.

1860.organization: Sundari Foundation, Inc. dba Lotus House
1860.description: The Lotus House Women’s Shelter Education and Employment program delivers life-changing employment and educational support, training, services, referrals and internships/employment and job placement opportunities to high special needs homeless women and youth. Through this vital program, women and families benefit from a robust education and employment program that supports their successful exit outside of the shelter system, helping them to learn, grow, thrive and lead lives of greater opportunity for themselves and their families. Investment in this program enables the most vulnerable in our community to break the cycles of poverty and homelessness, contributing to the overall growth of our community.
1860.purpose: The Lotus House Women's Shelter Education and Employment Program delivers life- changing employment and educational support, trainings, linkages, services and internship/ employment and job placement opportunities to high special needs women and youth experiencing homelessness. Helping them to heal, learn, grow, thrive and lead lives of greater opportunity for themselves and their families.
1860.activities: One on one education support, individual/group life skills training, computer access and instruction, employment supports/linkages, resume creation, job search workshop, access to professional attire, job readiness training, intensive vocational certification training, paid/unpaid employment internships, high school/GED completion support and other activities aimed at improving their lives.
1860.direct_services: One on one education support, individual/group life skills training, computer access and instruction, employment supports/linkages, resume creation, job search workshop, access to professional attire, job readiness training, intensive vocational certification training, paid/unpaid employment internships, high school/GED completion support and other activities aimed at improving their lives.
1860.population: All those served are high special needs women, youth and children who are experiencing homelessness in Miami- Dade County and are sheltered at our facility. Most have unmet medical needs, unmet mental health needs and little to no prior education/employment before entering our program. We expect to serve 255 individuals through this program during the grant period. Historically, our program has exceeded this number.
1860.outcome: 255 homeless women/female youth will participate in 75% (3 of 4) of the following benchmarks, annually: (1) One on One Education Support, (2) Life Skills Training , (3) One on One Employment Coaching and (4) Computer Access. 255 homeless women/female youth will participate in 50% of the following benchmarks, annually: (1) Obtain employment or increase employment by exit, (2) Complete a professional resume (3) Job search workshop and (4) Access to work clothing. Homeless women/female youth will participate in at least 1 of the 4 following benchmarks, annually: (1) Job readiness training, (2) Participate in on-site internship training.
