Students will gain real world knowledge on Entrepreneurship & Small Business by exploring the different career paths that exist within the sector.
2833.outcome: ESB Programs aim to create social and community impacts through reflection, education, and action. By brining people together explore purpose & vocation, students align their interests and passions with opportunities to serve their communities. The ESB participants serve as a community for each other.

2832.description: Florida International University (FIU) seeks to lead the development of a statewide medical imaging data repository that will modernize how Florida's Medicaid program stores, shares, and analyzes imaging data. The project's purpose is to reduce costs, improve care, and eliminate duplication by deploying a secure, interoperable, HIPAA-compliant imaging platform built on proven, production-ready technology.
2832.purpose: Florida International University (FIU) seeks to lead the development of a statewide medical imaging data repository that will modernize how Florida's Medicaid program stores, shares, and analyzes imaging data. The project's purpose is to reduce costs, improve care, and eliminate duplication by deploying a secure, interoperable, HIPAA-compliant imaging platform built on proven, production-ready technology.
2832.activities: Funds will support the design, integration, and operation of a secure statewide imaging repository enabling Medicaid providers to share and access imaging studies in real time. Activities include system integration, cybersecurity compliance, training, and statewide onboarding to reduce duplicate scans and improve care coordination.
2832.direct_services: Citizens will receive faster, more accurate diagnoses through statewide access to imaging data, quicker treatment and authorization decisions enabled by secure data exchange, and better coordinated care among hospitals, clinics, and agencies serving Florida's Medicaid population.
2832.population: Persons with poor physical health, physically disabled and the general public.
2832.outcome: Improved physical health outcomes for Medicaid patients through faster, more accurate diagnosis and reduced exposure to unnecessary repeat imaging.

3315.description: The West Inverness Trail Connector (WITC) will link the Withlacoochee State Trail near US 41N (northern City limits) with State-owned Whispering Pines Park, creating the final link of a triangle of trails. This connector will offer new opportunities for recreation, fitness, and tourism while also opening another multi-modal trail that can serve as an alternate to vehicular traffic which alleviates traffic on State and local roads.
3315.purpose: The WITC will provide a multi-modal path for pedestrians, students, bicyclists, residents, and tourists, to utilize. It can reduce vehicular traffic on roads and offer scenic enjoyment and health benefits to users.
3315.activities: The southern trailhead will have parking and the trail will transect the State-owned Whispering Pines and connect with the Withlacoochee State Trail.
3315.direct_services: Parking facilities and a scenic and safe multi-modal path will offer opportunities for birding, walking, bicycling, running, and other outdoor activities.
3315.population: Tourists, families, local, regional, and State visitors will be served by the WITC. Thousands of visitors and locals utilize the City's parks, Downtown Inverness, and the Withlacoochee State Trail each year.
3315.outcome: The trail will benefit the local population and visitors. Visitation data is compiled from the Citrus County Tourism Council.

3230.description: This project will advance the Florida Severe Weather Mesonet through continued technology modernization, statewide training, and operational readiness initiatives. Funding will support software and hardware enhancements, development of education and exercise programs for state and local emergency managers, and long-term sustainability of existing systems ensuring consistent, data-driven resilience across Florida’s emergency operations network.
3230.purpose: Enhance the Florida Severe Weather Mesonet through continued modernization of its hardware, software, and training infrastructure. This phase strengthens the network’s operational readiness, expands statewide coverage in both urban and fiscally constrained counties, and ensures that real-time, high-resolution environmental intelligence is fully integrated into emergency-management operations.
3230.activities: Funding will support the procurement and upgrade of weather monitoring units, the integration of new sensor types to expand data capabilities, and the enhancement of system reliability across the statewide network. The initiative also includes statewide training and exercise programs that strengthen the ability of emergency managers and local officials to interpret and apply Mesonet data in operational planning. In addition, the project will support continued improvements to the Mesonet’s data p
3230.direct_services: Citizens benefit directly through enhanced early warning, increased reliability of severe-weather alerts, and greater situational awareness for first responders, schools, and local governments. Public access portals and mobile interfaces provide hyper-local conditions and alerts, while government users leverage advanced dashboards for risk assessment and coordination before, during, and after seve
3230.population: This project serves the general population across the State of Florida, with emphasis on communities most vulnerable to severe weather. More than 800 public agencies, including emergency management, law enforcement, utilities, transportation, and school districts, will receive operational benefits. Indirectly, millions of Florida residents and visitors gain improved safety through access to real-time weather intelligence and public-facing alerting platforms.
3230.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is improved statewide readiness through expanded Mesonet coverage, strengthened system reliability, and broader use of weather intelligence in emergency management operations. Success will be measured through continued network uptime, participation in training and exercise programs, and increased integration of Mesonet data into emergency plans and decision-making processes.

3231.description: AMI, in cooperation with Gulf Coast State College, will define and implement additive manufacturing learning pathways that directly align to existing advanced machining programs hosted at the college. By utilizing previous advances at Gulf Coast, AMI will deploy additive tools and curriculum that aligns with industry recognized credentials. Also, existing and outdated additive technologies currently housed at the college will be revitalized and updated to allow for interdisciplinary training with the machining programs.
3231.purpose: The funding pool will be utilized to develop and deploy cross-disciplinary learning pathways between additive manufacturing and machining technologies.
3231.activities: Subject matter experts from AMI will advise and assist GCSC in building upon existing programs to greatly enhance the student experience. In addition, AMI will deploy appropriate learning tools and training guides to ensure program success.. This includes, but is not limited to, train the trainer materials and events, workshop material, and advanced training and student acquisition and retention activities.
3231.direct_services: Training programs will be made available to all eligible GCSC enrollees. Programs may also be developed to cater to the surrounding communities and primary education pathways.
3231.population: All segments of the population are eligible to engage and interact with this program. It is incumbent that the courses offerings align with the regional manufacturing imperatives as defined by employers.
3231.outcome: These programs are able to be delivered as stand alone certificate exercises or as part of the larger advanced manufacturing curriculum. This opens the opportunity to engage with regional industry to have their workforce re-skilled and up-skilled in a manner that is conducive to currently employed learners.

3234.description: The REACH Program educates students across various Florida counties empowering them to explore solutions and engage with our state’s natural resources. The program provides participants with both formal and informal educational opportunities where they can earn community service hours and provide service to their local community. Engagement opportunities are focused on leadership, citizenship, and conservationism to cultivate a culture of service with our youth.
3234.purpose: The goal is to further develop and expand the REACH program engagement and impact with Florida youth in grades K-12. Supplemental resources for formal and informal education will enable Reflection, Education and Action with meaningful learning and exploration to preserve our state's natural resources such as the Everglades and water.
3234.activities: The services being provided will impact students and teachers K-12 in the State of Florida via a supplemental program to impact formal and informal learning for the next generation of leaders to serve our state and local communities with leadership, citizenship and conservationism. Planned activities and resources will educate and inspire the youth to be advocates for civic service.
3234.direct_services: Education and Service Opportunities are provided to REACH program participants. Through direct service, students learn and discover their role in ensuring water security for our state. Through our multi year affiliating agreement with M-DCPS, professional learning opportunities are provided for teachers to support their mentorship of students with this mission.
3234.population: The target population to be served is students ranging from K-12th grade from underserved communities inclusive of economically disadvantaged and at-risk youth across Florida along with educators impacting these grade levels.
3234.outcome: The expected outcome is to supplement formal and informal learning to ensure a water-secure future for all. Data will be collected from participants across the various REACH pillars. Cultural experience will be met through attendance at our monthly engagement activities and service opportunities. Serving our local community allows participants to learn more about their community and state and the role they play in preserving our natural resources. Surveys will be conducted across pillars that will help us collect participant data on the areas of cultural engagement and quality impact.

3316.description: The Hermosa Lift Station Upgrade Project involves the rehabilitation and modernization of the main wastewater lift station in Hernando Beach. The lift station is a vital component of the Hernando County coastal community’s wastewater transmission system, collecting flow from six upstream pump stations. The Hermosa Lift Station currently operates under fluctuating pressures and flow cycles from six upstream lift stations. A recent engineering analysis concluded that the station must be upgraded to prevent sanitary sewer overflows, system backups for loss of power, and potential public health hazards. Additionally, its main wetwell and electrical components are vulnerable to flooding and must be elevated to ensure resiliency. This project will increase the pumping capacity of the station, raise the station and controls above the floodplain, and install a back-up diesel pump in case of a po
3316.purpose: Wastewater Lift station upgrade including larger pumping capacity, raised electrical controls and wetwell to prevent intrusion during coastal flooding, and a standby diesel pump for backup during power outages. This is a flood resiliency project for the coastal community Hernando Beach which has been repeatedly impacted by coastal flooding due to storms. Preventing sanitary sewer overflows in the waterways and within the community to protect public health and safety.
3316.population: The residents/businesses in Hernando Beach, approximately 5,000
3316.outcome: Reduction of wastewater spills caused from storm events. It can be measured by reducing the amount of reported spills.

3274.description: The funding will be used to replace the decades old boundary fence on the State-owned, City-leased, Whispering Pines Park.
3274.purpose: The fence will replace a decades old fence and reduce the likelihood that anyone will enter the park from unauthorized entrances.
3274.activities: The boundary fence will front various parts of the perimiter trail and reduce the entering from unauthorized entrances.
3274.population: Thousands of tourists, families, local, regional, and State visitors visit the park each year.
3274.outcome: The fence will benefit the local population and visitors.

3425.description: This project addresses critical gaps in the system identified in the 2025 Ernst & Young analysis by increasing access to free, evidence-based NAMI programs for youth, young adults (18-22) and families, growing the workforce of peer specialists with youth certification, and building partnerships in underserved and rural areas. Investing in youth- and family-centered peer support is a cost-effective, community-driven way to enhance behavioral health capacity and improve outcomes.
3425.purpose: The project goal is to deliver preventive, cost-effective, and highly accessible educational and support services for youth and families; outreach and awareness campaigns in schools and communities; peer-led information and referral services through the state Warmline; training new program leaders and support group facilitators; and training new certified youth or family certified recovery peer specialists.
3425.activities: The project will implement NAMI programs such as Basics, Ending the Silence, Family Support Group, Family-to- Family, and NAMI On Campus - free, peer-led programs that provide education, support, and mental health awareness for youth, young adults, and families; and other school- and community-based education and support. NAMI Florida’s youth-led NextGen panel will guide planning to assure relevance and impact.
3425.direct_services: Youth, young adults (18-22), and families across Florida will receive evidence-based education and peer-led support through local NAMI affiliates. Services include structured mental health education, facilitated support groups, peer-led presentations in schools, and personalized referrals to local resources. Young adults can receive access to training and mentoring to become certified peer special
3425.population: Middle and high school youths, young adults, and their families. Statewide, we anticipate directly serving 6,000 to 8,000 youth, young adults, and family members through in-person and virtual programming. This does not include indirect reach through outreach, social media, or awareness campaigns.
3425.outcome: Increase access to mental health education and peer support for youth, young adults, and families, expand certified youth and family peer specialist workforce, reduce preventable crisis admissions. Outcomes measured through participation logs, pre/post participant surveys, and Warmline utilization data. Metrics include number trained and certified as peer specialists (via Florida Certification Board), number of participants in NAMI programs, new NAMI On Campus clubs, peer employment. Qualitative/quantitative feedback from participants will assess improvement in knowledge, coping skills, satisfaction with services, and connection to care. Where available, data on school-based Baker Act report

3236.organization: Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of
3236.description: The purpose of Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of Florida’s Bigs Inspiring Scholastic Success (BISS) program is to help children reach their potential through professionally supported mentoring relationships with evidence-based impact, and a primary focus on improving the child’s ability to achieve academically through the positive influence of their volunteer mentor.
3236.purpose: The purpose of Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of Florida’s Bigs Inspiring Scholastic Success (BISS) program is to help children reach their potential through professionally supported mentoring relationships with measurable impact, and a primary focus on improving the child’s ability to achieve academically through the positive influence of their volunteer mentor.
3236.activities: Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of Florida (BBBSAF), through a statewide network of local affiliate agencies, provides high-quality mentoring services to youth in grades K–12 and students transitioning into postsecondary education. We serve youth identified as being at risk of academic failure due to factors such as low academic performance, chronic absenteeism, or economic disadvantage. Each youth participant is individually assessed to determine program eligibility and to create a persona
3236.direct_services: The funding for BISS is spent for direct program services and support for youth who are at-risk academically. BBBS local agencies will support delivery of one-to-one mentoring to individual youth. Mentor support activities including intake of volunteers and youth, assessments of prospective youth and volunteers; Level II background screening; case plan and youth development planning; case manageme
3236.population: BISS provides mentoring services and support for youth in grades K- 12 and students transitioning to post secondary education. Youth are determined at-risk of academic failure because of factors such as poor academic performance, a history of truancy, economic disadvantage, among others. BBBSAF will match an estimated 3,200 youth with mentors during the project year and during the project year every youth matched with a mentor will attend mentor sessions with their mentor.
3236.outcome: BISS incorporates the first goal of the State Board of Education’s K-20 Strategic Plan, which is to “increase the proficiency of all students.” BISS measures gains across four domains related to student learning gains, including academic performance, school attendance, grade level promotion, and behavioral outcomes – all of which lead to improved student learning. To ensure success, children and youth who participate in BISS receive regular mentoring sessions with homework and academic assistance as the key focus. Mentors address social, confidence and behavioral issues and encourage their Little to behave well in class, and provide positive role modeling on how to interact with others.

3275.description: The Kings Bay Restoration Project (KBRP) is a multi-phase initiative aimed at restoring and preserving the water quality and habitat in our Outstanding Florida Waterway. Led by the non-profit, Save Crystal River, the project continues to focus its multi-pronged strategy to restore, protect, and preserve the ecosystem through eelgrass, marsh, spring, and barrier island restoration while also employing system-wide strategies which prevent future shoreline, habitat and water quality degradation caused by high water events.
3275.purpose: These funds will restore, preserve and protect a critical habitat, which is designated as an Outstanding Florida Waterway. Our multi-pronged restoration strategy will improve water quality, reduce erosion, protect fish and wildlife habitat, increase water flow, and prevent future degradation of the ecosystem caused by high water events.
3275.activities: Our multi-pronged restoration strategy includes eelgrass restoration (algae removal & eelgrass replanting), restoration of spring flow by obstruction removal, installing living shorelines systems to preserve marsh islands and managing erosion control efforts to prevent water quality and habitat degradation in Kings Bay and its springs exacerbated by high water events.
3275.direct_services: The tourism industry is one of the largest economic drivers in the region. The loss of water quality (clarity) associated with current conditions and degrading habitat conditions could potentially cause a collapse of this economy. Improvements proposed by this project will help to improve and
3275.population: The citizens and the economy of the State of Florida , Citrus County, and the City of Crystal River, as well as the 350,000 local, national and international visitors per year that visit Kings Bay and Crystal River.
3275.outcome: The anticipated outcome is the overall improvement in the water quality and a thriving ecosystem as demonstrated by our project study performed pre and post restoration by an independent biologist.

3469.organization: Santa Rosa Board of County Commissioners
3469.description: The project involves seeking funding to extend the taxiway at the Whiting Aviation Industrial Park by approximately 500 - 600 linear feet. This extension aims to enhance the park's operational capacity, making it more attractive to aviation sector clients considering relocation to the State of Florida. The Whiting Aviation Industrial Park has established itself as a key hub for aviation-related businesses, providing a strategic location for companies involved in manufacturing, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services, as well as flight training and logistics. Extending the taxiway will create a more appealing environment for aviation sector clients, particularly those looking to relocate or expand operations in Florida. Improved facilities, can attract a diverse range of businesses, from small startups to large corporations seeking a strategic location with access to necessary av
3469.purpose: Extending the taxiway within the Whiting Aviation Industrial Park will open up additional capacity (acreage) to attract new businesses and aviation related companies, stimulating local economic growth and job creation. With the availability of an extended taxiway, the area can attract federal and private investments, leveraging the initial state funding to generate a larger economic impact. As other regions invest in their aviation infrastructure, it's crucial for Whiting Aviation Industrial Par
3469.activities: Taxiway extension construction is the primary activity and will involve the physical construction of the extended taxiway, which will require site preparation, paving, and installation of necessary infrastructure.
3469.direct_services: 1) Job Creation: The construction and subsequent operation of the extended taxiway will create both temporary and permanent job opportunities in various sectors, including construction, aviation services, and maintenance. 2) Economic Growth: As the industrial park attracts new aviation-related businesses, citizens will benefit from increased economic activity, leading to potential higher wages and
3469.population: 1) Local Residents: Citizens living in the surrounding areas will benefit from job creation, improved access to aviation services, and economic growth that enhances their quality of life. 2) Job Seekers: Individuals looking for employment opportunities in construction, aviation, and related sectors will have access to new jobs generated by the project and the businesses it attracts. 3) Local Entrepreneurs: Small business owners and entrepreneurs in the area can take advantage of increased econom
3469.outcome: Expected Benefits/Outcomes: 1) Economic Growth: Increased business activity and economic development in the region. 2) Job Creation: Generation of temporary construction jobs and permanent positions in new and existing businesses. 3) Expanded Business Opportunities: Attraction of new aviation-related companies, increasing the diversity of services offered in the park. 4) Increased Tax Revenues: Higher tax revenues that can be reinvested into community services and infrastructure. 5) Strengthened Regional Competitiveness: Positioning the park as a more attractive site for aviation businesses. Measurement: 1) Number of new jobs, number of new companies establishing in the industrial park, chan

3276.description: This funding will provide intensive support to help math teachers in Duval and Hernando school districts, to include: in- person math academies for teachers, embedded coaching support for classroom teachers, training for school and district math coaches, and facilitation of continuous improvement cycles for teachers and coaches. Ultimately, better prepared teachers will result in higher student achievement and more post-secondary opportunities for students in STEM careers.
3276.purpose: Research consistently shows that teacher expertise is the single most important in-school factor driving student achievement. The requested funds will support the delivery of Carnegie Learning's in-person Math Academies and ongoing coaching support for teachers and math coaches in Hernando and Duval County Schools. These activities are designed to build sustainable instructional capacity and directly strengthen classroom teaching, resulting in increased learning and higher achievement in student
3276.activities: The funding will allow for in-person math academies for teachers, embedded coaching support for classroom teachers, training for school & district math coaches, and facilitation of continuous improvement cycles for teachers and coaches in two districts during the 2026-27 school year (Hernando and Duval).
3276.direct_services: Ultimately the benefit of the services above is that students will receive better instruction in math, resulting in increased learning, improved test scores, access to higher level math and science courses, higher graduation rates, and more opportunities for students to pursue STEM careers.
3276.population: This project will be able to serve approximately 400 teachers and math coaches in grades K-12 across two districts.
3276.outcome: From this project, both districts should increase the percentage of students scoring proficient or above in mathematics on state assessments (FAST), increase passage rates of the Algebra 1 End of Course exam (thereby increasing graduation rate), and improve teacher quality in the district, as measured by self-surveys, student surveys, and formal evaluations. Better trained teachers and coaches will result in continued student improvement long after the pilot project ends.

3238.organization: The Arc of the St. Johns, Inc.
3238.description: The Arc of the St. Johns, Inc. seeks to design, expand and modernize our transportation maintenance facility at our main campus, located at 2101 Arc Drive, St. Augustine, FL 32084. This project addresses a critical need, as our organization currently maintains a fleet of 66 vehicles in a single-bay, open-air facility built over forty years ago. In the prior fiscal year, our transportation fleet amassed 707,388 miles. The expanded and modernized facility will provide the infrastructure necessary to ensure the reliability and safety of our transportation operations—an essential component in enabling individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities to access the programs and services they depend on every day.
3238.purpose: The funds requested will enable The Arc of the St. Johns, Inc. to meet both the current and future transportation needs of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Reliable and specialized transportation is essential to ensuring our clients can access vital programs, services, and community opportunities. Many of the individuals we serve exhibit challenging behaviors that make it unsafe or impractical for them to use public transportation. Our agency provides a critical safe
3238.activities: The purpose of the funds is to expand and modernize our transportation maintenance facility. This will allow us to meet the current and future transportation needs of our IDD clients.
3238.direct_services: The appropriated funds will provide citizens with intellectual and development disabilities safe and stable transportation for critical daily service they receive through funding from the Agency for Persons with Disabilities.
3238.population: The annual target population will approximately be 300 county citizens with intellectual and developmental disabilities. These citizens would not have consistent and dependable transportation without The Arc of the St. Johns, Inc.
3238.outcome: The appropriation will improve the stability of our fleet which in turn will ensure consistent and safe transportation services to the clients that we serve. Additionally, it will do the following: 1) Reduction in the number of out of service days for our vehicles 2) Provides us the ability to increase out fleet numbers to serve additional citizens in the county. 3) Reduction in costs for The Arc of the St. Johns, Inc. with the outsourcing of maintenance and repair costs.

2934.description: This funding request is expected to complete the state-funded portion of the new facility that will house the USF Bellini College of AI, Cybersecurity & Computing, which opened in Fall 2025 and has more than 3,000 students enrolled and approx. 80 faculty. USF received a record-setting $40 million philanthropic gift to establish the Bellini College, making USF one of the first universities in the nation to launch a dedicated college for artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and computing.
2934.purpose: In Fall 2025, USF formally launched the first college in the state focused on the rapidly evolving fields of artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, and computing. This new facility on the Tampa campus will principally house the USF Bellini College of AI, Cybersecurity & Computing's undergraduate, graduate & certificate programs that prepare students for high-demand careers and innovative research that leads to technological advancements in national and economic security.
2934.activities: This new facility on the Tampa campus will house the new college and present a unique opportunity to leverage the expertise on all 3 campuses of USF. This collaboration will create an interdisciplinary center of excellence in AI, cybersecurity education and research to continue to position Florida and the Tampa Bay region as a global leader in these critical, emerging, and high-paying, high-demand fields.
2934.direct_services: This state-of-the-art facility will be designed to foster innovation & collaboration & allow for the expansion of student programming and enrollments in AI, cybersecurity and computing. It will create a pipeline of highly skilled graduates entering the workforce in high-demand, high-paying jobs. The facility will allow faculty to perform top-tier research in AI & cybersecurity which will enhance n
2934.population: University students are the target population to be served, with the cybersecurity of Florida’s critical infrastructure, economic pillars, and private sector as indirect beneficiaries. Approx. 5,000 students per year are expected to be enrolled in the College once the facility is completed and fully operational.
2934.outcome: Improve quality of education: The Florida Board of Governors' Programs of Strategic Emphasis outlines a critical workforce need for graduates in fields like AI, cybersecurity, and computer science. This college will expand programs in those fields at USF, presenting an opportunity to proactively address the growing student demand in these fields and Florida's workforce needs. Success will be measured by the number of new highly skilled graduates and placements in high-demand jobs in AI, cybersecurity and related fields.

3426.description: In 2018, Flagler Hospital, Inc. launched BRAVE (Be Resilient And Voice Emotions), a youth mental health program to break down mental health stigma and to ensure that all students and families have access to mental health services. Using a hub model and a unified assessment, BRAVE serves as the hub for connection to behavioral health services throughout the state of Florida. BRAVE has access points within schools, behavioral health agencies, and community access points. BRAVE receives referrals directly from the Multi-Tiered System of Support(MTSS), the BRAVE program screens families for the most appropriate behavioral health services and links each family to one of our behavioral health partners for immediate connection to services and continues to support the family throughout treatment, for a minimum of 6 visits. This funding will allow the program to continue to expand to serve all 67
3426.purpose: BRAVE receives referrals directly from the Multi-Tiered System of Support(MTSS), the BRAVE program screens families for the most appropriate behavioral health services and links each family to one of our behavioral health partners for immediate connection to services and continues to support the family throughout treatment, for a minimum of 8 visits. This funding will allow the program to continue to expand to serve all 67 counties in Florida, expanding access for over 2.7 million students.
3426.activities: BRAVE will continue to serve all 67 Florida counties, with a specific focus on expanding to South Florida. This will be accomplished with the existing staff structure put in place last fiscal year in addition to, 3 new BRAVE Community Health Associates, 1 new BRAVE Team Lead, 2 new BRAVE Insurance Navigators and the addition of 1 Co- Responder. In addition to providing behavioral health navigation services to students and their families, Regional BRAVE Supervisors will lead the continued develop
3426.direct_services: Provide a Single point of access to connect with youth behavioral health services across the state of Florida; Social health needs assessment and behavioral health provider eligibility screening; Care Navigation to support family/youth during process of identifying and establishing relationship with behavioral health provider. The Co-responder will start working in St. Johns County to provide addi
3426.population: The BRAVE Program supports students with mental healthcare needs between Kindergarten to Grade 12. With an average referral rate of 2% and 2.8 million students in Florida, this expanded program is expected to serve 56,000 students and families.
3426.outcome: 1. Increase number of students identified (in school) with a behavioral health need that receive at least 1 visit with a behavioral health provider. TARGET= 90% 2. Decrease the length of time between identification of behavioral health need and first appointment with behavioral health provider. TARGET= 50% within 14 days, 90% within 30 days. 3. Maintain a program average of 7% or lower no-show rate for behavioral health appointments. The BRAVE program utilizes an electronic case management/ referral tool to support the coordination of clients. All stakeholders, including the client, have access to the system and are required to input standard data elements. This data is analyzed on a weekly

2782.description: Through its year-round StrongHer Mind, StrongHer Future initiative, TGI provides ongoing empowerment, leadership development, academic success support, financial literacy education, and community engagement opportunities that strengthen mental health and confidence in young women. This continuous programming builds momentum and prepares participants for the highlight of the year—the TGI Summer Program. The four-week, full-day camp serves over 100 young ladies, offering immersive experiences such as college tours, job shadow opportunities, field trips across Central Florida, and intensive workshops in empowerment, leadership, and career exploration. Together, the year-round initiative and summer program create a holistic pipeline of growth, ensuring participants are equipped to thrive academically, professionally, and personally while becoming leaders in their communities.
2782.purpose: Goal 1. Expand Year-Round Empowerment Programming: a) Strengthen StrongHer Mind, StrongHer Future with monthly workshops in leadership, mental health, financial literacy, and academic success. b) Increase participation and consistency of engagement throughout the school year. Goal 2. Deliver a Four-Week Summer Program Serving 100+ Girls: a) Provide immersive experiences including college tours, job shadowing, field trips, and empowerment workshops. b) Ensure equitable access by covering transpor
2782.activities: Monthly Programming: Leadership circles, financial literacy classes, mental health workshops, and community service projects. Summer Camp: Four weeks of full-day sessions with structured curriculum, guest speakers, college tours, and field trips across Central Florida. Career Exploration: Job shadow opportunities, mentorship pairings, and skill-building sessions in communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. Support Services: Transportation, meals, supplies, and scholarships to remove barriers
2782.direct_services: 100+ young women directly served through summer camp and year-round programming. Families and communities benefit from empowered youth who contribute through service projects and leadership initiatives. Local businesses and colleges engaged through partnerships, tours, and shadowing, strengthening community ties and workforce development.
2782.population: The primary target population is female youth in marginalized communities across Central Florida, ages 12-18. The agency will also focus on female youth who may benefit from empowerment, academic support, mental health education, and career exploration. The total reach is approximately 150-175 female youth annually with 50-75 participants engaged in the four week camp and 100+ engaged through monthly workshops, mentorship, and ongoing programming.
2782.outcome: Outcome 1: Increased confidence, leadership skills, and mental health resilience. Measured by: Pre- and post-program surveys, self-assessments, and facilitator evaluations. Outcome 2: Improved academic success and career readiness. Measured by: Tracking GPA improvements, college acceptance rates, job shadow participation, and skill-building milestones. Outcome 3: Strengthened community engagement and civic awareness. Measured by: Participation in service projects, attendance records, and qualitative feedback from families and community partners.

3459.description: PSC is a designated Purple Heart and Yellow Ribbon institution with nearly 21% of its student population military- affiliated (veteran, active duty or veteran/active duty dependent with benefits). To adequately service the men and women who serve our country, we need specialized services at all PSC campuses which will allow greater access for this growing population of military-affiliated students. In Fall 2024, this population was 1,882, and in Fall 2025, it is now 2,089, an 11% growth. In addition, PSC degrees and certificates help this population transition to becoming citizens of Florida with employment in Florida companies.
3459.purpose: The purpose of this project is to expand the services provided at our main campus to all of our satellite campuses. The military-affiliated (veterans, active duty and veteran/active duty dependents with benefits) population is significant in our service area. We have seen that in transitioning to civilian status, this population greatly benefits from assistance and counseling on academic and career paths as well as accessing their military benefits. When services are provided, the College has se
3459.activities: The services provided are a combination of assistance and counseling related to understanding and exercising military benefits and finding the best path for academic and career success that leads to employment and residency in our two county service area.
3459.direct_services: The direst service will be provided to the military-affiliated students who enroll and matriculate through to degrees and certificates. This also directly benefits Florida businesses with highly motivated and now properly skilled employees.
3459.population: The target population is the military-affiliated students (veteran, active duty & veteran/active duty dependent with benefits). Currently that population in Fall 2025 is 2,089, nearly 21% of our total students.
3459.outcome: The expected benefit is increasing the number of military-affiliated students to obtain degrees and certificates so they can become permanent employees and citizens in our two county service area and growing the state of Florida with talented and motivated people.

2825.organization: The School Board of Seminole County
2825.description: The opening of a Center for Early Learning in the Sanford-Midway community will serve the entire Seminole County region. Through the delivery of daily high-quality early learning experiences and training & support for parents, guardians, and members of the Seminole County community, the district seeks to promote long-term impact on the academic and economic success of the region.
2825.purpose: The renovation and repurpose of a vacated elementary campus for use as a Center for Early Learning will welcome young learners and their families in the Sanford-Midway community to engage in active development of their academic, social, & motor skills. As reported in the Annual Review of Public Health in April 2023, preschool education for 3- and 4-year-olds can reduce educational gaps and improve health and even lead to longer lifespans - the ultimate goal of this appropriation request.
2825.activities: The opening of a Center for Early Learning in the Sanford-Midway community will serve the entire Seminole County region. Through the delivery of daily high-quality early learning experiences and training & support for parents, guardians, and members of the Seminole County community, the district seeks to promote long-term impact on the academic and economic success of the region.
2825.direct_services: This project will provide direct services to students, families, and the Seminole County community include the delivery of daily high-quality early learning experiences, parent/guardian training, and collaboration with state/local agencies to promote community awareness and advocacy.
2825.population: This early learning program will provide critical literacy and child development education to young learners as well as support parents and families who are looking for high-quality early learning options.
2825.outcome: The impact of early learning on students' future success is well documented through thousands of research studies. Additionally, there is significant local demand for increased choice options for early learning.

3241.agency: Department of Business and Professional Regulation
3241.description: The goal of this marketing campaign is to extend tourism seasons beyond the typical patterns and support local communities with in-state visitors. This campaign is nimble and can respond following a natural disaster. Funds are transferred from the DBPR Hotels and Restaurants Trust Fund through Visit Florida to contract with the Florida Restaurant & Lodging Association (FRLA) to develop a coordinated marketing, media and events program to promote Florida tourism to residents of the state. The campaign has a private matching program and is conducted throughout the state, as approved by and monitored by Visit Florida and FRLA.
3241.purpose: This program will support the tourism and hospitality industry in smaller markets and during off season months. The private match of program dollars demonstrates support from organizations and entities across the state. Additionally, anecdotal support is available through letters and testimonials of previous partners.
3241.activities: Local financial impact to the tourism, dining and lodging industry as a result of marketing efforts and events.
3241.direct_services: Services for citizens include (but are not limited to) recreation, education and promoting the hospitality industry.
3241.population: Events have a positive financial impact to local food, hospitality, cultural and retail industries. Florida citizens and businesses benefit.
3241.outcome: These programs often assist with filling gaps in the season or extending tourism seasons, which helps local regions support the workforce. Event participating and attendees can be measured.

3605.organization: Lutheran Services of Florida, Inc. d/b/a LSF
3605.description: Research shows that anti-human trafficking programs incorporating peer mentors are highly effective in building social capital and improving participant outcomes. Peer support is closely linked to enhanced psychological well-being, resilience, and the prevention of re-victimization and recidivism. Peer-led approaches foster meaningful connections and provide survivor-centered, trauma-informed support that complements traditional professional services. The Anti-Human Trafficking Survivor Mentor Certificate Program directly addresses the need for survivor mentorship by equipping mentors with the skills and knowledge necessary to support trauma recovery, empower mentees and practice self-care.
3605.purpose: The Anti-Human Trafficking Survivor Mentor Certificate Program directly addresses the need for survivor mentorship by equipping mentors with the skills and knowledge to support trauma recovery, empower mentees and practice self- care. This ensures that mentors are not only effective in their roles but are also protected from teh long-term effects of vicarious trauma.
3605.activities: Funds will support creating and implementing a statewide certification program from survivor mentors. This includes developing a specialized curriculum co-authored by survivors. Training tools will include: identifying trafficking indicators, trauma-informed care for survivors, legal frameworks, victim rights and coordinated response strategies. Ongoing support to trainees post-training, evaluation to monitor and measure impact. The curriculum will be piloted with a cohort of survivors, with adj
3605.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services including: 1. Trauma-Informed Peer Mentorship, 2. Specialized Training for Mentors, 3. Support for Vulnerable Populations, 4. Community Awareness and Education, 5. Improved Community Safety and 6. Empowerment Through Skills Development.
3605.population: The target population served by this project includes survivors of human trafficking who have exited the life and wish to give back to the community as survivor mentors. These trained mentors will in turn serve 150 other victims/survivors, community partners and stakeholders of human trafficking helpingn to support and connect them with resources. The project is expected to create approximately 15 statewide trainers seeking certification in the first year, plus the survivors they will each suppo
3605.outcome: Reduction in incarceration costs, improved quality of life, improved survivor outcomes and an employment boost provided by this certification. These benefits will be measured by pre and post surveys given to training participants prior to the training and one year post training.

3242.description: Investing in advanced technology is about profoundly transforming the educational experience to better prepare students of all socio-economic backgrounds for the future. The Okaloosa County School District is one of the state’s top performing districts; however, adding much-needed additional instructional technology to our classrooms would provide the tools necessary to allow our students to climb even higher. With the addition in every classroom of a Clear-Touch Board, a teacher iPad with an Apple pencil, and a set of Virtual Reality glasses loaded with Prisms software (in Math and Science classrooms), Okaloosa School District would be able to provide an engaging, dynamic and interactive environment that will allow all of our students, regardless of socio-economic background, to thrive.
3242.purpose: The goal of equipping 23 classrooms in low socio-economic areas with these pieces of instructional technology is to create a more engaging, equitable and effective learning environment that not only increases state testing scores, but also prepares all students for the challenges and opportunities of the future.
3242.activities: Classroom instruction using advanced technology creates an engaging, equitable, effective learning environment, boosting test scores and readiness. Clear Touch Boards provide interactive lessons, teacher iPads enhance mobility and engagement, and VR glasses with Prisms software transform Math and Science through immersive experiences. These tools foster deeper understanding and student success.
3242.direct_services: Investing in classroom technology will facilitate high-engagement, interactive instruction, boosting student test scores and the Okaloosa School District’s ranking, making the county more attractive and useful to relocating families, while preparing all students for the modern workforce, equipping them with essential skills that benefit employers and strengthen the local community.
3242.population: 23 classrooms (approximately 600 students and their families, along with 23 classroom teachers) strategically selected in schools with high free/reduced lunch rates. Indirectly, all members of Okaloosa County will be served when these students enter the workforce as adults.
3242.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is that student scores will improve and the Okaloosa School District will be able to move into the top 5 of all school districts in the state of Florida. This will be measured annually by the components that are used by the state of Florida to determine school rankings.

3497.description: JESSIE'S PLACE COORDINATES THE MULTI-DISCIPLINARY INVESTIGATIVE PROCESS OF CHILD ABUSE CASES WITH DCF, LAW ENFORCEMENT AND THE CHILD PROTECTION TEAM. IT IS A CHILD-FRIENDLY FACILITY THAT RESPONDS TO CHILD VICTIMS OF ABUSE, NEGLECT, DRUG-ENDANGERMENT, AND VIOLENCE. JESSIE'S PLACE OFFERS TRAUMA-FOCUSED THERAPY AND ADVOCACY SERVICES TO THESE CHILDREN AND THEIR FAMILIES. IN 2025, JESSIE'S PLACE PROVIDED SERVICES TO 455 CHILDREN AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS INCLUDING 2,166 HOURS OF INDIVIDUAL THERAPY, APPROXIMATELY 600 HOURS OF GROUP THERAPY AND EDUCATION, AND 4,338 ADVOCACY SERVICES. WE ALSO PROVIDED PREVENTION CLASSES TO 4,060 STUDENTS IN CITRUS COUNTY SCHOOLS. IN 2025, WE RECEIVED STATE APPROPRIATIONS TO PLAN AND DESIGN A 7,500 SF RENOVATION AND EXPANSION OF OUR BUILDING. THE DESIGN WILL BE COMPLETED IN THE 2025 FISCAL YEAR. WE ARE REQUESTING FUNDING FOR CONSTRUCTION COSTS IN THE 2026-2027 FIS
3497.purpose: THE FUNDS WILL BE USED TO RENOVATE AND EXPAND OUR CURRENT FACILITY BY 7,500 SQUARE FEET. THE PROJECT WILL ALLOW US TO ADD MORE OFFICES AND THERAPY ROOMS SO CHILD VICTIMS OF ABUSE ARE NOT WAITING TO BEGIN THE THERAPY AND SUPPORT SERVICES THEY NEED TO OVERCOME THE TRAUMA OF THEIR ABUSE. OUR MAIN FACILITY LACKS THERAPY ROOMS AND OFFICE SPACE TO HOUSE SUFFICIENT STAFF TO MEET THE DEMAND FOR OUR SERVICES. WE NOW HAVE STAFF IN MULTIPLE LOCATIONS MAKING COMPREHENSIVE SERVICES MORE DIFFICULT TO PROVIDE,
3497.activities: EACH YEAR AN AVERAGE OF 500 CHILD ABUSE VICTIMS AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS RECEIVE SERVICES AT OUR CENTER. THESE FUNDS WILL ALLOW US TO INCREASE AND EXPAND ALL OF OUR EXISTING SERVICES AS WELL AS PROVIDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO ADD NEW SERVICES. OUR EXISTING SERVICES INCLUDE INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY AND GROUP THERAPIES, VICTIM ADVOCACY FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES, ABUSE PREVENTION EDUCATION, COMMUNITY EDUCATION, THERAPEUTIC SUPERVISED VISITATION, MULTI-DISCIPLINARY CASE REVIEW, FORENSIC INTERVIEWS, AND FORENS
