This lead to widespread destruction across the County and resulted in six tornado-related fatalities and one storm related fatality. A proper unified command vehicle will significantly improve emergency response capabilities by enabling faster decision-making, better coordination, more efficient deployment of resources, and ultimately saving lives by reducing recovery times during disasters.

3683.activities: This vehicle provides a centralized hub where responders and decision-makers can coordinate, communicate, and manage resources on site and in real time for emergency response, disaster management, and large-scale events.

3412.description: G3 Village is a moderate-income rental community for adults age 50+. They will be purpose-filled in their third quarter, living in a sustainable, agricultural homestead of 40 individual units of living. This independent living community will be service-minded with a modest worldview of taking care of the earth, growing plants, eating the harvest from those gardens and honoring their neighbors. Animal husbandry will include rotational grazing and well managed care. The land will actually be better in 15 years than when we start the project. People will find camaraderie, health, and joy in a lifestyle they enjoy and can afford.

3513.direct_services: Volunteering, and partnering with agencies to provide jobs as an introduction into becoming a productive citizen. Workforce Training, Food Management Certification and Social / Behavioral Education.
3513.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, Grade School students, High School Students, University and College students, Currently or formerly incarcerated persons, Drug offenders in criminal justice, Victims of Crime
3513.outcome: The exposure and enrichment which will be provided through the program. It will allow our participants to have exposure in areas which are fundamental to human growth and development. This can be used as a gauge for growth that follows, assessment before and after as well as evaluating their activities. These activities which will be qualified mentors and coaches to work throughout and deter bad behaviors.

3336.organization: Jacksonville Historic Naval Ship Assn DBA
3336.description: The Jacksonville Historic Naval Ship Assn now DBA Florida Naval Ship Historic Assn (due to the number of statewide visitors to the ex-USS Orleck (DD886) in Jacksonville and the over 20 Veterans Museum kiosks throughout the State requests funding to greatly expand one of the most STEM worthy areas of the ship (the Communications compartments), provide increased access to new areas on board for students and the public, such as the After Fireroom, and 5 Veterans Museum Kiosks.
3336.purpose: Expand opportunities for more student and public access by the refurbishment and renovation of the entire Radio Communication compartments to better provide real time STEM experiences for students and the public, 5 Veterans Museum Kiosks, and access to the After Fireroom.
3336.activities: Ongoing STEM projects related to shipboard communications, access to the aft fireroom where two of the ship's four boilers are located, and the manufacturing of at least 5 Veterans Museum Kiosks where Veterans stories are displayed after collection.
3336.direct_services: Classes in Seamanship, Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Math + History (SSTEAM+H), better access to historic locations on the ship such as Radio Central and supporting compartments, and also the ability to house overnight groups such as Scouts and veterans' groups. As the ONLY Naval Warship Museum in Florida, residents of the State will not have to travel to Charleston, SC nor Mobile, AL to
3336.population: To date, public attendance includes visitors from all 67 Florida Counties, all 50 States, and 465 Countries. These include: Veterans and their families, school age children and school tours, Title 10 disadvantaged children (some of whom have never been on the St Johns River), and persons with disabilities. In other words, all organized groups, events of honor, and the general public will always be welcome.
3336.outcome: Methodology employed will include the number of persons attending general STEAM+H classes, number of school tours for all ages, and surveys with direct feedback.

3421.description: This program educates and empowers the most vulnerable children (and their parents) to prevent them from becoming victims of online exploitation and child trafficking. Our program saves lives by creating connection, decreasing isolation, interrupting the 'by stander' affect putting the power of prevention in their hands.
3421.purpose: Our Impact Goals and Objectives are: 1. Increase awareness and educate the youth about human trafficking, online exploitation by learning the signs of trafficking, recruitment and grooming tactics, what actions can prevent it. 2. Demonstrate comprehension and knowledge of the topic by taking a post-test 3. Express what they learned in a small group setting through art and group sharing
3421.activities: Our program does more than educate about exploitation, it saves lives. This is accomplished through powerful and engaging conversation using the Socratic method of teaching, where the students do the critical thinking solving this issue over 3 50-minute or 2 90-minute sessions. Our programs increase knowledge, build social interaction skills, develop social media, online gaming and chatbot safety skills and transform attitudes, creating an extraordinary learning experience. Using multimedia we e
3421.direct_services: Our team delivers trauma-informed, youth-centered training designed to interrupt algorithm-driven pathways that expose young people to online grooming, manipulation, and irreversible harm. Over the past 10 years, we have educated more than 46,000 youth on the tactics used to lure them into situations they would never knowingly choose. Through this education, students learn they are not alone, that
3421.population: Our target population focuses on under served youth, middle school, high school students, including foster youth, youth engaged with the juvenile justice system and other at risk youth in our state.
3421.outcome: Our expected outcomes are: Increased knowledge of human trafficking indicators & improved personal safety; taking new actions proposed in the training, advocating for themselves or other along with learning and using the resources shared for assistance Methodology used: 1. Pre-tests and post-test to determine knowledge retained; 2. Issue a follow up survey 8 weeks after completion of the program to evaluate long-term impact.

3216.description: Funds will be used for the development and design to create the necessary activities to maximize self-help and independent living skills, provide greater autonomy, and empower enhanced connectedness, integration, and self- sufficiency for residents with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities and related disorders. In addition, funding will be used for transportation to support greater access to the community at large, as well as for additional recreational and developmental activities.
3216.purpose: Based on best practices, this programming supports individuals with IDD, providing assistance with activities of daily living to maximize independent living skills, autonomy, self-sufficiency, and community participation.
3216.activities: EmpowerAbility Programming (adaptive fitness classes, life skills workshops, social events/game nights, creative & programming arts, gardening program, community outings, community-based 5K outings, peer mentorship, & leadership, weekend programming). Accessibility Services, Marketing & Outreach, Program Supplies & Software, Community Guide Membership Scholarship.
3216.direct_services: Direct services include EmpowerAbility Programming for life skills development, health, and social wellness; accessibility services; and community integration activities.
3216.population: Target population is adults with Intellectual, Developmental, and other related Disabilities. Services will be provided to between 60 and 100 individuals.
3216.outcome: The program will deliver improved physical health, improved mental health, improved education, improved transportation, and improved safety for adults with IDD. These improvements will be measured and evaluated using a variety of tools, including but not limited to self-reporting questionnaires, measurements of participation in individual and community activities, assessments and feedback provided by program staff and health care professionals.

3362.description: Funds will support system evaluation, preliminary engineering, design, survey, permitting, and related technical services for critical upgrades to the City’s Water Treatment Plant, including pumping system improvements, process controls, and elevated storage tank modifications. These improvements will modernize aging infrastructure, improve reliability and efficiency, and strengthen long-term operational sustainability.
3362.purpose: The project will improve the reliability, efficiency, and safety of the City’s potable water system through critical upgrades to the Water Treatment Plant’s pumping systems, process controls, and elevated storage tank. These improvements will modernize aging infrastructure and operational sustainability.
3362.activities: The project will include system evaluation, preliminary engineering, design, survey, permitting, and preparation of technical documentation for WTP improvements. Work includes evaluating and upgrading pumping and electrical systems, integrating modern process controls and monitoring equipment, and assessing elevated storage tank modifications to enhance system efficiency and performance.
3362.direct_services: The project will ensure reliable, safe drinking water service to residents, businesses, and community facilities. Improved system controls and monitoring will provide consistent water pressure and quality, reduce service disruptions, and conserve resources, directly benefiting customers and protecting public health.
3362.population: The project will directly serve Crescent City’s approximately 1,700 residents and all customers connected to the municipal water system, including local businesses, schools, and critical facilities. The benefits extend to visitors and surrounding communities that rely on Crescent City’s water infrastructure for regional stability and growth.
3362.outcome: The project will enhance system reliability, improve water quality, and reduce operational costs. Success will be measured by decreased maintenance incidents, reduced non-revenue water losses, improved water pressure and flow consistency, and compliance with FDEP water quality standards verified through sampling, monitoring, and operational performance records.

3517.organization: Agudath Israel of America, Florida Office
3517.description: This project will expand the Florida Ozer Center's capacity to deliver comprehensive, statewide resource navigation and case management services. The initiative will assist families in accessing healthcare coverage, food and housing assistance, employment and job placement support, senior care resources, and specialized guidance for families of children with special needs. By connecting families to critical programs and services, the Florida Ozer Center will promote long-term stability, economic self-sufficiency, and improved quality of life across communities throughout the state.
3517.purpose: The requested funds will enable the Florida Ozer Center to provide individualized guidance to families on available community and state resources; assist residents in navigating and applying for benefit programs and health insurance coverage; offer personalized support to families of children with special needs; guide seniors in accessing health, housing, and elder care resources; and host educational events and webinars focused on financial literacy, job readiness, and employment networking—emp
3517.activities: Activities will include one-on-one consultations to assess individual needs; assistance with applications for benefits and resources; guidance on healthcare plan selection; and referrals to community partners and agencies for additional assistance. The Center will also conduct outreach and host community workshops on topics such as financial literacy, job preparedness, and employment networking. Specialized services will be provided for families of children with special needs and for seniors see
3517.direct_services: Direct services will include one-on-one consultations to advise individuals on available resources and assist them in accessing those programs through hands-on guidance and support throughout the process. The Center will also provide financial literacy education, job networking assistance, and related guidance to help individuals achieve long- term stability and self-sufficiency.
3517.population: The project will serve lower-income families and individuals experiencing hardship due to a variety of circumstances such as divorce, illness, or loss of employment. It will also support families of children with disabilities and special needs, as well as seniors in need of guidance and care navigation. The Florida Ozer Center anticipates assisting more than 1,100 individuals annually through one-on-one consultations, in addition to reaching hundreds more through educational events and community
3517.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is increased stability, economic self-sufficiency, and overall well-being for Florida families through improved access to essential resources such as healthcare coverage, food and housing assistance, employment opportunities, and support for seniors and children with special needs. Outcomes will be measured through comprehensive case management tracking, documenting the number of families served, services provided, and programs accessed, along with estimated financial savings, participant feedback, to evaluate sustained impact over time.

3119.description: The Emerald Trail is a planned 30-mile network of interconnected bikeways and multi-use paths designed to connect Jacksonville’s historic neighborhoods with key community destinations. Once complete, the trail will link 14 schools, numerous parks, local waterways, and the St. Johns River Northbank Riverwalk, creating a safe and accessible transportation and recreation corridor.
3119.purpose: The Emerald Trail is a 30-mile network of interconnected bikeways and multi-use paths connecting most of Jacksonville's historic neighborhoods, 14 schools, numerous parks, the St. Johns River, Northbank Riverwalk and waterways. This segment links Gateway Development/future Publix at the intersection of Hogan and Union Sts. through the Transit Oriented Development at Rosa Parks Station, to FSCJ Downtown and finally to Hogan's Creek.
3119.activities: The Emerald Trail network will comprise multi-use paths, street furniture, pedestrian-level lighting, wayfinding branded signage and pedestrian improvements at street crossings. It is being designed to encourage recreation, bicycle commuting and community connections among Jacksonville's historic neighborhoods and Downtown.
3119.direct_services: New multi-use paths, enhanced pedestrian crossings of streets, landscaping, pedestrian-level lighting, and minor drainage repairs will be designed and constructed as a part of this project.
3119.outcome: Improvement of physical health - determined by the number of bikers, joggers, etc. along the Trail. Enrich cultural experience - public meetings have demonstrated a strong community interest in the Trail. Improve transportation conditions - increase in bicycle commuters can be correlated with a decrease in vehicular commuters and reduce pollution. Increase in tourism - attracts new and younger residents who prefer urban living will demonstrate this outcome.

3490.description: Funding will provide access for ALS patients to receive comprehensive quality care through ALS Multidisciplinary Clinics in Florida. There are eight certified centers in FL: Mayo Clinic Jacksonville, UF Health Jacksonville, University of Miami, Holy Cross Health, Orlando Health, University of South FL, Nova SE, and UF Health Gainesville. This multidisciplinary approach is proven to increase life expectancy for ALS patients by 40%. The impact to the State is a reduction in costs in community-based/home-based care, Medicaid, and hospitalizations as well as increased federal/private investments in research and increase in medical tourism.
3490.purpose: Funding will expand access for Floridians living with ALS to receive high-quality, multidisciplinary care through eight ALS clinics statewide. This proven model improves quality of life, extends survival, and enhances access to needed supports and assistive devices. It also provides essential respite services for caregivers, reducing burnout and helping families sustain care at home, ultimately lowering state costs related to Medicaid, home-based care, and hospitalizations.
3490.activities: ALS patients will be provided with evidence-based care in a supportive, family-oriented atmosphere. Because ALS patients have difficulty traveling, the model brings professionals from multiple healthcare disciplines and allows an ALS patient to receive all necessary care during a single visit. The respite program will provide caregiver relief, reducing burnout and need for long-term care.
3490.direct_services: Physical therapy, neurology, respiratory therapy, occupational therapy, nutrition, speech/language pathologist and social work consultation. The respite program will provide in-home caregiver relief through home health, private duty or self-hired care.
3490.population: It is estimated that there are nearly 2,000 people living with ALS in Florida. The number of people treated for ALS during a given year is actually much greater because some pass away during the year and are replaced by others who are newly diagnosed. Additionally, military veterans are twice as likely to be diagnosed with ALS than those without a military background so this program supports our veterans as well. In fact, ALS is considered a "service-related disease" by the US Department of Defe
3490.outcome: Decreased costs related to community-based and home-based care services because ALS patients can live independently longer; reduced drains on Medicaid; reduction in frequency and length of hospital stays; less burden on transportation services for the medical needy thanks to coordination of care. Additionally, the program helps to increase research investment from the Federal Government and the Pharmaceutical Industry thanks to improved access to ALS patients.

3338.description: Supports looping, improved fire flows, and approximately 40 future residential connections. Increase sytem reliability by creating distribution main loops that 1) raise available fire flow at end-of-line locations, 2) open capactity headroom for new standard residential connections, and 3) reduces out of service customers during main breaks.
3338.purpose: Supports looping, improved fire flows, and approximately 40 future residential connections.
3338.activities: The Town will be able to offer water service to those residences along the line.
3338.direct_services: The Town will be able to offer water service to those residences along the line.
3338.population: 40 Residential customers will directly be effected. 2642 Residences potentially will continue to receive water services when system lines are down for repair.
3338.outcome: Benefits will be future revenues and customer satisfaction. Methodology will be measured by how many residences will not be out of service when lines go down.

3443.description: The City of Sebring is requesting funding to support the design and hardening of a recently purchased building that will serve as the new City Hall. This facility will house key municipal functions, including administrative offices, council chambers, and public service areas, making it the central hub for government operations and community engagement. Built under older codes, it requires storm hardening, roofing upgrades, reinforced windows/doors, elevator repairs, backup power, and accessibility compliance. Relocating here allows repurposing of the old City Hall for county use, saving taxpayer money and opening other property for business development.
3443.purpose: The goal is to protect the life, health, and safety of employees, elected officials, and the citizenry by creating a resilient City Hall that safeguards administrative and civic functions, ensures service continuity, and promotes economic development through repurposing of property in this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3443.activities: The City will secure professional and construction services to harden and modernize City Hall, including replacing the aging roof, installing storm-rated windows and doors, and addressing structural, accessibility, and security needs. The project will create a resilient and secure facility that safeguards employees and visitors while ensuring continuity of daily municipal operations. By consolidating services in a safe, efficient space, the City enhances public access, strengthens government ope
3443.direct_services: Safe, accessible City Hall for community engagement, permit services, and government interactions, with uninterrupted operations during disasters.
3443.population: The target population is the community of Sebring which is a Financial Disadvantaged Municipality (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) located in a Rural Area of Critical Economic Concern/Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes); Greater than 11,000 residents and an additional 13,000 utility customers from outside the city limits will be served.
3443.outcome: The expected outcomes include a safe, resilient, and accessible City Hall that protects employees, elected officials, and the public during severe weather while ensuring continuity of administrative operations, City Council meetings, and community services. Upgrades like storm-hardened windows and doors, roof replacement, elevator repairs, backup power installation, and ADA compliance will reduce long-term maintenance expenses and enable repurposing of existing City properties for county use and economic redevelopment, yielding taxpayer savings and fostering growth in this Rural Area of Opportunity. Outcomes will be measured via post-design and post-construction code compliance audits, facil

3380.description: The Sunrise Lane District Streetscape Improvements Project will revitalize a small business district at Sunrise Lane, Breakers Avenue, and NE 9th Street, near the intersection of SR A1A and Sunrise Boulevard. Improvements include widened sidewalks, enhanced lighting, safer pedestrian crosswalks, expanded landscaping, traffic calming measures, decorative pavement, murals, and new entryway features. These enhancements will create a safer, more attractive, and welcoming environment that supports local businesses, draws visitors, boosts tourism, and improves quality of life for nearby residents. By addressing safety concerns and underutilized storefronts, the project will transform the district into a vibrant commercial hub and strengthen its role as a key connector to Fort Lauderdale Beach and the surrounding community.
3380.purpose: The requested funds will support streetscape improvements in the Sunrise Lane District to enhance safety, accessibility, and economic vitality. By upgrading sidewalks, lighting, crosswalks, landscaping, and entryway features, the project will create a more inviting environment that attracts visitors, supports existing businesses, encourages new investment, and transforms the area into a vibrant, safe, and economically thriving destination for residents and tourists.
3380.activities: The funds will be used to implement streetscape enhancements including widened sidewalks, upgraded pedestrian crosswalks, enhanced lighting for safety, landscaping and urban canopy expansion, decorative pavement and mural installations, traffic calming measures, and new entryway features. These activities will create a safer, more attractive environment that supports local businesses, encourages tourism, and improves quality of life for nearby residents.
3380.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with safer pedestrian access through widened sidewalks, improved crosswalks, and enhanced lighting; a more attractive and welcoming public space with landscaping, murals, and decorative features; and an economically revitalized district that supports local businesses, tourism, and neighborhood livability.
3380.population: The project serves residents of adjacent condominiums, patrons of the anchor hotel, local businesses, and visitors to the nearby beach and SR A1A corridor. By revitalizing a key small business district, the improvements will directly benefit thousands of residents and employees in the area while attracting tens of thousands of tourists and visitors annually to the district.
3380.outcome: The project will transform the Sunrise Lane District into a safe, vibrant, and economically thriving destination. Benefits include improved pedestrian safety and accessibility, enhanced neighborhood aesthetics, increased business activity, higher property values, and growth in sales and tourism tax revenues. Outcomes will be measured by tracking pedestrian counts and safety metrics, monitoring business occupancy and sales tax data, evaluating property value trends, and collecting community and visitor feedback to assess satisfaction with the revitalized district.

3352.description: This project aims to construct the Lion's Camp Education Center at the Jacksonville Zoo and Botanical Gardens to provide educational programs and enhanced visitor experiences.
3352.purpose: The funds will be used to construct the Lion's Camp Education Center at the Jacksonville Zoo and Botanical Gardens, creating a dedicated facility for educational programs, science workshops, career events and community engagement that promote workforce development and enhance visitor experiences statewide.
3352.activities: The Center will offer statewide science workshops, STEAM-focused educational programs, career exploration events, and community engagement activities that provide hands-on learning experiences and promote workforce development.
3352.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from expanded educational programming, hands-on workshops, career development sessions, and community events, giving participants access to STEAM learning opportunities and workforce skills that enhance quality of life and economic mobility.
3352.population: The project will serve students (pre-K through college), educators, workforce participants, and families across Florida. Thousands of individuals are expected to participate annually in workshops, programs, and events.
3352.outcome: The expected outcomes include enhanced STEAM education and workforce readiness for participants, increased community engagement and tourism, and improved access to hands-on learning. Outcomes will be measured by tracking attendance and participation numbers, surveying participants for satisfaction and learning gains, counting the number and diversity of programs delivered, and monitoring educational or career advancement metrics such as enrollment in STEM fields or job placements.

3379.description: The requested funds would allow for the completion of Complete Street Project- Construction for Bougainvilla Drive and Poinciana Street. The second phase of this construction project will include stormwater, landscape and hard scape improvements on Bougainvillea Drive and Poinciana Street. The project will maximize water retention capacity, reduce resources to maintain landscaping, and reduce the risk of flooding
3379.purpose: Roadway and drainage improvements to maximize water retention capacity, reduce the risk of flooding, property damage and public safety hazards on the roadway and for better emergency vehicle access as the roadway serves as the main access road for the fire department.
3379.activities: Roadway reconstruction, construction of stormwater system, installation of catch basins, landscape improvements
3379.direct_services: Improved stormwater system to reduce flooding, protect water quality, minimize runoff and erosion on properties. The project will also enhance public safety by mitigating flooding that impedes entryway/exit access of the Town's fire station.
3379.population: The Town has approximately 6,200 residents and the population swells to over 10,000 during peak season. The Town is also home to many popular businesses as it is a popular tourist destination.
3379.outcome: Improved stormwater management- measured by: reduction in the overall intensity and duration of the flooding impacts that are occurring on the roadway. Improved transportation conditions- measured by: accident data, pedestrian activit , resident surveys, reduced flooding intensity and duration on roadways. Improved public safety- measured by: emergency response times during and following rain/flood events.

3343.description: Florida Humanities annually develops programs and resources that preserve Florida's rich history, promote civic engagement, and inspire reflection on our state's future. Funds will provide free accessible programming for cultural organizations across the state that reflect our state's role in the 250th anniversary of our nation.
3343.purpose: The funds will support programs and resources developed by Florida Humanities to preserve Florida’s rich history, promote civic engagement, and inspire reflection on our state's future, especially in commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the United States.
3343.activities: Florida Humanities will deliver free accessible programming for cultural organizations statewide, including educational events, public lectures, exhibits, and resources that highlight Florida’s role in the nation's history and encourage civic dialogue.
3343.direct_services: Citizens will receive public programming such as free lectures, exhibits, and cultural events, along with educational materials that deepen understanding of Florida’s history and heritage.
3343.population: The project serves Floridians statewide by partnering with cultural organizations across the state; thousands of residents are expected to participate in programs and events during the 250th anniversary commemoration.
3343.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased public awareness of Florida’s historical contributions and enhanced civic engagement. Success will be measured through attendance figures, participant feedback, and surveys assessing increased knowledge and engagement.

3488.organization: Dr. Stanley and Pearl Goodman JFS of
3488.description: This funding will expand GJFS' wraparound services to support 200 vulnerable adults in Broward County, focusing on Holocaust survivors and those 60+ who've experienced trauma. Broward is home to 1,200 Holocaust survivors and GJFS serves approximately 800 annually. Clients will receive personalized care plans including personal assistance, care coordination, nutritional support and transportation. The goal is to help these populations age with dignity, maintain independence, and access essential services at no cost.
3488.purpose: The specific goal that will be achieved is improvement of overall quality of life for Holocaust survivors and adults 60 and older who have experienced trauma.
3488.activities: The activities and services that will be provided to meet the intended purpose of these funds will support the expansion of wraparound services for vulnerable adults in Broward County, specifically targeting Holocaust survivors and older adults aged 60+ who have experienced trauma. Services provided will include personal in-home assistance, case management, transportation to medical appointments, and personalized care plans. The goal is to help these populations maintain independence, age with d
3488.direct_services: The direct services that will be provided to citizens by the appropriation project include personal assistance, case management and transportation services.
3488.population: The target population served by this project are Holocaust survivors and adults 60 and over who have experienced trauma. GJFS expects to serve 200 vulnerable adults with this funding.
3488.outcome: GJFS will measure service outcomes through client surveys, care coordinator assessments, and service utilization data (personal assistance hours, transportation). Mental health outcomes will be tracked via pre/post surveys and assessments on emotional well-being and isolation, alongside engagement metrics. Service utilization, including transportation trips and wait times, will also be monitored, with client satisfaction surveys evaluating the services. Overall impact will be measured by individuals served, job creation, healthcare benefits (reduced hospitalizations), and financial relief (reduced out-of-pocket costs), while focusing on mobility and community participation.

3346.description: The project aims to install equipment to upgrade existing passive stormwater ponds into dynamic outflow-controlled systems that ingest weather forecasting and real-time sensing for a variety of objectives (see 13a, specific purpose).
3346.purpose: Project objectives include the restoration of the natural hydraulic connection and function of the Indian River Lagoon. The benefits include improvement to water quality, mitigation of nuisance flooding, and improvement to downstream habitat.
3346.activities: Stormwater ponds will be upgraded with CMAC and other equipment to achieve the purposes of stormwater management, water quality improvement, flood mitigation, hydraulic connection, and habitat improvement.
3346.direct_services: Stormwater management services will be provided.
3346.population: An estimated 1.6 million residents within the Indian River Lagoon watershed will be served.
3346.outcome: Outcomes include restored natural hydrology, improved habitat conditions, decreased algal blooms and seagrass die- off events, reduced flood risk, increased economic activity, increased available detention capacity before storm events, aquifer recharge, and reduced nutrient and sediment loading to the Indian River Lagoon. These outcomes will be measured by coordinated water quality monitoring, reporting of flow dynamics of operated system vs. passive system, real-time water level monitoring, documentation of flooding incidents pre- and post-CMAC installation, integration with NOAA weather data, community surveys tracking flooding impacts, comparison of actual vs. modeled flood reduction usin

3301.description: The No Limits Method is an evidence-based framework under Therapeutic Education, designed to revolutionize instruction and care for students with disabilities. This funding will support an initiative that will provide an extensive, multi-phase professional training program for educators, therapists, and paraprofessionals, focusing on the integration of therapeutic practices within the classroom environment. Participants will learn to address physical, cognitive, and communicative barriers through individualized strategies, adaptive equipment, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The training promotes a deeper understanding of how movement, positioning, and sensory input impact learning and independence. The goal is to produce measurable improvements in student outcomes and strengthen educator effectiveness.
3301.purpose: Funding will support the implementation and expansion of the No Limits Method, an evidence-based therapeutic education framework that enhances learning and participation for students with disabilities. The initiative will deliver professional development for educators and therapists, and integrate adaptive, ADA-compliant tools to improve cognitive, communicative, and functional skills, strengthen instructional quality, improve educator retention, and create sustainable program impact.
3301.activities: Funds will expand the No Limits Method training system via multi-level digital training modules that equip educators, therapists, and administrators with practical strategies for teaching neurodivergent students to bridge gaps between therapy and instruction. Activities include trainings and evaluations to enhance instructional quality, collaboration, and outcomes for students with disabilities.
3301.direct_services: Funding will provide ADA-compliant training, tools, and support for educators and therapists to address students’ physical, cognitive, and communicative needs. The initiative enhances accessibility, student participation, and independence while improving staff retention and advancing education statewide. Content will integrate into DOE systems to ensure scalability, sustainability, and improved ed
3301.population: The project serves students with developmental and physical disabilities, including autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, genetic syndromes, traumatic brain injuries, and other neurodevelopmental disorders. It also supports educators, therapists, and paraprofessionals working with this population. Through statewide implementation, the program will impact thousands of students and hundreds of professionals annually, improving instructional quality and advancing exceptional education practices.
3301.outcome: The project will improve educational, physical, cognitive, communicative, and behavioral outcomes for students with disabilities through the No Limits Method under Therapeutic Education. Training equips educators and therapists to integrate therapy and education, enhancing engagement, regulation, and independence. Outcomes will be measured through pre/post assessments, progress tracking, and educator surveys—advancing greater understanding in the world of exceptional education.

3579.description: The City of Dunedin proposes replacing a non-redundant 100-year-old cast-iron water main beneath Bayshore Boulevard (Alt. U.S. 19 / SR 595) from San Salvador Drive to Buena Vista Drive N. The existing pipe is highly susceptible to corrosion and contamination. Replacement grossly reduces the risk of catastrophic failure, prevents traffic interruptions on evacuation routes, and safeguards lives through access to clean drinking water.
3579.purpose: The City of Dunedin proposes replacing a non-redundant 100-year-old cast-iron water main beneath Bayshore Boulevard (Alt. U.S. 19 / SR 595) from San Salvador Drive to Buena Vista Drive N. The existing pipe is highly susceptible to corrosion and contamination. Replacement grossly reduces the risk of catastrophic failure, prevents traffic interruptions on evacuation routes, and safeguards lives through access to clean drinking water.
3579.activities: The project will strengthen the City's water infrastructure, ensuring consistent water delivery to residents and to the fire prevention system. Replacement of the aging cast iron pipe will mitigate the threat of water contamination from breakage or degradation and potential from future storm surge submersal, safeguard public health, and ensure safe and clean delivery of water.
3579.direct_services: Replacing aging water mains will eliminate risks of leaks and cross contamination, ensuring the reliable delivery of safe, clean drinking water that meets state and federal health standards.
3579.population: This project will serve the over 40,000 residents and thousands of visitors to the City each year.
3579.outcome: Improved water quality. Water quality will be regularly tested for contaminants to ensure compliance with health regulations. System pressure and flow rates will be monitored to verify consistent and sufficient water delivery for consumption needs.

3404.description: The proposed funding will support the design and construction of the Taxiway E Extension at Cecil Airport, establishing a vital new connection to the east side of the airfield. This extension will provide direct access to the Otto Aerospace greenfield site, unlocking significant economic and development opportunities for Northeast Florida’s growing aviation and aerospace sectors. The project includes all design work, environmental review, and required permitting needed to advance construction and accelerate development across the airport’s east side.
3404.purpose: The requested funds will be used to extend Taxiway E at Cecil Airport, providing essential airfield access to the east side of the airport. This infrastructure improvement is critical to enabling Otto Aerospace to begin operations at Cecil, which will result in the creation of approximately 1,400 high-paying jobs. Additionally, this project will unlock future development opportunities for other aerospace companies, strengthening Cecil Airport’s role as a regional economic driver and supporting l
3404.activities: To achieve the intended purpose of extending Taxiway E and providing airfield access to the east side of Cecil Airport, the project will include comprehensive design and engineering services to develop detailed plans and specifications. It will also involve site preparation and construction, including grading, paving, lighting, and drainage installation, as well as environmental compliance activities such as completing the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) requirements to ensure regulator
3404.direct_services: Although the Taxiway E extension is primarily an infrastructure project, it provides substantial direct benefits to citizens through economic growth and workforce development. The project will enable Otto Aerospace to create approximately 1,400 high-paying jobs for local residents, stimulate regional economic activity that supports local businesses and service providers, and foster workforce devel
3404.population: The primary population served by this project includes residents of Northeast Florida, particularly those in Jacksonville and surrounding communities, who will benefit from new employment opportunities and economic growth. The project is expected to directly impact approximately 1,400 individuals through the creation of high-paying jobs at Otto Aerospace. Indirectly, thousands more will benefit from increased regional economic activity, expanded career pathways in the aviation and aerospace sect
3404.outcome: The project will generate measurable economic, operational, and community benefits by driving job creation and competitive wages, stimulating economic growth and private investment, enhancing operational capacity and safety, and expanding workforce development opportunities. These outcomes will be evaluated through key indicators such as the number of jobs created, local hiring rates, median wages and benefits, levels of private capital investment and facility development, the addition of new tenants, and increased tax revenues, culminating in successful project delivery. 3494.description: Recognizing Oslo's position as home to the largest pediatric population in Indian River County, with many children living in poverty, Treasure Coast Community Health has embarked on a transformative initiative to develop a new, state-of-the- art, 20,000+ square foot comprehensive healthcare center dedicated to pediatrics. 3350.description: This project is the second part of St. Lucie Village's Phase 2 Sewer project to construct a centralized sewer system to serve all 56 residential properties in the northeast portion of the Town, which will replace the use of septic tanks in that area. An Indian River Lagoon Water Quality Improvement Grant is being pursued for this force main construction. This second part will complete the home-to-force main connection for the 56 homes, and it includes construction of grinder pump stations, service boxes at the road or right-of-way, and service lines to complete the home-to-force main connection. It will also include decommissioning the septic tanks and abandonment of the drainfields. Phas
3350.purpose: The purpose of this project is to complete construction of a centralized sewer system to replace the use of septic tanks for all 56 residential properties in the northeast area of St. Lucie Village and eliminate the degradation of the Indian River Lagoon and the shallow aquifer caused by these septic tanks and the even greater degradation caused by frequent tidal flooding and resulting septic tank overflows onto land and sewage backups into homes. 3349.description: Technology, Innovation, Monitoring, & Education initiative built on decades of leadership by Mote fisheries/aquaculture research to grow and release 50,000+ snook per year under FWC guidance for recreational fishing.
3349.purpose: Recreational saltwater fishing is a multi-billion-dollar industry in FL and the common snook is recognized as one of the top targeted species. Environmental challenges and mass mortality events are impacting fishery and associated FL economic benefit. Mote is launching the integration of a Technology, Innovation, Monitoring, & Education initiative built on decades of leadership by Mote fisheries/aquaculture research to grow and release 50,000+ snook under FWC guidance for recreational fishing.
3349.activities: Commercial-scale numbers of fish being produced for stocking to keep the snook fishery sustainable. Maintaining ability to cultivate snook is critical to respond to fish kills associated with red tide, cold stuns, etc. Stocking supports working waterfronts & coastal communities who are dependent on economic output of recreational fisheries (3.9 billion in sales; >30,000 jobs).
3349.direct_services: Stock enhancement of snook provides a sustainable solution to maintain healthy fisheries. Services include economic stability for working waterfronts and jobs (>30K) associated with angling tourism (2.4 billion in value-added impact) in regions impacted by fish kills and habitat degradation.
3349.population: Stakeholder groups including the recreational saltwater fishing community and Florida schools. Thousands of Floridians and tourists who fish on Florida's west coast.
3349.outcome: Responsible Stock Enhancement efforts have proven contributions to local stocks and fisheries. Sustainable, land- based marine aquaculture production of fingerlings for release is relieving pressure on wild caught fishery resources. Federal and state annual recreational and commercial fishing industry reporting. Tagging, monitoring and fate tracking of released fish populations.

The system will also provide access to bi-directional real-time communication with law enforcement and applicable criminal justice agencies and include a survey tool to gauge victim satisfaction. This request will allow law enforcement agencies, funded with prior year funding, to continue services to the community. The additional funds will allow other law enforcement agencies to utilize the enhanced victim notific
3700.purpose: Receiving prompt case updates and knowing an offender's status (e.g., release, transfer, escape) allows victims to take necessary precautions to protect themselves and their families. Being informed about an offender's whereabouts can help alleviate anxiety and uncertainty, allowing victims to regain a sense of control. Timely notifications enable victims to seek restraining orders, modify custody arrangements, or take other legal actions if needed. Victim notification systems allow victims to e
3700.activities: The enhancements shall provide proactive text, email, and portal access; provide access to bi-directional real-time communication with law enforcement and applicable criminal justice agencies; provide for automated multi-agency notifications to be shared with partner agencies; and include a survey tool to gauge victim satisfaction. The system will create efficiencies for criminal justice agencies while enhancing victim services.
3700.direct_services: Citizens will begin to receive updates on the status from the initial 911 call for service and throughout the entire criminal justice process. This includes proactive text, email, and portal access and real-time communication capabilities with law enforcement, ensuring communication regarding incarceration status is received timely and in a manner conducive to the victim's needs. Initial results o

3700.outcome: This system will provide increased citizen engagement and transparency, empowering victims with the information they need to make informed decisions about their safety and future. Success will be measured through survey feedback and program metrics from crime victims and user agencies.

3390.description: The City of Plantation is seeking funds to assist with the costs with repair of safety items related to four (4) culvert and pedestrian bridges along Central Park Place. The project would address the poor condition of the bridges and guardrails. This project is presently in design (at City cost) so requested funds are for construction.
3390.purpose: Improve the safety and condition of the culvert bridges.
3390.activities: Repairs to culvert and pedestrian bridges.
3390.direct_services: Safe use of bridges by pedestrians.
3390.population: The City has a population of over 100,000 and is centrally located in Broward County.
3390.outcome: Improve the condition and safety of the culvert bridges, measured by the number of users.

3507.description: Cleary Blvd, between NW 82nd Avenue and Pine Island Road has experienced flooding/standing water during several rain events in recent years, including the April 2023 Broward Flooding. This project would provide additional drainage infrastructure in the area thereby reducing the hazards posed by flooding/standing water. The City of Plantation is seeking assistance with construction funding for this project.
3507.purpose: Reduction of flooding/standing water in the area will allow for safer transportation and reduce property damage during and after rain events. The area serves as a main access road for businesses, residents, and apartment complexes.
3507.activities: Construction of drainage infrastructure and related costs (striping, pavement marking, catch basins, curb and gutter, valve boxes and ADA ramps)
3507.direct_services: Safe, clear roadways during and following rain events in area prone to flooding.
3507.population: The City has a population of over 100,000 and is centrally located in Broward County.
3507.outcome: Reduction in flooding/standing water on Cleary Blvd. Measured by: Reduction in the amount of and duration of standing water on the roadway.

3391.description: This project is located in Plantation's Park East neighborhood. For years this neighborhood, which includes schools, churches, parks and residences, has been plagued with cut-thru traffic from State Road 7. Safety improvements planned for SR7 are expected to increase cut-thru traffic. This project provides for the construction of traffic calming features in the Park East neighborhood to help mitigate these impacts and provide for the safety of residents (project already in design).
3391.purpose: The funds would help expedite improvements intended to increase the safety of the neighborhood, which is plagued by cut-thru traffic from SR 7, and includes schools, churches, parks, and residences.
3391.activities: Construction of traffic calming features (roundabouts, chicanes).
3391.direct_services: Enhanced safety of students, residents, and visitors to parks and churches in the neighborhood.
3391.population: The City has a population of over 100,000 and is centrally located in Broward County.
3391.outcome: Enhanced safety of residents, visitors, and roadway users as measured by a reduction in cut-thru traffic and reduced vehicle speeds.

3419.description: The Adaptive Sports Performance & Recovery Initiative will provide US Citizens, Active Duty Military, Veterans and International individuals with disabilities and adaptive athletes access to state-of-the-art fitness, training, and recovery equipment in a fully accessible environment. The program will enable the participants to improve strength, mobility, endurance, and overall quality of life through hands-on, adaptive exercise and recovery opportunities.
3419.purpose: To provide all Active Duty Military, Veterans, US Citizens, and International individuals with limb loss or physical disabilities access to state-of-the-art adaptive fitness and recovery equipment(i.e. hyperbaric chambers, PEMF, VO2Max testing, etc). This initiative will create an inclusive training environment that promotes healing, independence, and improved quality of life through exercise, rehabilitation, and performance training.
3419.activities: Funds will be used to purchase, install, and maintain adaptive training and recovery equipment. This includes specialized strength and cardio machines, balance and mobility systems, and recovery technology designed to meet the unique needs of veterans and individuals with disabilities.
3419.direct_services: The project will directly serve all US citizens and eventually international individuals with limb loss or mobility limitations by providing access to adaptive exercise and recovery equipment that supports safe physical training, rehabilitation, and wellness. Participants will gain improved strength, mobility, and confidence in an inclusive environment.
3419.population: All generations with limb loss and mobility issues. We will not turn anyone away: economically disadvantaged persons, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, Preschool/grade school, high school, college students, elderly persons, Persons with poor mental health, or persons with poor physical health; We at full capacity we are set to served 10-30 living in campus dorm "Inpatient" and up to 400 individuals on an "Outpatient" schedule commuting daily, weekly or monthly visits.
3419.outcome: The Adaptive Performance & Recovery Initiative will improve physical and mental health, foster inclusion, reduce reliance on unhealthy coping strategies, and create economic opportunities for adaptive athletes; these outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-program functional assessments, validated self-report surveys, participant feedback, and tracking of in and out-of-town participation.

3451.description: The purpose of this project is to design the widening of a section of Babcock Street, Palm Bay, Florida from a two-lane to a four-lane roadway to address increased traffic volumes, decrease emergency response times, enhance commercial potential and facilitate the development of additional public transportation options for the community. The project will cover approximately 2,343 feet of roadway, extending 900 feet south of Malabar Road SE (State Road 514) to 3,243 feet south.

3451.direct_services: Design of a significant roadway project.

3451.outcome: This project will help improve traffic flow by reducing congestion and increasing capacity, thereby decreasing emergency response times and facilitating the development of additional public transportation options for the community, which will enhance connectivity. The benefits of improved transportation conditions can be measured by decreased emergency response times, increased safety through a reduction in crash rates on the specific section of the roadway, greater equity by improving mobility options and partnerships with local area transit and a decrease in travel times for roadway users.

3583.description: Requested funds will be used to support the Florida Center for Expanded Learning (FCEL) program, which focuses on expanding access to afterschool opportunities in afterschool deserts and improving overall program quality. The goal is to increase options for families and improve youth outcomes in Clay and Polk Counties.
3583.purpose: Requested funds will be used to support the Florida Center for Expanded Learning (FCEL) program, which focuses on expanding access to afterschool opportunities in afterschool deserts and improving overall program quality. The goal is to increase options for families and improve youth outcomes in Clay and Polk Counties.
3583.activities: Requested funds will expand afterschool access by adding program seats in high-need areas, supporting providers with training and coaching, implementing research-based enrichment, engaging families, and using data to strengthen quality and improve student outcomes in Clay and Polk Counties

3397.description: The Pathways to Success Project enables Urban Youth Impact (UYI) to advance its mission to love, equip, and empower inner-city youth to fulfill their God-given purpose. Grant funding will support the continued operation of UYI’s private school and afterschool programs, as well as critical capital improvements to its campus. Founded in 1997, Urban Youth Impact serves K–12 students through a comprehensive set of programs, including a private school, an afterschool leadership academy, outreach initiatives, and college and career preparation. Together, these programs provide academic support, mentorship, and leadership development that promote long-term success for inner-city youth and their families.
3397.purpose: Funds will support Urban Youth Impact’s work to provide high-quality education, after-school programming, and trauma care for children living in the inner-city. These students face significant barriers, including unstable home environments, exposure to violence, and struggling local schools. Our program offers a safe, structured place for up to 12-hours a day where children receive strong academics, counseling, mentorship and support to change the trajectory of at-risk youth.
3397.activities: Inner-city youth will be served all day as a result of the funds given, positively impacting their education and lives. We provide transportation to and from our campus, where they receive free private school education, meals, after-school arts and science programs, mentors, job training, and more. Funds for capital improvements will also enhance safety and security for all students.
3397.direct_services: Direct services that will be provided as a result of the funds requested include free transportation, private school education, mentors, quality after-school classes to learn hobbies, literacy intervention, and job training as the salaries of those staff will be provided for with the funds. Capital funds will indirectly benefit students by providing a safe, secure, and well-maintained environment.
3397.population: At-risk and underserved youth. Grade school, high school and college students. We expect to serve between 200-400
3397.outcome: The project will improve our students education. 90% of the youth will make improvements in reading and math and 60% of students meet or exceed the average national percentile ranking. In surrounding inner-city public schools, roughly 1 in 4 children can read on grade level. They are set up to fail if we do not intervene. Youth are given a free, private school education during the day, followed by literacy intervention in the afternoon if additional help is needed. Last year 77% of our students could read on grade level.

3450.description: This project will divert post-consumer glass from Tampa Bay bars and restaurants; process into clean, safe sand with an industrial glass pulverizer; and pilot beneficial reuses in partnership with state universities (sandbags for hurricane preparedness, playground surfacing, landscaping media, shoreline stabilization/resiliency). The model is based on Glass Half Full (New Orleans), which converts collected glass into sand/gravel for coastal restoration and disaster preparedness; they operate with an Andela GP-05L system rated ~1–2 tons/hour.

3584.description: The Lake City Fire Department is requesting funding to replace its aging frontline fire engine at the Lake City Public Safety Building. This engine, which serves the historic district and responds to the highest number of calls, is nearly 14 years old and has required extensive repairs in recent months. A new fire engine will enhance emergency response reliability, improve public safety, and ensure firefighters have the necessary equipment to protect the community efficiently. Funding this replacement is critical to maintaining effective fire protection services for Lake City residents.
3584.purpose: The funds will replace Lake City Fire Department's aging frontline fire engine, ensuring reliable emergency response and public safety. Serving the historic district, the 14-year-old engine requires frequent repairs. A new engine will improve response times, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance firefighter efficiency, ensuring continued protection for the community.
3584.activities: The funds will support fire suppression, emergency medical response, and rescue operations by replacing the aging frontline fire engine. The new engine will enhance response times, reliability, and firefighter safety while ensuring effective protection for the historic district and the broader community. It will also reduce maintenance downtime, allowing the Lake City Fire Department to maintain consistent emergency services, improve operational efficiency, and better serve residents in critical
3584.direct_services: The appropriation will provide enhanced fire protection, emergency medical response, and rescue services to Lake City residents. Replacing the aging frontline fire engine will improve response times, reliability, and firefighter effectiveness, ensuring rapid and efficient emergency services. Citizens will benefit from increased public safety, reduced risks from fire-related incidents, and improved
3584.population: The project will serve the residents, businesses, and visitors of Lake City, particularly those in the historic district and surrounding areas. The Lake City Fire Department responds to thousands of emergency calls annually, directly impacting approximately 12,000 residents within city limits and an additional 70,000 individuals in the surrounding Columbia County area. This investment ensures faster, more reliable emergency response services for the entire community.

A new fire engine will reduce maintenance costs and downtime, increasing operational efficiency. Outcomes will be measured through response time data, service call volume, equipment maintenance records, and citizen satisfaction surveys. These metrics will assess the engine’s impact on emergency services and overall public safety in the community.

3402.organization: The Center for Arts and Innovation
3402.description: The Center Presents Wonder Works: Florida Youth Innovation and Workforce Skills Initiative is a multi-county, youth focused program that strengthens creativity, innovation, and workforce readiness among Florida youth. The program delivers hands on, project based learning that connects creative thinking with real world career pathways, emphasizing problem solving, collaboration, communication, and skills aligned with Florida’s future economy. Funds will support statewide expansion of Wonder Works, providing innovation learning, design challenges, career exposure, and mentorship for students, while also supporting design work to ensure a future campus meets statewide needs.
3402.purpose: Funds will expand Wonder Works programming statewide to deliver innovation learning, design challenges, career exposure and mentorship for students. Programs strengthen communication, collaboration and problem solving to improve education outcomes and prepare youth for high demand jobs. A portion of funds will also support planning & design work to ensure the future campus meets statewide needs.

3435.organization: The Arc of Palm Beach County
3435.description: Funds will support the completion of a day facility and overnight shelter for people with disabilities located in Palm Springs, FL. 3435.direct_services: Daily use of the facility is for life-skills programming, vocational training, home management skill-building, and cultural enrichment for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities and autism. 3435.outcome: A special needs shelter will enhance safety, accessibility, and durability, ensuring uninterrupted services for medically fragile with disabilities. The project creates a secure, inclusive environment, allowing for greater independence, comfort, and continuity of vital services. Outcomes are measured by Accessibility Audits; Compliance with ADA and universal design standards; Stakeholder Feedback – Surveys from residents, staff, and families on facility improvements.

Arts-based learning integrated with Torah study, discussions, and community events boosts cognitive and social-emotional growth, empowers parents to extend learning at home, and fosters creativity, bonding, and a strong community.
3437.purpose: Expand preschool programs to create a holistic educational experience engaging children and parents. Integrating arts-based learning with Torah study, discussions, and community events will enhance children’s cognitive and social- emotional growth while empowering parents to extend learning at home, fostering creativity, family bonding, and a strong values-based Jewish community.

3499.description: Provide funding to the Department of Education (DOE) to expand high school completion access to DOE approved Virtual Instruction Providers of a dropout retrieval program for adults aged 21-26. Expanding age eligibility for high school completion to include adults and former dropouts is a proven public investment with measurable fiscal and social benefits. Research consistently shows that obtaining a high school diploma leads to higher earnings, increased tax revenues, and reduce public spending on welfare, healthcare and correctional systems.
3499.purpose: To allow re-engaged students to continue their coursework through district dropout retrieval programs without substantial disruption to their education setting. Providing more access for young adults to obtain their high school diploma through a less expensive virtual curricula environment creates higher earning potential and opportunities for these individuals. This is a proven public investment with measurable fiscal and social benefits for the state.
3499.activities: A fully virtual, DOE approved high school curricula including mentors and wrap around services to help ensure this population has the proper tools to successfully obtain their standard high school diploma.
3499.direct_services: In addition to the services provided to the students engaged in these programs described above, dropout retrieval programs engage in direct outreach to potential students to convince them to get back into the education system to obtain their high school diploma.
3499.population: Adults aged 21-26 who have completed some high school courses but have not yet obtained their high school diploma.
3499.outcome: More adults will obtain their high school diploma which will make them higher earners, increase tax revenues, and reduce public spending on welfare, healthcare and correctional systems. Providers will report how many adults are engaged in dropout retrieval programs with course completion and graduation rates.

3648.description: ZeroEyes is the industry's leading AI-based weapons detection solution. ZeroEyes will partner with Florida schools to deploy gun detection software on existing camera infrastructure across the State of Florida to mitigate gun violence.
3648.purpose: The additional funds will allow ZeroEyes to be installed on significantly more cameras across the district. The more ZE coverage there is, the more protected students will be from potential gun violence.

3648.direct_services: Citizens with children enrolled in the district will benefit with the added layer of protection at their kid's schools, while also making the schools not appear like a heavily guarded facility because the software layer sits on top of the already existing camera infrastructure.
3648.population: The target population are the students, teachers, and staff that work and learn withing the district.
3648.outcome: To measure the effectiveness of the ZeroEyes deployment, ZE can submit a report on how many guns were detected and alerted on campus.

3740.description: Pinellas County Urban League (PCUL) has embarked on an ambitious journey to rejuvenate the current building in St. Petersburg, Florida. The transformation will convert the existing structure into a two-story, 18-unit multifamily mixed-use development, combining contemporary living spaces with commercial opportunities. This adaptive reuse project aims to retain the building’s historical value while creating a modern and affordable community asset. The original 10,700- square-foot structure, built in 1966, will be expanded with a 3,000-square-foot addition, accommodating a range of studio and one-bedroom apartment layouts as well as amenity spaces. PCUL has owned the facility since 1989.
3740.purpose: This project seeks to address the shortage of affordable/workforce housing while preserving the building’s historical character and seamlessly integrating contemporary elements. This sustainable approach not only reduces waste but also conserves the cultural essence of the original structure. The design creates a lively and versatile environment, blending residential units with commercial and amenity spaces. The ground floor will feature a retail space for a store or cafe, a multi-purpose great
3740.activities: The mission of PCUL is to enable and empower African Americans and others who are under-served in our communities to achieve their highest human potential and secure economic self-reliance, parity, power, and civil rights. Our programs and services include education & community leadership, job training, placement & entrepreneurship, housing &community development and health & quality of life.
3740.direct_services: Our programs and services are designed to meet educational needs, support community succession planning, and increase family income. We focus on building generational wealth and providing safe, affordable spaces to live, work, and play. Additionally, we aim to enhance all aspects of health—financial, physical, and mental—ensuring a holistic approach to community well-being.
3740.population: The target population for this project includes residents of all ages. Serving an estimated 500 plus individuals annually taking into account the foot traffic generated by the commercial businesses that will occupy some of the 1st floor space.
3740.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to improve economic stability, educational outcomes, and overall well-being for underserved populations. Key outcomes include increased employment, reduced recidivism, improved health, and enhanced community engagement. The methodology for measuring success will involve tracking tenant participation in Urban League programs through surveys and data analysis.

3696.description: The Alliance for Aging is committed to helping older adults and individuals with disabilities remain independent and live with dignity in their own homes and communities. This initiative strengthens the Alliance’s Aging and Disability Resource Center screening and eligibility functions to ensure timely access to services while expanding in-home and community- based supports—including adult day care, home-delivered meals, homemaker assistance, and minor home repairs. By addressing the continuously growing demand for services, the project will prioritize seniors and individuals with disabilities who are homebound, socially isolated, or living with memory-related conditions, and provide vital relief to their overburdened caregivers.
3696.purpose: The project aims to enhance access to in-home and supportive services by increasing eligibility screenings and service delivery, promoting independent living for older adults and individuals with disabilities, address growing demands for services, and reducing the state’s total long-term care expenditures.
3696.activities: Strengthen the Alliance’s ADRC functions by providing an additional 10,000 screenings and eligibility determinations for older adults and individuals with disabilities in Miami-Dade County. This will ensure timely access to in-home and community-based programs. In addition, 136 individuals to receive supportive services such as Homemaker, Personal Care, Respite, Caregiver Stipend, Meals, etc. through contracted providers.
3696.direct_services: Older adults and individuals with disabilities served through this project will receive intake, information, referral/assistance services, direct in-home and supportive services such as Homemaker, Personal Care, Respite, Caregiver Stipends, and Meals, allowing them to remain safely in their homes and avoid institutional placement.
3696.population: Low-income and disadvantaged seniors age 60 and older, individuals with disabilities, individuals who are with overburdened caregivers, limited to no access to nutritious meals, and limited ability or access to needed home repairs or cleaning to ensure a safe living environment. It is expected that the project will serve between 100 and 200 individuals with in-home and supportive services while providing more than 10,000 additional ADRC screenings to individuals.
3696.outcome: This project will expand access to critical home and community-based services for the targeted population, improving their physical and mental health, reducing social isolation, and preventing unnecessary costly institutional placement. By strengthening the Alliance’s screening and eligibility functions and addressing the growing need for services traditionally offered through CCE, HCE, and ADI services, the project will enable more seniors and individuals with disabilities to live safely and independently at home, supporting caregiver well-being and lowering long-term care costs to the state. This group represents one of the most profoundly disabled populations and is identified as a top priority in the Strategic Plan of the Florida Division of Blind Services (DBS).The requested funding will empower DBS to maintain and enhance its residential program, which is specifically designed to foster independence through employment. By investing in this initiative, the agency can continue providing the intensive level of service required to meet the unique needs of this population—ultimately helping participants build meaningful careers and lead more self-sufficient lives.
3704.purpose: Funding is requested to provide specialized vocational services to Floridians who are blind with another significant disability. This population is considered to be the most significantly disabled and is a priority in the strategic plan of the Florida Division of Blind Services (DBS). The funding will enable the agency to provide the level of service required by DBS to sustain the residential program, which is designed to help this population achieve independence through employment.
