No longer sized appropriate for our student body and highly utilized. The proposed project will rebuild science laboratories in the initial phase and allow the college to continue operations adding 25,000 square feet. Broward College anticipates that the North Campus Building 56 & 57 Remodel will enable the addition of four associate degree programs, one bachelor's degree program, and seven certificate programs, resulting in 140 more degrees starting annually in the fall of 2027.

This project will include the creation of 10 science laboratories, 4 nursing laboratories, 1 health assessment lab, and 4 information technology laboratories to accommodate the increasing number of students pursuing STEM and Nursing pathways. These upgrades will expand program capacity, allowing more students to enroll and accelerating their progress toward certificates and degrees. Additionally, the renovations will improve scheduling efficiency particularly in high-demand cou

Key services include the creation of new labs to support STEM and nursing students, addressing the growing demand for skilled professionals. The project will also enhance educational facilities with modern science and IT labs, improving access to high-deman
2180.population: This project aims to serve students pursuing careers in Healthcare Sciences, Nursing, and Computer and Information Technology, with a particular focus on those enrolled at Broward College. According to the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity's Jobs by Occupation report for Broward County, Computer and Mathematical Occupations are projected to experience the third-highest growth between 2022 and 2030, with a 13.5% increase. The highest growth is projected in Healthcare Support Occupations,
2180.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is the increased capacity for students pursuing careers in healthcare, nursing, and technology. This will be realized through the development of new laboratories, improved educational facilities, and expanded student enrollment, all aimed at better preparing students to meet the rising demand for skilled professionals in these fields. Success will be measured by monitoring increases in student enrollment and graduation rates, particularly in high demand, "limited access" programs such as nursing. 1047.description: Law enforcement faces the challenge of maintaining public safety while apprehending those who attempt to flee. Vehicle pursuits, though sometimes necessary, create serious risks for the public, officers, and suspects. To address this, the proposed equipment will be installed on marked and unmarked patrol vehicles and strategically deployed to prevent suspects from escaping after committing crimes.
1047.purpose: Law enforcement faces the challenge of maintaining public safety while apprehending those who attempt to flee. Vehicle pursuits, though sometimes necessary, create serious risks for the public, officers, and suspects. To address this, the proposed equipment will be installed on marked and unmarked patrol vehicles and strategically deployed to prevent suspects from escaping after committing crimes.
1047.activities: Funds will support purchasing and installing pursuit-prevention equipment on marked and unmarked patrol vehicles, training officers on safe use, updating policies, and strategically deploying equipped vehicles. These actions reduce high-speed pursuit risks, enhance public and officer safety, and improve the effectiveness of suspect apprehension.
1047.direct_services: The requested funding will directly enhance public safety by reducing the risks associated with dangerous vehicle pursuits. Citizens will benefit from safer streets, as patrol vehicles equipped with pursuit-prevention technology will deter suspects from fleeing and minimize the likelihood of high-speed chases through neighborhoods and major roadways.
1047.population: The target population is the general public. Over 135,000 individuals will be served.
1047.outcome: The expected benefit is a reduction in the number and severity of high-speed vehicle pursuits, measured by tracking the total pursuits, pursuit-related accidents, and injuries to the public, officers, and suspects before and after equipment deployment. Outcomes will be measured by pre- and post-deployment data will be measured to determine reductions in pursuit frequency, severity of incidents, and injuries.

2021.description: The Loxahatchee River Preservation Initiative (LRPI) is a multi-agency partnership formed in 2000 with the single purpose of seeking out funding assistance for projects that would improve and protect the natural resources within the first federally designated Wild and Scenic River in the State of Florida. LRPI focuses on stormwater discharge and hydrologic improvements, along with septic to sewer conversions and habitat restoration projects designed to improve and protect the natural resources within the watershed. Revitalizing this important water body provides long-term environmental, recreational and economic benefits to the region. Each State dollar is matched at the local level on a minimum 50:50 cost share basis, with over $46 million in State funds having been effectively utilized for watershed restoration projects since its inception.
2021.purpose: Funds requested will support capital construction efforts designed to improve water and habitat quality within the Loxahatchee River and its watershed. Agency partners of LRPI, consisting of local government and water control representatives, as well as representatives from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and the South Florida Water Management District, ranked the proposed projects based on priority need and beneficial impacts to the river.
2021.activities: Projects include stormwater system improvements to reduce runoff and sediment loading into the Loxahatchee River and its tributaries, as well as exotic vegetation control and removal. Funds will be utilized primarily for capital costs associated with the various projects, with a small percentage utilized to contract consulting and engineering services to support the vegetation removal efforts.
2021.direct_services: Direct and secondary improvements to water quality, habitat quality and sediment quality within the watershed and surrounding urban environment.
2021.population: The target population served by this effort and associated projects includes the residents and numerous visitors of both Palm Beach and Martin Counties.
2021.outcome: Benefits will include the reduction of nutrient and sediment loading into the Loxahatchee River and its tributaries, along with vegetation management for the existing natural systems within the watershed. Methodologies to measure expected benefits of these efforts include water quality and biological monitoring.

1886.description: This project is for capacity expansion and process optimization of the City's Wastewater Plant to improve effluent water quality to meet FDEP advanced wastewater treatment (AWT) limits and increase reclaimed water production. The goal is to provide increased water quality benefits to Lake Apopka by reducing key nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus as well as lessening the need of potable water from the Floridian Aquifer for irrigation and providing source water protections.
1886.purpose: The specific goal is to provide increased water quality benefits to Lake Apopka by reducing key nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus as well as lessening the need of potable water from the Floridian Aquifer for irrigation and providing source water protections.
1886.activities: The proposed design will expand the current capacity from 4.75 to 7.5 million gallons per day treatment capacity and modifies the existing treatment standards to achieve Advance Wastewater Treatment (AWT) standards by using Membrane Bioreactors (MBR). With increased capacity and achieving AWT, the facility will meet or exceed stringent effluent objectives.
1886.population: City of Winter Garden and portions of Unincorporated Orange County. 50,000+ Users.
1886.outcome: Meet or exceed stringent effluent objectives of (5mg/L BODS, 5 mg/L Total Suspended Solids, 3 mg/L TN, 1 Mg/L TP) thereby removing key nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, which supports the growth of harmful algae and aquatic plants, such as hydrilla.

1708.description: The Pasco Sheriff's Office requests funding to fully build out and equip a forward operating center at our existing Trinity substation, which is much closer to the impacted areas west of US19 should we have another storm surge event than our existing storage location in Land O'Lakes. This location would provide for secure storage for water rescue vehicles, to include boats and high-water rescue vehicles, and would significantly reduce transit time to effected areas.
1708.purpose: The Pasco Sheriff's Office requests funding to fully build out and equip a forward operating center at our existing Trinity substation, which is much closer to the impacted areas west of US19 should we have another storm surge event than our existing storage location in Land O'Lakes. This location would provide for secure storage for water rescue vehicles, to include boats and high-water rescue vehicles, and would significantly reduce transit time to effected areas.
1708.activities: Better response to natural disaster/storm surge events in Pasco County through construction.
1708.direct_services: Better response to natural disaster/storm surge event.
1708.population: All citizens of Pasco County should we face another storm surge event/natural disaster.
1708.outcome: Better response to natural disaster/storm surge event.

1887.description: Jonathan's Landing is advancing groundbreaking workforce initiatives launched through Techtronic and now a second social enterprise in consumer-packaged goods (CPG), building on the success of mobile device repair. With 50 cohorts on track for certification and graduates already employed, this request expands instruction, new career tracks, and a housing pilot—positioning Florida as the national leader in workforce innovation, independence, and statewide replication for adults with autism.
1887.purpose: Jonathan's Landing is advancing groundbreaking workforce initiatives launched through Techtronic and now a second social enterprise in consumer-packaged goods (CPG), building on the success of mobile device repair. With 50 cohorts on track for certification and graduates already employed, this request expands instruction, new career tracks, and a housing pilot—positioning Florida as the national leader in workforce innovation, independence, and statewide replication for adults with autism.
1887.activities: Funding expands workforce pilots that upskill individuals with autism, addressing barriers that leave 727,000 Floridians with disabilities out of work. Activities include assessments, certifications, apprenticeships, and Manager-in-Training. Instructor Kits replicate programs statewide, adding mobile repair, culinary, CPG, and inventory pathways tied to independence.
1887.direct_services: Funding expands Skill Circuits beyond Techtonics's WISE mobile device repair to include new CPG career tracks, giving adults hands-on exploration and training. Participants advance into certifications in device repair, culinary, and inventory management, while a Manager-in-Training track builds peer mentorship and leadership statewide.
1887.population: Jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, high school students, and university/college students.
1887.outcome: Benefit: Over 500 neurodiverse adults will earn industry-recognized certifications in mobile device repair, CPG, culinary, and inventory management. Training elevates education to career-ready knowledge, equipping participants with transferable skills for in-demand jobs. Instructor Kits enable schools and nonprofits statewide to replicate this proven model. Measurement: Outcomes will be tracked through the number of certifications awarded, training milestones achieved, internships completed, and employment secured. Replication success will be measured by the number of schools and nonprofits adopting Instructor Kits, and by assessing student readiness across those partner sites.

2022.description: Palm Beach County is requesting $1 million in State funds to convert an existing facility into two critical programs: an 8- bed Youth Shelter and an 8-bed Medical Respite Shelter. The Youth Shelter will serve unaccompanied youth and young adults (ages 18–24) experiencing homelessness who are at high risk of exploitation, unsafe housing, or chronic homelessness. It will provide safe, short-term housing (up to 90 days), 24/7 supervision, case management, counseling, educational/vocational supports, and discharge planning toward reunification or stable housing. The Medical Respite Shelter will serve homeless individuals discharged from hospitals or identified by outreach teams who are too medically fragile for unsheltered living or congregate shelters. Both projects include capital improvements such as youth- appropriate residential space, fire system upgrades, and phased renovations to ens
2022.purpose: Unsheltered residents and medically fragile individuals have been identified as strategic priorities by the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners. By creating dedicated shelter capacity, the County will prevent youth homelessness from becoming chronic by providing immediate safe shelter, reduce risks of trafficking and unsafe living situations faced by unaccompanied youth, and provide medical respite beds for individuals discharged from hospitals or identified by outreach teams who are
2022.activities: The activities and services provided to meet the intended purpose of these funds include 24/7 supervision and a supportive environment to ensure safety and stability for youth and medically fragile individuals. Case management and individualized service planning will address housing, education, employment, and health needs, while counseling and crisis intervention will support mental and emotional well-being. Youth will have access to linkages with education, vocational training, and employment
2022.direct_services: The youth shelter delivered through this project will not only provide safe, stable housing for at-risk youth in Palm Beach County, but will also connect residents to a full range of wrap-around services designed to promote long-term stability. These include case management, educational support, life skills training, mental and behavioral health counseling, access to healthcare, mentoring, and lin
2022.population: The project will serve at-risk youth and young adults, ages 18–24, who are experiencing homelessness, unsafe housing, or other crisis situations that place them at high risk of exploitation, victimization, or chronic homelessness, as well as medically fragile individuals experiencing homelessness who are discharged from hospitals or identified by outreach teams and unable to safely recover on the streets or in congregate shelters. The facility will include 8 youth shelter beds, with each youth s
2022.outcome: The 8-bed youth shelter will provide at-risk youth in Palm Beach County with safe, stable housing and access to comprehensive supportive services. By offering short-term shelter and structured support, the project aims to prevent youth homelessness from becoming chronic, improve stability through education, employment, and housing resources, and reduce the risk of victimization associated with unsafe living situations, including street or couch-surfing environments. In addition, the 8-bed medical respite shelter will provide safe recovery space for medically fragile individuals experiencing homelessness who are discharged from hospitals or identified by outreach teams. Services include 24/7

1889.description: HTES is the only school in our Tri-County area dedicated to serving children in grades 6-12 with unique learning disabilities and challenges. We are currently operating at-capacity, and often times have to wait-list students. We have also implemented a school to work/post-secondary education Extended Transition Program for students beyond grade 12. We are requesting funding for a capital project to expand our campus to meet the rising level of need in our community and to house our new Extended Transition Program.
1889.purpose: The purpose of a campus expansion is to increase enrollment for grades 6-12 and house the new school to work/post- secondary education Extended Transition Program to help students transition successfully to life beyond grade 12. The goal is to address the rising level of need for effective, accessible Exceptional Student Education in our community and continue helping our students transcend their difficulties.
1889.activities: An expanded campus will allow HTES to increase enrollment to continue offering a comprehensive academic program for Exceptional Student Education based on state standards, and specialized instruction in identified areas. The Extended Transition Program provides a support structure beyond High School to help students obtain life skills, jobs, and/or higher education to promote self-sufficiency.
1889.direct_services: Funding requested will provide more classrooms for individualized learning plans, high-quality assessments, a 7:1 student: teacher ratio, intensive tutoring, college prep, vocational training, and independent-living skills for students to excel beyond high school. A bigger campus will allow us to enroll more students grades 6-12, and students beyond 12th grade with a 504 plan or IEP.
1889.population: The funds requested will serve economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, and developmentally disabled middle school, high school students and students up to age 22 with a 504 plan or IEP. We plan to expand our services to ~100 student enrollment capacity.
1889.outcome: We plan to improve quality of education for students with learning disabilities in our community. The measure of benefit or outcome will be increased enrollment in our 6-12th grade program and additional enrollment through the Extended Transition Program. The method for measuring the level of benefit or outcome will be increased enrollment in all programs. Additionally, we will measure the benefit of our programs through growth in fall and spring assessment scores and through anecdotal evidence from parents and student surveys. This will also create immediate job opportunities to accommodate an increased enrollment, which calls for a rising level of need for educators and paraprofessionals.

1008.organization: Before & After A/C Pilot Program Corp.
1008.description: The Before & After air-conditioning pilot program will install energy-efficient air-conditioning systems in select Florida Department of Corrections facilities including the Everglades and Homestead correctional institutions. The project addresses the need for climate control in the sleeping dorm areas including the two-man cells. This initiative serves as a model for modernizing Florida correctional infrastructure while promoting energy efficiency, reducing heat related health risks, and supporting humane living and working environments.
1008.purpose: The Before and After A/C Pilot corporation is requesting $450,000 to launch an air-conditioning pilot program at two Florida correctional facilities: Everglades Correctional Institution and Homestead Correctional Institution. This program will install energy efficient air-conditioning systems in dormitory and two- man housing areas that currently lack cooling. The goal is to reduce extreme heat exposure, improve living and working conditions, and create a safe environment.
1008.activities: Funds will support the installation of energy efficient air conditioning systems at selected correctional facilities, including site assessments, wall fabrication, and electrical preparation. Services include contracting license HVAC professionals, purchasing and installing mini split units, and monitoring temperature and energy performance. Additional activities include training staff and volunteers on equipment maintenance, data collection for program evaluation, and reporting outcomes to demo
1008.direct_services: The project will provide safer, healthier, and more humane living and working environments within Florida correctional institutions. By installing air-conditioning systems, the program directly improves physical and mental well-being for incarcerated individuals and staff, reducing heat related illnesses and stress. The project also benefits the public by supporting a more stable, efficient correc
1008.population: The project serves incarcerated individuals and correctional staff at Everglades, Homestead, and Miami Correctional Institutions. These facilities house approximately 4,500 inmates and employ around 900 staff members. The program will directly benefit both groups by improving environmental conditions, health, and safety within the facilities. The program also indirectly benefits families and communities through enhanced wellbeing and reduce strain on medical and correctional resources.
1008.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health by reducing extreme heat exposure for inmates and staff. This results in fewer heat-related illnesses, better sleep, and enhanced morale. The project will also improve facility efficiency and safety. Outcomes will be measured through (1) temperature and humidity monitoring, (2) health and incident reports, (3) staff and inmate surveys, and (4) energy usage data comparing pre-and-post-installation conditions to evaluate program success and scalability.

2853.description: This project will enhance life safety and emergency preparedness at Our Lady of Good Counsel Camp by mitigating risks from lightning, severe storms, tornadoes, hurricanes, and wildfires, as well as vulnerabilities caused by inadequate perimeter fencing. Planned improvements include a lightning detection and alert system, upgraded communication and public-address equipment, protective shutters, safe refuge areas, perimeter fire breaks, and 8,000 feet of new security fencing. These upgrades will protect more than 3,000 annual campers, staff, and visitors while strengthening the camp’s overall safety and resilience.
2853.purpose: The funds will implement essential life-safety improvements at Our Lady of Good Counsel Camp to protect campers, staff, and visitors from lightning, severe storms, tornadoes, hurricanes, and wildfires. Planned upgrades include a lightning detection and alert system, enhanced communication and public-address equipment, designated refuge areas, protective shutters, perimeter fire breaks, and new perimeter fencing. These measures will reduce risk to life and property while strengthening the camp’s
2853.activities: Activities will include installing a lightning detection and alert system, upgrading public-address and communication equipment, and constructing or retrofitting safe refuge areas in key camp buildings. Additional work will add protective shutters, create perimeter fire breaks, and clear vegetation to improve wildfire protection. About 8,000 feet of new perimeter fencing will secure the property and prevent unauthorized access. Staff will receive training on hazard awareness and emergency proced
2853.direct_services: The project will provide direct safety and emergency protection services to campers, staff, and visitors through real- time hazard alerts, rapid public-address notifications, and access to safe refuge areas during severe weather. It will also enhance year-round site security with new perimeter fencing, improved communication systems, and stronger coordination with local first responders. These upg
2853.population: The project serves youth, families, staff, and volunteers who attend programs at Our Lady of Good Counsel Camp, along with community and church groups that use the facility year-round. Each summer, about 600 campers and 40 staff participate in residential programs, with another 2,400 visitors attending retreats and special events throughout the year. Overall, the project will directly benefit more than 3,000 individuals annually by providing a safer and more resilient environment.
2853.outcome: The project will greatly enhance life safety and emergency preparedness by reducing exposure to lightning, severe storms, tornadoes, hurricanes, and wildfires. Expected outcomes include faster hazard detection and alerts, expanded safe refuge capacity, and stronger coordination with local emergency responders. Success will be measured through annual safety inspections, documented drills, and verification of system functionality and staff training compliance.

1326.description: Funds would be utilized to renovate and remodel 23,540 GSF of existing classrooms and labs and add approximately 1,800 SF. This project will enhance academic programming by modernizing teaching spaces and adding hands-on technology in multidisciplinary fabrication labs. It will rededicate spaces for foundational credit earning courses, providing students with a cutting edge academic experience. The creation of a flexible and modern teaching and training center will support enrollment growth through improved space utilization and allow SF to meet regional industry demand by expanding programs with identified occupational need while building capacity for future program development.
1326.purpose: (1) Expand instructional areas to create contemporary, collaborative teaching spaces for academic programs; (2) Enhance existing space to grow teaching and learning opportunities by combining student work with individual and small group spaces that integrate cross-disciplinary exposure and collaboration; (3) Modernize equipment and technology to ensure students have access to the latest tools and software essential to develop 21st century innovation skills for contemporary art practices, includi
1326.activities: Offer classes and workshops in various disciplines, fostering skill development that is transferable to subjects such as math, science, and language. Collaboration between faculty, students and the public, enriching the learning experience and fostering community engagement. Contributing locally to education, with outreach initiatives to under served populations and K-12 schools in the area.
1326.direct_services: Access to expanded learning opportunities through larger and better-equipped education spaces, leading to improved skill development and creative output; enhanced opportunities for students to gain educational exposure and valuable real-world experience in showcasing their work; access to modern technology and equipment to prepare students for the digital age; and workforce development through exp
1326.population: The project will serve approximately 2,500 students on an annual basis across multiple credit earning programs. All SF students will also have access to the fabrication lab, and the general public will benefit from hosted events at the facility. Specifically, this project targets academic programs with identified regional occupational need, such as graphic design, multimedia production and project management.
1326.outcome: This project would facilitate skill building and workforce development. It will increase student enrollment and provide a high-tech platform for collaboration with campus and community partners. SF anticipates improved student achievement due to increased access to state-of-the-art facilities, leading to higher graduation rates and post- graduation success, and greater community engagement. These outcomes will be measured by tracking enrollment and student success during coursework and after graduation, local economic impact studies, and the documentation of projects, exhibitions, events, workshops and partnerships.

1003.description: The ReMARCable Aquaponics Project will offer a new greenhouse approach to produce education & food for adults with developmental & physical disabilities who are food insecure. The Project assists adults living with unique abilities who live below the poverty level through training, education & improved mental health. The ReMARCable Aquaponics Project will also be used for educational, social and environmental awareness for school students & the community. This will be a collaboration with the SOS Foundation food pantry with their Farm-to-School grant. The Project also addresses food security and agricultural production. The structure for aquaponics is also hurricane resistant fresh grown fruits and vegetables during the recovery if a disaster of that magnitude occurs. This aquaponics greenhouse uses 95% less water than traditional systems. It creates no waste, uses no chemical fertilizer
1003.purpose: The goal for this project will be to provide training and education to 85 adults with intellectual and physical disabilities, school aged children and members of the community who are economically challenged. The Project seeks to improve their awareness of innovative horticultural, healthy food choices, therapeutic opportunities, and creation of a healthy lifestyle.
1003.activities: The MARC horticulturists and vocational trainer will provide job training in farming produce, environmental awareness, and food production to persons with intellectual and physical disabilities. MARC will also collaborate with the SOS Foundation, a local food pantry through their Farm-to-School grant to help with the education in local school classrooms. MARC and SOS will have 10 to 20 community groups per year to tour the facility to be educated on aquaponics and food sustainability.
1003.direct_services: Direct services will be job training in farming produce, agricultural awareness, and food production. Classroom education on the social, environmental and humanitarian advantages aquaponics provides as a reliable solution to food insecurity.
1003.population: 85 adults and teens with intellectual and physical disabilities, who are living at or below the poverty level. Community education to the classroom will target 300 or more students annually. Community outreach will target 100 to 200 members of the community annually.
1003.outcome: Individuals with developmental and physical disabilities will achieve benchmarks on their individual program goals. This will be measured by the vocational trainer and horticulturist daily, calculated monthly and submitted to APD quarterly. The school programs will be measured by the number of classroom trainings that occur monthly and reported annually. The community outreach will be measured by the number of groups that tour the aquaponics facility monthly and reported annually.

1710.description: The 1 Voice Foundation is a not-for-profit organization that services children who are suffering from pediatric cancer. The Foundation provides emotional, educational and financial support to pediatric cancer families treated at John Hopkins All Childrens Hospital, St. Josephs Childrens Hospital and Tampa General Hospital. ! Voice Foundation currently services Pinellas, Pasco, Hernando, Hardee, Hillsborough, Manatee and Sarasota Counties.
1710.purpose: Expansion of existing programming for children and families suffering for pediatric cancer. 1 Voice Foundation offers over 15 family support programs which include everything from assistance to pediatric care families with medical copays and basic needs (gas, food, rent, utilities) and everything in between. Beyond these family and child centric assistance program, the 1 Voice Foundation offers the Voices of Angels Bereavement Program in addition to research projects conducted by the Foundation.
1710.activities: 1 Voice Foundation works directly with licensed pediatric healthcare professionals ( Tampa General, Johns Hopkins All Childrens Hospital, St. Josephs Childrens Hospital and Moffitt's Adolescent Program) and families to provide needed funding and other support services to alleviate the overall burden caused by the illness. Families receive funding assistance through the "Helping hands" program within the 1 voice foundation.
1710.direct_services: Florida Families will be provided emotional, educational and financial assistance for pediatric cancer families. Operations for the many programs for patients and their families under the 1 Voice academy: Programs and resources to include Support groups, bereavement services, financial assistance, equine therapy, tutoring, toddler program, and siblings program among others.
1710.population: The target population served by this project are the children and families undergoing cancer treatment. 1 Voice has currently serviced nearly 800 families. We expect this trend to continue as we are able to enhance our 20 programs.
1710.outcome: The target population served by this project are the children and families undergoing cancer treatment. 1 Voice has currently serviced nearly 800 families. We expect this trend to continue as we are able to enhance our 20 programs.

1002.description: The project will provide a proven training and reentry program at two Florida facilities, to be identified by the Florida Department of Corrections (FDC), along with the addition of a career readiness instructor, support specialist, and post- release support services. The program will equip individuals for lasting careers in tech by offering full-stack coding instruction, industry certifications, and reentry support. Persevere has achieved remarkable results, including a recidivism rate far below the national average and an impressive percentage of graduates securing sustainable employment as a direct result of the skills learned through this program. This program will reduce recidivism, increase employment outcomes, and contribute to Florida’s workforce needs by preparing formerly incarcerated individuals for careers in the high-demand tech sector.
1002.purpose: The program will provide training and reentry services at two Florida facilities, to be identified by FDC, along with the addition of a career readiness instructor, support specialist, and post-release support services. The program will equip individuals for lasting careers in tech by offering full-stack coding instruction, industry certifications, and reentry support. Persevere has demonstrated its ability to reduce recidivism and increase employment outcomes for incarcerated individuals. Since
1002.activities: A comprehensive program designed to equip incarcerated individuals with the technical skills, career readiness, and reentry support necessary for long-term success, the Persevere program implements a proven and comprehensive model of service delivery. The program is centered on technology education and includes computer coding training resulting in six industry standard certifications. Career readiness training is delivered alongside coding education to support a successful transition from incar
1002.direct_services: The program will increase public safety and protect Floridians by providing meaningful technology and coding education to incarcerated individuals to jobs upon reentry and ultimately improve recidivism, expanding Persevere’s evidence-based coding program into two more facilities to serve a larger pool of students, ensuring they gain the skills, support, and opportunities needed for successful reen
1002.population: Incarcerated individuals within FDC. As the program continues to scale and expand, hundreds of incarcerated individuals will benefit over multiple years. By expanding this program, Florida will reduce recidivism, increase employment rates for formerly incarcerated individuals, and support Florida’s workforce needs by training individuals for high-demand technology careers, addressing critical labor shortages in the tech sector. This project will directly serve incarcerated individuals, but its i
1002.outcome: To equip incarcerated individuals with marketable technology skills, specifically six industry-recognized certifications. Florida employers will also benefit. Businesses in need of skilled technology professionals will gain access to a diverse, motivated talent pool. By lowering recidivism rates, this project will reduce incarceration costs and improve public safety for communities and taxpayers. To ensure accountability and measure impact, Persevere will implement a comprehensive performance tracking system. The use of data-driven tracking and continuous evaluation will ensure measurable, long-term success.

1890.description: Funding would be utilized for a comprehensive safety training program designed specifically for teachers, school staff, and administrators. Participants will engage in practical self-defense techniques that will enhance their situational awareness and boost their confidence in safeguarding themselves and those in their care.
1890.purpose: Promote a safe learning environment & fostering confidence for everyone. If educators are equipped with self-defense skills, there's sense of security which allows students to focus more. Encourages discipline, respect, and teamwork, essential qualities that contribute to a positive educational atmosphere. Valuable life skills, resilience, & ability to respond to challenging situations, enriching overall educational experience.
1890.activities: This program combines various approaches to equip individuals with the skills to become a hard target, focusing on the importance of mindset and situational awareness. Participants will engage in hands-on real-world scenarios and dynamic group discussions. This comprehensive training helps them recognize, avoid, and de-escalate potential conflicts before they escalate into physical confrontations.
1890.direct_services: Real-life self-defense training using a flashlight and pepper spray. This program is expected to reach a total of 1,440 citizens directly and up to 107,280 citizens indirectly.
1890.population: Teachers, administrators, additional school personnel, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, family and friends.
1890.outcome: Each participant will be required to complete a comprehensive questionnaire both before and after the training session. This assessment will help evaluate their initial knowledge, track progress, and measure the overall effectiveness of the training program.

1163.description: The City of Venice, Florida, owns and operates a 4.48 million gallons per day (mgd) reverse osmosis (RO) water treatment plant (WTP) that treats brackish source water from the 14 groundwater wells. The WTP produces a finished water product that meets or exceeds State of Florida and federal drinking water requirements. Finished water is pumped into city's water distribution system for potable water use. The current RO system is designed with four skids, and each skid supports a single stage filtration process with 60% recovery of the brackish feed water supply. This project would add additional membranes to increase water production by approximately 500,000 gallons per day. This project is considered critical infrastructure to support future population growth and enhance system reliability and resiliency.
1163.purpose: Increase water production by approximately 500,000 gallons per day. This project is considered critical infrastructure to support future population growth and enhance system resiliency. This water plant serves the entire community, residents, tourists and local businesses.
1163.activities: The city with the assistance of a consultant, is currently working on design and engineering to upgrade processes and integrate various existing systems. These funds will be utilized for the purchase and installation of the new treatment units, automation upgrades and auxiliary systems. Ultimately, the expansion enhances water quality and reliability, protects public health, supports community growth and strengthens system sustainability and resilience.
1163.direct_services: Direct services include improved drinking water quality, increased supply reliability, enhance public health protection, support for community growth (new homes, businesses and tourists) and greater system resilience.
1163.population: The entire City of Venice, residents, businesses and tourists, will benefit from adding more water production. Recent data show approximately 29,000 residents in the City of Venice.
1163.outcome: The addition of membranes to the treatment facility is expected to deliver a more reliable and higher-capacity water supply that consistently meets regulatory standards, improves drinking water quality, safeguards public health, and supports future growth. Outcomes will be measured through compliance with the state and federal water quality regulations, tracking of plant capacity versus demand, routine monitoring of key water quality parameters, reductions in service interruptions and boil-water notices, customer satisfaction feedback, and documentation of new service connections and population served.

3529.description: Webber International University, located in Polk County, seeks funding to enhance campus safety through upgraded surveillance, access control, and lighting; improved emergency communication; Sentinel training with PCSO; and safety education. Serving nearly 1,000 individuals, this initiative strengthens infrastructure, reduces response times, and fosters a secure learning environment.
3529.purpose: Strengthen campus safety and emergency preparedness at Webber International University by upgrading surveillance systems, implementing advanced access control, and enhancing coordination with local law enforcement, fire, and EMS. This $388,567 initiative improves crime prevention, accelerates emergency response, and ensures a secure, resilient learning environment for students, faculty, and staff.
3529.activities: The appropriation will directly benefit the campus population by providing real-time monitoring of facilities, enabling rapid emergency alerts, and offering proactive safety training. These services will enhance the university’s ability to prevent, detect, and respond to emergencies, thereby improving the overall safety and well-being of those on campus.
3529.direct_services: Real-time monitoring, emergency alerts, safety training to the campus community and surrounding area.
3529.population: The target population served by this project includes students, faculty, staff, and visitors to Webber International University. The initiative is expected to benefit more than 800 individuals annually. This includes full-time and part-time students, academic and administrative personnel, and guests who attend events or visit the campus for various purposes.
3529.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project include an enhanced sense of safety and security across the Webber International University campus, along with improved emergency preparedness and response capabilities. the initiative is designed to proactively address potential safety concerns and ensure a secure environment for all. Success will be measured through a combination of Clery Act statistics, internal incident reporting, and security audits.

2760.description: This project will make repairs and alterations to the City of Apopka's current training facility in order to be compliant with Florida Administrative Code 69A-37.060 in an effort to become certified as an approved Firefighter Recruit Training Facility. Money will be used to purchase the required tools, equipment, apparatus, and props for a certified firefighter recruit training facility.
2760.purpose: The goal is to make the necessary renovations to the existing training facility and purchase the required tools, equipment, apparatus and props to become a certified firefighting recruit training facility in compliance with Florida Administrative Code 69A-37.060. The City of Apopka will offer firefighter recruit training to high school aged students in the Central Florida area.
2760.activities: These funds will help create a certified firefighter recruit training facility for high school students in the Central Florida area. The training facility will offer fire and EMS training providing a direct pathway to certification and career readiness in the fire and emergency services field.
2760.direct_services: The firefighter recruit training facility will offer State of Florida approved curriculum in both Fire and Emergency Medical Services. This program will provide trained EMS's and firefighters for the Central Florida region providing emergency care to over 100,000 people in the region.
2760.population: The target population will be high school aged students and approximately 70 - 90 will be enrolled annually in the program. In addition, this program will provide trained EMS's and firefighters for the Central Florida region providing emergency care to over 100,000 people in the region.
2760.outcome: Enrollment, graduation and job placement of all students who attend the program, all of which are measured annually.

2762.description: The City of Apopka is seeking state grant funding for the urgent replacement and modernization of Master Lift Station #017, a critical wastewater asset that has exceeded its useful life and serves as a vital component of the City's collection system. Located within and serving portions of the Apopka Community Redevelopment Area (CRA), this project supports ongoing revitalization by ensuring reliable wastewater service, protecting public health, and strengthening community resilience.
2762.purpose: It will be able to fund the construction costs associated with the lift station replacement.
2762.activities: Existing lift station will be abandoned/ demolished. New lift station will be able to continue serving its existing customers.
2762.direct_services: The citizens, homes, business that are being served by the sewer network will be able to have continuous, uninterrupted service.
2762.population: The target population is the customers of Apopka Utilities. Approx 20,000 citizens is currently being served by this lift station.
2762.outcome: The expected outcome is that the new lift station will be put to service while maintaining uninterrupted service to the existing customers. The new lift station will also be able to handle the expected growth in population of the city in the future. The outcome will be measured by the frequency of which the new lift station will be serviced and maintained. If the new lift station functions properly and is able to handle the increased sewer flow in the region without accidents or spills, it is considered a success.

1892.description: As a part of a public partnership with the Lake County Board of County Commissioners, the Golden Triangle Regional Park consists of an East Campus and a West Campus to comprise Lake County's regional park system, as identified in the adopted Parks & Trails Master Plan. The West Campus is a 58-acre site located at the Woodlea Sports Complex in Tavares. Improvements to the park started more than a decade ago in 2013 with the addition of two (2) adult-size baseball fields. To maximize space, they were constructed on the far end of the park, away from the existing youth fields and other amenities. The following year field lighting was installed to allow for night-time play. Other improvements such as new irrigation throughout the park, laser grading, and re-sodding the existing youth-size fields have been major projects completed. We request this appropriation to expand on the park amenities

2674.description: Despite ongoing efforts to stabilize the workforce, the Florida Department of Corrections (FDOC) continues to see a decrease among workforce applicants, length of employment, and an overall decline in workforce size. In order to minimize attrition (employee turnover) and ensure a healthy pipeline of FDOC workforce, Qualtrics proposes the development and implementation of a full-scale Employee Retention Program to identify areas of opportunity across the employee lifecycle to most effectively support current and potential staff and retain them. Qualtrics will develop individual surveys and touchpoints to measure employee satisfaction and engagement across a number of key factors within their work day. This will enhance engagement of individual and collective staff to ensure transparency and accountability across the Department.
2674.purpose: The intended goal of the program is to 1) retain existing employees within the Department of Corrections and 2) support the development and culture of new talent to ensure a sustainable pipeline of employees now and into the future.
2674.activities: Software implementation and program consultancy will be provided throughout the life cycle of the program. Qualtrics is providing the program guidance, software platform, and support to ensure a successful implementation and intended purpose being met. All aspects of program development will be provided by Qualtrics and/or Qualtrics partners.
2674.direct_services: Citizens can be assured of the following 1) Community Safety - ensuring streets are safe and inmates housed 2) Employment Culture and Climate - Corrections staff working in safe conditions and needs being met (as described by them in survey responses) 3) Prison Safety and Satisfaction - higher satisfaction leads to decreased violence among inmates, leading to safer working and living conditions wi
2674.population: The target population is the Corrections staff statewide. A minimum of 30,000 staff are expected to be contacted throughout the life of the program.
2674.outcome: Through the use of Qualtrics proprietary technology and methodology, we should see increases in employee retention and satisfaction, as well as decreased in inmate violence.

1327.description: The Vet Resource Center will provide free early warning cancer detection for all Florida veterans exposed to burn pits and toxins using the Galleri test that detects 50 plus different types of cancer as early as stage 1. We track the progress of each test and help the veterans receive any needed cancer treatment. Currently, we provide this test at no cost to veterans that reside in Marion County through grants. We are the only nonprofit in the country that provides this test for our veterans. The Vet Resource Center is a 100% volunteer board. No one accepts a salary. We 100% support our veterans!
1327.purpose: Early warning cancer detection tests for veterans that have been exposed to burn pits and toxins. The Galleri test can detect over 50 different types of cancer at stage 1 or stage 2.
1327.activities: We provide the marketing and advertising of our early warning cancer detection program in order to identify and recruit Florida veterans that have been exposed to burn pits and toxins. We verify the veteran's status, register the veteran for the Galleri blood test and pay for the Galleri early warning cancer detection test. We track the progress of each test and help the veteran receive any needed cancer treatment.
1327.direct_services: 1,100 Grail Galleri early warning cancer detection tests for Florida veterans exposed to Burn Pits and Toxins while in service of our Country. We give the Galleri test free to these Florida veterans to catch over 50 plus different types of cancer at stage 1 or stage 2. Matching local and in kind donations will allow a total of 2,500 Florida veterans to receive the early detection cancer test.
1327.population: Over 2,500 Florida Veterans that have been exposed to burn pits and toxins will be tested for cancer by receiving the Galleri early warning cancer detection test for free.
1327.outcome: Florida veterans have to deal everyday with the fear that they will be hit with the ravages of cancer from their exposure to burn pits and toxins during their service to our country. Learning that they have no indications of cancer or catching cancer at early stages releases this constant strain on the mental health of these veterans. The testing improves the veteran's economic self sufficiency. The cost of early detected cancer treatment is over 10 times less expensive than in stage 3 or stage 4 and improves the use of Florida medical facilities because treating advanced cancer requires the use of many times more medical resources than the treatment provided when a cancer is detected early.

The agency offers a comprehensive approach to increasing protective factors that promote healthy families and increase social and community engagement. OMC facilitates these services out of multiple campuses and family resource centers strategically located in the greater Jacksonville and Sarasota/Bradenton areas. These centers offer a collaborative approach to care by maximizing the strengths of community providers, building trust in established partnerships, distributing tangible resources to asset limited, income-constrained, employed families, and providing intangible services such as evidenced-based parenting models to strengthen parenting skills and knowledge. The focus of this program is to equip pare
3320.purpose: Expand direct services and concrete support for parenting households with guardianship or custody of one or more children ages 0-17. The prevention programs will include community education, a parent advisory committee, and implementation of a protective factors modality, coupled with trauma-informed practices to mitigate the risk of adverse childhood experiences.
3320.activities: Qualified staff will provide direct services for parents and their children. Services may include distribution of goods, administering evidence-based curriculum training, life skills training, job skills training, financial literacy supports, referrals to continued education, nutritional support, and other community resources such as mental and behavioral health referrals.
3320.direct_services: As identified by individual need, to include a combination of: family support, education, case management, vocational skills, parenting skills, residential care, financial management, and access to mental/behavioral health services.
3320.population: The target population includes vulnerable adults 18+ who are pregnant or parenting children aged 0-17, and who have custody/guardianship of at least one child, and who are at risk of child welfare involvement. This may includes persons experiencing joblessness, mental health crises, homelessness, substance abuse recovery, domestic abuse recovery, survivors of sex-trafficking, and/or other economically disadvantaged populations. OMC expects to serve 250+ annually.
3320.outcome: 1.) Increased concrete support as a protective factor. This will be measured through the completion of one or more of the following on a program participant's service plan: a) linkage to an external referral, b) distribution of tangible goods, c) positive change from pre- to post- score of the "Protective Factors Survey". 2.) Increased social support as a protective factor. This will be measured through self-reporting within the discharge plan and/or by a positive change in the client survey. 3.) Reduced allegations of abuse, maltreatment, neglect. This will be documented via self-reporting and through weekly check-in meetings listed in client case files in the electronic client database.
