1125.description: The City of West Melbourne proposes to construct a new box culvert beneath Henry Avenue, near the intersection with Doherty Drive, to replace the existing undersized and irregularly configured storm sewer system. Currently, stormwater from the existing ditch on the north side of Henry Avenue flows through two 48-inch pipes into an existing collection box. A third 48-inch storm sewer also discharges into this collection box. From the collection box, a single 48-inch pipe conveys the stormwater to the existing regional canal system on the south side of Henry Avenue. This configuration can cause stormwater to back up in the system north of Henry Avenue and contribute to localized flooding during storm events. Installation of a properly sized box culvert will eliminate these hydraulic bottlenecks, improve conveyance, and ensure free flow of water between the regional drainage ditch north of
1125.purpose: The funds will be used to construct a new box culvert beneath Henry Avenue to replace the undersized storm sewer system, improve stormwater flow, reduce localized flooding, and enhance public safety and infrastructure resiliency.
1125.activities: Activities will include designing and constructing a properly sized box culvert beneath Henry Avenue, removing existing undersized pipes, installing new stormwater infrastructure, and coordinating with roadway improvements to ensure improved drainage and reduced flooding.
1125.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with improved stormwater management, reducing localized flooding, protecting property and roadways, and ensuring safer travel and enhanced public safety during storm events.
1125.population: The project serves residents, businesses, and commuters in the area surrounding Henry Avenue and Doherty Drive in West Melbourne who are affected by localized flooding and stormwater issues.
1125.outcome: The project will reduce localized flooding along Henry Avenue, improve stormwater conveyance from the northern ditch to the regional canal, enhance roadway safety, and protect surrounding properties and infrastructure. The outcome will be measured by the successful construction and commissioning of the new box culvert, confirmation of improved stormwater flow through hydraulic modeling and inspections, and monitoring during storm events to verify reduced flooding and proper system performance.

1126.description: The City of West Melbourne is requesting funding for the construction of a new, higher-capacity, and more resilient industrial injection well system to support long-term wastewater management. The City’s current municipal injection well has been in operation for more than 40 years and is approaching the end of its reliable service life. Reliance on this aging infrastructure creates increasing risks of system failure, limited capacity, and potential environmental harm. The proposed project will provide critical new capacity, improve system resiliency, and ensure the City can effectively manage wastewater well into the future. By reducing dependence on the existing injection well, the new system will help safeguard against issues such as vertical migration and failures during high flow events, both of which pose risks to groundwater resources. This initiative represents a proactive investm
1126.purpose: The requested funds will allow the City of West Melbourne to construct a new, higher-capacity and more resilient industrial injection well to replace reliance on its 40-year-old municipal well. This project will ensure long-term wastewater management capacity, reduce the risk of environmental harm, and protect groundwater resources by preventing system failures and potential contamination during high flow events.
1126.activities: The funds requested will support all activities and services necessary to design, construct, and test a new deep industrial injection well, installation of wellheads and valves, and injection testing to ensure reliable, resilient wastewater management.
1126.direct_services: This important project will provide West Melbourne residents and businesses with reliable and resilient wastewater management, reducing the risk of system failures, environmental contamination, and protecting groundwater resources for the community.
1126.population: The project serves the residents, businesses, and industries of the City of West Melbourne who rely on the municipal wastewater system.
1126.outcome: The project will provide the City of West Melbourne with a higher-capacity, resilient industrial injection well, ensuring reliable wastewater management, reducing environmental risks, and protecting groundwater resources. Citizens and businesses will benefit from reduced risk of system failures and potential contamination. This will be measured by successful construction and commissioning of the industrial injection well, completion of injection testing to confirm operational capacity, and ongoing monitoring to ensure reliable wastewater disposal and no adverse impact on groundwater quality.

1038.organization: Palm Beach County Board of County
1038.description: This project will elevate an already popular park facility into a premier cross country venue, delivering both community and economic benefits. By enhancing the course, the park will better serve local high schools, running clubs, and regional competitions, while also strengthening Palm Beach County’s position as a sports tourism leader. Sports tourism generated over $23 million in direct economic impact last year, with public parks and recreation facilities contributing more than one-third of that total. The $850,000 investment in course improvements is projected to be recouped within three years through event-driven tourism alone, while the improvements themselves will last far longer, continuing to generate sustained economic activity. The ripple effect is significant: local hotels, restaurants, and small businesses will benefit from increased room nights and visitor spending, while r
1038.purpose: The requested funding will assist with the construction of a regional cross country facility which is anticipated to attract larger regional, state and national cross country events. At completion the amenitized facility is expected to provide another sports tourism destination for Palm Beach County.
1038.activities: The location currently hosts cross country meets for schools in Palm Beach and Broward counties. Construction of a restroom, awards stand, storage and other infrastructure improvements will allow the facility to host additional meets and accommodate more teams for larger events.
1038.direct_services: The funding will provide for an expanded cross country facility that will be open to all citizens when not in use for cross country events.
1038.population: Two distinct populations will be served by the project: 1) School aged cross country athletes (College, High School and Middle School). 2) Any citizen interested in a designated safe area to walk or run without interruption. Over 50,000 athletes and local citizens are expected to utilize the facility annually upon completion.
1038.outcome: The expected outcome of this construction project is the increased use of the facility by both citizens and athletes. The Parks and Recreation Department uses Placer.ai to track park visitation. The Department will analyze data prior to and after the completion of the amenities to accurately measure changes in facility use.

1321.description: The proposed infrastructure improvements to the gravity sewer collection system are designed to mitigate elevated risks of infiltration and exfiltration, thereby reducing the likelihood of sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) at manholes and pump stations—events that pose a direct threat to the Indian River Lagoon (IRL). These upgrades also help prevent capacity- related issues at the treatment facility, ensuring more efficient wastewater treatment and minimizing surface water discharges into the IRL.
1321.purpose: The proposed infrastructure improvements to the gravity sewer collection system are designed to mitigate elevated risks of infiltration and exfiltration, thereby reducing the likelihood of sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) at manholes and pump stations—events that pose a direct threat to the Indian River Lagoon (IRL). These upgrades also help prevent capacity-related issues at the treatment facility, ensuring more efficient wastewater treatment and minimizing surface water discharges into the IRL.
1321.activities: The project will have an environmental purpose, the project enhances ecological resilience in the adjacent aquatic ecosystems of the Indian River Lagoon Estuary and the Atlantic Ocean by preventing sewage overflows and leaks that contribute to eutrophication and water quality degradation.
1321.direct_services: The project safeguards public health by containing wastewater, preventing contamination of clean water sources, and mitigating environmental pollution. Its passive, gravity-based design and precise engineering enhance resilience, making the system less vulnerable to power outages and mechanical failures.
1321.population: This project will serve the more than 11,000 residents of Cocoa Beach, as well as the approximately 2.5 million tourists who visit annually. Additionally, through memorandum of understand (mou) agreement, the City of Cocoa Beach provides sewer collection to neighboring communities, including Cape Canaveral, Satellite Beach, Port Canaveral, and Patrick Space Force Base, further extending the regional impact of this critical infrastructure investment.
1321.outcome: This project will address elevated risks of infiltration and exfiltration, helping to prevent sanitary sewer overflows that reduce capacity in the sewer conveyance system and treatment plant. By minimizing discharges to surface waters, the project will help keep excess nutrients out of the environment. It will also reduce strain on equipment, conserve resources, and lower restoration needs. As a key component of responsible wastewater management, the project will enhance the collection, treatment, and reuse of wastewater, ultimately protecting vital water resources.

2823.description: Florida Gateway College recently received a donation of a 2-story vacant medical practice building located in downtown Lake City. The value of this donation was appraised at $1.25M. This donated building will vastly expand our allied health programs and allow FGC to produce more medical professionals for our community. The roof and HVAC systems will need to be replaced along with other minor interior modifications.
2823.purpose: This donated building will vastly expand our allied health programs and allow FGC to produce more medical professionals for our community. The roof and HVAC systems will need to be replaced along with other minor interior modifications.
2823.activities: This donated building will vastly expand our allied health programs and allow FGC to produce more medical professionals for our community. The roof and HVAC systems will need to be replaced along with other minor interior modifications.
2823.direct_services: This donated building will vastly expand our allied health programs and allow FGC to produce more medical professionals for our community. Students will now have even more access to the health professions in FGC's current programs and expanded programs due to this newly available space.
2823.population: Allied health students in Baker, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, and Union Counties will be served by this project. The number of individuals will become tens of thousands over time.
2823.outcome: The expected benefit is that more students will have access to current and expanded healthcare related professions. This outcome can be measured by enrollment and completion data.

1182.description: Funds are being requested for design of Phase 7 - Sand Dollar and Sand Pine Road. The planning study recommended drainage improvements consisting of lining of the aging Corrugated Metal Pipes (CMP); replacement of curb inlets and associated piping; the addition of a second inlet to ensure adequate inlet capacity for areas to the west; and replacement of drainage structure in residential backyards. Construction was funded by County and ARPA funding for Phase 1 in the approximate amount of $3,524,518. The contractor was recently issued a construction notice to proceed for Phase 1. Brevard County is also anticipating receipt of FY 26 State funding through FDEP totaling $1,764,078 to construct the Phase 2 ($3.5M) project with a 50% County match. The County is awaiting notification of funding through a federal appropriation for the Phase 4 ($4M) project (50% County match). The overall project
1182.purpose: The specific purpose to be achieved by this funding request is to design improvements to alleviate flooding that occurs along Sand Dollar Road and Sand Pine Road in Brevard's Stormwater District 4 Indialantic Region. The project will also improve water quality in the Indian River Lagoon by improving stormwater resiliency in the area.
1182.activities: Proposed improvements include: • Lining of aging Corrugated Metal Pipes (CMP) • Replacement of two (2) pairs of curb inlets and associated piping along Sand Dollar Road and Sand Pine Road • Addition of second pair of inlets along the streets to ensure adequate inlet capacity for depressional areas to the west • Drainage structure impacts at residential backyards may require replacement
1182.direct_services: The proposed improvements will alleviate flooding issues in neighborhoods within the Indialantic region.
1182.population: The target population are the residents of the area around the identified areas of flooding including Sand Dollar Road and Sand Pipes Road. Approximately 5000 individuals will be served by the overall proposed improvements.
1182.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of the project is the replacement and/or upgrades the drainage systems to reach an acceptable level of service for flood control throughout the project area. The outcome will be measured during rainy conditions in the area to determine whether the improvements alleviated flooding by allowing the runoff to flow to the three (3) existing outfalls.

3155.description: This is a request to revert and reappropriate a project funded within the Fiscal Year 2025-26 General Appropriations Act, Specific Appropriation 2245A (SF 2039 and HF 1351). The project was funded at $400,000. The Gilchrist County Fire Rescue requested funds to purchase a Ford F-550 XLT 4x4 SD Crew Cab (4-Door) Commercial Chassis, Mini Pumper specifically equipped and designed to meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards. The purchase and delivery of the mini pumper may not occur prior to the end of the FY 25-26 fiscal year. If the funds are reverted and reappropriated for the same purpose, it would allow Gilchrist County and the manufacturer to meet estimated deliverables. Given the rural landscape of Gilchrist County, characterized by long response times and a lack of hydrants, it is vital to maximize personnel deployment while minimizing the amount of equipment used.
3155.purpose: The mini-pumper provides enhanced maneuverability allowing access to narrow roadways, limited access areas and supports emergency needs during storms. Its versatility enables it to serve as a first response vehicle equipped with advanced life support and capable of transporting four dual-certified responders for both fire and medical emergencies. It also acts as an extension to pump water in areas with limited access. The compact design facilitates quick responses, ensuring effective transport o
3155.activities: This first response vehicle is designed to transport four firefighters and medical personnel to manage both fires and medical emergencies. It is suited for tackling brush and structure fires, provides Advanced Life Support, and is equipped for confined space rescues and vehicle extrications. Furthermore, it supports community fire safety programs to improve preparedness and enhance safety.
3155.direct_services: The purchase of the mini-pumper will improve overall response times, provide greater access to rural areas, the ability to extend the range water can be delivered from a tanker truck with continuous flow that is to large to gain access, and provide greater response capabilities during severe weather conditions. Quick response and recovery depends on the ability to respond with the right equipment
3155.population: The population of Gilchrist County of over 17,864 (aka: Springs Capital of the World) and about 40,000 annual visitors. Gilchrist is a rural community covering an area of 349 sq miles and a population density of 51 persons per sq mile with no county fire hydrants. We are a rural area of concern with agriculture being its largest industry.
3155.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is an enhanced emergency response capacity, improved public safety, and increased readiness to address community needs. The outcome will be measured through quantitative metrics such as reduced emergency response times, increased operational efficiency, and enhanced coordination between emergency services. Qualitative indicators, including citizen feedback and incident reports, will also gauge the project's success in providing a safer and more secure environment for the Gilchrist community.

3156.description: This is a request to revert and reappropriate project funded within the Fiscal Year 2025-26 General Appropriations Act, Specific Appropriation 2245A (SF 2040 and HF 1352). The Gilchrist County Fire Rescue requested funds to purchase an E-1 Pumper-Tanker 2500 gallon Combination apparatus specifically equipped and designed to meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards. The purchase and delivery of the pumper tanker may not occur prior to the end of the FY 25-26 fiscal year. If the funds are reverted and reappropriated for the same purpose, it would allow Gilchrist County and the manufacturer to meet estimated deliverables. Given the rural landscape of Gilchrist County, characterized by long response times and a lack of hydrants, it is vital to maximize personnel deployment while minimizing the amount of equipment used.
3156.purpose: This is a request to revert and reappropriate funding for FY 25-26 for the same purpose. We need to replace two aging fleet vehicles. Adding this combination apparatus that has a high capacity for water carrying, along with the versatility of a pumper, will allow us to transport the necessary personnel and equipment, along with enough water to effectively respond to service calls. This will enable GCFR to manage fire emergencies more efficiently, maximize our inventory use, and reduce budget ove
3156.activities: The first response vehicle is specifically engineered to transport water directly to fire sites and pump it onto the flames, streamlining operations by negating the necessity for separate pumper and tanker vehicles. Its cab has the capacity to accommodate the same number of personnel as both of those vehicles combined. This innovative service enhances the efficiency of fire emergency management. Furthermore, it actively supports community fire safety initiatives aimed at improving preparedness a
3156.direct_services: This 2,500-gallon combination pumper-tanker will effectively handle the majority of the county's fire emergencies. Acquiring this pumper-tanker will enhance overall response times and improve our response capabilities. Quick response and recovery relies on having the right equipment and personnel available to manage emergencies and prevent the loss of life and property.
3156.population: The population of Gilchrist County of over 17,864 (aka: Springs Capital of the World) and about 40,000 annual visitors. Gilchrist is a rural community covering an area of 349 sq miles and a population density of 51 persons per sq mile with no county fire hydrants. We are a rural area of concern with agriculture being its largest industry.
3156.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is an enhanced emergency response capacity, improved public safety, and increased readiness to address community needs. The outcome will be measured through quantitative metrics such as reduced emergency response times, increased operational efficiency, and enhanced coordination between emergency services. Qualitative indicators, including citizen feedback and incident reports, will also gauge the project's success in providing a safer and more secure environment for the Gilchrist community.

2821.description: Request $2,000,000 in non-recurring GR to provide staff retention bonuses to juvenile justice direct-care staff employed by contracted providers of the Florida Department of Juvenile Justice. Current contracted employees working directly with children under the Department's care, control, and custody would receive annual retention compensation based on longevity of employment and performance.
2821.purpose: Retain direct care staff providing critical services in community based prevention, diversion/redirection who keep kids from moving to the deep end of the juvenile justice system.
2821.activities: Increase public safety for Floridians, provide greater continuity of care for at-risk children, and save taxpayer dollars.
2821.direct_services: Retain staff for better continuity of services to at-risk children which helps reduce recidivism.
2821.population: Children under the direct supervision of these employees will be supervised by a higher quality of staff that is consistent with the general principles of the Roadmap to System Excellence, reducing recidivism and CCC incidents.
2821.outcome: Retain staff for better continuity of services to at-risk children which helps reduce recidivism.

1178.description: Remove and replace approximately 6,400 sq. ft. of wood decking with composite decking. Using composite decking will increase the life span of the pier.
1178.purpose: New pier decking will assure the safety of visitors, enhance the appearance of the pier and allow boaters, fishing and other water activities involving the pier to be utilized safely.
1178.activities: Fishing, boating, scenic views, serenity and safety of all users.
1178.direct_services: The decking on the pier is deteriorating making it unsafe for its users.
1178.population: Citizens of the City of Melbourne and Brevard County.
1178.outcome: Enjoyment by all that use the pier.

1024.organization: Palm Beach County Board of County
1024.description: The Morikami Museum and Japanese Gardens is an internationally celebrated and locally loved attraction that will celebrate its 50th anniversary in the near future. The Amanohashidate (bridge to heaven) garden expansion at the Morikami Museum will enhance the attraction of the facility and the experience of attendees, boosting the local economy in many ways. With over 200,000 annual visitors, the expansion will increase visitation from across the nation and internationally increasing tourism in the local economy. The garden expansion is consistent with the destination's master plan benefiting residents and visitors as the institution continues to build a bridge between Japan and South Florida.
1024.purpose: Funding for the Amanohashidate Garden phase 1 expansion at the Morikami Museum and Japanese Gardens is essential as the museum approaches its 50th anniversary in 2027. With over 200,000 annual visitors, the expansion will enhance the visitor experience, attract national and international tourism, boost the local economy, and preserve the museum’s century-old mission of fostering cultural understanding between Japan and Florida.
1024.activities: Activity undertaken in this project would be the construction of the aforementioned infrastructure at the Morikami Museum and Japanese Garden.
1024.direct_services: The direct service provided by this project is enhanced infrastructure that would drive economic and tourism benefits, as well as provide a community with an increased cultural drive.
1024.population: The target population for the project’s outcome are citizens of Florida, including the 200,000 annual visitors that enjoy the unique Morikami site and gain a greater understanding of Japan an its relationship to South Florida. More specifically, the project targets visitors to Florida and Palm Beach County discovering this connection while supporting our local economy. The project will provide for an expansion that will allow for an increase in visitor capacity at the museum and gardens.
1024.outcome: The expected outcome of the project would be a sizable increase in visitation to the Japanese garden that would drive provide positive economic benefits to the local community through tourism. Data collection surveys would be utilized to note several categories, including physical health, mental health, cultural experience. Additionally, the county would track visitation data as it relates to increased tourism and economic activity.

1081.organization: Palm Beach County Board of County
1081.description: Improving accessible beach infrastructure at this location will ensure that all seniors, veterans, individuals with disabilities, and families with mobility needs can fully experience the natural beauty and recreational opportunities our coastline offers. Beaches are the number one tourist destination in Palm Beach County and ensuring they are fully accessible is a priority identified in our county-wide needs assessment. Serving both citizens and visitors of Palm Beach County since 1988, Ocean Inlet Park is a vital hub of recreation and aquatic activity. This project will provide accessibility from the parking located on the west of A1A through a redesigned, improved and safer pedestrian beach access point for the park on the east side of A1A.
1081.purpose: The requested funding will assist with the planning and design of a fully accessible pedestrian beach crossover at Ocean Inlet Park which will attract citizens and visitors of all abilities to this beach. At completion, the much needed public beach access is expected to provide an excellent opportunity for the public to enjoy the mental and physical health benefits of being outdoors and that visiting this beach park provides. Beaches are an economic driver in Florida and making this beach more a
1081.activities: Planning, design and permitting consultant services will be provided through this funding to meet the intended purpose of these funds. This is a critical step in the planning, design and construction process.
1081.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide for a fully accessible pedestrian beach crossover at Ocean Inlet Park which will serve citizens and visitors of all abilities. This was a high need identified by our community during our parks master planning process. The central location in Palm Beach County is beneficial in many ways for this area of the County to realize economic benefit through visitor sp
1081.population: Two distinct populations will be served by the project: 1) The general public with and without accessibility needs, strollers, and mobility devices visiting the beach 2) Tourists with and without accessibility needs, strollers, and mobility devices visiting the beach. Over 350,000 beach goers are expected to utilize the accessible beach crossover annually upon completion.
1081.outcome: The expected outcome of this construction project is improving accessibility and visitation to this outdoor recreation site; improved visitor satisfaction and improved pedestrian safety. This will be measured throughout Placer.ai visitation measurement data collection tool, feedback received by our staff, and evaluation of pedestrian incident report frequency.

This platform will include multilingual access in Spanish and Creole, ensuring equitable participation from South Florida’s diverse business community. By accelerating local sourcing and supplier matchmaking, it will reduce costs, strengthen small business visibility, minimize supply-chain disruptions, and increase intrastate trade. The initiative promotes job creation, manufacturing resilience, and a stronger regional identity within Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, and Monroe Counties.
1027.purpose: Funds will launch the South Florida Supply Chain Connector to strengthen regional manufacturing and procurement networks by mapping suppliers, buyers, and manufacturers across key sectors such as marine, biotech, food, construction, and export logistics. The project enhances CONNEX Florida with a bilingual platform (Spanish and Creole) to expand access for businesses of all sizes. The initiative will accelerate local sourcing, connect companies with nearby suppliers, and reduce dependence on out
1027.activities: The project will design, build, and operate the South Florida Supply Chain Connector as a bilingual regional overlay to CONNEX Florida. Activities include mapping manufacturers, suppliers, and buyers across Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, and Monroe Counties; clustering data by industry; and conducting outreach, onboarding, and verification of participating businesses. One-year professional contracts will support operations, data analysis, outreach coordination, vendor liaison, legal and compli
1027.direct_services: The South Florida Supply Chain Connector will directly serve businesses and residents by creating a bilingual online platform that connects manufacturers, suppliers, and buyers across the region. Businesses will gain free access to a searchable supplier database, matchmaking tools, and training on how to secure contracts and reduce costs through local sourcing. Citizens benefit through job creatio
1027.population: The South Florida Supply Chain Connector will serve manufacturers, suppliers, and business buyers located across Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, and Monroe Counties. The target population includes small, medium, and large companies in key sectors—marine, biotech, food production, construction, and export logistics—as well as entrepreneurs seeking entry into supply-chain markets. The project will also support workforce development by connecting local jobseekers with expanding manufacturers. Duri
1027.outcome: The South Florida Supply Chain Connector will strengthen regional manufacturing, reduce supply-chain disruptions, and increase intrastate procurement by linking buyers, suppliers, and manufacturers through a bilingual digital platform. Expected outcomes include measurable growth in local sourcing, job creation, and procurement cost savings. The project will also improve access for businesses in key sectors and enhance economic resilience across four counties. Outcomes will be tracked using platform analytics, business onboarding data, procurement value shifts, and quarterly performance reports comparing baseline metrics to post-implementation results.

1127.description: The Indialantic Fishing Pier, located on the Indian River Lagoon, has been a beloved landmark for nearly 25 years. Extending 400 feet into the lagoon, the pier features built-in seating along the walkway, lighting, side rails, and a covered observation deck at its western end. This inviting space offers residents and visitors opportunities to fish, relax, observe local wildlife, and enjoy breathtaking sunsets over the water. The estimated total cost of the refurbishment is $890,000. This amount may be divided between the main walkway portion and the observation deck. While the original pier was built using marine-treated wood and stainless-steel fasteners, the Town is exploring the use of durable composite material to provide greater longevity and reduce future maintenance costs.
1127.purpose: These funds are being requested to replace a current pier that was built over 25 years ago and has deteriorated. By updating the pier, it will become ADA compliant. This will allow the public to access the pier which is over the Indian River Lagoon. The pier can be used for fishing, education and observation of the wildlife of the Indian River Lagoon.
1127.activities: The Indialantic Fishing Pier, located on the Indian River Lagoon, has been a beloved landmark for nearly 25 years. Extending 400 feet into the lagoon, the pier features built-in seating along the walkway, lighting, side rails, and a covered observation deck at its western end. This inviting space offers residents and visitors opportunities to fish, relax, observe local wildlife, and enjoy breathtaking sunsets over the water.
1127.direct_services: In addition to recreation, the pier serves as an educational resource. Oyster beds have been installed nearby to help improve water quality in the Indian River Lagoon, and informational signage educates visitors about the lagoon’s delicate ecosystem.
1127.population: All residents of Florida to include visitors from out of state.
1127.outcome: The use of the pier for outdoor activity such as fishing. It will also be an observation point for the Indian River Lagoon and education about the lagoon.

1328.description: The Pearl Project's goal is to provide life-changing support to the youngest victims of the opioid crisis. Babies exposed to substances in utero face developmental, physical, and behavioral challenges that can last a lifetime—affecting their ability to thrive at home, in school, and in the community. The Pearl Project will provide evidence-based, trauma- informed trainings and coaching for caregivers and services to children that promote emotional and relational health.
1328.purpose: To expand The Pearl Project's evidence-based, trauma-informed trainings and coaching for caregivers and services to children that promote emotional and relational health.
1328.activities: Caregivers will be trained in Trust-Based Relational Intervention (TBRI) practices to increase their ability to appropriately respond to a child who has been negatively impacted by substances (including parental substance abuse and prenatal substance exposure). Families will have access to individual coaching and ongoing support to ensure th family is fully supported.
1328.direct_services: Provide caregivers with evidence-based, trauma-informed trainings (virtually and in person) designed to meet the unique needs of children with a history of trauma and impacts of substance abuse. Regular support groups and individual coaching calls will be offered to help with the implementation of new skills. Circle of Security classes will be offered to help caregivers improve attachment with the
1328.population: More than 800 parents and caregivers, and dependent and adopted children.
1328.outcome: Improved mental health: Participants will experience less stress in the home, more connected relationships, leading to improved mental health outcomes. Improve quality of education: Parents will learn to advocate for their children and will be able to help teachers know how to meet their unique needs. This will lead to fewer behavior incidents and improved learning outcomes. Track and report all outcomes.

1179.description: The City is undertaking redeveloping Provost Park in the Diamond Square Community. This project represents a long- overdue investment in equity, safety, and inclusion for an underserved community. The City has already invested over $1.7 million to redevelop a portion of the park and now is adding in new accessible playground equipment, new soccer mini-pitches, and a fitness court. This project supports healthier lifestyles, deters crime and creates a safe, welcoming environment for residents.
1179.purpose: The City is undertaking redeveloping Provost Park in the Diamond Square Community. This project represents a long- overdue investment in equity, safety, and inclusion for an underserved community. The City has already invested over $1.7 million to redevelop a portion of the park and now is adding in new accessible playground equipment, new soccer mini-pitches, and a fitness court. This project supports healthier lifestyles, deters crime and creates a safe, welcoming environment for residents.
1179.activities: With this redevelopment project, Provost Park will have accessible playground equipment, the only playground with this type of equipment in the City, new facilities for youth soccer programming, and fitness equipment that can allow individual and group fitness activity. This project supports healthier lifestyles, deters crime, and creates a safe space for youth and families.
1179.direct_services: Access to healthy recreational alternatives that can provide a safe environment for families in the Cocoa community and another alternative for youth to have access to a sport that can provide opportunities for continuing education. Also, the accessible playground equipment provides direct recreational opportunities for handicap youth in the Cocoa community that don't have this type of equipment.
1179.population: Elderly, youth and economically disadvantaged persons in the surrounding community that will utilize the facilities.
1179.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, protect the general public from harm, reduce recidivism, reduce substance abuse, and divert from the criminal and juvenile justice system by providing recreational opportunities. This can be measured through usage reports.

1019.description: BSI is seeking support to renovate its facility as a one-of-a-kind community offering. BSI provides comprehensive wraparound services that strengthens children and families by promoting self-sufficiency and healthy relationship courses. Headquartered in the heart of South Dade for over 30 years, BSI's existing facility structure does not meet the demand of the 11,000 families served yearly. This initiative will empower Be Strong Village to provide integrated, family strengthening services to families.
1019.purpose: BSI is seeking support to renovate its facility as a one-of-a-kind community offering. BSI provides comprehensive wraparound services that strengthens children and families by promoting self-sufficiency and healthy relationship courses. Headquartered in the heart of South Dade for over 30 years, BSI's existing facility structure does not meet the demand of the 11,000 families served yearly. This initiative will empower Be Strong Village to provide integrated, family strengthening services to fam
1019.activities: The facility will empower families, strengthen relationships, and promote long-term family stability. Ultimately, BSI desires to reduce the risk of child abuse, neglect, and family disruption.
1019.direct_services: Families will be able to access family-strengthening services such as complimentary parenting education & marriage courses and support through evidence-based and evidence informed strategies, youth development services, case management and care coordination services, and support to help families build safe and stable environments.
1019.population: Families, single parents and married parents with poor mental/physical health, at risk youth, homeless but employed families, grade school students, high school students, and university/college students.
1019.outcome: Be Strong Village will serve as a safe haven with community benefit measured by: 1) Centralizing services for 11,000 families annually measured by client intake and enrollment assessments; 2) Improving access to parenting skills, healthy marriage courses, fatherhood courses, youth development services, and family engagement opportunities as measured by parenting skills surveys and family engagement surveys; and 3) Improved access to care coordination that links heads of households to resources as managed by BSI's data management system.

1052.organization: Ruth & Norman Rales Jewish Family Services
1052.description: The JFS Keep Families Working Summer Camp Scholarship Program ensures that children from lower-income (under 200% FPL and ALICE level) families in Palm Beach County have access to safe, enriching experiences during summer and school breaks while providing essential childcare support for working parents.
1052.purpose: The funds will provide scholarships for summer camp or school break camps for children from lower-income (under 200% FPL) ensuring access to safe, enriching activities that support child development and enable parents to maintain employment.
1052.activities: The program will fund camp scholarships that subsidize the cost of attendance, allowing children to participate in academic, social, and recreational activities, including specialized camps for children with disabilities and critical needs.
1052.direct_services: The project will provide financial assistance in the form of camp scholarships, allowing children to attend local, specialized, and disability-inclusive camps while supporting parents by providing reliable summer childcare. All clients who receive scholarships will be connected with the wide array of wrap around services at JFS, such as behavioral health, food pantry, and our pediatric therapy cli
1052.population: The target population includes children from lower-income families in south Palm Beach County. Approximately 250 children from 167 families are expected to be served.
1052.outcome: The project will benefit families by reducing financial strain, supporting child development, and enabling parents to maintain employment. Outcomes will be measured through the number of scholarships awarded.

1430.description: Complete phase two of construction for up to 14 new independent recovery homes for individuals transitioning from Residential Level II and IV Opioid and Substance Use Disorder treatment in Rural North Florida.
1430.purpose: Developing Independent Recovery homes for individuals and families transitioning out of treatment back into the rural communities. This will help increase available opioid residential treatment capacity in level II & IV.
1430.activities: Begin next phase of construction for additional recovery homes consistent with master campus plan.
1430.direct_services: Increase the number of independent recovery homes for transitioning residents from opioid residential services. This will provide safe, stable supportive housing while assisting with reintegration back to community.
1430.population: Individuals diagnosed with Opioid Use Disorder, or other Substance Use Disorders who may be at risk of involvement in the criminal justice, child welfare, or residing in, but not limited to, the Second Judicial Circuit of Florida.
1430.outcome: Increase the number of Independent Recovery homes up to 14. Count number of available beds, by licensed level of care, prior to the project and after the project completes and measure the number increased.

1431.organization: Safe Families for Children Alliance Florida
1431.description: Safe Families for Children (SFFC) Rural Reach Initiative will utilize funds to engage faith communities to recruit, train, vet and professionally support volunteers in rural areas which are typically under resourced for the purpose of stabilizing families who are in crisis to prevent child abuse and deflect families from unnecessarily entering into the child welfare dependency system. Socially isolated families in crisis are most vulnerable, but SFFC can connect those families with local volunteers to instantly enlarge that family's network of support.
1431.purpose: Funds received will be utilized to create community-based circles of support in rural counties with the purpose of stabilizing families to prevent child abuse and deflect families from unnecessarily entering into the child welfare dependency system. Families who are otherwise isolated will be connected with supportive volunteers in their own communities.
1431.activities: SFFC (an evidence-based Family First Prevention program) will hire staff in rural counties to engage faith and community partners. SFFC will recruit, vet and oversee volunteers to support at risk families with children ages 0-18. Funds will also cover background checks, liability insurance and training for volunteers who are directly serving local families.
1431.direct_services: Direct services include temporary child hosting, parent mentoring, transportation, day time child care and connection to resources. These connections result in long term, natural relationships which outlast the need for formal support thus, the family experiences a decrease in social isolation and an increase in safety and stability.
1431.population: Target populations for this project include jobless persons, economically disadvantaged person, at-risk youth, homeless persons, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, victims of crime, and single parents with children under the age of 18.
1431.outcome: The family being served will experience an increase in their own Protective Factors which in turn will prevent any possibility of child abuse occurring. The extended family-like relationships built with volunteers will resolve that family's social isolation. Parent mentors will identify and develop a goal plan which will help the family become both stable and successful. SFFC will use the PFS2 assessment to monitor the progress of the family.

2854.description: The Pinellas County Housing Authority (PCHA) is requesting funds for Mills, a proposed seventy-eight (78) unit fully affordable apartment community located in Tarpon Springs along Alternate U.S. 19 (1800 South Pinellas Avenue, Tarpon Springs, 34689). The Mills development will serve as a vital addition to Pinellas County’s affordable housing portfolio, addressing a significant gap in workforce housing within the northern region of the county. Tarpon Springs remains under-served in affordable and workforce housing options, making Mills a strategically important investment to ensure that local employees, seniors, and families have access to quality, stable, and affordable homes near employment centers, public transportation, and essential community services.
2854.purpose: Pinellas County Housing Authority's (PCHA) Mission is to provide quality affordable housing. The Mills project provides that housing. Tarpon Springs remains under-served in affordable and workforce housing options, making Mills a strategically important investment to ensure that local employees, seniors, and families have access to quality, stable, and affordable homes near employment centers, public transportation, and essential community services.
2854.activities: The Pinellas County Housing Authority (PCHA) will develop, manage, and operate the Mills, a seventy-eight (78) unit, fully affordable and workforce housing community located in Tarpon Springs. The purpose of this development is to expand access to safe, high-quality, and permanently affordable housing for working families in an area of Pinellas County that is currently under-served. In addition to providing stable, long-term housing, PCHA will ensure that Mills becomes a hub for resident enrichm
2854.direct_services: Permanent Affordable and Workforce Housing Health and Wellness Services Educational and Skill-Building Programs Workforce readiness and job training programs Financial Literacy and Homeownership Preparation Personal Development and Family Support Services
2854.population: Target Population: 78 families - serving approximately 200 individuals
2854.outcome: The $1.5M state funding will help in the construction of 78 new apartments with an average rental rate of the 60-AMI level per apartment. The difference between a 60-AMI and market rate apartment in Pinellas County is $860/month x 78 units x 12 months = $804,960 savings per-year indefinitely for 78 families.

1895.description: Develop and build golf course best management practices certification program participant record keeping and tracking tools, including a registry of certified individuals. Additionally, on-line training resources will be developed and deployed.
1895.purpose: Funds will solely be used to reimburse UF-IFAS to build golf course best management practices certification program participant record keeping and tracking tools including, but not limited to, a registry of persons certified. Additionally, on-line training resources will be developed and deployed.
1895.activities: Web-based tools and resources will be developed to track golf course BMP training program participants and to monitor the effectiveness of the program.
1895.direct_services: Tools and systems will be put into place allowing program participants to remain in compliance with training program requirements.
1895.population: Golf course employees who will receive training to remain in compliance to preserve ecosystems. Approximately 250 individuals will be trained per year.
1895.outcome: Requested funds will be used to develop professionally scripted and curated content for use in golf course BMP trainings and educational programming. Compliance with golf course BMP practices help ensure the healthy land- based and aquatic ecosystems are preserved. Water quality monitoring program and input reductions, practices recommended in the BMP certification program, are measured over time through industry benchmarking surveys.

1329.description: Renovation of the existing outpatient building on SMA's Marion County campus will improve access and care for clients requiring both behavioral health and primary physical health care. By integrating primary care and pharmacy services with existing behavioral health services, individuals with co-morbid conditions will have access to comprehensive care in one location. This approach will reduce hospital emergency room visits and repeat hospitalizations, while improving care coordination and access to services, as well as maximizing the utilization of the Marion County Central Receiving Facility and System for behavioral health.
1329.purpose: Renovations will improve access and care for clients requiring behavioral and primary healthcare. By integrating primary care and pharmacy services with existing behavioral health services, clients with co-morbid conditions will have access to comprehensive care in one location. This approach will reduce emergency room visits and repeat hospitalizations, while improving care coordination and maximizing the utilization of Marion County's Central Receiving Facility.
1329.activities: The activities associated with this capital renovation project include the costs of permitting, renovation costs, and furniture/fixtures/equipment costs for the 21,339 square foot building providing integrated outpatient services. Through these activities, access to care will increase, adding professionals, and additional services will be offered.
1329.direct_services: The services provided in the renovated building will include a behavioral health outpatient clinic, primary care clinic, GME program, and pharmacy services. These services will be provided to all Marion residents. While insurance and first party fees for services will be utilized, no one will be denied care due to an inability to pay for services.
1329.population: The target populations to be served include: persons with poor physical health, persons with poor mental health, the economically disadvantaged, at risk youth, drug users (in health services), drug offenders (in criminal justice), elderly persons, and persons experiencing behavioral and physical co-morbidity and in need of integrated care. The total number to be served will be in excess of 800 individuals annually.
1329.outcome: 75% of clients will keep scheduled follow up appointments for behavioral health; 90% of clients discharged from the Adult and Children's Crisis Stabilization unit will not be readmitted within 14 days; 75% of clients receiving Medication Assisted Treatment will remain in services for 90 days. All outcomes to be measured in the SMA Electronic Health Record.

1310.organization: Habitat for Humanity of Marion County, Inc.
1310.description: Habitat for Humanity of Marion County seeks to acquire and hold land in perpetuity through a community land trust, ensuring long-term sites dedicated to the construction and sale of affordable homes. Through this initiative, Habitat will purchase 30 undeveloped lots to build 30 high-quality homes, providing stable housing opportunities for families under 120% of the area median income. The full development is anticipated to be completed within a 2.5-year period, creating lasting community impact and expanding access to affordable homeownership for local families.
1310.purpose: Habitat for Humanity builds and sells affordable homes that transform families and strengthen communities. Safe, stable housing empowers families to achieve financial stability, improve health, and pursue education. As a result, children improve academically, parents advance professionally, and neighborhoods become safer and more vibrant. The result is a stronger, more resilient community where families can thrive and neighborhoods become safer and more vibrant.
1310.activities: Construction of safe and affordable homes. Throughout the process, families will complete sweat equity hours and attend monthly workshops on budgeting and home maintenance. With coaching and support, families will learn to manage finances and care for their home, resulting in a safe, stable environment that supports their children’s education.
1310.direct_services: This project provides families with the opportunity to own and maintain an affordable home. Decent, affordable housing improves physical and mental health. Homeownership has been shown to lead to higher rates of high school graduation and college attendance, with children of low-income homeowners being 11% more likely to graduate from high school and 4.5% more likely to complete post-secondary edu
1310.population: Habitat for Humanity will serve families with annual incomes between 30% and 120% of the area median income (AMI), ensuring that affordable homeownership opportunities reach those most in need. We plan to provide safe, stable housing for 30 families, empowering them to achieve long-term financial stability and improved quality of life.
1310.outcome: Habitat for Humanity is committed to expanding access to affordable homeownership for families in need. Our strategic approach focuses on increasing the number of homes we build each year, ensuring that more families have the opportunity to achieve the stability, security, and empowerment that come with owning a safe and affordable home.

1020.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1020.description: Neighborhood Farms USA (NFUSA) is a 3 year-old 501 (c) 3 non-profit that promotes hard work, healthy food, and strong communities. We promote the many benefits of agriculture while teaching kids and families to grow their own food in their own backyards or balconies. Together, we turn unused land into productive gardens that feed local families and strengthen the community with home-grown, nutrient-rich food. Our educational programs promote sustainable agriculture, hands-on training and scholarships for urban farmers, customized digital content, and getting back to the basics that built America: good soil, good food, and good people.
1020.purpose: Bringing back rural values and respect for agriculture. Build local independence. NFUSA helps towns grow neighborhood farms that cut dependence on big corporations or handouts. Kids gain real-world business and science education, along with after-school activities that keep them out of trouble. Seniors stay active and connected. Families eat better. Communities get stronger. Hands on education for a new generation of farmers, nutrition-rich food and awareness in kids to prevent illness.
1020.activities: We train future farmers, offer scholarships, and provide practical agricultural content. Neighborhood farms grow fresh, healthy food while giving families and youth hands-on experience. Through workshops, community events, online seminars, product reviews, we provide the means for self-reliance, and independent access to food by working the land. We promote farm-to table restaurants, growing local, and food as a means to a healthier lifestyle and wellness discipline.
1020.direct_services: Hands-on farm training, nutrition education, and scholarships for students and local leaders. We'll train local urban farmers on best practices, new technology, and pest-control guidance. We develop school and community programs to teach neighborhood farming to kids and seniors and offer food-security initiatives ensuring fresh, locally grown food.
1020.population: This project enables everyone with a balcony or backyard easy access to information to turn idle land into sources of fresh, local food. Our community impact with neighborhood gardens will benefit over 1000 residents. Students gain hands-on learning and after-school programs, senior stay active and engaged, and at-risk neighborhoods activate idle spaces to benefit from nutrition, composting, and waste-management education that strengthens neighborhoods.
1020.outcome: 10-14 micro gardens (neighborhood farms) activated. 1900 volunteer hours to manage gardens. 10-15 internships and scholarships awarded to local neighborhood farmers/grow leaders. 100 hours of hands-on training per scholarship participant (cohort of 15 expected). 4,000 total hours of content watched by individual constituents (estimated over 48,000 followers on social media). Improved food access for 2000+ residents. Measured by volunteer/class attendance, size of community population, and media consumption recorded.

1059.description: This request is to assist in the construction of new residential treatment facility or those with substance use and mental health disorders. The facility will be located adjacent to and replace our current dated residential treatment facility at Krome Avenue in Homestead. This facility will double our capacity from 60 to 120 beds and triple the amount of space available (7,700 sq. ft. vs. 24,500 sq. ft.) for clients and program staff members. This new facility is anticipated to serve an additional 300 individuals per year, reducing the significant strain on system ERs, CSUs, and local waitlists for treatment. The requested funding represents 10% of the total project budget of $9.98 million.
1059.purpose: These funds will assist in the construction of a new residential facility for those with substance use and mental health disorders. The new facility will allow us to double the number of individuals served (from 300 to 600), reduce treatment wait times and the prevalence of substance use in the community, improve the physical and mental health of those receiving treatment, reduce recidivism and repeated use of higher cost ER and crisis stabilization services, increase the number individuals that
1059.activities: The requested funds will support critical pre-construction and facility readiness activities necessary to complete and operationalize our residential treatment program. Specifically, state appropriations will be used to cover soft costs including attorney’s fees, permitting fees, and architectural/design services required for compliance, planning, and execution of facility development and construction. Additionally, funds will be allocated to purchase essential furniture, fixtures, and equipment
1059.direct_services: Direct services provided include Residential Level II substance use and mental health treatment, which includes transitional housing, individualized assessments and treatment planning, group and individual therapy, case management, peer support services, housing navigation, employment assistance, STI prevention and intervention, medical care, medication management, and medication-assisted treatmen
1059.population: The target population served by our residential treatment program is uninsured, underinsured, indigent, and homeless adult males experiencing substance use and/or mental health disorders. Additionally, we maintain designated beds for specific subpopulations including homeless veterans, individuals living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA), and those at high risk of opioid overdose. We anticipate serving 600 unduplicated individuals annually, double to number currently being served.
1059.outcome: - 60% of participants will complete treatment with at least a 30-day period without using illicit drugs or alcohol (FASAMS State data) - 90% of participants will not need acute care (CSU) for a mental health episode from admission to discharge (DCF IRAS data, chart review) - 95% of program participants will be linked to primary care services (Case/chart reviews) - 94% will be discharged to stable housing (FASAMS State data) - 10% will experience a change in employment status from admit to discharge (FASAMS State data) - % change in adults arrested 30 days prior to admit vs prior to discharge will be 15% (FASAMS State data)

1129.organization: Amigos of our Park d/b/a Amigos Foundation
1129.description: The funds will be expended on educating newly minted US Citizens on the values of the American way of life through exploration of career and mentorship opportunities, the importance of civic engagement, and value of work and self- sufficiency.
1129.purpose: The funds will be expended on educating newly minted US Citizens on the values of the American way of life through exploration of career and mentorship opportunities, the importance of civic engagement, and value of work and self- sufficiency.
1129.activities: Mentorship and career guidance assistance for newly minted US Citizens Citizenship Prep Courses Education of US History and Civics Voter Registration.
1129.direct_services: Mentorship and career guidance assistance for newly minted US Citizens Citizenship Prep Courses Education of US History and Civics Voter Registration.
1129.population: Jobless persons, Economically disadvantaged persons, Grade school students, High school students, University/college students, greater than 800.
1129.outcome: We plan to work with more than 1000 newly minted legal immigrants and educate them about integrating into American society including making them aware of career opportunities and resources, assist in securing mentorship training and internship programs and help them become successful and self-sufficient citizens. We secure over 40 mentors and volunteers, and we assign 25 newly young immigrants to each mentor to execute this works in assigned small groups will make us more successful and have a better way to measure the success of these young people.

1695.description: Peanut Island, a 79-acre jewel in the Lake Worth Inlet, has been part of Palm Beach County's history since its creation in 1918. Once a dredging byproduct, it is now a treasured public park and ecotourism destination. At its heart sits the former U.S. Coast Guard Station (1936)—a site of national significance. This station played a vital role in coastal defense during World War II, the Cuban Missile Crisis, and houses the unique John F. Kennedy Military Presidential Bunker built in 1962 as an emergency refuge near the President's Palm Beach home. This project will restore the Coast Guard Station, Boathouse, Presidential Bunker, and surrounding grounds, creating a dynamic, interactive museum. Visitors will be able to explore educational, maritime, and environmental exhibits. By revitalizing these historic facilities, the project will preserve national history, expand educational opportuni
1695.purpose: The requested funding will assist with the restoration of the Coast Guard complex and Kennedy Bunker which, at completion, is anticipated to become a historical tourist attraction as well as an environmental education center for local residents and school aged children.
1695.activities: At completion the restored structures are expected to serve a dual function as both a historical and environmental education center. Programming will focus on the history of the Coast Guard facilities and Kennedy Bunker, the Intracoastal Waterway and the Port of Palm Beach. Environmental education is expected to focus on the local reef system, local aquatic flora and fauna as well as efforts to restore the water quality within the Intracoastal Waterway.
1695.direct_services: The project will directly serve citizens by providing safe recreational facilities, a public education center with historical and environmental programming, opportunities for school and community engagement, and restored natural habitats that enhance both learning and quality of life for local residents and visitors.
1695.population: Two distinct populations will be served by the project: 1) Local and regional residents, particularly those school aged students visiting on a field trip and those visiting other portions of the island. 2) Out of state residents visiting Palm Beach County for vacation. Over 75,000 tourists and local residents are expected to visit the facility annually upon completion.
1695.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is for the facility to become a popular regional attraction for Palm Beach County. The Parks and Recreation Department uses Placer.ai to track park visitation. The Department will analyze data prior to and after the completion of the facility to accurately measure changes in visitation.

1693.organization: Palm Beach County Department of Airports
1693.description: Utility, drainage, and parking improvements are needed at LNA to support the redevelopment of the existing fixed base operator site, enabling the construction of new terminal and hangar facilities at the Airport. Tenant and user parking along the southwest will be improved and separated by fencing from the airfield enhancing safety and security. Phase 3 development consists of reconfiguring the central access road and parking area, stormwater collection system and drainage network and electrical and utility infrastructure. Phase 4 development includes a new 26-foot-wide access road along the southwest hangars, a vehicle parking lot with approximately 110 new parking spaces, and a new drainage network and accompanying stormwater collection system improvements.
1693.purpose: This project will enable economic growth for the community. The current facilities to be improved are aging, severely constrained, and unable to meet demand. Separating tenant and user parking from the airfield will also provide enhanced safety and security of the airport.
1693.activities: The funds will be used to construct the project which enables reconfiguration of facilities to more closely align demand and capacity.
1693.direct_services: Improved facilities and economic impact of fixed base operator services for local and transient users.
1693.population: Airport tenants and users. By 2044, approximately 154,000 annual aircraft operations are forecasted for the airport. With each operation is an opportunity for airport tenants to provide services including fuel sales, maintenance, flight training, charter operations, and aircraft storage.
1693.outcome: The FAA encourages airports to be financially self-sustaining. This project will increase operating revenues to the airport and enhance economic benefit to tenants from the community. An increase in revenues and leased parcels/facilities will measure success.

1697.description: The Lake Worth Lagoon Initiative (LWLI) was created to define and evaluate the status of the entire watershed and propose actions to improve and protect the natural resources within the lagoon. LWLI is supported by Palm Beach County, South Florida Water Management District, Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Florida Inland Navigation District, Florida Fish & Wildlife Conservation Commission, and the League of Cities, which have all endorsed the LWL Management Plan. This watershed-based plan includes projects to restore sea grasses, mangroves and oysters, cap muck sediments, construct storm water control projects, and septic-to-sewer conversions. Revitalizing this important water body provides long-term environmental, recreational and economic benefits to the region. Each State dollar is matched locally at a minimum 50:50 cost-share basis. Through this program, over $26 milli
1697.purpose: Funds requested will support capital construction for septic to sewer conversions and restoration projects, along with bathymetric survey to drive collective management efforts to improve water quality, habitat quality and coastal resiliency within the Lake Worth Lagoon. The Steering Committee of the Lake Worth Lagoon Initiative, consisting of local government representatives as well as representatives from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, the South Florida Water Management Di
1697.activities: Projects include construction necessary for septic to sewer conversions, living shorelines and shoreline enhancement.
1697.direct_services: Direct and secondary improvements to water quality, habitat quality, sediment quality and coastal resilience.
1697.population: The target population served by this effort and associated projects includes the residents and numerous visitors of Palm Beach County and the local marine industry.
1697.outcome: Benefits will include wastewater system improvements and the creation of coastal habitat to improve the water quality, ecological conditions and coastal resiliency of the Lagoon. Methodologies to measure expected benefits of these efforts include water quality and biological monitoring, and the acreage of habitat created/restored.

2036.description: To provide adaptive and inclusive therapeutic programs for developmentally disabled and low-income youth/at-risk youth, in school, after school and summer programs. Therapeutic components include functional life skills, communication and social skills, gross and fine motor skills, health, wellness, fitness and character building. An instructional component is incorporated into the program to train certified racquet sports professionals and certified therapists to serve these individuals in this environment.
2036.purpose: To deliver adaptive and inclusive therapeutic programs for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, as well as low-income and at-risk youth, while training certified racquet sports professionals and therapists to effectively serve these communities. Our vision is to establish Florida as an international hub for adaptive and inclusive therapeutic sports, creating both transformative opportunities for participants and meaningful pathways to employment.
2036.activities: Funding will expand life skills, community inclusion, and independence of individuals with ASD and DD. LSA teaches social communication and adaptive behavior on the tennis court, strengthening skills for community settings such as the workplace and social gatherings. Funding will provide for coordination, training of coaches and therapists (and college students in training), and outreach/inclusion of under-represented populations, including individuals who would not otherwise have access to thes
2036.direct_services: To provide adaptive and inclusive therapeutic programs for developmentally disabled and low-income youth/at-risk youth. Therapeutic components include fine and gross motor skills, communication and social skills, health, wellness, fitness and character building. A instructional component is incorporated in the program to train certified tennis professionals and certified therapists to serve these
2036.population: Persons with Intellectual/Developmental Disabilities and at-risk youth. 1500 individuals will be served with this project.
2036.outcome: 1) 85% of 1500 participants will show measurable improvements in tennis skills, fitness, adaptive behavior, social communication, and measures of well-being, according to personalized therapeutic plans/metrics. Therapists collect, monitor and report data for individualized treatment plans, tracked via HIPAA compliant electronic medical records. 2) Community/tennis participation rate of neurodiverse individuals will increase by 15% annually, increasing diversity and inclusion in Florida communities. The Bloomerang registration platform will assess the number (and percentage increase) of LSA program participants per location in FL annually. 3) Family members of neurodiverse individuals will re

1694.organization: Palm Beach County Board of County
1694.description: The proposed Sports Field House at Okeeheelee Park represents a strategic investment in Palm Beach County’s recreational infrastructure and economic vitality. Design of this state of the art indoor facility will serve as a central hub for sports and community events, significantly enhancing local recreational opportunities and driving substantial economic benefits to the region. This project is consistent with our community-wide recreation needs assessment, Parks Master Plan, and Tourism Master Plan. The Sports Field House design will include locker rooms, meeting spaces, training facilities, restrooms, and concessions with a large flexible multi-court space supporting a wide range of sports. Sports tourism accounts for more than 28% of all tourism in Palm Beach County. This facility will nurture local talent, promote wellness, and generate continued and sustained economic growth through
1694.purpose: The requested funding will assist with the planning and design of a state of the art Sports Field House at Okeeheelee Park which will attract larger regional, state and national sports tourism events. At completion, the much needed indoor facility is expected to provide an excellent sports tourism destination for this region of Florida while also benefiting local recreation teams for Palm Beach County.
1694.activities: Planning, design and permitting consultant services will be provided through this funding to meet the intended purpose of these funds. This is a critical step in the planning, design and construction process.
1694.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide for a state of the art indoor sports field house facility open to all citizens when not in use for sports tourism events. This was a high need identified by our community during our parks master planning process. The central location in Palm Beach County is beneficial in many ways for this area of the County to realize economic benefit through visit spending
1694.population: Two distinct populations will be served by the project: 1) Competitive athletes participating in courts sports (volleyball, basketball, futsal, pickleball, etc). 2) Any citizen interested in a designated indoor safe space to play. Over 240,000 athletes, spectators and local citizens are expected to utilize the facility annually upon completion.
1694.outcome: The expected outcome of this construction project is correcting a lack of indoor sports facility infrastructure in this Region for both citizens and athletes. The Parks and Recreation Department uses Placer.ai to track park visitation. The Department will analyze data prior to and after the completion of the amenities to accurately measure changes in park use. Also working closely with our sports tourism partners, we analyze data on economic benefit of our sports facilities.

1111.description: Funding needed for critical stormwater improvements identified in the City’s Stormwater Master Plan as the H1 Basin. This shovel-ready project, with design completed using a Rural Infrastructure Fund (RIF) Grant in FY22-23 (#D0261), addresses long-standing water quality issues and frequent flooding affecting both residential and commercial areas. Located in a historically financially disadvantaged community designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity, the project will install modernized stormwater conveyance infrastructure to improve water quality, reduce pollutants, and enhance public health, safety, and property protection. It will also reduce roadway flooding, prevent loss of economic activity, and improve overall community resilience.
1111.purpose: The goal is to protect life, health, property and the environment by implementing critical stormwater improvements in the H1 Basin service area. The project is identified as a priority in the City’s Stormwater Master Plan that reduces flooding, improves stormwater management, and water quality for residents and businesses and protection of Lake Okeechobee Estuary (BMAP).
1111.activities: To seek contractual services through the City's procurement policies and regulations for project management, engineering, permitting, bidding, construction observation, engineering during construction, and completion of modern stormwater conveyance infrastructure.
1111.direct_services: Direct services are flood protection, safer travel, reduced property damage, and improved water quality for citizens and businesses by replacing outdated stormwater systems. Improves the quality of life, health and safety for this Rural Area of Opportunity.
1111.population: Target population includes the State as the project improves water quality protecting State water resources, Lake Okeechobee, the western Glades communities, businesses and visitors, and the general population of Belle Glade, which is a historically disadvantaged municipality that is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity.
1111.outcome: The H1 Basin project will reduce flooding, protect homes and businesses, the environment and improve water quality. It will enhance public health and safety while supporting economic stability. Success will be measured through engineering inspections, water quality monitoring, and tracking of flood-related incidents.

1896.description: Redevelopment of the 220-acre Nutrient Reduction Facility which operates by alum being added to the water and the resulting "floc" being removed from settling ponds to a series of naturally vegetated cells that would filter water of nutrients, act as flood protection, provide habitat for wildlife, and serve as a location for public education and recreation. In addition, it would also reduce the long-term operational costs associated with utilizing the alum process of removing excess nutrients.
1896.purpose: Redevelopment of the 220-acre Nutrient Reduction Facility which operates by alum being added to the water and the resulting "floc" being removed from settling ponds to a series of naturally vegetated cells that would filter water of nutrients, act as flood protection, provide habitat for wildlife, and serve as a location for public education and recreation. In addition, it would also reduce the long-term operational costs associated with utilizing the alum process of removing excess nutrients.
1896.activities: A master site plan and design and engineering to redevelop the existing Nutrient Reduction Facility into a series of filtrations ponds to improve water quality, provide additional flood protection, improve habitat for wildlife and provide education and recreation opportunities to the public.
1896.direct_services: When the project is completed, the construction phase it will provide improved water quality, flood protection, protect wildlife and biodiversity, provide for outdoor based education and recreation. It will also reduce the long-term operating costs of the existing facility.
1896.population: Residents and visitors of Lake County. The project will benefit the county's population of approximately 444,204 residents and the thousands of annual visitors who utilize Lake County's waterways, parks and recreational areas. Educational and recreational components are expected to directly serve over 20,000 individuals annually through public access, outreach events, and environmental education programs.
