1896.outcome: Improved water quality, flood mitigation, improve wildlife habitat, education opportunities, and tourism. Water quality monitoring, pedestrian and vehicle count data, and educational programing participation

1897.description: Remove built up sediments and vegetation which impair the natural flow of water between Pine Meadows Conservation Area and Trout Lake. To reduce flood risks, improve downstream water quality, and restore public access for passive recreation.
1897.purpose: Remove built up sediments and vegetation which impair the natural flow of water between Pine Meadows Conservation Area and Trout Lake. To reduce flood risks, improve downstream water quality, and restore public access for passive recreation.
1897.activities: Remove built up sediments and vegetation which impair the natural flow of water between Pine Meadows Conservation Area and Trout Lake. To reduce flood risks, improve downstream water quality, and restore public access for passive recreation.
1897.direct_services: Reduce flood risks, improve downstream water quality, and restore public access for passive recreation.
1897.population: The project will serve residents and visitors of Lake County, particularly those in Eustis, Mount Dora, and unincorporated Pine Meadows Area who benefit from flood protection. The directly affected population is estimated at 10,000 to 15,000 residents, with additional regional benefits for surrounding communities and visitors who utilize the Pine Meadows Conservation Area for recreation.
1897.outcome: Reduce flood risks, improve downstream water quality, and restore public access for passive recreation. Water quality and flow monitoring.

1172.description: The legislative funding will allow the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office (MDSO) to bolster law enforcement prevention and response for large-scale events, such as the G20 Summit, as well as other large-scale events across Miami-Dade County. MDSO anticipates increased costs due to critically necessary enhanced public safety and anti-terrorism measures to ensure the safety of all residents and visitors for these global events.
1172.purpose: Improved security and enhanced anti-terrorism measures at global events in Miami-Dade County
1172.activities: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations
1172.direct_services: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations
1172.population: All residents and visitors in Miami-Dade County; over 5 million persons
1172.outcome: This initiative involves law enforcement prevention and response into events such as the G20 Summit and other high- profile events. By conducting anti-terrorism operations at large scale events, MDSO intends to curtail violence and keep the community safe for its residents and visitors. Increased law enforcement and public safety operations will be measured by MDSO tracking data

1153.description: The Town of Cutler Bay (“Town”) is requesting $1,000,000 for Capital Improvements to improve the stormwater management system and treat runoff pollutants in Biscayne Bay and the Lakes by the Bay (LBTB) Community. The funding request is to implement the Town’s Lakes by the Bay shovel-ready project which aims to install 8,905 linear feet of new drainage systems, including exfiltration trenches, to improve water quality in the project area. Drainage improvements mitigate flooding leading to collector roadways, public transportation, and evacuation routes on SW 216 Street and Old Cutler Road.
1153.purpose: The project aims to improve water quality and mitigate flooding in a hazard area. The existing drainage infrastructure in the Sub-Basins do not treat or discharge adequate runoff to meet the desired performance criteria adopted in the Town’s Stormwater Master Plan.
1153.activities: Based on the Capital Improvement recommendations listed in the Town’s Adopted Stormwater Master Plan, existing catch basins will be modified or reconstructed as required to provide sediment traps (sumps) and pollution retardant baffles to protect the French drains and weir structures shall be installed prior to each outfall to restrict the discharge of pollutants to the community lake.
1153.direct_services: The proposed project reduces the flood risk for the residents of Cutler Bay and protects the Town's evacuation routes. Since incorporation, the Town has adopted higher regulatory standards and, currently, adheres to the base flood elevation standard, plus 1ft. above. Due to the efforts of the Public Works Department, the Town is currently rated by FEMA as a Community Rating System 3 which provides
1153.population: The Town of Cutler Bay's population is 43,958 (Census 2022), this project supports the entire community as well as Biscayne Bay.
1153.outcome: The benefit/outcome of this Project is the decreased amounts of pollutants into Biscayne Bay & surrounding communities such as LBTB, coming from the Town's outfalls which empty directly into the Bay. The methodology for measurement includes the implementation of water quality treatment data collection, which measures and quantifies the proposed reduction load of pollutants to the bay. Proposed reductions are: 92.7% reduction in Total Phosphorus, 89.5% reduction in Total Nitrogen, and 90.6% reduction in Total Suspended Solids.

1154.description: The Town of Cutler Bay seeks $1,000,000 in match funding for its Brownfield Site Restoration Project at 20951 Old Cutler Road. The project will remove soil contamination across 16 acres to develop Legacy Park & Municipal Complex. Environmental mitigation protects the Biscayne Aquifer (groundwater), which supplies over 5 Million Florida residents drinking water. The project is shovel-ready, in the permitting phase, and aims for remediation completion by December 2027.
1154.purpose: The project aims to remove and remediate soil contamination across the 16-acre site, ensuring the land is safe for public use.
1154.activities: This cleanup effort eliminates heavy metals, pesticides, herbicides, and arsenic, which can pose severe health risks to the community.
1154.direct_services: The new complex will be a central gathering place that will become the heart of the community. It will feature 12 acres of park space and 4 acres of municipal building(s) that will house the Town Hall, a Police Station, and a Community Center with a Pool.
1154.population: The project serves the general population of the Town of Cutler Bay (Approximately 43,000) and surrounding neighborhoods in South Miami-Dade County.
1154.outcome: The project protects public health through the remediation of harmful toxins in the soil. The project allows the Town to develop the property into the "Legacy Park & Municipal Complex" which will be the central hub of the community. It creates a sense of community, increases access to park space, and attracts new business to the Town's Old Cutler Road commercial district. Benefits will be measured by the completion of the project and tracking of events held at the project site along with tracking new businesses through commercial permits.

1225.description: Florida Studio Theater (FST) is investing in a new multi-use project that will include 57 new workforce housing units and 127 new downtown parking spaces, as well as a new main stage and two new cabaret theaters. The area's shortage of workforce housing makes it imperative that FST provide accommodation for its visiting artists and arts workers while also serving its robust and growing audience. The workforce housing units will be used by FST guest artists and Sarasota's year-round arts workers and local workers seeking affordable housing. The new parking spaces will be shared with the local community to improve parking needs in the heart of Downtown Sarasota's economic center during peak business hours. The state's investment will leverage the $44 million FST has already raised in non-state funding to support the project.
1225.purpose: The construction of an 8 story multi-use building, which will include 18 2 bedroom/2 bath units for workers seeking workforce housing in downtown Sarasota, 39 extended stay studios for the 250+ guest artists FST employs annually, 127 new parking spots to be shared with the local community to improve parking needs, a new main stage, and 2 new cabaret theatres. When the extended stay suites are not under contract, they will be offered to local workers seeking affordable housing.
1225.activities: Funds will support the development of new workforce housing units for over 100 workforce employees, shared community parking. These improvements address critical housing, and infrastructure needs while strengthening Sarasota’s cultural and economic vitality. Over 40,000 Florida resident subscribers, 225,000 live attendees, and more than 40,000 students statewide will directly benefit.
1225.direct_services: Workforce housing will be the primary service provided, including 57 new workforce housing units reaching over 100 workforce employees and 127 new downtown parking spaces, as well as a new main stage and two new cabaret theaters. The multi-use project will also facilitate cultural programs that serve the public and students in K-12 schools throughout the State who participate in FST programming.
1225.population: This project will serve residents and visitors to Sarasota County including over 100 workforce employees, visitors through 127 new parking spots in Downtown Sarasota, 40,000 Florida resident subscribers, 225,000 live attendees and more than 40,000 students throughout Florida who participate in FST programs will directly benefit from the project.
1225.outcome: Once complete, FST anticipates a 30% increase in operations. This will grow employment from 94 annual FTE to over 120 FTE. Over 350 construction jobs will be created in the construction of the Artist Plaza. Over 100 workforce employees will be able to live near their workplace in downtown Sarasota. Results will be measured through increased ticket sales, student participation, new jobs created, new housing and new parking spaces used by patrons, residents and businesses.

1134.description: Florida Early Learning Corps combines the power of AmeriCorps with evidence-based practices to fill the opportunity gap in Florida through individualized literacy and numeracy intervention support to PreK students. The program will recruit, train and place AmeriCorps members in the highest need zip codes to deliver a data-based, problem-solving model of literacy instruction to children age 3 to 5.
1134.purpose: Funding will expand Florida Early Learning Corps' geographic reach and impact on the early literacy and numeracy skill-building of our state's youngest learners. An appropriation amount of $750k will facilitate Florida Early Learning Corps' expansion from 136 to 178 tutors who will serve more than 2,500 at-risk students, ensuring they are prepared for success in Kindergarten.
1134.activities: Early Learning Corps is a proven model that accelerates literacy skills and Kindergarten readiness for high-need preschoolers. Full-time tutors work with PreK teachers to implement evidence-based interventions, individualized tutoring plans, formative assessments at least three times per year to ensure growth, extensive data systems that provide quality assurance, and multi-layer coaching.
1134.direct_services: The instructional model focuses on integrating the "Big Five Essential Literacy Predictors outlined by the National Early Literacy Panel (2008) into all aspects of the daily classroom routine. The program includes an immersive "push- in" component, where tutors provide (1) whole-class literacy enrichments for all students, (2) targeted small group experiences, and (3) one-on-one interventions.
1134.population: In a state where more than 18% of children live in poverty (FL Chamber of Commerce, 2023), Florida Early Learning Corps serves those who are among the most at risk: 96% of Florida Early Learning Corps students are eligible to receive free and/or reduced price lunch, an indicator of poverty. This is higher than the average of Florida students overall (53.8%) (FL Department of Health, 2024). Our 178 tutors will each serve 15 students resulting in more than 2,500 students receiving individualized t
1134.outcome: We expect the following outcomes for students by the end of the 2026-27 school year: -70% of 4-5 year olds will meet or exceed their target growth in literacy and early numeracy skills needed for Kindergarten. -80% of children will complete family literacy and numeracy activities at home with a parent or guardian. -70% of all children will meet or exceed their age-level benchmarks for each skill.

1173.description: Adults living with severe and persistent mental illness (SPMI) lack the vocational skills needed to succeed in today's workforce. The Mental Health Clubhouse Supported Employment program is an evidence-based service that helps people living with SPMI find jobs in the competitive marketplace leading to financial self-sufficiency and a better quality of life. With state support, the Academy (based in Sarasota) launched a new Clubhouse in Bradenton. State funding would match $1.5 million in private support from individuals and local charitable foundations to equip 250 Academy members from both the Sarasota and Manatee campuses with the skills needed to acquire competitive employment. A minimum of 100 Academy members will be placed in career-based employment with up to 45 local business partners who employ Academy members.
1173.purpose: State funding would match $1.5M in private support, as well as funding from Manatee County and local charitable foundations, to equip 250 Academy members (adults living with serious mental illness) from both the Sarasota and Manatee campuses with the skills needed to acquire competitive employment. In addition, a minimum of 100 Academy members will be placed in career-based employment with up to 45 local business partners who employ Academy members. As evidence of the Academy's job placement suc
1173.activities: The Academy at Glengary and the Academy at Bradenton will provide hands-on vocational training while equipping Clubhouse members with the skills and industry certifications needed to fill the staffing needs for area employers. This will increase financial independence of adults living with SPMI, thereby transitioning individuals from being a tax burden to taxpayers.
1173.direct_services: 250 Academy members (adults living with SPMI) from both the Sarasota and Manatee campuses will be equipped with the skills and certifications needed to acquire competitive employment. At a minimum, 100 Academy members will be placed in career-based employment with up to 45 local business partners who partner with the Academy to employ its members.
1173.population: 250 Adults with Severe and Persistent Mental Illness in Sarasota and Manatee Counties.
1173.outcome: The program will ensure that the Academy at Glengary and the Academy at Bradenton are filling the staffing needs for area employers while equipping Clubhouse members with the skills needed to fill jobs, increasing economic self- reliance while reducing their dependency on state benefits. Success factors include the number of members who are placed in jobs in the community through Transitional, Supported and/or Independent Employment, and the number of business employers/partners recruited for member employment, and the reduction in hospitalization rates and emergency services. (Baker Acts).

2038.description: The ARC Health and Wellness Complex is a comprehensive, inclusive, and hurricane-resilient campus in Port St. Lucie serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) and their families. It includes a Therapeutic Intervention Program (TIP) Center, an Acute Healthcare Group Home, and a final phase of buildouts including sensory rooms, therapy spaces, hurricane hardening, and outdoor accessibility features. The campus will also serve as a special needs hurricane shelter within a 15-mile radius and provide vocational, therapeutic, and residential services.
2038.purpose: Specific purpose or goal: Complete the final phase of the ARC Health and Wellness Complex to provide comprehensive, inclusive, and hurricane-resilient services for individuals with I/DD. Land will receive final zoning and land use approvals. Construction of fully accessible facility will commence and be completed to provide Direct Services: Therapies, vocational training, residential care.
2038.activities: Activities and services: Construction of fully accessible facility will commence and be completed to accommodate up to provide Direct Services: Therapy, vocational training, residential care, hurricane sheltering, community events, and training programs for individuals with I/DD.
2038.direct_services: The ARC Health and Wellness Complex is a unique, collaborative effort encompassing six professional disciplines, (behavioral, physical, occupational, speech, recreation, and music therapies), providing intense and direct treatment services for children and adults with I/DD. Direct Services: Therapies, vocational training, residential care, hurricane shelter for individuals with I/DD. Direct servic
2038.population: Target population: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (children and adults). Estimated to serve over 300 individuals annually.
2038.outcome: Expected outcomes: Improved physical and mental health, increased economic self-sufficiency, reduced institutionalization costs, and enhanced emergency preparedness.

1900.description: LSSC has been implementing improvements to its HVAC systems across all campuses to enhance system effectiveness and efficiency. New controls and updated air handlers are more efficient and allow for long-term cost savings to the college and would eliminate the expense of constant repairs to outdated, failing systems.
1900.purpose: This project includes a $100,000 contribution from Lake-Sumter State College for a total project cost of $530,000. New controls and updated air handlers are more efficient and allow for long-term cost savings to the college and would eliminate the expense of constant repairs to outdated, failing systems.
1900.activities: Replacement of aged-out HVAC systems (including exhaust fans, air handlers, coil units, and transformers) across all campuses. Retrofit of automated logic controllers into current controls system for Student Services Building and Health Sciences Center on the Leesburg Campus.
1900.direct_services: This HVAC upgrade will directly serve Florida citizens by ensuring optimal learning conditions for students pursuing their education. Reliable climate control creates comfortable classrooms where students can focus on coursework without environmental distractions, supporting better academic performance and completion rates. This is an investment in an environment where students can perform at thei
1900.population: The target population is Lake and Sumter Counties. As the fastest growing college in the FCS for two straight years, Lake-Sumter currently serves 11,500 students each year and continues to expand its enrollment to serve additional learners throughout the community.
1900.outcome: Modern, efficient systems also reduce operational costs, allowing the college to redirect savings toward instructional programs and student services. This will create an environment where students can perform at their better, which ultimately produces well-educated and prepared graduates for Florida's workforce. Measurement will ensure tracking to ensure completion of projects as well as data showing improvements in indoor air quality.

1902.description: Lake and Sumter Counties share a long and successful history of agricultural endeavors making LSSC the perfect place to train a workforce for modern agricultural sciences to further strengthen the agricultural history in our area. This program will offer AS degrees and certifications and will serve as a pathway to bachelor’s degrees in agricultural sciences at the University of Florida and the State University System.
1902.purpose: This project includes a $100,000 contribution from Lake-Sumter State College for a total project cost of $500,000. This program will offer associate degrees and certifications and will serve as a pathway to bachelor’s degrees in agricultural sciences at the University of Florida and the State University System.
1902.activities: Following research into labor market demands and workforce availability in Lake and Sumter Counties, these funds will support the launch of a new associate degree program in agriculture. This program will establish a seamless educational pathway, allowing students to transition from related career and technical education programs at local high schools, then transfer to the State University System to complete their bachelor's degrees.
1902.direct_services: This program will directly serve Lake and Sumter County citizens by training the next generation of agricultural professionals for our region's thriving $86+ million agricultural economy. Students will gain accessible, affordable AS degrees and certifications close to home, with seamless pathways to University of Florida and State University System bachelor's programs.
1902.population: The target population is Lake and Sumter Counties. As the fastest growing college in the FCS for two straight years, Lake-Sumter currently serves 11,500 students each year and continues to expand its enrollment to serve additional learners throughout the community.
1902.outcome: This program will prepare students on an agricultural career's pathway toward high-demand fields in Florida's agricultural economy.

1903.description: Safety and security of our students, faculty, staff, and visitors is a top priority. The ZeroEyes surveillance system would better secure our campus to threats from active assailant by utilizing cutting-edge technology. Additional cameras in existing coverage gaps will improve our readiness. Some of our existing locks and doors are out of date and do not allow for lockdown in the event of a threat. These updates will allow LSSC to create a lockdown-ready campus environment.
1903.purpose: This project includes a $330,000 contribution from Lake-Sumter State College for a total project cost of $950,000. This project will include the implementation of ZeroEyes surveillance system, additional cameras, and lockdown readiness improvements on all campuses.
1903.activities: This project will enhance security across all Lake-Sumter State College locations through advanced surveillance, upgraded infrastructure, and modernized access controls. Funds will support implementation of the ZeroEyes surveillance system, which uses artificial intelligence to detect threats and accelerate emergency response. Outdated locks and door hardware will be replaced or upgraded to enable rapid lockdown capabilities and add remaining buildings into the centralized access control system.
1903.direct_services: The upgrades foster a secure learning environment where students (and their families know) can focus on their education with confidence in their personal safety and wellbeing. This infrastructure supports proactive threat prevention and emergency responsiveness essential for student protection on campus.
1903.population: The target population is Lake and Sumter Counties. As the fastest growing college in the FCS for two straight years, Lake-Sumter currently serves 11,500 students each year and continues to expand its enrollment to serve additional learners throughout the community.
1903.outcome: The project creates a safer campus where students and employees feel secure, fostering a positive learning environment. Outcomes will be measured by incident reports and system reliability checks.

1053.description: For over 50 years, the Faulk Center for Counseling has provided low-cost/no-cost mental health services to economically disadvantaged and uninsured individuals, families, and children in Palm Beach and Broward Counties (and statewide via telehealth). Serving approximately 2000 clients annually, the Center utilizes doctoral interns and graduate students to deliver personalized counseling and mental health services. To meet the community demand for our services, in light of a well-documented public mental health crisis and concurrent shortage of qualified mental health professionals, we seek funding -- with matching dollars from the City of Boca Raton and Palm Beach County -- to support two full-time Registered Mental Health Interns (RMHIs) and a part-time Qualified Supervisor. This appropriation will support our capacity to provide individual, couple, family, and group therapy, all superv
1053.purpose: For years now, Florida has been suffering from a well-documented mental health crisis and an alarming shortage of qualified mental health professionals. The APA has also found that economically disadvantaged populations suffer from poor mental health outcomes at much higher levels due to inaccessibility of mental health care services, cultural stigma surrounding mental health care, and overall lack of awareness. With a primary focus on low-income children, adults, seniors, and families, the Faul
1053.activities: Clients who receive counseling services are provided a treatment plan based on their individual needs and approved therapies. Progress is measured based on improvements from baseline assessments of symptomatic and functional impacts, identified during the initial intake and early sessions. Issues being treated are often the result of many underlying and intertwined dynamics. Clinicians are aware of this and are trained to adjust their approach, strategies, and timeline for progress to match that
1053.direct_services: Clients work one-on-one with a mental health clinician in a safe, caring, and confidential environment. Weekly group counseling and support groups provide opportunities to reduce isolation, receive peer support, and collectively heal. Services to vulnerable populations, including uninsured and economically disadvantaged individuals, families, and children, are targeted through on site programs. Re
1053.population: The target population for counseling services is economically disadvantaged, uninsured, and/or underinsured clients in need of mental health services who reside in Palm Beach County and/or Broward County (or statewide via telehealth). The Faulk Center provides mental health and counseling services to approximately 2,000 individuals, families, and children each year, with funding from the City of Boca Raton, Palm Beach County, and a network of private grants and supporters.
1053.outcome: Progress is measured by the reduction or leveling off of symptomatic impacts and increases in self-esteem, self-worth and/or functional improvements such as better self-care, control of negative/disrupting behaviors, or increased engagement in community, home, school and/or work life, as measured by clinical notes, clinical observation and client feedback.

1029.description: The goal is to increase the number of students able to fully utilize their earned digital credentials to access/apply and submit transcripts/other educational records to FL higher-ed institutions (2yr and 4yr) during the application process. The goal is to make this process more secure, efficient and streamlined for students and schools to electronically issue, manage and verify these vital educational credentials. These funds will be utilized to on board 25,000+ high school and post-secondary education students at Miami-Dade Public Schools (MDCPS).
1029.purpose: To increase the number of students able to fully utilize their earned digital credentials to access/apply and submit transcripts/other educational records to FL higher-ed institutions (2yr and 4yr) during the application process. The goal is to make this process more secure, efficient and streamlined for students and schools to electronically issue, manage and verify these vital educational credentials. These funds will be utilized to on-board 25,000+ high school students at MDCPS.
1029.activities: Provide access and efficient on-boarding processes for MDCPS students to have access to a secure digital credential wallet to hold and use official copies of their transcripts and other vital documents. Instructions for downloading and the setup of the free digital wallet app, from the 2 App Stores. On-boarding to the free service. Educating students/families of the service and digital wallet.
1029.direct_services: To provide educational materials (print and video) that explain the benefits to having secure and verifiable credentials all in one place: their mobile device. Provide on-boarding events, both in-person and virtual, that are efficient in receiving their digital wallet and instructional as to the features and functions of the digital student wallet and credentialing service.
1029.outcome: Improve quality of education: Educational pathways offered to students via the AI-powered credential analysis service. The provided educational and career marketplace service within the App, then utilizes their credential analysis and facilitates connections to additional educational opportunities to enhance their career pathways. Measurement of overall percentage of students on-boarded to their wallet, who then go on to use the educational pathways credential analysis tool. Also, survey results that measure student satisfaction rates, engagement levels and ultimately success in getting connected to valuable educational opportunity choices, that expand economic pathways.

3543.description: The original Hardee Senior High School, built in 1948, has long been a symbol of pride and history for Hardee County. While no longer used for daily instruction, it continues to serve limited administrative purposes. The School District proposes a full renovation to create a centralized district office. Currently, district operations are spread across four sites, creating inefficiencies and high maintenance costs. Consolidating into one modernized location will improve operations, reduce expenses, and allow surplus properties to be repurposed. The project also includes restoring the historic Joel Evers Gymnasium, which serves as a key venue for youth athletics and community events. Renovating both facilities will preserve important local landmarks while enhancing district efficiency and expanding opportunities for community engagement.
3543.purpose: The requested funds will achieve several key goals. Consolidating four district offices into one location will enhance efficiency, communication, and access for staff, parents, and the community. It will also increase collaboration among district leaders and strengthen support to schools, improving overall educational outcomes. The project preserves a historic building while creating a safe, modern workspace, reduces maintenance and utility costs, and allows surplus properties to be repurposed.
3543.activities: The requested funds will support the planning, design, and renovation of the historic 1948 Hardee Senior High School into a centralized district office, uniting four administrative sites. This consolidation will enhance efficiency, collaboration, and leadership support across all schools. Activities include infrastructure modernization, safety and ADA upgrades, and restoration of the Joel Evers Gymnasium. The project will improve access to services, create a safe and efficient work environment,
3543.direct_services: The appropriation will provide direct services to citizens by centralizing key district functions—such as Human Resources, Exceptional Student Education, Finance, Grants, and Adult Education—into one accessible location. This will improve service delivery and communication for families, employees, and community members. The project also includes the renovation of the Joel Evers Gymnasium, which su
3543.population: The target population includes the 4,200 students of the School District of Hardee County, from preschool through high school, along with their families and the district’s 553 employees. This diverse group includes economically disadvantaged students, at-risk youth, homeless students, and those with developmental or physical disabilities. The project will directly serve these individuals by improving access to district services and educational support in one centralized, inclusive location. It w
3543.outcome: The expected benefits of this project include increased fiscal stewardship, improved operational efficiency, enhanced collaboration among district leaders, and stronger support for schools and families. Consolidating four district offices into one modern, accessible facility will reduce maintenance and utility costs while improving service delivery. Outcomes will be measured through annual budget savings, reduced operational costs, improved response times, and staff collaboration surveys, demonstrating greater efficiency and accountability in district operations.

3666.description: The City of Punta Gorda respectfully requests $2 million in state funding to assist homeowners with elevating flood- prone residential properties. Punta Gorda faces increasing risks from sea level rise, storm surge, and heavy rainfall. Elevating homes is a proven strategy to protect lives, reduce property damage, and lower disaster recovery costs.
3666.purpose: The City will administer a Home Elevation Assistance Program to reduce flood vulnerability and improve resilience by: • Providing direct grants to eligible homeowners. • Following FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) guidelines. • Requiring documentation of property ownership, SFHA location, flood insurance, and income. • Prioritizing vulnerable residents, such as seniors on fixed incomes. • Ensuring compliance with FEMA and Florida Building Code standards. • Verifying elevation certificates
3666.activities: Assist homeowners with elevating flood-prone residential properties. Punta Gorda faces increasing risks from sea level rise, storm surge, and heavy rainfall. Elevating homes is a proven strategy to protect lives, reduce property damage, and lower disaster recovery costs.
3666.population: Historic District residents with repetitive losses. 10 homeowners in the first year.
3666.outcome: • Reduce repetitive loss properties and future NFIP claims. • Lessen economic burdens on families and taxpayers. • Lower flood insurance premiums through community-wide risk reduction. • Advance state and local resilience and disaster mitigation priorities.

1436.description: The purpose of this project is to upgrade and expand technology infrastructure across district schools to support high quality digital learning and to enhance instructional delivery. This project will fund the purchase and installation of new classroom technology such as interactive displays, student laptops, instructional software, and network improvements. This will ensure that all students- regardless of socioeconomic status- will have access to reliable digital learning resources aligned with state standards. These improvements will strengthen instructional effectiveness, boost student performance, and better prepare graduates for college and workforce success in a technology driven society.
1436.purpose: The funds will be used to upgrade and expand classroom technology to support digital learning, improve instructional delivery, and enhance student engagement. The goal is to ensure that all students have access to modern, reliable technology that aligns with state curriculum standards and prepares them for college and career readiness in a digital economy.
1436.activities: Project activities include the purchase and installation of updated classroom technology such as interactive displays, student devices, secure network infrastructure, and instructional software.
1436.direct_services: This project will directly benefit students, teachers, and the broader school community by providing access to advanced instructional technology and digital resources. Citizens will also benefit through improved educational outcomes, better preparation of students for the workforce, and expanded opportunities for technology-driven community education programs.
1436.population: The target population includes approximately 2300 students and 188 instructional staff members who will utilize the upgraded technology daily. In addition, local families and community members will benefit from access to enhanced digital learning environments and community engagement initiatives supported by the new technology infrastructure.
1436.outcome: Expected outcomes include increased student achievement, improved technology proficiency, greater instructional efficiency, and equitable access to digital learning tools. Success will be measured by analyzing student performance data, teacher usage reports, network reliability metrics, and survey feedback from students and staff on technology effectiveness.

1441.description: The purpose of this project is to replace the ballfield lighting (poles, luminaries, wiring and controls) with a new code- compliant LED system that meets current IES recommendations. Work includes demolition, new concrete foundations, galvanized steel poles, LED sports lighting, infield/outfield aiming, electrical distribution, surge protection, networked controls, commissioning, and as built documentation.
1441.purpose: Currently, the antiquated lighting proves to be worsening over time. It also cost the city much more in electrical expense to utilize the lighting as it sits today. With proper funding, the city will be able to convert the existing lighting to LED which will provide a cost savings on utility cost of operating.
1441.activities: The city will procure services to demo and remove the existing lights on the baseball field, erect new poles. and construct new LED lights.
1441.direct_services: The citizens will be able to utilize Corey Baseball Field with proper lighting.
1441.population: Many people in the community utilize the park. Funding this project would go a long way to modernize this park and increase usage.
1441.outcome: The new lights will be the method in which the projects benefits and outcome are measured. The city can also track usage of the field.

1085.description: Sudden Cardiac Arrest is the leading cause of death on school campuses, in student athletes, and arguably among all children. Research shows that 1 in 300 children have a detectable and potentially life-threatening heart condition. Recognizing this tragedy, the Legislature passed, and the Governor signed SB 1070, requiring all first-time student athletes in Florida High Schools to receive an ECG screening. Who We Play For (WWPF) brings lifesaving electrocardiogram (ECG) heart screenings to tens of thousands of students and student-athletes across every region of Florida. State support will enable WWPF to provide ECG heart screenings for 33,000 students aged 10 to 22, empowering hundreds of students and families with critical health information, creating a safer future for our youth and preventing the unimaginable.
1085.purpose: Reduction of Sudden Cardiac Arrest in the young. Funds will be used to deliver non-invasive, 5-minute electrocardiogram (ECG) heart screenings to 33,000 young people across Florida. Research indicates 1 in 300 kids will have a detectable, life-threatening heart condition; therefore, WWPF can expect to save approximately 110 young lives. WWPF has identified over 500 children with deadly heart conditions through screenings of children who had passed their regular physicals.
1085.activities: Who We Play For will host heart screening events in partnership with local schools and community organizations, advancing the standard of care for 33,000 students between the ages of 10 and 22-years across the state.
1085.direct_services: WWPF will deliver non-invasive, 5-minute electrocardiogram (ECG) heart screenings to 33,000 students across FL. The ECG readings are then sent to and read by a pediatric cardiologist, and the results are returned to the student or parent/guardian. Support is provided when next steps are needed to mitigate or eliminate any health threats to the child.
1085.population: This project will serve up to 33,000 Florida students and student-athletes between the ages of 10 and 22, as well as their families.
1085.outcome: Who We Play For anticipates that, of the 33,000 students that will be screened, 3% or 990 students, will be flagged for follow up care. Of this group, hundreds will be identified with minor heart conditions and approximately 110 students will have a life-threatening heart condition that the State's investment can save from a tragic ending.

1333.description: The City currently runs three (3) wells to supply water for Belleview's utility customers. The wells operate on a constant basis. Hydropneumatic tanks are designed to maintain the on-demand water pressure without causing constant wear to the well pumps and booster pumps, which are extremely costly to maintain and repair. Additionally, it provides increased water storage for the growing population to receive the best quality of water the City can provide.
1333.purpose: Due to growth in the City of Belleview, new commercial and residential developments are in various stages of planning and building. The construction of this hydropneumatic tank will allow the City's utility to provide services.This project directly affects the water infrastructure in the city. Constructing this hydro tank will provide capacity, better pressure, water quality and more availability to residential and commercial development.
1333.activities: The construction of the hydropneumatic tank will eliminate pump lag time on the well and maintain water pressure throughout the entire city's water infrastructure.
1333.direct_services: The citizens will receive a more efficient water system.The addition of the Hydropneumatic tank will increase reliability of the water plant and maintain safe water quality for citizens.
1333.population: The City of Belleview serves approximately 8,000 people in the area with water services.
1333.outcome: Provide a new hydro tank to the well and serve citizens with water during critical times without resulting in funds being expended for expensive repairs on the infrastructure. This will be measured by the completion of the project.

1136.description: Page by Page, Inc. is a 501c3 entity that has been in existence for over 10 years. With the headquarters in Miami Dade, the book collections that are conducted within the local elementary school are re distributing books to children who are housed at Camillus House, Chapman Partnership, attend Breakthrough Miami, Big Brothers Big Sisters, and 15+ other charities within Florida. Not only do children receive books for free but the children within the book collection schools are taught to be student ambassadors and learn leadership and organizational skills. Page by Page attends book fairs, sponsors Pop Up Free Book Fairs throughout the community and has a virtual library on its site for remote locations. Currently, two apps have been created to share books within communities and allow kids free access to millions of books on their phone. Publishing a curriculum for Florida. After School Pr
1136.purpose: We hope to publish a statewide curriculum with the Florida After School Program. This curriculum will be an outline and instructional manual to run Page by Page Book Drives in communities throughout the State of Florida. The goal is to teach children and school administrators how to conduct the book drives and to donate the books to local charities in a streamlined way to empower grade level readers to organize a school wide event that takes a community to complete while resulting in thousands o
1136.activities: The activities will be to draft an outline of the curriculum and work with Florida After School Program's guidelines to meet their criteria of a curriculum that is publishable. This will involve using specific software for publishing and graphic designers to create the illustrations, layout, and format.
1136.direct_services: The direct service will be to provide a free Page by Page After School Curriculum available to all that will show the community how to enrich the literacy skills for all members of their community by operating a book collection and redistributing the books into the hands of children. It will also show grade level reading children that they have the power to make a difference in the world and are e
1136.population: The target population is every child in the State of Florida who can either benefit from free books or a child that wants to learn how to help others. A third party that benefits are the members of a community because this curriculum is a community event which brings people together to help others.
1136.outcome: We have circulated over 800,00+ book to more than 3.5 million children throughout the world. We expect by creating this curriculum, we feel we can impact potentially 18 million children in the State of Florida, either by enriching their literacy skills by having increased access to books or by teaching the children about literacy, being made aware of the need of literacy for all, or teaching them organizational skills to make a difference.

2858.description: The awarded monies will help fund construction of the Hillsborough County African American Arts and Cultural Center. The 50,000 square foot facility will include a range of public experience spaces, meeting spaces, galleries, labs, studios, educational classrooms, café, administrative support offices, interior and exterior special event spaces, and parking.
2858.purpose: The awarded monies will help fund construction of the Hillsborough County African American Arts and Cultural Center. The 50,000 square foot facility will include a range of public experience spaces, meeting spaces, galleries, labs, studios, educational classrooms, café, administrative support offices, interior and exterior special event spaces, and parking.
2858.activities: Construction activities and services include site work, demolition of existing antiquated facilities, and phased construction of new improvements with associated, necessary infrastructure.
2858.direct_services: The AAACC will focus on African American art, culture, and history in a centralized location within the Tampa Bay region. This includes a large gallery space for displaying the work of local artists, along with educational classes and experiences for children, students, and families. It will also serve as a historical and cultural hub celebrating African American life and contributions.
2858.population: The target audience for the African-American Arts and Cultural Center consists of three main market areas. Culture seekers who are active and engaged consumers of African-American arts, culture, and history. Skill seekers with specific interests and learning objectives can partake in education or studio classes. Enriching education experiences offering augmented curriculum and advanced common core. Center attendance, surveys, and overall community betterment
2858.outcome: It will focus on African-American art, culture, and history in a centralized location within the Tampa Bay region. This includes a large gallery space for displaying the work of local artists, along with educational classes and experiences for children, students, and families. It will also serve as a historical and cultural hub celebrating African-American life and contributions.

2466.description: Police and Fire are located within the City Hall complex. The condition of the roadways surrounding the complex play a critical role in the City’s response time. For southern and western portions of the City, 25th Avenue S. serves as the starting point for emergency vehicles. Stormwater improvements proposed on this roadway will result in the roadway being clear for passage for larger and more intense storm events. The placement of additional structures will reduce spread of flow allowing for response speeds to remain rapid resulting in improved public safety.
2466.purpose: To standardize the cross slope and longitudinal profile of the road while also improving stormwater collection capabilities and reducing spread of flow. This will allow emergency vehicles to safely increase speeds thereby reducing response times.
2466.activities: Design, permitting and infrastructure construction services.
2466.direct_services: Improved response time for emergency calls as well as improved motorist safety.
2466.population: Citywide benefits will be realized through reduced response times (~ 12,000 people).
2466.outcome: This projects effectiveness will ultimately be gauged by the anticipated reduction in response times.

2468.description: The Gulfport Marina is an economic engine for the City. With nearly 200 wet slips, the Marina provides public access to the waterfront. The roadway network surrounding the Marina is low-lying and, during non-extreme tides, many of the roads are nearly impassable. The use of remote-actuated valves in lieu of backflow valves provides protection against sunny day flooding without the increased head (and higher water levels) typically experienced during rain events. This pilot project could be implemented throughout other areas of the City, County and State. Water level sensors would also be installed. Not only would these sensors support the automated actuation of the valves, but they would also support a public-facing portal that would inform the community of when higher tides are experienced. Increased awareness of the current tidal conditions, coupled with the increased protection provid
2468.purpose: To mitigate for the adverse impacts that tidal flooding has on the accessibility and overall customer sentiment to the Gulfport Marina, the City's economic engine. This project also proposes a public awareness campaign element that notifies the general public of tidal fluctuations and how these tides are associated to flooding.
2468.activities: Design, permitting and infrastructure construction services.
2468.direct_services: Maintenance and improvement of economic activity at the Marina and improved response time for emergency calls as well as improved motorist safety during times of tidal flooding. Also, reduced tidal flooding will improve wastewater facilities and reduce the likelihood of SSOs, thereby protecting and improving water quality of Clam Bayou.
2468.population: Citywide benefits will be realized through increased economic activity at the Marina (~ 12,000 people).
2468.outcome: Outcomes will be measured by 1.) Reduction in emergency calls for stranded vehicles. Also, reduced emergency vehicle response time during certain tidal flooding scenarios. 2.) Slip renewals and overall marina occupancy after installation of the tidal isolation technology. 3.)Reduced saltwater intrusion can be demonstrated by lower run times and chloride concentrations within the wastewater stream. 4.) water quality improvements will be realized through reduced likelihood of SSOs and oil transport where vehicles interact with the saltwater.

1445.description: During the recovery from Hurricane Idalia and Hurricane Helene, the Edward Perry Sports Complex housed a volunteer village and many mutual aid workers from across the state. Sheriff's Offices sent resources to help Lafayette County in a variety of ways including maintaining law and order. These improvements will retrofit the park to continue to be a place to host these resources.
1445.purpose: An increase in security and accessibility in the park.
1445.activities: The activities and services provided will be the increase of lighting in the entire park, including the soccer field, to house a volunteer village or first responders during hurricane recovery efforts. Handicap accessibility will be improved to allow access to the entire park. The security in the park will improve due to the fencing and traffic control.
1445.direct_services: The direct service will be an improved response to natural disasters.
1445.population: All Lafayette County residents. Individuals expected to be served would be 7,500.
1445.outcome: Increased use of the park during blue skies and gray skies. The use of the park can be monitored.

1446.description: This request will provide the construction of a mutli-purpose building for Lafayette County. The building can also be used as a hurricane shelter. We do not currently have a shelter rated for winds above 120 mph. This shelter will have enough space to house residents, residents with special needs, pets and first responders. It will allow our school to stay open the maximum amount during events. Currently, the school can't resume classes until the shelter closes. The building will be able to withstand 160 mph winds, making the shelter available in any hurricane.
1446.purpose: The purpose of the funds will be a multi-purpose building. One purpose of the building will be a shelter during hurricanes. Lafayette County does not have a building anywhere in our county capable of housing evacuees during a hurricane with winds in excess of 120 mph.
1446.activities: This funding will be used to construct the multi-purpose building.
1446.direct_services: The direct service will be a multi-purpose building for the people of Lafayette County. The building could serve as a storm shelter during hurricanes. The building could also house first responders during a storm, they will be available to help in recovery efforts as soon as the storm passes.
1446.population: The target population is people in substandard housing, mobile homes and travel trailers. However, it will not be limited to those people. This building will serve 400 people during one event, but many more than that over the life of the building.
1446.outcome: The benefit will be a building that the people of Lafayette County can use to host large events. The building will be open during storms allowing the general public a place to seek refuge. The outcome will be measured by the number of injuries or deaths during hurricanes.

1090.description: This project will improve stormwater flooding in the southwest quadrant of SR64 and SR789 bounded by Old Gulf Drive. Improvements will include piping, ditches, infiltration areas, tidal check valves, and improved roadways in the area. During flooding events, storm water backs up into roadways throughout the City. Flooded roads negatively impacts quality of life, damages vehicles, and leads to home flooding. Repeatedly submerged roads also reduces their life impacting citizen's and tourist travel. Reducing flooding reduces impacts to homeowners and lessens private property damage. It improves quality of life for safer mobility. Vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians can move without risk of life and fear of damage to vehicles. Longer infrastructure life with less roadway repairs requiring lane and road closures means tax dollars can be spent elsewhere.
1090.purpose: The purpose of this proposed project is to reduce flooding of the southwest quadrant of SR 64 and SR 789.
1090.activities: During flooding events, storm water backs up into roadways throughout the City. Flooded roads negatively impacts quality of life, damages vehicles, and leads to home flooding. Repeatedly submerged roads also reduces their life impacting citizen's and tourist travel.
1090.direct_services: Reducing flooding reduces impacts to homeowners and lessens private property damage. It improves quality of life for safer mobility. Vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians can move without risk of life and fear of damage to vehicles. Longer infrastructure life with less roadway repairs requiring lane and road closures means tax dollars can be spent elsewhere.
1090.population: All traveling public throughout the City is impacted by improving flooding in the area of this project. On any given day there is approximately 20,000 AADT traveling along the edge of this project area.
1090.outcome: The City held a Stormwater Program public meeting where the majority of those in attendance and those speaking desired reducing flooding throughout the City and also received emails requesting improving stormwater flooding. Flooded roads negatively impact quality of life, damage vehicles, and leads to home flooding. Repeatedly submerged roads also reduces their life, causing costly repairs. Number of times street flooding occurs during high tide and/or major rain storm events.

2686.description: Construct a parallel 8-inch water main along County Road 108 connecting to the Whisper Ridge infrastructure to ensure reliable service to the FAA Jacksonville Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC ZJX). The facility, employing over 400 personnel, is a critical regional employer. Recent testing showed dangerously low pressures that triggered alarms and forced use of its backup system, underscoring the urgent need for redundancy and improved fire protection.
2686.purpose: To construct a parallel 8-inch water main along County Road 108 connecting the Town’s Water Treatment Plant to the existing Whisper Ridge main, ensuring reliable water service, adequate pressure, and fire-flow capacity to the FAA Jacksonville Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC ZJX) and surrounding service area.
2686.activities: Project activities include construction of approximately 4,300 linear feet of 8-inch water main, installation of valves, fittings, hydrants, directional drilling, tie-ins to existing mains, and restoration. Engineering design and permitting are funded by the Town.
2686.direct_services: The project will provide reliable potable water service, increased system redundancy, and improved fire protection for residents, businesses, and critical facilities, including the FAA facility that employs over 400 personnel.
2686.population: Serves the Town of Hilliard’s northern service area, including the FAA ARTCC facility, local businesses, and residential customers—benefiting approximately 3,000 people and safeguarding 400+ regional jobs.
2686.outcome: Benefit: Improved water system reliability, fire protection, and economic stability through continued FAA operations and system redundancy. Measurement: Verified through pre- and post-construction fire-flow and pressure testing, operational data confirming sustained FAA service reliability, and documentation of uninterrupted facility operations.

1031.description: Women of Tomorrow (WOT) empowers 2,700 at-risk teenage girls across 119 Florida public high schools each year, providing pathways out of poverty and reducing high school dropout rates through mentoring by accomplished professional women, college scholarships, and real-world career exposure. With an extraordinary 99% high school graduation rate and 94% continuing on to higher education, WOT has awarded more than $9 million in college scholarships to date. Funding will support the implementation of critical programming focused on personal safety, violence prevention, and career exploration in public safety fields—equipping mentees with the tools they need for both personal security and long-term financial success.
1031.purpose: State funding will support the creation of new programming focused on personal safety and violence prevention through mentoring and career development. WOT mentees are identified as at risk for high school dropout due to challenges such as limited opportunity, domestic abuse, or exposure to addiction, making prevention efforts both life- changing and lifesaving. This targeted curriculum will reach 2,700 at-risk students across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach Counties, along with the program’
1031.activities: Through expertly designed mentoring sessions, field trips, and summits, mentees will engage with topics such as human trafficking, self-defense, substance abuse prevention, bullying, and cybersecurity, building awareness, critical thinking, and decision-making skills. These experiences will be paired with career exploration in public safety fields, including the military, law enforcement, intelligence, legal professions, emergency management, and criminal investigation. This initiative will equi
1031.direct_services: The Public Safety and Violence Prevention curriculum will be delivered through mentoring sessions, guest speakers, educational videos, expert-led summits, career-focused field trips in law enforcement and the armed forces, and alumnae chapter meetings. The initiative will introduce new violence prevention topics for mentors, mentees, and school coordinators; host career-focused field trips availab
1031.population: WOT serves 2,700 students annually across 119 public high schools in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach Counties. 95% percent of participants are minority students, and nearly half are the first in their families to pursue higher education. Mentees are selected based on criteria such as risk of high school dropout, exposure to abuse, involvement in criminal activity, or academic challenges. Despite these risk factors, 99% of WOT mentees graduate from high school, demonstrating the program’s pro
1031.outcome: WOT empowers at-risk students to transform obstacles into opportunities by providing exposure, motivation, and the confidence to create brighter futures for themselves, their families, and their communities. Through targeted mentoring and career-focused experiences, mentees gain the knowledge and life skills to avoid risky behaviors, stay in school, and pursue higher education and meaningful careers. Program effectiveness will be measured through mentee surveys, graduation and postsecondary enrollment data, and year-end reports from partner school districts. Continuous progress monitoring, through mentor feedback and direct communication with schools, will ensure accountability, data-driven

3406.organization: River City Education Services Inc dba River
3406.description: River City Science Academy (RCSA) operates six charter schools in Duval County, Jacksonville, Florida. The network includes four K–8 campuses, one K–5 campus, and one 6–12 campus. Currently, RCSA Middle-High Campus serves approximately 1,026 students — 437 middle schoolers and 589 high school students. The RCSA High School Project aims to establish a dedicated high school campus to serve all RCSA students matriculating from 8th grade, as well as new students from other public and private schools and surrounding counties. The current RCSA Middle-High campus has limited capacity as most seats are filled by existing middle schoolers who roll over into 9th grade. RCSA has executed a long-term land lease agreement (40 years with two 10-year extensions) with Florida State College at Jacksonville (FSCJ) to construct the new high school on FSCJ’s Southeast Campus, located at: 11901 Beach Blvd, J
3406.purpose: The RCSA High School Project aims to establish a dedicated high school on FSCJ’s Southeast Campus to serve all RCSA students matriculating from 8th grade, as well as new students from other public and private schools in Duval and surrounding counties.
3406.activities: The funds will be used for the construction of the new RCSA High School located on the Florida State College at Jacksonville (FSCJ) Southeast Campus. Activities include site preparation, building construction, engineering, architectural design, permitting, and related infrastructure to establish a modern, fully equipped educational facility.
3406.direct_services: RCSA High School will be a tuition-free public charter school open to students in Duval and nearby counties. It will offer a high-quality STEM education with AP Capstone, dual enrollment, and the opportunity to earn an AA degree from FSCJ, preparing students for college, careers, and future workforce needs.
3406.population: The project will serve high school students residing in Duval County and surrounding areas who seek a high-quality, tuition-free public STEM education. The school will provide equitable access for all students, including English Language Learners (ELL), students receiving Special Education services, economically disadvantaged students, as well as students coming from private schools or being homeschooled.
3406.outcome: The project will provide students with access to a high-quality, STEM-focused, tuition-free high school education, including AP Capstone, dual enrollment, and the opportunity to earn an AA degree from FSCJ. It will improve academic achievement, college readiness, workforce skills, and equitable access for diverse populations, including ELL, Special Education, economically disadvantaged, private, and homeschooled students. Methodology for Measuring Outcome: Outcomes will be measured through student enrollment and retention data, academic performance indicators (GPA, standardized test scores, AP and dual enrollment participation), graduation rates, and college matriculation data. Additional me

2130.description: Forever Family®, now in its third decade, is the only coalition of major broadcast television stations (ABC, NBC, CBS, and FOX) united to enhance child safety, preserve families, recruit foster and adoptive parents, and support youth transitioning out of foster care. FY24/25 ROI: Forever Family® leveraged approximately $7.27 million in earned media value, generating more than 30 million viewer impressions statewide. The program is on track to exceed these results in FY25/26. Through consistent broadcast media exposure, Forever Family® not only addresses immediate needs but also builds a sustainable support system for Florida’s children and families, leveraging broadcast media to foster community involvement and lasting change. The vast reach of Forever Family® has led to thousands of children finding loving families, the recruitment of countless dedicated foster parents and mentors, and
2130.purpose: Forever Family® news segments shine a light on vital prevention services that strengthen families, decrease foster care entries, and dramatically increase the number of foster and adoptive families in Florida, while rallying community support for teens aging out of care. This pioneering initiative secures up to $10 million in media exposure and 50 million impressions annually through exclusive partnerships with ABC, NBC, CBS, and FOX, hosted by top news anchors.
2130.activities: Forever Family® will continue to work with the Department of Children and Families, Community Based Care Lead Agencies, and statewide child welfare agencies to research, write, produce, and air television news stories and promotions that directly support Florida's at-risk children and families. Forever Family® will leverage media airtime to raise awareness and connect viewers who want to help - or who are in need of help - with their local agencies.
2130.direct_services: Forever Family® generates millions of media impressions, focusing on vital support for at-risk children and families, promoting foster and adoptive family recruitment, and assisting youth transitioning out of foster care. News stories are also featured on social media and distributed to child welfare agencies to enhance recruitment efforts and prevention initiatives.
2130.population: Children and teens at risk of entering and within the dependency system, families including persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, developmentally disabled, drug users, young adults, economically disadvantaged persons, victims of crimes. Target populations expected to be served: 800+
2130.outcome: Strengthening families and providing permanency leads to improved physical health, mental health, educational outcomes, general public safety, enhanced self-sufficiency, reduced recidivism, reduced substance abuse, diversion from criminal justice/ juvenile justice system. Strengthening families, permanency = net savings to state and tax payers. Outcomes are measured by number of stories, commercial reach, viewing impressions, market size.

1043.description: It is the goal of the mentoring program to improve college readiness and retention rates and improve workforce readiness amongst emerging Miami youth. The program design provides ongoing opportunities for youth to engage in college preparatory and workforce readiness activities at a variety of sites throughout South Florida. OYC's College and Career Readiness component offers effective year-round college preparation services which increase the number of youths enrolling in college, imparts knowledge of the college admissions and financial aid process and improves preparedness for post- secondary success.
1043.purpose: The Overtown Youth Center College and Career Readiness program aims to increase students’ knowledge of college and career options, providing jobs and internships and improving financial literacy. The goal is to develop youth who contribute to a thriving community with a vibrant workforce by ensuring each student is equipped with the tools to succeed and have the ability to impact their communities.
1043.activities: Services include expanding college and career readiness programming to serve youth starting in kindergarten through 12th grade with homework assistance, tutoring, mentoring, STEAM enrichment, ACT/SAT testing preparation, career assessments, college preparation, financial literacy, and internship/job placement.
1043.direct_services: Coordinators provide ongoing student support using individual case management to track progress towards post- secondary goals. Our services include daily monitoring, mentoring, counseling, and support. Student report cards are collected directly from Miami-Dade County Public Schools to monitor the progress of the students in core academic content areas. An Individual Success Plan (ISP) is used for
1043.population: Funding serves 100 youth in grades K-12 who reside in under-resourced communities throughout South Florida. The program considers factors such as students attending under achieving schools, students from low-income households, those with limited access to college exposure and career readiness opportunities.
1043.outcome: The Overtown Youth Center - College and Career Readiness programs are designed to equip students with the essential skills and knowledge needed for post-secondary success and competitive careers. The expected benefits include; Enhanced Academic Proficiency, Increased College Readiness, Career Exploration and Preparation, and the Development of Essential Soft Skills which foster critical thinking, effective communication, and teamwork, which are crucial for success in both academic settings and the workplace. To measure these outcomes, the project will employ a multi-faceted approach that includes: Individual Case Management and Mentoring, Academic Assessments, Enrichment and Enhancement acti

2133.description: The City of Tamarac (City) seeks state funding to purchase a mid-mount aerial platform ladder truck, such as a 100-foot tower ladder with a bucket (e.g., equipment comparable to the Pierce Enforcer 100AAT, Sourcewell Base Spec 296). This apparatus would provide elevated rescues, rapid access to upper floors, and higher water-flow capability, extending current reach beyond mid-level structures. The overall build timeline is estimated to range from twelve months to as long as forty-six months from order. This project prepares Tamarac for vertical rescue in a largely built-out city and aligns public-safety capacity with Florida’s Live Local Act, Broward County’s 10-Year Affordable Housing Master Plan, and the City’s Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code updates allowing for greater height and density.
2133.purpose: The purpose is to acquire a mid-mount aerial platform ladder truck, such as a 100-foot tower ladder with a bucket, to extend Tamarac Fire Rescue’s reach beyond mid-level structures as Tamarac, a largely built-out city, redevelops upward. The goals are to ensure rapid response and life safety before taller buildings are constructed and occupied, aligning capacity with the City’s Comprehensive Plan, Broward County’s 10-Year Affordable Housing Plan, and Florida’s Live Local Act.
2133.activities: The activities and services include procuring, outfitting, and placing into service a mid-mount aerial platform ladder truck with a 100-foot bucket, ensuring Tamarac Fire Rescue has the apparatus needed for elevated rescues, fire suppression, and emergency response as redevelopment brings taller buildings.
2133.direct_services: The direct services to citizens include rescues and evacuations from upper floors, faster fire suppression in taller buildings, improved EMS access, and enhanced incident control. This aerial apparatus will provide life safety protection by extending capabilities beyond current mid-level reach.
2133.population: The target population is the entire community of Tamarac, including residents, workers, and visitors who rely on fire rescue services. With a population of more than 74,000 and growing, all individuals in the city, as well as those in future high-rise developments, will directly benefit from the enhanced capabilities of this apparatus.
2133.outcome: This project protects the public by enabling safer rescues and more effective fire suppression in taller buildings, improving physical health through faster EMS access and evacuations, and supporting economic activity by giving investors confidence in reliable life-safety coverage. Outcomes will be measured by: (1) improved response times, incident results, annual fire-loss trends, and patient survival; (2) tracking redevelopment approvals and occupancy; and (3) readiness reports and ISO fire service rating performance.

2134.description: This Phase 1 project modernizes aging water distribution and fire protection infrastructure in Tamarac, Broward County. It will replace undersized 1973 cast-iron mains with new 6- and 8-inch HDPE mains, renew service lines, install new valves, add additional hydrants to improve coverage, and restore pavement after utility work. The work addresses frequent breaks, boil-water notices, and service interruptions and is designed to meet required fire-flow and water- pressure standards so the community receives reliable, safe service and improved emergency response and firefighting capability.
2134.purpose: The requested funds will assist the city with replacing undersized and deteriorated 1973 cast-iron water mains and hydrants, adding additional hydrants to improve coverage, and restoring pavement. The goal is to ensure reliable drinking water, reduce main breaks and boil notices, meet required fire-flow standards, and reduce unplanned road closures while improving emergency access in the community.
2134.activities: Activities and services will include replacement of deteriorated water mains, renewal of service lines, installation of new valves, addition of fire hydrants to improve coverage and fire protection, and pavement milling and resurfacing to restore roadways after utility work.
2134.direct_services: Direct services to citizens by this project include more reliable drinking water, improved fire protection from added hydrant coverage and fire flow, fewer service interruptions and boil-water notices, and safer streets from pavement restoration after utility work. These services will protect public health and safety, support emergency response, and maintain essential infrastructure in the communi
2134.population: The primary population served is the Westwood community in Tamarac, which includes approximately 5,000 residents. However, the benefits extend beyond this neighborhood by strengthening the city’s interconnected water distribution and fire protection system. Improved reliability, fire flow, and roadway conditions support not only the local community but also nearby residents, businesses, and emergency services that depend on uninterrupted water supply and access.
2134.outcome: Expected benefits are improved fire protection, reliable drinking water quality, reduced water-quality risks, fewer water main breaks and shutdowns, improved transportation conditions, and greater service reliability for residents and businesses. Outcomes will be measured by comparing pre- and post-project data, such as NFPA fire-flow tests, compliance/boil-notice and sampling reports, utility break/outage log, call-center complaints, and work-order/traffic records.

1592.description: The funds requested for this project are specifically aimed at upgrading and enhancing the capacity of Sewer Pump Station #4, which has reached the end of its life expectancy and experienced frequent malfunctions resulting in significant repair costs. The goal is to prevent failures that could lead to serious environmental issues such as the discharge of raw wastewater into the ocean, deep well injection, and contamination through underground irrigation. This will include the purchase of a backup bypass pump to be used if this or pumps #1, #2 or #3 are down to maintain proper pressure for service.
1592.purpose: The funds will upgrade Sewer Pump Station #4, which is outdated and prone to failures causing environmental risks like raw wastewater discharge. The upgrade aims to enhance capacity and reliability to prevent these failures, protect the environment, and serve the community effectively. This will also reduce costly repairs and extend the station’s lifespan, ensuring safer, uninterrupted wastewater management for residents and public facilities in the service area.
1592.activities: The project includes purchasing, delivering, and installing larger pumps, electric motors, and new pipes. Existing piping will be relocated to fit the new system, supported by an extended concrete base. Engineering and planning will ensure the modifications integrate smoothly with current infrastructure, improving station reliability and capacity to handle wastewater effectively.
1592.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with more reliable wastewater management services, reducing the risk of environmental contamination and public health hazards. By upgrading the pump station, the community will experience fewer service disruptions caused by equipment failures, thus ensuring that facilities such as the Recreation Center, Park, and School receive continuous and safe sewage processin
1592.population: The target population includes the largest service area covered by the Sewer Pump Station #4, which encompasses a significant portion of the community. This includes residential neighborhoods as well as key public facilities such as the Recreation Center, Park, and School. Although an exact number is not specified, it is clear that thousands of residents rely on this station for essential wastewater services, making the project crucial for a broad and diverse population.
1592.outcome: Benefits include fewer malfunctions, reduced repair costs, extended station life, and environmental protection. Outcomes will be measured by tracking malfunction frequency, monitoring maintenance expenses, assessing system uptime, and conducting environmental impact reviews. These metrics will demonstrate improved reliability and reduced risk of contamination following the upgrade.

2860.description: Funding is requested to expand Day Reporting Center (DRC) pilot projects, replicating the success of the Circuit 10 (Lakeland) DRC in another Judicial Circuit, in partnership with the Florida Department of Corrections. The DRC provides a structured, non-residential alternative to incarceration for eligible felony offenders, offering daily support and probation supervision.
