The program provides individualized assessments, evidence-based substance use and mental health treatment, cognitive and life skills training, regular drug testing, and accountability checks. It supports family reunification, aftercare, and offers gender-specific, trauma-informed care. Community partnerships help clients with education, employment, housing, transportation, and healthcare.
2860.purpose: Funding is requested to expand Day Reporting Center (DRC) pilot projects, replicating the success of the Circuit 10 (Lakeland) DRC in another Judicial Circuit, in partnership with the Florida Department of Corrections. The Day Reporting Center (DRC) serves as a structured, non-residential alternative to incarceration for eligible felony offenders. Participants receive daily support and guidance in an environment that combines probation supervision with intensive, evidence-based services and trea
2860.activities: The program provides individualized assessments, evidence-based substance use and mental health treatment, cognitive and life skills training, regular drug testing, and accountability checks. It supports family reunification, aftercare, and offers gender-specific, trauma-informed care. Community partnerships help clients with education, employment, housing, transportation, and healthcare.
2860.direct_services: The Day Reporting Center (DRC) is a structured, non-residential alternative to incarceration for eligible felony offenders. It provides daily support, probation supervision, and intensive, evidence-based services to address criminal behavior and support probation completion. Goals include reducing recidivism, increasing successful completions, promoting accountability, and saving costs.
2860.population: The DRC will provide a structured, non-residential alternative to incarceration for justice-involved adults on felony probation. The program addresses critical barriers to successful supervision and reintegration. These challenges contribute to high rates of probation failure and recidivism. The DRC model integrates probation supervision with evidence-based treatment, cognitive and life skills programming, employment and educational support, and trauma- informed care to promote long-term success
2860.outcome: be measured? The DRC provides a structured, non-residential alternative to incarceration for eligible felony offenders, offering daily support and probation supervision. Gateway delivers on-site services including risk assessment, evidence-based curricula, outpatient substance use disorder treatment, drug testing, anger management, batterer’s intervention, employment and life skills, wellness, and personal finance. Research shows high-quality DRCs reduce incarceration and recidivism rates, helping participants rebuild their lives and reintegrate into the community, aligning with FDC’s mission. Outcomes will be measured by tracking participant engagement and completion rates for each service,

1237.description: Juvenile drug courts are dockets within juvenile courts for cases involving substance abusing youth in need of specialized treatment services. The focus is on providing treatment to eligible, drug-involved juvenile offenders with the goal of reducing recidivism and substance abuse. The programs allow for intensive judicial supervision of youth that would not ordinarily be available in the traditional juvenile court process. Each participant will receive individual, group and family counseling as well as weekly random drug testing, and residential services as needed, provided by IMPOWER. Participants will be seen in court in front of the judge on a monthly basis or as determined by the court. Youth work a 4 phase program granting them access to therapeutic services in a gradual step down process while being closely monitored by clinical staff and juvenile court. Upon successful completion
1237.purpose: Maintain, enhance and expand the juvenile drug court program in Seminole County. Florida, like other states, is seeing an increase in additions related to opioid usage as well as other drugs. Seminole County Court has a long tradition of diverting youth through drug court to obtain treatment and avoid having an arrest on their record. The program has been successful, particularly over the past year with enhanced clinical supervision and staff.
1237.direct_services: Intensive Substance Abuse Out Patient services: Drug screenings, individual, group and family counseling, residential treatment and case management.
1237.population: At-risk youth ages 12 - 18 in Seminole County FL. Youth are facing juvenile charges related to an offense involving substance or tested positive at time of arrest. 51-100 youth.
1237.outcome: % of change in the # of children arrested 30 days prior to admission vs 30 prior to discharge. % of participants in Juvenile Drug Court who complete the first 60 days will test negative on weekly random drug screenings 30 days prior to discharge. % of participants who begin Juvenile Drug Court program successfully complete program and thus will be diverted from additional criminal sanctions from the juvenile court system.

1057.description: Arc Broward operates critically necessary programs at its 8-acre main campus located in Sunrise. The campus includes three buildings which are vital to the daily delivery of 15 programs and wrap around supports to children and adults in its three adult day programs, a developmental preschool, an after school program, two transition programs and three post- secondary education programs, as well as our mission based enterprises. On any given day, the campus supports over 370 children and adults with disabilities, and their families, 200+ team members and 20 volunteers/guests. Grounded in discipline, accountability, and personal responsibility, ACT drives academic achievement, school attendance, and workforce readiness. Since 2012, ACT has achieved a 100% high school graduation rate and 90% college placement rate, impacting over 16,000 Florida students and families. Thanks to the 2025-2026 state appropriation, ACT has been able to expand its proven model across Pinellas and Hillsborough counties and, with state support in 2026-2027, will extend this effective model into Manatee and Sarasota counties—ensuring taxpayer dollars strengthen schools, families, and the workforce.

2863.activities: State support strengthens ACT’s proven, results-driven programs that equip students with essential skills—leadership, communication, critical thinking, entrepreneurship, and financial literacy - that prepare them to excel in school and life. ACT’s workforce track gives high school students hands-on training aligned with Florida’s business needs so they graduate career-ready, reducing future costs for remedial training and strengthening the state’s talent pipeline.

Unnecessary flooding and erosion can affect hundreds of private property owners. Inadequate flow can negatively impact thousands. It is critical that the City of Safety Harbor maintain these ponds.

3548.description: Design and installation of a mechanical dewatering system at City of Wauchula Wastewater Treatment Plant to reduce sludge volume, improve disposal efficiency, and lower long-term operational costs. The proposed centrifuge dewatering is a mechanical process that uses centrifugal force to separate water from solid particles in a sludge or slurry. This process is commonly used in wastewater treatment and other industries to reduce the volume of sludge and produce a drier, more manageable "cake" for disposal or further processing. Funds used for contractual services for design, bidding, permitting, construction engineering inspection, project management and construction services to install the system.

1103.description: The Town of Southwest Ranches is requesting funding assistance to install municipal water lines to our Town Hall and Police Station, located at 13400 Griffin Road. Laboratory analysis of the drinking water samples for our well water have historically exceeded the state-mandated Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs) for Arsenic, Sodium, Total Dissolved Solids, Chloride and Iron, which is detrimental to public health.

1103.population: Installing modern water infrastructure will benefit the entire population of Southwest Ranches by ensuring uninterrupted service for emergency and law enforcement operations and strengthening the Town’s ability to serve residents during and after climate-related disruptions.

The level 2 center provides intensive inpatient and outpatient treatment, with the capacity to house up to 30 males and 10 females, providing treatment and case management. The goal is to break the cycle of "catch, treat and release", providing treatment through this unique partnership with AdventHealth.

The level 2 center provides intensive inpatient and outpatient treatment, with the capacity to house up to 30 males and 10 females, providing treatment and case management. The goal is to break the cycle of "catch, treat and release", providing treatment through this unique partnership with AdventHealth.
1239.activities: The Seminole County Sheriff's Office Hope for Healing Center is a pilot project that has a secure facility capable of providing temporary housing for 30 males and 10 females while awaiting placement to a long term substance abuse treatment facility. 1240.description: The Florida Economic Consortium requests continued support for its Community-Based Health & Wellness Initiative addressing diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol in Lake, Seminole, Orange, Lake & Volusia Counties. By funding this initiative, the Legislature can improve long-term health outcomes while generating substantial taxpayer savings and advancing Florida’s commitment to healthier, more resilient communities.
1240.purpose: Over the course of the term of the contract the requested funds will support Life N Balance by FEC, a community- based health and wellness initiative led by certified health workers. Through workshops and one-on-one engagement, participants managing diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol will gain knowledge and preventative strategies to reduce complications, improve long-term outcomes, cut indigent care costs, and save taxpayer dollars.
1240.activities: Life N Balance by FEC will deliver workshops on chronic disease management, distribute tailored education, and provide on-site screenings for glucose and blood pressure. Participants will receive individualized health & wellness consultations, supported by community outreach and recruitment. Program impact will be measured through data- driven evaluation and surveys to ensure outcomes and accountability.
1240.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide citizens with direct health screenings for diabetes, hypertension, and cholesterol; individualized consultations with community health workers; distribution of tailored educational materials; interactive workshops on prevention and management; and accessible outreach to connect families with resources that improve long-term health outcomes.
1240.population: The target population includes uninsured, underinsured, and at-risk individuals in underserved communities who are managing or at risk for diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol. The project is expected to directly serve approximately 500–600 individuals annually through screenings, workshops, and consultations. Special emphasis will be placed on reaching populations with limited access to preventive care and health education resources.
1240.outcome: The expected outcome is improved long-term health for individuals managing diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol, with reduced reliance on emergency care and lower indigent care costs. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-program health screenings, participant surveys, and data analysis on knowledge gains, behavioral changes, and healthcare utilization.

1066.description: Southwest Ranches is requesting funding to purchase of a new Advanced Life Support (ALS) Type I Class A pumper fire apparatus with a minimum tank capacity of 1,000 gallons for our fire department. This will significantly enhance our ability to respond to structural fires, wildland incidents, and medical emergencies. It will benefit all Southwest Ranches residents, visitors, businesses, and motorists traveling along US 27 and Interstate 75 who need emergency services. Our department also participates in mutual aid agreements with Cooper City, Pembroke Pines, Davie, and Weston, ensuring regional emergency response capabilities.
1066.purpose: The purchase of a new Advanced Life Support (ALS) Type I Class A Pumper, staffed by cross-trained firefighter paramedics, will significantly strengthen our department’s ability to respond to structural fires, wildland incidents, and medical emergencies. This multifunctional apparatus will be equipped to perform both fire suppression and ALS-level medical care, enabling our personnel to deliver critical, life-saving treatment at the scene while maintaining full operational readiness for fire and
1066.activities: Purchase of a new Advanced Life Support (ALS) Type I Class A pumper fire apparatus with a minimum tank capacity of 1,000 gallons for our fire department.
1066.direct_services: This apparatus will be equipped to deliver both fire suppression and ALS-level medical care, ensuring our first responders can provide life-saving front-line critical care while maintaining operational readiness.
1066.population: The benefits of this acquisition extend beyond the Town of Southwest Ranches, serving residents, businesses, and visitors, as well as motorists traveling along U.S. 27 and Interstate 75 who may require emergency assistance. Our department also participates in mutual aid agreements with surrounding jurisdictions—Cooper City, Pembroke Pines, the Town of Davie, and Weston. Collectively, these municipalities represent a regional population of approximately 390,000 residents.
1066.outcome: This investment will directly improve public safety, reduce response times, and strengthen our community’s resilience. This will be measured in response times and service call outcomes.

1065.description: A 22,000 sq. ft. well-known hub for Fire Rescue and Community Engagement was built in 1958. Originally located on Powerline Road, Deerfield Beach’s Fire Station 4, located at 928 E. Hillsboro Boulevard, closed in 2011 following the merger of the City’s Fire Department with Broward Sheriff’s Office (BSO) Fire Rescue; however to improve response times its doors reopened. Today, this historic site—located at the corner of Hillsboro Boulevard and US-1/Federal Highway, the main gateway to our beach—is serving the community in new and meaningful ways. The building now houses both BSO Fire Rescue operations and the Police Athletic League (PAL), a vital initiative of the Broward Sheriff's Office. The central HVAC and rooftop units are in poor condition and not tied to the property, creating poor air flow and distribution, producing humidity inside the facility. The electrical panels are at full
1065.purpose: The goal achieved by completing repairs to the fire station is allowing the fire station to remain operable and livable for the first responders housed at the facility. A rehabilitation project for fire station #4 can significantly enhance its functionality, safety, and community relations while ensuring the well-being of firefighters and the public they serve.
1065.activities: The request is for a rehabilitation project of fire station # 4 to maintain a safe and healthy environment for first responders to provide services to residents of Deerfield Beach. The rehabilitation project will consist of a roof replacement, exterior painting and door replacements.
1065.direct_services: Firefighters respond to fires, medical emergencies, hazardous material incidents, and other emergencies to ensure public safety. Direct Services include: Emergency Response, Fire Prevention, Public Education, CPR and First Aide Training, Community Engagement, and Disaster Preparedness. These services are aimed at enhancing community safety and promoting awareness of fire hazards and emergency prep
1065.population: Fire Station 4 is located on the intersection Hillsboro Blvd and US-1/Federal Highway, the main gateway to the City's Beach. This fire station serves the downtown area, municipal beach, the City Pier, with various businesses, parks, and cooperate headquarters. The building now houses both BSO Fire Rescue operations and the Police Athletic League (PAL), a vital initiative of the Broward Sheriff's Office.
1065.outcome: The expected benefit of the rehabilitation project to the fire station is improved safety, better living conditions, community engagement, attracting talent and enhancing the public image.

1337.description: The Estella Byrd Whitman Community Health Center has demonstrated rapid growth and measurable impact, expanding patient visits from 321 in 2023 to over 5,000 year-to-date in 2025. With limited space and resources, the Center has delivered comprehensive primary care, chronic disease management, and preventive services to Marion County’s most vulnerable populations. This funding request supports expanded capacity, improved efficiency, and enhanced service delivery — including on-site radiology, lab testing, and care coordination — to meet rising demand and reduce health disparities.
1337.purpose: The funds will help us expand access to care for underserved residents in Marion County by strengthening patient navigation, improving operational capacity, and aligning our data systems with reporting requirements. This support will reduce avoidable ER visits and improve health outcomes through timely, community-based care.
1337.activities: The program will provide patient navigation and care coordination—including outreach, scheduling, and referrals —expand clinical access with additional primary care and behavioral health visits and same-week scheduling, and conduct mobile/community outreach through screening events and home visits. We will deliver targeted care management for high-risk patients with individualized plans and social-needs referrals, implement standardized data collection with quarterly outcomes tracking, and suppo
1337.direct_services: The project will provide direct access to comprehensive primary care services, including preventive care, chronic disease management, acute illness treatment, lab services, and on-site diagnostic X-ray imaging. Patients will be able to receive evaluation, diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up care within the same visit, reducing delays and eliminating the need for external referrals for bas
1337.population: The project serves uninsured, underinsured, and low-income residents of West Ocala and surrounding communities in Marion County, including individuals with chronic health conditions who often experience delays in care due to transportation, financial barriers, and limited provider availability. The service area has documented health disparities and a high rate of preventable emergency room utilization. The center is projected to serve at least 1,800 unique patients in FY 2026, generating more th
1337.outcome: The project will reduce delays in diagnosis and treatment by allowing patients to receive primary care and X-ray imaging in one location, improving continuity of care and reducing preventable emergency room utilization. Outcomes will include increased same-day diagnostic services, improved treatment adherence, and faster follow up care. Progress will be measured through: Monthly patient visit volume, Number of on-site X-rays completed Reduction in off- site referral wait times, Follow-up appointment adherence rates and Reduction in avoidable ER visits among established patients.

1723.description: Pinellas County completed a Preliminary Engineering Study focused on improving capacity, operational efficiency, and transportation safety on East Lake Rd in northern Pinellas County. The County is currently coordinating with FDOT to complete a full PD&E study. The corridor parallels US 19 and is a major arterial roadway that serves as a primary connector between Pinellas and Pasco Counties and as an evacuation route. This request (Phase I) includes capacity improvements between Curlew Rd to Tarpon Woods Blvd; intersection improvements and bridge widening.
1723.purpose: The preliminary engineering study indicates that widening the roadway and bridges and implementing intersection improvements along the corridor will significantly improve the traffic level of service during peak periods (capacity) and reduce the number and severity of crashes.
1723.activities: The county is currently funding the PD&E and the design services for several of the improvements which are all underway. The specific activities are the construction services necessary to implement the structural improvements and the operational elements of the intersections are handled by the county through both equipment and technology.
1723.direct_services: Improved roadway capacity, more efficient transportation services, and intersection improvements that are safer and more effective.
1723.population: Residents of the East Lake area and commuters from Pasco, Hillsborough and Hernando Counties as well as those within Pinellas County.
1723.outcome: Reduced congestion, travel delays and number of crashes. The county utilizes IVA and other traffic technology to monitor and report traffic outcomes. This system will be utilized to compare pre to post project benefits.

1724.description: Through partnerships with local organizations, academic institutions and businesses, CodeBoxx Foundation identifies and supports high-potential, non-traditional students who might not otherwise connect with coding schools and technology training. In addition to building strong foundations in software development, CodeBoxx places a special focus on upskilling the local workforce in technology and in-demand AI skills needed for today's fast-moving economy. State funding will support 12-15 technology boot camps with cohorts of 20-25 participants each who are equipped to hit the ground running and get the job done at a lower price point than university graduates. In addition, the program will provide the support needed to deliver wrap-around services (career training, job placement, and case management) while expanding the program’s scope and reach to include specialized tracks in high-deman
1724.purpose: CodeBoxx will host 12-15 boot camps with cohorts of 20-25 participants each, as well as courses in critical technology sectors including AI and cybersecurity, leading to immediate employment and long-term financial security for 200+ Florida residents. 85% of CodeBoxx graduates who have completed the program have been placed in jobs immediately upon graduation at partner companies such as eBay, Humana, Spontivly Bedrock, iDimension, RevStar, and even CodeBoxx.
1724.activities: CodeBoxx will host technology boot camps, develop AI-focused courses, provide cybersecurity training and other specialized tracks in high-demand fields and early tech and AI training for high school students to build diverse pathways to meaningful employment.
1724.direct_services: 200+ individuals will be equipped to enter the technology workforce supported by essential wrap-around services including career training, job placement, ongoing mentor support and case management, ensuring comprehensive support throughout their training.
1724.population: Agile training programs like CodeBoxx help residents—including youth and underserved populations—adapt quickly to shifting economic conditions. Offering a faster, more affordable alternative to traditional degree paths, CodeBoxx supports underemployed and career-changing adults while advancing Florida’s goal of becoming the nation’s leader in workforce education—producing job-ready technologists who strengthen the state’s innovation economy and resilience to economic change.
1724.outcome: CodeBoxx anticipates that state funding would provide immediate employment leading to long-term financial security for over 200+ Florida residents. This outcome will be measured through employment placement of students. With state support, 300+ students have been served through CodeBoxx programs to date, with 85% of graduates placed in jobs immediately upon graduation at partner companies such as eBay, Humana, Spontivly Bedrock, iDimension, RevStar, and even CodeBoxx itself.

1083.description: The School District of Palm Beach County is dedicated to academic excellence and workforce readiness, especially in the Glades Region. West Technical Education Center (WTEC) is key to this mission, preparing students for post- secondary education and high-demand careers. A $944,841.65 appropriation for FY 2026–2027 will strengthen WTEC’s programs, facilities, and capacity to produce industry-certified, job-ready graduates. This investment will close critical gaps in secondary and adult education, align training with business and industry needs, and position WTEC as a regional hub for high-wage, high-demand career preparation, advancing Florida’s workforce and economic growth goals.
1083.purpose: The School District of Palm Beach County seeks $944,841.65 for FY 2026-27 to expand West Technical Education Center’s role in workforce preparation. Funds will enhance Secondary (Culinary, Automotive/Diesel) and Adult Education (Welding, CDL, Health Science) through equipment, simulators, infrastructure, and $72,500 in scholarships—aligning programs with industry demands for job-ready, certified graduates.
1083.activities: Funds will support career development and workforce training in culinary, automotive/diesel maintenance, welding, health sciences, and commercial vehicle driving, providing citizens with hands-on education and industry certifications for immediate employment and career advancement.
1083.direct_services: Funds will provide citizens with hands-on training, industry certifications, and job placement support in culinary arts, automotive/diesel maintenance, welding, health sciences, and commercial vehicle driving, equipping them with skills for immediate employment and career advancement in high-demand industries.
1083.population: The majority of the funds requested will serve jobless persons, economically disadvantaged individuals, at-risk youth, and homeless populations. Additionally, the program will extend its support to students at both the high school and university or college levels. These target groups have been identified as those most in need of resources and opportunities to improve their economic stability, educational attainment, and overall well-being. It is expected that 200 to 400 individuals will be serve
1083.outcome: 1. Improve Quality of Education Measure: Program completion rate — 60% of students must complete their program. Impact: Meeting or exceeding this benchmark demonstrates effective instruction, student engagement, and curriculum relevance, reflecting overall improvement in educational quality and program success. 2. Increase Economic Activity Measure: Job placement rate — 70% of graduates must secure training-related employment, military service, or continue their education. Impact: Higher placement rates indicate stronger workforce participation, contributing to local employment growth, increased household income, and regional economic development. 3. Enhance Economic Self-Sufficiency Measure

2314.description: Expand and increase residential and non-residential capacity for a prevention centric program that is designed to keep families together to avoid entrance into the foster care system and therefore avoid the trauma of family separation and negative economic impacts to the state. The prevention program, to include community education, utilizes a protective factors approach and trauma informed practices promotes healthy family functioning and economic self sufficiency.
2314.purpose: Expand and increase residential/non-residential capacity for a prevention centric program that is designed to keep families together to avoid entrance into the foster care system & therefore avoid the trauma of family separation and negative economic impacts to the state. The prevention program, to include community education, utilizes a protective factors approach, evidence-based parenting curriculum, & trauma informed practices, promotes healthy family functioning & economic self sufficiency.
2314.activities: Provide direct care services for single moms and their children. Services include secure housing for clients participating in the residential program, evidence-based parenting curriculum, life skills training, job skills training, financial literacy, educational classes, and nutrition as well as community education/outreach services.

2314.population: Persons with poor mental health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, homeless, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, University/college students, and struggling single mothers with children. More than 200 people will be served through both direct care service and community education/outreach services.

Improve quality of education- Plans of Service, Life Skills Training, Vocational Guidance, PFS or other comparable assessment tool. Improve transportation conditions-Individualized Plan of Services goals as established at admission and evaluated on a monthly basis and at completion of the program. 2452.description: The Central Receiving Facility (CRF) will provide integrated crisis stabilization and addiction receiving facility services as defined in 65E-12.110 FAC. The CRF will provide access 24 hours/7 days a week to mental health crisis stabilization and addiction detoxification services that do not exist in Flagler County. The CRF will function as an access point for all SMA services. Individuals will receive assessment and stabilization services regardless of ability to pay. Flagler County government dedicated a $10,000,000 state appropriation to the construction of the CRF and a $1,214,278 land match. SMA provided additional $4,000,000 for construction.
2452.purpose: Flagler County currently has no Baker Act/Marchman Act receiving beds. The goal is to establish a Central Receiving Facility (CRF) in Flagler County that will allow for a comprehensive community Central Receiving System of Care. The CRF will include the core component of an Integrated Stabilization Unit, providing 20 Baker Act/Marchman Act Receiving beds. Flagler County government dedicated a $10,000,000 state appropriation to the construction of the CRF and a $1,214,278 land match. SMA provided
2452.activities: The Central Receiving Facility will provide access 24 hours/7 days a week to crisis stabilization and detoxification services that currently do not exist in Flagler County. In addition, it will function as an access point for all of the other services offered by SMA Healthcare. Individuals will receive assessment and stabilization services regardless of the individual's ability to pay.
2452.direct_services: The Central Receiving Facility will provide integrated crisis stabilization and addiction receiving facility services as defined in 65E-12.110 FAC. This includes, but not limited to, close medical observation, use of medication-assisted treatment, physical exam within 24 hours of admission, a biopsychosocial assessment, emergency medical services as needed, the development of a discharge plan begi
2452.population: The target population includes: Persons with poor mental health, illicit and prescription drug abusers (in health services), persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, individuals experiencing homelessness with a behavioral health disorder, currently or formerly incarcerated persons with a behavioral health disorder, and drug offenders (in Criminal Justice).
2452.outcome: 100% entering ISU will receive a physical health assessment. 100% discharged will be linked with ongoing care. 50% will attend ongoing care within 30 days of discharge. 75% will not be re-admitted within 90 days of successful completion. 70% will successfully complete the program. Data is collected at admission, discharge and throughout the episode of care and recorded in each patient's electronic health record. Reports are subsequently generated from querying the electronic health record database.

3551.description: Funds used for environmental permitting, site development and construction to complete Phase 2 of the Multi- Governmental Complex, a consolidated facility to house 10 county departments and services under one roof. The project addresses deficiencies in current facilities that are over 60 years old and fail to meet modern accessibility, fire code, and environmental safety standards. Once completed, the project will centralize operations, improve efficiency, and reduce costs for taxpayers while allowing the courthouse, state probation, and Public Defender’s Office to expand into existing facilities. This initiative will also provide secure, modern workspaces and improved public access to services for residents in this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3551.purpose: Goal is to complete Phase 2 of the Multi-Governmental Complex, consolidating 10 county departments into a modern facility that replaces buildings more than sixty years old. The project will centralize government operations, improve public access to services, enhance efficiency, and allow the existing BOCC building to be re-purposed for judicial expansion, including the courthouse, state probation, and Public Defender’s Office.
3551.activities: Activities funded will include Phase 2 : site development, environmental permitting, engineering, and construction of the new complex. These services will provide a safe, accessible, and efficient space for county government operations, ensuring compliance with current codes and supporting long-term county growth.
3551.direct_services: Direct services to citizens includes better operations of County services due to consolidation into one complex reducing the need to travel to several outdated buildings. Provides for easier access, efficient and effective services; reduction of operating costs with savings to the citizenry located in this Rural Area of Opportunity. The new facility will improve customer service, reduce wait times
3551.population: Hardee County is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served. The project also benefits the court system users through the re-purposing of existing space for judicial functions.
3551.outcome: The expected outcomes include improved government efficiency, reduced operating costs, better customer service, and expanded judicial capacity. Success will be measured by completion and certification of the facility, documented relocation of county departments into the complex, reduction in operating costs from consolidation, improved accessibility compliance, and increased citizen satisfaction as reported through service surveys and usage statistics.

3552.description: This project will harden and modernize the Hardee County Annex 1 Facility to improve safety, security, accessibility, and operational efficiency for public service operations. Improvements include expanding office space, installing enhanced security systems, addressing ADA compliance, and performing resiliency upgrades to ensure continuity of government operations. The project will allow essential public services to be delivered safely and efficiently to residents of this Rural Area of Opportunity.

This will safeguard personnel, citizens, and visitors while enhancing operational efficiency and providing reliable continuity of public service delivery.

Activities include structural updates, expanding office space, enhancing security features at building entrances, upgrading systems for resiliency, and ensuring the facility complies with ADA and current safety codes that may include new roof, removal of both interior stair cases; design and build
3552.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from a hardened safer, more secure accessible, and modernized facility that provides enhanced public access to government services. Improvements will reduce risks to staff and visitors, ensures essential public services operate effectively, and provide a reliable hub for government operations, improved operational capacity, and public access to essential public services meeti
3552.population: Hardee County, which is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served.
3552.outcome: Expected outcomes include enhanced public safety, improved ADA accessibility, reduced risks from structural vulnerabilities, and more efficient service delivery. Success will be measured through project completion certifications, inspections, ADA compliance verification, testing of security and resiliency systems, and documented operational improvements.

3554.description: Hardee County seeks funding to replace its outdated, 44-year-old library with a new 15,000 sq. ft. centrally located facility. The project will address changing community needs and technology demands by providing modern learning spaces, expanded educational programming, enhanced technology access, and public meeting areas. The new library will ensure accessibility, safety, and quality educational opportunities for residents of this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3554.purpose: The project’s purpose is to construct a safe, modern, and accessible county library that replaces the existing 44-year- old facility. The new 15,000 sq. ft. library will provide adequate space for technology, educational programs, lifelong learning resources, and community services that reflect the county’s growing needs and commitment to education. The facility will host literacy programs, job skills training, cultural activities, and technology access, while providing modern spaces for tutorin
3554.activities: Funding to be used for land acquisition and contractual services for planning, architectural/engineering design, permitting, project management/administration, engineering during construction, construction observation, and construction through the County's procurement policies and procedures.
3554.direct_services: Citizens will directly benefit from access to expanded library programming, improved technology resources, and safe, ADA-compliant facilities. The library will provide access to health and workforce resources, educational opportunities, and community meeting spaces in a centrally located, modern facility. The facility will host literacy programs, job skills training, cultural activities, and techn
3554.population: The project serves the general population of Hardee County and with visitors 25,000 individuals expected to benefit directly from expanded library access. Key groups include economically disadvantaged families, students, elderly persons, and residents without access to broadband or technology at home.
3554.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved quality of education, workforce development, enriched cultural experiences, and enhanced quality of life. Benefits will be measured by library attendance, program participation, technology use, user surveys, increases in checkouts, and utilization of meeting and co-working spaces.

3556.description: Design and construct a new 3,600 sq. ft. metal Facilities Maintenance Warehouse (60'×60') adjacent to Public Works to house locksmith operations, signage production, county-wide equipment storage, essential office space, and workshop areas. The facility will improve efficiency, safety, and organization of county maintenance operations and support timely delivery of public services. The project serves all Hardee County residents and is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO).
3556.purpose: Goal is to design and construct a 3,600 sq. ft. Facilities Maintenance Warehouse (60'x60' metal bldg.) to be located adjacent to Public Works that will house locksmith operations, signage production, county-wide equipment storage, essential office space, and a workshop. 3556.outcome: Safe, organized warehouse facility improves maintenance efficiency. Better service response times and reduced delays. Improves physical and mental health of staff through safe, modern working conditions. Supports transportation and infrastructure upkeep.

3559.description: Hardee Lakes Park is a County-owned park that requires major upgrades to essential utilities, including water, wastewater, and electrical systems, along with modern infrastructure improvements. The purpose is to provide safe, accessible, and sustainable outdoor recreational opportunities while protecting the environment and supporting economic development. Improvements will install new water, wastewater, and electrical utilities, upgrade infrastructure to meet regulatory standards, and reduce pollutants impacting state waters. This investment ensures the park can continue serving the community and visitors while aligning with the State Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP) and Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) objectives
3559.purpose: Goal is to upgrade Hardee Lakes Park with essential utilities of water, wastewater, electrical services and modern infrastructure to properly serve the community and protect the environment. This investment ensures safe, accessible outdoor recreational opportunities at this popular County-owned park while supporting environmental sustainability, economic development and long-term park operations and management in this Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO). Improves the quality of life, health, safety

3559.direct_services: Direct services to citizens is safe, compliant recreational facilities with reliable utilities for residents and visitors, improves water quality, physical health; protects the environment through proper wastewater, water, and electric infrastructure, preventing pollution and preserving natural habitats providing for improved quality of life and health.
3559.population: Hardee County, which is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served.

3560.description: Resilient hardening is needed at four public service complexes — the Civic Center, Sheriff’s Offices, Fleet Services, and Public Works Administration Buildings — that include replacing aging roofs and reinforcing facilities to ensure they remain operational during hurricanes, tornadoes, and other disasters. This investment protects first responders, citizens, essential equipment, and community assets, safeguards public safety, and maintains continuity of essential services and emergency response operations in Hardee County, a designated Rural Area of Opportunity.
3560.purpose: The goal is to harden & modernize four critical public service facilities so they remain safe & operational during hurricanes, tornadoes, & other disasters, protecting staff, citizens, and assets. Includes replacing old roofs/ reinforcing facilities to ensure they remain operational during hurricanes, tornadoes & other disasters. This investment protects 1st responders, citizenry, essential equipment & community assets, safeguards public safety, maintains continuity of critical essential service
3560.activities: To seek contractual services through the County's procurement policies and procedures for planning, design, engineering and architectural services, permitting, bidding, project management and administration, construction observation, engineering during construction, and construction and renovation of four old critical county facilities with hardened roofs and structural improvements.
3560.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens include continuous access to essential emergency services, public safety operations, county functions by ensuring 4 critical facilities remain safe, operational, and resilient during hurricanes, tornadoes and other disasters in this Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO).
3560.population: Hardee County, which is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that is located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served.
3560.outcome: Resilient public service facilities that remain fully operational during hurricanes, tornadoes, and other natural disasters. 2867.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2867.description: This transformative initiative bridges food security, environmental stewardship, and workforce development to uplift at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged communities. By integrating wilderness education, community gardening, nutrition programs, and sustainable job training, it fosters self-sufficiency, enhances physical and mental well-being, and creates tangible economic opportunities. With robust community and legislative support, this project cultivates long term resilience—empowering future generations to thrive.
2867.purpose: The funds will expand access to wilderness education, community gardening, nutrition programs, and workforce training for at-risk youth and economically disadvantaged communities. This initiative promotes food security, environmental stewardship, and overall well-being while creating sustainable jobs in agriculture and related fields. By fostering self-sufficiency and resilience, the project equips participants with essential life skills and helps reduce disparities in health, education, and eco
2867.activities: The funds will support immersive wilderness education, hands-on agricultural training, and expanded community gardens to enhance food security. Participants will gain workforce skills through job training in sustainability, while structured nutrition, cooking, and wellness programs promote long-term health. By integrating education, economic opportunity, and environmental stewardship, this initiative empowers communities to achieve lasting self-sufficiency and resilience.
2867.direct_services: The funds will support immersive wilderness education, hands-on agricultural training, and expanded community gardens to strengthen food security. Participants will gain workforce skills through sustainability-focused job training, while structured nutrition, cooking, and wellness programs promote long-term health. By integrating education, economic opportunity, and environmental stewardship, this
2867.population: The project serves at-risk youth, economically disadvantaged individuals, the unemployed, the homeless, and those facing health challenges. It also supports students and individuals impacted by the justice system. By providing resources, education, job training, and wellness programs, the initiative helps vulnerable populations build self-sufficiency and aims to serve 400–800 participants directly.
2867.outcome: This project will strengthen food security, improve health outcomes, create jobs, and promote environmental stewardship. Success will be measured through increased access to fresh food, participation in wellness programs, job placements in agriculture and sustainability, and environmental impact from garden expansions and community cleanups. Metrics include participant engagement, pre- and post-assessments, employment rates, and sustainability reports.

3682.description: Funds will support critical hardening safety improvements, including a complete remodel, new HVAC system, roof, and windows, to create a safe, healthy, and functional facility for essential public health services. The building also houses the Supervisor of Elections; the project ensures continuity of both health and civic services and is the most cost-effective approach compared with new construction. The current Hardee County Health Department, a 35,010-square-foot facility built in 1997, is uninhabitable due to mold, severe air quality issues, and antiquated structural defects.
3682.purpose: Goal is to harden and remodel the Health Department/Supervisor of Elections building to correct severe air quality and structural deficiencies and modernize systems, ensuring safe, compliant, and reliable delivery of essential public health and civic services to this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3682.activities: To seek contractual services through the County's procurement policies and procedures for engineering and architectural design, permitting, bidding, project management/administration, construction observation, engineering during construction, and construction.
3682.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens include safe, functional Health Department for public health services in a secure, ADA-compliant Supervisor of Elections facility, maintaining continuity of essential services for residents in this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3682.population: Hardee County which is a financially disadvantaged community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) located in a Rural Area of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes), citizenry, visitors, tourists, business community and surrounding areas. Greater than 27,000 expected to be served.
3682.outcome: Expected benefit is improved physical and mental health outcomes for employees and visitors via healthier indoor environment; continuity of essential services; protection of the general public from harm. Measured by employee/citizen feedback, attendance and health records, facility occupancy, continuity of operations, and maintenance reports.

1458.description: This request is for construction of a new building on TSC main campus to provide academic space for expansion of the College's dental hygiene program and the creation of a new culinary and hospitality program. This will provide advanced academic programming and high-tech simulation labs for the dental hygienist and dental assistant programs and will allow TSC to increase enrollment to meet local demand. It will also provide for the creation of a commercial kitchen and applied learning laboratories for a new culinary program. Both programs have a 7% job growth rate.
1458.purpose: This 24,000 sf building will house the TSC Dental Hygiene Program and new Culinary Program. Our region is designated as a Dental Health Professional Shortage Area. The dental programs will greatly improve access to care and both programs will strengthen the economic vitality of our community. Dental hygiene and dental assisting are all high-wage (average $67,946 dental) and high demand (7% growth) jobs.
1458.activities: These funds will be used to construct a new 24,000 sf building on the TSC main campus, for expansion of the dental hygiene program and a new culinary arts program.
1458.direct_services: These programs will provide educational opportunity to citizens in the region and will make high-wage and high- demand jobs available to them. It will produce qualified individuals to fulfill a great need in the community. According to a study by the Health Resources and Services Administration, Florida ranks at the bottom in percentage of children receiving dental care and 25% of third-graders ha
1458.population: Creation of the new TSC Applied Learning Center for Health & Hospitality will serve individuals looking for stable careers with potential for high wages (average $67,946 dental and $60,990 culinary). It will also serve the dental community and hospitality industry by providing qualified employees - both have a 7% growth rate and cannot fill vacancies. It will also serve the greater community by filling this void and by providing services to low income individuals and families at the on campus de
1458.outcome: Provide dental care to low income and limited access individuals - Report on the number served through the clinic. Improve economic opportunity for hundreds of students by providing workforce training and quick employment - Track the number of students enrolled in the program, graduates and employment data. The commercial kitchen applied learning laboratory will be available to provide high quality services to cultural events in the community at low cost - Track all services provided for College and community events.

1067.description: In the FY 25-26 GAA, $900,000 was appropriated (SA 2251B) to construct the first hardened fire station in the Town of Southwest Ranches (Town). However, due to inflation, the construction costs have risen significantly. The total project cost was anticipated to be $7.5 Million but is now $9.5 Million. Therefore, the Town is requesting an additional $900,000 from the State to complete this critical project. Funds will be used for design, engineering, site-work, and construction of a new fire station for the Town, which will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding and improving the fire and EMS service to the community with the goal of saving lives and property.
1067.purpose: Funds will be used for design, engineering, site-work, and construction of a new fire station for the Town, which will replace the Town's only fire station - a modular trailer. Currently, during storms the Town’s fire personnel must evacuate the modular trailer station and relocate to an adjacent city’s fire station, which is 3.5 miles away and does not have the capacity to accommodate the Town’s five firefighters on shift. This project will result in shorter response times, greatly expanding an
1067.activities: Southwest Ranches has no hardened facilities to provide emergency fire and EMS services that are rated to withstand the impact and effects of a major hurricane or flooding. The fire station will enhance safety of all citizens and visitors of Southwest Ranches. The station will provide immediate access to emergency services for the population across the thirteen square miles and benefit our mutual aid partners.
1067.direct_services: The services provided will include fire and medical services in the form of emergency response. Additional services provided will include fire prevention education, community risk reduction, emergency management, and training opportunities for firefighters to better serve the citizens.
1067.population: This project will benefit all Town of Southwest Ranches residents, visitors and businesses. It will also benefit motorists traveling along US 27 and Interstate 75 who need emergency services. This department provides mutual aid to the surrounding communities as well.
1067.outcome: The benefit will be faster response to fires, disasters, and citizens in need of life-saving medical treatment. This will be measured by improved response times to the area. Emergency response times are recorded and will be used as part of the methodology to measure success.

1688.description: Our Sacred Academy serves children and young adults with the most profound developmental and behavioral challenges. Most students have been turned away from other schools or therapeutic programs. The Behavioral Challenges Therapeutic Inclusion Program – A Last Chance for Success establishes a structured therapeutic inclusion model providing behavioral stabilization, life skills development, and compassionate exposure to community and vocational settings.
1688.purpose: Our Sacred Academy serves children and young adults with the most profound developmental and behavioral challenges. Most students have been turned away from other schools or therapeutic programs. The Behavioral Challenges Therapeutic Inclusion Program – A Last Chance for Success establishes a structured therapeutic inclusion model providing behavioral stabilization, life skills development, and compassionate exposure to community and vocational settings.
1688.activities: The program integrates applied behavior analysis (ABA), sensory integration therapy, and adaptive life skills instruction for nonverbal and self-injurious students. It represents a final opportunity for meaningful growth, communication, and inclusion for children otherwise at risk of institutionalization.
1688.direct_services: The program will reduce behavioral crises and self-injurious behaviors through structured therapeutic intervention. Increase functional communication and independent life skills among participants. Provide inclusive community experiences to improve socialization and confidence. Demonstrate a replicable model for serving Florida’s most behaviorally challenged students.
1688.population: Persons with Autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, AHDH, medical needs, severe behavior challenges Persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, at risk youth, developmentally disabled, grade school students, middle/high school students. Amount to be served: 51-100
1688.outcome: Staff will use goal-tracking checklists updated daily during instruction and community outings. Regular health assessments and caregiver feedback will document improvements. Behavior Support Staff will track incidents using behavior data logs and intervention progress notes. Standardized mental health screening tools (e.g., Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire) administered quarterly.

1084.description: The Utilities Department seeks funding to implement a comprehensive Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Cybersecurity Improvement Plan to safeguard the City’s water and wastewater operations. This project will replace and upgrade outdated SCADA software, network equipment, and security mechanisms that are currently beyond their useful life and no longer supported with essential firmware or security patches. The initiative will establish modern IT security protections, policies, and procedures to ensure the ongoing resilience of critical infrastructure. By enhancing cybersecurity and system reliability, this project will reduce the risk of service disruptions, protect against cyber threats, and ensure compliance with state and federal standards for utility operations. These improvements will directly benefit residents and businesses by securing the safe and continuous deliver
1084.purpose: The requested funds will enhance the City of Miramar’s Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to improve cybersecurity, system reliability, and operational efficiency across the city’s water and wastewater infrastructure. The project will protect critical infrastructure against cyber threats and ensure uninterrupted, safe water service delivery to residents.
1084.activities: Funds will be used to upgrade and harden existing SCADA network components, replace outdated programmable logic controllers (PLCs), install secure firewalls and intrusion detection systems, and integrate continuous monitoring tools. Additionally, cybersecurity training will be provided to City staff to improve incident response and compliance with state and federal water security standards.
1084.direct_services: The project will provide residents and businesses with reliable, secure, and continuous access to clean drinking water and effective wastewater services. By safeguarding operational systems from cyberattacks or failures, the project ensures public health protection and consistent utility performance for all Miramar water customers.
1084.population: The target population includes all City of Miramar residents, businesses, and institutions connected to the municipal water and wastewater system—approximately 140,000 individuals. The project also benefits regional partners through improved resilience in the broader South Broward utility network.
1084.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved system security, reduced risk of cyber intrusion, enhanced system uptime, and regulatory compliance with water security mandates. Performance will be measured by incident response times, reduction in system vulnerabilities identified through periodic cybersecurity audits, and uninterrupted service reliability metrics tracked through the City’s SCADA system.

1122.description: This project would provide for the construction of an air pavilion to cover the basketball courts at Oveta McKeithen Park and keep the elements from impacting residents. The air pavilion would be open-sided, so it would still provide for users to experience fresh outdoor air but would not experience the heat of the sun and the hazards of the rain. The air pavilion would be raised high enough to allow for both competitive and recreational basketball play. In an event of a COVID-19 outbreak this area would be suitable for outdoor meetings as well.
1122.purpose: The request of funds would allow the City to accommodate more youth and adults in the City through City sponsored basketball program year-round. This proposed air pavilion project would provide a covered space over 2 additional basketball courts by providing a common space for sports and recreation. Placing an air pavilion over the courts would foster a sense of community; becoming a gathering spot where residents can meet, socialize, and build lasting friendships, enhancing social cohesion.
1122.activities: An air Pavilion would allow for additional programs year-round such as youth basketball, adult basketball, volleyball, and pick ball.
1122.direct_services: Direct services include access to a centrally located park for residents of all ages to share a common space for sports and recreation year-round despite the weather conditions in south Florida.
1122.population: The proposed air pavilion would be installed in an underserved low-to-moderate area in the City adjacent to the Stanely Terrace Apartment Complex a large HUD funded affordable housing complex. As a result of Oveta McKiethen Park being centrally located, the park will be utilized by all 87,000 residents of the City.
1122.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of the air pavilion at Oveta McKeithen Park would provide a covered space over 2 additional basketball courts by providing a common space for sports and recreation. Placing an air pavilion over the courts would foster a sense of community; becoming a gathering spot where residents can meet, socialize, and build lasting friendships, enhancing social cohesion. Parks and Recreation would complete community surveys to gage the community usage of the facility as well as staff would create additional programming, removing current wait list for recreational programs.

Over past 15 years a significant number of survivors have moved to Central Florida. Our program provides for the health and well being of this elderly and disadvantaged population.
1089.purpose: Providing care-support to Holocaust survivors living in Jewish Family Services of Greater Orlando service area. Funding will go directly to services due to the systems currently operating

1140.description: The project includes construction of drainage wells, installation of a new stormwater pump station with backup power, and full system connectivity to improve flood resilience and stormwater management. It addresses chronic drainage deficiencies in one of Key Biscayne’s most densely populated neighborhoods, home to 5,000 residents across 1,500 housing units. Recurring flooding during heavy rainfall and tidal events poses significant risks to public safety, property, and infrastructure. These improvements are essential to protecting public safety, infrastructure, and property values in a vulnerable coastal community. Without funding, the Garden District will continue to suffer from disruptive and hazardous flooding, damaging homes, vehicles, and infrastructure. Failure to secure the required matching funding will also jeopardize eligibility for millions in federal HMGP resources. The Villa
1140.purpose: The requested funds will be used to improve flood resilience and stormwater management in Key Biscayne’s Garden District, one of the Village’s most densely populated and flood-prone neighborhoods. The goal is to eliminate recurring flooding that threatens residents, damages homes and infrastructure, and disrupts emergency access during heavy rainfall and tidal events.
1140.activities: The Village will design, permit, and construct new drainage wells and a modern stormwater pump station equipped with backup power. These upgrades will be fully integrated into the existing stormwater network to enhance drainage capacity and reliability. The project also includes environmental compliance, performance testing, and ongoing monitoring to ensure the system meets design and safety standards.
1140.direct_services: Residents will directly benefit from significant reductions in flooding, safer roadways during storms, and protection of homes, vehicles, and public spaces. The improvements will also ensure that emergency vehicles and essential services can safely operate during heavy rainfall or tidal events, improving overall public safety and quality of life.
1140.population: The project serves approximately 5,000 residents living in 1,500 housing units within the Garden District. This neighborhood is one of the most densely populated areas of Key Biscayne and among the most vulnerable to flooding. The entire Village population will also indirectly benefit from reduced emergency response costs and infrastructure damage.
1140.outcome: The project is expected to reduce flooding during major storm and tidal conditions. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-construction flood event data and on-site water level monitoring. Additional performance indicators include a decrease in flood-related emergency calls, property damage reports, and resident feedback collected after completion.

1217.description: The funds being requested will replace the existing roof infrastructure at the Center for Excellence in Early Education's (CFE) Demonstration School and the Children’s Advocacy Building which houses instrumental community-based organizations. This complex is critical to maintaining continuing children and family services throughout the county and continuing early learning research throughout the State of Florida.
1217.purpose: Funding for the Children’s Complex roofing will ensure the continuity of service of the Center for Excellence in Early Education's Demonstration School, 21 Early Head Start sites, academic research and the Children's Trust operations.
1217.activities: Two roofs will be removed and replaced with tapered insulation roofing systems, totaling 33,638 sq ft with a life expectancy of 20-25 years . Services will include all labor, materials, equipment, insurance, permits and engineering required.
1217.direct_services: No direct services will be provided to citizens.
1217.population: Nearly half a million Miami-Dade households are either in or one emergency away from falling into poverty. United Way Miami supports Asset Limited Income Constrained Employed families through an extensive range of programs addressing immediate needs and providing resources for long-term financial resilience. We invest in nearly 100 community programs and support 17 additional initiatives and direct services, all centered around the proven pillars of success: health & wellbeing, education and eco
1217.outcome: In the unprecedented heavy rain periods in south Florida in 2023 and 2024, various leakages have taken place, affecting operations. The Miami-Dade County Head Start program has provided written warnings on the state of the roof for the CFE. Since our early education work began, we have served over 36,000 children and provided over 34,000 early care professionals with professional learning opportunities . With new roofs, we will continue to educate and prepare our future workforce and provide opportunities to alleviate the teacher shortage in Florida.

1142.description: Zoo Miami, in conjunction with FWC, proposes to build an on-site manatee rescue, rehabilitation, and release critical care center. Currently, there are only four manatee critical care centers in the United States, with the closes one being in Orlando. For injured or sick manatees, this means they must be transported over several hours before receiving appropriate medical care. At the request of the State of Florida and FWC, the funds would support the planning, designed, and construction of the manatee critical care facility, This is the first phase of a multi-year project culminating in a $15 million+ state-of-the-art facility dedication to saving Florida's manatees. Funding of this first phase will allow Zoo Miami and FWC to more quickly open the critical care facility and start rescuing, rehabilitating, and releasing manatees.
1142.purpose: At the request of the State of Florida and FWC, the funds will support the planning, design, and construction of the manatee critical care facility. This is the first phase of a multi-year project culminating in a $15 million+ state-of-the-art facility dedicated to saving Florida's manatees. Funding of this first phase will allow Zoo Miami and FWC to more quickly open the critical care facility and start rescuing, rehabilitating, and releasing manatees.
1142.activities: Upon completion, Zoo Miami will have the capability to transport, house, care for, and release sick and injured manatees. Medical services include capabilities to perform advanced medical examinations, necessary surgical procedures, and individualized dietary plans to treat manatees affected by boat strikes, fishing entanglements, disease, and other maladies. Zoo Miami will be one of only five acute care facilities in the country.
1142.direct_services: Florida manatees are considered a keystone species, instrumental in maintaining the ecosystem of our bays and beaches. Preserving these areas for the public to enjoy is critical to South Florida's perception and tourism. On-site, citizens will get to see and learn about manatees, the dangers they face, and things they can do to help save the species.
1142.population: General public in the South Florida region Zoo Miami guests, numbering approximately 1 million per year
1142.outcome: Rescue, rehabilitation, and release of numerous manatees in South Florida. The methodology for measuring outcomes will include manatee intake records, number of successful releases, and recorded contacts with FWC and other organizations. Zoo Miami is accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums, who will provide regular inspection as part of their accreditation process.

1070.outcome: Infrastructure improvements, including utility access within Blanche Ely Estates, will create safer, affordable housing for low-income and senior residents. The project will create short-term construction and infrastructure-related jobs, as well as long-term property management and maintenance. Blanche Ely Estates will contribute to long-term neighborhood revitalization and community pride by replacing blighted areas with high-quality, affordable housing. The methodology in which we will measure the outcome will be through r

1197.description: This project will facilitate enhancing stormwater outfalls draining in College Road, N Stock Island. Additionally, this project will help manage area mangrove overgrowth that are impeding water flow and water quality.
1197.purpose: The primary purpose of this project is to mitigate ponding on the roadway which provides for a clear path of travel for several critical and primary uses and buildings, including Lower Keys Medical Center (Hospital), Monroe Co Sheriffs Department, the College of the Florida Keys, and the Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority.
1197.activities: Funds will be allocated to an awarded contractor to perform construction and mitigation within the City of Key West and College Rd.

All residents living on the North side of Stock Island will have the greatest level of service along with the area commercial uses in the area.
1197.outcome: The expected benefit will be improved drainage for developed areas, that depend on the proper flow of tidal and stormwater through the outfalls and associated lines. A simple methodology is the timing of outgoing tides that will actually fall and not remain at elevated levels due to impacted drain lines and outfalls.

2446.description: Flagler County is seeking funding to improve CR 304, a key asphalt-paved roadway that serves as a vital connector and evacuation route. CR 304 links US-1 to SR 11, and through CR 305, it provides access to US-17 and SR 100. The resurfacing of CR 304, improvement of three outdated bridges, and replacement one box culvert will increase resiliency and emergency response for the safety, mobility and economic competitiveness as well as quality of life for the businesses and residents driving along this roadway.
2446.purpose: Flagler County is seeking funding to improve CR 304, a key asphalt-paved roadway that serves as a vital connector and evacuation route. CR 304 links US-1 to SR 11, and through CR 305, it provides access to US-17 and SR 100. 2446.activities: Flagler County will utilize the funds to complete segment 1 of CR 304 including roadway resurfacing and a box culvert replacement; and then utilize the remainder of funding to complete segment 2 including resurfacing a 7.75 mile portion and improvements to three bridges. 2446.direct_services: This is a shovel ready project that is divided into two segments. Facility improvements include pavement resurfacing, sign & pavement marking, and drainage. CR 304 includes three bridges/one box culvert all in need of replacement or improvements to expand their lifespan for another 20 years. This corridor serves as an evacuation route that is vital for emergency response, and economic commerce.
2446.population: CR 304 connects US-1 to SR 11 and then connects US-1 to SR 100 and US-17 through CR 305. As such CR 304 is a major connector to many evacuation routes and will see increased traffic volumes with projected population growth in the future. We expect that the target population is not only Flagler County residents (130K) but also our surrounding communities including Volusia, Putnam and St. Johns Counties.
2446.outcome: CR 304 is a major connector to many evacuation routes and the resurfacing of the roadway and improvements to three bridges with replacement of a box culvert will improve traffic conditions, prevent flooding ,improve stormwater management by reducing discharge and businesses will be able to carry on without interruptions. The measures used include number of residents indicating they were not hampered during evacuation due to flooding of the roadway, businesses indicate an increase in activity and high quality drinking water is extracted from in-county sources.

2455.purpose: The funds requested will be used to replace and extend aging water mains, improving the City’s water distribution system. Residents and businesses will benefit from increased water reliability for daily needs, improved fir

2457.description: Funds will support design, permitting, bidding, construction, and construction administration for process control and monitoring upgrades at the City’s wastewater treatment facility. These improvements will provide real-time monitoring of system conditions to optimize treatment efficiency and effluent quality, supporting corrective actions under FDEP Consent Order OGC No. 25-1664 and advancing nutrient-reduction goals within the Lower St. Johns River Main Stem BMAP and Crescent Lake.
2457.purpose: The project will improve treatment efficiency, reliability, and compliance at the City’s Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) through process control and monitoring system upgrades. 2457.direct_services: The project will protect public health and the environment by ensuring high-quality wastewater treatment and reliable facility operation. 2457.outcome: The project will improve treatment efficiency. Success will be measured through improved effluent quality.
