2042.organization: University of Miami, Miller School of Medicine
2042.description: The Florida Stroke Registry (FSR), mandated by state law, is dedicated to driving an effective statewide stroke system of care. Our efforts involve: 1) measuring, tracking, benchmarking and reporting the quality of stroke care; 2) conducting interdisciplinary collaboration towards the development of interventions advancing stroke care for all; and 3) incorporating patient-centric outcomes to create meaningful education and community awareness for stroke prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation.
2042.purpose: Building on past 9 years of state funding, FSR aims to maintain Florida’s preeminent national position in quality stroke care by measuring and tracking care metrics; advancing the quality of stroke care to improve Floridians quality of life; ensuring secure data interoperability across multiple phases of care; implementing evidence-based community stroke education to improve stroke outcomes; increasing FSR’s interdisciplinary networks to enhance collaboration and develop meaningful interventions
2042.activities: Evidence-based results to improve the quality of stroke care for all Floridians by: 1) Ensuring standardized, secured, submission and collection of stroke data across 190 hospitals; 2) Producing data driven reports to track, measure, and benchmark stroke performance and outcomes; 3) Driving a complete system of stroke care; 4) Expanding stroke education reach though on-line content dissemination; and 5) Strengthening the registry’s stroke “victor” advisory committee to guide and provide feedback
2042.direct_services: The FSR serves Floridians by monitoring hospital quality of stroke care. FSR reports created for hospitals and EMS track, benchmark, and provide a roadmap to improve care which directly impacts Floridians. Moreover, community health literacy such as stroke recognition and the urgency of rapid transport to a hospital is provided through FSR- derived community education, publicly available resources
2042.population: Direct collaboration will occur with 190 participating Florida hospitals (95% of FL stroke centers), statewide EMS Directors, paramedics, and EMS agencies to strengthen collaboration and enhance systems of stroke care. Our stakeholders have increased (600+) and expanded to include various health professionals (clinicians, pharmacists, paramedics, stroke coordinators, community health care workers, mobile integrated health professionals). Our collaborative focus population are Floridians at risk
2042.outcome: FSR evidence-based efforts impacts hospital stroke performance improvements, increasing the numbers of stroke patients receiving life-saving treatments and improving stroke outcomes. By translating data into action, the FSR drives an effective system of stroke care. Through multi-agency/disciplinary collaboration, the FSR’s longitudinal tracking and measuring of stroke data linked across the pre and/or post hospital phase of care not only informs interventions, guidelines, and policy, but also directly improves the quality of life of all Floridians.

2524.description: The City of St. Augustine (City) seeks funds for continued design and construction (Phase II) of a new, resilient structure on A1A to serve as a Community Point of Distribution of resources during a natural disaster for City residents living on Anastasia Island, a meeting space and a replacement fire station to serve Anastasia Island and Downtown. This will allow for mobility improvements to the intersection of the existing fire station located at A1A and Red Cox Road for improved traffic and pedestrian safety.
2524.purpose: Improved public safety with addition of a community point of distribution, replacement of a fire station and improved traffic safety at location of current station.
2524.activities: Construction will provide improved service to both City and County residents after natural disasters and during emergency response times. The relocation of the fire station and addition of a community point of distribution onto the City-owned parcel on A1A will allow for construction by FDOT of an improved intersection at A1A and Red Cox Road for improved traffic and pedestrian safety.
2524.direct_services: Direct services for City and County residents include improved intersection safety at A1A and Red Cox Road, the addition of a community point of distribution following natural disasters, and a modernized fire station.
2524.population: All residents, businesses and visitors in the surrounding area will benefit from the community distribution point following a natural disaster.All residents, businesses and visitiors moving through this area will benefit from the safety improvements at A1A and Red Cox Road. All residents, businesses and visitors will benefit from a resilient, modernized fire station.
2524.outcome: The expected benefits include allowing emergency personnel to remain stationed at this location to serve the City and County residents of Anastasia Island during a weather event as well as a reduction in traffic related accidents in the area.

2529.description: Roughly 20 veterans die by suicide every day, and K9s For Warriors is committed to change that. Determined to end veteran suicide, K9s For Warriors provides highly-trained service dogs to military veterans suffering from PTSD, traumatic brain injury and/or military sexual trauma. With the majority of our dogs coming from high-kill rescue shelters, our innovative program allows the Warrior/K9 team to build an unwavering bond that facilitates their collective healing and recovery. During the 3-week training process, veterans learn and practice skills that allow them to regain their independence. The program goes further than handing over a leash and sending veterans on their way — K9s For Warriors’ staff provides resources to veterans long before they walk through the doors, and the relationships formed during their stay remain long after they return home. For more information, visit www.k
2529.purpose: K9s For Warriors is committed to ending veteran suicide and returning veterans to a life of dignity and independence. This funding will cover construction costs necessary increase the number of veterans receiving a service dog, direct peer support, suicide intervention, crisis intervention, and family/spousal support.
2529.activities: K9s For Warriors provides a trained service dog, lifelong peer-to-peer support, suicide intervention, crisis intervention, family and spousal support, and assistance with any other issues that a veteran may need assistance with to maintain stability in their life. K9s also provides training and support focused on the unique needs of family members serving as caregivers for our veterans.
2529.direct_services: K9s For Warriors trains and pairs veterans with an ADA protected service dog and provides direct peer support, suicide intervention, crisis intervention, and family/spousal support. Additionally, K9s provides provides training and support focused on the unique needs of spouses, children, and other family members serving as caregivers for our veterans.
2529.population: Veterans of all eras diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, and/or MST and their caregivers. Over 200 are expected to be served.
2529.outcome: Higher morning Cortisol output, indicative of healthier stress levels; reduced PTSD symptoms; better physiological well-being. Standardized PTSD assessments such as the PCL-5 will be used.

2566.description: This project will restore a blighted, county-owned facility into the Veteran Futures Academy — a workforce and civic hub led by a veteran-founded nonprofit. The center will offer construction training, skills workshops, and public programs for veterans, youth, and working families. Backed by over $225,000 in private and in-kind support, this initiative transforms an underused asset into a lasting resource for job readiness, community engagement, and historic preservation — all with minimal cost to the state.
2566.purpose: The project will fully rehabilitate a blighted, county-owned facility into the Veteran Futures Academy — a center dedicated to helping military members separating in Florida transition successfully into civilian life through job training, placement support, and civic engagement. The facility will also serve as a resource for local residents, strengthening the community while honoring the service of those who defended it.
2566.activities: Funds will be used for capital improvements, including roofing, HVAC, insulation, and site work needed to restore the building for public use. Once operational, the center will host construction training for veterans and youth, home maintenance and tool-use workshops, community meetings, and public education events.
2566.direct_services: Construction and skilled trades training for separating military members and at-risk youth. Career preparation and job placement support through partnerships with local employers and trade associations. Public workshops on home maintenance, tool use, and financial literacy. Community access to renovated public space for meetings, workshops, and civic engagement. Optional use as an emergency respon
2566.population: The primary target population is military members separating in Florida, with a focus on those transitioning into the civilian workforce. The program also serves veterans, at-risk youth, and working-class families by providing access to job training, community programs, and public workshops. The facility is designed to be inclusive and multi-functional, serving an estimated 300 to 500 individuals annually through training programs, community events, and civic uses.
2566.outcome: The project will improve veteran workforce outcomes, revitalize a blighted public asset, and expand access to civic programs. Success will be measured by training enrollment, job placement, event participation, and completion of key construction milestones (CO, ADA compliance, etc.).

1229.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1229.description: The Beginning Farmer and 4-H Youth Agriculture Education Complex would create a demonstration and incubator farm for aspiring farmers and ranchers, as well as for 4-H youth to implement agriculture and horticultural projects. This is a vital step in supporting the agriculture industry, contributing to the local economy and food system, and helping youth obtain valuable experience and education relevant to career paths including farmer, veterinarian, or entrepreneur.
1229.purpose: Sarasota County has acquired a property with existing barns, animal pens, and pastures that with renovations could serve as a demonstration and incubator farm and ranch and location for 4-H youth to house their agriculture- and horticulture-related projects. This hands-on learning environment will support both adults and youth and grow the agricultural economy.
1229.activities: This project will help the agriculture industry and youth overcome challenges including access to land, educational needs, market access, and workforce development. The Livestock Incubator will provide a space and training for aspiring ranchers to practice and learn before they take the step of purchasing property of their own. The 4-H Youth will be able to learn in an intergenerational environment and house their projects for hands-on learning and career development.
1229.direct_services: Beginning farmers could farm small plots for produce and test meat and egg business plans in a low-risk environment. They would receive training and support for market development and coordination for contribution of products to families facing food insecurity. The project would also provide locations for 4-H youth projects and educational programming for the general public on food systems.
1229.population: Beginning farmers and ranchers, youth in 4-H programs, veterans, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, K-12 students, general public.
1229.outcome: The project will have benefits for aspiring farmers and ranchers in supporting their business development goals, growing the local economy and providing workforce training. That will also support preservation of agricultural heritage, environmental protections through application of farming best practices, and increased resilience of the local food system. The youth programs will support leadership development, career exploration, hands-on learning, and active, healthy living. Outcomes will be measured through comprehensive evaluation surveys, observations, data tracking of number served, knowledge gained, and behavior changed, as well as jobs and business enterprises created.

1093.description: The Research University Alzheimer’s Research Using Exablate Neuro Focused Ultrasound program advances Florida’s capabilities to address neurological and neurodegenerative diseases through applied R&D and clinical translation. Building on prior investments in HIFU and LIFU systems installed across Florida’s hospitals and research institutions, the program supports continued technology development, system optimization, and statewide clinical trial readiness. Funds intend to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic applications for Alzheimer’s, brain cancer, addiction, PTSD, Parkinson’s, OCD and other neuro disorders. This initiative strengthens Florida’s leadership in noninvasive neurotechnology, expands patient access to innovative treatments, and fosters public-private collaboration to accelerate deployment of next- generation brain health solutions.
1093.purpose: The Research University Alzheimer’s Research Using Exablate Neuro Focused Ultrasound program advances Florida’s leadership in next-generation high- and low-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU/LIFU) R&D and clinical trial deployment. Building on prior state investments that established HIFU/LIFU systems across Florida’s academic and hospital networks, the program supports continued system innovation, proof-of-concept studies, and translational readiness for neurological and neurodegenerative disea
1093.activities: Funds will be expended on activities that advance Exablate Neuro focused ultrasound R&D and statewide and, international clinical capabilities. Deliverables include system and software enhancements, proof-of-concept studies, pilot data generation, and preparation for multicenter clinical trials targeting neurological and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s, brain cancer, addiction, PTSD, and Parkinson’s. Activities may strengthen Florida’s hospital and research infrastructure, improv
1093.direct_services: Direct services supported by this appropriation will expand access for Florida patients to advanced, noninvasive focused ultrasound trial diagnostics and trial treatments for neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, including potentially Alzheimer’s, brain cancer, addiction, PTSD, OCD, Stroke and Parkinson’s. Funds will facilitate applied R&D, clinical trial implementation, and technology enh
1093.population: The target population includes elderly individuals and patients affected by neurological, neurodegenerative, and related brain or behavioral health disorders, including Alzheimer’s, brain cancer, Parkinson’s, PTSD, addiction, OCD, and stroke. The program also serves economically disadvantaged and underserved populations who may not otherwise have access to advanced noninvasive treatment options. Through Florida’s hospital and university trial networks, the initiative is expected to directly serv
1093.outcome: The expected outcome is the continued advancement and validation of noninvasive Exablate Neuro focused ultrasound technologies that may expand Florida’s capacity to diagnose and treat neurological and neurodegenerative disorders in trials. Applied R&D and clinical implementation are anticipated to broaden advanced therapeutic trial opportunities enhance patient access to advanced trials, and strengthen Florida’s leadership in next-generation neurotechnology. Measurable outcomes will derive from R&D milestones, and program progress reports. This framework provides a flexible, evidence-based approach to evaluating scientific, clinical, and economic impact statewide.

1465.description: The Aucilla Research Institute (ARI) will continue to provide historical, archaeological, and scientific education programs, exhibits and opportunities to a region of Florida which is traditionally under-served for such programs. In addition, ARI will expand both the number and types of programs available and continue to improve programs previously created through expansion of on-line resources and continued receipt of student and educator feedback.
1465.purpose: The specific purpose and goal of the funding requested is to provide educational programs and resources in support of multiple student populations (public, private, and home schoolers) for the areas of the Big Bend and northern Florida which are traditionally under-served.
1465.activities: The activities and services provided will include classroom and field programs for students and educators within the area served; video classes and instructional resources which can be used by educators and students; training for educators to allow such programs and resources to be provided by each district and school for their students; and improvement based on feedback and assessment results.
1465.direct_services: Direct services provided will include classes, both within classrooms and in the field, provided by ARI, creation of educational resources as requested by educators, administrators and others based on existing needs provided by educators and administrators; and hands-on training of educators in the programs created so they can be used throughout the area served in the future.
1465.population: Pre, grade and high school students as well as home school students and at risk students, underserved and low- income communities who have little or no access to such programming. The target area includes Madison, Taylor, Dixie, Hamilton, Suwannee, Leon, Wakulla, Jackson, Franklin and Jefferson Counties. The total student population in these areas is 75,994.
1465.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is the providing of educational opportunities and resources throughout the area served that are normally not available for students in the region, including particularly under-served communities and districts, and the engagement of students in the learning process through “hands-on” learning. The methodology for the measurement of these projected outcomes includes both direct measurement of improved student learning through test scores and through feedback from both students and educators.

1094.description: This project seeks funding for the construction and equipping of two state-of-the-art surgical technology laboratories and a comprehensive nursing simulation center. These facilities will serve as critical infrastructure to expand healthcare workforce training capacity in Florida, addressing the growing demand for skilled surgical technologists and registered nurses.
1094.purpose: The goal of the funds are to address the needs of two High Demand, High Skill, High Wage occupations identified by CareerSource Central Florida, CareerSource Tampa Bay, CareerSource South Florida. The project will fund the construction and equipping of two state-of-the-art surgical technology laboratories and a comprehensive nursing simulation center. These facilities will serve as critical infrastructure to expand healthcare workforce training capacity in Florida.
1094.activities: A surgical technology program will be added to the Tampa and Orlando (Winter Park) locations of Herzing University. Additionally, an additional nursing simulation lab will be located outside of Central Florida to support training for hybrid nursing options currently available at the university.
1094.direct_services: Students in both the surgical technology programs and nursing program will have direct patient interaction when completing clinical rotations required in their program of study.
1094.population: Jobless persons, University / College Students, General public that utilize healthcare services in Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Lake, Hillsborough and Miami-Dade Counties. Students served should be 100 - 150 / year; General Public served will be > 1000.
1094.outcome: The project is expected to help address the workforce demand for surgical technology and registered nurses which is currently projected. Each surgical technology program is expected to produce 10 - 15 graduate per year three years after the first cohort starts the program and the nursing simulation lab will support the graduation of an additional 30 nursing students per year 4 years after enrollment of the first cohort utilizing the space. Graduation rate will be determine by number of students who successfully complete the program in a given year.

2448.description: The City's Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) discharges its treated effluent into the Matanzas River. Under the 2021 provisions of Sec. 403.064 (17) FS, such discharge will no longer be permitted: by Dec 31, 2031, the City will be required to re-use the effluent. Due to its high salinity content, the current effluent would not be compliant with the re-use (reclaim) standards identified in Chap 62-600 FAC. The City seeks complementary funding to acquire and install a reverse osmosis package system that will reduce the salinity to compliant levels.
2448.purpose: Compliance with State regulations related to the use of reclaimed water (re-use) as defined in Chap 62-600 FAC and as required under the provisions (2021) of Sec. 403.064 (17) FS.
2448.activities: The City will acquire a reverse osmosis treatment package system which will be incorporated into the operations of the City's Wastewater Treatment Plant, allowing for the reclamation and re-use of treated effluent.
2448.direct_services: By satisfying the State requirements for reclaimed water, citizens will have access to reclaimed water for non-potable purposes: for example, irrigation, decorative water features, and wetland rehabilitation.
2448.population: The primary target population is the residents of Flagler Beach (population approximately 5,500, which is part of both Flagler and Volusia Counties), but the greater benefit is to the residents of Florida given the adoption of the re-use standards by the Florida Legislature as a desired benefit to everyone throughout the State.
2448.outcome: The effluent, with the integration of the reverse osmosis system, will be compliant with State regulatory standards for reclaimed water. The effluent, as is the current practice, will be monitored on a frequent and regular basis.

1199.description: The requested funds will enable the construction of a vital reverse osmosis facility on Crawl Key, Marathon, FL. This facility serves a dual purpose; first, it acts as a crucial backup water source during emergencies, safeguarding against disruptions causes by disasters or damaged transmission lines. Secondly, it addresses the pressing need for additional water supply due to population growth and restrictions on Biscayne aquifer withdrawals.
1199.purpose: The requested funds will directly support the establishment of a reverse osmosis facility on Crawl Key, Marathon, FL. This critical infrastructure will provide a reliable and secure water source, ensuring uninterrupted service to citizens during emergencies and times of increased demand due to population growth and aquifer limitations.
1199.activities: The funding will be used to design, bid, permit, and construct a new reverse osmosis facility to provide uninterrupted access to safe and reliable drinking water during emergencies and periods of heightened demand. This facility acts as a crucial lifeline in times of need, enhancing overall community resilience.
1199.direct_services: The funding will enable the operation of a new reverse osmosis facility, ensuring citizens have uninterrupted access to safe and reliable drinking water during emergencies and periods of heightened demand. This facility acts as a crucial lifeline in times of need, enhancing overall community resilience.
1199.population: Residents and visitors to the Florida Keys will all benefit from this project.
1199.outcome: Provision of a reliable and secure water source to provide uninterrupted service to visitors and residents during emergencies and increased demand.

2449.description: Critical City facilities housing public safety (constructed in 1994, 2008) and maintenance (1990) operations are vulnerable to Intracoastal flooding during severe weather events. Stormwater improvements, including new drainage features and a berm westward of the facilities, have been designed to mitigate flooding to ensure continuity of public safety operations during emergencies. The design effort was funded through FEMA HMGP (Project 4486-016-R). The design is under final review by the St. Johns River Water Management District and the United States Army Corps of Engineers. Upon approval and permitting, the City can proceed with construction of the improvements.
2449.purpose: When constructed, the improvements will prevent Intracoastal and tidal flooding of critical City facilities and enhance drainage conveyance and capacity. These facilities were rendered inaccessible due to flooding following Hurricane Irma.
2449.activities: Re-grading and re-paving of the facility tarmacs and aprons will be completed. New drainage facilities will be constructed and existing facilities expanded. A berm will be constructed westward of the City facilities.
2449.direct_services: Citizens will be reassured that public safety and maintenance operations will be sustained during emergency conditions, enhancing the City's ability to protect lives and property.
2449.population: The residents of Flagler Beach (estimated population 5,500, including several households in Volusia County) will directly benefit from this project as well as many other Flagler County residents due to the mutual aid provided by the City of Flagler Beach to the City of Palm Coast and Flagler County.
2449.outcome: The expected benefit is the long-term protection of City facilities, including the staff, vehicles, equipment, and supplies housed in the facilities. The measure of the effectiveness of this project will be confirmed when future flooding is prevented.

2567.description: The Town of Welaka seeks funding for Phase 2 of its Wastewater Treatment Facility Expansion and Upgrades project to increase treatment and effluent disposal capacities, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen system reliability and resiliency. This Phase 2 WWTF Expansion and Upgrades project will build upon the Town's Phase 1 WWTF project, which will modernize critical wastewater infrastructure allowing the Town to meet advanced waste treatment standards, provide redundancy to meet future regulatory and service demands, and ensure the facility can accommodate residential, economic / commercial, and regional growth.
2567.purpose: To complete Phase 2 of the Town’s Wastewater Treatment Facility Expansion and Upgrades project by constructing advanced waste treatment and capacity improvements necessary for long-term regulatory compliance, operational reliability, and system redundancy. Completion of this critical Phase 2 will allow for significant economic growth within this area of Putnam County and allow for additional customers to connect to centralized sewer system.
2567.activities: Activities and services will include updated design/permitting and construction to expand the Town’s wastewater treatment and effluent disposal capacity, modernize key process systems, and improve efficiency, reliability, and resiliency. The project will upgrade and add to critical municipal infrastructure to ensure long-term compliance and dependable service for residents, businesses, and future development.
2567.direct_services: Reliable, compliant wastewater treatment service that safeguards public health, supports business and institutional operations, and ensures system resiliency for residents and utility customers. Additionally, improved water quality from the WWTF meeting advanced waste treatment limits provides for a healthier environment and ecosystem, particularly with Welaka being located along the St. Johns Riv
2567.population: Approximately 800 residents within the Town of Welaka, plus local businesses, schools, and critical facilities. The expanded system will also support future development, economic growth, and regional connections/extensions, allowing for septic-to-sewer conversions.
2567.outcome: Improved wastewater treatment and effluent disposal capacity, reliability, redundancy, and compliance; measured through FDEP permit monitoring reports, effluent quality testing, and documented reduction in operational downtime or violations.

2568.description: The septic-to-sewer project will raise socio-economic status of West Augustine, improve groundwater and well quality, and increase storm resiliency by constructing a sanitary sewer system. The project will connect existing homes and eliminate septic tanks that contribute to deterioration of groundwater quality and "float" during storm events, causing significant environmental and health hazards in the surrounding area. The project will make new workforce housing viable on available parcels by providing sewer availability.
2568.purpose: Centralized public sewer system, utility services, elimination of septic systems and increased opportunity for future economic development in the area.
2568.activities: The addition of public sewer systems and utility services will eliminate the use of septic systems. Specifically, it will connect customers to municipal sewer while removing septic tanks and drainfield mounds from the customer's backyard.
2568.direct_services: Centralized public sewer system, utility services, elimination of septic systems, connection to municipal sewer, removal of septic tanks and drainfield mounds.
2568.population: All citizens/residents within the project area will be served. Existing and future area residents are expected to be served. All citizens in the entire surrounding area will benefit from the elimination of environmental and health hazards.
2568.outcome: Improve Physical Health. Enhance/ preserve/ improve environmental and fish/ wildlife quality. Increase or Improve economic activity by increasing assessed home value and making new workforce housing feasible. Improve wastewater management. Improve stormwater management. Improve groundwater quality. Improve surface water quality.

2570.description: This project creates an advanced technology training center with programs in aerospace technology, avionics, welding and HVAC. The Center for Aerospace and Advanced Technical Education (CAATE) will be located at DSC's New Smyrna Beach/Edgewater Campus, less than 50 miles from the Kennedy Space Center. These programs help fill needed positions in all types of manufacturing, especially operations related to space and aviation. Students can be work-ready in less than one year in three of these programs.
2570.purpose: To create a training center on an existing college campus, with state of the art training equipment to prepare students for high-wage, high-demand jobs in aerospace, avionics, welding and HVAC. Will serve all ages and backgrounds of students, from high school dual enrolled to returning veterans to mid-life career changers. Most credentials can be earned in less than one year.
2570.activities: Training in four academic programs: Aerospace Technician (2-year Associate of Science degree); Avionics (1-year career certificate); Welding Technology (1-year career certificate) and HVAC (1-year career certificate).
2570.direct_services: Train and prepare workers to take high-demand, high-wage positions in surrounding industries, particularly aviation manufacturing. Local employers have expressed great support for the expansion of these programs to the southeast Volusia area.
2570.population: Over 200 students can be enrolled in these programs at full capacity. These programs serve students looking for high demand, high wage careers, and also benefits local manufacturers who are seeking a trained workforce in the immediate region.
2570.outcome: The expected outcome is to produce graduates well trained in industry-standard technology in four areas critical to the manufacturing industries in the region. Outcomes can be measured by number of graduates of each program and number placed in area jobs following graduation.

2572.description: Completion of critical campus safety improvements partially funded by the Florida Legislature in 2025-26. Implementation of a centralized door access control system, expansion of campus-wide video surveillance and upgrade and expansion of an outdoor emergency public address system. This project covers seven campuses and centers at DSC, which serves 23,000 students and members of the public.
2572.purpose: Project implements safety measures that provide centralized controlled access to all buildings across seven campuses that serve 23,000 students. Provides Campus Safety office emergency response and lock down capabilities, enhancing student and employee safety and asset protection. Improves video surveillance and upgrades emergency public address system.
2572.activities: Installation of card reader system on all exterior doors on seven campuses, allowing controlled lockdown of any or all buildings. Installation of additional necessary video surveillance and upgrade to emergency public address system.
2572.direct_services: Increased safety of 23,000 DSC students, as well as employees and visitors to campus.
2572.population: 23,000 Daytona State College students, as well as employees and daily visitors to any of the college's seven campuses and centers.
2572.outcome: Increased safety in cases of emergency and fewer loss of assets.

2573.description: This project seeks funding to acquire advanced hypersonic research equipment that will expand experimental and educational capabilities in high-speed aerospace science. The equipment will provide hands-on learning for over 800 students annually while supporting faculty and researchers in developing innovative materials, communication systems, and control technologies. It will also create jobs for researchers and students and foster long-term economic growth through startups and industry collaboration. These efforts will enhance education, strengthen the workforce, and promote advancement in high-tech innovation.
2573.purpose: This project seeks funding to acquire advanced hypersonic research equipment that will expand experimental and educational capabilities in high-speed aerospace science. The equipment will provide hands-on learning for over 800 students annually while supporting faculty and researchers in developing innovative materials, communication systems, and control technologies. It will also create immediate jobs for research staff and student assistants and foster long-term economic growth through startup
2573.activities: The proposed equipment will enable integrated research and hands-on education, producing high-quality data and fostering collaboration across disciplines. These efforts will drive technological innovation, support research, and prepare a skilled workforce for future advancements in hypersonic and aerospace technologies.
2573.direct_services: The appropriation for the hypersonic research project will provide direct services to citizens through education, workforce development, and economic growth. The new equipment will engage students, faculty and researchers in hands-on research, preparing them for high-demand STEM careers that support the aerospace industry. It will create immediate job opportunities, while promoting long-term emplo
2573.population: This initiative will serve a diverse population of students, faculty, researchers, and startup collaborators. More than 800 students annually will gain hands-on experience using advanced testing and diagnostic equipment, strengthening their technical and analytical skills for careers in aerospace, engineering, and advanced manufacturing. Faculty and researchers will benefit from expanded research capacity, enabling innovative studies and interdisciplinary collaboration. Startups and industry par
2573.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project include enhanced educational quality, expanded research capacity, and measurable economic growth. The hypersonic research equipment will provide hands-on learning for over 800 students annually, support faculty-led innovation, and stimulate job creation through research positions, internships, and startup development. These outcomes will strengthen the regional workforce, promote technological advancement, and increase collaboration between academia and industry. The methodology for measuring success will include tracking student participation, faculty research projects, external funding secured, and industry partnerships formed. Additional indicators su

2574.description: For the construction of Volusia County's first-ever Consolidated Sheriff's Office Headquarters—an investment addresses a long-standing gap in public safety infrastructure. Currently, the Sheriff's Office operates from a portion of the fourth floor of a county building and has never had a dedicated facility. This new headquarters will: enhance public safety by centralizing law enforcement operations, enabling faster response times, and improving coordination across departments; strengthen emergency preparedness through the relocation of the backup Volusia Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP), ensuring continuity of 911 services during crises; achieve cost savings by consolidating resources, reducing overhead, and eliminating operational inefficiencies; and increase community engagement by providing a permanent, accessible location for outreach, education, and public interaction.
2574.purpose: The funds requested for building a new centralized VSO headquarters will achieve multiple goals, including:(1)Increased Public Safety: A modern, well-equipped headquarters will enhance the ability to respond to emergencies and maintain public safety; (2) Cost Savings: Over time, the centralized facility will generate cost savings through shared resources, reduced rent/maintenance costs, and improved operational efficiency; (3) Public Emergency Response: The headquarters will be located on higher
2574.activities: Activities & services that will be provided to meet the intended purpose of the funds include the following: (1) Law Enforcement Operations-The headquarters will house command staff, administrative staff, support staff, investigative staff & patrol under one roof allowing for coordination of daily operations and emergency situations to include faster response times and increased public safety;(2)The headquarters will consolidate/centralize services including IT, payroll, human resources, finance
2574.direct_services: (1)Enhanced Public Safety-Enhanced coordination/response times for emergency/non-emergency incidents, ensuring the safety & security of the community;(2) Space for community meetings, workshops, and events aimed at building relationships & trust between law enforcement and citizens;(3) dedicated area for Victim Advocates to provide support & resources to victims of crimes including advocacy, couns
2574.population: This population encompasses a diverse demographic including families, businesses, and tourists seeking various services from the Volusia Sheriff's Office. The 2022 U.S. Census showed approximately 580,000 residents in Volusia County, Florida. In 2023, Volusia County saw approximately 10.14 million visitors during special events like Bike Week, the Daytona 500 and other NASCAR races, festivals, etc. This project will serve any/all the residents, businesses, and tourists seeking law enforcement se
2574.outcome: (1)Enhanced Public Safety-improved coordination & faster response times to emergencies; (2) Operational Efficiency- streamlined processes & reduced redundancies leading to cost savings; (3) Community Engagement-strengthened relationship between law enforcement and the community through outreach programs & public services; (4) More efficient use of resources including equipment and personnel;(5) Overall Cost Savings-reduced spending on multiple office locations/utilities. Methodology for Measuring Outcomes:(1) Response Times-monitoring/comparing response times to emergency calls before & after the new headquarters is operational; (2) Cost Savings- tracking budget reports to identify cost savi

2575.description: The goal of this project is to equip DSC's Center for Aerospace and Advanced Technical Education (CAATE) with advanced equipment standard in the fields of aerospace, avionics, HVAC and welding technology. Training on industry- standard equipment best prepares new graduates to be ready to work, supplying much needed technical workforce support for burgeoning industries in Volusia and Flagler counties.
2575.purpose: The goal of this project is to equip DSC's Center for Aerospace and Advanced Technical Education (CAATE) with advanced equipment standard in the fields of aerospace, avionics, HVAC and welding technology. Training on industry-standard equipment best prepares new graduates to be ready to work, supplying much needed technical workforce support for burgeoning industries in Volusia and Flagler counties.
2575.activities: The equipment supports instruction in four high-demand, high-wage areas in workforce: aerospace technician, avionics, welding and HVAC. This equipment will be industry-standard, purchased in consultation with program advisory boards made up of local employers.
2575.direct_services: Instruction in four high-demand, high-wage programs, ensuring graduating students are ready to work on equipment currently used in manufacturing industry in our region.
2575.population: Over 200 students will be served by these programs at full capacity. The area manufacturers will benefit from a trained, ready-to-work workforce.

Each participant is matched with a mentor from a technical or creative profession who provides guidance and real-world insight. 1466.description: Funding is requested for construction of a new, modern Fire Rescue Station #3 to replace the aging facility on Shadeville Road that is deemed unsafe as the current building shows structural instability from potential sinkholes, posing risk to personnel and equipment. The new station will ensure uninterrupted emergency response service to eastern Wakulla County (County), protecting residents, businesses, and infrastructure. The County will fund land purchase and design; state funds will support sitework, CEI services, & construction. This area is designated as a Rural Area of Opportunity (RAO). We estimate the following costs would be the County’s contribution: $150K for 5 acres of land & $200K for engr/design totaling $350K.
1466.purpose: Goal is to construct a safe, modern fire rescue facility that ensures continuous emergency and fire-rescue operations for eastern Wakulla County, a Rural Area of Opportunity, near Opportunity Park that eliminates structural hazards from sinkhole activity. Protection of life, health, property, the environment and safety of the community. We estimate the following costs would be the County’s contribution: $150K for 5 acres of land & $200K for engr/design totaling $350K.

1469.description: Funds are needed for preliminary engineering, planning, and design of new sewer infrastructure to serve the eastern portion of Wakulla County. The project will consolidate and expand three existing smaller sewer systems — Opportunity Park/Winco, St. Marks, and River Plantation Estates — into a unified regional wastewater system. The improvements will protect the Wakulla Springs Basin, reduce nutrient loading, support septic-to-sewer conversions, and enhance environmental and public health in this designated Rural Area of Opportunity.
1469.purpose: Goal is to improve life, health, safety, property and the environment with the design of sewer infrastructure that consolidates and expands three existing systems into a unified regional sewer system that improves wastewater management and reduces nutrient loads and for protection of the Wakulla Springs Basin (BMAP), State protected water resources.

1469.direct_services: Direct service is improved wastewater management, protection of the environment and public health, and long-term reduction of nutrient loading through future central sewer connections; Improving the quality of life, health, safety, protection of natural resources and property in eastern Wakulla County, including Opportunity Park/Winco, St. Marks, and River Plantation Estates.
1469.population: State of Florida is served by this project as removal of TMDLS, protection of Wakulla Springs Basin addresses State & Federal permitting agencies water quality/quantity priorities; Wakulla County is designated as a Rural Area of Critical Economic Concern per Executive Order #11-81; and as outlined in F.S. 288.0656 Rural Economic Development Initiative (REDI) as a Rural Area of Opportunity;

1595.description: The East City Drainage Canal Improvements project will address severe and repetitive flooding in the Kissimmee East City Ditch area by constructing a new bypass to replace a failed private drainage system. The existing private system, originally intended to convey stormwater from the Kissimmee Homes and Kissimmee Court Apartments to the City’s drainage canal, has collapsed and no longer functions as designed. As a result, stormwater is trapped within the neighborhood, causing flooding that affects nearby single-family homes and more than 200 vulnerable households in the North Kissimmee area. The project will design and construct a public bypass connection to restore proper stormwater flow from Benita Street to the City’s East Ditch Canal, which discharges into Mill Slough then to Lake Tohopekaliga.
1595.purpose: The requested funds will be used to construct a new public bypass drainage system to redirect stormwater flow from a failed private system into the City’s East City Drainage Canal. Replacement of the existing structure is necessary due to irreparable foundation damage caused by unsuitable underlying soils and the building’s age.

The existing facility has been subject to leaks and compromising evidence due to its location in the building and proximity to moisture- producing HVAC equipment. Replacing this critical infrastructure will strengthen investigative operations, ensure proper chain-of-custody protocols, and support the overall effectiveness of public safety services.

2984.description: Baker Senior Center Naples offers mental health counseling on an outpatient basis to seniors and their families.

2984.population: The targeted population are seniors age 60 and older. In 2022, a third of the population in Collier County was age 65 plus, a 25% growth rate from 2015. This portion of the population is projected to grow another 24% in the next five years. Collier County faces a major deficit of mental health providers which particularly impacts older adults. 2984.outcome: This project will help to increase affordable access to mental health services for seniors. Seniors will be measured through before and after surveys provided to clients served.

2987.description: Marco Island has numerous dead-end canals with impaired stagnant oxygen-depleted salt water with diminishing marine life. Interconnecting large-diameter culverts are needed to connect the canal waters north and south of San Marco Rd. which bisects the island. Construction of the interconnecting culverts will allow tidal flushing to eliminate the dead-ends at San Marco Rd and restore the water quality. This request is to partially fund the completion of one of the interconnecting culverts.

Interconnecting large-diameter culverts are needed to connect the canal waters north and south of San Marco Rd. which bisects the island. Construction of the interconnecting culverts will allow tidal flushing to eliminate the dead ends and restore the water quality. This request is to partially fund the completion of one of the interconnecting culverts.
2987.activities: Construct a large diameter culvert complete with seawall penetrations and inlets to accommodate canal water flow between two dead-end canal segments.
2987.direct_services: Improves the water quality in the dead-end canals to minimize the die-off of marine life and minimize the occurrence of algae and oxygen-depleting biological organisms.
2987.population: This project will benefit the entire population of the City of Marco Island, estimated is approximately 17,500, as well as seasonal visitors that increase our population to approximately 45,000.
2987.outcome: 1. Improve environmental, fish and wildlife quality by increased flushing action will increase the amount of oxygen in the canal waters therefore improving the habits for fish and wildlife, and will be measured by monthly water testing by the City in these canal water basins. 2.Improve Stormwater management by completing one more project from our Master Planned Stormwater Management Program we are advancing toward overall Stormwater containment. The installation of swale inlets tied into the tide-leveling pipe system is expected to significantly reduce street flooding during typical storm events.

1242.description: Recovery Connections of Central Florida is a Recovery Community Organization, a non-profit that is locally governed by people in the recovery community. Recovery Connections offers services and resources that include multiple pathways to long-term sustainable recovery from substance use disorder (SUD). All services are provided by Certified Recovery Peer Specialists (CRPS), who have lived experience recovering from SUD. The CRPS team is uniquely positioned to encourage and provide hope, listen without judgment, and help people navigate the world of recovery. Recovery Connections partners with community organizations to have CRPS team members on-site to provide mobile recovery support services to help people struggling with substance use issues. By meeting people where they are, the organization is breaking down barriers to care. From January - December 2024, the number of community partn
1242.purpose: Certified Recovery Peer Specialists (CRPS) will provide mobile recovery support services to help those who are uninsured and under-insured and struggling with substance use issues. With lived experience, the CRPS team is uniquely positioned to encourage and provide hope, listen without judgment, and help navigate a complex system of care. By partnering with community organizations and providing services on-site, we are reducing burden on under- resourced providers and removing barriers to care.
1242.activities: Mobile recovery support services will be provided by a CRPS on-site at community partner organizations within our four-county footprint. Our CRPS team will facilitate recovery support services sessions (RSS), conduct outreach, and provide connections to critically needed resources through information and referrals (IR). The CRPS team uses their lived experience to encourage, support, and inspire.

1242.outcome: Benefits or outcomes for individuals include improving physical health, improving mental health, enhancing specific individual's economic self-sufficiency, reducing recidivism, and reducing substance abuse. Coaching from Certified Recovery Peer Specialists helps individuals work towards self-determined goals included in an ongoing Recovery Management Plan. Outcomes are measured through the Recovery Capital Scale assessment, which measures internal and external assets used to initiate and sustain recovery. Goal is to increase a participant's Recovery Capital Scale by 25%.

Several nearby communities—including Mas Verde Mobile Home Park and Beacon Hill Colony are located immediately adjacent to the affected drainage corridor and are vulnerable to flooding during major rain events. The City of Lakeland completed a preliminary engineering evaluation of the drainage conveyance system and assessed stabilization alternatives to address significant slope erosion. Five alternatives were evaluated and ranked based on hydraulic performance, slope stabilization effectiveness, expected service life,
2315.purpose: Stabilization of a severely eroded drainage conveyance to protect the adjoining roadway.
2315.activities: Construction services to enclose the eroded drainage conveyance with underground drainage pipe.

2315.population: The project area is primarily high and medium-density moderate to low-income residential land use. Several hundred single-family residential properties are located to the east.
2315.outcome: Enclosing the drainage conveyance after installing underground drainage piping will eliminate erosion and destabilization of the conveyance and protect the roadway, protecting the health and safety of roadway users.

3609.organization: Cross and Anvil Human Services, Inc.
3609.description: Cross and Anvil Human Services, Inc., custodians of record of the Lincoln Cemetery seeks to restore the historic African American Cemetery and maintain this cemetery for the African American population of Pinellas and Hillsborough counties whose loved ones are buried here. At present, there are known to be three civil war veterans buried in the Lincoln Cemetery, which are: John W. Sharter—who served in the Spanish-American War, in Company K Third Confederate Infantry; Joseph Brownlow - who served in Company A of the Second Calvary Florida; and John Lasker - who served in Company F first N.C. Colored H. Also, Elder Jordan, who donated land for Jordan Park Housing Complex, built the Jordan Dance Hall; a social gathering place for local African-American residents. This popular Hall was later named the Manhattan Casino.
3609.purpose: Lincoln Cemetery will be restored with several updates and enhancements to be completed. This will allow families visiting their loved ones in the cemetery to be able to locate and commune with them.

3609.direct_services: Caretaker Services will allow individuals to locate their loved ones in this historic cemetery.
3609.population: The families of the deceased throughout the United States, and Pinellas and Hillsborough counties in Florida. The individuals to be served is unlimited.
3609.outcome: Established in 1926, Lincoln Cemetery was the main burial ground for the African-American population in St. Petersburg. Records search shows the first funeral took place on February 4, 1928 for 19-year-old John Peterson. Restoring this cemetery is essential in allowing the African-American community to have pride in their ancestors resting place, which has been a continuing problem.
