It will improve economic activity by protecting public and private infrastructure, measured by the dollar amount of property and contents saved from destruction during emergency incidents.

2049.organization: City of Palm Beach Gardens Police
2049.description: This project will help fund two drones as first responder locations in Palm Beach Gardens to allow for rapid emergency response with live streaming aerial views that will enhance first responder and public safety, allow for faster emergency response, provide critical situational awareness, expand collaboration with neighboring agencies, and increase operational efficiency.
2049.purpose: This project will enhance first responder and public safety, allow for faster emergency response, provide critical situational awareness, expand collaboration with neighboring agencies, and increase operational efficiency.
2049.activities: The drone as a first responder system is capable of launching an automated response to a 9-1-1 call within twenty seconds and arrival on a scene within one and a half minutes. When not in use, the drone is housed in a weatherproof docking station where the drone is charged and maintained in a constant state of readiness. The rapid emergency response provides real-time streaming video for critical situational awareness to both first responders before they arrive and emergency managers ensuring ad
2049.direct_services: This project will serve the general public with improved emergency response and enhanced public safety.
2049.outcome: This project will allow for faster emergency response, increased operational efficiency, and safer emergency resolutions. These outcomes can be measured empirically through Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) Data, Commission for Florida Law Enforcement Accreditation (CFA) Reporting, and Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies (CALEA) Reporting.

2052.description: State appropriations would be allocated for the redevelopment of the existing community center in East Stuart to include a modern expansion of the facility and hardening of the future structure so that the community may also use the building as a community shelter during storm events. Currently, the city does not have a Category 5 wind-rated public shelter for its more than 19,000 residents during an emergency.
2052.purpose: State appropriations would be allocated for the redevelopment of the existing community center in East Stuart to include a modern expansion of the facility and hardening of the future structure so that the community may also use the building as a community shelter during storm events. Currently, the city does not have a Category 5 wind-rated public shelter for its more than 20,000 residents during an emergency.
2052.activities: The hardened community center will promote health and wellness programming and recreation programs, thereby fostering intergenerational connections within the entire city. The facility is in the geographically center of the city which will provide access to the entire community.
2052.direct_services: The requested funds will modernize an existing community center and help expand educational, recreational and health quality services to citizens. It would also provide citizens with a safe shelter place during severe weather events.
2052.outcome: A modernized community center that doubles as an emergency shelter provides substantial benefits by increasing the community's resilience and social cohesion. This dual-purpose model offers a safe and secure place for residents year- round and becomes a vital hub for disaster relief when needed, leveraging resources efficiently and strengthening community ties. Outcomes will be measured through participant surveys, comments, and suggestions, which will be used to guide improvements to programs and activities.

1920.description: The requested funds will support Just Write Consulting (JWC's) mission to provide Floridians with workforce training as well as job placement. Funding will enhance vocational programs, cover certification costs, and support placement services, equipping participants with the skills and stability needed for self-sufficiency.
1920.purpose: The requested funds will support JWC's mission to provide Floridians with workforce training as well as job placement. Funding will enhance vocational programs, cover certification costs, and support placement services, equipping participants with the skills and stability needed for self-sufficiency.
1920.activities: Funds will directly support citizens who will receive personalized workforce training, job placement assistance, plus access to counseling and mentorship. The program helps Floridians and veterans earn certifications, secure stable employment, achieve lasting housing, and build financial independence.
1920.direct_services: Funding will enable citizens to earn certifications through individualized workforce training, secure employment with job placement support, and attain long-term housing and financial stability.
1920.population: Jobless persons and economically disadvantaged persons
1920.outcome: Eighty (80%) percent of active participants will secure employment or increase their income after program completion and Seventy-Five percent (75%) of active participants will achieve and maintain employment for at least six months. The methodology by which the outcome will be measured through job placement records, employment verifications, and participant income reports. Further self-sufficiency will be measured through employment verification, and follow- up participant surveys.

2184.description: This project will mitigate and reduce localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhance protection of residential homes from flood events, increase drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods. This is through the permitting and construction of new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2184.purpose: The specific goal is to construct the project for the purpose of mitigating and reducing localized flooding and standing rainwater, enhancing protection of residential homes from flood events, increasing drainage capacity, reducing the probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, and protecting of private property and life in Miami Lakes' residential neighborhoods.
2184.activities: Permit and construction of a new drainage system including new catch basins, manholes, drainage pipes, exfiltration trenches (French drains), milling and resurfacing of roadway, and signing and pavement markings.
2184.direct_services: The direct service will be increased drainage capacity and reduced street flooding in the drainage basin which will lessen impact to property of over 79 residential homes.
2184.population: The target population is the surrounding residential community. Increased drainage capacity in this area would directly benefit over 79 properties which is estimated to be over 230 individuals.
2184.outcome: Expected benefits include improved drainage, reduced localized flooding, increased drainage capacity, improved stormwater management, eliminated standing rainwater, reduced probability of mosquito-transmitted diseases to the public, reduced impact to property and life, enhanced environmental protection to the general public, improved transportation conditions, and improved groundwater and surface water quality. Outcome will be measured by field inspection and documentation of rainfall events. Project will create specific contractor, engineer, environmental, and consultant immediate job opportunities in stormwater and construction management measured by contractual agreements.

3566.organization: Alpha and Omega Freedom Ministries Inc.
3566.description: Alpha and Omega is seeking funding for operations, payroll and Fixed Capital Outlay repair projects; Payroll for 10 employees at $194,272. Operational Expenses at $175,611; Fixed Capital Outlay Repair Projects consisting of new roof on apartment building $125,700; Termite Tenting on 4 buildings $41,129; Electrical Conjunction/Meter Boxes $37,500. This Request will complete our Fixed Capital Outlay Projects and secure funding for the only Emergency and Transitional housing for the survivors of D/V, Sexually Trafficked and Homeless individuals and families. We have no additional resources for this population within a 60 mile radius of our facility. This Request will complete our Fixed Capital projects and secure our ability to continue providing quality services to our clients and the communities we serve.
3566.purpose: Funding for operations to enable us to continue providing essential services to survivors of Domestic Violence and homeless women and children. Fixed Capital funding will provide for necessary repairs to our facilities and ensure Florida Housing and DCF guidelines are in compliance for housing fit for human habitation.
3566.activities: Activities include program deliverables such as shelter operations and supplies, case management, counseling appts, program classes, client court appearances, transportation to employment, school and medical and mental health appts. Services provided are Insurance on property, buildings and auto's protecting staff and clients from loss or injury. Utilities, sanitation services, home and office supplies, on-site nightly management and security ensuring client safety and meeting DCF program requir
3566.direct_services: Direct services to the public are counseling, nutritional meal planning, parenting, budgeting, breaking D/V and anger management cycles, and development of calming coping skills when experiencing trauma triggers. We offer these services to the public, DCF referrals, court ordered community service, Tri County Human Services and we work with area churches as an added means of community support.
3566.population: Target populations are women and children experiencing trauma due to Domestic Violence and/or homelessness and sexual trafficking. Target ages for women are between 18 and 60 years old and children and youth from newborn through high school. We also receive women who have successfully completed 6-to-8-month rehabilitation programs.
3566.outcome: Outcomes are providing a program which focuses on stability and sustainability of women and mothers. These measures produce a physically, emotionally, financially, intellectually and spiritually whole individual and family. Clients work to regained their sense of self-worth, self-assuredness and self-reliance. These measures decrease recidivism rates and enable us to deliver reports to county and state officials and our funders. Our methodology is employed on a repetitive basis. We employ training through counselors, teachers and case managers who track client progress using identified benchmarks such as, client behaviors, willingness and accomplishing program goals, sustained employment, ap

1100.description: Keralty Compassionate Communities (KCC) is dedicated to fostering stronger, healthier communities by empowering residents to take an active role in their health outcomes. KCC will implement a pilot program focused on cultivating "Compassionate Neighborhoods" in the 33030-zip code of Homestead, FL, to convene residents with local community health workers (CHW) to identify pressing health and social needs, share their experiences, and build a foundation for long-term, sustainable health improvements. This request will consist of asset identification, leadership development, needs assessment and resource connection that will allow KCC to greatly strengthen the resilience of residents in Homestead who are burdened with health challenges. In partnership with Florida International University (FIU), FIU- STATCONSULT and students will provide data collection and analysis. Hispanic of Florida, su
1100.purpose: Keralty Compassionate Communities (KCC) will implement a pilot program focused on cultivating "Compassionate Neighborhoods" in the 33030-zip code of Homestead, FL, to encourage healthy communities and convene with local leaders and families to empower 600 residents and identify candidates to serve as Community Health Workers (CHW).
1100.activities: KCC will assess the self-agency and perceptions of a primarily Latino community and the unique challenges of residents seeking healthcare and tailor support to stimulate a sense of belonging and connectedness. KCC will employ CHWs from Homestead neighborhoods to collaborate with partners to identify pressing health and social needs and to create digital and physical spaces for residents. Initial assessments will be conducted through virtual and in-person focus groups and further feedback will be
1100.direct_services: KCC will conduct outreach, community events, in-person and digital town halls, focus groups, cultural celebrations, and wellness activities to address the community’s mental and physical health and combat negative health determinants. Building on the insights gained from events, 3 local CHWs will serve residents as trusted liaisons to equip and connect community members with tools to identify and
1100.population: KCC will serve residents in the 33030-zip code of Homestead. In 33030, 68% of this area’s population is Latino, comparatively lower than other Miami-Dade districts. Residents are described as living in rural and geographically isolated areas, have high rates of poverty, with a median household income of $29,994 lower graduation rates and higher unemployment rates, food insecurity, limited access to affordable healthcare, and low community engagement, which contributes to negative physical and me
1100.outcome: This project’s outcomes include improved health awareness, decreased social isolation/loneliness, enhanced community resilience, and strengthened partnerships. This program utilizes a methodology centered on empowering local residents to activate their assets and drive positive change. Keralty introduced its Compassionate Communities Model focused on the following steps: 1. We listen and work together as a community; 2. Identify problems together in the community; 3. Empower communities to care for themselves: 4. Bring solutions through our compassionate communities of care sustainable solutions. KCC prioritizes community voices through targeted interventions and support and building the cap

2397.description: PD&E and Design of State Road 24 (Archer Road) 4 Lane Widening Design from Tower Road west of Gainesville to SW 122nd Street
2397.purpose: The Design phase of this agreement is estimated at $5,500,000.00 utilizing FDOT methods; however, the total request is being split into 2-years ($2,750,000.00 / year). Provide increased level of service (LOS) for vehicular traffic, including the movements of goods, and safe travel for emergency services.
2397.activities: Alachua County and the State of Florida Department of Transportation have executed Contract No. G3784, FPN 449844-3-34-01 for the PD&E and Design Phase of the Project with a tentative completion date of June 30, 2027. The Design phase of this agreement is estimated at $5,500,000.00 utilizing FDOT methods; however, the total request is being split into 2-years ($2,750,000.00 / year). The County will secure Professional Consulting Services in accordance with Chapter 287.055, F.S. Upon execution of
2397.direct_services: The project will have a positive impact on the community by significantly reducing traffic congestion, which in turn will lead to shorter commute times and increased safety for all road users. By improving the flow of traffic, citizens will be able to have increased access to local businesses, boosting economic growth and creating job opportunities. Widening this section of SR 24 will accommodate
2397.population: The proposed SR 24 (Archer Road) 4-Ln Widening will serve the traveling public between Tower Road West of Gainesville to SW 122 St. The recorded vehicular count by the Florida Department of Transportation in 2023 was 23,500 AADT. Traffic Volumes historically, have increased by an average of approximately 2%, per year.
2397.outcome: Provide increased level of service (LOS) for vehicular traffic, including the movements of goods, and safe travel for emergency services. Level of Services are managed and monitored by FDOT. Emergency Services can provide response time logs.

1123.organization: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Palm Beach
1123.description: Too often, the veterans in our community are quietly struggling behind closed doors. Many live in leaking roofs, broken windows, or unsafe conditions they cannot afford to fix. Because of the mental challenges they face, they are not reaching out for help themselves. Instead, it is partners like the United, and the Wounded Veterans Relief Fund who bring their names to us, knowing these men deserve better. With state support of $920,000, we will serve 20 veterans through home rehabilitation. This includes large-scale rebuilds for veterans whose homes are beyond repair, as well as targeted critical repairs.
1123.purpose: The goal of the requested funds is to enhance housing stability and safety for veterans. The funding will support the major rehabilitation of and critical repairs to existing homes, ensuring safe, affordable, and resilient housing for this priority population.
1123.activities: To fulfill the purpose of the $920,000 appropriation, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Palm Beach County will carry out targeted home construction and repair projects, focusing on veterans. Additionally, we will provide homeownership and financial literacy training to help homeowners successfully manage and maintain their homes.
1123.direct_services: The appropriation will directly fund the rehabilitation and repair of homes, prioritizing veterans in Palm Beach County. Eligible individuals will gain access to safe, affordable housing, fostering long-term stability and self-sufficiency. Additionally, homeowners will receive guidance on home maintenance and financial responsibility. Through these efforts, we aim to strengthen the community by en
1123.population: The project’s target population includes veterans within Greater Palm Beach County. Additionally, we are committed to assisting families earning below 80% of the area median income in Palm Beach County. Additionally, we are committed to assisting families earning below 80% of the area median income, as defined by HUD. Through this initiative, we expect to support approximately 20 households, befitting around 45 individuals, helping to address critical housing needs across income levels in our co
1123.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is to increase access to safe, affordable housing and preserve existing home for veterans and families earning below 80% of the area median income in Palm Beach County. This will contribute to a stronger, more stable community by ensuring housing security for those who sustain and serve it. To measure the project’s impact, we will track the number of homes rehabilitated and repaired, as well as the demographics of the households served. Additionally, periodic homeowner surveys will assess satisfaction, long-term stability, and overall community integration, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the project’s success.

1922.description: To ensure the designed planning of infrastructure and capacity of water, wastewater, and reuse is adequate for the addition of the Lake County fairgrounds and sports complex, along with surrounding communities that are currently on the utilities system. The utility planning will need to be done in advance prior to the Fairgrounds planning. This determines what the surrounding transmission utilities can supply and to ensure no detrimental effects have occurred on the existing user.
1922.purpose: The design is for future fairground use along with a sports complex use for the general public.
1922.activities: The design is for future fairground use along with a sports complex use for the general public.
1922.direct_services: The design is for future fairground use along with a sports complex use for the general public.
1922.outcome: The design is for future fairground use along with a sports complex use for the general public. This can be measured by the number of attendees at the fairgrounds for multiples events and uses, along with the sign-up count for the sports complex.

1341.description: Research shows that former foster youth are less likely to finish high school or become employed & have difficulty maintaining employment. Funding will prepare foster teen moms & at-risk teens for the workforce through civics, educational, vocational (hospitality, culinary, nursing assistant, daycare worker, mortuary cosmetology), medication management, mental health, and life skills training. Many of the girls participating in the program are 16 and 17 years old with only a 7th grade education. This prep vocational program will give them what they need so that they can get a job and their GED, to experience economic freedom.
1341.purpose: The funding will allow us to provide educational and mentor services for foster teen moms, teens in foster care, and youth who are at-risk of sex trafficking including life skills, job training (hospitality, culinary, nursing assistant, daycare worker, mortuary cosmetology), mental health support, medication management, DJJ support, and include an aging out of foster care support group. It will include GED tutoring and civics courses.
1341.activities: Many teens that arrive at Hands of Mercy Everywhere are in 10th grade with a 4th grade education. Many are not able to attend regular high school because they are so far behind academically. This funding will allow us to provide a real life and prep vocational education for the teens.
1341.direct_services: Prep Vocational and life-skills education: hospitality, culinary, nursing assistant, daycare worker, mortuary cosmetology, GED prep
1341.population: Girls in foster care that are teen moms or are pregnant, teens who have been/are at risk of sex trafficking. Around 100 individuals will be served.
1341.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is that these teens who have not been able to receive an education because of life situations will be able to get a job, become an adult and be able to take care of their babies. The methodology will be measured by how many teens complete the program, obtain jobs and own a car.

1218.description: The Food & Nutrition for All (FNFA) Collaborative is a county-wide, multi-sector initiative that coordinates food distribution, emergency food relief, and nutrition access resources across high-need communities in Miami-Dade County. The program activates trusted community partners, trained Community Liaisons, and a digital food-finder platform to connect residents to real-time, vetted opportunities in their neighborhood, Together we are reducing barriers to healthy food while strengthening emergency preparedness, community engagement, and health access in the long-term.
1218.purpose: This request will support food access coordination and resilience in Districts 38, focusing on the most vulnerable areas and populations and increasing the reach of critical nutrition resources. Through direct support, calendar/map systems, partner-led programming, and community-led outreach, this work addresses gaps in service delivery and ensures families can access healthy food, in their neighborhoods, especially in times of need.
1218.activities: The FNFA initiative will strengthen local food systems and improve nutrition access by upgrading infrastructure at six food access sites (e.g., pantries, farms, hubs); hosting 24+ Wellness Days featuring food distributions, preventive health screenings, and nutrition education; supporting six culturally tailored nutrition workshops and six garden-based learning sessions; sustaining a countywide Community Food Finder platform (directory, calendar, and map); awarding $150,000 in mini-grants to gra
1218.direct_services: The appropriation will directly support residents by expanding access to free, healthy food through coordinated distributions, community fridges, and gardens; offering culturally grounded nutrition education and health screenings; providing real-time resource navigation through the FNFA Community Food Finder tool; and funding local organizations that deliver essential food relief services. These e
1218.population: •Low-income families •Uninsured or underinsured individuals •Elderly adults •Families with children •Families experiencing crisis, unemployment, or disaster impacts
1218.outcome: This project will improve food and nutrition access for residents in Miami-Dade, especially in District 38. It will support partners in hosting food distributions, provide 10+ mini-grants for community-based services, and expand the FNFA Community Food Finder to help residents locate free food and support. Impact will be measured through the number of residents reached, events held, and partner activities, along with survey feedback and usage data from the Food Finder platform.

1220.description: The Simon Wiesenthal Center, Inc. (SWC) and its acclaimed Museum of Tolerance Los Angeles has launched a fleet of Mobile Museums of Tolerance (MMOT) in Illinois, Canada, New York, and California, and soon the newly purchased and retrofitted two MMOTs for the state of Florida will come online in February 2025.
1220.purpose: Over the last several years, especially after the Hamas terrorist atrocity of October 7, 2023, there has been a historic rise in acts of intolerance and biased-based hate crimes. The MMOT is a traveling education center that uses immersive technology and facilitated dialogue to deliver carefully designed workshops that cover topics including antisemitism and hate, the lessons of the Holocaust, the Civil Rights movement, and digital media literacy, all taught age-appropriately. MMOT workshops emp
1220.activities: Operations and coordination of two Mobile Museums of Tolerance as they travel across Florida, providing a dynamic educational experience challenging students, educators, and community members to ignite action against antisemitism, racism, prejudice, and hate to advance the creation of a more just and compassionate society.
1220.direct_services: The MMOT brings the field trip experience directly to schools, libraries, and other community venues with workshops on topics including the Holocaust, Rights, Antisemitism, Understanding and Combating Hate, and Digital Media Literacy.
1220.population: In addition to serving elementary and high school students and colleges, the MMOT is an educational resource for teachers, faith groups, law enforcement agencies, government leaders, and the community at large.
1220.outcome: The MMOT will inspire Floridians to stand up to hate and contribute to positive social change.

2578.description: Also known as the Andrew Anderson House, the Markland House is a historic mansion built in the Greek Revival style. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on December 6, 1978. Funds will allow the College to make infrastructure upgrades to the historic building to ensure the continued use of it for students, faculty, staff, alumni and the general public.
2578.purpose: Also known as the Andrew Anderson House, the Markland House is a historic mansion built in the Greek Revival style. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on December 6, 1978. Funds will allow the College to make infrastructure upgrades to the historic building to ensure the continued use of it for students, faculty, staff, and the public.
2578.activities: Markland House is currently used for faculty offices, student learning and project spaces, and for public events, which provide service to citizens. It is also vital to the citizens of Florida that the state invests in the preservation of historically significant buildings.
2578.direct_services: Repairs to the building allow Markland to remain economically viable and available for public events. The addition of an elevator and additional restrooms provide enhanced ADA accessibility for the public.
2578.population: K-20 students, faculty, staff and alumni of Flagler College, and the general public. Over 5,000 individuals are expected to be served.
2578.outcome: Renovation and preservation of the historic landmark will allow the campus and the public to continue to experience the building in enriching ways and educational and cultural programming for students and visitors to Markland will continue - measured by the number of student and community activities in cultural programs provided in the building. The project will also ensure the structural integrity of the building for students and members of the public visiting Markland House - measured by Florida Building Codes.

2582.organization: Goodwill Industries of North Florida, Inc.
2582.description: According to the Florida Department of Corrections Florida Prison Recidivism Report published in July 2024 , Putnam County has the 5th highest recidivism rate in the state. This initiative, in partnership with Operation New Hope, will continue to expand our A-STEP (Academic Support Through the Employment Process) to Putnam County with the desired outcome of reducing the recidivism rate. Report Here: FDC Florida Prison Recidivism Report Published July 2024: https://fdc- media.ccplatform.net/content/download/25944/file/FDC%20Recidivism%20Report%202019%20Cohort%20July%202024 .pdf
2582.purpose: Reduce recidivism by providing a minimum of 100 individuals who have been affected by the justice system in Putnam and surrounding counties, with access to post-secondary education opportunities to elevate earning potential and job security by securing industry credentials and certifications. In addition, providing necessary wrap-around services including job placement, mental health therapy, housing, transportation, childcare and emergency services as needed.
2582.activities: Provide services which include pre-release and post-release services. On the pre-release side, we can provide certification and training opportunities for the clients. On the post release side, the A-STEP team provides 1 on 1 case management including connecting clients with other needed social services, educational planning for the clients program of choice, job placement and retention services.
2582.direct_services: Direct services include an in-person interview to discuss academic program selection, Education Navigators assist candidates with program enrollment, financial aid application, course selection and creating a plan to remove any barriers one might have. Additional services include childcare, transportation, financial literacy, and emergency services as needed.
2582.population: The target population served are citizens affected by the justice system. We have a current MOU with the Department of Justice and a referral relationship with the local correctional institution in Putnam County. In 2024-2025, with the $500,000 award from the State of FL, Goodwill served 121 individuals with 196 credentials awarded and a 93% success rate. In 2025-2026, with $100,000 award received from the state, Goodwill has enrolled 27 individuals in the program in 3 months from July 1, 2025 t
2582.outcome: Individuals will be provided with education and employment opportunities to gain meaningful employment. Outcomes will be measured by certifications achieved, recidivism rates, and jobs placed. The expected outcome is a measurable reduction in the recidivism rate for Putnam and surrounding counties. Our goal is for the next publication of the FDC Florida Prison Recidivism Report to show Putnam County with a reduction in its recidivism rate.

2186.organization: Victory For Youth, Inc dba Share Your Heart
2186.description: Victory for Youth (VFY)/ Share Your Heart (SYH) supports and provides food and supplies, vocational job training, placement and mental health screening services, and youth development programs to individuals, seniors, children, victims of domestic violence and families in crisis or distress in an effort to increase family stability and decrease involvement in government systems.
2186.purpose: 1) Support federal, state and local efforts in increasing family stability and decrease involvement of government systems by assisting families and individuals in distress; 2) Expand the service area and locations throughout the Northwest, Southern, Suncoast, Central, Northeast and Southeast DCF Regional Districts; 3) Provide Vocational Job training, placement and mental health screening services throughout the state; 4) Provide and expand Youth Development programs; 5) Support local emergency m
2186.activities: The activities and services will include: providing food, clothing and supplies and emotional/spiritual support at our service locations and to referrals received from our increasing number of partners with memorandums of understanding; developing a network for volunteers; providing job training and placement, CERT training for emergency situations and volunteer trainings; supporting special events such as food distributions and community events; and assisting the Emergency Management Department
2186.direct_services: Families, children, elderly, veterans and others in need will be provided with supplies, clothing and services, including emotional/spiritual support in times of distress and/or disaster. Specially trained volunteers will be available to assist government entities in times of disaster. Mental health screenings and job training and placement will be available to all individuals as needed.
2186.population: The target population is families and individuals that are experiencing hardships in times of distress including but not limited to elderly, adults, disabled, veterans, abused, abandoned and neglected children and victims of crimes throughout the state of Florida. We expect to serve 30000-50000 individuals.
2186.outcome: Expected benefits include Improved physical, nutritional and mental health by providing nutritional food, necessities and emotional/spiritual support; increased protection of the general public from harm and improved emergency response time by trained volunteers; and enhanced individual economic self-sufficiency and diversion from criminal behavior by providing job training, placement services and youth development programs. Outcomes measured by quantity and dollar value of food distributed and number of people served and trained.

1476.organization: America's Second Harvest of the Big Bend,
1476.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1476.description: This request aligns with the State of Florida’s priorities for strengthening community resilience and emergency preparedness. It seeks funding to construct and equip a state-of-the-art Production Kitchen that will enhance the region’s capacity to respond quickly during disasters. The facility will include commercial-grade ovens, steam kettles, blast chillers, and packaging systems to prepare nutritious, ready-to-eat meals for daily use and emergency response.
1476.purpose: Funds will support renovation of the Production Kitchen space and purchase of commercial cooking equipment. The kitchen will prepare nutritious meals for daily feeding programs and produce thousands of hot meals within hours during disasters, strengthening food access, local response capacity, and community resilience.
1476.activities: Increase access to fresh, hot, and nutritious food for low-income and food-insecure children and families in rural food deserts. Generate more than $9 million in annual food cost savings for low-income families through targeted distribution services. Provide critical food support during emergencies and natural disasters affecting Florida schools, businesses, and families.
1476.direct_services: • Increase access to fresh, nutritious food distribution for low-income, food-insecure children and families in rural food deserts. • Generate additional food cost savings for low-income families of over $9,000,000 through targeted food distribution services. • Provide essential basic needs support during emergency response and natural disasters impacting Florida schools, businesses, and families.

This 16-county region in North Florida includes Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Franklin, Gadsden, Gulf, Hamilton, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Suwanee, Taylor, and Wakulla counties. Within this service area: • 55% of the population, over 280,000 people, fall within the ALICE category (2023 United Way of the Big Bend / United Way

Job Creation and Economic Impact: Generate jobs and contracts through a $4 million capital project, encompassing permits, property development, construction, manual labor, and direct services associated with facility expansion. Significant Food Cost Savings: Achieve over $9,000,000 in food cost savings for low-income, food-insecure families across 16 rural North Florida counties. Meal Production: Produce a substantial number of hot and frozen healthy prepackaged meals annually fo

1477.description: This program delivers essential services to individuals experiencing homelessness throughout the Big Bend Region, including emergency shelter, mental health care, and diversion programs that help people transition from homelessness to stability. Funding will strengthen program capacity and sustainability, enabling us to directly serve an estimated 1,500 people.
1477.purpose: To reduce homelessness and support stability in the Big Bend Region by providing emergency shelter, mental health, and diversion services to those in need, reaching an estimated 1,500 individuals annually.
1477.activities: Diversion Services: Keeps people from entering the shelter by helping them find stable, affordable housing or assist with rent/utilities to keep people in their homes Emergency Shelter: Overnight and day program Mental Health services: Counseling and medication management Primary Care Services: Free in-house medical care available for clients and the greater community
1477.direct_services: Diversion Services: Keeps people from entering the shelter by helping them find stable, affordable housing or assist with rent/utilities to keep people in their homes Emergency Shelter: Overnight and day program Mental Health services: Counseling and medication management Primary Care Services: Free in-house medical care available for clients and the greater community
1477.population: Target population are those experiencing homelessness, housing instability and joblessness. Includes elderly, persons with poor mental and physical health, economically disadvantaged, formerly incarcerated persons and victims of crime.

1480.organization: Life Management Center of Northwest Florida,
1480.description: State funds were previously allocated by a legislative special project to renovate this Gulf County outpatient behavioral health clinic which was severely damaged by Hurricane Michael in 2018. As a result, mental health and co-occurring substance use evaluation and treatment services for children and adults were substantially decreased for the residents of Gulf County. This project will provide funding to re-establish and increase outpatient evaluation and treatment services for children and adults with severe and persistent mental illnesses and adults with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders.
1480.purpose: State funds were previously allocated by a legislative special project to renovate this Gulf County outpatient behavioral health clinic which was severely damaged by Hurricane Michael in 2018. Funding is now needed to re-establish services in this underfunded outpatient clinic facility. Funding will provide for outpatient evaluation and treatment services for children and adults with severe and persistent mental illnesses and adults with co-occurring substance use disorders.
1480.activities: Provide outpatient evaluation and treatment services for children and adults with mental health or co-occurring substance use disorders.
1480.direct_services: Outpatient mental health and substance use evaluation and treatment services for children and adults will be provided through this project.
1480.population: Persons with mental health or co-occurring substance use issues living in Gulf or Calhoun county. Telehealth services will also be provided as requested for persons in Bay, Holmes, Jackson and Washington Counties. A total of 101-200 children, adults, and families are expected to be served.
1480.outcome: Provide outpatient evaluation and treatment for persons with mental health and co-occurring substance use disorders. Maintain data on numbers of persons served. Compile data on days within the community on each person served. Maintain data on levels of functional impairment.

1124.description: The Community Connections Council (C3) is transforming how 211 Broward connects residents to care by replacing one-time referrals with a coordinated, closed-loop system that ensures residents actually receive help, not just phone numbers. C3 Navigators assess needs, make digital referrals, and confirm outcomes across a secure network of health, housing, workforce, and social-service providers. Requested funding will accelerate C3’s growth by enrolling additional partner agencies, increasing Navigator capacity for enhanced follow-up and care coordination, and strengthening the administrative and data infrastructure required to scale and track measurable results.
1124.purpose: 211 Broward launched the C3 coordinated care network in Broward County to enable social service and healthcare providers to securely share client information and confirm outcomes. The goal this year is to scale C3’s network of providers and operational capacity to serve more Floridians through verified, closed-loop referrals, improving system efficiency, accountability, and ensuring reliable access to critical services.
1124.activities: Recruit and onboard 50 new provider partners into the C3 network, increase Navigator staffing to manage higher referral volume, provide hands-on follow-up to confirm services were delivered, and strengthen strategic partnerships and data coordination to support long-term sustainability and measurable outcomes.
1124.direct_services: Residents will receive live, personalized support from C3 Navigators who assess needs, deliver electronic referrals to vetted providers, and follow up to confirm that services were successfully received. This ensures residents are not left to navigate the system alone and provides reliable access to housing, financial assistance, behavioral health, and other critical stabilizing services.
1124.population: The C3 Network will serve anyone in need, but focus populations include seniors, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, and those struggling with poor physical or mental health. Over the next year, C3 is projected to serve approximately 2,000 residents with current Navigator capacity, and 8,000 with expanded staffing through this funding request.
1124.outcome: 90% of participants seeking healthcare will be connected to a physical health provider or resource that confirms the care was received and had a positive impact. Closed loop system will track and demonstrate percentage achieved. Client/member will indicate improved physical health through follow-up. 85% of participants seeking behavioral health services will be connected to a mental health provider or resource that confirms the care was received and had a positive impact. Closed loop system will track and demonstrate percentage achieved. Client/member will indicate improved well-being through follow-up.

1112.description: The Boca Raton Achievement Center is dedicated to helping teens and young adults with autism and related disabilities learn the skills they need to successfully navigate a productive and independent life. The BOOST program focuses on teaching participants hard and soft skills necessary to obtain and maintain employment. Through the BOOST program, students explore and practice skills from a wide range of vocations, both on-campus and in the community, to help them identify their strengths and interests. The program includes comprehensive components to prepare them for productivity and success in the workplace. BOOST includes job training, employment coaching, scheduling, interviewing, appropriate communication skills, transportation and financial literacy training. The program assists students overcoming challenges and obstacles and ensures they have every opportunity to become dependable
1112.purpose: BOOST is a Job Skills training and placement program for persons with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and related disabilities. The Boca Raton Achievement Center is dedicated to helping teens and young adults with developmental disabilities learn the skills they need to successfully navigate a productive and independent adult life. The BOOST program focuses on teaching and training participants the necessary hard and soft skills and providing necessary supports to obtain and maintain employment.
1112.activities: The BOOST program will hone employment skills from a wide range of vocations, both on-campus and in the community, and includes comprehensive components to prepare participants for productivity and success in the workforce. BOOST includes job training, employment coaching, scheduling, interviewing, appropriate communication skills, generalization of skills to multiple environments, transportation and financial literacy.
1112.direct_services: community and promote acceptance and inclusion in a variety of occupations. Also, explore opportunities and training in small business creation and production of retail products and services, such as shredding, recycling, assembly, art and greeting cards, soap, candles, gardening, IT, etc.
1112.population: Up to 50 individuals with Autism, physical, developmentally and intellectually disabled, high school and young adult participants.
1112.outcome: Job training to increase chances of employment and provide income, self-sufficiency and increased commerce. Getting individuals with autism and related disabilities out of their homes and working in the community inspire many to patronize those businesses and support their independence. Many participants who are not excelling academically often have other skills and talents in addition to acute perseverance. Exploring other abilities and preferences to increase participants desire to perform certain jobs helps them become more proficient in targeted job skills. All training, performance and placement metrics will be tracked monthly with quarterly progress updates and an annual program report

1483.description: Suwannee County was impacted by four disasters within a 13 month period - Idalia - Aug 2023, Tornadoes - May 2024, Debby - Aug 2024, Helene - Sept 2024. The rare occurrence of so many storms in such a condensed time period created a severe and repetitive impact on infrastructure, homes, business/industry, agriculture, and water quality from winds and inland flooding. Funds would be used to design a regional storm shelter facility for surrounding counties and all Floridians.
1483.purpose: Planning a regional emergency shelter for the residents of the North Florida Region to provide essential services and facilities to those who have limited resources during a storm evacuation event. Citizens will have a safe space to evacuate to for shelter, food, water, medical care and support.
1483.activities: Design and engineering services and master planning for the regional shelter.
1483.direct_services: Provide an essential service during an emergency storm event to those needing to evacuate areas of the State. Will provide for shelter, food, water, medical and other support.
1483.population: Any and all residents of the North Florida region and ultimately across the entire state if needed. Over 1400+ capacity of the shelter.
1483.outcome: Protect the evacuated public from harm during an emergency - facility registration/check-in log Increase tourism through use of the facility during blue sky days - # of events, participation, revenue Increase economic impact - tax revenue, jobs Construct stormwater system for FDOT on property for adjacent state maintained road planned improvements

2194.description: Funding is requested to 1) extend our M-F home delivered nutritional hot meal program for frail homebound elderly clients to include seven day a week breakfasts and weekend lunch deliveries, 2) provide physical and mental health support activities (including but not limited to- chair yoga, dance, personal training, tai chi for arthritis, meditation) and 3) provide acts-based recreational activities that promote socialization and target the isolation and depression prevalent in senior populations (including but not limited to-painting, drawing, sewing, fiber arts, book club, trivia and movie club).
2194.purpose: The goal is to improve the physical and emotional wellbeing of Miami Springs/Virginia Gardens seniors by providing consistent and nutritional meals, physical activities, enrichment, educational programs and vital social interaction.
2194.activities: The activities and services that will be provided by the City of Miami Springs that will meet the intended purpose of these funds include vital health support and recreation activities and an expansion of home delivered meal services. Health support and recreation activities will include, but are not limited to, chair yoga, personal training, tai chi, mindfulness, meditation, dance classes, painting classes, drawing classes, sewing and fiber arts, music, book club, trivia and movie club. Home de
2194.direct_services: Approximately 39,000 home delivered breakfast meals, 11,300 weekend homebound lunch meals, 2040 one-hour physical and mental health support classes, 1100 one-hour recreation activities classes.
2194.population: Underserved low-income senior citizens who are residents of the City of Miami Springs and the City of Virginia Gardens, Florida. 800+ Seniors are expected to be served.
2194.outcome: The expected outcome is improved nutrition for our frail and elderly housebound clients and stabilized or improved physical and mental health for seniors who are able to come to the Adult Community Center. The outcomes will be measured through annual client assessments completed and recorded in the State of Florida CIRTS system.

2195.description: This project consists of the roadway improvements on the Oakwood Drive corridor from East Drive to Palmetto, to accommodate pedestrian, bicycle and vehicular activity and to address public safety. Construction to provide roadway resurfacing, re-striping to ensure safer roads, optimize traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve overall safety and transportation efficiency. Project to include the cost of engineering, CEI Services, architectural design, permitting, construction management and cost estimating.
2195.purpose: To optimize traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve overall transportation safety and efficiency.
2195.activities: Project to include the cost of engineering, CEI Services, architectural design, permitting, construction management, cost estimating and construction (roadway milling and repaving, and re-striping).
2195.direct_services: Enhance public safety by constructing roadway improvements to Oakwood Drive spanning from East Drive to Palmetto Drive.
2195.population: This project holds significant importance as it falls within a service area that the city has identified as a top priority due to its proximity to parks, elementary schools, and will safeguard pedestrians of all age groups.
2195.outcome: Improve overall transportation efficiency and implement safety measures.

2196.description: As part of the City of Miami Springs’ Centennial Celebration, the city is seeking State of Florida funding to install a permanent public statue honoring City founder Glenn Hammond Curtiss. Widely recognized as the Father of Naval Aviation, Curtiss revolutionized military flight, and his aircraft played a critical role in World War I through reconnaissance, training, and coastal defense. His innovations laid the groundwork for modern naval air operations and helped establish the United States as a leader in aviation. In addition to his national impact, Curtiss shaped the development and identity of Miami Springs through his vision for community planning and growth. The proposed memorial—a professionally crafted statue with educational elements—will celebrate his legacy, strengthen local heritage tourism, and provide an enduring historical landmark for residents and visitors. State support
2196.purpose: Glenn Curtiss is widely recognized as the Father of Naval Aviation. His groundbreaking advancements in aviation technology directly shaped the development of seaplanes and aircraft used by the United States Navy. During World War I, Curtiss-designed aircraft played a vital role in America’s early military aviation efforts, contributing significantly to reconnaissance, training, and coastal defense. His contributions laid the foundation for modern naval air operations and propelled the United Sta
2196.activities: The memorial will be open day and night to all residents and visitors alike with the purpose of preserving the historical significance of Glenn Curtiss' contributions to this country.
2196.direct_services: The memorial will educate visitors as to the significant impact Glenn Curtiss had on this country.
2196.population: All residents and visitors to the city.
2196.outcome: The benefit of this project is the preservation of the historical significance of Glenn Curtiss contribution to the country.

1118.description: SCF requests $5 million of a total $16 million project cost to build a permanent structure, replacing aged portables, to house SCF's Venice Collegiate School, a public charter high school providing accelerated dual enrollment opportunities to local students. The project costs include site development and design to support a 22,000-square foot mixed use building housing classrooms, collaborative space, and administrative offices.
1118.purpose: In partnership with SCF, collegiate students gain access to a unique dual enrollment program that enables them to earn an associate in arts degree simultaneously with their high school diploma. Additionally, SCFCSV has articulation agreements with New College and FGCU to offer our graduates scholarships for another three years of tuition at local institutions.
1118.activities: SCF requests $5 million of a total $16 million project cost to build a permanent structure, replacing aged portables, to house SCF's Venice Collegiate School, a public charter high school providing accelerated dual enrollment opportunities to local students. The project costs include site development and design to support a 20,000-square foot mixed use building housing classrooms, collaborative space, and administrative offices.
1118.direct_services: The State College of Florida Collegiate School is a tuition-free public charter high school, sponsored by Sarasota County Schools. The charters are a division of the State College of Florida, Manatee-Sarasota and offer accelerated dual enrollment allowing students to graduate with their high school diploma and associate in arts degree in the same week.
1118.population: Local high school students, grades 9-12, up to 400 students.
1118.outcome: In partnership with SCF, collegiate students gain access to a unique dual enrollment program that enables them to earn an associate in arts degree simultaneously with their high school diploma. Additionally, SCFCSV has articulation agreements with New College and FGCU to offer our graduates scholarships for another three years of tuition at local institutions. Measures include grade progression, test scores, graduation rates and participation and recognition in extracurricular activities, as well as acceptance into state universities.

2197.description: George T. Baker Aviation Technical College will continue to elevate and amplify the quality of aviation education in Miami-Dade County. The equipment requested will support this specialized training for individuals keen on pursuing careers in aviation maintenance, aerospace, electronics, and avionics. The project aims to enhance aviation career opportunities by providing the tools and training students will need.
2197.purpose: George T. Baker Aviation Technical College will continue to elevate and amplify the quality of aviation education in Miami-Dade County. The equipment requested will support this specialized training for individuals keen on pursuing careers in aviation maintenance, aerospace, electronics, and avionics. The project aims to enhance aviation career opportunities by providing the tools and training students will need.
2197.activities: High school students can benefit from dual-enrollment programs, while post-secondary offerings place significant emphasis on the highly regarded Air Traffic Controller and Private Pilot Ground School programs. Moreover, programs will cover areas such as Aviation Airframe Mechanics, Aviation Power-plant Mechanics, Aerospace, and Avionics. Funding the needed equipment would support these initiatives.
2197.direct_services: High-quality sheet metal equipment and aircraft engines play a vital role in aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, and performance, ensuring safety and efficiency in the aerospace industry. Dual-enrolled students will gain hands-on experience in aviation assembly, avionics, and aircraft maintenance, while post-secondary students explore specialized fields such as Air Traffic Control and Avionics.
2197.population: Approximately 800 high school students, post-secondary students, jobless/at-risk/economically disadvantaged persons, and all others interested in entering the aviation industry will be served by this project.
2197.outcome: The expected outcomes are to improve the quality of education and create job opportunities in the aviation and aerospace sectors. Students can pursue careers aligned with their training, such as Air Traffic Control, Avionics Systems, Drone Maintenance and Piloting, Private Pilot Ground School Theory, and Airframe and Power-plant Mechanics. This will be measured by program enrollment, program completion, job placement rates, licensure attainment, and FAA Norms Reports.

2198.description: The Breast Cancer and Heart Disease Health Literacy Advocate Program (BCHDHLA) is a proven, evidence-based initiative designed to reduce two of Florida’s leading causes of largely preventable death—breast cancer and heart disease. The program mobilizes cohorts of college students and low-income residents as Health Literacy Advocates, empowering them with vital knowledge in prevention, early detection, and healthy lifestyle practices. Participants extend this impact by sharing knowledge within their families and communities, multiplying outreach and measurable outcomes. By improving health literacy statewide, the program promotes earlier detection, adherence to preventive care, and reduced hospitalization rates—yielding long-term savings in healthcare expenditures and lives saved.
2198.purpose: Requested funds will expand non-traditional, evidence-based health education to improve health literacy with a focus on breast cancer and heart disease, two of the most costly and leading causes of largely preventable deaths in Florida. These funds will empower college students and low-income individuals with measurable increased knowledge needed to live disease deterrent lifestyles which has been proven to save lives, reduce healthcare costs, and improve public health outcomes.
2198.activities: To meet the intended purpose of the requested funding, digital curriculum delivery will be provided to college students about breast cancer, heart disease, disease prevention, early detection, clinical trials, and the SDOH. Participants will share gained knowledge with their peers to broaden the impact. Additionally, low-income individuals will receive health education through community outreach engagement and health educational materials at their retail worksites and where they shop.
2198.direct_services: This appropriation project will directly provide: 1) virtual interactive education about breast cancer, heart disease, disease prevention, early detection, clinical trials, and SDOH to citizens attending post-secondary academic institutions. 2) low-income citizens with critical health education about breast cancer, heart disease, disease prevention, and early detection through their participation
2198.population: The Breast Cancer and Heart Disease Health Literacy Advocate Program will educate 900 multi-disciplined college students including future healthcare professionals about breast cancer, heart disease, disease prevention, early detection, clinical trials, and SDOH; and 300 low-income individuals will receive health education about breast cancer, heart disease, disease prevention, early detection, and clinical trials. In total 1,200 individuals will be served through virtual health education and dir
2198.outcome: The expected benefit is increased health literacy about breast cancer and heart disease among college students and low-income individuals. Success will be measured by 1) 900 college students completing virtual education with assessments documenting increased knowledge; and advocacy documented by 3,000 social media impressions and at least 9,000 engagements 2) 300 individuals experience increased knowledge as documented at health educational rallies and by surveys conducted with individuals after receiving health education packages.

1374.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1374.description: A Land Remembered, Patrick D. Smith's bestselling novel that spans three generations of Florida pioneers, is being adapted into a multi-part television series that will celebrate the state's rich history and cultural heritage. This timeless story captures the spirit of resilience, hard work, and perseverance that defined early Floridians and shaped the foundation of modern Florida. The project will rely heavily on Florida's post-production industry, employing local editors, designers, videographers,and technicians. The production will utilize in-state post-production facilities and media service companies to complete editing, sound design, and visual effects. This commitment to using Florida-based professionals and facilities will generate local economic impact, support the state's growing film workforce, and demonstrate the value of investing in Florida's creative industries.
1374.purpose: The requested funds will be allocated to post-production activities for the series, ensuring the use of local facilities and professional expertise to achieve excellence in quality and the successful completion of both the scripted series and the educational documentary component.
1374.activities: The funds will support post-production activities including editing, sound design, and voice recording utilizing local facilities. In addition, they will cover salaries for editors, consultants, and creative professionals, prioritizing the engagement of local expert talent to ensure a high-quality final product.
1374.direct_services: The project will provide direct educational and cultural benefits to Florida citizens by ensuring the authenticity and quality of a series that reflects the state's heritage and environment. The accompanying educational documentary, to be developed in collaboration with Florida educators and experts, will serve as a high-quality learning tool, designed to integrate seamlessly into school curriculu
1374.population: The project will serve Florida's students, educators, and citizens involved in education, agriculture, and sustainability. It is expected to reach thousands statewide through the series and educational documentary, and to engage broader national and international audiences. The project will showcase Florida's growth and progress while honoring its proud pioneer history and contributions to innovation and environmental stewardship.
1374.outcome: The project will deepen public and educational understanding of Florida's history, agriculture, and environmental leadership. The A Land Remembered educational documentary will serve as a dynamic classroom tool, supporting curriculums statewide. Outcomes will be measured through educator adoption, institutional partnerships, and audience engagement data from the series, reflecting a stronger, more accurate perception of Florida's heritage and progress.

1214.description: Construction of the project will provide the withdrawal, storage, treatment and conveyance facilities necessary to meet regional drinking water needs through 2044 using alternative water supply. The facilities include a new intake and pump station on Peace River, a new 9 billion gallon above ground raw water reservoir, pump station and conveyance piping to send water to the water treatment plant and the addition of 24 MGD of treatment capacity.
1214.purpose: Construction of the Project will provide the withdrawal, storage, conveyance and treatment facilities necessary to meet the regional drinking water needs through 2044 using an alternative water supply. The facilities include a new intake and pump station on Peace River, a new 9 billion gallon above ground raw water reservoir, a pump station and conveyance piping to send water back to the water treatment plant and the addition of 24 MGD of treatment capacity.
1214.activities: The construction of approximately $615 Million in capital infrastructure to provide an additional 24 MGD of drinking water to the region to meet growing water supply demands with an alternative water supply through 2044.
1214.direct_services: This Project provides a reliable and safe drinking water supply for public health, safety and welfare for the residents of Charlotte, DeSoto, and Sarasota Counties and the City of North Port.
1214.population: The four-county region comprising the Authority's service area has a population of approximately 1,100,000 residents. The Authority's regional water supply system connects to utilities serving most of that population and in 2024, approximately 31 MGD of drinking water was supplied from Authority facilities to meet regional public drinking water needs. This Project will provide an additional 24 MGD to the region to meet rapidly increasing water demands of our members through 2044.
1214.outcome: This Project provides resilient water supply infrastructure to the region to meet future potable water supply demands for economic development and public health and safety. It enhances regional water supply resiliency to disasters such as drought, floods, hurricanes, and climate change. The outcome will be measured through improving water supply availability and maintaining the current high standards for drinking water quality under all foreseeable conditions. In addition, by using an alternative water supply, the Authority is able to avoid groundwater withdrawals in a region that is in a Water Use Caution Area.

2199.description: Since 1948, Youth for Christ Miami and Broward have empowered students ages 11–19 in underserved communities to thrive academically, emotionally, and socially. Through mentorship, life skills development, and positive youth engagement, we equip young people with the tools to make healthy choices, build resilience, and cultivate balanced lives that promote long-term success in school and beyond.
2199.purpose: By providing consistent, caring mentors and evidence-based guidance, the program will strengthen resilience, reduce risky behaviors, and empower students to thrive in school, at home, and in their communities. The requested funds will allow Youth for Christ Miami and Broward to expand mentorship and life-skills programming that supports at-risk youth in achieving academic success, emotional stability, and personal growth.
2199.activities: We provide innovative programs utilizing consistent mentoring in Juvenile Detention Centers, underserved neighborhoods, school campuses and strategic youth centers. We teach life-skills classes, goal setting, conflict resolution, and decision making. We use trauma-informed, evidence-based practices, family meals, and round table discussions to deepen our impact by addressing the emotional and behavioral roots of student struggles. This integration helps youth regulate emotions, build resilience,
2199.direct_services: Our intervention programs throughout Miami and Broward funnel youth through large group programs that lead to small group mentoring and one-on-one follow up. This personal involvement allows mentors to directly address unique needs and refer to additional community-based support services.
2199.population: The target population is at-risk youth ages 11–19 from under-resourced schools and communities across Miami-Dade and Broward counties, many of whom face academic struggles, trauma, and unstable home environments. Through mentorship, life-skills development, and trauma-informed Rebalance programming, the Youth Matter Mentorship Program expects to serve approximately 4,000 students this fiscal year, equipping them to succeed academically, emotionally, and socially.
2199.outcome: Expected outcomes include stronger relationships, better attendance, reduced behavioral incidents, and healthier decision-making. Success will be measured through pre- and post-program surveys, attendance tracking, mentor evaluations, and school feedback on academic and behavioral progress.

1486.organization: The Holistic Plan of Care, Inc.
1486.description: The Holistic Plan of Care (HPOC) Program is a Substance Abuse and Mental Health Outpatient Treatment Program for individuals who are struggling with alcohol, drug, and mental health challenges. Our goal is to provide the wrap around services needed for clients that are struggling with mental health challenges, substance abuse disorders, anger management, grief and loss, and/or parenting challenges. Our goal is to use these funds to reduce recidivism and provide the counseling needed for this clientele serving from a holistic approach.
1486.purpose: The HPOC Program is a non-profit 501(c)3 Substance Abuse, Mental Health Outpatient Treatment Program. Majority population are struggling with alcoholic/drug/ & mental health. Our goal is to provide the wrap around services needed for clients that are struggling with mental challenges, substance abuse disorders, anger management and parenting. Our goal to use these funds to reduce ricidivism and provide the counseling needed for this clientele serving from a holistic approach.
1486.activities: Intake, Orientation, Iindividual Sessions, Group Sessions, Psychosocial Assessments, Initial Service Treatment, Individual Treatment Plans, Lifeskills, Educational Materials, Referrals, and Workbooks.
1486.direct_services: Substance Use Disorder Counseling, Mental Health Counseling, Anger Management Counseling, Grief & Loss Counseling, Parenting Counseling, Individual and Group Sessions.
1486.population: The target population consists of elderly persons, person with poor mental health, jobless persons, at risk youth, drug users, currently and formerly incarcerated persons, drug offenders and victims of crime. Between 400 - 800 individuals to be served.
1486.outcome: Reduction in Criminal Activity; How it Protects the Public: Reduces the risk of substance-related crimes by addressing addiction & mental health challenges. Provides participants with anger management and conflict resolution skills, decreasing violent behavior. Metrics: Reduction in arrests, enforcement for substance related offenses; Method of Measurement: Monitor participant arrest records in partnership with local law enforcement, pre & post program assessments on aggression and behavioral risks. Public Safety through Reduced Recidivism.

1599.description: Replace and upgrade existing network of lightning detection and warning systems in the City of St. Cloud.
1599.purpose: The funding will directly provide enhanced public safety services to residents and visitors using City of St. Cloud parks and outdoor facilities by providing real time lightning alerts and continuous Public Safety monitoring.
1599.activities: The City will procure a vendor to replace all eight existing lightning detection and alerting systems located across six key public sites: Lakefront Park, The Ranch, Chris Lyle Aquatic Center, Hopkins Park, Ralph V. Chisholm Park, and Stephanie Leigh Rothstein Memorial Park.
1599.direct_services: The funding will directly provide enhanced public safety services to residents and visitors using City of St. Cloud parks and outdoor facilities by providing real time lightning alerts and continuous Public Safety monitoring. This will create safer conditions for all residents participating in outdoor recreation, sports and community gatherings at City parks and facilities.
1599.population: This project is designed to serve the general public rather than a specific demographic group. The primary beneficiaries include all residents, visitors, and community members who utilize the City’s parks, recreational areas, and outdoor facilities. By implementing real-time lightning alert systems and continuous Public Safety monitoring, the project will enhance safety for anyone using these spaces during periods of inclement weather. Because the system will be accessible across all City parks
1599.outcome: The primary expected outcome of this project is improved public safety and enhanced operational efficiency within the City’s parks and outdoor facilities. By providing earlier warnings of lightning activity, the system aims to reduce the risk of lightning-related injuries, minimize disruptions to recreational and community activities, and support timely decision- making for facility evacuations. To measure the effectiveness of the project, the City will track and compare key performance indicators before and after system implementation.

1487.description: This request will be for a modernized facility to house fire and EMS operations in the Crossroads area of Hamilton County. The current facility is not constructed to commercial standards, has perennial pest and damage issues, and contains no restroom facilities. New facility will contain ADA complaint restrooms, a hardened shelter facility for first responders, and will meet all NFPA and current Florida building codes. Facility will also house community outreach programs and house full-time EMS/ Fire staff as well as support air transport of medical patients
1487.purpose: Current facility is not constructed to commercial standards. Has perennial pest and damage issues, contains no restroom facilities. New facility will contain ADA complaint restroom, a hardened shelter facility for first responders, and will meet all NFPA and current Florida building codes. Facility will also house community outreach programs and house full-time EMS/ Fire staff as well as support air transport of medical patients.
1487.activities: Construction of a safer facility that is complaint with Florida building codes and all NFPA requirements. This facility will feature a hardened shelter for first responders as well as ADA compliant restrooms and a landing site for air transport of medical patients, and space for full-time fire and EMS staff.
1487.direct_services: Fire and EMS services will be located and dispatched from this location on a full-time basis. Additionally, there will be a landing pad for air-transport of medical patients from the site as need arises. Furthermore, the facility will house various community outreach programs that cannot currently be accommodated by the current facility.
1487.population: This facility will serve the entire northern region of Hamilton County, some 5,000 to 7,000 people, in addition to response to incidents along the I-75 corridor.
1487.outcome: The presence of a hardened shelter facility for first responders will allow the staging of emergency personnel during weather events for more rapid response after. Facility will also house community outreach programs and house full- time EMS/ Fire staff as well as support air transport of medical patients. Response times will fall and positive health/ property outcomes in the area will increase.

1490.description: Acquire and ready strategic industrial land in Liberty County to attract high-wage employers and diversify the tax base. Funds cover land purchase and initial site-readiness steps (environmental due diligence, survey/title, geotech, preliminary engineering, utilities/access planning, and site certification prep). The project positions Liberty County to compete for private investment and job creation consistent with successful rural NW Florida models.
1490.purpose: Acquire and ready strategic industrial land to attract high-wage employers, diversify the tax base, and create durable jobs in Liberty County.
1490.activities: Land purchase; due diligence (environmental, survey, title, geotech); master planning; utility and access engineering; site readiness/certification; marketing package preparation.
1490.direct_services: Indirect capital project enabling employer recruitment, job creation, and long-term economic growth (improved access to quality jobs; reduced out-commuting).
1490.population: Economically disadvantaged residents, jobseekers, veterans, and the general public; countywide impact (~8,500 residents).
1490.outcome: Create specific immediate job opportunities Measure: construction/site-prep jobs; Method: contractor payroll/certified job reports. Increase or improve economic activity Measure: private capital investment; added taxable value; new square footage; Method: permits, investment docs, tax roll data. Enhance specific individuals’ economic self-sufficiency Measure: local hires at above-average wages; Method: employer verification, wage records. Protect the general public from harm (controlled industrial design, emergency access) Measure: compliance milestones; Method: approved site plans, fire/EMS access certifications. Other – Rural industrial site readiness Measure: acres certified shovel-ready;

1493.description: Liberty County (County) requests funds for the purchase of a commercial fire tanker. The County is a fiscally constrained rural community with limited tax base and sizable areas without fire hydrants. Fire suppression depends heavily on mobile water supply apparatuses. The current tanker fleet is outdated and unreliable. This funding request enables replacement with a modern 3000-gallon E-ONE Wetside Tanker, improving public safety, compliance, and disaster readiness. The project ensures the County can maintain essential emergency response capability despite limited local resources.
1493.purpose: To acquire a 2026 E-ONE 3000-gallon tanker to improve fire suppression capability, water supply delivery, and emergency response in rural, unhydranted areas across Liberty County.
1493.activities: Funds will be used to purchase, equip, inspect, and place the fire tanker into operational service; train personnel; and integrate the vehicle into county-wide fire response operations.
1493.direct_services: Provides reliable mobile water supply and firefighting capability for residential, commercial, agricultural, and wildland fire incidents, ensuring public safety and emergency response readiness.
