1493.population: Entire Liberty County population (approx. 8,500 residents), including rural communities and volunteer fire districts covering 836 square miles.
1493.outcome: Increased fire suppression capacity in rural areas Reduced property loss and response time NFPA-compliant equipment for firefighter safety Enhanced wildfire and disaster response capability Measured by: Incident reports, water-delivered logs, ISO fire ratings, average response time, and reduction in mutual aid dependency.

1216.description: Funds will be used to support a comprehensive modernization of patient rooms, nursing stations, and group therapy spaces; installation of anti-ligature and fall-prevention fixtures; improved lighting; and the addition of specialized furniture and equipment to promote mobility, dignity, and engagement. These enhancements will ensure the unit meets current behavioral health design standards. We will also be tailoring our units to best fit their designated demographic, with two adult units for both standard and high-acute patients, and a specialized third unit to serve our senior population.
1216.purpose: These funds will allow for the optimized operation of a specialized Senior Care Unit, designed to specifically cater to our vulnerable geriatric patients. Staffing such a unit properly requires a significant upgrade to standard unit staffing, in order to meet the physical, mental, and emotional needs of a senior population.
1216.activities: Therapeutic engagement with both individual and group therapy together with medication management and appropriate discharge planning.
1216.direct_services: Therapeutic engagement with both individual and group therapy together with medication management and appropriate discharge planning.
1216.population: We will be servicing the geriatric population who suffer from significant mental health issues and substance use disorder.
1216.outcome: We will be improving our patients' mental health and wellbeing, as patients will display lower levels of depression and anxiety upon discharge. This will be measured using clinically-proven tests for depression and anxiety administered upon admission and again at discharge.

2325.description: Add 10,000 square feet of office and support space to the existing 11,750 square foot Emergency Operations Center building. (EOC) The expansion will add new offices for Polk County emergency management staff, multi purpose space for training and expanded EOC operations, restrooms, storage, and mechanical/electrical rooms. Original EOC functional rooms have been lost due to staff being relocated from other facilities to the EOC. Breakout rooms have been turned into offices and the multi-purpose room now houses the County Citizens Information Line call center. The dining area does not have adequate space or equipment to accommodate the increased number of staff required to report to the EOC during activations.
2325.purpose: The expansion will add new offices for Emergency Management staff, multi purpose space for county wide training and expanded EOC operations, restrooms, storage, and mechanical/electrical rooms. Expansion of the facility is the most viable and economically feasible option to meet current and future needs of the Emergency Operations Center.
2325.activities: Activities in this capital project include design, permitting, construction, and inspection/closeout.
2325.direct_services: No direct services will be provided by this project.
2325.population: This project will serve all of Polk County, one of the fastest growing Counties in the United States with a population in 2025 of 881,584 citizens.
2325.outcome: The benefit of this project will be greater efficiencies in emergency operations and increased service to our communities and citizens. Analysis following Hurricane Ian (2022) and Hurricane Milton (2024) determined the Polk County EOC does not have adequate space or capabilities for sufficient disaster response and recovery operations.

1728.description: Designate the Pasco County Behavioral Health Receiving System as a Coordinated Receiving System that will provide an array of evidence-based crisis services as outlined in 394.4573(2)(b), F.S. Target populations include adults needing immediate voluntary or involuntary crisis services, as well as adults in need of evaluation and/or stabilization under the Baker Act or Marchman Act.
1728.purpose: Designation of the Pasco County Behavioral Health Receiving System that will provide an array of evidence based crisis services as outlined in 394.4573(2)(b), F.S. Target populations include adults needing immediate voluntary or involuntary crisis services, as well as adults in need of evaluation and/or stabilization under the Baker Act or Marchman Act.
1728.activities: The Coordinated Receiving System will establish a "no wrong door" philosophy for residents in need of crisis services in collaboration with local law enforcement, CFBHN Managing Entity, local government, area hospitals/emergency departments, designated receiving facilities, first responders, and behavioral health transportation vendors.
1728.direct_services: Direct services will be provided by qualified professionals and include 24/7/265 crisis support. Emergency services (triage, screening, evaluation, diagnosis); medical evaluation; inpatient crisis stabilization;inpatient withdrawal management; case management; care coordination; recovery supports; information and referral; medication management, medication assisted treatment, and urgent care.
1728.population: Adults in need of evaluation and/or stabilization under the Baker Act or Marchman Act (elderly, persons with poor mental or physical health, economically disadvantaged adults, homeless, substance users, currently or formerly incarcerated adults, drug offenders). Over 800 adults served annually.
1728.outcome: Physical health improvement through screening at admission and upon discharge. Linkage to or collabration with primary care physician measured by individual health status - medical record. Pre and post physical health screening. Improved mental health and increased quality of life per self report. Diversion from acute care with linkage to Urgent Care Center. Rapid access to care. Measured by evidenced based screening and assessment tools. Decreased readmission rates and increased engagement at point of discharge or transition to Urgent Care Center. Ability to return quickly to community. Turnaround time and reduced wait times for law enforcement drop off to Integrated Stabilization Unit meas

1201.organization: Habitat for Humanity of the Upper Keys
1201.description: Funds will be used to identify and purchase land and build affordable housing for Monroe County's workforce. This aligns with the statutory mandate for the Florida Keys, an Area of Critical State Concern, to offer affordable housing near employment opportunities. Additionally, the project will enable all three Habitat for Humanity affiliates in the Florida Keys to continue to complete new housing construction and explore opportunities to rehabilitate existing homes.
1201.purpose: Funds will be used to identify and purchase land and for the construction of affordable housing for Monroe County's workforce, in alignment with the statutory requirement the Florida Keys face as an Area of Critical State Concern to provide affordable housing in proximity to places of employment. This project will allow all three Habitat for Humanity affiliates in the Florida Keys to complete construction of new housing and identify opportunities for rehabilitating existing housing stock.
1201.activities: Funds will be used to provide much needed affordable housing for the workforce of the Florida Keys and to rehabilitate existing housing stock. These properties will help give residents the ability to live in the same community where they work.
1201.direct_services: Development of new and rehabilitated housing for income qualified residents of the Florida Keys.
1201.outcome: Completion of construction and renovation projects in Monroe County that establish additional affordable housing stock for Monroe County's workforce.

3303.description: Expansion of the existing Wastewater Treatment Plant, from 2.97 MGD to 6.0 MGD, to keep up with sustained, unprecedented growth. The project also includes a conversion from secondary treatment to Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) in order to improve effluent quality.
3303.purpose: The existing Wastewater Treatment Plant has reached its permitted capacity and needs to be expanded to handle current and future flows. Conversion from secondary to Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) is also required to be compliant with Florida Statutes. The goal is to accomplish the expansion and AWT upgrade without substantially increasing utility rates for financially vulnerable residents.
3303.activities: The existing Wastewater Treatment Plant will be expanded from 2.97 MGD to 6.0 MGD (Phase I & II). Advanced Wastewater Treatment upgrades will also occur during the expansion process.
3303.direct_services: All citizens will benefit from the increased capacity and AWT upgrades at the Wastewater Treatment Plant. The plant has reached its capacity and efforts to augment current processing are extremely expensive. The wastewater treatment process is an essential service that is becoming increasingly more expensive for our residents.
3303.population: The City of Haines City has a population of 37,272 people, of which 24% are elderly, and 14.6% of the total population are economically disadvantaged. Children comprise 21.9% of the population with 21.4% of those children living in a household that is below the poverty level. All of the residents will benefit from this project; however, over half of the residents are part of the target population.
3303.outcome: Wastewater treatment capacity will increase and effluent quality will improve to AWT standards. Measurements will be obtained by recording daily influent flows and effluent quality.

1208.description: The Cuban Museum seeks $550,000 in nonrecurring state appropriations to support educational programming, community outreach, and facility enhancements that aim to preserve and promote the Cuban American history and culture in the State of Florida. Funds will be used for interactive exhibits, digital archives, student tours, and for the creation of cultural programming that directly serves the public. This request supports Florida's interest in preserving immigrant heritage and strengthening civic engagement through arts and humanities.
1208.purpose: To increase public access to Cuban American history and culture, expand educational programming, and preserve historical collections.
1208.activities: Development of rotating exhibits, archival digitization, guided tours for school children, lecture series, and cultural workshops.
1208.direct_services: Free or low-cost admission events, educational programming for K-12 students, senior engagement programs, and public lectures.
1208.population: General public, with emphasis on school-age children, educators, senior citizens, and the South Florida immigrant communities. Anticipated service: 50,000+ individuals annually.
1208.outcome: Increased cultural literacy, tourism impact, preservation of historical records, and measurable increases in museum attendance. Methodology: attendance tracking, survey data, and program participations metrics.

3004.description: Joint partnership with the City of Marco Island to convert septic tanks to a sanitary sewer system while enhancing the stormwater system to reduce flooding and improve water quality to reduce nutrient loading in the sensitive Rookery Bay waters. This project will address stormwater flooding concerns and existing septic system failures during rainfall events. The project is located in unincorporated Collier County, but within the sewer service area of the City of Marco Island.
3004.purpose: Reduction of structure and street flooding along with construction of stormwater quality treatment features and sanitary sewer collection facilities to eliminate the need for existing septic tanks and reduce nutrient loading to the Rookery Bay waters.
3004.activities: Prepare a master plan to allow for the construction of stormwater and sanitary sewer collection facilities to alleviate the frequency and severity of flooding while also reducing potential nutrient loading into Rookery Bay.
3004.direct_services: To provide a reliable sanitary sewer collection service and a functional stormwater treatment and discharge system that will reduce the frequency and severity of structure and street flooding.
3004.population: The entire area of Isles of Capri will benefit from this project.
3004.outcome: Reduce standing water in the neighborhood, improve water quality by eliminating pollutants and decreasing nutrients in the water prior to the discharge into the sensitive waterbodies.

3006.description: The Collier County Water Sewer District’s (CCWSD) wastewater system covers more than 165 square miles and has more than 1,500 air release valves (ARVs). ARVs release excess air out of the sewer system for efficient and reliable operation. Air trapped inside the system causes corrosion, pump failure, flow issues, or pressure surges. Many of the system's ARVs are inoperable, not functioning correctly, and require replacement. These problematic ARVs risk damage to the utility system or failure leading to leaks in the community or environment. This project will help mitigate the risks to waterways, communities, and residents impacted by ARV failures. The scope of work includes replacement of three groups of ARVs (ARV groups generally consist of six to eight ARVs).
3006.purpose: Replacement of ARVs which are inoperable, not functioning correctly, and require replacement. These problematic ARVs risk damage to the utility system or failure. This project will help mitigate the risks to waterways, communities, and residents impacted by ARV failures. The scope of work includes replacement of three groups of ARVs (ARV groups generally consist of six to eight ARVs).
3006.activities: The Collier County Water Sewer District covers more than 165 square miles and has more than 1,500 ARVs. ARVs release excess air out of the sewer system for efficient and reliable operation. Air trapped inside the system causes corrosion, pump failure, flow issues or pressure surges. Many of theh system's ARVs are inoperable, not functioning correctly and require replacement. The problematic ARVs risk damage to the utility system or failure leading to leaks in community and/or environment.
3006.direct_services: This project will help mitigate the risks to waterways, communities, and residents impacted by ARV failures. ARV failure can lead to catastrophic pipeline and equipment damage, water contamination, and raw sewage spills, which are worsened by Florida's high water table and storm surge. There are currently 700 ARVs which are inoperable or not functioning correctly flagged for replacement.
3006.population: The Collier County Water Sewer District provides sanitary sewer service for over 245,000 residents. ARV's are required based on the pressurized wastewater pipe's installation (high points, long runs, decreases in upwards slope, increases in downwards slope, etc.) and are more commonly located along major transmission corridors for the overall utility.
3006.outcome: This project will help mitigate the risks to waterways, communities, and residents impacted by ARV failures by reducing the likelihood of ARV failure.

2402.description: Volusia County Schools is expanding its CTE programs to meet the workforce demands of the Aviation/Aerospace and Advanced Manufacturing industries in East Central Florida. With $974,000 already secured for instructional equipment, technology, and materials, the district is launching Advanced Aerospace and Aviation Maintenance programs to provide students with industry-aligned training and certifications. However, additional funding is critical to constructing an on-site airplane hangar. These programs align with regional labor market needs and offer students access to dual enrollment opportunities and industry-recognized certifications. Additional funding is essential to construct the hangar, a critical component for hands-on training, and to support the continued growth of these high-demand programs, strengthening Florida’s aviation, engineering, and aerospace workforce pipeline.
2402.purpose: The requested funds will be used to construct an airplane hangar, a critical facility for Volusia County Schools' Advanced Aerospace and Aviation Maintenance programs. This hangar will provide students with hands-on training in aircraft maintenance, aerospace technology, and industry-certified skills, ensuring they are job-ready for high-demand careers.
2402.activities: The $1,000,000 will fund the design, engineering, and construction of an airplane hangar to support hands-on aviation maintenance training. This facility will provide students with real-world experience in aircraft systems, maintenance procedures, and industry certifications, ensuring they are prepared for high-demand aerospace careers.
2402.direct_services: The appropriation will fund the construction of an airplane hangar to support hands-on aviation training for high school students. This facility will provide CTE in aircraft maintenance and aerospace technology, equipping students with industry certifications and job-ready skills. Graduates will be prepared for high-wage, high-demand careers in Florida’s growing aerospace industry, benefiting loca
2402.population: The target population for this project includes high school students enrolled in Volusia County Schools' Advanced Aerospace and Aviation Maintenance programs, particularly those pursuing careers in aviation and aerospace technology. Initially, the program will serve 150-200 students annually, with the capacity to expand to 450 students as the program grows.
2402.outcome: This project will provide hands-on training in aviation maintenance and aerospace technology, preparing students for high-wage, high-demand careers in the aerospace industry. By constructing an airplane hangar, students will gain real- world experience, industry certifications, and career pathways, strengthening Florida’s aerospace workforce pipeline. The success of this project will be measured through student enrollment and completion rates, the number of industry certifications earned, participation in work-based learning opportunities such as internships and preapprenticeships, and post-graduation employment or enrollment in related postsecondary programs. Additionally, feedback from ind

2688.description: Cornerstone Classical Academy seeks funding to purchase 17 acres for its new Wildlight campus in Nassau County, a replication of its A-rated high-performing charter school. Acquiring this site will enable future development of a classical, content-rich K–12 public school focused on academic excellence, civic literacy, and character formation. The project supports state priorities to expand educational access, create jobs, and promote sustainable community growth.
2688.purpose: The funds will be used to purchase 17 acres for the development of Cornerstone Classical Academy's new Wildlight campus as the first charter school in Nassau County. This acquisition secures a permanent site for a high-quality public K-12 school that will expand educational access, support regional growth, and provide the foundation for future construction of facilities promoting academic excellence and civic education.
2688.activities: Activities include identifying, purchasing, and preparing land for the new Cornerstone Classical Academy Wildlight campus. Services will involve property evaluation, surveying, environmental review, legal and title work, and initial site planning. These steps will ensure the land is fully ready for future development of a state-compliant K-12 educational facility.
2688.direct_services: The project will directly benefit Nassau County families by securing land for a future Cornerstone Classical Academy campus, ensuring long-term access to a high-quality public K-12 education. This investment supports community growth, creates the foundation for new teaching jobs, and expands educational opportunities that promote civic literacy and workforce readiness.
2688.population: The target population includes K-12 students and families in Nassau County and surrounding areas seeking a high- quality public education. Once developed, the Cornerstone Classical Academy Wildlight campus is projected to serve more than 1,000 students at full capacity, with an initial enrollment of approximately 700 students, benefiting both students and the broader community through educational and economic growth.
2688.outcome: The project will expand educational access in Nassau County by securing land for a new Cornerstone Classical Academy campus. Expected outcomes include increased K-12 enrollment capacity, job creation, and strengthened community growth. Success will be measured by completion of land acquisition, readiness for site development, enrollment projections, and future construction milestones reported to the Florida Department of Education.

1701.description: The current modular building FDOH-Marion utilizes for its Belleview clinic is 25+ years old and is well past its expected life cycle. This project is to construct a new site-built health facility on the existing property to replace the aging modular building currently in use. The current structural condition of the facility is in fair to poor condition and there are minimal possibilities to remodel the building to make it more compatible with current health care facility functions. The new facility will be a modern site-built facility that is designed to provide health care services to the residents of southeastern Marion County. It will be designed to 140 MPH wind loads to allow it to withstand hurricane-force winds and be operational after such an event to aid in the recovery efforts.
1701.purpose: The funds requested will be used for the construction of a new FDOH-Marion clinic in Belleview.
1701.activities: The new, updated clinic will provide the general public access to governmental health services in areas such as clinical and nutrition services, community health planning and statistics, emergency preparedness, environmental health, infectious disease services, wellness programs, overdose prevention, and minority health equity.
1701.direct_services: The new FDOH - Marion clinic will provide services in clinical and nutrition services, community health planning and statistics, emergency preparedness, environmental health, infectious disease services, wellness programs, overdose prevention, and minority health equity.
1701.population: The population targeted will be Marion County residents in the Belleview area who are seeking treatment at an FDOH facility.
1701.outcome: The new, updated clinic will be a modern site-built facility, and will be designed to 140 MPH wind loads to allow it to withstand hurricane-force winds and be operational after such an event to aid in the recovery efforts. Additionally, the new space will allow the FDOH - Marion team to offer their services in a manner better suited to caring for the local population. This will be measured by comparing the number of residents served in the various areas in the old vs the new clinics.

1345.description: The Lowell area has been identified with soil contamination detected above FDEP's provisional cleanup target levels. Marion County has developed a concept plan to extend a centralized potable water system into the Lowell area which would provide clean drinking water to the citizens within the area, to include the State Fire College and other state-run facilities in the vicinity.
1345.purpose: The goal of the project is to bring clean drinking water to Lowell residents, the Florida State Fire College, and the other state-run facilities in the area.
1345.activities: The funds will be used to construct a new 12-inch water line extension for approximately 35,513 feet or 6.73 miles in length with valves, fire hydrants and a water booster station.
1345.direct_services: The project would provide a central potable water system which would eliminate the need of individual domestic and state-run water wells in the Lowell area.
1345.population: The project will target residential and governmental well users located in the Lowell area of Marion County.
1345.outcome: By providing a central potable water system, the residents and state-run facilities in the Lowell area would have the opportunity to disconnect from local wells and instead connect to municipal drinking water. The central water system also provides improved fire flow to the Lowell Area to improve fire protection. The county would measure the potable water connection rate in the Lowell area to include the Florida State Fire College, other state-run facilities, and property owners along the proposed water main route.

3407.description: Brooks Rehabilitation will transform two outside courtyards, into the NextGen Ability Play Zones; one-of-a-kind therapeutic environments that combine the joy of play with evidence-based therapeutic tools to help children achieve their highest level of recovery. One will be constructed in Jacksonville, FL and the other in Daytona Beach, FL. Both will include: adaptive equipment, interactive technology, and sensory-rich design into a safe, inclusive environment for children of all abilities.
3407.purpose: Brooks Rehabilitation will transform two outside courtyards, into the NextGen Ability Play Zones; one-of-a-kind therapeutic environments that combine the joy of play with evidence-based therapeutic tools to help children achieve their highest level of recovery. One will be constructed in Jacksonville, FL and the other in Daytona Beach, FL. Both will include: adaptive equipment, interactive technology, and sensory-rich design into a safe, inclusive environment for children of all abilities.
3407.activities: Renovation of the space to provide physical therapists, recreational therapists, and occupational therapists an innovative space to advance the care of pediatric patients with a disability. Increasing outcomes for Medicaid recipients to prevent failure to thrive. Create a pediatric play space with a specialized physical therapy and occupational therapy in a community setting allowing for peer to peer interaction.
3407.direct_services: Physical therapy: activities of mobility, strength and fitness Occupational therapy: activities of daily living, recreation and cooking Psychology: behavior analysis and coaching Dietary/Nutrition: counseling and education Community reintegration: leisure skills
3407.population: Persons with a disability. Medicaid recipients. Economically disadvantaged individuals. At-risk youth. Developmentally disabled children. Students of all ages and abilities. It is expected that 200-400 children per year will benefit from this project.
3407.outcome: By using targeted interventions, the pediatric patient will increase independence in activities of daily living. The young person will be assessed upon admittance using industry standard methods and specialized equipment. The individual will have access to innovative therapy techniques along with state of the art technology. The young person will again be assessed at a mid point and the throughout care for remarkable gains.

2696.description: Jacksonville School for Autism (JSA) is a not-for-profit private school established in 2005 in support of children and young adults with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD). Since then, the school has seen tremendous growth. JSA started with 2 students and 2 staff and has slowly and intentionally grown to support 60 students with over 50 teachers and therapists! With 1 in 31 children diagnosed with Autism, JSA continues to experience significant growth in student enrollment and program development. A core focus for JSA’s Supportive Transition and Employment Placement (STEP) Program is creating transition-supporting, mission-based enterprises. JSA provides job skill training and coaching to young adults with developmental disabilities. These students are from Northeast Florida area including the following counties: Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau and St. Johns. Through our programs, JSA continues
2696.purpose: JSA's Vocational STEP Program provides students with job seeking skills, job development and placement, functional daily living and social skills, and employment coaching. Funding will be used to develop and expand on-campus enterprises where the skills and interests of the students are aligned with professional job skills to meet the individual's ability and overcome disabilities. JSA also provides on-campus and community-based vocational opportunities with strategic community partnerships.
2696.activities: JSA seeks funding to create a holistic transition initiative. This initiative encompasses several key components: expanding JSA's vocational enterprises to accommodate for a larger number of students, establishing a practical daily living skills curriculum, introducing a social and leisure program, and procuring essential equipment to support students in both the classroom and community settings.
2696.direct_services: The STEP program partners with a diverse range of local businesses while also building unique student-run enterprises. From confidential shredding, sourcing locally-grown produce, and engaging in screen printing to cultivating an aquaponic greenhouse, assembling luminary kits, creating artwork, and exploring culinary experiences, our program provides meaningful opportunities for skill-building.
2696.population: The group of people that this project will serve are students age 14 to adulthood. Program participants include current pre-vocation and vocation students at JSA as well as post-secondary students from other private and public programs. JSA serves populations of individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). We enroll individuals from the surrounding counties of Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau and St. Johns. Our current placement of families crosses all ethnicities and economic backgrounds; autism
2696.outcome: The expected benefit of JSA's Vocational STEP Program is to essentially provide our vocational students with more and more job opportunities, supportive employment placements, and on-campus job enterprises. Our students and young adults have the skills necessary to be successful and productive members in both their home and community; we just need to provide additional resources for them to be able to THRIVE! JSA uses Excel & Central Reach to track skill development over multiple job coaching environments.

2585.description: Advanced Manufacturing International (AMI), in coordination with Daytona State College, will help expand existing entrepreneurial and advanced manufacturing lab space on both the main campus and the Advanced Technical Center Campus. Advanced technologies, such as additive manufacturing, will be deployed with associated certificate training programs.
2585.purpose: It is intended that the funding will be used to deploy advanced manufacturing equipment and associated certificate training. In conjunction, the development of these spaces will generate the opportunity for additional community engagement. By opening the space to more than just enrolled students, DSC can have a greater impact on the community as a whole. Advanced technologies, such as additive manufacturing, will be deployed with associated certification training programs.
2585.activities: Additional instructor training will be completed through this effort promoting a broader understanding of advanced technologies for the training team. Also, the space will be cross functional and allow for non-engineering students to interact with the technologies and potentially incorporate them into their own learning pathway.
2585.direct_services: Training on advanced technologies deployed will be incorporated into DSC's model. Secondly, the space will provide for not just the exploration of technologies, but the true hands on use for the purposes of learning production.
2585.population: The space will be open to all DSC students, both current and former. Additionally, it is intended that this space be open at some regular cadence for the larger Daytona community.
2585.outcome: Developing this space will allow existing programs to leverage technologies previously not available. There will also be opportunity to capture new learners that may be interested in the space and subsequently enroll in a program to build knowledge, skills, and abilities.

2586.description: The requested funds will enable the replacement of the 2-inch galvanized water main serving North 3rd Street with 6- inch water mains. The current water main system is at the end of its useful life and is susceptible to failure due to pipe corrosion. This corrosion causes lower water quality and prevents the system from supporting area fire hydrants. The old pipes currently deliver water that is discolored from rust and has a metallic taste. The corroded pipes have reduced volume and pressure. Replacing the water main will improve water quality and quantity and will enhance fire protection for the city's residents.
2586.purpose: The requested funds will enable the replacement of the 2-inch galvanized water main serving North 3rd Street with 6- inch water mains. The current water main system is at the end of its useful life and is susceptible to failure due to pipe corrosion. This corrosion causes lower water quality and prevents the system from supporting area fire hydrants.
2586.activities: Construction of new larger water mains will support enhanced fire service to residents. Further, replacing the water main will improve water quality and improve the flow quantity.
2586.direct_services: The old pipes currently deliver water that is discolored from rust and has a metallic taste. The corroded pipes have reduced the volume and pressure of the water flowing through them. Replacing the water main will improve water quality and quantity and will enhance fire protection for the city's residents.
2586.population: There are100 residences in the water main replacement area representing more than 200 citizens who will directly benefit from the water improvements.
2586.outcome: The old 2-inch galvanized pipes currently deliver water that is discolored from rust and has a metallic taste. The corroded pipes have reduced the water volume and pressure. Replacing the water main with 6-inch PVC pipe will improve water quality and quantity and will enhance fire protection for the city's residents.

2588.description: Since 2017, the Lower St. Johns River (LSJR) lost 99% of all submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) and natural recovery has been slow and unable to overcome grazing pressure in most parts of the river. Phase 1 of the project was funded in FY 24-25 allowing for the first 40 acres of restoration to occur. The goal is to continue these efforts in Phase 2 of the project by restoring an additional 80 acres of native SAV using nursery grown plants and herbivory exclusion devices. The project will be monitored over a three-year time period and the results will be used to guide transformational restoration to the river.
2588.purpose: The goal of this project is to restore 80 acres of native SAV in the Lower St. Johns River in areas that have been shown to be limited by grazers.
2588.activities: The project will allow for restoration of native SAV by installing 262,000 native SAV planting units. Additionally, the plants will be protected form grazers with 4,400 herbivory exclusion devices. Maintenance of plants and cages will occur monthly over a one-year period post installation. Project results will be documented in a three-year monitoring program.
2588.direct_services: The project will improve water quality, enhance recreational/commercial fishing, and improve the tourism industry. Improved water quality means more fish will be available for recreational anglers, increasing local economic activity at bait and tackle shops, restaurants, hotels, etc. The University of FL completed a study in 2015 to quantify the value of the LSJR to local residents and found that
2588.population: The target population are individuals that live and vacation on the St. Johns River between Clay & St. Johns County. The St. Johns River watershed covers nearly 16% of the state and is home to over five million people.
2588.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is the restoration of 80 acres of native SAV in the Lower St. Johns River. The project will be monitored for a period of three-years to measure both qualitative and quantitative benefits.

1650.description: Funds will be allocated for the replacement of an outfall segment at SW 34th Court and SW 24th Ave, and installation of a new outfall at SW 34th Court and SW 26th Terrace - both outfalls discharge into the same basin. This project is located in a residential corridor and an industrial area with commercial warehouses and businesses. Due to aging and insufficient stormwater infrastructure, the neighborhood experiences frequent localized flooding during moderate to heavy rainfall events, with conditions that disrupt daily life and pose significant risks to public health and safety.
1650.purpose: The funds will support the replacement of a non-functional stormwater drainage system and outfall and introduction of a new stormwater drainage system and outfall, thereby reducing flooding risks in this vulnerable neighborhood.
1650.activities: The contractor will mobilize construction crew and replacement and install the modern stormwater infrastructure.
1650.direct_services: The project will provide improved flood protection, better stormwater management, and enhanced resilience to heavy rainfall, benefiting public safety and property values.
1650.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, schools, churches, law enforcement, and visitors in the impacted drainage area, with over 5,000 estimated individuals benefiting directly from reduced flooding and improved drainage.
1650.outcome: The expected outcomes include reduced flooding incidents, enhanced water quality in the receiving water body, and increased community resilience. These will be measured through pre- and post-construction flooding data, water quality monitoring, and feedback from our affected residents and businesses.

2059.description: The GoWest program will provide public transportation to the City of Westlake. Currently there is no public transportation to the city. The GoWest program will operate as a hybrid deviated route providing same day route operations on weekdays between 6-10am and 3-9:30pm. For expedited travel the program will only serve limited stops.
2059.purpose: The GoWest project will provide a boost to local businesses, increasing foot traffic and encouraging people to shop locally, if they are able to travel conveniently and affordably. Improved Access to Jobs allowing workers to reach more job opportunities further from home and increase employment rates. Employers will have the advantage to have a larger labor pool.
2059.activities: The GoWest project will provide the first public transportation option into the City of Westlake improving transportation conditions for individuals that work in the City.
2059.direct_services: The direct service of having a public transportation option for individuals that work in Westlake but live in other parts of the county. Such a service will address the gaps of service outside the more densely populated eastern side of the county.
2059.population: Individuals that utilize public transportation to get to work.
2059.outcome: Direct services will improve transit connectivity opportunities for residents and for commuters supporting the local workforce. Specifically, Economic benefits (Affordable mobility, Supporting Employment, boosting local economy) by providing low-cost transportation options, increasing access to businesses, shops and services, and connecting workers to jobs, training and education opportunities. Environmental benefits also in the reduction of air pollution, lowered carbon footprint and decreasing traffic congestion. Emergency benefits in disaster response to provide evacuation options, in the event of hurricanes, floods, or other emergencies and Community resilience in efforts to provide reli

1654.description: Funds will be allocated for the replacement of a water main segment at Stirling Road and 1st Avenue and replacement of a water main segment at 3rd Avenue. This water main improvement project is pivotal to the long-term transformation and revitalization of this area, which is set to undergo significant redevelopment over the next five years. The project will complete a looped system, enhancing water quality, pressure, and reliability in the area. This is located near City Center, a business and Entertainment District, containing commercial, retail and residential, and is a key component of the City’s redevelopment corridor.
1654.purpose: The funds will support the replacement of two aging water main segments in Dania Beach's central corridor, enhancing water infrastructure reliability and capacity in preparation for the development of the Arts and Entertainment District.
1654.activities: The project will involve installation of new water mains to ensure improved water service and reliability. The funds will also support ongoing engineering services during the construction phase.
1654.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with improved water pressure, enhanced service reliability, increased water quality, and reduced risks of water main failures or service disruptions.
1654.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, and visitors in the central corridor, located one mile south of Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood airport and adjacent to the Federal Highway/US-1 corridor. An estimated 4,000 individuals will be impacted through improved water services.
1654.outcome: The expected outcomes include reduced service disruptions, improved water quality, and increased capacity for future development. These will be measured through system performance data (e.g., reduced repair incidents) and unhindered development in the Arts and Entertainment District.

1259.organization: The Mental Health Association of Central
1259.description: The MHACF Seminole County Free and Charitable Mental Health Clinic works to bridge the significant gap in access to mental health care for uninsured, underinsured, and economically disadvantaged individuals. The program provides no- cost mental health services to the uninsured in order to meet the rising demand for mental health care and ensure underserved populations have access to timely and effective support. The clinic offers a wide range of mental health services, designed to address individual and community mental health needs. The Goals and Objectives inlcude: 1. Increase access to quality mental health care services for uninsured populations across the state of Florida 2. Provide early intervention and reduce the severity of mental health crises in children and adolescents. 3. Reduce reliance on emergency rooms and crisis response services by offering preventative care. 4. Educat
1259.purpose: The Mental Health Association of Central Florida respectfully requests funding to support the ongoing operations of its free and charitable mental health clinic located n Seminole County, Florida. This clinic provides essential mental health services to underserved individuals, including those who are uninsured or underinsured and face significant barriers to care. To address issues of access, the clinic offers telehealth and in person services, ensuring that any Florida resident—regardless of w
1259.activities: The state appropriation requested by the Mental Health Association of Central Florida will fund activities and services that address the mental health needs of underserved communities in Florida.
1259.direct_services: Direct services include: Free individual counseling/therapy sessions for individuals struggling with depression, anxiety, trauma, and other mental health challenges. Support groups for topics such as grief, stress management, addiction recovery, and social support. Case Management that will assist clients in accessing local, state, and federal resources for mental health care, housing, food securi
1259.population: The project will serve uninsured, underinsured, and economically disadvantaged individuals who face significant barriers to accessing mental health care. The clinic aims to serve approximately 1,200 individuals annually, with an initial goal of reaching 600–800 clients in its second year of operations.
1259.outcome: The project aims to deliver measurable improvements in mental health access, treatment effectiveness, and community well-being for the uninsured. The anticipated benefits and outcomes include: 1. Increased Access to Mental Health Services 2. Reduction in Mental Health Crises at emergency departments 3. Enhanced Community Awareness and Education The Methodology for Measuring Outcomes will include client demographics, service utilization, and retention rates through a centralized data management system as well as client surveys like the PHQ9 and the GAD7.

1396.description: This project will allow for the continuation of the Village's successful public transit system, serving close to 60,000 riders annually. The Village's public transit system helps to: 1) alleviate traffic congestion on US 1, 2) provide transportation options to places of employment, and, 3) serve as a lifeline for elderly residents and those without vehicles, providing access to grocery stores and medical appointments.
1396.purpose: Continuation and enhancement of the successful local public transit system.
1396.activities: The Village will continue to provide and enhance it's public transit system, available to residents and visitors.
1396.direct_services: Provision of on demand and/or fixed route public transportation options within the Village.
1396.population: All residents and visitors to the Village will benefit from this project.
1396.outcome: Continuation and enhancement of the successful public transit system in the Village, with close to 60,000 riders served annually.

1143.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of Broward County
1143.description: Boys & Girls Clubs empower youth to reach their full potential through after-school and summer programs focused on Academic Success, Health & Well-being, Character & Leadership, and Life & Workforce Readiness. This project will support the construction and renovation of a designated Teen Space to strengthen engagement and expand program capacity. Planned improvements include the project will renovate an adjacent building to create a connected Teen Center with an open-concept design for specialized programming. Improvements include constructing a link between the two buildings, removing interior walls, installing new flooring, and updating electrical and lighting systems. The existing Club will also receive fresh paint, surface repairs, and refinished interiors.
1143.purpose: Chartered in 1965, Boys & Girls Clubs of Broward County serves more than 8,000 youth ages 6-18, throughout Broward County. Our equation for success includes providing after school and summer programming in four areas of impact: Academic Success, Health & Well-being, Character & Leadership, and Life & Workforce Readiness. Capital improvements will ensure that our members continue to have a safe space to learn, develop and reach their full potential as productive, caring, and responsible citizens.
1143.activities: These funds will enable the construction of Carol Boies Teen Center, complete repairs, and renovation of the Club to create a new designated specialty space to serve members. This initiative will ensure we continue providing out-of- school time activities that address the educational, personal, and vocational needs of underserved, at-risk youth in Broward County.
1143.direct_services: Clubs provide high-yield educational, healthy lifestyle and leadership programs to youth with both environmental and individual risk factors. Our programs strive to have an impact on our members' development, while seeking to empower youth to lead productive lives by ensuring that they have the proper skills to pursue future education and careers.
1143.population: The target population includes economically disadvantaged individuals and at-risk youth, specifically grade school and high school students, with an estimated 200–400 members expected to be served through this project.
1143.outcome: This project will serve youth, providing a safe and supportive environment that promotes overall well-being and future success. Members will benefit from improved physical health through free nutritious meals and fitness programs, and enhanced mental health through evidence-based initiatives that build resilience, coping skills, and emotional awareness. Educational outcomes will strengthen through homework support, project-based learning, and technology, while cultural enrichment programs such as art, music, and recording sessions expand creative expression. Substance prevention and positive youth development programs equip members with the confidence and refusal skills to make healthy choic

1203.description: Funds will support critical capital improvements at the City of Key Colony Beach Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) to maintain advanced wastewater treatment (AWT) performance and regulatory compliance. The project will enhance system reliability, resilience, and treatment efficiency—protecting nearshore waters and sensitive marine ecosystems that define the Florida Keys.The project will help sustain high-quality effluent standards and nutrient reduction goals.
1203.purpose: The project will support critical capital improvements needed to maintain advanced wastewater treatment (AWT) performance, protect nearshore water quality, and ensure regulatory compliance. The upgrades will enhance treatment reliability, system efficiency, and long-term resiliency for the community.
1203.activities: Activities include design, permitting, bidding, construction, and engineering services during construction. Improvements may involve treatment system upgrades, replacement of aging mechanical and electrical components, enhanced process controls, and other capital improvements necessary to maintain AWT standards and reliable facility operations.
1203.direct_services: The project will provide residents, visitors, and businesses with reliable, high-quality wastewater treatment that protects the health of the community and the surrounding marine environment. Maintaining AWT performance reduces nutrient loading and helps safeguard the coastal waters that support recreation, tourism, property values, and the City’s overall quality of life.
1203.population: The project will directly serve approximately 525 full-time residents, as well as seasonal residents, tourists, and local businesses that rely on the City’s wastewater system. It also benefits the broader community that depends on the Florida Keys’ coastal waters for recreation, fishing, tourism, and economic activity.
1203.outcome: Expected benefits include improved treatment reliability, sustained AWT effluent quality, maintain low nutrient discharge, and enhanced environmental protection. Outcomes will be measured through effluent monitoring, Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs), regulatory compliance evaluations, system performance data, and reductions in maintenance issues or treatment disruptions.

1204.description: This project will repair up to 14.3 miles of direct seagrass injuries in Biscayne Bay through a combination of topographic restoration and seagrass planting. Seagrass restoration using sediment tubes is a highly effective method shown to expedite recovery. Healthy seagrass meadows serve as the foundation of Biscayne Bay's aquatic ecosystem providing forage, habitat, and nursery area for fish and other animals that depend on it. This project also includes an educational outreach program to inform boaters of restoration efforts and safe boating practices.
1204.purpose: The primary goal of this project is to restore and enhance up to 14.3 miles of damaged seagrass meadows within Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve that have been damaged by direct boater impacts.
1204.activities: This project will allow for topographic restoration of damaged seagrass meadows through the installation of 23,000 sediment tubes. Supplemental planting will also occur to further expedite seagrass recovery in damaged areas.
1204.direct_services: The project will improve water quality, enhance recreational/commercial fishing, and improve the tourism industry. Improved water quality means more fish will be available for recreational anglers, increasing local economic activity at bait and tackle shops, restaurants, hotels, etc.. According to the South Florida Water Management District, the Bay contributes $64B in Miami-Dade County/yr.
1204.population: The target population are individuals that live and vacation in Miami-Dade County. It is estimated that approximately 448,000 jobs depend on Bay-related activities. These jobs will be safeguarded with improvements in water quality resulting from enhanced seagrass meadows in Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve.
1204.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is the restoration and enhancement of seagrass in up to 14.3 miles of prop scars through topographic restoration and supplemental planting. Treated scars will be monitored for a period of 3 years compared to reference areas. Supplemental planting will also occur to further expedite seagrass recovery in damaged areas. The recovery of seagrass in treated scars will be documented and reported.

2838.description: This project's goal is to significantly enhance our community's resilience to storm-related emergencies by enabling the rapid connection of backup generators to 78 lift stations. The current system is based on obsolete proprietary hardware. This aligns with the state's broader goals of strengthening critical infrastructure and safeguarding Florida's tourism-driven economy by preventing sewage backups that can lead to waterway contamination and beach closures.
2838.purpose: This project's goal is to significantly enhance our community's resilience to storm-related emergencies by enabling the rapid connection of backup generators to 78 lift stations. This aligns with the state's broader goals of strengthening critical infrastructure and safeguarding Florida's tourism-driven economy by preventing sewage backups that can lead to waterway contamination and beach closures.
2838.activities: Funds will be used to cover the cost of construction to build the connection boxes and ensure sewage overflows during storm-related emergencies occur less.
2838.direct_services: An improved and resilient sewer system in storm-related emergencies.
2838.population: This project protects all citizens of Clearwater connected to our sanitary sewer system. By upgrading a wide range of lift stations across the city, this project will directly safeguard over 117,000 residents, as well as our vital tourism population, from the public health risks and property damage associated with sewage backups during storm-related power outages.
2838.outcome: The ability to quickly connect backup generators will prevent widespread sewage backups to protect public health and property during storm-related emergencies. Less reports of sewage backups during these emergencies will ensure that the project has served its purpose.

1496.description: This is a request to revert and reappropriate funds receiving in the FY 2025-2026 General Appropriations Act, Specific Appropriation 2245A. Franklin County received $577,440 (SF 2308) to purchase a Toyne Freightliner top mount commercial fire engine. A purchase order was signed and submitted to Toyne Tactical Fire on July 8, 2025 to purchase the truck. With the delay in building the freightliner, Franklin County will not receive the truck until April 19, 2027. The pumper / tanker that is being built is critical for the safety and fire protection needs of Eastpoint. The truck that is being replaced is the primary main truck and is 20 years old.
1496.purpose: This is a request to revert and reappropriate funds received in the FY25-26 GAA to the FY 26-27 fiscal year. The specific purpose and goal that will be achieved with these funds is to replace the primary truck that is currently in service. The apparatus is critical for the safety and fire protection of the community. The primary truck currently in use is over 20 years old and is at the end of its service.
1496.activities: We have constant contact with the State Fire Marshall's Office regarding the agreement in place for these funds. Currently, our agreement with the Department of Financial Services ends on June 30, 2026. The purpose of this request is to extend the use of these funds. The truck was ordered on July 8, 2025 with a delivery date of April 19, 2027.
1496.direct_services: The truck will help the Eastpoint VFD to respond and act effectively to any emergency situations in the immediate area and surrounding communities, including structure fires and forest fires which is increasing due to the fuel load left behind from Hurricane Michael.
1496.population: The truck will be housed at the Eastpoint Fire Department. The targeted population will be the entire county to respond and support all the VFDs in Franklin County and the surrounding counties. The current population of Franklin County is 13,330 residents with an additional 20,000 plus visiting the area every year.
1496.outcome: Increased fire protection and protection of life and property. This will be measured by the decrease in fire loss and increased public safety. An additional benefit is that a 20 plus year old end of service truck will be replaced.

3567.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3567.description: The Florida Agriculture Restoration & Biochar Initiative expands Florida’s first biochar-based circular economy to restore soils, reduce agricultural waste, and strengthen rural communities. Biotech Applied Research (BAR), in partnership with IDEAS For Us, will convert dead and cleared citrus wood into high-value biochar used for soil improvement, water retention, and nutrient reduction. Funds support mobile carbonization operations, regional biochar processing, workforce development, and STEM training. The program processes 10,000+ tons of biomass annually, creates 25–55 jobs, and trains 150+ students through accredited partners. Biochar will be distributed to farmers, research partners, and community restoration projects across Central Florida.
3567.purpose: The State’s investment will expand BAR’s biochar production operation to address Florida’s agricultural crisis. With 90% of citrus production declining due to disease and hurricanes, these funds convert dead biomass from devastated groves into valuable soil amendments, strengthening farm productivity. The program will deploy production equipment to process 10,000+ tons annually, create 25-30 STEM jobs in rural Hardee County, and strengthen regional infrastructure for innovative biochar/agricultu
3567.activities: BAR will purchase and deploy two additional mobile carbonization units to process dead citrus biomass at source locations, reducing transportation costs and increasing recovery efficiency. Established apprenticeship curriculum partnerships with local high schools and community colleges will create structured training pathways in biochar production and soil science. Monthly field demonstrations will serve high school classes and career training programs, which can be scaled to municipalities who
3567.direct_services: Rural youth and job seekers will access paid apprenticeships and entry-level STEM positions in biochar production and equipment operation, with structured career advancement pathways. High school and college students will participate in bootcamps, internships, and field training at biochar deployment sites, preparing for promising careers within America's bio-economy. State funds enable 500 tons o
3567.population: This project primarily serves residents, landowners, and organizations in Central Florida with priority on Hardee County communities facing economic decline. Direct beneficiaries include agricultural producers seeking to restore and improve underutilized farmland, rural job seekers and youth entering STEM careers, and high school students in agricultural and environmental science programs. The project will create 25-30 direct jobs in biochar operations and train over 150 students through STEM ap
3567.outcome: Expected outcomes include 25-30 jobs, 150+ students trained in STEM, 25 farmers adopting biochar, 1000 tons produced, and $4-$6 agricultural return per $1 invested. To ensure accountability, measurement protocols will be implemented: employment records will track job creation, retention, and wage data; student credentials and assessments will verify STEM skill development; farmer surveys and field records will document biochar usage and impact; production logs will maintain transparent supply chain accounting; and cost-benefit analysis will compare farmer productivity gains and input cost reductions. Partnership with UF IFAS will establish research protocols to monitor soil water retention,

3657.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3657.description: Establish the Florida Native Seed Partnership and implement the Florida Native Seed Research and Marketing Program (subject to the passage of SB-290 or similar legislation). Over a 3-year period, funds will support research to expand the availability and uses of native seed, strengthen the market position of Florida’s native seed industry, and create the state’s first coordinated system for seed collection, certification, storage, research and distribution. This program will increase reliable access to regionally appropriate native seed, supporting growers, restoration, pollinators, agriculture and communities while strengthening Florida’s economy and environment.
3657.purpose: Establish the Florida Native Seed Partnership and implement the Florida Native Seed Research and Marketing Program (subject to the passage of SB-290 or similar legislation). Over a 3-year period, funds will support research to expand the availability and uses of native seed, strengthen the market position of Florida’s native seed industry, and create the state’s first coordinated system for seed collection, certification, storage, research and distribution. This program will increase reliable ac
3657.activities: Develop seed production plots, train growers, certify native seed and wildland harvests, conduct research, purchase startup equipment, and build a public-facing portal to share data, connect partners and coordinate seed supply statewide.
3657.direct_services: The project supports jobs, reduces maintenance costs, and enhances community resilience through expanded use of native plants. Citizens also benefit from restored landscapes, roadside beautification, pollinator habitat and healthier ecosystems.
3657.population: The project directly serves native seed growers, researchers and land managers who produce and use native seed. It indirectly benefits Floridians statewide through restored habitats, cleaner waterways, enhanced recreation areas and more resilient communities.
3657.outcome: Increase supply of regionally adapted native seed to improve restoration success, biodiversity, and economic opportunity. Progress measured by certified species produced, seed quantities available, acres restored and number of trained participants.

1346.description: We believe that one of the best ways to help communities prosper is through entrepreneurship. Creating a business incubator in West Ocala will help residents create their own jobs and wealth generators. Utilizing the expertise of the Ocala Metro CEP team, the incubator will bring extensive entrepreneurial programming and support to this diverse, under resourced community. It will also provide spaces for businesses to grow and thrive in a visible location known to the local community. The funds will purchase up to 12 cottage-style shops, built off-site and transported, to create a vendor village. The site will need to be prepped with necessary electrical, fiber Internet, lighting, security cameras and hardscaping. Each shop will house a business in the incubator program. The City of Ocala will provide a central office for incubator services and a restroom.
1346.purpose: The funds will purchase up to 12 cottage-style shops, built off-site and transported, to create a vendor village. The site will need to be prepped with necessary electrical, fiber Internet, lighting, security cameras and hardscaping. Each shop will house a business in the incubator program. The City of Ocala will provide a central office for incubator services and a restroom.
1346.activities: The incubator will provide office space with Internet and utilities included, one-on-one technical assistance, financial literacy programming, entrepreneurial mindset training, Kauffman FastTrac Program (10-week ideation to launch training), networking and mentorship opportunities. The site will be a vendor village of cottage-style shops, lending itself well to retail vendors & community events.
1346.direct_services: The incubator will provide office space with Internet and utilities included, one-on-one technical assistance, financial literacy programming, entrepreneurial mindset training, Kauffman FastTrac Program (10-week ideation to launch training), networking and mentorship opportunities. The site will be a vendor village of cottage-style shops, lending itself well to retail vendors & community events.
1346.population: Jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, high school students, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, Other - Supporting individuals interested in starting or growing a business.
1346.outcome: Expect to serve 200-400 individuals. Registrations and survey mechanism to measure.

2479.description: 3DE by Junior Achievement is an instructional model for high school education aimed at systemically reengineering the traditional high school experience to provide economic opportunity for all students. Implemented in 32 public high schools between 9 partnering school districts in Florida (as of fall 2026), 3DE is providing quality education through core competency development and business case methodology to over 10,0000 students with specially trained teachers and over 100 partnering employers representing in-demand industries like cybersecurity, manufacturing, law enforcement, financial services, construction, and more that play a key role in curriculum design and delivery. As part of a 3DE cohort, students come out of their 4-year high school journey with a better understanding of how to tackle real-world problems, demonstrate key soft-skills, and explore careers that best align with
2479.purpose: The goal of this project is to provide career readiness and economic opportunity to high school students through core competency development and business case methodology by assisting in funding the expansion and sustainability of the 3DE by Junior Achievement instructional model in existing public high schools in partnership with key school districts and local business communities. This funding would serve over nearly 10,000 high school students across the State of Florida and support a path fo
2479.activities: Funding will assist Junior Achievement in the implementation and sustainability of 3DE in Florida public high schools, serving over 10,000 students enrolled/to be enrolled in this innovative instructional model. Funding will help support on- site and off-site 3DE/Junior Achievement staff, specialized teacher trainings, curriculum development, integration of business case methodology with volunteers, off-site events, career readiness and workforce development activities, student services, and mor
2479.direct_services: Direct services to high school students in the 3DE instructional model include competency development, applied learning to real-world business problems, and being a part of a supportive, inclusive culture of excellence and stability within existing public high schools as members of the 3DE cohort (1/3 of student population - whole school). This includes the service of over 1000 business volunteers
2479.population: Target population for this project are public high school students enrolled/to be enrolled in the 3DE instructional model. Typically, one-third of the student population at a given school is enrolled in 3DE, with the selection process being a combination of feeder-school recruitment, self-selection, and shepherding by school administration. A 3DE cohort is intended to mirror the demographics of the host school, from socioeconomic status (60% + on F/R lunch) to race/ethnicity, gender, and academi
2479.outcome: The expected outcome of expanding and scaling 3DE is to bring 3DE to more public high schools statewide and thereby enroll more students in its instructional model. Benefits include increased academic performance, school stability, school competitiveness, teacher retention/satisfaction, and a persistent talent pipeline of more fully-prepared and competent youth for post-secondary institutions, employment, and entrepreneurship.

1269.description: Crossroads Corral began in 2015 and is a Central Florida nonprofit organization dedicated to improving mental health and overall well-being through equine-assisted programs. Our mission is to empower individuals and families to heal, grow, and find hope through the unique connection between humans and horses. We serve veterans, first responders, survivors of trauma, youth facing emotional challenges, and individuals navigating mental health struggles. Through evidence-informed equine-assisted learning and therapy sessions, participants build confidence, develop coping skills, and experience emotional healing in a safe, supportive environment. Crossroads Corral partners with licensed mental health professionals and certified equine specialists to deliver impactful, trauma- informed programs. By combining the power of horses with compassionate human guidance, we foster resilience, connecti
1269.purpose: With the funding provided, our program can operate and serve individuals who cannot afford to pay for therapy services. Our therapy horses can be cared for by our Barn Manager and we can provide scholarships for individuals and families to received mental health services.
1269.activities: Crossroads Corral will use these funds to expand and sustain our equine-assisted mental health and wellness programs serving veterans, first responders, trauma survivors, and at-risk youth across Central Florida. Activities will include individual and group equine-assisted learning sessions, equine-facilitated therapy with licensed mental health professionals, and specialized workshops focused on stress management, emotional regulation, and resilience building.
1269.direct_services: Crossroads Corral will provide direct, no-cost equine-assisted mental health and wellness services to citizens of Central Florida, including veterans, first responders, trauma survivors, and at-risk youth. Participants will engage in individualized and group sessions facilitated by certified equine specialists and licensed mental health professionals. These services include equine-assisted learnin
1269.population: The target population for this project includes veterans, active-duty military members, first responders, survivors of trauma and domestic violence, at-risk youth, and individuals facing mental health challenges in Central Florida. These populations are often underserved and experience higher rates of stress, PTSD, anxiety, and depression. The number of clients expected to be served is 150.
1269.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is improved mental health, emotional resilience, and overall well-being among veterans, first responders, trauma survivors, and at-risk youth participating in Crossroads Corral’s equine-assisted programs. Participants are expected to experience reduced symptoms of anxiety, depression, and PTSD, as well as increased self-confidence, communication skills, and coping strategies. Outcomes will be measured using a combination of pre- and post-program assessments, participant self-evaluations, and facilitator observations. Standardized tools such as the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) may be used to assess chang

1501.description: Statewide K–8 financial literacy initiative providing in-school lessons, hands-on budgeting and saving simulations, early entrepreneurship activities, and a financial literacy app for students in rural and economically disadvantaged communities.
1501.purpose: The purpose of this project is to deliver statewide K–8 financial literacy instruction that builds early money- management skills, strengthens long-term workforce readiness, and expands economic mobility in rural and economically disadvantaged communities. Funds will support in-school lessons, budgeting and saving simulations, early entrepreneurship activities, parent engagement workshops, and a financial literacy app for students. This initiative complements existing Florida Department of Educa
1501.activities: Funds will support in-school and after-school financial literacy lessons, budgeting and saving simulations, early entrepreneurship projects, teacher support materials, parent engagement workshops, and use of the Money Smart Kids app to reinforce learning and track student progress.
1501.direct_services: Direct services include age-appropriate financial education for K–8 students through interactive lessons, hands-on money activities, and guided use of a financial literacy app, as well as parent sessions that help families support healthy financial habits at home.
1501.population: Grade school students (K–8) At-risk youth Economically disadvantaged persons Rural communities General families participating in financial workshops Estimated number to be served: Approximately 1,800–2,000 K–8 students statewide in FY 2026–2027.
1501.outcome: Benefits/Outcomes: Improved financial literacy knowledge among K–8 students. Increased awareness of saving, budgeting, and responsible spending. Stronger decision-making and goal-setting skills at an early age. Methodology: DOE-aligned pre- and post-assessments. App analytics (lesson completion and quiz performance). Teacher feedback forms and parent surveys. Annual outcome report submitted to the Department of Education.

2480.description: By expanding the Man Up Coaching and Mentoring program, the State can further reduce the long-term burdens associated with fatherlessness through upstream interventions that prevent homelessness, joblessness, incarceration, and mental or substance-related crises. Scaling this work requires recruiting more volunteer coaches to be the one caring adult fatherless males need, as well as building a broader network of resources to support fatherless youth, young men, and potential fathers statewide. These efforts curb criminal activity, boost confidence, and increase the likelihood of graduating and finding full-time employment, ultimately saving Florida millions in welfare and social service costs over the coming decade.
2480.purpose: To continue to reduce costs the State of Florida traditionally incurs due to the impacts of fatherlessness by expanding the Man Up Coaching and Mentoring program to impact more youth, young men, and potential fathers. Expansion of upstream efforts to curtail homelessness, joblessness, incarceration, and mental/substance rates among at-risk constituents includes recruiting more volunteer coaches and creating a wider net of resources for the fatherless.
2480.activities: Research shows that a single committed adult can redirect the life of someone affected by fatherlessness. At-risk male youth & young men are paired with trained, supported mentors and/or staff/foster parents who offer stability and guidance into adulthood. Participants receive an individualized plan to grow into manhood, experience community, and learn essential life skills.
2480.direct_services: Increased effort in recruiting & training mentors/coaches to serve as positive, consistent, male role models for those impacted by fatherlessness. Direct care provided through training on self-leadership, healthy masculinity, and providing wraparound supports. Creating communities that provide lifelong support. Participating in activities that inspire personal growth (vocational, educational, emot

Demographics include roughly 50% Caucasian, 45% African American, and 5% other.
2480.outcome: By elevating awareness of the impacts of fatherlessness, this project will increase the pool of qualified volunteer mentors and coaches. With more trained men modeling healthy masculinity for youth, young adults, and potential fathers, participants will develop greater emotional maturity, confidence, and readiness to contribute positively to their communities. All of this will result in an ROI to the State of Florida of over 500%

1505.description: The purposes of these funds are to provide technology for the at risk youth we serve in order to better enrich their education, to increase the educational materials we are able to provide the students, and to purchase a van to assist in transportation for the students.
1505.purpose: The purposes of these funds are to provide technology for the at risk youth we serve in order to better enrich their education, to increase the educational materials we are able to provide the students, and to purchase a van to assist in transportation for the students. Technological inequities and transportation challenges jointly affect underserved students, especially in rural and low-income communities. Research shows that access to education depends on the intersection of digital inclusion

We would also like to purchase a new van to be able to provide daily pickup and delivery services for the students.
1505.direct_services: We will be providing device loans to our students in the form of chromebooks as a means of addressing technology inequities within our community. We will also be providing our students with access to customized math and reading tools, which act as companions to our curriculum, to help address the literacy disparities faced by our youth.
