Improvements in attendance will be measured by comparing student monthly attendance ratios throughout the year, with an anticipated steady increase in monthly attendance by all students participating, as well as increase the number of students we are able to serve due to a lack of steady transportation.

3568.description: The City of Bowling Green is requesting funding to purchase Public Safety Equipment for the Bowling Green Police Department. This will equip the Department with essential public safety tools: including a marked patrol vehicle, in-car radios, rifle suppressors, AEDs, and ballistic protection. This will enhance officer readiness, improve emergency response, and ensure community safety in compliance with modern policing standards.
3568.purpose: The funds will improve officer safety, enhance emergency response capabilities, strengthen communication during critical incidents, and ensure the Police Department has the essential equipment needed to protect the community effectively.
3568.activities: The Police Department will deploy upgraded patrol operations, provide rapid medical response using AEDs, improve tactical response with safety equipment, and ensure reliable communication through updated in-car radios, all supporting safer and more effective law enforcement services.
3568.direct_services: The requested funding will directly provide citizens with safer streets, faster emergency response, and enhanced police protection. Upgraded vehicles, radios, AEDs, and protective equipment will better equip officers to safeguard the community and ensure reliable, modern public safety services.
3568.population: The project serves the residents, businesses, and visitors of the City of Bowling Green. Approximately 3,000 or more individuals are expected to benefit from improved public safety, faster emergency response times, and enhanced law enforcement protection.
3568.outcome: The project will improve officer safety, increase the effectiveness of emergency response, and enhance community protection through upgraded equipment and reliable communications. Outcomes will be measured by tracking response times, documenting AED deployments, monitoring equipment reliability, evaluating incident resolution efficiency, and reviewing annual safety reports reflecting reductions in injuries, delays, and equipment failures.

A modern, secure facility will provide law enforcement with the space, technology, and hardened infrastructure needed to protect residents, coordinate emergency operations, and maintain order during hurricanes and other crises. The integrated staff emergency shelter ensures that essential personnel can remain on-site and fully operational when conditions are at their worst, allowing continuous response, quicker decision- making, and uninterrupted public safety services. While the primary need centers on police and emergency functions, the inclusion of a new City Hall is also vital, as it houses the administrative and operational functions that support daily services, permits, utilities, planning, and communication with the
3569.purpose: The funds requested will be used to construct a modern, secure Police Department Facility and Staff Emergency Shelter that strengthens public safety, enhances emergency response capabilities, and ensures continuity of government during disasters. The project will provide a hardened facility where law enforcement and essential personnel can safely operate before, during, and after emergencies, allowing uninterrupted protection of residents and faster, more coordinated response efforts. The projec
3569.activities: The activities and services provided through this project will directly support enhanced law enforcement operations, emergency response, and continuity of essential government functions. The new Police Department will deliver improved public safety services, including crime prevention, investigations, patrol operations, and centralized emergency coordination. The integrated Staff Emergency Shelter will allow essential personnel to remain on-site during hurricanes and other disasters, ensuring un
3569.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with improved public safety, faster emergency response, and uninterrupted access to essential City services. A modern police facility enhances protection and response capabilities, while the hardened complex ensures that permitting, utilities, planning, and public communication remain operational before, during, and after emergencies.
3569.population: The target population served by this project is the entire community of Bowling Green, including residents, businesses, and visitors who rely on law enforcement, emergency response and essential municipal services. The project is expected to directly serve approximately 3,000 or more residents, with additional impact on surrounding rural areas during emergencies.
3569.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is improved public safety, stronger emergency response capabilities, and uninterrupted delivery of essential municipal services. The outcome will be measured by reduced emergency response times, documented continuity of operations during storms and other disasters, increased availability of City services, improved police operational efficiency, and post-event evaluations showing that essential functions remained operational.

1506.description: This request will be for a state-of-the-art EOC hardened facility to replace a 60 year old re-purposed building. The new EOC will be safe and accessible for public and service personnel. It will be the headquarters for county fire and EMS services, as well as county Emergency Management. The current facility was originally a shop classroom at an old high school. The current building was damaged during hurricane Helene and is unsafe for continued use in future weather events. Moreover, the current facility is a re-purposed school originally constructed in the 1960's and does not meet modern standards.

It will be the headquarters for county fire and EMS services, as well as county Emergency Management. The current facility was originally a shop classroom at an old high school. 1506.activities: All county emergency management activities will be located at the facility. Providing a safe, secure central facility will provide necessary emergency activities during hurricanes, fires, and other local emergencies. Additionally, space will be provided for a hardened shelter in the event of inclement weather events.
1506.direct_services: All county emergency management activities will be located at the facility (Fire, EMS, and Emergency Management).Also, there will be hardened shelter facilities available for community members to utilize during weather events.
1506.population: This facility will serve the entire population of Hamilton County, some 14,000 people.
1506.outcome: Facility will provide safe, secure, organized, centralized location for emergency response to weather events and other disasters, as well as provide a centralized location for many of the county's emergency services to meet and train, thus providing better communication and coordination. This coordination will also provide decreased response times and increased organizational capacities to better serve the community. Also, the facility will be safer for both first responders and the public.

1508.description: The project will renovate Gretchen Everhart School's outdoor play areas, which are currently inaccessible, outdated, and unsafe. Existing equipment and surfaces prevent students with profound disabilities from active play. Funds will create a fully accessible, inclusive, and safe outdoor space with adaptive equipment, sensory areas, and accessible pathways that support physical, social, and emotional development.

Existing equipment and surfaces prevent students with profound disabilities from active play. Funds will create a fully accessible, inclusive, and safe outdoor space with adaptive equipment, sensory areas, and accessible pathways that support physical, social, and emotional development.
1508.activities: Activities will include the removal of outdated, inaccessible equipment and installation of new ADA-compliant play structures, sensory and mobility features, and accessible surfacing. Services will include design, site preparation, construction, and safety inspection.
1508.direct_services: The project will provide direct services to students with disabilities by giving them safe, accessible opportunities for physical activity, social interaction, sensory engagement, and therapeutic play. It will offer an inclusive environment that supports development, independence, and well-being, directly enhancing the daily educational and recreational experiences of the school community.
1508.population: “The target population is students at Gretchen Everhart School with profound physical, cognitive, and sensory disabilities. The playground will serve approximately 100 students annually, providing an inclusive environment that supports physical activity, social interaction, and overall development.
1508.outcome: An accessible playground improves physical health by encouraging movement that builds strength, balance, coordination, and endurance. For students with disabilities, it provides safe opportunities for therapeutic exercise that supports mobility goals and reduces sedentary behavior. Regular play enhances cardiovascular health, flexibility, and motor planning, while fostering independence and physical confidence. Measured outcomes will include improvements in mobility, balance, coordination, and strength as documented by physical or occupational therapists; increased duration and frequency of active play; reduced sedentary time; achievement of individualized therapy goals.

1271.description: The Winter Park Chain of Lakes receives inflow from the Loch Haven Chain of Lakes via Howell Creek and Alice’s Pond within Mead Gardens. This project proposes the application of EutroSORB to continuously sequester nutrients as water flows into Alice’s Pond, transforming the site into a nutrient reduction facility. The pond currently contains legacy sediment loads that release excessive nutrients into the water column, necessitating removal to restore ecological balance. By reducing nutrient concentrations, this project will improve water quality throughout the interconnected lake systems of Winter Park and Maitland, benefiting both Orange and Seminole Counties. As the headwaters to Lake Jesup and the St. Johns River, these improvements will also support the protection and restoration of Outstanding Florida Waters. City will fund ongoing O&M costs as contributing cost share.

Physiochemical and biological sampling and reporting that includes numerical data expressing trend-lines.

1324.description: SR 426 is a 14.5 mile long roadway, in Metropolitan Orlando, extending eastward from SR 424 in Orange County to SR 46 in Seminole County. It connects Geneva, Oviedo, Goldenrod, Winter Park, and Fairview Shores, and is a crucial connector to regional arterials SR 434, SR 436, US 17-92, and Interstate 4. Its most congested segment is in the City of Winter Park where it is the primary east-west roadway. A major choke point in that segment is the intersection of SR 426 and Denning Drive where the four-lane roadway has no exclusive left-turn lanes to facilitate eastbound to northbound movements and westbound to southbound movements. As a result, significant bottlenecks often develop and reduce the capacity of the four-lane roadway to or below the capacity of a two-lane roadway. Through the addition of exclusive left- turn lanes, this project will result in significant congestion relief and im
1324.purpose: These funds will result in significant improvement to safety, significant decrease in congestion, and decreased response times for first responders.
1324.activities: Engineering designs and studies, the construction of turn lanes and traffic signal modifications, and project oversight consistent with FDOT's best practices, will be performed.
1324.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from significant safety improvements, much improved travel time, and reduction in response times by First Responders.
1324.population: The target population comprises the residents and businesses in Southeast Seminole County and Northeast Orange County, including a number of incorporated cities. Over 130,000 residents are expected to be served by the improvements.
1324.outcome: The expected benefits will include reduction in crashes and injuries, significantly improved travel time for commuters, and reduction to First Responder travel times. Standard Before and After engineering and planning studies, as well as industry standard capacity and level of service analyses will predict and measure the outcomes.

1231.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1231.description: Breeding and rearing Florida Stone Crabs in inland recirculating aquatic systems, with no interference with the Gulf or waters of the state, to protect those environmental resources. These funds will help support an entirely new agriculture industry to the State of Florida. The stone crab demonstration project utilizes a best practices approach to sustainable commercial aquaculture production that addresses the growing demand for safe seafood resources by Florida Consumers.
1231.purpose: Establishing a sustainable aquaculture industry for Florida Stone Crabs to significantly increase the currently limited harvest size of this iconic seafood product. Our sustainable aquaculture approach eliminates pressure on wild populations and natural habitats while boosting the state's agricultural output. This farming method poses no impact or pressure on existing wild stone crab populations or their habitats.
1231.activities: For the last five years, the research for this project has been conducted at Mote Marine Institute to determine the feasibility of breeding and rearing Florida Stone Crabs in inland recirculating aquatic systems, with no interface with the Gulf or Florida waters, in effort to protect our state's environmental resources. This project is now production-ready and these funds will support this new farming industry.
1231.direct_services: Florida's stone crab industry contributes over $30 million to the state's economy each year and is one of the most expensive seafoods you can buy. The price and value of stone crab claws is steadily increasing so the efforts ensure the crab population stays healthy and bountiful, while satisfying consumer demand. Improve agricultural production/promotion/education; Enhance/preserve/improve environ
1231.population: These funds will help support an entirely new agriculture industry to the State of Florida. The stone crab demonstration project utilizes a best practices approach to sustainable commercial aquaculture production that addresses the growing demand for safe seafood resources by Florida Consumers.
1231.outcome: Raising crabs in a controlled setting, aquaculture can supplement wild stocks, potentially creating a more consistent supply to meet consumer demand and protect the wild population. This would help safeguard the livelihoods of fishermen, seafood markets, and restaurants that depend on the stone crab industry.

1731.description: PEMHS/Eleos has been providing acute inpatient crisis care for over 40 years. The population served are uninsured, underinsured, indigent, and those at risk, who present as suicidal, homicidal and unable to care for themselves due to mental illness. The goal of the project is to increase safety by replacing the roofs on our crisis stabilization unit and staff buildings. The roofs have been patched and over time have reached the end of their useful life. This will ensure the ability to continue to provide services and shelter in place in case of threat of a hurricane or other natural disaster, allowing us to remain operational during and after an emergency event. It is time and labor intensive as well as costly to transfer individuals in need of acute inpatient care to other facilities. This can also place a strain on EMS and other already over burdened transport services during these tim
1731.purpose: The goal is to harden our Crisis Stabilization Unit and staff buildings by replacing roofs that have been patched and have reached the end of their useful life. This will ensure that services are provided and those housed will be safe and able to shelter in place in case of a hurricane or natural disaster and receive uninterrupted care, and that the facility can remain operational during and after an event.
1731.activities: The crisis stabilization unit provides services for individuals who present as a danger to themselves or others or who are unable to care for themselves due to a mental illness. They require acute inpatient care and are in need of safety monitoring, individual and group counseling, medication if needed, medical assessment and evaluation, and collaborative discharge planning. This funding will allow us to harden our buildings to be able to shelter in place to continue needed services, instead of
1731.direct_services: Services provided are crisis hotline support, crisis stabilization services, safety monitoring, assessment and examination for medical needs, psychiatric evaluation to determine if Baker Act criteria is met, medication if needed, group and individual therapy and collaborative discharge planning. These funds will allow those persons in psychiatric crisis, and in need of safe and secure level of car
1731.population: The target population are individuals who meet Baker Act criteria and are a danger to themselves or others, and unable to care for themselves due to mental illness, uninsured, low income, homeless, and those at risk. These individuals meet indigent financial criteria and have no means of paying for these services to access care. 4,700 individuals are served by the facilities that will be improved by these funds.
1731.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is that individuals can remain safely housed in a familiar setting with familiar staff during a hurricane, or other emergency event and receive uninterrupted mental health services identified by the treatment team. The project will eliminate or reduce transfer of individuals to local hospitals and reduce the strain placed on EMS and other transport services. The methodology used to measure this outcome is the number of times the facility was able to shelter in place during a hurricane or other disaster during the life of the replaced roofs.

1273.description: The A-FIRST project is an innovative system that transforms storm water into reclaimed water supplement, reducing withdrawals from the Floridan Aquifer and protecting the Wekiva Basin, one of Florida’s most sensitive and valuable ecosystems. The proposed upgrade will rehabilitate the RAF’s (a key component of the A-FIRST project) critical aging infrastructure and double its treatment capacity from 3.0 to 6.0 MGD. The proposed improvements will ensure treatment reliability, redundancy, compliance with stringent water quality standards and provides additional reclaimed water for the region.
1273.purpose: The project will double treatment capacity from 3.0 to 6.0 MGD of stormwater for use as a supplement for reclaimed water for irrigation uses. This innovative system transforms stormwater into reclaimed water, reducing withdrawals from the Floridan Aquifer and protecting the Wekiva River and Basin, one of Florida’s most sensitive and valuable ecosystems. By doubling the treatment capacity the project will help reduce Floridan Aquifer withdrawals by providing reclaimed water for irrigation. Improv

1273.direct_services: Expands regional reclaimed capacity/supply to supporting partner cities. The treatment capacity of the RAF will increase from 3.0 MGD to 6.0 MGD, allowing additional stormwater to be treated at the RAF and used as reclaimed water supplement. Use of treated stormwater as reclaimed water supplement will reduce the need for high quality groundwater from the Floridan aquifer for non potable irrigation
1273.population: The project primarily benefits neighboring communities within the regional reclaimed water partnership area. The approximate populations of these interested communities are as follows: City of Ocoee – 51,000; City of Winter Garden – 48,000; City of Winter Park – 30,000; City of Mount Dora - 18,000 and Seminole County – over 200,000 residents. It should be noted that reclaimed water from this project will be delivered in bulk quantities to participating utilities, and the actual population served
1273.outcome: The projects is expected to benefit in the following ways: - Reduce Floridan Aquifer withdrawals by providing reclaimed water for irrigation - Improve groundwater and surface water quality - Protect the Wekiva River & Basin - Advance Wekiva BMAP & CFWI compliance

1418.organization: Hearing the Ovarian Cancer Whisper, Inc.
1418.description: H.O.W.’s Glenda M. Wright Angel Fund provides financial assistance to women battling ovarian cancer, allowing them to focus on healing rather than financial hardship. The program helps cover essential living and medical expenses, including rent, utilities, transportation, and treatment-related costs. With additional funding, the Angel Fund can expand its reach to support approximately 40 women and extend the duration of assistance to three months, offering greater financial stability and continuity of care throughout treatment.
1418.purpose: The funds will provide financial assistance to women undergoing ovarian cancer treatment, helping them maintain access to care, complete prescribed treatment plans, and reduce the stress and anxiety caused by financial hardship.
1418.activities: The funds will provide direct financial assistance to women who are experiencing financial hardship. Assistance will cover essential living and medical expenses such as rent, utilities, transportation, and medications. The aid will help women maintain stability and access to care throughout their treatment.
1418.direct_services: Each recipient of an award will receive approximately $5,000 per month for three months to help pay for rent, utilities, transportation, medical costs, and other essential expenses during treatment.
1418.population: Women in Florida undergoing treatment for ovarian cancer who are in financial need.
1418.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project are reduced barriers to treatment and improved health and quality-of-life outcomes for women with ovarian cancer. H.O.W. will measure these outcomes by tracking treatment adherence, continuity of care, and self-reported health status from participants and providers. Additionally, pre- and post- assistance surveys will be conducted to assess changes in stress levels, emotional well-being, and financial stability among recipients.

1509.description: The Infinite Spectrum Foundation provides hands-on creative media and workforce training for neurodiverse youth to empower individuals on the autism spectrum through confidence building and skill development. Participants learn filmmaking, content creation, graphic design, and/or podcasting while strengthening communication, social skills, and teamwork. The program also offers access to essential technology such as cameras, iPads, and audio equipment that many families cannot afford. Each student completes projects that build a digital portfolio and prepare them for future employment opportunities. Funding will support instructors, equipment, and program operations to serve youth across Leon County and expand meaningful pathways to independence.

Students receive hands-on tech and media training, social skill development, paid internship stipends, and one-time business incentives. Programs are led by certified instructors and guest mentors, offering both structured classes and individualized guidance.
1509.direct_services: Participants gain access to professional equipment, software, and materials, allowing them to build digital portfolios, showcase their work publicly, and develop confidence and community engagement. Mentorship and career support help prepare participants for internships and future employment opportunities.
1509.population: This project serves teens and young adults on the autism spectrum, ages 12–22, in Leon County, with approximately 30 - 45 individuals expected to engage annually across all programs.
1509.outcome: Participants will gain technical expertise, creative storytelling and marketing skills, and professional readiness. Outcomes will be measured through completed digital portfolios, certifications earned, internship placements, job placements, and participant and family feedback.

2241.outcome: CP Works will expand to employ 20 Chapman clients through its bridge employment program and will enhance our current efforts of assisting 550 clients through workforce development and employment initiatives. The program will help homeless men and women obtain employment fostering housing stability and ensure they participate in 75% (3 of 4) of the following benchmarks: 1) one-to-one education support, 2) life skills training, 3) one-to-one employment coaching, and 4) upskills/reskills apprenticeship. Additional success metrics for CP Works include the number of participants transitioning into stable employment and housing, and the acquisition of at least one industry-recognized credential.

1519.description: Clean Start Initiative, Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting individuals recently released from incarceration or drug rehabilitation centers by providing mentoring and resources for successful reintegration into society. Our mission is to break the cycle of recidivism and poverty affecting our communities, particularly among minority populations, through holistic support and reestablishing connections with families. We are seeking $150,000.00 to fund our 12-step mentoring program designed to support participants through structured weekly sessions, ensuring they have access to essential resources provided by government agencies and private institutions. Over the past five years, Clean Start Initiative, Inc. has successfully mentored over 500 individuals, leading to improved family dynamics, reduced recidivism, and increased community involvement. With your fi
1519.purpose: The Clean Start Initiative's 12-step program includes structured weekly sessions that blend mentoring, life skills training, and family engagement. The objective is to provide ongoing support for participants throughout their reintegration process.
1519.activities: Week Focus Area 1 Orientation 2 Self-Assessment 3 Life Skills Development 4 Health & Wellness 5 Family Dynamics 6 Community Resources 7 Personal Goal Setting 8 Coping Strategies 9 Networking Skills 10 Mock Interviews 11 Implementation of Goals 12 Program Evaluation & Celebration
1519.direct_services: 1. Introduce participants to the program's structure, establish rapport, and set personalized goals. 2. Facilitate discussions around personal experiences, challenges, and strengths. 3. Workshops on budgeting, job searching, and effective communication. 4. Discussion on physical and mental health resources, including substance abuse recovery techniques. 5. Engage family members in discussions abou
1519.population: Plan to serve: 1 - 800 participants per year in the below demographics Racial Demographics Age Distribution Economic Status African American 58% 18-25 22% Below Poverty Line 78% White 35% 26-35 41% Working Class 15% Hispanic 5% 36-45 25% Middle Class 5% Other 2% 46+ 12% Other 2%
1519.outcome: Goals and Objectives 1. Reduce Recidivism: Decrease the rates of re-incarceration by 15% among participants. 2. Family Reconnection: Assist 80% of participants in reconnecting with at least one family member through our resources. 3. Employment: Secure jobs for 70% of program graduates through workforce development coaching

1522.description: The funds will equip Gadsden County Sheriff, Fire Rescue, and 911 Dispatch with reliable, P25-compliant interoperable radios, strengthening coverage and coordination within the county, across the region, and with state agencies during disasters and critical events. These enhancements will improve responder safety and support more effective mutual aid to neighboring areas.
1522.purpose: The requested funds will equip Gadsden County Sheriff, Fire Rescue, and 911 Dispatch with dependable, P25- compliant interoperable radios to strengthen coverage and coordination across the county, region, and with state and federal agencies during disasters and critical incidents. These upgrades will improve responder safety and support more effective mutual aid to neighboring communities.
1522.activities: The project will deliver secure, reliable SLERS radio communications that enable first responders to respond quickly and accurately to emergencies within the county while also supporting mutual aid coordination with state and federal users.
1522.direct_services: Once completed, the upgraded systems will enable first responders in Gadsden County to deliver faster, more accurate, and effective responses to emergency service requests.
1522.population: This project will serve Gadsden County’s residents, along with local businesses, schools, and visitors. By improving emergency communications, it will ensure faster, safer responses to protect the entire community while also strengthening mutual aid for surrounding areas and travelers through the county.
1522.outcome: The expected benefits provided by the implementation of this project include improved communication for sheriff, Fire Rescue, and emergency services with P25-compliant equipment, improving coverage and interoperability, and reduced response times. Outcomes will be measured by tracking response times and incident resolution.

1524.organization: Brehon Institute for Family Services, Inc.
1524.description: Founded in 1992, Brehon House provides safe, transitional housing for unhoused, pregnant women and their infants in Tallahassee. At no cost to residents, the program offers a stable, nurturing environment with comprehensive services aimed at improving outcomes for both mothers and children. Brehon House accommodates six women, along with their newborns and toddlers, at a time. Eligible residents must be 18 or older, pregnant upon enrollment, homeless or in unsafe living conditions, and free from a criminal history that poses a risk to others. Residents must also agree to abide by house rules. Brehon House supports mothers by offering a safe space for them and their children (up to age 3), helping break the cycle of homelessness and promoting healthy pregnancies and early childhood development.
1524.purpose: Funds will support direct client assistance to enhance service delivery and promote longer term stabilization for families. Technology funds will upgrade all staff computer stations to improve documentation, case management, and service delivery. Updated computers will ensure efficient administrative operations and accurate recordkeeping. Additionally, computers will be available for residents to pursue education, job searches, and skill-building opportunities that support long-term stability an
1524.activities: Activities include providing financial aid such as rental and utility assistance, meeting essential shelter needs, and supporting individualized services that help residents achieve stability, self-sufficiency, and long-term housing security. Additionally, more access to technology for workforce training, job searching, and educational pursuits.
1524.direct_services: The appropriations will enhance the current service delivery and provide the ability to expand our efforts for longer term client stabilization. Direct client assistance such as financial assistance when entering into housing or financial assistance in securing the necessary documentation (ID, birth certificates, etc) to qualify for housing. Clients will meet with the case manager once a week to d
1524.population: The target population for this program is unhoused, pregnant women and their children. We anticipate serving at least 25 women and children annually.
1524.outcome: The expected benefit and outcome of this project is to increase the longevity of client stabilization. The overarching goal is to reduce recidivism into shelters. By providing direct client assistance, we are able to alleviate a portion of the financial burden that residents experience. In doing so, we are able to stabilize them longer term.

1275.organization: Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts
1275.description: The Sound System Renovation Project will modernize the audio infrastructure of one of Florida’s most celebrated cultural venues- Walt Disney Theater in the Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts. As the premier amplified performance space in Central Florida, the theater hosts Broadway productions, comedy shows, musical concerts, community events, and educational programs that enrich and inspire audiences. This project will enhance the experience for audiences and performers alike, expand programming opportunities, and ensure greater accessibility for all patrons. Investing in this technological modernization strengthens Florida’s position as a leader in the performing arts and supports a vibrant, inclusive cultural ecosystem that benefits the entire community, the state and the world.
1275.purpose: The project will modernize the decade-old Walt Disney Theater sound system to deliver world-class audio, improving clarity in every seat, reducing load-in time, lowering rental costs, and enhancing assisted-listening access. This investment protects revenue, keeps the venue competitive for first-run tours, and reinforces the Dr. Phillips Center as a premier cultural destination attracting audiences locally, statewide, and internationally.
1275.activities: The funds will be used to implement a comprehensive upgrade of the Walt Disney Theater’s sound system. This includes assessing the current infrastructure, procuring professional-grade audio equipment, and installing and integrating the new system to ensure seamless operation for all types of performances. The project will also include calibration and testing to optimize sound quality, as well as training for theater staff to operate and maintain the system effectively. These activities will enha
1275.direct_services: The enhanced audio infrastructure will provide direct services to citizens by delivering a high-quality auditory experience for every performance. Audiences will benefit from clearer, more immersive sound during Broadway productions, orchestral concerts, community events, and educational programs, while also providing performers with the tools and equipment necessary to deliver an elite performanc
1275.population: The largest target population served by this project includes local residents and over 75 million visitors from across Florida and around the world who not only attend performances but also perform a plethora of shows at the Walt Disney Theater. Welcoming nearly 500,000 patrons annually, the theater plays a vital role in driving tourism and enriching Florida’s cultural landscape. The upgraded sound system will enhance the experience for every guest, attract new productions and audiences, and str
1275.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a fully modernized sound system that delivers superior audio quality, reliability, and accessibility for all performances at the Walt Disney Theater. This enhancement will improve the audience experience, expand programming capacity, and attract new touring productions, community events, and visitors from across the state and beyond. The project’s success will be measured through key performance indicators, including patron satisfaction surveys, audience attendance data, increased event bookings, and positive feedback from performers and production partners. Together, these metrics will demonstrate the project’s role in strengthening Florida’s cultural

2009.organization: Lee Health System, Inc. d/b/a Lee Health
2009.description: The Lee Health Graduate Medical Education Center at Gulf Coast Medical Center will serve as a regional hub for physician training in high-demand specialties. The state-of-the-art facility will include simulation labs, classrooms, and clinical education space to expand the physician workforce and improve access to quality care across Southwest Florida.
2009.purpose: Funds will support construction of the Lee Health Graduate Medical Education Center at Gulf Coast Medical Center, expanding capacity to train physicians in high-demand specialties. The project will strengthen Florida's healthcare workforce and improve access to quality care.
2009.activities: Funds will be used for fixed capital construction of the Graduate Medical Education Center, including design, permitting, site development, facility build out, and installation of simulation and clinical training infrastructure to support physician education and workforce expansion.
2009.direct_services: The project will expand access to care by increasing the number of physicians trained and retained in Southwest Florida. Citizens will benefit from enhanced availability of healthcare providers, improved patient outcomes, and strengthened medical and trauma services.
2009.population: The project serves patients across Lee, Charlotte, Collier, Hendry, and Glades Counties. Lee Health provides over one million patient contacts annually. The center will train up to 400 residents each year, expanding the physician workforce and improving access to care across the region.
2009.outcome: The project will expand Florida's physician workforce, improving access to care and patient outcomes across Southwest Florida. Success will be measured by the number of residents trained and retained locally, program accreditation outcomes, and annual economic impact analyses.

2010.description: The Institute of Health Careers, Inc (IHC) aims to bridge the gap between the supply and demand of knowledgeable and trained health care professionals in the SW Florida region (Lee, Collier, Glades, Hendry, Charlotte counties), by addressing and alleviating the nursing shortage crisis. This project request is for educating and training Home Health Aides (HHAs), Certified Nursing Assistants (CNAs), and Medical Assistants (MAs) within our communities. IHC intends to service 120 students follows, 60 CNAs, 48 HHAs, and 12 MAs, if approved. Our licensed and accredited institution provides rigorous curriculums and prepares our graduates for real life experiences, thus producing highly competent and industry ready healthcare professionals capable of providing high quality care in an array of settings.
2010.purpose: The goal is to address the growing need for healthcare professionals for Florida's aging population, specifically SW Florida; whereby reducing the number of job vacancies and increasing the workforce. This will result in students earning in-demand industry credentials to begin financially sustainable careers.
2010.activities: Successful completion of the training program will lead to employment opportunities within the healthcare sector. Our Academic support personnel will assist students with credentialing exam preparation and job readiness.
2010.direct_services: Provide financial support that allows students to complete their program, whereby resulting in employment and self sufficiency.
2010.population: The targeted population is the unemployed, underemployed, single parents, minorities, socially/economically disadvantaged, at-risk age-appropriate persons, high school/college students, and persons wanting to upskill. IHC is expected to serve 120 persons.
2010.outcome: Increase the healthcare workforce, decrease vacancies, provide grants to persons who would not have been able to financially afford the training, job placement, high wage jobs, providing job stability and opportunities for career development/advancement in the healthcare sector, and strengthening the economy. IHC is required to track, maintain detailed documentation of, and report student retention, graduation, completion, placement, and credentialing data by ABHES (accreditor) and Florida CIE annually.

2437.description: Sanibel’s shared use path system (26 miles) experienced damage from the storm surge wash over and subsequent damage from debris placement on the ROW from Hurricanes Ian, Helene, and Milton. Sanibel is requesting funds to repair/repave and elevate where needed, approximately 10-12 miles of the shared use path system. The system is critical in supporting resident transportation year round and heavy use by visitors during the busy tourist season. During various times of the year, Sanibel's roadway system which also provides the only access to Captiva (unincorporated Lee County) is congested and the shared use path provides a safe and well used alternative means of transportation that is separated from vehicular travel ways.
2437.purpose: Repair and potentially widen and/or elevate portions of the shared use path for safe use by walkers, runners, and bicyclists.
2437.activities: Repair/repave, widen, and elevate where needed, approximately 7-9 miles of the shared use pathway on Sanibel that has been damaged from the storm surge and storm debris from Hurricanes Ian, Helene, and Milton.
2437.direct_services: Sanibel residents and visitors will benefit from improvements that will make the shared use path system safer for public use.
2437.population: The general public will be served by the project. Approximately 100,000+ people will be served by this project annually.
2437.outcome: A safe shared use path for use by walkers, runners, and bicyclists. Outcome measured by sustained/increased use of the shared use pathway.

2082.description: The purpose of this project is to build on previous restoration efforts in the Caloosahatchee River Estuary (CRE) by restoring an additional 50 acres of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV), specifically tape grass (Vallisneria neotropicalis). This is part of a larger effort to restore over 352 acres in the CRE.
2082.purpose: The purpose of this project is to provide an additional 50 acres of habitat restoration in the Caloosahatchee River. This project will help achieve transformational change within the river.
2082.activities: The funds will be spent on project management; cultivation/installation of 256,250 nursery-grown tape grass plants; protection of plants with 1,250 herbivory exclusion cages and navigational aids for boaters; maintenance of the herbivory exclusion cages and plants; reporting and scientific review; and a public outreach campaign.
2082.direct_services: The project will provide direct services to citizens in Lee County by improving CRE water quality and clarity; reducing harmful algal blooms; creating habitat for important recreational fish species; improving natural infrastructure resiliency; enhancing ecotourism and other recreational opportunities; and building resiliency.
2082.population: Both the local and state economy will benefit from this project. The local economy includes Lee County's population of over 822,000 Floridians and FL's population of over 22 million (based on the 2022 U.S. census).This project will have direct positive impacts to the seafood industry, ecotourism industry, recreational boating industry, real estate industry, and the tourism industry since each of these industries are dependent on healthy habitats and clean water. The indirect benefits of this pro
2082.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is the restoration and enhancement of 50 acres of native SAV in the Caloosahatchee River. Installed planting units will be monitored for three years and an ecological study will occur to further quantify project impacts. A portion of the monitoring will be conducted by Florida Gulf Coast University.

1176.description: Citywide stormwater infrastructure and canal embankment assessments and rehabilitation to increase stormwater delivery capacity and reduce the development of depressions and cracks on other right of way improvements (i.e. asphalt surfaces, swales, curb/gutters, and sidewalks) due to subsurface settlement. Restoration of stormwater infrastructure improvements for resiliency is necessary in order to continue protecting the community, property and the environment, while preserving drainage basins and mitigating flood risks.
1176.purpose: Attain and maintain adequate stormwater system and infrastructure resiliency and functionality.
1176.activities: Citywide stormwater infrastructure and canal embankment rehabilitation will increase stormwater delivery capacity and reduce the development of depressions and cracks on other right of way improvements (i.e. asphalt surfaces, swales, curb/gutters, and sidewalks) due to subsurface settlement. Restoration of stormwater infrastructure improvements for resiliency is necessary in order to continue protecting the community, property and the environment, while preserving drainage basins and mitigating
1176.direct_services: Services include conditions assessments and/or infrastructure repairs and rehabilitation.
1176.population: City of Margate with a population of approximately 60,000.
1176.outcome: Protection of the ecosystem which thrives within and around the canal system. A reduction in incidence of flooding under normal rainfall conditions. Improve system resiliency against sea level rise. Benefits can be measured by comparing improvements before and after as well as measured incidence of flood damage.

1372.description: This project will enhance a critical one mile roadway corridor by improving safety, accessibility, and resilience. This corridor serves more than 44,000 people in Broward County, including over 4,000 local residents, and accommodates 12,000 daily trips. The corridor connects two major roadways that provide access to the barrier island, and serves as the only alternative evacuation route to A1A. These improvements will create a safer, more accessible, and resilient transportation corridor.
1372.purpose: These enhancements will provide safer pedestrian access for children and a significant elderly population who use the corridor to reach important destinations for recreation, mobility, and social engagement. Our stormwater upgrades will also support emergency response operations, as this is a major route for first responders. Together, these improvements will create a safer, more accessible corridor.
1372.activities: These improvements will create a safer, more accessible, and resilient transportation corridor that supports daily mobility, emergency preparedness, and community connectivity.
1372.direct_services: Safer pedestrian access for children and a significant elderly population who use the corridor to reach important destinations for recreation, mobility, and daily needs.
1372.population: All 4,000 residents and visitors- over 44,000 people.
1372.outcome: The benefits are safety, pedestrian and traffic flow and will be measured by reporting pedestrian-related incidents and improved safety perceptions among residents. Enhanced lighting, sidewalks, and drainage will decrease environmental and crime-related risks, with surveys showing higher levels of safety and greater pedestrian activity during evening hours.

1614.description: To design, pilot, and make statewide-ready, a family-based digital addiction and mental health program that started in Leon County schools and Sheriff's Department. Our website, brochures, other materials, gives parents and youth shared tools to reduce harmful screen use. The project has two parts: (1) Family Digital & Mental Health Bootcamp and (2) spreading information, resources, and solutions for Digital Addiction with a cyber-bullying emphasis: ParentDigitalAnswers.org. Bill Montford and David Sikes of the state superintendent's office wants this in all 67 county school districts.
1614.purpose: The requested funds will directly support our most effective outreach tool: high-quality printed brochures that drive parents, grandparents, and youth to our educational website, ParentDigitalAnswers.org. While we actively use modern digital platforms, our data shows that brochures remain our strongest catalyst for engagement, prompting families to seek deeper guidance online. Our overarching mission is to combat digital addiction by equipping families with clear, practical knowledge about the r
1614.activities: To advance our mission and maximize the impact of grant funding, we deliver a range of educational presentations and community outreach services tailored to schools, families, and local leaders. Our presentations vary in length and depth to meet the needs of each audience. For example, our 20-minute briefing to the Leon County School Board was so effective that the district purchased 6,000 brochures and distributed 100 to the front office of each of its 47 schools. We also provide longer, one-ho
1614.direct_services: This project will deliver a wide range of direct services to citizens, ensuring families receive practical, accessible guidance on digital safety. Local residents will benefit from our Public Service Announcements (PSAs), which have already aired more than 3,000 times on local ABC, CBS, and NBC affiliates, significantly expanding community awareness. We also conduct educational sessions at school
1614.population: This project serves families, students, educators, and public safety personnel across 17 counties west of Madison and Taylor counties. Our outreach focuses primarily on school-aged youth ages 8 to 18, as well as the parents, grandparents, guardians, teachers, and law enforcement officers who support them. College-age students have also shown strong interest and benefit from our presentations. In Leon County (Tallahassee) alone, we have delivered over 50 presentations to school groups, sheriff’s
1614.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a measurable increase in family awareness, safety, and balance regarding digital use, along with a reduction in digital-related harms such as cyberbullying, excessive gaming, and exposure to unsafe online content. To evaluate these outcomes, we rely on surveys and data collection from schools, parents, and community partners. For example, the Leon County School District distributed a districtwide survey to all 47 schools—including principals, assistant principals, counselors, social workers, psychologists, and district staff—regarding the frequency and impact of cyberbullying. Survey results confirmed that every school experiences cyberbullying weekly,

1525.description: The Florida Sheriffs Association proposes building the Florida Sheriffs Youth Learning Center as a place for children to visit and learn more about the honor and tradition of serving in law enforcement. The center and annex building will be a facility for youth to explore the possibilities of a future career as a law enforcement officer, correctional deputy, dispatcher or civilian employee in a sheriffs office by connecting them with a series of interactive displays, videos and activities that will inspire them.
1525.purpose: The Florida Sheriffs Association proposes building the Florida Sheriffs Youth Learning Center as a place for children to visit and learn more about the honor and tradition of serving in law enforcement. The center will be a facility for youth to explore the possibilities of a future career as a law enforcement officer, correctional deputy, dispatcher or civilian employee in a sheriffs office by connecting them with a series of interactive displays, videos and activities that will inspire them.
1525.activities: The Florida Sheriffs Youth Learning Center will be a place for children and young adults to be exposed to the values of a career in law enforcement. Visitors will get to experience the more than 200 year history of the office of sheriff in Florida as well as learn about how law enforcement officers, dispatchers and correctional deputies work to keep citizens safe.
1525.direct_services: There will be a theater room for viewing an educational history film. Visitors will also have opportunities to use a driving simulator, experience receiving and dispatching calls for service and well as engage in numerous interactive displays that will motivate them to both appreciate and consider a career in law enforcement.
1525.population: Children and young adults will experience a variety of displays and experiences that will educate them on the numerous roles inside a sheriff's office. Visitors will learn about the 200 year history of the office of sheriff in Florida. They will find out how sheriffs and their deputies worked to make many of the cultural progresses that led Florida to become the 3rd largest state in the country. More than 800 children a year are expected to visit the center.
1525.outcome: Children and young adults will experience a variety of displays and experiences that will educate them on the numerous roles inside a sheriff's office. Visitors will learn about the 200 year history of the office of sheriff in Florida. They will find out how sheriffs and their deputies worked to make many of the cultural progresses that led Florida to become the 3rd largest state in the country. Visitors will be asked a series of questions upon departure to gain a better understanding of what they learned at the center.

2881.organization: The Packs of Love Foundation, Inc
2881.description: The Packs of Love Foundation serves as a trusted resource and passionate advocate for youth in foster care and young adults transitioning out of the system. Through our four core pillars: crisis stabilization, life skills development, scholarship advancement, and pathways to normalcy. We’re committed to empowering futures by providing access to essential resources, transformative workshops, and meaningful opportunities that nurture their educational, financial, and personal well-being. Project: To sustain the longevity of our impact & continue supporting the personal well-being of youth in foster care & young adults aging out.
2881.purpose: To sustain the longevity of our impact & continue supporting the personal well-being of youth in foster care & young adults aging out. We'll build capacity by hiring staff to sustain & build programs like expanding crisis stabilization efforts through care packages, offering life-development workshops & scholarships to impact the futures of individuals affected by foster care & fostering normalcy for high school seniors who need help participating in prom, senior photos, & graduation activities.
2881.activities: We will hire & train staff & expand our care package donation program, our life skill workshop offerings, which will strengthen the impact of our Promise Pathway Program, & build our Pathway to Normalcy Program to assist high school seniors in foster care with senior year & graduation activities.
2881.direct_services: Direct services include care package distribution, individualized life-skills coaching, mentorship, scholarship disbursement, and youth engagement workshops. Each service directly benefits youth in foster care and young adults transitioning out by reducing barriers to stability, improving emotional well-being, and increasing their access to education and community resources. Families and caregiver
2881.population: Target population: At-risk youth, High school students, Economic disadvantage persons, Victims of crime, Homeless, Persons with poor mental and physical health. Age: 14-21 During the 2026-2027 fiscal year, we plan to serve 51-100 youth through our four pillar programs.
2881.outcome: Improve physical and mental health by providing essential hygiene products, coping tools, and wellness resources that promote confidence and self-care. Enhance educational and economic outcomes through financial literacy, career readiness, and mentorship that strengthen life skills and self-sufficiency. Foster emotional stability and a sense of normalcy by offering consistent support systems that nurture belonging, build resilience, and celebrate milestones. Promote healthy decision-making and reduce risks of substance abuse through positive engagement, guidance, and trauma-informed mentorship. Progress will be measured through care package tracking, pre- and post-program surveys, mentorship

1147.description: In FY 2021–2022, 1,739 youths were arrested in Miami-Dade, continuing a long-term decline. A University of Miami and Miami-Dade Economic Advocacy Trust study found youth arrests dropped 76% from 2010 (6,986) to 2022 (1,654), though there was a slight increase from 2021 to 2022. The share of arrested youth residing in Miami-Dade fell from 94% in 2010 to 90% in 2022. To further reduce arrests, Regis House, Inc. proposes expanding its diversion program with mental health counseling and family therapy to address underlying issues. Research shows family-based diversion reduces rearrest rates to 4%, compared to 17% overall, strengthening communities.
1147.purpose: Funding this program strengthens protective factors for high-risk youth and their families, reducing recidivism and promoting prosocial behaviors. With over 154,000 Miami-Dade residents uninsured and many underinsured (U.S. Census), access to mental health services remains a challenge. This investment helps address community needs and lowers the long-term costs associated with crime recidivism.
1147.activities: The Adolescent & Families Outpatient Program (AFOP) works to prevent crime and reduce recidivism through timely interventions for high-risk youth and families. It promotes prosocial behaviors by teaching conflict resolution, communication, and problem-solving skills while addressing trauma, poverty, peer influence, and mental health, including substance abuse. AFOP reinforces positive behaviors, improves court compliance, and helps youth with criminal histories become contributing members of soc
1147.direct_services: This year-round program operates at two Miami-Dade locations and offers in-person and Telehealth counseling, individual and family therapy, and parenting sessions by licensed professionals and supervised interns. Youth and families receive a comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment, with adolescents completing at least 12 therapy sessions and substance testing. Guardians join parenting and family
1147.population: The program serves adolescents arrested or cited and mandated to mental health counseling, mainly from low- income, high-crime areas. Common charges include aggravated assault, burglary, auto theft, and firearm possession; 90% are from minority groups. The goal is to enroll 180 youth annually, providing group, individual, and family therapy based on biopsychosocial assessments, plus weekly youth and parenting sessions. Regis House has partnered with the Department of Juvenile Justice and Miami-D
1147.outcome: The program builds resilience in youth and families, reducing rearrest rates and costly confinement (averaging $588/day). Each adolescent is assigned a lead counselor who reports monthly to probation officers. Fewer than 10% are expected to be unsuccessfully discharged due to rearrest, with a 70% successful discharge rate and 90% satisfaction among participants. Enrollment lasts at least three months, averaging 45 participants at any time.

1301.description: Palm Beach State College would like to expand its current automotive/diesel certificate program to help certify more technicians in diagnosing and repairing electric vehicles. Training future students in learning how to diagnose and repair EVs/hybrids & alternative fuel vehicles will benefit the community, state and population at large as more employees in this industry and aims to address the growing demand for skilled technicians in the emerging field of electric vehicle technology.
1301.purpose: Creating a new curriculum and training future students in learning how to diagnose and repair EVs/hybrids/alternative fuels will benefit the community, state and population at large as more of those cars will be manufacture, purchased and driven. By expanding Palm Beach State College's current automotive program, we will be preparing future students to meet the evolving needs of the automotive industry. This expansion is essential given the increasing prevalence of electric vehicles/hybrids on t
1301.activities: Students should be able to complete their cohort in approximately 8-9 months and therefore be placed at local dealerships, fleet management services and/or other arenas to fill talent pipelines rather quickly.
1301.direct_services: The benefits of this expansion are multi-faceted. Firstly, it equips our students with the expertise required to diagnose and repair electric vehicles/hybrids, positioning them as highly valuable assets in the workforce. As more individuals choose electric vehicles, the demand for technicians with specialized skills in EV/hybrid maintenance will continue to rise. Secondly, this initiative aligns w
1301.population: Palm Beach State College anticipates serving anywhere between 100-200 students in our first year the program is offered. The target population would consist of unemployed people looking to gain a new skill/certificate for work in an up-and-coming automotive industry, high school and college level students looking for the same, as well as anyone in the workforce looking to upskill their current automotive technology skills or those seeking this program out as a potential next career move.
1301.outcome: By expanding Palm Beach State College's program to include electric vehicle/hybrid training, we are not only meeting the demands of the evolving automotive landscape but also contributing to the creation of a skilled workforce. This, in turn, helps establish a pipeline of qualified technicians who can seamlessly integrate into the automotive industry, ultimately benefiting the community, the state, and the broader population. As we anticipate the continued growth of the electric vehicle/hybrid market, this initiative positions our programs to be a leader in providing education that is both forward-thinking and responsive to industry needs. 2060.description: The purpose of the funding is to continue strengthening the statewide ecosystem fueling therapeutic innovation and biotech development and to cultivate thematic centers of excellence poised to address grand challenges in health research facing people in Florida and beyond. Plans envision growing the institute's faculty roster of principal investigators, expanding and updating its core scientific services, and building up its emerging centers of excellence.
2060.purpose: The purpose of the funding is to continue strengthening the statewide ecosystem fueling therapeutic innovation and biotech development and to cultivate thematic centers of excellence poised to address grand challenges in health research facing people in Florida and beyond. Plans envision growing the institute's faculty roster of principal investigators, expanding and updating its core scientific services, and building up its emerging centers of excellence.
2060.activities: Funds will support cutting-edge medical research and the expansion of the biotech ecosystem in Florida.
2060.direct_services: Wertheim UF Scripps Institute laboratories apply expertise in chemical biology, structural biology, microbiology, immunology, neuroscience, and molecular medicine to advance drug discovery. The Institute has identified strategic opportunities to augment faculty expertise, broaden fellowship opportunities, jumpstart scientific innovation, enhance/expand SUS access to exceptional core facilities.
2060.population: Thousands of target populations, including elderly, persons with poor mental and/or physical health, disabled persons, high school students and college students. Also, Florida-based companies aimed at accelerating development of innovative medicines.
2060.outcome: Impactful research on extending and improving the lives of Floridians; new innovative medicines; increased research through the Natural Products Discovery Center to benefit Florida's agricultural industry; increased capacity for undergraduate, graduate, and post doc research as well as training the next generation of researchers based in Florida; and job partnerships and growth in the bio-tech industry.

2767.description: A one-year pilot serving ~100 adults (veterans, and displaced workers) in Central FL. Delivers 12-week job- readiness/soft-skills, digital/financial literacy, and civic re-entry. Provides employment referrals, and referrals to licensed mental-health/substance-use counselors. Includes monthly Fitness & Wellness Day (exercise, stress-management, nutrition). Targets: improved employability and wellness, reduced recidivism/substance use, and increased self- sufficiency & community stability.
2767.purpose: To provide adults—including returning veterans, and displaced workers with comprehensive job-readiness, workforce resilience, civic education, and wellness services that improve employability, reduce recidivism, and promote physical and mental health.
2767.activities: Includes job-readiness and soft-skills training, digital literacy instruction, financial literacy, civic engagement education, mental-health and substance-abuse referrals, employment referrals, and monthly Fitness & Wellness Days to support physical and emotional wellness.
2767.direct_services: Participants receive a 12-week training program, access to job referrals, civic education workshops, and wellness activities. Each participant receives individualized mentorship, completion certificates, and follow-up coaching.
2767.population: Returning veterans, and adults displaced by economic or government layoffs (approx. 100 participants per year).
2767.outcome: Improved physical and mental health, reduced recidivism and substance abuse, adult diversion from the criminal justice system, enhanced economic self-sufficiency and family stability, immediate job opportunities, civic and cultural enrichment, and strengthened community reintegration.

1656.organization: Florida Alliance for Assistive Services and
1656.description: Funding will be used to continue the growth of assistive technology services provided by FAAST, the states assistive technology program, to individuals who have disabilities. All services are provided at no cost to Floridians. The funds will go directly to program costs for the FAAST regional demonstration center partners with a focus on meeting increased needs to continue providing expanded services while also creating new regional partners to fill service gaps in outlying areas. Prior non-recurring funding allowed for service expansion with the addition of new centers that have targeted outlying areas, and this funding will help FAAST support continued expansion.
1656.purpose: The specific purpose of this funding request is to allow FAAST to continue to provide assistive technology (AT) access and services to all Floridians with disabilities through an expanded network of regional demonstration centers (RDC) and collaborative partners. Through prior non-recurring funding, FAAST was able to expand the RDC network resulting in an increase of over 50% in services provided. While this was very successful, data shows that there is still a need to bridge gaps in geographica
1656.activities: FAAST will create better access to assistive technology and assistive technology services to outlying areas while increasing services in core service areas through greater collaboration with other disability, education, and employment service partners. School to work transition and aging/staying in place will be focus areas. Existing regional demonstration centers will become better equipped to serve the areas that are outside of their direct service area. Additionally, these areas will be provi
1656.direct_services: Citizens will be provided with greater access to the core services of FAAST which include AT device demonstrations, allowing for the comparison of various types of AT to assist in decision making activities. AT device trainings which provide citizens with the knowledge and ability to use AT, short term device loans which allow citizens to take home or have AT shipped to them for the purpose of usi
1656.population: The target population consists of: Individuals of any age who have any disability including elderly persons; family members and caregivers of those individuals; anyone else interested in or working with the disability community where assistive technology access or knowledge will improve the work, they provide to those with disabilities. Approximately 2,000 additional individuals will be served through the increased funding bringing total FAAST services provided to over 28,000 for the upcoming ye
1656.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is increased and improved independence for individuals with disabilities through increased access to assistive technology services. Current measurement tools will be incorporated into the project. Performance Measures are collected and reported through an annual progress report requested by the Administration for Community Living and the Florida Department of Education (included in the contract with DOE). Survey questions used to address performance measures are: primary purpose for which demonstrated assistive technology is needed and decision-making outcome; primary purpose of short-term loan and decision-making outcomes; reason for accessing loaned assi

1657.description: This request will modernize aging infrastructure at the outdoor Markham Park Shooting Range, Skeet and Trap in Broward County, heavily used by law enforcement and and regional residents, by replacing 38-year-old range canopies and shelters, upgrading range lighting and flooring, improving ADA-accessible parking and walkways, and constructing a new cart/storage facility. These improvements will enhance safety, access, longevity and energy efficiency of a heavily used public training and recreation facility.
1657.purpose: The funding will directly benefit regional residents, including law enforcement which heavily uses the range, by providing a safe, accessible, and modernized public shooting and training facility. Improvements support law enforcement and community firearm education, ADA access, recreational programs, and competitive events, ensuring long-term use of a heavily used Broward County public amenity.
1657.activities: The demolition of deteriorated range structures, construction of new canopies, shelters, and roofs, installation of LED lighting and wood baffling, replacement of floors with concrete slabs, addition of ADA-compliant parking and walkways, and construction of a new cart and equipment storage facility.
1657.direct_services: This project will provide a safe, accessible, and modernized public shooting and training facility. Improvements support law enforcement and community firearm education, ADA access, recreational programs, and competitive events, ensuring long-term use of a heavily used Broward County public amenity.
1657.population: Citizens in the region seeking to use the target range including police officers. 30,000+ individuals are expected to be served.
1657.outcome: This project will create a safer environment for citizens, law enforcement training, and recreational users, reducing risk of injury and improving overall range safety. The improvements include hardening the structures for hurricane resistance.

1928.description: The City of Groveland is requesting funds for the construction of a new North Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) to address critical capacity, reliability, and redundancy in its wastewater system. The proposed 1 MGD facility will replace the aging Sunshine WRF, which is nearing its design capacity and surrounded by wetlands requiring costly mitigation. A proposed site is located on city-owned property. The proposed North WRF will serve the growing North Sewer Service Area, including accepting flows from the City of Mascotte under an interlocal agreement. The project includes construction of infrastructure needed to improve efficiencies and resiliency and address regional growth.
1928.purpose: The goal that will be achieved is the construction of a new 1 MGD North Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) that will replace the aging Sunshine WRF and provide reliable, resilient, and efficient wastewater treatment. This facility will address current and projected capacity constraints and support regional sewer service including from the City of Mascotte that Groveland has an interlocal agreement with. The project will also improve infrastructure safety and reliability, reduce reliance on onsite
1928.activities: The activities include construction and infrastructure development supporting a new 1 MGD North Water Reclamation Facility (WRF). These activities include constructing lift station infrastructure at the existing Sunshine WRF, installing wastewater force main to the North WRF, building a reclaimed water main and storage tank, and repurposing existing infrastructure to enhance transmission capabilities to the extent possible.
1928.direct_services: By replacing the aging Sunshine WRF, the new facility will improve treatment capacity and reliability, while supporting the regional service commitment with the City of Mascotte.
1928.population: City of Groveland, population 20,621; City of Mascotte, population 7,407. Total number of individuals expected to be served = 28,028.
1928.outcome: The expected outcome of the North WRF project is the development of a modern, centralized wastewater treatment facility that improves the City's ability to manage current and future wastewater demands. By replacing the aging Sunshine WRF, the new facility will improve treatment capacity and reliability, while supporting the regional service commitment with the City of Mascotte. The outcome will be measured by tracking average daily flow against design capacity and monitoring compliance with FDEP permit requirements. Metrics will include system reliability, successful redirection of wastewater flows, and reduced reliance on OSTDS systems.

1409.description: The City of Palm Bay (City) requests funding for site work for Fire Station 8. Fire station 8 to serve the increased population in the northwest section of the city and Heritage High School. Through innovative design, this site work will serve the fire station itself but will also provide wastewater infrastructure for the area.
1409.purpose: The specific purpose of this funding request is to provide the site work for Fire Station 8. This critical site will support the needs of the northwestern portion of the city. In addition to housing the station, this site is also being designed for shared storm water of the city's station development and future widening of Malabar Road.
1409.activities: The City has a prototype station currently designed and under construction. As such, the City will be able to move quickly to build the future fire station, using the prototype design. The City also has contracted Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) firms to expedite construction of the station. Funding for the design and construction elements of the station will be planned for Fiscal Year 2027.
1409.direct_services: Palm Bay Fire Rescue provides an all-hazard response so this fire station will provide immediate fire and EMS responses to this growing area, thereby reduicing response times for more efficient operations and performance of life saving interventions.
1409.population: Residential occupancy, moderate commercial and a high school facility. 2500 - 3500+ citizens.
1409.outcome: The new fire station is expected to improve response times by six minutes and will likely decrease homeowners’ insurance liability by improving the ISO rating. It will also house a mutual aid vehicle from Brevard County.

1281.organization: City of Palm Bay - Police Department
1281.description: The City of Palm Bay is the owner and operator of the Range, a public safety facility that serves residents, businesses and visitors throughout the region. This facility functions as a premier training site for law enforcement agencies across Central Florida, impacting over 8.8 million residents. This new development will honor Sgt. Frank Tobar and will establish a Citizens Police Academy program designed to promote public safety through education, transparency and community engagement. This initiative supports multiple Legislative priorities, including SB1804 and SB1880, by enhancing law enforcement training, providing tools to combats serious crime and protecting its citizens. The project aligns with priorities set by, Department of Justice (DOJ), Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC), and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). It will strengthen inter-agency interoperab
1281.purpose: Assist the City modernize the Range, and provide better equipment for our officers and those from partner agencies. The training facility will promote officers to respond safely, effectively, and professionally, ensuring the protection of both law enforcement personnel and the communities we serve. Increase public safety and emergency response is the overall benefit and outcome while increasing competence, confidence and community orientation of law Enforcement professionals by providing scenari
1281.activities: Assist the enhancement of the current features: 40-Acres of Land, Live Fire Shoot House, 50 Yard Firearms Range, Rifle Range (100 Yard and 400 Yard), Search and Rescue Dive Pond, Skills and Obstacle Training Course, 60 Foot Tactical Rappel Tower, & Training Simulator. The site will continue to provide law enforcement and fire-rescue agencies a centralized, modern, and comprehensive training facility for all disciplines of public safety.
1281.direct_services: The Range-Training Facility functions as a central hub for regional agencies, bridging training gaps, especially for small towns and rural departments that often lack access to a high-quality simulation environment. Strengthens disaster and major event preparedness- including for mutual aid deployments. Integrate state-of-the-art simulation technology, live defensive tactics environments, and scen
1281.population: This project will impact all residents, businesses and visitors of Palm Bay as well as other neighboring jurisdictions who benefit from the training facility. There are over 8.8 million residents in the Central Florida region.
1281.outcome: The City will ensure that the project meets rigorous standards of fiscal efficiency, sustainability, and equitable access. This will be measured by the reduction in crime statistics overall, and efficient and effective response to events. Advocate, promote and facilitate continuous education and skills development for local, state, and federal Law Enforcement Officers.

1277.description: The Aspire - Seminole CCBHC Implementation Project supports implementation of a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic in Seminole County. Funding for this project will support initial assessments, triage, and diagnosis or individuals with mental health, substance use and co-occurring disorders; 24-hour mobile crisis intervention including assessment; safety and crisis planning; stabilization; and linkage and referrals to appropriate services for adults experiencing severe emotional or mental health crises.
