In the 2025-26 GAA: Line Item 196A SPECIAL CATEGORIES MEDICAID SERVICES TO INDIVIDUALS and Line Item 363 SPECIAL CATEGORIES GRANTS AND AIDS - CONTRACTED SERVICES FROM GENERAL REVENUE FUND directed AHCA and DCF to collaborate with community behavioral health providers in development of the CCHBC model. Additionally, DCF shall establish a certification process no later than June 3
1277.purpose: The Aspire - Seminole CCBHC Implementation Project will support Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic required services. Specifically, the project will support Screening, Assessment, and Diagnosis for individuals in crisis or needing evaluation, and Mobile Response Teams (MRT) providing immediate, on-demand crisis intervention to individuals experiencing behavioral health emergencies, with a strong emphasis on trauma reduction, stabilization, and diversion from restrictive or punitive sys
1277.activities: The Aspire - Seminole CCBHC Implementation Project supports the implementation of a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic in Seminole County. This includes Screening Access and Diagnosis; Mobile Response Services; Crisis Stabilization & Detoxification; Inpatient, Outpatient and Residential Treatment; Medication Assisted Treatment; Primary Care; and Case Management/Care Coordination.
1277.direct_services: Funding for this project will support initial assessments, triage, and diagnosis or individuals with mental health, substance use and co-occurring disorders; and 24-hour mobile crisis intervention including assessment; safety and crisis planning; stabilization; and linkage and referrals to appropriate services for adults experiencing severe emotional or mental health crises.
1277.population: The target population for this project the Adults and Adolescents with integrated behavioral health care needs. The project anticipates serving more than 800 individuals.
1277.outcome: 1) Increase access to community-based screening and assessment services. 2) 80% of mobile crisis referrals will be responded to in 60 minutes or less. 3) 80% of individuals will be connected to follow-up services within 72 hours of mobile response. 4) 70% of mobile crisis encounters will be resolved in the community without hospitalization or law enforcement involvement. These outcomes will be measured by documenting the number of individuals screened and assessed per month/quarter; and through the use of dispatch logs and mobile team time-tracking systems, referral tracking systems and EHR appointment logs, and mobile crisis encounter reports and disposition logs.

1360.description: The purpose of the funding request is to design intersection improvements at Malabar Rd. SE and Emerson Dr., Palm Bay, Florida to include adding lanes, conversion from a diagonal span to mast arms with lighting, passive pedestrian detection and emergency vehicle preemption. This project will improve traffic flow and help enhance public safety at the intersection by easing congestion and reducing delays.
1360.purpose: The purpose of this project is to enhance traffic flow and improve public safety by reducing traffic congestion at the intersection of Malabar Road SE and Emerson Drive, Palm Bay, Florida. This intersection has an approximate average daily traffic (ADT) of 39,620 and the project improvements will help ease congestion, reduce delays, and lower emissions upon completion.
1360.activities: The City will issue a bid solicitation for the design of intersection improvements at Malabar Road SE and Emerson Drive, Palm Bay, Florida, to include adding lanes, conversion from diagonal span to mast arms with lighting, passive pedestrian detection and emergency vehicle preemption. The City will maintain all public improvements.
1360.direct_services: There are no direct services provided to citizens for the project design. When the project is constructed, emergency response times should decrease, providing a direct service to citizens.
1360.population: Once the project is constructed, the target population served by this project will be the residents of Palm Bay and Brevard County along with visitors.
1360.outcome: Upon the completion of construction, the expected benefit of this project is improved traffic management and a reduction of accidents for all roadway users at the intersection of Malabar Road SE and Emerson Drive, Palm Bay, Florida. The outcome can be measured by analyzing traffic data at the intersection for a reduction in roadway accidents.

1289.description: The project will support Step Up Suncoast’s acquisition of its leased facility, ensuring uninterrupted access to vital programs for low-to-moderate-income residents. Step Up Suncoast provides housing and utility assistance, early childhood education, family support, career attainment programs, and other essential services that strengthen local economic stability. Ownership redirects $673,452 annually—previously spent on rent, taxes, and admin costs—into direct services and program growth, totaling nearly $7 million over a decade. Securing the facility provides a permanent base, eliminating disruption risks and strengthening operational stability for Florida’s working families, seniors, and at-risk populations. Step Up Suncoast will leverage $6.15 million in matching federal, local, and private funds, demonstrating broad community support and ensuring long-term sustainability aligned with
1289.purpose: The funds requested will be used to purchase Step Up Suncoast, Inc.’s primary facility. This acquisition will eliminate annual lease payments and redirect approximately $673,452 per year into direct services for low- to moderate-income residents, including housing, education, and employment support. Facility ownership will provide long-term savings, ensure uninterrupted program delivery, and allow Step Up Suncoast to expand its impact and serve the community more efficiently.
1289.activities: Step Up Suncoast, Inc. provides education, individualized coaching, referrals, and financial assistance to individuals and families working to overcome crisis situations and achieve long-term economic self-sufficiency. The organization offers comprehensive services tailored to the needs of the entire household. Through the acquired facility, Step Up Suncoast will continue delivering a broad array of programs, including housing and utility assistance, early childhood education, family stabilizati
1289.direct_services: Direct services provided to citizens through this appropriation project will include housing and utility financial assistance, disaster recovery support, home weatherization, free tax preparation and filing, career attainment services, and parenting education and support. The project also anchors the delivery of year-round, center-based early childhood education—encompassing nutrition and developm
1289.population: The target population for this project is low- to moderate-income (LMI) residents across the Suncoast region, including households experiencing financial hardship, families with young children, seniors, and individuals seeking economic self-sufficiency. The project is expected to serve over 6,000 unduplicated individuals annually through direct services, with cumulative impact continuing to grow throughout and beyond the 20-year mortgage period. By anchoring core services in a permanent, communi
1289.outcome: The primary benefit of this project is the redirection of approximately $673,000 in annual facility costs into expanded direct services for low- to moderate-income citizens. Immediate, quantifiable cost savings will be realized through property tax exemptions, reduced rent payments, and minimized lease administration expenses. For clients, expected outcomes include improved wages and career prospects, increased financial and housing literacy, reduced home energy bills, enhanced health and safety, and better school readiness and age-appropriate development for young children. Outcomes will be measured using a combination of client surveys, developmental screenings, home energy audits, home ev

1274.description: The City of Sanford is continuing to do what it can, within its purview, to protect the water quality of the Middle Basin by reducing sanitary sewer overflows and minimizing effluent discharges to the River. To achieve this, the City has focused on finding and removing sources of I/I into the sanitary sewers. Reduction of I/I of storm-water is achieved by improving aged sewer system infrastructure (over 100 years) and reducing the impact on the WWTP. The City estimates that there is more than 1500 brick manholes with I/I and the study identified over 370 brick manholes with severe I/I that require replacement or rehabilitation, in addition to miles of degraded pipeline requiring rehab. The City’s proposed infrastructure improvement will include installation of manhole smart covers and remote pump station telemetry for improved flow monitoring of the collection system and reducing dischar
1274.purpose: Reduction of infiltration and inflow (I/I) of storm-water by improving aged sewer system infrastructure and reducing the impact on the wastewater treatment plant. In September 2020 during a heavy rainfall event 2 SSO occurred which resulted in FDEP issuing to the City a consent order. Ongoing I/I evaluation pipe LF has identified some of the contributing areas that require immediate attention. By the year 2025 over 110,000 LF of sewer pipes were lined and 235 brick manholes rehabilitated and two
1274.activities: Lining of gravity sewer pipelines and manhole rehabilitation to reduce inflow and infiltration.
1274.direct_services: The City’s sewer infrastructure lining project will assist to improve surface water quality within the Middle Basin, an impaired body of water prioritized by the St. River Water Management District (SJRWMD) SWIM Act of 1987. Improvements will eliminate surcharging of wastewater infrastructure for 25-year critical events and reduce 100-year critical event flooding from discharging into Lake Monroe.
1274.population: All City residents (approximately 60,000) and regional residents utilizing Lake Monroe, St Johns River and Blue Springs for recreational use. Reducing the nutrients in Lake Monroe will impact many more residents of Central Florida since the Lake feeds into St John’s river.
1274.outcome: Reduction in discharge to lake Monroe resulting in reduction in nutrient discharge. Improved lake water quality, improved recreational use of the lake, quality of life for area residents. Due to continuous upgrading of the infrastructure since the storm event of 2004 treated wastewater discharge to Lake Monroe has decreased by 85%, storm event discharge to the lake is the methodology to measure outcome.

1392.organization: Guardian Angels Medical Service Dogs, Inc.
1392.description: Guardian Angels Medical Service Dogs Inc. (GAMSD), a nonprofit headquartered in Williston Florida, serves permanently disabled veterans and their families by training and donating medical service dogs to those in need. Demand for service dogs has dramatically increased, and GAMSD now cares for over 70 dogs at its Florida campus. Recent very severe hurricanes have caused operational challenges that force the relocation of outdoor-housed dogs indoors for protection. Training must halt, storm damage must be repaired, and dogs experience training setbacks. Capital funds will construct a training building with attached 34'x100' housing units and 10'x20' outdoor runs. Indoor, climate-controlled canine housing will safeguard dogs, trainers and recipients during severe storms and reduce program disruptions. Operational funds will ensure training continuity and safety during construction.
1392.purpose: The goal is to reduce wait times and improve outcomes for veteran applicants experiencing depression, suicidal ideation, PTSD, or mobility challenges. They need service dogs for confidence, safety, stability, and independence. Major storms damage our outdoor housing yards, halt training, and leave applicants and those needing successor dogs waiting longer. Timely access helps veterans more quickly achieve self-sufficiency.
1392.activities: Activities include constructing a 40’x50’ climate-controlled indoor training building with attached 34’x100’ dog housing and 10’x20’ outdoor runs. The facility will feature a dedicated training room, resilient infrastructure, secure fencing, and a standby generator. During construction, operations will be adjusted to maintain safety and continuity of training and care.
1392.direct_services: Permanently disabled Florida citizens will directly benefit from timely pairing with highly trained service dogs that mitigate mobility impairments, seizure and diabetic disorders, hearing loss, and PTSD symptoms. Climate-controlled housing ensures training continuity, reducing delays and enabling faster placement of service dogs to residents statewide.
1392.population: The project serves permanently disabled Florida veterans, first responders, and civilians who apply for medical service dogs. Each year, 30–40 Floridians are expected to receive service dogs from GAMSD, positively impacting not only recipients but also their families and caregivers. We expect to serve 400 Florida recipients plus family/caregivers within 10 years.
1392.outcome: Expected outcomes include uninterrupted training operations, faster pairing of dogs with recipients, and improved recipient outcomes such as reduced isolation, increased independence, and enhanced quality of life. Outcomes will be measured through program records (number of dogs housed, trained, and paired annually), reduction in training delays, and quarterly evaluations of recipient progress and well-being.

2336.description: The Student Achievement Center (StAC) is a 134,400-GSF facility dedicated to student success, retention, and career readiness. It will provide tutoring, advising, and collaborative learning spaces, as well as career services and engagement areas that foster student connection and achievement. The StAC is the first Florida Poly facility designed specifically for student academic and personal support, critical to meeting the university’s enrollment growth goals and strengthening Florida’s high-tech talent pipeline.
2336.purpose: The requested funds will allow Florida Polytechnic University to construct the Student Achievement Center, a critical facility designed to enhance student success, improve retention and graduation rates, and support workforce readiness. This center will serve as the hub for academic support, career services, and collaborative learning spaces, ensuring students have the resources they need to excel in STEM fields and contribute to Florida’s high-tech economy.
2336.activities: The funds will be used to construct and equip the Student Achievement Center with state-of-the-art facilities designed to support student success. This includes the development of study spaces, tutoring centers, and collaboration areas where students can engage in peer learning and faculty mentorship. The facility will also house career services that connect students with internship opportunities, industry mentorships, and professional development programs that prepare them for Florida’s workfor
2336.direct_services: The Student Achievement Center will provide a range of direct services to Florida Poly students, including enhanced access to academic support through tutoring, advising, and mentorship programs. The facility will also strengthen career readiness by offering job placement services, employer networking opportunities, and internship coordination. Additionally, it will provide collaborative learning
2336.population: The primary beneficiaries of this project are Florida Polytechnic University students, who will have access to critical resources that support their academic and professional development. As enrollment expands, the center is expected to serve over 3,000 students annually. Secondary beneficiaries include Florida’s high-tech employers, who will gain access to well-prepared STEM graduates, as well as the broader Central Florida region, which will benefit from an increased supply of skilled workers
2336.outcome: The Student Achievement Center is expected to improve student retention and graduation rates by providing enhanced academic and career support services. The success of the project will be measured by tracking institutional data on student retention, progression, and degree completion rates. Additionally, job placement rates will be monitored through career services to assess how well graduates transition into Florida’s STEM workforce. Industry engagement and internship participation rates will also serve as indicators of the center’s impact in connecting students with high-tech career opportunities.

1347.organization: CDL State Consortium / State College System
1347.description: The CDL State Consortium addresses Florida’s critical shortage of commercial truck drivers by expanding affordable, accessible CDL training statewide. With 18,000 unfilled CDL positions and heavy/tractor-trailer drivers ranked as Florida’s second highest-demand career for 2032, the project strengthens the state’s supply chain, supports economic growth, and provides high-paying job opportunities to unemployed, under-employed, formerly incarcerated, and economically disadvantaged Floridians. Funds will provide tuition support for up to 700 new drivers through Consortium partner institutions, helping stabilize Florida’s transportation workforce and ensuring timely delivery of goods statewide.
1347.purpose: To reduce Florida’s severe shortage of CDL drivers, protect the state’s supply chain, and meet projected workforce demand by expanding CDL training capacity and producing job-ready commercial drivers statewide. Heavy and tractor- trailer drivers are projected as the second most in-demand career in Florida for 2032.
1347.activities: Provides 160 hours of CDL Entry-Level Driver Training, testing, and certification through a statewide consortium of colleges and training partners. Includes hands-on instruction, curriculum delivery, and access to training equipment and testing centers.
1347.direct_services: Provides tuition grants that reduce or eliminate the cost of CDL training, directly benefiting low-income individuals, unemployed or under-employed adults, formerly incarcerated individuals, and students seeking high-wage, high- demand careers.
1347.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, jobless persons, at-risk youth, homeless individuals, university/college students, formerly incarcerated Floridians, and the general population. Estimated number served: 401–800 Floridians
1347.outcome: The project increases workforce participation in the transportation and logistics sector by producing new licensed CDL drivers, which reduces delivery costs, strengthens supply chain reliability, and boosts economic activity. CDL careers provide median salaries of ~$70,000, supporting economic self-sufficiency for participants. Outcomes will be measured through employment placement data, wages, recidivism tracking (for formerly incarcerated trainees), the number of certified drivers trained, and Department of Education/Department of Commerce labor-market metrics.

1348.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1348.description: This project supports hands-on agricultural, aquaponics, and environmental education programs that enhance STEM and STEAM learning in schools throughout Florida. The initiative introduces students to sustainable farming, nutrition, and environmental conservation while providing schools with the infrastructure needed to operate gardening, aquaculture, and outdoor learning systems. The goal is to increase student engagement, improve academic performance, promote healthier eating habits, and expand awareness of agricultural and environmental career pathways.
1348.purpose: To provide agricultural, aquaculture, and environmental education integrated with STEM/STEAM learning, improving test scores, supporting sustainability education, and expanding student engagement statewide.
1348.activities: School gardening programs, aquaponics systems, hands-on agricultural learning, teacher training, curriculum delivery, environmental restoration activities (fish tagging), and outdoor learning.
1348.direct_services: Students receive hands-on agricultural, aquaculture, and environmental instruction that improves nutrition, critical thinking, STEM engagement, outdoor activity, and environmental awareness.
1348.population: The project serves economically disadvantaged students, homeless students, developmentally and physically disabled students, preschool through university-level students, returning and disabled veterans, and individuals participating in school life-skills programs. More than 800 individuals are expected to benefit from these programs across multiple schools statewide.
1348.outcome: The project is expected to improve STEM and STEAM educational outcomes, increase agricultural and environmental literacy, enhance nutrition habits, improve physical activity, and strengthen students’ confidence and mental well-being. Success will be measured through pre- and post-program testing, FAST score comparisons, student and teacher surveys, participation levels, activity tracking, and data collected from environmental activities such as fish tagging and sustainability assessments. These metrics will demonstrate improvements in academic performance, engagement, and environmental understanding.

1226.description: Miami-Dade County has experienced a significant surge in fraudulent activities in condominium and homeowners' association fraud. By targeting the financial underpinnings of these offenders, law enforcement can dismantle criminal organizations whose crimes often results in theft of funds from the association, unwarranted fines and penalties to the associations, and most disheartening, loss of property for some of the most vulnerable victims. Many of our elder population live on fixed incomes and cannot financially afford rise in the homeowner's association dues, which results in a forced sale of their property or foreclosure.
1226.purpose: Reduce HOA fraud in Miami-Dade County
1226.activities: To identify fraudulent criminal activities in condominium and homeowners' associations; provide resources to review financial records associated with these cases; assist in community outreach to educate homeowners on how to be vigilant by attending association meetings, how to request financial records to ensure that their board is acting in their best interests and to create educational pamphlets that can be disseminated at these events to serve as a reference for homeowners.
1226.direct_services: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations.
1226.population: Residents and homeowners in Miami-Dade County.
1226.outcome: Reduction in HOA fraud, increased education and support for property owners in Miami-Dade County, and increased law enforcement operations as measured by MDSO tracking data.

1417.description: Modernize infrastructure of several zoo exhibits and areas in order to provide a better guest experience and ensure continued accreditation by the Association of Zoos & Aquariums. The zoo must maintain its AZA accreditation to retain many of its most popular species, that are part of AZA Species Survival Plans (SSPs) or Saving Animals from Extinction (SAFE) programs. We're always working to improve our guest experience to be more accessible to people of all backgrounds and abilities.
1417.purpose: Modernize infrastructure of several zoo exhibits and areas in order to provide a better guest experience and ensure continued accreditation by the Association of Zoos & Aquariums. The zoo must maintain its AZA accreditation to retain many of its most popular species, that are part of AZA Species Survival Plans (SSPs) or Saving Animals from Extinction (SAFE) programs. We're always working to improve our guest experience to be more accessible to people of all backgrounds and abilities.
1417.activities: The zoo will be able to continue to offer the public the opportunity to see and learn about local and regional wildlife, as well as wildlife from many other areas of the world. It will also allow the zoo to continue offering important informal learning programs to Central Florida resident, and it will allow the zoo to continue to be a tourism driver for Central Florida, bringing more than 140,000 people to the area from 100 miles away or more annually.
1417.direct_services: 1. Access to quality STEM education programs 2. Ability for the public to see and learn about species from around the world. 3. Opportunity for accessible, entertaining, educational experience for individuals and families.
1417.population: General population that visits the zoo, as well as Zoo staff and volunteers. The Zoo attracts more than 400,000 visitors per year.

1667.description: The City owns and maintains 15 seawalls for a total of 1,800 LF. The existing seawalls are built for a lower sea level and have a current age of approximately 65 years. The funds will be used to provide much needed repairs to the aging seawalls, which will allow the existing seawalls to serve their remaining service life.
1667.purpose: Lighthouse Point is a small residential community and faces challenges in securing funding for large projects. The City maintains 15 seawalls for a total of 1,800 LF. The existing seawalls are built for lower sea level and have a current age of approximately 65 years. The funds will be used to provide much needed repairs to the aging seawalls, which will allow the existing walls to serve their remaining service life.
1667.activities: Seawall repairs offer environmental advantages by protecting habitats and reducing erosion. By preventing soil from washing away and limited sediment runoff, repaired seawalls stabilize shorelines and prevent damage to aquatic lift and residential properties.
1667.direct_services: The seawall repairs will provide essential protection to homes, preventing costly damage from erosion and flooding.
1667.population: City of Lighthouse Point residents will be served by this project. This project can extend the functional life of the seawalls for many years, possibly decades.
1667.outcome: The construction project will prevent costly damage from erosion and flooding. The repairs will prevent the loss of soil behind the walls, which can undermine the foundation of adjacent homes, roads, or other structures. Project benefits will be measured by site observation, including feedback from the community, and reduced sediment runoff into waterways.

1300.description: Family Reconnection Program (FRP) strengthens families impacted by incarceration by facilitating consistent parent- child visitation, literacy-based engagement, and caregiver support. The program nurtures healthy communication and emotional resilience to reduce the trauma and stigma children experience when a parent is incarcerated. By restoring family connections, it promotes improved mental health, stronger family stability, and reduced recidivism.
1300.purpose: To strengthen families affected by incarceration by providing evidence-based parental education, literacy based communication between incarcerated parents and children, logistical visitation support, caregiver empowerment, and wrap around assistance throughout the year. The initiative mitigates child trauma, promotes stability, improves literacy outcomes, and decreases future recidivism.
1300.activities: Parenting education, child literacy recordings, caregiver resources, monthly visitations, and family empowerment events.
1300.direct_services: Visitation coordination for children with incarcerated parents Literacy and emotional bonding activities Caregiver navigation and resource connection Family stabilization supports
1300.population: FRP serves incarcerated parents within Florida correctional institutions and their children and caregivers across the Broward who are separated by incarceration and face financial and transportation barriers to maintaining contact. The program primarily targets economically disadvantaged families affected by parental incarceration, with priority given to those demonstrating high need for family stabilization and emotional support.
1300.outcome: FRP is expected to strengthen family bonds, improve mental and emotional well-being among children and caregivers, and reduce recidivism by maintaining consistent parent child contact during incarceration. Outcomes will be measured through pre and post participation surveys, facilitator observations, and participant feedback assessing changes in stress, communication, and family connection. Data will be analyzed quarterly to track progress and reported as part of annual performance evaluations.

1533.description: The purpose of this project is to retrofit the Leon County Hazardous Devices Vehicle that provides explosive ordnance disposal (EOD), hazardous materials, and bomb response services across 13 counties. The current vehicle has been in service for over 20 years and mission critical systems (communication, electronics, generator, etc.) are at end of life. LCSO owns the only explosive devices robot in the region, and the current box on the truck is not suitable for its transport and deployment. The retrofit is needed to keep the asset in service. This resource deploys to college football games and large events like the upcoming World Cross County event scheduled in Leon County.
1533.purpose: The purpose of this project is to retrofit the Leon County Hazardous Devices Vehicle that provides explosive ordnance disposal (EOD), hazardous materials, and bomb response services across 13 counties. The team also provides dignitary protection in the capital region and technical support to SWAT. The current vehicle has been in service for over 20 years and while the chassis and basic systems remain sound, mission critical systems (electronics, communication, generator, etc) are at end of life.
1533.activities: The retrofit of this specialized vehicle will ensure the team is prepared and equipped to provide rapid response capabilities for incidents involving hazmat, bomb threats, and high risk law enforcement operations. The team can neutralize threats, conduct decontamination, support dignitary security, and enhance tactical operations to provide safety to citizens during emergencies.
1533.direct_services: Keeping this resource in service will ensure it can continue to be used to deliver essential public safety and emergency services to protect citizens, property, and the environment during hazardous and high-risk events across 13 counties. The service mitigates the risks associated with hazardous materials, explosives, and complex emergencies. This also promotes safety and confidence of citizens by
1533.population: This asset services the following counties. Leon Wakulla, Gadsden, Jefferson, Franklin, Liberty, Columbia, Dixie, Hamilton, Lafayette, Madison, Suwanee, and Taylor. All citizens and visitors will be served. In addition to the general population, first responders are target population as well.
1533.outcome: Hazardous materials or explosive incidents are mitigated. Measured by the number of incidents where the threats were safely neutralized. Reduction in the number and severity of physical health incidents including musculoskeletal injuries, exposure to hazardous materials, and blast-related injuries. Measured by the number of hazardous devices or explosive events mitigated by the hazardous devices team.

1534.description: The collaborative Capital Region Real Time Crime Center (CRRTCC) serves as a vital asset for Region 2, including state government headquarters. The current equipment is slated to reach the end of its operational life in 2026. This project will fund the replacement of advanced computer hardware, a high-definition video wall, and state-of-the-art monitors to ensure continued efficiency and effectiveness in operations. This project will also fund a WESCAM MX-10 imaging system surveillance camera to install on the Aviation Unit aircraft for law enforcement operations. The camera includes multiple daytime cameras, thermal/FLIR cameras and multiple lasers. It is an essential tool for performing airborne law enforcement duties.
1534.purpose: To enhance the technological capabilities of the CRRTCC and joint Aviation Unit by replacing outdated computers, monitors, and the existing video wall, and by acquiring an advanced imaging camera for the law enforcement aircraft. These upgrades will strengthen real-time surveillance, intelligence gathering, and incident response by ensuring video feeds and systems can be integrated and displayed in the CRRTCC to provide more effective coordination during large-scale incidents and investigations.
1534.activities: The latest processors with high-performance specifications and high-resolution monitors will ensure analysts can efficiently process large amounts of data from sources such as surveillance cameras license plate readers, and social media feeds. Upgrading video wall technology will enable live feeds and critical alerts. The imaging system will allow for effective airborne law enforcement duties.
1534.direct_services: Airborne law enforcement services such as missing person searches, tracking fleeing vehicles that cannot be pursued on the road, disaster response, crowd management and event safety, traffic monitoring, and direct observations of incidents or criminal activity. Citizens benefit through rapid assessment, coordinated response of direct services, and enhanced response coverage and community safety.
1534.population: The CRRTCC is a joint asset of the Leon County Sheriff's Office, Tallahassee Police Department, FSU Police Department, and Florida Department of Law Enforcement. This regional asset serves the citizens of Leon and the surrounding counties. The Aviation Unit primarily serves Region 2, but is considered a statewide asset.
1534.outcome: Location of missing/lost person, recovery of stolen vehicles, and avoidance of vehicle pursuits. Increased percentage of cases cleared due to situational awareness and rapid access to visual evidence. Number of lost/missing person searches, recovered stolen vehicles, fail to stop/vehicle pursuits, and investigative assists. The number of investigations utilizing real-time video and data feeds. The number of cases solved by intelligence pushed rapidly by the RTCC. Early identification and coordinated intervention can result in the diversion of individuals from the criminal justice system. Real-time surveillance can alert personnel to behavioral distress, substance use, or minor public order i

1535.description: The purchase of four (4) Drones as First Responder (DFR) to be docked in the Capitol complex area. The DFRs will support threat awareness during demonstrations within the Capitol complex, Governor's Mansion, legislative chambers, Supreme Court, county courthouse, city hall and other nearby critical state/local infrastructures.
1535.purpose: Provides first responders quick live video footage and dignitary protection personnel within 90 seconds of receiving the threat, immediately providing information for threat awareness prior to first responders arrival. Relevant example of use cases would be situations such as a recent threat to the Florida Governor's Mansion involving a proposed sniper identifying individuals outside the mansion or a terrorist attack of any nature where an enhanced mission safety awareness is necessary.
1535.activities: Live video footage provided to first responders and dignitary protection personnel within 90 seconds of receiving the threat, immediately providing information for threat awareness prior to first responders arrival.
1535.direct_services: Currently, there are no pre-positioned DFRs capable of a 90 second response and immediate video feed available to first responders via cellphone and mobile data computers; for use in priority call responses, or major events within the Capitol complex area in support of threat awareness at critical infrastructure.
1535.population: In Tallahassee/Leon County, Region 2, the state Capitol complex, Governor's Mansion, legislative chambers, Supreme Court, county courthouse, city hall and other nearby critical state/local infrastructures.
1535.outcome: Reduction in average response time to critical incidents within the Capitol-area complex, leading to improved medical outcomes for injured individuals and enhanced officer safety. Create a baseline of data collection. Next, implement incident response time tracking. Finally, document the outcome of the tracking compared to the baseline data collection.

1205.organization: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine
1205.description: The purpose of State of Florida funding initiative was to advance high-quality HIV/AIDS cure and vaccine research through pilot awards to address the healthcare needs of Florida citizens. Pilot awardees secured federal funding, with an ROI of $12 in federal funding for every $1 in state pilot funding, and made significant advances in identifying a way to cure and prevent HIV. Given these breakthroughs, we are requesting funds that will allow us to move rapidly to the development of an effective cure for HIV. Such a cure would be transformational for the State of Florida.
1205.purpose: The purpose of State of Florida funding initiative was to advance high-quality HIV/AIDS cure and vaccine research through pilot awards to address the healthcare needs of Florida citizens. Pilot awardees secured federal funding, with an ROI of $12 in federal funding for every $1 in state pilot funding, and made significant advances in identifying a way to cure and prevent HIV. Two of our awardees published with Dr. Ronald C. Desrosiers: one on an AIDS cure strategy and the second on significant a
1205.activities: Funded activities will be to develop promising research with a strong potential for drug development and eventual commercialization of a HIV/AIDS cure. In addition, a clinical research unit at Jackson Memorial Hospital and a pediatric research unit will be supported, which supports state and federal research by supplying crucial patient samples.
1205.direct_services: Funding will support a clinical research unit at Jackson Medical Hospital which facilitates clinical services and clinical research studies that provides access to cutting edge therapies for Florida citizens.
1205.population: This program directly impacts over 132,000 Floridians living with HIV/AIDS. This program also directly impacts Floridians at risk of contracting HIV. The HIV+ population in Florida is almost twice the national average and Florida consistently ranks in the top 3 states with the highest rates of new HIV infections. This represents a significant health care cost to the State of Florida. We are now rapidly moving to the development of an effective cure for HIV/AIDS.
1205.outcome: This program benefits people living with HIV, who lose on average 6 years of life due to comorbidities such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, neurologic disorders, and cancer. This program also increases clinical research support, patient access to cutting edge treatments, and new research and biotechnology jobs in Florida through federal dollars brought in by awardees. The benefits of this program will be measured through recruitment data from the clinical research unit; investments in the state in the biotechnology sector; and the amount of federal funding secured. The treatment of HIV and HIV-associated comorbidities is a substantial financial burden on Florida’s healthcare system. Res

1565.description: The City of Gretna Fire Rescue Department currently holds an ISO rating of -10. The department's primary fire engine, a 1990 E-One, is 35 years old—well beyond the NFPA 1900 & 1901 standards, which recommend a 15-year service life for front-line apparatus. To improve emergency response capabilities and reduce the city's ISO rating, the department has been actively pursuing funding to acquire essential apparatus and equipment. This new truck will play a crucial role in achieving that goal, enhancing both efficiency and community safety.
1565.purpose: This new apparatus will significantly enhance our firefighting capabilities by providing a faster and more robust water supply for fire suppression incidents. Its advanced design ensures improved efficiency and reliability in critical emergency situations. As the first-line engine/pumper, it will play a vital role in responding to emergencies, improving overall response times, and ensuring safety.
1565.activities: This apparatus will reduce response times while carrying all essential tools and equipment for fire suppression, vehicle crashes, and light to medium rescues, enhancing efficiency and community safety.
1565.direct_services: This apparatus will reduce response times while carrying all essential tools and equipment for fire suppression, vehicle crashes, and light to medium rescues, enhancing efficiency and community safety.
1565.population: Approximately 1600 citizens of the city Gretna, 50,000+ citizens of Gadsden County and enhanced prevention, safety and response to the city's Interstate 10 corridor.
1565.outcome: Primary outcome is a reduction in our ISO rating. This will be measured by requested ISO audits when determined to be appropriate.

1619.description: IMPACT is seeking funds to acquire and renovate a 31,000 sq ft campus addition located directly next to our current campus footprint. Acquisition of this building will significantly enhance our ability to deliver high-quality special needs education, therapy services, workforce development, and inclusive community programming in one centralized, secure campus location. IMPACT Academy will increase enrollment from the current 25/26 school year enrollment of 67 to 115- 120 students, providing more children with access to individualized education in a supportive environment. The expansion will also reduce therapeutic wait times for hundreds of families currently seeking occupational, physical, speech, ABA, and music therapy. This investment will create a sustainable, long-term resource for children and young adults with developmental and learning differences within the 13 counties we serve.
1619.purpose: MPACT is seeking funds to acquire and renovate a 31,000+ square-foot addition to our campus. This expansion will significantly enhance our ability to deliver high-quality special needs education, therapy services, workforce development, and inclusive community programming in one centralized, secure location. With this acquisition, IMPACT Academy will increase enrollment from the current 25/26 school year enrollment of 67 to 115-120 students, providing more children with access to individualized
1619.activities: With this funding, we will acquire the physical space needed to offer physical, occupational, speech, and applied behavior analysis therapy services to even more families, while increasing our Academy enrollment from the current 25/26 school year enrollment of 67 to 115-120 students. This investment will allow IMPACT to create a fully integrated “Town Center” featuring on-site retail storefronts providing training and workforce opportunities for young adults with special needs. Through partnersh
1619.direct_services: An increase in educational opportunities with the addition of classrooms and additional space that will provide enhanced experiential learning environments for our students. Our individualized physical, occupational, speech and applied behavior analysis therapy services will be expanded with this funding to provide the best possible outcomes for each family. Funding will also allow expansion to ou
1619.population: Developmentally and physically disabled youth from the ages of 6 weeks to 22 years of age. Persons with poor mental and physical health including preschool, grade, and high school students. IMPACT also serves young adults who are post high-school in our transition program up to 22 years of age. IMPACT will have provided more than 50,000 total hours of therapies to 550+ families in 2025 alone. The demand for our services continues to increase each year.
1619.outcome: IMPACT will be able to serve a broader population of families improving their physical & mental health, instill career readiness for students after graduation, and provide meaningful career opportunities, as we hire more staff to work with additional children & young adults. This space also includes dedicated spaces for mentorship, counseling, and daily life skills training to support young adults as they transition into adulthoods. The methodology to measure these benefits includes baseline standard periodic testing, school & therapeutic assessment tracking, workforce training assessment tool, career placement following graduation, and tracking of independent living skills.

1572.description: The Public Safety Complex will be constructed to be a Cat. 5 hurricane rated structure. The Complex will house Emergency Management, EMS, Fire Rescue services, and a portion of law enforcement. The existing EOC is not large enough to accommodate essential personnel in a severe weather or disaster event and can only seat a maximum of 14 in the conference area. The Complex will offer special needs sheltering services. Currently, there are no special needs sheltering facilities in the County. Taylor County suffered catastrophic losses from both Hurricanes Idalia and Helene and is a RAO and REDI area.
1572.purpose: The goal of the Public Safety Complex is to have a facility large enough to efficiently and effectively operate in the event of a disaster or catastrophic event. The existing EOC does not have the capacity to accommodate multiple agencies or have sufficient area for pre and post disaster planning and recovery. The new facility will provide a special needs sheltering area. The Complex will offer combined services which will enable the County to better serve and provide for the safety and welfare
1572.activities: Emergency Management, Emergency Medical Services, Fire Rescue, and law enforcement will be co-located in the Complex with the primary focus being Emergency Management. In addition to these services, special needs sheltering facilities will be available in the Complex. The proposed Complex will be constructed to Cat 5 hurricane rated standards ensuring for the continuity of operations and services.
1572.direct_services: Direct services will be Emergency Management services including pre and post-disaster planning and recovery. EMS, fire protection, and law enforcement services will also be provided. Currently there are no special needs sheltering facilities in the County. Those with special needs must be transported out of County for sheltering during an emergency or catastrophic event. The Complex will provide a
1572.population: The entire population of Taylor County will be served. In addition, the facility would be available to other counties in the region should they need support or mutual aid. The Complex will benefit the entire Big Bend region.
1572.outcome: Taylor County will have an adequate facility for Emergency Management to effectively operate and ensure the continuity of operations and disaster recovery efforts. In addition, the facility will offer EMS, Fire Rescue and law enforcement services. The Complex will offer sheltering facilities for special needs as well as essential personnel. It has become very obvious during pre-landfall and post-recovery efforts resulting from Hurricanes Idalia and Helene, the facility is critically needed by Taylor County.

2736.description: The Shady Grove project will be the construction of a hurricane rated, resilient fire station with storage for equipment, apparatus and vehicles. The building will be located on land owned by Taylor County (County). The facility will have sufficient parking for firefighters and emergency response personnel. The site will serve as a disaster recovery staging area for the north end of the County. The facility has an estimated cost of $2M and the County was awarded a budget appropriation FY 23-24 in the amount of $1M. The entire County suffered catastrophic loss from Hurricanes Idalia and Helene including the Shady Grove community.
2736.purpose: The purpose is the construction of a hurricane rated, resilient fire station and public safety facility. Currently Shady Grove Fire Rescue is located in a small, older shed like structure which does not have storage for equipment and apparatus. There is no adequate parking. The north end of the County does not have a disaster recovery area and this facility will be able to provide those services. The entire County suffered catastrophic loss from Hurricanes Idalia and Helene and this facility is
2736.activities: The station will provide facilities and resources for improved fire protection and emergency response services for Shady Grove and the north end of the County. In addition, mutual aid is provided to the adjacent counties of Madison and Jefferson which will benefit from the station. The new station will substantially reduce response times with adequate equipment stored on site. Shady Grove is located 16.6. miles from the County's primary fire station which currently provides the majority of fire
2736.direct_services: The facility will provide substantially improved response times for fire protection and emergency services. In addition, the north end of the County will have a facility equipped to provide disaster recovery services.
2736.population: The target population is the community of Shady Grove as well as the north end of the County. Madison and Jefferson County will both benefit as mutual aid is provided when so needed. Approximately 4,000 citizens over 200 square miles will be served.
2736.outcome: All emergency calls are recorded and monitored. An expected outcome of the project is substantially reduced response times which can be tracked and documented. Another outcome will be the extended life of emergency response and fire vehicles, equipment, and apparatus with adequate storage and protection from the weather. There is currently no disaster recovery facility in the north end of the County and the new station will be able to provide those services.

1570.description: The proposed project is to replace Air Handler Units (AHU's) and duct work at Taylor County Courthouse. Southern Earth Sciences completed a Mold Testing Report & Work Plan due to ongoing air quality concerns. It was determined in the study, one of the key problems is the existing AHU's. The units have not been replaced since 1981 and are in poor condition. Due to age and being full of insulation, the duct work cannot be cleaned. The Courthouse suffered damage from Hurricane Helene which further exacerbated the AHU problems. Adequate AHU's are essential to improve air quality and to remove particulates from the air.
1570.purpose: The purpose of the funds is the purchase and installation of five new Air Handler Units (AHU's) and the replacement of duct work in the Courthouse. There have been ongoing concerns on the air quality in the Courthouse and in a study completed by Southern Earth Sciences it was determined that replacing the AHU's and duct work was critical for air quality improvement and the health and welfare of the Courthouse employees as well as the many citizens who access the facility for services. The AHU's
1570.activities: The replacement of the AHU's and duct work will greatly improve the air quality in the Courthouse. The AHU's will ensure the air is balanced and moisture is removed from the humid environment thus eliminating the potential of mold growth. The roof damage from Hurricane Helene has exacerbated the growth of mold and contaminants and the replacement of the AHU's is critical to ensure for a safe, healthy work environment for employees including those who work in the Court System as well as the many
1570.direct_services: Due to the current concerns of the Courthouse air quality and a documented study confirming the concerns are valid, the direct services will be ensuring the Courthouse has good air quality throughout the facility. The new AHU's and duct work upgrades will ensure particulants such as pollen, dust, and other contaminates are removed from the air.
1570.population: All citizens who access the Courthouse will be served by the project as well as the employees who work in the facility including the Court system. More than 150,000 individuals will be served annually.
1570.outcome: The new AHU's and duct work will ensure for a safe and healthy environment for both employees and the many citizens who access the facility including the courtrooms and associated offices. Ensuring for public safety, and a healthy and environmentally safe facility is the expected benefit and outcome of the project.

1757.description: This project requests funding for the construction of a 10 bay t-hangar unit at the Perry-Foley Airport which will substantially assist in economic growth and development not only for the Airport but also for Taylor County. The County was awarded a FDOT grant for the design and permitting of the t-hangar facility. The County expected to receive an additional $1.8M for the construction of the facility. However, this funding is no longer available. An Economic Recovery Study completed for the County determined the Airport and the development thereof is essential for County wide economic development and growth.
1757.purpose: The construction of the t-hangars will encourage economic development and growth at the Airport. It was determined in an Economic Recovery Study funded by FL Commerce that development at the Perry-Foley Airport is essential for economic development in the County. There is a great deal of interest in t-hangar facilities at the Airport to accommodate private and commercial aircraft and encourage new businesses to locate in Taylor County. Existing hangars located at the Airport are leased and there
1757.activities: The t-hangars will facilitate Airport growth and economic development in the area as well as the Big Bend Region. As a fiscally constrained County which lost both primary employers in 2023, a working, viable Airport encourages businesses to locate in the area. Support services such as hotels, restaurants, and retail outlets also benefit from a busy, growing Airport.
1757.direct_services: The new t-hangars will assist with airport growth and development which stimulates the local economy. The County is working hard to recruit new businesses to locate in the area after the permanent closure of Georgia-Pacific which had a significant negative impact on the community. It is proven statistically a viable working Airport provides unlimited economic growth and opportunities to communitie
1757.population: The target population is the entire County as well as the Big Bend Region. Airports stimulate economic growth and development which is critical for the local economy. The loss of anticipated funding is devastating to the County due to serious fiscal constraints.
1757.outcome: Economic development and growth is critical to Taylor County. General aviation airports significantly impact rural communities by acting as economic drivers, providing essential infrastructure for local businesses and new business development. They also stimulate tourism and job creation in numerous areas of support services. In addition adequate airport facilities encourage aviation business related growth such as mechanics or flight schools thus additional job creation opportunities.

1568.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1568.description: The scope of work is the construction of a steel covering for a 150 x 250 outdoor arena to serve as an Agriculture Center. The covering is essential for converting the arena into a facility that has unlimited potential to host agricultural, livestock, festivals, and entertainment events. Being located on the grounds of Forest Capital Hall which hosts numerous festivals and events through the year, the Ag Center is in an ideal location to promote tourism and economic development. The scope of work also includes the installation of a covered seating area with fans at the Heritage Pavilion also located at the Park.
1568.purpose: The Florida agriculture and related industry generates over $182.6 billion in revenue annually with the equine industry generating $12.8 billion. With this, there is definitely a need for Agriculture Centers in the state with an emphasis on the showing of livestock. The addition of a covered seating area at the Heritage Pavilion will enable the County to host events in inclement weather. The County will have the assistance of the Chamber of Commerce and Tourism Development to bring multi-day eve
1568.activities: The County will be working with Taylor County Chamber of Commerce and Tourism Development to bring multi-day events to the Center and Heritage Pavilion. As the County is rural and the economy being largely based on agriculture, there is a great deal of interest in hosting events at the Park. The Park improvements will enable multiple events over multiple days to be hosted thus promoting tourism and economic development.
1568.direct_services: Direct services will provide the opportunity for all ages and abilities to participate in or spectate agricultural, livestock, and entertainment events in a safe, family friendly environment. The Ag Center will provide the County the facility and resources needed to host multi-day events and activities. The covered seating area at the Heritage Pavilion will also encourage multi-day events thus inc
1568.population: The target population is citizens who participate or enjoy being spectators at agriculture and livestock activities as well as entertainment events. Quite a few local children participate in 4-H and showing livestock and as there are no facilities available in the County at this time, they must travel outside the County to participate in these events and activities. The County's primary goal is to host multi-day agriculture, livestock, and entertainment events and shows to promote tourism and ec
1568.outcome: The outcome will be the ability to host multi-day agricultural, livestock, and entertainment events. With the steel covering, over the arena and covered seating at the Heritage Pavilion, inclement weather will not have a negative impact on events hosted at the facility. As a fiscally constrained County which has suffered catastrophic losses from Hurricane's Idalia and Helene and the loss of the two primary employers, tourism and economic development is critical for the area.

1567.description: The tourism development project is the construction of lighting, sidewalks, and seating at the new softball field at Taylor County Sports Complex which will enable the County to host larger scale tournaments and events. The softball field is essential for tourism development .It is anticipated each tournament the County hosts will have the ability to bring in over 1,200 visitors per event. Per tourism development studies, each visitor brings in an average of $87 per day for overnight stays, thus bringing in $104,400 per day on average for each event. As a rural, fiscally constrained County, this will have a tremendous economic impact on the local economy.
1567.purpose: The installation of lighting, sidewalks, and seating at the new softball field will enable the County to host large scale tournaments which will be beneficial and essential for tourism development in the community. The estimated economic impact is $104,400 per day for each tournament, a substantial amount for a fiscally constrained County. The Complex is the ONLY public facility in the County which has the ability to host tournaments and promote tourism.
1567.activities: The installation of lighting, sidewalks, and seating at the new softball field will enable the County to host large scale tournaments, thus benefiting the local economy and the promotion of tourism. As a fiscally constrained REDI community and RAO, the development and creation of economic and tourism opportunities is criticial. The additional softball field will also ensure the County has the facilities needed to accommodate all local children and provide the opportunity for all to participate i
1567.direct_services: At this time, there is not sufficient facilities available to accommodate all who wish to participate in local softball programs and the new field will provide adequate recreational facilities to all who wish to participate. The Sports Complex has been key in providing tourism development opportunities for the community and is heavily used year round. Hosting multi-day events has the potential to
1567.population: The target population is children and families however, one of the key goals of the continued development of the Sports Complex is the ability to host tournaments and events to benefit the local economy. As the Sports Complex is heavily used year round, more than 250,000 are expected to be served.
1567.outcome: The installation of lighting, sidewalks, and seating at the new softball field will aid in the continued development of the Sports Complex and associated economic and tourism development. In addition, the existing fields are used to capacity at this time and the additional field will allow more children and youth to participate in outdoor recreational opportunities.

3292.description: The program is designed to improve response efficiency, reduce dispatcher workload, and enhance community engagement. Both teams will collaborate on data analysis, workflow design, and implementation planning to ensure effective deployment and measurable operational impact.
3292.purpose: This initiative will pilot an AI-powered support solution to assist with non-emergency call management and related operational workflows. The program is designed to improve response efficiency, reduce dispatcher workload, and enhance community engagement. Both teams will collaborate on data analysis, workflow design, and implementation planning to ensure effective deployment and measurable operational impact.
3292.activities: Answering non-emergency calls that come into from citizens, documentation and call forwarding/routing as necessary.
3292.direct_services: Answering non-emergency calls that come into from citizens, documentation and call forwarding/routing as necessary.
3292.population: Elderly persons Persons with poor mental health Persons with poor physical health Jobless persons Economically disadvantaged persons At-risk youth Homeless Developmentally disabled Physically disabled
3292.outcome: Protect the general public from harm (environmental, criminal, etc.) - The project will improve public safety by ensuring emergency dispatchers are available to respond to true emergencies rather than being occupied with non-emergency calls. The level of benefit will be measured by the reduction in dispatcher time spent on non-emergency calls and the decrease in average response times for emergency incidents, tracked through call-handling and dispatch performance metrics.

1561.description: The former school building, significantly damaged during Hurricane Idalia, had its roof replaced using insurance funds. However, the interior remains water-damaged and non-compliant with current codes. The requested funding will support comprehensive renovations to meet code standards and fortify the structure for use as an evacuation shelter during future catastrophic events for the citizens of Lee, and others in Madison County. The building will also serve as a multi- use facility during non-catastrophic events.
1561.purpose: The former school building will be completely renovated and strengthened to function as an evacuation shelter for residents of the Town of Lee, and others in Madison County, during catastrophic events. During non-catastrophic events, the building will be utilized as a multi-use facility.
1561.activities: The architectural, MEP, and structural design of the building will be provided to meet the intended purpose of these funds.
1561.direct_services: The renovated building will directly benefit the citizens of Lee, and others in Madison County, by providing a safe space to shelter during catastrophic events. During non-catastrophic events, the renovated building will be utilized as a multi-use facility.
1561.population: The project will serve the Town of Lee (estimated 2025 population of 383), as well as others in Madison County.
1561.outcome: The project aims to provide a strengthened evacuation shelter for the citizens of the Town of Lee, and others in Madison County, during catastrophic events. This will be measured by tracking its occupancy rate during catastrophic events. The project will also enhance physical and mental health by offering a venue for physical activities and community events, tracked by participant and event numbers. Additionally, it will boost economic activity by renting building space, with success measured by rental revenue.

1560.description: Maintain and expand evidence-based, free-of-charge therapy for children and families experiencing grief and loss in North Florida. These include the Tallahassee and Pensacola locations as well as materials distribution, therapy kits, training for schools and counselors in Escambia, Leon, Santa Rosa, Walton, Jefferson, Okaloosa, Jackson, Gulf, Holmes, Bay, & Liberty counties. The program serves children who have lost a family member, had a family member deployed, jailed, who abandoned them, were removed from the home, or experienced a disaster. Most are referred from DCF, the managing entity, Gulf Coast Kid's House, or other providers.
1560.purpose: Maintain and expand evidence-based, free-of-charge therapy for children and families experiencing grief and loss in North Florida. The program serves children who have lost a family member, had a family member deployed, jailed, who abandoned them, were removed from the home, or experienced a disaster. Childhood behavioral health services reduce short and long term risk factors such as suicidality, violent criminality, poor academic performance, and substance abuse. Every $1 spent saves state $7.
1560.activities: Individual and group therapy and evidence-based, therapist led support groups for children experiencing grief and loss and their families, camp connect (intensive therapy camps for children), school-based support, professional workshops, community resources and grief education, parent packs, crisis response for schools, law-enforcement, agency referrals, parent education.
1560.direct_services: Provide free-of-cost evidence based therapy for children experiencing grief and loss. Results in reduction of depression, anxiety, PTSD, edubstance dependence, poor academic performance, self-harm, suicide, mortality, and violent criminality. Six-therapy sessions reduce risk factors by 20% with improved results with continued services.
1560.population: Persons with poor mental health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, victims of crime, and their families. More than 2000 people in the target population are expected to be served.
1560.outcome: Improve mental health, improve quality of education, protect the general public from harm, increase and improve economic activity, enhance specific individuals economic self sufficiency, reduce recidivision, reduce substance abuse, and divert from Criminal/Juvenile Justice System. Data is populated via EMR and reported to ME. Client and Family intake and Post Services Surveys, during sessions. Engagement with DJJ, DCF, ME and other providers.

1929.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1929.description: An Agriculture Tech Wet Lab Innovation Hub. Florida's first integrated AG-TECH, Life Sciences and Wet Lab facility, a coalition of Public-Private Partnerships with regional business and educational partners including IFAS, Lake County ED, Lake-Tech, Florida High Tech Corridor and others. Focus on applied research, training, R&D to include but not limited to Agri-tech, plant science, food science, soil, water systems, growers, food producers and the study into Agri-aerospace biotech and mart-ag. Goal is to simulate real-world agricultural environments to improve life science commercialization processes. This will advance innovative workforce, economic diversification, job creation and agricultural innovation for start-ups, researchers and industry.
1929.purpose: To advance agriculture, life science, innovation and collaboration throughout the academic, economic development and workforce impacts in the Lake county and surrounding regions for food sciences, R&D to improve food safety, water, and plant sciences throughout the region.
1929.activities: Collaborative and shared space, wet labs, regulatory oversight, wet labs and sharing opportunities with IFAS, UF/Lake Tech, High Tech Corridor, Bio Florida, producers and growers throughout the state of Florida to support commercialization.
1929.direct_services: Direct and indirect job growth, opportunities for startups, and advancements in R & D in each of these sciences, and new training and workforce trainings.
1929.population: Agricultural sector, life sciences, manufacturing, growers, producers, researchers, logistics, lake county residents.
1929.outcome: Create 90-115 Direct jobs, start up and tenant companies, approximately 37 and indirect jobs, 63. Each direct job supports additional 1.8-2.2 jobs in local economy.

2138.description: As a safety net provider in Broward County that serves more than 25,000 people annually, we provide behavioral health services to the most vulnerable individuals with severe and persistent mental illness. Two of our residential treatment campuses where 84 mentally ill adults reside are in need of generators, replacement of flooring, bathrooms, paint and furnishings; one outpatient location that serves 3,000+ adults is in need of a roof that can withstand storms. Funds will be utilized to ensure safe operations and to ensure we can remain open to the public during and post hurricane related emergencies.
2138.purpose: The purpose of these funds is to be able to safely operate our residential and outpatient facilities during and post hurricane force winds. We have two residential treatment campuses where 84 mentally ill adults reside that require generators,replacement of flooring, bathrooms, paint, and furnishings; and one outpatient location that serves 3,000 adults that is in need of a roof that can withstand storms. Funds would be utilized to purchase a roof, generators, replacement of flooring, bathrooms,
2138.activities: Funds will be utilized to install generators, replace flooring, bathrooms, paint and furnishings at two residential treatment campuses serving 84 adults with severe and persistent mental illness and to install a new roof for an outpatient facility serving over 3,000 individuals so that we can safely remain operational during and post hurricanes.
2138.direct_services: Residential treatment to include housing, medication management, individual, group and family therapy, case management, peer recovery support, psychosocial rehabilitation and supportive employment and outpatient services to include medication management, primary care, individual, group and family therapy, case management, peer recovery support, psychosocial rehabilitation.
2138.population: Over 3,000 individuals will be served annually. Target populations include individuals with mental illness, persons with poor physical and mental health, homeless individuals, economically disadvantaged individuals.
2138.outcome: a. Two residential campuses will have generators to operate the facility and new flooring, paint, bathrooms and furnishings in case of severe wind damage so that we can safely house and treat residents in and post hurricanes as measured by the completion of the installation of 2 generators and installation of replacement flooring, bathrooms, paint and furnishings. b. One outpatient facility will have its roof replaced to withstand hurricane force winds so that we can remain open to the public post hurricanes as measured by the completion of the installation of the new roof.

2369.description: The funds will be used to extend an 8" water main along 10th Avenue N from east of Lynwood Drive to Summer Street. This extension will increase fire flow in the area from less than 500 gallons per minute (gpm) to over 1,000 gpm. The water main extension will also create a looped configuration to improve operational efficiency and reliability and will grow the Lake Worth Beach water service area to provide an opportunity to serve more water customers.

2369.outcome: Increased fire flow availability, increased potable water system reliability, increased potable water quality, and expanded service area to provide potable water service to new customers.

1151.description: Nicklaus Children's Heart Institute provides free and accessible electrocardiogram (EKG) screenings to tens of thousands of student athletes throughout South Florida yearly. These screenings play a vital role in detecting underlying heart conditions that can lead to sudden cardiac events in otherwise healthy young athletes. This funding request would bolster these efforts and provide funding for an additional 15,000 screenings.
1151.purpose: Enable the Nicklaus Children's Heart Institute to provide 15,000 free and accessible electrocardiogram (EKG) screenings to student athletes throughout South Florida.
1151.activities: Provide 15,000 free and accessible EKG screenings and interpretations for student athletes in South Florida.
1151.direct_services: Timely EKG screenings and interpretations that help detect underlying heart conditions in otherwise healthy student athletes.
1151.population: Student athletes of all ages, sports, and socioeconomic backgrounds. Approximately 15,000 individuals.
1151.outcome: That parents and student athletes have as complete a picture as possible of students' health prior to competing in athletics. To measure the efficacy of the program, the State could compare the following prior to and after implementation of the program: 1) public knowledge about the pros of an EKG screening, 2) accessibility of EKG screenings, 3) the number of detected underlying heart conditions.

2370.description: The funds will be used to reroute a force main that currently carries raw sewage from the Town of Lantana to a manhole in the City of Lake Worth Beach gravity sewer system. The flow volume and turbulence is overwhelming the gravity system, causing maintenance activities to be delayed and residents in the area to experience sewer backups and unpleasant sewer odor. The force main will be extended to the Lake Worth Beach Master Pump Station to bypass the gravity system entirely.
2370.purpose: The funds will be used to reroute a force main that currently carries raw sewage from the Town of Lantana to a manhole in the City of Lake Worth Beach gravity sewer system. The flow volume and turbulence is overwhelming the gravity system, causing maintenance activities to be delayed and residents in the area to experience sewer backups and unpleasant sewer odor. The force main will be extended to the Lake Worth Beach Master Pump Station to bypass the gravity system entirely.

2370.population: Lake Worth Beach and Lantana. Approximately 54,000 individuals.
2370.outcome: Ability to maintain and extend service life for critical wastewater infrastructure. Reduced sewer backups and odor in the immediate vicinity.

1363.description: This project will upgrade the treatment plant to advanced waste treatment standards (5.0 mg/L TSS, 5.0 mg/L CBOD, 3.0 mg/L TN & 1.0 mg/L TP).
1363.purpose: Reducing nutrient loads on the Indian River Lagoon.
1363.activities: The construction/enhancement of the treatment plant to achieve reduced nitrogen and phosphorus in its reclaimed water.
1363.direct_services: The reduction of nutrients going into the Indian River Lagoon (IRL) will benefit the health, safety and welfare of the community and the direct benefit will be a more resilient wastewater treatment facility with generator power capabilities and the case of storm or power outage.
1363.population: The city's population is approximately 30,000 citizens. The upgrade of the wastewater treatment facility to AWT not only benefits the city's population, but it will also significantly reduce the nutrients in the IRL resulting in a much broader improvement of the water quality for the region.

These capabilities will allow Florida Tech to provide certification training and labs for composite skills as well as support Florida industry cluster product development to include aerospace and marine applications.

These capabilities will allow Florida Tech to provide certification training and labs for composite skills as well as support to Florida industry cluster product development to include aerospace and marine applications.

Composite materials familiarization and skill training are slated to be provided to industry workforce and students. Advanced composite prototyping and testing with industry partners to advance "Stay in Florida" efficiencies and competitiveness in the marketplace will be available.

Measurements will include workforce groups, students, faculty and companies accessing and utilizing equipment as well as increasing the number of industry workforce, students, faculty and partners exposed to advanced composite training methods.

Cocoa High is one of our priority schools in the district and serves a significant amount of our special population groups identified by federal Perkins V legislation. This program will hopefully draw students into the school from out of zone and increase enrollment at Cocoa.

This HS program has a Postsecondary avenue for graduates to follow within the County. 1279.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is to prepare students with Career-Ready skills that reinforce the skills needed to perform as an entry level worker in the Firefighting industry. These services will provide domestic violence survivors and their families, including pets, safety from abuse and the ability to move forward successfully with safety and independence.
1681.purpose: Emergency shelter and outreach services which will provide safety to survivors of domestic violence and their families and pets.

This initiative directly supports Governor Ron DeSantis’ statewide commitment to expanding Florida’s housing supply, increasing affordability, and promoting pathways to homeownership through public-private collaboration and strategic community reinvestment. And finally, award of grant allows the project to leverage federal and private dollars. This is a true public/private partnership housing imitative. The requested funds will be used for predevelopment and other activities that are essential precursors to the construction of 4-6 new affordable, for-sale housing units. These homes will provide working families with stable, attainable homeownership opportunities while fostering long-term neighborhood stability and generatio

Revitalize an underserved community by improving housing quality, safety, and appearance. Leverage public investment to attract additional private and nonprofit development in the area. To
