Progress will be tracked through project management reports, construction milestones, sales documentation, and compliance records to ensure transparency and accountability throughout implementation.

2774.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2774.description: The Florida Food Security Project is designed to implement a comprehensive set of initiatives aimed at reducing food insecurity among youth, adults, and families across our service area. This project prioritizes four key areas: resource accessibility, nutrition education and awareness, community engagement, and coordinated support. By increasing access to healthy food options, empowering residents through education, and fostering stronger community partnerships, the project seeks to build a sustainable network of support that helps individuals move from food insecurity to long-term stability.Through collaborative efforts with schools, local organizations, and faith-based partners, the Florida Food Security Project will not only address the immediate need for food but also strengthen the systems that ensure equitable access for all Floridians.

1373.organization: Advocacy Resource Center, Marion Inc. DBA

Through comprehensive services including Adult Day Training (with life-skill classes like cooking, exercise, computer use, hygiene, community outings and productive day activities), residential habitation and group homes, supported independent living, and transportation, we tailor support to each person’s unique talents, goals and needs. Our programs remove barriers to productive community engagement, foster independence, promote social inclusion and enable participants to contribute in ways that reflect their abilities, not their limitations.

1373.activities: The funds will enable us to deliver robust life skills development programs through our Adult Day Training (ADT) and Residential living services. Clients will engage in hands on training in areas such as cooking, personal hygiene, philanthropy/social engagement, computer skills, arts & crafts, and recreation/community outings. The project is shovel-ready, designed to prevent shoreline erosion, protect water quality, provide safe docking, and support new waterfront development to include modern multifamily housing, expanded marina services, retail, dining, tourism and fishing destination that will generate economic activity, expand safe harbor options, and improve quality of life for this financially disadvantaged municipality in a Rural Area of Opportunity.
2543.purpose: Goal is to complete 500 linear feet of new seawall at the City’s marina, located at the mouth of the Caloosahatchee River (a BMAP area), to prevent further shoreline erosion, protect natural resources, and meet high demand from boaters, mariners, and visitors. The new seawall will connect to the existing structure, add 300 feet of boat mooring facilities, and create a safe, modernized harbor that supports tourism and economic development in a financially disadvantaged community located in a Rura
2543.activities: Funds used to seek contractual services through the City's procurement policies and procedures for engineering during construction, bidding, project management, administration and seawall construction to complete 500 LF of new steel seawall with a concrete cap, install 300 feet of new mooring facilities with utilities, and complete shoreline stabilization within the marina basin. These activities will directly improve the marina’s resilience, expand capacity for boat traffic, and protect the Cal
2543.direct_services: The project will directly benefit residents, mariners, and visitors by protecting the Caloosahatchee River shoreline, expanding mooring facilities, and ensuring safe, well-equipped docking infrastructure. The seawall will improve public safety during storms by providing secure tie-ups, enhance recreational opportunities, and create a stronger foundation for tourism that supports the new waterfront

Seagrass cleans the water, stabilizes the sediment, provides critical habitat and food for many species, and sequesters carbon. By expanding into a 5th phase, the seagrass has a greater chance to reach a critical mass scale and naturally expand outside of the planted areas. Planting sites will be located in areas that encourage natural recruitment into surrounding barren areas; have adequate light availability; and have stable salinity conditions and sufficient water quality necessary for survival and widespread expansion. Herbivory exclusion devices will be strategically placed over planting units to prot
2553.purpose: The goal of this project is to expand on previous phases of seagrass restoration in the Fort Pierce Inlet area of the IRL. By adding a 5th phase of this project, the seagrass in the Fort Pierce area have a better chance to reach a critical mass scale where it can naturally expand on its own resulting in double, triple, or even quadruple growth outside of planted areas. Seagrass can reset an ecosystem and prevent the costs associated with mitigating harmful algal blooms (HABs). Enhanced meadows w
2553.activities: An additional 20 acres within the IRL will be restored. Nursery-grown seagrass will be planted, protected, and monitored. Planting sites will be strategically located in areas that encourage natural recruitment into the surrounding barren areas; have adequate light availability; and provide stable salinity conditions and sufficient water quality necessary for seagrass survival and widespread expansion. The long-term goal of this project is to demonstrate the effectiveness of using nursery-grown
2553.direct_services: This project will improve water quality in the IRL by restoring 20 additional acres of seagrass. Restored seagrass will provide habitat and protection for fish and other marine life, while providing a continual food source for manatees. Robust seagrass communities help reduce the risk of flooding to build community resilience. Seagrass also creates drag in the water column, which attenuates wave e

The project is expected to improve academic performance, reduce healthcare disparities, and enhance long-term well- being by ensuring early detection and treatment of vision issues in underserved children. By providing screenings, on- site exams, prescription glasses, and specialist referrals, the initiative will help children see clearly—leading to improved literacy, greater classroom engagement, and higher graduation rates.Outcomes will be measured through comprehensive data tracking and impact assessments, including the number of children screened, glasses distributed, and referrals completed. Follow-up evaluations will assess improvements in academic performance and complian

1770.description: This project provides a comprehensive Village-wide septic to sewer conversion assessment. The assessment begins the planning process to hold convert existing properties and remaining areas within the Village from septic to sewer including high priority critical areas identified in the Village Vulnerability Study. A consultant will provide a gravity sewer force main master plan, including pipe length, pump station locations connection points, system modeling. The Village recognizes that due to the potential future conditions/impact associated with sea level rise and storm surges that an assessment and plan must be put into place to alleviate potential septic tank failures and the release of nutrients in the environment, aquifer and local bodies of water.
1770.purpose: This project aims at completing a comprehensive Village-wide septic to sewer conversion assessment. The Village estimates that 1200 homes are currently on septic tanks. The Village recognizes that due to potential future conditions and impacts associated with sea level rise and storm surge that an assessment and plan must be put into place to alleviate potential septic tank failures and the release of nutrients into the environment and local water bodies, including nearby canals and, Biscayne Ba
1770.activities: Consultant will be reatained to evaluate and create a master plan for a gravity sewr and force main system to abandon residential septic tank connerctions Village-wide.
1770.population: This project will benefit the community as a whole, but there are approximately 1,200 homes still on septic tanks.
1770.outcome: The expected benefit or outcome of this project is enhancement, preservation, environmental improvement and wildlife quality. The Village of Biscayne Park goal is to provide a detailed assessment of specific watershed loads affecting the Village’s waterway system to serve as a guide for targeting watershed nutrient management. Results will show any elevated levels of nitrogen and phosphorous. This project will also improve groundwater, drinking water and surface water quality.

1824.description: Playground improvements to the Village of Biscayne Park's only Tot Lot for a community of 3,300 residents and surrounding neighborhoods. This Tot Lot is utilized by three (3) neighboring jurisdiction, North Miami, El Portal Miami Shores and Unincorporated Miami Dade County. The Tot Lot Equipment is over tenth-five (25) years with replacement parts increasing harder to get. The Village is unique in that it does not have any commercial tax base.
1824.purpose: Playground improvements to the Village of Biscayne Park's only Tot Lot for a community of 3,300 residents and surrounding neighborhoods. This Tot Lot is utilized by three (3) neighboring jurisdiction, North Miami, El Portal Miami Shores and Unincorporated Miami Dade County. The Tot Lot Equipment is over tenth-five (25) years with replacement parts increasing harder to get.
1824.activities: Funds will be utilized to service the recreational needs for families with small children - ages 0-5 years old. The Tot Lot is currently heavily used both during the week-day and on weekends. It is used and enjoyed by the community for families of all economic/ social backgrounds.
1824.direct_services: Citizens from the surrounding neighborhoods benefit from use of an recreational area that is a has safe equipment and meets the needs of the community. Parks and Recreation is a vital element for the needs of safe, vibrant community to prosper. Families need a place to attend with small children to play and interact with other families.
1824.population: The target population served by this project will be preschool students, grade school students and families. No more than 800 individuals are expected to be served.
1824.outcome: This will allow for recreational area where family can gather and enjoy physical activity which can be measured by the number of families that are actively using the equipment through the week and on weekends. Promoting and increasing a healthy life-style.

1615.description: Provide funding to implement an African American History Summer Institute for teachers. This program will provide three days of professional learning for teachers through Miami-Dade County Public Schools. The institute aims to increase teachers' knowledge of African American history, emphasizing the content and required instructional approaches as stated in Florida State Statute 1003.42, section H inclusive of subsection 3. AAH success stories in Florida will be emphasized. Program will enable M-DCPS to maintain its exemplar status, designated by the Governor's AAH Taskforce.
1615.purpose: Provide funding for an African American History (AAH) Summer Institute servicing Miami-Dade County Public School teachers; consisting of three professional learning days. The institute aims to increase teachers' knowledge of AAH, regarding the topics/instructional approaches stated in Florida State Statute 1003.42, section H & subsection 3. AAH success stories in Florida will be emphasized. Program will enable M-DCPS to maintain its exemplar status, designated by the Governor's AAH Taskforce.
1615.activities: 3 days of in-service for teachers, pedagogical assistance, content experts, and hospitality/facilities rental.
1615.direct_services: The African American Summer Institute offers three days of professional development for teachers through Miami- Dade County Public Schools. It aims to increase teachers' knowledge of African American history, culture, societal contributions and to provide them with the tools they need to effectively teach this required topic to their students.
1615.population: The target population includes 100 teachers, as well as all grade school and high school students throughout Miami- Dade County Public Schools who will be taught African American history.
1615.outcome: The expected outcome and benefit of this project are to enrich the cultural experience and to improve the quality of education for students to learn about African American history. This outcome will be measured through formal evaluations and surveys that teachers, students and parents will complete.

1616.description: Miami-Dade County Public Schools requests funding to ensure sufficient staffing of an M-DCPS Marketplace at a Community Resource Hub in an under-served area of Miami-Dade County. The goal is to ensure equitable access for students and families to basic necessities such as food and nutrition assistance, school apparel, shoes, toiletries and school supplies at no cost in a dignified manner. All items are new and secured through the establishment of business and community partnerships.
1616.purpose: Funding will provide sufficient staffing of an M-DCPS Marketplace at a Community Resource Hub in an under-served area of Miami-Dade County. The goal is to ensure equitable access for students and families to basic necessities such as food and nutrition assistance, school apparel, shoes, toiletries and school supplies at no cost in a dignified manner. All items are new and secured through the establishment of business and community partnerships.
1616.activities: Funds provided will support essential staffing to maintain and oversee daily operations at an M-DCPS Marketplace at a Community Resource Hub. Staff will assist visitors in accessing basic necessities, such as school apparel, shoes, food/nutrition assistance, toiletries and school supplies, and connect community members with vital resources.
1616.direct_services: M-DCPS Marketplace staff at a Community Resource Hub will provide food and nutrition assistance, brand new school apparel, shoes, toiletries and school supplies at no cost. These services empower families, alleviate financial burdens, and foster economic mobility, ultimately enhancing academic achievement and strengthening the overall success of the community.
1616.population: Over 800 preschool, grade school and high school students and families in Miami-Dade, specifically those who are economically disadvantaged, at-risk, homeless, and jobless.
1616.outcome: M-DCPS Marketplaces at Community Resource Hubs provide economic support to students and families, improving physical health, enhancing economic mobility and self-sufficiency, and positively impacting students' overall wellbeing and contributing to their academic success. This will be measured through the quantitative data of number of students and families receiving assistance.

1617.description: This M-DCPS Mental Health Pilot Program will utilize the BASC-3 BESS (Behavioral and Emotional Screening System) as a prevention measure aiming to efficiently and accurately identify students in grades 4-8, at risk of behavioral, emotional, or social difficulties. The project will include professional development sessions for school staff to enhance proficiency in administering the screener, interpreting results, and developing targeted interventions. Additionally, the program will provide resources for students and families to address identified needs. Screenings will be conducted only with parent consent.
1617.purpose: The funds requested are intended to use the BASC-3 BESS (Behavioral and Emotional Screening System) as a prevent measure to efficiently and accurately identify students in grades 4-8 who may be at risk for developing or already experiencing significant behavioral, emotional, or social difficulties. The professional development will enhance staff knowledge and proficiency in utilizing the assessment instrument, gathering data, and providing students and families with supplementary resources. Scre
1617.activities: The project directly benefits educators, parents, and students who are involved in a child's education and well-being. The information obtained from the BASC-3 BESS can be used to prioritize students for further assessment, guide intervention planning to develop targeted interventions, track a student's progress over time and evaluate the effectiveness of the interventions.
1617.direct_services: The screening will be used as a prevent measure to efficiently and accurately identify students in grades 4-8, who may be at risk for developing or already experiencing significant behavioral, emotional, or social difficulties. Professional development and training for staff will enhance knowledge and proficiency in utilizing the assessment instrument, gathering data, and providing resources to fa
1617.population: This initiative will benefit over 800 students in grades 4-8 in Miami-Dade by improving early identification, as well as teachers/administrators/counselors who will be receiving professional development and training.
1617.outcome: The project aims to improve mental health outcomes for students in grades 4-8 by using the BASC-3 BESS to identify and address behavioral, emotional, and social challenges early, enabling timely and targeted interventions. Outcomes will be measured through data reports tracking the Behavioral and Emotional Risk Index, teacher and parent feedback on behavioral changes, and progress monitoring to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions.

2540.description: The North Bay Village Outfall Valves Upgrade Phase II will install specialized in-line rubber duckbill backflow prevention devices throughout the Village's storm water infrastructure system. These devices will be strategically placed citywide, on the Village's drainage structures along the seawall to prevent unwanted backflow that can cause surcharging and flooding during storm events. The valves feature a maintenance-free design with no mechanical parts or fasteners that could fail or corrode. The project will help protect residential and commercial areas from flooding while reducing maintenance costs and preventing damage to the storm water infrastructure system.
2540.purpose: These funds will achieve enhanced flood protection for North Bay Village through the installation of state-of-the-art backflow prevention valves. The project will prevent tidal waters and storm surge from backing up through the stormwater system, protecting roads, homes, and businesses from flooding while preserving the integrity of the Village's infrastructure.
2540.activities: The Village will perform an engineering analysis of outfall locations citywide, and state funding would provide for the procurement of appropriate valve sizes and specifications, installation of duckbill check valves at identified outfall points, and post-installation testing to ensure proper operation.
2540.direct_services: This project will provide critical flood protection services to the community by preventing tidal backflow and storm surge from entering the stormwater system. The installations will operate automatically based on pressure differential, requiring no external power or manual intervention, while allowing normal stormwater drainage to continue unimpeded during regular conditions.
2540.population: The target population served by this project is the entire population of North Bay Village. About 10,000 individuals are expected to be served.
2540.outcome: The expected outcomes include reduced flooding incidents, decreased infrastructure damage, and lower maintenance costs. Success will be measured through monitoring of flood incidents before and after installation, tracking maintenance requirements and costs, and conducting regular inspections to verify proper valve operation and effectiveness.

1401.description: The Project will enhance the Bal Harbour south inlet waterfront corridor, a critical public access route adjacent to Baker’s Haulover Inlet. The improvements will address documented safety concerns along a narrow and heavily used shoreline path that lacks adequate railings, controlled access points, and emergency response features. The scope includes new over-water lookout platforms to reduce crowding, steps to provide safe and stable access to the water’s edge for first responders, shade structures to protect pedestrians from heat stress, and pedestrian railings to prevent falls. These upgrades will reduce risk of injury, improve storm surge and emergency response conditions, and ensure safe year-round use for residents, visitors, and public safety personnel.
1401.purpose: The funds requested will enhance public safety along the Bal Harbour waterfront by constructing designated overlooks, shade structures, and pedestrian railings that prevent falls, reduce crowding, and provide controlled access to the shoreline. These improvements will create a safer environment for residents, visitors, and first responders year- round.
1401.activities: Activities and services will include construction administration, installation of over-water lookout platforms, pedestrian railings, shade canopies, steps to the water’s edge, and placement of site furnishings, lighting, and signage, all coordinated to improve safety, comfort, and guided public access along the waterfront corridor.
1401.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with direct services including safe and continuous public walking access along the waterfront, shaded rest areas and overlooks for comfort, safe vantage points and steps for interaction with the water’s edge, and improved safety through railings, lighting, and wayfinding signage
1401.population: The project will serve residents, visitors, and first responders by improving safety along a high-traffic public waterfront corridor. The area is one of Bal Harbour’s most visited locations and attracts a significant number of tourists each year. More than 3,000 individuals are expected to benefit from these improvements annually.
1401.outcome: The expected outcome of the project is improved safe and enjoyable public access to Bal Harbour’s waterfront, with enhanced comfort, designated overlooks, and guided pedestrian circulation that reduces unsafe off-path use and protects the shoreline. Success will be measured by completion of the constructed improvements within scope and budget, compliance with permitting and safety standards, and observable increases in safe public use as documented through site inspections, maintenance records, and visitor feedback.

1356.description: In 2025 the Legislature appropriated $2.38 Million out of a $4 million funding request to help make repairs and renovate water-damaged areas at the Orlando Museum of Art (OMA) This year's request will complete the much-needed renovations to water damaged areas including the walls, ceilings, floors, bathrooms, and other public spaces. This funding will help protect the $40 million art collection housed at OMA.
1356.purpose: The funds will support the capital project and help the OMA continue to steward its 40+million-dollar collection. This appropriation will repair all water damaged areas, upgrade all public spaces including, but not limited to, the education and exhibition wings.
1356.activities: The OMA presents 4-5 special exhibitions annually in addition to 4-5 additional exhibits curated from its permanent collection. These exhibitions will inform an industry-leading 12-month calendar of education programming for intergenerational audiences. OMA also hosts field trips from local school districts and home schools.
1356.direct_services: As a result of this funding, OMA will be able to provide enhanced direct services to include annual exhibitions (such as the highly respected Florida Prize in Contemporary Art), in-demand arts education (including workshops, camps, tours, and lectures) and art wellness activities.
1356.population: The target population to be served this project is the general public. An anticipated 155,000 people will be served by the OMA each year over the next five years.
1356.outcome: Expected benefits and outcomes of this project include: 1) enriched cultural experience for visitors, 2) improved facilities for extensive educational programming 3) a first-rate facility that attracts tourists and increases cultural tourism as evidenced by ticket sales outside our local area 4) economic growth in jobs and vendor opportunities. *The methodology that will be used to measure these includes participant surveys, feedback from artists, arts educators and other collaborators, event attendance, the Arts and Economic Prosperity Calculator, and ticket sales.

2594.description: JFCS will maintain the capacity to provide outpatient services such as mental health and substance abuse counseling and psychiatric services, to youth and adults involved in/at-risk of being involved in the Child Welfare system in Alachua, Baker, Bradford and Union Counties. Services will help at-risk families (with little to no access to limited community resources) strengthen healthy family functioning, keeping children and families safe, secure and thriving, physically, socially and emotionally. Funding will help subsidize sliding fee scale counseling and psychiatric services to lower income uninsured individuals in the community who do not have access to timely behavioral health services. Funding will also help remove barriers to access, by providing resources such as, but not limited to transportation assistance to/from sessions and equipment/tablets for tele-health services.
2594.purpose: JFCS will maintain capacity to provide outpatient mental health and substance abuse counseling, and psychiatric services, to lower-income children, teens and adults in Baker, Bradford, Union and Alachua Counties. JFCS currently operates a child welfare case management program in these counties. Services will help at-risk families involved in or at-risk of becoming involved in the Child Welfare system strengthen healthy functioning, helping children and families achieve safety and permanency. Fun
2594.activities: Licensed and license-eligible therapists will provide outpatient mental health counseling services to children, teens and adults, as well as outpatient substance abuse treatment to teens and adults and parenting education. Funding will help subsidize sliding fee-scale services, provide additional program oversight, psychiatric evaluation and medication management services and help remove barriers to access for at-risk individuals. To remove barriers to access, the majority of services will be pr
2594.direct_services: Clients will receive a bio-psychosocial evaluation, treatment plan, counseling sessions and discharge planning. Sessions will typically be weekly, for up to 4 months. Clients may also receive psychiatric evaluation and medication management services, as well as parenting education using a nurturing parenting or other evidence-based curriculum. Additional support to access services may include tran
2594.population: JFCS (under contract with the lead agency, Partnership for Strong Families) provides Child Welfare Case Management services in Baker, Bradford, Union and Alachua Counties. The target population for this project is children, teens and adults engaged in services within the JFCS Child Welfare Case Management program. Clients are either involved in the Dependency Court system or at-risk of becoming involved, and in need of outpatient mental health, outpatient substance abuse and/or psychiatric/med m
2594.outcome: This funding would help lift up these rural communities. Families are operating in crisis mode, and need accessible, timely, affordable mental health care to cope with chronic stress, trauma and fractured family relationships. Accessible mental health and substance abuse counseling is imperative. Substance use is an issue in roughly 80% of child welfare cases. Providing in-home services along with hands-on parenting education will strengthen parent engagement and improve outcomes for children. We expect 80% of clients will reduce their disruptive symptoms as measured by discharge summaries and/or progress note review. We also expect that 80% of dual-diagnosis clients with co-existing mental

1934.description: Valencia College requests $15,001,464 to complete the funding for a much-needed second building for the Lake Nona Campus, which has already grown to serve more than 1,500 FTE in a single building. The new building will support additional degree and certificate programs that will meet growing workforce demands in Orange and Osceola counties, preparing students for high-skill, high-wage careers that are in high demand in advanced manufacturing, technology, and healthcare, and will support state STEM initiatives. The funds will also support a remodel of 6,000 SF of Building 1 to refurbish labs and student support spaces.
1934.purpose: These funds will support a much-needed second building for the Lake Nona Campus, which has already grown to serve more than 1,500 FTE. The building will support new degree and certificate programs that will meet the demands of the growing workforce in Orange and Osceola counties, preparing students for high-skill, high-wage careers that are in high demand in advanced manufacturing, technology, and healthcare, and will support state STEM initiatives.
1934.activities: Construction of classroom and lab spaces to be used for training citizens for high-demand, high-skill, high-wage jobs in technology, advanced manufacturing, and healthcare occupations. This new building will also support increased participation by dual enrollment students from Lake Nona High School located on the property adjacent to Valencia's Lake Nona Campus.
1934.direct_services: Creation of new jobs during the construction phase. Once completed, training of approximately 3,500 additional students annually in science, technology, engineering, and mathematical areas foundational to high-demand, high-skill, high-wage jobs in advanced manufacturing, technology, healthcare and other STEM fields.
1934.population: The target population for this project includes college students, high school students, jobless persons, and economically disadvantaged individuals. The addition of a second building at the Lake Nona Campus is expected to serve an additional 3,500 students each year.
1934.outcome: The project will create additional capacity at the Lake Nona Campus to reduce enrollment bottlenecks overall. This will increase enrollment at the Lake Nona Campus, increase enrollment in workforce programs, increase the number of graduates, and reduce the over-utilization of facilities. This will be measured by: number of students enrolled overall; number of students enrolled at Lake Nona Campus; number of students enrolled in workforce programs; number of graduates in workforce programs; more acceptable facilities utilization rates.

2417.description: Hurricane Idalia (2023) brought a record ~6.8 ft storm surge (above high tide), causing significant damage to Dock Street and Historic Cedar Key. Hurricane Helene (2024) caused a record 9.2 ft storm surge which was the worst storm damage in modern history for Cedar Key, with infrastructure sustaining significant damage. Road flooding impacted recovery efforts to the most impacted areas. This project features innovative wave attenuation devices (which have been deployed by FDOT and other Florida governmental organizations) to attenuate 90% of wave energy, protecting Dock Street and the economic center of Cedar Key from continuing deterioration due to sea level rise and the threat of catastrophic failure from natural disasters.
2417.purpose: Project was created in response to Hurricane Idalia where flood storm surge battered Dock Street and historic Cedar Key with transportation and other infrastructure sustaining significant damage, along with flooded, damaged roads hampering recovery efforts. Project features include wave attenuation devices that will stop 90% of wave energy, protecting Dock Street and the economic center of Cedar Key from future catastrophic failure associated with natural disasters and sea level rise.
2417.activities: Project will feature proven wave attenuation devices that will be used to protect Dock Street and the business district in historic Cedar Key from storm surge and flooding to create a more resilient location allowing for improved access and mobility into the community, risk prevention, mitigation, remediation, and improvements to the area.
2417.direct_services: Safe access to a public road (Dock Street) with a 90% risk reduction in flooding and disruption of a critical transportation route for residents and visitors
2417.population: Levy County and the City of Cedar Key serving over 800 residents and visitors annually.
2417.outcome: The project would improve transportation conditions by stabilizing Dock Street and nearby roads, reducing storm surge, erosion, washouts, road undermining, and flooding that can block access to businesses and homes. This ensures safer, more reliable travel for residents, visitors, and emergency vehicles, even during storms or high-water events. Project could also provide mitigation offsets, and improved water quality and habitat benefits.

1935.description: Tiny Talkers Initiative: Our Tiny Talkers Initiative aims to provide an additional 600 Duval County 2 - 6-year-olds, located at 30 more preschools, with diagnostic screenings, evaluations and treatments (as needed) of speech/language disorders including: oral motor speech disorder, receptive and expressive language disorder, stuttering/disfluency, and apraxia. Our early intervention speech-language initiative leverages community partnerships with preschools, which allow us to utilize their space so we can serve the children in the place that's most convenient for them and their caregivers.
1935.purpose: Continuation of the Tiny Talkers Initiative, which aims to provide 600 Duval County 2 - 6-year-olds, located at 30 more preschools, with diagnostic screenings, evaluations and treatments (as needed) of speech/language disorders including: oral motor speech disorder, receptive and expressive language disorder, stuttering/disfluency, and apraxia. Our early intervention speech-language initiative leverages community partnerships with preschools, which allow us to utilize their space so we can serve
1935.activities: Provide speech-language screenings, evaluations and treatment (if needed) to children identified as most in need of speech-language support and provide educational materials to parents, caregivers and childcare facility staff to identify children with speech-language deficits, understand the importance of evaluating and treating it and support the work done in therapy sessions, with clinicians.
1935.direct_services: Provide speech-language screenings, evaluations and treatments (if needed) to preschool aged children identified as most in need of speech-language development so they may enter elementary school with identical communication skills as their same aged peers.
1935.outcome: Improve quality of education: For every child entering into therapy, a unique set of goals is set based on standardized testing. Progress is monitored and recorded on each of those goals. Goals are updated accordingly. Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS- 5) or other standardized age-appropriate assessments are used to identify any deficits and develop an individual plan for each child. The PLS-5 provides a comprehensive development language assessment for children from ages birth to 7. It assesses nine major areas of auditory comprehension.

2781.description: To strengthen and equip individuals, especially caregivers, justice-impacted adults, and trauma survivors—as they pursue healing, independence, and long-term stability. Healing Horizons 101 offers the support necessary to access essential resources, foster personal growth, and secure meaningful employment or vocational opportunities, including pathways into the workforce, military service, and community service roles. Caregivers, in particular, often experience secondary trauma as they watch a loved one shift from strong to weak, from capable to dependent, or from mentally sharp to forgetful. Our programs help them recognize and address this hidden emotional burden while continuing their journey toward resilience and recovery.
2781.purpose: The requested funds will allow Healing Horizons 101 to provide trauma-informed services that strengthen caregivers, trauma survivors, and justice-impacted individuals. Funding will support structured trauma-healing groups, caregiver tools and training, coping-skills development, and community support circles. It will reduce caregiver burnout, improve emotional stability, and connect participants to vocational and workforce pathways. Overall, these funds will expand access, increase capacity, and
2781.activities: Funds will support trauma-informed services including: -- Facilitated trauma healing group sessions. -- Caregiver support workshops addressing burnout and secondary trauma. -- Individual stabilization coaching and crisis-prevention support. -- Workforce and vocational pathway assistance for participants seeking stability and employment. -- Resource navigation to connect families with community and mental health services. -- Program surveys and evaluations to measure outcomes and improve service
2781.direct_services: The appropriation will provide direct services including trauma-healing group sessions, caregiver support workshops, coping-skills training, mental-health and stress-reduction activities, participant assessments, vocational and workforce readiness guidance, and referrals to community resources. These services directly support caregivers, trauma survivors, and justice-impacted individuals in achiev
2781.population: The target population includes caregivers, trauma survivors, justice-impacted individuals, veterans, and adults experiencing emotional stress or instability. The program also serves caregivers supporting loved ones with terminal illness, physical decline, cognitive impairment, or other conditions that create secondary trauma
2781.outcome: Expected Benefit or Outcome: Improved emotional stability, reduced caregiver burnout, stronger coping skills, and greater overall well-being for caregivers, trauma survivors, veterans, justice-impacted individuals, and those supporting loved ones with terminal illness. Methodology: Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-surveys, participant feedback, attendance data, and facilitator observations to track changes in stress levels, coping skills, and overall progress.

2599.description: The funds will be used for the design phase of the Ludlam Trail Corridor. The Ludlam Trail is a 5.6-mile greenway corridor from SW 80th St to NW 7th St (between 69-70 Avenues) including dedicated pedestrian and bicycle pathways. It will be used for non-motorized active transportation to work, school and play and connects to 5 greenways, 4 parks, 2 transit hubs and 3 schools. Ludlam Trail is designated as a priority trail by the Florida Dept. of Environmental Protection.
2599.purpose: The funding requested would be allocated toward the design of the Ludlam Trail Corridor, a shared use path for non- motorized transportation and recreational uses. The Ludlam Trail Corridor will consist of dedicated pathways for bicyclists and pedestrians, and includes six pedestrian bridges over roadways and canals to provide for safe crossings and connectivity.
2599.activities: Design of the Ludlam Trail Corridor will provide opportunities for residents and visitors to Miami-Dade County with options for non-motorized transportation and connectivity to residential areas, parks, schools, transit hubs, economic activity areas. Additionally, the trail will provide opportunities for recreation, increased health and wellness, and social activities.
2599.direct_services: This project will directly improve safety for bicyclists and pedestrians along 5.6 continuous miles to schools, parks, businesses, and shopping. It will connect more than 40,000 people in a half-mile walkable service area to 3 greenways, 5 schools, 4 parks, and 2 transit hubs. It will be a catalyst to increase civic participation and unite the social fabric of the community creating a better quali
2599.population: The project will serve residents across Miami-Dade County and visitors of all ages and abilities. Tens of thousands of individuals will benefit from the project.
2599.outcome: -Increased physical activity and improved mental health in the community for residents living near the trail and residents and visitors of Miami-Dade County, measured via Health Impact Assessment. -Improved bicycle and pedestrian safety, as well as provide a safe route to schools, measured via number of bicyclist and pedestrian injuries/deaths in the vicinity. -Reduced congestion on local roads due to an alternative means of non-motorized transportation, measured via Traffic Impact Studies.

1304.description: The project involves enhancing stormwater management practices in the project area by implementing engineering strategies to mitigate flooding in the public right-of-way, thereby raising the area's stormwater drainage system, and improving the Level of Service protection for both water quantity and water quality. Project location: Grand Avenue from Brooker Street to Jefferson Street.
1304.purpose: The goal of the Grand Ave / Brooker Street project is to reduce flooding and protect properties and possible life by raising the area's drainage system to provide a standard Level of Service to mitigate flooding by installing 535 linear feet of French drains, three (3) drainage inlets, and six manholes. Project seeks to improve the storage capacity and conveyance of the stormwater drainage infrastructure. Project location: Grand Avenue from Brooker Street to Jefferson Street.
1304.activities: Installation of 535 linear feet of French drains, three (3) drainage inlets, and six manholes.
1304.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
1304.outcome: Mitigate flooding by improving the stormwater drainage infrastructure—measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

1260.description: The project will address increased skill building and community integration opportunities for adults with significant disabilities. Brevard’s Adults with Disabilities project is designed to: 1- Provide life skills training to those who are not currently able to sustain community employment. 2- Increase independence by teaching functional community and safety skills and decrease reliance on state funding. 3 - Enhance access to community involvement and enrichment activities. 4- Enhance the current adult educational environment to promote life-long learning.
1260.purpose: To increase life and community safety skills, build independence and ensure community involvement by adults with significant disabilities.
1260.activities: Specific, highly-detailed curriculum will be used to train the many areas of life skills and expected behaviors in the community. Funding will also allow our participants with disabilities to participate in the community as much as possible, which is accomplished via community trips to local resources (library, Career Source, local employers, volunteering, etc.).
1260.direct_services: Adults with disabilities will receive intensive classroom instruction; participate in community practicums; hear from community leaders and other speakers; engage in numerous involvement outings and complete volunteer projects at multiple community-based organizations.
1260.population: Adults with disabilities who need further life skills training; current and future participants in our Adult Day Training program who want to improve their life skills and become more fully engaged citizens. At a minimum, 80 individuals will be served.
1260.outcome: 1- 100 percent of participants will complete a skills interest inventory to access training, integration and development needs. 2- 100 percent of participants will demonstrate appropriate social and interpersonal skills in both workplace and community based settings. 3- At a minimum, 70% of participants will participate in two community integration activities per month.

1996.description: Save Lives and Bridge Divides by providing police officers the effective training they desperately want and need at a fraction of traditional costs using groundbreaking simulation technology infused into real-world theme-park inspired environments. Studies consistently prove the most effective form of police training to be immersive scenario-based training. Decision Tactical’s modern facility enables officers to practice proper response to crisis situations in highly- immersive stress-inducing environments before facing them on the streets. This greatly improves policing skills including stress inoculation, threat assessment, bias-free policing, de-escalation, emotionally-disturbed-person engagements, tactical movement and active-assailant response.
1996.purpose: Significant improvement in policing skills including stress inoculation, threat assessment, bias-free policing, deescalation, emotionally-disturbed-person engagements, tactical movement and active-assailant response. In turn, lives of both officers and the public at large are saved. Decision Tactical's unique training environment puts LEOs in real-world settings – from mall shopping centers to dimly lit hallways. Threats can emerge from any angle, replicating the unpredictable nature of real-lif
1996.activities: Scenario-based training for LEOs at less than the cost of ammo. DTAC’s engineers maintain and operate the hyperefficient facility, allowing targeted repeatable training at a fraction of the time and cost. This means more training opportunities for officers on critical skills. Proprietary technology captures movement, concealment, communication, and every aspect of performance. Post-training reviews allow for in-depth analysis and precise corrections, maximizing the impact of each training sessio
1996.direct_services: Training the LEOs receive will result in better public safety. The LEOs will have better training how to interact with different types of people and in stressful situations. LEOs will be better trained in de-escalation and develop stronger deescalation skills, resulting in fewer incidents that require use of force. When use of force is required, LEOs will have utilized these skills in advance to h
1996.population: Law enforcement officers in Seminole, Orange, Volusia, Polk, Lake, Brevard, Marion, Sumter and Osceola counties are the target population for this project. 5,000 LEOs will be trained with these funds. The impacts on the communities they serve are exponential as every person and situation that a trained LEO encounters will have a better interaction and a better outcome. We will match state grant to maximize LEO enrollement.
1996.outcome: The benefit of this project is to have better trained Law Enforcement Officers. We expect them to not only be peace keepers and enforce the law but also social workers and to have skills where most have not had proper training. This training will result in better outcomes with LEO interactions including an increase in incidents with successful deescalation resolving the issue, reduced use of force, safer and more effective use of force when necessary, and an overall improved view of LEOs. In addition, LEOs will get the support they need, enhancing their mental health, and keeping more LEOs on the job instead of leaving due to the stress that they are not trained to.

1358.description: DMF Employment Opportunities’ target population are adults, ages 18 to 60, with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) who wish to gain full-time employment and become self-reliant in South Florida. The Employment Project currently has 77 Employer Partners and 155 participants employed in a variety of fields. The model implemented by DMF Employment Opportunities (DMF) follows a 5-step process that aligns with the evidence-based practice of Customized Employment with a customer focus on the employer and the addition of extended services for the employee. This approach has proven to be successful in generating stable employment while encouraging the hiring of individuals with intellectual and development disabilities (IDD) through long-term partnerships beyond the traditional 90 to 150-day period.
1358.purpose: The funds will specifically help sustain extended services integral to maintaining long-term employment outcomes for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). An investment in extended services yields positive employment outcomes for young adults with IDD, which leads to economic growth and less dependence on government assistance.
1358.activities: Offer extended services to at least 200 individuals seeking employment, currently employed, or recently employed to obtain or maintain employment and ensure the employees thrive or grow in their current positions. This includes: (1) Weekly: Engage participants technologically to build work and independent living skills while preventing isolation and promoting mental wellness (2) Weekly and monthly: Peer group meetings, counseling sessions, and social skills training facilitated by a mental healt
1358.direct_services: Eligible citizens will receive intensive supported employment services in accordance with the Customized Employment model adopted by DMF Employment Opportunities. The appropriation project will specifically fund intensive job coaching to ensure transition into stable employment and extended services to maintain employment.
1358.population: All participants served are adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities who seek employment and self- reliance in South Florida. DMF expects to place participants in 35 new job opportunities during the project period. The 153 participants currently employed will continue to access services to maintain employment and the 70 participants seeking employment will receive job and life skills trainings until a job opportunity is identified that matches the participants skills and intere
1358.outcome: Activities focused on continuous support for both the employer and the employee with a disability beyond the traditional 90 to 150-day period will be provided to ensure long-term employment outcomes for program participants. -Secure 15 new job opportunities with new or existing Employer Partners -Place 35 new participants in employment. -80% of participants will remain employed with the same Employer Partner for a minimum of 1 year; 70% for over 2 years - Increase work hours or hourly rate for 15 new or existing participants.

The project incorporates important stormwater improvements, including a drainage swale on the west side of Gadson Street, which is necessary due to the expansion of impervious area within the FDOT right-of-way. The trail is routed along the east side, using parcel AltKey: 1437423, because constraints like utilities and city design standards limit placement options. The alignment is designed to swing around an existing utility pole and comply with buffer and width requirements, providing the needed connection to the SR 50 sidewalk while integrating adequate stormwater management measures The project is partially funded by a local foundation (Live Well Foundation of South Lake), benefits very-low, low
1938.purpose: The specific purpose and goals to be achieved by the requested state funds are to construct critical infrastructure improvements along Gadson Street Trail. These funds will enable the installation of ADA-compliant sidewalks and walkways, enhanced stormwater management systems, and roadway upgrades. The project aims to improve pedestrian safety, increase accessibility, reduce flooding, and protect water quality in Lake David. Ultimately, the funds will support community revitalization, environmen
1938.activities: Construction of ADA-compliant walkways, installation of advanced stormwater management systems (such as bioretention areas, swales, and drainage structures), roadway reconstruction. These activities will improve pedestrian safety, accessibility, flood mitigation, and water quality, directly supporting community revitalization and environmental resilience within the project area. All work will be performed in compliance with state and federal grant requirements and will benefit low- to moderate-i
1938.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to citizens by constructing new ADA-compliant walkways for safer, more accessible pedestrian routes; improving stormwater management to reduce flooding and enhance water quality; upgrading roadways for better traffic flow and safety; and stabilizing the shoreline with native vegetation to protect the local environment. These improvements will
1938.population: The target population served by this project is the residents of the City of Groveland, specifically those living in the Gadson Street corridor. The project service area is comprised of greater than 51% low- to moderate-income individuals, ensuring the project primarily benefits these groups. The City of Groveland has a population of 18,505 (2020 Census), and while the exact number of individuals directly served will depend on the final project boundaries, the improvements are designed to benefi
1938.outcome: The project is expected to deliver safer, more accessible pedestrian routes, improved stormwater management to reduce flooding and enhance water quality and upgraded roadways. These outcomes will increase walkability, public safety, environmental resilience, and overall quality of life for residents, especially those in low- to moderate-income areas. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the completion of ADA-compliant sidewalks and walkways, the installation and performance of stormwater systems, and the reduction in localized flooding incidents. Additional metrics may include pre- and post-project pedestrian counts, resident satisfaction surveys, water quality testing in Lake David, and do

1311.organization: The Housing Authority of the City of Key
1311.description: The Lang Milian Apartments is a 136-unit public housing community that was built in 1941 and located on +/- 8.77 acres owned by the Housing Authority of the City of Key West, Florida (the KWHA). Due to physical obsolescence of the structures, the KWHA plans to demolish the entire site and rebuild, utilizing primarily first bond proceeds from the sale of private activity bonds together with investment raised from equity in exchange for 4% low-income housing tax credits that are allocated in conjunction with the bonds. The KWHA plans to increase the overall number of new units to 196 (60 incremental units).
1311.purpose: The project will replace aging, substandard housing with new, code-compliant affordable units, improving safety, resilience, and quality of life for low-income residents while maintaining the community’s essential affordable housing stock.
1311.activities: Activities funded through this request will include site preparation, demolition of existing obsolete housing structures, and construction of new, code-compliant affordable housing units. Additional activities will include necessary infrastructure improvements, such as utilities, drainage, and access, along with associated planning, engineering, and permitting services. These activities will result in the creation of safe, resilient, and energy-efficient homes for low- income residents in Key We
1311.direct_services: The project will directly provide safe, decent, and affordable rental housing for low-income residents of Key West. By replacing obsolete units with new, resilient, energy-efficient homes, the project will improve living conditions, enhance housing stability, and support the local workforce and families in Monroe County.
1311.population: The target population includes low-income individuals and families in Key West who are in need of affordable, safe, and sustainable housing. The project will replace obsolete housing units with new affordable rental units, serving 196 households, or an estimated 400 residents (1 BR - 79; 2 BR – 74; 3 BR – 43). Priority will be given to income-qualified households consistent with Florida Housing Finance Corporation and HUD program guidelines.
1311.outcome: Benefit: Provide safe, affordable, and resilient housing for low-income residents in Key West. Measurement: Track the number of completed units, households served, compliance with building and energy standards, and adherence to affordability requirements.

The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance.
1413.purpose: Reduction in flooding and protection of properties on SW 153 Street from SW 103 Place to SW 106 Avenue by installing 580 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 14 drainage structures. The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance.
1413.activities: Installation of 80 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 14 drainage structures.

1413.outcome: Mitigate flooding by improving the stormwater drainage infrastructure—measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

The project involves raising the area's stormwater drainage infrastructure to provide a standard level of service to mitigate flooding and increase storage capacity and conveyance.
1414.purpose: Reduction in flooding and protection of properties on SW 200 Terrace from SW 129 Avenue to SW 130 Avenue by installing 400 linear feet of exfiltration trenches and 7 drainage inlets. 1759.description: The proposed renovation site at 6015 Pointe West Blvd. Bradenton, Fl was constructed in 1998 as an ambulatory surgery center (ASC) that ceased to operate. Upon MCR leasing the facility with plans to operate an ASC and bring much needed access to care to the uninsured and underinsured, the licensure requirements changed. MCR must renovate a portion of the facility to comply with Florida statutes and improve access to care for the underserved.
1759.purpose: The proposed renovation site at 6015 Pointe West Blvd. Bradenton, Fl was constructed in 1998 as an ambulatory surgery center (ASC) that ceased to operate. Upon MCR leasing the facility, MCR planned to operate an ASC and bring much needed access to care to the uninsured and underinsured (target population). MCR engaged a consultant to review the location's compliance with license requirements. MCR must renovate a portion of the facility to comply with Florida statutes to operate an ASC which will
1759.activities: The facility will be renovated to address licensure improvements. Once completed, the location will provide an additional access point for needed surgical procedures, specifically for the target population. The ASC is a less expensive alternative to uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid and commercial plans than having certain procedures conducted at a hospital. The less expensive option creates the opportunity, especially for those who are uninsured and underinsured, to elect to have earlier diagno
1759.direct_services: Once renovated, MCR will offer an access point for any person in the community needing non emergent services specifically the target population. Specialty services include, but are not be limited to cardiology, podiatry, dermatology, gynecology and gastroenterology. Offering these services at an ASC would be less expensive for the uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid and commercial plans than at an o
1759.population: All residents will have access to services provided. As a Federally Qualified Health Center, MCR offers its services regardless of the persons ability to pay and offers a sliding fee discount program for office visits. It is estimated approximately 13,000 patients will receive services at the location from specialty providers. Those who are identified as needing surgical procedures will be scheduled at MCR's ASC rather than the hospital.
1759.outcome: The benefit would be realized after the renovation is completed and an access point is established to provide services to the target population - uninsured and underinsured. The project outcome can be measured through receipt of the certificate of occupancy issued by Manatee County Government and receipt of the license to operate an ASC issued by the State of Florida.

1357.organization: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
1357.description: The state’s one-time investment will ensure the Frost Planetarium at the Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science (Frost Science) remains a world-class resource for immersive science communication, STEM education, and community engagement across Florida. The current 8K dome projection system, in operation since the museum’s opening in 2017, is nearing the end of its useful life and must be replaced with a new laser projection system to prevent significant operational disruptions and rising maintenance costs. This initiative will safeguard an essential piece of Florida’s scientific, educational, and cultural infrastructure; support workforce development in technology and innovation; and ensure cultural assets continue to serve as engines of economic growth. With over $103 million in annual economic impact statewide, Frost Science continues to boost tourism and enhance quality of life
1357.purpose: The requested funds will address the urgent and unavoidable need to replace the Frost Planetarium’s current projection system, which is nearing the end of its operational life and must be replaced to avoid significant disruptions to programming. The aging, bulb-based technology is at the end of its life, and there is no annual service available to maintain it, making continued operation unsustainable. This funding will ensure the planetarium remains operational while enabling the broader moderni
1357.activities: To fulfill the goals of this project, Frost Science will install a new state-of-the-art laser projection system in the Frost Planetarium. These enhancements will expand the museum’s ability to deliver dynamic educational programming that aligns with school curricula, while also offering immersive learning experiences for visitors of all ages, from early childhood to senior citizens. The new infrastructure will support advanced visual storytelling and enable collaborations with academic and nonpr
1357.direct_services: This appropriation will directly benefit Florida citizens through enhanced access to educational programming in the upgraded Frost Planetarium. The immersive experience will include live science shows, astronomy demonstrations, and educational content aligned with Florida education standards. Students and educators will benefit from hands-on training opportunities, and academic partners will have
1357.population: The target population includes K–12 students, teachers, college students, senior citizens, and general museum visitors. Approximately 58,600 students visit the museum annually on field trips and will benefit from free Frost Planetarium shows. Over 1,700 students from 37 schools participate in the museum’s STEM Designation program, and more than 200 educators engage in professional development annually. In total, the Frost Planetarium currently draws over 460,000 guests each year, making this pro
1357.outcome: This project is expected to improve educational access, enhance guest satisfaction, lower operational costs, and expand career-building opportunities in key STEM and creative technology fields. Outcomes will be measured through several methods: annual attendance data, satisfaction and feedback surveys, program participation tracking, and reporting from academic and nonprofit partners. We will also track reductions in maintenance costs, particularly related to the replacement of projection bulbs, which currently exceed $100,000 annually. Together, these metrics will provide a clear picture of the project’s return on investment for the State of Florida.

1740.description: Improving drainage and stormwater systems with a reduction of debris entering the system. A street sweeper will be purchased and utilized regularly. This sweeper will also support surrounding cities as needed.
1740.purpose: Improving drainage and stormwater systems with a reduction of debris entering the system. A street sweeper will be purchased and utilized regularly. This sweeper will also support surrounding cities as needed
1740.activities: Clean streets will attract more residents and tourists to the area for walking or running along the adjacent sidewalk. The applicant will frequently count the number of people using pathways and streets and survey their opinions of their experiences.
1740.direct_services: Clean streets will attract more residents and tourists to the area for walking or running along the adjacent sidewalks. The applicant will frequently count the number of people using the pathways and streets and survey their opinions of their experiences.
1740.outcome: The reduction in vegetative debris and trash from entering the stormwater/waste water system will greatly improve the quality of the system. Additionally, the mechanical sweeper will prevent debris and trash from entering waterways where fish and wildlife exist. The applicant will encourage citizen groups to annually survey fish and wildlife in the area and report increases in natural activity to the Town and the Town will further report to the Department of Natural Resources.

2538.description: Miami-Dade County Seaport Department, PortMiami, is in critical need of funding assistance for a portion of the cost to replace the North Bulkhead. The overall North Bulkhead Improvement project will reconstruct and realign six berths along the north side of PortMiami within 7 years, including design. These specific funds will go towards both the engineering/soft construction phase which commences in Summer 2025, and the final construction of the first berth, which commences in January 2027.
2538.purpose: The overall North Bulkhead Improvement project will reconstruct and realign six berths along the north side of PortMiami within 7 years, including design. These specific funds will go towards both the engineering/soft construction phase which commences in Summer 2025, and the final construction of the first berth, which commences in January 2027.
2538.activities: Funds for this project will go towards typical construction activities for a new bulkhead including new berthing structures, expansion and reconstruction of the existing apron to tie into the new berthing structure, upgraded stormwater drainage system, scour protection, mooring and fendering systems, concourse expansion, and new utilities as needed, including water, electrical, and IT. After completion of the first berth, the terminal will re-open and able to accept the largest cruise vessels in
2538.direct_services: The North Bulkhead Improvement project will support port operations by providing a stable and safe bulkhead for 6 berths at PortMiami, for both present and future needs of the cruise industry in the State of Florida. In calendar year 2023, PortMiami supported 21,689 direct jobs and $376.9 million of state and local taxes in cruise activity alone.
2538.population: PortMiami, a Miami-Dade County department, is a regional asset and generates employment for residents in south Florida. According to the 2023 Local and Regional Economic Impacts of PortMiami study prepared by Martin Associated in March 2024, these 6 berths generously contributed to over $10.1B in economic activity, 8 million cruise passengers, and 31,000 direct and indirect jobs. This number will continue to grow as these new bulkheads will have built-in flexibility to accommodate all cruise ves
2538.outcome: This project will provide a low maintenance, new bulkhead, marine apron, and berthing and mooring facilities that, as a system, have a serviceable design life of at least 75 years and safely support cruise ships and terminal operations. This outcome will be measured by tracking the completion date in accordance with the project schedule.

1303.description: The City of Miramar’s Lift Station Improvements Program will rehabilitate and upgrade 136 wastewater lift stations citywide. These upgrades will replace aging pumps, valves, and controls to prevent failures, reduce emergency repairs, and ensure reliable wastewater service. The project will improve system efficiency, protect public health, and maintain compliance with environmental regulations.
1303.purpose: The requested funds will support the City of Miramar’s Lift Station Improvements, upgrades and rehabilitation, which upgrades over 130 lift stations citywide.
1303.activities: The project will fund construction and rehabilitation of lift station components including pumps, valves, wetwells, telemetry systems, and supporting infrastructure. Activities include replacement of aging equipment, preventative maintenance upgrades, and compliance-related improvements.
1303.direct_services: The project will provide residents with improved wastewater management, reduced risk of sewage overflows, and enhanced environmental protection. This directly benefits citizens through safer neighborhoods, reduced health hazards, and more reliable utility service.
1303.population: The project serves the entire population of Miramar, approximately 135,000 residents, as well as businesses and institutions connected to the City’s wastewater system. This includes schools, hospitals, commercial centers, industrial facilities, and municipal buildings that rely on consistent and secure wastewater infrastructure to operate effectively. By safeguarding service reliability, the project not only protects public health and the environment but also ensures uninterrupted operations for
1303.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved wastewater system reliability, fewer emergency repairs, reduced regulatory citations, and extended infrastructure lifespan. Success will be measured by tracking reduction in system failures, frequency of emergency repairs, compliance with EPA/DEP standards, and operational cost savings.

1312.description: The Rise Miami-Dade Loan Fund is a revolving loan fund created for local small business owners to provide an easy access to capital at an affordable rate. Small business owners that have been in business for a minimum of two years, with less than 50 employees, less than $5 million in gross annual sales, and a personal credit score of 620 or higher can apply for up to $75,000 with a five-year repayment period at a rate of Prime minus 1%.
1312.purpose: The funds will be directly lent out to small business owners in Miami-Dade County, utilizing a revolving loan model that continues to reinvest repaid funds into new loans, sustaining a long-term cycle of opportunity and helping small business owners build credit, grow revenue, and contribute to local job creation.
1312.activities: Funds will be lent out to qualifying small businesses in Miami-Dade County at a low interest rate, generally unavailable from private lenders, the proceeds from which are reinvested into the RISE program fund to continue to provide affordable capital to other businesses.
1312.population: Small business owners and underserved small businesses in Miami-Dade County will be served by the funding. 25-50 individuals will be served, though the long-term number could be substantially greater due to the program's model of reinvesting proceeds and the impressively low delinquency rate that the RISE program boasts, as well as the trickle- down benefits reaped from jobs that the recipient businesses create.
1312.outcome: Increased economic activity and job creation. Increased economic activity shall be measured by recording the annual revenue of recipient businesses when receiving the loan, then again 12 months after receiving the loan. Job creation shall be measured by recipient providing information on number of employees of business before receiving loan and 12 months after receipt of funds.

1350.description: The City of Hawthorne seeks funding to replace critical components at its aging wastewater treatment facility to maintain reliable, efficient, and compliant operation. Improvements include replacement of the clarifier drive unit, installation of a new flow meter, and stainless-steel diffusers to improve treatment performance and energy efficiency. These upgrades are essential to prevent equipment failure, reduce operating costs, and protect public health and the environment while ensuring continued regulatory compliance and extending the life of the facility.
1350.purpose: The purpose of this project is to replace deteriorated components at Hawthorne’s wastewater treatment facility to ensure reliable and compliant operation. The improvements will enhance treatment performance, reduce operating costs, and protect public health and the environment while extending the useful life of the existing facility.
1350.activities: Funds will be used for construction and engineering services during construction to replace critical components at the City’s wastewater treatment facility. Work includes installation of a new clarifier drive unit, flow meter, and stainless- steel diffusers, along with project management and contractor coordination to ensure proper installation and system functionality.
1350.direct_services: The project will ensure reliable wastewater treatment service for residents and businesses, protecting public health, preventing environmental contamination, and supporting safe, sustainable living conditions within the community.
1350.population: The target population served by this project includes the residents and businesses within the City of Hawthorne who rely on the wastewater treatment facility for safe and reliable wastewater disposal. The project will directly benefit approximately 1,500 individuals by ensuring continued access to essential sanitation services, protecting public health, and supporting the local economy.
1350.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to improve the reliability, efficiency, and compliance of Hawthorne’s wastewater treatment facility, ensuring continuous operation and protection of public health and the environment. The outcome will be measured through ongoing observation of treatment system performance, documentation of maintenance activity, and review of operational and compliance records maintained by City staff.
