Remote monitoring and AI tools to prevent chronic disease complications. Workforce support with modern digital tools to lower the administrative burden and extend reach Stronger data sharing/cybersecurity to ensure compliance and patient trust.
1997.purpose: Upgrade of Meditech Electronic Health Record (EHR) system from version 6.0 to Expanse. Expansion of digital health and telehealth to boost access and reduce avoidable ER visits. Remote monitoring and AI tools to prevent chronic disease complications. Workforce support with modern digital tools to lower their administrative burden and extend reach. Stronger data sharing/cybersecurity to ensure compliance and patient trust.
1997.activities: AI-enabled coordination to cut avoidable ER visits. A Digital Health Command Center for disaster readiness Integration of social data to advance equity. Workforce training via TEACH/LINE-aligned
1997.direct_services: 24/7 telehealth access to doctors and specialists. Home-based remote monitoring for seniors and high-risk groups. Digital maternal/child health support, via patient apps for reminders and secure messaging. Digital continuity of care during hurricanes to keep Brevard residents connected even when in-person care is unavailable.
1997.outcome: (1) Reduced Emergency Room vists. (2) Expanded access to care through Telehealth, Remote Monitoring, (3) Artificial Intelligence and Digital Coordination.(4) Workforce enablement with digital tools and TEACH/LINE training, (5) Equity gains for Medicaid, rural, and underserved groups.(6) Secure, interoperable information technology (IT) with Health Iinformation Exchange (HIE), (7) A digital command center ensuring continuity of care during disasters. Key Performance Indicators will be designed to measure these outcomes.

2657.description: These funds will be used for construction of the Biscayne-Everglades Greenway (BEG) Segment D, a 2.5-mile segment of the greenway between SW 117th Ave. and SW 137th Ave. along the Mowry Canal and SW 320th St. in southern Miami-Dade County, east of Homestead. The Biscayne-Everglades Greenway will be the first non-motorized trail in the country to connect two National Parks and would have an immediate impact to Homestead and the surrounding communities in southern Miami-Dade County.
2657.purpose: These funds will be used for construction of the Biscayne-Everglades Greenway (BEG) Segment D, a 2.5-mile segment of the greenway between SW 117th Ave. and SW 137th Ave. along the Mowry Canal and SW 320th St. in southern Miami-Dade County, east of Homestead. The Biscayne-Everglades Greenway will be the first non-motorized trail in the country to connect two National Parks and would have an immediate impact to Homestead and the surrounding communities in southern Miami-Dade County.
2657.activities: These funds will contribute directly to the construction activities of the BEG, which when complete, will provide citizens with new access to two National Parks, as well as an alternative mode of transportation and opportunities for physical activity and outdoor recreation.
2657.direct_services: The BEG will provide citizens with facilities for active transportation, outdoor recreation, physical activity, and connection to other area trails. This project will be the first non-motorized trail in the country to connect two National Parks and would have an immediate economic impact to Homestead and other communities in southern Miami-Dade County.
2657.population: The project is targeted to serve the 2.8 million residents of Miami-Dade County as a form of non-motorized transportation in a rapidly-growing area of the County that lacks facilities. This includes elderly persons, persons with poor mental or physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, developmentally or physically disabled, preschool students, grade school students, high school students, as well as university and college students.
2657.outcome: Project benefits include physical and mental health improvements, quality of life enrichment, cultural experience enrichment, environmental enhancement/preservation/improvements, improved bike and ped safety, safe route to schools, transportation conditions improvement, economic activity improvements, increased tourism, immediate job opportunities, and individuals' economic self sufficiency enhancements. Methodology for measures include health impact assessments, event attendance and greenway usage counts, heat index and tree canopy calculations, numbers of bike and ped injuries and deaths, traffic impact studies, trail user surveys and economic impact studies, sales revenues and sales tax g

1583.description: The purpose of the funding request is to restore an area of mangroves protecting our drinking water. In 2019 the County surveyed mangrove die-off areas around Biscayne Bay and through inter-agency coordination with state and federal agencies identified management actions that can restore the coastline. This technique was used in 2008 by the County to enhance and restore a mangrove forest in Coral Gables and the county would like to scale the technique to south Dade county.
1583.purpose: Restoration of a mangrove forest to improve water quality and protect our drinking water. This technique was succesfully used in in the past to enhance and restore a mangrove forest in Coral Gables, and the County would now like to scale the technique to South Dade County.
1583.activities: Growing, site preparation, installation and maintenance of mangrove forest.
1583.direct_services: Improved water quality as a result of strategic mangrove restoration.
1583.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served by improved water quality.
1583.outcome: Elevation of mangrove forests will increase the stage of freshwater when implemented at a watershed scale. This protects groundwater from saltwater intrusion—measured by number of trees planted as well as accretion (elevation) of muck soils.

2605.description: The Mizell Stormwater Management Facility (SWMF) conveys and treats stormwater runoff from the City of St. Augustine Beach. The Mizell SWMF's master stormwater pump station discharges to the Matanzas River via the Mizell outfall. Erosion and sedimentation has led to the outfall's deterioration. The project consists of design, permitting and construction of approximately 631 feet of water application retaining wall to stabilize the outfall south bank and mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties.
2605.purpose: Enhance durability of the south bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact. Critical infrastructure preservation by sustaining the outfall's volumetric capacity and pollution prevention (erosion of adjacent properties) into this tributary of the Matanzas River. Reduce 1) cost of proactive and 2) frequency of reactive emergency maintenance along this vital outfall segment.
2605.direct_services: An increased Level of Service (LOS) by constructing durable and resilient critical infrastructure to minimize upstream flooding by sustaining the outfall conveyance's volumetric capacity. Stabilize the outfall south bank to mitigate present and projected surge impact and erosion of adjacent properties. Reduction in frequency of reactive emergency maintenance empowers staff to focus on other areas.
2605.population: City of St. Augustine Beach residents and a portion of St. Johns County residents. Greater than 7,000 individuals are served.
2605.outcome: Stormwater management improvement: 1) Reduce floodwater inundation depth and duration: Regularly updated Vulnerability Assessment/modeling. 2) Protect water resources: Inundation depth and duration measurements. 3) Reduce impact to public assets: City staff observations of road inundation and drainage structure performance. 4) Influence potential for flooding on adjacent properties: Resident interviews, # of Public Works work orders related to flood damage and track number of related resident comments or complaints.

1584.description: This project matches a one time disbursement of tree/understory planting funds to enhance public land in Miami-Dade County such as Camp Matecumbe for beautification, urban cooling and water management. Specifically planting funds will be targeted in areas that enhance flood absorption areas (FLIP metric: open space), wellfields, dry ponds, and stormwater storage areas which can significantly alleviate storm water storage needs during storm events.
1584.purpose: Native vegetation in wellfields displace ecosystem disturbances that can create risks for drinking water. Vegetation intercept pollutants from entering the groundwater. The project will improve water management capabilities by leveraging water management footprints to store and filter water. Numerous models nationwide demonstrate the water absorption capacities of vegetation, particularly trees.
1584.activities: Growing, site preparation, installation and maintenance of native vegetation on public land in Miami-Dade County for stormwater mitigation and water quality improvement.
1584.direct_services: Improved water quality and stormwater mitigation as a result of tree installation.
1584.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served by improved water quality.
1584.outcome: Improved water quality and stormwater mitigation as a result of planting native vegtation on public land—measured by number of trees planted and quantity of stormwater absorbed by vegetation using iTree or similar tree benefit model.

1314.description: The Miami-Dade County Department of Solid Waste Management (DSWM) currently operates a fleet of day cab truck tractors that uses diesel fuel. The fully electric day cab truck-tractor will allow the department to test the capabilities of this rapidly emerging technology, which eliminates the use of diesel fuel and fuel leaks during transport, generates zero emissions, and significantly reduces operating noise. Therefore providing residents a far more environmentally friendly truck.
1314.purpose: The Department of Solid Waste Management (DSWM) currently operates a fleet of day cab truck tractors that uses diesel fuel. The fully electric day cab truck-tractor will allow the department to test the capabilities of this rapidly emerging technology, which eliminates the use of diesel fuel and fuel leaks during transport, generates zero emissions, reduces maintenance costs and significantly reduces operating noise. Therefore, providing residents a far more environmentally friendly truck.
1314.activities: Transfer of municipal solid waste delivered to DSWM Transfer Stations by various cities and DSWM Collections Operations, which was generated from bi-weekly residential waste collection services provided to all homes within Miami-Dade County.
1314.direct_services: Transfer of municipal solid waste to landfills and/or rail yards which is collected from residences of Miami-Dade County, twice a week, 52 weeks a year.
1314.population: The residents of Miami-Dade County who live or work within a 1/4 mile of the truck route would be the target population. It is estimated that along the truck route there are an approximately 150,000 persons.
1314.outcome: A fully electric vehicle has great environmental benefits, zero emissions. There will be substantial savings on maintenance, tires, brakes, fuel, etc. when compared to the cost of maintaining a standard diesel truck. It will also be a quieter vehicle on the routes. Benefit will be measured by cost of maintenance on truck as well as cost to charge the vehicles on annual basis versus cost of diesel.

2608.description: Mossman Home Preservation Foundation seeks funding to finalize the acquisition of the Mossman property, in order to preserve the historically significant buildings for the benefit of our small, rural community of Melrose. The Florida Trust for Historic Preservation has recognized Mossman Home & Hall as an endangered property in urgent need by inclusion on its 11 To Save list for 2025.
2608.purpose: Funds will be used to complete the acquisition, fully secure permanent ownership of Mossman House and Hall, to preserve the historic buildings and grounds for the benefit of Melrose residents.
2608.activities: Mossman Home Preservation Foundation board members will volunteer their time and skill set to complete the acquisition of the property through a funded property agreement and deed acquisition.
2608.direct_services: Post acquisition, Mossman will continue to provide monthly Art Walk exhibits, gallery sales for local artists, entrepreneur opportunities through markets, many and varied class opportunities for residents, holiday/special events for families, preservation of historic buildings, models of sustainable agriculture, and education on local Florida history.
2608.population: Rural families, children, elderly, veterans, disabled, minorities, and all residents of Alachua, Bradford, Clay, Putnam, and Marion counties. Annual visitation is approximately 10,000 individuals.
2608.outcome: Permanent preservation of one of Florida's most endangered historic sites (as designated by the Florida Trust's 2025 "11 to Save" list); protection of a unique legacy of women's history in Florida; long-term stability of an entirely volunteer- run community arts/education center currently serving 10,000 people/yr; preservation of gathering/green space (1.8 acres with heritage oaks and a food forest) at the physical heart of Melrose, countering the ongoing loss of historic structures and rural charm in the town. Methodology: Property ownership secured- recorded deed showing transfer of full title; continued operation as a community center-without interruption/relocation; preservation of the h

2794.description: This project delivers critical safety and accessibility improvements to support pedestrian and bicycle traffic associated with the new Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB) and the St. Johns River-to-Sea Loop (SJR2C). Currently, pedestrians and cyclists must travel within active vehicular lanes to access Anastasia State Park and the St. Augustine Amphitheatre. The proposed improvements will create dedicated, ADA-compliant mobility pathways that separate non-vehicular users from traffic.
2794.purpose: This program addresses multiple safety and site accessibility needs for incorporating pedestrian hybrid beacon (PHB) related pedestrian traffic and SJR2C bicycle traffic into Anastasia State Park & the St. Augustine Amphitheatre. Pedestrians & cyclists currently utilize vehicular traffic lanes to access the park & venue. This project provides a safer, dedicated pedestrian path, 2 shuttle bus stops w/ sheltered waiting pavilions, a dedicated ride-share waiting area, & a bike-share outpost.
2794.activities: We will extend existing pedestrian sidewalks to connect directly with the new FDOT Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB) crossing, establish a dedicated lane for ride-share and shuttle operations, and construct an ADA-compliant pedestrian waiting platform to support these mobility services. Improvements also include installation of bike-share stations and bicycle racks aligned with the City of St. Augustine’s Mobility Plan, as well as EV charging stations consistent with the City’s sustainability goals
2794.direct_services: New, expanded, and safer access routes into Anastasia State Park and its associated facilities, including recreation areas, interpretive programming spaces, cultural arts venues, and free community programming sites.
2794.population: Residents and Tourists seeking access to Anastasia State Park and the St. Augustine Amphitheatre by foot. Estimating 250,000 to 500,000 annually.
2794.outcome: The project will improve pedestrian and bicycle access to Anastasia State Park and the St. Augustine Amphitheatre, enhancing overall safety and multi-modal mobility. Project success will be evaluated through a combination of quantitative and qualitative measures, including: (1) exit surveys and bike-share utilization data to document the number of attendees arriving by foot or bicycle and to assess perceived safety and comfort; (2) ride-share utilization data and exit surveys to track the volume of patrons using ride-share services and to identify pickup and drop-off patterns; (3) surveys of vehicle activity at the newly designated ride-share platform; (4) documentation of standing- water fr

1317.description: The City’s Utilities Infrastructure Electrical System, originally built in the 1970s, is now nearing its 55th year of existence, significantly exceeding the usual lifespan of electrical equipment within water and wastewater facilities, which typically ranges between 30 to 35 years. Though maintenance has been completed over the decades, the system is eroded from storm events and it is crucial to replace the entire system, including its generator power source. The Project will construct and elevate new electrical systems, install new generator/s and fuel storage facility, and bury power lines underground for continuous Plant operations, even during storms. The estimated construction cost is $20.6 million. The City submitted a Resilient Florida Grant to assist in funding the construction phase. State funding is requested for contractual services towards the construction phase. The City wil
1317.purpose: The specific goal of the funds requested is to improve resiliency, mitigate flooding and erosion, and support uninterrupted municipal Water and Wastewater operations by constructing and elevating new electrical systems and generator(s), fuel storage facility, and burying power lines underground for continuous Plant operations even during disasters and major storm events.
1317.activities: Funds will be used for Contractual Services essential for the Construction Phase upgrading of critical assets, including installing new emergency generator(s) and fuel storage facility, constructing new electrical systems, elevations to mitigate flooding and erosion, and undergrounding of power lines.
1317.direct_services: This Project will enhance and optimize water and wastewater services to citizens by providing vital electricity and generator power source which adapts a regionally significant asset. This WTP/WWTP (Plant) services areas that extend outside of the municipal boundary of Cooper City. This Plant provides water services to portions of the Town of Davie and the Town of Southwest Ranches, our neighborin
1317.population: All City residents - 34,400. Completed by an independent contractor, the 2024 Water and Wastewater Master Plan Update prioritized this Project for a new electrical system, generator(s), fuel storage facility, and all systems required for immediate and crucial upgrades to provide uninterrupted treatment operations during power outages, strengthen emergency preparedness, and ensure WTP/WWTP reliability and efficiency. Direct services to citizens include improved operations and continuous power sou
1317.outcome: Constructing the new electrical systems and generator(s) power source for the Plant reduces the risk of flooding and loss of power at the Plant. Benefits include increased resilience of the Plant and all the critical assets that rely on its services through the construction of new electrical systems, generator(s), and associated diesel fuel storage facility for backup power and resilience to support uninterrupted operations and the mitigation of the electrical system erosion at the City’s WTP/WWTP. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured are enhanced operational efficiency and uninterrupted power supply during storms or severe weather events.

1846.description: Improvements to the City's Water Treatment Plant will bring the system into 4-log compliance and allow for better utilization of onsite storage capacity. Four-log compliance requires a water production facility to achieve 99.99% removal or inactivation of viruses, which offers significant benefits for public health and operational efficiency, including ensuring that 99.99% of viruses are inactivated or removed while providing a reliable level of treatment to help ensure consistent water quality.
1846.purpose: Improve physical health of the public by reducing waterborne illness risk. By effectively treating source water, 4-log compliance dramatically reduces the risk of viral illnesses, including gastroenteritis and other diseases caused by fecal contamination.
1846.activities: Protect the general public from harm. A 4-log reduction means that for every 10,000 viral particles, only one may survive. This significantly minimizes the risk of infectious diseases and is required for disinfectants in high-risk environments like hospitals and for safe drinking water.
1846.direct_services: Protect the general public from harm. A 4-log reduction means that for every 10,000 viral particles, only one may survive. This significantly minimizes the risk of infectious diseases and is required for disinfectants in high-risk environments like hospitals and for safe drinking water.
1846.population: All water customers of the City of Titusville water system.
1846.outcome: Improvements in measurable water quality parameters.

1558.description: The Charlie Ward Champions Ranch, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, will be a 112-acre sports, educational enrichment, recreation and wellness campus empowering youth and families in the Big Bend region and surrounding counties, to become lifelong champions. Construction for this multi-phased project begins with Phase 1A in 2026, which establishes core infrastructure, the Café/Multipurpose Barn, & shared outdoor facilities to activate programs immediately. Phase 1B will follow with the Indoor Turf Barn, Skill Development and Counseling Center, allowing the Ranch and its 30 partner organizations to scale research-based programs combining athletics, academics, mentoring, and the arts with STEM, literacy, workforce readiness, and parent upskilling. Together, this Collaborative Collective Impact ecosystem ensures consistent, measurable outcomes.
1558.purpose: Funds will complete Phase 1A infrastructure so programs can begin immediately, delivering research-based youth and family services across twelve counties. This investment boosts Florida’s workforce pipeline through STEM and career readiness, provides safe after-school access, and leverages major private funding to accelerate a high-impact, statewide legacy project.
1558.activities: Funds will launch Phase 1A programs with our collaborative partners (Cal Ripken, Sr. Foundation, Rebound & Recovery, TSC, Byrd Counseling, etc.), offering STEM, mentoring, tutoring, performing arts, digital navigation, youth, adolescent and family therapy & workforce upskilling in the Café space, plus outdoor sports and fitness activities. These services will immediately benefit youth and families in 12 NW Florida counties.
1558.direct_services: Youth from the counties across the Big Bend region will receive safe, structured services including supervised sports, academic support, mentoring, CRSF Badges & Baseball, CRSF STEM activities, performing arts, life-skills and Rebound & Recovery therapeutic workshops, and digital navigation and recreation for seniors. Parents & youth gain job-readiness support, and multiple partners deliver these
1558.population: Champions Ranch will serve at-risk youth, economically disadvantaged families, individuals with mental or physical health challenges, people with developmental or physical disabilities, preschool through college students, the elderly, and those formerly incarcerated. Based on our projections, we expect to reach approximately 3,000 people in our first year from Leon County and counties across the Big Bend region and scale from there.
1558.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural and agricultural education, strengthen environmental stewardship, and enhance academic outcomes. It will boost regional tourism, create economic impact, and foster greater community unity. By providing safe, structured activities, it will also divert youth from the criminal and juvenile justice systems. Outcomes will be measured through participation data, health and academic indicators, economic and tourism metrics, surveys, and partner evaluations.

1557.description: The City of Perry (City) request funds to replace fire hydrants within the City. Each fire hydrant, valve, and associated materials is approximately $6,500, with installation costs of about $1,500 per hydrant, for a total estimated project cost of $792,000. Twenty-one fire hydrants were identified as being in a failed state, four were rated very poor, and seventy- four were rated poor.

1556.description: The City of Perry (City) is requesting state appropriations to support the acquisition of property for the construction of a new Fire Station. The City has identified a 4.83 -acre parcel as the ideal location to meet current and future public safety needs. An independent appraisal determined the fair market value of the property to be $950,000; the City anticipates a cost of approximately $10,000 for a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.
1556.purpose: The City of Perry (City) is requesting state appropriations to support the acquisition of property for the construction of a new Fire Station. The City has identified a 4.83 -acre parcel as the ideal location to meet current and future public safety needs. An independent appraisal determined the fair market value of the property to be $950,000; the City anticipates a cost of approximately $10,000 for a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.
1556.activities: A modern Fire Station that will enhance emergency response capabilities, improve public safety infrastructure, and better serve the residents and businesses of Perry This investment supports the State of Florida’s commitment to improving rural emergency preparedness and ensuring equitable access to critical life safety infrastructure

1556.outcome: The facility will provide adequate fire protection and emergency response services to the citizens of Perry, FL and the surrounding area. The facility will also serve as a disaster recovery staging area, to be measured through an improved ISO score.

1555.description: The City of Perry is re questing funding assistance in the amount of $595,677 for the purchase of a Vacuum Jetter Truck to support the City’s Sewer Department in maintaining critical wastewater infrastructure. This equipment is essential to ensuring the reliable operation of the City’s sanitary sewer system and will also provide valuable support to the Water, Gas, and Stormwater Departments
1555.purpose: The City of Perry is re questing funding assistance in the amount of $595,677 for the purchase of a Vacuum Jetter Truck to support the City’s Sewer Department in maintaining critical wastewater infrastructure. This equipment is essential to ensuring the reliable operation of the City’s sanitary sewer system and will also provide valuable support to the Water, Gas, and Stormwater Departments
1555.activities: A new vacuum jetter truck would allow City crews to efficiently clean and maintain sewer mains, clear debris and grease buildup, and quickly respond to blockages before they develop into public health hazards or property damage events. In addition to sewer maintenance, this equipment would also be a shared resource across multiple departments.
1555.direct_services: The acquisition of a new Vacuum Jetter Truck will significantly enhance operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and help protect public health and the environment. By investing in this equipment, the City of Perry will be better equipped to maintain its utility infrastructure, extend the service life of critical assets, and provide more reliable service to residents and businesses.
1555.outcome: Efficiently clean and maintain sewer mains, clear debris and grease buildup, and quickly respond to blockages before they develop into public health hazards or property damage events, done by resident feedback and water testing.

1554.description: This project will involve repaving, excavation, removal of unstable sub-grade materials, and replacement with engineered fill capable of supporting long-term structural integrity. We have obtained an estimate to make the permanent repair of $2,041,743.
1554.purpose: Reconstructing the roadbed to address its underlying structural deficiencies is a necessary solution. This project will provide a smoother, safer, and substantially more durable roadway surface that benefits every city department and resident.
1554.activities: This fundamental improvement will extend the long-term lifespan of the roadway and significantly enhance overall emergency response efficiency.
1554.direct_services: Stephens Street provides access to residential neighborhoods as well as an apartment complex that provides accessible and affordable housing for individuals with disabilities. Despite repeated resurfacing efforts over the years, the roadway continues to experience significant and recurring settlement, creating deep depressions and uneven pavement.
1554.outcome: Stephens Street’s current state directly impacts critical emergency response times for Police, Fire, and EMS units, as well as routine operations for City sanitation, utility, and maintenance vehicles. project will provide a smoother, safer, and substantially more durable roadway surface that benefits every city department and resident. Measured by improved response times.

1553.description: The Perry Police Department requests $250,000 in state funding for planning and design of a new Evidence Management and Security Facility to bring the City into compliance with modern forensic and statutory standards. Current conditions are cramped, fragmented, and outdated, place the integrity of evidence and officer safety at risk. This investment will fund professional design plans for a secure, compliant, and expandable facility that protects public trust in the justice system.
1553.purpose: The Perry Police Department requests $250,000 in state funding for planning and design of a new Evidence Management and Security Facility to bring the City into compliance with modern forensic and statutory standards.
1553.activities: Current conditions are cramped, fragmented, and outdated, place the integrity of evidence and officer safety at risk.
1553.direct_services: This investment will fund professional design plans for a secure, compliant, and expandable facility that protects public trust in the justice system.
1553.population: General Public all residents of the City.
1553.outcome: The new facility will incorporate dedicated, specialized zones essential for modern forensic compliance: a controlled biohazard drying area, a designated space for the safe packaging of dangerous evidence, and a properly filtered and climate-controlled environment specifically for the secure storage of narcotics and other sensitive materials. Measured by reduced conviction times and officer feedback.

1552.description: This funding will allow the College to expand its existing, high-demand welding program by renovating an existing adjacent space on North Florida College's main campus in Madison, FL. The welding program is currently operating at capacity and is running both day and night classes to serve the College's six-county service district of Hamilton, Jefferson, Lafayette, Madison, Suwannee, and Taylor counties. Expansion is critical to meet statewide need and to admit students currently waitlisted.
1552.purpose: Welding is a high-wage, high-demand field, and this funding will allow the College to expand the existing high-demand welding lab space to accommodate the demand for the program.
1552.activities: Renovation of a facility allowing for expanded instruction of a high-demand workforce program.
1552.direct_services: Education - This renovation will expand a high-demand workforce education program will be offered to the citizens of Hamilton, Jefferson, Lafayette, Madison, Suwannee, and Taylor counties.
1552.population: Citizens in North Florida College's six-county service district - Jefferson, Taylor, Madison, Lafayette, Hamilton, and Suwannee counties - are the target population. This project will allow for sixty-three (63) more students to enroll in the college's welding program per academic year. This program will operate Fall, Spring, and Summer terms and will operate night and day classes and will provide certificates in Welding Technology and Advanced Welding Technology.
1552.outcome: This Legislative Appropriation will allow North Florida College to expand high-demand workforce program offerings for many years into the future. The welding program is a high-wage program that will provide highly qualified workers to the the College's service district and throughout the State of Florida.

1549.description: The Carrabelle Post Office, city-owned since 1961, remains vital to the community. The building now requires exterior tuckpointing and interior hazardous materials abatement to restore its condition. As a REDI community with limited resources, the City seeks assistance to preserve this important facility and ensure continued service and long-term sustainability.
1549.purpose: The Carrabelle Post Office was constructed in 1961 in a Mid-Century Modern style. It features a one-story design with decorated exterior brick. The front of the building has a floor-to-ceiling wall of glass that serves as its entryway. Additionally, there are eight awning-type windows, four on each side of the building. The building's low-profile, shallow- pitch roofline adds to its retro charm. Inside, the design emphasizes clean lines and minimal decoration, which remains influential in modern
1549.activities: The Carrabelle Post Office will continue to daily operations while also serving as historic architecture.
1549.direct_services: Currently, the Carrabelle Post Office services the citizens of Carrabelle with all USPS packages and services. Through the proposed renovations, the Post Office will continue to serve Carrabelle while preserving the historic architecture.
1549.population: The proposed target population are the citizens of Carrabelle, Lanark Village, Carrabelle Beach and others who receive USPS services from this location. This project will also serve tourism as a historic landmark in Carrabelle. The approximate population is 5,114.
1549.outcome: The Carrabelle Post Office will continue to daily operations while also serving as historic architecture.

1849.description: The matching state appropriation will transform Alexander Island into a premier river front nature park, with scenic trails, kayak launches, fishing pier, and observation towers. The project will include ADA-accessible restrooms and parking. The 224 acre project provides the non-boating public riverfront access to the St. Johns, and preserving natural habitats. This investment enhances recreation, tourism, economic development, and environmental stewardship in one the state's highest priorities greenways, the Wekiva-Ocala Greeway.
1849.purpose: Alexander Island will be developed into a nature park with trails, kayak launches, a fishing pier, and observation towers will draw visitors from across the region. Its unique riverfront setting and recreational opportunities make it a destination for outdoor enthusiasts, boosting tourism, supporting local businesses, and raising the profile of DeBary as a recreation and eco-tourism destination.
1849.activities: Accessible trails for walking, running, and cycling Kayak and canoe launches for river recreation Fishing pier for angling opportunities Observation towers for wildlife viewing and nature appreciation ADA-compliant parking and restrooms ensuring inclusive access Educational programs on river health and conservation These services provide recreation, learning, and wellness opportunities
1849.direct_services: Fishing pier for angling opportunities Observation towers for wildlife viewing and nature appreciation ADA-compliant parking and restrooms ensuring inclusive access Educational programs on river health and conservation These services provide recreation, learning, and wellness opportunities
1849.population: The entire City of DeBary, in addition to tourists and visitors. It is anticipated that over 20,000 people a year will visit.
1849.outcome: Alexander Island Riverfront Park will enhance and preserve local ecosystems by restoring native habitats, protecting wetlands, and improving water quality along the St. Johns River. The project will create safe environments for birds and wildlife, support biodiversity, and provide observation areas that promote conservation and appreciation of Florida’s natural beauty. The City will continue to partner with the Audubon Society and the Florida Native Plant Society to monitor and survey birds and plants on the property. Creating Alexander Island Riverfront Park will boost community physical health by offering scenic trails, kayaking, and outdoor recreation that encourage walking, paddling, and

1548.description: The City of Carrabelle proposes the design and installation of approximately 2,500 linear feet of new 8-inch water main extending from Oak Street to Carlton Avenue. The City of Carrabelle provides water services to Carrabelle, Lanark Village and St. James Bay through one main lines on the north side of US Hwy 98. During the case of a break in the line or maintenance of the line, customers east of the breakage/repairs may have little to no water service. This extension will establish a looped water system, improving service reliability and enhancing fire protection capabilities. By increasing system redundancy, the project strengthens the City’s water infrastructure and improves resilience against both natural and man-made hazards.
1548.purpose: The specific purpose of this project is to provide customers with water services, prevent water line stagnation and increased fire flow protection during natural and man-made events.
1548.activities: This extension will establish a looped water system, improving service reliability and enhancing fire protection capabilities and increasing system redundancy.
1548.direct_services: Customers will be provided with water services, better water quality by preventing water line stagnation and increase fire flow protection during natural and man-made events.
1548.population: Residents of Lanark Village East and West.
1548.outcome: The specific purpose of this project is to provide customers with water services, prevent water line stagnation and increased fire flow protection during natural and man-made events.

1546.description: The funds will enhance storm resiliency by paving eroded dirt segments and resurfacing damaged paved segments across three roadway sections (0.49 miles) impacted by Hurricane Helene. Severe rutting and standing water previously blocked emergency access and resident evacuation. These improvements will ensure safe, reliable, routes during future storms.
1546.purpose: The funds will enhance storm resiliency by paving eroded dirt segments and resurfacing damaged paved segments across three roadway sections (0.49 miles) impacted by Hurricane Helene. Severe rutting and standing water previously blocked emergency access and resident evacuation. These improvements will ensure safe, reliable, routes during future storms.
1546.activities: Activities include paving eroded dirt segments, resurfacing damaged paved segments, grading and stabilizing roadbeds, and improving drainage to prevent washouts. These upgrades will restore safe access for residents and emergency services, strengthen storm resiliency, and maintain critical routes during severe weather.
1546.direct_services: The funding will provide paved and resurfaced roads, improved drainage, and stabilized roadbeds to ensure safe, reliable access for residents and emergency services. These upgrades will reduce flooding impacts, maintain critical routes during storms, and strengthen community resiliency.

1546.outcome: Improved road accessibility during and after severe weather; faster emergency response times; fewer incidents of vehicle damage from poor conditions; and increased efficiency in maintenance and public works due to dependable roads. Methodologies by which to measure these outcomes include: track the number of days roads remain open during and after severe weather; compare historical and current average emergency response times; collect and analyze municipal and resident vehicle damage claims linked to road conditions; and track the number of completed maintenance and public works tasks monthly.

3606.description: Funds will complete design, permitting, construction, and engineering services during construction to harden CKWSD’s water system, including tank rehabilitation, SCADA upgrades, generator power, meter replacement, and a hardened operations center outside the flood zone. The project received 55% funding from the Supplemental Appropriation for Hurricanes Helene and Milton (SAHM) within the Waccasassa Water and Wastewater Cooperative (W3C) award; this request covers the unfunded 45%.

3606.direct_services: The project will provide reliable potable water service to residents, businesses, and critical facilities by reducing storm- related outages, improving water quality and pressure stability, and restoring essential water system functions after hurricanes.
3606.population: The project serves the entire Cedar Key Water & Sewer District service area, including all residential, commercial, and tourism-related customers. Approximately 800 residents, along with local businesses and visitors, will benefit.
3606.outcome: Expected Benefit: Improved water service reliability, drinking water quality, system resilience during hurricanes, and reduced storm-related service disruptions. Methodology: Measured through DEP compliance data, SCADA system performance, reduced boil-water notices, continuity-of-service records, and post-storm operational logs.

1542.description: In 1984, the Florida Legislature appropriated funds to be used in the planning, property acquisition, and site development for a new engineering campus to serve as the FAMU FSU College of Engineering. Currently, the College shares classroom space in FSU's Mag Lab, Research Buildings A & B, as well as offices and conference rooms. Study space is in hallways and lobby areas. Events that require auditorium space must be scheduled in spaces on the FAMU or FSU campus when available, and there is no space to display projects and achievements. To accommodate the projected growth of the College in all these areas, completion of the originally conceived three-building complex now becomes a matter of urgency. The requested funds will be used for the planning of a 163,867 gross square foot addition to Building C of the college.

To accommodate the growth of the college, completing of the originally conceived three-buildin

1602.description: Stabilize nearly 7,000 linear feet of eroded canal bank along the C-31 canal linking East Lake Toho and Lake Toho. This will restore the canal to its intended capacity, which is critical to controlling flood waters during major rainfall events.
