The 340B program requires drug makers to provide medicines at reduced prices, allowing safety-net providers to expand access, sustain care, and serve vulnerable residents. Florida DOH identifies STD prevention as a priority, and state law (§384) acknowledges rising STD rates and the need for prevention and treatment. DOH further reports increasing chlamydia and gonorrhea in Volusia and nearby counties. Without conversion, $40M in direct healthcare services will be lost.
1999.purpose: To deliver no-cost, same-day STD prevention and treatment in Volusia, Orange, Flagler, and Duval counties while sustaining 340B eligibility to ensure access to essential medicines for STD treatment. We aim to reduce transmission through expanded lab testing, timely medications, and partner notification, and to decrease costly ER visits by shifting care to clinics. Improved health outcomes include higher cure rates, fewer reinfections, and stronger linkage to primary care. Untreated STDs often im
1999.activities: Activities and services: intake/eligibility and risk assessment; lab testing for HIV, syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomonas, hepatitis A/B/C, and HSV; point-of-care and send-out assays with same-day results when feasible; 340B procurement and dispensing of essential medicines; on-site treatment and counseling; partner notification and expedited partner therapy; vaccination referrals (hep A/B, HPV); case management for scheduling, navigation, and reminders; linkage to primary/behavioral car
1999.direct_services: Direct services to residents include intake and risk screening; confidential STD testing (HIV, syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomonas, hepatitis A/B/C, HSV) via rapid and send-out labs; same-day evaluation and treatment when indicated; onsite dispensing of essential medicines through 340B; prevention and safer-sex counseling; partner notification and expedited partner therapy; vaccination ref
1999.population: The target population is **uninsured, underinsured, and homeless residents age 18 and older** living in Volusia, Orange, Flagler, and Duval counties. These individuals face high barriers to healthcare access and are at increased risk of untreated infections. The program will directly serve an estimated 6,000–9,000 adults annually, with outreach and partner notification extending prevention and treatment benefits to 15,000+ more residents, reducing transmission and improving community health.
1999.outcome: Expected outcomes: faster diagnosis and cure; reduced transmission and preventable ER use; taxpayer savings via clinic care and 340B access to essential medicines for STD treatment; stronger linkage to primary care; stability for adults 18+ in Volusia, Orange, Flagler, Duval. Methodology: track patients served, time-to-treatment, cure and 90-day reinfection, partner-notification completion, ER diversions, cost avoided/ROI, positivity rates, linkage outcomes; report quarterly dashboards and annual evaluation. Validate with chart audits and hospital data; compare to FL DOH targets and baselines.

1541.description: The FSU Health Deferred Maintenance project addresses critical infrastructure and building system needs within the university's health and research facilities to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. The project focuses on renewing and modernizing HVAC, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, as well as addressing structural and environmental deficiencies that impact daily operations. These improvements will directly support high-quality medical education, research, and healthcare services, while ensuring compliance with health and safety standards. By extending the lifespan of essential facilities and enhancing operational efficiency, the project safeguards the long-term functionality of FSU Health, benefiting students, faculty, staff, and the broader Florida community.
1541.purpose: The funds will be used to modernize and repair critical building systems, HVAC, electrical, mechanical, and plumbing, to ensure FSU Health facilities operate safely, efficiently, and in compliance with health and safety standards.
1541.activities: The project will modernize core infrastructure by upgrading aging building systems, improving structural integrity, and correcting environmental issues to enhance reliability, safety, and operational efficiency across FSU Health facilities.
1541.direct_services: The project will enhance the quality and safety of medical education, research, and patient care services delivered through FSU Health, ultimately improving access to high-quality healthcare for Florida residents.
1541.population: The project serves FSU Health students, faculty, researchers, and patients in Leon County and the broader North Florida region, supporting high-quality education, research, and healthcare services that strengthen the area’s medical and economic infrastructure.
1541.outcome: The project will result in safer, more efficient, and longer-lasting health and research facilities that support uninterrupted education, research, and clinical operations. Success will be measured through reduced maintenance needs, improved energy efficiency, compliance with health and safety standards, and enhanced facility performance metrics.

1291.description: This project expands neuroscience-based, specialized trauma interventions and comprehensive wraparound services for veterans, spouses, and children in order to prevent veteran suicide. Funding supports intensive mental health treatment, case management, family counseling, physical and wellness services, and the construction of additional lodging to accommodate more veterans for overnight clinical programs following the loss of the organization’s facility in Hurricane Debby (August 2024). The initiative aims to achieve an 85% improvement rate in trauma, depression, and related risk factors while building resilience and healthy peer support networks.
1291.purpose: To reduce veteran suicide by providing rapid, specialized trauma interventions with an 85% improvement rate in trauma, depression, and related symptoms. The program strengthens resilience, builds peer support, and expands access to neuroscience-based treatments and family services.
1291.activities: Funds will expand mental health services including outreach, initial and follow-up assessments (including screening for suicidal ideations), specialized mental health interventions, case management, and wraparound therapeutic services delivered in-person and via telehealth. Services also include mental health care for family members to address whole- household challenges.
1291.direct_services: Neuroscience-based individual therapy, group sessions, marriage and family counseling, chronic pain treatment, equine therapy, chiropractic care, medical massage, acupuncture, nutrition, yoga, martial arts, health coaching, and peer-support activities.
1291.population: Persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, physically disabled, Disabled Military Veterans. Number expected to be served: 401–800.
1291.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health by decreasing chronic pain, improving sleep and energy levels, reducing trauma, depression, suicidal ideation, and reducing dependence on drugs, alcohol, and prescription medication. Veterans will experience improved functioning, healthier relationships, and increased peer support. Partnerships with Veteran Court will reduce recidivism, while wraparound services strengthen family stability and social connection. Outcomes will be measured through TSQ trauma screenings, PHQ-9 depression screenings, self- assessment evaluations, satisfaction surveys, annual veteran suicide reports, and data tracked by Florida Courts related to recidivism outco

1704.description: The Mobile Stroke Treatment Unit (MSTU) is a specialty equipped ambulance with a portable CT scanner, specialty trained staff and stroke specific medications to diagnosis and treat stroke patients in the field. This saves valuable time and brain cells (each minute is 2 million brain cells saved) which leads to improved clinical patient outcomes. The MSTU operates in the county in which it operates but also supports surrounding rural counties with disparate access to stroke care. The MSTUs operate in Gainesville, Jacksonville and The Villages but provide rendezvous with the following additional counties: Bradford, Levy, Putnam, Marion, Dixie, Lafayette, Taylor, Suwannee, Columbia, Union, Gilchrist, Baker, in negotiation for rendezvous with Lake, Hernando and Citrus.
1704.purpose: Continued operations of the mobile stroke treatment unit fleet throughout the state of Florida. By receiving stroke care more quickly in the field, patients suffer less long term disability from stroke.
1704.activities: The MSTU brings expert stroke care to the patient in the field, allowing for quicker diagnosis and treatment of stroke.
1704.direct_services: Faster diagnosis and treatment of stroke, improving clinical outcomes for patients.
1704.population: Alachua and surrounding counties; Duval and surrounding counties; Sumter / Lake / Marion counties and surrounding counties. With the ability to provide mutual aid rendezvous with the MSTU, there is a larger service area of stroke response with the MSTU.
1704.outcome: Increased percentage of patients treated with IV thrombolytics within 60 and 90 minutes from symptom onset and improved clinical outcomes at 90 days post stroke as measured by a disability score, called the Modified Rankin Scale score (mRS). With treatment on the MSTU as compared to going to the emergency department by standard EMS, patients will be treated more frequently within 60 and 90 minutes from symptom onset and have less disability at 90 days post stroke.

1538.description: In response to a growing demand for services, Bond Community Health Center, Inc. proposes to expand its operations and establish a comprehensive men's health center to improve the overall health and welfare of men living in Leon and surrounding counties by offering men “a place of their own” to not only receive primary care, and specialty care, but also an avenue to address trauma, depression, stress, anger, and substance abuse by accessing behavioral health services and counseling, legal aid, financial education and fathering support. Bond will develop a 1.88 Acre site located on S. Monroe Street, Tallahassee for the construction of expanded general health services and a Men’s Health Center and Conference Center. The health center will be approximately 26,000SF and the Conference Center shall be 3,000SF to 4,000SF will be used for training and educational purposes.
1538.purpose: With this funding, Bond hopes to serve more patients/residents who will receive primary and preventative medical care (family medicine, diabetic education, and nutrition services); Mental Health (assessments, family counseling, coping training, and substance abuse counseling and treatment); urology (early diagnosis and treatment); laboratory; assistance with common legal problems, financial counseling, and referrals. This will be made possible by the expansion of the center and, consequently, th
1538.activities: Bond CHC will provide primary care, outpatient urology care, wellness and fitness services, mental health/substance abuse services, fathering and family counseling, legal aid, case management and transportation.
1538.direct_services: Patients will receive primary and preventative medical care (adult medicine, diabetic education, and nutrition services); Mental Health (assessments, family counseling, coping training, and substance abuse counseling and treatment); urology (early diagnosis and treatment); laboratory; financial counseling, assistance with common legal problems and referrals.
1538.population: Under-served communities living in Leon, Gadsden, Wakulla, Jefferson, Madison, Calhoun, and Franklin county. Approximately 4,000 are expected to be served annually.
1538.outcome: The expected benefits include improvement in blood pressure and diabetes control, early detection and treatment of prostate and colorectal cancer, improvement in depression and anxiety symptoms, decrease in substance abuse rates, lower rates of interaction with the criminal justice system. The chronic disease and behavioral health outcomes and changes from the baselines will be measured against national standards such as HEDIS and the federal Uniform Data System quarterly and annually. Substance abuse remission will be measured with random drug testing and 6 month and 1 year testing. A reduction in recidivism will be measured by re-arrest rates of the patients receiving counseling.

1294.description: The Florida State University (FSU) Institute for Pediatric Rare Diseases is a visionary initiative aimed at revolutionizing the landscape of pediatric rare disease diagnosis and treatment. Addressing the slow progress in this field, the institute adopts a unique approach to collectively tackle various pediatric rare diseases. With a strategic focus on biomedical research, education, patient care, community engagement, and technology commercialization, the institute envisions becoming a premier center in Florida. The subsequent fiscal year aims to pivot towards clinical research, seek extramural funding, and establish a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Lab. Long-term goals include statewide expansion of newborn screening, partnerships with biomedical pharmaceuticals, and the creation of a patient care and research arm.
1294.purpose: To advance knowledge, providing early diagnosis, delivering comprehensive clinical care, and offering education and support for children with rare genetic conditions and their families. The institute strives to make a lasting positive impact on the lives of these children and their families while contributing to research and public health in the field of pediatric rare diseases.
1294.activities: Collaborate with experts in genetics, pediatrics, and public health to design a comprehensive newborn screening. Establish state-of-the-art CLIA certified genetic testing laboratories equipped for high-throughput genetic screening equipment which will be provided by FSU valued at $1.5m.
1294.direct_services: Collaborate with experts in genetics, pediatrics, and public health to design a comprehensive newborn screening. Establish state-of-the-art CLIA certified genetic testing laboratories equipped for high-throughput genetic screening equipment which will be provided by FSU valued at $1.5m.
1294.population: The primary target population for the FSU Institute for Pediatric Rare Diseases is children who are affected by rare diseases. The institute aims to develop innovative approaches for the diagnosis and treatment of these rare diseases, with a focus on early detection through newborn screening. Additionally, the institute's vision includes community engagement and outreach, suggesting a broader interest in raising awareness and providing resources for families and communities affected by pediatric
1294.outcome: The project will contribute valuable data for research, advancing our understanding of rare diseases and potentially leading to new treatment options. Also, it will establish state-of-the-art Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) certified genetic testing laboratory equipped for high-throughput genetic screening. Labs that are CLIA certified meet the federal regulations and standards for facilities that test human specimens for health assessment or to diagnose, prevent, or treat disease.

2243.description: To expand the Lucy Fernandez Foundation’s boating-safety education and advocacy programs while establishing a modest leased space to conduct training, community outreach, and daily operations. Funds will enhance program delivery, strengthen partnerships, and support feasibility planning for long-term facility needs under the statewide FLY HIGH, BIRD “Have Fun. Be Safe.” initiative.
2243.purpose: To expand the Lucy Fernandez Foundation’s boating-safety education and advocacy programs while establishing a modest leased space to conduct training, community outreach, and daily operations. Funds will enhance program delivery, strengthen partnerships, and support feasibility planning for long-term facility needs under the statewide FLY HIGH, BIRD “Have Fun. Be Safe.” initiative.
2243.activities: The Foundation will continue its established boating-safety and education programs throughout FY 2026–27, expanding its reach and impact through community outreach, advocacy, youth engagement, and education. Funding will strengthen local and statewide prevention efforts and create opportunities to introduce innovative, collaborative content promoting safer waterways across Florida.
2243.direct_services: Boating-safety education courses, leadership training, community outreach, and advocacy for families, youth, and recreational boaters—delivering practical knowledge, hands-on learning, and life-saving awareness to prevent accidents and promote responsible recreation. Programs will be developed and delivered in a professional, learning- focused environment that fosters engagement and stewardship.
2243.population: Target populations include families, youth, and the general public—particularly students from middle school through university, as well as recreational boaters and watercraft users. The project is expected to directly serve more than 800 individuals through education, outreach, and prevention-based programs.
2243.outcome: The project aims to improve boating-safety awareness and responsible recreation among families, youth, and boaters locally and statewide by reducing preventable accidents and promoting a culture of safety and stewardship. Outcomes include increased participant knowledge, safer boating behaviors, and stronger community collaboration through education and advocacy. Success will be measured through program attendance logs, training completion records, and participant surveys documenting knowledge gains and behavioral impact. Partner feedback from schools, agencies, and industry collaborators, along with social media analytics and outreach metrics, provides both quantitative and qualitative evid

1531.description: This project will add a Dewatering Device to the city's Waste Water Treatment Plant. The plant utilizes drying beds to filter out water and bake solid waste in the sun before disposal. A dewatering device will enable the city to keep up with waste water demand without the need to contract sludge removal companies. The dewatering device will enable the city to continue removing sludge during the rainy season or periodic inclement weather. The dewatering device will enable the city to better maintain necessary and specified conditions within the waste water treatment plant and process.
1531.purpose: Creation of resiliency and redundancy for treatment of solids extracted from waste water; ability to perform treatment during periods of wet weather, thus reducing the risk of backup/overflow.
1531.activities: Planning, design, construction, and supervision of project by City of Monticello and qualified contracted personnel.
1531.direct_services: Resiliency and redundancy of their city's waste water collection and treatment system. Assurance that their city's waste water treatment plant is being proactive to prevent contamination of the land and groundwater by overflow or back up of sewage.
1531.population: City of Monticello Greater than 2,700 people
1531.outcome: Creation of resiliency and redundancy for treatment of solids extracted from waste water; ability to perform treatment during periods of wet weather, thus reducing the risk of backup/overflow: Ability to keep up with demand and specified parameters.

1298.description: The City of Parkland will improve the facilities at Pine Trails Park to provide people of all abilities the opportunity to enjoy the physical and mental health benefits of outdoor play.
1298.purpose: The primary purpose will be to improve the facilities at Pine Trails Park to provide people of all abilities the opportunity to enjoy the physical and mental health benefits of outdoor play.
1298.activities: An accessible, enjoyable large community park will be available to the public.
1298.direct_services: The City's Pine Trails Park will continue to provide accessible recreational opportunities to park patrons.
1298.population: All park patrons will be served, drawing residents from the northwest region of Broward County, expected to exceed 50,000 annually.
1298.outcome: The project will promote an active lifestyle for people of all abilities.

1604.description: While the United States celebrates our 250th anniversary, this project addresses critical structural needs associated with Osceola County’s Historic Courthouse, Florida’s oldest and still functioning courthouse. This project will allow this historic landmark to be preserved and function for many years to come by repairing the courthouse's roof and cupola.
1604.purpose: The improvements to the facility will allow the residents of Osceola County to use the Historic Courthouse for many years to come.
1604.activities: The Historic Courthouse is utilized for grand jury selection and as an overflow courtroom. The facility is also utilized as a public venue and office space.
1604.direct_services: The improvements to the facility will allow the residents of Osceola County to use the Historic Courthouse for many years to come.
1604.outcome: Continued use of the Historic Courthouse for court functions and private events. This will be measured by the number of court activities and private events held.

1351.description: The purpose of this funding request is to perform injection grouting and lining of the City of Ocala's sewer pipes and manholes that have degraded over time. During normal operations the degraded sewer infrastructure allows sewer flows to leak into surrounding soils as they flow to the water reclamation facility. During storm events the degraded sewer infrastructure allows stormwater to leak into the sewer pipe and flow to the water reclamation facility.
1351.purpose: The primary objective of the project is to injection grout and line degraded sewer lines and manholes to prevent ex- filtration (leaking) of sewage flows into groundwater and infiltration of groundwater into sewage flows. This will not only reduce nutrient loading in the Silver Springs and Rainbow Springs Basins, but it will also lower the treatment of effluent at the water reclamation facilities and prevent sanitary sewer over flows during storm events.
1351.activities: Ex-filtration (leaking) of sewage into the groundwater contributes to nutrient loading of the spring shed. Infiltration of groundwater during storm events causes sewer to backup into homes and business and surcharging of manholes resulting in contamination of storm water with raw sewage. By lining the pipes and manholes, it prevents both the ex- filtration and infiltration of sewage flows.
1351.direct_services: Reduce nutrient loading of Silver Springs by eliminating leakage of raw sewage into the spring shed, reduce residents cost for transporting and treating wastewater and minimize the liability from water pollution and public health risks by eliminating sanitary sewer overflows during storm events.
1351.population: Residents within City of Ocala limits with aging infrastructure. These areas are defined on the City's GIS mapping system with the age and type of pipes, in the City's Wastewater Master Plan and is being currently evaluated with the Condition Assessment Plan.
1351.outcome: Injection grouting and lining of sewer pipe and manholes requires no digging, this process works to grout, line and seal multiple angles, and it can protect the sewer system from debris buildup, corrosion, leaks and root intrusion. After the grouting and liner is in place, leak test and camera inspections are performed.

1605.description: This project will provide enhanced judicial security for judges that work out of the Osceola County Courthouse. Currently, they park in a judicial parking lot next to the courthouse that had walls, but no roof. The project would construct a freestanding roof and install an enhanced security gate to the currently walled off judicial parking lot, thereby giving judges with the Ninth Judicial Circuit additional security while entering or leaving the Courthouse.
1605.purpose: Provide judges with the Ninth Judicial Circuit additional security while entering or leaving the Courthouse.
1605.population: Judges of the Ninth Judicial Circuit. 25-50 individuals
1605.outcome: Increased safety. Decrease in security incidences.

1318.organization: The Housing Authority of the City of Key
1318.description: KWHA seeks funding to upgrade its after-school classroom with technology that supports academic growth & career exploration for children living in public housing. The project will provide new computers, printers, a 3D printer, professional video camera, software such as Microsoft Office & Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, & Premiere. This will give students hands-on experience in engineering, graphic design, video editing, and photography. It will create an engaging, future-focused learning environment where low-income youth can build digital literacy & gain access to resources that support long-term academic and workforce success.
1318.purpose: The requested funds will upgrade the Key West Housing Authority’s after-school classroom with modern technology, including computers, a 3D printer, professional video cameras, and software for productivity, design, and video editing. The goal is to provide low-income youth living in public housing with access to tools and training that support academic achievement, digital literacy, STEM education, and creative career exploration.
1318.activities: The classroom will be equipped with computers, a 3D printer, professional video cameras, standard printers, and software including Microsoft Office & Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere. Students will engage in hands-on activities such as 3D design & printing, graphic design, photography, video production, and digital learning projects. An IT professional will maintain the equipment & provide technical support, ensuring students have reliable access to technology and guidance to develop ski
1318.direct_services: Children living in public housing will have access to a fully upgraded after-school classroom where they can use computers, a 3D printer, professional video cameras, & software for productivity, design, and video editing. Direct services include hands-on instruction in 3D design and printing, graphic design, photography, video production, & digital learning projects. Students will receive guidance
1318.population: The target population is school-age children living in public housing in Key West, particularly those from low-income households with limited access to technology and STEM resources. The project is expected to serve approximately 50 children annually through hands-on use of upgraded classroom technology, training, and guided learning activities. The KWHA expects the number of children served will increase as word spreads about the new and exciting technology available in the classroom.
1318.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to provide children living in public housing with access to technology, building on digital literacy, STEM skills, creative learning, & career exploration. Students will gain hands-on experience which can improve academic performance & prepare them for future opportunities. The outcome will be measured by tracking participation, documenting completed projects, monitoring skill development through instructor observation, and gathering feedback from students and parents on technology use & engagement.

1223.description: This project will construct a new, dedicated basketball practice facility and repurpose the current practice courts into a 1,500-seat women's volleyball arena. The new facility will include modern training, recovery, locker room, equipment, and office spaces to support both men's and women's basketball, while the renovated spaces will provide purpose-built amenities for women's volleyball. Together, these upgrades enhance daily athletic operations, improve the student- athlete experience, and address Title IX facility requirements.
1223.purpose: The funds will create a new basketball practice facility and convert existing courts into a dedicated women's volleyball arena, providing modern training, recovery, and support spaces. This investment enhances student-athlete development, daily operations, and ensures Title IX facility requirements are met.
1223.activities: The project will fund construction of a new basketball practice facility and the conversion of existing courts into a women's volleyball arena. Renovations will include updated training, recovery, locker, office, and equipment spaces. These improvements support daily athletic operations and enhance the overall student-athlete experience.
1223.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with access to enhanced collegiate athletic events, including a modern women's volleyball arena with expanded seating. It will also support community engagement through camps, clinics, and youth programs hosted in the upgraded facilities.
1223.population: The target population includes student-athletes in the men's and women's basketball programs and the women's volleyball program, along with coaches and support staff. Indirectly, the facilities will serve spectators, community members, and youth participants, with an estimated 2,000–3,000 individuals benefiting annually through events, training, and programs.
1223.outcome: The expected benefit is an improved quality of education and athletic experience for student-athletes, along with enhanced program under Title IX. This will be measured through student-athlete academic performance, retention and graduation rates, satisfaction surveys, and usage metrics of the new and renovated facilities.

1795.description: To provide substance use treatment services specifically dedicated to homeless Veterans who are not currently receiving VA benefits. These services aim to address the critical needs of Veterans experiencing homelessness and chronic homelessness, as well as those who are legally involved and financially disadvantaged, who otherwise cannot afford substance use treatment. We strive to enhance the quality of life for these Veterans and support their journey toward becoming productive and contributing members of Florida’s communities, all while returning a cost avoidance of over $800,000 YTD or over 7,000 bed days by diversion of individuals from jails and institutions into substance use residential programming with this state investment. Our mission is to ensure no Veteran is left behind due to financial or systemic barriers, reinforcing our commitment to those who have served our country.
1795.purpose: The funds requested will be used to operate a comprehensive residential treatment program designed to address substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health challenges among homeless and chronically homeless Veterans, as well as other indigent individuals in the community. The program aims to provide a safe and structured environment where clients can access evidence-based clinical treatment, counseling, case management, and life skills development. The ultimate goal is to help clients a
1795.activities: The requested funds will support a therapeutic community providing comprehensive services to address substance use and promote recovery. Key activities include: Clinical Services: Evidence-based treatment and therapeutic interventions for substance use. Counseling: Individual, group, and family sessions to build emotional stability, peer support, and family relationships. Case Management: Coordinated care connecting clients to essential resources like housing and healthcare. Education and Employ
1795.direct_services: The requested funds will support a residential Level IV treatment program providing comprehensive, client-centered care in a structured and supportive environment. Services include evidence-based clinical treatment for substance use, individual and group counseling, and family counseling to rebuild relationships. Clients will receive case management to access resources like healthcare, housing, an
1795.population: Veterans are the primary target population for this residential treatment program, with a strong focus on homeless and chronically homeless veterans in the community. The program prioritizes veterans without benefits, providing them with the necessary support to establish connections with the VA and facilitating their transfer to a VA-funded program once they are eligible. For veterans who are not eligible for VA benefits, the program offers tailored services to address their unique needs. In ad
1795.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to help homeless and chronically homeless veterans, along with other indigent individuals, overcome substance use disorders, improve mental health, and reintegrate into the community. The program aims to reduce homelessness, enhance self-sufficiency, and increase access to healthcare, education, and employment opportunities. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of individuals who transition to stable housing, using case management and housing data. Substance use recovery will be assessed with standardized tools, while mental health improvements will be measured through the PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Employment and education outcomes will be monitored

1606.description: McCormick Research Institute enhances the physical, emotional, and psychological well-being of veterans through equine-assisted therapy and horsemanship. Our programs—therapeutic riding, adaptive groundwork, and veteran retreats—use the unique bond between horse and human to foster healing, resilience, and confidence. Services address challenges such as PTSD, anxiety, depression, and mobility limitations. McCormick never charges veterans or their families for participation. Requested funding will sustain and expand access to these life-changing programs, ensuring continuity of care and the ability to serve more participants in the coming year.
1606.purpose: Funds requested will support McCormick Research Institute’s evidence-based equine-assisted therapy programs for veterans. Our ongoing research demonstrates significant reductions in PTSD symptoms among participants, validating the effectiveness of our model. Funding will sustain and expand these programs, providing free access to therapeutic riding and equine-assisted activities that improve emotional well-being, resilience, and quality of life for veterans coping with trauma and transition.
1606.activities: McCormick Research Institute will provide equine-assisted therapy and traditional counseling services specifically designed to support the emotional, psychological, and physical well-being of veterans. Programs will include mounted and unmounted equine therapy sessions, guided by certified therapeutic riding instructors and licensed mental health professionals. These services help veterans reduce PTSD symptoms, build resilience, and improve overall quality of life at no cost to participants.
1606.direct_services: McCormick Research Institute will provide Central Florida veterans with a range of equine-assisted and traditional therapeutic services, including therapeutic horseback riding, equine-assisted psychotherapy, and adaptive horsemanship programs. Veterans will also have access to individualized counseling sessions and specialized retreats designed to promote healing, reduce PTSD symptoms, and support
1606.population: McCormick Research Institute’s veteran programs serve Central Florida veterans coping with post-traumatic stress, traumatic brain injuries, depression, anxiety, and other service-related challenges. The project also provides continued engagement opportunities through our veteran volunteer program and mounted drill team, fostering camaraderie, purpose, and peer support. With the requested funding, McCormick expects to serve approximately several hundred veterans annually through more than 1,000 e
1606.outcome: The expected outcome of McCormick Research Institute’s veteran programs is measurable improvement in mental health and overall quality of life, including significant reductions in PTSD symptoms. In collaboration with the University of Central Florida and the local VA, McCormick conducts ongoing research to evaluate the effectiveness of equine- assisted therapy. Veterans complete pre- and post-program clinical assessments and validated surveys measuring PTSD, depression, anxiety, and well-being to document and quantify therapeutic impact.

2175.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2175.description: The new Fairgrounds project will be complete in 2026, hosting the first Fair in November 2026. We are planning on constructing four stand-alone restroom buildings throughout the site and near the new Amphitheater.
2175.purpose: Construct Restroom Buildings for the public to use during events. The restrooms will also be utilized by local EOC personnel during storm preparations.
2175.activities: Provide restroom space for general public, first responders, and EOC personnel during Fair activities and natural disaster staging.
2175.direct_services: Provide restroom space for general public, first responders, and EOC personnel during Fair activities and natural disaster staging.
2175.population: Northeast Florida residents and visitors. Over 200,000 visitors annually to the fair. Will be a year-round facility serving the region.
2175.outcome: Provide hardened facilities for general public and first responders. Constructed restrooms will provide better facilities than portable restrooms.

3187.description: The Holocaust Museum & Education Center welcomes more than 7,000 visitors and 3,500 students to its Naples location. As a museum that teaches the lessons of the Holocaust, the state-sponsored genocide of more than 6,000,000 European Jews during World War II, there is a security concern that it may become a target the same antisemitic violence that has been on the rise since October 2023. It has been recommended by security experts that our museum expand our security to cover the times when we host field trips from southwest Florida public and private schools. This will build upon previous efforts which allowed for armed security during the hours when we welcome regular (non-school) visitors, monitored security cameras, and training.
3187.purpose: After a threat assessment conducted in late 2024 and due to the shocking rise of antisemitism, we have determined that it is imperative to employ armed security personnel for all hours when individuals are working at or visiting the museum, maintain and update security equipment, and regularly train Museum staff and volunteers.
3187.activities: The armed security guard's hours will be increased to not only cover the time when the museum is open to the general public but will also include the hours when our staff welcome students and educators who come on field trips as well as during public programs. The museum will also maintain, and update as needed, its security cameras and equipment and continue to provide security training to its staff and volunteers.
3187.direct_services: The Museum welcomes more than 10,000 visitors (general admission and field trips) each year. This funding will allow for a safe, uninterrupted experience for visitors, volunteers, and staff.
3187.population: Our target population is local students and educators from public and private schools, grades 5 through 12, local residents, seasonal residents, tourists, volunteers, and staff.
3187.outcome: As a result of this project, our visitors, staff, volunteers, and other constituents will have peace of mind knowing that the Museum is ensuring a safe and secure environment.

1352.description: The purpose of this project is to install 5,500 linear feet of 12-inch force main that will connect to lift station 83 on SW First Lane, with the option to bypass lift station 83 as needed. By increasing the size of the force main this allows approximately 1,500 homes to connect to the sanitary sewer system preventing them from installing septic tanks.
1352.purpose: The primary objective of the project is to install centralized sanitary lines and send flows to the wastewater treatment plant instead of having homes install septic tanks.
1352.activities: Funds will cover the installation of 5,500 linear feet of 12-inch force main that will connect to lift station 83 on SW First Lane, with the option to bypass lift station 83 as needed.
1352.direct_services: New homes would be able to connect to the centralized sanitary sewer. By connecting new homes to the sanitary sewer this would prevent them from having septic tanks that can impair the Rainbow Springs spring shed. Thus preventing total nitrogen that is produced due to On-site Sewage Treatment Disposal Systems (OSTDS) from impacting the Upper Floridan Aquifer.
1352.population: Roughly 1,500 homes would be able to connect flows to lift station 83.
1352.outcome: By increasing the size of the force main this allows approximately 1,500 homes to connect to the system preventing them from installing septic tanks. This prevents approximately 21,516 lbs of TN from ever contaminating the groundwater annually. Based on data that the loadings in pounds of nitrogen per OSTDS in Rainbow Springs spring sheds is approximately 9.92 lb-N/person, and the household average in Marion County is 2.41 persons.

The project consists of construction of a mast arm traffic signal at the intersection of SW 42nd Street/SW 32nd Street and SW 7th Avenue. In addition, the project includes the installation and extension of left-turn lanes on SW 42nd Streets, as well as asphalt milling and resurfacing.
1381.purpose: The specific purpose of the project is to enhance intersection safety and operational efficiency, as well as reduce traffic delays, travel time, and associated costs. The project includes construction of a mast arm traffic signal at the intersection of SW 42nd Street/SW 32nd Street and SW 7th Avenue. In addition, the project includes the installation and extension of left-turn lanes on SW 42nd Streets, as well as asphalt milling and resurfacing.

The proposed project will support academic excellence, innovative teaching methods, and foster community benefiting FSU faculty and students, as well as the broader Tallahassee and Florida communities.

The goal is to support academic excellence, foster innovation and collaboration, and create spaces that prepare students for 21st-century careers while benefiting the broader Tallahassee and Florida communities.

Specific activities include upgrading classrooms and labs to support hands-on hospitality training and experiential learning. New administrative and educational spaces will be created for the Dedman College of Hospitality, including specialized areas for hospitality technology and interprofessional curricula. Renovations will also include the enhancement of meeting and event spaces for academi
1353.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services by enhancing educational opportunities for students at FSU. The renovated Middleton Center will offer upgraded classrooms and training facilities for the Dedman College of Hospitality, supporting the growth of academic programs. The renovated Middleton Center will provide infrastructure to support expansion of new and existing educational prog
1353.population: The target population served by this project is FSU students, specifically those enrolled in the Dedman College of Hospitality and related programs. The expansion and renovation will accommodate the current 618 students, with the capacity to support future growth. The project is expected to serve an increased number of students through expanded undergraduate and graduate programs, including the Global Club Management and Leadership major.
1353.outcome: The remodeling of the current Middleton Center will be a fundamental step in the further development of the academic and athletic programs of FSU, growing the numbers of graduates that directly contribute to the Florida economy through their leadership and participation in the large and important hospitality and recreation sectors. These expanded facilities will also serve to promote tourism in Tallahassee. The new and extensively remodeled facilities will provide long-lasting impact on economic development, accelerate innovation, expand educational opportunities, create community leaders of the future, and provide an important axis serving Tallahassee community need. 2993.description: The purpose of this project is to extend municipal sewer services to the Sunny Grove Community which currently has a package treatment plant. This will eliminate a source of bacteria and nutrients to the Estero River and Estero Bay (Florida's first aquatic preserve dedicated by the State Legislature in 1966 and expanded in 1983). The project will improve the quality of water in the Estero River and Estero Bay which will improve the environment and protect human health. This funding will directly offset the cost to the residents of the Sunny Grove Community.
2993.purpose: The purpose of this project is to extend waste water infrastructure to the Sunny Grove community and demolish its package waste water treatment plant to eliminate a source of bacteria and nutrient pollution to the Estero River and Estero Bay.
2993.activities: Construction of a sewer lift station and force main to connect Sunny Grove to municipal sewer. Demolish the package waste water treatment plant.
2993.direct_services: The citizens within the Sunny Grove community will receive municipal sewer service and not longer own/operate the package waste water treatment plant.
2993.population: The residents of Sunny Grove and the general public will benefit from the project via improved water quality in the Estero River and Estero Bay.
2993.outcome: The expected benefit from the project is improved water quality within the Estero River and Estero Bay. The outcome will be measured by the water quality in the Estero River and Estero Bay.

1286.description: Funding would provide support the Broward County Continuum of Care for citizens in need of behavioral health interventions/services/supports within the array of general or crisis behavioral health related services. Services would include: Behavioral Health Services/Supports, Maternal Services / Supports or Youth Violence Prevention Services. Previous FY funding enabled the program to provide essential behavioral health services to an additional 152 individuals in all categories, county-wide.

1288.description: The proposed Clinic for Research and Treatment (CRT) is an innovative center that includes training, development, and therapeutic initiatives designed to enhance the quality of life for veterans by equipping them with essential life and self- regulatory skills. We have partnered with The Veterans Trust to research a program named Race Camp that uniquely blends elements of simulated racing with evidence-based psychological approaches to help participants improve their mental and physical health.
1288.purpose: Improved mental health of veterans by alleviating symptoms of PTSC in veterans, including symptoms of trauma; improve self-confidence and quality of life for veterans and their families.
1288.activities: Clinicians will administer the PTSD scale, the difficulties in emotion regulation scale, trauma symptoms inventory, and quality of life scale. Veterans will participate in monitored sessions of simulated driving to determine levels of anxiety under stress.
1288.direct_services: Pre-evaluation, monitoring and training, participation in simulated driving sessions, evaluation by scientific tools for improved mental health, counseling on techniques to address stress.
1288.outcome: Improved mental health evaluated by the PTSD scale, the difficulties in emotion regulation scale, trauma symptoms inventory, and quality of life scale.

1305.description: Preserve valuable green space by creating a community park.Restore one of the area’s only private undeveloped acreage and transform it to a natural habitat, create natural walking trails, wildlife viewing areas and provide parking to support community access. The projece will enhance local biodiversity and provide a place for citizens, families and neighbors to recreate.

Maximze the other JFED campus programs such as raquet center, youth camp, event center, future aquatic center and holocaust education center.

Approximately 89% of Sarasota’s population holds a high school degree and 27% a Bachelors or higher. The assumption is the region in health conscious. 2961.description: Seybold Serves is a food service nonprofit with a mission serving two main groups: providing meals and clean water to those facing homelessness and those facing disaster. This funding will go to expanding our operation. We will be purchasing a trailer for transportation and storage, food preparation and serving equipment, generators, and communications equipment.
2961.purpose: This equipment will help us expand our mission of feeding those who need it, specifically those experiencing homelessness and disaster.
2961.activities: We will be holding mobile kitchens in areas of high homelessness and disaster areas in which we will provide hot meals and clean water, basic human needs. We will also bring prepared meals to these same areas when mobile kitchens are not viable.
2961.direct_services: We serve hot meals and provide clean water to those in need, especially those facing homelessness and disaster.
2961.population: We mainly serve the homeless and those experiencing disaster. We expect to serve in excess of 500 people in the capital region and Central Florida.
2961.outcome: Regular nutrition improves mental health and meal programs help connect those in need with services. Regular nutrition improves physical health and connects the homeless with services. Feeding the hungry reduces crime.

1939.description: Enhance on-going efforts to keep our students, teachers and staff safe and in a monitored environment, coupled with the recent fatal shootings in Christian schools, we are looking to upgrade our security systems with new cutting-edge technology, electronic door access controls, video monitoring systems with AI security cameras that include fire and explosive detections, weapon detection, facial screenings, etc. for 3 campuses for over 1,450 students from ages PK3 (3 years old) to 18 (12th Grade).
1939.purpose: Enhance on-going efforts to keep our students, teachers and staff safe and in a monitored environment, coupled with the recent fatal shootings in Christian schools, we are looking to upgrade our security systems with new cutting-edge technology, electronic door access controls, video monitoring systems with AI security cameras that include fire and explosive detections, weapon detection, facial screenings, etc. for 3 campuses for over 1,450 children from ages PK3 (3 years old) to 18 (12th Grade)
1939.activities: These security enhancements will serve to keep safe and protect the thousands of students, families, church members, community members and businesses who visit and utilize our school campuses year-round, seven days a week.
1939.direct_services: Safer facilities for our students from the ages of 3 years old (PK3) - 18 (12th Grade) along with their families, community members and elderly grandparents who visit them year-round to mitigate harm to individuals from random school shootings or suspicious persons on site etc.

1748.organization: Josefa Perez de Castano Kidney Foundation,
1748.description: Our program aims to provide nutritionally balanced, no-cost meals to low-income seniors and adults with disabilities, particularly dialysis patients, at their dialysis treatment centers in Miami-Dade County. This service addresses the heightened risk of malnutrition that dialysis patients face, supporting their health and enhancing their quality of life. By offering meals at no charge, we also help alleviate economic burdens for these vulnerable groups.
1748.purpose: To support the Daily Nutrition Meals Program for low-income disabled seniors receiving dialysis, we aim to enhance their health and improve their quality of life. This initiative is crucial for disabled elders who often face isolation and depression due to loneliness and their illness.
1748.activities: Our nutrition program helps low-income elderly seniors. Our services aim to enhance the quality of life for Miami-Dade County residents. Kidney dialysis patients are at a high risk of malnutrition due to their treatments. Our nutrition program also provides economic assistance to these individuals.
1748.direct_services: Delivered meals, to elderly & disabled low-income residents at risk of hunger and malnutrition. screening and assessments, social interaction, telephone reassurance and other services provided to at-risk and homebound elders.
1748.population: We are committed to supporting approximately 200 low-income seniors (60+)who are dialysis patients by providing them with nutritious lunch meals. Understanding the challenges they face, these meals will be delivered directly to their dialysis centers to ensure they have access to healthy food during their treatment.
1748.outcome: Ensure elderly disabled dialysis patients receive proper nutrition, reducing the risks associated with malnutrition and supporting overall health. Regularly assess the satisfaction and well-being of our clients through surveys conducted by program staff and social workers during and post-program.

1523.description: To respond to the rising community need for emergency behavioral healthcare for patients presenting to the Emergency Department, Tallahassee Memorial Healthcare (TMH) plans to construct a specialized 10-bed psychiatric diversion unit immediately adjacent to the TMH Emergency Department where patients with emergency psychiatric and/or substance use conditions can receive urgent and specialized care and treatment.
1523.purpose: The 10-bed Emergency Department diversion unit provides psychiatric assessment, stabilization, and disposition to inpatient services and/or outpatient services for children and adults experiencing a mental health and/or substance use emergency. The unit will provide psychiatric, nursing, and social work services in a specialized care unit designed for optimal outcomes for individuals with persistent mental illness.
1523.activities: Provide stabilization of mental health and/or substance use issues and conditions through the provision of psychiatric assessment, behavioral health nursing services, medication administration, and social work services designed to alleviate crisis and refer individuals to the most appropriate levels of continued care.
1523.direct_services: The 10-bed Emergency Department diversion unit serves all individuals from the Leon and surrounding counties who are experiencing a mental health and/or substance use emergency and will provide on-site evaluation, treatment,and stabilization as well as aftercare plans to ensure quality outcomes.
1523.population: The 10-bed Emergency Department diversion unit will serve adults and children in need of mental health and/or substance use services in Leon and the surrounding counties. The 10-bed diversion unit will serve approximately 3,300 individuals in need of crisis mental health and/or substance use services and will be operable on a 24/7 basis.
1523.outcome: The 10-bed diversion unit will provide immediate psychiatric treatment for individuals presenting to the Emergency Department in psychiatric crisis which will result in a reduction in recidivism. The 10-bed unit will be monitored through already existing measures and levels of recidivism will be measured prior to and following implementation of the unit.

This restructuring will strengthen victim safety, eliminate service gaps, and create a unified trauma-informed response system. The Marion County Hospital District (MCHD) has historically managed appropriations to ensure financial and program accountability and currently provides free space for domestic violence outreach services and the Sexual Assault Center, significantly reducing provider costs.The transition to a dual-certified provider will create a funding shortfall due to startup expenses, staffing requirements, training, and overlapping operational needs. Without supplemental funding, the county risks reduced shelter capacity, limited forensic exam availability, and interruptions in crisis
1705.purpose: The requested funds will ensure uninterrupted domestic violence and sexual assault services during Marion County’s July 1, 2026 transition to a new, dual-certified provider. Funding will cover critical transition costs, including staffing, training, and operational adjustments required to merge both programs, maintain shelter capacity, and sustain forensic exam and crisis response services. This support will stabilize the system during restructuring and protect survivor safety across the county.
1705.activities: The requested funds will support the full range of domestic violence and sexual assault services needed to ensure a smooth transition to a dual-certified provider. These funds will maintain 24/7 emergency shelter operations, hotline response, advocacy, safety planning, case management, and sexual assault forensic exams. They will also support the staffing, hiring, and specialized training required for dual certification, as well as outreach services provided in the free facilities offered by MCH
1705.direct_services: The appropriation funds will directly support 24/7 emergency shelter, crisis intervention, and safe housing for survivors of domestic violence. They will fund domestic violence and sexual assault hotline services, safety planning, and in- person advocacy for individuals in crisis. Funds will also support Sexual Assault Forensic Exams (SANE services), including medical care and immediate victim acc
1705.population: The target population for this project includes survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in Marion County, as well as their children and family members who require safety, crisis intervention, and trauma-informed support. This project will primarily serve individuals experiencing immediate danger, seeking emergency shelter, requesting sexual assault forensic exams, or needing advocacy and safety planning. Based on current service trends, the merged dual- certified provider is expected t
1705.outcome: The project is expected to ensure uninterrupted, trauma-informed domestic violence and sexual assault services for individuals and families in Marion County during the transition to a dual-certified provider. The anticipated outcomes include improved survivor safety, increased access to emergency shelter and forensic exams, stronger coordination with law enforcement and healthcare partners, reduced service gaps, and a more efficient and unified system of care. These outcomes will be measured through standardized data collection and performance tracking, including the number of survivors served, shelter utilization, hotline call volume, forensic exams completed, advocacy contacts, safety plan

1625.description: Funding will enable the Wakulla Senior Center to serve as a post storm recovery center by proving emergency resiliency and accessibility upgrades to include the installation of an emergency generator for reliable power during outages, the replacement of 6 aged AC units for climate control and ADA upgrades throughout the building for better accessibility.
1625.purpose: Providing a post storm recovery location for the seniors of Wakulla County
1625.activities: Climate controlled Shelter, internet, transportation, hot meals, individual assistance as needed

1515.description: The City of Madison seeks funding to replace 3,200 linear feet of aging 6-inch ductile iron waterline with new 6-inch PVC pipe and 3,200 linear feet of deteriorated 10-inch sanitary sewer line with new 10-inch pipe. These upgrades will improve system reliability, reduce leaks, and prevent costly emergency repairs. The City has secured a FY 2024-2025 SCOP grant to resurface the 0.42-mile roadway segment above these utilities, making it both cost-effective and operationally efficient to complete underground improvements concurrently. Coordinating these projects minimizes future disruptions, preserves roadway integrity, and ensures long-term infrastructure sustainability.
1515.purpose: The City of Madison seeks funding to replace 3,200 linear feet of aging 6-inch ductile waterline with new 6-inch PVC and 3,200 linear feet of deteriorated 10-inch sanitary sewer line with new 10-inch pipe. The City has received a FY 2024-2025 SCOP grant to resurface the 0.42-mile segment of roadway above these utilities, making it cost-effective and efficient to complete underground improvements concurrently.
1515.activities: Activities include replacing 3,200 feet of aging 6-inch waterline with new PVC and 3,200 feet of deteriorated sewer line with new 10-inch pipe. Services provided will improve water delivery, reduce leaks, enhance sewer reliability, and ensure efficient coordination with roadway resurfacing for cost savings and minimal disruption.
1515.direct_services: Funding will provide citizens with reliable water and sewer service by replacing aging lines while roadway resurfacing occurs. The City has received a FY 2024-2025 SCOP grant to resurface the 0.42-mile segment of roadway above these utilities. Coordinating these projects saves costs, minimizes disruptions, and ensures long-term infrastructure efficiency.
1515.population: The projects target population includes approximately 3,000 residents of the City of Madison who rely on municipal water and sewer services.
1515.outcome: This project prevents water and sewer line leaks, contamination, and service failures that could expose residents to health hazards or property damage. The project also reduces costly emergency repairs and service disruptions, which protects businesses and supports growth. Finally, coordinating with roadway resurfacing saves money and minimizes downtime, improving economic efficiency. Methodologies to measure these outcomes include: tracking reductions in leaks and sewer overflows; tracking cost savings from avoided emergency repairs and coordinated construction; and monitoring water quality reports for pollutants before and after the project.

1638.organization: Women In Distress of Broward County, Inc.
1638.description: This project supports a mobile advocacy program. This program is similar to crisis intervention for substance abuse and mental health services. Domestic Violence advocates would dispatch out to scenes where domestic violence has occurred and work directly with victims. Derma Scanners allow for the advocates to assist law enforcement and advocates to get pictures of bruises before they show.

1513.description: This project automates all Career and Technical Education compliance and data for the DOE, School districts, Career Source, Govs office in near real time. It tracks the data and informs the administrator as to what is needed for the student to attain the credential and automates a lot of the work that CTE directors are supposed to be doing but few do. Provides raw number of students in the pipeline for specific industries for job placement.
1513.purpose: The system provides one stop online digital data collection and reporting platform for each district regarding CTE, certification, where the student is in the process, reports CTSO hours, work base learning hours, inventory management for CTE programs and shares all the data with DOE, Career Source, Legislature and OPB. Data is available in seconds instead of days or weeks.
1513.activities: Tracking and reporting on costs, career readiness, students in the employee pipeline and other features for multiple state agencies including commerce to help with company recruitment as well as DOE, Legislature and OPB to have instant data into CTE courses, usage and other data to help make funding decisions.
1513.direct_services: Parents and students will be informed and have more efficient CTE programming within their Districts. Administrators will have a more streamlined process for managing CTE reporting and duties.
1513.population: The future workforce population within the Florida educational system. Mainly students to increase school to job pipeline and identify the number of potential employees ready to work in given sectors.
1513.outcome: State agencies will have near real time data regarding the future workforce stemming from CTE in Florida. State agencies also will have the capability of dissecting the financial costs associated with individual CTE programs to make better policy decisions around CTE funding. District administrators will have less administrative burden. Students will have more efficient CTE programs.

2941.description: The City of Fanning Springs received a Water and Springs Restoration grant through FDEP for $15M to expand the regional wastewater treatment facility and accompanying spray field to meet the Fanning Manatee Priority Focus Area laws and their standards for nitrogen and contaminant levels. The project has been stalled for over two years due to failed negotiations to secure a large enough land parcel to accommodate the additional acres for the spray field expansion. The only available parcel of land is above fair market value, and the funds allocated in the grant only cover land acquisition up to fair market value. The City of Fanning Springs is requesting $600,000 to allow for the purchase of a 133-acre parcel that is directly next to the current wastewater treatment plant. This land acquisition would allow for construction to begin and prevent losing the already allocated grant funds whil
2941.purpose: The City of Fanning Springs was awarded a Water and Springs Restoration grant through the Florida Department of Environmental Protection to expand the regional wastewater utility plant and surrounding spray field. Within the awarded $15 millions grant, $500,000 is reserved for land acquisition for the spray field expansion. The appropriation request is to match the asking price of the only available land near the plant large enough to accommodate the spray field expansion. The funds will be used
2941.activities: The parcel to be acquired will allow for construction to begin on the Fanning Springs Wastewater Treatment Plant and Spray field Expansion which will provide wastewater treatment services to a greater number of developments in the region, including the Lancaster Correctional Facility.
2941.direct_services: The land will serve as the site of the expanded spray field that is required to accommodate the increased wastewater flow from surrounding businesses, residential properties, and state institutions. Failure to acquire the land will put the grant funds in jeopardy and place the current wastewater plant in jeopardy of non-compliance with permit and regulatory requirements for effluent quality.
2941.population: The target population to be served is the Suwannee River Water Management District. The expanded Advanced Wastewater Treatment Facility will serve as a regional facility for citizens of Levy, Gilchrist, and Dixie County.
2941.outcome: The project benefit upon completion will be an expanded spray field for increased capacity of wastewater to be treated according to the Suwannee River Basin Management Action Plan which will enhance, preserve, and improve the surrounding environment water quality, protect the public from harmful wastewater contaminants, improve wastewater management, storm water, drinking water quality, and surface water quality by reducing the amount of toxic containments found in wastewater and reduce the level of nitrogen and other regulated parameters to comply with the Fanning Manatee Priority Focus Area laws and regulations.

2942.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2942.description: The Gilchrist County Rodeo Arena is a key community venue used for rodeos, livestock shows, youth events, and local celebrations. This project will fund the purchase and installation of seven (7) large industrial fans to improve air circulation and comfort within the arena.The fans will help reduce heat, improve safety for participants and spectators, and allow the facility to be used more frequently throughout the year. Enhancing the arena’s environment supports community engagement, local events, and economic activity in Gilchrist County.
2942.purpose: The funds will be used to improve comfort, safety, and usability of the Gilchrist County Rodeo Arena by installing seven (7) industrial ceiling fans. This enhancement will reduce heat, increase air circulation, and allow the arena to be used more frequently for community events, youth programs, and public gatherings throughout the year. The project supports the county’s goal of maintaining safe, functional, and accessible public facilities for residents and visitors.
2942.activities: The project will include purchasing and installing seven (7) industrial ceiling fans in the Gilchrist County Rodeo Arena. Activities include procurement of equipment, electrical and structural installation, and inspection to ensure compliance with safety and building standards.
2942.direct_services: The project will provide a safer, more comfortable public facility for citizens attending events, rodeos, livestock shows, and community gatherings. Improved ventilation will directly benefit all users by reducing heat stress and enhancing air quality.
2942.population: The project will serve Gilchrist County residents, visitors, youth organizations (such as 4-H and FFA), and event participants. The arena hosts an estimated 5,000–7,000 individuals annually, all of whom will benefit from the improvements.
2942.outcome: The expected outcome is improved comfort, safety, and increased usage of the arena throughout the year. Success will be measured by: A reduction in heat-related complaints or incidents during events. An increase in event bookings and attendance after installation. Positive feedback from community groups and event organizers.

1504.description: Franklin County is requesting funding to provide the 50% non-Federal cost share for a shoreline modeling and sediment transport study focused on Bob Sike’s Cut and surrounding areas of St. George Island. This project is being advanced through a partnership with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) under its Planning Assistance to States program. The County seeks to procure professional engineering services to generate science-based data that will improve understanding of shoreline erosion, sediment movement, and inlet dynamics. These insights are critical for guiding future restoration, storm protection, and beach management strategies. The scope of work for this effort has been formally approved by USACE’s division office, ensuring technical rigor and alignment with Federal planning standards.
1504.purpose: The primary objective of this project is to develop a regional sediment budget and modeling tool to better understand inlet morphology and shoreline change affecting Franklin County’s barrier islands. These coastal systems are dynamic and vulnerable to erosion, storm impacts, and sea level rise. The total project budget is $600,000, structured as a 50/50 cost share between Federal and non-Federal sources. This funding will support all study phases, including data collection, modeling, analysis,
1504.activities: The main tasks are listed below: 1. Gather and assess existing information in the area, including native sediment characteristics, topographic and hydrographic surveys, shoreline positions, hydrodynamics and existing numerical modeling tools. 2. Develop updated shoreline changes and sediment budgets. 3. Determine approximate modeling suite and domain setup. 4. Calibrate and validate using historical data (waves, water levels, shoreline change and observed sediment transport). 5. Hindcast modelin
1504.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with improved coastal protection by supporting data-driven shoreline management and erosion mitigation. Residential development on St. George Island began in the 1980s, roughly two decades after the construction of the St. George Island Channel, which continues to influence sediment movement and shoreline vulnerability. In 2024, a restoration feasibility study wa
1504.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a scientifically validated understanding of sediment transport, shoreline change, and inlet dynamics affecting St. George Island and adjacent coastal areas. This will directly inform erosion mitigation, storm protection, and long-term beach management strategies. The methodology centers on the development and application of the Coastal Modeling System (CMS), which will simulate how sediment particles move within the system. Modeling inputs will include hydrodynamics, existing bathymetry, native sediment characteristics, and historical hydrologic data. The model will be calibrated and validated using historical shoreline change and sediment transport re

2951.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2951.description: Clay County will construct a consolidated fleet center aimed to combine three of the County's fleet centers into one. This center will consolidate fleets for Clay County Fire Rescue and the Clay County Sheriff's Office.
2951.purpose: A consolidated fleet center will increase efficiency across Clay County's public safety and sheriff's departments, in addition to other County operations. The new fleet center will enhance the County's capabilities to protect and perform regular maintenance on vehicle assets.
2951.activities: Activities and services provided include the construction of a consolidated fleet center to serve the County operations.
2951.direct_services: Once the facility is operational, public safety personnel will have improved capabilities to provide emergency response services to Clay County residents.
2951.population: The target population served by this project is the general population in Clay County (236,760).
2951.outcome: Benefits to the project include increased efficiency and enhanced capabilities for County operations to protect and perform regular maintenance on vehicle assets.

3582.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
3582.description: The Historic Clay County Courthouse was constructed in 1889 and placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975. Funds are requested to preserve the facilities at the Historic Triangle and Courthouse, which needs necessary roof repairs to maintain structural integrity and protect preserved interior spaces. The Historic Courthouse is currently used for Teen Court programs and is a venue for events such as mock trials, plays, swearing-in ceremonies, photo shoots, and public tours.

1646.description: Funds will be used to expand the pipeline of qualified new teachers entering the education profession in Florida. The Teacher Accelerator Program (TAP) is an innovative initiative to mitigate the teacher shortage across Florida. TAP will expand into Broward County and expand school partnerships. TAP provides college seniors not majoring in education and career-changing professionals with Bachelor's degrees not in education with a clear pathway to teaching.
1646.purpose: Funds will be used to expand the pipeline of qualified new teachers entering the education profession in Florida across Miami-Dade County and Broward County. Funds will support TAP’s planned expansion to train 250-300 new teachers in its fifth year of programming. In the four years since its inception, TAP has already trained 400+ new teachers and continues to expand each year. Funding will directly support the hands-on, summer internship training experience portion of TAP candidates' training a
1646.activities: TAP candidates will be supported through the first component of training--the TAP course, which is developed in partnership with college and university partners. During the summer internship, TAP participants are provided with hands-on teaching experiences with mentor teachers in partnership with public school and charter school partners. TAP participants work directly with experienced teachers and meet with education coaching staff to further develop their teaching skills. They meet 5 times per
1646.direct_services: TAP provides direct services to individuals through teacher recruitment, preparation, and training. TAP begins with a 3-credit course at the University of Miami, Miami-Dade College, Broward College, Barry University, or Florida International University. The course is tailored to college seniors not majoring in education and career changing professionals who hold bachelor’s degrees not in the field
1646.population: TAP serves college seniors and professionals with bachelor’s degrees not in the area of education. TAP’s target population is made up of individuals who would not otherwise consider a career in education. Though TAP trains teachers, this has an impact on the number of students who have access to a full-time, qualified teacher, enhancing student learning outcomes across South Florida.
1646.outcome: Aligning with TAP’s identified 5-year Goals and Objectives, TAP has facilitated the successful training of over 400 teachers in the first 4 years of the program. The expected outcome is that in year 5, TAP will train and place 250-300 new teachers across public and private schools. This program will ensure that hundreds of additional students will have qualified teachers who otherwise may have been seated in an empty classroom. TAP uses data driven research methods. TAP’s evaluation includes community-based participatory research practices through focus groups and multi- stakeholder partners.

1383.purpose: The primary goal of this project is to stabilize the Wagner Creek embankments to prevent erosion, enhance structural integrity, and protect surrounding infrastructure.
