1383.direct_services: The Wagner Creek Embankment Stabilization and Right-of-Way Improvements Project will provide several direct services to citizens, enhancing safety, accessibility, and infrastructure resilience. These services include Enhanced Public Safety, infrastructure & Transportation Upgrades and Environmental & Community Benefits.
1383.population: The target population served by this project includes Local Residents, Commuters and Pedestrians, Local Businesses and Vulnerable Populations.
1383.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of the Wagner Creek Embankment Stabilization and Right-of-Way Improvements Project include Enhanced Public Safety, Improved Infrastructure Resilience, Environmental Benefits and Community Well-Being.

1973.description: The Gainesville Fire and Rescue seek replacement of a re-purposed reserve apparatus deployed into front-line service following the annexation of the SW portion of the City of Gainesville, which resulted in a substantial increase in call volume. The Fire Rescue covers 62.4 Square miles with regional specialty deployment to 11 counties. This request will ensure that it has a reliable, NFPA-compliant frontline engine, restore reserve fleet capacity, and reduce long-term maintenance costs associated with running reserve apparatus as front-line units.

1747.description: The funds will address a project in the East Flagami community of the city which experiences significant flooding during king-tides, rain events, and effects of the sea-level rise. These funds will be used for right-of-way improvements including new and upsized stormwater inlets and pipes, exfiltration trenches, and a new stormwater pump station with injection wells.
1747.purpose: The funds requested will be used to reduce neighborhood flooding, improve stormwater capacity, and enhance public safety by constructing new and upsized stormwater inlets and pipes, adding exfiltration trenches, and building a new stormwater pump station with injection wells. These improvements will increase system reliability, protect infrastructure, and improve roadway access during heavy rain events.
1747.activities: Activities and services funded through this request will include engineering design, permitting, and construction of key stormwater infrastructure improvements. These activities include installing new and upsized stormwater inlets and pipes, constructing exfiltration trenches, and developing a new stormwater pump station with injection wells. Project management, inspection, and testing services will also be provided to ensure the system operates effectively and meets all regulatory standards.
1747.direct_services: The appropriation will provide direct services to residents by reducing flooding in neighborhoods and public roadways, improving stormwater drainage, and enhancing overall public safety during heavy rainfall events. Citizens will benefit from more reliable roadway access, reduced property damage, improved water quality, and faster drainage due to upgraded stormwater infrastructure and the new pump
1747.population: The target population served by this project includes residents, businesses, and visitors within the affected drainage basin and surrounding neighborhoods.
1747.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a significant reduction in neighborhood and roadway flooding, improved stormwater management capacity, and enhanced public safety and mobility during heavy rainfall events. The upgraded drainage infrastructure—including new and upsized inlets and pipes, exfiltration trenches, and the stormwater pump station—will increase system reliability and reduce the frequency, duration, and severity of flood conditions.

Increasing access to fresh produce, whole grains, and protein, which helps stabilize blood sugar, blood pressure, and nutrient levels. Providing consistent food supply, which reduces stress—a major factor in overall health. The stress that food insecurity caused has an overall negative effect.

By making these programs available statewide, the initiative equips K–20 students with essential life skills, including confidence, critical thinking, and effective communication. The program strengthens civil discourse, promotes a deeper understanding of America’s founding principles, and reinforces civic pride and patriotism. Additionally, participation in structured speech and debate activities has been shown to improve Social Studies, English Language Arts (ELA), and English Language Proficiency (ELP) outcomes. This appropriation will ensure that students across Florida—regardless of location—benefit from these transformative academic and civic-learning opportunities.
1588.purpose: The requested funds will expand access to high-quality civic literacy and speech and debate programs across Florida, eliminating the geographic gaps that prevent students in many regions from participating. This investment will equip K–20 students with essential life skills, confidence, critical thinking, and effective communication, while promoting civil discourse, patriotism, and a deeper understanding of our founding principles. 1588.activities: The requested funds will support the Florida Debate Initiative’s statewide civic literacy and speech and debate programs across all 67 school districts, including American Dream Debates for ESOL students, the Veterans Day Speech Contest, Salute to Service, ProCamp for varsity competitors, DebatEd 101 and 201 for new and advanced coaches, Middle School Camp, High School Camp, the Summer Coach Retreat, the Civics Immersion trip to Washington, D.C., and the FDI Fellows college internship program. T
1588.direct_services: The project will provide students across Florida with direct access to speech and debate instruction, civic literacy education, competitive debate opportunities, debate camps, leadership and civics immersion experiences, coach and teacher training, and rehabilitative debate programming for youth in DJJ facilities. These services give students essential skills in communication, critical thinking, a
1588.population: The target population includes K–20 students across all 67 Florida school districts—approximately 2.8 million students, each of whom has access to the Florida Debate Initiative's statewide programs and services. Direct participants include ESOL students, rural and high-need communities, middle and high school speech and debate students, participants in programs such as American Dream Debates, the Veterans Day Speech Contest, Salute to Service, ProCamp, and debate camps, as well as novice and adv
1588.outcome: The project will improve civic literacy, communication skills, critical thinking, and academic performance for students across all 67 districts, while expanding access to high-quality speech and debate programs for ESOL students, rural and high-need communities, and justice-involved youth. Outcomes will be measured through student participation data, academic indicators, pre- and post-assessments, coach evaluations, DJJ behavioral measures, and statewide access tracking. The assessment process will be established by the FDOE.

2254.description: A continuation of the approved 2025-26 FY budget, the VetConnect Solution will help identify veterans to provide services and experiences that matter. Each year some veterans do not get the critical support and services. They get lost navigating complex systems or do not know what support is available. States often have siloed systems of record, resulting in lost funding for veteran support. Identifying veterans in your community is the first critical step in a process of outreach, engagement, and service navigation to support our veterans.
2254.purpose: The funds will help support Florida veterans and the employees that serve them in several ways. First, by providing information and advocacy to all Florida veterans, their families, and survivors; and assisting them in obtaining all Federal and State benefits due to them. the funds will also improve the long term health care services eligible to Florida veterans. Finally, the funds will help provide effective and responsive management to support divisions and programs serving veterans.
2254.activities: The Vet Connect solution will increase identification of veterans and awareness to engage them in needed services. It will quantify and qualify veterans for available services as well as engage them to understand their specific needs. The feedback obtained from Florida veterans and FDVA employees will improve the processes and programs as well as enhance staffing and resources
2254.direct_services: Applying learnings from other states, FDVA can identify, contact, and serve an additional 880,000 to 1,100,000 more Florida veterans. The advanced listening systems and employee engagement programs can increase federal benefits owed to Florida veterans which can result in an uptick in many state programs to support veterans, such economic and health outcomes for veterans.
2254.population: All Veterans in the State of Florida; both those the state is aware of and those that are unaccounted. This is as many as the 1,500,000 current veterans in the state plus as many as 1,100,000 more.
2254.outcome: Veterans who have access to VA services tend to have better health outcomes, lower unemployment, and lower homelessness compared to those without access. By identifying all veterans in the state, understanding their needs and connecting them to services, the Vet Connect program can improve veteran and employee experiences with automations and workflows.

2260.description: Project scope targets existing rights-of-way within the City of San Antonio suitable for enhancement, including construction of new sidewalks, extension of existing sidewalks, and installation of more effective stormwater management infrastructure. This project aims to increase pedestrian safety and walkability between the City's residential areas to it's commercial/recreational core areas, while addressing outdated stormwater mitigation methods that create obstacles for both pedestrian and vehicle traffic.
2260.purpose: Project goal is to expand infrastructure to increase pedestrian safety and encourage alternative means of access from the City's residential areas to it's commercial/recreational area. Installation of sidewalks within rights-of-way will also require modification to existing stormwater infrastructure, to accommodate the added walkway structures and improve stormwater mitigation methods in the area.
2260.activities: Enhanced pedestrian walkways will be available to connect the residential areas to the City's commercial/recreational quarter, including access to amenities such as municipal parks. Stormwater management projects in overlapping areas will reduce instances of standing water and flooding, servicing both vehicular traffic in the areas and encouraging use of the new walkways.
2260.direct_services: Alternate means of transportation will be encouraged with construction of public sidewalks. Stormwater management in the same areas will see a reduction in hazards such as standing water, vegetative overgrowth, and failing infrastructure due to maintenance concerns.
2260.population: The target population is the general population of San Antonio residents, not restricted to those residing in the target areas due to the availability of public roadways.
2260.outcome: Expected benefit is an increased amount of public walkways available, connecting existing walkways with no concrete ending location, and further interlinking the different areas of the City. Improvement of stormwater infrastructure in the same areas will enhance safety for both pedestrians and vehicles, and extend the longevity of existing road and walkway infrastructure. More efficient stormwater mitigation practices will lead to a reduction in expenses associated with repairs and maintenance by the City's Public Works Department over an extended period of time.

2263.description: A Door of Hope (ADH) will expand recruitment and licensing activities to provide safe, stable homes for children in high- need regions. TBRI trainings will make families more resilient and prepared to support the children who need more acute care in the system. Collectively, these activities will bolster the State's number of foster families and the average retention rate.
2263.purpose: A Door of Hope (ADH) will expand recruitment and licensing activities to provide safe, stable homes for children in high-need regions. Families will have access to more frequent fast-track licensing options, closing the State's critical shortage of licensed families. TBRI trainings will make families more resilient and prepared to address childhood trauma. Collectively, these activities will bolster the State's number of foster families and the average retention rate.

ADH families foster 3x longer than the State average, reducing costly turnover, saving thousands in repeated home studies and training, and delivering high ROI for Florida. In essence, ADH preserves childhoods while making foster families more resilient.

2788.description: This project strengthens the resilience and security of the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system at the Regional Surface Water Treatment Plant by replacing its aging infrastructure, which is now over 20 years old. The existing system will be modernized with more robust hardware and software to enhance reliability, security, and protection against cyber and operational threats. The upgrade includes replacing all Programmable Logic Controllers across the facility and upgrading SCADA servers, critical equipment, and instrumentation to harden the system against vulnerabilities. Additionally, the project will modernize the human-machine interface, implementing the latest version of AVEVA System Platform to improve functionality, situational awareness, and overall system defense.
2788.purpose: This project strengthens the resilience and security of the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system at the Regional Surface Water Treatment Plant (SWTP) by replacing its aging infrastructure, which is now over 20 years old. This system is responsible for controlling the treatment and delivery of a significant portion of the clean, safe water our agency provides. It is essential to the operation of our water delivery network, ensuring the reliable supply of over 90 million gallons
2788.activities: Delivering quality drinking water to more than 2.6 million people in the Tampa Bay Region.
2788.direct_services: Direct services for this project include ensuring the delivery of quality drinking water to residents of member governments in the Tampa Bay Region.
2788.population: More than 2.6 million people in the Tampa Bay Region, served through our member governments that include Pinellas, Pasco, Hillsborough Counties, City of Tampa, City of Saint Petersburg, and City of New Port Richey.
2788.outcome: This system is responsible for controlling the treatment and delivery of a significant portion of the clean, safe water our agency provides. It is essential to the operation of our water delivery network, ensuring the reliable supply of over 90 million gallons of high-quality drinking water daily to the Tampa Bay region. The outcome will be measured by the data quantifying the delivery of safe, quality drinking water.

3381.description: Goodwill SWFL's Collier County Community Resource Center and MicroEnterprise Institute Center (CRC) is dedicated to serving as a welcoming hub for workforce development, small business development and community engagement. This aligns with Goodwill's mission to empower individuals to succeed in today's dynamic job market through thoughtfully designed programs that emphasize the importance of up-skilling in professional, digital, financial and soft skills. Along with driving economic development in the county, the project will promote collaboration among community members by providing meeting rooms, training areas and offices. Collier County will have dedicated space for recruiting and other needs.
3381.purpose: The goal of this project is to expand workforce and small business development services to the constituents of Collier County. Doing this will drive measurable economic development in Collier County. It will provide a space for Collier County to have training and recruiting spaces for their efforts, and will provide a collaborative space for Goodwill's valued partners who are dedicated to serving and uplifting Collier County by providing impactful services.
3381.activities: Goodwill will provide their data driven, thoughtfully designed workforce and small business development services. The workforce development services provided will be digital literacy training which includes Microsoft Suite and AI training, resume development, interview prep, and soft skills classes. Through the small business development program, low to moderate income individuals will learn how to start or strengthen a small business that thrives in the county, this includes classes on business
3381.direct_services: Services provided by Goodwill or in collaboration with other agency are: Workforce Development service - Microsoft Suite training, Google AI training, Senior Plant classes, ESL classes, Resume and Interview workshops, Soft Skills workshops, Citizenship Classes, Financial Literacy Classes, Nutritional Classes, Homeownership Workshops. Small Business Services - Classes that teach Business Concept, M
3381.population: Goodwill services are open to anyone who needs them, but the targeted demographic includes individuals with disabilities, barriers to employment, low-to-moderate-income individuals, and seniors. Goodwill expects to provide an average of 2,200 services to 1,100 individuals annually. Through community partners and local county initiatives, the annual number served is expected to reach 2,500 individuals.
3381.outcome: The expected benefits from this project is to drive economic development through job creation, education, training, and business creation. Goodwill uses a case management system that helps to track and report client milestones, success, job acquisition, retention and businesses created.

2268.description: Pasco County is partnering with the City of Dade City to build a 50,000 sq. foot multi-functional complex in a campus- like setting that will also serve as a regional emergency shelter. The center will house a storm hardened gymnasium, several breakout activity and meeting rooms, and satellite Public Services Branch offices, including Veterans’ Services. Total project cost $40,000,000, Local Match $20,000,000, State funds requested $20,000,000.
2268.purpose: To provide a county emergency shelter and recreation complex in an area where there is none. 77,340 people These funds will help to fund a building that will provide a regional shelter when needed; daily recreational activities for the residents of Pasco County; and a larger space for Veteran's and Community Services.
2268.activities: During severe weather events, and other emergency events, the building will serve as a much-needed regional shelter. During normal times, the building will offer a multi-purpose facility. The Veteran's and Community Service offices will offer a full array of services for Veterans and Citizens in the need of help.
2268.direct_services: -Sheltering during storms. -Recreational activity. -Services to help veterans and the community with benefits.
2268.population: The targeted population for this facility is the residents in the east side of Pasco County (Dade City, Zephyrhills, Wesley Chapel, etc.). During storms it will also serve the sheltering needs of surrounding counties. The east side of the county is home to over 150,000 residents or ~20% of the total population of the county.
2268.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to provide a much-needed space for sheltering in east Pasco County, in addition the facility will be used for multi-purpose activities. The success of this project will be measured by the amount of people that use the facility on a regular basis. The other measure will be when the facility is needed to shelter the general population during and after an disaster storm events.

2270.description: At Quantum Leap Farm (QLF), our mission is to transform lives by harnessing the healing connection between humans and horses through equine-assisted therapies. This request supports our veteran and military family programs, including Therapeutic Riding, Hippotherapy, military retreats, EASE mental health sessions and veteran Family Fun Days. These programs help veterans and their families manage symptoms of PTSD, depression, and anxiety, build coping skills and foster resilience. This funding request will help fill the gap in funding for our military programs in the upcoming year, as QLF never charges military clients or their families to participate. $294,700 would cover the financial need for these program sessions: • (7 retreats / 56 veterans) 5-Day Military Retreats • (288) Therapeutic Riding • (400) EASE therapy (groups and individuals) • (48) Hippotherapy • (100) Retreat follow-up
2270.purpose: Equine-Assisted Therapy Programs provided by Quantum Leap Farm will improve quality of life, and the physical, social and emotional well-being of military service members, veterans and family members. Specific programs will produce measurable improvements in self-confidence, healthy coping skills and stress management skills, and reductions in symptoms related to PTSD, depression and suicidal ideation.
2270.activities: Quantum Leap Farm will provide Equine-Assisted Therapy Programs and activities especially designed to support the physical, social and emotional well-being of military service members, veterans and their families. All Equine-Assisted Therapy Programs at Quantum Leap Farm are facilitated by qualified therapeutic riding instructors, or licensed and specially certified mental health and other medical professionals.
2270.direct_services: Quantum Leap Farm’s programs for military service members include an array of equine-assisted therapies including Therapeutic Horseback Riding, Hippotherapy, Equine-Assisted Psychotherapy (EASE Program), Family Fun and Re- integration Days and Therapeutic Retreats with follow-up sessions. (Please see attached program description)
2270.population: Quantum Leap Farm’s programs for military service members, veterans and family members serves individuals and families navigating reintegration issues, living with post-traumatic stress, traumatic brain injury, chronic pain, suicidal ideation, and military sexual trauma among other service-related physical, intellectual, emotional and moral injuries. After funding is awarded, we expect to serve approximately 500 individuals a year through more than 1,100 sessions. Specific data collected will va
2270.outcome: Participants in all programs will self-report via questionnaires. Depending on which program they participate in, they will report on physical and emotional changes including their feelings of self-confidence, their repertoire of healthy coping skills and stress management skills, and on their overall quality of life. Participants in EASE or Retreat Programs will also complete psychosocial surveys/instruments designed to measure changes in symptoms related to PTSD, depression, and suicidal ideation.

2272.description: With support from our legislative partners, we can ensure that no child is denied services due to financial hardship. Since insurance rarely covers equine-assisted therapies, we depend on donors and state funding to provide these life- changing services to children at little to no cost to their families. Our goal is to expand our reach and serve more children in our region who are waiting for the opportunity to heal and thrive alongside our horses. We plan to strengthen our current programs, launch new initiatives that empower our participants, and broaden our community impact, all while continuing to offer exceptional care to our herd and maintaining essential operational resources.
2272.purpose: Our goal is simple: no child is denied services due to financial hardship. Since insurance rarely covers equine-assisted therapies, we rely on donors and state support to ensure that children who need these life-changing services can access them at little to no cost to their families. With support from our legislative partners, we can expand our reach to serve more children throughout our region who are waiting for the opportunity to heal and thrive alongside our horses.
2272.activities: Funds will support equine-assisted therapies that improve physical, emotional, and developmental outcomes for children. Services include physical and occupational therapies incorporating hippotherapy, behavioral health support, equine-facilitated learning, Horse Powered Reading®, and caregiver resources that help families reinforce progress at home.
2272.direct_services: Physical and occupational therapies incorporating hippotherapy, emotional and behavioral support, equine-facilitated learning, Horse Powered Reading®, and various resources and means of support for caregivers and the community.
2272.population: We provide equine-assisted services to children ages 2–18 who are navigating significant obstacles in their daily lives. We serve children from nine counties throughout central Florida who primarily: have physical, developmental, or learning disabilities, are coping with emotional or behavioral health challenges or trauma, are children of military families, are in the foster care system or have been recently adopted, or are undergoing or recovering from cancer treatment. We expect to serve 100-1
2272.outcome: Enhance physical and mental health by improving quality of life and fostering independence through equine-assisted therapies. These activities improve walking, balance, core strength, body awareness, and coordination, as well as help to develop coping skills for challenges like depression, PTSD, and anxiety. Participants also gain confidence by learning to focus, reduce distractions, and improve situational awareness. Outcomes are measured through therapist- administered assessments at intake and discharge.

2273.description: The Florida Veterans Legal Helpline (FVLH) staff will provide direct legal assistance to low-income veterans to reduce civil law barriers that threaten the individual's employability, their individual or family financial stability and independence, their ability to gain and sustain employment, or their ability to build and sustain individual/family assets. FVLH attorneys will provide direct advice and assistance to low-income veterans over the phone, schedule appointments for extended services with full-time attorneys who focus solely on veterans, and coordinate referrals to partners throughout the State of Florida. This FVLH will provide access to service for a population that would otherwise not have access to legal advice and representation.
2273.purpose: The Florida Veterans Legal Helpline (FVLH) staff will provide direct legal assistance to low-income veterans to reduce civil law barriers that threaten the individual's employability, their individual or family financial stability and independence, their ability to gain and sustain employment, or their ability to build and sustain individual/family assets. FVLH attorneys will provide direct advice and assistance to low-income veterans over the phone, schedule appointments for extended services w
2273.activities: The Florida Veterans Legal Helpline (FVLH) attorneys will provide direct advice and assistance to low-income veterans over the phone, schedule appointments for extended services with full-time attorneys who focus solely on veterans, and coordinate referrals to partners throughout the State of Florida. This FVLH will provide access to services for a population that would otherwise not have access to legal advice and representation.
2273.direct_services: The Florida Veterans Legal Helpline (FVLH) attorneys will provide direct advice and assistance to low-income veterans over the phone, schedule appointments for extended services with full-time attorneys who focus solely on veterans, and coordinate referrals to partners throughout the State of Florida.
2273.population: Low-income veterans and their family members throughout the State of Florida.
2273.outcome: Access to legal advice and assistance at no cost to eligible veterans to reduce civil law barriers that threaten the individuals employability, their individual or family financial stability and independence

2274.description: Support is requested to renovate an existing facility, expanding behavioral health services while integrating discount pharmacy services to make mental health, substance use disorder services and pharmacy services accessible for low- income and/or uninsured community residents. The renovation will convert open spaces into patient care rooms for therapy and expand the discount pharmacy to accommodate patient needs.
2274.purpose: The funding requested will be used to renovate a facility enabling the community health center to increase access to care for residents in need of mental health, substance abuse disorder and opioid use disorder. The main goal of this request is to obtain vital funds to renovate the facility and optimize open spaces by converting them into patient care rooms.
2274.activities: Upon completion of the renovation project, mental health and discount pharmacy services will be provided for low- income, uninsured, and/or vulnerable population enabling them to be productive citizens.
2274.direct_services: Healthcare services will be directly provided to citizens by Premier upon completion of the renovation of the facility.
2274.population: The target population includes all residents in need of mental health, substance misuse disorders or discount pharmacy services, especially the medically needy, uninsured, and/or low-income Pasco County residents.
2274.outcome: Upon completion of the facility renovation, the outcome of the project will be additional patient care areas to accommodate the patient needs in the community. The expected benefit is improved health status for the population served. The outcome will be measured through core clinical quality metrics using the health center's electronic health record system (EPIC).

2275.description: Operation New Uniform, a Florida-based 501(c)(3) veteran service organization, is dedicated to empowering Service members, Veterans, and Military Spouses to transition successfully into purposeful and stable careers. Through personalized career coaching, counseling, and training, the program addresses the needs of the unemployed and underemployed, equipping them with the tools to thrive professionally. To date, Operation Uniform has completed 71 classes with over 750 graduates.
2275.purpose: Operation New Uniform (ONU) delivers transformative transition training for Servicemembers, Veterans, and Military Spouses, with the sole mission of helping them "find their new uniform" in the business world. Without this support, many of these individuals could face unemployment or underemployment. Impressively, 97% of ONU graduates secure meaningful employment within just four months of completing the program, earning an average salary of $94,000.
2275.activities: Operation New Uniform (ONU) offers tailored transition training for Servicemembers, Veterans, and Military Spouses. Students can learn either in-person or online to meet their unique learning needs. Beyond ONU's proprietary training curriculum, the program hosts networking events throughout the year, providing students with valuable opportunities to connect with local business leaders and recruiters, helping them "find their new uniform" in the professional world.
2275.direct_services: Operation New Uniform (ONU) provides direct services that include comprehensive training and instruction, available both in-person and online, as well as hosting networking events. These initiatives are designed to support transitioning Servicemembers, Veterans, and Military Spouses in successfully "finding their new uniform" in the business world.
2275.population: Operation New Uniform (ONU) serves a dedicated target population of Servicemembers, Veterans, and Military Spouses, providing transformative support to over 260 individuals annually.
2275.outcome: Measurements are tracked in Salesforce (methodology). Please take a moment to view the testimonial of two ONU graduates, Gary and Kristi, which clearly illustrates ONU's impact: https://tinyurl.com/2s3p6jze

3373.description: Construction of two (2) potable raw water wells within the City's primary wellfield to sustain yield, reliability, and redundancy .
3373.purpose: Provide infrastructure improvements that will aid in sustaining an uninterrupted water supply to the residents of the City of Naples; construct replacement potable raw water wells 410 & 418 within the Golden Gate Wellfield to sustain yield, reliability, and redundancy as recommended within the City's Adopted Integrated Water Resource Plan (2008, 2022 update), in addition to recommendations resulting from a well field evaluation study provided by Water Science Associates (2024-2025).
3373.activities: Construction of raw water production wells Nos. 410 and 418.
3373.direct_services: Infrastructure improvements that will aid in sustaining an uninterrupted water supply to the residents of the City of Naples.
3373.population: Directly impacts approximately 83,000 residents that are served by the City's water distribution system.
3373.outcome: Reduce infrastructure failures and minimize the potential for interrupted water supply service (pumping activities). This project will also assist in reducing the demands on the City's Coastal Ridge well field, which is located in close proximity to the coastline and is therefore more susceptible to saltwater intrusion in the future. SCADA system reporting and monitoring that includes, but not limited to, pumping logs, pump run times (hourly/daily), pump tests, draw down curves, changes in well capacity, water quality and compliance testing, unplanned outages, sustainable yield compliance, and maintenance logs.

2240.description: Overnight shelter buses provide refuge for up to 20 homeless individuals by offering 20 beds, restrooms, and storage in a retrofitted bus, which parks at an approved Orange County Site. This project is meant to be a partnership between Orange County and a nonprofit aiming to provide immediate shelter and connect clients with case management services and resources to help them find permanent housing. Clients will receive the services during the day at a homeless drop- in service center operated by a nonprofit. The shelter bus is estimated to provide up to 1,700 overnight stays annually.
2240.purpose: Reintegration of unhoused individuals. Providing homeless individuals with immediate shelter and the opportunity to become self-sufficient. Response to HB 1365 (2024) - Fla. Stat. 125.0231
2240.activities: Intensive case management Mental Health and Substance Abuse Assistance. Primary Health Care referrals. Placement into transitional housing or drug treatment, if applicable. Placement into permanent housing and referrals to full-time employment opportunities.
2240.direct_services: Intensive case management Mental Health and Substance Abuse Assistance. Primary Health Care referrals. Placement into transitional housing or drug treatment, if applicable. Placement into permanent housing and referrals to full-time employment opportunities.
2240.population: Unhoused population in Orange County (male and female individuals, no families). May have substance abuse or mild mental health disorder. Must be motivated to exit homelessness.
2240.outcome: We will utilize data from homeless management information system (HMIS) of: How many clients transition into treatment How many clients transition into permanent housing How many clients obtained full-time employment How many clients reported positive changes in health and mental health outcomes

2489.description: To increase affordable access to golf for children ages 3-18 who are Youth on Course members (no cost).
2489.purpose: To grow and inspire young people to learn the lifelong values of the game of golf. There is no cost associated with the membership.
2489.activities: Funds would offer grants for golf for Youth on Course members in Florida. There is no cost associated with the membership.
2489.direct_services: More than 75 golf courses currently partner with Youth on Course to provide young Florida golfers with low cost access to golf via Youth on Course. With additional funds, Youth on Course will increase the number of courses and the number of families served where youth members will have access to play for $5 or less per round.
2489.population: All of Florida's youth, age 3-18. More than 10,000
2489.outcome: Youth in Florida will learn values that are unique to golf that are transferable to all areas of life, once they become adults. Constant surveys can be used to measure the final outcome.

1742.description: This project will provide flood prevention improvements as well as better water quality around Gulfview Ridge and Florida Oaks Subdivisions within the City, also known as the Ross Property area. This area experiences flooding mostly due to a lack of adequate drainage conveyance within the ditch. The total cost of design and construction is $3,416,637. The City is requesting $1,708,318.50 in State Appropriations Funding (50%) with the City providing $1,708,318.50 (50%) in matching funds. The City's match would include all of the design costs and half of the construction cost.
1742.purpose: This project will provide flood prevention improvements and better water quality around the Gulfview Ridge and Florida Oaks Subdivisions within the City.
1742.activities: Flood prevention and better water quality will be provided by adequate drainage conveyance within the ditch.
1742.direct_services: The residents in this area of the City will benefit from improved flood prevention and better water quality.
1742.population: Approximately 180 homes will benefit from this project.
1742.outcome: This project is expected to provide flood prevention improvements and better water quality in the Gulfview Ridge and Florida Oaks Subdivisions within the City of Tarpon Springs.

1743.description: This project will mitigate flooding that occurs east of the Pinellas Trail within the City from Harrison Street south to East Curlew Place. Flooding can be resolved by improving the existing 30-inch trail cross-drain to minimize trail overtopping and to decrease the wetland recovery periods. The total cost of design and construction is $351,416. The City is requesting $175,708 (50%) in State Appropriation Funding with a $175,708 (50%) City match. The City's match would include all of the design costs and half of the construction cost.
1743.purpose: This project will mitigate flooding that occurs east of the Pinellas Trail within the City from Harrison Street south to East Curlew Place.
1743.activities: Flooding can be resolved by improving the existing the 30-inch cross drain to minimize trail overlapping and to decrease the wetland recovery periods.
1743.direct_services: This project will mitigate flooding to the area east of the Pinellas Trail from Harrison Street south to East Curlew Place.
1743.population: Approximately 1524 parcels will be served by this project
1743.outcome: This project is expected to mitigate flooding east of the Pinellas Trail

1590.description: As Florida communities continue to face growing division, misinformation, and extremism that affect schools and public safety, The Holocaust Memorial Resource & Education Center of Florida (HMREC) seeks a one-time, non-recurring $700,000 state investment to expand its educational programs under the umbrella of the Take Action Institute as HMREC prepares for the opening of the Holocaust Museum for Hope & Humanity in 2028. The program builds statewide capacity for conflict de-escalation, civic responsibility, and critical thinking education, supporting the infrastructure for a self-sustaining statewide initiative that will continue to expand as the Holocaust Museum for Hope & Humanity opens in 2028.
1590.purpose: This initiative addresses increasing conflict and polarization in classrooms and communities. The Take Action Institute equips teachers, students, and law-enforcement officers with tools to de-escalate tension, strengthen civic trust, and apply history to present-day challenges. This $700,000 non-recurring request will create the infrastructure for a self- sustaining statewide initiative that will continue to expand as the Holocaust Museum for Hope & Humanity opens in 2028.
1590.activities: Funding will specifically support: development/distribution of civic education curriculum, conflict resolution resources, mobile exhibit assets, technology platforms for use across program areas; expanding the Teachers Institute to increase statewide attendance; experiential professional development opportunities for law enforcement; a portion of HMREC education staff salaries; and an independent program evaluation to measure participant learning outcomes, behavioral impact, and program effectiv
1590.direct_services: UpStanders: Civic, mental health, and character education for 20,000+ students annually. Dr. Norman M. Wall Teachers Institute: Summer and yearlong online training for 1,000+ educators statewide. CitizenU: Year-round training for 500+ law enforcement and corrections officers focused on leadership, de-escalation, and public trust.
1590.population: Students (K-12), teachers, and law enforcement professionals across Florida. First-year reach: ˜21,500 participants. This state supported investment establishes a baseline for continued growth without recurring full funding.
1590.outcome: Strengthens Florida’s capacity to address conflict and prevent extremism through education and professional training. Improves school safety, teaching quality, and law enforcement professionalism. Promotes critical thinking, civic responsibility, and public trust while driving economic and cultural activity through statewide training events. Measured by surveys, registration data, and program evaluations.

3252.description: We are constructing a 17,000 square-foot facility that will accommodate many more healthy services to promote positive aging and social inclusion at all ages in our community. We are the primary hub for human services in South Collier County, where a majority of the population is 65 years or older (57% and increasing on Marco Island). By constructing new space dedicated to senior programming, we will also free more shared space in our existing facility for youth programming.
3252.purpose: The funds requested will support the expansion of program space geared toward older adults for activities that focus on fitness, wellness, and socialization. Offices will also be available for essential mental health and medical partners to provide physical and cognitive assessments and therapies.
3252.activities: Wellness classes such as yoga, Tai Chi, and mindful movement will be geared toward seniors. An activities room will provide a space for groups to gather, socialize, and play games. Community partnerships will be utilized to promote medical integration options such as physical therapy, cognitive assessments, weight and nutrition programs, strength training, and chronic disease support.
3252.direct_services: The Adult Social and Wellness Center within the new Healthy Living Center will serve as a central hub for South Collier seniors. The Center will provide communal meals, nutritional support, educational seminars, volunteer opportunities, social inclusion, and recreational activities. Space also will be provided for intergenerational social interaction and programming.
3252.population: This project will serve over 10,000 community members. The target population for the Adult Social and Wellness Center includes the elderly, those with poor physical and mental health, physically disabilities, the economically disadvantaged, veterans, and many others. Community members of all ages will be served by a new fitness center, library nook, healthy cafe, reflection room, and social spaces.
3252.outcome: The National Council on Aging states that senior program participants have higher levels of health, social interaction, and life satisfaction. Community partners will assess attendees in all health, nutritional, and training programs. This may include weight management, biometrics, aerobic fitness, and flexibility. Classes will provide information to the community and will be assessed based on attendance. In many programs related to chronic disease, assessments are continual in an attempt to manage and delay the onset of symptoms. Additional evaluation will be obtained through surveys that measure life satisfaction and a sense of well-being.

3246.description: Project BUILD SWFL is seeking an appropriation to purchase two heavy-equipment simulators with six trade simulations (e.g., excavator, small dozer, compact track loader, etc.) to expand Project BUILD SWFL’s DOE-approved pre- apprenticeship. The simulators enable young adults ages 17 to 24 who are unemployed, underemployed, or disconnected from traditional education or career pathways, including youth transitioning from foster care, returning citizens, and community members to train safely for high-demand construction roles, earn industry credentials (OSHA- 10/30, PIT), and secure jobs averaging $22–$30/hour across Collier and Lee counties.
3246.purpose: The purpose of these funds is to expand Project BUILD SWFL’s Florida Department of Education approved construction pre apprenticeship program by purchasing two heavy equipment simulation units with six industry recognized equipment types. The simulators will increase access to hands on workforce training across Collier and Lee counties, leading directly to high wage employment in the skilled trades. The program serves young adults ages 17 to 24 who are unemployed, underemployed, or disconnected
3246.activities: Students will receive industry aligned instruction including OSHA safety, equipment controls, simulated jobsite operations, and employer led demonstrations. The program combines classroom learning, supervised simulation hours, mentoring, job readiness instruction, and direct employment support. Project BUILD SWFL will also coordinate transportation, provide personal protective equipment, and facilitate paid work based learning in partnership with local construction employers.
3246.direct_services: Participants will receive construction career training, credential testing, work based learning wages, employment placement, and individualized support to overcome barriers to work. The mobile nature of the simulators will allow underserved communities to access services directly without requiring transportation to centralized facilities.
3246.population: The project serves young adults ages 17 to 24 who are unemployed, underemployed, or disconnected from education including foster care youth, justice impacted individuals, and community members seeking skilled trades careers. The program will train 100 to 120 individuals annually across Collier and Lee counties.
3246.outcome: The expected outcomes are increased employment in high demand construction occupations, reduced crime and recidivism among justice impacted participants, and greater economic mobility for youth transitioning into adulthood. Success will be measured by enrollment tracking, credential verification, job placement rates, starting wages, retention after 6 and 12 months, and employer satisfaction surveys.

1385.description: Inclusion Revolution’s Integrated Jobs Program prepares and places adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) into competitive employment in Sarasota and Manatee counties. The program provides individualized job development, coaching, and ongoing support so participants can secure meaningful work, earn wages, and be fully included in workplaces. State funding will support a program administrator, job coaches, transportation, employer education, and wage support for paid internships when needed. These services reduce barriers that keep adults with IDD out of the workforce (employer readiness, individualized coaching, and transportation) and replace them with a supported pathway into jobs. The requested funds will allow Inclusion Revolution to serve approximately 70 participants from Sarasota and Manatee counties each year, match them with inclusive employers, and provid
1385.purpose: The requested funds will expand Inclusion Revolution’s Integrated Jobs Program so that adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) in Sarasota and Manatee counties can obtain and maintain competitive, integrated employment. The primary goal is to increase the number of participants with IDD who secure paid jobs in community businesses at or above minimum wage and who are still successfully employed at 6 and 12 months.
1385.activities: • Outreach and intake for adults with IDD and their families in Sarasota and Manatee counties • Individualized vocational assessment and job readiness planning • Job development and employer matching based on participants’ strengths, interests, and support needs • On-site job coaching during onboarding and the first 90 days of employment, with tapering support as the participant gains independence • Ongoing follow-along support to address any workplace issues and help participants advance in the
1385.direct_services: Direct services to citizens will include: • One-to-one job coaching and employment support for adults with IDD • Assistance with job search, resume development, and interview practice • On-site coaching during the first days and weeks of employment • Ongoing individualized support to maintain employment, resolve issues, and build workplace social skills • Guidance to families and caregivers on how
1385.population: The target population is adults (typically ages 18 and older) with intellectual and developmental disabilities living in Sarasota and Manatee counties who are seeking competitive, integrated employment. Many participants are low- to moderate-income, and most have experienced long-term exclusion from the workforce.
1385.outcome: Expected benefits/outcomes include: ¿• Increased number of adults with IDD securing competitive, integrated jobs¿• Increased wages and hours worked for participants¿• Improved workplace social skills, independence, and self-confidence among participants¿• Increased number of employers in Sarasota and Manatee who successfully hire and retain employees with IDD¿• Reduced isolation and increased community inclusion for adults with IDD. Measurement methodology: • Tracking of job placements, wages, hours, and job type for each participant • Employment retention measured at 3/6/12 months • Number of employers engaged, trained, and employing individuals with IDD • Pre- and post- surveys of particip

2611.description: The City of Palatka Fire Department seeks state assistance to purchase a new aerial ladder truck to replace an aging 2001 model that no longer meets NFPA standards. The new truck will enhance fire suppression and rescue operations for multi-story structures, industrial sites, and key public facilities. In addition, it will help the City maintain its ISO Class 3 insurance rating.
2611.purpose: The City of Palatka Fire Department seeks state assistance to purchase a new aerial ladder truck to replace an aging 2001 model that no longer meets NFPA standards. The new truck will enhance fire suppression and rescue operations for multi-story structures, industrial sites, and key public facilities. In addition, it will help the City maintain its ISO Class 3 insurance rating.
2611.activities: The Palatka Fire Department serves over 10,000 residents and multiple large inustrial users, such as Georgia Pacific and Seminole Electric. The new truck will enhance fire suppression and rescue operations for multi-story structures, industrial sites, and key facilities.
2611.direct_services: Improved protection of citizens lives, property and environment.
2611.population: The target population to be served would be elderly persons and the general public. The individuals expected to be served are roughly 800.
2611.outcome: The goal of this project is to protect the general public from various things such as environmental or crime related issues. The expected benefit is that the ladder truck will improve the ability of the Palatka Fire Department to protect the general public from the threat of a fire. This would be measured by monitoring the response times, analyzing fire incidents and other forms of emergency services.

2614.description: Veterans Village will provide subsidized shelter for our veterans, case management, resource and referral services, employment related services, assistance with applying for benefits they may be entitled to. Case managers and mentors will work with the veterans to help them stabilize and become successfully housed by connecting them with all the resources they need to stabilize. Safe, clean and affordable housing units will be available for shelter. Veterans will be employed, as available, to provide services in an effort to better connect with the clients.
2614.purpose: Veteran will stabilize and maintain housing whether they stay at Veterans Village or move into housing in the community. Veteran will improve their physical and mental health and reduce substance/alcohol abuse. Improve their employment possibilities through access to educational opportunities, economic self-sufficiency, and job opportunities.
2614.activities: Provide subsidized shelter for our veterans, case management, resource and referral services, employment related services, assistance with applying for benefits they may be entitled to. Mentors will be available to work with the veterans to help them stabilize and be successful in housing.
2614.direct_services: Shelter our veterans in a safe, clean and affordable housing unit Case management to transition from being homeless to becoming housed Case management to connect resources for stabilization Employment of veterans to aid in rendering services
2614.population: Veterans which may include: elderly, persons with poor physical/mental health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, homeless, physically disabled, drug users in health services, drug offenders, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, victims of crime.
