2292.purpose: To expand safe housing and resource center operations serving individuals and families facing homelessness, crisis, or recovery needs including survivors of human trafficking. Funding supports housing, case management, job training, peer recovery, and mental-health services to promote stability, safety, and long-term independence across the Tampa Bay region.
2292.activities: Funding will support emergency and transitional housing placement, daily access to food, hygiene, transportation, case management, mental-health support, peer recovery services, job training, education assistance, and coordinated services for at-risk youth, families, and survivors of human trafficking.
2292.direct_services: Direct services include emergency and transitional housing, meals, hygiene items, transportation support, case management, peer recovery coaching, mental-health referrals, job and life-skills training, GED support, and ongoing stabilization services for at-risk youth, families, and survivors of human trafficking.
2292.population: Economically disadvantaged individuals, at-risk youth, young adults aging out of foster care, families experiencing homelessness or crisis, persons with poor mental/physical health, victims of crime, and individuals who have experienced or survived human trafficking.
2292.outcome: Benefits: Improved housing stability, mental and physical health, employment, and education outcomes for at-risk youth, families, and trafficking survivors. Reduced homelessness, recidivism, and crisis-system involvement. Measurement: Data collected through case notes, housing records, employment verification, counseling logs, and follow-up outcome tracking.

2293.description: Dredging and restoration of the Barnett Road Drainage Retention Area (DRA) to restore design capacity, reduce flooding risk, protect property, and improve surface water quality. The Barnett Road DRA serves a large residential area and has experienced significant sediment buildup and vegetation growth, reducing its stormwater storage and treatment capacity. Sediment removal will restore the basin’s function, reduce flooding during heavy rain events, and improve downstream water quality. The project is identified as a priority in the City’s Stormwater Capital Improvement Plan and supported by findings from the City’s ongoing Stormwater Master Plan, which documents reduced capacity and loss of functionality due to sediment accumulation.
2293.purpose: The goal of this project is to dredge and restore the Barnett Road Drainage Retention Area (DRA) to protect nearby neighborhoods from repeated flooding and stormwater overflow. Over the years, the basin has filled with sediment and vegetation, reducing its ability to hold and filter stormwater during heavy rains. By restoring this DRA, the City will improve neighborhood drainage, reduce flood risks for homes along Barnett Road, Woodland Drive, and Windy Way, and enhance public safety.
2293.activities: Funds will be used to dredge and restore the Barnett Road DRA by removing sediment and restoring vegetation. These activities will improve stormwater storage, reduce neighborhood flooding, and enhance overall drainage system performance.
2293.direct_services: Residents and businesses will benefit from reduced flooding risk, lower property damage, improved drainage reliability, and cleaner surface waters flowing into local creeks and wetlands.
2293.population: Economically disadvantaged residents in older neighborhoods, plus general population. Neighborhoods around the Drainage Retention Area (DRA) are low/moderate income. Flood protection benefits entire community.
2293.outcome: Protect the public from flooding by reducing roadway closures and property flooding near Barnett Road during heavy rainfall. Improve stormwater management by restoring the Barnett Road DRA’s original storage and treatment capacity. Success will be measured through post-dredge inspections and surveys verifying restored capacity, reduced flooding reports in Public Works logs, and improved surface water quality based on sampling at the DRA outfall.

2294.description: The City of Brooksville seeks state funding to enhance pedestrian safety and accessibility through the construction and repair of sidewalks, ADA-compliant crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and safety striping along key corridors near schools, residential neighborhoods, and downtown. Many sidewalks are deteriorated or missing entirely, forcing pedestrians to walk along roadways with limited visibility. This project will improve connectivity, reduce pedestrian accidents, and provide safe routes for residents and students, supporting the City’s goal of improving transportation safety and mobility for all users.
2294.purpose: To improve pedestrian safety and accessibility by constructing and repairing sidewalks, upgrading ADA-compliant crosswalks, and installing pedestrian signals along key routes near schools, neighborhoods, and downtown Brooksville. The project will enhance walkability, reduce pedestrian accidents, and provide safer routes for residents and students.
2294.activities: Funds will be used to design, construct, and repair sidewalks; upgrade ADA-compliant crosswalks; install pedestrian signals; and add safety striping and signage along key corridors to improve pedestrian accessibility and safety.
2294.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from improved safety, reduced pedestrian accidents, ADA accessibility for disabled residents, and better walk-ability connecting neighborhoods, schools, and businesses.
2294.population: Daily users, physically disabled, including schoolchildren and seniors. Safe routes to school, mobility/ADA accessibility/compliance.
2294.outcome: Increase pedestrian counts (average daily trips) by up to 25% along completed sidewalk corridors. Conduct pedestrian counts before and after construction using traffic counters or manual counts. Reduce pedestrian crash incidents by approximately 20% within targeted improvement areas. Monitor Florida DOT crash data (Signal Four Analytics database) annually, comparing three years before and after project completion. Construct or repair approximately 1–1.5 miles of sidewalks and 6–8 ADA-compliant crosswalks/signals. Post-construction as-built surveys will confirm completed improvements and locations.

2295.description: Since the brutal Hamas attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, the Tampa JCCs and Federation has faced a sharp rise in threats fueled by hate and antisemitism. Despite the partial release of hostages, the situation remains volatile, demanding continued vigilance. Furthermore, the FBI’s 2024 Hate Crime Report showed anti-Jewish hate crimes rose to 1,938 incidents—a 6% increase over 2023 and the highest number ever recorded. This marks the fourth year of our successful multi-year preventative security initiative, proven effective in protecting our community. Funding has enabled us to maintain armed security guards, support staff overseeing security operations, and provide educational programs that combat antisemitism and promote awareness. This initiative was designed to prevent and respond to potential threats against the Jewish community in the greater Tampa area. We are proud to report th
2295.purpose: This request represents Phase 3 of our local security initiative, which has been funded by the Florida Legislature for the past four years. Although the hostages have been released, the situation remains volatile and demands continued vigilance. The risks facing the greater Tampa Jewish community have grown significantly, compounded by the sharp rise in antisemitism repeatedly documented in FBI reports. Funding this project has enabled — and will continue to enable — the implementation of robust
2295.activities: Our facilities are open to the entire community, Jewish and non-Jewish, offering services such as after school care, summer camp, fitness facilities, a public art center, a business accelerator, an event center, a social services agency and more. We receive over 1,000 visitors per day on average and often much more than that on any given day. All persons using or visiting our JCC facilities will benefit from increased security and lives may very well be saved. The educational component will help
2295.direct_services: Visitors to the Shanna and Bryan Glazer JCC will experience a higher level of safety. This funding will allow us to be as prepared as possible to deal with life-threatening situations. We serve as first stop for security information throughout the community and a conduit to those with the greatest expertise.
2295.population: All users of and visitors to the Shanna and Bryan Glazer JCC will benefit from this increased security. More than 1,000 people visit the JCC every day and, on some days, that number exceeds 2,000 visitors. We estimate that greater than 300,000 people visit this JCC every year.
2295.outcome: We hope that we never have to demonstrate how prepared we are to deal with emergency situations, but chances are we will at some point. The expected benefit is that our preparedness will save lives and prevent any harm intended for our members, guests and staff. This will be an ongoing effort and, in light of the significant growth of antisemitism and anti-Zionism in our state, country and around the world and due to the war in Israel, there's no end in sight. We will also continue to provide educational programs for people of all faiths to help learn to identify and combat antisemitism.

1613.description: Justice Academy is a program to teach students ages 12-21 how to convert their energy into positive community action by learning in a practical manner how an ideas become law. At the end of a series of lessons directed at understanding the state legislative process, including committee and caucus meetings, the students will meet in a mock legislative session. Each team recruited for local high schools will be trained on proposing and promoting their ideas leading to the mock legislative session. The team most successful in passing bills will be declared winners with proposed internships awarded to participants with local legislators.
1613.purpose: We aim to teach students the process of how they can effect change in their communities that are alternatives to frustration or inaction. Youth often feel that the government is not within their control or understanding. With the actual hands on process of this program, we hope to demystify the legislative and governing process. We can instill a sense of empowerment through this program.
1613.activities: The program is designed to have different schools compete against each other in the successful passing of “legislation”. This will be accomplished by teaching the students of role of legislative causes and actually having students meet in caucuses. Students will also be assigned to “legislative committees," which will meet to study and vote on proposed student bills. Ultimately, the various schools/communities will meet at the Mock legislative session when all bills passed by various committees
1613.direct_services: This is a direct benefit to the students in the schools who participate in the process, all of whom would be citizens of the counties in which the schools is located.
1613.population: The program is designed so that the mentors will provide monthly reports as to the progress on the curriculum and the students under their supervision. These reports will gauge the effectiveness of the teacher and the capacity of the students to understand the material and the exercise. Additionally, the work product, that is the number and quality of the type of legislation, can be graded to gauge the understanding of issues raised during their caucus meetings. Finally, the number of bills prod
1613.outcome: The program is designed so that the mentors will provide monthly reports as to the progress on the curriculum and the students under their supervision. These reports will gauge the effectiveness of the teacher and the capacity of the students to understand the material and the exercise. Additionally, the work product, that is the number and quality of the type of legislation, can be graded to gauge the understanding of issues raised during their caucus meetings. Finally, the number of bills produced and ultimately passed by the student legislature can be graded to gauge the effectiveness of the team. The expected benefit is that we will develop students that are better prepared to lead their

2299.description: Tamps Theatre's work will encompass the full decorative restoration of the auditorium and modernizing the Theatre's technology, infrastructure, and new two-story education wing to position the Theatre for its next century of service.
2299.purpose: The goal is to complete the restoration and renovation work of the historic Tampa Theatre by the 100th anniversary of the Theatre's opening on October 15, 2026. This work encompasses a full decorative restoration of the auditorium, modernization of the Theatre's infrastructure, and creation of a new two-story education wing that transforms long- dormant spaces into modern educational facilities position to the Theatre for its next century of service.
2299.activities: This project will help Tampa Theatre serve our community by meeting the needs of modern film and entertainment technology and providing space and resources for educating the next generation of historians, filmmakers, and arts appreciators. Tampa Theatre provides artistic and educational programs for the greater Tampa Bay area in a significant historic landmark. The Theatre currently offers more than 1,000 events a year, and this project will allow the Theatre to expand its programs to include a
2299.direct_services: Tampa Theatre, a 1,238-seat former movie palace built in 1926, hosts new and classic film programs, concerts, and community special events. The Theatre's Summer Film Camp for children is the centerpiece of its education program that also includes field trips and life-long learning programs which will be greatly expanded with this capital project.
2299.population: Tampa Theatre opens its doors to every walk of life and does not have a specific target population. Our attendance last year was more than 125,000 patrons. We anticipate a dramatic increase in attendance and a more meaningful experiences with each patron.
2299.outcome: The benefits are two-fold: preserving one of Tampa's most important buildings and modernizing its infrastructure to meet the needs of the rapidly evolving film and media landscape as well as provide more programming to educate the next generation of historians, filmmakers, and arts appreciators.

1577.description: In 2013, the Florida Park Service took control and assumed management of Silver Springs, merging it with the adjacent Silver River State Park, forming Silver Springs State Park (SSSP). In 2014, the state's Unit Management Plan for SSSP included creating a public swimming area at the headsprings and the construction of a mooring/convenience dock downriver from the headsprings. In 2016, Wild Waters Waterpark was closed, and the infrastructure of the park was removed in 2019. Since the state gained ownership of the park almost a decade ago, a host of improvements have been discussed and planned; however, few have come to fruition as the projects, including reopening swimming at the springs, have been mired in bureaucratic processes. Marion County has coordinated with DEP and SSSP leadership in an effort to move the project forward. After consultation with stakeholders, the project designed
1577.purpose: The funds will be use for project construction to create a public swimming area at the headspring of Silver Springs.
1577.activities: The goal of this project is to return swimming to Silver Springs as instructed by the state in 2014.
1577.direct_services: Citizens once again will be able to swim in Silver Springs.
1577.population: General population, no specific group will benefit from funds.
1577.outcome: Returning swimming to Silver Springs adds an additional activity for park visitors to engage in, which could lead them to spend longer durations in the park. Further, reopening the springs for swimming will draw in visitors looking for a natural, aquatic experience. This will be validated by checking park attendance figures and surveys to check how long attendees are staying at the park.

1578.description: Through the requested appropriations funding, the Friends of Bradford-Ma Barker house will be able to finish the restoration and improvement projects associated with this historic preservation site. Currently, the site is not ADA accessible, is lacking certain structures to complete the historical accuracy, and is in need of an interpretive center exhibit.
1578.purpose: Through the requested appropriations funding the Marion County Board of County Commissioners will be able to finish the restoration and improvement projects associated with this historic preservation site. Currently, the site is not ADA accessible, is lacking certain structures to complete the historical accuracy, and is in need of an interpretive center exhibit.
1578.activities: Construction of the interpretive center will provide static and video instruction, displays, artifacts, and other items needed to enhance the interpretation of the exhibit. Completion of the improvement projects will ensure that visitors have a comfortable experience while visiting the site.
1578.direct_services: The facility will provide self-guided and docent tours that focus on the story of the property and its profound impact on the FBI's history.
1578.population: The majority of funds will not benefit a specific group but is intended to benefit all visitors to the site and Marion County. Currently, operating in a private tour-only capacity, the site sees just shy of 5,000 visitors a year, with the expectation the amount will grow exponentially once the updates are complete.
1578.outcome: Increased visitors resulting in increased economic activity, increased heritage tourism opportunities for visitors to Florida/Marion County, increased knowledge of America during the Roaring '20s and Early Depression Era as it relates to certain sub-cultural practices, political and social influences, inform visitors on the precursor to America's FBI and its work fighting organized crime during the 1920s and Depression Eras. The construction project itself will employ professionals (architects, engineers), tradesmen (contractors, sub-contractors), and the positions that support them (clerical, management). The ongoing operation of the site will result in future paid employment opportunities.

2764.description: Samaritan Village's (SVI) Transitional Safehouse Program holistic and long-term healing to human trafficking survivors in Central Florida. This innovative program provides up to 3-5 years of support at 3 locations in Orlando. The program's multi-tiered, holistic, and trauma-informed care is survivor-centered and includes safe housing, therapy, clinical services, substance recovery, and independent living skill development focused on safe community reentry. This program will continue SVI's mental health services, including access to a full-time therapist with specialization in trafficking and complex trauma.
2764.purpose: Samaritan Village’s Transitional Safehouse Program's goal is to provide safe housing and restorative care for up to 15 adult female survivors of human trafficking at 3 locations in Orlando. FL. These mental health services will meet the survivors’ unique mental and emotional health needs, ensuring seamless and integrated care that enhances the program’s effectiveness.
2764.activities: Samaritan Village’s Transitional Safehouse Program will expand its mental health services to include additional access to licensed mental health support, ongoing professional development for clinical staff, and the continuation of clinical and recovery services that empower survivors to heal from trauma, take back their lives, and become catalysts for change in their communities.
2764.direct_services: Direct services will include access to a full-time therapist(s) with specialization in trafficking and complex trauma, supervised intern positions which will facilitate more timely assessments and continuity of care, ongoing professional development for clinical staff, safe housing, clinical services such as medical and dental care, case management, independent living skills, substance recovery, s
2764.population: Samaritan Village (SVI) serves up to 15 survivors of human trafficking in Central Florida, primarily females ages 18 to 44, between 3 safehouses in Orlando. In 2023, the Statewide Council on Human Trafficking reported 25 long-term beds available for survivors in Central Florida —SVI provides 15 of those beds. SVI’s structured and trauma-informed services align with the Governor’s legislation and the Statewide Council on Human Trafficking’s recommendations to combat human trafficking.
2764.outcome: Samaritan Village’s (SVI) Transitional Safehouse Program’s outcome is to provide a safe place for human trafficking survivors to heal from trauma, recover from addiction, and take back their lives. SVI evaluates program effectiveness through assessments, inquiries, observations, case note reviews, and surveys from participants, staff, and volunteers. The Clinical Director and other staff collaborate and use the Apricot Case Management system and RTI International’s OHTS tool to track survivors' progress.

1744.description: The City of New Port Richey plans to replace and enlarge an old water line and install sewer lines to replace private septic tanks in the Town and Country Villas neighborhood, a 185-lot area prone to repetitive flooding due to its low elevation in a flood zone. This project aims to improve infrastructure resilience against storms and rising sea levels, enhance water quality, and reduce public health and environmental risks. Currently, flooding causes septic tanks to overflow, contaminating groundwater and posing health hazards, especially in this low-income community where septic maintenance is often unaffordable. Septic tanks are major sources of groundwater pollution, spreading harmful pathogens. By replacing septic tanks with sewer lines and upgrading water infrastructure, the project will reduce contamination risks and improve overall community health and safety as environmental thre
1744.purpose: The project aims to replace and enlarge an old potable water line and install sewer lines to replace septic tanks in the Town and Country Villas neighborhood. This will improve infrastructure resilience against storms and rising sea levels, enhance water quality, and reduce public health risks from sewage contamination. It also supports better stormwater management and addresses health hazards in this low-income, flood-prone community. Additionally, the project aligns with zoning changes promoti
1744.activities: The project involves upgrading the potable water main to improve supply and reliability, replacing private septic tanks with new sanitary sewer lines to reduce groundwater contamination and health risks, and enhancing stormwater management to prevent flooding. These improvements will support community health, environmental quality, and align with zoning changes encouraging safer, elevated housing.
1744.direct_services: Residents will benefit from a safer, more reliable water supply via the upgraded water main and access to a new sanitary sewer system, eliminating private septic tanks and reducing sewage-related health risks. Improved stormwater management will decrease neighborhood flooding, protecting homes and property. These services collectively enhance public health, environmental safety, and community resi
1744.population: The target population is the residents of the Town and Country Villas neighborhood, a 185-lot subdivision primarily occupied by low-income households. This community is especially vulnerable due to its location in a flood-prone area below the base elevation, facing repetitive flooding, septic tank failures, and related health risks. The project aims to serve these residents by improving their water and sewer infrastructure, reducing environmental contamination, and enhancing overall public healt
1744.outcome: The project will improve public health and safety by replacing septic tanks with a reliable sewer system, reducing groundwater contamination and health risks. The upgraded water line will ensure a dependable supply, while enhanced stormwater management will boost resilience to flooding and rising sea levels, protecting homes and property. Overall, it will create a healthier, safer, and more resilient community with better infrastructure and environmental conditions.

2616.description: Kids Bridge Family Visitation Center has served St. Johns and surrounding counties since 2002, providing trauma- informed supervised visitation and family support to more than 2,000 children and families in crisis. Kids Bridge offers a safe, stable environment where children can maintain healthy relationships with their parents during times of separation, instability, or court involvement. The facility now faces urgent structural needs that threaten its ability to operate safely. The Enrichment Center roof is failing, interior damage is worsening, and the emergency stairway, handicap-access ramp, and sections of the Main House require immediate repair or replacement. Requested funds will replace the failing roof, repair interior damage, and restore critical safety and accessibility structures, ensuring Kids Bridge remains a secure, functional, and healing environment for vulnerable child
2616.purpose: The requested funds will be used to complete essential safety and structural repairs at the Kids Bridge Family Visitation Center. These repairs—including roof replacement, interior ceiling restoration, emergency stairwell and handicap ramp repairs, and replacement of rotten exterior wood—will protect the integrity of the building, prevent further deterioration, and maintain full accessibility for families. Ultimately, this investment ensures Kids Bridge can continue providing court-ordered super
2616.activities: The requested funds will help Kids Bridge Family Visitation Center maintain uninterrupted trauma-informed services by ensuring the facility’s safety and structural integrity. After repairs, Kids Bridge will continue offering supervised visitation and monitored exchanges in a safe, neutral, child-centered setting for families facing domestic violence, high-conflict custody issues, or child welfare involvement; trauma-informed enrichment that builds emotional regulation, resilience, healthy commun
2616.direct_services: The requested appropriation will allow Kids Bridge Family Visitation Center to continue delivering essential trauma- informed services to children and families in crisis across St. Johns County and nearby areas. Services include supervised visitation and monitored exchanges for families impacted by domestic violence, substance abuse, child welfare cases, or high-conflict custody; trauma-informed e
2616.population: The project serves children and families in crisis, including those affected by domestic violence, child abuse or neglect, parental substance abuse, high-conflict custody cases, and court-ordered supervised visitation. Kids Bridge also supports non-offending parents, caregivers, guardians, and individuals in the Batterers Intervention Program working toward accountability and safer relationships. Since 2002, Kids Bridge has served over 2,000 families and now supports 150–200 families each year a
2616.outcome: Expected Benefits / Outcomes: Facility repairs will ensure Kids Bridge Family Visitation Center remains safe, accessible, and fully functional for children and families in crisis. Expected outcomes include improved safety and stability for children in supervised visitation and enrichment programs; healthier parent-child relationships with reduced trauma exposure; increased accountability and community safety through the Batterers Intervention Program; and sustained access to trauma- informed services and supports for over 100 families annually. Methodology: Outcomes will be achieved through targeted repairs to the roof, ceilings, emergency stairwell, handicap-access ramp, and deteriorated ex

1468.description: To remove accessibility barriers and upgrade City-owned facilities to meet current ADA accessibility standards, including compliant ramps, doors, walkways, elevators, and restroom facilities. The project improves accessibility across multiple municipal buildings, parks, and public rights-of-way consistent with the City’s ADA Transition Plan and Title II requirements.
1468.purpose: To remove accessibility barriers and upgrade City-owned facilities to meet current ADA accessibility standards, including compliant ramps, doors, walkways, elevators, and restroom facilities. The project improves accessibility across multiple municipal buildings, parks, and public rights-of-way consistent with the City’s ADA Transition Plan and Title II requirements.
1468.activities: Directly benefits residents, visitors, and employees accessing City facilities and public spaces.
1468.direct_services: Directly benefits residents, visitors, and employees accessing City facilities and public spaces.
1468.population: Target Populations: Physically disabled, Elderly persons, General public. Estimated to serve >10,000 individuals annually through improved access to civic facilities, parks, and pedestrian routes.400 maximum characters allowed.
1468.outcome: Expected benefit includes: (1) improved transportation conditions through remediated sidewalks, curb cuts, and other accessibility improvements planned to improve pedestrian traffic conditions by removing barriers; (2) increased economic activity through improved access supports local economic drivers — parks, cultural venues, and commercial corridors — by providing more options for visitors and residents with limited mobility; (3) and improved quality of life for residents and visitors by ensuring barrier-free access to civic, cultural, and recreational amenities. The methodology to measure the outcomes will include: (1) the City's Click2Fix reporting system for residents to report accessib

1591.description: The request is for assistance with upgrades for the Sanford Civic Center. This mid-century modern building is used for private and public events. Built in 1958, the Civic Center was initially called the "most modern structure of its kind in the country". The Civic Center is one of the 50 flagship structures featured in Florida’s Mid-Century Modern Architecture by the UF School of Architecture. Funds will be used to replace or upgrade electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems.
1591.purpose: The request is for assistance with upgrades for the Sanford Civic Center. This mid-century modern building is used for private and public events. Built in 1958, the Civic Center was initially called the "most modern structure of its kind in the country". The Civic Center is one of the 50 flagship structures featured in Florida’s Mid-Century Modern Architecture by the UF School of Architecture. Funds will be used to replace or upgrade electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems
1591.activities: The Civic Center hosts many small to medium events of up to 500 attendees for local non-profit organizations, businesses, and individuals. Build in 1958, it continues to be the primary event space in Sanford and hosts banquets, public meetings, cat shows, coin shows, back-to-school events, food giveaways, and private events.
1591.direct_services: Upgrades will allow the City to continue to provide a quality, safe, affordable venue and keep an historic building in active use.
1591.population: The target population is the citizens of Sanford, surrounding communities and Seminole County.
1591.outcome: The project will allow the city to continue to provide a safe and affordable venue for our citizens. The methodology of benefit will be measured by the attendance figures for both public and private events.

1643.description: The proposed 2,000 sq ft expansion of our Senior Center aims to enhance services over 260 registered seniors, many living in underserved communities. Currently at full capacity, the center limits access to essential fitness, wellness, and enrichment programs. The new space will allow for health and wellness classes, arts and hobby programs, and educational workshops without scheduling conflicts. This project creates a safer, more accessible, and efficient environment for older adults' physical, mental, and social well-being aligning with state goals to promote independence, reduce isolation, and enhance quality of life.
1643.purpose: The requested funds will be used to expand and enhance the Senior Center’s capacity to deliver high-quality programs that promote health, wellness, and social engagement for older adults. The goal is to increase program participation by at least 25% within the first year of completion. As a result, the center will operate more efficiently, serve more participants, and achieve measurable improvements in seniors’ physical health, mental well-being, and quality of life.
1643.activities: The expanded Senior Care will provide a broader range of activities and services designed to improve the health, independence, and overall well-being of older adults. Programs will include enhanced fitness and wellness classes such as Chair Yoga and Zumba. Educational and enrichment services will also be expanded to include computer literacy training, gardening programs, and monthly lectures focused on healthy living, and safety.
1643.direct_services: The funds will allow the Senior Center to provide direct, in-person services that enhance the daily lives of older adults in the community. These services will include expanded health and wellness programs and educational enrichment, such as fitness classes, fall-prevention activities, and routine health screenings; nutritional support and education, promoting healthy eating and disease prevention
1643.population: The target population for this project is older adults aged 55 and above, primarily those living at or below the poverty level and on fixed incomes within the local community. Currently, the center serves approximately 260 registered members, with average daily attendance of 80–85 seniors and up to 120 participants during special events. Upon completion of the 2,000-sq-ft expansion, the center expects to increase its service capacity by at least 25%, allowing it to accommodate over 325 registere
1643.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is an overall improvement in the health, well-being, and quality of life of older adults through expanded access to fitness, wellness, educational, and social programs. The project will result in increased participation in center activities, greater program efficiency, and enhanced community engagement. Seniors will benefit from improved physical health, reduced social isolation, and stronger mental wellness through consistent, accessible programming in a safe and welcoming environment.

1641.description: Vocational and educational programming in corrections utilizing virtual reality technology to improve literacy, workforce preparation, and the attainment of CTE credentials.
1641.purpose: Workforce readiness of FDC inmates with guided effort to prepare them for quality careers in high demand fields that are essential to Florida's economic growth and need. This will include both CTE curriculums as well as literacy and academic progress, with focus on attaining high school diplomas, as opposed to a GED, for those that lack them currently as this can increase their earning potential post release by up to 50%.
1641.activities: As proved in previous pilots with FDC, students will engage in learning through virtual reality headsets in career oriented curriculums that allow them to attain nationally recognized credentials in high demand skilled labor fields. Virtual Reality CTE coursework will vary from construction fields to emerging technology and CDL programming. Adult phonics and Ability to Benefit programming ensures these students have access to Pell funding (Workforce Pell will be implemented in 2026 after passage
1641.population: 500 individuals who are currently incarcerated by the Florida Department of Corrections will participate in the program.
1641.outcome: As in prior pilots conducted by FDC with Promising People, the number of nationally recognized career credentials attained will be measured as well as high school diplomas earned for those that lack them. The combination of a high school diploma and these nationally recognized career certifications will enable these individuals to find employment post release and therefore reduce the likelihood of them recidivating reducing the burden of the state to have to incarcerate them in the future. Florida's economy currently badly needs the type of workforce this program will create.

2096.description: The purpose of the requested funds is to provide a secure shelter for local residents and their pets and visitors at the marina and campground during storm and hurricane activities. Given that the City of Pahokee has direct access to Lake Okeechobee, this proposed hardening will create the city's only hurricane-proof shelter, ensuring safety and protection for the community in times of crisis.
2096.purpose: The purpose of the requested funds is to provide a secure shelter for local residents and their pets and visitors at the marina and campground during storm and hurricane activities. Given that the City of Pahokee has direct access to Lake Okeechobee, this proposed hardening will create the city's only hurricane-proof shelter, ensuring safety and protection for the community in times of crisis.
2096.activities: The activities and services provided will be create a hurricane-proof shelter for local residents and their pets by hardening the gymnasium with new windows, doors, security cameras, etc.
2096.direct_services: The direct services provided will be the safety and protection of families and their pets during a natural disaster.
2096.population: The target population are all residents within the City of Pahokee.
2096.outcome: The expected benefit is to protect the general public by providing shelter during storm/hurricane for those in need of a safe place to reside if there is a need to evacuate substandard housing. It will also serve as a safe place for the homeless and other vulnerable populations during times of need for safe sheltering. This will be measured by the number of people utilizing the facility during times of evacuations.

1679.description: Funds will improve stormwater infrastructure in Hallandale Beach's Northeast Quadrant, enhancing resilience and safety in response to frequent flooding. The project secures critical evacuation routes, reduces roadway LOS deficiencies, and supports economic stability. Aligned with Florida's resilience goals, it strengthens public safety, promotes sustainable urban water management, and reduces the number of repetitive flood-loss properties in Hallandale Beach. The project will increase the capacity of two (2) stormwater pump stations, each with a wet well, valve vault, injection wells and associated cabinets and controls.
1679.purpose: The funds requested will enhance stormwater infrastructure in Hallandale Beach's Northeast Quadrant, aiming to improve flood resilience and safety in areas frequently impacted by flooding. The project will secure critical evacuation routes, reduce roadway LOS deficiencies, and support economic stability. It aligns with Florida's resilience objectives by strengthening public safety, promoting sustainable urban water management, and protecting the community against severe weather and escalating en
1679.activities: The activities funded will include comprehensive stormwater management services aimed at reducing flood risks and protecting key assets such as residential structures, roads, and evacuation routes from potential flood damage. These services will involve infrastructure improvements, enhanced runoff management, and system modernization to ensure the City's resilience against flooding and long-term environmental challenges.
1679.direct_services: The project area has the highest concentration of repetitive flood loss properties in the city (FEMA NFIP Repetitive Loss Database). 2670.description: Comprehensive academic tutoring across all core subjects, individualized mentoring to improve behavior and attendance, college and career readiness programs including SAT/ACT prep and financial aid guidance, and cultural enrichment activities that foster creativity, confidence, and community engagement among participating youth.
2670.purpose: The requested funds will expand and enhance academic support, career readiness for at-risk youth in Florida’s most underserved communities. The program aims to increase high school graduation rates, improve academic performance, and boost college enrollment through targeted tutoring, behavior and attendance interventions, and mentorship. By equipping youth with essential skills and resources, the initiative fosters long-term economic mobility and community transformation.
2670.activities: The program will provide targeted academic tutoring in core subjects to improve student performance, along with behavior and attendance monitoring to ensure consistent engagement. College and career readiness services will include mentorship, SAT/ACT preparation, financial aid guidance, and career exploration workshops. Additional services will include access to study materials, leadership development activities, and support networks to enhance long-term success.
2670.direct_services: The appropriation will provide direct services to at-risk youth, including academic tutoring, behavior and attendance monitoring, college and career preparation, and youth employment opportunities. Students will receive targeted support in core subjects, SAT/ACT prep, mentorship, and financial aid guidance to improve graduation and college enrollment rates.
2670.population: The project serves at-risk youth, economically disadvantaged individuals, jobless persons, those with poor mental or physical health, homeless individuals, and juvenile offenders. It specifically targets high-risk communities where youth are most vulnerable to crime and poverty. The initiative is expected to serve between 201 and 400 individuals annually, providing them with the resources and opportunities needed to achieve long-term success.
2670.outcome: The project will improve academic performance, graduation rates, college enrollment, and youth employment opportunities in underserved communities. Success will be measured through reading levels, attendance records, graduation rates, ACT/SAT scores, and college acceptance rates. Employment outcomes will be tracked using participant surveys, pre/post-program and assessments to evaluate skill development. Quarterly reviews will ensure accountability and continuous improvement.

1408.description: The Statewide Teacher Retention & Selective Teacher Talent Placement targets top-tier educators, former military personnel, and nontraditional candidates to become highly effective teachers in Florida. For more than 20 years, this program has strengthened the teacher workforce, developed future school leaders, and delivered tailored, school- specific professional development in collaboration with principals. In alignment with the state's streamlined teacher training initiatives, we provide ongoing support to school administrators, instructional coaches, and teachers throughout the year while simultaneously recruiting highly selective candidates to commit to teaching in Florida's schools.
1408.purpose: The requested funds will expand the Statewide Teacher Retention & Selective Teacher Talent Placement initiative to increase the number of well-prepared, high-performing teachers in Florida's classrooms. Funding will enhance recruitment, training, and year-round professional support for current & aspiring teachers, ensuring schools especially those in high-need and rural areas have access to skilled educators who improve student learning and strengthen the long-term teacher pipeline.
1408.activities: Activities and services will include recruiting and selecting top-tier college students, former military members, and nontraditional candidates to serve in Florida schools; providing pre-service and ongoing training focused on effective instruction and classroom management; offering school-based coaching and mentorship throughout the year; and partnering with principals to deliver customized professional development that supports teacher growth, retention, and student achievement.
1408.direct_services: The appropriation will provide direct services to Florida students and schools through high-quality instruction and teacher support. College students, former military members, and new educators will receive hands-on training and coaching to deliver effective teaching in K12 classrooms. Students will benefit from improved instruction, smaller learning groups, and higher academic achievement, while
1408.population: The target population includes K12 students attending Florida's high-need and rural schools, along with novice and aspiring teachers participating in the training and support program. The project is expected to directly serve over 2,000 teacher trainees and impact more than 13,000 students statewide through improved instruction, targeted tutoring, and enhanced classroom support.
1408.outcome: The project will increase student achievement in reading and math and strengthen Florida's teacher pipeline by preparing and retaining effective educators in high-need schools year round. Outcomes will be measured through student progress monitoring and state assessment data to track academic growth, teacher retention and placement data to assess workforce impact, and participant surveys evaluating preparedness, classroom effectiveness, and intent to remain in the teaching profession.

3107.description: This request is for the funding necessary to conduct a PD&E study for the development of an agriculture center on the campus of Deane Bozeman School. The proposed building would include 6 classrooms set up for agriculture classes, a conference room, a lab with kennels, examination area, scales and washdown area, and a shop for housing welding and agriculture mechanics. Directly adjacent to the building we propose a large animal barn and a covered 150x150 arena with seating, for animal training and to host shows/events. The addition of these facilities would further enhance the educational opportunities available to students enrolled in this nationally recognized program. Additionally, this site could assist with our disaster sheltering requirements to support the community in times of need as Deane Bozeman School is our only animal-approved shelter in Bay County. Currently, animals are s
3107.purpose: The purpose is to conduct a PD&E study to develop an FFA facility extending CTE options within Bay County in the field of agriculture, animal husbandry, business and medicine
3107.activities: Enhance K-12 education opportunities for a rural part of the county. Additional services supporting shelter operations of evacuees with pets
3107.direct_services: PD&E study of facilities providing K-12 citizens enhanced FFA opportunities and CTE training in agriculture, animal husbandry, agribusiness and medicine. Additionally, Deane Bozeman School in Bay County's primary shelter facility during evacuation.
3107.population: The PD&E study will design a K-12 facility for over 300 FFA students; and shelter for pets of approximately 800 hurricane evacuees.
3107.outcome: The PD&E study will set the foundation for a facility increasing K-12 CTE and FFA opportunities. The Bay District School enrollment FTE will certify increased enrollment.

1415.description: This funding request would establish a robotics surgery program within Nicklaus Children’s Heart Institute to advance pediatric and congenital cardiac care. Robotic-assisted surgery has revolutionized cardiac care through greater precision, smaller incisions, and faster recovery. Florida's pediatric and congenital heart disease patients stand to benefit significantly from this technology.
1415.purpose: Enable the Nicklaus Children's Heart Institute's surgeons to conduct technologically enhanced surgeries.
1415.activities: Purchase and installation of a robotic surgical system.
1415.direct_services: Precise, less-invasive cardiac surgeries accessible to newborns, infants, children, and young adults. Also, education and training on cutting-edge technology for physicians, nurses, fellows, and residents.
1415.population: Pediatric and congenital heart disease patients. The surgical system should aide the surgical team for years to come, so numerous patients, families, and health care professionals will be served by it.
1415.outcome: That surgeons are able to perform more precise and less invasive heart surgeries. To measure the efficacy of the program, the State could compare the following prior to and after implementation of the program: 1) precision and size of incisions and 2) recovery time.

2956.description: This initiative expands access to dental and behavioral healthcare statewide through Florida’s network of free and charitable clinics. Funds will support workforce development, purchase of equipment and supplies, clinic infrastructure improvements, operational support, and outreach to underserved populations. The goal is to improve oral and mental health outcomes, reduce reliance on emergency rooms, and close critical care gaps for uninsured Floridians.
2956.purpose: To expand access to essential dental and behavioral healthcare for underserved Floridians by strengthening clinic capacity, improving infrastructure, and supporting culturally appropriate, evidence-based services.
2956.activities: Hire licensed providers and support volunteers, purchase equipment/supplies, cover labs and prescriptions, expand behavioral health counseling, and implement targeted outreach programs.
2956.direct_services: Comprehensive dental care (cleanings, fillings, dentures, extractions) and behavioral health services (counseling, coordination, prescriptions).
2956.population: Elderly, economically disadvantaged, uninsured/working poor, persons with poor physical/mental health, homeless, disabled, students (preschool–college), at-risk youth, incarcerated/reentry populations, drug users/offenders, victims of crime, and general underserved Floridians. Estimated 800+ served statewide.
2956.outcome: Improve physical health: More dental patients served, reduced wait times, fewer preventable ER visits. Improve mental health: Increased counseling sessions and prescriptions, greater stability for patients with chronic conditions, reduced behavioral health ER use. Methodology: Quarterly reporting from clinics capturing patient volume, procedures performed, service delivery, ER diversion data, and ROI analysis.

2620.description: U.S. Census data shows a 76% population increase in St. Johns County since 2010, creating rapid business growth and a rising need for workforce development. By 2031, 72% of U.S. jobs are expected to require postsecondary education or training. The requested funds will support the second year of operations for Goodwill of North Florida’s A-STEP program and GoodCareers Center in Epic Village, St. Augustine. Although the county is expanding, 66% of its workforce remains employed outside the area. The GoodCareers Center addresses this gap by offering no-cost job leads, career counseling, skill-building workshops, and access to on-site interviews and computers for résumé preparation and job searches. Through A-STEP, an Education Navigator helps participants complete education and training certifications, creating pathways to meaningful, sustainable employment.
2620.purpose: The request seeks continued funding for the North Florida GoodCareers Center in Epic Village, St. Augustine. Since opening on August 22, 2025, the center has served 352 individuals with resume building, job searches, and placements, and five students have begun their A-STEP (Academic Support Through the Employment Process) journey. Continued funding will sustain these essential career and education services for the community.
2620.activities: The GoodCareers Center offers free job leads, career counseling, and skill-building workshops to local residents seeking employment. The center provides access to on-site job interviews and computers for resume writing and job searches. In addition, a Goodwill A-STEP education navigator will support participants as they pursue their educational goals and complete career training certifications.
2620.direct_services: Direct career services include career counseling, job search workshops and on-site job interviews. Through Goodwill's A-STEP program, the education navigator assists with enrollment, financial aid, and course selection, while helping participants overcome barriers like childcare, transportation, and textbook costs.
2620.outcome: Equipping residents with the tools they need to secure employment will strengthen economic activity across St. Johns County. By expanding access to education and workforce services, the county can become a community where people want to live and work—and where businesses want to invest and grow. Program outcomes, including job placements and increases in participants’ earning potential, will be tracked and measured.

2301.description: Request $2,000,000 to upgrade and modernize water meters of approximately 15,000 residents throughout the County with new advanced metering infrastructure that provides real-time usage data, improved billing accuracy, reduce meter reading costs, and enhance outage and low-leak detection capability.
2301.purpose: Request $2,000,000 to upgrade and modernize water meters for approximately 15,000 residents throughout the County with new advanced metering infrastructure that provides real-time usage data, improved billing accuracy, reduce meter reading costs, and enhance outage and low-leak detection capability.
2301.activities: New advanced metering infrastructure that provides real-time usage data, improved billing accuracy, reduce meter reading costs, and enhance outage and low-leak detection capability. A strategic initiative for Hillsborough County is focused on water conservation and improved operational efficiencies.
2301.direct_services: Providing more information to residents regarding their actual usage; this new advanced metering infrastructure aims to improve billing accuracy and help residents make smarter choices with their water usage.
2301.population: Upgrade and modernize water meters of approximately 15,000 residents throughout the County
2301.outcome: Decrease in water consumption, decrease in overuse, increase in compliance with regulations, increased efficiency in addressing unknown leaks at residential properties. Implementation of smart metering dashboard and analytics that will provide more accurate information to consumers regarding their household water consumption; viewing a household's water bill prior to installation of smart meter versus after.

2302.description: Request $675,000 to establish a Hillsborough County Fire Rescue Fallen Firefighter Memorial to honor those who have died in the line of duty over the last 50 years.
2302.purpose: Request $675,000 to establish a Hillsborough County Fire Rescue Fallen Firefighter Memorial to honor those who have died in the line of duty over the last 50 years.
2302.activities: HCFR desires to construct a memorial to honor fallen firefighters who died in the line of duty over the course of the past 50+ years.
2302.direct_services: This memorial will pay tribute to the sacrifice these individuals made to the community. There is presently no formal recognition or memorial of their service.
2302.population: Hillsborough County residents will be directly served by investments in emergency response and recovery
2302.outcome: HCFR desires to construct a memorial to honor fallen firefighters who died in the line of duty over the course of the past 50+ years. This memorial will pay tribute to the sacrifice these individuals made to the community. There is presently no formal recognition or memorial of their service. This is an opportunity for citizens and students to learn about community firefighter heroes. Memorial attendance, surveys, and overall community betterment.

Graduates of this program are equipped with industry-recognized certifications and hands-on experience, making them immediately valuable additions to a Florida based workforce; specifically, for flood mitigation resilience and adaptation solutions targeting structural elevation and dry and wet floodproofing.
2495.purpose: The Flood Mitigation Industry Association (FMIA), a 501c3, represents the flood mitigation industry. The FMIA has designed a comprehensive, certified training program, aimed at placing people into good jobs that advance coastal/inland resilience and adaptation; assist communities to adapting to increased flooding events; assist employers in developing a 21st-century workforce, equipped with a series of certifications to include: OSHA 30, NCCER Core, CPR, Skid loader and Rigging (United Rentals),
2495.activities: The CREST FMIA team will bring a pre-designed 6-week comprehensive curriculum package to the Tampa Bay region; with the goal of training a highly skilled workforce a combination of skills (listed above); targeting low-income community members; to be hired into good paying positions in high demand structural elevation and dry and wet floodproofing sectors. Subject Matter Experts (SME's) from various parts of the industry will be brought into the Tampa Bay region to teach these highly specialized
2495.direct_services: The direct services that will benefit the citizens will be: 1) a trained flood mitigation and adaptation workforce that will help with employer needs to full in-demand, 21st century jobs in the Tampa Bay region 2) an increase in related job hires from a trained workforce which will drive economic growth 3) economic infusion from the various local systems the training program will hire/rent/engage
2495.population: CREST FMIA seeks to recruit trainees from Florida's: Financially Disadvantaged Community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.); Financially Disadvantaged Municipality (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.); and areas of Economic Concern. Collaboration with multiple local Community Based Organizations (CBOs) will also assist in trainee recruitment. Target participants will include: persons benefiting from programs such as SNAP, WIC, TANF; communities that are income challenged; women, disconnected youth, members of religious minor
2495.outcome: The CREST FMIA program will offer a variety of benefits to the Tampa Bay region to include; an increase in resilience and adaptation to extreme flood events with reduced recovery time; creation of sustainable, in-demand, 21st century jobs that drive overall revenue base (employers, and employees); reduction of recovery time after flood events with an eye on economic development and sustaining tourism; securing asset valuation for homes/buildings; reduction of insurance costs. We will use a data management system called Apprenticescope to quantify some of the following: wage/wage growth/employer engagement/number of hired workers; wraparound services engaged with and associated financial in-k

Bradenton has a long history with MLB and this partnership, along with partnerships with the Housing Authority, Manatee School Board, Police Athletic League and Manatee County, will create a world class facility. The park will provide space for sports events, festivals, local markets, playground and other local activities with buildings for restrooms and concessions.
1762.purpose: The purpose of this project is to create a recreation complex for the benefit and enjoyment of residents and visitors to the City of Bradenton. Bradenton has a long history with MLB and this partnership, along with partnerships with the Housing Authority, Manatee School Board, Police Athletic League and Manatee County, will create a world class facility. The park will provide space for sports events, festivals, local markets, playground and other local activities with buildings for restrooms and
1762.activities: Bradenton City Park will offer local baseball teams with the fields needed for practice and competition. It will also include playground, restrooms and concession areas that will allow other community activities. The inclusion of a Police Athletic League Center will compliment the elementary school within the limits of the project to provide a wide range of services.
1762.direct_services: Sports activities, recreation, park and green areas, community center.
1762.population: The target population is the under served community surrounding the area where the park is located. The area and community also includes an elementary school and a proposed Police Athletic League Community Center. Both children and young adults at risk will benefit from the positive impact this project will provide.

These opportunities are currently not available in the scale the park will provide to the residents of the city. The engagement of the general population in the type of activities that the park will provide will be evidence of the positive impact this project will have to the residents and visitors to the City of Bradenton.

1863.description: The Bradenton Fire Department seeks $187,500 in state appropriations to replace outdated fire station alerting systems. The current systems are beyond end of life. The funds would be to replace the current outdated systems at two fire stations with station alerting systems that meet the health and safety industry standards (heart health tones, lighting, etc.).
1863.purpose: The Bradenton Fire Department seeks $187,500 in state appropriations to replace outdated fire station alerting systems. The current systems are beyond end of life. The funds would be to replace the current outdated systems at two fire stations with station alerting systems that meet the health and safety industry standards (heart health tones, lighting, etc.).
1863.activities: Implementation and integration of new technology which requires service from Manatee County Radio Division, Manatee County ECC, City of Bradenton IT, and the station alerting vendor. The current system will be decommissioned after install of the new systems.
1863.direct_services: This project directly benefits citizens by ensuring that firefighters have a reliable and timely dispatch notification system to better enhance emergency response times.
1863.population: All 72 City of Bradenton Fire Department shift firefighters and all those within the city limits (2020 US Census population of 55,698 with more than one million city visitors annually).
1863.outcome: Firefighter safety, operational efficiency, and compliance with national safety standards will be achieved. Simultaneous dispatching with Manatee County EMS will be feasible. The firefighters will have a reliable and timely dispatch notification system to better enhance emergency response times.

1982.description: The proposed AI and Machine Learning Laboratory will assist the Strategic Investigations Division and multiple inner agency task forces to better anticipate and counter new threats to public safety in Broward County. It will focus on the latest advancements in AI and ML technologies for statistical investigations, field investigations, threat detection, and developing algorithms. This new technology will allow the Sheriff's Office to collaborate with their law enforcement partners to deploy Investigative techniques to identify and prevent a broad arena of public safety threats, including narcotics, money laundering, terrorism, internet crimes against children, human trafficking, internet financial fraud, and gang activities locally and statewide.
1982.purpose: The Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Laboratory will assist the Strategic Investigations Division, Real Time Crime Center and multiple task forces to better anticipate and counter new threats to public safety in Broward County. The lab will focus on the latest advancements in AI and ML technologies to enhance statistical investigative techniques, field investigations, threat detection through the development, testing and use of algorithms and machine learning models.
1982.activities: The most advanced investigative techniques will be utilized to identify and prevent a broad arena of public safety threats including narcotics, money laundering, terrorism, internet crimes against children, human trafficking, internet financial fraud, and gang activities.
1982.direct_services: Enhanced public safety through successful interventions/arrests.
1982.population: The almost 2 million residents and estimated 14 million visitors to Broward County.
1982.outcome: Number of successful interventions/arrests across a wide variety of criminal investigations enhanced by statistical investigative techniques, environmental mapping and threat detection made possible by the use of algorithms and machine learning models.

1689.description: CentsBuilders equips Middle & High School students, who are new to earning income, with financial literacy and digital skills to build lifelong habits, foster generational wealth, and boost career readiness. The program’s coaching, curriculum, and community engagement support economic mobility and reduce risks like eviction and dropout.
1689.purpose: The requested funds will equip Palm Beach County youth (ages 13–18) from low- to moderate-income households with essential financial literacy and digital skills. Through CentsBuilders, participants will receive hands-on training in budgeting, saving, credit, banking, mobile banking, online safety, financial technology, entrepreneurship, resume preparation, and investing. The program’s goal is to foster long-term financial stability, career readiness, and generational wealth, with a special focus
1689.activities: CentsBuilders equips Middle & High School students, who are new to earning income, with financial literacy and digital skills to build lifelong habits, foster generational wealth, and boost career readiness. The program’s coaching, curriculum, and community engagement support economic mobility and reduce risks like eviction and dropout.
1689.direct_services: The funding will provide Middle & High-School youth with financial literacy and digital skills training, including budgeting, saving, credit-building, banking, mobile banking, online safety, financial technology, entrepreneurship, resume preparation, and investing. Services include coaching, guest speakers, and access to the IBM SkillsBuild learning platform.
1689.population: Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, Grade school students, and High school students will be served. Approximately 100-200 youth are expected to be served.
1689.outcome: CentsBuilders will increase or improve economic activity and self-sufficiency of youth participants. These outcomes will be measured by the increase of financial and digital literacy and improvement on action plans. Pre- and post- assessments will measure changes in participants’ financial and digital literacy collected before and after the program. 1690.description: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County is requesting a $1.5 million grant to finalize the funding for construction of a new 31,000 square foot Boys & Girls Club and Workforce Readiness Center in West Palm Beach's Dreher Park. Construction of the Club will provide 800 youth from six to 18 years of age with a safe and educational haven each day after school and throughout the summer and non-school days. The location of the Club will enable the organization to reach youth in a low-income area - particularly teens who have few, if any, options for their out-of-school time.
1690.purpose: The requested funds will close the gap to reach $18 million required to complete the construction of the new 31,000 square foot Boys & Girls Club and Teen Workforce Readiness Center in West Palm Beach, Florida. The Club will provide 800 youth from six to 18 years of age with a safe and educational haven each day after school and throughout the summer and non-school days. The location of the Club will enable the organization to reach youth in a low-income area - particularly teens who have few, i
1690.activities: After school and summer programming is often cost prohibitive for low-income families, the new Club will provide an affordable ($30 annual membership fee), quality program to parents that would otherwise have no option but to have their child home alone each day after school and in the summer in unsupervised and often dangerous situations. The Club will be open from 2PM to 8PM each day after school and from 7:30AM to 6PM on non-school days and throughout the summer to provide much needed support
1690.direct_services: In keeping with the needs of the area’s youth, the main Club will be comprised of two distinct wings to provide numerous age specific flex areas for high yield learning opportunities. The youth wing for children from 6 to 12 years of age is 6,716 sq ft and includes both junior and cadet activity centers, a technology lab, cultural arts center, and academic center. The 8,671 sq ft Workforce Readine

According to the 2020 Census, more than 2,100 children between the ages of 5 and 19 live within one mile of the new Clubhouse. More than 70% of the children live in households with annual incomes at or near poverty as the average per capita income is $28,351 and one out of every 10 children live in households with an annual income of less than $15,000. 1690.outcome: BGCPBC programs help youth to improve academic performance, physical health, and mental health. Programs will also support transportation for families, enrich cultural experiences, help to reduce childhood hunger and substance use and abuse, and divert youth from the Juvenile Justice system. Teen workforce readiness programs will improve economic activity and enhance economic self-sufficiency. Program outcomes will be measured through pre- and post- tests, responses to BGCA’s research-based National Youth Outcomes Initiatives survey, school report cards and state standardized test scores, graduation rates, collaboration with the Dept. of Juvenile Justice, and acceptance into secondary educat

1878.description: This project seeks funding to replace outdated protective gear and acquire modern safety equipment for Greenacres Fire Rescue personnel. As front-line responders, our firefighters rely on National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) - compliant gear to safely perform life-saving duties during fires, medical emergencies, and other operations. Replacing worn or expired equipment, including bunker gear, air packs, ballistic gear, helmets and more will ensure full compliance with current safety standards, reduce risk of injury or contamination, and extend the operational readiness of our department.
1878.purpose: To replace expired, outdated and worn protective gear and acquire modern, NFPA-compliant safety equipment, ensuring Fire Rescue personnel can perform emergency response duties safely, maintain compliance with current safety standards, reduce risk of injury, and sustain operational readiness.
1878.activities: The funds will support the purchase and distribution of updated protective gear and safety equipment, including S.C.B.A. Air Pack, air bottles, fill station, bunker gear, ballistic vest/helmets, and various safety detectors.
1878.direct_services: The project ensures firefighters are properly and safely equipped to provide safe, effective fire, medical, and disaster response, directly protecting the residents.
1878.population: The project serves all 45,000 residents of Greenacres, as well as more than 2,000 residents of the City of Atlantis, where the City provides fire rescue services. By ensuring firefighters are properly equipped, the project supports safe and effective emergency, fire, and medical response for both communities.
1878.outcome: The project will enhance firefighter safety and emergency response for Greenacres residents. Success will be measured by completing equipment replacement, ensuring compliance, reducing injuries, and verifying operational readiness through inspections and drills.

1758.description: This innovative project is a law enforcement transformation in the delivery of co-occurring behavioral health and substance abuse treatment for those judicially incarcerated in Franklin, Gulf, Calhoun, and Liberty counties. The 32-bed corrections facility expansion will provide regional “in-house” 24-hour/7-day crisis intervention, stabilization, targeted case management treatment, and rehabilitation. This comprehensive continuum of care will reduce recidivism, enhance public safety, reduce individual corrections FTE/facility & operation costs.
1758.purpose: It is our intention to construct a 32 bed/12,000 sq.ft. corrections treatment pod, for co-occurring behavioral health and substance abuse, adjacent to our existing jail facilities. This facility will be an "in-house" licensed behavioral health and substance abuse facility. It will provide 24-hour/7days a week crisis transport, stabilization, and treatment through a collaborative partnership agreement with the four Sheriffs of Franklin, Gulf, Calhoun, and Liberty County. This licensed facility an
1758.activities: This facility will be a licensed 24 hour/7days a week behavioral health and substance abuse crisis and treatment facility portal for inmates with complex, high acuity based co-occuring diagnosis within the four counties. The facility will provide an "in-house" multidisciplinary team, including psychiatrist, licensed MSW/therapist, care coordinators, and community outreach/reentry specialist that will guide the inmate with post release navigation and community reintegration. The facility will pro
1758.direct_services: The evidenced based statistics demonstrate significant public safety impacts including a significant reduction of incarceration trends, unemployment rates with the formerly incarcerated, and individual/families within the State Medicaid and/or DCF agencies. The collective clinical and financial synergies and economies of scale within this 4 county model will dramatically reduce taxpayer responsibi
1758.population: This facility will target the highest acuity scaled inmates within the four county correction facilities. Our interdisciplinary team will assist the other county jails based on crisis stabilization, assessment, and portal navigation of the projected behavioral health/substance abuse individuals within their current jail rosters. We anticipate screening 26-50% of the inmate population based on internal metric data.
1758.outcome: This facility will follow statutory guidelines (Chapter 397) and Chapter 65D-30 of the Florida Administrative Code. The evidence based studies suggest that cognitive-behavioral programs while incarcerated reduce recidivism by 15% with some studies showing trends upward to 30%. Recidivism will be tracked internally utilizing linear correlation coefficient statistics modeling. Psychiatric and addiction best practice (CMS) guidelines will be implemented and outcome measures reported. Utilizing DCF and AHCA annual reviews audits and measures will be followed.

1972.description: The STEM and AI Esports Workforce Development Project expands access to high-quality, technology-driven learning curriculum experiences that prepare high schools students for emerging technology and AI careers in the digital economy. The project integrates esports learning curriculum, industry certifications, and internships to build workforce skills by engaging Florida high school students through relevant, hands-on learning that strengthen Florida’s talent pipeline and address workforce gaps in the technology sectors.
1972.purpose: The specific purpose of the project is to use technology to address workforce development needs by expanding digital career skills among high school students. It aims to prepare Florida’s future workforce for technology-driven careers, aligning education with industry demand rather than addressing internal state IT needs.
1972.activities: Florida high school students will have an opportunity to participate and complete innovative esports curriculum and learning in vital technology, AI, and IT workforce skills. Students will also earn industry recognized certifications and participate in internships.
1972.direct_services: Florida high school students will receive hands-on STEM, AI, and esports-based career training that leads to industry certifications and paid or credit-bearing internships, directly preparing them for emerging technology jobs.
1972.population: The project serves Florida high school students, particularly those in underserved or underrepresented communities who need access to workforce training in technology and AI careers. The program is expected to expand to serve multiple schools statewide, reaching hundreds of students in its first year, with capacity to expand annually as additional districts participate.
1972.outcome: The project will increase the number of Florida students who are prepared for technology and AI careers by building workforce skills, earning industry certifications, and completing internships. Outcomes will be measured through student enrollment and completion rates, credential attainment, internship placement data, and post-program employment or continued education tracking.
