Patient outcomes will be reported using American Heart Association platforms for blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose levels for those with Type 2 Diabetes.
1686.purpose: To provide access to opportunities for free physical activity throughout Palm Beach County, serving approximately 20,000 residents of all ages in low-income communities. 75 patients at health clinics with 1 or more Cardiovascular Disease risk factors will be enrolled, tracked, and guided through physical activity opportunities. Patient outcomes will be reported using American Heart Association platforms for blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose levels for those with Type 2 Diabetes.
1686.activities: Digital Vibez will engage 20,000 residents in all age groups and across the county to participate in community events and activities such as Family Fun Fitness Days, Senior Stretch & Strength, among many more programs planned throughout the year. A target cohort of patients will be tracked, and their outcomes will be tracked using American Heart Association (AHA) platforms and guidelines.
1686.direct_services: The direct services for the Digital Vibez Health Initiative include: Free consistent exercise classes for seniors and residents of all ages. Data will be tracked and their outcomes will be measured using American Heart Association (AHA) platforms and guidelines for 75 patients monitored by a clinic.
1686.population: Digital Vibez will engage 20,000 residents including families and senior citizens in low-income communities and those in areas of higher reported MetS and related health conditions.
1686.outcome: The expected outcome is to improve the physical well-being of participants—primarily older adults and individuals managing chronic health conditions—through consistent, accessible, and engaging movement classes. Participants will experience increased physical activity levels, improved mobility, enhanced cardiovascular health, reduced risk factors associated with metabolic syndrome, and greater confidence in managing their own health. Additional benefits include reduced social isolation, increased community connectedness, and measurable improvements in overall quality of life. The outcomes will be measured through a combination of participant surveys and attendance tracking. A cohort of 75 pa

1754.description: This project seeks funding to construct a weather-protected, multi-purpose outdoor area for low-income seniors participating in the city’s hot meals program. The purpose is to expand safe, accessible space for physical activities, social engagement, and health education while reducing overcrowding during meal service. Seniors in this program often face mobility challenges, chronic health conditions, and social isolation. By creating an inclusive outdoor environment, we will provide year-round opportunities for wellness and community connection.
1754.purpose: The area will host low-impact exercise classes such as chair yoga, stretching, and walking groups to improve mobility and balance. It will provide space for wellness programs, including nutrition education, workshops, and mental health support sessions. This space will provide a safe, comfortable environment for physical activities and social interaction, while addressing overcrowding during meals.
1754.activities: Physical wellness activities; such as chair yoga, stretching, and walking groups to improve strength, and mobility for those able. Health and nutrition education workshops on chronic disease management, and fall prevention to support long-term wellness. Social engagement group activities including arts and crafts, gardening, and cultural events. Mental health support for well-being. Expanded meal service.
1754.direct_services: Direct services include access to hot meals for the low-income seniors of the community who are congregate and homebound participants. Organized recreational events, and wellness activities will be held to promote physical health, social connection, and active aging.
1754.population: This project is primarily for the senor population of Miami-Dade county who reside in or near West Miami. The outdoor facilities will be used by the community at large and benefit young and old.
1754.outcome: The project will ensure seniors have hot-meals, improve senior health, reduce isolation, and increase participation in physical activity. Outcomes will be measured through program enrollment, usage rates, participant feedback, and health improvement surveys.

3422.description: The goal is to replace the failing Lakeview Circle Bridge to protect public safety, ensure access for residents and emergency services, and mitigate flood risk. The current undersized structure, a choke point for a 380-acre basin, was inundated during Hurricanes Sally and Michael. Funds will build a resilient bridge to restore hydraulic capacity, reduce flooding, and improve water quality by restoring proper conveyance, which enables the future implementation of stormwater treatment systems.
3422.purpose: The specific goal is to replace the failing Lakeview Circle Bridge to protect public safety, ensure reliable access for residents and emergency services, and mitigate flood risk. The current undersized structure acts as a choke point for a 380-acre basin and was inundated during Hurricanes Michael and Sally, cutting off the sole access for a residential community.
3422.activities: The funds will provide for professional services for the engineering, design, and permitting of the bridge replacement, as well as the construction services needed to build the new, resilient structure.
3422.direct_services: This project directly provides citizens with safe and reliable transportation, enhanced flood protection, and uninterrupted emergency services. By replacing the failing bridge that serves as the sole access point for a neighborhood, residents will no longer risk being isolated during storms.
3422.population: The project directly serves the residents of the nearly 50 homes in the Lakeview Circle neighborhood who rely on the bridge for sole access. Additionally, the bridge provides access to a public boat ramp, serving the broader community of Panama City Beach residents and visitors who use the area for recreation, with an estimated overall total population served ranging from 200-400.
3422.outcome: The expected benefits are the protection of public safety, the improvement of transportation, and the enhancement of stormwater management, which in turn supports environmental quality and local economic stability. The measurements include: Public Safety & Transportation: The primary measure is the elimination of impassable flooding at the sole access point for nearly 50 homes. The methodology will be to document, via visual inspection and post-storm reports, that the bridge remains open 24/7 during major storm events, preventing the multi-day closures that isolated the community during past hurricanes. Stormwater & Environmental Improvement: The primary measure is a calculated increase in h

2701.description: Planned to A.T. is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to serve young people to improve their futures through financial wellness education. We launched our My Money Grows financial wellness curriculum in 5 Duval County Public high schools throughout the 25’ - 26’ school year. The feedback has been incredible from teachers and students. It has gone so well that we are in discussion at the board level to help design the financial wellness course for all high school students, using our curriculum. At minimum the board would like to expand into even more high schools next school year. This funding would support the expansion of our curriculum into 4 more high schools in Duval County for the 2026- 2027 school year.
2701.purpose: The main goal of our curriculum is to make it as easy as possible for teachers to tackle this new requirement, meet the Florida teaching standards, and for students to truly be engaged. Our curriculum is designed to not just teach concepts but reward implementation of healthy financial habits in real time. Thanks to our partners like The Jacksonville Jaguars students can work towards game tickets and apparel as they meet their financial goals. We successfully launched the program with phenomenal
2701.activities: Teachers will receive a training video and all course materials. They will have the opportunity to join a live Q&A session with Planned to A.T. as a follow up. Students will cover topics such as evaluation of spending, need vs wants, budgeting, reading paystub and bank statements, taxes, and setting financial goals. Each topic require them to practice in real time with their finances. Teachers will have an allotted amount of time to implement curriculum and towards the end of the program partici
2701.direct_services: Proven effective financial wellness education that has the potential to shift the state of lower-income communities over time.
2701.population: Approximately 600 students between 4 different Title I Schools will benefit from this program.
2701.outcome: Teachers will be able to implement financial literacy with ease and students will learn and meet the state requirements associated with the course. We use a surveys at the beginning and end of our program for both the teachers and students. Teachers report on the ease of use of materials, student engagement and retention of concepts learned. Students report on engagement, concepts learned, and habit implemented.

2700.description: Grant to use as local match for future potential awards for this project. This project will address critical infiltration and inflow issues by rehabilitating aging infrastructure, reducing stormwater intrusion, and alleviating strain on the wastewater treatment facility. This request follows discussions with Senator Yarborough and reflects the Town’s commitment to efficient use of state and federal resources.
2700.purpose: The funds will rehabilitate critical sewer infrastructure, including 46,500 linear feet of sewer pipe, 11 new manholes, 140 rehabilitated manholes, 48 point repairs, 4,400 linear feet of new force main, and one lift station. This will address infiltration and inflow issues, reduce stormwater intrusion, prevent overflows, and alleviate strain on the wastewater treatment facility. Additionally, the funds will support engineering services during construction, ensuring proper administration and over
2700.activities: The funds will support activities and services essential to the construction phase of the project. These include the rehabilitation of 46,500 linear feet of sewer pipe, construction of 11 new manholes, rehabilitation of 140 existing manholes, completion of 48 point repairs, installation of 4,400 linear feet of new force main, and rehabilitation of one lift station. Additionally, the funds will cover engineering services during construction, such as construction administration and resident observ
2700.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with improved wastewater infrastructure, reducing the risk of sewer overflows and environmental contamination. It will enhance the reliability and efficiency of the sewer system, ensuring proper wastewater management and protecting public health. By addressing infiltration and inflow issues, the project will also help reduce operating costs, which could stabilize
2700.population: The target population served by this project is the approximately 3,000 residents of the Town of Hilliard. The project will benefit all citizens by improving the reliability, efficiency, and capacity of the sewer system, protecting public health, and supporting the Town’s long-term growth and development.
2700.outcome: The project will result in a more reliable sewer system, reducing overflows, lowering operating costs, and supporting the Town’s growth. Benefits will be measured by monitoring reductions in infiltration and inflow, preventing overflows, and improving system capacity. Success will also be assessed through operational cost savings and the system’s ability to handle population growth.

2960.organization: Clay County Board of County Commissioners
2960.description: Moccasin Slough, located off of Highway 17 on Fleming Island, is a 255-acre park adjacent to the St. Johns River. The County will continue work on features included in the site plan based on funding availability.
2960.purpose: Moccasin Slough, located off of Highway 17 on Fleming Island, is a 255-acre park adjacent to the St. Johns River. The County will continue work on features included in the site plan (i.e. boardwalk, observation tower, learning spaces) based on funding availability.
2960.activities: Clay County's Parks and Recreation Department hosts activities at Moccasin Slough such as Art in the Park, Nature Walks, and Educational Sessions on topics such as wildlife. The activities are often offered to all ages, with some designed specifically for certain age groups. The new amenities at Moccasin Slough will create the potential for education collaborations with organizations such as the Audubon Society.
2960.direct_services: Increased capacity at Moccasin Slough would allow for more capacity at the park, and an increase in community events that encourage education and public programming. The project aligns with the board approved County-wide strategic plan and the Parks and Recreation Master Plan.
2960.population: The General Public of Clay County (236,760) is the target population.
2960.outcome: Benefits to the project include improved educational opportunities, improved mental and physical health outcomes, and potential ecotourism. These outcomes will be measured by park visitation numbers, number of educational programs provided, and an increase in local bed taxes.

2972.organization: Alachua County Board of County Commission
2972.description: To construct a 6 story Fire Training Tower with props on property owned by Alachua County. Currenlty, the space is adjacent to a 5,000 square foot classroom. Once complete, the department would seek certification from the Florida Bureau of Fire standards and Training (BFST). Once certified, the facility would be used to train the 300 firefighters at Alachua County Fire Rescue, other fire departments within the region, and host academies to train future firefighters
2972.purpose: A fire training tower provides the public benefit of improving firefighter effectiveness and safety, leading to reduced civilian injuries, deaths, and property damage during real-world fire events. Realistic training in controlled environments in a tower increases their skills, efficiency, and confidence in handling complex scenarios, ultimately making the community safer.
2972.activities: The department will conduct live fire training as described in National Fire Protection Association Statndard 1403 and scheduled training as outlined by the Insurance Service Office (ISO). Additionally, once completed the department will seek certification from the Florida Bureau of Fire Standards and Training as a recognized state training center to host Fire Minimum Standards Classes and a cadre of other fire related certification courses.
2972.direct_services: The citizens will benefit by ensuring firefighters are safer, more efficient, and better prepared to handle emergencies, ultimately leading to reduced property damage and saving lives. The department will also provide "Citizen Academy Days" and "ACFR Youth Days" to educate the public on fire safety and department operations improving community- fire department relationships.
2972.population: All Alachua County citizens and visitors. Once the site is certified the benefit will extend to the region.
2972.outcome: By increasing the ability to train the nearly 300 firefighters in Alachua County, the public will benefit by more efficient operations and safety. ISO ratings are a benchmark as to the effectiveness of a fire department. Currently, ACFR has a rating of 3. It is believed that with the new Tower, the rating could be reduced to a 2. This will be realized by less expensive home-owners insurance premiums.

1877.description: The purpose of this project is to upsize sanitary sewer capacity with a larger pipe and ensure utility resilience by replacing a fragile asbestos (AS) pipe with a durable high-density polythylene (HDPE) pipe. The 4000' length of sewer force main currently serves 13,600 residents and 165 businesses. As the commercial corridor redevelops, capacity will be in place to serve new businesses.
1877.purpose: The purpose is to upsize sanitary sewer capacity with a larger pipe and ensure utility resilience by replacing a fragile asbestos (AS) pipe with a durable high-density polythylene (HDPE) pipe. The 4000' length of sewer force main currently serves 13,600 residents and 165 businesses. As the commercial corridor redevelops, capacity will be in place to serve new businesses
1877.activities: The proposed project will improve wastewater management by ensuring continued sanitary sewer service to existing customers (13,600 residents and 165 businesses) and resilient, increased capacity to serve redeveloping properties in the service area.
1877.direct_services: Replacement of the frail asbestos pipe will increase sewage flow capacity with a larger sized HDPE pipe.
1877.population: The project directly serves 13,600 residents and 165 businesses, but also provides cross-connection in the wastewater collection system.
1877.outcome: The need for the sewer line replacement (to increase capacity size and replace frail asbestos pipe) is included in the Wastewater Master Plan, which was adopted by the Village Council in 2019. The completion of the project (nstallation of 4000 linear feet of 12" HDPE pipe) is the metric.

2979.description: A critical connector between two state roads (SR 331/Williston Rd which is part of Florida's highest priority SIS system and SR 121/SW 34th St) in proximity to I-75, via extending SW 47th Avenue. This will result in decreased congestion and enhanced safety along two major state-owned corridors heavily utilized by the University of Florida's professional and research workforce, as well as residents, across multiple counties in the North Central Florida region.
2979.purpose: To construct a critical connector between two state roads (SR 331/Williston Rd which is part of Florida's highest priority SIS system and SR 121/SW 34th St) in proximity to I-75, via extending SW 47th Avenue. This will result in decreased congestion and enhanced safety along two major state-owned corridors heavily utilized by the University of Florida's professional and research workforce, as well as residents, across multiple counties in the North Central Florida region.
2979.activities: No direct services are part of this construction.
2979.direct_services: No direct services are part of this construction.
2979.outcome: Benefits: Decreased congestion and enhanced motorist safety as part of the state's highest priority Strategic Intermodal System (SIS); Safety enhancements will decrease the number of severe traffic crashes and cause less disruptions to traffic; Improved accessibility to jobs, goods and services to those commuting from surrounding counties (i.e., Levy County, Marion County). Methods: Traffic counts; multi-modal counts; transit headways; delays (comparison of before/after conditions); Measure of traffic volumes and crash incidence along surrounding corridors; Land development levels; sale tax proceeds.

2980.description: The City of Waldo seeks funding to replace approximately 3,800 linear feet of aging 8-inch terracotta (vitrified clay) gravity sewer line along State Road 24 (SR 24) with new PVC pipe, install 16 precast manholes, and replace 22 service connections. The existing sewer infrastructure is more than 50 years old and is highly susceptible to cracks, breaks, and infiltration that can overload the treatment system and contaminate groundwater.This project will be completed in coordination with the Florida Department of Transportation’s SR 24 Concrete Pavement Replacement Project (FPN 447203-1) to avoid future roadway excavation and costly reconstruction. The improvements will also support the Orange Creek Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) by reducing inflow and infiltration that contribute to nutrient loading in the region’s groundwater and surface waters. The project will modernize critical w
2980.purpose: The purpose of this project is to replace aging terracotta (vitrified clay) sewer lines along State Road 24 that are prone to cracks, leaks, and infiltration, which can contaminate groundwater and overload the treatment system. The improvements will modernize critical wastewater infrastructure, ensure reliable service, and support the Orange Creek Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) by reducing nutrient loading and protecting environmental and public health. The City of Waldo has very limited fi
2980.activities: Funds will be used for engineering design, permitting, construction, and engineering services during construction. Construction activities include replacement of approximately 3,800 linear feet of 8-inch vitrified clay gravity sewer with new PVC pipe, installation of 16 new precast manholes, and replacement of 22 sewer service connections, along with site restoration and coordination with FDOT’s SR 24 roadway reconstruction project.
2980.direct_services: The project will provide reliable and uninterrupted wastewater service to residents and businesses along the State Road 24 corridor, preventing sewer leaks, backups, and environmental contamination. These improvements will protect public health, preserve groundwater quality, and ensure dependable utility service for the citizens of Waldo.
2980.population: The target population served by this project includes the citizens and businesses of the City of Waldo, which has an estimated population of approximately 824 residents. The project will directly benefit all utility customers by ensuring reliable and safe wastewater service, protecting public health, and supporting the community’s long-term sustainability.
2980.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is the replacement of deteriorated terracotta gravity sewer lines to eliminate leaks, reduce groundwater infiltration, and prevent system overflows that threaten public health and the environment. The outcome will be measured through maintenance and inspection records documenting reduced infiltration and inflow volumes, fewer emergency repairs, and improved wastewater system performance following construction.

1687.organization: Ferd & Gladys Alpert Jewish Family Service
1687.description: The funds will be used to provide a day program for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities and/or severe mental health conditions, who will engage in educational workshops, fitness programs, and other activities that promote independence, develop cognitive skills and enhance quality-of-life for families. The activities are led by trained professionals.
1687.purpose: The funds will be used to provide a day program for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities and/or severe mental health conditions, who will engage in educational workshops, fitness programs, and other activities that promote independence, develop cognitive skills and enhance quality-of-life for clients and their families. The activities are led by trained professionals.
1687.activities: Group classes will be provided on enhancing coping skills, managing illness, and fostering healthy communication and social skills. Classes such as arts and crafts, cooking, and fitness activities will also be taught.
1687.direct_services: Credentialed professional staff will perform assessments of clients' daily living activities, adaptive skills, and IQ to create a personalized activity plan tailored to functioning and interests. Adults with special needs and severe mental illness will engage in activities that reduce isolation and promote social and cognitive skills twice a week at no cost to families without financial resources.
1687.population: 100+ adult individuals who reside within approximately 15 miles of JFS' Palm Beach Gardens facility serving with adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities as well as severe mental health conditions will be evaluated by credentialed behavioral professionals.
1687.outcome: Clients’ daily living abilities will be assessed using the DLA-20, along with adaptive skills and IQ. Activity choices will be based on assessment scores. Group leaders will track engagement and participation. The DLA-20 will be administered at onset, midway, and at the end of FY2026–27. The Vineland-3 comprehensive assessment will be used at the start and end of FY2026-27 to evaluate and track clients with intellectual disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, and related needs to guide targeted activity plans and measure adaptive-skills progress. The WAIS-5 will be used at the onset to measure IQ. All test results will be tracked in Welligent Electronic Health Record software. Quality Assura

2995.description: The Arc of Bradford County is looking expands it's business operations to promote economic development for the agency and the individuals which it serves. As a rural area of opportunity, we believe this program will provided the investment needed to promote sustainability in the agency and long-term growth for the community. Specifically, this funding will expand transportation access for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities who lack transportation services, provide more job opportunities for those individuals, and will increase the economic impact in the community at large.
2995.purpose: This goals of these funds is to build the capacity of the Arc to provide quality services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
2995.activities: Individuals who receive employment through this project will receive on the job training for the first year of employment to increase their ability to be successful on the job. Individuals will participate in work projects and receive support from staff who are trained to provide support to individuals with IDD or mental health concerns.
2995.direct_services: Individuals working will be providing a much needed service to the community by producing a consumable product, benefiting the community at large. Individuals who are receiving employment from the project will be provided an overall better economic situation and receive supports needed to be successful in the community.
2995.population: The primary target population for this project is jobless individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities and/or mental health concerns. This project seeks to expand the Arc's current work program and add additional jobs, doubling the current workforce.
2995.outcome: The expected outcomes include improved mental health services and expansion, transportation, increased economic activity, creating immediate job opportunities, and enhancing individual's self-sufficiency. Measurements include self- report and assessments, staff observations, quantifiable data from increased numbers in various categories, supplemental information and training, and co-occurring services through the program.

2999.description: Design, permit, and construct approximately 4,800 LF of new water main to serve the Police Training Grounds and Lawtey Correctional Institution. The City’s aging and deteriorated potable water system is composed of thin-walled PVC and corroded ductile iron lines prone to leaks, pressure loss, and frequent breaks. The system cannot deliver adequate fire flow to protect and serve these critical facilities, which house about 800 inmates and employ roughly 200–250 staff.
2999.purpose: To replace deteriorated and undersized water mains serving the Police Training Facility and Lawtey Correctional Institution, improving fire protection, water pressure, and reliability for critical facilities and the surrounding community.
2999.activities: Design, permitting, and construction of new water mains, valves, fittings, and fire hydrants, including installation, testing, and site restoration to improve system capacity and performance.
2999.direct_services: Reliable and safe potable water service, improved water pressure, and enhanced fire protection for residents, local businesses, and major public employers.
2999.population: Approximately 700 residents within the City of Lawtey, plus the Lawtey Correctional Institution, which houses about 800 inmates and employs 200–250 staff, as well as the Police Training Facility.
2999.outcome: The project will improve system reliability, fire-flow capacity, and water quality while reducing water loss. Success will be measured through pre- and post-construction fire-flow tests, water pressure monitoring, and reduced leak and repair frequencies.

3000.description: Replace a single lane concrete bridge that has limited weight capacity with a two lane FDOT compliant bridge structure.
3000.purpose: The goal is to replace a single lane concrete bridge that has limited weight capacity with a two lane FDOT compliant bridge structure.
3000.activities: Upon completion of the project, vehicles that previously could not cross the bridge structure safely (i.e. fire apparatus, delivery vehicles, construction vehicles et al) will now pass safely to and from the Bradford Sportsman Farm. Non- commercial traffic will also travel more safely with the two lane bridge rather than the current one lane bridge.
3000.population: The target population are sportsmen that utilize the sporting clay facility for recreation, fund raising tournaments and professional clay shooting events. The facility also hosts other service club events such as the Rotary Beast Feast fundraiser. The facility is also widely used by gun enthusiasts for target practice at the various gun ranges located at the facility. The Bradford County Sheriff's Office SWAT team also utilizes the facility for its recurring training. The annual number of trips
3000.outcome: The benefit to the public is a safer travel experience while visiting the Sportman's Farm and providing a more efficient and effective point of ingress and egress for emergency vehicles. This will also provide for expedited egress in the unlikely event the facility needed to be evacuated due to emergency.

3354.description: The City of Starke is surrounded by large tracts of undeveloped land in the unincorporated County. The city has sufficient wastewater treatment capacity to accommodate future growth. This project is to request funding for a sewer Bypass project to extend wastewater service to a new development proposed northwest of the city. This project will not require significant modifications or upgrades to the current sewer infrastructure, ensuring a more streamlined implementation process while maintaining service reliability.
3354.purpose: Funds will be used construction activities for a sewer Bypass project to extend wastewater service to a new development proposed northwest of the city.
3354.activities: Construction activities for a sewer bypass to extend wastewater service to a new development proposed northwest of the city. This project will not require significant modifications or upgrades to the current sewer infrastructure, ensuring a more streamlined implementation process while maintaining service reliability.
3354.direct_services: Wastewater service will be provided to citizens of the new development.
3354.population: The target population population served by this project are citizens of the new development northwest of the city.
3354.outcome: Construction activities for a sewer bypass to extend wastewater service to a new development proposed northwest of the city. This project will not require significant modifications or upgrades to the current sewer infrastructure, ensuring a more streamlined implementation process while maintaining service reliability.

3013.description: Funds for this project will be used for the replacement of approximately 2,600 existing potable water meters and approximately 102 irrigation meters with new Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) capable meters to provide accurate readings for water usage by customers and efficient data collection for the City.
3013.purpose: Funds for this project will be used for the replacement of 2,612 existing potable water meters and 102 irrigation meters with new Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) capable meters to provide accurate readings for water usage by customers and efficient data collection.
3013.activities: 2,612 existing potable water meters and 102 irrigation meters will be replaced with new Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) capable meters
3013.direct_services: This is a construction project which will will enhance customer affordability through accurate metering, reduced water loss, and operational efficiencies that limit future rate increases.
3013.population: 2,612 existing potable water meters and 102 irrigation meters will be replaced.
3013.outcome: The outcome expected by this project is accurate readings for water usage by customers and efficient data collection.

3015.description: This project will combat the pandemic "Nature Deficit Disorder," which studies have shown is the root cause of many mental and physical illnesses. The funding will help create a Gateway Outdoor Center near a high traffic intersection (I- 10 & I-75) to connect all ages (from the region) to the outdoors and agriculture of North Florida. Using state-of-the-art technology, this engaging center will provide highly simulated experiences designed to connect visitors with, and be a gateway to, the actual outdoors and agriculture. The center will be used 2 days per week for regional elementary school field trips and will service many other sectors of society through interactive classes and workshops. Further, the Gateway Outdoor Center will ensure Florida remains the Fishing and Boating Capital of the World.
3015.purpose: The purpose of the non-reoccurring funding is to create a Gateway Outdoor Center that highlights the valuable outdoor recreational opportunities and agricultural culture of North Florida, within the "Fishing & Boating Capital of the World." The Center will connect people to agriculture and the outdoors by providing hands-on, highly simulated experiences designed to enrich cultural engagement, enhance economic development and promote innovation. See video at: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uTQJ
3015.activities: Outdoor and agricultural experiences in North Florida will be provided through hands-on simulation inside the Center and designed to be a gateway to the actual outdoors throughout neighboring counties in the region. Visitors of all ages will have a chance to try different outdoor experiences such as: boating, archery, aqualture, cave diving, silvicultural aging, fishing, etc. The Center will be used 2 days per week for regional elementary school field trips and curriculum, while being open to pr
3015.direct_services: Opportunities to learn, support and connect with the outdoors and agriculture through state-of-the-art technology while also serving as a gateway (visitor center) hub to real experiences in the region. The Center will be used 2 days per week for regional elementary school field trips and curriculum.
3015.population: Over 100,000 visitors of all ages will have an opportunity to connect with the outdoors and agriculture. The Center will then direct visitors to explore the outdoors in nearby couties.
3015.outcome: Increased awareness and appreciation for the outdoors and agriculture will be measured using pre/post surveys. Also, the FWC will partner with the Department of Health and IFAS Extention to measure improvements in health as well as the Tourism Development Council to monitor visitor impacts on the region.

3018.description: This request will allow for needed renovation of 7,500 sqf including the jail kitchen, dining area, laundry room, and medical suite. The improvements will include physical environment, plumbing, electrical and other needed improvements at the Columbia County jail. This project will allow for a better environment for inmates and the corrections staff of the Columbia County jail.
3018.purpose: Improvements to the laundry, kitchen, and medical suite will allow for better health among the inmates, correction, and staff of the Columbia County jail. The medical suite improvements will allow for a cleaner environment for inmates and staff.
3018.activities: This request will allow for needed physical environment, equipment replacement, plumbing, electrical and other needed improvements at the Columbia County jail. This will be a 7,500 sqf area of space in the laundry, kitchen/cafeteria, and medical suite. This project will allow a better environment for inmates and the corrections staff of the Columbia County jail.
3018.direct_services: The funds in this request will allow for a better functioning jail for deputies, correction officers, and inmates.
3018.population: Deputies, correction officers, and jail staff, as well as currently incarcerated individuals at the Columbia County jail.
3018.outcome: Better health conditions as well as improved public infrastructure- reduced capital improvements over time.

3019.description: Funds will support design, permitting, and construction of a new septage receiving and pretreatment station at the St. Margarets WWTF. The project will safely receive, screen, pretreat, and meter hauled septage; protect downstream treatment processes from shock loads; generate new utility revenue; reduce improper disposal of septage; and improve nutrient management within the Santa Fe BMAP and the Ichetucknee PFA, helping protect regional water quality.
3019.purpose: To design and construct a new septage receiving and pretreatment station at the Lake City SMWWTF to safely receive, screen, and condition septage, protect biological treatment processes, support regional springs protection, and eliminate improper disposal within the Santa Fe BMAP and Ichetucknee Priority Focus Area.
3019.activities: Design, permitting, bidding, construction, and construction-phase engineering for a new septage receiving station, including screening, flow equalization, odor control, blower and diffused air improvements, electrical/instrumentation, and modifications to existing tankage.
3019.direct_services: The project will prevent septage-related plant upsets, reduce risk of environmental contamination, enhance regional water quality, and ensure safe, compliant septage disposal for local haulers and businesses.
3019.population: The project serves Lake City’s ˜13,000 residents, businesses, critical facilities, the broader utility service area, and surrounding communities that rely on the Santa Fe Basin, Ichetucknee Springs system, and regional groundwater resources. Septage haulers and their customers will also benefit from safe, reliable disposal and treatment.
3019.outcome: The project will improve treatment stability, protect effluent quality, reduce nutrient loading to the Santa Fe Basin and Ichetucknee Springs, increase operational capacity, and generate new utility revenue. Benefits will be measured through influent/effluent nutrient data, plant operational reports, compliance records, septage volumes received, and reductions in treatment upsets or violations.

3021.description: The funds will purchase equipment for the Columbia County School District to purchase Class “B” Bi-Directional Amplifier (BDA) and a battery backup unit for each school facility in Columbia County Schools. Due to the structure of each building, radio signals can be intermittent in school facilities. This project will enhance first responders radio signals in school facilities during incidents.
3021.purpose: The funds will purchase equipment for the Columbia County School District to purchase Class “B” Bi-Directional Amplifier (BDA) and a battery backup units for each school facility in Columbia County Schools. Due to the structure of each building, radio signals can be intermittent in school facilities. This project will enhance first responders radio signals in school facilities during incidents.
3021.activities: The funds will purchase equipment for the Columbia County School District to purchase Class “B” Bi-Directional Amplifier (BDA) and a battery backup units for each school facility in Columbia County Schools. This project will enhance first responders radio signals in school facilities during incidents.
3021.direct_services: The primary beneficiaries of this equipment will be students, first responders, faculty and staff members of the Columbia County School District.
3021.population: Greater than 800. Students, staff, first responders.
3021.outcome: Stronger communication signals within school buildings.

3024.description: Best Buddies is a non-profit organization that creates opportunities for one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, leadership development, inclusive living, and family support for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). This project will engage 3,200 participants across 140 middle and high school based chapters in Florida. Best Buddies will create one-to-one peer mentoring friendships between students with and without disabilities, provide leadership trainings and facilitate social group activities, allowing students with IDD to learn vital social skills that will help them become more independent, more integrated into their school and community, and more employable as they transition into adulthood.
3024.purpose: Best Buddies utilizes a one-to-one peer mentoring model. A typical peer is matched in a one-to-one friendship with a student with an IDD, giving these students the opportunity to learn vital social skills. Students with IDD become more independent, more integrated into their school and community, and more employable as they transition into adulthood. Best Buddies staff will recruit and manage volunteer leadership teams from these schools to create peer-mentoring friendships between students with IDD and their typical peers. Best Buddies staff will also deliver leadership training to students with and without disabilities, as well as social and recreational group activities.

Staff will also provide regional trainings and awareness activities. Area directors oversee the program staff and provide direct program support to both the schools and staff.

The project will serve 6,800 participants, ages 10-22. The project will serve students in the following counties: Bay, Brevard, Broward, Clay, Collier, Duval, Flagler, Hillsborough, Lake, Lee, Leon, Marion, Martin, Miami- Dade, Orange, Osceola, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinella, Sarasota, Seminole, St. Johns, Sumpter, and Walton.
3024.outcome: Through Best Buddies, students with IDD will develop social skills to be college and career-ready and become more socially integrated into their school communities. Best Buddies conducts an annual survey to evaluate the success of our program. This includes re-roofing, re-flooring, adding air conditioning, upgrading the electrical, interior and exterior improvements, storm water drainage, cafeteria reconstruction, kitchen repairs and ADA compliant plumbing upgrades.

These initiatives also strengthen the talent pipeline for Florida's high-tech and defense sectors, ensuring a competitive workforce that aligns with state economic priorities. By fostering innovation and equipping students with 21st-century skills, this investment directly benefits Florida's economy, security, and long-term prosperity.

Teachers will receive training in subjects such as computer science, robotics, cybersecurity, aerospace, and data science, equipping them with the knowledge needed to provide high-quality instruction. Schools and programs will be provided with advanced technology, including robotics kits, drones, 3D printers, and
3077.direct_services: Services include hosting STEM events and competitions; teacher professional development in CS, mathematics, science, and STEM; distributing advanced technologies such as 3D printers, drones, and science tools, facilitation of CS festivals, implementation of high-quality STEM programs to foster digital literacy and career readiness aligned to FL economic needs, serving over 120,000 students.

To measure these outcomes, we will monitor enrollment in STEM courses and advanced coursework, participation in professional development, student performance on state and local assessments, and participation in events. 3051.description: The project will construct a new Upper Floridan Aquifer (UFA) well to enhance water supply reliability and system redundancy. This well will provide a sustainable potable water source, improve operational flexibility, and ensure consistent service to meet current and future community demand.
3051.purpose: Provides a high-quality potable water source with naturally low turbidity and mineral content. Helps maintain balanced aquifer recharge by supporting controlled withdrawals that stabilize groundwater levels.
3051.activities: The project will construct a new Upper Floridan Aquifer (UFA) well to enhance water supply reliability and system redundancy. This well will provide a sustainable potable water source, improve operational flexibility, and ensure consistent service to meet current and future community demand.
3051.direct_services: Enhances system redundancy and operational reliability during maintenance, peak demand, or emergency conditions. This new well provides an additional high-quality potable water source for Lee County to serve rapidlly growing areas including Lehigh Acres and surrounding communities.
3051.population: The population of Lehigh Acres and other residents of Lee County will benefit from the use of Floridan Aquifer ground water preventing saltwater intrusion into other aquifers and provide a high-quality potable water source with naturally low turbidity and mineral content.
3051.outcome: Helps maintain balanced aquifer recharge by supporting controlled withdrawals that stabilize groundwater levels. Monitor groundwater elevations and rainfall data to assess aquifer stability trends over time. Collect and analyze UFA wellwater samples for key parameters and verify compliance with FDEP standards.

3052.description: Extending the water mains in the south section of the Lehigh Acres water distribution system will provide potable water service to a new elementary school.The new elementary school is located in an area where there is a high-density area of children in a growing area within Lehigh Acres, near the SR 82 commercial corridor. The project is a significant initiative with several potential benefits for the community including a safe, reliable potable water source.
3052.purpose: Extending the water mains in the south section of the Lehigh Acres water distribution system will provide potable water service to a new elementary school. The new elementary school is located in an area where there is a high-density area of children in a growing area within Lehigh Acres, near the SR 82 commercial corridor. The project is a significant initiative with several potential benefits for the community including a safe reliable potable water source.
3052.activities: Connection to the potable water system reduces the need for individual residential wells used for drinking water and irrigation. This will assist to reduce the daily withdrawal volume of water from the sandstone acquifer by private wells.
3052.direct_services: Clean potable water compliant with the State and Federal drinking water standards will be provided to residents. Providing potable water to a new elementary school promotes education for the local area and reduces traffic and transportation to other schools outside the area at present.
3052.population: The citizens of Lee County and particularly those living in the Lehigh Communtiy will benefit from the new watermains. Providing clean water from the Upper Floridan Aquifer will ensure the sandstone aquifer retains sufficient water resources and thus prevent saltwater intrusion into the sandstone aquifer. This will prevent salt becoming a problem in irrigation water and water used for other purposes.
3052.outcome: Measure the number of new connections connected to the potable water system. Measure the number of students enrolled in the elementary school who reside in the Lehigh Acres community.

The project will reduce sanitary sewer overflows, improve nutrient removal, and support continued reliable wastewater service and environmental protection for the rapidly growing Lee County - Lehigh Acres area.
3053.purpose: The funds will be used to design and construct improvements at the Lehigh WWTF to increase capacity, enhance treatment, and ensure permit compliance. The project will reduce sanitary sewer overflows, improve nutrient removal, and support continued reliable wastewater service and environmental protection for the rapidly growing Lee County- Lehigh Acres area.
3053.activities: Expand sewer treatment capacity and increase resiliency during severe weather events to eliminate/reduce sewage seepage, reduce the nutrient loading in stormwater, groundwater & surface water & mitigate the risk of red tide to the area.
3053.direct_services: The wastewater treatment plant will be expanded to accomodate tremendous growth ocurring in Lee County and will protect citizens from overflows of wastewater which can be a public health concern and cause other health concerns such as red tide.
3053.population: All of the population of Lehigh Acres and will benefit all the citizens of Lee County by providing additional wastewater treatment capacity thus helping to maintain water quality and reduce nutrient loading.
3053.outcome: Expand sewer treatment capacity and increase resiliency during severe weather events to eliminate/reduce sewage seepage, reduce the nutrient loading in stormwater, groundwater & surface water & mitigate the risk of red tide to the area.

This clinic will provide Primary Care, Behavioral Health, Women's Health, on-site laboratory and pharmacy services for family members of all ages, and administrative support to ensure integrated care delivery. It will be a patient- focused facility that improves health outcomes by offering comprehensive, coordinated services in one location.
2812.purpose: Agape will establish a full-service community health clinic that expands access to essential healthcare for underserved residents. Programming is faith-based and targeted to tackle top criminogenic factors of participants at several remote facilities statewide. Emphasis is placed on warm handoff into the community.

Funding would allow MOV to hire staff to enhance current services in four FDC prisons and begin programming in eight additional facilities. Programming is faith based and targeted to tackle top criminogenic factors while inside facilities. Emphasis is placed on a warm handoff into the community. Case managers support job placement, life skills and promote public safety.
2717.activities: In person instruction; group work; individual work; religious services; work readiness curriculum; educational obtainment; soft skills and life skills training; budgeting and financial security; family reconciliation; addiction and recovery activities; responsible parenting and mentorship.
2717.direct_services: Virtual learning; case management; mentors and staffing.
2717.population: Florida Department of Corrections male inmates. We expect to serve approximately 800 inmates in FY 2026/2027.
2717.outcome: Improved Mental Health - Reduce participant criminal thinking and anger management by 85%. This will be measured through participant surveys. Improve Quality of Education - Ensure 80% of eligible participants who desire a HSD or GED successfully complete the learning modules through VR headsets. Public Safety - 100% of participants releasing from incarceration will receive case management services, support and follow up for a minimum of 3 months post release. Improve Economic Activity - MOV will partner with 25 employers and receive information on the benefits of hiring ex- offenders. Enhance Participant Economic Self-sufficiency - 85% of participants will grow in budgeting and money managem

2152.description: This research program will investigate the impact of an indoor Olympic training facility in Central Florida, using data- driven research to quantify the return on investments in public skateboard infrastructure and services which are largely unprecedented. We will also create 5 smaller outdoor programs in locations across the state in order to provide a broad data set that is actionable statewide.
2152.purpose: Because skateboarding has little to no precedent within formal institutions, this funding request is intended to create clear documentation for the value to be gained by making Florida the national leader in world class skateboard facilities, and the potential for vast returns on the development of youth, community, and economy through direct investment in skateboard infrastructure.
2152.activities: The creation of a temporary indoor air conditioned skate facility. The creation of 5 satellite placemaking programs that will combine public skate structures, with edible landscaping to provide the context for a powerful youth development program. Participants will receive free skate lessons from skateboard community leaders, manage agriculture, and sell crops at a local farmers' market.
2152.direct_services: This program provides a free space to skateboard indoors regardless of temperature or precipitation, creating a safe predictable destination where people can take part in a healthy activity. This program creates 20+ jobs, employing leaders from 5 skateboard communities to run a mentorship program based on growing edible landscaping, and selling it at a local farmers' market. Mentorship for youth.
2152.population: While this program is designed to serve the general public, direct services to citizens target young people between the ages of 13 and 24, at the time when they are most in need of environments that support safe learning, and experimentation.
2152.outcome: This project will invest money into the creation of a public skateboard spaces, with accompanying programs designed to support the healthy and safe development of young people. We will partner with UCF researchers to define appropriate research protocols to quantify the affects of money spent on infrastructure and services. The result will be a collection of data and information that allows government organizations across the state to implement effective skateboard programs. 3257.description: The STARability Foundation requests funding to support program expansion capacity within Phase 1 of our Capital Campaign, which is transforming a 42,000-square-foot facility on a five-acre campus in Naples, Florida, into a regional hub for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). STARability is a leader in providing innovative programs, including the Trailblazer Academy, which offers community-based skill development focused on eight core life skills that promote social inclusion and independence. Staff assess each participant’s abilities and create individualized plans supporting goals such as employment readiness, personal finance, and self-advocacy. When participants are ready to explore career options, our Vocational Services team provides customized training, coaching, and job placement to address barriers to employment. This investment will help triple ou
3257.purpose: To support and expand our innovative Trailblazer Academy, a community-based program for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities focused on life-skill development and vocational training, while advancing our phased expansion to a larger permanent campus to increase capacity, address a growing waitlist, and broaden access to programs that foster life enrichment, community engagement, and greater independence.
3257.activities: Funds will support the program and building expansion projects underway, including STARability's full-time Trailblazer Academy and center-based programs, providing life-skills education, vocational training, community engagement, and job placement with coaching. Additional staff and adaptive resources will allow 3-times more individuals with IDD to reach independence in our new permanent space.
3257.direct_services: As an approved Florida Department of Education Vocational Rehabilitation provider, STARability will deliver job training, career counseling, interview preparation, and on-the-job coaching for individuals with IDD. Funds will expand these direct services, helping more citizens obtain and retain meaningful employment.
3257.population: The population served includes: persons intellectually and/or developmentally disabled, persons physically disabled, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons. We expect to serve between 400-800 people.
3257.outcome: The expected benefits and outcomes of this project include: improving physical health, improving mental health, enriching cultural experience, improving quality of education, increasing/improving economic activity, creating specific immediate job opportunities, and enhancing specific individual's economic self-sufficiency. The methodology by which these outcomes will be measured include assessing individuals in eight life-skill areas outlined by Virginia Commonwealth University, tracking experiences, tracking employment status from job seeker to placement success, and surveying the target population and caregivers.

3536.description: The project establishes a Career and Technical Education program focused on water management, wastewater treatment, and ecology to address Florida’s shortage of certified operators and an aging workforce nearing retirement. Funding will provide industry-standard equipment, treatment simulators, and highly trained staff to deliver hands-on labs, simulations, internships, and certification preparation. Students will graduate with workforce-ready skills for immediate employment or postsecondary study, creating a direct pipeline of qualified professionals. The program strengthens regional infrastructure by supporting municipalities, employers, and communities with a new generation of skilled operators.
3536.purpose: The funds will establish a Career and Technical Education program that equips students with industry-recognized training in water management, wastewater treatment, and environmental systems. The goal is to create a skilled workforce pipeline that addresses the statewide shortage of certified water system operators, ensures workforce readiness, and supports municipalities and employers in meeting critical infrastructure needs.

These activities will ensure workforce-ready training that equips students for immediate employment or continued postsecondary study while addressing regional workforce needs.
3536.direct_services: The project will provide students with direct access to technical education, hands-on training, and preparation for certification in water management and treatment. These services create immediate career opportunities for graduates while strengthening the regional workforce pipeline. The program will provide access to industry- standard training and certifications in water management and treatment, preparing students for immediate entry into the workforce or continued postsecondary study. While the program will serve a broad and growing number of students each year, the primary impact is expanding
3536.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is a stronger, career-ready workforce equipped with industry certifications in water management, wastewater treatment, and environmental systems, addressing the shortage of qualified operators in Southwest Florida. Benefits include improved educational opportunities for students, immediate job placement potential, and long-term support for municipal infrastructure. Outcomes will be measured by student enrollment and retention, completion of technical coursework, attainment of certifications, workforce placement data, and employer feedback to ensure the program meets both educational and regional workforce needs.

1626.description: CASL will provide affordable housing and supportive services which will ensure people have access to permanent housing in their communities. The program will serve Floridians with severe mental health disorders, veterans with disabilities, youth aging out of foster care, and adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities. The model is designed to prevent and reduce homelessness, reduce recidivism to homelessness, jails, CSUs, and hospitals by helping people attain independence and achieve permanent, safe, affordable housing. Approximately 90% of our residents have an income of $0 to $11,316 per year, fair market housing is not affordable. We have consistently delivered a significant reduction in acute care costs exceeding 80 percent. Per OPPAGA Report 24-10: "The statutory goal of Florida's housing strategy is to ensure that every resident has safe, decent, and affordable housing."
1626.purpose: CASL will provide affordable housing and supportive services which will ensure people have access to permanent housing in their communities. The model is designed to prevent and reduce homelessness, reduce recidivism to homelessness, jails, CSUs, and hospitals by helping people attain independence and achieve permanent, safe, affordable housing.The Shimberg Center for Housing Studies at the University of Florida 2024 Annual report indicates a shortage of 2,113,914 units for renter households at
1626.activities: Permanent housing (e.g. homes/duplexes/apartments), case management, care coordination, crisis intervention, supportive housing/living, financial management, peer support, outreach, transportation, and benefits management services; as well as, advocacy on behalf of the clients in an effort to mitigate challenges, barriers, and obstacles enable to ensure clients achieve and maintain permanent housing in the community.
1626.direct_services: Our case managers provide the services listed in 13b directly to clients helping them develop literacy skills, job skills, budgeting, healthcare access, transportation, accessing community resources and services, computer skills, nutrition and meal planning, communication skills, personal hygiene and home management, and security and safety management.
1626.population: The populations served include adults with mental health disorders, substance use disorders, verterans with disabilities, youth aging out of foster care, adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities, and adults who are homeless and have one or more disabling conditions. CASL expects to serve 1200+ people.
1626.outcome: The project offers housing and supportive services, ensuring the basic need of having shelter is achieved by program participants; thereby assisting the State of Florida with reducing homelessness and managing and improving the system of care. Individuals must have shelter to avail themselves of mental health, addiction, educational, vocational, and medical services. The outcomes will be measured by individuals served and remaining in an independent living situation (permanent supportive housing).

Florida has the highest SCD prevalence, and the FDA's approval of gene therapies, including functional cures that requires specialized blood collection, processing, storage, and transport systems. In many transfusion cases in Florida, the SCD recipient may not receive blood products that are best matched for the patient. By increasing awareness within Florida's African American population and providing Free Sickle Cell Trait testing for African American blood donors will be more beneficial to the patient. Last year's state investment provided foundational equipment. Continued funding supports the advanced systems, supplies, and QC needed to produce the critical blood products, while expanding outreach to ethnic donors whose matched blood is essential for tre
1622.purpose: Strengthening Florida's research and treatment capacity for Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) will reduce long term healthcare costs, lower reliance on state supported programs, and improve quality of life for 13,886 Floridians suffering from SCD. Enhanced lab systems, donor screening, molecular testing, cellular processing, analysis technology, and community outreach support development of curative gene therapies and build a rare donor repository accessible to hospitals across Florida. This work aligns
1622.activities: Activities include collecting, processing, and preparing blood products, along with community awareness efforts that support gene therapy research and treatment for Sickle Cell Disease, hemophilia, and select blood cancers. Funds will provide free Sickle Cell Trait testing for African American donors. Furthermore, these expanded services will strengthen donor screening, molecular testing, and laboratory analysis to identify rare blood types and build a Florida rare donor repository. Rare units c
1622.direct_services: Free Sickle Cell Trait testing for African Americans when they donate blood which will be done in tandem of increased education and awareness of ethnically matched blood to improve patient outcomes. Enhanced laboratory capacity for specific genetic and molecular testing. Build and maintain a rare donor repository for Sickle Cell Disease, hemophilia, and blood-related cancers for patients receiving
1622.population: Sickle Cell Disease disproportionately impacts the African American community, so much of the project will impact this community. However, the genetic testing and rare donor repository will also help those suffering from hemophilia, and blood-related cancers. The program supports minority blood donors, researchers, clinicians, and patients statewide.

2097.description: To repair and restore 30+ year old athletic fields at Jupiter Community Park (the largest park that serves regional constituents) through laser grading, irrigation and drainage repair, and sod replacement. These enhancements will improve storm water management and drainage, reduce maintenance downtime to increase field availability, and ensure safe playable fields for 100,000 attendees annually. This project is a strategic initiative for the Town and has widespread Town Council support resulting in prioritized CIPs.
2097.purpose: To repair and restore 30+ year old athletic fields at Jupiter Community Park (the largest park that serves regional constituents) through laser grading, irrigation and drainage repair, and sod replacement, as the life expectancy of the turf fields are approximately 15 years. These enhancements will improve stormwater management and drainage, reduce maintenance downtime to increase field availability, and ensure safe playable fields for at least 100,000 field users annually.
2097.activities: The project will fund design, engineering, and construction to restore athletic fields at Jupiter Community Park through turf replacement, laser grading, and irrigation and drainage repairs. These improvements will provide safer, more reliable fields that support year-round play, reduce closures, and enhance recreational opportunities for residents of all ages.
2097.population: Over 300,000 residents, visitors, and organized sport leagues across the region.
2097.outcome: Improve field drainage, reduce runoff into storm drains, and create safer playing surfaces. These enhancements will increase playable days for youth and adult sports, support tournament hosting and boost regional tourism. Town staff will monitor field drainage, track field usage, and analyze reduction in maintenance needs.

2064.description: Hanley's program provides the highest level of behavioral healthcare for peripartum woman. Pregnant moms live in Hanley's newest community learning parenting, life and job skills, while participating in medical, psychological, and clinical treatment for their behavioral health conditions. Specialists will focus on caring for babies who have been prenatally exposed to substances. Hanley's program will teach employability skills and job training, while providing housing for mom and baby.
2064.purpose: The appropriation will help construct a residential treatment facility for peripartum women and their children. Rooms will house women, babies and older children who have been reunified with a now-sober mom.
2064.activities: Pregnant and postpartum moms with their children will live-in residence in Hanley's newest living, learning community, learning parenting, life, and job skills, while participating in medical, psychological, and clinical treatment for their behavioral health conditions.
2064.direct_services: Medical, psychological, and clinical treatment for behavioral health conditions, plus instruction in parenting, life skills, as well as employability and education/job training. Children will receive specialized care from therapists who specialize in the shortfalls experienced by children exposed to substances in utero.
2064.population: Between 12-24 women at any one time. Rooms will be convertible housing either two pregnant moms, or one postpartum mom with her baby and older children. The women served will be the State of Florida residents with the vast majority having been trafficked or who are living below the poverty line.
2064.outcome: This program has a number of goals, including breaking the intergenerational cycle of addiction, helping moms to begin their journey of recovery, providing extra care, support and services for children exposed to substances in utero, and helping return a stable family unit back into the community.
