1819.direct_services: Increased safety for student pedestrians through delineated buffers separating student walking paths from local and visitor traffic.
1819.population: Students attending Plantation Key Elementary/Middle School, Coral Shores High School, and Treasure Village Montessori School. The adjacent neighborhoods, of which next to Plantation Key Elementary/Middle school has one of the highest residential populations in the Village. 4,945 residents out of the total 7,000 residents in the Village live on Plantation Key, where the three schools are located. Of which, 15% are under the age of 18.
1819.outcome: The expected benefits are increased safety, and reduced stress of students walking those routes currently. Surveys can be conducted after construction to measure the increased feeling of safety, and data will monitored though the tentative Safety Action Plan.

1837.description: This project involves the completion of pre-construction activities including the design, final engineering, and permitting for an erosion control project to protect the only reach of US Highway 1, a critical evacuation route, that washed away in 2017 during Hurricane Irma. Included in this design and engineering phase is wave attenuation and sediment transport modeling. This project builds upon the successful deployment of the same wave attenuation and erosion control technology deployed by the Florida DOT on the Sunshine State Highway in central Florida. A feasibility study has already been performed for the project.
1837.purpose: The goal achieved through the funds requested will be completion of pre-construction activities to bring this project to shovel ready. The ultimate goal of the construction project is to provide erosion control to safeguard against storm surges and sea level rise.
1837.activities: Bathymetric and environmental surveys, conceptual design, pre-application meetings, public outreach efforts, design, permitting, and wave attenuation modeling services.
1837.direct_services: The protection of the only evacuation route in the Florida Keys, US Highway 1 from impacts associated with storms and increasing high tides.
1837.population: Any travelers to the Florida Keys and the residents of the Village of Islamorada (est 7,000), as well as residents of the Florida Keys living south of Islamorada (est 62,000) which use this route as their primary evacuation route during extreme weather events.
1837.outcome: In addition to the transportation infrastrcture protection, as was the case on the DOT's Sunshine State Highway Project, the deployment of wave attentuation devices at this location will increase the abundance of submerged and emergent aquatic vegetation, biologic growth on the breakwater structures, and result in the accretion of sediment to build the coastline providing additional buffering to the coastline and road. The breakwater and entire project footprint would be monitored by consultants on a bimonthly basis for changes in all the specific measurements noted.

2653.description: The purposes of these funds are to support the indigent care mission in Jacksonville. Currently, UF Health in Jacksonville runs at a significant deficit and requires additional resources to meet the uncompensated care needs for the benefit of the community.
2653.purpose: The purposes of these funds are to support the indigent care mission in Jacksonville. Currently, UF Health in Jacksonville runs at a significant deficit and requires additional resources to meet the uncompensated care needs for the benefit of the community.
2653.activities: Indigent patient care for the Northeast Florida community
2653.population: Elderly persons; persons with poor mental health; persons with poor physical health; jobless persons; economically disadvantaged persons; At-risk youth; homeless, developmentally disabled, physically disabled; and drug users. Over 800 individuals in the target populations are expected to be served.
2653.outcome: Improve Physical Health- UF Health is providing medical services to improve physical health for the community through indigent care. Methodology: Number of patients served, and quality of care received.

1855.description: The purpose of the requested funds is to restore and strengthen Captiva’s coastal resilience by revegetating storm- impacted dunes with diverse native species, improving dune stability, enhancing wildlife habitat, and reducing vulnerability to future hurricanes and erosion. It will also support replacement of invasive plants that were part of a strategic island wide removal.
1855.purpose: State funding would help revegetate Captiva’s storm-damaged dunes with diverse native plants. After Hurricanes Ian, Helene, and Milton, this vegetation is essential to stabilize sand, strengthen dune structure, speed recovery, and provide important wildlife habitat while improving long-term coastal resilience. It will also support replacement of invasive plants that were part of a strategic island wide removal.
1855.activities: The project will restore native dune habitat and replace invasive vegetation across approximately 24,000 linear feet of shoreline, increasing vegetative cover by at least 50%. This enhanced plant diversity will improve dune stability, reduce erosion, and create foraging and nesting habitat for shorebirds, pollinators, and other wildlife, resulting in a measurable increase in wildlife use and ecosystem function.
1855.direct_services: Revegetation stabilizes the dunes, helping them absorb storm surge and wave energy. This reduces erosion and lowers the risk of flooding and overwash, providing natural protection that helps keep the public, homes, and infrastructure more safe during hurricanes and severe weather.
1855.population: The residents and visitors of the island of Captiva are the target population. The island currently has over 300 full time residents and receives tens of thousands of visitors annually.
1855.outcome: The project will revegetate roughly 24,000 linear feet of shoreline, increasing vegetative cover by at least 50% and enhancing habitat for shorebirds, pollinators, and other wildlife. Benefits will be measured through vegetation monitoring, dune-elevation surveys, and wildlife observations to document ecological improvements and track dune stability over time

1988.description: SalusCare operates a recovery community in the heart of downtown Fort Myers. At any given time, more than 100 individuals can be beginning and maintaining their sobriety on this campus. The campus is near a park where homeless individuals are known to gather. The entire campus is currently totally open and unprotected. After consultation with the Ft. Myers Police Department, further security is needed to have a safe and drug-free campus.
1988.purpose: The residential campus will be safe and drug-free.
1988.activities: Accessible behavioral health treatment for adults in a safe and drug-free environment.
1988.direct_services: Accessible behavioral health treatment for adults in a safe and drug-free environment.
1988.population: Adults who are beginning or in recovery from substance use disorder and individuals with a co-occurring disorder. More than 400 individuals per year are served from this campus.
1988.outcome: We expect to have less incidents of vandalism, theft and potential violence. This will be measured by a reduction in incident reports and less police interaction.

1856.description: JA’s Pre-Apprenticeship Program prepares graduating high school seniors for employment and apprenticeship opportunities in high-demand industries. Over the past 3 years, 134 graduates have secured jobs or apprenticeships. State funds will support and expand the program in Broward, Lee and Collier Counties, serving 5 key industries: Maritime, Construction, Telecommunications, Water and Healthcare. These expansions address critical workforce shortages and help more students enter in-demand fields.
1856.purpose: The purpose of the requested funds is to support and expand Junior Achievement’s Pre-Apprenticeship Program for graduating high school seniors and young adults in Broward, Lee, and Collier Counties. The program prepares students for employment and apprenticeship opportunities in high-demand industries including Maritime, Construction, Telecommunications, Water, and Healthcare. The goal is to address workforce shortages while helping students transition directly into in-demand career pathways.
1856.activities: The pre-apprenticeship program provides 50 hours of employability skills and financial literacy instruction and 100 hours of technical, hands-on training. Activities include industry site visits, employer-led workshops, and instruction aligned with workforce certifications. Students also participate in career exploration and training designed to prepare them for entry-level employment or apprenticeships.
1856.direct_services: Direct services include workforce readiness training, career exploration, and hands-on technical instruction. Participants are provided opportunities to earn industry-recognized certifications such as OSHA-10, CPR/First Aid, Forklift, NCCER Core, and career-track–specific credentials. The program also connects students to employment interviews and paid job or apprenticeship opportunities.
1856.population: The target population includes economically disadvantaged and at-risk high school students and young adults ages 17–24. Services are provided primarily to students preparing to enter the workforce in Broward, Lee, and Collier Counties. The project is expected to serve between 201 and 400 participants during the fiscal year.
1856.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved workforce readiness, increased attainment of industry certifications, and placement into employment or apprenticeship opportunities. Outcomes will be measured using participant surveys, pre- and post-tests, attendance and completion records, and tracking of certifications earned. Employment placement and follow-up data are also used to assess program success.

2672.description: Establishes a hub to train future policymakers, civic leaders, and public service professionals. Produces 50 Civic Fellows annually with 85% placement in public service roles, generating a $2M annual impact in public sector innovation and workforce readiness, and a 3:1 return in statewide economic and social value through leadership development and civic engagement.
2672.purpose: The funds will establish the Civic Engagement Institute at Florida A&M University, a statewide hub for civic education, leadership training, and community engagement. The Institute will prepare students for public service careers, strengthen civic literacy, and expand Florida’s pipeline of policy and community leaders.
2672.activities: Funds will support development of a civic leadership curriculum, training for 50 student Civic Fellows each year, public policy and advocacy workshops, and monthly academic and civil discourse events across colleges and schools. The Institute will also host community forums and outreach programs that connect citizens to policymaking processes.
2672.direct_services: The Institute will offer hands-on training, policy education, and civic engagement opportunities to students and community members. Fellows will engage in service projects, assist in campus and community dialogue events, and partner with public agencies to advance community-informed decision-making.
2672.population: The project will serve students, small farmers, agribusiness professionals, and residents in underserved rural and urban areas across Florida. It is expected to directly benefit more than 800 individuals annually through research, training, and outreach initiatives.
2672.outcome: The project will serve Florida A&M University students, local residents, and community partners engaged in civic learning and leadership development. The Institute will train 50 Civic Fellows annually and reach more than 1,000 participants through workshops, public events, and community collaborations.

1944.description: The City of Mascotte requests funding for relocating its Public Works facility from its current flood-prone location, identified in a Resilient Florida Vulnerability Assessment and Adaptation Plan, to a safer site. This relocation will safeguard essential services, including water and sewer maintenance, roadway clearance, debris management, and emergency response coordination, while reducing risks from repetitive flooding. The new facility will also incorporate a workforce training area, strengthening regional emergency preparedness and disaster recovery capabilities.
1944.purpose: The goal is to relocate Mascotte’s Public Works facility from a flood-prone site to a safer location, ensuring uninterrupted delivery of essential municipal services, including water and sewer maintenance, roadway clearance, debris management, and emergency response coordination,
1944.activities: The funding will cover pre-construction activities, like planning, designing, and engineering, and construction of a new facility, including a workforce training area.
1944.direct_services: A workforce training area within the new Public Works facility will be a service provided to the citizens.
1944.population: The target population served by this project is all residents of Mascotte, population 6,609 as of the 2020 census, as well as residents within Lake County that rely on the emergency preparedness and disaster recovery assistance provided by Mascotte's Public Works.
1944.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is relocating the Public Works facility from its current flood-prone area, ensuring continuity of essential municipal services. The methodology to measure this outcome is to track the number of days essential services remain fully operational during storm events after relocation versus historical information about disruptions.

1945.description: Montverde requests funds to match existing local funds for the creation of its first ADA-compliant public park. This initiative will upgrade key recreational facilities with ADA-compliant features ensuring safe, equitable access for residents of all abilities. By removing physical barriers, the project promotes outdoor recreation, strengthens community connections, and supports long-term development. It aligns with the State's ongoing public health and safety goals by fostering outdoor physical activity and overall well-being. This project will allow the Town to strive for excellence in accessibility, meeting the standards established by the Americans with Disabilities Act and enhancing quality of life for all residents and visitors.
1945.purpose: Funds will be used to construct ADA-compliant features at the park ensuring safe, inclusive access for all users and to meet the standards established by the Americans with Disabilities Act.
1945.activities: Montverde’s first ADA-compliant park will help in fostering equitable access, community pride, and long-term development.
1945.direct_services: An ADA-accessible park in Montverde will directly provide safe, inclusive recreational opportunities for residents of all abilities, enabling access to outdoor activities, community events, and wellness programs that promote physical and mental well-being.
1945.population: The target population served by this project includes all residents and visitors who an require an ADA accessible outdoor area and their families and friends. The total population of Montverde is approximately 1,800.
1945.outcome: The project's benefit will be to create Montverde’s first ADA-compliant park, expanding safe and equitable access to recreational facilities, promoting physical and mental well-being, and strengthening community connections for residents of all abilities. The method by which it will be measured by tracking park usage before and after improvements.

2150.organization: Ferd & Gladys Alpert Jewish Family Service
2150.description: Funds will continue the CALL Service, which reaches 3,000 households each year. It is a centralized intake and referral program providing free comprehensive telephone assessments to identify the callers' needs and connect them with Alpert Jewish Family Services and/or other community programs. Master's degree level professionals provide customized referrals for mental health counseling, psychiatry services, food assistance, and specialized care for the vulnerable and in emergency situations.
2150.purpose: Funds will continue the CALL Service, which reaches 3,000 households each year. It is a centralized intake and referral program providing free comprehensive telephone assessments to identify the callers' needs and connect them with Alpert Jewish Family Services and/or other community programs. Master's degree level professionals provide customized referrals for mental health counseling, psychiatry services, food assistance, and specialized care for the vulnerable and in emergency situations.
2150.activities: The CALL Service is a centralized intake program with master’s level professionals who provide telephone-based assessments to identify the needs of the caller and quickly connect them with referrals to resources available in the community.
2150.direct_services: The CALL service provides a quick assessment and rapid response to ensure residents in need are connected with Alpert JFS services or other community resources to identify and locate mental health counseling and/or psychiatry, food assistance, waiting lists for affordable housing, specialized care for seniors, veterans, and people with disabilities, e.g., or help with various emergency situations.
2150.population: The CALL Service serves all demographics, including but not limited to all socio-economic populations: children, adults, seniors, Holocaust survivors, all religious affiliations, persons with disabilities, and, in many cases, working families with constraints of limited household income and personal assets. Anticipated impact through the CALL Service in AJFS' catchment area is 7,500 individuals.
2150.outcome: The CALL Service will rapidly connect people in emergency situations with needed community resources. Approximately 90% of callers receive call-backs with referrals within 24-48 hours. By addressing the caller's emergency need(s), depression, anxiety etc. are alleviated via rapid response and a workable, solution-oriented action plan crafted with the caller. The mental health of household members is improved immediately with increased access to a wide network of community resources. Alpert JFS maintains a comprehensive Performance Quality Improvement (PQI) program to evaluate success and continually improve outcomes. The PQI Director writes quarterly PQI Reports that summarize response time

1946.description: Montverde requests funds to assist in creating a continuous, safe pedestrian network that connects key destinations, including Montverde Academy, with the downtown area. By repairing deteriorated sidewalks, adding well-lit pathways, and installing clearly marked crosswalks, the project addresses critical safety concerns while promoting walkability and accessibility for all residents and visitors. These improvements align with the governor’s priorities of health, safety, and economic development, fostering a vibrant downtown that attracts businesses, boosts local commerce, and supports job growth. Backed by strong community support, this initiative will transform Montverde into a safer, more connected, and economically resilient community.
1946.purpose: The requested funds will be used to improve downtown connectivity and pedestrian safety by repairing sidewalks and improving pedestrian infrastructure to create safe, accessible routes for residents to the downtown area and for students traveling to Montverde Academy.
1946.activities: The project will include repairing and replacing deteriorated sidewalks and adding clearly marked crosswalks to ensure safe pedestrian routes. These activities will create a connected, walkable downtown that enhances safety for residents and students.
1946.direct_services: The direct services provided to citizens is to create a connected, walkable downtown that enhances safety for residents and students.
1946.population: The target population served by this project includes all residents and visitors to Montverde's downtown area. The total population of Montverde is approximately 1,800.
1946.outcome: The project's expected outcome will be to reduce pedestrian hazards, enhance safety, and encourage economic growth by attracting visitors and businesses, ultimately strengthening Montverde’s community vitality and quality of life. The method by which it will be measured by pedestrian traffic counts and analysis of local economic indicators such as business activity and visitor numbers before and after improvements.

2089.description: The Gadson Street Sidewalk & Trail project will add a new sidewalk/trail and lighting along Gadson Street from Parkwood Street to SR 50, supporting safer and healthier transportation options. The project incorporates important stormwater improvements, including a drainage swale on the west side of Gadson Street, which is necessary due to the expansion of impervious area within the FDOT right-of-way. The trail is routed along the east side, using parcel AltKey: 1437423, because constraints like utilities and city design standards limit placement options. The alignment is designed to swing around an existing utility pole and comply with buffer and width requirements, providing the needed connection to the SR 50 sidewalk while integra
2089.purpose: The specific purpose and goals to be achieved by the requested state funds are to construct critical infrastructure improvements along Gadson Street Trail. These funds will enable the installation of ADA-compliant sidewalks and walkways, enhanced stormwater management systems, and roadway upgrades. The project aims to improve pedestrian safety, increase accessibility, reduce flooding, and protect water quality in Lake David. Ultimately, the funds will support community revitalization, environmen
2089.activities: Construction of ADA-compliant walkways, installation of advanced stormwater management systems (such as bioretention areas, swales, and drainage structures), roadway reconstruction.These activities will improve pedestrian safety, accessibility, flood mitigation, and water quality, directly supporting community revitalization and environmental resilience within the project area. All work will be performed in compliance with state and federal grant requirements and will benefit low- to moderate-in
2089.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to citizens by constructing new ADA-compliant walkways for safer, more accessible pedestrian routes; improving stormwater management to reduce flooding and enhance water quality; upgrading roadways for better traffic flow and safety; and stabilizing the shoreline with native vegetation to protect the local environment. These improvements will
2089.population: The target population served by this project is the residents of the City of Groveland, specifically those living in the Gadson Street corridor. The project service area is comprised of greater than 51% low- to moderate-income individuals, ensuring the project primarily benefits these groups. The City of Groveland has a population of 18,505 (2020 Census), and while the exact number of individuals directly served will depend on the final project boundaries, the improvements are designed to benefi
2089.outcome: The project is expected to deliver safer, more accessible pedestrian routes, improved stormwater management to reduce flooding and enhance water quality, and upgraded roadways.. These outcomes will increase walkability, public safety, environmental resilience, and overall quality of life for residents, especially those in low- to moderate-income areas. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the completion of ADA-compliant sidewalks and walkways, the installation and performance of stormwater systems, and the reduction in localized flooding incidents. Additional metrics may include pre- and post-project pedestrian counts, resident satisfaction surveys, water quality testing in Lake David, and

1790.description: This project educates the public about exploitation and human trafficking by providing training and resources to staff, community members, and survivors. It will expand services by hiring additional staff to support more clients and strengthen community advocacy. Survivors will receive essential interpersonal skills and education programs, empowering them to rebuild their lives with guidance from trained and dedicated staff.
1790.purpose: The requested funds will directly expand our capacity to prevent human trafficking and support survivors. Funding will allow us to provide specialized training and educational resources to staff, community members, and vulnerable populations, strengthening public understanding of exploitation and how to respond safely. It will also support the hiring of additional trained personnel, enabling us to assist more clients through trauma-informed case management, advocacy, and community outreach. Surv
1790.activities: Activities and services funded through this project will include: Survivor Services: Case management, life-skills workshops, and access to mental-health therapy to promote healing and independence. Community Outreach: Educational presentations, events, and partnerships that increase awareness and prevent exploitation. Staff Training & Capacity: Targeted training for staff and hiring additional personnel to expand service delivery. Operational Support: Essential resources and tools that ensure ef
1790.direct_services: Direct services will include: Survivor Support with case management, life skills training, medical and mental health assistance, education support, and emergency aid; Youth Education through an updated app and outreach for trafficking prevention; Community Awareness via campaigns, events, and partnerships; and Enhanced Services with staff training and expanded access through new hires.
1790.population: The target population includes survivors of human trafficking and exploitation, vulnerable youth, community members, and frontline staff who benefit from prevention education and training. Through direct services, outreach, and training initiatives, the project is expected to serve more than 800 individuals over the funding period.
1790.outcome: Expected Benefit/Outcome: The project will expand our ability to prevent trafficking and support survivors by increasing trained staff, improving community education, and strengthening trauma-informed services. Survivors will gain essential life skills and stability, and the community will be better equipped to identify and respond to exploitation. Measurement Methodology: Track survivor progress (housing, life-skills, employment, case-management goals). Measure community education impact through training attendance and pre/post surveys. Monitor staff training completion and caseload capacity. Track total individuals reached through services and outreach. Success will be measured through pro

1820.description: The requested funds will support critical improvements to Bridge #876010, located at NE 18/SW 162 Avenue over the C-103 Canal in a rapidly developing and heavily traveled area of Homestead. Built in 1966 and deemed structurally deficient during a 2023 FDOT inspection, the bridge requires significant rehabilitation to meet current demand. The planned improvements will increase elevation, expand capacity to four travel lanes, and add sidewalks and bicycle lanes, improving long-term resilience.
1820.purpose: The requested funds will support critical improvements to Bridge #876010, located at NE 18/SW 162 Avenue over the C-103 Canal in a rapidly developing and heavily traveled area of Homestead. Built in 1966 and deemed structurally deficient during a 2023 FDOT inspection, the bridge requires significant rehabilitation to meet current demand. The planned improvements will increase elevation, expand capacity to four travel lanes, and add sidewalks and bicycle lanes, improving long-term resilience.
1820.activities: The activities and services include the construction needed to improve Bridge #876010 to accommodate the ongoing improvements at the SW 162nd/NE 18th Avenue corridor; upgrade roadway drainage and safety features; and deliver the infrastructure necessary to improve mobility and enhance multimodal access.
1820.direct_services: The requested funding will provide direct services to residents by improving the safety, functionality, and reliability of Bridge #876010. Enhancements to the bridge will support smoother traffic flow, strengthen structural performance, expand multimodal access for pedestrians and cyclists, and ensure a safer and more efficient crossing for all users in this growing community.
1820.population: This project serves the general public. The amount of individuals expected to be served is > 800.
1820.outcome: The bridge improvements will improve transportation by widening the bridge to four lanes, raising its elevation, and adding sidewalks and bike lanes to enhance mobility and safety. The benefit will be measured by analyzing traffic flow data, monitoring reductions in congestion and travel delays, tracking pedestrian and cyclist usage, and evaluating accident reports post-construction.

1965.description: This project will deliver 18 affordable housing units in Belle Glade, an under served community with limited housing options and high socioeconomic need. By pairing housing with up skilling and credentialed training, residents will gain access to living-wage careers, fostering financial stability and personal wealth. This holistic approach strengthens families, reduces poverty, and expands Palm Beach County’s tax base, driving long-term economic growth and community revitalization.
1965.purpose: Complete additional affordable housing units to increase the inventory of units in Belle Glade. Once completed and the units are occupied, providing supportive services, and educational and training opportunities to a low income community. It will increase personal wealth, generational wealth and lead to an increase in Florida's GDP and tax revenue.
1965.activities: Complete additional affordable housing units to increase the inventory of units in Belle Glade. Once completed and the units are occupied, providing supportive services, and educational and training opportunities to a low income community. It will increase personal wealth, generational wealth and an increase in Florida's GDP and tax revenue.
1965.direct_services: This funding request will increase affordable housing units for the citizens of Belle Glade, Florida. This region is in dire need of affordable units.
1965.population: 25-50 individuals will be served initially by these units. The target population is economically disadvantaged persons, the elderly, those who are unemployed or struggle to find affordable housing options in the area.
1965.outcome: Through the provision of affordable housing and connection of residents to support services for education, job readiness training, employment opportunities, and workforce training the project will improve economic self-sufficiency, increase economic activity, and improve the mental health of residents.

2498.description: The Starkey Road Basin Watershed Management Plan, completed in 2012, identified improvements designed to provide flood control and water quality benefits. This project is a combination of three recommended improvements identified in the study.The project is predicted to significantly reduce road flooding and eliminate structure flooding within the area. The flood mitigation measures will also reduce sediments, debris, nutrients, toxic materials, and pathogens carried into connecting channels and waterways and results in critical water quality benefits for Long Bayou.
2498.purpose: The goal of the project is to mitigate flood risk to homes and businesses and improve water quality in the Starkey Road Basin.
2498.activities: The project proposes upgrading the culverts and ditches at Starkey Road on Channel 10 near the East Bay Oaks Mobile Home Community and at Lake Palms Drive on Channel 10. The project also proposes to construct new storm pipe and structures between the Dahlia Place and Gardenia Place roadway cul-de-sacs and regrade the south-flowing tributary ditch to expand the bottom width and recreate a positive ditch bottom gradient for connection to Channel 10.
2498.direct_services: No direct services will be provided to citizens.
2498.population: No individual services will be provided with the requested funds.
2498.outcome: The expected outcome of the project is significant flood risk reduction in the Starkey Road Basin as well as improved water quality for Long Bayou. Re-evaluation of flood risk and monitoring of water quality will be used to measure the outcome of the project.

2499.description: The Allens Creek Basin Watershed Management Plan, completed in 2013, identified improvements designed to provide flood control and water quality benefits. The project is predicted to significantly reduce road flooding and eliminate structure flooding within the area. The project will also reduce sediments, debris, nutrients, toxic materials, and pathogens carried into nearby waterways and Old Tampa Bay and results in substantial water quality benefits.
2499.purpose: The purpose of the project is to significantly reduce flood risk to homes in the Allens Creek Basin and improve water quality in Old Tampa Bay.
2499.activities: Installation of larger pipes and culverts and addition of pipes to run parallel to current infrastructure in order to mitigate flooding along St. Paul's Drive, Bellair Road, and Deville Drive.
2499.direct_services: No direct services will be provided to citizens.
2499.population: No individuals will be served by the project.
2499.outcome: The expected benefit of the project will be significant flood risk reduction to homes in the Allens Creek Basin, particularly along St. Paul's Drive, Deville Drive, and Bellair Road, and reduction of sediments and toxins flowing into Old Tampa Bay via Allens Creek. Re-evaluation of flood risk and ongoing water quality monitoring will be used to measure the outcome of the project.

2101.description: This high impact tutoring program strengthens Florida's most hard to reach students in rural schools by training and paying top college students to deliver high-impact tutoring that boosts literacy and numeracy. We are targeting the rural districts of Gadsden, Jefferson, Wakulla and surrounding areas. Tutors earn up to $2,400, and gain classroom experience. They often go on to become teachers within our network, creating a powerful now-and-later strategy to raise student achievement and build the next generation of Florida educators. This project will support an increase in workforce development and experience for our next generation of college graduates.
2101.purpose: Our goal is to train/hire college students to earn up to $2400 and gain classroom experience. They often go on to become teachers within our network, creating a powerful now-and-later strategy to raise student achievement and build the next generation of Florida educators. As a result of improving workforce development for college students, K-12 students will improve in literacy and numeracy through high impact tutoring.
2101.activities: The state allocation will support High Impact Tutoring training and direct tutoring services for K12 students in high needs rural areas: Gadsden, Jefferson, Wakulla, Alachua and surrounding areas. Funds will be used to recruit, train, and pay college students and aspiring educators to deliver consistent, high-quality tutoring sessions that strengthen literacy and numeracy outcomes for students in need.
2101.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide High Impact Tutoring for K12 students focused on improving reading and mathematics skills. These services will directly support college students receive income while in school and simultaneously support students literacy and numeracy growth, ensuring they receive consistent, data-driven academic support throughout the school year.
2101.population: This project will serve K12 students, particularly those in under-resourced or hard-to-staff areas, by providing consistent academic support through High Impact Tutoring. It will also benefit college students and young adults seeking employment, offering them paid opportunities to work with at-risk youth while gaining skills and exposure to the education profession. The project is expected to serve over 500 of K12 students and engage dozens of college-aged tutors across participating regions.
2101.outcome: Outcomes will be measured through student progress monitoring data, including improvements in reading and math benchmark assessments, attendance and engagement metrics, and tutor participation and retention rates. Additionally, surveys and follow-up tracking will assess how many tutors pursue careers in education, demonstrating the programs impact on workforce development.

1788.description: The City of Homestead needs these funds to establish a Joint Operations Center (JOC) that will serve federal, state, and local public agencies. No such venue currently exists in the south Miami-Dade County region, making coordination between public safety agencies during local critical incidents difficult. The region is growing rapidly through increasing development and population numbers, making this area increasingly vulnerable to natural and man-made threats.
1788.purpose: The City of Homestead needs these funds to establish a Joint Operations Center (JOC) that will serve federal, state, and local public agencies. No such venue currently exists in the south Miami-Dade County region, making coordination between public safety agencies during local critical incidents difficult. The region is growing rapidly through increasing development and population numbers, making this area increasingly vulnerable to natural and man-made threats.
1788.activities: Homestead serves the surrounding communities and is located 30+ miles from the county's operations center. Homestead requires a fully capable fixed/permanent JOC rather than the current "pop-up-style” EOC operation. This will reduce response times, ensure the coordination and unity of effort among multiple emergency management organizations, agencies and jurisdictions.
1788.direct_services: Coordinated preparedness, response, and recovery operations that will assist area residents during disasters. This includes first responder assistance, relief supply coordination, early warning, border security, and information gathering/sharing.
1788.population: This project will help the general public by way of first responder assistance and disaster mitigation/recovery, among many other features. The project will expect to serve > 800.
1788.outcome: Ability to coordinate first responder assistance, relief supply delivery, early warning dissemination, border security operations, and information gathering/sharing. Number of lives saved, properties protected, limited or no fatalities/injuries, quantity of relief supplies delivered, number of public information notices disseminated.

1984.description: The Country Club Drive / Aventura Mall Roadway and Stormwater Resilience Improvement Project is essential for enhancing roadway infrastructure in a high-traffic corridor. It addresses nonpoint source pollution from impervious roadway surfaces, manages flooding to prevent traffic disruptions, and ensures compliance with environmental regulations while safeguarding nearby water bodies. By strengthening stormwater management along this key economic artery, the project supports roadway sustainability, prevents costly pavement damage from water infiltration, reduces hydroplaning risks for vehicles, and aligns with state transportation policy priorities for resilient, flood-resistant roads.
1984.purpose: Design integrated roadway-stormwater treatment systems to reduce nonpoint source pollution from vehicle traffic, achieving annual reductions of 217 lbs total nitrogen and 67 lbs total phosphorus, while enhancing roadway safety through flood mitigation and ensuring regulatory compliance to protect environmental resources and traffic flow.
1984.activities: Site assessment of roadway impervious areas; public and water quality testing along traffic corridors; engineering design for roadway solutions (e.g., bioswales adjacent to lanes, permeable pavements for safer driving surfaces); public engagement on traffic impacts and signage for construction zones.
1984.direct_services: Safer, more reliable roadway access through reduced flooding and hydroplaning risks; enhanced water quality protects public health by minimizing contamination in roadside ditches and reducing pest breeding in standing water near travel lanes.
1984.population: General public, including Aventura residents (~40,000) and Aventura Mall visitors (~30 million annually).
1984.outcome: Improved roadway resilience, reduced traffic disruptions from flooding, and enhanced environmental quality; measured via pre/post water sampling along road edges, Best Management Practice (BMP) efficiency assessments for pavement integration, traffic safety audits (e.g., incident rate reductions), and annual reports on pollutant and flood event decreases.

The project is specifically designed to address Aventura’s unique needs, including the protection of the Aventura Mall—one of the nation’s largest retail destinations—and enhanced security for local synagogues and other places of worship. 2534.description: The project is to resurface two roads in West Kendall, SW 26th Street from SW 142nd Avenue to SW 147th Avenue, and SW 42nd Street from SW 142nd Avenue to SW 147th Avenue.
2534.purpose: The area described has been identified by the Miami-Dade County as in need of resurfacing and other improvements.
2534.activities: The project is to resurface two roads in West Kendall, SW 26th Street from SW 142nd Avenue to SW 147th Avenue, and SW 42nd Street from SW 142nd Avenue to SW 147th Avenue.
2534.population: Residents of the West Kendall area, as well as anyone else who travels in the area, will be served by resurfaced roads.

1785.description: Miami-Dade Fire (MDFR) will purchase an All Hazards Emergency Support Trailer to effectively support field operations with modern and reliable technology that enables communications in emergency situations. The trailer will replace the department’s existing 20-year-old tactical communications trailer that has obsolete and inoperable communications systems that do not meet the department's operational needs. Acquiring a new trailer will enable the department to operate safely, efficiently, and flexibly, enhancing its ability to respond to diverse incidents throughout the county and the state.
1785.purpose: The goal of this project is to strengthen MDFR's ability to respond to both natural and man-made disasters that directly impact the safety and well-being of the community at the local, regional, and state levels. The All Hazards Emergency Support trailer will contain mission-ready computer systems to ensure real-time communication, data management, and technical support in the field. Additional equipment on the trailer will enable the Tactical Communications Bureau to diagnose and repair crucial
1785.activities: The funds will be used to purchase and outfit an all hazards emergency support trailer that will enable interagency collaboration during large-scale incidents. Currently, MDFR has an outdated 20-year old communications trailer, where the original communications components are obsolete and incompatible with current systems. The new trailer will support real-time communications, data management, and field-based technical support while housing Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) and a diagnos
1785.direct_services: After implementing this project, citizens will benefit from improved interagency communication and response to threats and emergencies and will receive an overall more cohesive approach to emergency operations as a result of reliable and consistent communications systems. Aside from mission-ready computer systems, the all hazards emergency support trailer will also provide field-based technical su
1785.population: This project will benefit the general population in Miami-Dade County of more than 2 million people as it will improve overall emergency response throughout the region to navigate a wide range of complex threats. This trailer will enable real-time data management and technical support. By improving interoperability and on-site technical capabilities, this trailer will ensure MDFR and its regional, state, and federal partners can easily communicate with each other and respond swiftly and effectiv
1785.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to improve interoperability amongst South Florida First Responder agencies. The trailer will be equipped with technology and communications equipment to support essential interoperable communication systems including radios, satellite links, and emergency lighting during field operations. It can be deployed to support Specialized Response Teams, neighboring fire departments, and mutual aid partners for large- scale emergencies, making it a regional asset for multi-agency response. The improved interoperability can be measured by the coordination and response provided when a large scale event occurs and requires multiple agencies for a unified command.

2054.description: This project will use five separate and distinct non-profit organizations to provide hands on face-to-face mentoring for 125-150 high school age students in grades 9-12 and introduce the students to high wage careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.
2054.purpose: The funds will be used to provide mentoring and programmatic services to high school teens, grades 9-11, mentoring services, and introduction to processionals in the Science, Technology, Engineering and Math areas, and to expose, introduce and make high school teens aware of career opportunities in Technology, Science, Engineering, Vocational Careers and the United States Military.
2054.activities: Mentoring and life coaching skills and services will be provided to 150-200 high school age teens, including field trips, personal contact and mentoring by S.T.E.M. professionals and seminars, workshops and presentations that introduce and make the high school teens aware of the plethora of careers in the S.T.E.M. workplace via college, vo-tech schools, apprenticeships and United States Military.
2054.direct_services: Mentoring and life coaching skills and services will be provided to 150-200 high school age teens, including field trips, personal contact and mentoring by S.T.E.M. professionals and seminars, workshops and presentations that introduce and make the high school teens aware of the plethora of careers in the S.T.E.M. workplace via college, vo-tech schools, apprenticeships and United States Military.

2054.outcome: 125 - 150 students will be mentored and exposed to a multitude and plethora of careers in S.T.E.M. through bi-weekly workshops, field trips and exposure to stem careers and stem professionals.

2151.description: Treasure Coast Wildlife Center (TCWC), located in Palm City, Florida, serves primarily Martin County, as well as seven surrounding counties across the Treasure Coast region. Situated on 300 acres of beautiful South Florida wildlands, TCWC provides critical wildlife rescue, rehabilitation, and education services that support both local ecosystems and the broader community. Each year, TCWC cares for approximately 3,000 injured, orphaned, or displaced wild animals—a number that continues to grow annually. we are seeking funding to support and expand the operations of our Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. This investment will allow us to strengthen and reorganize our facilities, education department, and operations team to better serve our expanding community and the increasing number of animals in need.
2151.purpose: The requested funding will support our ongoing operations and enable the completion of the expansion and renovation of our Education Department, educational exhibits, and Education Center. The Treasure Coast Wildlife Center provides a diverse range of educational programs, interactive exhibits, and hands-on learning experiences—including insights into wildlife rehabilitation. These programs are designed to engage a wide range of individuals and provide broad accessibility and learning for all.
2151.activities: The Treasure Coast Wildlife Center is a dynamic educational facility offering interactive experiences aimed at deepening understanding of native Florida wildlife, aimed at engaging and inspiring individuals to take an active role in conserving our vital natural resources. The Center serves as an education hub and provides residents and visitors opportunities to engage with Florida wildlife.
2151.direct_services: The Treasure Coast Wildlife Center provides valuable benefits to the local community by offering public access to the Education Center during operational hours, including weekends. Visitors will have the opportunity to engage with a wealth of information on native inland wildlife species and environmental conservation, fostering a deeper understanding of the region’s natural resources.
2151.population: The residents of the Treasure Coast, all of Florida and all visitors to Florida.
2151.outcome: The benefit will be greater education to the public at large, but namely preschool students, grade school students, high school students, and university students. The success will be measured by the quality of events hosted at the new Education Center.

1783.description: My Childhood Cancer Navigator (formerly SebastianStrong Foundation Childhood Cancer Hope Navigator) provides support through a team of navigators who serve as a concierge resource for families and pediatric cancer hospitals. The team helps families understand treatment options, clinical research, and available resources. The team also addresses emotional, logistical, and financial challenges from diagnosis through survivorship and bereavement.
1783.purpose: The funds will support My Childhood Cancer Navigator, a statewide program that provides families facing childhood cancer with a real time concierge team that helps them understand treatment options, clinical research, and available resources. The program reduces barriers to care by offering one to one guidance on emotional, logistical, financial, and educational challenges from diagnosis through survivorship and bereavement.
1783.activities: A childhood cancer health navigator provides essential support from diagnosis through survivorship and bereavement by coordinating care, assisting with insurance and financial aid, connecting families with emotional and psychosocial support, educating on treatment options and clinical trials, guiding access to resources, and helping families navigate the healthcare system.
1783.direct_services: Coordinating care, assisting with insurance and financial aid, arranging transportation and lodging, connecting families with emotional and psychosocial support, educating on treatment options, guiding access to clinical trials and resources, and providing support for school accommodations as well as caregiver and sibling specific needs.
1783.population: Children with cancer or in survivorship, their caregivers, and siblings, and bereaved caregivers and siblings. >800 individuals expected to be served.
1783.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health outcomes for children with cancer by helping families understand treatment plans, clinical trials, and available support while reducing delays caused by logistical, financial, or communication barriers. It will improve access to education by assisting with continued learning during treatment, school accommodations, and reintegration. Outcomes will be measured through program documentation that tracks individuals served, services delivered, treatment-related education provided by the nurse navigator, emotional support offered, barriers resolved, school-related assistance completed, and the completion of referrals to counseling, peer programs

1801.description: The purpose of the proposed project is to implement the final stage of the Gadsden County Emergency Operations Center and Public Safety Complex Project to include the Emergency Operations Center, E911 Office, 911 Communications Center and Sheriff’s Office Law Enforcement and Administrative offices. The requested amount to complete the final stage of this project is $750,000. The requested funds are critically needed to provide, furnishings, IT/Communications and Audiovisual equipment necessary to operate the new facility.
1801.purpose: Funding will be used to implement the final stage of the Gadsden County Public Safety Complex, which includes the Emergency Operations Center (EOC), Communications Center and Sheriff's Office. The requested amount to complete the final stage of this project is $750,000. The requested funds are critically needed to provide, furnishings, IT/Communications and Audiovisual equipment necessary to operate the new facility.
1801.activities: The provision of disaster and emergency related activities and services that are normally associated with and provided by EOCs across the nation and those unique to Gadsden County. It will also provide a dedicated, unified EOC Command Center, E911 Office, 911 Communication Center and law enforcement for all disaster and emergency planning, response and recovery activity for Gadsden County.
1801.direct_services: All emergency and disaster planning, recovery, and response activities will be coordinated and implemented under one roof to include those of law enforcement, fire/EMS, and emergency management. This will ensure emergency and disaster related services, activities, communication, and information needs are conducted in a cohesive and timely manner to citizens, visitors, businesses, and partners.
1801.population: Provides 24/7 services to all citizens, businesses and visitors of Gadsden County.
1801.outcome: The EOC and Public Safety Complex will provide an efficient coordinated emergency response to natural or manmade disasters that affect citizens, businesses and visitors of Gadsden County. It will improve law enforcement and fire/ EMS response time and quality of life. The project will also improve the coordination, collaboration and training efforts of local first responders. This will be measured by increased efficiencies and effectiveness of emergency response through training, exercises and real event responses. The construction of a new EOC and public safety complex provides a multi-purpose facility which consolidates staffing of communications, law enforcement, fire and EMS to provide e

1786.description: Establishment of a disaster recovery facility in Gadsden County, strategically positioned within Talquin's service area. This facility will serve as a hub for processing mutual aid crews during storms, providing essential services such as lodging, meals, vehicle fueling, and laundry facilities for external utility crews engaged in disaster response. Its location provides the ability to provide assistance to crews deployed statewide to address natural disasters.
1786.purpose: The funds will support Talquin in establishing a disaster recovery facility in Gadsden County, strategically positioned within our service area.
1786.activities: This facility will serve as a hub for processing mutual aid crews during storms, providing essential services such as lodging, meals, vehicle fueling, and laundry facilities for external utility crews engaged in disaster response. Its location provides the ability to provide assistance to crews deployed statewide to address natural disasters.
1786.direct_services: The establishment of this facility will enhance Talquin's capacity to safely and swiftly restore electric, water, and wastewater services in the aftermath of a natural disaster.
1786.population: All persons living in Gadsden County and the surrounding areas, which is a high-poverty and high-minority area.
1786.outcome: This facility will support the swift restoration of essential utility services, provide essential support to mutual aid crews arriving from out of town, and enhance Talquin's capacity to safely and swiftly restore electric, water, and wastewater services in the aftermath of a natural disaster.

1829.description: This project would include the replacement of manually-read water meters with remotely-read smart water meters. This project is to attempt to move the City of Bristol to utilize a more modern and efficient way of collecting water meter readings. This will reduce the manpower required to manually read meters and will allow the small City staff to spend more time on maintenance issues. Furthermore, the new meter technology can assist with the detection of leaks quicker which can reduce water losses for both the City and residents.
1829.purpose: These remotely-read meters will reduce man hours required in the field for meter reading so staff can spend more time on maintenance of the water system. The meter technology under this proposal provides continuous customer data and allows for early detection of water leaks/loss. The system will also provide the city with operational detail such peak flows for each customer. The system will also reduce revenue loss from inaccurate metering.
1829.activities: Design and construction of remotely-read meter system to help the City reduce costs associated with water leaks. Project will also help the City conserve water by assisting with early identification of leaks. The increased efficiency in meter reading will allow for the limited City staff to prioritize efforts on system maintenance and improvements.
1829.direct_services: New meters will be provided to all citizens connected to the Bristol public water system. As a result of these improvements the accuracy of the meters will be improved and early leak detection will be provided. This will allow the City to accurately bill the customers for true water usage while reducing the losses down stream of the meters.
1829.population: This project will benefit the entire City of Bristol, approximately 915 individuals.
1829.outcome: The proposed project will allow the City of Bristol to more closely monitor water usages and reduce the amount of unaccounted for water losses. Early leak detection will allow the City to reduce unnecessary groundwater withdraws. The City provides reports to the WMD regarding water losses. The volume of unaccounted for losses is expected to decrease as a result of this project.

2113.organization: The Florida Center for Early Childhood, Inc.
2113.description: Early Childhood Court (ECC) is a specialized court model serving infants and young children, ages 0-6 (extended to 10 in special circumstances), who have experienced removal from their families due to abuse and/or neglect. When families with at least one child under the age of five enter the dependency system, parents are offered the choice between participating in ECC or the traditional dependency process. The program recognizes the importance of early, intensive, and trauma-informed intervention during children’s formative years. Key features include a multidisciplinary team approach, specialized court proceedings, parental supports and services, early developmental and mental health interventions, and coordinated, relationship-based care. Program expansion this year increases staff capacity to serve sibling groups and children up to age 10, ensuring more families receive timely, compr
2113.purpose: Funds will support the ECC program in improving access, service quality, and achieving timely permanency for young children. Goals include: serving a minimum of 40 families annually through expanded staffing capacity; achieving permanency 20% faster than for non-program children; reducing recidivism by at least 9% compared to non-program participants; ensuring 98% of enrolled children/families have no re-abuse/neglect. Includes ability to serve sibling to age 10, improving family stability.
2113.activities: Intensive case management, child-parent psychotherapy, therapeutic consultation, supervised visitation, transportation, and crisis intervention for children and families. Monthly judicial review hearings ensure coordinated care and timely permanency. Increased family capacity, reduced wait times for therapy, and the ability to serve older siblings to preserve family unity.
2113.direct_services: Case management services, child-parent psychotherapy, therapeutic consultation with foster parents, teachers, other caregivers, child/foster parent transportation, supervised visitation, crisis intervention services for children, foster/adoptive parents and birth parents.
2113.population: Target populations include: persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, at-risk youth, developmentally disabled, drug users, preschool students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, victims of crime. Number of children to be served are between 51-100.
2113.outcome: Outcome 1- All children enrolled in the program will receive medical care, as needed, and all immunizations will be received on time. Methodology: Case manager will document all medical issues, doctor visits and dates of immunizations. Outcome 2- Child will resolve trauma related abuse and/or neglect and removal from home with improved coping skills. Methodology: Child trauma checklist completed at enrollment and every three months while in program. Outcome 3- Parent(s) will resolve underlying trauma and improve parent-child relationship. Methodology: Parent trauma checklist and Parent-Child Quality Relationship Scale completed at enrollment and every three months while enrolled in program.

These more than 50 programs and 10 schools offer 13 distinct sports, providing diverse and meaningful opportunities for youth to participate and grow. These programs are annually reaching over 15,000 Pinellas County children, giving young people the opportunity to experience the value of being part of something larger than themselves while developing the foundational skills and values that will guide them through the next phases of their lives. CFY Pinellas utilizes attendance at a Pinellas County Schools Title 1 elementary or middle school as a key indicator of need, helping ensure that cost, access, and safe equipment are never financial barriers to participation.
1792.purpose: CFY Pinellas supports over 15,000 youth from 7,000 families across Pinellas County, with a focus on students from Title 1 schools. The organization's goal is to remove obstacles to participation in youth athletics and water safety programs, ensuring every child can join a team in a safe and inclusive environment. CFY’s strategy involves breaking down financial barriers related to access, safety, and transportation, particularly for children in Title 1 schools. Participation in youth athletics an
1792.activities: CFY is dedicated to providing equal access for all by empowering under-resourced organizations and teams throughout the county, allowing every child the chance to play, participate, and thrive. Since 2021, CFY has expanded its supported program network from 11 to 50 and currently covers 13 different types of sports, ensuring a wide variety of opportunities for young athletes across the county.
1792.direct_services: To remove obstacles to participation in youth athletics and water safety programs in Pinellas County, ensuring every child can join a team in a safe and inclusive environment. CFY’s strategy involves breaking down financial barriers related to access, safety, and transportation, particularly for children in Title 1 schools.
1792.population: CFY Pinellas supports over 15,000 youth from 7,000 families across Pinellas County, with a focus on students from Title 1 schools.
1792.outcome: Participation in youth athletics and water safety programs transform young lives, build character, foster resilience, and strengthen communities. Despite these benefits, many children in Pinellas County still lack access to these essential programs. CFY is dedicated to providing equal access for all by empowering under-resourced organizations and teams throughout the county, allowing every child the chance to play, participate, and thrive.

1868.description: The requested funds will expand access and availability of high-fidelity wraparound (HFW) services to support families with children experiencing a behavioral health crisis. Children facing a crisis often encounter delays between the start of the crisis and the initiation of crisis-response services. These delays are caused by limited access or availability, stigma related to behavioral health issues, and inconsistent “warm hand-offs” across providers. Such delays often result in an increased need for higher-level services, such as emergency room visits, CSU, or DJJ programs. Family peer support with High-Fidelity Wraparound enhances engagement and decreases delays in diagnosis and treatment. HFW is a structured, team-based approach involving families, providers, and natural supports to keep everyone connected and involved in the decision-making. The program provides early intervention t
1868.purpose: The requested funds will support services for families with children aged 12 to 17 who are undergoing a behavioral crisis. Community Care for Families (CCF) helps these children and their families achieve stability, safety, and better emotional well-being. CCF is a partnership between the Florida Center for Early Childhood and NAMI Sarasota and Manatee Counties. The Florida Center offers strong clinical expertise, while NAMI provides extensive experience in peer support. The program will address
1868.activities: An individualized team plan tailored to the child and family includes: Engagement (orientation, crisis stabilization, strengths and needs, engagement), Planning (team plan, crisis plan), Implementation (focused on building trust and logistics, updating the plan as needed), and Transition (transferring skills to youth and family, planning for case closure, and follow-up after graduation). Using HFW, a family or parent peer contacts the family within 24 hours to stabilize the situation, using clin
1868.direct_services: A four-part approach helps youth and families learn how to access resources and seek help from others to overcome their challenges. The program’s components are 1) youth and family prioritize needs, 2) natural supports, 3) integrated planning, 4) self-efficacy. High fidelity wraparound, an evidence-based practice, collaborates with families and youth to develop cohesive, personalized support plans
1868.population: The target population includes families and youth aged 12 to 17 at risk in Sarasota, Manatee, and DeSoto counties. There has been a significant rise in at-risk youth entering out-of-home care due to parental inability to cope or willful abandonment. These youth are facing behavioral health crises, and high-fidelity wraparound services intervene early, ideally before the youth requires more costly care. We expect to serve up to 200 youth and families. Youth may be referred by any individual or or
1868.outcome: Teens in crisis and their families achieve stability, safety, and improved emotional well-being within 12 months. Seventy percent of families will experience these improvements, along with a reduction in needs that hinder functioning and an increase in family strengths. Additional goals include a decrease of five or more points in the life functioning domain score within six months of enrollment. The methodology used is the CANS (Child and Adolescent Needs and Strengths). High-fidelity wraparound benefits include increased permanency and stability, decreased residential restrictiveness, improved behavioral and mental health, better academic and early care outcomes, fewer safety issues, and s

1869.description: The Bradenton Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) is currently permitted for 9MGD using advanced treatment and high- level disinfection to produce reuse quality water. While the bulk of this water is sold as reclaimed water the remainder is currently discharged to the Manatee River. To replace this with a more productive use, the City has designed and constructed an underground injection well, which sends the excess water over 1,600 feet below the ground surface. This provides three-fold benefits of improving water quality at the Manatee River, recharging the state’s groundwater resources, and combating saltwater intrusion. The well drilling phase of the project was completed this year and design of the pump station to integrate the aquifer recharge well into the existing treatment process is well underway. This application is for partial funding of the construction of the pumping facility
1869.purpose: The projects primary goal is to provide a rise in the elevation of the potentiometric groundwater surface of the Upper Floridan aquifer to help restore aquifer levels in the Most Impacted Area within the Southern Water Use Caution Area (SWUCA). The AR well will also benefit by reducing nutrient loading to the lower Tampa Bay Estuary.
1869.activities: Injection of treated effluent has several positive environmental impacts, a reduction of the total nitrogen load to the Manatee River, thereby reducing conditions that are favorable for algae blooms as well as reinforcing the salinity barrier in the aquifer to mitigate salt water intrusion into the water supply.
1869.direct_services: Direct services are an alternative disposal method to river discharge during wet weather conditions when reuse water consumption is low helping to improve water quality in the Manatee River.
1869.population: The City of Bradenton residents as well as the tourists and residents throughout western Manatee County. The project serves to improve water quality, a total nitrogen load reduction, to the Manatee River; the rive represents approximately 25% of the tourism economy in the County.
1869.outcome: The nutrient load reduction, approximately 15 tons per year of nitrogen, is the primary visible benefit of the project and will be measured through regular sampling events in the river. The less visible, but equally as important benefit, is the protective measures provided in the aquifer to reinforce the salinity barrier to keep salt water intrusion from reaching potable water wells in the County.

1802.description: Currently there are over 3,000 residents living off unmaintained roads in Leon County as well as 90% of 96.9sq mi. having no hydrants. These residents as well as many we help through mutual aid with surrounding counties during natural disasters have limited to no access with a standard fire engine. The goal of the mini-pumper is to allow a large pump (1250 gpm) to gain access and to relay water down the long distance to the main road by tankers to allow protection of life and property by cutting down on response times without compromising output of resources. Currently the truck is loaned to the department from the Fire Chief's family business, since we could not find a fire truck to fit into the station (26 feet). The current truck is a 1986 GMC with manual shift. The current size for fire trucks are 30-35 feet long, 10-12 feet tall and the station is the size of a two bay home garage t
1802.purpose: To have an apparatus that can reach hard to get to or non-accessible areas, homes, and residents by a standard engine. To expand the station to allow for exhaust ventilation to reduce possible carcinogens, able to hold a current NFPA fire apparatus, and add an air compressor for our breathing apparatus.
1802.activities: The mini-pumper will be able to not only gain access where standard fire engines cannot but also allow the same type of pump through a relay system to provide the water necessary to save life and property. Provide a side room for safe storage of gear and firefighters out of the bay, to reduce exhaust and therefore carcinogens, and have an air compressor for our breathing air.
1802.direct_services: Fire and medical protection for the over 3,000 residences in the rural part of Leon County alone as well as more in surrounding counties that we provide mutual aid to during natural disasters/ calls for assistance. Also will have a functioning fire station to be used for drop off points during disasters. Health and safety of firefighters through safer apparatus and reduced carcinogens The firefigh
1802.population: The main target population that we directly serve is about 7,271 citizens within 96 square miles of northeast Leon County. Many within the areas that require this apparatus have wood-framed homes, are econimally disadvantaged by lack of general funds, insurances, and many fall within physical/mental disability as well as elderly.
1802.outcome: Currently, we sit at a 3/3x Insurance Services Office (ISO) and about a 15 minute response from the beginning of many of the dirt roads to the end of the road. The goal will include increasing ISO rating to lower homeowner's insurance premiums as well as access to areas currently not reachable by standard engines. Safer conditions through safer apparatus and reduced carcinogens.The project can be measured through updated air compressor from the current 3.2 cfm model as well as going from a one room bay to a multi-room bay that allows for the reduction in exhaust inhalation/transfer to gear.

2116.description: The City of Bradenton is requesting state funding to replace the Bradenton Police Department’s outdated Computer- Aided Dispatch (CAD) system with a modern, fully integrated platform. The current system is technologically obsolete and limits the department’s ability to coordinate efficiently with fire and emergency medical services. A new CAD system will improve emergency response times, enhance officer safety, and strengthen interoperability among regional public safety agencies. The upgraded system will include advanced mapping, real-time unit tracking, and full compatibility with Next Generation 911 standards. This investment will ensure reliable and secure communication during critical incidents and major emergencies. 1823.description: The Miami-Dade Water and Sewer Department (WASD) is upgrading the wastewater treatment plant with a molecular sieve system, which will make operations safer, cheaper, and more reliable. The current system is aging, prone to costly breakdowns, and requires annual shutdowns that waste time and money. The new equipment eliminates these problems by removing harmful contaminants before they can damage the system, saving millions over time while ensuring a steady, high-quality oxygen supply for wastewater treatment. The new system extends the plant's useful life by 20-30 years.
