1823.activities: The funds will be spent on the purchasing of a new molecular sieve system for Miami-Dade County's regional wastewater treatment plant.
1823.direct_services: This project will provide residents with improved wastewater service reliability, reduce disruptions and flooding risks, and strengthen public health and neighborhood resilience through modernized infrastructure.
1823.population: Residents of Miami-Dade County, benefiting more than 2.8 million people, including the local community within the project area.
1823.outcome: The project enhances the County's wastewater treatment plant, reducing operational expenses and preventing costly emergency interventions funded by rate-payer dollars. This upgrade safeguards critical infrastructure, ensuring uninterrupted wastewater treatment that protects public health, preserves environmental quality, and supports sustainable community growth. Program effectiveness will be evaluated through comparative analysis of pre- and post- upgrade operating budgets to quantify annual cost savings and long-term financial benefits.

2621.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2621.description: Epic-Cure Inc. is requesting $600,000 to construct a dock-height foundation and loading bay for the 10,550 square foot Food Security Distribution Center in St. Augustine, Saint Johns County, Florida. Epic-Cure has (a) secured $2.0 million of the required $3.6 million for the completion of the Center, (b) purchased the land for the facility, and is in the Entitlements and Permitting phase of construction with an expectation that it will be shovel ready by April 2025. With major food banks cutting back operations, and as the USDA eliminates programs, the construction of the dock height foundation and loading bay will permit semi tractor trailers to safely and efficiently deliver bulk food donations, allowing Epic-Cure to fill the gaps from those program cuts and expand into Clay County to feed the food insecure and hungry there.
2621.purpose: By creating a dock-height foundation/loading bay, Epic-Cure will be able to receive bulk food donations (by the semi truckload), which will more than double its food operations capacity (logistics, storage, cold storage) to provide food to the food insecure in NE Florida. Epic-Cure intends to fill the gap of lost food due to cutbacks by the USDA and downsizing by Feeding Northeast Florida. Additionally, Epic-Cure intends to expand its operations to other NE Florida counties beginning with Clay C
2621.activities: Already the largest food pantry in NE Florida, Epic-Cure will be able to increase its intake and output of food for distribution, serving food pantries (in bulk) and individuals (currently about 6,000 weekly), processing more food that might otherwise have gone to waste in land fills (emitting harmful greenhouse gases like methane). The goal is to improve health outcomes and socio-economic conditions, saving city, county, and state resources.
2621.direct_services: 1. Distribution of food to the food insecure. 2. Nutritional, cooking education: hands-on classes for Title-1 students and veterans suffering physical and mental health issues associated with their service to our country. 3. Engagement of senior citizens as volunteers, connecting them with purposeful activities that enrich, prolong lives. 4. Reduce health problems through education, healthy foods
2621.population: Among the food insecure, we count the elderly/retirees, children under 18, veterans and active military personnel, the impoverished, those of historically disadvantaged lineage (people of color, for example), the deaf and blind, the homeless, formerly incarcerated persons, people with drug and alcohol problems, battered women and children, the working poor, single parent households, those living in rural food deserts and children in Title-1 schools. We currently serve more than 65 pounds of food
2621.outcome: The material expansion of food intake capacity for the Epic-Cure program afforded by this grant and the facility it creates will reduce the number of food insecure people in Northeast Florida and thereby improve economic, social, and health outcomes throughout the community. The dock-height foundation will permit receipt of massive food donations to expand reach (Clay County, etc.) and fill Federal budget cut gaps. We will measure outcomes through metrics such as the increasing number of people served, the amount of food rescued and distributed to people, the demographics of people served (seniors, military/vets, children, etc.), people reporting reduced food insecurity and gaining access to

2246.description: Requested funds will replace and upgrade approx. 2.25 miles of undersized water mains to 8in and 12in diameter, ensuring improved water quality for customers. Leak detection will identify aging mains for replacement, completing the replacement of the most urgent segments in Citywide. These upgrades will enhance water conservation, reduce water loss, improve fire flow and protection, and ensure compliance with Florida's Lead & Copper Rule Revision, and provide efficient water flow.

The benefit will be measured by performing regular water quality tests, tracking reductions in contaminant levels, monitoring improvements in water pressure and flow, and analyzing customer feedback on water quality.

3125.description: Bay County is undertaking the construction of a new sewer treatment plant to serve the rapidly growing western portion of the County. As residential, commercial, and industrial development accelerates in the West Bay area, the demand for reliable and environmentally responsible wastewater infrastructure has increased significantly. The new treatment facility will provide the essential capacity required to support current needs while preparing the region for sustained long-term growth. The project includes the design, engineering, and construction of a modern sewer treatment plant equipped with advanced treatment technologies that meet or exceed state and federal water quality standards. The facility will be strategically located to efficiently collect and treat wastewater from expanding communities throughout western Bay County, ensuring that development can continue without straining ex
3125.purpose: The funds will finalize design and implement the construction phase of the project. The goal is to ensure that Bay County can accommodate continued population growth while also protecting the environment. Expanding the sewer plant will reduce reliance on septic tanks—especially those located near West Bay and its tributaries, which are designated Outstanding Florida Waters (OFW).
3125.activities: Initial construction phase of the wastewater facility.
3125.direct_services: An increased ability to provide adequate services to the citizens of the county by allowing for the additional improvements to the county's wastewater system.
3125.population: The target population are the citizens of Bay County.
3125.outcome: Funding will be utilized to construct a wastewater treatment facility to serve the fastest growing area of Bay County. The measure of the benefit will be the amount of additional sewer capacity provided to Bay County. The outcome will be measured by the amount of additional sewer capacity.

1951.description: Requested funds will be used to create Forces of Nature: Weathering the Extreme, a new permanent exhibit hall that explores the science, technology, and human impact of severe weather events, with a focus on Florida’s unique climate. Designed as a dynamic learning environment, the exhibit will engage visitors in understanding how hurricanes, lightning, tornadoes, floods, and other extreme weather phenomena shape our world and how science and engineering help us prepare, respond, and adapt.

Designed as a dynamic learning environment, the exhibit will engage visitors in understanding how hurricanes, lightning, tornadoes, floods, and other extreme weather phenomena shape our world and how science and engineering help us prepare, respond, and adapt.

Guests will engage in activities such as analyzing hurricane data using live satellite imagery and radar models, investigating the physics of lightning, and connecting Florida’s climate to global weather events from earthquakes and wildfires to tsunamis that shape community preparedness.

Exhibit content will align with academic state standards for science, integrating weather and climate education from basic observations in early grades to complex system interactions and severe weather prediction.
1951.population: The target population to be served by this exhibit is OSC attendees of all ages, both local visitors and tourists. OSC serves over 611,000 annual visitors.
1951.outcome: Forces of Nature will: 1) Enrich cultural experience: Visitors will demonstrate increased curiosity and confidence in the role of science and technology in safeguarding our communities following their visit. This will be measured using a post-visit survey. 2) Improve quality of education: Field Trips students will demonstrate increased understanding of weather-related Florida state science standards. This

3126.description: Removal of all remaining damaged lighting infrastructure. purchase and installation of light Poles, Sports Light Package With Side Mount for Round Poles, High Power LED Sports Lights and all necessary additional activities and equipment. NOTE: The town has requested funds for this project, before. The Town has been working HARD to secure other funding. The original request was $1m. The town DID received partial grant, completing SOME of the original need. The Town has also, now, come up with innovative ways to bring down the cost. The town's request is now less than HALF of what it once was.
3126.purpose: The purpose of these funds would be to provide working recreational infrastructure to a rural area, that the town or surrounding communities would not otherwise reasonably be able to afford to replace at the time it was damaged.
3126.activities: The Town will contract with a several providers to replace old and damaged recreational infrastructure. This will mainly include lighting and related support infrastructure such as wiring, pole installation, etc.
3126.direct_services: The administration of a municipal recreational program with a high participation rate.
3126.population: The residents of the Town of Sneads, Fla and and Jackson County; as well as the residents of surrounding communities in Calhoun, Gadsden and Liberty Counties.
3126.outcome: This project will provide recreational opportunities to under served children and young adults in Sneads and surrounding areas. It is commonly known that a tight knit community with significant parental involvement leads to better outcomes for children and young adults. This recreational infrastructure will provide opportunities to families, not just children, to participate in community activities as a family unit. The Town is able to record the number of participants in community sports. The Town expects a quick increase of participants in community sports activities upon completion of this project. This can be recorded.

3127.description: The Town of Snead's (Town) current public safety facility is a very old metal fabricated structure. A new public facility is on the Town's long-term plan. The Town has the opportunity to purchase an existing facility that would work very well for the needs of the Town. This opportunity, while unexpected, would be significantly less expensive for the residents versus future options. These funds would go to purchase an existing facility that is centrally located for the Town and for providing calls for service to Highway 90 and Interstate 10 as needed.
3127.purpose: Purchase of an available facility that would be utilized as the Sneads public safety facility.
3127.activities: The Town will purchase an old facility from a local group that was previously used for something else. Activities are that of a standard government real estate purchase.
3127.direct_services: Acquisition of a public safety site/facility for the citizens of the Town of Sneads and surrounding areas that are serviced by the Sneads Fire Department.
3127.population: The residents of the Town of Sneads, Fla and eastern Jackson County. This facility will also serve the residents of surrounding communities such as Calhoun and Liberty Counties, Marianna, and Chattahoochee; as needed.
3127.outcome: The new facility will enhance the Fire/EMS Department’s ability to protect the public by improving response times, operational reliability, and readiness for fire, medical, and hazardous environmental incidents. A safer, newer, structure also reduces operational risks that can delay or hinder emergency protection services. Protection improvements will be measured by comparing pre- and post-relocation response times, incident mitigation outcomes, and service availability during emergencies. Additional indicators include reductions in equipment downtime and increased capacity to respond to fire, medical, and environmental hazards.

1791.description: The project includes multi-use space supporting the academic program (classrooms, study, and offices), administrative support (campus safety, records & registration, finance, employee support services, IT), student services including a common dining space, and various site improvements. With the growth planned for the College, this project will provide necessary space for new programs. This building will also provide space for existing programs that have been displaced due to planned demolition of buildings.

1791.direct_services: Student instruction and study space, lab space, faculty space and support, administrative and student support.
1791.population: Students, faculty, staff and community. Over 1000 will be served.
1791.outcome: Utilization of the space by the intended population will be the measurement of success.

1831.description: The Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) – Sewer Force Main Rehabilitation project will extend the lifespan and improve the reliability of aging wastewater force mains along Capital Circle Northeast. Using trenchless CIPP technology, the project will reinforce existing pipe segments from within, reducing the need for full replacement, minimizing service disruption, and preventing potential leaks or overflows. This improvement strengthens wastewater system resiliency, protects environmental and public health, and supports long-term infrastructure stability for Tallahassee and surrounding communities.
1831.purpose: The project will rehabilitate aging wastewater force mains using Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) technology to extend pipe life, prevent failures and overflows, and protect public health and the environment. This will improve system reliability, reduce emergency repair costs, and strengthen long-term infrastructure resiliency.
1831.activities: Activities include preparing, lining, and rehabilitating existing wastewater force mains using Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) technology. Services will include pipe cleaning, inspection, structural lining, curing, and post-construction testing, along with necessary engineering and project management to ensure system reliability and long-term performance.
1831.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with reliable and uninterrupted wastewater service by reducing the risk of pipe failures and sewer overflows. This helps protect public health, prevent environmental contamination, and ensure the community continues to receive safe and dependable utility services.
1831.population: The target population includes all residents, businesses, and institutions served by the City of Tallahassee’s wastewater system. The project is expected to benefit over 200,000 people by ensuring reliable wastewater service and protecting public health and the environment across the service area.
1831.outcome: The project will improve reliability of the wastewater system, extend the life of aging force mains, and reduce the risk of sewer overflows and environmental contamination, enhancing public health and system resiliency. Success will be measured by tracking reductions in pipe failures, emergency repairs, and overflow incidents, along with improved system performance and regulatory compliance.

2217.description: The Stronger Choices Initiative empowers youth, parents, and community members to make healthier, informed choices through drug prevention education, dialogue, and collaboration. By addressing risk behaviors such as substance use and misuse, and promoting wellness, legal awareness, and positive decision-making, this multi-event effort strengthens prevention, communication, and resilience across generations in Hialeah.

By addressing risk behaviors such as substance use and misuse, and promoting wellness, legal awareness, and positive decision-making, this multi-event effort strengthens prevention, communication, and resilience across stake holders, community partners and generations in the City of Hialeah.

2217.direct_services: YDD: Evidence based participatory method where youth discuss drug prevention awareness around community stakeholders. KTL: Students and parents obtain an understanding of the law to avoid unlawful behaviors. PPW V&O: Sessions to connect the importance of physical, emotional and social awareness to reduce substance use among youth. STS: culminating event including partners, stakeholder & educators

3130.description: This appropriation supports the strategic expansion of Chipola College's Welding Technology program from 46 to 60 seats and the modernization of the Advanced Manufacturing program with Industry 4.0-capable equipment including enterprise-level PLCs, collaborative robotics, and industrial networking systems. The investment directly addresses critical workforce shortages in Northwest Florida's manufacturing sector. Chipola College is the only comprehensive welding and manufacturing training provider across its five rural counties serving communities with zero alternatives for workforce training in these high-demand fields.
3130.purpose: Expand welding capacity by 30% (46 to 60 seats); Modernize Advanced Manufacturing with Industry 4.0 equipment; Train 190 students over 2 years; Produce 142 program completers with industry certifications; Generate $1.42 million annual wage increase; Position Chipola College as regional industry 4.0 workforce leader.
3130.activities: Welding instruction with VR simulation and hands-on training; Advanced Manufacturing curriculum (enterprise PLCs, collaborative robotics, metrology, networking); Industry certification preparation (AWS, MSSC, NIMS, FANUC); Job placement assistance; Customized incumbent worker training.
3130.direct_services: Affordable workforce training leading to $16-$22/hour careers; Industry certifications at no additional cost; 85% job placement rate; Career pathways without leaving rural Northwest Florida; Economic opportunity for under-served populations.
3130.population: High school graduates, adults seeking career change, displaced workers, veterans; Expected to serve 190 students over 2 years, 142 completers; Service area: Jackson, Calhoun, Holmes, Washington and Liberty counties.
3130.outcome: Benefits: 142 skilled workers entering manufacturing economy; 85% placement rate within 6 months; $10,000 average wage increase over high school diploma; $1.42M annual regional wage impact. Measurements: Student enrollment/completion tracking (FETPIP data); Certification pass rates; Employment placement surveys; Wage data from employers; CAPE Performance Funding metrics; Annual legislative reporting.

3142.description: The hardening and mitigation activities that are proposed within this project within Jackson County (County) would provide greater protection to the Fire Rescue Station during natural disasters and severe weather events. This could allow the facility to remain operational during the the most critical times and protect the vital first responders so that they may attend to Jackson County citizens in the aftermath of a natural disaster or severe weather event. Project would include design and renovation of facility consisting of new wind rated exterior envelope, generator with ATS, building insulation, HVAC, and other exterior safety fixtures.
3142.purpose: The hardening and mitigation activities that are proposed within this project would provide greater protection to the facility during natural disasters and severe weather events. This could allow the facility to remain operational during the the most critical times and protect the vital first responders so that they may attend to Jackson County citizens in the aftermath of a natural disaster or severe weather event.
3142.activities: All involved Jackson County Staff will work closely together to proceed with the improvements to the facility by lining up large scale purchasing, procuring engineering and design services, and procuring construction work to be performed.
3142.direct_services: While no additional services would be added or provided directly to citizens as a result of this project. The project would allow for quicker, continued, and uninterrupted first responder service to be provided by the facility to all citizens. The primary services are Fire Rescue and Emergency Medical Services.
3142.population: This Fire Rescue Station primarily serves the central and northern portions of the County, but the entire population of Jackson County could benefit from this project. Project Funds would not not benefit one specific group.
3142.outcome: The expected outcome of the project is to harden the Fire Rescue Station which will mitigate against future damages from Natural Disasters and/or sever weather events that will provide the benefit of faster and uninterrupted service following the event(s).

3132.description: Increase white fleet vehicles for student transportation for second chance bus routes, summer school routes, and extracurricular routes. Supports smaller group transportation. Decreases overall transportation costs and allows bus fleet to last longer due to less use. Saves on costs for extracurricular to maximize funding use for other costs like uniforms and other fees to improve programs. Allows transportation staff without CDL.
3132.purpose: Provide lower cost transportation for schools for extracurricular and intra-curricular activities. 55% reduction in mileage costs. Save on average 61,000 miles from going onto school buses, extending their lifespan. Allow for low cost second routes to pick up students that missed the first bus to increase attendance and student achievement.
3132.activities: Transportation services at a lower cost for schools. Small groups of students like BETA club, track teams, golf teams, FFA, etc. would have access to transportation at a reduced cost. Driver does not have the possess a CDL for these vehicles.
3132.direct_services: Students will have access to safe and lower cost transportation services for programs that are small and financially strained. Provide a second chance for pickup in the morning.
3132.population: Students at all Jackson County Schools will have access to the transportation services. All extracurricular and intra- curricular programs will have access to scheduling the vehicles for their events. Each year approximately 1000 students could benefit from this resource, or about 20% of the student population.
3132.outcome: Estimated cost savings of $410,728.86 over a twelve-year period. Mileage savings from not using buses is estimated at 61,671 miles. A 55% reduction in travel costs charged to student programs would put $34,227.41 per year back into those programs to benefit students.

3089.description: Funds will expand access to comprehensive autism/neurodevelopmental evaluations for children in Florida, ensuring early identification when intervention has the greatest impact on brain development. Early diagnosis improves outcomes, reducing lifetime care costs by up to $1.2M per individual. This project addresses delays in diagnosis, which often exceed 2 years, ensuring children access life-changing intervention services at the earliest, most critical window.
3089.purpose: Funds will expand access to comprehensive autism/neurodevelopmental evaluations for children in Florida, ensuring early identification when intervention has the greatest impact on brain development. Early diagnosis improves outcomes, reducing lifetime care costs by up to $1.2M per individual. This project addresses delays in diagnosis, which often exceed 2 years, ensuring children access life-changing intervention services at the earliest, most critical window.
3089.activities: The project will provide comprehensive neurodevelopmental evaluations for children aged 16 months - 8 years, including diagnostic testing, and individualized reports. Families will receive care coordination to connect them with intervention services quickly. Funds will support staffing for evaluations, purchase of advanced diagnostic tools, and outreach.
3089.direct_services: Comprehensive autism evaluations for children aged 16 months - 8 years, including standardized diagnostic assessments, and individualized reports. Families will receive personalized guidance and care coordination to access critical early intervention services without delay.
3089.population: The target population is children aged 16 months through 8 years across Florida, with a focus on underserved and at- risk communities experiencing barriers to early autism diagnosis. The project aims to serve at least 300 children annually, ensuring they receive comprehensive evaluations and timely referrals to intervention services. By prioritizing early identification, the project addresses developmental disparities and improves outcomes for Florida's youngest, most vulnerable citizens.
3089.outcome: The project aims to achieve earlier identification of autism and related disabilities in children aged 16 months through 8 years, ensuring timely access to intervention services during the most critical period for brain development. The expected benefits include improved developmental outcomes, reduced long-term care costs, and enhanced family support. Outcomes will be measured by tracking the number of children evaluated annually (target: 300), the average age at diagnosis (goal: under 9 years), and the time to intervention following evaluation.

2218.description: The Jimmy Graham Foundation's Aerospace & Technology Pathway introduces students to hands-on STEM learning through aviation, mechanical, and engineering experiences. This initiative aims to inspire youth to pursue career paths in the aerospace industry by engaging them in flight training, maintenance workshops, and engineering labs. Students gain direct exposure to aircraft operations, mechanics, and flight simulation, culminating with in-air flight experiences.

Creation of job opportunities through internships and training placements. This will be measured by programming tracking and FM logbook hours. 3. Enhance economic self- sufficiency of graduates entering aviation training or college stem programs. This will be measured by follow-up surveys and placement records.

3134.description: Provide startup costs for year one of the JROTC Program for the Jackson County School District. Provides additional work readiness development through industry certification. Provides the district with a valuable resource for students and community.
3134.purpose: Create opportunities for 50-75 students to prepare for military careers. 90% pass rate on the industry certification exams.
3134.activities: 180-days of instruction in the JROTC program. Community services such as parades, color guard presentations at events, and support of Veteran's Programs at school.
3134.direct_services: Provide community services by the cadets at Veteran's Programs, parades, and sporting events. Add a layer of pride and patriotism to Jackson County that is currently missing from the school district.
3134.population: 50-75 students enrolled in the program annually to support industry certification and preparation for careers in the United States Military. 5,000+ community members viewing and participating in community events where cadets from the JROTC Program will presents colors for the National Anthem, host events for Veteran's Programs, and provide community services.
3134.outcome: Prepare 50-75 students for careers in the United States Military and earn industry certification for high school acceleration. Become a patriotic workforce ready cadre of leaders.

2157.description: The Counseling On Us matches qualified individuals seeking mental health care with licensed counselors for up to one year, free of charge. To accomplish this, clients contact Counseling On Us and request an interview where they will be able to ask questions and indicate the reason they are seeking counseling. If qualified, Counseling On Us pairs them with a therapist who has donated their time for them for up to one year for free of charge. Counseling On Us also provides basic instruction (outreach classes) free of charge; life skills, professional skills, health and wellness classes. In addition, we provide continuing education classes (CEUs) for our counselors free of charge.
2157.purpose: The funds requested will be used to expand access to free mental health counseling services for underserved individuals and families across Florida. Florida consistently ranks near the bottom nationally in mental health care access and thousands of residents go without needed care each year due to financial barriers. Counseling On Us, a program of Toobox4Life, is dedicated to closing this gap by recruiting licensed mental health counselors to provide pro- bono counseling.
2157.activities: Free mental health counseling and outreach programs (life kills, professional skill and health/wellness classes)
2157.direct_services: Mental health care (counseling) and outreach programs and supportive classes (resume writing, parenting, financial, nutrition, etc)
2157.population: Any Florida resident who is 18 years of age or older in any of the 67 counties. In 2026, 100 constituents; in 2027, 250 constituents and in 2027, 500 constituents.
2157.outcome: Depending on the diagnosis, a reduction in self-reported "days of poor physical health" among participants, a reduction in somatic symptom burden among participants and improvement in sleep quality. Target within 12 months: reduction in PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, an increase on the Harvard Flourishing Index, and where indicated a reduction in suicidal-ideation item (PHQ-9). Administer brief surveys at intake and discharge, and 3-mo intervals depending on length of care. Also, standardized measures collected at intake, session 4, discharge, and 3-mo intervals depending on length of care.

3090.description: Bradford County has a goal to replace an aging fire engine. Our front-line apparatus was handed down from the previous volunteer fire department. Our front-line engine has been plagued with costly repairs and extended down time. Over the past year, our crews have spent the majority of their time in our spare apparatus, which includes one engine from 1998, and two engines from 2000. Safety and reliability has vastly improved over the past 23 years.

New engines will ensure reliable delivery of these life-saving tools to vehicle crash scenes when needed.
3090.population: This project will serve the entire population of Bradford County. Approximately 29,000.
3090.outcome: Quicker response times to patients in need of life-saving medical treatment. Improved apparatus reliability and decreased repair costs. This will be measured by response time data, as well as vehicle repair cost data.

2008.description: Operation Light Shine (OLS) is requesting funding in support of the Southwest Florida INTERCEPT Task Force (Collier, Lee, and Hendry Counties), a public/private partnership in the fight against child exploitation and human trafficking. Funding supports the establishment and maintenance of a laboratory facility, investigative technology, and salary reimbursement to participating law enforcement agencies for assigned Task Force personnel. Currently, the project is funded through private OLS donations totaling $840,000, made possible through the contributions of donors such as the Tim Tebow Foundation and other OLS supporters.
2008.purpose: The TASKFORCE brings together local, county, state, and federal partners in a coordinated effort to combat child exploitation and human trafficking. These public/private resources will facilitate the investigation, charging, prosecution, and prevention of criminal activities.
2008.activities: Funding supports the establishment and maintenance of a laboratory facility, acquisition of investigative technology, and salary reimbursement to participating agencies for assigned law enforcement task force personnel. These public/private resources will facilitate the investigation, charging, prosecution, and prevention of criminal activities related to child exploitation and human trafficking.
2008.direct_services: These funds directly support local law enforcement in their public safety mission to combat child exploitation and human trafficking within the community.
2008.population: The funds used to support law enforcement's efforts will benefit every citizen in Southwest Florida, particularly those residing in counties with INTERCEPT task force representation. Citizens will benefit from the more efficient use of law enforcement resources and safer communities.
2008.outcome: This funding will increase law enforcement's ability to investigate and prosecute child sexual exploitation and human trafficking cases. As a result of more efficient resources, law enforcement will be able to rescue more children and human trafficking survivors. In addition to the INTERCEPT task force data, each county keeps data on every investigation, arrest, indictment, and prosecution.

2221.description: HBI is a career training organization in the building industry. HBI prepares participants with the skills and experience needed for successful careers through vocational training, job placement services, certification programs textbooks and curricula. The Building Careers for Veterans program promises job readiness and career connections for eligible veterans/military personnel and families as well as transitioning veteran offenders seeking vocational skills & employment opportunities. The goal is to assist participants to become self-sufficient and gainfully employed within the community and to provide opportunities for stackable, portable, industry-recognized credentials in high-growth, high- demand careers. Students are trained in a multiplicity of jobs and careers, resulting in increased marketability and employment options. Services also enable businesses to obtain highly skilled, c
2221.purpose: Enhance specific individual's self-sufficiency, increase or improve economic activity and improve quality of education by offering vocational skills, certifications, job readiness, and placement assistance to veterans/military personnel and families as well as transitioning veteran offenders. Fees for services are as follows: • Enrollments: $3,000/participant, • Training Completions: $2,500/participant, • Employment Placements: $3,600/participant, • Raise/Promotion in Employment: $2,400/particip
2221.activities: Initial assessment interview, develop service plan and goals with action steps, enrollment, training, certification and/or credential attainment, and job placement assistance.
2221.direct_services: The HBI Building Careers for Veterans Program promises job readiness and career connections for eligible veterans/military personnel and families as well as transitioning veteran offenders seeking vocational skills & employment opportunities. The goal of the program is to help participants become self-sufficient and gainfully employed within the community and to provide opportunities for stackable
2221.population: Veterans/military personnel and families as well as transitioning veteran offenders, including jobless persons, homeless, economically disadvantaged persons, physically disabled, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, and drug offenders (in criminal Justice). Between 100 and 200 are expected to be served.
2221.outcome: Improve quality of education through vocational skill completion and training completion; measured by the number of industry-recognized credentials earned as a result of the training. Increase or improve economic activity by adding skilled labor to the workforce; measured by the number of job placements. Job creation; measured by the number of HBI staff positions funded by the program. Enhance specific individual’s economic self-sufficiency by ensuring gainful employment of program participants; measured by the number of participants placed in employment and initial wage earned. Divert from Criminal Justice system by providing gainful employment of program participants; measured by the Numbe

1857.description: The funds will be used to construct a private school for children with autism from Kindergarten to graduation serving Lee and the surrounding counties. The school will provide a standard curriculum tailored to each child's skills and needs. It will also integrate vocational training and workforce opportunities, and wraparound clinical support.
1857.purpose: The funds will be used to construct a private school for children with autism from Kindergarten through 12th grade serving Lee, Charlotte and the surrounding counties. The school will provide a standard curriculum tailored to each child's skills and needs. The program will integrate vocational training and workforce opportunities, and wraparound clinical support.
1857.activities: Thrive Academy-Babcock Ranch will provide a standard curriculum tailored to each child's needs and skill level. The program will integrate vocational training and workforce opportunities, and wraparound clinical support to each student.
1857.direct_services: Direct services include instruction by certified teachers, workforce and vocational training, clinical (Applied Behavioral Analysis, Occupational Therapy, and Speech), services. The Academy will provide collaborative opportunities with local businesses. Extra curricular activities will include sports and arts programs.
1857.population: The target population served are students with autism. Between 100-200 individuals will be served.
1857.outcome: Students with autism will have access to an individualized education with needed supports to graduate and obtain employment. The students will have access to medically necessary services to increase their ability to function independently. They will also participate in extracurricular activities uniquely designed to their needs to increase physical activity. The students will also participate in workforce training, internships, and job placements as part of their education. Parents will be able to access services to assist their children. Outcomes will be measured by individual student success and number of students who attend the school and secure employment.

1989.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
1989.description: The Florida Organized Retail Crime Exchange (FORCE) currently exists and is administered under the Office of the Attorney General. FORCE is a public/private partnership that was formed to facilitate enhanced communication and collaboration between retailers, law enforcement and prosecutors in the fight against organized retail crime. This project will provide funding needed to operate and maintain a statewide intelligence sharing and platform in support of FORCE.
1989.purpose: These funds will be used to administer technology that allows strengthened collaboration between retailers and law enforcement, by providing real-time actionable intelligence on organized retail crime offenders and criminal activity occurring in Florida's retail stores. This collaboration contributes to safer communities and safer shopping environments by reducing both property crime and the violence that often accompanies it. This tool helps law enforcement and prosecutors pursue more serious c
1989.activities: Funds will be used to contract with a third-party vendor to provide and maintain an intelligence-sharing platform in support of the Florida Organized Retail Crime Exchange (FORCE). This secure platform currently supports collaboration among retail, law enforcement, and prosecutors with more than 1,200 users statewide. The program is designed to strengthen the public-private partnership between retailers and law enforcement through real-time intelligence exchange in the fight against organized re
1989.direct_services: This service leads to enhanced public safety, and safe and secure retail environments by reducing violent incidents associated with organized retail crime. These services also protect consumer costs as retail theft drives up prices for consumers. By reducing ORC losses, the platform helps mitigate the “theft tax” that gets passed on to citizens in the form of higher prices. ORC networks are often
1989.population: The FORCE intelligence sharing platform is currently utilized statewide by retailers, state and local law enforcement agencies, local prosecutors, and the Office of the Attorney General. The technology is currently in use by over 1,200 users statewide representing over 150 retail brands, and 120 law enforcement agencies.
1989.outcome: The project is expected to continue to foster increased collaboration and intelligence sharing between law enforcement agencies and retailers statewide resulting in decreased retail theft and successful prosecution of cross-jurisdictional organized retail crime cases. The outcome will be measured by monitoring of data sharing analytics and documentation of successful case prosecutions that are facilitated or enhances by the use of the platform.

2088.description: Demolition of an obsolete existing 1980's structure (old library facility) not conducive to rehabilitation. A new multi-story emergency response center will be constructed using code-plus development standards. The center will house sleeping and bathrooms/showers quarters, meeting spaces, communication/media facilities, an on-site generator, large meeting space to accommodate at least 75 people.
2088.purpose: The Emergency Response Center will be a collaborative location housing multiple government agencies including the Sheriff's Office and the City's Neighborhood Services (daily) that respond to emergency events. Additional space will house other emergency management personnel before, during and after disaster events and may be used as an intake facility and distribution center following disasters.
2088.activities: The facility will be a collaborative location in Bonita Springs that will house multiple emergency agencies during gray sky events and the Lee County Sheriff's Office and City's Neighborhood Services in blue sky events.
2088.direct_services: The building will house emergency agencies/personnel and essential city personnel that will be able to respond more quickly to the community following a disaster.
2088.population: The target population will be the citizens of Bonita Springs as well as the surrounding communities. During and following a disaster the City could serve as many as 50,000+ persons.
2088.outcome: The facility will be the only city sponsored emergency response center that will have the capability to house multiple emergency management agencies/personnel, city staff, centralize communication and coordination following a natural disaster. Outcomes will be measured by quicker response times, better communications between emergency agencies, ability to deploy "boots on the ground" sooner

3137.description: The goal of NextStep at Endeavor Academy is to build an inclusive community where the benefits of educating and employing individuals with autism are broadly understood. Adults with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) will receive curriculum, services, and supports needed to complete intensive learning experiences to increase their ability to maintain competitive employment and live independently. NextStep’s short courses also provide coaching and instruction for the neurodivergent population.
3137.purpose: The goal of NextStep at Endeavor Academy is to build an inclusive community where the benefits of educating and employing individuals with autism are broadly understood. Adults with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) will receive curriculum, services, and supports needed to complete intensive learning experiences to increase their ability to maintain competitive employment and live independently. NextStep’s short courses also provide coaching and instruction for the neurodivergent population.
3137.activities: Direct instruction in Learn4Independence® coursework, applied learning in job settings (volunteer, paid and unpaid internships, competitive employment, and self-employment), direct instruction in independent living skills, and applied learning in the community and through the residential component of NextStep Academy; direct instruction in social competencies offered across all settings.
3137.direct_services: Direct instruction in both classroom and natural (applied) settings; job coaching; help with identifying and accessing natural supports at work and in the community; assessment; targeted goals (employment, social, communication, independent living); maintenance of goals; follow-up checks to measure long-term progress after completing the program.
3137.population: The target population served by this project will include adults with autism who have aged out of the K-12 educational system but still need support for success. These individuals may be jobless, economically disadvantaged, developmentally disabled, and/or college students. This project also serves autistic teens in employment readiness courses.The project will serve between 51-100 individuals.
3137.outcome: Participants enrolled in NextStep's Transition Academy will complete the Learn4Independence® coursework (a 32- course curriculum focusing on employment/life skills). Each course has lessons in the areas of work, finances, safety, relationships, organization, nutrition, community, health, problem-solving, etiquette, transportation, and living independently. Participants enrolled in NextStep's Transition Academy will receive experience and support in an employment setting. Outcomes will be measured through participant mastery of the coursework modules. and individualized goals related to employment and living independently. Outcomes will also be measured in the number of participants maintaini

3138.description: Jackson County is seeking funding to improve water storage in the Marianna service area to provide reliable, high- quality potable water for citizens and businesses. A new water storage system is needed to provide emergency supply to the north end of the system and regulate pressure as demand increases in the area.
3138.purpose: The goal of the funds requested for the proposed project would allow for the design and construction of a new Water Storage Facility in the Marianna service area. The increased storage will serve the growing business corridor of the I- 10 and Hwy 71 area. This facility will ensure the ability of economic growth, provide emergency reserves during high- demand periods or unexpected service disruptions, while also improving pressure regulation across the system.
3138.activities: The new water storage system that would have a capacity to service the growing I-10 and Hwy 71 area would be accomplished through engineering, design, construction, and construction inspection activities. The completed system would provide proper water storage and better maintain pressure balance for the system.
3138.direct_services: Continuous, well pressurized water for citizens and businesses located within the project area.
3138.population: The target population of the proposed project are citizens and businesses located around Marianna, primarily along Hwy 90, Hwy, 71, and I-10. The number expected to be served will continue to grow along with this corridor.
3138.outcome: The outcome of the construction of the water storage system would be to provide emergency reserves during high- demand periods or unexpected service disruptions, while also improving pressure regulation across the system. This may be measured by monitoring number of disruptions or service calls in the area due to available water or pressure.

3139.description: Jackson County is seeking funding to improve water storage in the Marianna service area to provide reliable, high- quality potable water for citizens and businesses. Adding a new well will extend the life of existing pumping equipment and ensure continued operation during maintenance or repairs.
3139.purpose: The goal of the funds requested for the proposed project would allow for the design and construction of a new Water Well at an existing site located near the intersection of Interstate 10 and Highway 71, to provide additional pumping capacity to this rapidly expanding area. By adding the additional well it will ensure uninterrupted economic growth, diversify, the available pumping sources, the system will operate more efficiently, have increased capacity, and with greater redundancy.
3139.activities: The new production well would provide additional pumping capacity to service the growing I-10 and Hwy 71 area would be accomplished through engineering, design, construction, and construction inspection activities. The completed well would help meet the increased demand of potable water, extend the operational life of existing equipment by reducing strain, and ensure uninterrupted service in the event of another well requiring maintenance or repair.
3139.direct_services: Increased production of potable water for citizens and businesses located within the project area.
3139.population: The target population of the proposed project are citizens and businesses located around Marianna, primarily along Hwy 90, Hwy, 71, and I-10. The number expected to be served will continue to grow along with this corridor.
3139.outcome: The outcome of this project enhance the reliability and sustainability of the County's potable water. The new well will extend the life of existing pumping equipment and ensure continued operation during maintenance or repairs. This may be measured by monitoring number of disruptions or service calls in the area.

3150.description: An evidence-informed Military Child & Family Tool Kit designed and created for teachers with ready-to-use resources to support military kids succeed in preschool. The tool kit will provide ideas, tips, structured activities, materials, and resources for Childcare Network educators to pilot with military children currently being served in our Florida programs.
3150.purpose: The goal is to design, print, and deliver a comprehensive Educator Tool Kit for Florida's Military Kids to support early childhood educators working with children from military families by providing them with the guidance, activities, and resources needed to promote a successful preschool experience.
3150.activities: To achieve the creation of the Educator Tool Kit for Florida's Military Kids, activities will include researching evidence- based practices, curating age-appropriate stories, projects, and activities, and developing practical tips tailored to the social-emotional and transitional needs of children in military families. Services will encompass collaboration with early childhood experts and military family advocates, content design and printing, and distribution of the physical tool kit to early l
3150.direct_services: Military-connected children will receive appropriate educational experiences to help them build greater emotional stability and resilience and support their consistent learning and development. The Tool Kit will serve as a professional development resource, enhancing educator confidence and competence in addressing the unique needs of this population.
3150.population: The target population is estimated to be 300 and includes children in military families, school-age children, military- connected preschool students, and the teachers that serve these children every day at our high quality Childcare Network centers across Florida.
3150.outcome: Research shows that children in military families often face unique challenges such as frequent relocations and adapting to new environments. By equipping preschool educators with effective tools, the project aims to strengthen the quality of care and education for military-connected children, ensuring they receive the stability and support necessary for healthy development. Military parents may provide anecdotal observations of emotional well-being.

1816.description: The program is intended to expand implementation of the classical education model by supporting professional development, specialized teacher compensation, supplemental technology, instructional materials, and promotional efforts. The program will serve up to 250 students, enhancing educational opportunities and expanding school choice within the district.
1816.purpose: The funds requested are intended to expand implementation of the classical education model by supporting professional development, specialized teacher compensation, supplemental technology, instructional materials, and promotional efforts. The program will serve up to 250 students, enhancing educational opportunities and expanding school choice within the district.
1816.activities: The appropriation project directly benefits students by offering an additional choice in learning opportunities within Miami-Dade County Public Schools. Thus, M-DCPS would afford families with a school-wide choice option. It facilitates the transformation of a traditional public school into a classical education school, marking the first school-wide choice program of its kind.
1816.direct_services: Parents and students will have access to an alternative educational model, which in turn will expand school choice options. Students enrolled in the Classical Education school will receive a comprehensive education that includes courses in literature, grammar, reading, math, foreign language, science, social studies, art, and music.
1816.population: This project aims to serve and support up to 250 students within Miami-Dade County Public Schools.
1816.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to provide students with a comprehensive classical education curriculum that fosters critical thinking, cultural literacy, and interdisciplinary learning, ultimately enhancing their academic success and preparation for real-world applications. The outcome will be measured through student assessments like the Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST), monitoring proficiency in key subjects, and tracking enrollment and application interest to gauge program effectiveness.

2222.description: The legislative funding will allow MDSO to upgrade the Sheriff's Training Center, by (1) purchasing a mobile canopy system, which will provide desperately-needed sanctuary from sun exposure and inclement weather allowing for law enforcement personnel to enjoy continued opportunities for firing range practice in any environment, and (2) upgrading severely eroded berms in the range causing dangerous conditions such as ricocheting rounds.
2222.purpose: Much-needed upgrades to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Training Center, which will impact not only MDSO but also entities who use and/or train at the facility, including the Secret Service, FBI, US Military, Miami-Dade Corrections and Rehabilitation, and Miami-Dade College academy students.
2222.activities: Much-needed upgrades to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Training Center.
2222.direct_services: Increased law enforcement and public safety operations.
2222.population: State and National Law Enforcement Personnel and Trainees, as well as all residents and visitors in Miami-Dade County; over 5 million persons.
2222.outcome: Improved skill level proficiency, efficiency, safety, and morale for law enforcement personnel and trainees, and increased law enforcement and public safety operations as measured by MDSO tracking data.

2897.description: This funding strengthens oversight and accountability of Florida recovery residences while ensuring access to safe, high-quality recovery residences. The project expands statewide education the recovery capital resources which has been successfully launched which are integral to certification and positive resident outcomes. The project also supports provider education, compliance training, and quarterly engagement to increase provider performance transparency.
2897.purpose: This funding strengthens oversight and accountability of Florida recovery residences while ensuring access to safe, high-quality recovery residences. The project expands statewide education the recovery capital resources which has been successfully launched which are integral to certification and positive resident outcomes. The project also supports provider education, compliance training, and quarterly engagement to increase provider performance transparency.
2897.activities: Outreach and training will be provided statewide to strengthen provider engagement and compliance. Recovery residences will have access to a recovery capital resources that track resident progress and outcomes and provide insights to guide decisions, improve services, and support accountability, while expanding oversight and quality of certified beds across Florida.
2897.direct_services: Insights from recovery capital tools will guide improvements and accountability. In 2025, 70% of recovery residence FARR inspections resulting in a corrective action plan; although only 5% of CAPS were for major violations, this shows room for improvement. Statewide outreach and training will strengthen provider engagement and compliance providing better resident outcomes and success.
2897.population: Substance use disorder and co-occurring conditions can affect individuals across all population groups. This project serves a broad range of Floridians, including people who are economically disadvantaged, unemployed, veterans, homeless and individuals returning to the community from incarceration or supervised programs. It benefits recovery housing providers and residents by supporting safe, stable and supportive housing environments. The project currently reaches approximately 290 certified pr
2897.outcome: Expected Outcome:Strengthen oversight, accountability and compliance within recovery housing; enhance provider competency through statewide provider development and compliance support. Methodology for Measurement: Measured through provider participation in development and compliance activities, certification progress among existing operators and aggregate recovery capital data reflecting resident engagement and stability.

1812.description: The project expands Miami-Dade County Public Schools' Voluntary Prekindergarten (VPK) programs by creating new Reggio Emilia and Montessori classrooms across multiple schools throughout the district. These hands-on, inquiry-based models foster creativity, curiosity, and critical thinking while supporting the Florida Department of Education's goal of Kindergarten readiness and strengthening parental choice through additional early learning options.
1812.purpose: The project expands Miami-Dade County Public Schools' Voluntary Prekindergarten (VPK) programs by creating new Reggio Emilia and Montessori classrooms across multiple schools throughout the district. These hands-on, inquiry- based models foster creativity, curiosity, and critical thinking while supporting the Florida Department of Education's goal of Kindergarten readiness and strengthening parental choice through additional early learning options.
1812.activities: The project will establish new Voluntary Prekindergarten (VPK) classrooms throughout multiple Miami-Dade County Public Schools using Reggio Emilia and Montessori approaches. This expansion will increase access to quality early learning opportunities and enhance parental choice programs for families across the district.
1812.direct_services: Students will receive daily instruction in hands-on, inquiry-based environments designed to strengthen early literacy, numeracy, and problem-solving skills. Families will benefit from greater access to education philosophies through VPK programs that prepare children for Kindergarten readiness while expanding educational options throughout several schools in the district.
1812.population: Over 800 preschool students throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools.
1812.outcome: Both the Reggio Emilia and Montessori prekindergarten programs improve the quality of education by viewing the child as a competent, active participant in their own learning. They share a foundation in child-centered learning and use a carefully prepared environment as a key to better prepare students for success in Kindergarten. The measurement used may include FAST Star Early Literacy scores to show a higher percent of students scoring at Kindergarten readiness proficiency.

1842.description: Our state-of-the-art native wildlife hospital enables Pelican Harbor to deliver the highest quality of patient care and serve as a hub for conservation awareness and education. Through the creation of outdoor habitats, including pens, pools, and educational signage, we are expanding our care for sick, injured, and orphaned native wildlife and enhancing our environmental education programs to engage more children, families, and community groups about Florida’s native wildlife and ecosystems.
1842.purpose: Our new native wildlife hospital enables Pelican Harbor to deliver the highest quality of patient care and serve as a hub for conservation awareness and education. Through the creation of outdoor habitats on a 2.6-acre campus, including pens, pools, and educational signage, we are expanding care for sick, injured, and orphaned native wildlife and enhancing our environmental education programs to engage more children, families, and community groups about Florida’s native wildlife and ecosystems.
1842.activities: These funds will be used to complete the construction of new outdoor wildlife habitats including pens, pools, and educational signage at Pelican Harbor’s new wildlife hospital and education center.
1842.direct_services: This request is for Capital Outlay funds only . No direct services will be provided to citizens by the appropriation project.
1842.population: The funds requested for the project are for Capital Outlay, not populations to be served. Once this project is completed, we will be able to meet the increased need for treating sick, injured, and orphaned native wildlife with the goal of releasing healthy animals back into the ecosystem. We also plan to expand program opportunities and the number of stakeholders by 10 to 20 percent in the first year, to engage more children, families, and community groups in conservation education.
1842.outcome: The new facility will be South Florida’s premier native wildlife hospital and education center; a hub for community activity offering high-level animal care as well as educational programming to raise awareness of the threats facing wildlife and the environment, and solutions for preserving and protecting these resources. Pelican Harbor utilizes WRMD software to measure and track all data related to each patient, including species, type of injury, location found, treatment plan, and release information. This data is used to inform the environmental education program and shared with other wildlife centers.

2159.description: SCORE, a 503c(3), has served entrepreneurs for 60+ years with federal funding—ending in 2025. We urge Florida to step in. In 2024 alone, SCORE Florida delivered, through a volunteer network, 65,758 services, launched 5,694 businesses, and created 11,834 jobs statewide. Our proven model transforms entrepreneurs into thriving business owners, multiplying every dollar invested into lasting economic impact. Help us continue driving Florida's prosperity and strengthening communities across the state.
2159.purpose: SCORE FL's goal is to help build the economic strength of the state by supporting small business start ups, growth and continue to thrive. This will provide small business strength across the state and create jobs in the state. Services are provided by volunteers at no salary cost.
2159.activities: SCORE will provide one-on-one mentoring to small businesses across the state. Additionally, webinars will be provided for educational purposes to this population. Live seminars and events will also be provided at the local level. Again, all services are provided by volunteers.
2159.direct_services: SCORE will provide one-on-one mentoring to small businesses across the state. Additionally, webinars will be provided for educational purposes to this population. Live seminars and events will also be provided at the local level.
2159.population: We cross all demographic lines to support small businesses. In 2024 we provided 41,737 workshop sessions and 24,021 mentoring sessions totally 65,758 services to Florida residents, as defined by their provided zip codes. We anticipate similar services in 2026.
2159.outcome: We measure seminar attendance and mentoring sessions and track through our Customer Relations System.

2518.description: The Healing and Empowerment Circles will provide structured, trauma-informed sessions each month for survivors of sexual trauma across Central Florida. Facilitated by licensed clinicians and trained peer advocates, the program creates a safe, supportive environment where participants can process trauma, build coping strategies, and strengthen emotional resilience. Each session combines evidence-based healing practices, psychoeducation, guided reflection, and community connection.
2518.purpose: The funds will establish monthly trauma-informed Healing and Empowerment Circles that provide survivors of sexual trauma with accessible support, guided coping strategies, and connections to community resources. This program will create a safe, structured pathway for emotional healing, resilience building, and long-term recovery for survivors across Central Florida.
2518.activities: Monthly Healing and Empowerment Circles will provide trauma-informed group sessions for survivors of sexual trauma, offering education on coping skills, guided reflection, and peer support. Licensed clinicians and trained advocates will facilitate sessions and connect participants to community resources for ongoing recovery.
2518.direct_services: Survivors will receive free, trauma-informed group sessions that promote healing, coping, and resilience. Services include monthly facilitated circles, access to licensed clinicians and advocates, emotional support, resource navigation, and referrals to community-based counseling and recovery programs.
2518.population: The target population served by this project includes economically disadvantaged persons, university/college students, and victim of crime. The projected number of individuals is 200-400.
2518.outcome: Expected benefits include increased access to trauma-informed healing spaces, improved coping and emotional resilience for survivors, and greater connection to community resources. Outcomes will be measured through attendance tracking, pre/post self-assessments, participant surveys, referral logs, and follow-up evaluations to assess ongoing recovery and engagement.

3153.description: In support of Eglin Air Force Base and the region, numerous orphan parcels are being primed for development by Eglin and other stakeholders. Potential development in the Poquito Area includes a research & technology park, attainable housing, commercial businesses, hotels, convention center, Victory Village (800 retired military senior living residents, skilled nursing facility, & an EMS station). The above-mentioned projects will provide direct benefits to Eglin and the community. For these projects to occur, major water & sewer infrastructure needs to be installed, including a master lift station, 4.7-mile sewer force main, & a 1-mile potable water main. These development projects cannot occur without these water/sewer projects. The water main project will also increase water pressure and supply for existing customers in the Poquito area. Stakeholders on this project include Okaloosa Co
3153.purpose: The construction of new water and sewer infrastructure to support population growth, economic growth, environmental protection, general well-being of the public, job opportunities, improve wastewater management, and subsequently drinking water quality.
3153.activities: The funds will be used for the construction of new water and sewer infrastructure, including the following: - New master lift station - 4.7-mile wastewater forcemain - 1-mile of potable water main
3153.direct_services: The direct services include new water & sewer infrastructure to new and existing customers, improving water pressure and fire flow as well as supporting local economic growth. The new watermain will provide sustained pressure to customers in the Poquito area, as well as higher fire flows. The new master lift station and forcemain will enhance the existing wastewater system in the area as well as e
3153.population: The population within Poquito Bayou, approximately 2,500 people, as well as the potential population growth from proposed development in the area. The expansion is currently planned for 350-500 residential units (townhomes and multi family residences) which could house up to 1,330 additional residents, at the County's current populatoin of 2.66 persons per household. Additional temporary residents will be served by the addition of a proposed convention center and adjacent hotel.
3153.outcome: The expected outcome is the completion of the construction of the necessary water and sewer infrastructure to support future development in the area, as outlined above. In addition, Victory Village has dedicated a portion of land for a utility easement so the lift station and all necessary pipeline can be constructed.

2520.organization: Mentors for Fatherless Children and Abused
2520.description: The Mentors For Fatherless Children and Abused Families Corporation (MFCAF) Family Support and Engagement Program provides evidence-based mentorship, family stabilization, and emotional intelligence education for youth ages 10–18 and their families in Orange, Seminole, and Osceola Counties. This program delivers one-on-one and group mentoring, family case management, and skill-building workshops to strengthen communication, reduce behavioral challenges, and improve mental and emotional resilience
2520.purpose: The funds will enable Mentors For Fatherless Children and Abused Families Corporation (MFCAF) to establish Central Florida’s first Intervention and Family Resource Center — a trauma-informed, community-based hub designed to prevent youth delinquency, strengthen families, and expand access to emotional intelligence education, mentorship, and workforce development.
2520.activities: Renovate and equip a safe, compliant facility for mentorship and family services. Provide trauma-informed mental health counseling and therapy. Deliver youth mentorship programs focused on leadership, decision-making, and emotional regulation. Conduct family workshops on communication, financial literacy, and wellness. Offer case management and referral services to connect families with housing, education, and employment support.
2520.direct_services: Residents will receive no-cost or low-cost family mentoring, counseling, and educational workshops designed to prevent at-risk behavior and promote mental health. Services include one-on-one mentorship, family therapy, career development sessions, and youth engagement activities that build confidence, resilience, and responsibility.
2520.population: The project targets at-risk youth ages 10–18, families in crisis, and economically disadvantaged adults in Orange and Seminole Counties.¿Estimated Number Served: Approximately 400 individuals annually, including 250 youth and 150 parents/guardians.
2520.outcome: Improve mental health: 70% of participants report lower stress and improved emotional control (measured through pre-/post-assessments and therapist evaluations). Reduce recidivism: 60% of youth avoid further involvement in the juvenile justice system within 12 months (tracked via case management and county data). Enhance family stability: 65% of families demonstrate improved communication and family functioning (evaluated through surveys and counselor reports). Increase employment readiness: 50% of adult participants secure or maintain stable employment (verified through self- report and follow-up interviews).

2899.description: Think Big for Kids mission is to break the cycle of poverty by preparing kids for today's workforce. We partner with companies, such as ReliaQuest and A-LIGN, from diverse industries to support our unique “Three Pillars” approach incorporating career exploration, mentorship, and job readiness & placement. The funds will be used for mentor training, paid internships, apprenticeships, scholarships, software application upgrades and training materials to prepare low income youth for the workforce.
2899.purpose: Think Big for Kids mission is to break the cycle of poverty by preparing kids for today's workforce. We partner with companies, such as ReliaQuest and A-LIGN, from diverse industries to support our unique “Three Pillars” approach incorporating career exploration, mentorship, and job readiness & placement. The funds will be used for mentor training, paid internships, apprenticeships, scholarships, software application upgrades and training materials to prepare low income youth for the workforce.
2899.activities: In alignment with our mission, the funds will be used to prepare and place youth in the Florida workplace. Specifically through career exploration, mentorship and job readiness & placement. We will provide students with job shadowing, internships, skill-building workshops, scholarships, a software application and mentors to prepare them for post- graduation and enter the workforce.
2899.direct_services: Think Big offers monthly career showcases, mentor and volunteer training, paid internships to students working in regional businesses, apprenticeship programs, scholarships, job readiness workshops and job shadow opportunities. The software application allows students, mentors and employers the ability to find resources, collaborate and serve as a communication tool to access our program.
2899.population: Economically disadvantaged people, at-risk youth, grade school students, high school students, and college students. >800.
2899.outcome: Increase and improve economic activity- Think Big will track the student's entry into the workforce, including what industry, job type, title and salary they are earning. Create specific immediate job opportunities- We will measure by number of kids attending workshops, number of internships, job shadowing, apprenticeships and their careers entering the workforce. Enhance individual's economic self- sufficiency- Through tracking the number of students in the program, activities- based, mentor progress, number of internships, apprenticeships, scholarships and the job and salary of the student. We have CRM tools used for detailed reporting and tracking of the students journey, including a ment

1976.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
1976.description: FLIPANY’s Healthy Youth Practices Everywhere (HYPE) program builds strong, active, and resilient Florida youth by teaching lifelong fitness, nutrition, and self-management skills. Working with schools and youth organizations, HYPE provides hands-on cooking lessons, physical activity, and family wellness support to promote healthy routines, academic success, and reduced long-term health risks. This initiative supports the Governor’s Make America Healthy Again mission by preventing chronic disease before it begins and preparing children to lead healthy, productive lives. State funding will expand capacity to meet rising demand and serve an additional 10,500 youth with structured fitness, nutrition education, and family-focused wellness programming.
1976.purpose: Funds will expand FLIPANY’s Healthy Youth Practices Everywhere (HYPE) program, which supports the Governor’s Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) mission by promoting health through nutrition education, healthy meals, and mentored physical activity. The program will reach 1,000 children ages 3–15 with nutrition education and physical fitness programming and 3,000 youth ages 5–14 with healthy meals during out of school time, improving dietary knowledge and long-term health outcomes.
1976.activities: FLIPANY will deliver cooking and nutrition education sessions, mentored fitness classes, and family wellness engagement as well as healthy meals during out of school time across Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade Counties to prevent chronic disease and obesity before they begin and promote healthy lifestyles supporting the Governor’s Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) mission.
1976.direct_services: Through its Healthy Youth Practices Everywhere (HYPE) program, FLIPANY will provide nutritious meals, hands-on cooking and nutrition lessons, and guided physical activity sessions for children and families in South Florida, improving access to healthy food, physical fitness, and preventive wellness education.
1976.population: This project will serve youth populations who are economically disadvantaged, experiencing poor physical health, or identified as at-risk. The program specifically targets preschool, grade school, and high school students, with a focus on supporting children and teens who lack equitable access to health, wellness, and nutrition opportunities. The initiative is expected to benefit approximately 10,500 youth annually.
1976.outcome: This project will improve physical health, mental well-being, nutrition knowledge, and family self-sufficiency. 70% of youth will adopt or intend to adopt healthier physical activity and eating habits, and 70% will show improved self- management and resilience. 75% will demonstrate increased nutrition knowledge and ability to make healthy food choices. Families will report greater ability to prepare affordable, nutritious meals at home. Outcomes will be measured through pre/post surveys, tests, fitness logs, rubrics, participant feedback, and mentor observations.

1978.organization: University of Florida College of Medicine

FAIHT has secure data enclaves and AI deployment tools as its core structure. FAIHT operates through 3 integrated hubs: Gainesville Applied Research Translational Hub (advancing AI diagnostics and clinical tools via HiPerGator supercomputer), Jacksonville Applied Research & Medical Education Hub (community health innovation and workforce development), and Campus Without Borders Education Hub (graduate programs, industry partnerships, statewide upskilling).

Training and apprenticeships will prepare students and workers for fulfilling, well-paid careers. The AI Policy Analysis Lab and community outreach will boost Floridians’ digital health literacy and identify pote
