It will also create new “AI for Health” apprenticeship jobs for high school graduates and early-career workers and benefit patients through safer, smarter, and more accessible care. Funds will protect Floridians’ privacy while advancing AI to improve patient outcomes, build a vibrant AI health sector, and make Florida the national leader for effective medical AI policy. 3326.description: The Emergency Backup Generators – Wastewater System Resiliency project will install backup generators at 17 critical wastewater pump stations across the City of Tallahassee. These generators will ensure continuous operation during power outages caused by hurricanes or severe storms, preventing wastewater overflows and environmental contamination. The project strengthens storm resiliency, protects public health, and safeguards water quality throughout Tallahassee and neighboring counties.
3326.purpose: The project will install emergency backup generators at 17 critical wastewater pump stations to ensure uninterrupted operation during storms and power outages. This will strengthen system resiliency, prevent wastewater overflows, protect public health, and safeguard the environment while supporting statewide infrastructure hardening and environmental protection goals.
3326.activities: Activities include purchasing and installing emergency backup generators at 17 critical wastewater pump stations, along with required site preparation, electrical connections, and engineering work. These improvements will ensure reliable wastewater service during power outages, prevent overflows, and enhance the system’s overall resiliency and environmental protection.
3326.direct_services: The project will provide citizens with reliable wastewater service during storms and power outages, preventing sewer overflows and environmental contamination. This ensures continued protection of public health, clean waterways, and resilient infrastructure for residents and businesses throughout Tallahassee and surrounding counties.
3326.population: The target population includes residents, businesses, and institutions served by the City of Tallahassee’s wastewater system. The project will benefit more than 200,000 people across Tallahassee and surrounding areas by ensuring reliable wastewater service, protecting public health, and preventing environmental impacts during severe weather events.
3326.outcome: The project will enhance wastewater system reliability, prevent overflows, and protect public health and the environment during power outages. Success will be measured by tracking system uptime during storms, reduction in sanitary sewer overflow incidents, improved compliance with environmental standards, and decreased service disruptions, demonstrating strengthened resiliency and environmental protection.

1962.description: Tallahassee International Airport (TLH) is establishing a Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) spanning an 11-county area between I-75 and Port St. Joe to boost international commerce, attract businesses, enhance market competitiveness, and drive economic growth. To support operations, TLH will upgrade an existing facility to meet Customs and Border Protection standards, integrating logistics infrastructure and inventory control systems to manage freight and support business needs efficiently.
1962.purpose: This project will provide necessary capital improvement in order to establish a Foreign Trade Zone in the region.
1962.activities: To prepare for Zone operations at TLH, an existing facility will be modified to comply with Customs and Border Protection's stringent security standards. TLH's improved FTZ site will include a warehousing management system and computerized inventory control to track freight.
1962.direct_services: Shipping and manufacturing businesses that import and export merchandise can take advantage of the FTZ to significantly reduce the cost of customs duties, taxes, and tariffs and improve their supply chain operations.
1962.population: The target population is businesses intending to import or export goods internationally and residents who will benefit from the increased goods and lower prices as a result. This would put the expected number of individuals to be served between 500,000 and 1,000,000.
1962.outcome: The FTZ will increase and improve economic activity by encouraging international commerce and attracting shipping and manufacturing businesses to the Northwest and North Central Florida Region. The Zone will help forge partnerships between the public and private sectors and ultimately improve freight, transportation and logistics in the region. Increased and improved economic activity will be measured by tracking the number of aligning industries that are attracted to Northwest and North Central Florida as a result of the FTZ. The volume of regional freight activity can also be measured and tracked by entities such as the Florida Department of Transportation and the Capital Region Transporta

2165.description: The purpose of this program is to eliminate hazardous and substandard housing conditions affecting low- to moderate- income homeowners facing economic hardship. Program funding will be used to rehabilitate homes over 59 years old through essential improvements such as electrical, HVAC, and ADA-compliant upgrades, along with kitchen, bathroom, accessibility, and flooring enhancements. These investments will help reduce code enforcement liens and prevent foreclosures, while enabling senior residents to age safely in place and avoid unnecessary institutionalization.
2165.purpose: The purpose of the program is to assist seniors and low- to moderate-income residents in remaining safely and healthily in their homes. By addressing critical home repairs and modifications, the program helps prevent code enforcement liens and foreclosures that could result in homelessness or institutionalization. This initiative promotes housing stability, supports independent living, and enhances the overall health and well-being of vulnerable community members.
2165.activities: Licensed contractors will provide essential home repairs for seniors and low- to moderate-income homeowners in the Malibu Groves neighborhood, addressing critical infrastructure, health and safety, and ADA-related needs. If approved, these repairs will include electrical and HVAC upgrades, ADA improvements, bathroom and kitchen renovations, flooring, and enhanced accessibility. By targeting these key areas, the program ensures that homes are safe, functional, and accessible, enabling residents t
2165.direct_services: Construction and repair upgrades will be implemented in an aging, 59-year-old community to support economically disadvantaged homeowners. These interventions will bring homes up to current code standards, reducing the risk of code enforcement liens, foreclosures, and potential institutionalization. By addressing critical housing deficiencies, the program promotes safe, healthy, and sustainable liv
2165.population: This project will serve seniors and low- to moderate-income homeowners in the Malibu Groves neighborhood. Each year, the program will provide support to five to ten homeowners, focusing on critical home repairs and modifications that promote safe, healthy, and accessible living conditions. By targeting this population, the program ensures that limited resources are directed to those most at risk of housing instability and code enforcement actions.
2165.outcome: Providing direct services to homeowners in the Malibu Groves neighborhood will result in repaired homes that are safe, decent, and sanitary. These improvements will help prevent foreclosures and homelessness while supporting seniors in remaining in their homes, thereby reducing the risk of institutionalization. By investing in the health and safety of residents’ homes, the program promotes long-term housing stability, community resilience, and overall well- being for vulnerable populations.

1806.organization: Dixie County Board of County Commissioners
1806.description: Dixie County received funding in FY 23-24 for the purchase of a tanker (SF 2269). The County requests the remaining funds to revert and be appropriated to allow the County to update the fire tanker. The requested remaining funds from line 2479A appropriated in FY 2023-24 will be spent to update the fire tanker with equipment and accessories including hose lines and other various furnishings. This will increase efficiency and ensure that citizens and property are protected during a fire.
1806.purpose: The requested remaining funds from line-item 2479A appropriated in FY 2023-24 will be spent to update the fire tanker with equipment and accessories including hose lines and other various furnishings. This will increase efficiency and ensure that citizens and property are protected during a fire.
1806.activities: Adding additional equipment, apparatus, and accessories to the new tanker truck will increase firefighting efficiency, enhance service capabilities, and expand reliability when firefighters respond to a call.
1806.direct_services: If funding is received, new equipment will allow Dixie County to provide improved services to citizens during a fire, including increased water delivery, shortened fire suppression times and expanded service to citizens in the County’s most rural areas. Citizens will also be able to have increased trust in updated equipment for the tanker.
1806.population: Dixie County. Thousands of individuals will be served.
1806.outcome: Updated equipment and accessories on the tanker will allow for enhanced fire and emergency services to citizens. This helps Dixie County protect the general public from harm of fires. Once updated equipment is placed in the tanker, metrics such as fire suppression times, water delivery, and the rescue of individuals during a fire can be measured.

2505.description: Pinellas County Schools is committed to advancing workforce and economic development by expanding workforce training and dual enrollment opportunities in high-demand career programs. With support through a state capital investment, the modernization of Pinellas Technical College’s St. Petersburg campus will enhance its appeal and functionality as a high-quality postsecondary institution. This project aligns with Florida’s talent pipeline priorities and will increase the number of skilled graduates entering Florida’s workforce, generating increased economic returns to the state within their first year of employment.
2505.purpose: Pinellas Technical College’s St. Petersburg campus will be modernized to strengthen its position as a high-quality postsecondary institution. The project will expand workforce training and dual enrollment opportunities in high-demand career programs in alignment with Florida's economic and talent development goals.
2505.activities: Pinellas Technical College’s St. Petersburg campus will undergo facility upgrades that modernize its instructional training environments. This capital investment will enhance the campus’s appeal to prospective and current students, creating opportunities to increase high school career dual enrollment and boost enrollment in high-demand workforce and trades programs.
2505.direct_services: Pinellas County, the Tampa Bay Region, and the State of Florida will benefit from an increased number of skilled graduates entering the workforce. These individuals will generate increased economic returns to the state within their first year of employment.
2505.population: The target population includes high school students and adults in St. Petersburg and its surrounding areas. Currently, more than 1,500 students are on the combined waitlist for PTC's HVAC, Electricity and Practical Nursing programs.
2505.outcome: The modernization of Pinellas Technical College’s St. Petersburg campus is expected to increased enrollment of high school students and adults in high-demand career and workforce programs. Increased enrollment will produce more graduates who enter Florida’s workforce with industry-relevant skills, contributing to the state’s talent pipeline. The outcomes will be measured by year-over-year student enrollment, successful completion of programs, attainment of industry certifications or credentials, and graduate employment rates and job placement in high-demand fields.

The Project will recruit and partner with leading Florida technology companies in areas such as autonomous technology, 3D manufacturing, DNA sequencing, battery cell technology, etc. The Project supports economic development and will serve as a model for the state.
2506.purpose: Design and build technology-focused corporate fronts in partnership with leading Florida corporations. These spaces in the Innovation Center will provide middle school students with state-of-the-art, hands-on learning experiences in emerging and disruptive technologies. The project will foster collaboration between public and private sectors in support of education and workforce development, drive economic growth by attracting and showcasing technology companies, and establish a state and nation
2506.activities: High-tech corporations will develop learning modules in partnership with PCS and in consultation with ARK Invest analysts to recreate actual operations taking place within their corporations. Students will engage and learn about various disruptive technologies that are shaping the present and future world and workforce. Students will benefit by learning about these technologies as well as understanding what it takes to study and participate in these select industries.
2506.direct_services: The Innovation Center will deliver hands-on, standards-aligned learning in a variety of areas such as engineering, physics, biology, environmental sciences, medical sciences, finance, economics, computer programming, and technology. Students will participate in pre- and post-visit classroom lessons that bookend the immersive experiences at the Center, further strengthening academic achievement and
2506.population: The project will serve over 5,000 PCS middle school students annually, plus students from neighboring districts through field trips. It will also impact the entire State of Florida by providing a statewide model for learning, enabling other districts to visit, learn, and replicate.
2506.outcome: The development and launch of an Innovation Center featuring high-demand, emerging/disruptive technology companies, as measured by the number of companies that participate in the Center), which will serve as statewide model and provide opportunities for other counties to visit, learn and replicate. Student participation in the Center activities will be measured using the schedule of activities and field trips hosted in the Center.

1843.description: Further develop, enhance and expand innovative science-based coral restoration technologies that have demonstrated success, allow for physical coral habitat restoration work to be completed, provide ex-situ life support systems for threatened coral types, increase genetic diversity for reproduction and out-planting. The funding is also for developing additional strategically located in-situ and ex-situ coral nurseries for increasingly efficient and efficient coral reef habitat restoration.
1843.purpose: Further develop, enhance and expand innovative science-based coral restoration technologies that have demonstrated success, allow for physical coral habitat restoration work to be completed, provide ex-situ life support systems for threatened coral types, increase genetic diversity for reproduction and out-planting, and develop additional strategically located in-situ and ex-situ coral nurseries for increasingly efficient and efficient coral reef habitat restoration.
1843.activities: Expand science-based technology to enhance resilient coral restoration and increase survival, develop strategically located nurseries for efficient and effective restoration along entire FL reef tract, educate the public and visitors on value of coral reefs, and expedite recovery from extreme temperature and disease events, while establishing contingencies for future extreme environmental events.
1843.direct_services: Florida's coral reefs are the third largest living reef on the planet. The direct services of restored coral reefs are their numerous ecological, aesthetic, economic and cultural functions - providing habitats for over 6,000 marine species, attracting 16 million visitors per year, and supports over 71,000 local jobs, drawing $6.3 billion to Florida economy.
1843.population: All Florida residents and visitors, specifically commercial and recreational fishing, diving, restaurant, hotel and tourism industries. Millions of individuals are expected to be served.
1843.outcome: Restored coral reefs benefiting Florida's coastal ecology and economy. FWC grant agreement deliverables will ensure outcomes are achieved.

2622.description: Design, permitting, and construction of Segment 4 of the Regional Corridor from I-295 to US-1 in Jacksonville, FL. This regional transportation corridor will improve traffic circulation and pedestrian safety from US-1 in Northeast St Johns County to I-295 and SR-202 (JT Butler Blvd) in Jacksonville's southside. The facility will include multi-use paths for pedestrians, bikes, and alternative modes of transportation. Segment 4 provides the central connection to the existing transportation network and links US-1 and SR-9B. The Regional Corridor will provide parallel routes for local and regional traffic using US-1, SR-9B, and I-295.
2622.purpose: The goal is to efficiently add roadway capacity in the center of Jacksonville's busiest area. This cost effective investment in a regional transportation corridor will improve traffic circulation and pedestrian safety from Northeast St Johns County and on Jacksonville's southside. The facility will include multi-use paths for pedestrians and bikes. Segment 4 provides the central connection to the existing transportation network and links US-1 and SR9B if widened from 2 to 4 lanes.
2622.activities: The funds will be used to widen the planned Segment 4 roadway from 2 to 4 lanes. By widening and networking with surrounding roadways as it is being constructed, it will provide alternative routes for regional and local traffic. This Regional Corridor allows traffic to avoid congestion on some of Jacksonville's most heavily traveled roadways: US-1, SR-9B, and I-295.
2622.direct_services: Citizens will have alternative routes available for commuting to work, school, or other commercial needs. Civil resources like schools and parks have also been master planned along the corridor to serve the region.
2622.population: The improvement would benefit the 986,000 citizens of Jacksonville and 333,000 citizens of St Johns County.
2622.outcome: To reduce the heavy congestion on US-1 by providing travelers a safe alternative route to their regional destinations. With the State's participation, the landowner can expand the planned roadways to provide capacity for regional traffic at a fraction of what it would cost a public agency to widen the roadway later. The benefit will be measured by the annual traffic on US-1, SR-9B, and I-295.

1808.description: The purpose of the project is to upgrade the athletic track and field to make it accessible to all students and community members of Franklin County as our only consolidated school complex. We will ensure ADA compliance for the field, including accessibility. Modern operational equipment will be installed, the track will be a meter track, required by FHSAA interscholastic athletic competition. The track surface will be updated with polyurethane black matting for performance and safety.
1808.purpose: Support for the project has been expressed by community members and stakeholders for many years. The school superintendent is requesting upgrades and renovations as part of safety and community improvement planning. Franklin County would like to host other schools to participate in events on our campus, which in turn brings revenue into our community.
1808.activities: A modern, safe and organized school promotes opportunities for our students and local stakeholders to utilize the track and field for school and community events, skill development in athletics and life skills, fitness and social bonding. Practices and games will be held here as well as community events. The current state of track is a liability and hazardous.
1808.direct_services: The track can be used as a walking/recreational track for after school, the Fall Festival, Homecoming Events, church and community events. It will be ADA compliant so we can foster an inclusive and equitable environment for all citizens of Franklin and surrounding counties.
1808.population: The targeted population includes the majority of the citizens in Franklin County, Florida. Elderly persons, persons with special needs, economically disadvantaged, at risk youth, preschool students, students grades K-12, college and university students.
1808.outcome: The benefit will be the overall accessibility and required updates to host community events, sporting events as well as community based events in a safe, friendly environment. Success will be measured by the number of events hosted annually.

3196.description: The City of Mary Esther urgently needs to complete the replacement of the aging water mains beneath and adjacent to Highway 98. This infrastructure, installed after World War II, is now fragile and inaccessible, causing frequent line failures, discolored water issues, and the risk of system-wide service outages (one such outage recently occurred) due to obsolete fire hydrants and a lack of isolation valves. An initial phase, from Hurlburt Field to Andalusia Road, was funded by an FDEP Pilot Water Grant. The requested appropriation will fund the second and final phase, which extends from Andalusia Road to the eastern City limits.
3196.purpose: The funds will achieve comprehensive improvement in system reliability, fire protection, water quality, and water pressure for residents and businesses along the critical Highway 98 corridor.
3196.activities: Activities include design, engineering, easement acquisition, construction, and construction administration of the new water mains and system upgrades.
3196.direct_services: The project will directly provide reliable access to potable water and fire protection for the service area.
3196.population: The entire City of Mary Esther (estimated at 4,493 residents) is the target population, benefitting from enhanced system resilience and reduced service disruptions. The project will directly serve approximately 300 residents and businesses along the replacement route with upgraded water mains, water valves, and modern, breakaway fire hydrants.
3196.outcome: Expected benefits are a quantifiable decrease in non-revenue water loss and an increase in service reliability, critical outcomes given the system's fragility (e.g., the June 2025 system-wide outage from an obsolete fire hydrant strike). Outcomes will be measured by monthly water loss reports, tracking the frequency of line repairs and breaks, and verifying improved fire protection through post-construction flow testing to document water pressure and availability.

This request would allow for survey, environmental, design permitting, inspection and construction to ensure funds are spent in the best ways to address the needed upgrades.

The community center will provide indoor space for events, classes and training hosted by the public. Town and County staff, various school extracurricular club and will be the voting district precinct.

3148.outcome: Upgrades to the Argyle Fire Department would provide enriched cultural experiences for people who attend events held at the facility. Improve education would be provided with the facility offering training and educational seminars. Public educational events for fire safety and offer trainings and seminars. The number in attendance would be completed prior to and following construction. Transportation facilities would be improved by providing paved parking areas, and engineering inspection would be completed to evaluate improvements prior to and following construction and upgrades.

2071.description: Indian River State College (IRSC) is seeking $9.9 million in 2026-2027 non-recurring capital outlay project funding to expand Indiantown HS to include athletic facilities for state supported physical education programs and the opportunity to compete in interscholastic athletic programs. After building the $33.3 million school with a majority of private funding and achieving an 'A' grade, IRSC is now asking for additional support from the State for planning, engineering, and construction dollars to bring this much-needed project to fruition. Physical education programs and interscholastic athletic opportunities play a key role in student retention/success, and these facilities at Indiantown H.S. will help the school adhere to FLDOE physical education recommendations and requirements. IRSC has secured $2 million in private funding for the project.
2071.purpose: Planning, engineering and construction of athletic facilities for Indiantown High School. Project will include but not be limited to locker room/wet room facilities, concessions, covered sport-court area, and full competition track and football/soccer field. Facilities will be primarily used by IHS students for physical education programs and the opportunity to compete in FHSAA sanctioned athletics.
2071.activities: The planned facilities expansion will enable physical education programs to take places at IHS, a necessary programmatic addition for the grades 9-12 experience. IHS students will also have the opportunity to compete in intra- district athletic competitions as a school.
2071.direct_services: The Village of Indiantown's only high school will have healthier, more focused students as a result of incorporating athletic opportunities.
2071.population: High School Students, Community Members - 200-400 annually, tens of thousands over time.
2071.outcome: Stronger student success metrics. School grades. Retention rates. Student persistence. Individual student score/grade improvements.

3203.description: The City of Paxton's sanitary sewer system has been experiencing pump and forcemain failures due to excessive pressure in the system. The goal of this project is to alleviate the high pressures in the transmission system which are a result of small diameter pipes for exceptionally long distances. The project proposes to up-size the forcemain piping and improve the pump stations as required to adapt to the changed pumping conditions.
3203.purpose: The goal of the project is to eliminate the pump and forcemain failures, along with lift station overflows, being experienced by the City of Paxton due to high pressures in the transmission system which are the result of small diameter pipes running for exceptionally long distances.
3203.direct_services: The citizens of Paxton will get a direct benefit from the project by having a more reliable sewer system for years to come. Improved collection system capacity will help to increase development in the community which will improve job prospects and citizen's quality of life.
3203.population: The target population is the residents of the City of Paxton who use the sewer service and future sewer customers. The City of Paxton has a population of approximately 670.
3203.outcome: The outcome of the project will be upgraded sewer collection system. The project will improve the capacity of the sanitary sewer collection and transmission system allowing more customers to connect to the City's system, reducing the amount of septic tanks that will need to be constructed and reducing the number of sanitary sewer overflows.

Measured by Progress Reports; Report Cards; Mentorship logs indicating growth strengths, challenges and improvements for each youth. Pre and Post Career Exploration Portfolios

3205.description: The funds will be used to replace the stadium bleachers at Vernon High School Memorial Stadium located in Vernon, Florida. Currently, the stadium capacity is 1658. The stadium serves not only the Vernon schools but the entire Vernon community. The existing stadium seating was originally constructed in the late 1970s, with a seating upgrade completed in 1989. Since that time, the structural stands have only received repairs on an as-needed basis. The stands are also due for ADA updates. The replacement of the bleachers is necessary to ensure

This will allow for the district to have an updated facility to host future educational and community events.

Approximately 20,000 people would be served throughout the year to host school and community events throughout the year.

3208.description: The proposed project includes the rehabilitation two of the City’s three wells (Well #1 and Well #2). Both wells are in poor condition and are presently not being utilized. This results in the City’s entire system being served by only one well. The City is presently utilizing a CDBG-NR to fund some rehabilitation, but had to reduce the scope of the needed repairs due to budget limitations. The funding requested herein will be used to supplement the CDBG-NR funding to complete all of the needed repairs.
3208.purpose: The goal of the project is to rehabilitate two wells, effectively upgrading the City of Vernon's water system and increasing its resiliency. The proposed improvements will also allow the City to comply with FDEP requirements to maintain a redundant water source.
3208.activities: The project will be bid and constructed.
3208.direct_services: The citizens of Vernon will get a direct benefit from the project by having a more reliable water system for years to come. Increasing the number of wells the City can depend on increases the resiliency of the water system and brings the City into compliance with FDEP.
3208.population: The target population is the residents of the City of Vernon who use the water service and future water customers. The City of Vernon has a population of approximately 730 people.
3208.outcome: The outcome of the project will be an upgraded and more resilient water system. The City will measure the success of the project by confirming that the rehabilitated wells are operational and meet the water demands of the City. Another notable success of the project will be the ability for the City to maintain continuous water service during routine maintenance or unexpected outages at Well No. 3.

1836.description: This project seeks to expand fecal indicator bacteria (FIB) monitoring at recreational waterways throughout Biscayne Bay, augmenting the Florida Healthy Beaches program by expanding the geographic area of the program. Weekly FIB sampling and environmental data collection using industry standard data collection device to ensure a holistic approach. Test results will be shared and accessible to the public through digital channels. Leveraging advanced statistical tools, we will analyze existing datasets, providing robust insights for agencies and policymakers.
1836.purpose: This program will augment existing weekly water quality monitoring at recreational waterways, providing test results to the public via digital channels. We will also apply novel, advanced statistical tools to analyze existing water quality datasets. This program will raise awareness about water quality challenges and solutions with the public. The goals are to improve public health, increase water quality awareness, and provide robust data analysis for agencies and policymakers.

1836.population: The target population includes: elderly persons, students at all ages (preschool, grade school, high school, university/college), the general public, general water-based stakeholders, and immunocompromised individuals. Over 100,000 individuals are expected to be served.

1882.description: This program supports veterans with service-related brain trauma by providing complementary and proven brain-health treatments, including ketamine-assisted therapy, stellate ganglion blocks (SGB) to "reset" the sympathetic nervous system and a neuroendocrine and biochemical restoration protocol that reduces brain inflammation, stabilizes brain chemistry, and improves cognitive and emotional functioning. These treatments, under close clinical supervision, help veterans reduce symptoms, regain stability, and return to fuller participation in family and community life. We work in partnership with the Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs by sharing outcome data and educating counselors so effective emerging treatments can be better understood and potentially made accessible to more veterans.
1882.purpose: The primary objective for Year 2 is to further reduce the systemic and practical barriers that prevent Florida veterans from accessing evidence-based and innovative brain-health treatment modalities. Funding will support three key strategies: Transportation stipends to ensure veterans can consistently attend treatment appointments; dedicated clinical coordination to guide veterans through complex care pathways, and expanded education and training for VA and community counselors on invisible woun
1882.activities: Continue providing veterans access to the Millennium Health Brain Resiliency Program, monthly ketamine treatments, adding SGBs, as proven neuroendocrine/biochemical restoration treatment modalities with integration support. Adding key services and activities that remove barriers to participation, include transportation stipends for veterans who cannot safely drive, a dedicated clinical coordinator to manage intake, scheduling, and follow-up, and expanded education for VA and community counselors
1882.direct_services: Veterans will receive a comprehensive brain-health intake that screens for Repeated Blast Exposure, PTSD, and related conditions, followed by lab-based assessment through Millennium Health to develop individualized treatment plans. Eligible veterans will be referred for ketamine-assisted or SGB treatments with integration support. To ensure access, the project will provide transportation stipends
1882.population: Veterans with a range of physiological brain conditions—including traumatic brain injuries (with emphasis on blast- related injuries), co-occurring mental health challenges, and substance use disorders—who are at elevated risk of aggression, self-harm, or suicide will be prioritized for services. The program will serve approximately 100 Florida Veterans, providing coordinated neurorestorative and supportive interventions that promote recovery, reduce risk, and help participants return to stable,
1882.outcome: The program is expected to improve veterans’ physical and mental health, reduce substance use/misuse, increase self-sufficiency, and decrease anxiety/aggression for safer family and community interactions. Outcomes will be measured through pre/post assessments, functioning scales, treatment completion data, and follow-up evaluations. Veterans are already reporting that these treatments “gave them their lives back,” reflecting gains in stability and the ability to support themselves and their families. A clinical researcher will assess and tabulate all the data into a comprehensive clinical study.

The goal of these

As needed, clients will also receive targeted case management and psychiatric/medication management support.The project will provide mental health and educational workshops that build coping skills, increase awareness, and strengthen overall well-being. Substance abuse prevention services will offer education and support to individuals struggling with or at risk of drug use. Workshops will provide participants with

2404.description: The project will acquire and preserve the natural floodplain function of two undeveloped, low-lying properties in the 500- year flood zone. The properties are surrounded by developed single-family homes lying within a closed drainage basin with no outfall. Acquisition ensures availability for future stormwater improvements in this area, as recommended by the Town's Watershed Master Plan.
2404.purpose: The project will acquire and preserve the natural floodplain function of two vacant, low-lying properties within the 500- year flood zone, ensuring availability for future stormwater improvements, as recommended by the Town's Watershed Master Plan. Both properties are in a closed basin. If not purchased by the Town, the properties could be developed for single-family homes, which would severely interrupt the properties' natural drainage function and preclude future drainage improvements.
2404.activities: Initially, the project will preserve the area's natural floodplain drainage function. In the future, the Town will design and construct stormwater retention facilities on the purchased property. These facilities will connect directly to and expand the existing stormwater facilities to the north and south, significantly increasing system capacity.
2404.direct_services: In the short term, the project ensures that no new development will worsen the existing drainage condition. The project area is surrounded by single-family homes within a closed drainage basin in the center of Ponce Inlet. With no natural outfall, this area experienced the worst flooding from Hurricanes Ian and Milton, and remains among the most vulnerable to recurrent flooding and stormwater accu
2404.population: The project will help protect 77 single-family residential structures in the immediate vicinity, along with the Town's Public Works facility and associated infrastructure.
2404.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is to reduce flooding impacts, improve stormwater system performance, and enhance overall community resilience to major rainfall and tidal events. By acquiring and converting up to two strategically located vacant residential lots in a flood-prone area, the Town will increase stormwater retention capacity, decrease runoff into adjacent neighborhoods, and lessen the frequency and duration of localized flooding. The project success will be determined by quantifiable reductions in flood impacts, measurable improvements in drainage system efficiency, and documented enhancements in water quality and community resilience.

2405.purpose: The requested funds will support dredging near the Turnbull Bay Canal Bridge to restore water flow through the removal of built up sediment, reduce neighborhood flooding, and improve tidal exchange and water quality in Rose Bay.
2405.activities: Construction/Dredging of Turnbull Creek Canal near the Turnbull Bay Canal Bridge.
2405.direct_services: The project will deliver critical flood protection and drainage improvements for residents in New Smyrna Beach, especially during hurricanes and intense rainfall. The improved capacity due to sediment removal will allow for water offshed
2405.population: This project would directly benefit residents near the Turnbull Canal and Rose Bay Area. Additionally, due to improved drainage, this project would also affect the City as a whole. This area has a large percentage of low and moderate income residents that are signficantly affected by extreme weather events.

2169.description: The Healing Community program is a collective, safe, and transformative space for women who have survived domestic violence and sexual abuse. The funds will be used to purchase a building to provide group workshops, educational talks with mental health experts, along with practical tools for emotional healing, empowerment, and prevention. The program helps participants heal from trauma, builds support network, promotes self-sufficiency, and breaks the cycle of violence. Victims of domestic violence will have a safe place of refuge during their time of distress. They will be afforded temporary housing assistance, mental health counseling, food, clothing and case management to help in their transformation.
2169.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested is to purchase a building to house the "Healing Community" program. The goal is to transform lives of survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking to become productive citizens.
2169.activities: The building will be used to provide group workshops, educational talks with mental health experts, practical tools for emotional healing, empowerment and prevention workshops that will promote self-sufficiency and confidence.

Services include facilitator-led lessons, hands-on projects, career exploration sessions, and connection to resources that improve youth safety, skills, and future readiness.
2170.direct_services: Youth will receive direct in-person services, including career assessments, workforce readiness instruction, financial literacy training, mentoring, project-based learning, and structured activities that build communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving. Programs provide safe, supervised environments and individualized support to help youth plan for long term success.
2170.population: The project serves jobless persons, economically disadvantaged youth, and at-risk middle and high school students ages 11–18. These students face limited access to structured enrichment, career training, and future-planning support. The program will provide direct services to approximately 100 youth annually, offering career readiness instruction, life- skills development, and safe, supervised activities designed to improve long-term education and workforce outcomes.
2170.outcome: The project will improve education, economic self-sufficiency, and reduce juvenile justice involvement. Outcomes include 75% of youth increasing knowledge and identifying a career path while building decision-making and life skills. Progress will be measured through pre/post assessments, Positive Youth Development Index scores, pathway tools, and attendance and engagement tracking.

2002.description: The current City Public Works facility is operated out of an inadequate metal warehouse/garage-style building constructed in the 1990's. The city has previously contracted for architectural schematics and design for a new hurricane-hardened Public Works facility, which is at 30% design completion. This funding request will help bring architectural and design to 100%.
2002.purpose: Funding a new, storm-hardened Public Works facility will ensure public utility operations are protected and remain viable in situations of hazardous weather events, and allow emergency streets and stormwater staff to properly respond to the community needs before, during, and after hurricanes and other disaster related events that impact the citizens and local area.
2002.activities: Public Works provides services for the operational maintenance of streets, stormwater, right-of-ways, city parks and sidewalks. The funding will facilitate the architectural schematics and design being completed from 30% design to 100% design for a new hurricane-hardened facility.
2002.direct_services: Ensure there is an adequate base of operations to ensure the over 14,000 citizens of Orange City, in addition to an estimated 35,000 daily visitors, have access to safe city streets, parks and sidewalks as quickly and efficiently as possible after a major weather incident.
2002.population: All estimated 14,882 permanent residents of the city, as well as transient business visitors of around 35,000 per day who come to Orange City every day to utilize our medical services, retail shopping, and restaurant outlets.
2002.outcome: The most critical benefit will be to provide a hurricane-hardened Public Works facility that will ensure the safety of personnel, coupled with ensuring the City's ability to respond before, during and after weather and disaster related events and disasters.

2411.description: The Watermain Replacement project is to provide for necessary watermain replacements throughout the City of Deltona’s service area. Project in general consists of Construction of replacement potable water distribution mains including associated restoration work (pavement, curb, driveways and sodding). The City has approximately 455 miles of watermains. The City of Deltona offers water services to approximately 36,800 customers both within the City and outside. Much of the infrastructure was installed in the 1960-1970’s and has exceeded its useful life. The City budget’s approximately $1M annually for watermain replacement, but that funding is insufficient to keep up with the needed replacements.
2411.purpose: Completion of Groups 2, 3 & 4 Watermain Replacements within budget, according to the scope of work and wilthin the period of performance.
2411.activities: Replacement of watermains that service the Deltona Water service area.
2411.direct_services: Assurance of reliable water services with limited interruptions due to watermain breaks.
2411.population: Deltona Water customers are the target population. Estimated 2,500 customers to be served.
2411.outcome: The reduction in the number of watermain breaks throughout the service area will provide the measurement that the project was sucessful. This project should also see a reduction in water quality complaints to the utility.

2410.description: The Cured In Place Pipe & Infrastructure Lining project will correct structural integrity issues of failing sanitary sewer lines and infrastructure. Failure of the sanitary sewer lines & infrastructure is due to factors such as age and increased stress due to population growth. This infrastructure places the community at risk due to high probability that a sewer line collapses or otherwise becomes compromised requiring immediate repair, placing the public and environment at risk from Sanitary Sewer Overflows.
2410.purpose: Completion of lining of pipes & infrastructure as priortized based on recent inspection findings. This lining of pipes will reduce inflow and infiltration resulting in less unwarranted flow to the waste water treatement plants and less stress on the sanitary sewer system as a whole.
2410.activities: The completiion of pipe & infrsatructure lining from the priority listing.
2410.direct_services: Assurance of consistant sanitary sewer service with limited interruptions due to infrastructure breaks.
2410.population: Target population is the entire collection customers estimated at 7,500 customers.
2410.outcome: The reduction in the number of sanitary sewer breaks throughout the service area will provide the measurement that the project was sucessful.

2389.description: The Greynolds Raptor Center Septic-to-Sewer Project will complete the necessary infrastructure to support the renovation of a former fire station at Greynolds Park into a Raptor Rehabilitation Center operated by the Museum of Science in partnership with Miami-Dade County. The project will replace the outdated septic system with a sewer line connection to meet environmental standards and secure the occupancy permit. Once complete, the Center will provide the community with environmental education, wildlife rehabilitation programming, and conservation services for children and adults, while advancing Miami-Dade County’s strategic conservation goals.
2389.purpose: The funds will be used to design and construct the septic-to-sewer conversion at the Greynolds Raptor Center, replacing the outdated septic system with a connection to the County’s sewer line. This will ensure compliance with environmental standards, secure the occupancy permit, and allow the facility to open and operate as a community resource providing wildlife rehabilitation, environmental education, and conservation programming for children and adults.
2389.activities: The requested funds will support the design and construction activities necessary to remove the existing septic system and connect the Greynolds Raptor Center to the County’s sewer line. These activities will include engineering design, permitting, construction of sewer infrastructure, and final inspections to ensure compliance with environmental standards. Once complete, these funds will allow the Center to operate and provide direct services to the public, including wildlife rehabilitation, en
2389.direct_services: The requested funds will provide citizens with direct access to environmental education and conservation services by enabling the septic-to-sewer conversion necessary for the Greynolds Raptor Center to open and operate. Once complete, the Center will deliver wildlife rehabilitation, education, hands-on experiences with local wildlife, and nature- based programming for children and adults.
2389.population: The project will serve the general public, including children, families, and schools across Miami-Dade County, with a focus on underserved communities near Greynolds Park. Once operational, the Center is expected to serve over 10,000 individuals annually through educational programs, community events, and conservation activities
2389.outcome: The expected outcome is compliance with environmental standards through septic-to-sewer conversion, enabling the Center to open and serve over 10,000 visitors annually with conservation and education programs. Outcomes will be measured by project completion, environmental compliance reports, program attendance tracking, visitor surveys, and wildlife rehabilitation data.

2004.description: Folds of Honor requests support to provide statewide educational scholarships for Florida spouses and children of fallen or disabled service members and first responders. These families often face significant financial challenges after a service related death or disability. Scholarships will cover verified unmet needs for K through 12 students and higher education students. Folds of Honor directs ninety one percent of annual expenses to scholarship programs. This ensures the funds requested by the State of Florida directly support Florida families who have sacrificed for our safety and freedom.
2004.purpose: The funds requested will provide direct educational scholarships to Florida spouses and children of fallen or disabled service members and first responders. These families often face significant financial strain after a life altering loss or injury. This support will cover verified unmet needs for K12 and higher education students, reducing the number of unfunded Florida applicants. 91% of annual expenses support scholarship programs, ensuring the funds directly benefit Florida families who have
2004.activities: The funds will provide Florida students with educational scholarships that cover tuition, required fees, textbooks, tutoring, and essential academic expenses. All awards are based on verified unmet need. With ninety one percent of expenses supporting scholarship programs, these funds directly strengthen educational access for families of fallen or disabled heroes.
2004.direct_services: The funds will support Florida families by providing educational scholarships that help students access stable and uninterrupted schooling. Services include assistance with tuition, instructional materials, tutoring support, and other verified academic expenses for K12 and higher education students. Each scholarship is awarded after a thorough review of eligibility and unmet need. With ninety one
2004.population: The project serves Florida spouses and children of fallen or disabled service members and first responders. These families have experienced significant sacrifice and often face financial barriers to education. The requested funds are expected to support about one hundred Florida students through full scholarships, with additional students receiving partial assistance.
2004.outcome: The project will expand educational access for Florida families of fallen or disabled service members and first responders by reducing the number of unfunded applicants. Outcomes will be measured by the number of Florida recipients funded, total scholarship dollars distributed, and recipient academic progress. All data is tracked through the Folds of Honor scholarship portal and verified by the Scholarship Team.

2751.description: This funding will provide the preliminary conceptual design of a sanitary sewer extension project to serve the Biscayne Shores neighborhood, including approximately 170 properties. The project is bounded by NE 111 St. to the North, NE 108 St. to the South, Biscayne Blvd. to the West and Bayshore Drive to the East and will include the preliminary design of the force main, pump station, and gravity sewer system.
2751.purpose: This funding will provide the preliminary design of a sanitary sewer extension project to serve the Biscayne Shores neighborhood, including approximately 170 properties. The project is bounded by NE 111 St. to the North, NE 108 St. to the South, Biscayne Blvd. to the West and Bayshore Drive to the East and will include the preliminary design of the force main, pump station, and gravity sewer system.
2751.activities: Funds will support preliminary planning and engineering for the Biscayne Shores sanitary sewer extension, including conceptual design of the gravity system, force main, and pump station; site assessments; utility coordination; and development of cost estimates and permitting needs. These activities will prepare the project for final design and construction to serve approximately 170 properties.
2751.direct_services: This project will provide residents in the Biscayne Shores neighborhood with access to reliable centralized wastewater service, reducing the risk of septic system failures, groundwater contamination, and flooding-related public health concerns. The project will support long-term community resilience by improving environmental protection, safeguarding Biscayne Bay, and ensuring uninterrupted wastew
2751.population: Residents of Miami-Dade County, benefiting more than 2.8 million people, including the local community within the project area.
2751.outcome: Outcomes Redirect wastewater from aging septic systems to the sanitary sewer network, eliminating nutrient and bacterial pollution sources that threaten groundwater and Biscayne Bay. Methodology Track the number of septic systems decommissioned and properties connected to the sanitary sewer system.

2386.description: This project will retrofit, harden, increase the capacity of the existing pump station, and enable the optimization of its operation. It will improve storage and conveyance capabilities by mitigating flooding and reducing nutrient loading in the drainage basin, thereby improving the flood quantity and water quantity level of service. Project location: NE 150 Street & N. Spur Drive.
2386.purpose: The purpose of this project is to enhance the capacity of the existing pump station, optimizing its operation to prevent flood related damage to the roadway and adjacent properties and to stop pollutants from entering the stormwater systems and impacting the water quantity and quality in the Biscayne C-8 Canal watershed basin in Miami-Dade County. The pump station's electrical and mechanical components will be upgraded, hardened and elevated to resist flooding and sea level rise scenarios. Proje
2386.activities: Upgrade, hardening, and elevation of the pump station's electrical and mechanical components to resist flooding and sea level rise scenarios
2386.population: General—thousands of individuals will be served.
2386.outcome: Mitigate flooding by increasing and enhancing the capacity of the existing stormwater pump station (Biscayne Gardens Stormwater Pump Station)—measured by decrease in flooding incidents and reduction in the number of flood complaints received.

2390.description: Protective safety bollards and active barriers will be installed along the pedestrian Beachwalk ensuring a secure walkway to residents and the City's millions of visitors annually.
2390.purpose: Protective bollards and active barriers will serve a dual purpose: preventing vehicle intrusion and preserving the scenic shoreline. Miami Beach's investment in this initiative ensures an enduring, secure, and safe pedestrian walkway on the Beach appealing to both our city residents and our 8.8 million visitors annually.
2390.activities: Funds will be used for the construction and installation of bollards and active barriers along the pedestrian walkway on the Beach. The installation of the bollards will enhance and provide security for the visitor and resident experience along the Beachwalk.
2390.direct_services: The area's high popularity necessitates pedestrian and cyclist safety. These bollards and active barriers will deter vehicle access while maintaining the natural shoreline beauty. This investment will secure an iconic Beachwalk experience, fostering tourism and local enjoyment alike.
2390.population: The City's residents (over 80,000) and over 8 million annual visitors, and tourists to the area.
2390.outcome: A safety and security assessment conducted by Gannet Fleming identified several access points as highly vulnerable to vehicular access. The report ranked access points by their vulnerability using a Design Basis Threat methodology and recommendations were made for vehicle barriers / bollards for each access point. This Project would implement barriers to these highest vulnerable areas prioritized. The installation of safety bollards and active barriers not only enhances security but also plays a significant role in preserving and improving the natural environment along the Beachwalk, aligning with Miami Beach's goal of creating a secure and cherished coastal experience for residents and visi

2388.description: The water distribution system for the City of Opa-locka is more than 60 years old, the city is in need of replacing exisiting water mains, corroded iron pipe, PVC pipes that are constantly breking and a section of abestos cement pipes that will need to replaced in the future. Based on the assessment report the city needs to replace the faulty and very old water distribution system.
2388.purpose: The water distribution system for the City of Opa-locka is more than 60 years old, the city is in need of replacing exisiting water mains, corroded iron pipe, PVC pipes that are constantly breking and a section of abestos cement pipes that will need to replaced in the future. Based on the assessment report the city needs to replace the faulty and very old water distribution system.
2388.activities: The portion being requested is for design planning and construction which will include: - Assessment - Planning and Design
2388.direct_services: The drinking water lines located in the Miami Gardens area are constantly breaking due to the age of the system. The environmental impacts from the deteriorated plumbing include holes in pipes formed through corrosion, which allow the influx of contaminants into drinking water systems, the loss of the water resource itself, and resultant property damage.
2388.population: The target population to be served by this project are elderly persons, economically disadvantaged persons and the residents of the City of Opa-locka and visitors. Roughly 800 or more individuals are expected to be served.
2388.outcome: The benefit is to improve physical health by reducing risks of cross-contamination in drinking water supply. This can be measured by analyzing through a 3rd party the characteristics of the water such as temperature, dissolved mineral content and bacteria. Reduction in the number of breaks and leakage events can be measured by monitoring the environmental impacts from deteriorated plumbing in piped formed through corosion. Improve in drinking water by replacing the coroded pipes and monitoring the quality of water through laboratory analysis.

1980.description: The City of Opa-locka has a dire need to enhance and improve its financial processes, city-wide and require technology for resolve. Conversion to a government based financial software is the outstanding catalyst for the City to provide accurate, timely and efficient financial reports to Department of Financial Services and stakeholders alike.
1980.purpose: The City will convert its financial software to a modern government based program which will allow inter-departmental communication and connectivity. Timely reporting, analysis of data and efficient processing of needs across functions such as Accounts Payable, Debt Service, Budget and Human Resources will be achieved.
1980.activities: Personnel in each department will be trained to utilize this software, as applicable. Real time communication across departments will be enabled and facilitate in the deliverance of reliable reports.
1980.direct_services: There are no direct services that will be provided to citizens.
1980.population: This software will be utilized by personnel in departments of Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology, Building and License, Code Compliance, Capital Improvement Programs and others as needed. The City has over 115 FTEs and each will, at minimum, benefit from access to a cohesive payroll portal.
1980.outcome: The expected benefit is to improve the financial performance of the City. Production of financial reports, completion of cross departmental processes and seamless functions in comprehensive financial software. This will be measured by timely deliverance of financial reports leading up to complaint issuance of audit reports.

1981.description: The specific purpose of the funds requested is to develop and implement a comprehensive training program for school personnel, focusing on early mental health intervention. This initiative is accomplished through a formal Certificate in School Mental Health Support. The focus is on equipping them with skills to effectively recognize, assess, and respond to the early mental health needs of middle school students, fostering a healthier and more supportive learning environment. Activities and services provided include interactive workshops, access to mental health toolkits, and ongoing support from mental health professionals. These services aim to ensure that educators are well-prepared to meet the mental health needs of their students effectively.
1981.purpose: This grant will increase access to mental health support within school systems by equipping school personnel with the skills and knowledge to act as first-level interventionists. Through specialized training, school personnel will learn to recognize the early manifestations of mental health concerns in their students and respond effectively. This training will empower educators to de-escalate challenging behaviors, provide initial support, and identify when and how to connect students with appro
1981.activities: This initiative involves the completion of a Certificate in School Mental Health Support by 35 school professionals, which activities include curriculum development, training in evidence-based practices for mental health support, early intervention, and resilience-building strategies tailored to middle school students. It will also include crisis intervention skills, resource development, mentorship and networking opportunities, as well as follow-up support, assessment and program outcomes on bo
1981.direct_services: The initiative will provide the following direct services to participants: a) Mental Health Training for School Professionals: Prepare 35 school personnel with the skills to recognize and address mental health issues in middle school students, b) Crisis Response Preparedness: Enable school staff to handle mental health crises effectively, fostering safer school environments for all students, d) Su
1981.population: The primary target population for this initiative includes 35 school professionals and will impact approximately 6,000 students. These students represent a diverse demographic with varied cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds, many of whom face barriers to accessing mental health services. By training these school professionals, this initiative will indirectly serve these students by significantly increasing the mental health support available within their schools.
1981.outcome: The Uplifting School Mental Health Initiative will have a transformative impact on Miami-Dade’s middle school students. By training 35 school professionals, the program will enhance the availability and quality of mental health support within schools. Specifically, it will increase access, promote early intervention, improve academic performance, and foster resilience. The following methods will be employed to measure the success of the initiative: Pre- and Post- Training Assessments, Student Impact Surveys, School Performance Metrics, and Follow-Up Evaluations.

2384.description: The First Responder Risk Detection training is a comprehensive, evidence-based program designed to equip first responders and healthcare workers with the essential tools needed to safely and effectively support individuals experiencing a suicidal crisis. The training emphasizes objective, structured approaches to crisis intervention—focusing on clear assessment methods, evidence-informed decision-making, and standardized protocols that reduce reliance on subjective judgment or emotional reactions. Participants learn to recognize warning signs, conduct systematic risk assessments, and apply de-escalation techniques rooted in proven practices. In addition, the training directly addresses common stigma and stereotypes about people experiencing suicidal thoughts, helping responders understand the complex factors that contribute to crisis and challenging assumptions that can interfere with co
2384.purpose: The primary purpose of the requested funds is to develop and implement a comprehensive, evidence-based suicide skills training program that equips first responders and police officers with the objectivity, knowledge, tools, comfort and confidence needed to effectively identify, assess, and intervene during suicide-related crises. These funds will support the creation of a structured curriculum grounded in best practices, led by qualified mental health professionals with specialized expertise in
2384.activities: The First Responder Risk Detection training funded through this initiative will deliver a structured, evidence-based activity designed to strengthen the preparedness of first responders and police officers when encountering individuals in crisis. Core training components begin with a review of the factors that negatively influence perception and behaviors towards suicidal individuals, such as judgments based on stigma, stereotypes, culture, and personal experiences, which have been found to infl
2384.direct_services: This First Responder Risk Detection training will directly enhance the ability of first responders and police to respond and react more effectively and safely to individuals experiencing a suicide crisis by equipping them with practical, evidence-based tools for assessment, communication, and de-escalation. Through structured instruction and realistic scenario-based practice, participants will lea
2384.population: The target population for the First Responder Risk Detection training includes first responders and public safety professionals such as police officers, firefighters, EMTs, and 911 dispatch personnel—individuals who are often the first point of contact for people experiencing individuals with a suicidal crisis. Because these professionals routinely encounter high-stress situations, equipping them with specialized training ensures they are prepared to recognize risk, respond effectively, and conn
2384.outcome: The benefits of this training will be measured using a combination of quantitative and qualitative evaluation tools designed to assess changes in knowledge, confidence, and skill application. Before and after the training, participants will complete validated surveys and questionnaires that measure attitude toward people in suicide crisis, comfort level with suicide assessment, their confidence with approaching situations needing de-escalation and intervention strategies, and their overall readiness to respond to crisis situations. These instruments will help determine how effectively the training improves practical competencies and whether additional support or follow-up modules are needed.

1991.description: Establish a Workforce Education Center (WEC) to provide education and economic development opportunities for South Hills. Co. The center will meet critical demands; as the surrounding areas have reported 24% growth in the total population and 42% growth in 9-12 grade students between 2015 and 2020. The facility will mediate critical instructional space shortages and function as a comprehensive training center for high wage careers in the healthcare, business, and technology fields.
1991.purpose: The WEC will provide workforce training and job placement services for high wage occupations, as well as a space for large-scale training and professional development opportunities for local industry. The WEC will offer a full scope of student services, including advising, financial aid, veterans' services, counseling and career resource.
1991.activities: The WEC will provide workforce training and job placement services for high wage occupations, as well as a space for large-scale training and professional development opportunities for local industry. The WEC will offer a full scope of student services, including advising, financial aid, veterans' services, counseling and career resource
1991.direct_services: The WEC will be a multi-function, multi-use space for instruction, workforce training, local stakeholder development, and community events and programming. The WEC will also serve as a hub for high-value, non-profit agencies to increase public access to services like job placement, food and nutrition support, and childcare
1991.population: Elderly persons, jobless persons, economically disadvantaged persons, at risk youth, developmentally disabled, physically disabled, veterans, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, currently or formerly incarcerated persons.
1991.outcome: The center will provide instructional space for more training programs in business, computers and technology, and healthcare and provide dedicate space for veteran support services for veterans seeking training or education. HCC's enterprise resource system will track performance data for each student including: (1) certifications, degrees or licenses earned, (2) career placement, (3) rate of transfer to advanced education or training.

2119.description: The Centerstone Trauma Recovery Center will provide trauma-focused treatment, training, and support services in Manatee, Sarasota, and DeSoto Counties. The Center currently serves sexual assault survivors in all three counties. This funding would enable the Trauma Recovery Center to serve adults, adolescents, children, and their families who have experienced traumatic events; serve veterans and families who have unique needs, support development of a trauma-informed community through training and education; provide training and education to providers regarding best practices for working with victims, military and other cultural competence, and best practices for working with veterans; obtain safe housing for trauma survivors.
2119.purpose: Reduce the negative impacts of trauma on the lives of trauma survivors.
2119.activities: Evaluation, therapy, care coordination, peer support, mentoring, linkage to additional resources, supported housing, community education.
2119.direct_services: Evaluation, therapy, care coordination, peer support, mentoring, housing, training, community awareness and education.
2119.population: Adults, children and families dealing with trauma. Community members. We estimate 1200 clients and family members will be served through mental health care, support, trauma training, and education.
2119.outcome: Outcomes: 1. Establish a community-based, culturally competent, quality, accessible program to provide and increase access to effective trauma-focused treatment and service systems. Measured via numbers served, accessibility of services and education. 2. Improve health status outcomes for trauma survivors. Measured via evidence-based evaluation tool

3322.description: The Florida Caregiving Youth Outlier Project (CYOP) for At-Risk Student-Caregivers will extend the reach of the Caregiving Youth Project (CYP) to Florida middle and high school students who provide care for family members but are not currently served through our in-school programs. CYOP focuses on identifying these “outlier” students and providing targeted resources and support. Key initiatives include: 1. Expanding services to Woodlands Middle School and others. 2. Developing and implementing awareness tools for school staff, addressing challenges from high school staff turnover. 3. Delivering the updated Skills Building Curriculum 2.0 and 3.0 to outlier schools. 4. Continuing individualized support for Caregiving Youth receiving services both at home and outside of school.
3322.purpose: 1. Increase access to support for Caregiving Youth at Woodlands Middle School, a Title 1 school seeking assistance and other schools as resources allow. 2. Equip school staff with orientation tools to understand and assist Caregiving Youth. 3. Develop and deliver Skills Building curriculum to outlier schools, strengthen student leadership, social-emotional skills, and caregiving management. 4. Sustain support for "outlier" students, ensuring they receive all program services except the in-school
3322.activities: 1. Launch program at Woodlands Middle School and other schools. 2. Produce staff orientation videos, determine placement on the School District and individual school websites, and distribute to staff. 3. Implement Skills Building 2.0 and 3.0 lessons to outlier schools. 4. Provide comprehensive support for Caregiving Youth, including: - Out-of-school services: camps, educational and recreational events throughout the year. - At-home services: tutoring, respite care, family assessments, and other
3322.direct_services: 1. Full Caregiving Youth Project (CYP) services will be delivered to students at Woodlands Middle School and others as resources allow. 2. Out-of-school support, including camps, recreational and educational events, at-home services such as tutoring, respite care, family assessments, and other individualized assistance, as well as community connection resources, will be provided to “outlier” stude
3322.population: This project serves middle and high school students who are Caregiving Youth, an often invisible and underserved population. In the U.S., over 6 million children provide care to ill, disabled, or aging family members. In Florida, >290,000 public middle and high school youth sacrifice their childhood to shoulder adult responsibilities. Through this expansion, we expect to directly serve 697+ Caregiving Youth and their families in Palm Beach County while reaching many more through school awareness
3322.outcome: 1.Save staff time – Orientation videos supplement in-person school visits and help address high staff turnover while educating personnel. Measured by: Director collects productivity info from Family Specialists monthly; number of video views. 2. Orient new school staff – Video ensures all personnel can begin to learn and understand Caregiving Youth sacrifices and needs. Measured by: Feedback from Family Specialists and School Principals and staff; number of video views and post video questions. 3. Improve student well-being – Skills Building 2.0/3.0 teaches coping, leadership, and social-emotional skills. Measured by: Post-workshop qualitative and quantitative feedback. 4. Increase student s

2372.description: The Lakeside Park Bulkhead Replacement & Groin Reinforcement project will address significant shoreline erosion and infrastructure deterioration along the park’s Intracoastal Waterway frontage. This project will replace the aging bulkhead, reinforce the existing groin structures, and enhance/refurbish the vegetation, to stabilize the shoreline, protect public park facilities. These improvements will enhance surface water quality by reducing sediment runoff and turbidity, increase the shoreline’s resilience to storm events, and extend the usable life of this popular public recreation area for residents and visitors.
2372.purpose: The project will protect public infrastructure and preserve the uniquely recreational shoreline at Lakeside Park, ensuring continued public access to safe waterfront recreation and mitigate against flood damage to the residential properties that share the canal. By reinforcing the shoreline and groins, the project will extend the lifespan of the man- made beach by an estimated 20 years and protect adjacent municipal assets from erosion and storm damage.
2372.activities: The bulkhead and groins are located mostly on the south side of Lakeside Park, directly on the Lake Worth Lagoon. This public, neighborhood park offers a variety of recreational amenities such as basketball and volleyball courts, community gathering pavilions, open green space, a playground, a walking trail, and waterfront access. This is one of the Village's most popular outdoor destinations, with visitors from several neighboring municipalities frequenting the park on a regular basis. Supporti
2372.direct_services: North Palm Beach is a passionate community focused on environmental stability and enhancements, as well as recreational opportunities. Completion of this project, which includes enhancing and refurbishing the vegetation along the shoreline/berm, will reduce shoreline erosion and sediment runoff into the Intracoastal Waterway. Stabilizing the shoreline will help to decrease turbidity and suspended
2372.population: The targeted population served by this project are the residents of North Palm Beach (approximately 13,500 people) and surrounding municipalities.
2372.outcome: The replacement of the deteriorating bulkhead, reinforcement of the groin structures, and enhanced vegetation will reduce shoreline erosion and sediment runoff into the Intracoastal Waterway, and will protect public infrastructure to preserve the recreational shoreline at Lakeside Park, ensuring continued public access to safe waterfront recreation and park amenities.

2026.description: The FDA approved REMIND Alzheimer's Study, sponsored by Renew Charitable Foundation, Inc., is a clinical investigation evaluating the safety and feasibility of using the Symani Surgical System and (super) microsurgical techniques in deep cervical lymphovenous bypass surgery for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. This robotic- assisted procedure leverages Symani's precision to reconstruct the deep cervical lymph nodes (dCLNs), potentially improving lymphatic drainage, reducing neuroinflammation, slowing disease progression, and enhancing the removal of Aß and other neurotoxins from the brain. All funding will cover patient care/services ($85k per patient) for up to 20 patients across two Florida healthcare sites.
2026.purpose: Funds will support the launch of a first-in-the-nation clinical trial evaluating a novel microsurgical approach to improve lymphatic clearance in the neck for patients with Alzheimer's. This state-supported study will help establish clinical evidence for a potentially disease modifying treatment. Funding will accelerate patient enrollment, site activation, and data collection, positioning the state as a national leader in Alzheimer's innovation and potentially opening a new pathway that addresse
2026.activities: Clinical Site Preparation/Training - equipping surgeons and staff for lymphatic bypass procedures in the neck.
