Patient Recruitment / Screening - identify Alzheimer's patients through partner hospitals/memory centers Surgical/Clinical Ops - perform surgeries under standardized protocol with rigorous safety and data monitoring. Data Collection - capture pre and post op imaging, cognitive, and biomarker data to assess changes/impact. Regulatory Reporting - submit safety and efficacy data to FDA and
2026.direct_services: This project will provide direct clinical and health benefits to citizens affected by Alzheimer's disease. Patients receive access to an innovative surgical treatment aimed at improving lymphatic drainage in the neck. Expanded access to advanced clinical care. Creation of specialized training opportunities for local surgeons, nurses, and researchers. Improved diagnostic and monitoring services for
2026.population: Patient aged 50 or older; Mild to moderate Alzheimer’s Disease according to National Institute of Aging-Alzheimer’s Association (NIA-AA) criteria including a positive amyloid PET or CSF analysis; CDR-SB score within the mild to moderate range; mild is 4.5 to 9.0 and moderate is 9.5 to 15.5; Confirmed extracranial lymphatic dysfunction in the head & neck region as identified by preoperative MRI; Patient or legal representative consent for participation. Up to 20 patients to be included.
2026.outcome: The expected outcome is to demonstrate that improving lymphatic drainage in the neck can enhance clearance of brain waste and potentially slow/modify Alzheimer's progression. Expected benefits include improved cognitive function and motor skills. Enhanced quality of life for patients and caregivers. Increased clinical and research capacity within state hospitals. Methodologies include: Clinical Assessments, Biomarker Testing, Imaging, Safety, and Patient Reported Outcomes.

2373.description: This project will be for the design of water quality improvements for three roads within the Village of North Palm Beach. They include localized flooding relief, relief from surging tideflow, and water quality improvements including a septic to sewer conversion for all three roadways.
2373.purpose: These funds will be utilized to create a design for the future infrastructure improvements.
2373.activities: The funding will be used to create engineering plans for septic to sewer conversion as well as water quality improvements.
2373.direct_services: The citizens will receive plans for future construction improvements to improve remove their septic systems and localized flooding and water quality.
2373.population: The target population will be a localized residents with many on fixed incomes on three local streets. There are approximately 300 residents directly affected and approximately 1000 additional residents whose water quality along the nearby canal will be improved.
2373.outcome: The expected benefit of the project will be improved water quality along the Earman River in the Village of North Palm Beach. The annual MS4 permit for Palm Beach County has a water monitoring station at the outlet of the Earman River and the ICW that reports water quality every year. This will be used to measure the differences in water quality after the proposed work is completed.

3581.description: Valerie's House, a non-profit organization in Florida with the sole mission to help grieving children and families after the death of a parent or sibling, has experienced tremendous growth. More than 71,000 children are grieving in the regions served by Valerie's House. After experiencing the death of a parent or sibling, Valerie's House provides personalized therapy from qualified on-staff mental health professionals, and peer-to-peer support groups to help change the trajectory of bereaved children's lives. Valerie's House also supports the growing number of Floridians over age 65 who are now taking on the responsbility of caring for their grandchildren because their children have died.
3581.purpose: The purpose of Valerie's House is to serve grieving children after they experience the death of a parent or sibling by providing personalized therapy from qualified on-staff mental health professionals, and peer-to-peer support groups, to help change the trajectory of their lives. 1 in 6 children will experience the death of a parent or sibling in the State of Florida before the age of 25. (CBEM, 2025). Valerie's House also supports the growing number of Floridians over the age of 65 who are now
3581.activities: Individual mental health counseling from qualified on-staff professionals, peer-to-peer grief support groups, family financial and income assistance after the death of a spouse, school support groups, college and trade school scholarships for grieving children wanting to further their education and better their lives, and mentoring.
3581.direct_services: Direct services received by citizens to include: Individual mental health counseling from qualified on-staff professionals Peer-to-peer grief support groups Family financial and income assistance after the death of a spouse School support groups in Lee, Charlotte, Collier, Sarasota, Hendry, Desoto and Hardee counties including juveniles who may be at risk or are already involved with the justice s
3581.population: The target population is the estimated 71,000 grieving Floridians in the regions served by Valerie's House with an expansion into the Heartland in 2027. The project, over the course of one year, will support approximately 1,500 grieving children and caregivers who are bereaved due to the loss of a family member due to many types of cancer, heart attacks, active-duty military, car accidents, suicides, and overdoses. Bereaved families served by Valerie's House are our community's most at risk and
3581.outcome: Valerie's House outcomes for those participating consistently demonstrates that 75% now see hope for their future, indicate they have at least one trusted adult in their life, have higher self esteem, less negative incidents in school and have improved grades. These are all indicators that a child's life is on the right path after the death of a loved one. Methods used are observations made by qualified, on-staff professionals and mental heath counselors, case file notes, caregiver surveys, report cards, school evaluations and self-reporting surveys.

2367.description: Renovation of the Town's Police Department Emergency Operations Center. The current open space will be transformed into a multi-use facility that will include an Emergency Operations Center, a Real Time Crime Center, an events and ceremony area, as well as a training and lecture room.
2367.purpose: A unified and centralized location for a multitude of situations the Police Department faces.
2367.activities: Construction/Construction Management: Renovation of the Town's Police Department Emergency Operations Center.
2367.population: Residents, visitors and business owners totaling approximately 13,000.
2367.outcome: Enhanced situational awareness, reduction in crime, preparedness severe weather events, improved public safety, and improved coordination/communication.

2795.description: In lieu of upgrading an undersized pipe that carries over 90% of the Town's wastewater, that has had failures, and is past it's useful life, the Town has opted to upgrade the pipe to an adequately sized replacement; upsizing of the Trunkline to provide capacity based on future population projections. The Town’s recent growth and potential development of additional parcels and re-development will accelerate the need to upsize the Trunkline to provide additional capacity to prevent surcharge occurring within the system.
2795.purpose: Upsizing of the Trunkline to provide capacity based on future population projections.
2795.activities: Replace a degraded clay and steel 18in wastewater line with an upsized HDPE sewer line to accommodate increased flow.
2795.direct_services: Reliable and environmentally sound sewer conveyance system.
2795.population: Residents, visitors and business owners totaling approximately 13,000.
2795.outcome: The outcome will be measured by the reduction in sanitary sewer overflows, reduced lift station pump run time, and reductions in inflow and infiltrations.

3538.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3538.description: Construction of an Animal Control Adoption Building adjacent to the existing animal control facility. The proposed building will house safe and healthy animals suitable for adoption and provide the pubic a safe environment to view and interact with adoptable pets. The current facility houses all animals, including those deemed dangerous, sick animals, and quarantined animals. The additional simple facility will provide for separation of healthy animals and the public from those that are not healthy, or adoptable for various reasons.
3538.purpose: Public safety and welfare by providing separation of healthy adoptable pets, providing the pubic a place to enter, view, and interact with adoptable animals that are free from illness or other ailments that make them unsuitable for adoption at a given time. The facility will also serve as a an emergency boarding facility for healthy, vaccinated pets during disaster events.
3538.activities: A separate building for the public to interact with adoptable animals housed in animal control.
3538.population: General public of the County. Service available to the general public at large. DeSoto county's current population is approx. 35,000 residents.
3538.outcome: Increased access to adoption facility by providing a separate area. Number of visits and adoptions will be the measure.

2375.description: The Thompson River is a vital part of the city’s stormwater management system that is in need of significant restoration. This project will consist of dredging the river to establish proper cross sections, regrading the riverbank, and installing sod revetment mats for long term bank stabilization behind the residential homes, commercial businesses, PreK-8 private school, and recreation facilities along the Thompson River to prevent flooding, increase stormwater storage capacity, and improve water quality.
2375.purpose: This project will restore a river with sedimentation build-up and bank erosion to its original condition. Dredging and bank stabilization will protect property by preventing localized flooding, create additional stormwater storage, and improve water quality that drains into intracoastal state waters.
2375.activities: Dredging to restore cross sections, regrading riverbank, and installation of sod revetment mats for long term bank stabilization.
2375.direct_services: The project will protect the property of residents and businesses adjacent to the river, improve water quality draining into state waters, and overall enhance flood prevention throughout the city due to increased stormwater capacity.
2375.population: Both the immediate neighborhoods, school, and businesses adjacent to the river and residents citywide will benefit from preventing localized flooding, creation of additional stormwater storage, and improved water quality that drains into intracoastal State waters.
2375.outcome: Flood prevention, improved water quality, and increased stormwater capacity. The outcome will be measured by cubic yards of debris/sedimentation removed, feet of canal bank stabilized, and increased stormwater conveyence.

2360.organization: City of Palm Beach Gardens Engineering
2360.description: RCA Boulevard is a two-lane undivided public roadway that is need of significant improvements. This project is for the expansion and modernization of RCA Boulevard. The improvements include increased lane sizes, street lighting, turn lanes, stormwater piping, and reconstruction of deteriorating sidewalks. This project will improve traffic congestion, accessibility to a commercial district, and drainage conditions on RCA Boulevard through roadway and drainage improvements.
2360.purpose: This project will improve traffic congestion, accessibility to a commercial district, safety, and drainage conditions on RCA Boulevard.
2360.activities: Construction of increased lane sizes, street lighting, turn lanes, stormwater piping, and sidewalk reconstruction.
2360.direct_services: This project will improve traffic congestion, accessibility to a commercial district, safety, and drainage conditions.
2360.population: The project will serve the general population and the significant number of individuals who live, work, and shop in the mixed-use district.
2360.outcome: Reduction of traffic congestion. Outcomes will be measured empirically through traffic studies. Improved vehicular and pedestrian safety. Outcomes will be measured by number of traffic or pedestrian accidents. Stormwater piping will enhance stormwater storage, prevent localized flooding, and improve water quality into the C-17 Canal. Outcomes will be measured by linear feet of stormwater pipes installed and increased stormwater capacity.

2075.description: The requested funds will support needed renovations and redesign of the city services courtyard and parking lot to better accommodate daily operations and expand public use. Renovations include a reconfiguration of parking to increase capacity and circulation, enhanced outdoor gathering space, construction of a sidewalk for public access to memorial art installations, and needed lighting, landscaping, shade structures, accessibility upgrades. Design services awarded, construction planned.
2075.purpose: Increased capacity and use of an important public space, better access to government services and community programs, opportunities for civic engagement, events, etc.
2075.activities: Renovation of the public courtyard and parking lot to support public events, community programs, and daily City operations.
2075.direct_services: Improved capacity and ability to access the area for services, public events, civic engagement, community programs, and gatherings.
2075.population: The City of Coconut Creek has a population of around 58,000 - it's anticipated that visitors from surrounding jurisdictions will also benefit from greater access to the memorial art installations, including the Tree of Life Marjory Stoneman Douglas Memorial, and a one-of-a-kind Holocaust Memorial that will be installed in January 2026.
2075.outcome: Increased capacity and usability of outdoor event space and improved access of memorial art installations; Increased operational space for public engagement with government services; Improved accessibility and pedestrian circulation; More events, attendees, and vendor participation. Measured by: Facility usage reports; ADA compliance and inspection reports; parking capacity and circulation; program participation; and event scheduling and participation.

2077.description: Citywide stormwater infrastructure and canal shoreline restoration and rehabilitation and dredging will increase stormwater delivery capacity and reduce canal embankment failure due to erosion and potential settlement. Restoration of stormwater infrastructure and canals, earthen embankments and envisioned improvements to their resiliency is necessary to protect the community, property and the environment, while preserving drainage basins and the canal systems as intended.
2077.purpose: Protect the community, property, and the environment, while preserving drainage basins and the canal systems as intended. Increase stormwater delivery capacity and reduce canal embankment failure due to erosion and potential settlement.
2077.activities: Pipe lining, pipe removal and replacement, canal embankment restoration, and dredging by third party vendors.
2077.direct_services: Safe roadways, protection against property damage, healthier environment
2077.population: The City has a population of around 58,000 - thousands of residents, visitors, and businesses within the city would benefit from this citywide project. The surrounding region also benefits from the protection of canal ecosystems.
2077.outcome: Protection of the ecosystem which thrives within and around the canal system. Reducing erosion and safeguarding adjacent infrastructure such as buildings and roadways. Improved stormwater conveyance through inlets, pipes, culverts and canals. Increase water storage capacity by rehabilitating existing infrastructure and improving conveyance system. Measurement is based on actual conditions, total community cost associated with damage due to adjacent infrastructure, nutrient loads, and level of service.

2092.description: To address safety concerns at the midway point of the Coast-to-Coast Trail (C2C) and its intersection with Lake Minneola, a State Sovereign Land, this project will construct a plaza space and docks for up to 40 watercrafts. With no public docking facilities on the Clermont Chain on Lakes this project will support and enhance the safety of pedestrian, bicycle and water traffic thus spurring economic development and enhanced tourism opportunities.
2092.purpose: To address safety concerns at the midway point of the Coast-to-Coast Trail (C2C) and its intersection with Lake Minneola, a State Sovereign Land, this project will construct a plaza space and docks for up to 40 watercrafts. With no public docking facilities on the Clermont Chain on Lakes this project will support and enhance the safety of pedestrian, bicycle and water traffic thus spurring economic development and enhanced tourism opportunities.
2092.activities: Located at the midpoint of the C2C trail, the proposed project includes redevelopment of the 8th Street area to include seating, picnic areas, enhanced flow of pedestrian and bicycle traffic on the trail and an artistic monument highlighting and recognizing Florida’s C2C trail and Clermont’s history as a model community for trail users. Additionally, the project calls for the installation of a docking facility for between over 40 watercrafts. This docking facility will provide access to the C2C
2092.direct_services: Enhanced safety of recreational spaces, trail connections, access to downtown Clermont from the Clermont Chain of Lakes.
2092.population: Residents and visitors of Clermont and Lake County. Approximately 1,000,000 residents and visitors expected.
2092.outcome: The benefits will be increased visitors and users of the trail and docks. This amount can be counted by staff and monitored daily.

1990.description: An investment of funding will support Breakthrough Miami to continue to advance a strategic growth plan to expand reach and impact in Florida, growing our newest site in Miami Dade County to serve 175 new 5th-8th grade students and preparing for an additional and new Breakthrough program/site to open in 2025-26 and toward the future capacity of 160 high schoolers from Broward and Palm Beach Counties. These expansion efforts will support continued and sustained growth towards a total capacity of nearly 2k students each year, thereby increasing Florida's young talent pool and equity while fostering the next generation of leaders.
1990.purpose: Funding will advance academically talented students in FL, increase college attainment and workforce readiness. Breakthrough Miami Scholars graduate high school (100%), enroll in college (98%), and complete degrees at nearly double the rate of their peers. An investment will expand our reach toward the future capacity of 160 high schoolers from Broward and Palm Beach Counties and growing our West-Dade site to a capacity of 175 5th-8th graders, advancing our goal of serving 2K Scholars annually.
1990.activities: Funding supports recruiting the new class for 2026-2027 and expansion; delivering evidence-based year-round tuition- free academic and social enrichment program; providing school options advising (uniquely supporting families in navigating school choice); expanding services to meet evolving needs of students (resiliency, mental health, and social services), workforce development and transportation.
1990.direct_services: Direct services are Breakthrough's evidence-based 8-year, school year and summer tuition-free academic and social enrichment program using a students-teaching-students model to increase academic for traditionally marginalized 5th- 12th grade students, preparing and supporting them to thrive in rigorous high schools, college and growing workforce development opportunities for our Teaching Fellows.
1990.population: Since its founding in 1991, Breakthrough Miami has supported over 3,000 Scholars to maximize their potential, provided unparalleled service leadership experiences to more than 2,500 Teaching Fellows and 4,400 Volunteers over 34 transformative summers. Programming leverages year-round host site school partnerships at 8 schools across Miami-Dade County and in 2025, a new Breakthrough site was opened in summer 2025 serving students in West Miami-Dade County. Acceptance into the program is based on
1990.outcome: Breakthrough Miami will grow and foster the newest site in Miami Dade County to increase enrollment of students to 175, intending to increase our total capacity to nearly 2,000 5th-12th grade students. Increase student enrollment in advanced courses (70%), participants reaching GPA of 3.0 or higher (60%), graduating high school (100%) and enrolling in college (95%). Serve at least 1700 5-12th grade students from under-resourced communities, 160 Teaching Fellows (17–24-year-olds), 40 Success Coaches and over 400 Volunteers. Continue to provide early paid/stipend summer work experience for 180 17-24 year-olds to serve as Teaching Fellows and Teaching Assistants. Supervised by certified teacher

2627.description: The City of Jacksonville is seeking to incorporate fencing, bollards, lighting, and landscaping/hardscaping around the east side of downtown Jacksonville to improve pedestrian and bicyclist safety. This area is undergoing a revitalization with over $2 billion in public and private investment in this area, including a hotel and office complex. It is necessary to improve vehicular, bicycle and pedestrian circulation and supporting infrastructure to ensure safe and efficient circulation.
2627.purpose: The east side of downtown Jacksonville is undergoing an economic revitalization, including a hotel and office complex, with over $2 billion in public and private investment to make this area a destination for visitors. This funding will allow for capital improvements that will ensure pedestrian and bicycle safety for citizens visiting the area.
2627.activities: These improvements including fencing, gates, and bollards as well as landscaping and hardscaping will ensure that pedestrian visitors and bicyclists to the newly revitalized downtown Jacksonville can move around the area safely.
2627.direct_services: As we see continued growth in this area, this will continue to attract more and more visitors. By constructing various safety measures in the east downtown Jacksonville development, this will ensure that safety precautions are in place for safe pedestrian and bicyclist movement throughout the area.
2627.outcome: Fencing, gates, and bollards as well as landscaping and hardscaping to improve pedestrian circulation and to provide physical barriers that protect pedestrians and bicyclists from vehicular traffic. A more efficient flow through Jacksonville's downtown sports and entertainment area should help increase the number of events and the number of guests visiting venues in the area.

2628.description: Funding will be used to make full time Jewish day schools and pre-schools secure with professional security guards, transportation and facility hardening as needed.
2628.purpose: Full time Jewish Day Schools and preschools will be more secure against the anti-Semitic and terroristic threats they face.
2628.activities: Full-time Jewish day schools and preschools will use funding for: security personnel, training, physical target- hardening, and transportation services (usable for daily transport of K–12 students to/from school). Schools may not access other state security or transportation funding programs except the State NSGP. Unspent funds must be reverted and reappropriated to remaining eligible schools.
2628.population: More than 24,000 Jewish preschool and K-12 students, approximately 3,125 teachers and school staff and thousands of parents.
2628.outcome: Increased security measures to prevent antisemitic and terrorist incidents to the Jewish day school community.

2029.description: The Miami-Dade Age-Friendly Initiative (AFI) is a countywide effort to improve livability and support healthy aging across Miami-Dade County. AFI brings together local governments, community organizations, healthcare partners, businesses, and residents to strengthen policies, systems, and environments that help residents live safely, actively, and independently. Through community engagement, municipal support, and cross-sector collaboration, the AFI advances improvements to create more inclusive, connected, and age-friendly communities for people of all ages. The AFI centers community-led planning and decision-making to ensure that local priorities and resident voices guide age-friendly action.
2029.purpose: The requested funds will sustain and expand the Miami-Dade Age-Friendly Initiative (AFI), improving livability and the health and wellbeing of older adults across Miami-Dade County. AFI’s goal is to ensure that residents of all ages can live safely, actively, and independently in their communities by supporting local governments, cross-sector partners, and the residents they serve with the tools and back-bone support needed to advance community-led policy, systems, and environmental changes that
2029.activities: Funds will support: technical assistance and training for municipalities to plan and implement changes that improve livability for older adults; community engagement and leadership development to empower residents to participate in local decision-making; cross-sector coordination to align resources, improve efficiency, and implement the Age- Friendly Community Action Plan to strengthen aging-related efforts; the development of resources—such as municipal level assessments, Age-Friendly Report Ca
2029.direct_services: The AFI will: expand opportunities for civic participation and intergenerational engagement; provide local training and leadership development that empower older adults to advocate for their community’s needs; and strengthen coordination to address the factors that impact the health and wellbeing of older adults, with a focus on the 8 Domains of Liveability (including improved access to housing, t
2029.population: The target population includes older adults (age 60+), their caregivers, and families in Miami-Dade County. The AFI aims to improve liveability for the the older adult population 60+ years and older in Miami-Dade (615,007 residents 60). The initiative will place particular focus on residents experiencing economic or social insecurity, poor health outcomes, and social isolation.
2029.outcome: Expected outcomes include: an increased number of municipalities committed to becoming age-friendly and adopting age-friendly policies, systems, and environmental changes; improvements in community livability indicators (e.g., transportation access, housing options, outdoor spaces, and social participation); greater resident and stakeholder engagement in local planning and advocacy; and strengthened coordination across agencies and partners serving older adults. Outcomes will be measured through: tracking municipal participation and implementation progress.

2172.description: A youth empowerment program providing mentorship, emotional support, cultural identity education, family restoration workshops, vocational exposure , leadership development, and a culminating ceremony for vulnerable latina teens across Central Florida.
2172.purpose: Empower at-risk latina youth mentorship, emotional development, cultural identity and family healing.
2172.activities: Mentorship, life-skills workshops, emotional wellness training, scholarships guidance.
2172.direct_services: Mentoring, cultural programs, restoration workshops, resilience development.
2172.population: Latina teens (13-16) Estimated 45-75 youth + 150 family members.
2172.outcome: 75% improve emotional readiness, 100% cultural engagement, 60% vocational readiness.

2419.organization: Levy County Board of County Commissioners
2419.description: The equipment is essential to ensure the county’s ability to offer residents core services by maintaining power during outages. The County will be enabled to achieve increased “power resiliency” in the event of severe winds, flooding and/or loss of electrical power.
2419.purpose: The equipment is essential for the County to provide its citizens with key government services during extreme weather events.
2419.activities: Installation of permanent generators will allow residents to be able to continue to receives essential services in the event of a power outage. The generators will provide two separate feeds coming into the main office building. Each feed is on a 400 amp breaker panel.
2419.direct_services: Levy County citizens will not experience an interruption in services based upon power outages and the County will be able to achieve power resiliency during emergency events.
2419.population: The project will serve the general population serving thousands of residents.
2419.outcome: The County will be able to provide power to county buildings to ensure a continuation of government services during emergency events. These benefits will be measured on the level of services offered during emergency events.

2422.organization: Levy County Board of County Commissioners
2422.description: The County is requesting funding for the construction of a new Class III landfill cell designated for debris at the Levy County Solid Waste Facility as the current C&D cell is nearing full capacity. This is needed to provide for a regional disposal facility for C&D debris, yard waste, and non-hazardous materials. The debris is then processed, contained and disposed of in accordance with FDEP regulations.
2422.purpose: The County is requesting funding for the construction of a new Class III landfill cell designated for debris at Levy County Solid Waste Facility as the current C&D cell is nearing capacity. This is needed to provide for a regional disposal facility for C&D debris, yard waste and non-hazardous materials.
2422.activities: Construction of a new Class III landfill cell will allwo for additional capacity to provide for a regional disposal facility. The debris is then processed, contained and disposed of in accordance with FDEP regulations.
2422.direct_services: Without this expansion, the County will be unable to maintain compliant disposal operations, increasing the risk of illegal dumping, transport costs to out-of-country facilities, and delayed recovery operations after future disasters.
2422.population: The general public will the target population served and this will be greater than 800 individuals.
2422.outcome: Without expansion, the risk of illegal dumping will be increased. Reduction in the number of illegal dumping incidents.

2930.description: The University Oaks system mains are in need of replacement as they are deteriorating, which is leading to water loss and inefficiencies. Replacing the old mains will help conserve water, lower operational costs and reduce waste.
2930.purpose: The University Oaks system mains are in need of replacement to address existing water loss and inefficiencies.
2930.activities: Replacing the old mains will help conserve water, lower operational costs and reduce waste. These improvements are crucial for meeting water quality and regulatory standards.
2930.direct_services: These upgrades will improve water conservancy by maintaining system integrity.
2930.population: In addition to current residents served by this system, this project will support growth through future capacity as demand continues to grow. The impacted individuals will be greater than 500.
2930.outcome: Replacing the old mains will help conserve water, lower operational costs and reduce waste. The County will observe the protection of aquifer resources and reduction in environmental stress.

2105.description: The Tiny Home Community (THC) will provide safe, affordable and accessible housing for veterans and seniors in Gadsden County. The latest US Census shows that 20.0% of the county's population is 65 years of age or older. The 2016-2020 5-year American Community Survey estimates show that the county's median household income was $41,135; about 15.2% of families and 21.3% of the population were below the poverty limit with 10.0% in the age 65 or older group. The THC will consist of 56 rental units, a community center, a community garden and a laundry center and will provide independent living at a reduced cost to residents.
2105.purpose: The Tiny Home Community will provide safe, affordable and accessible housing for veterans and seniors in Gadsden County. Twenty percent of the county's population is 65 years of age or older; this supportive housing will consist of 56 rental units and will give residents a meaningful quality of life and a place to call home in their latter years of life. The goal is to provide independent living at a reduced cost to residents and taxpayers when compared to institutional or residential care.
2105.activities: The requested funds will provide for pre-construction, development and construction of an affordable housing community. The Tiny Home Community will consist of 56 rental units as well as a community center, community garden and laundry center. In addition, recreational and community building activities will be offered to the residents.
2105.direct_services: By providing affordable rental units in a community setting, the overall demand for direct support services for activities of daily living will be reduced. In addition, the Tiny Home Community concept of peer-to-peer support and neighbors- helping-neighbors can become a reality and services paid by taxpayers can be decreased.
2105.population: Economically disadvantaged individuals, such as veterans and seniors, will be targeted for the Tiny Home Community. For Gadsden County, 56 individuals will be served. However, the Tiny Home Community in Gadsden County will be a model which can be replicated in other areas throughout Florida; the number of individuals will vary based on available funding, community support and the number of potential renters in the other areas.
2105.outcome: The Tiny Home Community will improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural experience, increase/improve economic activity, create job opportunities and enhance the renters' economic self-sufficiency. Methods for measuring these benefits/outcomes include reports reflecting data related to residents; initial intake and follow-up survey information; number of residents participating in activities; tracking emergency room and urgent care visits; economic reports reflecting revenue and job opportunity increases; and payment history for rent purposes.

2507.description: The Autumn Run Dredging project involves dredging three neighborhood ponds to remove accumulated sediment, repair damaged head walls and restore proper water flow. This work will enhance environmental quality, improve stormwater management and reduce the risk of flooding and erosion. The project will ensure safer and more sustainable ponds for the community.
2507.purpose: The goal of this project is to restore the three ponds in the Autumn Run neighborhood to full functionality be removing sediment buildup and repairing damaged infrastructure. This will improve water flow, prevent erosion and support healthy ecosystems. Additionally, it will enhance neighborhood safety and preserve the ponds as valuable resources.
2507.activities: This project will provide dredging of three neighborhood ponds to remove accumulated sediment, repair and stabilize damaged head walls and restore proper water flow. Additional activities include sediment disposal, site cleanup and minor landscaping around pond edges as needed.
2507.direct_services: Citizens wil directly benefit from reduced flooding and improved stormwater management, enhancing safety around the neighborhood. They will enjoy cleaner, healthier ponds that support local wildlife with the added aesthetic appeal of the community's natural spaces.
2507.population: The target population for this project is the residents of the Autumn Run neighborhood including families, seniors and children.
2507.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is safer, healthier and better-managed ponds that reduce flooding risk, improve water quality and support local ecosystems. This will be measured by monitoring water levels, sediment depth, flow efficiency, water clarity and indicators of aquatic health before and after the project.

2508.description: This project involves the rehabilitation of an aging wastewater master lift station and the rehabilitation of its associated force main. The primary goal is to increase system system capacity and reliability to safely convey wastewater while supporting future development opportunities. The upgrades will reduce the risk of overflows and environmental contamination. Modernized pumps, controls and corrosion-resistant piping will enhance operational efficiency, protect public health and support economic development in the service area.
2508.purpose: The specific purpose for this project is to rehabilitate the aging master station and replace the deteriorated force main to ensure safe, reliable wastewater conveyance. The goal is to increase system capacity, prevent overflows, protect public health and support future community and economic growth.
2508.activities: To achieve this project's purpose, activities will include rehabilitating the master lift stations vaults, replacing aging pumps and electrical systems and upgrading control and monitoring equipment. This project will also involve replacing the existing force main with corrosion-resistant piping, installing new valves and implementing environmental protections. These activities will ensure reliable wastewater transfer, prevent overflows and enhance system efficiency.
2508.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with reliable wastewater services that reduces the risk of sewer overflows and backups, protecting homes, business and public health. It will also support community growth and enable new development.
2508.population: This lift station is strategically located adjacent to the Gateway Centre, a major business park for the City and currently serves approximately 70 target industry businesses and approximately 1,640 full-time target industry employees not to mention hundreds of residential properties. With this project, the upgraded system will increase capacity, allowing more businesses in the area to ber served, while ensuring reliable sanitation.
2508.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is enhanced wastewater system reliability, increased capacity to support new and existing businesses and reduced risk of overflows or environmental contamination. This outcome will be measured by tracking the frequency and volume of sewer overflows, monitoring pump performance and documenting the number of new businesses connected to the upgraded system.

2509.description: The primary goal of this project will be to modernize critical utilities and transportation corridors to better serve the community. This project will replace aging asbestos water mains with safe, reliable infrastructure, upgrade drainage systems to reduce flooding and enhance pedestrian safety with improved sidewalks, crossing and traffic-calming measures. By prioritizing safe routes to school for children, this effort will create a healthier, more accessible and resilient street that supports both neighborhood mobility and long term public safety.
2509.purpose: The specific purpose of this project is to achieve the dual goal of protecting public health and ensuring children have safe, reliable routes to and from school, while also improving the overall transportation network and resilience of 60th Street for the community.
2509.activities: This project will deliver transportation-focused improvements by reconstructing 60th Street with upgraded drainage to prevent flooding and ensure reliable travel along with replacing deteriorated water mains beneath the roadway. Safe routes to school will be strengthened through new sidewalks, ADA-compliant crossing and measures to reduce vehicle speeds.
2509.direct_services: This project will provide citizens with direct services including safe sidewalks and crosswalks for walking and biking, reliable road access free from flooding and cleaner drinking water through the removal of asbestos water mains. Residents and school children will benefit from safer travel conditions and more dependable transportation routes along 60th Street.
2509.population: This project serves residents, school children and commuters along 60th Street, with a particular focus on children traveling to nearby schools. It is expected to benefit approximately 3,500-4,000 individuals, including daily pedestrians, cyclists and drivers.
2509.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is a safer, more reliable transportation corridor that supports children walking and biking to school, reduces pedestrian and vehicle accidents and prevents flooding-related disruptions. These outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-construction data collection including pedestrian and bicycle counts, traffic speed and crash reports, school attendance rates and water quality testing results.

2510.description: Funds will support the renovation of The Museum's third floor, creating an ongoing exhibition and experiential site for The Wiesel Collection. Renovation needs include construction of secure, climate- and humidity-controlled gallery areas to protect artifacts from deterioration, technology-enabled displays and interactive features to provide deep access to Wiesel's writings, speeches, and teachings, reconstruction of his personal office with digital enhancements, creation of a flexible classroom and meeting space to better serve Florida's students, teachers, and community groups, and construction of dialogue and reflection areas that encourage civic conversations about human dignity and responsibilities of citizenship.
2510.purpose: Funds will renovate The Museum's third floor to create permanent exhibition space and an experiential hub for The Wiesel Collection, preserving Holocaust survivor and Nobel Laureate Elie Wiesel’s legacy. Renovation will include secure, climate-controlled galleries, interactive displays, Wiesel’s reconstructed office, and flexible classroom and reflection spaces. This hub will provide additional Holocaust education resources for Florida K-12 students and attract researchers and scholars worldwide
2510.activities: Funds will enable renovation of The Museum’s third floor, including secure, climate-controlled galleries, interactive displays, technology-enabled exhibits, reconstruction of Elie Wiesel’s office, flexible classroom space, and dialogue and reflection areas. These improvements create the infrastructure and tools needed to deliver immersive Holocaust education programming.
2510.direct_services: Funding will provide over 380,000 students, 1,000 teachers, and 24,000 annual visitors with access to Holocaust education through interactive exhibits, classroom instruction, and reflection spaces. Visitors will engage with Wiesel’s artifacts and writings, participate in educational programming, and gain hands-on learning experiences, preserving the legacy of Nobel Laureate Elie Wiesel.
2510.population: Students, educators, scholars, and visitors from Florida and beyond will be able to access this collection. The Museum annually engages with over 380,000 students and educators as well as more than 24,000 individuals who visit The Museum.
2510.outcome: Improve the quality of Holocaust education throughout Florida and the country, enrich the cultural experience for more than 380,000 who engage with The Museum annually, and increase tourism to the Tampa Bay region. The Museum will deploy a series of student, educator and visitor surveys after interaction with the collection.

2512.description: The Tampa Bay community continues to face lasting emotional strain from Hurricanes Helene and Milton, affecting families, seniors, and first responders across nine Florida counties and straining local behavioral health systems. Florida lacks a centralized, updated inventory of resources, leaving gaps in care and limiting access, especially for underserved families. Requested funds will strengthen systems by building a comprehensive service inventory, real-time 988 dashboards, and accessible directories, improving coordination, closing service gaps, and ensuring timely support for recovery and future storm preparedness, enhancing long-term community resilience.
2512.purpose: The requested funds will strengthen behavioral health systems across nine counties (Pinellas, Pasco, Hernando, Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, Lee, Hendry and Glades) by building a comprehensive service inventory, real-time 988 dashboards, and accessible directories. These tools improve coordination, close service gaps, and ensure timely access to care for individuals, families, and seniors still recovering after Hurricanes Helene and Milton and will be in place in preparation of future storms enhanc
2512.activities: Activities include creating a regional inventory of behavioral health services, developing interactive 988 data dashboards, and producing 100,000 printed and digital directories. Services will connect individuals, families, and seniors to timely mental health support, enhance provider coordination, and ensure accurate, up-to-date resources for disaster recovery and long-term resilience.
2512.direct_services: Citizens will gain direct access to behavioral health resources through 100,000 printed and digital directories, real-time 988 crisis data, and improved referral connections. Florida residents still dealing with the impacts of Hurricanes Helene and Milton, and future storms will be linked to counseling, crisis support, and local services, ensuring timely care and reducing gaps in behavioral health
2512.population: This initiative is expected to directly serve over 50,000 and be accessible to 3 million residents in these counties including individuals impacted by Hurricanes Helene and Milton who are still seeking resources, while preparing for future storms and producing findings and tools that can be scaled statewide.
2512.outcome: Success will be measured by the number of individuals reached through the project.

2513.organization: Menorah Manor Inc d/b/a Menorah Life
2513.description: Serving six counties along Florida’s central Gulf Coast, Menorah Life is a not-for-profit senior living community with an unparalleled legacy of care and excellence. For over four decades, its services, programs, healthcare and lifestyles have offered seniors – and their families – a caring environment for the many stages of the aging journey. Over 65% of residents are funded by Medicaid. While rooted in Jewish values, Menorah Life welcomes residents of all faith and backgrounds. An independent campus security and vulnerability assessment identified several critical security upgrades to secure the facility against antisemitic attacks, as well as natural disasters such as hurricanes. State funding would support the acquisition and installation of critical safety enhancements. These measures are essential for the physical protection and security of over 900 elderly residents served each ye
2513.purpose: Menorah Life is a nonprofit senior living community that is a sanctuary of dignity, tradition and compassionate care for seniors rooted in Jewish values. These funds will support acquisition and installation of key safety upgrades identified in an independent security and vulnerability assessment, including enhanced security features, perimeter lighting, and emergency call technology. More than 900 senior residents and over 250 staff will be better protected from antisemitic threats and from hur
2513.activities: Funds will be for critical safety and security upgrades; new fire alarm system, upgraded video surveillance, reinforced perimeter lighting, full-coverage generators, fencing, bollards and emergency call systems to harden the campus against antisemitic attacks and to ensure safe on-site sheltering and continuity of care during hurricanes when residents, families and staff remain on campus.
2513.direct_services: This project will provide direct life-safety services to 900 residents and over 250 staff and visitors: 24/7 threat detection and alerting, secure monitored access, physical barriers against intrusion, reliable generator power to sustain medical care and safe sheltering, improved lighting for safety, and immediate emergency call response for seniors.
2513.population: This project will serve residents, staff, families, and the general public who live at and visit Menorah Life. Over 1150 individuals will be served - 900 seniors annually plus 250+ staff and families.
2513.outcome: Installation of a modern fire alarm system will ensure rapid detection and notification in the event of a fire, reducing risk of injury or loss of life. Security upgrades will deter unauthorized access, safeguard property, and create a safer environment for all who use the facility. These improvements will reduce potential harm and ensure compliance with safety standards. Outcomes will be measured through inspection and certification records, compliance with fire and safety codes, and documented reduction in security incidents. User feedback and staff observations will also be collected to assess improvements in public safety perception.

2515.description: The Jim and Heather Gills YMCA is a primary service hub for the YMCA of Greater St. Petersburg, serving 10,181 member families and 719 children. Legislative support will fund Phase 2 renovations to this 25-year-old facility to finish build-out of interior space for youth development, family engagement, and evidence-based health programs; correct accessibility barriers; and strengthen campus security with the installation of perimeter fencing, doors with electronic locks, security cameras, and outside lighting for parking facilities. These infrastructure upgrades allow the Y to safely and effectively meet growing demand in a facility already operating at high utilization. The requested state investment represents less than 10% of the total project cost.
2515.purpose: The Gills YMCA is entering Phase 2 of renovations to a 25-year-old, high-use facility serving 10,181 member families. State support will allow the Y to complete build-out of new space for health, youth development, and family engagement programs; eliminate accessibility barriers that limit use by seniors and people with mobility needs; and install security upgrades ensuring the campus can continue to safely and effectively serve a growing community and sustain programs already in high demand.
2515.activities: Funds will complete interior build-out for program rooms, add fixtures/equipment for health cohorts and youth/family sessions, retrofit entrances and routes for ADA access, and install upgraded security systems including perimeter fencing, doors with electronic locks, and outdoor lighting to protect a high-use site and allow uninterrupted operation during peak hours and emergencies.
2515.direct_services: The Gills YMCA serves 10,181 member families and 719 children. Funds will increase available slots in structured after-school, camp, and youth leadership programs; expand access to evidence-based prevention and recovery cohorts for adults and seniors; provide on-site supports for families; improve access for residents with mobility needs; and deliver a safer, more reliable campus.
2515.population: 10,181 families are enrolled as members of the Gills YMCA which serves over 20,000 individuals annually throughout southern Pinellas with two wellness facilities, three resource centers, three preschools, and 24 before and after school childcare locations to include three middle school academic enrichment academies. Low income and underserved residents are able to take advantage of free programming offered at this facility. The YMCA has financial assistance available based on need, and no one is
2515.outcome: The project will (1) improve physical health by expanding access to evidence-based prevention and recovery programs, (2) improve mental health by reducing isolation and stress through structured youth and family engagement, and (3) protect the public from harm by upgrading campus security with the installation of perimeter fencing, doors with electronic locks, security cameras, and outdoor lighting providing supervised, safe spaces during high-risk hours. Outcomes will be measured through membership enrollment, increased enrollment in programming offerings, and surveys of YMCA program users.

2107.description: $500,000 request to continue non-recurring funding provided in the current year to sustain current operations and allow for strategic expansion. The program now serves 442 K-12 schools and 17 colleges throughout the State of Florida. The program brings young people with and without disabilities together to compete in athletic competitions, to engage in youth leadership and advocacy activities, to promote whole school engagement through activities that further the acceptance of youth with disabilities, and to promote sports/play programs and opportunities for younger children with disabilities to improve physical, cognitive and social skills through the Young Athletes Program. There is both anecdotal and quantitative evidence that supports the effectiveness of the program in promoting participation of young people with disabilities in school activities and a reduction in harmful behavior
2107.purpose: The program furthers the State's goal to increase participation of students with intellectual and developmental disabilities(I/DD) in schools; instill lifetime understanding in future generations of the value of their peers with I/DD; reduce behaviors such as bullying; increase general physical fitness levels of children with I/DD; improve self- confidence and social skills of children with I/DD; provide opportunities for children with I/DD to participate in school leadership activities.
2107.activities: Athletic competitions (some formally sanctioned by the FHSAA) that allow children and youth with & without disabilities to compete together; Leadership development activities that bring children & youth with & without disabilities together to plan & execute public service projects; whole school engagement activities promoting meaningful participation by children with I/DD in their schools.
2107.direct_services: Services as described in b. above are provided to students, faculty, support personnel, and family members.
2107.population: K-12 and college students with and without disabilities. Over 600 students impacted in Special Olympics College programs and over 2230,000 students impacted via the Unified Champion Schools and Young Athletes Program and service projects throughout Florida.
2107.outcome: Increase understanding and acceptance of young people with intellectual and developmental disabilities in the school community. Improve self-confidence, social and motor skills, and improve physical fitness levels of young people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Data is managed based upon participation rates along with periodic surveys of young people, parents, and school system personnel to measure attitudes and outcomes.

2516.description: State support funds consultants for site planning, theater planning, architectural drawings, and a capital campaign to build an intimate fully equipped 325-seat theater facility that shall enrich and balance Dunedin's entertainment and educational scene and drive economic growth. A full range of performing arts will showcase regional talent and small hall touring shows while supporting local residents and attracting visitors. For nearby charter and public schools, it will provide educational opportunities for long term community impact while keeping ticket prices affordable.
2516.purpose: Our first major step, a formal Feasibility Study for Dunedin Public Theater, was completed on Nov. 6, 2025, by national consulting firm Keen Independent Research of Phoenix, Arizona. “Based on the study findings and current market conditions, a 325-seat theater has potential to be successful in the Dunedin marketplace." It will serve as a vital educational and community resource for the next 50–75 years. Next steps require consultants specializing in site planning, theater planning, architectura
2516.activities: State support in FY 2026-2027 would fund next strategic steps in realizing a fully equipped theater in Dunedin — through the contracting of consultants for site planning, theater planning (factual cost estimates), architectural drawings and a capital campaign for the purchase of land and state of the art production and sound.
2516.direct_services: When state-funded deliverables are complete and the theater opens, it will provide the cultural asset Dunedin has long lacked. It will create jobs, expand theater education and student job training, offer affordable venue rentals for artists and community groups, and broaden Dunedin's entertainment and educational landscape with accessible ticket pricing.
2516.population: Tampa Bay residents and area visitors including Preschool, Grade School, High School and University/College aged students. Adults of all ages including Seniors. Approx 24,000 annually.
2516.outcome: The Dunedin Public Theater will establish a much-needed 325-seat performing arts venue that expands access to performing arts programming, strengthens local economic activity, supports artists, and provides new educational and community engagement opportunities for Dunedin and the surrounding region. Impact will be measured through attendance and ticket data, number of events and users, economic indicators, participation in educational programs, and surveys of patrons and partners.

2517.description: The requested funds will enhance campus security at Northside Christian School through critical infrastructure upgrades, including secured perimeter fencing, badge-only entry, and an advanced intruder alert PA system. These measures will strengthen emergency response, protect students and faculty, and align with best practices recommended by the Pinellas County Sheriffs Office to ensure a safe learning environment.
2517.purpose: The requested funds will enhance campus security and emergency preparedness at Northside Christian School, ensuring a safe and secure learning environment for students, faculty, and families. These upgrades will include securing the campus perimeter with fencing and controlled access points, installing badge-entry systems for all classrooms, upgrading surveillance with advanced security cameras, and implementing an enhanced intruder alert system with improved communication features. These measur
2517.activities: The requested funds will enhance Northside Christian School’s security infrastructure as part of a broader campus renovation initiative, ensuring a safe and protected learning environment for students, faculty, and families. These improvements will strengthen campus security, increase emergency preparedness, and provide law enforcement with better monitoring and response capabilities, ensuring the long-term safety and well-being of our school community.
2517.direct_services: These improvements will ensure a safer learning environment, improve emergency response coordination with law enforcement, and protect students, faculty, and visitors from potential security threats.
2517.population: Our students, faculty, and staff. The target population for this project includes students, faculty, staff, and visitors at Northside Christian School, a Pre-K–12 private school in St. Petersburg, Florida. The project will directly serve over 800 individuals daily, including approximately 920 students and 150 faculty and staff, as w
2517.outcome: Expected Benefit & Outcome: This project will significantly enhance campus security by aligning Northside Christian School with Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office (PCSO) safety recommendations, ensuring a more secure, controlled environment for students, faculty, and visitors. Key benefits include: Improved Emergency Response Times – Upgraded surveillance and controlled access points will allow for faster identification of threats and more efficient coordination with law enforcement. Increased Situational Awareness – Enhanced security cameras and monitoring systems will provide real-time insight into campus activity, allowing for proactive threat mitigation. Safer Lockdown Environments – Badge

2111.description: The AI Deep Dive Workforce Training Program expands Florida’s talent pipeline in one of the state’s fastest-growing high-skill sectors: artificial intelligence, digital media, and creative technologies. This program provides accelerated workforce training, industry-recognized skill development, and job placement pathways for residents of Miami-Dade County, with a focus on economically disadvantaged populations, career seekers, veterans, recent graduates, and career-transitioning adults. The program directly supports the state’s priorities by strengthening Florida’s future-ready workforce, enhancing statewide competitiveness, and equipping residents with skills aligned with high-wage, high- demand industries. Training modules include AI literacy, generative media tools, applied digital storytelling, data-driven content production, ethical AI practices, and entrepreneurship fundamentals. F
2111.purpose: To expand Florida’s AI and digital media workforce pipeline, ensuring residents have access to industry-led, future- ready skill development aligned with high-wage, high-demand technology careers.
2111.activities: Activities and services provided - AI workforce bootcamps (6 per year) - Training in generative AI, XR, digital media, and applied creativity - Hands-on career projects and portfolios - Industry-recognized micro-credentials - Small business AI adoption workshops -Employer matchmaking and job placement support
2111.direct_services: Direct services to citizens: - Free or subsidized workforce training - Certification preparation - Access to technology and equipment - Career counseling and job placement support - Employer-facing workforce readiness services
2111.population: Target population & number served: - Unemployed job seekers - Economically disadvantaged residents - Recent graduates - Women re-entering the workforce - Veterans Estimated number served: Over 300 annually Small business owners Creative industry freelancers
2111.outcome: Outcome Measures: - Over 300 trained participants - 70% job placement or wage improvement within 6 months - 80 small businesses receiving AI training - 200 industry-recognized certifications issued - 60% participation from disadvantaged households Methodology: - Pre/post assessment - Job placement tracking - Employer surveys - Attendance & certification records - Workforce impact reporting via DOE-compatible metrics

2248.organization: South Florida Council, Inc. Boy Scouts of
2248.description: Scouting-Character Ed will collaborate with school districts to deliver Florida mandated "Character Education" programs per statute 1003.42(s) and verified by the DJJ quarterly program delivery report to meet or exceed requirements to a set number of students. The project provides a classroom based character education for students in schools with focus on ALTERNATIVE, at-risk, low performing, and Title 1 schools and to provide students with learning opportunities, mentor- ship, and life skills.
2248.purpose: Scouting-Character Ed will collaborate with school districts to deliver Florida mandated "Character Education" programs per statute 1003.42(s) and verified by the DJJ quarterly program delivery report to meet or exceed requirements to a set number of students. The project provides a classroom based character education for students in schools with focus on ALTERNATIVE, at-risk, low performing, and Title 1 schools and to provide students with learning opportunities, mentor-ship, and life skills.
2248.activities: The Scouting-Character Education program is delivered to students through enhanced instruction, mentoring activities, and leadership training, and added value activities that offer additional character building opportunities. Students will advance through their grade specific program and earn achievements and awards. Lesson have character trait themes woven into the activities.
2248.direct_services: The Scouting-Character Education program is delivered to students through enhanced instruction, mentoring activities, and leadership training, and added value activities that offer additional character building opportunities. Students will advance through their grade specific program and earn achievements and awards. Lesson have character trait themes woven into the activities.
2248.population: Grade school and high schools students. The number of individuals served is based on provided funding. Prior years at $500,000 have yielded over 15,000 students receiving programs. The cost of implementation per student decreases as the funding increases and scales.
2248.outcome: Improve quality of education, reduce recidivism, divert from criminal/Juvenile justice system. Performance data includes quarterly implementation reports, end of year evaluation reports, project deliverable forms, quarterly program activity report, forms, verification of staff and teacher training, and pre- and post- surveys. Increasing knowledge and awareness of positive character traits to enable and empower students to make better short term and long term decisions.

2110.description: This program provides students in grades 9–12, especially in rural and under-served communities, with life-changing mentorship, hands-on music career exposure, financial literacy, and leadership development through the Music, Money & Mindset curriculum. Participants will engage in music career exploration, skill-building, work-based learning experiences and opportunities for paid job shadowing preparing them for meaningful careers and entrepreneurship. Supported through satellite centers and a train-the-trainer model, the program builds sustainable local capacity in North Florida as a pilot program for statewide implementation.
2110.purpose: The goal is to strengthen workforce readiness, improve graduation outcomes, increase postsecondary enrollments, gain more industry certifications, and boost local economic activity as students gain in-demand skills and enter the workforce, strengthening the region’s talent pipeline and long-term economic growth. The requested funds will deliver a youth-focused career and technical education program that equips high school students with skills in music, media, and creative technology.
2110.activities: The program will provide hands-on instruction in digital music production, songwriting, publishing and promotion, multimedia and creative technology, one-on-one and group mentoring, mental health and career coaching, workforce and financial guidance, and postsecondary planning. Students will participate in credential-based training, career exploration, and industry exposure through satellite centers and community partnerships, building skills and experience to succeed academically and transition
2110.direct_services: High school students across North Florida will receive career and technical education, mentorship, career guidance, and paid work based learning experiences. Educators will become trained in music business principles through Train the Trainer sessions. Citizens benefit through a stronger, skilled local workforce, increased graduation and postsecondary success, and youth prepared to contribute to t
2110.population: The target population is high school students (grades 9–12) in North Florida, particularly those in rural, underserved, or economically disadvantaged communities. The project will serve an estimated 85 students in the pilot year. 25 educators will be trained to deliver the curriculum.
2110.outcome: The project is expected to increase graduation rates, career readiness, entrepreneurship, and employment among high school students. Outcomes will be measured through attendance and participation records, graduation data, credential attainment, pay records, surveys of students and parents, mentor reports, and follow-up on post-graduation education, certifications, or employment in creative and technical fields. A scalable pilot model for future statewide replication will be developed.

2723.description: The Last Ones of Auschwitz preserves what are likely the final raw testimonies of living survivors and converts them into modern educational tools tailored for GenZ, including non-Jewish students in marginalized communities. The project combines a published testimony book with a digital platform to deliver interactive content aligned with how today's youth learn and engage. By transforming oral history into accessible, relevant resources, the initiative combats rising Holocaust denial, misinformation, and antisemitism. It promotes moral literacy, empathy, and social responsibility while reinforcing historical accuracy in school curricula. As we approach the post survivor era, this program safeguards truth, empowers students to recognize and respond to hate, and helps protect the broader community from harm.
2723.purpose: Funds will be used to print and distribute The Last Ones of Auschwitz testimony book and develop a digital learning platform to reach Gen Z students, particularly non-Jewish youth in underserved communities. By converting final survivor accounts into modern educational tools, the project strengthens Holocaust education, combats denial and antisemitism, and builds moral literacy. Funding ensures preservation of truth in the post-survivor era and equips students to recognize and stand against hate
2723.activities: Activities include printing and statewide distribution of The Last Ones of Auschwitz to 32,500 8th grade students in underserved Florida schools; developing companion digital content; providing teacher training and classroom discussion tools; aligning materials with DOE Holocaust standards; and delivering survivor testimony-based lessons to enhance moral literacy and combat antisemitism.
2723.direct_services: The funds will provide 32,500 8th grade students in underserved Florida communities with The Last Ones of Auschwitz book, paired with classroom materials and digital access to survivor testimony. Students receive direct Holocaust education aligned with DOE standards, promoting empathy, critical thinking, and tools to recognize and reject antisemitism and hate in their daily lives.
2723.population: The primary target population is 65,000 Gen Z students, with emphasis on non-Jewish youth in underserved or marginalized communities who may have limited access to Holocaust education. The program also reaches educators, school systems, and community leaders seeking tools to counter rising antisemitism and hate. Secondary beneficiaries include Jewish students seeking cultural continuity and broader community members impacted by historical misinformation. By focusing on young learners, the projec
2723.outcome: Students will gain at least a 65% increase in understanding of the Holocaust and antisemitism, with over 85% reporting greater willingness to intervene or report hate-based incidents. Participating schools and communities will target a 25% reduction in antisemitic rhetoric or acts within 12 months. The project strengthens historical literacy, promotes empathy, and equips Gen Z—especially non-Jewish students in underserved areas — to recognize, resist, and prevent hate, ensuring survivor testimony drives social responsibility.

2081.description: The WOW Center is a nonprofit adult day training center in Miami, providing education, life skills, and vocational training for adults with developmental disabilities aged 21 and older. With a focus on independence and workforce readiness, the center serves over 200 individuals, helping them build skills for meaningful employment and community engagement. Additionally, our Wellness program supports aging and low-mobility individuals with tailored activities that promote engagement and enhance their quality of life.
2081.purpose: The funds will ensure adults with developmental disabilities receive the support, training, and services needed to build independence, strengthen life and work skills, and participate more fully in their community. This investment promotes stability, opportunity, and long-term quality of life.
2081.activities: The funds will support instructional, workforce, and community-based activities that help adults with developmental disabilities build daily living skills, strengthen communication, develop job readiness, and engage safely in their community. Services include guided learning, coaching, practice opportunities, and individualized support.
2081.direct_services: The requested funding will support direct services, including daily educational programs, pre-employment training, and hands-on learning experiences for adults with developmental disabilities. These comprehensive services will focus on enhancing life skills, job readiness, and community integration, ensuring that each individual has the tools needed to thrive. Through personalized instruction, ind
2081.population: The program will serve approximately 200 adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities, ranging in age from 21 and older. These individuals often face significant barriers to employment, and this initiative will provide the necessary education and training to bridge that gap.
2081.outcome: This project aims to enhance independence and community integration for adults with developmental disabilities through structured training and hands-on learning. Success will be measured using personal outcome assessments, functional evaluations, and community participation tracking. Regular feedback from individuals, families, and employers will provide insight into program effectiveness. These measures will ensure individuals gain essential skills for meaningful employment and improved quality of life.

2030.description: The Artful Hands Initiative is a barrier-free, art-based and skill-based workforce development program operated by Born Artful Inc. The program provides accessible training opportunities for individuals of any education level, removing traditional barriers to participation through hands-on creative instruction and practical skill development. Participants gain marketable skills, workforce readiness training, and pathways to employment or entrepreneurship while contributing to cultural and community enrichment.
2030.purpose: To provide accessible, art-based and skill-based training that enables individuals of any education level to develop employable skills, workforce readiness, and economic opportunity.
2030.activities: Hands-on arts and skills instruction; workforce readiness training; creative workshops; skill certification preparation where applicable; entrepreneurship exposure; and community-based learning opportunities.
2030.direct_services: Direct instruction, hands-on training, skill development workshops, materials access, mentorship, and workforce preparation services.
2030.population: At-risk youth, economically disadvantaged individuals, jobless persons, students, and adults with limited access to traditional education or training pathways. Number served annually: 50–75 participants
2030.outcome: Participants will complete skill-based training programs, develop employable and transferable skills, improve workforce readiness, and gain access to meaningful employment or entrepreneurship opportunities. Outcomes will be measured through enrollment records, program completion tracking, skills assessments, and participant progress documentation.

2351.description: The goal of the project is to market and promote Florida as a screen production destination. The screen production industry in Florida dates back more than 100 years. Telling the Florida story to the worldwide audience will help attract high-wage, high-tech jobs to Florida to be filled by Florida residents, helping to grow and diversity Florida's economy while enhancing tourism.
2351.purpose: The goal of the project is to market and promote Florida as a screen production destination. The screen production industry in Florida dates back more than 100 years. Telling the Florida story to the worldwide audience will help attract high-wage, high-tech jobs to Florida to be filled by Florida residents, helping to grow and diversity Florida's economy while enhancing tourism.
2351.activities: Possible outlets to tell the story include but are not limited to displays at airports featuring famous films and television series filmed in Florida, advertisement in industry trade magazines/websites, online (web or app) film tourism guided tour of famous sites in Florida where movies and television series have been filmed, and sponsorship and participation in various film festivals, trade shows and conferences ensuring the Florida message is present.

When an average feature film or television series films in a location, they spend $20 million in the local community while hiring 1,500 Floridians. One single production can put $150,000 per day directly in the pockets of citizens and small businesses. In 2023, the average annual wage for a film

The Florida Department of Commerce tracks a number of things that, in recent years, have declined.
