2074.description: The Municipal Waste Reduction and Research Using Cerawave Microwave Plasma program advances Florida’s leadership in sustainable waste-to-energy innovation through continued deployment of Cerawave microwave plasma gasification technology. Building on the initial pilot verified by the University of Florida Institute for Food and Agricultural Sciences, Phase 2 will operationalize and expand full-scale conversion of municipal solid waste and disaster debris into clean power, fuels, and chemical feedstocks. The program reduces landfill dependency, biosolids, and greenhouse gas emissions while enhancing energy resilience, environmental protection, and economic growth. It strengthens public- private collaboration, creates skilled jobs, and establishes a scalable model for integrating advanced plasma-based waste processing into Florida’s municipal and industrial infrastructure.
2074.purpose: The purpose of this appropriation is to advance Florida’s waste reduction and energy resilience goals through deployment and validation of Cerawave microwave plasma technology, verified by the University of Florida’s Institute for Food and Agricultural Sciences. Funds will support scaling operation of a system that converts municipal solid waste and biosolids into renewable fuels, clean energy, and chemical feedstocks. The project directly reduces landfill use, biosolid accumulation, and greenho
2074.activities: Activities will include deployment, operation, and performance validation of Cerawave microwave plasma technology for converting municipal solid waste and biosolids into renewable fuels, clean energy, and chemical feedstocks. 3680.description: Request for state funds for the acquisition of necessary rights-of-way and design services to expand the second mile of CR 769 from a 2 lane to a 4 lane roadway. Funds will be used by the County to acquire land and for FDOT to order design for the second phase of the project. CR 769 is over capacity in the urban area of south county, creating a dangerous and congested roadway connecting Charlotte and DeSoto Counties, providing direct access to I-75. Funding will allow the project to move forward in a meaningful way, while the first mile is programmed for construction in state FY 2027-2028 at a cost of approximately 30M.
3680.purpose: Expansion of phase II of CR 769 from a 2 lane to a 4 lane roadway to improve roadway safety, relieve congestion, provide for easier ingress/egress for existents urban neighborhood and commercial businesses along the roadway. Accommodate for land entitlements for Metro Development Group's "Oakstone" housing project consisting of 1800 units and DR Horton's Cayman Lakes Development, consisting of an addition 650 units. Prevent major traffic stacking issue along this section of roadway and providing
3680.activities: Position Phase II of the project to program to be ready to program for construction funding. The additional Right-of- way is necessary and the design portion of the project has not been programmed for funding. The request is for GR state funding.
3680.direct_services: Traffic congestion relief and roadway safety improvements.
3680.population: General public and state travelers that use the road to traverse the state and to access I-75. The Lake Suzy area is the only urban service area in DeSoto County. CR 769 is the only access road from the commercial and high density residential area. The traffic has made it very difficult and created unsafe conditions as residents exit and enter their respective neighborhood roads.
3680.outcome: Expediting the second phase of the project to move to construction sooner in effort to relieve the congestion and safety of these segments of the roadway.

2226.description: The Downtown Doral Arts District will be the City of Doral’s blueprint to creating safe, convenient, and sustainable transportation options that meet the needs of the community and increases accessibility. The proposed roadway and infrastructures improvements shall include pedestrian connectivity, connectivity with the City’s bicycle network, on-street parking, lighting, landscaping, signing and pavement markings, signage, traffic calming improvements, stormwater improvements, harmonization with adjacent properties, traffic and transit analysis, and NW 84th Avenue shall include a Bus/Trolley route/lane.
2226.purpose: Complete Streets Program Adaptive Re-use of the Doral Arts District between NW 58th Street - NW 54th Street and between NW 87 Ave- NW 79 Ave. The Project includes roadway reconstruction, new sidewalks, parallel parking, storm-water drainage, and additional trolley stop, bike lanes and lighting.
2226.activities: Funds will be spent for the construction phase of the adaptive Re-use of Doral Arts District between NW 58 St and NW 54 St and between NW 87 Ave and NW 79 Ave.
2226.direct_services: The Project includes roadway reconstruction, new sidewalks, parallel parking, storm-water drainage, bike lanes (where possible), and street lighting. This will increase pedestrian safety and will also serve as a mitigation initiative to help prevent flood related losses.
2226.population: General (The funds will be benefiting no specific group). Doral residents and commercial area constituents and clients.
2226.outcome: Prevent/minimize flooding and ponding along roadway segment. Installation of street lighting and sidewalk installation. Flooding and ponding are not visible during major storms. Increase light for visibility and pedestrian safety. Minimize congestion by roadway widening and provide alternative transportation via bike paths. Decrease of traffic congestion and increase of bicycle traffic. Adaptive Re-Use is to improve the conditions of the Doral Arts District to increase tourism for locals.

2230.description: The goal of the program is to provide a daily healthy meal to the elderly participants in our community in either the form of a visit to one of our congregate sites or through a delivery carrier for those who are unable to visit a site. A daily balanced provision of a meal coupled with nutritional education will establish a strong core value to living a healthier longer life. The City of Hialeah has over 1,000 participants and continue to serve our special population is of the utmost importance.
2230.purpose: The funds will be used to improve the physical wellbeing of the elderly population in the City of Hialeah.
2230.activities: The City shall serve balanced nutritional meals at no cost to program participants served with the highest standards and coupled with classes to help them understand the goals of these meals and their importance. This would require staffing to maintain quality control, temperature integrity, safety, and cleanliness standards
2230.direct_services: Through the provision of congregate and home-delivered meals, the funding can enrich the quality of life of the elderly citizens of Hialeah by nurturing healthy eating habits. Funding will also contribute to education using both mass education presentations and one-on-one nutrition counseling.
2230.population: Elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, persons with poor physical health, economically disadvantaged persons, and the physically disabled
2230.outcome: Nutritional aides and certified dietitians will work to execute healthy, nutritious, and balanced meals for program participants and all efforts will be reported.

2231.description: This request is to fund the creation of the Real Time Operation Center for the Hialeah Police Department. The center will assist the police department enhance their response time, be more proactive in their fight against crime and strengthen police officer safety when responding to calls for service.
2231.purpose: Assist the police department enhance their response time, be more proactive in their fight against crimes and strengthen police officer safety when responding to calls for service.
2231.direct_services: Enhance police services to provide a safer community.
2231.population: Residents of the City of Hialeah and all visitors.

2380.outcome: Rehabilitation of existing Surficial Aquifer System (SAS) water supply wells will protect public health by eliminating E- coli bacteria which is a disease causing organism that has been detected in some existing drinking water supply wells. Additionally, this will allow the city to optimize its wellfield operation to minimize potential impacts to wetland systems while reducing the risk of salt water intrusion.

2382.description: Replace the existing sanitary forcemain that crosses the Intracoastal Waterway, that is old failing forcemain that had four pipe breaks, and conveys all of the wastewater collected on Singer Island and the Town of Palm Beach Shores to the mainland. It is necessary to design the pipe replacement as failure of this pipeline would result in loss of service and environmental damage if sewage were to continue to be released into the pristine waterway. Also, replace the existing potable water main that crosses the Intracoastal Waterway that provides drinking water to Singer Island and the Town of Palm Beach Shores. It is necessary to design the pipe replacement as a failure of this water main, which was constructed in the 1950s, would result in loss of adequate service of drinking water and fire protection to citizens and businesses.

2362.description: The Town of Mangonia Park has engaged in a multi-year strategy to spur economic development. The study identified five roads in town that are functioning as poor or failing. These roads are in direct support of businesses that support the Port of Palm Beach. Funds will go towards repaving these five critical roads.

In order to develop this 52-acre site into a mixed-use development, upgrades to the water plant will be necessary for storage, treatment, and capacity.

The mission of the Giving Closet Project (GCP) is to provide clothing and hygiene products to students experiencing chronic and situational poverty. In today's challenging landscape, where unstable environments, homelessness, and limited access to vital resources cast shadows on the educational journey, students are facing unprecedented struggles stemming from situational poverty. 2639.description: Path to College, a 501(c)3 organization, requests funding to deploy a comprehensive college prep and workforce development program designed to prepare low income youth to fill identified gaps in the labor market. Through an interconnected system of education, college prep, & personal development programming, a population of up to 3,000 students will access programming that will help them thrive in high school while setting them up for success in a post- secondary setting. This project will cultivate a robust talent pipeline in Florida, harnessing the inherent talents of students while helping them pursue careers that will ultimately give their families a path to positive economic mobility.
2639.purpose: This program will empower Path to College to deploy a comprehensive college prep and workforce development program designed to prepare low income youth to fill gaps in the labor market identified by the state and the Palm Beach County Business Development Board. Through an interconnected system of education, college prep, & personal development programming, a population of up to 3000 students will access programming. This project will cultivate a robust talent pipeline in Florida, harnessing the
2639.activities: Path to College will provide low income youth with college prep and workforce development through tutoring, college coaching, and workforce training aimed at specific career paths. Through immersive workshops, hands-on experiences, and individual mentoring support the program will prepare youth for college and success in emerging careers that fill gaps in Florida's workforce.
2639.direct_services: The funding builds upon efforts made possible by previous state funding to provide direct academic support and workforce development. Services include mentoring for students, hands-on career exploration workshops, tutoring, financial literacy education, internship matching, alumni coaching, project-based training, and other immersive experiences to build future career skills.
2639.population: This project will serve up to 3,000 low income students in Palm Beach County. All students attend Title 1 schools and/or will demonstrate a need for services by documenting their family's financial position.
2639.outcome: Benefits/outcomes include improved access to high-quality education, improved economic standing for those served, enhanced access job opportunities, increased availability of a highly trained workforce, enhanced economic self- sufficiency, and improved mental health. Path to College has a rigorous program evaluation in place already that is built on regular surveys, touchpoints, and internal KPIs. These will be utilized to ensure ongoing success in achieving program goals.

2440.organization: Leesburg Regional Medical Center, Inc d/b/a
2440.description: Our community faces a growing shortage of primary care providers amid a rapidly aging population with increasingly complex health needs. This initiative seeks to recruit and retain essential primary care physicians to expand access, strengthen continuity, and ensure patients receive timely, local, and compassionate care close to home.
2440.purpose: Goal 1: Recruit and retain essential primary care providers to expand access for our aging, medically complex population—ensuring every patient has timely, local, and coordinated care close to home. Goal 2: Build a sustainable primary care workforce to meet rising community demand, close critical gaps in access, and strengthen the foundation of lifelong health and wellness across our region.
2440.activities: Expanding our primary care workforce will increase access points for timely, local care—enabling earlier cancer detection, improved preventive screenings, and better chronic disease management. With additional providers, we can strengthen outreach and grow participation in community health and wellness events to advance overall population health.
2440.direct_services: Primary care providers will deliver comprehensive services including preventive screenings, annual wellness visits, chronic disease management, cancer detection, and immunizations. They will coordinate referrals to specialists, offer same-day appointments for acute needs, and participate in community health events to provide education, risk assessments, and connections to ongoing care.
2440.population: Elderly persons, persons with poor mental health, poor physical health, developmentally or physically disabled, high school aged persons and older, currently or formerly incarcerated persons, and victims of crime.
2440.outcome: (1) Increased access to preventive and primary care services (2) Reduction in emergency department visits and hospital readmissions through improved care coordination (3) Increased participation in community health programs (4) Expanded access to integrated behavioral health services within primary care (5) Enhanced provider ability to identify and address social determinants of mental health

2442.organization: Leesburg Regional Medical Center, Inc. d/b/a
2442.description: The funds requested will support the purchase and installation of a dual-energy 7500 Spectral CT at UF Health Leesburg Hospital to enhance rapid stroke diagnosis and expand advanced imaging services. Lake County reports an age-adjusted stroke death rate of over 40 per 100,000—one of the highest in Florida, and with a growing senior population, demand for timely neurological care continues to rise. The Spectral CT will provide faster, more accurate stroke imaging, supporting UF Health Leesburg’s path toward thrombectomy-capable and comprehensive stroke center certification while also improving diagnostic precision across oncology, cardiac, and vascular care.
2442.purpose: The funds requested will be used to acquire and install a dual-energy 7500 Spectral CT at UF Health Leesburg Hospital, providing advanced, high-definition imaging to support faster and more accurate diagnosis of stroke and other critical conditions. By enabling earlier detection of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, the technology will improve time- to-treatment metrics, increase eligibility for advanced interventions, and enhance overall diagnostic capacity across neurological, cardiac, vascular,
2442.activities: Funds will support the installation and staff training to operate a dual-energy 7500 Spectral CT system at UF Health Leesburg Hospital, delivering advanced stroke and neurological imaging on-site. Activities include system integration, technologist education, and protocol optimization for rapid stroke diagnosis and intervention. These services will shorten diagnostic and treatment times, improve recovery outcomes, and enhance imaging quality across multiple specialties, including oncology, cardi
2442.direct_services: Direct services include rapid, high-definition CT imaging for stroke, neurological, and complex medical cases within UF Health Leesburg Hospital. Patients will receive faster evaluation, earlier intervention, and more accurate diagnoses—improving treatment decisions and outcomes while expanding access to advanced imaging and specialty care for the growing Lake and Sumter County communities.
2442.population: Residents in Lake and Sumter counties, a combined population of approx. 600,000 lives.
2442.outcome: The project will shorten time-to-diagnosis, increase access to advanced stroke care, and improve survival and recovery outcomes for patients across Lake and Sumter Counties. It will also advance UF Health Leesburg’s progress toward thrombectomy-capable and comprehensive stroke-center certification. Expected impact includes a 10–15% reduction in treatment delays and improved recovery outcomes for hundreds of patients annually.

2441.description: The Town is requesting funding for the construction of the North Water Treatment Plant. Final Phase, construction.

The Town has already drilled new wells and needs to build the new treatment plant to replace the North Well, an aging, outdated facility that is failing, costly to maintain, and located in a leased FDOT right-of-way of State Hwy 19 and CR 48. The well and treatment plant pro
2441.activities: The project includes the construction of a water treatment plant as required by the St. John's River Water Management District, alleviating future local stress on the upper aquifer. The associated treatment plan will include current technologies and reduce the costs burden of repairing outdated and failing infrastructure.
2441.direct_services: Direct and secondary improvements to water access and quality, including flow and pressure for fire protection.
2441.population: The target population is the residents of the Town of Howey-in-the-Hills and the current consumers within the Interlocal Service Boundary Agreement. The population is currently around 1,800.
2441.outcome: Benefits will include continued availability of potable water, increased flow and water pressure for fire protection and reduction in repair and maintenance costs. Outcomes will be measured through monitoring and reduction in service outages.

2127.description: Provide transportation to and from Jewish Day School to help ensure the safety & security of the students and school facility. Buses will help streamline the process of drop-off & pickup, and will limit the number of private vehicles entering the school property allowing for greater control of the area. In light of the heightened security threat facing the Jewish community, this will add another layer of protection. Additionally, it will allow for more people to seek employment.

The buses will help streamline the process of drop-off & pickup and will limit the number of private vehicles entering the school property allowing for greater control of the area. In light of heightened security threats facing the Jewish Community, this will add another layer of protection. In addition, it will allow for more people to seek employment.

This process will enable students and families to have a more effective and focused educational experience in school. Providing transportation will also alleviate traffic and secure the soft target of carpool lanes. We will have periodic assessments and require school administrators to provide reports. We will also have random site visits.

2304.description: Exhibits in the Tampa Firefighters Museum (TFFM) were planned and installed more than twenty years ago. The current exhibits are in need of being updated, repaired, or replaced. Most of the current exhibits are static, ones that visitors view as they walk by. The TFFM has a severe lack of interactive exhibits, exhibits that reach out and engage the visitor. Interactivity, whether it be physical or electronic, allows the visitor to have a better experience and walk away with a better understanding of the artifacts being displayed. The Board of the TFFM is looking to contract with a museum designer to assist with the four stages of updating the current exhibits. The designer would help Board members conceptualize new exhibits; design the exhibits; build and install them. In addition to reimagining the museum exhibits, the museum memorial room is in need of redesigning and refurbishing. Thi
2304.purpose: The Tampa Firefighters Museum is planning to contract with a museum/exhibit designer to assist with the four stages of updating the current exhibits. The designer would help Board members conceptualize new exhibits; design the exhibits; build and install them.
2304.activities: The exhibits will provide visitors the opportunity to learn home fire safety habits through hands on and interactive activities. They can also learn what it means to be a firefighter with activities such as feeling the weight of the equipment a fully turned-out firefighter wears to a fire or experience sliding down a fire pole or climbing a ladder. TFM will tell the stories of the many of the department's firsts; first motorized apparatus, first fire alarm system, first African Americans, first
2304.direct_services: The Tampa Firefighters Museum preserves the heritage of Tampa's Fire Department. The museum tells a unique history as a former fire station with exhibits on local service history, firefighting memorabilia & vehicles.
2304.population: Although Tampa is in its name, the fire museum serves as a reservoir for public safety artifacts and stories from the entire Bay area and beyond. Currently, the fire museum hosts an average of 600 visitors monthly. These include tour groups from schools, community groups, and individual walk-in visitors.
2304.outcome: Preserving the history of emergency responders is a worthy benefit within itself. Preserving the history of those brave responders in a way that is accessible, interesting, and maybe even a little bit fun will make the fire museum a greater asset for now and into the future. The success will be measured by the increase in attendance to the fire museum and its continued service to the community.

2643.organization: Florida Federation of Garden Clubs, Inc.

The construction of the olympic size pool located at Wekiwa Springs State Park, was originally funded by the Florida Federation of Garden Clubs as part of their Youth Camp experience. Each summer at the Park, campers at Wekiva Youth Camp, a nonprofit, ACA- accredited residential nature camp for 3rd–8th grade children, sponsored by the Florida Federation of Garden Clubs, Inc., experience “the Real Florida” while learning about conservation, native ecosysems and wildlife, and the importance of protecting our natural environment. For over 50 years, this unique camp—recently named one of Newsweek’s Best Summer Camps in America, has inspired thousands of young people to appreciate and support our natural resources. It is not only a place where children learn, but also a place where they unplug from screens,

2321.description: Funding will support construction of a new multipurpose community center to meet the needs of our growing community.
2321.purpose: The goal and purpose of a new community center will be to enhance social connection, promote access to recreational opportunities, support education and learning, provide services for diverse populations, economic development, improve health and wellness, support safety and crime reduction, and environmental sustainability.

To meet the intended purpose of funding for such a project, the center should offer a variety of activities and services that align with the needs and interests of the local community such as recreational, social, and cultural events.
2321.direct_services: Services that will be provided include exercise activities, art, music, and lab space, and educational classes for youth and adults ranging from regional history to practical skills.

2321.outcome: Expected benefits would be improved community engagement, social cohesion, enhanced physical and mental health, increase access to educational opportunities, economic growth and local business support, promotion of cultural diversity and inclusion, and safety and crime reduction. The methodology for measurement will be tracking attendance at events and programs, participant surveys, participant feedback, business participation records and impact, employment data, police reports, crime statistics, and constant data collection.

2710.description: To develop units of affordable housing, consisting of one, two and three bedroom units, in Nassau County on land that Affordable Housing First has already purchased. We will rent to individuals/households earning less than 80% of Area Median Income, with a specific focus on individuals and families in the 30-50% AMI range. This will assist many residents who must commute long distances to work in Nassau County and bring additional economic activity to Florida and Nassau County.

We will rent to individuals/households earning less than 80% of Area Median Income, with a specific focus on individuals and families in the 30-50% AMI range. This will assist many residents who must commute long distances to work in Nassau County and bring additional economic activity to Florida and Nassau County.

Annual studies by Nassau County will allow us to track this statistic and we will be able to track our specific impact.

2329.description: Several areas of our city experienced flooding in 2024 for the first time in decades due to Hurricane Milton. This project will help restore proper flow through these conveyances, reducing the future threat of flooding in these areas.
2329.purpose: Clearing and improving stormwater conveyances (such as Spartman Branch, Mill Creek, Eastside Canal, Westside Canal, and Itchepakasassa Creek) as part of a flood mitigation program, restoring proper flows, and responding to issues noted as a result of Hurricane Milton. This will improve stormwater flows through this area to avoid future flooding.
2329.activities: Mechanical clearing of vegetative debris and other unwanted items within the banks of these stormwater conveyances.
2329.direct_services: Improved flow of stormwater through these conveyances will reduce or eliminate flooding issues encountered following Hurricane Milton.

2329.outcome: By improving the flow of these stormwater conveyances and restoring their capacity, residents and businesses in the nearby areas will see reduced flooding during severe storm events.

A new hire will lead these efforts in responding to critical cases which is where our team has developed both a network and expertise to address these emergency situations. Funding will also support direct costs of transitioning services and employment support. Our mentor leadership program is the only in person program of its type.

2720.description: PEER Link expands peer and family support to offer individualized support with peer navigation and resource referral to prevent mental health crises and co-occurring substance use. PEER Link provides no cost and no eligibility obstacles for individuals and families waiting for or unable to access therapeutic services using empowerment of peer support. Peer specialists for youth, families and individuals intervene offering immediate help, connection to care, sustainable recovery, and workforce development through certified recovery peer specialist training. Youth efforts focus on prevention and coping skills for at-risk youth aged 12-17 for suicide and substance use.
2720.purpose: Prevention of mental health crisis and suicide, reducing relapse and enhancing long-term recovery saving the state money by the reducing the need for ER visits and Baker Act's and freeing up the limited number of psychiatric beds. PEER Link provides an immediate solution to fill the gaps identified in the Behavioral Health Gap Analysis completed by Ernst & Young for DCF by filling treatment gaps with availability of peer support, recovery gaps to increase access to recovery orientated services,
2720.activities: Through no cost and no eligibility requirements, PEER Link utilizes specialists for youth, families, and individuals involved in behavioral health systems and treatment centers to intervene before and during crisis offering immediate help, providing individualized and customized support to build recovery plans, guidance to access care and navigate systems, and education and promotion of empowerment skills to sustain recovery.
2720.direct_services: Outreach and engagement at key intervention points, courts, crisis stabilization units, Baker Act facilities, 988 warm hand-offs. Personalized recovery goal setting and system navigation across substance use and mental health treatment. Education, support, and suicide prevention through evidence-based and evidence-informed training. Workforce development for peers seeking to maintain recovery with
2720.population: NAMI's free programs are available to any individual impacted by mental illness/co-occurring substance use regardless of race, age, or economic status. Individuals living with mental illness are often without income, insurance, or family support. PEER Link serves individuals in more than 4 urban and rural counties, and even more through virtual programs. We deliver evidenced-based prevention and care for youth, young adults, adults, and families that supplement traditional behavioral health serv

A performance evaluation system measures and tracks individuals and family peer progress focused on improved ability to manage crisis situations, reduced stress and/or isolation, access to needed treatment and/or support services, and an understanding of the signs and symptoms and how to access help, as well as progress focused on improved emotional regulation, managing challenges, coping s

2785.description: The funds from this request will support the development of the JSO's Patrol-Led Drone First Responder (DFR) program which will deliver drone-based real-time intelligence to first responders by supporting more comprehensive and adaptable responses across the entire city. The drones, deployed from patrol vehicles, are expected to improve response times, direct the efficient deployment of resources in the field, and improve officer safety.
2785.purpose: The Drone First Responder Program will allow patrol units to rapidly deploy drones for both interior and exterior missions. This capability will provide immediate real-time intelligence during critical incidents, search and rescue operations, and other emergencies. The goal is to enhance response time, situational awareness, and overall public and officer safety.
2785.activities: The program will create a patrol-based drone program that provides real-time aerial intelligence to patrol officers and investigators across the city by equipping them with internal and external drones. Internal drones will be deployed in enclosed spaces to assess the safety of a structure while external drones can be used in open-air settings for missing persons and post-disaster.
2785.direct_services: Officers typically respond to one call after another while facing improbable situations with limited information, and every second counts when Jacksonville’s citizens need assistance. The program will provide real-time information to first responders, resulting in a more informed and rapid response when citizens need it most. Fixed wing mapping is essential during endangered missing persons cases.
2785.population: This project will enhance the overall safety, security and well-being of the nearly one million citizens residing in Duval County.
2785.outcome: The anticipated benefits include: reduced response time, improved situational awareness, overall increase in successful outcomes during critical incidents and rescue operations. These outcomes will be measured by drone operators who will document the deployment and use of program-related drones to measure the benefit of the program.

2734.description: BSO is requesting funding to strengthen our fire rescue division in the area of equipment, training and protective gear. This request supports secondary sets of firefighting gear for regional firefighters. This directly aligns with statewide efforts to enhance firefighters’ health and safety while complying with recent legislation prohibiting the use of toxic substances known as PFAS in newly manufactured turnout gear. The request for a simulator, which would be housed in the BSO Research, Development and Training Center (RDTC), would allow firefighters to gain hands-on experience with fire pump panel operations in a safe, controlled, low-risk environment. The request for an advanced methane detector device to enhance the agency’s hazardous materials detection and response capabilities will ensure operational readiness. This device will be utilized in a variety of operational environment
2734.purpose: This request supports secondary sets of firefighting gear for regional firefighters. This directly aligns with statewide efforts to enhance firefighters’ health and safety while complying with recent legislation prohibiting the use of toxic substances known as PFAS in newly manufactured turnout gear. The Fire Engine Pump Simulator would allow firefighters to gain hands-on experience with fire pump panel operations in a safe, controlled, low-risk environment and finally the request for an advance
2734.activities: Training will be conducted utilizing the Fire Engine Pump Simulator to ensure operational readiness. The Advanced Methane Detector Device will be readily available for any hazardous material spills. And lastly the Fire Rescue Turnout Protective Gear will enhance the safety of the men and women serving their community while reducing the potential for injury.
2734.direct_services: Citizens and visitors will benefit from this project request by having well trained and equipped fire rescue personnel at their service 24/7.
2734.population: The target population that will be served by this request extends to the residents and visitors of Broward County as well as the fire fighters who serve their communities and reside within the tri-county area. Broward County is a well known tourist destination for many events that attract global visitors, and the requested equipment and training will benefit a large population of residents and visitors that utilize the Broward County Sheriff's Office fire rescue services.
2734.outcome: The expected benefit for this project request is overall improvement in the area of training, as well as having protective gear that is reliable for fire fighters to use in the field. Training, meeting accreditation and acquiring and maintaining the most effective equipment in fire rescue is a priority of the agency. By ensuring the above metrics are met the outcome from this request increases our agencies success in the field. Training records are analyzed to ensure that all fire rescue personnel will benefit from the training and equipment utilized.

3408.description: The requested funds will support the expansion of the reuse water system in Nassau County to increase reclaimed water availability for irrigation. This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long-term water resource sustainability in the service area.
3408.purpose: The project will construct improvements to the reclaimed water system, including expansion of the reuse distribution network, installation of supporting infrastructure, and system upgrades to deliver additional reclaimed water for irrigation. These activities will increase reuse availability and reduce potable water use in the service area.
3408.activities: The project will provide citizens with increased access to reclaimed water for irrigation, reducing potable water demand and helping maintain reliable, cost-effective water service. This will support long-term water supply sustainability for the community. Reducing reliance on groundwater withdrawals helps protect the aquifer from over- extraction and saltwater intrusion.
3408.direct_services: The requested funds will support the expansion of the reuse water system in Nassau County to increase reclaimed water availability for irrigation. The project will provide reuse to a townhouse development and to future development of commercial and residential projects. This project will reduce potable water demand, support community growth, and promote long-term water resource sustainability in t
3408.population: These activities will increase reuse availability and reduce potable water use in the current service area. Increased reclaimed water availability through construction of reuse water mains supports future residential and commercial development and reduces potable water demand, lowering long term utility costs. Reduction in potable water withdrawals and increased reuse irrigation helps conserve regional freshwater and protect natural ecosystems.
3408.outcome: Reducing reliance on groundwater withdrawals helps protect the aquifer from over-extraction and saltwater intrusion. Track the number of new reuse connections and compare annual reclaimed vs. potable water usage in utility reports. Measure annual potable water savings (gallons) and increased reclaimed water usage through utility reporting and compliance documents. Measure reduction in surface water effluent volumes using annual NPDES or DEP reporting. Track number of new reuse connections and compare with potable water usage reports.

2805.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Florida
2805.description: Camp Deep Pond serves 5,000 young people every summer with an engaging outdoor recreational experience, most of whom live in inner-city Jacksonville. The Maintenance & Storage Structure in this project will be 4,000 square foot (50 x 80) that stores and protects all equipment for the months camp is closed. This will ensure our valued equipment stays in good condition, and ensure it is not being used while Camp is closed. (Camp runs June-August.) For example, the structure will store a $50,000 slide which is in the lake for three months of the year, canoes, kayaks, life jackets, camp bus and camp van, bikes, fishing poles, archery equipment, etc. The goal is to sustain the life of our equipment over the long run, and to prevent any possibility of theft or unauthorized use.
2805.purpose: To serve 5,000 young people at the camp each year, we must have a way to preserve and sustain our equipment from year to year. From the high value items such as our $50,000 slide that floats in the pond June - August, to our vehicles, fishing, archery and boating equipment, they need to be secured. At Camp Deep Pond we are developing character in young people by helping them achieve social, emotional and physical wellness. We strive to reduce the tendencies of youth to be involved in violence an
2805.activities: BGCNF will build build a Maintenance and Safety Structure to store valuable Camp equipment. This will enable us to continue to provide a true summer camp experience in an outdoor setting to thousands of at-risk youth each year. Camp programs and activities include archery, fishing, science and technology (STEM rocket program), biking, kayaking, canoeing, swimming, FFCWCC's "Project Wild" and "Project Aquatic Wild" curriculum, BGCNF's "Ultimate Journey" curriculum, and a variety of sports. These
2805.direct_services: Direct services that we provide at Camp include transportation, healthy meals and snacks, personal character and team development lessons, outdoor adventure and educational opportunities for personal growth and discovery, all in a true camp setting that many youth have never experienced before. Our goal is to reduce violence, increase education and hope, and help young people reach their full pote
2805.population: The target population includes young people who are at risk, ages 6 to 18, live in the urban core, and/or live on the margins of the federal poverty line. We will serve 5,000 youth over the year, primarily June - August. At BGCNF, we serve all young people ages 6-18; typically Club members reside in low-income households with more than 94% of them participating in the free or reduced-fee lunch program at their schools. Without BGCNF providing the summer camp experience at Camp Deep Pond, these y
2805.outcome: Our goal is to ensure the longevity of our Camp equipment, protecting it from unauthorized use, theft, and exposure to the elements when Camp is closed for the majority of nine months a year. This will enable us to provide an extraordinary Camp experience to young people in the Northeast Florida region.

3312.description: The funds will complete the hydrogen sulfide removal improvements required for the Crawford Diamond Water Treatment Plant to meet FDEP drinking water standards. Testing confirmed elevated hydrogen sulfide levels in the raw water, and this greensand filter upgrade is essential before the facility can deliver compliant, safe, and reliable water needed to support future tenants at the Crawford Diamond Industrial Park, a major regional economic catalyst for large- scale industrial employers.
3312.purpose: The funds will install the hydrogen sulfide removal and filtration improvements required for the Crawford Diamond Water Treatment Plant to meet FDEP drinking water standards. This upgrade is essential for providing compliant, safe, and reliable water service needed before industrial tenants can occupy the Crawford Diamond Industrial Park, a major regional economic catalyst.
3312.activities: Activities include engineering design, permitting, procurement, construction of the filtration system, installation of treatment equipment, electrical and controls integration, startup, testing, and engineering services during construction. Services include project management, regulatory coordination, and all tasks required to achieve FDEP operational approval.
3312.direct_services: The project ensures delivery of safe, compliant drinking water for existing and future commercial and industrial customers served by the Crawford Diamond Water Treatment Plant. It protects the public from exposure to elevated hydrogen sulfide levels, supports long-term system reliability for major industrial users, and enables future employment opportunities by allowing large-scale industrial tena
3312.population: The project serves all Town of Callahan utility customers and future users within the Crawford Diamond Industrial Park service area. At build-out, the industrial park is projected to support major employers generating an estimated 500–2,100 direct and indirect jobs in Nassau County and the broader Northeast Florida region.
3312.outcome: The project will improve drinking water quality by removing hydrogen sulfide and meeting FDEP treatment standards, allowing reliable service to future industrial users at Crawford Diamond. Outcomes will be measured through certified compliance sampling documented in Monthly Operating Reports (MORs), FDEP operational approval, and tracking of reported job creation as tenants locate within the industrial park.

2352.description: The Town of Belleair has two bridges, both built in 1950, that lead to finger islands. These bridges were rebuilt in 1984, but are currently scour critical. There are indications of backfill leakage on both, as well as deep erosion holes adjacent to the wingwall caps. This erosion extends under the concrete approach apron for one of the bridges. The Town of Belleair intends to utilize funds to repair the bridges according the FDOT standards, as a plan of action has already been developed for both bridges.
2352.purpose: The bridges will be repaired and reinforced, resulting in them lasting many more years and the plan of action being completed, as directed by the Florida Department of Transportation. This will provide safer bridges for travel to residential homes and less mitigation efforts in the future.
2352.activities: Installation of rip rap and articulated concrete block to repair and reinforce the bridges.
2352.direct_services: Safer and structurally sound bridges for vehicles and pedestrians.
2352.outcome: Improved bridge safety and quality; regular inspection program, underwater inspection, and inspections after significant storm events will show outcome. Current bridge inspection will be compared with future bridge inspection to show marked improvement.

2541.description: The specific purpose of the funds being requested is to purchase a Rapid Emergency Response Vehicle, which will improve the city's emergency response capabilities, provide rapid support in crisis situations, enhance public safety, and ensure that first responders have the specialized equipment needed to effectively protect and assist the community during emergencies.
2541.purpose: The specific purpose of the funds being requested is to purchase a Rapid Emergency Response Vehicle, which will improve the city's emergency response capabilities, provide rapid support in crisis situations, enhance public safety, and ensure that first responders have the specialized equipment needed to effectively protect and assist the community during emergencies.
2541.activities: The funds will be used to purchase and fully equip the Rapid Emergency Response Vehicle, and deploy the vehicle for rapid response to critical incidents such as natural disasters, mass casualty events, hazardous material situations, and large-scale public safety emergencies—ensuring the community receives specialized, on-scene support when it is most needed.
2541.direct_services: The funding will provide citizens with direct services such as rapid emergency response during disasters or crises, on- scene support for medical, rescue, and public safety incidents, advanced communication and coordination capabilities in emergencies, and protection through specialized equipment deployed wherever and whenever critical incidents threaten community safety.
2541.population: The equipment will serve the more than 220,000 residents of the City of Cape Coral.
2541.outcome: This equipment protects people from harm by allowing first responders to quickly arrive on scene with specialized tools and technology to address medical emergencies, rescue operations, hazardous materials, and critical incidents, ensuring citizens receive timely care, coordinated public safety responses, and enhanced protection during disasters or crises. These benefits are measured by tracking response times to emergencies, recording the number and type of incidents successfully managed with the vehicle, assessing reductions in injury or loss during major events, reviewing community safety outcomes, and collecting feedback from responders and citizens after deployment in real-world situati

2560.description: Funds provided support Florida Repertory Theatre’s arts in education outreach programs which serves students in grades K-12 including classroom touring and lunchbox productions, on-site and on-location musical theatre and acting workshops, conservatory workshop series, main stage and special productions and summer camp program. Programs are fully supported by college apprenticeship/intern program with interns overseeing all aspects of production while gaining valuable experience.
2560.purpose: Funds support Florida Repertory Theatre's Arts in Education Initiative which serves more than 30,000 students per year in Lee County and the surrounding region. Students from grades K-12 are audience to both in-school and in- theatre productions. Program is supported by innovative internship/apprenticeship program where recent college graduates support all aspects of the program.
2560.activities: The Florida Repertory Theatre Arts in Education Initiative offers K-12 students the opportunity to experience theatre and performing arts. Students will enjoy age-appropriate, curriculum focused live theatre productions with the option of viewing in the theatre or on-location at their school. Students will also have the opportunity to participate in more in- depth programs, including musical theatre and acting workshops, summer camp and summer intensives.
2560.direct_services: K-12 offerings include main stage and lunch box productions with many performances offered on the school campus (Recent performances include Hamlet, Shrek, Jr., Refugee based on the book by Alan Gratz), Midsummer Night's Dream), Summer Camp, Summer Intensives, Conservatory, Theatre for Young Arts, mini stars
2560.population: The target population are students in grades K-12 who are audience to the main stage and lunchbox productions, including on-site and on-location performances. The Florida Repertory Theatre serves more than 30,000 students per year in Lee, Collier, Charlotte, Glades and Hendry Counties. Recent college graduates participating in the apprenticeship/internship program are also served. Participants in the apprenticeship/internship program support all aspects of the fine arts initiative including acti
2560.outcome: The Florida Repertory Theatre Arts in Education Initiative provides the students who see an age appropriate, curriculum focused theatre production with a higher quality education. Theatre boosts comprehension and increases retention of written material by providing additional context, helping students visualize the settings, actions and character emotions. Students who see the programming or participate in an arts program will have an enriched cultural experience, preserving traditions and nurturing creativity. The methodology of measuring the success of our programs is through parent, teacher and student surveys.

2438.description: Funding will be used to mitigate regular flooding in the Tradewinds area of Sanibel by reconstructing stormwater drainage. The flooding issues in this neighborhood were exacerbated by recent hurricanes. Historically, this area was designed to drain to the Gulf. However, subsequent changes to environmental regulations required the removal of the Gulf outfall, increasing the frequency of flooding of roadways and property. The City has funded ($96,000) and completed design for this shovel ready project. Mitigating the direct impact of flooding of public roadways, private property, and improving the overall resilience of the Tradewinds neighborhood and adjacent subdevelopments is the primary goal. Requires dry season construction.
2438.purpose: Sanibel is requesting a state appropriation of $4.2 million to fully fund implementation of this stormwater improvement project. The City has funded ($96,000) and completed design for this shovel ready project. Mitigating the direct impact of flooding of public roadways, private property, and improving the overall resilience of the Tradewinds neighborhood and adjacent subdevelopments is the primary goal.
2438.activities: State funds will be used to construct the designed stormwater improvements.
2438.direct_services: This project will significantly improve stormwater drainage in the Tradewinds neighborhood and mitigate regular flooding of roadways and private property.
2438.population: The general public will be served by the project. 68 residential and resort structures will be directly served by this project and an additional 200 structures will be indirectly served by mitigating stormwater flow from the Tradewinds are to adjacent subdevelopments. Additionally, thousands of people who use the Tradewinds roads will benefit from reduced roadway flooding.
2438.outcome: Protect economic losses from property damage related to regular flooding of the Tradewinds area.

2842.description: The primary goal of this project is to accommodate the significant growth in Southeast Lee County. By connecting the new Southeast Force Main Segment 2 to the new Southeast Advanced Water Reclamation Facility, this project will expand wastewater treatment capacity, improve service reliability and provide access to central sewer connection and ensure compliance for long-term sustainability.
2842.purpose: The primary goal of this project is to accommodate the significant growth in Southeast Lee County. By connecting the new Southeast Force Main Segment 2 to the new Southeast Advanced Water Reclamation Facility, this project will expand wastewater treatment capacity, improve service reliability and provide access to central sewer connection and ensure compliance for long-term sustainability.
2842.activities: This project involves the construction of the force main and associated appurtenances to connect the new Southeast Force Main Segment 2 to the new Southeast Advanced Water Reclamation Facility, which will directly expand wastewater treatment capacity, improve service reliability and provide access to central sewer connection and ensure compliance for long-term sustainability.
2842.direct_services: The new force main will increase wastewater treatment capacity supporting significant residential and commercial growth in Southeast Lee County. This project also ensures reliable infrastructure reducing the need for septic tanks and protecting the local environment from nutrient loading.
2842.population: The target population is residents within unincorporated areas in Southeast Lee County. The number of individuals expected to be served is more than 800.
2842.outcome: The reduction of nutrient loading of phosphorus and nitrogen from added septic tanks. The benefit will be connection to central sewer. The increase in wastewater treatment capacity for the Southeast Lee County region will be measured by the additional permitted capacity for wastewater treatment from regulatory agencies.

2843.description: Lee County Utilities (LCU) is requesting funding to advance its Alternative Water Supply (AWS) program through the construction of a new raw water transmission pipeline to convey brackish groundwater from five new supply wells in the North Fort Myers area. Funding is requested to construct approximately 5 miles of raw water transmission pipeline to connect five new brackish groundwater wells to the North Lee County RO Water Treatment Plant for potable water production.
2843.purpose: Lee County Utilities (LCU) is requesting funding to advance its Alternative Water Supply (AWS) program through the construction of a new raw water transmission pipeline to convey brackish groundwater from five new supply wells in the North Fort Myers area. Funding is requested to construct approximately 5 miles of raw water transmission pipeline to connect five new brackish groundwater wells to the North Lee County RO Water Treatment Plant for potable water production.
2843.activities: By developing brackish groundwater for potable distribution, this project provides a reliable, drought-resilient source of drinking water, safeguards long-term water supply, and enhances system flexibility. In addition, shifting demand to brackish sources promotes natural recharge of shallow aquifers, protecting regional water resources and supporting sustainable growth.
2843.direct_services: The project will provide potable water supply and fire protection to the North Lee County distribution system.
2843.population: Current and future customers receiving potable water services from the North Lee County WTP. More than 800 individuals are expected to be served.
2843.outcome: Reduced reliance of shallow aquifers allowing for natural recharge, protecting regional water resources and supporting sustainable growth. This will be measured by the additional permitted capacity for use of brackish water supply from regulatory agency.

2542.organization: Lee County Board of County Commissioners
2542.description: Provide funding to Lee County to construct a new 6' sidewalk and 5' path along Pine Ridge Rd from San Carlos Blvd to Summerlin Rd, to increase the safety of the pedestrians and bicyclists by providing a safe place to walk and ride. This project corridor is identified as part of the Florida Department of Transportation Shared-Use Non-motorized (SUN) Trail Program that was established in 2015.
2542.purpose: Provide funding to Lee County to construct a new 6' sidewalk and 5' path along Pine Ridge Rd from San Carlos Blvd to Summerlin Rd, to increase the safety of the pedestrians and bicyclists by providing a safe place to walk and ride. This project corridor is identified as part of the Florida Department of Transportation Shared-Use Non-motorized (SUN) Trail Program that was established in 2015.
2542.activities: The funding will be used to assist the County with construction of a new sidewalk on Pine Ridge Rd.
2542.direct_services: Construction of this project will provide a safe sidewalk and path Pine Ridge Rd that will eventually connect to the FDOT Sun Trail system.
2542.population: The majority of funds will benefit no specific group. The individuals expected to be served are greater than 800.
2542.outcome: Providing a safer bike and pedestrian facility for the community. This will be measured by reviewing and comparing pedestrian crash statistics after the sidewalk is built.

2432.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
2432.description: The funding for the master plan, design and/or construction of facilities and amenities for the Mike Greenwell Regional Park.
2432.purpose: Provide for a master plan to incorporate facilities, stormwater management, and park amenities.
2432.activities: Conceptual and buildable designs as funding allows; and/or construction of park amenities.
2432.direct_services: The master plan, design and/or construction of improvements to this site will maximize the property as a dynamic, diverse community hub. This investment will foster job creation, build economic resilience through diverse event and program offerings, and will support local cultural, educational and community events.
2432.population: Lee County's residents (>800,000), most notably the eastern region of the County (Lehigh Acres, Alva, etc.).
2432.outcome: Agricultural education is the primary mission of the SWFL Ag Expo. By partnering with UF/IFAS, Lee County 4-H, FFA, Lee County School District, and the FGCU School of Agribusiness, upgraded facilities will provide exponential opportunities for agricultural promotion and education. ultural experiences will be enriched and preserved through cultural-related program and events at the fairground and event center. Benefit measured through Tracking of increased traffic, participation, programs/events, educational offerings, school field trips, etc.

2431.description: During Hurricane Ian's landfall in September 2022, a storm surge of five to seven feet caused severe damage to the Fort Myers Beach (FMB) Water Reclamation Facility (WRF). This led to widespread electrical failure as the floodwaters caused saltwater intrusion and submerged much of the ground-level equipment. The proposed scope of work will replace the previous treatment process with new, Biological Nutrient Removal, which is needed to achieve advanced treatment of wastewater.
2431.purpose: The purpose of this project is to rehabilitate the FMB WRF, due to loss of treatment capacity, aging infrastructure and damages sustained during Hurricane Ian (Sept. 2022), to include hazard mitigation and flood-proofing elements, to provide a climate-stable facility for uninterrupted treatment of domestic wastewater to a coastal community. The requested funding will be used to construct three Biological Nutrient Removal trains.
2431.activities: Construction of three Biological Nutrient Removal (BNR) trains.
2431.direct_services: The FMB WRF treats wastewater from residential and commercial properties within the Town of Fort Myers Beach and adjacent unincorporated areas of Lee County, which comprises approximately 27% of LCU’s service area wastewater flows primarily in the southwest region of the county. This represents a total estimated population of 168,114.
2431.population: All customers receiving essential wastewater services from the FMB WRF, greater than 800 people.
2431.outcome: The project will be constructed to prevent power interruption due to electrical catastrophic failure resulting in widespread service area sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs), exposing the public to pathogens from untreated wastewater. This will be measured by the increased reliability of infrastructure by reduced number of outages or service disruptions due to electrical failures.

2427.description: This will adapt the interior design of Wilson G. Specifically, this project will continue a statewide network by providing the Learning Blade career awareness and interest system to primarily middle schools and other K-12 schools statewide and allow schools to interact with each other. This system is currently successfully offered statewide in 13 other states and has demonstrated excellent results over the past 10 years. These risks are heightened for youth with child welfare involvement and those from marginalized backgrounds. National data also shows that Black youth and LGBTQ+ youth are experiencing the steepest increases in suicide attempts, underscoring the urgency for targeted, community-based

2234.description: Funding for this project will equip the City of Hialeah with a volumetric concrete truck capable of producing high-quality concrete on-site and on-demand, eliminating delays caused by plant availability or inconvenient ready-mix delivery schedules. This advanced equipment allows crews to adjust mix design, slump, strength, and admixtures in real time to meet exact engineering specifications, an essential capability for the small, scattered, or unpredictable repair volumes common in municipal work. By generating only, the material needed at each location, the volumetric truck significantly reduces labor hours, boosts productivity, and removes costly scheduling conflicts and short-load fees associated with traditional ready-mix suppliers.

Raising the elevation of the road will result in an overall better performing and safer public roadway and restore the flow of water in and around the area that is impeded by the causeway.

2555.description: The MAG Foundation USA is a Florida-based high-performance training program that prepares elite male gymnasts to represent the United States in international competition and the Olympic Games. The program provides world-class coaching, integrated sports medicine and performance services, Olympic-level training equipment, and essential athlete living support, enabling athletes to train full-time in Florida. State appropriations funding is essential to sustain and expand these services, address the rising costs of elite training and medical care, and ensure that Florida remains a nationally recognized hub for men’s gymnastics. 2555.outcome: Expected outcomes include improved athlete health and retention, increased national team selections, international medal performances, and successful qualification of athletes for Olympic competition. 2741.description: To reduce maternal morbidity and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes among women who experience hypertensive disorders of pregnancy such as preeclampsia. The program leverages remote patient monitoring (RPM) technology to optimize pregnancy outcomes, integrate cardiac risk assessment, and extend care into the postpartum period — a vulnerable time when 80% of maternal mortality can be prevented. Key objectives include identifying women at risk, monitoring biomarkers, integrating data into care pathways, and building a longitudinal database to inform national standards of care.
2741.purpose: Hypertensive disorders complicate 14.2% of Florida pregnancies and cause 18.2% of pregnancy-related deaths. The state's maternal mortality rate is 18.5 per 100,000 live births, rising to 24.1 within 42 days postpartum. Most deaths—35–56% after discharge and 75% within 60 days—occur when follow-up lapses. The goal is to reduce preventable postpartum hypertension–related long and short-term morbidity and maternal mortality in Florida through implementation of a structured remote monitoring program
2741.activities: 1) Remote blood pressure monitoring and follow-up for up to 500 postpartum women annually. 2) Education and care coordination with cardiology and connection to primary care for high-risk mothers statewide. 3) Integration of cardiology and obstetrics for improved long-term outcomes.
2741.direct_services: HeartWise provides technology-enabled postpartum care for women with pregnancy complications. Services include remote monitoring using connected BP devices, daily data review with clinical follow-up, education on nutrition and risk management, and coordinated referrals to primary care and Cardiology to optimize long term health.
2741.population: The target population is women with pregnancy complications (preeclampsia, and gestational hypertension) 200-400 is the target population.
2741.outcome: Expected Measurable Outcomes:1) Reduce severe hypertension episodes and preventable ICU admissions, 2) Reduce readmissions for postpartum blood pressure complications and 3) Increase postpartum follow-up rates and medication adherence. Outcomes will be tracked through electronic health records (EHRs), remote monitoring data, and follow-up documentation. Baseline metrics will be established from prior-year data at participating hospitals. Key indicators—such as hypertension episodes, ICU admissions, readmissions, referral and follow up with Cardiology and adherence to long term care plan—will be compared pre- and post-implementation.
