Through these enhanced facilities, youth ages 6–18 will benefit from sports, recreation, health and wellness activities, and soft skill development in communication, teamwork, and resiliency to support academic and leadership grow.
2728.direct_services: The Basketball Pavilion contributes to local economic stability by offering accessible after-school and summer programs that allow parents and guardians to work full-time, confident their children are safe and engaged in positive activities, At the same time, the programs empower youth to excel in school and prepares teens for the workforce through career exploration, leadership training, and job-
2728.population: The club is located in a low income Census Tract, with 75% of our current club families considered low income. We expect to serve 400 youth and teens annually. We charge a nominal fee and provide scholarships to families to need which helps level the playing field by providing access to high quality educational programs in underserved communities.
2728.outcome: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Lee County’s Basketball Pavilion will advance the State of Florida’s goals for youth development, public health, education, and workforce readiness. By providing young people with safe, structured opportunities for recreation, learning, and leadership, the project directly supports the State’s investment in building stronger communities and a healthier, more productive future workforce. Outcomes are measured through school issued report cards and graduation rates, daily participation attendance and our National Youth Outcome Initiative survey which measures youth experience and outcomes.

2642.description: YReads/YMCA Reads! is an after-school mentoring and tutoring program in Florida designed to support students in kindergarten through 4th grade who are reading below grade level. The program partners with teachers and school administrators to identify students performing in the lowest 25% in reading, specifically those scoring Achievement Levels 1 and 2 on state assessments.
2642.purpose: The goal of the YMCA Reads program is to reduce the number of students not reading at grade level. The YMCA Reads program successfully closes the achievement gap in students' reading performance with structured curricula delivered by well-trained teachers and mentors. The YMCA Reads program teaches literacy skills to students via small group tutoring/mentoring. Mentoring enhances academic achievement through relationship building and increased academic self-esteem from learning to read.
2642.activities: Individualized and small group lessons and interactive instruction based on Systematic Instruction in Phonologic Awareness, Phonics and Sight Words, as well as differentiated instruction in reading comprehension and vocabulary acquisition.
2642.direct_services: Direct evidence-based reading instruction to struggling readers in grades K-4 with input from classroom teachers and reading coaches.
2642.population: The YMCA Reads program serves K-4 students who are reading below grade level, with a focus on those from low income and under-resourced communities. The program is expected to serve approximately 1,000 students across multiple YMCA sites in Florida.
2642.outcome: Expected benefits and outcomes are the improvement of literacy skills among K-4 students reading below grade level, with a focus on increasing reading fluency, comprehension, and overall academic confidence by providing structured tutoring and mentorship. The program’s impact will be measured using a combination of pre- and post-program reading assessments. Additional evaluation methods include teacher feedback, student progress reports, and attendance tracking to assess engagement and consistency in participation.

2845.description: Within the City of Fort Myers, over 500 properties are unserved by sewer. This utility gap which impacts a few thousand residents. This conversion is essential to reduce ground pollution, protect stormwater systems, and ensure resilience in the event of a disaster. An investment from the legislature for this critical project would allow the City to design and construct the first phase of this conversion for residents in critical need.
2845.purpose: The requested funds will allow the City of Fort Myers to provide septic conversion for residents currently unserved by sewer.
2845.activities: Design and construction of new sewer utilities.
2845.direct_services: Residents will be provided with critical sewer infrastructure reducing ground water pollution and protection of stormwater systems.
2845.population: The total project intends to serve approximately 500 disadvantaged households within the City of Fort Myers.
2845.outcome: Converting septic systems to central sewer systems allows for wastewater to be treated at a facility designed to remove a much higher percentage of nitrogen. While studies indicate that a conventional septic system can remove only 10-40% of nitrogen, a properly designed sewer system can remove upwards of 80% of nitrogen through its treatment process, effectively eliminating most of the nitrogen that would otherwise leach into groundwater from a septic system.

3260.description: This funding expands Not One Left Alone (NOLA) Individual Resilience Program (IRP) from private to public schools. IRP is a Framework for Emotional Regulation and Academic Success. Every student will receive early screening, with targeted, science-backed resilience training for those needing support.
3260.purpose: By expanding NOLA's IRP from private to public schools, close to 10,000 Pasco County students will receive evidence-based support to improve their mental health and academic performance. This will become a case study for future expansion efforts. By strengthening focus, stress regulation, memory, and confidence, the IRP fosters lifelong coping skills, improves well-being, and builds stronger schools and communities.
3260.activities: Every student will complete the MIQ Mental Health Screening to help schools identify those who may benefit from added support with focus, learning, or emotional regulation. This research-based tool enables early, proactive intervention. Selected students participate in 32–40 in-school sessions using biofeedback, mindfulness, and movement to strengthen attention, calm, and confidence, benefiting schools and communities alike.
3260.direct_services: Identified students will receive 32–40 in-school resilience sessions over a semester or as needed, offered as an elective during the school day. School liaisons will be trained and supported to deliver sessions with ongoing expert oversight. Through biofeedback, mindfulness, and movement training, students build healthier stress responses, sharper focus, and lasting confidence.
3260.population: The Individual Resilience Program will serve Pasco County, Florida, reaching students across the district. Approximately 10,000 students in grades 6–7 will complete the initial screening, with about 40% identified through results to receive targeted resilience training. This rollout focuses on early adolescence, when emotional regulation and stress management skills have the greatest long-term impact.
3260.outcome: Expected outcomes include measurable gains in focus, emotional regulation, and classroom performance. Each student completes pre and post assessments using validated biometric measures such as heart rate variability to show improved stress response. Schools will report on attendance, academic performance, and discipline outcomes, including fewer detentions, referrals, and the need for de-escalation or resource officer support. Track and report the number of individuals served, broken down by demographic, and pre- and multiple post-survey results.

3261.organization: Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of
3261.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
3261.description: Bigs in Blue is an interactive mentoring program offered by Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of Florida (BBBSAF). At-risk youth are paired with assessed and trained adult mentors who become role models and provide positive guidance and direction. Sessions are held in the community, at schools, at workplaces, at BBBS partnering organizations, or virtually. Mentoring activities focus on educational support/academic enhancement, career exploration, experiential learning, and/or developing skills and abilities that will lead to improved potential, confidence & self-sufficiency. The Bigs in Blue program also positively impacts communities by establishing and strengthening mutual friendship and trust between young people, their families, and first responders.
3261.purpose: Bigs in Blue is an interactive based mentoring program offered by Big Brothers Big Sisters Association of Florida (BBBSAF), facilitated by its local member agencies, that connects youth with first responders in communities, building strong, trusting, lasting relationships. Through high quality, professionally supported mentoring, young people have a greater opportunity to grow up to be confident, competent, caring adults. These relationships build strong bonds between first responders and the fa
3261.activities: BBBSAF will manage and provide programmatic and financial oversight to the BBBS local agencies (subcontractors). Local agencies will make and support new and existing mentoring matches between youth and first responders. Matches will receive a range of services: recruitment, assessment, training, matching, monthly mentoring, and match support from a trained BBBS professional.
3261.direct_services: Mentoring activities will focus on educational support/academic enhancement, career exploration, experiential learning, and/or developing skills and abilities that will lead to improved potential, confidence & self-sufficiency. Youth will be mentored for a minimum of once per month. Sessions will be held in the community, at schools, at first responder workplaces, at BBBS partnering organizations,
3261.population: The Bigs in Blue program serves youth who are at-risk of poor academic performance, behavioral issues, family dysfunction, and other situations that may lead to negative future outcomes. Mentors are active and/or retired first responders (i.e., law enforcement, EMT, Fire/Rescue, State Attorneys, etc.).
3261.outcome: Matches meet monthly for site or community-based mentoring sessions with mentors who are first responders to engage in academic enrichment activities and community engagement, such as outings to museums, parks, recreational events. Additionally, matches will spend time job shadowing/career exploration at law enforcement entities. The benefits are that youth will: gain extra support necessary to improve and excel in their academic career; learn about law enforcement or other first responder careers in their community. Those experiences can lead to a more positive & fulfilling future. The Youth Outcome Survey is a BBBS assessment tool used to evaluate a youth's change in skills and behaviors,

3495.description: Mid Florida Community Services, Inc. Children's Advocacy Center of Hernando County (CAC) coordinates the multidisciplinary investigative process of child abuse cases with DCF, law enforcement and the child protection team. It is a child-friendly facility that responds to children who are child victims of sexual abuse, physical abuse, threatened harm, drug-endangerment, mental injury, neglect, and witnesses of domestic violence. Additionally, the CAC has a trauma treatment program for child victims of sexual abuse. We have purchased property, designed and are currently breaking ground on the new building which is a result of the state funds awarded to Mid Florida Community Services, Inc. in 23/24 and 24/25.
3495.purpose: Funds will be used to finish constructing the 10,000 sq foot building for the Children's Advocacy Center of Hernando County. The building will provide a safe, child friendly environment for children to disclose abuse & heal from it. It will include medical rooms for rape exams, interview rooms, observation rooms for law enforcement & DCF to observe the interviews, and trauma therapy rooms. This will allow the CAC to bring all the staff under one roof which is in the best interest of child victim
3495.activities: The funds will be used to construct the new building to provide services which include: forensic/specialized interviews, assessments, forensic medical exams, multi-disciplinary staffing, advocacy, deposition/court accompaniment, case management, individual and family therapy for child victims and their non-offending caregivers and siblings and adults who have been sexually abused as children.
3495.direct_services: Services include: forensic/specialized interviews, assessments, forensic medical exams, multi-disciplinary staffing, advocacy, deposition/court accompaniment, case management, individual and family therapy for child victims and their non-offending caregivers and siblings. The CAC also provides therapeutic treatment for adults who have been sexually abused as children.
3495.population: Children ages 0-17 who are victims of physical abuse, sexual abuse, neglect, human trafficking, child sexual abuse material, pornography, drug endangered, who witness domestic violence, survivors of homicide as well as adults who were sexually abused as children are eligible for services. Non-offending family members such as siblings, parents, or grandparents are also eligible for services. The CAC expects to serve over 800 children and family members this current fiscal year and expect that fig
3495.outcome: The expected benefit is to enhance child abuse investigations and increase prosecution rates with child abuse cases, protecting children from harm; improving their physical and mental health, reducing substance abuse; reducing recidivism. The CAC provides a multidiscipline-coordinated investigative response with DCF, law enforcement, child protection team and the state attorney where the outcome of the interview and medical are discussed, referrals for therapy made, and collectively discussing what needs the family has. Pre and post assessments are completed with therapy and evidence-based trauma therapy is utilized. 90% of children served will see a reduction in trauma. Cases are tracked to

3610.description: Zero Hour Life Center (ZHLC) seeks $30,000 to support Peer Power 2026, an annual statewide retreat designed to strengthen Florida's peer recovery workforce. The retreat provides Certified Recovery Peer Specialists (CRPS) and other peer professionals an opportunity to rejuvenate, network, and enhance their professional skills. Over two days, attendees participate in facilitated workshops, professional development sessions, and discussions led by state and national leaders in recovery-oriented care. The focus is on building recovery capital, enhancing self-care, and deepening the understanding of the critical role peers play in supporting individuals and communities in recovery.
3610.purpose: The requested funds will support Peer Power 2026, a statewide retreat that strengthens Florida’s peer recovery workforce by providing affordable access to professional development, wellness activities, and recovery- capital–building workshops. Funding will reduce participation costs, offer scholarships for peers with financial need, and expand access for those in rural or underserved areas. The event helps prevent burnout, increases workforce retention, and equips Certified Peer Recovery Special
3610.activities: Funds will support a two-day professional development and wellness retreat that includes peer-led workshops, recovery capital–building sessions, keynote presentations on the impact of peer services, facilitated networking events, skill-building trainings, wellness and rejuvenation activities, and access to recovery-friendly local resources. Activities are designed to enhance peer competencies, prevent burnout, strengthen collaboration among Certified Peer Recovery Specialists, and improve servic
3610.direct_services: The project will provide direct services to Certified Peer Recovery Specialists and peer support workers, including training in recovery support competencies, facilitated workshops to build individual recovery capital, professional development sessions to strengthen their ability to serve vulnerable populations, and structured wellness activities to reduce burnout and improve retention. By equippi
3610.population: The target population for this project is Florida's peer recovery workforce, including Certified Peer Recovery Specialists, peer support staff, and individuals in training for peer certification. The retreat is designed to increase access for peers from rural, underserved, and low-income communities. Peer Power 2026 is expected to serve approximately 75–100 participants through direct training, workshops, and wellness programming.
3610.outcome: The expected outcomes include increased peer workforce competency, reduced burnout, improved retention, and strengthened recovery capital among participants, leading to higher-quality peer support services across Florida. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-event surveys assessing knowledge gained, confidence in peer support skills, and wellness indicators; participant feedback on training effectiveness; tracking scholarship utilization; and follow-up surveys 60 days after the retreat to evaluate sustained impact on professional practice and service delivery.

3262.description: LifeStream Behavioral Center proposes the development of a 16-bed Level 2 residential care facility dedicated to serving our senior population diagnosed with dementia and/or other cognitive impairments. This proposal advocates a compassionate, community-based alternative to the Baker Act for individuals with dementia and/or other cognitive impairments in Citrus County, Florida. This initiative reflects LifeStream’s commitment to expanding access to compassionate, specialized care for vulnerable populations in need of both short-term stabilization and long-term support. The proposed program emphasizes preserving dignity and independence and reducing unnecessary psychiatric hospitalizations and other costly care.
3262.purpose: The primary goal is to divert improper Baker Acts and provide a safe, structured, and therapeutic environment for adults experiencing moderate to severe cognitive decline. The program will offer individualized care plans tailored to each resident’s cognitive, emotional, and physical needs. The facility will support both short-term respite and long-term residential stays. LifeStream will promote dignity, autonomy, and quality of life through evidence-based practices and person-centered care. This
3262.activities: The facility will be strategically situated within LifeStream’s existing behavioral health campus to ensure seamless integration with medical, pharmacy and psychiatric services. It will provide 16 private and semi-private beds, designed to accommodate both ambulatory and non-ambulatory residents. The environment will be a secure, homelike setting with therapeutic design features including sensory rooms, memory aids and calming decor. Enhanced safety protocols will include wander management syste
3262.direct_services: • 24-hour supervision and assistance with activities of daily living (ADLs) • Medication management and coordination with primary care and neurology providers • Cognitive stimulation therapies and structured recreational activities • Behavioral health support including crisis intervention and psychiatric consultation • Family education, caregiver support, and discharge planning
3262.population: The facility will serve Citrus County, FL senior adults diagnosed with: alzheimer’s disease; vascular dementia; Lewy body dementia; frontotemporal dementia; mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia; and, other neurodegenerative conditions affecting cognition. Residents may be referred from hospitals, outpatient clinics, family caregivers, or other residential programs requiring a higher level of supervision and support. The anticipated number to be served is 51-100 and their families/ca
3262.outcome: LifeStream anticipates the following outcomes: • Reduction in hospital readmissions and emergency interventions • Improved behavioral stability and emotional well-being • Enhanced caregiver satisfaction and reduced burnout • Increased access to long-term care options for cognitively impaired individuals

3586.description: This request is for the expansion of Citrus County's existing judicial and government complex in downtown Inverness. As Citrus County continues to grow, the demand for judicial services is projected to continue increasing, and with the current County Courthouse operating at or near full capacity, it has become critical to expand the existing judicial and government footprint. If funded, this request will support the acquisition of real property surrounding the existing courthouse and will also support initial design of infrastructure necessary for the expansion. This investment builds on the County's existing $8 million local commitment.
3586.purpose: These funds will support the acquisition of strategically located properties and the preliminary design of infrastructure necessary to expand the judicial and governmental facilities in downtown Inverness. As court operations expand, ensuring appropriate separation of judicial staff, inmates, and the public will become increasingly important to ensure safety for all parties. If funded, this will allow the County to begin acquiring key parcels surrounding the Courthouse as well as begin the desig
3586.activities: With these funds, Citrus County will be able to begin acquisition of key parcels surrounding the Citrus County Courthouse. Moreover, the County will begin the initial design work for the infrastructure necessary for the expansion; this will include feasibility and space-needs planning, preliminary site concepts, and early design work needed to support future judicial facility expansion.
3586.direct_services: As a result of this funding, Citrus County can begin the necessary process of beginning to expand its judicial and governmental footprint at the Citrus County Courthouse. Due to the continued population growth of Citrus County, this expansion has become necessary and, once completed, will improve the public's access to courts, enhance safety and security, and support efficient court operations.
3586.population: The target population for this project includes any and all individuals that utilize the Citrus County Judicial and Government Systems. It is expected that this will include the population as a whole as any individual could potentially need to utilize the services provided in the Citrus County Courthouse.
3586.outcome: If funded, some of the expected benefits that would be experienced by this project include the protection of the general public from harm related to safety within the Courthouse, improvements to economic activity related to the use of the Courthouse, and general improvements to the ability to provide safe and efficient access to court operations in Citrus County to the general public. These outcomes can be measured through the use of tracking documents detailing milestones through the land acquisition and initial design processes.

2929.description: The Academy of Spectrum Diversity was built to serve children who have any intellectual or developmental disability, regardless of their level of functionality or placement on the spectrum of their disability. This project will allow for expansion of Services to add to existing enrollment. This will come through enabling the Academy of Spectrum Diversity to retain-recruit-support high qualified staff.
2929.purpose: The funds requested will support the expansion of our school by allowing us to serve an additional 50 students. These funds will be used to increase instructional capacity, enhance classroom resources, and ensure appropriate staffing and support services. This growth will enable us to maintain small class sizes, provide individualized instruction, and continue delivering high-quality academic and social-emotional programming to a larger student population.
2929.activities: The funds will support the expansion and delivery of comprehensive educational services designed to meet the diverse needs of our student population. This includes core academic instruction, individualized educational support, and specialized interventions. In addition, the funds will provide life skills training focused on independence, communication, and daily living skills; pre-employment training that builds workplace readiness, job exploration, and soft skills; and college preparation cours
2929.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct educational and support services to citizens through structured academic instruction, individualized learning support, and targeted interventions. Students will receive life skills training to promote independence and daily functioning, pre-employment training focused on workplace readiness, career exploration, and soft skills development, and college
2929.population: The target population served by this project includes kindergarten through 12th grade students with developmental and educational needs who require individualized academic instruction, life skills development, and transition support. The project is designed to serve students across all grade levels who benefit from specialized educational services. Through this appropriation, the program expects to serve a total of approximately 120–150 students, including an expansion to support an additional 5
2929.outcome: The expected outcome of this project is to prepare students to become self-sufficient, employable, and productive members of the community. Graduates will demonstrate increased independence, readiness for employment or postsecondary pathways, and a reduced reliance on long-term community support. Outcomes will be measured through formal assessments conducted seven times per year, along with continuous progress monitoring using academic data, life skills benchmarks, and vocational readiness indicators.

3265.organization: Habitat for Humanity of Pinellas County, Inc
3265.description: Addressing the lack of affordable homeownership within Hernando Counties. Funding will be dedicated to support the construction of 28 affordable homeownership units in Hernando County on Century Drive. These activities include infrastructure development, architectural, civil engineering and other related expenses that are necessary for the successful completion of the development. Hernando County Board of County Commissioners has provided the land for development and is fully vested in the project.
3265.purpose: Addressing the lack of affordable homeownership within Hernando County. Funding will be dedicated to support the construction of 28 affordable homeownership units in Hernando, on formerly county owned property on Century Drive. These activities include infrastructure development, architectural, civil engineering and other related expenses that are necessary for the successful completion of the development.
3265.activities: Habitat for Humanity Tampa Bay Gulfside will act as the sole developer for the affordable housing development that receive funding, managing all aspects of construction which includes, selecting contractors, subcontractors and overseeing their work. Lastly, our organization will ensure each unit is occupied by income-qualified homeowners.
3265.direct_services: Habitat builds and sells homes at no profit and no interest to households who do not qualify for a traditional mortgage. The program prepares homeowner partners to be successful homeowners through an education curriculum of 36 classes, from budgeting to home maintenance. The program is predicated on the principle of a hand-up and not a handout. Homeowners purchase their home from Habitat and are p
3265.population: Population served by this funding will be income-qualified homeowners at or below 80% of the area median income as determined by HUD adjusted for family size. Anticipated total individuals directly served is between 100 to 125.
3265.outcome: Ultimate success will be measured by a homeowner receiving the keys to their new home and officially becoming the newest homeowner in Hernando County. If awarded funding, ultimate program success would be measured by the number of homes constructed, number of successful homes sold to income qualified homeowners and ensuring all homeowners are paying no more than 30% of their gross monthly income to their housing expenses.

2834.organization: Inspired by Education LLC dba eSpired
2834.description: Provide a custom curriculum for all public schools in accordance with SB 1264 (2024) on the History of Communism.
2834.purpose: The goal is to provide a custom curriculum for all public schools in accordance with SB 1264 (2024) on the History of Communism.
2834.activities: A custom curriculum will be developed in accordance with Florida state education standards. Through a statewide license, all school districts in the state will have access to the custom K-12 curriculum on the history of communism.
2834.direct_services: Florida students and teachers will have access to a uniform curriculum aligned to Florida's standards on the history of communism. All lessons will be designed with the student in mind and with the goal of maximizing engagement, learning and mastery of the material.
2834.outcome: As a result of a new unified curriculum, Florida students will be able to show mastery of new standards on the history of communism. Assessment tools will be included with each lesson.

3266.description: Pace Hernando is currently housed in portables located on the J.D. Floyd Elementary School property as a temporary location. Funds are being requested to complete the building project located at 10386 Chalmer Street, Spring Hill, FL 34608. Pace Hernando operates 250 days per year and serves approximately 150 girls at risk of Juvenile Justice System involvement annually. The facility will include a safe location for classroom, counseling, and other school safety features. Pace Hernando has been in operation since 2017 and is in need of expansion to further community services to girls ages 11-17 in the Hernando County community.
3266.purpose: The building will be utilized to serve approximately 150 girls annually who are at risk of Juvenile Justice System involvement. This project aligns with Hernando County's commitment to investing in programs that strengthen the community through education, opportunity, and prevention. The completion of the new Pace Hernando Building will expand the Pace Hernando's ability to meet the increasing demand for services in our county while enhancing safety, accessibility, and technology to better suppo
3266.activities: Girls receive wrap around social services such as therapy, counseling, and life skills. Girls in the Pace Center also receive their full academic school day, with education provided by Florida certificated teachers. Services are provided in a trauma-informed, gender-responsive, and strength-based environment.
3266.direct_services: The building will house a Pace Center, including a full academic staff, social services staff, and administrative staff. Pace Hernando staff will provide comprehensive social services and the full academic school day to girls at risk of delinquency through our Pace Center and wrap around services to girls. Case management for the girls' families is also provided.
3266.population: The funds will serve a target population of at-risk girls between the ages of 11 and 17, in grades 6-12. This includes, but is not limited to, girls with poor mental and physical health; economically disadvantaged; homeless; developmentally disabled; formerly incarcerated youth who are at risk for recidivism; and victims of crime. It is expected that Pace Hernando will serve approximately 150 girls annually, based on recent census.
3266.outcome: Girls will learn to better manage and improve their emotional, mental, physical health and increase their self-efficacy (Schwarzer Self-Efficacy Scale). Girls who spend 90 or more days at Pace will: improve in at least two academic criteria (Salesforce and Exponent Case Management); increase protective factors (Positive Youth Development Inventory scale); increase college and career readiness (ONET and community engagement); and decrease involvement with Juvenile Justice System (FLDJJ Comprehensive Accountability Report).

3211.description: The City of Mexico Beach is requesting nonrecurring funding to complete an engineering evaluation of the existing wastewater master lift station (MX-1), the force main wastewater line to Bay County, and a potential wastewater treatment facility. This evaluation will assess the current system conditions, operational vulnerabilities, and feasibility of relocating the lift station to reduce flood and storm surge risk from natural disasters. This effort will also include the preparation of a Preliminary Engineering Report (PER) and supporting technical documentation necessary to submit an application to the State Revolving Fund (SRF) Program for construction funding in the future. This request does not include any construction.
3211.purpose: The goal of this project will be to determine a more ideal location for the City's Master Lift Station (MX-1). The City of Mexico Beach has been issued a Consent Order from Florida Department of Environmental Protection due to the number of sewage spills at MX-1 and is currently on a monitoring plan to address further spills. In addition, the funds will be used to evaluate the City's waste water system and feasibility of a dedicated WWTP in Mexico Beach. The funds will be used to draft an SRF Pr
3211.activities: The funds will be used to draft an SRF Preliminary Engineering Report and application.
3211.direct_services: This project will address the waste water issues within the City and a engineering report will be developed to be submitted for an SRF application.
3211.population: This project will serve all residents of the City of Mexico Beach (over 1,400 residents) as it will address the master lift station that serves the entire City and it will address the need for a dedicated WWTP in the City of Mexico Beach.
3211.outcome: The methodology by which this outcome will be measured is an engineering report to be submitted as part of an SRF application that will result in a loan to the City that can be used to address the waste water issues and needs identified in the report.

3212.description: Dellwood Volunteer Fire Department (Dellwood VFD) requests funds to be used for the purchase of a new Pumper/Tanker Fire Apparatus. Currently, the Dellwood VFD relies on an aging/failing fleet that often impacts response and response times threatening residents and their property. This apparatus will harden fire and rescue services in the Dellwood Community along with much of unincorporated Jackson County. Many residents depend on the vital fire and rescue services provided by the Dellwood VFD.
3212.purpose: Using the funds requested to purchase a desperately needed new fire apparatus, all residents within the Dellwood community (and many unincorporated areas within Jackson County) will receive uninterrupted and improved fire and rescue services.
3212.activities: Dellwood VFD will continue to provide Fire Protection & Rescue Services.
3212.direct_services: Uninterrupted and Improved Fire Protection & Rescue Services.
3212.population: The entire population in the Dellwood community and many residents in unincorporated Jackson County will benefit. Dellwood VFD also provides vital services in an area with multiple evacuation routes and heavily utilized by out of state tourist traffic. Census data is not readily available for Dellwood - most sources refer back to county population. Population figures are estimated, but due to DVFD's mutual aid agreement with Jackson County, up to 47,319 people receive benefit from this project.
3212.outcome: This project will allow for the continued provision of adequate fire and rescue services in and around Dellwood - improvements may be measured in terms of response time and frequency of 'downed' equipment. Additionally, area ISO ratings are directly impacted by the availability of reliable fire protection.

2732.organization: City of St. Pete Beach - St Pete Beach Fire
2732.description: The City of St. Pete Beach - St. Pete Beach Fire Rescue (City) seeks to replace the fire station that was completely destroyed by Hurricanes Helene and Milton with a new facility designed to meet FEMA compliance standards. This station is critical for housing first responders serving the southern end of the City. Rebuilding will strengthen emergency response, enhance resilience, and ensure the fire department can protect the community against future storms
2732.purpose: Replace the fire station that was completely destroyed by Hurricanes Helene and Milton with a new facility designed to meet FEMA compliance standards. This station is critical for housing first responders serving the southern end of the city. Rebuilding will strengthen emergency response, enhance resilience, and ensure the fire department can protect the community against future storms
2732.activities: The new station will house fire apparatus, firefighter quarters, and administrative offices. It will provide public outreach, education, and continuing training for fire personnel. Emergency Management staff will use EOC space to restore services quickly after disasters. Elevated above the floodplain,the facility ensures immediate operation and resilience for the community.
2732.direct_services: This elevated, hardened facility will serve as an EMS/Fire response station and Emergency Operations Center during disasters. It enables first responders to return to the barrier island and provide critical services as soon as flooding recedes. Currently, only a temporary public safety facility exists to conduct lifesaving operations immediately after a storm or disaster.
2732.population: The residents and visitors of St. Pete Beach.
2732.outcome: The facility will improve the community's health by ensuring faster response times, particularly for fire suppression and Advanced Life Support (ALS) services. Built to withstand severe weather, The new station will provide uninterrupted operations during disasters, reducing delays in medical care and fire protection. Modern facilities also enhance safety for first responders, ensuring reliable service delivery. The benefit of the facility can be measured by tracking response times, comparing pre/postconstruction data to ensure faster emergency services. Metrics like incident outcomes, community satisfaction surveys, and operational continuity during severe weather events will demonstrate it

3217.description: The City requests funding for the design and construction of the roadway, water and sewer utilities required to extend Marquis Way East Connector Road and connect it to SR-20 East. Building this alternative route will create traffic flow and safety improvements that alleviate congestion through Freeport’s main arterial interchange (SR-20/US 331) and provide more efficient and convenient access to housing developments and commercially zoned corridors.
3217.purpose: The City requests funding for the design and construction of the roadway, water and sewer utilities required to extend Marquis Way East Connector Road and connect it to SR-20 East. Building this alternative route will create traffic flow and safety improvements that alleviate congestion through Freeport’s main arterial interchange (SR-20/US 331) and provide more efficient and convenient access to housing developments and commercially zoned corridors.
3217.activities: The project will include the construction of a roadway, potable water and sewer collection system elements that support long term population and capital investment advancements. Increased infrastructure will provide for new events, visitors and demands for local goods and services that will increase the median household income, homeownership and employment rate.
3217.direct_services: Consistent with the City’s comprehensive plan, and the broader infrastructure plans, the project will continue to link road networks to increase assessibility, safety and economic growth by reducing the mean travel time. Economic development will be encouraged through on going construction and maintenance job creation and new business developments.
3217.population: The general public is the target population and the number of individuals expected to be served is greater than 800.
3217.outcome: The project will support long term population and capital investment advancements through on going construction and maintenance job creation and new business developement. The observed impact will be an increase in median household income, home ownership and employment rates.

3300.description: Fort Freedom aims to reduce the Veteran suicide rate and heal the wounds of PTSD by providing transformative programs that empower Veterans to reclaim their lives.
3300.purpose: Fort Freedom aims to reduce the Veteran suicide rate and heal the wounds of PTSD by providing transformative programs that empower Veterans to reclaim their lives.
3300.activities: Funds will be directly used to support veterans entering our 12-week programs. They will also be used to support male/female veterans and their families or loved ones in our virtual telehealth curriculum.
3300.direct_services: Our 12-week life-restoring program is supported by holistic and wellness based services. Services included are: trauma therapy, equine therapy, physical training. Pathfinder/experiential therapy, movement/posture therapy, spiritual life coaching, horticulture therapy, and meal planning.
3300.population: Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Jobless persons, Physically disables, Veterans.
3300.outcome: Fort Freedom’s program reduces PTSD symptoms, lowers suicide risk, and improves Veterans’ emotional, physical, and social wellbeing. Outcomes are measured through weekly clinical self-assessments, pre- and post-program evaluations, case management notes, attendance tracking, and alumni follow-ups to verify sustained stability, improved functioning, and successful reintegration into civilian life.

3222.description: The Washington County Board of County Commissioners (County) is requesting consideration for appropriations for the SR-79 corridor and the Old Shores Destination Golf Course Fire Station. The County wants to maximize the positive economic growth, being proactive in-conjunction with the development of the Old Shores Destination Golf Course with these improvements. This will also include a standalone training facility for the fire department to continue in their training skills, knowledge, and improve safety for the community. A better ISO rating can result in lower insurance premiums for homeowners and businesses, reflecting the county’s commitment to fire prevention and protection. This investment in infrastructure underscores Washington County’s dedication to safeguarding lives and property while promoting community resilience.
3222.purpose: The Old Shores Fire Station will be located along SR -79 corridor to enhance public safety and improve ISO ratings along the underserved community. The County wants to maximize the positive economic growth and being proactive in-conjunction with the development of the Old Shores Destination Golf Course with these improvements. This will also include a standalone training facility for the fire department to continue in their training skills, knowledge, and improve safety for the community.
3222.activities: Construction of a new fire station along the SR-79 corridor will enhance public safety and emergency response capabilities for the community and surrounding areas of Washington County. The Old Shores Destination Golf Course will have a positive impact among the community, and this fire station will be located along an underserved community for future growth.
3222.direct_services: Safety, proper infrastructure, and preparedness are the top priorities in the development of the new fire station. This project is designed to ensure that firefighters have access to modern equipment, efficient facilities, and comprehensive training that will enhance their ability to respond to emergencies quickly and effectively. This would lead to improved Insurance Services Office (ISO) ratings
3222.population: The construction of a new fire station in Washington County would directly benefit its approximately 35,000 residents by enhancing emergency response capabilities across the entire community. With improved infrastructure, first responders would be better equipped to handle fires, medical emergencies, and natural disasters more efficiently, reducing response times and increasing overall public safety. The fire station would ensure that fire and emergency personnel have the necessary resources to
3222.outcome: A new fire station would aid the 79 corridor and new golf course in emergency response times. As this community continues to grow, the efforts of the county are stretched thin, this will help facilitate these issues and help the county be more prepared for tragedies in the area. A new fire station would decrease emergency response times and help improve ISO ratings. Additionally, this investment in infrastructure and training underscores Washington County’s dedication to safeguarding lives and property while promoting community resilience.

3224.description: The purchase of emergency generators will play a crucial role in maintaining essential government services for residents during power outages as the result of emergency weather events. This will increase the City’s “power resiliency” in the event of severe winds, flooding and loss of electrical power.
3224.purpose: The purchase of emergency generators will play a crucial role in maintaining essential government services for residents during power outages as the result of emergency weather events. This will increase the City’s “power resiliency” in the event of severe winds, flooding and loss of electrical power.
3224.activities: The purchase and installation of emergency generators.
3224.direct_services: These generators will allow the City to maintain operation and avoid an interruption in essential government services during severe weather events.
3224.population: The general public will be the population served by this project and the number of individuals is over 800.
3224.outcome: The City will be able to provide power to City buildings to ensure a continuation of government services during emergency events. The City will then achieve a greater degree of “power resiliency.”

3226.description: Requested funds will be used to purchase two four-wheel-drive trucks that will support emergency management and public safety efforts in Washington County, as the Washington County Sheriff’s Office has recently undertaken emergency management services within the County. Funding for these emergency management trucks will enhance response and coordination during disasters and emergencies, providing streamlined and efficient response from emergency officials.
3226.purpose: Requested funds will be used to purchase two four-wheel-drive trucks that will support emergency management in Washington County, as the Washington County Sheriff’s Office has recently undertaken emergency management services within the County. Funding for these emergency management trucks will enhance response and coordination during disasters and emergencies, providing streamlined and efficient response from emergency officials. Officials will also be able to use the trucks to assist with wate
3226.activities: These funds will increase the capabilities of the Washington County Sheriff’s Office and emergency management within the County. Response to emergency events, including natural disasters or public safety emergencies, will be enhanced by this project.
3226.direct_services: Citizens will benefit from improved response times during emergencies. The trucks will serve individuals in need during an emergency and will also assist in damage assessment, road closures and community engagement following an emergency.
3226.population: The general public and those experiencing emergencies will be served. Thousands of individuals will be served by this project.
3226.outcome: The emergency management trucks will improve physical health outcomes and help protect the general public from harm during emergency situations. Response times can be used to measure the outcome and the health outcomes of victims can be measured following an emergency. An increase in the number of calls for service can also be tracked.

2787.description: Hurricane/Disaster Evacuation Shelter/Disaster Recovery Facility: There are currently no evacuation centers appropriate for horses/Large animals in the tri-county area. Fox Lea Foundation to build 2 (two) Hurricane-Rated Barns that would provide evacuation centers plus disaster recovery headquarters for Horses and Large Animals in the Tri-County area (Sarasota, Charlotte, DeSoto). Exterior would be hurricane rated; interior would contain restroom, shower, and small kitchen facilities for caretakers and first responders. Fox Lea Foundation will coordinate with State, County, and Local officials to develop and execute disaster response plan for large animals. Fox Lea Foundation has worked closely with first responders and city/state/county officials to provide disaster response over the past several years and can share statistics/data from prior hurricanes/floods.
2787.purpose: The purpose of these funds would be to provide an evacuation center/disaster response facility for horses and other large animals, their caretakers and first responders. There are currently NO evacuation facilities for horses or other large animals in the tri-county area (Sarasota County, Charlotte County, and DeSoto County. The closest horse- and large-animal friendly facilities are in Ocala, and there are limited facilities in Manatee and Hillsborough Counties. When the buildings are not in us
2787.activities: Hurricane evacuation for horses, large animals, and their caretakers. Staging area for disaster preparation, response, and recovery. Central location to stage supplies, disaster relief, and veterinarian services before, during and after storms/natural disasters. Provide ongoing planning and education to people with horses and large animals on how to prepare and respond to a natural disaster.
2787.direct_services: By protecting horse/livestock and providing relief before/after storms, we will protect agricultural production. By educating the target audience, we will prevent damage to production and provide education on best practices in preparing horses and livestock for natural disasters. We will also offload some of the recovery coordination from the state/county/city responders by assisting with and coor
2787.population: Horse owners and large animal owners that need or want to evacuate animals and their caretakers in advance of and following natural disasters. It is estimated that the facility would serve 200-300+ people.
2787.outcome: Having local evacuation facilities for horses and large animals will relieve traffic from having to evacuate horses/animals to Ocala/Wellington prior to storms. It will encourage people that own large animals to evacuate with their animals vs. staying at home in harm's way. The facility can be used for relief efforts, for both horse owners and agricultural (cattle, pigs, etc.) Outside of use in natural disasters, having permanent stabling facilities at Fox Lea Farm during non-disaster times will increase attendance at our horse shows, resulting in increased economic impact to the state and Sarasota County.

3227.description: Funding will be used to purchase upgraded equipment for an existing public safety communications tower. These equipment upgrades will harden communication between law enforcement/first responders and significantly enhance public safety radio coverage across the County and surrounding areas for every law enforcement officer and first responder. Completion of the upgrades to the existing tower will lead to enhanced public safety services.
3227.purpose: The Washington County Sheriff’s Office serves as the only entity in the County to receive and dispatch all 911 calls for every first responder, including fire, EMS, and law enforcement in the County and its municipalities. With population and traffic continuing to grow along key routes, including SR 77, SR 79, SR 20, and Interstate 10, funding to complete these upgrades is critical in supporting first responders in a fiscally-constrained County.
3227.activities: Upgrades to the tower will ensure first responders throughout Washington County are able to securely respond and communicate immediately in the event of an accident, natural disaster or emergency. First responders radio channels will be secure, leading to uninterrupted service, quick response times, and increased public safety.
3227.direct_services: Law enforcement services, emergency medical services (EMS), fire services and emergency communications will be provided to citizens in an enhanced manner. Emergency management and disaster services will also be strengthened by this funding, further increasing public safety.
3227.population: The general public, citizens, and visitors. Thousands of individuals will be served.
3227.outcome: This project will lead to improved physical and mental health outcomes for individuals in need and protect the general public from harm. Hardening the communications tower infrastructure will allow law enforcement and first responders to serve more individuals, keep communication secure, and streamline operations. Law enforcement and first responder response times can be measured, while the coverage and security of the tower upgrades can also be monitored.

3229.description: The construction of a new roadway linking 37th Avenue to create direct access to the new 58-acre Park and Administration Building. In addition to enhancing economic development and access to jobs/public services, the roadway will help improve transit access, reduce congestion, and add an important entry to a public park. The road will create a T intersection at the main roadway for the Park and a 4-way intersection at the corner of 17th Street and 37th Ave.
3229.purpose: The requested funds will facilitate the construction of a new roadway linking 37th Avenue to create direct access to the new 58-acre Park and Administration Building. In addition to enhancing economic development and access to jobs/public services, the roadway will help improve transit access, reduce congestion, and add an important entry to a public park. The road will create a T intersection at the main roadway for the Park and a 4-way intersection at the corner of 17th Street and 37th Ave.
3229.activities: The requested funds will facilitate a connection to the newly constructed park and the administration building, optimizing accessibility and mitigating congestion around the site. The project will also upgrade critical infrastructure, including sidewalks, while boosting mobility, and regional connectivity to support economic growth.
3229.direct_services: The funding will improve accessibility, safety, and mobility by constructing a roadway/sidewalk connecting vehicles/pedestrians to park and the Administration Building. This project will increase pedestrian access, reduce congestion, and foster economic growth by enhancing access to government buildings and recreational spaces, while creating a safer streets for neighbors to utilize.
3229.population: Elderly persons, Persons with poor mental health, Persons with poor physical health, Economically disadvantaged persons, At-risk youth, physically disabled, grade school students, high school students, university/college students, general population. >800 individuals.
3229.outcome: Improvement of physical and mental health, enrichment of cultural experience, preservation of the environment, protection of the general public from harm, improvement of transportation conditions, improvement of economic activity, and increase in tourism. The methodology of measuring these outcomes included data collection/analysis and usage of the infrastructure.

3035.description: To establish a new City-operated senior nutrition program providing both Meals for the Elderly (MFE) congregate dining and Meals on Wheels (MOW) home-delivered meals for elderly Homestead residents, addressing unmet needs caused by Miami-Dade County waitlists, limited South Dade coverage, and high demand for nutrition support among elderly residents.
3035.purpose: To establish a new City-operated senior nutrition program providing both Meals for the Elderly (MFE) congregate dining and Meals on Wheels (MOW) home-delivered meals for elderly Homestead residents, addressing unmet needs caused by Miami-Dade County waitlists, limited South Dade coverage, and high demand for nutrition support among elderly residents.
3035.activities: Congregate senior meals (MFE); Home-delivered meals (MOW); Wellness programming and social engagement.
3035.direct_services: The program will deliver prepared meals to homebound seniors and provide hot congregate meals to the elderly at a City facility, improving nutrition, reducing food insecurity, and supporting independence for elderly residents.
3035.population: Elderly persons throughout the City of Homestead. The amount of individuals expected to be served is > 800.
3035.outcome: Physical health improvement will be measured by the number of meals provided, changes in seniors' nutritional-risk scores, and indicators such as weight stability and self-reported health status. These outcomes will be assessed through intake screenings, reassessments, and documented meal delivery logs. This will also be measured as part of Quality of Life in our Strategic Plan

Those who target Jews are more likely to hold anti-democratic views that threaten safety broadly. This initiative intercepts hate, strengthens trust across differences, and makes FL the nation’s safest choice for Jewish students and their allies.

2792.direct_services: Educational and cultural programming, including workshops to counter misinformation and and antisemitic rhetoric, cultural programming to highlight Jewish heritage, values, and traditions, fostering understanding across diverse student and community populations. Outcomes will be measured via tracking of antisemitic threats or attack; pre- and post- scientific surveys of students perceptions of safety including a comparison of these data to other campuses without this intervention.

2910.description: Miami Fashion Week is an annual, multi-day fashion, technology, and education-driven event that serves as a strategic economic development and tourism initiative for the State of Florida. The program acts as a catalyst for a rapidly growing global fashion industry at a critical moment of expansion, positioning Miami and Florida to compete as leading international hubs. The project integrates runway shows, technology-enabled experiences, and educational programming in partnership with Florida-based institutions, while engaging local vendors, workforce, and creative professionals. Miami Fashion Week generates billions of global media impressions, significantly increasing Florida’s international visibility and driving tourism, hospitality activity, and local spending. By supporting an industry that generates millions of dollars in economic impact, creates jobs, and attracts global attention
2910.purpose: The funds requested will support the planning and execution of Miami Fashion Week as a statewide economic development and cultural tourism initiative. The primary goal is to strengthen Florida’s position—particularly Miami—as a global hub for fashion, creativity, and innovation while generating measurable economic impact for the state. The funding will be used for core event production, engagement of Florida-based vendors and workforce, marketing and international promotion, and educational prog
2910.activities: The funds will support key activities required to produce Miami Fashion Week as a multi-day economic development and cultural tourism initiative. These include event production and venue operations, runway shows and industry programming, and the engagement of Florida-based vendors, workforce, and creative professionals. Funding will also support marketing and international outreach to attract visitors, media, and industry stakeholders to Florida, as well as educational and workforce development
2910.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide direct services to Florida residents through public-facing cultural programming, educational opportunities, and workforce participation. Citizens will have access to exhibitions, panels, and community- oriented events that celebrate creativity, culture, and innovation within the state. The project will also deliver direct educational and professional developm

The project also serves the general public through accessible cultural programming and community-facing events. Indirectly, the project will reach hundreds of thousands of individuals through media exposure, digital platforms, and tourism-related activity, generating broader economic and cultur
2910.outcome: The expected outcomes of this project include increased tourism, economic activity, job creation, and enhanced national and international visibility for the State of Florida. The project will generate measurable benefits through visitor spending, hotel room nights, engagement of Florida-based vendors and workforce, and expanded educational and professional opportunities for residents. Outcomes will be measured using attendance data, hotel occupancy and room-night reports, visitor origin data, number of local vendors and workers engaged, student participation metrics, and media and digital reach analytics. Post-event reporting and economic impact analysis will be used to evaluate overall proj

3461.description: Sacred Heart Hospital is the largest provider of women's health care in the NW region. Over 70% of all babies in the region are born at Sacred Heart Pensacola and as the 10th largest Medicaid provider in the State, a large proportion of patients are Medicaid recipients. The hospital delivers over 4,400 babies each year and operates the region's only level III NICU - caring for the tiniest and most vulnerable babies. One of only twelve Regional Perinatal Intensive Care Centers (RPICC), Sacred Heart seeks to modernize and expand it's women's perinatal specialty unit which serves high risk moms.
3461.purpose: Funds will be used to modernize and expand the perinatal specialty unit within Sacred Heart's Women's Hospital which will serve mostly Medicaid high risk moms and babies.
3461.activities: comprehensive maternal care will be given to the patient(s) to ensure a health outcome for mom and baby
3461.direct_services: health care services will be provided to high risk moms and babies
3461.population: Medicaid and high risk moms and babies
3461.outcome: We will be measuring maternal health outcomes and expect those to improve with this specialty unit. Measurements include c-section rates, birth weight, length of stay, etc.

3467.description: Construct a new ~0.75-mile two-lane connector between Med-Crest Drive and Duggan Avenue, completing a local route that allows travel from Highway 90 to the I-10 interchange (Exit 56) without entering SR 85. The project improves safety, mobility, and emergency access for an economically disadvantaged area, provides alternate access to medical and commercial facilities, and reduces dependency on SR 85 for local traffic.
3467.purpose: To provide an alternate north–south route north of I-10 that improves safety, mobility, and emergency access for residents, while reducing congestion on SR 85 and improving connectivity to medical, commercial, and residential areas.
3467.activities: Construction of the roadway with curbs, drainage, and sidewalks to provide safe, efficient travel for vehicles and pedestrians, and to enhance emergency response and evacuation capacity.
3467.direct_services: The project provides citizens with a safer and more efficient local travel route, reducing travel time, improving emergency access, and supporting local economic activity through improved connectivity.
3467.population: Economically Disadvantaged Persons, General Public, Physically Disabled (accessibility benefit). Estimated Population Served: 10,000 + residents north of I-10
3467.outcome: The project will improve transportation conditions by constructing approximately 0.75 miles of new roadway linking Highway 90 to I-10 (Exit 56). Safety and mobility will be enhanced by reducing local dependency on SR 85 (˜ 50,000 AADT) and improving emergency and evacuation routes. Economic activity will increase through improved access to medical and commercial areas. Benefits will be measured through post-construction travel-time and traffic-volume studies, emergency-response data, and tracking of new development and business activity along the corridor.

3267.description: This request is for an expansion of the septic-to-sewer infrastructure in Floral City and represents a critical environmental and public infrastructure priority for Citrus County. This request is to reduce nutrient loading into the Homosassa Springshed by redirecting wastewater flows from multiple aging wastewater treatment plants to the City of Inverness Wastewater Treatment Plant. This will directly support nutrient reduction goals outlined in the Homosassa/Chassahowitzka Basin Management Action Plan and will support the decommissioning of multiple small package plants and the expansion of centralized sewer service in the Floral City area.
3267.purpose: The funds will enable construction of a pump station and forcemain to connect the Floral City Elementary Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) to the City of Inverness wastewater system. This connection will support the decommissioning of small package plants, expand centralized sewer service in the Floral City area, and advance Basin Management Action Plan (BMAP) nutrient-reduction goals.
3267.activities: If funded, Citrus County will begin construction of a master sewer pump station at the Floral City Elementary Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) site as well as construction of approximately 18,700 linear feet of 8" wastewater forcemain. This will include engineering design, permitting, and construction engineering inspection.
3267.direct_services: The completion of this project will result in a significant reduction in the nutrient loading into the Homosassa Springshed by redirecting wastewater flows from multiple aging wastewater treatment plants to the City of Inverness Wastewater Treatment Plant. Additionally, the project will enable many new residential sewer connections and the connection of multiple existing and aging package plants i
3267.population: The target population directly served by this project would be the current residents in the Floral City area that will be able to connect to the new centralized sewer once this project is completed. This would include some commercial property, multiple mobile home parks, and numerous residential properties in the Floral City area. Moreover, as a result of the decrease in nutrient loading to the area, the entire Homosassa Springshed would experience a net benefit.
3267.outcome: Some of the expected benefits of this project would be enhancements and improvements to environmental and wildlife quality, improvements to groundwater quality, improvements to drinking water quality, and improvements to surface water quality. The methodology to measure these outcomes will be volume of flow from WWTP x (current effluent TN from plant - effluent TN from receiving WWTP) x conversion = lbs-TN/yr. Current TN from both plants is the average TN from each of the plants as listed on the monthly DMRs).

3313.description: This regional park located on three hundred acres of State-owned land, leased by the City of Inverness from the Florida Forest Service for the benefit of the City of Inverness, Citrus County, and regional and State of Florida Residents, will benefit from the addition of an RV Campground to serve as an economic driver and to help the long term financial sustainability of the park and park lease.
3313.purpose: The RV Campground project will provide short term lodging opportunities for sports league families, Withlacoochee State Trail Visitors, and tourists that visit the City of Inverness and Citrus County.
3313.activities: The RV sites will will offer temporary lodging opportunities in the 300 acre State-owned park, where trails, aquatics, sports fields, courts, and recreation areas exist.
3313.direct_services: Overnight camping, with water and electric hook up, access to restrooms and showers and the many existing amenities in the park.
3313.population: Tourists, sports leagues, families, local, regional, and State visitors will be served by the RV Campground. Thousands of visitors and locals utilize the park, Downtown Inverness, and the Withlacoochee State Trail each year.
3313.outcome: The RV Campground will benefit the campers but will also provide an important and needed revenue stream to assist with the parks maintenance. Visitation will be tracked using a reservation system and data compiled from the Citrus County Tourism Council.

3462.description: To secure Gulf Breeze Hospital, a critically important acute care facility serving the people of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties and the only hospital on the peninsula, from the effects of storm, hurricane, or other natural disaster through partial funding of a storm hardening capital improvement project.
3462.purpose: To secure Gulf Breeze Hospital, a critically important acute care facility serving the people of Santa Rosa, Escambia and Okaloosa counties and the only hospital on the peninsula, from the effects of storm, hurricane or other natural disaster damage through partial funding of a storm hardening capital improvement project.
3462.activities: Infrastructure upgrades and flood mitigation measures.
3462.direct_services: Gulf Breeze hospital provides emergency and acute care services, as well as intensive care services and other specialty units. The Andrews Institute for Orthopedic and Sports Medicine is also located at this facility.
3462.outcome: The facility will be able to provide emergency and acute care services to the residents and tourists in the counties it serves. Assurances that the hospital will be able to remain open after a storm, hurricane or other natural disaster occurs.

By providing free legal services and representation we assist individuals and families regain personal and economic stability and safety, join the work force and become contributing members of our State. The legal services that we provide our clients with help them obtain employment, health insurance, driving privileges, an education, housing, and help them to achieve a better future.

We attend Veterans' treatment court and GRACE Court weekly (Grace Court is for victims of Human Trafficking) to offer legal representation to veterans and victims of human trafficking in need.

All legal services provided including Court Representation will be documented in our legal Server Case Management system. The goals of the project are to serve as a home base for the Waterways Division, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation (FWC) and Hernando County Sheriff's Office’s Marine Unit while allowing inter-agency cooperation and coordination for all issues/concerns on Hernando County waterways. The proximity of the project location allows for quick access to Gulf waters and associated rivers and tributaries. The current facility required extensive damage assessment post natural disaster before staff could begin to address damage assessment of public wa
3314.purpose: The goals of the project are to serve as a home base for the Waterways Division, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation and the Hernando County Sheriff’s Office while allowing inter-agency cooperation and coordination for all issues/concerns on Hernando County waterways. The proximity of the project location allows for quick access to Gulf waters and associated rivers and tributaries. 3314.activities: Construction of a facility with direct connection to a main access channel that can be utilized by several agencies would provide several benefits to State waters such as increased response time to water emergencies, accessibility of boating equipment to assist with in-water rescues, safety zone for inclement weather, increased coordination of agencies, and swift repair of aids to navigation.

3780.description: Almarante Fire District (AFD) seeks replacement of Fire Engine Pumper. We currently have two pumpers. One is a 1997 and the other is a 2001. Both have been in for multiple repairs the past few years. The pumps on both engines failed test this past year. We were able to rebuild the 1997 and the 2001 pump had to be down-graded. It is imperative to plan for a replacement due to rising maintenance cost, decreased reliability, and potential safety or compliance issues associated with older engines. We currently service 83 miles (53,120 acres) in our District, in addition to responding to the Dorcas area 40N. We are first alarm to five districts and second alarm to two. This pumper would be used to provide services to help respond to the safety and security issues in the North.
3780.purpose: Due to the cost of repairs and decreased reliability of both our pumpers. Our goal is to have a replacement apparatus before having one or both fail. It is imperative we make plans to be able to protect and serve our district and those that pass through,
3780.activities: Almarante Fire District will be able to respond to fire calls with a more reliable and dependable engine. Throughout this past year we have had one of the two engines in for repairs for over 90 days. While one engine is in for repairs, hoping the other holds out. Almarante trains weekly and we have been fiscally responsible with our funding. We did self-audit our tax rolls to ensure we were receiving correct assessments.
3780.direct_services: Almarante will be able to respond to emergencies with a modern engine. That is more reliable and dependable to better serve our community.
3780.population: There is approximately 2,225 people in the Almarante Fire District. With a Pre k-12 school less than three miles from the station. We also serve parts of the Dorcas Fire District section 40N. In addition to mutual aid for surrounding departments.
3780.outcome: Maintenance cost, especially major repairs, have increased significantly with the age of our trucks. By replacing the engine pumper, We, can lower the expense and keep a more predictable maintenance budget. The new engine will be more dependable and our chance to provide safety, security and save property will be enhanced.

3603.description: Blackman Fire District Corporation seeks funding to expand on-site apparatus capacity to improve our ability to provide immediate, coordinated life-saving response, aligning with the emphasis on preparedness and rapid incident stabilization and prioritizes reducing loss of life and property by improving resilience and operational capacity for hazard response as stated in the State Hazard Mitigation Plan. 3270.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3270.description: Jericho Road Ministries seeks funding to renovate a 4,500 sq. ft. facility at 1167 Howell Ave, Brooksville, FL to improve our free weekly food distribution to local neighbors in need. Improvements include new flooring, wiring, storage, drywall, and commercial freezers. This project will create a safe, efficient, and dignifying space to serve families facing food insecurity. The Food Barn will also benefit our food management for our recovery centers which houses and feed over 70,000 meals a year.
3270.purpose: The funds will be used to renovate a 4,500 sq. ft. facility at 1167 Howell Ave, Brooksville, FL to expand and improve Jericho Road Ministries’ food distribution services. Renovations include new flooring, wiring, storage, drywall, and commercial freezers, creating a safer and more efficient space for serving food-insecure families and individuals.

3270.direct_services: Citizens will receive free weekly groceries and 3 meals for residents daily. The renovated building will allow a safer, more efficient, and more dignified distribution environment, improving access to reliable nutrition for local families.
