3271.description: The Hernando County Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) proposes a transformative infrastructure project at the Brooksville–Tampa Bay Regional Airport (BKV) to rehabilitate an abandoned runway into an active taxiway and extend water and sewer utilities across the airport's infield. This initiative will unlock more than 423 acres of aviation and industrial sites, significantly enhancing the airport's operational capacity and attractiveness to aerospace, aviation, manufacturing and logistics industries. The project directly aligns with Florida's economic, workforce, and aerospace priorities and supports key provisions of Senate Bill 1662, recently signed by the Governor to modernize and grow Florida's aviation and logistics sectors and expand aerospace-related real estate and protect space-designated territories.
3271.purpose: The taxiway resurfacing will significantly enhance airside infrastructure while unlocking more than 195 acres of service-ready aviation sites with the addition of essential water and sewer utilities. This project also unlocks a 228-acre site on the southwest side of the proposed taxiway, which is a designated Duke Energy Readiness site. This project will accommodate larger facilities for aircraft services, repair and storage, as well as support related manufacturing and logistics enterprises. Th
3271.activities: BKV and the Hernando County Office of Economic Development will market the facility to prospective aerospace, aviation, and manufacturing companies both domestically and internationally. The Office of Economic Development partners with Florida Commerce and Select Florida to expand marketing activities.
3271.direct_services: The resurfacing project will greatly increase the capacity to locate aerospace, aviation, manufacturing and logistics companies and create long-term career opportunities and promote sustainable economic growth in Hernando County and the broader Tampa Bay region. The project also directly aligns with statewide technical training and apprenticeship goals matching students and underemployed workers w
3271.population: Hernando County has a labor force of 92,000 people who can benefit from increased job and career opportunities. Students, adults and underemployed workers can benefit from new training programs and apprenticeships which will match workers to the job demands of new businesses. Local and regional aviation businesses will have an improved taxiway designed to today's construction and safety standards.
3271.outcome: The project will benefit the local and regional economy and generate direct benefits for local businesses, Hernando County and the regional workforce. The project is expected to attract private investment and create skilled career opportunities in aviation related sectors. The Tampa Bay Regional Planning Council completed an economic impact report which shows a total economic impact of $154,600,000, $83,200,000 in labor income, $25,400,000 in new annual revenue, and $97,200,000 in GDP contribution.

2737.description: This project will work to restore Lake Jackson's aquatic ecosystem by mechanically removing invasive aquatic vegetation including tussocks and nutrient-rich lake-bottom muck. Cypress IWLA will work with Ducks Unlimited to maximize benefits for waterfowl and wildlife as well as recreational access. This project will also improve navigation on the Lake. Rather than disposing of it as waste, the collected material will be processed into a natural soil amendment.
2737.purpose: To restore Lake Jackson's aquatic ecosystem by removing nutrient-rich lake-bottom muck and mechanically removing invasive aquatic vegetation including tussocks. These efforts will improve habitat for wildlife and waterfowl as well as navigation and recreational access on the Lake.
2737.activities: Removal of nutrient-rich muck and invasive vegetation. The collected material will be processed into a natural soil amendment and applied on nearby agricultural lands.
2737.direct_services: The project will enhance recreational access and use of Lake Jackson, one of North Florida's most important recreational fishing and hunting locations.
2737.population: The funds will benefit the general population in North Florida and Tallahassee that recreate on Lake Jackson.
2737.outcome: This project is expected to improve water quality and habitat structure, resulting in enhanced conditions for waterfowl and other aquatic wildlife. Project success and habitat improvement will be documented through fixed-point before-and- after photographic documentation, water clarity measurements, vegetation coverage observations, and wildlife utilization records to visually and quantitatively demonstrate these improvements.

Based on sound research confirming its effectiveness, this project shifts learning from memorization to an active scientific practice, to help build problem-solving, and collaboration skills.

Based on sound research confirming its effectiveness, this project will minimize teacher training time and will ultimately equip students for careers in the tech economy by fostering critical skills like problem-solving and teamwork.
3272.activities: Provide high quality Science learning materials and experiences for students that align with Next Generation Science standards and the necessary professional development and training so that students are prepared for careers in the tech and STEM economy.
3272.direct_services: Direct provision of standards-based Science kits designed to equip students with skills for the modern Science and STEM-driven economy.

With affordable, ready to-use materials, and minimal teacher training requirements this project will enable students to explore scientific and engineering practices while fostering critical skills like problem-solving and teamwork. 3235.description: This program, with research conducted by the Tallahassee Orthopedic Clinic Foundation, Inc ("TOCF"), aims to position Florida as a leader in developing regenerative stem cell therapies for orthopedic care, wound healing, and pain management. It advances innovative rehabilitation techniques that accelerate recovery and improve outcomes. The initiative also emphasizes public education to help Floridians prevent and manage orthopedic injuries. By expanding access to cutting-edge regenerative treatments, it ensures that citizens benefit from the latest medical breakthroughs.
3235.purpose: The goal of the project is to lead the state and nation in research and development of regenerative stem cell therapies in orthopedic, wound care, and pain management and educate the citizens of Florida on the prevention and treatment of orthopedic injuries. The goal is to develop innovative rehabilitation techniques that expedite the healing process and provide increased access to treatment options for all Florida citizens to cutting edge medical treatments.
3235.activities: The TOCF will complete clinical research investigations to address unmet clinical needs of the Florida people to investigate the efficacy and safety of stem cell therapies, to investigate alternative treatment methods, and to educate the people of Florida on additional options for treatment.
3235.direct_services: Successful research and development will result in cutting edge therapies as well as improve the quality of life for orthopedic and pain management patients and help with educating the public on the benefits of stem cell therapies.
3235.population: Individuals who suffer from musculoskeletal injuries, have poor mental or physical health, or are physically disabled, and who are between the ages of 16–80, will be included in this project. We expect to serve approximately 200–400 individuals.
3235.outcome: Improved mobility, decreased pain, better treatment for wound management including diabetic wounds, bed sores, and poor circulation ulcers; Enhanced repair for damaged cartilage, tendons, ligaments, and bones; Lowered risk of complications compared to surgery; Enhanced management of chronic pain without reliance on addictive painkillers. Documented treatment outcomes will be shared with the medical industry and the public.

The project will add two flexible spaces, an additional classroom, expanded partner areas for early identification, adaptive play spaces, and a therapeutic open gym with private rooms for occupational, speech, physical, and behavioral therapies. Designed for children with complex developmental, medical, and behavioral needs, this expansion will double enrollment, improve early intervention access, and strengthen partnerships with UF Health CARD, FDLRS, and Early Steps while reducing strain on other public resources and improving lifelong outcomes.
3237.purpose: The Therapeutic Learning Center (TLC) at The Arc of the St. Johns seeks funding to expand and improve its campus, adding classrooms, adaptive play areas, therapy and partner spaces, and a therapeutic open gym. The project will double enrollment and expand after-school and summer programs, supporting children with developmental, medical, behavioral, sensory impairment, and mobility needs to meet growing demands and improve access to early identification and supports.

It will increase access to early identification, diagnostics, resources, services, and family training while removing barriers and ensuring seamless, wraparound continuity of care from identification through transition to primary school—empowering children and families to rea
3237.direct_services: The initiative will provide citizens—particularly young children and families impacted by complex developmental and medical needs—with expanded access to specialized early education, therapeutic, and family support services. Through a coordinated, transdisciplinary model, families will receive comprehensive assistance including early identification and diagnostic evaluations, individualized interv
3237.population: The target population is any individual, caregiver, or family impacted by developmental differences, medical complexity, behavioral concerns, and other related developmental disabilities in St. Johns County and surrounding areas.
3237.outcome: The project will result in measurable improvements in early childhood outcomes and family stability for citizens served. Specifically, it will: Increase the number of children with complex developmental needs who receive timely diagnosis, intervention, and educational placement. Strengthen families’ ability to support their child’s development through training, coaching, and access to coordinated community resources. 3655.description: A pumper/tanker brings water to fires in rural communities that can't be guaranteed service by fire hydrants or other means. The three fire engines used by Holt Fire District--a 2005, a 2003 and a 1996--have all been driven on interstates, state and county roads, unpaved roads, and potholed and washed-out roads and private drives. Of HFD's three engines, only one (2003) was purchased new, through a grant; the other two were donated from other departments. A new pumper/tanker will bring an increased water capacity of 1,000 gallons to fires near farmhouses, barns, fields and forests, far from any existing hydrant system.
3655.purpose: A 66% increase of water capacity by a new pumper/tanker will provide additional firefighting capabilities to serve the Holt community as well as those served by our mutual aid partners Crestview Fire Department and Baker, Blackman, North Okaloosa and Harold Fire Districts.
3655.activities: Holt specifically--and north Okaloosa in general--is very rural. Outside of "city" structures, people rely on well water. When a fire breaks out in those rural areas without a hydrant system, firefighters need to carry water to the scene. A new pumper/tanker will allow firefighters to more effectively fight fires in areas lacking fire hydrant services.
3655.direct_services: A pumper/tanker is the number one resource needed to successfully fight structure fires. A new pumper/tanker will provide increased safety to families, businesses and properties in Holt as well as to parts of north Okaloosa and east Santa Rosa counties.
3655.population: Holt Fire District primarily serves the 57-square-mile community of Holt consisting of more than 3,000 people. HFD also responds to mutual aid/auto aid calls in the neighboring communities of Baker, Blackman and Crestview in Okaloosa County and Harold in Santa Rosa County. Additionally, HFD is responsible for 9 miles of Interstate 10, U.S. Hwy 90 and the CSX railroad, all of which run through the Holt community.
3655.outcome: In addition to the all-important response time to an emergency, equipment and resource availability are key to responsive fire capability. These measures assess a fire department’s ability to respond to emergencies efficiently, mitigate loses and help safeguard the community. A new pumper/tanker will become HFD's primary response engine, which will increase water availability as well as reliability--two measures of HFD's efficiency.

Our target neighborhood is a low income, at risk neighborhood in Orlando called Parramore. We develop at risk grade school youth through our daily, year round program in all areas of life--including academic, social, and emotional.

Our target neighborhood is a low income, at risk neighborhood in Orlando called Parramore. We develop at risk grade school youth through our daily, year round program in all areas of life--including academic, social, and emotional.

Students receive a daily character lesson, art enrichment, life & wellness enrichment, and access to a licensed mental health counselor

They receive an hour of tutoring each day, emphasizing their reading and math fundamentals. Staff mentor each of our students twice a week at their school. Students receive breakfast and lunch (summer), and healthy snacks.
3239.population: Economically disadvantaged youth and families, at risk youth, grade school age. 75-125
3239.outcome: Improve mental health benefit: Program participants are taught how to understand and manage emotions, how to respond to conflict in healthy ways. Measured by a decrease in behavioral issues at home/school. Improve quality of education benefit: Program participants receive one hour of academic tutoring per day. Measured by seeing 100% of enrolled students being at or above their reading and math grade level. Improve economic activity benefit: After school programming allows parents to work full time jobs while their students are cared for. By focusing on education, program participants will be prepared for college and career, improving the economic viability of the community.

3277.description: Responders First provides behavioral health care services to First Responders/Military and their spouse/significant other during a five day Wellness Program who are facing life challenges that stem from emotional difficulties associated with their stressful work experiences. This includes challenges and difficulties with daily life functioning including but not limited to symptoms of Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, anxiety, chronic pain, and substance use. Each five day program (for a total of four programs) will provide these services for four to six participants.
3277.purpose: Funds will be spent on a five day Wellness Program and other related costs to provide free alternative behavioral health therapies for First Responders/Military and Spouse/Signifigant Other affected by career related PTSD. The Responders First Wellness Program is based on a model initiated by the US Special Operations Command (SOCOM).
3277.activities: Four 5-day Responders First Wellness Programs, and passenger van for transportation.
3277.direct_services: Each 5-day program will provide for, four to six participants, alternative behavioral health therapies to aid their coping with PTSD.
3277.population: First Responders/Military Spouse/Significant Other with poor mental health and coping skills due to PTSD. Sixteen to twenty four individuals will be served over the four Responders First Wellness Programs.
3277.outcome: The Responders First Wellness Program uses evidence-based modalities which have been thoroughly researched with Combat Veterans that were deployed in Vietnam, Operation Enduring Freedom (OEF), and Operation Iraqi Freedom (OIF). Responders First provides these modalities in a proven five day retreat-based wellness program. Pre and Post assessments will be conducted, and data will be collected by Evaluation Data Solutions, LLC. These alternative behavioral health therapies have been shown to reduce PTSD symptoms with

3455.description: The National Flight Academy will continue to innovate and inspire students to seek further education and careers in STEM fields by using funding from the State of Florida to maintain and expand the educational programs and opportunities through the unique Naval Aviation themed immersive experience on board the simulated training carrier AMBITION. Funding will be used to update and enhance existing programs and technology, maintain critical IT infrastructure and equipment and fund salaries for personnel vital to program delivery.
3455.purpose: The goal of the National Flight Academy's program is to inspire and engage students in STEM fields through the delivery of immersive and innovative educational programs that highlight the value of various technical career pathways. The funds will be used to enhance and update existing programming and ensure the viability of technology that supports program delivery.
3455.activities: The project will involve the delivery of existing program offerings aboard NFA's simulated aircraft carrier AMBITION. The existing programming will be updated and refreshed to maintain its position as a unique world class immersive experience ensuring Florida students are exposed to a wide range of career and technical fields. The immersive experience is meant to inspire and challenge students to explore further education and careers in STEM fields.
3455.direct_services: Educational program services will be provided to Florida students and teachers.
3455.population: The target population is middle school and high school students (ages 10-17). with an added focus on at risk youth. NFA anticipates serving in excess of 1800 students in FY26-27.
3455.outcome: The National Flight Academy performs educational assessments on all students participating in the 6-day Deployment program. NFA utilizes these assessments to determine students baseline STEM knowledge at the beginning and end of the program week to measure retention of knowledge and effectiveness of instructional content. Pre and post test data are compiled and analyzed to check for improved outcomes each week. Data is also collected through alumni surveys to track the impact NFA had on graduates educational and career aspirations and outcomes.

Students will use specialized equipment, engage in competitive simulations, and participate in events that mirror real- world challenges, reinforcing STEM concepts and preparing them for high-demand career pathways.
3243.direct_services: Direct services provided through this funding will include access to specialized technology, structured team-based strategic activities, coaching in systems thinking and decision-making, and participation in competitive events that reinforce STEM concepts. These services will support student growth in critical thinking, collaboration, and real-time problem solving.
3243.population: STEM Students in Okaloosa County School District; In excess of 500
3243.outcome: Improved education quality will be measured by increased student performance on assessments and scenario-driven tasks. Growth in participation and achievement in STEM-related strategic scenarios will also reflect deeper engagement and skill development in critical thinking and decision-making. Impact will be measured through comparative assessments, strategy, and decision-making. Additional indicators include increased student participation in structured strategic activities and documented growth in teamwork, communication, and problem-solving during simulated scenarios.

3460.description: This project seeks to empower UWF students to fully leverage their earned digital credentials when applying to jobs and submitting transcripts and other educational records. The goal is to make this process more secure, efficient and streamlined for students & schools to electronically issue, manage and verify vital educational credentials. Project funding will be used to implement the solution at UWF, provide training to UWF staff (IT, Registrar, etc.) and inform and onboard UWF students.
3460.purpose: This project seeks to empower UWF students to fully leverage their earned digital credentials when applying to jobs and submitting transcripts and other educational records. The goal is to make this process more secure, efficient and streamlined for students & schools to electronically issue, manage and verify vital educational credentials. Project funding will be used to implement the solution at UWF, provide training to UWF staff (IT, Registrar, etc.) and inform and onboard UWF students.
3460.activities: Provide access and efficient onboarding processes for UWF students to have access to a secure digital credential wallet to hold and use official copies of their transcripts and other vital documents. Instructions for downloading and the setup of the free digital wallet app, from the 2 App Stores. Onboarding to the free service. Educating students/families of the service and digital wallet.
3460.direct_services: To provide educational materials (print and video) that explain the benefits to having secure and verifiable credentials all in one place: their mobile device. Provide onboarding events, both in-person and virtual, that are efficient in receiving their digital wallet and instructional as to the features and functions of the digital student wallet and credentialling service.

3460.outcome: Improve quality of education: Educational pathways offered to students via the ai-powered credential analysis service. 3464.description: This project will expand the hands-on job training, life skills education, and community-based vocational programs that prepare participants for meaningful employment and greater independence. The project will allow Vision of Hope to increase enrollment capacity, reducing the waitlist, and offering families in the community hope for the future of their child's life.
3464.purpose: This project will expand the hands-on job training, life skills education, and community-based vocational programs that prepare participants for meaningful employment and greater independence. The project will allow Vision of Hope to increase enrollment capacity, reducing the waitlist, and offering families in the community hope for the future of their child's life.
3464.activities: Activities and services that will be provided are first, the renovations of an already established training center for classrooms, then on to vocational education programs focused on workplace readiness, self-advocacy, and job exploration. There will be hands-on training in custodial, landscaping, retail, food service, and clerical job skills as well as life skills and independence training.
3464.direct_services: The project will provide direct vocational training, job readiness instruction, and life skills development for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Services will include hands-on training in work-related tasks, community-based employment experiences, job coaching, and personal skill-building designed to promote independence and self-sufficiency.
3464.population: Elderly persons, poor mental health, poor physical health, jobless individuals, economically disadvantaged persons, developmentally disabled, physically disabled. Between 100 and 200 individuals served.
3464.outcome: Improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural experience, improve quality of education, increase economic activity, create job opportunities, and enhance economic self-sufficiency. Measured through: Behavioral observation checklists completed by staff to track increases in positive behaviors (engagement, communication, participation) and decreases in negative behaviors (withdrawal, frustration, behavioral incidents. Tracking participation in community outings. Vocational skill assessments, etc.

2826.description: K9s United is a non profit organization based in Jacksonville, FL and is committed to supporting and honoring K9s who detect, protect and serve communities across the state by giving them the necessary equipment and quality of life during and after their service. Founder, Debbie Johnson, had the idea after hearing of the tragic death of Baron, a local K9. She felt moved to attend his funeral and consequently help. She enrolled in the Civilian Law Enforcement Academy, it was during a ride along, & subsequent meetings at the Sheriff’s Office, that she learned of budgetary needs not being met by allocated funding. When a request is made we go directly to the vendor, negotiate a discount and donate the equipment directly to the agency.
2826.purpose: Monies will be used to fund our program so that we can continue to provide much needed equipment not being met with agency budgets (heat alarms, bulletproof vests, bitesuits, tracking harnesses etc). Monies will also be used to provide much needed training seminars (such as tracking and decoy) for K9 Handlers throughout the state of FL.
2826.activities: Monies will be used to fund our program so that we can continue to provide much needed heat alarms, bulletproof vests, inserts for K9 vehicles, provide dogs for agencies in need in addition to hosting free advanced training seminars throughout the state of FL. Our goal is to continue to help supplement what is not being met due to agency budget constraints.
2826.direct_services: K9s Units are utilized to assist LE professionals in their community with crime prevention through education & presence. They also assist in criminal enforcement with dangerous suspect location & apprehension, narcotics & explosive detection, and evidence location & recovery. They also assist with locating lost children & adults, or adults who have walked away on foot due to mental disabilities.
2826.population: Elderly, persons with poor mental health, at risk youth, developmentally disabled, drug users, preschool, grade school and high school students and victims of crime.
2826.outcome: K9 Units will receive much needed advanced training through free seminars that we host along with training equipment to better serve their communities. We will be following up with handlers who we have directly helped in improving their skills to evaluate their progress, as well as seeing them the following year in training and observing the improvements they have made through evaluation in training.

2806.description: SOF Missions provides a four-pillar whole health program to at risk Veterans at no cost to them. Our goal is to build resiliency in Veterans that has a positive and lasting effect on their life, their families, their communities, and their interactions with others. We aim for each Veteran to show improvement in their overall psychological, physical, spiritual, and social health.
2806.purpose: The requested funds will support construction of the SOF Missions Center of Excellence, a dedicated facility focused on veteran suicide prevention, mental health, and holistic wellness. Expanding the proven Be Resilient Program, the Center will provide evidence-based, faith-integrated care that restores purpose and resilience, strengthens statewide partnerships, and enhances Florida’s capacity to save lives and support veterans and their families.
2806.activities: SOF Missions offers a unique approach to combat veteran suicide and provide care through a whole health intradisciplinary model—The Resiliency Project is a four-pillar program that addresses the areas of psychological, physical, spiritual, and social wellness. Care plans are provided through three main delivery methods: Clinics, Coordinated Care, and Collaborative Care.
2806.direct_services: Services available for psychological care range from peer-based programs, mental health therapy, and creative therapy. Spiritual care includes education, mentorship, and support groups. Physical care includes physical therapy, alternative PTSD/TBI treatments, cognitive rehab therapy, and sleep therapy. Lastly, social care includes recreational therapy, service animals, and service projects.
2806.population: Persons with poor mental health Persons with poor physical health Physically disabled Veterans, active duty service members, and their families 300 people are expected to be served
2806.outcome: Improved mental, physical, social and spiritual health for veterans, active duty service members and their families. Methods used to measure the outcome will include: Physical Health -Lab marker changes at initial and follow up appointments. (ex: hormone, cholesterol, and vitamin levels) - Functional Movement Screening - Selective Functional Movement Assessment - Wearable sleep monitoring devices - Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) to assess pain Mental Health - Improved score on Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) Depression measure - Improved score on PCL-5 PTSD checklist Social and Spiritual Health - Increased participation in leisure activities - Greater ability to maintain positive friendshi

3458.description: The purpose of this project is to convert customers on septic tanks to sanitary sewer service in an area that is lower income and has poor drainage.

3458.outcome: Connection of properties currently served by septic tanks to central sanitary sewer. This should help with economic development in the area by redevelopment and infill. Additionally it should improve surface water runoff quality and quantity.

2783.purpose: To provide mental health services to first responders that do not qualify under the current post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) statutory language in F.S. 112.1815, to ensure access to certified mental health counselors for first responders who are in crisis.

2814.description: The Community Integrated Employment (CIE) Program will provide students and postgraduates of the North Florida School of Special Education with functional education, workforce readiness training, early employment opportunities, and essential social skills. Through a combination of classroom instruction, hands-on work experiences, and individualized support, the program is designed to increase each participant’s likelihood of securing and maintaining compensated employment.

The program will increase the likelihood of obtaining compensated employment. We will track progress yearly & collect data on program enrollment, employment, work retention, & independent living status to inform program goals.

2814.direct_services: Vocational training skills and supported on-the-job training in the community and on our on-campus job sites are provided by our teachers and microenterprise managers that work alongside our students to help them achieve success.
2814.population: Target population are transitional and post-graduate students with intellectual and developmental differences. 100-200 individuals estimated to be served.
2814.outcome: The program is expected to increase students’ employment readiness, long-term job success, and overall independence. Program impact will be assessed by collecting data on student enrollment, employment outcomes, job retention rates, and independent living status to measure progress toward these benefits.

2904.description: In 2019, St. Pete Youth Farm was established to provide access to nutritious food in South St. Petersburg, FL. We encourage leadership, entrepreneurship and career readiness to develop future leaders in our community. We are seeking funding to expand program opportunites for additional youth. Skills such as learning how to grow food, harvesting and providing produce to the impacted community creates caring and civicilly engaged adults. Teens learn public speaking, wellness and nutrition, and how to manage finances in a safe and supportive environment.

2904.direct_services: Local HS students have the opportunity to learn about innovative food production systems and the mechanisms behind creating their own small business. 100% of food grown goes to local families who access the food 4 days per week directly from the farm (harvested by our teens).

2828.description: Over the course of one year, the Sowing SEEDS Project equips students for life, post high school graduation. Students attend a total of 15 workshops which equate to 40-hours of instructor-led training. After successfully completing the training and development segment, students complete a part-time internship experience where they receive hands-on experience in an environment that aligns with their career aspiration, an adult mentor, and a paycheck. At the end of this experience, students document the knowledge, skills, and abilities acquired during both the training and development segment as well as the internship experience. SEEDS is an acronym which stands for Striving for Excellence through Education, Development, and Service.
2828.purpose: The goals of the Sowing SEEDS project are to equip participants with valuable knowledge and skills, positioning them for a successful future; foster a sense of empowerment and confidence in participants as they matriculate to higher levels of learning; expose participants to diverse career options and professional environments, and provide high- quality internship experiences so that youth are able to get hands-on experience, and adult mentor, and a paycheck (to assist with college expenses).
2828.activities: The program includes 10 months of training and development. Each month, the focus is on personal, academic, and/or workforce development. Workshops are facilitated by experts in the designated field. Additionally, program participants are able to practice newly learned skills during their six-week, internship experience (which is completed in a safe, professional environment that directly aligns with their career aspiration).
2828.direct_services: Direct services that the Sowing SEEDS Project provides citizens on the First Coast include training and development in the areas of: effective communication skills (verbal and nonverbal), effective writing skills, resume building skills, effective interview skills, networking skills, financial management skills, and time management skills. Additionally, the program focuses on health & wellness, ti
2828.population: The targeted population are high school students who reside in Duval, Clay, St. Johns, Nassau, and Baker counties. Such students are economically disadvantaged, at-risk, as well as those from the ‘general’ population.
2828.outcome: The Sowing SEEDS Project is designed to equip youth with personal, academic, and workforce development skills. Participants graduate from the program with hands-on experience and an adult mentor. Having both increases the likelihood of individuals becoming gainfully employed thus reducing Florida’s unemployment and underemployment rates. The methodology by which this outcome is measured is through the AnnieRuth Foundation's alumni program where direct interaction with former graduates, including completion of surveys, will take place.

2829.description: The Nature-Based Wellness Workforce Initiative aims to develop a diverse workforce of health professionals skilled in nature-based wellness practices, including traditional herbal medicine, meditation, forest bathing, ecological wellness, and holistic healing. The program will train doctors, nurses, naturopaths, herbalists, and others in traditional herbal practices for natural healing. Key goals include building a skilled workforce, preserving traditional knowledge, promoting sustainability, expanding access to wellness for underserved communities, integrating therapies into conventional healthcare, and advancing research. The initiative fosters collaboration, public awareness, and the use of natural healing in mainstream wellness, emphasizing ethical resource use and a balance between mind, body, and spirit.
2829.purpose: The Nature-Based Wellness (NBW) Workforce Initiative, proposed by Nwamara Center for Integrative Health, seeks funding to train a diverse workforce in NBW practices like traditional herbal medicine and plant therapies. It aims to integrate traditional healing with modern healthcare, preserve ecological knowledge, promote sustainability, and expand access to holistic care in underserved communities. The initiative emphasizes research, collaboration with healthcare providers, and building professi
2829.activities: The Nature-Based Wellness Initiative will offer natural healing activities and herbal workshops, including training in medicinal tea making, tincture making, emotional support therapy "Bach Flowers", and gardening to develop traditional healing skills. Sustainability will be emphasized through composting and eco-friendly practices. Professional development will include entrepreneurial training and certification to enhance credibility. These services aim to foster economic self-sufficiency, promo
2829.direct_services: The funding will provide citizens with a variety of workforce support services, including workshops, entrepreneurial guidance, and sustainability education. Participants will earn certifications to boost job credibility and create entrepreneurial opportunities. The initiative will support careers in the wellness sector, promote eco-conscious practices, and focus on creating long-term, stable emplo
2829.population: The target population for this project includes jobless persons, economically disadvantaged individuals, university/college students, and elderly persons. The initiative is expected to serve 55 individuals, providing them with skills in nature-based healing practices, sustainability, and entrepreneurship to improve their economic and physical well-being, while creating long-term opportunities for personal and professional growth.
2829.outcome: This initiative aims to improve physical and mental health, enrich cultural experiences, enhance education, and increase economic activity. Outcomes will be measured through pre- and post-training evaluations assessing knowledge in health practices, cultural enrichment, and sustainability. Economic growth will be tracked by monitoring entrepreneurial ventures and income, with follow-up surveys at 6 months to a year. Success will be indicated by participants’ improved health, cultural understanding, education quality, and increased local economic activity.

3319.description: ZooTampa will use the funds to improve the conservation of endangered Florida wildlife with vital hospital equipment, a vehicle for fieldwork on panthers and other species; small facility renovations to support manatee critical and rehabilitative care; and the addition of a panther rehabilitation habitat. ZooTampa is Florida's only nonprofit manatee critical care center and a primary partner with FWC in conserving state and federally recognized and endangered and threatened species.
3319.purpose: ZooTampa will use the funds to improve the conservation of endangered Florida wildlife with vital hospital equipment, a vehicle for fieldwork on panthers and other species; small facility renovations to support manatee critical and rehabilitative care; and the addition of a panther rehabilitation habitat. ZooTampa is Florida's only nonprofit manatee critical care center and a primary partner with FWC in conserving state and federally recognized and endangered and threatened species.
3319.activities: ZooTampa's animal care staff will use the essential equipment and renovated facilities to enhance the care and treatment of endangered Florida wildlife, including animals at the Zoo and in the field. Repairs to vital manatee life support system equipment will ensure that ZooTampa can continue to provide critical and rehabilitative care as a primary partner with FWC in manatee conservation. The addition of a large outdoor habitat adjacent to the Veterinary Hospital will allow the Zoo to provide t
3319.direct_services: More than 1.2 million visitors per year will be able to see the conservation efforts of ZooTampa's dedicated animal care staff as they help to preserve endangered native species for the benefit and enjoyment of Floridians, now and for generations to come.
3319.population: The target populations served by this project are the residents of and visitors to the Tampa Bay region. More than 1.2 million residents and visitors are expected to be served annually.
3319.outcome: The funding will enable ZooTampa to expand its treatment capabilities for endangered wildlife including manatees at the Manatee Critical Care Center, wildlife in the field, and at the Veterinary hospital. The Zoo will also expand its ability to care for Florida panthers with a new rehabilitative habitat. ZooTampa documents and reports all medical treatments according to industry standards and regulations.

3614.description: The requested funding amount will be used to reimburse child welfare provider agencies who were not paid by Embrace Families prior to their contact with the DCF being withdrawn. These agencies have performed child welfare services, as a contract provider on behalf of the State of Florida, and are owed these funds.
3614.purpose: Support Abused, Abandoned, and neglected children
3614.activities: These funds will be used to reimburse agencies for services that have already been provided to vulnerable children and families, who are/were being served through the child welfare system during Embrace Families contract period.
3614.direct_services: Reimbursement for services already provided to vulnerable children and families.
3614.population: Youth, At-Risk Youth, Abused, Abandoned, and neglected children.
3614.outcome: The expenditure of funds requested will be used to reimburse child welfare providers agencies who provided child welfare services on behalf of the State of Florida. Unpaid services has resulted in a shortfall in the budgets of these provider agencies, having a negative fiscal impact on their agency, impacting their ability to continue to provider services to children in foster care.

3068.description: Bethune-Cookman University is seeking funding to expand the John W. Miller Center located in Hastings to meet the increasing demand for nurses in St. Johns, Flagler, and Putnam County. Currently, the center services non-traditional students in Bachelor of Science in Nursing and Certified Nursing Assistant programs through evening and weekend courses. Funds would be used to retrofit current campus spaces into modern nursing labs and classrooms.
3068.purpose: Bethune-Cookman University is seeking funding to expand the John W. Miller Center located in Hastings to meet the increasing demand for nurses in St. Johns, Flagler, and Putnam County. Currently, the center services non-traditional students in Bachelor of Science in Nursing and Certified Nursing Assistant programs through evening and weekend courses. Funds would be used to expand the center to retrofit current campus spaces into modern nursing labs and classrooms.
3068.activities: Proposed funding will be used to expand nursing education and workforce training to non-traditional students in Hastings. Activities and services will include offering BSN and CNA programs, partnerships with local healthcare providers for clinical training and job placement, and more. These efforts will address critical nursing shortages, improve access to education and support economic growth.
3068.direct_services: Non-traditional students in Hastings will receive a comprehensive nursing education, hands-on clinical training, and job placement assistance.
3068.population: The project seeks to target non-traditional college students in the tri-county region of St. John's, Flagler, and Putnam. We anticipate that the project will assist unemployed and/or economically disadvantaged individuals.
3068.outcome: The expected benefits/outcomes of this project include the improvement of nursing education in the tri-county region, improvement to economic activity in the region and the creation of job opportunities within the Miller Center. Outcomes will be measured by quarterly reports that examine changes in enrollment and program completion data. Reports will also include post-program completion job placement for individuals who have passed the NCLEX. Job creation will be measured by the number of vacant teaching positions that are filled once the expansion of the center is complete.

3308.description: The Pensacola and Perdido Bays Estuary Program (PPBEP) will utilize funds to advance implementation of PPBEP's Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan (CCMP) by supporting 600 hectares of oyster habitat restoration through the Oyster Restoration Initiative and by supporting 2 miles of stream restoration to reduce flooding and improve water quality through the Carpenter Creek Restoration. Funding also supports water quality improvements, monitoring to inform natural resources management, community grants, and community outreach.
3308.purpose: Funding will support implementation of the Estuary Program Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan (CCMP) by advancing priority actions including a bay-wide monitoring program, public education, and partial construction of a bay-scale oyster restoration project in East, Blackwater, Escambia, and Pensacola Bays. Funding will support construction of 5 acres of oyster habitat restoration, leveraging ~$15 million from NOAA and the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation to restore ~200 acres of
3308.activities: Construction of 5 acres of oyster habitat restoration in East, Blackwater, Escambia, and Pensacola Bays; final design and easements for the Carpenter Creek Restoration Project; enhanced water quality monitoring in the Pensacola and Perdido Bay watersheds; improvement in water quality through reduction of bacteria, nutrients, algae blooms, and/or total suspended solids entering surface waters in the Pensacola and Perdido Bay watersheds; and community engagement through the Estuary Program's educa
3308.direct_services: Funding will directly result in the creation of 5 acres of subtidal oyster habitat in the Pensacola Bay System and leverage ~$15 million from NOAA and the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation to restore ~200 acres of oyster habitat, improving water quality and the oyster fishery. Implementation of the Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan (CCMP) and the Pensacola Bay Oyster Fisheries and
3308.population: Target population is the citizens of the Pensacola and Perdido Bay watersheds and all visitors to the area. 315,000 residents and 2.2 million visitors are expected to be served through the restoration of Carpenter Creek, water quality monitoring, water quality improvement projects, education/outreach activities, and the restoration of a sustainable oyster fishery associated with this funding request.
3308.outcome: 1) 5 acres of oyster habitat restored through PPBEP Oyster Restoration Initiative. 2) 20 tons of oyster shell recycled for use in oyster habitat restoration. 3) Final design, permitting, and easements needed to construct the Carpenter Creek Restoration Project, reducing flood stagging by approximately one foot in around Davis Highway and Sacred Heart Hospital. Funding will allow the Estuary Program to implement a multi-tiered bay-scale oyster restoration project to support a sustainable oyster fishery in the community. Water quality will be improved as measured by monitoring of sites where water quality hard and soft infrastructure improvements are made. Better water quality from this projec

2830.description: The funds will support the continuation of the annual Cuban-American Studies Institute, a five-day professional development program for educators established by Miami-Dade County Public Schools in partnership with Florida International University. The goal is to enhance teachers' knowledge and instructional practices in Cuban-American history, as required in Florida State Statute 1003.42(2).
2830.purpose: The funds will support the continuation of the annual Cuban-American Studies Institute, a five-day professional development program for educators established by Miami-Dade County Public Schools in partnership with Florida International University. The goal is to enhance teachers' knowledge and instructional practices in Cuban-American history, as required in Florida State Statute 1003.42(2).
2830.activities: Funds will support five days of in-service professional development for teachers, including pedagogical assistance, content expert presentations, and cost associated with hospitality/facilities rental.
2830.direct_services: Funds will directly support teachers by strengthening their ability to serve Miami-Dade’s largest immigrant student group. Training will include three days on the political and economic history of Cuba, Miami, and Florida, and two days supporting instruction on Victims of Communism in the U.S. Government course.
2830.population: The target population includes 200 high school social studies teachers throughout Miami-Dade County Public Schools.
2830.outcome: The expected outcome and benefit of this project are to enrich the cultural experience and improve the quality of education for students to learn about Cuban-American History as part of their U.S. Government classes. This outcome will be measured through formal evaluations and surveys that teachers, students and parents will complete.

3500.description: This project supports critical facility improvements at Trinity Rescue Mission’s St. Johns County campus, which provides residential housing and workforce development services to homeless and economically disadvantaged individuals. Funding will be used for renovations to worn residential rooms and replacement of the septic system and drain field to ensure safe, sanitary, and reliable operations. These improvements will enhance housing quality, protect resident health, and strengthen long-term operational stability.
3500.purpose: The goal of this project is to improve the safety, reliability, and quality of residential housing for homeless individuals by modernizing living spaces and addressing critical infrastructure needs. These upgrades will enhance service capacity, reduce long-term maintenance costs, and improve outcomes for individuals working toward housing stability and economic self-sufficiency.
3500.activities: Benefits include improved public health, increased housing stability, reduced homelessness, enhanced economic self- sufficiency, and improved wastewater management. Outcomes will be measured through reductions in maintenance costs, facility disruptions, homeless-related arrests, and increased participation in employment and recovery programs.
3500.direct_services: The project provides safe residential housing, sanitary living conditions, and uninterrupted access to shelter, meals, job training, and recovery services.
3500.population: Homeless, jobless, economically disadvantaged, and currently or formerly incarcerated individuals. Expected to serve 40-50 individuals annually.
3500.outcome: Benefits include improved public health, increased housing stability, reduced homelessness, enhanced economic self- sufficiency, and improved wastewater management. Outcomes will be measured through reductions in maintenance costs, facility disruptions, homeless-related arrests, and increased participation in employment and recovery programs.

2962.description: The requested funds will be used to retrofit current property owned by Bethune-Cookman University to create a hurricane shelter in the Daytona Beach area. Volusia County is currently designated as having a special needs shelter deficit and only one current shelter exists in the Daytona Beach area. The requested funding will allow the university to improve the structural integrity of the current facility to meet federal and state hardening standards to meet the requirements to become a hurricane shelter.
2962.purpose: The requested funds will be used to retrofit current property owned by Bethune-Cookman University to create a hurricane shelter in the Daytona Beach area. Volusia County is currently designated as having a special needs shelter deficit and only one current shelter exists in the Daytona Beach area. The requested funding will allow the university to improve the structural integrity of the current facility to meet federal and state hardening standards to meet the requirements to become a hurricane
2962.activities: Bethune-Cookman University's on campus shelter will allow citizens in the East Central Florida region to have a safe, secure location during natural disasters.
2962.direct_services: The campus hurricane shelter will provide a safe, secure location for citizens in the region during natural disasters. Following the findings of the study by DEM, the shelter will have an emphasis on special needs individuals.
2962.population: There is no specific target population for this project. However, the shelter will serve as an emergency evacuation shelter during times of natural disasters in the Volusia County area with preference given to individuals with special needs. It is anticipated that the target population will exceed 800 individuals.
2962.outcome: The completion of the shelter at B-CU will improve public safety and protect members of the public from environmental harm. By placing a shelter in the Daytona Beach area, over 85,00 residents in the city will have one additional shelter with preference given to individuals with special needs. The impact of the project will be measured by the number of residents who utilize the shelter in times of natural disasters.

3587.description: This request is for the planning and design of a new, purpose built, Regional Public Safety Training Center that can adequately support the multifaceted training and requirements of Fire Rescue, Law Enforcement, Emergency Services personnel, and School Board personnel. This training center would not only support the needs of Citrus County, but could also be a valuable resource for the potential training needs of surrounding counties including, but not limited to, Sumter, Levy, and Marion. The proposed site could accommodate facilities such as a firearms range and driver training course which could further reduce reliance on out-of-county resources.
3587.purpose: These funds will allow for the planning and design of a Regional Public Safety Training Center that will enhance collaboration among local and regional public safety agencies by providing a centralized location for advanced, multidisciplinary training opportunities. This training center would not only support Citrus County's training needs, but for the potential training needs of surrounding counties including, but not limited to, Sumter, Levy, and Marion.
3587.activities: Through these funds, Citrus County will be able to conduct site evaluations, feasibility studies, preliminary planning and engineering, coordination with regional public safety agencies, and potential land acquisition for the future training center.
3587.direct_services: This appropriations request will establish the necessary groundwork to begin the creation of a future Regional Public Safety Training Center that will enhance emergency response capabilities, improve training quality, and strengthen regional coordination with neighboring counties.
3587.population: The target population served by this project will be the residents of Citrus County as a whole. In general, residents will be served by ensuring that critical law enforcement officers, fire rescue personnel, emergency services personnel, and school board personnel are best trained for the variety of possible scenarios that they could encounter during the daily course of their duties. Therefore, Citrus County's residents as a whole, as well as our neighboring counties', would be served by this pr
3587.outcome: Some of the benefits of this project will be improved public safety readiness and improvements to economic activity by allowing for the foundation of a regional training hub that strengthens the public safety workforce and supports long- term economic resilience. Another benefit would be improvements to emergency response capabilities through the development of a coordinated regional plan. These outcomes would be measured through completion of planning studies, site analyses, preliminary engineering, and other planning documents.

3280.description: This purpose of this request is to assist with repairs and improvements to the Chassahowitzka River Campground in Homosassa. In 2024, multiple hurricanes impacted Citrus County, resulting in significant damage to the various structures located within the campground. Citrus County as well as the Southwest Florida Water Management District have identified a variety of critically impacted infrastructure that will need to be repaired or improved to ensure safe and efficient use of the campground. These include improvements to the parking lot, the boat launch area, restrooms, as well as additional repairs throughout.
3280.purpose: The funds will enable Citrus County to make significant repairs and improvements to the Chassahowitzka River Campground after the substantial damage the property sustained as a result of the 2024 hurricane season. The Chassahowitzka River Campground provides essential access to one of Florida's most pristine spring-fed river systems, and by making these improvements, Citrus County demonstrates its commitment to environmental stewardship and providing access to Florida's natural beauty to residen
3280.activities: If funded, Citrus County will be able to implement significant repairs and improvements to the Chassahowitzka River Campground. These improvements would include but are not limited to repairs to the existing parking lot, new restroom facilities, updates to the existing electrical system within the campground, improvements to the boat launch area, and more. These renovations will significantly improve the safety and efficiency of the campground for visitors.
3280.direct_services: The completion of this project would result in significant improvements to the safety and efficiency of the Chassahowitzka River Campground. By improving the ability for residents and visitors to access and safely utilize the campground, Citrus County will be able to continue to preserve access to one of Florida's most pristine spring-fed river systems while also continuing to attract residents an
3280.population: The target population directly served by this project would be residents of Citrus County, as well as visitors, that utilize the campground in an effort to engage in recreational and educational activity in on one of Florida's most pristine spring-fed natural environmental assets. The campground can provide access to this piece of Florida's natural environment to dozens of families at a time, and can operate throughout the year.
3280.outcome: Some of the expected benefits would be improvements to access to an environmentally sensitive asset within Citrus County while preserving the ecological integrity of the asset. Moreover, if funded, this project is expected to result in improvements to physical health, mental health, enrichment of cultural experience, access to environmental assets, tourism, and more. These benefits can be measure through the use of surveys provided to visitors of the campground after improvements are completed.

3233.description: Funds will be used to expand the successful use of the Peregrine platform to integrate more critical data sources across FDEM Region 9 into the data analytics platform. This will enable use of the platform to integrate emergency management and operations data to create broader regional information sharing and collaboration before, during and after emergencies.
3233.purpose: Implementation of software will lead to measurable improvements in personnel hours saved and actionable insights that will reduce disaster preparation, response, and recovery times. The software will provide first responders, emergency management personnel, and public safety leaders with real-time, accurate, and integrated information to make critical decisions to prepare for, respond to, and recover from hurricanes and other natural disasters.
3233.activities: Dedicated professional and technical implementation specialists to ensure successful software implementation, data integration, dashboard and report building, and end user training.
3233.direct_services: Benefits to citizens include but are not limited to, emergency services making data-informed resource requests, leveraging historical data to improve preparedness strategies, bolstering search and rescue efforts, and accelerating reimbursement and recovery efforts.
3233.population: Florida Division of Emergency Management Region 9 County Residents. Sarasota, Charlotte, Lee, Collier, Hendry and Glades Counties. Approximately 2.02 million individuals live in FDEM Region 9.
3233.outcome: Implementation of software will lead to measurable improvements in personnel hours saved and actionable insights that will reduce response and recovery times. It will also lead to increased visibility and transparency in recovery assessments. Those success factors can be evaluated using real-time and historical data within the analytics platform.

2923.description: These funds are specifically designated to expand our national clinical functional precision oncology program, myFORCE. The program aims to provide personalized treatment options for pediatric and adult cancer patients who have exhausted standard care, guiding physicians toward the most effective and least toxic therapies available. This initiative positions Florida as a global leader in precision oncology.
2923.purpose: These funds are specifically designated to expand our national clinical functional precision oncology program, myFORCE. The program aims to provide personalized treatment options for pediatric and adult cancer patients who have exhausted standard care, guiding physicians toward the most effective and least toxic therapies available. This initiative positions Florida as a global leader in precision oncology.
2923.activities: Functional Ex Vivo Drug Testing (CLIA-certified assay) at a service-based fee for all advanced cancer patients (adults and pediatrics).
2923.direct_services: Drug sensitivity testing for individualized treatments in advanced cancer patients.
2923.outcome: Disappearance of disease- overall best response and progression-free survival.

2908.description: L3’s statewide Career Mentoring & Pathway Forward Program hosted on college and trade school campuses, building a workforce pipeline for Florida by preparing middle and high school students from low to moderate income families for postsecondary education, skilled trades, and high-demand careers. Students receive career readiness training, industry exposure, and career mentoring that strengthens economic mobility and long-term workforce outcomes.
2908.purpose: L3’s statewide Career Mentoring & Pathway Forward Program hosted on college and trade school campuses, building a workforce pipeline for Florida by preparing middle and high school students from low to moderate income families for postsecondary education, skilled trades, and high-demand careers. Students receive career readiness training, industry exposure, and career mentoring that strengthens economic mobility and long-term workforce outcomes.
2908.activities: Activities include curriculum-based mentoring, community workshops, leadership and career readiness training, Florida Ready to Work credentials, Bright Futures and financial aid guidance, skilled trades and college exposure through Weekend at College program, job-shadowing tools, and book scholarships.
2908.direct_services: Students receive mentoring, career and college readiness training, leadership development, online curriculum access via program-issued tablets, job-shadowing tools, trades and technical career exposure, campus-based programs, financial aid and Bright Futures guidance, community workshops, and book scholarships to support postsecondary success.
2908.population: Students in middle and high school (11-18) seeking guidance, mentor ship, and resources to prepare for college, careers, and leadership roles. Our participants face barriers such as limited access to career development opportunities, professional mentor ship, and leadership training. Serve 51-100 participants statewide.
2908.outcome: The project will increase career readiness, credential attainment, and postsecondary participation for middle and high school students. Students will gain exposure to college, skilled trades, and higher-wage career pathways, strengthening Florida’s future workforce and improving long-term economic mobility. Outcomes will be measured through participant enrollment and completion data, Florida Ready to Work credential attainment, pre- and post-assessments, surveys, mentor reports, attendance records, and tracking of postsecondary enrollment, training participation, or workforce placement

3317.description: Expand public access to the St. Johns River and create a vibrant, one-of-a-kind waterfront experience for residents and visitors. This public investment strengthens and complements surrounding private and public developments, including the Museum of Science and History (MOSH), the Four Seasons Hotel with its adjoining marina and restaurant, the capital improvements to the Jaguars Stadium, and the USS Orleck warship museum along one of the nearby piers.
3317.purpose: The goal is to increase the public's access to the St. Johns River and create a unique waterfront experience for citizens and visitors. This public investment into our waterfront enhances other adjacent private/public investments, including the Museum of Science and History (MOSH), the Four Seasons Hotel and adjacent marina and restaurant, as well as the capital investment into the Jaguars Stadium, and the USS Orleck - a warship museum along on of the piers.
3317.activities: This project creates a unique opportunity for Jacksonville's citizens, as well as visitors from NE Florida and beyond to enjoy activities such as fishing, boating, and other passive and active endeavors that extend fromt the City-funded public park on adjacent uplands.
3317.direct_services: Direct services are bringing the public to the waterfront though an immersive park experience that can only be realized by leaving the uplands into the St. Johns River. Typically, this can only be achieved by boat, which most citizens and visitors do not have access. The transformation of former industrial edges into public spaces will enhance the Riverwalk and create additional cultural hubs.
3317.population: General Population; Estimated to help >800 people
3317.outcome: The project is expected to increase public access to the St. Johns River, activate the waterfront, and strengthen economic development by enhancing the appeal and usability of the riverfront for residents, visitors, and adjacent private/public investments.

3327.description: This project will restabilize the deteriorating earthen dam at Antler Pond, a vital structure that impounds stormwater and provides essential flood control for the surrounding community. Future deterioration exacerbated by massive rainfall and flooding can result in dam failure which could lead to the sudden, rapid, and uncontrolled release of impounded water – and associated loss of human life and property destruction.
3327.purpose: This project will re-stabilize the deteriorating earthen dam at Antler Pond, a critical piece of infrastructure that manages stormwater and provides vital flood control for the surrounding area. The dams weakened condition presents a growing threat to public safety and property, as ongoing deterioration increases the risk of structural failure during major storm event.
3327.activities: Restabilization of the deteriorating outfall structure of the earthen dam to toriginal design conditions.
3327.direct_services: The dam provides flood control in the surrounding area but, if it failed, the flooding can be catastrophic. This project seeks to restabilize the deteriorating dam to prevent catastrophic dam failure and protect human life, property and the environment.
3327.outcome: While continuing to protect the local area against flood risks, this restabilization of the deteriorating dam will ensure optimal functioning and prevent failure - and, most importantly, the associated property damage, lifeline disruption (utilities), business disruption, displacement of families from their homes, and environmental damage.

3120.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3120.description: This project will build upon previous successful submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) plantings that created over 48 acres of native submerged aquatic vegetation under an MOU with SJRWMD at permitted locations in Lake Apopka. This funding would allow for an additional 120 acres to be planted under direction from SJRWMD.
3120.purpose: To plant 120 acres of SAV in permitted areas in Lake Apopka in coordination with and under direction of SJRWMD.
3120.direct_services: The project will utilize interns from state universities as well as improving the Lakes ecosystem through water quality improvements and improvements to critical habitat and nursery area for hundreds of species of aquatic life.
3120.population: Students and the general population that enjoys Lake Apopka.
3120.outcome: The successful planting of 120 acres of SAV in Lake Apopka to restore critical habitat and improve water quality and overall ecosystem health of the Lake. Monitoring of restored areas will be published in accordance with permit requirements. All data will be documented and processed for review. Benefits will be measured by tracking quarterly production of SAV.

3328.description: The Woodville Sewer System Project (Phase 2) will improve the water quality flowing to Wakulla Springs, a shared state and local priority. This phase will expand central sewer service to over 350 properties within the Wakulla Springs Primary Springs Protection Zone to significantly enhance the water quality in the region. Leon County ensures that there is no cost to individual property owners for their septic-to-sewer conversion when they apply through the County’s “Connect to Protect” program.
3328.purpose: This critical initiative is to expand central sewer service to over 350 properties and achieve significant water quality improvements within the Primary Springs Protection Zone which will to reduce nitrogen loading to Wakulla Springs by providing central sewer service for the Woodville community. The County ensures no cost for individual property owners for these septic-to-sewer conversions.
3328.activities: The Woodville Sewer System Project (Phase 2) will improve the water quality flowing to Wakulla Springs, a shared state and local priority. This project implements the Upper Wakulla River Basin Management Action Plan to reduce nitrogen loading to Wakulla Springs by providing central sewer service for the Woodville community. This project phase will support septic-to-sewer conversion to over 350 properties properties within the Primary Springs Protection Zone, with over 1000 properties to be conve
3328.direct_services: Property owners in the Woodville Rural Community will continue to benefit from the County's efforts (in partnership with the State) to protect and improve water quality throughout southern Leon County with the removal/upgrade of hundreds of septic systems, investing millions of dollars in local infrastructure, and enhancing neighborhoods to safeguard the environment for future generations.
3328.population: Leon County residents will benefit from this project.
3328.outcome: The expected benefit of the project is to improve public health and environmental protection through expanded central sewer service. By connecting over 350 properties to a centralized system, the project will reduce pollution from individual septic systems, protecting local springs, groundwater, and surface waters in the Primary Springs Protection Zone, the Upper Wakulla River, and Wakulla Spring.

3063.organization: The College of the Florida Keys

This project aims to enhance the efficiency, capacity, and reliability of the existing chiller plant systems, which serve as the backbone for cooling operations at the Key West Campus. Our current infrastructure is increasingly unable to meet the growing demand for cooling services.

The main campus provides the citizens physical access to public higher education facilities in Key West and the Tuga Clinic, which provides community health care services in partnership with the Department
3063.population: The College of the Florida Keys' target population for the Key West Campus serves more than 1,500 students, employees, and community members.
3063.outcome: Enhanced indoor air quality and consistent temperature control across campus facilities. Conduct pre- and post- upgrade air quality assessments to measure outcomes. Increased student and employee comfort, resulting in higher attendance rates and improved academic performance. Avoid potential campus closures which result in class cancellations due to the chiller plant system requiring repairs during high climate temperatures (May through September). As the number of qualified patients and certified physicians grows, the demand for accurate, science-based education is critical. The Cannabis Education Clearinghouse (Can-Ed, Inc.), a Florida-based nonprofit organization, serves as a trusted provider of continuing medical education (CME) events that connect physicians, scientists, regulators, and industry professionals to promote safe and compliant patient care.
3064.purpose: • Provide CME-Accredited Training for physicians, nurses, and allied staff on low-THC cannabis and medical marijuana treatment protocols. • Strengthen Public Health Outcomes by promoting responsible, data-driven use of medical cannabis within Florida’s statutory framework. • Support Regulatory Compliance through education that aligns with Florida Department of Health and OMMU guidance. • Encourage Research Collaboration among universities, licensed medical marijuana treatment centers (MMTCs), an
3064.activities: Use of Funds: • Program coordination and curriculum development • Conference facility and logistical expenses • CME accreditation and faculty honoraria • Outreach and physician registration subsidies for rural participants Outcome Metrics: • Number of CME credits awarded • Number of participating physicians and healthcare professionals • Regional event attendance and participant satisfaction • Post-event compliance and practice improvement surveys

3064.population: Medical Marijuana Qualified Physicians and supporting medical staff as well as over 900,000 Florida residents that have their medical marijuana cards,
3064.outcome: The level of benefit will be measured through a combination of quantitative and qualitative performance metrics designed to evaluate educational impact, compliance outcomes, and participant satisfaction.

These programs include art, dance, music, theatre, chorus, band, orchestra, entertainment technology, and fashion design. The goal is to address access gaps by expanding equitable, quality arts education and preparing students for success in college, careers, and the creative arts field.
