This vital work will prevent immediate and long-term facility failures and directly serve the approximately 1,100 students, faculty, and staff across both campuses. By mitigating the severe health and safety risks from chronic water intrusion, we will strengthen the structural integrity of the buildings and significantly extend
3287.activities: This project will provide a quality roof to a K-8 public school that also serves as a storm shelter for the western communities of Glades County and surrounding areas. It will also improve the flat roofing systems at MHMHS. In addition to structural integrity of the buildings, this project will help to mitigate indoor air quality by reducing the effects of water intrusion such as mold growth.
3287.direct_services: The roof replacement will provide for a safe and healthy facility for the students of Glades County as well as storm sheltering for all of Glades County residents and surrounding areas.
3287.population: Approximately 1100 kindergarten to 12th grade students and 100 staff members will directly benefit.
3287.outcome: The project ensures an optimal learning environment for approximately 1,500 students and staff by achieving Full Regulatory Compliance with SREF standards and eliminating critical structural deficiencies. This includes the mitigation of health hazards, specifically mold and mildew risks caused by water intrusion, resulting in an Enhanced Safety and Health profile for the learning spaces. This project will also provide improvements to the Glades County shelter for our Western communities.

3288.description: The requested funds are essential for replacing end-of-life air handling systems at the WGS campus, ensuring a healthy, safe, and optimal educational environment for students, faculty, and staff. Replacement of aged compressor, air handler, and Dedicated Outside Air Systems—all past their end-of-life—will restore the highest standard of indoor air quality and mitigate airborne pathogens, pollutants, and humidity-driven mold proliferation, reducing student and staff absenteeism.
3288.purpose: The requested funds are essential for replacing end-of-life air handling systems at the WGS campus, ensuring a healthy, safe, and optimal educational environment for students, faculty, and staff. Replacement of aged compressor, air handler, and Dedicated Outside Air Systems—all past their end-of-life—will restore the highest standard of indoor air quality and mitigate airborne pathogens, pollutants, and humidity-driven mold proliferation, reducing student and staff absenteeism.
3288.activities: The requested funds are essential for replacing end-of-life air handling systems at the WGS campus, ensuring a healthy, safe, and optimal educational environment for students, faculty, and staff. Replacement of aged compressor, air handler, and Dedicated Outside Air Systems—all past their end-of-life—will restore the highest standard of indoor air quality.
3288.direct_services: This funding guarantees a healthy, safe, and optimal educational environment for Glades County citizens (students, faculty, and staff) at the West Glades School campus. Upgraded DOAS and AC components ensure the highest indoor air quality. This mitigates pathogens, pollutants, and mold by controlling humidity.
3288.population: Approximately 650 kindergarten to 8th grade students and 45 staff members will directly benefit.
3288.outcome: Modern climate control ensures a productive learning environment. New systems provide optimal thermal comfort and healthy carbon dioxide levels. Replacement of end-of-life AC and DOAS units restores the highest indoor air quality. This mitigates pathogens, pollutants, and mold proliferation, directly reducing student and staff absenteeism and maximizing instructional time. These outcomes can be measured by annual State Requirements for Educational Facilities (SREF) inspections.

3289.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3289.description: The purpose of the funds requested are to address food insecurity and improve access to supportive services for underserved residents in Highlands and Hardee Counties. The program will combine food distribution efforts with on-site, in-person support from Community Care Navigators to connect ALICE (Asset-limited, income-constrained, employed) families to health care, mental health resources, housing assistance, and health tools so that they can live their lives to their fullest potential.
3289.purpose: The purpose of the funds requested are to address food insecurity and improve access to supportive services for underserved residents in Highlands and Hardee Counties. The program will combine food distribution efforts with on- site, in-person support from Community Care Navigators to connect ALICE (Asset-limited, income-constrained, employed) families to health care, mental health resources, housing assistance, and health tools so that they can live their lives to their fullest potential.
3289.activities: Activities include bi-monthly distributions, pop-up distributions in known food deserts and underserved populations, and support from Community Care Navigators through referrals, service connection, and tools to support healthy lifestyles. Navigators and food distribution partners will track data on the number of individuals served, pounds of food distributed, and services offered.
3289.direct_services: Citizens will receive emergency food assistance as well as access to healthcare resources, mental health services, preventive care , education support, childcare, housing/rent assistance, free health tools or nonprofit resources that will help them to thrive in their community and live life to its fullest potential. The purpose is to lessen the gap for families living below the ALICE threshold.
3289.population: The target population are those individuals who fall below the ALICE (Asset-limited, income-constrained, employed) threshold and are economically disadvantaged. The program will serve several thousand individuals across the two counties.
3289.outcome: Navigators complete daily reports on community interactions, tracking resources shared and whether they directly connected individuals, such as calling to make an appointment or setting up an account online. During the first two months of the current program year, navigators attended 38 events to share health tools and resources, providing 81 referrals and distributing 1,079 resources. We will also track the number of individuals and families who attend food distributions. Additionally, the Navigators will track the number of individuals or families they have assisted and will provide follow-up when necessary to ensure they are following through on any programs or services they signed up for

3290.description: The requested funds will be used to replace roofs at Avon Park Middle and Fred Wild Elementary, as well as to replace HVAC systems at Avon Elementary and Sun n' Lakes Elementary and Lake Placid High. These renovations are necessary to improve building integrity, energy efficiency, and overall learning conditions for Highlands County School District elementary, middle and high school students.
3290.purpose: The requested funds will be used to replace the roofs at Avon Park Middle and Fred Wild Elementary, as well as to replace HVAC systems at Avon Elementary and Sun n' Lakes Elementary and Lake Placid High. These renovations are necessary to improve building integrity, energy efficiency, and overall learning conditions for Highlands County School District elementary, middle and high school students and achieving the district's goal of providing safe, healthy, and comfortable learning environments t
3290.activities: The activities funded will include the removal and replacement of the existing roofs at two schools and the installation or upgrade of HVAC equipment at three schools. Services will involve contracting licensed construction and HVAC professionals to perform the work, conducting inspections to ensure quality and safety, and coordinating with school staff to minimize disruption to students and instructional time.
3290.direct_services: The appropriation project will provide citizens (students, teachers, and the broader school community) with direct benefits including safe, healthy, and comfortable learning and working environments. By replacing the roof and upgrading HVAC systems, the project ensures reliable indoor climate control, improved air quality, fewer disruptions to instruction, and safe facilities for educational activ
3290.population: The target population served by this project includes approximately 2,800 students and over 250 school employees across the affected schools. These individuals will directly benefit from improved safety, comfort, and air quality resulting from the roof replacement and HVAC upgrades.
3290.outcome: The expected benefits of this project include creating safe, healthy, and comfortable learning and working environments, improving student focus and attendance, reducing health-related absences, minimizing classroom disruptions, and supporting extracurricular activities. The outcomes will be measured by monitoring classroom temperature and air quality, tracking student attendance and health-related absences, surveying staff and students on comfort and engagement, assessing participation in extracurricular activities, reviewing energy usage and cost savings, and conducting facility condition assessments before and after the improvements.

3333.description: The requested funds will support the construction of a secure, climate-controlled archival storage facility to preserve the National Navy UDT-SEAL Museum's growing collection of irreplaceable historical materials with a value over $2 million. This project ensures long-term protection against Florida's extreme weather, expands storage capacity, and supports digitization and public access. It secures the legacy of Naval Special Warfare for future generations through responsible stewardship.

This project ensures long-term protection against Florida's extreme weather, expands storage capacity, and supports digitization and public access.

The Navy SEAL Museum in Fort Pierce, Florida, is a premier destination in St. Lucie County, attracting Florida citizens and tourists from across the United States and around the world. Every day, the museum welcomes visitors from northern, central, and south Florida, making it a major point of interest for both residents and international travelers alike. In excess of over 500 individuals on an annual basis.

This project ensures long-term protection against Florida's extreme weather, expands storage capacity, and supports digitization and public access. 3291.description: Aerial photography for property appraisers in counties with populations greater than 25,000 but less than 50,000 (Okeechobee) scheduled for aerial flights in 2026-27.
3291.purpose: Aerial photography for property appraisers in counties with a population greater than 25,000 but less than 50,000 (Okeechobee) scheduled for aerial flights in 2026-27.
3291.activities: The Department of Revenue in conjunction with the property appraiser in Okeechobee County will be able to obtain aerial photography.
3291.direct_services: Citizens are able to access aerial photography on a statewide basis. Greater accuracy and equity in assessments in the named county(ies).
3291.population: The target population is Okeechobee County. Population is greater than 38,000.
3291.outcome: The method of measuring level of benefit would be qualitative and reflected in better accuracy of assessments and property identification. Because the aerial photography is oftentimes shared with other local governmental entities, level of benefit would be reflected in 911 programs, emergency management, planning and zoning, and building departments.

3516.description: The City of Dunedin seeks funding for a high water rescue vehicle. Hurricane's Helene and Milton provided a unique experience for our coastal community. Throughout the two storms, Dunedin Fire and Rescue responded to 65 rescue calls removing 96 individuals from unsafe conditions from the several hundred calls that came in. Water rescue using John boats was tenuous using unsafe and inadequate equipment to rescue residents. This project would allow the purchase of a high water rescue vehicle for the City of Dunedin Fire Rescue to ensure future storm and high water events provide for safe evacuation of residents.
3516.purpose: Ensure the safe rescue and transport of residents during flooding or high water emergencies.
3516.activities: The City of Dunedin Fire Rescue will utilize the high water rescue vehicle during storm events or other high water events to perform rescue and relocation of residents impacted by emergencies.
3516.direct_services: Safe transport, evacuation, and rescue of residents and visitors.
3516.population: This project will serve the over 40,000 residents and thousands of visitors to the City each year.
3516.outcome: Tracked number of rescue or evacuations utilizing this piece of equipment.

3636.organization: St. Lucie County Board of County
3636.description: St. Lucie County was devastated by six confirmed tornadoes spawned by Hurricane Milton. This lead to widespread destruction across the County and resulted in six tornado-related fatalities and one storm related fatality. A proper unified command vehicle will significantly improve emergency response capabilities by enabling faster decision-making, better coordination, more efficient deployment of resources, and ultimately saving lives by reducing recovery times during disasters.
3636.purpose: A unified command vehicle provides numerous benefits to support response and recovery operations such as 1) allowing quick deployment to incidents, ensuring immediate response capabilities, 2) serve as a hub for emergency personnel to coordinate strategies and responses, 3) provides connectivity (satellite, radio, and cellular systems) in areas where traditional network is unavailable, 4) facilitates the seamless exchange of data, including live video feeds, GIS Mapping, and situational updates.
3636.activities: This vehicle provides a centralized hub where responders and decision-makers can coordinate, communicate, and manage resources on site and in real time for emergency response, disaster management, and large-scale events.
3636.direct_services: Coordination and deployment of immediate needs resources to residents affected by a human-made or natural disaster.
3636.outcome: 1. Rapid Deployment to affected area - Bring decision-makers and emergency personnel directly to incident site for faster response reducing delays in assessing situation and deploying resources to protect and assist the public. 2. Enhanced communication and coordination - Provides reliable communication channels to stay connected even when traditional infrastructure is damaged. 3. Operational independence - Functions autonomously with its own power supply, climate control, and communications systems. 4. Visible presence for public confidence - Reassures the public that professionals are managing the situation effectively. 5. Mitigation of further harm - Prevents miscommunication or delays in

3580.description: Restoration of the public fishing pier, day docks, ferry dock and emergency rescue vessels for the Pinellas County Sheriffs and Dunedin Fire Rescue boats. The Marina is a keystone to the community and a hub of activity for events, businesses, parkland, recreational and commercial fishing and activities. Restoring use will support businesses, restore tourism via day and ferry boat use, support commercial and recreational use, and restore emergency services.
3580.purpose: The Marina is a keystone to the community used by residents, business, and visitors alike, it is a hub of activity for events, surrounding businesses, parkland, recreational and commercial fishing and activities. It is estimated Hurricane impacted businesses by a loss of over $1M in revenue, residents displaced, and lack of emergency support by the Fire and Sheriff boats. Based on an engineering study, estimated repair and replacement is approx $18M. 3580.direct_services: Restoration of marina returns activity to this central hub - including events, transportation services, emergency services (fire boat and Sheriff's boat), supports tourism and economic development via day dock usage, boat ramp usage and commercial vessel usage. In addition surrounding businesses have been impacted by the closure and lack of activity. Residents have been unable to access vessels an
3580.population: Directly, Dunedin Residents of approximately 36,000 and indirectly, Pinellas County Residents and Vistors, which is over 1 million.
3580.outcome: The outcome impacts many areas - tourism: restoring visitors to marina as a focal point of the community, events like Piper on the Pier and watching sunsets, and restoring transportation services (Clearwater Ferry) measured in visitor counts and transport usage; economic development: supporting local businesses in the surrounding areas that have been impacted and suffering measured in business revenue; recreation for day dock users, slip renters, boat ramp users,kayak and youth small boat sailing measured in user counts; commercial fishing and tourism vessel measured in business revenue and guest counts; safety and security of returning fire boat and Sheriff boat measured by calls and dispat

3334.description: "Lift Every Voice and Sing," also known as "The Harp", was created by renowned artist, Augusta Savage. Augusta was born and raised in Green Cove Springs, Florida, and was commissioned to create a plaster sculpture for the 1939 World's Fair. The work was inspired by the hymn "Lift Every Voice and Sing." With no funding to preserve or cast into bronze, the work was destroyed. As the copyright is in the public domain, this funding request is for the creation of the first full size bronze replica of "The Harp" in the country to broaden awareness of the rich historical significance of the artist and her connection to Northeast Florida.
3334.purpose: Reproduction of this artwork in a more durable medium will provide lasting access to art, enhance livability, attract development, increase tourism, generate economic impact and increase national attention and publicity for the State of Florida and the City of Jacksonville. Moreover, it will provide a reference to the history associated with the Lavilla neighborhood, also known as the "Harlem of the South".
3334.activities: Creation of a full-size plaster mold and full pattern rubber production mold; structural engineering, bronze casting with mounting, transportation, permitting, site work and installation to realize the artwork, educational resources and publicity
3334.direct_services: 1. Increased access to arts and culture in the downtown footprint 2. Greater community engagement and traffic to other downtown amenities such as paid parking, restaurants, lodging and other downtown merchants 3. Educational enrichment
3334.population: As the sculpture will be freely in the public domain it is difficult to gauge how many individuals will experience this artwork. However, it is likely that most local residents will experience this artwork at some point. As the first full size replica of this historic masterpiece, the artwork will also attract national attention and visitors from across the country to learn about and experience this work in person.
3334.outcome: The sculpture will be a large-scale effort which will provide work for a number of trades to realize. It will increase tourism by enhancing the cultural experience and historical awareness of Augusta Savage. The education of students at the University of Florida Graduate School will be significantly enhanced by a tangible reminder of what the Lavilla neighborhood was like at the turn of the 20th century. These outcomes will be measured by a local economic impact study, feedback, surveys and media coverage.

3445.description: The purpose of the funding is to expand existing advanced manufacturing learning pathways that focus on defined regional manufacturing needs at Indian River State College. Existing programs must be expanded laterally to include new pathways to meet the regional workforce need. This can include advanced mechatronics, fiber and optical training's, and cybersecurity as it relates to manufacturing operational technology.
3445.purpose: The purpose of the funding is to expand existing advanced manufacturing learning pathways that focus on defined regional manufacturing needs at Indian River State College. Existing programs must be expanded laterally to include new pathways to meet the regional workforce need. This can include advanced mechatronics, fiber and optical training's, and cybersecurity as it relates to manufacturing operational technology.
3445.activities: The deployment of technology and associated training materials is one main activity. The identification of opportunities to merge and enhance existing training offerings. Deploy programs that drive student enrollments and instructor acquisition.
3445.direct_services: Training's are made available to all students enrolled in IRSC. The IRSC will also be engaged with industry experts to help understand the new possible learning pathways.
3445.population: The target population is all perspective learners in the region. This includes: Current and future students Upskilling learners Re-Skilling Learners
3445.outcome: Developing this space will allow existing programs to leverage technologies previously not available. There will also be opportunity to capture new learners that may be interested in the space and subsequently enroll in a program to build knowledge, skills, and abilities.

3357.description: The project will transition the Sea Pines neighborhood from septic systems to a gravity sewer system. Instead of septic tanks, the area will have a gravity main which flows into pump stations, and a force main leading to the County’s central sewer network and wastewater treatment facility. Approximately 229 parcels within the Sea Pines are expected to benefit from this project. This project will provide an estimated 1,040 pounds per year of nitrogen load reduction.
3357.purpose: The project will transition the Sea Pines neighborhood from septic systems to a gravity sewer system. Instead of septic tanks, the area will have a gravity main which flows into pump stations, and a force main leading to the County’s central sewer network and wastewater treatment facility. Approximately 229 parcels within the Sea Pines are expected to benefit from this project. This project will provide an estimated 1,040 pounds per year of nitrogen load reduction.
3357.activities: Pasco County Utilities will use the funds provided, as well as local match, to hire a consultant to construct the gravity sewer system. Pasco County Utilities has hired a consultant for the design of the system. Local match funds will be provided for the project, and internal operations and maintenance funding secured so the system will remain operable into the future.
3357.direct_services: Construction of sewer main in Sea Pines and related conveyance systems. Legislative appropriations funding will not be utilized to connect homes to the sewer system.
3357.population: The target population are residents of Sea Pines. 229 parcels are expected to be converted. Currently, about 1,500 people live in the neighborhood. The sewer system will serve the neighborhood far into the future, serving and untold number of families in its lifespan.
3357.outcome: This project will provide an estimated 1,040 pounds per year of nitrogen load reduction. This Florida Department of Environmental Protection, in partnership with the Southwest Florida Water Management District, are responsible for nitrogen load reduction methodology.

3446.description: Indian River County Utilities (IRCU) is extending sewer service to connect properties on septic systems. This requires reciprocal drinking water service connections. IRCU is requesting funding for the drinking water infrastructure. Most homes in this community are on the waterfront of the Indian River Lagoon (IRL) which is an impaired waterbody under a basin management action plan. The homes are currently served by individual wells and septic tanks that may be leaching harmful nutrients into the IRL. These homes are required to connect to service or upgrade their septic tanks to nutrient reducing tanks by 2030 to meet state law.
3446.purpose: Construct the drinking water lines to provide water service and allow metering of water and wastewater to assist with the overall purpose of replacing septic tanks with central sewer to comply with state law.
3446.activities: Construction of the drinking water lines will allow water and sewer service to be provided to the residences
3446.direct_services: Drinking water lines. The drinking water lines allow sewer lines to be used at the properties.
3446.population: 110 homes will be served by this project
3446.outcome: 110 homes connect to municipal water and sewer service. 1,271 TN lbs/yr will not be going into the Indian River Lagoon (BMAP area) by removing septic tanks to reduce algae blooms. Drinking water infrastructure is needed to support sewer management and tracking. The nutrient loading calculation is provided by DEP for the BMAP. The number of homes connected to water and sewer will be documented by the number of new customers with water bills in the project area.

3633.description: This project will enhance the efficiency and resilience of the existing stormwater conveyance infrastructure by implementing targeted modifications at Childs Park. The primary focus is the modification of the sediment sump, a critical component in managing surface water runoff. These upgrades aim to optimize sediment capture, reduce system blockages, and improve overall conveyance performance. The project directly supports community resilience goals by mitigating surface water flooding.
3633.purpose: This project will enhance the efficiency and resilience of the existing stormwater conveyance infrastructure by implementing targeted modifications at Childs Park. The primary focus is the modification of the sediment sump, a critical component in managing surface water runoff. These upgrades aim to optimize sediment capture, reduce system blockages, and improve overall conveyance performance. The project directly supports community resilience goals by mitigating surface water flooding.
3633.population: The visitors and residents of City of St Petersburg and the Childs Park neighborhood. Over 250,000 annually
3633.outcome: The subject project will enhance stormwater conveyance capacity within the service area, reducing flooding potential and minimizing risk to vulnerable public and private assets. By improving drainage performance and system resilience, the project mitigates the likelihood of damage or loss during major storm events and supports long-term community protection.

3358.description: Removal of septic tanks and connection to City sewer and/or water systems. A similar initiative was successfully implemented in 2022 through a federal funding award (Award No. 319, C9-99451522) in the amount of $774,000. This project facilitated the replacement of 77 single-family home septic systems. The project is now nearing completion, with all major components finalized. This next phase will continue this success.
3358.purpose: The primary purpose of this project is to reduce nitrogen pollutants from Kings Bay (project is less than 0.75 miles from Kings Bay/Crystal River waterway) per our adopted BMAP, while secondarily providing reliable sewer and/or water to under served neighborhoods.
3358.activities: Removal of septic tanks to provide reliable sewer and reduce nitrogen pollutants.
3358.direct_services: Better water quality for the Bay and increased level of service from the City.
3358.population: The residents of the affected area - approximately 77 Homes
3358.outcome: The primary purpose of this project is to reduce nitrogen pollutants from Kings Bay (project is less than 0.75 miles from Kings Bay/Crystal River waterway) per our adopted BMAP, while secondarily providing reliable sewer and/or water to under served neighborhoods. This will be measured by the number of tanks removed.

3504.organization: Amigos Together For Kids, Inc. d/b/a/ Amigos
3504.description: The program is designed to educate new and expecting parents and caregivers on understanding infant crying and preventing shaken baby syndrome (abusive head trauma). Using the evidence-based Period of PURPLE Crying curriculum, the program equips families with the knowledge and tools to navigate the challenging early months of parenting with confidence and care. The program teaches parents about the natural and temporary patterns of infant crying, emphasizing that crying is a normal developmental stage. Through interactive workshops, participants learn about the six characteristics of PURPLE crying—Peak of crying, Unexpected, Resists soothing, Pain-like face, Long- lasting, and Evening—and effective, safe soothing techniques to manage these behaviors.
3504.purpose: The overarching goal of the program is to educate new and expecting parents about infant crying and the prevention of shaken baby syndrome (abusive head trauma). The primary goal is to increase parents' knowledge of normal infant crying patterns, as outlined in the evidence-based Period of PURPLE Crying curriculum, and equip them with effective and safe soothing techniques. By empowering parents with this knowledge and skills, the program aims to reduce caregiver stress, prevent abusive behavior
3504.activities: The program will provide direct services to new and expecting parents, including educational workshops based on the evidence-based Period of PURPLE Crying curriculum. These workshops will teach parents about normal infant crying patterns, soothing techniques, and ways to prevent shaken baby syndrome (abusive head trauma). Participants will receive printed and digital educational materials, hands-on guidance from trained facilitators, and access to culturally relevant resources in multiple langua
3504.direct_services: Conduct educational workshops led by trained facilitators to teach parents about infant crying, soothing techniques, and child safety. Provide evidence-based resources in the form of brochures, videos, and digital materials to reinforce learning at home. Implement community outreach initiatives to engage families in underserved areas, ensuring widespread access to the program.
3504.population: The program targets new and expecting parents, caregivers, and families with infants, particularly those at risk of experiencing stress or lack of support during the early stages of parenthood. Special emphasis is placed on serving underserved and vulnerable communities, including low-income families, single parents, and those with limited access to parenting resources and education. The program is expected to serve approximately 300 individuals annually, including parents, caregivers, and famil
3504.outcome: The expected benefit of the program is to increase parents’ and caregivers’ knowledge about normal infant crying patterns and safe soothing techniques, reducing caregiver stress and the risk of shaken baby syndrome (abusive head trauma). The program aims to foster healthier parent-child relationships, improve parenting confidence, and promote safer, nurturing environments for infants. Additionally, the program seeks to reach underserved communities, ensuring equitable access to critical education and resources. The program’s outcomes will be measured through: *Pre- and Post-Tests: Parents and caregivers will complete surveys before and after workshops to assess changes in their knowledge of

3595.description: The Center strengthens Florida’s early childhood workforce by assuring the quality of trainers and training, guiding educators through the state’s professional development system, and connecting them to the TEACH scholarship to support career growth, retention, and high-quality practice.
3595.purpose: The Center strengthens Florida’s early childhood workforce by assuring the quality of trainers and training, guiding educators through the state’s professional development system, and connecting them to the TEACH scholarship to support career growth, retention, and high-quality practice.
3595.activities: The Center will qualify and support trainers, develop and review high-quality training, guide educators through a navigable professional development system, ensure quality assurance, develop professional standards and ethics, track progress and outcomes, and conduct outreach to promote workforce development and retention statewide.
3595.direct_services: The Center will support trainers, create access to high-quality training and the TEACH scholarship, guide educators through a navigable professional development system, implement professional standards and ethics, monitor learning progress, and engage educators directly to strengthen workforce development and retention statewide.
3595.outcome: Increase in the percentage of early childhood educators completing state-approved, high-quality professional development and demonstrating improved competency in early learning standards. Studies show that limited access to high-quality early learning is a major barrier preventing parents from working. By improving the quality and availability of early childhood education, the Center ensures children are in safe, developmentally appropriate care, enabling parents to work, maintain stable employment, and participate fully in the workforce.

3436.description: As part of the revitalization and activation of the Midtown area, the City has planned the replacement of existing utility infrastructure, drainage systems and pedestrian access improvements. This project is an important catalyst for redevelopment, preparing the way for new businesses, residents, and economic growth. This critical infrastructure construction provides the pathway for future investments, including the Salvation Army Center of Hope Campus, in the area.
3436.purpose: These funds will support the infrastructure developments throughout the Midtown area including water and sewer upsizing as well as the development of stormwater systems and pedestrian access. These infrastructure improvements will support the continued economic development in the area.
3436.activities: The proposed funds will be used toward design and construction of the proposed infrastructure assets.
3436.direct_services: In addition to the benefits from future developments, citizens will experience greater resilience in the area due to additions of stormwater systems, drainage, and green infrastructure. Existing utility lines are 30-50 years old and susceptible to failure during storm events, which would leave this community at risk of not having access to clean water and sanitation. Additionally, the area does no
3436.population: The Midtown area is a 44 block area, but the impacts will be citywide as a new area will bring new housing developments, new businesses, additional tourism, and continued growth.
3436.outcome: New infrastructure to promote increased pedestrian access to the Midtown area. This increase will enhance economic revitalization which could be measured through pedestrian traffic studies and business impact surveys.

3400.description: The Town of Davie will purchase and install an extraction/evacuation system in all six fire stations with the purpose of removing the exhaust gases and airborne particulates from bay areas, reducing the exposure of our firefighters to carcinogenic chemicals.
3400.purpose: The Town will purchase and install an extraction/evacuation system in all six fire stations with the purpose of removing the exhaust gases and airborne particulates from bay areas, reducing the exposure of our firefighters to carcinogenic chemicals.
3400.activities: An extraction/evacuation system will be installed in all six fire stations.
3400.direct_services: The services are indirect since it is not a location where members of the public frequent. However, Davie Fire stations are safe havens and our fire rescue personnel spend a significant amount of time at these facilities.
3400.outcome: The Town will purchase and install an extraction/evacuation system in all six fire stations with the purpose of removing the exhaust gases and airborne particulates from bay areas, reducing the exposure of our firefighters to carcinogenic chemicals.

3432.description: The Florida SOF Recovery & Resilience Initiative expands Task Force Dagger Special Operations Foundation (TFDSOF)’s continuum of care for wounded, ill, and injured Special Operations veterans and their families. The program provides immediate recovery interventions and sustained engagement through FL based rehabilitative adaptive events, access to mental health treatments, and ongoing wellness support and resources. This holistic, long-term approach keeps veterans engaged in a consistent pipeline of care that strengthens recovery, stability, and reintegration. Continued investment increases the number of Florida SOF veterans served and positions the state as a leader in innovative, family-centered veteran recovery.
3432.purpose: The funds requested will directly support three goals: (1) expand the number and capacity of Florida-based Rehabilitative Adaptive Events (RAE), (2) increase access to health treatments, education, and recovery resources for Special Operations veterans and their families, and (3) strengthen overall stability by keeping participants connected to ongoing support throughout their recovery journey. These investments ensure more SOF veterans and their loved ones receive the long-term care and continu
3432.activities: The funds will support a full continuum of recovery services for Florida’s Special Operations veterans and their families. Activities include the delivery of Florida-based Rehabilitative Adaptive Events (RAE) tailored to individual veterans, couples, or full family units; coordination and facilitation of advanced mental health and clinical treatments; and access to ongoing recovery resources and wellness support that strengthen both individual and family healing. The program also maintains struc
3432.direct_services: The project will provide direct services to Florida citizens—including SOF family members, volunteers, and Florida- based nonprofit and business partners—through expanded Rehabilitative Adaptive Events, increased access to health treatments and recovery resources, and structured opportunities for ongoing support. Services include family-inclusive adaptive recovery activities, coordination of menta
3432.population: The project serves wounded, ill, and injured Special Operations Forces veterans and their families residing in or traveling to Florida for recovery support. The target population also includes Florida citizens who participate as family members, volunteers, service providers, and nonprofit or business partners supporting program delivery. The initiative is expected to directly serve more than 200 individuals.
3432.outcome: The expected benefits include improved physical, mental, and emotional recovery for Special Operations veterans; strengthened stability and resilience for their families; and deeper community engagement across Florida as more citizens participate in and support these initiatives. Outcomes will be measured through participant counts, pre/post- program assessments that track changes in well-being, follow-up engagement data demonstrating continued connection to care, family feedback surveys, and community involvement metrics reflecting volunteer participation and the number of Florida partners engaged.

3351.description: This project helps new and expanding employers address critical workforce shortages by providing a steady flow of better prepared and vetted candidates for skilled trades roles. The initiative delivers hands on technical training, certification preparation and career readiness for home school students, high school students and youth ages 18 to 24. Programs introduce youth to technical careers they may not have considered and connect them directly with multiple hiring employers. Funding supports instructors, equipment, learning systems and work based learning experiences across manufacturing, utilities, public works and stormwater. These services strengthen the regional talent pipeline, support employer growth and expand career opportunities for youth, including those who are low income, economically disadvantaged or transitioning out of foster care.
3351.purpose: Funds will help new and growing employers expedite hiring by partnering with AmSkills through expanded hands on training and career readiness for home school students, high school students and youth ages 18 to 24. Support will prepare candidates for skilled trades jobs in manufacturing, utilities, public works and stormwater, strengthen the regional talent pipeline and advance statewide workforce and economic development priorities.
3351.activities: Activities conducted through the services offered in the Rapid Employment Workshops, Career Discovery Bootcamps and Internships include hands on technical training, learning management systems for hybrid learning and soft skills, resume and interview training for careers in manufacturing, utilities, public works and stormwater. Equipment will be used for training, vetting and upskilling during apprenticeships or after hire.
3351.direct_services: Services include rapid employment workshops, career discovery bootcamps, internships and hands on technical training that prepare students and youth for jobs in manufacturing, utilities, public works and stormwater. Participants receive instruction, industry certifications, employer interviews and pathways to apprenticeships and immediate employment.
3351.population: The project serves home school students, high school students, youth ages 18 to 24 and individuals who are low income or economically disadvantaged, including teens transitioning out of foster care. Many youth are unsure of their career direction, and these programs introduce them to technical careers they may not have considered by combining career discovery, hands on training and direct exposure to multiple employers. The program is expected to serve approximately 150 to 250 individuals each y
3351.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to increase the number of students earning industry-recognized credentials and entering skilled trades careers and/or apprenticeships. Students will gain hands-on experience, certifications, and employability skills that prepare them for immediate entry into the workforce. Outcomes will be measured through the number of students enrolled, certifications earned, successful program completions, and job or apprenticeship placements. Additional metrics will include employer feedback and student post-program surveys to assess skill development and career readiness.

3395.description: Crystal River’s City Hall has sustained repeated flooding from major storm events, most recently Hurricanes Idalia and Helene. (Previously, the facility also flooded during the No Name Storm of 1993 and Hurricane Hermine in 2016). The facility served not only as the City’s administrative center but also as a law enforcement substation. The plan to reconstruct an elevated, and resilient facility in its original downtown location is both necessary and fiscally responsible. State investment of $5,000,000 will help ensure continuity of essential services for the city and surrounding areas.
3395.purpose: The facility will consist of a two-story structure with the first floor only used for parking and/or such uses which would able to be suspended in advance of a large coastal surge. (Elevation must be above the 100 year, 2070 projected coastal surge elevation – a minimum of 9 feet above the current grade of the existing city hall).
3395.activities: As a City Hall location the needs of the City of Crystal River residents will be served from this new building. This will include city government functions (planning & zoning, growth management/building dept, public works, parks & recreation, utilities & administration) as well as a public safety facility/Sheriff's office substation (which serves Crystal River and surrounding Citrus County areas).
3395.direct_services: Permitting, Water and Sewer, public records, public council meetings, parks and recreation information, local events information hub, facilitation of garbage services, payment of parking citations, zoning issues, and more.
3395.population: Citizens of Crystal River and the surrounding areas will be served with the Sheriff's office substation. More than 3,500 people will be served at this location.
3395.outcome: Setting an example to citizens on resiliency and mitigation for future storms. An elevated structure will allow the City to resume services quickly after a flood event in lieu of months or years of renovation before occupancy is possible.

3398.description: Crystal River continues to advance multimodal transportation options that enhance mobility and improve visitor access throughout the community. Safe, permitted golf cart crossings at priority intersections along US 19 will support connectivity between key commercial, recreational, and residential areas. With an estimated cost of $200,000 for the initial improvements, this project represents a cost-effective step toward a more accessible and tourism-friendly corridor.
3398.purpose: With an estimated cost of $200,000 for the initial improvements, this project represents a cost-effective step toward a more accessible and tourism-friendly corridor. Safe, permitted golf cart crossings at priority intersections along US 19 will support connectivity between key commercial, recreational, and residential areas.
3398.activities: Safe, permitted golf cart crossings at priority intersections along US 19 will support connectivity between key commercial, recreational, and residential areas.
3398.direct_services: A safe and legal option for golf cart crossing.
3398.population: Local citizens, and tourists. City population is 3,500; annual visitors near 100,000.
3398.outcome: A safe and legal option for golf cart crossing measured by FDOT data.

3573.description: The project will include the completion of the Family Recovery Building, Site Plans, Permitting Costs, Staff Housing, Transition House, Recreation Hall, BBQ Area, Paving, Parking, Beautification (sod, landscaping, lighting, etc.), furnishings, industry equipment, vehicles and more. Cross Training is a one year in-resident drug and alcohol regeneration program for young men ages 18-25 battling with addiction. It is a very structured program that leads men to a relationship with Christ and teaches them how to be a man of integrity. Cross Training Ministries provides a safe place for young men to change from destroying themselves and their families, and from being a burden to their community; to become the man God created them to be, restore the relationships damaged, and to give back to the community. The young men develop work skills through our mowing industry, teaching them good work et
3573.purpose: Provided funds will assist in building and completing a facility that will continue to help young men in addiction. The future plans will expand the program to meet the needs while in the program and once graduated. The transition house will enable graduates to stay in a safe environment, while pursuing jobs and further life skills and stability. The funds will also provide on-site housing for staff and their families.
3573.activities: Architectual plans, construction, labor, paving, lighting, furnishings, vehicles and equipment for the industry, and any and all aspects necessary to complete the project.
3573.direct_services: Cross Training Ministries accepts young men from all over the State of Florida, and from many walks of life. Families are restored, and many of the young men that have graduated have families of their own and are successful businessmen. As part of the program, we often give back to the local community by volunteering at events to help set up, tear down, etc. We help people with moving, and help as
3573.population: CTM targets young men that struggle with addiction, and their families. We provide co-dependency classes for the parents to prepare them for what to expect once the men return home. We have had over 200 young men come through the program since our established date in 2004. Our goal is to help as many young men as possible. It is often said that one person can impact up to 7 people, to put a number on how many individuals will be served is nearly impossible!
3573.outcome: To continue to help young men. It is measured by the number of men that graduate from the program and are given the tools to live a successful, drug-free and purpose filled life!

3388.organization: School District of Palm Beach County
3388.description: The Boca High Robotics Program is seeking funding to expand and strengthen its impact through the construction of a dedicated robotics lab and the acquisition of advanced technology and equipment. This new space will provide students with a collaborative, hands-on environment designed to support engineering, programming, and problem-solving at a high level. In addition to outfitting the lab with essential tools, computers, robotics kits, and fabrication equipment, the requested funding will help sustain the program long-term by supporting competition travel, ongoing equipment purchases, and maintenance. This investment will allow the Boca High Robotics Program to grow in both size and scope, ensuring students have continued access to real-world STEM experiences that prepare them for college, careers, and leadership in technology-driven fields.
3388.purpose: To establish a dedicated robotics lab at Boca High School, expand FIRST-aligned robotics teams, and fund equipment, competition fees, travel, event hosting, and mentor training so more students, including those from underserved backgrounds, can access high-quality STEM education and workforce pathways.
3388.activities: Hands-on robotics instruction in a dedicated lab, team-based engineering projects, preparation and travel for FIRST competitions, and hosting local scrimmages and qualifiers for Palm Beach County teams.
3388.direct_services: Students will gain access to modern robotics equipment, safe lab space, travel to regional, state, and national competitions, and mentoring that builds STEM, coding, engineering, and advanced manufacturing skills.
3388.population: Students within Palm Beach County, roughly 200.
3388.outcome: Increase in the number of robotics teams, students served, competitions attended and hosted, and industry- recognized certifications earned each year. Short-term paid or volunteer roles for students in mentoring, event operations, and lab support created through the program.

3372.description: The Florida Institute of Oceanography (FIO) at USF conducts marine research and STEM education through the advancement and the availability of infrastructure and the enabling of outcomes that benefit the people of Florida. On its fleet of marine research vessels, which are shared by all SUS and other research partners in the state, FIO conducts world-class research to protect and advance Florida. This funding will be used to perform critical maintenance and modernize research and other equipment on the research vessels, which will extend the service life of the vessels and enhance and expand the state’s marine research capabilities.
3372.purpose: The funding will be used to modernize and maintain equipment that will help understand critical issues such as water quality and quantity, red tides and other harmful algal blooms, sand movement and availability for healthy beaches, fisheries resources, accurately tracking whale and other marine mammal migrations to co-exist with economically important uses such as shipping, ports, tourism and fishing and will also result in new research opportunities for students and researchers statewide.
3372.activities: Maintenance and a refit and remodel of the research vessels so that the ships are safe for extended time at sea and technologically advanced research can be performed. The modernized equipment is needed to recruit world-class researchers and conduct preeminent oceanographic research. The maintenance is needed for safety purposes and to extend the useful life and seaworthiness of the vessels.
3372.direct_services: This funding will provide students with a unique mix of at-sea and on-shore training and mentoring opportunities to help build skills in the field of Ocean STEM. The vessels engage students who don't have ready access to sea-going platforms. The vessels' maintenance and repairs and new equipment and technology will provide students access to marine science through at-sea experiences.
3372.population: High school, college, and university students and university and state researchers. Approximately 400 individuals are expected to be served.
3372.outcome: Improve quality of education: The equipment will help understand critical issues such as water quality and quantity, red tides and other harmful algal blooms, sand movement and availability for healthy beaches, fisheries resources, accurately tracking whale and other marine mammal migrations to co-exist with economically important uses such as shipping, ports, tourism and fishing. The methodology by which this outcome will be measured is new research opportunities for students and researchers statewide.

3387.description: The funds will be used to restore and upgrade a historic landmark fountain that was built before local and state recordkeeping began. The project will not only preserve an important piece of community history but also improve public safety. The area surrounding the fountain includes a poorly lit pathway that serves as part of an official evacuation route used by more than 20,000 residents. Upgrading the lighting and surrounding infrastructure will enhance visibility, accessibility, and safety.
3387.purpose: The funds will be used to restore and upgrade a historic landmark fountain that was built before local and state recordkeeping began. The project will not only preserve an important piece of community history but also improve public safety. The area surrounding the fountain includes a poorly lit pathway that serves as part of an official route used by more than 20,000 residents. Upgrading the lighting and surrounding infrastructure will enhance visibility, accessibility, and safety.
3387.activities: The project will include the restoration of the 99-year-old historic fountain and the enhancement of surrounding infrastructure to create a safer and more functional environment. These enhancements will support safer roadway conditions and improve emergency roadway management along a designated evacuation route used by more than 20,000 residents.
3387.direct_services: The funding will provide citizens with a safer, better-maintained roadway and improved lighting along a key evacuation route. These upgrades will enhance pedestrian/vehicle safety, ensure better visibility at night, and support efficient emergency management. In addition, the restoration of the historic fountain will enhance the areas appearance and preserve and important landmark.
3387.population: Elderly persons, Developmentally disabled, Physically disabled, Preschool students, Grade school students, High school students, University/College students, General (The majority of funds will benefit no specific group). Great than 800 individuals.
3387.outcome: The expected benefit of the Camino Real Fountain Improvement is to enrich cultural experience, enhance environmental quality, protect the general public from harm, improve transportation conditions, increase economic activity, increase tourism, improve stormwater management, improve groundwater quality, and improve surface water quality. The outcome will be measured through resident and tourist satisfaction, water quality monitoring, changes in traffic incidents, near-misses, or pedestrian accidents along Camino Real before and after the lighting upgrade, businesses' satisfaction, and monitoring the efficiency of stormwater systems.

3472.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3472.description: Across Florida, animal shelters are under tremendous strain. Rising intake numbers, limited staffing, inconsistent training, and fragmented resources threaten the wellbeing of animals and the stability of the communities these shelters serve. Frontline teams are overwhelmed; standards of care vary widely, and preventable challenges - particularly related to community cats - continue to drain time and resources. HSSC's TAILS Program is a strategic, collaborative solution designed to change that. This program design is scalable throughout the state.
3472.purpose: The TAILS Program is a collaborative, capacity-building initiative that brings municipal and private shelters together to model, mentor and share best practices, training, resources, and capabilities. Led by the Humane Society of Sarasota County, TAILS strengthens animal welfare across our region by providing: Mentorship & Coaching, Training & Workforce Development, Shared Resources and Expertise, and making Trap, Neuter, Vaccinate, & Return - TNVR core component of lifesaving services.
3472.activities: 1. HSSC will partner with a minimum of 5 animal welfare shelters to collaborate and mentor for better outcomes. 2. HSSC will provide at least 1,000 TNVR services to feral community cats.
3472.direct_services: Citizens will be positively impacted by addressing the growing feral cat population. Through TNVR, there will be a reduction in disease transmission, nuisance behaviors and feral cat population growth. This process improves the community who can become voluntary trappers.
3472.population: Target population is other animal welfare organizations looking to improve outcomes for animals in their care and to positively support the community. Additionally, the community as a whole is served by reducing the feral cat population. We will partner with a minimum of 5 organizations directly, all serving a different geographic region to expand project reach and impact. # served/impacted will vary depending on what region the partner organizations serve but could exceed 1 million based on cou
3472.outcome: 1. Partner with a minimum of 5 shelters to provide mentoring regarding best practices and standard operating procedures. Measured by documented partnerships (name, region, # of animals served, etc.) and services provided to improve outcomes. 2. Provide 1,000 TNVR surgeries to address the feral cat population. Documented by date, M/F cat, and zip code the cat was trapped within.

3599.description: The City of Plantation has already installed license plate readers (LPR) in portions of the community with good results. The City is requesting funding to expand this program adding additional LPRs in "hotspots". Funding will also enhance efforts to integrate LPRs with other systems such as body worn cameras, etc. As the City is centrally located in the heart of Broward County, strategic positioning of additional LPRs beneficially contributes to the safety of the region.
3599.purpose: Strategic use of additional LPRs will help improve public safety, accelerate incident resolution, aid in the detection/apprehension of criminals, aid in locating/rescuing vulnerable individuals/victims, and improve regional crime fighting and incident response efforts through collaboration.
3599.direct_services: Enhanced public safety in the region.
3599.population: The City has a population of over 100,000 and is centrally located in Broward County.

Measurement: number of crimes against persons in areas served by LPRs; number of crimes against property in areas served by LPRs; arrest rates in areas served by LPRs; vulnerable persons served by LPRs; Regional response aided by Plantation LPRs

3506.description: The City of Plantation has two pedestrian bridges that extend into a wetlands area and are greatly enjoyed by bird enthusiasts and other environmentalists. In recent years these bridges have fallen into disrepair. The City is seeking funding to assist with the costs of repair/replacement. The City has completed an assessment is anxious to move forward with the repairs.
3506.purpose: Safe, continued enjoyment of wetlands and nature accessible by two pedestrian bridges in Volunteer Park that are in need of repairs or replacement.
3506.direct_services: Safe, usable pedestrian bridges that allow access to wetlands and nature in an urban environment
3506.population: The City has a population of over 100,000 and is centrally located in Broward County
3506.outcome: Improved opportunities for physical activity and enjoyment of nature. Measured by: number of people using the bridges.

3475.description: The requested funds will launch and sustain a mobile outreach unit equipped with Wi-Fi, air conditioning, and workspace, staffed by two Navigators five days a week. This unit will bring health insurance and safety-net program enrollment assistance, education, and resources directly into underserved communities, reducing barriers and expand access to resources, community programs, and public benefits in Hernando, Hillsborough, Polk, Pinellas and Pasco Counties.

3635.description: The Pinellas County Urban League (PCUL) is requesting a one-time investment from the State of Florida to develop a state-of-the-art Community Resiliency and Recovery Hub and headquarters. This facility will serve as a catalyst for economic mobility by providing educational enhancement, entrepreneurship support, and workforce training. The commercial space will feature a digital tech theater, an innovation center, and collaborative workspaces. Additionally, micro-retail and Class A office rental space will contribute to the revitalization of the Historic Deuces Corridor, fostering business growth and community development. This development will serve as a catalyst for economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, and community-driven innovation, ensuring that prosperity is not only achieved but sustained for future generations.
3635.purpose: The funds will be used to develop a new mixed-use building in St. Petersburg’s Deuces Neighborhood, which will become the new home for the Pinellas County Urban League (PCUL). This development will feature class A commercial spaces and amenities, a community Emergency Operations Center, digital tech lab, bank other employers and the core programs of the PCUL including education, job training, housing, and health services.
3635.activities: The facility will also be an ongoing source of family-friendly enrichment activities, which are absent on the corridor, apart from the growing number of festivals and special events on the Deuces. PCUL programs such as Wellness Wednesdays, Food Truck Fridays, Entrepreneurship Mixers, PCUL Live and other unique programs serve hundreds of community members each month and will bring to the Deuces a week-in-week-out schedule of activities for family members at every age and stage.
3635.direct_services: Our programs and services are designed to meet individual family needs, support community succession planning, and increase family income. We have dedicated navigators and coaches to help families where ever they may be on their journey. Focusing on providing safe, affordable spaces to live, work, and play. Additionally, we aim to enhance all aspects of health—financial, physical, and mental—ensur
3635.population: The target population for this project includes all residents who are looking for an opportunity to support small businesses and to take advantage of a one-stop shop type of destination place. It is expected that over 100,000 individuals will be served annually.
3635.outcome: The expected benefit of this project is to improve economic stability, educational outcomes, and overall well-being for underserved populations. Key outcomes include increased revenue for business owners, increased employment opportunities for citizens reduced recidivism, improved health, and enhanced community engagement. The methodology for measuring success will involve the annual economic impact analysis of businesses in the development, tracking participant enrollment in programs and service offerings and health improvements through surveys and data analysis.

The goal is to improve kindergarten readiness statewide by providing science-based, adaptive instruction that closes early learning gaps, especially in small and rural communities.

3430.direct_services: Young children will receive personalized early literacy and math instruction that builds foundational skills for kindergarten. 3430.outcome: Improved kindergarten readiness and early literacy/numeracy proficiency for pre-K learners. Measurement: Growth in early literacy and numeracy skills, including increased STAR Early Literacy scores and higher rates of children meeting Florida’s kindergarten-readiness benchmarks.

3525.description: Expand workforce training program to expand current warehouse training program and add CDL driver training. Along with the training programs, provide case management, certification, life skills, and job retention education.

3525.population: Feeding South Florida will focus on unemployed or underemployed individuals who are currently accessing government assistance. Over the course of a year, Feeding South Florida will enroll 200 low income individuals in the workforce training program. This number will continue in perpetuity.
3525.outcome: The benefit to the students is increased skills and knowledge in a trade with living wage and realizes a reduction in reliance to government assistance. The benefit to employers is a stable candidate with a working knowledge of the industry.

3509.description: Construction of a living shoreline including mangrove planters and other components to restore an eroded, degraded shoreline and create valuable intertidal and emergent habitat. Completed project will promote shoreline resiliency and protect existing upland roadway infrastructure.

3601.description: Martin County seeks funding to support the design and construction of a state-of-the-art rail station in Stuart, Florida. This investment will provide much-needed passenger rail service for both residents and visitors of the Treasure Coast region. The project will help to reduce intercity travel time, lower vehicle operating costs, decrease crashes, stimulate economic development, reduce air pollution, and enhance the quality of life for the millions of people who live and visit the city of Stuart and Martin County. The Martin County Brightline Station Project comprises several components, including a train station, platform, parking facilities, and rail infrastructure. The station will be approximately 8,000 square feet in size, with an adjacent platform measuring about 600 feet in length. In addition to the station and platform, the project includes necessary rail improvements to facil
3601.purpose: Martin County seeks funding to support the design and construction of a state-of-the-art rail station in Stuart, Florida. This investment will provide much-needed passenger rail service for both residents and visitors of the Treasure Coast region. Funding will help to reduce intercity travel time, lower vehicle operating costs, decrease crashes, stimulate economic development, and enhance the quality of life for the millions of people who live and visit the city of Stuart and Martin County.
3601.activities: A passenger rail station in Martin County will provide service to Miami, Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton, West Palm Beach, and Orlando International Airport. The project will reduce vehicle miles traveled, alleviate traffic congestion, and decrease commuter travel time. Shifts from vehicles to train trips will help to eliminate automobile crashes in the region.
3601.direct_services: The Martin County Brightline Station will directly serve residents across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties, with a combined population of over 700,000 people. This project will have the ability to serve the millions of annual visitors to Martin County. The project will also provide commuter travel services between the northern Treasure Coast counties and Palm Beach County.
3601.outcome: Construction will create immediate job opportunities measured by job growth, wage increases and training opportunities. This will increase tourism to and from the region measured by visitor counts, tourism industry revenue and hotel visitation. The station will increase accessibility to Treasure Coast businesses for all of South Florida and 3 international airports. It will improve highway safety by reducing vehicle miles, reducing accidents and congestion.

3505.description: St. John Bosco Clinic is a free clinic providing primary and preventive care and some specialty care services to individuals living in Miami-Dade County who are uninsured and below the 200% Federal Poverty Level. As a free clinic, St. John Bosco Clinic, relies on the support of volunteers, licensed healthcare providers and support staff to meet the needs of the clinic patients. The clinic provides primary care to adults and children through a model of care that primarily uses Advance Practice Registered Nurses with the support of volunteer physicians, many of who are specialists that see patients in their private office pro-bono. Patients who have medical needs beyond the scope of the clinic are referred to other community programs better suited for their needs. The clinic works with these patients to ensure a transition of care. The clinic offers screening, diagnostics, treatment and fo
3505.purpose: To Provide comprehensive primary care services by ensuring access for the underserved and uninsured in Miami- Dade County. The clinic services identify, prevent and treat the most prevalent conditions. Access to this level of healthcare will give individuals the ability to care for their health before conditions lead to complicating disabilities, loss of productivity and even prevent deaths. Such healthcare access reduces the overall cost to the healthcare delivery system.
3505.activities: Chronic disease management is key to maintaining a healthy community, as such, patients will be supported through access to medications, health education and tools necessary to manage conditions. Activities that support facilitating access to the targeted population (those who are uninsured, underserved and living below the 200% federal poverty level).
3505.direct_services: Primary and preventive care. Referrals to a network of volunteer specialists and navigation to other programs when the care needed is outside the scope of clinic services. Prescription assistance program and navigation to low cost medications. Assistance with supplies and tools necessary to self- manage conditions and Laboratory and diagnostic exams.
3505.population: The target population includes: Elderly persons, people with poor mental/physical health, unemployed. The target population is over 800 people.
3505.outcome: 1.Reduction in elevated blood glucose AIC to7%. 2.Reduction in cholesterol ratio to <4. 3.1,000+ unduplicated individuals will have access to healthcare. 4.4,000 clinic encounters for initial and follow up care. 5.700 individuals screened for cancer (cervical, breast, colorectal)

Because the needs of this population are complex, the families we serve often have limited access to care, inclusive community events, and opportunities for social and life skills development.

This includes respite services for parents and caregivers of children with special needs, and family-friendly community events they are to be a part of without worry or limitations. Because the needs of this population are complex, many of the families we serve have very limited access to care and sensory inclusive/accessible events.
3522.activities: I.M.P.A.C.T. Program runs out of POSABILITY’s “Emmalee’s Clubhouse" which is a one-of-a-kind facility that allows us to connect with more underserved families and to recruit volunteers, teaching them how to interact with individuals with disabilities and their families. From here we provide support groups, after school programs, art classes, and respite programs.

3602.purpose: This project will improve the safety and walkability of the Garden and Alcaniz Street districts and neighborhoods; avoid flooding to local businesses; and allow the site to be utilized for research, community and neighborhood activities in a downtown urban environement.

3602.direct_services: This flood mitigation project will directly fund local trademen and labor force as well as professional engineers and environmental specialists.
3602.population: Upon project completion the target population is local youth and adults participating in scientific and community events.
3602.outcome: Increased public and community activity on site measured by the number of events held and the number of participants in these events.

3489.description: Seffner Christian Academy opened in 1983 and currently serves over 750 students. Our school hopes to expand and start serving children with special needs in our area which desperately needs additional space to serve more children with these needs. We hope to provide a well-rounded, tailored experience to learning to encourage and grow student interest for children with these unique educational needs. Funds will be used to build and operate a building to serve children with special educational needs including autism and other related needs.
