3489.direct_services: Educational instruction for children with unique educational needs to help them prepare to be productive citizens of the state.
3489.population: This project will serve children with unique educational needs, including those in preschool, grade school, and high school.
3489.outcome: Classrooms will have space for collaborate learning and hands on activities. New classroom will be designed and constructed to meet children with special needs to ensure a secure and supportive learning environment for all students. The outcomes will be measured through student performance in the classroom.

3523.description: Warrior Wellness Program will offer 22 Accelerated Wellness Programs (AWP). The AWP is a 5-day intensive program offering highly effective therapies such as Accelerated Resolution Therapy, adaptive yoga, Integrative Restoration, physical fitness and mindfulness techniques such as vision boarding and art therapy. Program outcomes for the AWP shows participants show an average reduction of 60% in PTSD, 68% in Depression and 65% in Anxiety.
3523.purpose: Warrior Wellness Program's goal is to provide veterans and active-duty military personnel an opportunity for healing. The men and women who served our country will attend the Accelerated Wellness Program providing them increased access to Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART) and other alternative therapies that effectively treat symptoms and issues related to trauma, post-traumatic stress, anxiety, depression and more, which will result in improved mental health and wellness.
3523.activities: Warrior Wellness Program will offer 22 Accelerated Wellness Programs (AWP). The AWP is a 5-day intensive program offering highly effective therapies such as Accelerated Resolution Therapy, adaptive yoga, Integrative Restoration, physical fitness and mindfulness techniques such as vision boarding and art therapy.
3523.direct_services: The organization will provide mental health and wellness services including Accelerated Resolution Therapy, a proven therapy that works in 1-5 sessions to provide healing for veterans and active-duty military members experiencing post- traumatic stress symptoms including depression and anxiety. Adaptive Yoga & iRest are provided together to increase body awareness and improve sleep outcomes. Mindf
3523.population: This project will deliver services to 125 veterans and/or active-duty service members and their spouses who suffer from issues related to post-traumatic stress, anxiety and depression due to the traumas of war. Services will be delivered through Warrior Wellness Program's Accelerated Wellness Program, a 5-day intensive program providing an array of effective mental health and wellness therapies.
3523.outcome: Participants will experience a reduction in PTSD, depression, anxiety and stress. In addition, they will experience an increase in resiliency and community engagement. Pre- and post- assessments are conducted and use valid and reliable measures of psychological and physical health including the Post-Traumatic Checklist and the Brief Symptom Inventory. An external evaluator uses the data collected to perform an extensive analysis to produce a comprehensive program evaluation on overall service impact.

3521.description: Advantage Aging Solutions, the Area Agency on Aging serving the Big Bend region, will deploy an advanced telehealth CareStation to expand access to primary, urgent, and behavioral health services for underserved older adults. The project establishes a secure, ADA- and HIPAA-compliant clinical station in a publicly accessible community building located in an area with limited and unreliable access to timely primary care. Through real-time virtual visits with licensed clinicians, integrated diagnostics, and e-prescribing capabilities, the CareStation will enable older adults to receive high- quality care closer to home, reduce avoidable emergency room utilization, and address longstanding barriers such as provider shortages, transportation limitations, and broadband challenges. The program will operate in coordination with local community partners to strengthen the regional aging services
3521.purpose: Funds will support acquisition of an OnMed CareStation to expand access to primary, urgent, and behavioral health services for underserved older adults in Gadsden County and the Big Bend. The advanced telehealth station provides private, HIPAA-compliant virtual visits with clinicians, diagnostics, and prescription support, reducing barriers caused by provider shortages, transportation challenges, and connectivity issues.
3521.activities: These funds will be used to provide primary, urgent, and post-acute care for patients who face access gaps to healthcare. Our medical providers are equipped to diagnose and treat a wide range of illnesses, including but not limited to: upper respiratory infections, skin symptoms, cardiovascular, and ocular complaints.
3521.direct_services: The CareStation will provide residents direct access to virtual clinicians supported by real-time tools: blood pressure cuff, weight scale, stethoscope, oximeter, and high-definition exam camera. Clinicians can assess vitals, perform guided exams, and issue e-prescriptions, delivering convenient, comprehensive care in underserved communities.
3521.population: The target population is medically underserved older adults in Gadsden County who lack reliable access to primary and urgent care. A single CareStation is expected to serve approximately 1,200 individuals per year. Gadsden County has no rural or critical access hospital and only limited FQHC availability, creating significant barriers for seniors who face provider shortages, long travel distances, and transportation challenges. The CareStation will offer a consistent, local, and high-quality acc
3521.outcome: The project will improve physical and mental health for underserved older adults by providing timely access to primary, urgent, and behavioral care. Outcomes will be measured by tracking unique and repeat patients served, reductions in avoidable emergency department use, and the number of referrals made for behavioral health support and follow-up services.

3537.description: Our goal is to secure land and establish an American Legion Post at Babcock Ranch. American Legion Post 415 at Babcock Ranch is already in existence, with 100 proud members. What we lack is a dedicated facility where we can hold our meetings. This post would serve as a welcoming space for veterans to connect with one another, relax, share a meal or a drink, and build camaraderie. It would also provide a venue for hosting fundraisers and community events, allowing us to give back and support the broader community
3537.purpose: We aim to establish a building that will provide secure storage for American Legion items, serve as a dedicated space for holding meetings, and offer a welcoming environment for members to come together and socialize. This facility would host social gatherings and community fundraisers, strengthening camaraderie among veterans while supporting the broader community.
3537.activities: The facility will host a variety of activities and services, including monthly meetings for the American Legion, the Auxiliary, the Sons of the American Legion, and the Legion Riders. In addition, it will serve as a venue for larger gatherings such as district meetings, Southern Area meetings commanders’ meetings, and state conferences.
3537.direct_services: “We aim to support veterans in need while also providing services to schools that help students earn scholarships. In addition, we back programs such as Boys State, Girls State which guide young people in understanding how our government operates."
3537.population: "Babcock Ranch is a veteran- friendly community committed to supporting veterans, their families, and their children. Our goal is to welcome them, help the population grow, and ensure they understand the resources and services our community provides."
3537.outcome: "The benefits include providing veterans with a place where they can connect with one another, better understand their benefits, feel secure, and take pride in bringing their families. Success will be measured by the growing number of veterans who join the American Legion each year."

3640.description: This project will permit and construct service laterals to convert 350 residential septic systems (OSTDS) to central sewer connections within the Okeechobee Utility Authority (OUA) service area. Work includes permitting, abandonment of existing septic tanks, installation of sewer piping from each home to the street-side connection, and site restoration. This effort directly benefits low-income homeowners by alleviating financial hardship while improving groundwater and surface water quality and removing public health threats. The project is located in a designated Rural Area of Opportunity.
3640.purpose: Reduce pollutants, protect life, health and safety. This funding will help to alleviate some of the financial burdens put on homeowners due to the requirement to connect per local land development regulations & per 381.00655 F.S. Removal of OSTDS enhances localized groundwater & surface water quality & removes a potential public health threat to this Rural Area of Opportunity.
3640.activities: Activities include obtaining contractual services to permit and construct service lateral from existing OSTDS to central sewer connections through the OUA's procurement policies and procedures.
3640.direct_services: Improves and protects life, health and safety of the community and State water resources. With the removal of approximately 350 septic tanks and their daily loads of nutrients to soils, groundwater and surface waters, water quality will be improved. This project also eliminates a potential public health threat due to poor soils conditions, flooded drain fields and small lots.
3640.population: Target population is low income individuals in the OUA utilities service area, Approximately 350 individuals are expected to be served in this Rural Area of Opportunity. The State
3640.outcome: Benefit is reduction of old, unreliable leaking septic tank systems in the Lake Okeechobee Basin and Estuary/ BMAP area where daily loads of nutrients to soils, groundwater and surface waters, water quality will be improved. This project also eliminates a potential public health threat due to poor soils conditions, flooded drain fields and small lots. Completion and certification of the project.

3638.description: The project will install approximately 10,000 commercial and residential Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) telemetry water meters within the Okeechobee Utility Authority (OUA) service area. These automated two-way communication meters provide operational detail, including peak flows per user, conserve water resources, reduce revenue loss from inaccurate metering, and enhance leak detection, security, and resilience. Homeowners will be able to identify and repair leaks quickly, lowering costs and preventing property damage.

3638.activities: Activities include purchase and install of AMI Infrastructure digital water meters for commercial and residential users through the OUA's procurement policy and procedures.
3638.direct_services: Direct services to citizens is the capability to notify the OUA/customer 24/7/365 of high flow, therefore, saving excessive use of a natural resource while saving the customer financial resources.
3638.population: The State through the protection of waters of the State in the Lake Okeechobee Estuaries and surrounding areas. Additional benefits is increased levels of service expected by visitors to and residents of Okeechobee County which are Financially Disadvantaged Community (ch. 62-552, F.A.C.) that located in a Rural Area of Economic Concern/Rural Area of of Opportunity (s. 288.0656, Florida Statutes).
3638.outcome: Expected benefit is that the AMI water metering telemetry system improves water conservation including drinking water due to automated monitoring water usages and reduction of unaccounted for water losses. Early leak detection reduces unnecessary drinking water quality usage. Decrease of unaccounted water usage/leaks is expected as a result of the AMI digital telemetry system. Conserving and protecting drinking water sources.

The lighting on the overpass will illuminate the surrounding areas and enhance public safety.

The ZeroEyes platform is the most proactive and actionable early-warning system on the market, allowing users to "Save time, save lives". ZeroEyes will partner with Florida schools to deploy gun detection software on existing camera infrastructure across the State of Florida to mitigate gun violence.
3685.purpose: The additional funds will allow ZeroEyes to be installed on significantly more cameras across the district. The more ZE coverage there is, the more protected students will be from potential gun violence
3685.activities: ZeroEyes will add server capacity and begin monitoring double the amount of cameras across the district for brandished firearms, and providing 24/7 human verification monitoring, troubleshooting / maintenance, quarterly software updates.
3685.direct_services: Citizens with children enrolled in the district will benefit with the added layer of protection at their kid's schools, while also making the schools not appear like a heavily guarded facility because the software layer sits on top of the already existing camera infrastructure.
3685.population: The target population includes students, teachers, and staff that work and learn within the district.
3685.outcome: To measure the effectiveness of the ZeroEyes deployment, ZE shall submit a report on the number of guns detected and verified on campus.

3701.agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
3701.description: The request is to meet the salaries for staffing the only food distribution center and increase capacity for food storage to under served families in Hardee County. We transport and distribute food to our counties local food pantries and citizens in need.
3701.purpose: Request for a walk in cooler and freezer for food storage. In addition to cooler and freezer equipment we are requesting funding for five positions. (1) Full-time Executive Director Position $40,000 (1) Full-time Operations Manager $40,000 (3) Part-time Positions: (1) Logistics/ Warehousemen $20,000 (1) Maintenance Supervisor $20,000 (1) Food Bank Manager $5,000
3701.activities: Weekly food distribution and appropriate cooling and freezing of food products for consumption safety. Distribution to Hardee County food pantries to serve citizens no transportation means to our site and delivery to elderly communities. Our staff oversees and fulfills these processes.
3701.population: Over 5000 under-served individuals and families in Hardee County.
3701.outcome: Expected benefit is to increase the capacity to store and freeze necessary food products for consumption. Outcomes are measured by our reporting to USDA for products of distribution and by number of pounds of foods received and distributed data recorded in CRM platform by Operations Manager.

3687.description: This program supports the production and expanded accessibility of a premier cultural event that delivers high-quality arts and educational programming to Florida residents. The initiative prioritizes free and low-cost access for students and the broader public, ensuring meaningful participation in world-class cultural experiences regardless of economic barriers. By enhancing public programming and community engagement, the program strengthens Florida's cultural profile, drives economic activity, and broadens statewide access to globally recognized arts and educational opportunities.
3687.purpose: What is the specific purpose or goal that will be achieved by the funds being requested? The funds will strengthen the production and accessibility of a premier cultural event, expand high-quality public programming, and ensure that Florida residents—including students—can participate in and benefit from world-class arts and educational experiences at little to no cost. This investment elevates Florida’s cultural profile, supports economic activity, and broadens community access to globally reco
3687.activities: State support will strengthen the production and operations of one of the world’s leading cultural showcases, ensuring a seamless experience for exhibitors, attendees, and participating institutions. It will also expand high-value public programming at the Miami Beach Convention Center—such as Conversations and Digital Dialogues—offering free, accessible cultural content that elevates Florida.
3687.direct_services: The funding will provide direct benefits to Florida residents through expanded free public programming, including access to Conversations, Digital Dialogues, and other cultural sessions at the Miami Beach Convention Center. It will support school group participation and youth arts education activities, offering students enriching, curriculum-aligned experiences at no cost.
3687.population: Florida residents—including students, educators, families, and underserved communities—who benefit from free or low-cost access to world-class arts, educational programming, and related cultural and economic opportunities, as well as local workers and businesses supported by increased cultural tourism.
3687.outcome: The funding is expected to enrich cultural experiences and improve the quality of education by expanding free and reduced-cost public arts programming and student access to world-class cultural sessions, with participation measured through attendance and engagement metrics. Additionally, the investment aims to increase economic activity and tourism by attracting global visitors and supporting alternative transportation options, with outcomes tracked through event attendance, economic impact studies, and usage data

3739.description: Continuation of innovative and interactive virtual components of the statewide museum designed to educate audiences worldwide.
3739.purpose: To preserve, promote, and highlight the contributions of civil rights pioneers, regardless of race, color, creed, or national origin. Funding will also be used to enhance the statewide museum’s reach and access.
3739.activities: Development of educational virtual exhibitions, digital resources, and interactive museum features to promote awareness of Florida’s civil rights history.
3739.direct_services: Provision of historical education, cultural resources, and online exhibits to citizens and visitors, highlighting significant civil rights and educational achievements across Florida.
3739.population: General public and educational institutions statewide; specific estimates not provided.
3739.outcome: Increased public understanding of civil rights history and education in Florida, expansion of statewide cultural engagement through digital museum initiatives, and enhanced accessibility to museum resources.

3699.description: The Village of Indiantown seeks funding to construct a new Multipurpose Fire Station and Emergency Operations Center (EOC) that will serve as the community’s central hub for fire response, emergency management, disaster coordination, and public safety operations. Indiantown is a rapidly growing rural community with limited emergency infrastructure and no hardened facility capable of withstanding major storm events or safely housing emergency personnel during hurricanes. The proposed multipurpose facility will provide a hurricane-rated fire station, dedicated EOC space, training and coordination rooms, emergency communications capabilities, and areas for staging personnel and apparatus. This project directly addresses the Village’s urgent need for improved response times, enhanced emergency readiness, and a safe, modern building to coordinate multi-agency operations during hurricanes, wil
3699.purpose: The requested funds will support construction of a Multipurpose Emergency Operations Center (EOC) that will provide a hurricane-hardened facility for emergency management, disaster coordination, and the staging of fire and EMS resources serving the Village of Indiantown. This project will improve regional response capabilities and ensure that critical public safety operations can continue during hurricanes and other major emergencies.
3699.activities: The new facility will provide space for emergency management operations, multi-agency disaster coordination, and the staging and support of fire, EMS, and law-enforcement resources during both routine incidents and major events. It will also offer a safe, hardened location for communications, planning, public safety briefings, and community protection activities during hurricanes and other emergencies.
3699.direct_services: The facility will provide residents with improved emergency response, reliable disaster coordination, and a safe, hardened location for public safety operations during hurricanes and other major events. It will also enhance service delivery by reducing response times, improving communication among agencies, and ensuring continuous emergency support for the community when it is most needed.
3699.population: The target population is the approximately 7,000 residents of the Village of Indiantown, as well as those in the surrounding rural service area. The facility is designed to support current needs and projected growth to more than 10,000 residents, ensuring emergency operations, disaster response, and public safety services remain sustainable as the community expands.
3699.outcome: The primary benefit of this project is a significant improvement in emergency preparedness, response times, and community protection during hurricanes, wildfires, and other major incidents. The new EOC will strengthen regional resiliency by providing a centralized, hardened location for coordinated public safety operations. Outcomes will be measured through reduced emergency response times, improved incident coordination metrics, and the facility’s ability to maintain continuous operations during declared emergencies.

3684.description: Union county schools is seeking operational support due to declining enrollment resulting in financial deficits.
3684.purpose: The district will be able to keep from going into a deficit due to lack of funds.
3684.activities: The district will be able to serve the students and maintain a safe learning environment.
3684.direct_services: The district will still be able to provide all required services to students.
3684.population: The students and citizens of Union County.
3684.outcome: The district will be able to stay functioning as normal.

3707.description: The Certified Greatness Mentor Credential (CGMC) will train and certify 50 mentors to serve up to 400 middle and high school students in South Palm Beach County. Using evidence-based frameworks, mentors will build student trust, belonging, and engagement. Funds will support coordination, training, stipends, and evaluation—strengthening a sustainable mentoring pipeline that improves student outcomes and community connection.
3707.purpose: The Certified Greatness Mentor Credential (CGMC) will train and certify 50 mentors to serve up to 400 middle and high school students in South Palm Beach County. Using evidence-based frameworks, mentors will build student trust, belonging, and engagement. Funds will support coordination, training, stipends, and evaluation—strengthening a sustainable mentoring pipeline that improves student outcomes and community connection.
3707.activities: Funds will support mentor training, certification, and deployment to serve middle and high school students in South Palm Beach County. Activities include mentor recruitment, training, coaching, and ongoing support that directly improve student engagement, belonging, and academic outcomes.
3707.direct_services: Certified mentors will provide students with weekly mentoring sessions focused on goal-setting, academic support, and social-emotional growth. Services include consistent relationship-building, guidance, and encouragement that help students improve attendance, confidence, and school success.
3707.population: Economically disadvantaged persons; At-risk youth; Grade School Students; High School students
3707.outcome: 400-students receiving consistent, structured mentoring 50 mentors trained and certified through CGMC 10–12 school/community sites implementing the program Increases in attendance and grades; decreases in discipline referrals. Data will be collected from school partners through attendance, grade, and behavior reports; pre- and post- mentor/mentee surveys; and program tracking tools measuring mentor consistency, engagement, and student self- reported belonging.

3736.description: Pathways to Prosperity (P2P) respectfully requests support from the Florida House of Representatives Appropriations Committee to expand and enhance our Circles Palm Beach County Economic Mobility initiative. This expansion will deepen our current support for individuals striving to overcome poverty and achieve self-sufficiency and launch a new business incubator to empower aspiring entrepreneurs within our community.
3736.purpose: Pathways to Prosperity (P2P) respectfully requests support from the Florida House of Representatives Appropriations Committee to expand and enhance our Circles Palm Beach County Economic Mobility initiative. This expansion will deepen our current support for individuals striving to overcome poverty and achieve self-sufficiency and launch a new business incubator to empower aspiring entrepreneurs within our community.
3736.activities: Shared office space and equipment, access to accounting and legal services, business coaching and mentorship, workshops on business planning, marketing and finance, networking opportunities with local business leaders and assistance securing startup funding.
3736.direct_services: Consultation with accountants and attorneys to assist with business registration, licensing, tax planning and compliance; Coaching and mentoring one-on-one and group sessions with experienced business coaches, educational workshops on business planning, digital marketing, financial management, legal structures and accessing capital; Networking w/local business leaders.
3736.population: Jobless persons; Economically disadvantaged persons; university/college students
3736.outcome: 40% of participants enrolled in the Circles Palm Beach County initiative will increase income or enroll in vocational/education training that provides opportunity for the increase or obtain new employment with increased income. 50 participants will engage in savings match initiative; 10-15 new businesses launched through the incubator, 80% of incubator participants improve their FICO score by at least 50 points and 40% of incubator participants achieve measurable business revenue by end of 1 year. School transcripts and enrollment; paystubs which we collect on a monthly basis. Savings match measured by bank statements; new businesses as evidenced on Sunbiz.org; Credit Scores will be measured

3692.description: Renovate existing classroom space and construct adjoining Workforce Training Center for existing program utilization and provide needed additional space for planned program expansion to meet local workforce needs in the construction and maritime sectors.
3692.purpose: To provide training, a facility with significant open floor space, 16' or higher ceilings, adequate power, and a ventilation/exhaust system is required. SJR State does not have a facility of this type on any of its campuses. As a result, the college has been unable to offer instructional programs in building trades, a high demand trade for the service areas. In addition, the college will be launching a new maritime academy to prepare individuals for this growing industry in northeast Florida.
3692.activities: Provide instructional space for maritime and building trades to support workforce needs in the College's service district. Funding this capital improvement project will allow the College to develop comprehensive career and technical education programming to meet workforce needs in Putnam County.
3692.direct_services: As the construction and marine industries are growing robustly in the College's service district and there is currently no facility at the College's three campuses configured to facilitate instruction in these fields, this project will allow the College to create and confer new degrees and certificates to graduates who will immediately fill positions needed by local and regional employers.
3692.population: The target population for this project are jobless and economically disadvantaged persons and college students. The project expects to generate over 75,000 student credit hours and serve approximately 2,100 individuals across the lifetime of the building.
3692.outcome: The project will improve the quality of education for individuals in the region by preparing graduates for jobs in construction and maritime targeted industries. The project will support an increase in the number of construction and maritime jobs, and will create specific job opportunities for those employed by the College to teach in these programs. Success would be measured by surveying those who employ program graduates, post-completion employment data in the construction and maritime sectors in the service district, as well as wage data for those employed.

3690.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
3690.description: Florida consistently ranks as a top destination for human trafficking activity. At a single center in Tampa, limited capacity prevented 91% of victims from accessing vital restorative transition housing and support programs. Working with community experts, No More has developed a plan to add transition program capacity, so more victims are served more effectively.
3690.purpose: Florida is consistently ranked in the top 5 states nationwide for calls to the Human Trafficking Hotline. With so much activity, according to a recent survey, there was a list of 152 victims waiting to enter into restorative transition programs. Working with community experts, No More has developed a plan to add transition program capacity, so more victims can be served more effectively.
3690.activities: Collaborating with leading programs in the area, we will add capacity and staff to walk victims through recovery.
3690.direct_services: Working with our implementing partners, we will provide the following services: comprehensive, evidence-based, trauma-informed and recovery-oriented residential services for clients and ongoing communication with members of the collaborative.
3690.population: The target population is victims of crimes, specifically human trafficking. We will serve 200-400 victims.
3690.outcome: For survivors - Through transitional services, human trafficking survivors will see improved physical health, mental health, job training and support. Outcomes will be measured by the number of survivors served and Case Manager recorded observations. For the community - By removing human trafficking victims from the community, the opportunity for abuse will be reduced.

3694.description: The Village South, Inc. will purchase a generator for the Broward Community Behavioral Health Center that serves Floridians from Broward and surrounding counties with substance use and mental health disorders with short-term residential treatment and a crisis stabilization unit. The generator will enhance resiliency for the facility during loss of power due to natural disasters such as hurricanes. It will enable hundreds of under-resourced Floridians from Broward and surrounding counties with substance use and/or mental health disorders to access life-changing science-based recovery-oriented services, diverting many from the criminal justice system, improving self-sufficiency, and strengthening families.
3694.purpose: The Broward Community Behavioral Health Center serves Floridians from Broward and surrounding counties with substance use and mental health disorders with short-term residential treatment and a CSU. The generator will enhance resiliency for the facility during loss of power due to natural disasters such as hurricanes. It will enable hundreds of under-resourced Floridians from Broward and surrounding counties with substance use and/or mental health disorders to access life-changing science-based
3694.activities: The Broward Community Behavioral Health Center It will provide key behavioral health services to under-served adults, many entwined with the justice system needing combined treatment for coexisting substance use and mental health disorders.
3694.direct_services: Services will include short-term residential treatment and a crisis stabilization unit. This includes secure residential behavioral health treatment using science-based programs and practices, adult forensic mental health, medication assisted treatment, case management, peer support, life skills, family counseling as needed, employment and vocational training and linkages, a full array of medical
3694.population: The Broward Community Behavioral Health Center serves Floridians from Broward and surrounding counties with substance use and mental health disorders. Is is estimated that 51-100 individuals will benefit from the generator. This diverse group encompasses people from all genders, adult age groups, racial and cultural backgrounds, socio- economic standings, and various educational and employment histories. Specifically, our program aims to assist individuals with co-occurring behavioral health dis
3694.outcome: We anticipate that participants will show marked improvements in mental health symptoms and overall mental functioning. Another significant objective is to reduce recidivism by diverting individuals from the criminal justice system. Also, we aim to see decreased recidivism rates among participants during the program and after their discharge. Additionally, we aspire for our participants to remain drug-free and not relapse during their treatment. To gauge the effectiveness of these interventions, we will rely on program data, documenting individual participant progress as recorded by our dedicated staff.

3715.agency: Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
3715.description: Educate Teen Drivers about the importance of Traffic & Road Safety. Promote the usage of Safe Driving Habits with a focus on Teen Driver seatbelt compliance and curtailing distracted, impaired, aggressive, drowsy driving, and more. Develop teen leaders and instill the importance of civic engagement & making positive contributions to the community. Support and advance Florida Teen Driver's Education programs.
3715.purpose: Save lives, by reducing crashes on Florida roadways. Reduce fatalities and injuries. Make Florida roads safer for all drivers. Educate teen drivers of the importance of adhering to traffic laws.
3715.activities: Teen Driver Safety School Assemblies, road safety teen advisory board, distracted walkers' safety committee, leadership training, community & civic engagement programs, teen road safety advocate program, teen impact contest with awards & incentives, education & information on new traffic laws on Dori Saves Lives website student portal, teaching to concentrate on driving at all times.
3715.direct_services: In person Teen Driver Safety School Assemblies, these programs are designed to directly impact teen drivers and instill safe driving habits to help reduce distracted driving crash injuries and fatalities. Also, our video series will be watched by hundreds of thousands of students, who will receive community service hours after submitting homework online. Hands-Free School Zone Vests, Signs, Cards.
3715.population: At risk-youth, grade school students, high school students, and university/college students. > 100,000
3715.outcome: We receive feedback through surveys and emails to determine success rates. This provides us with information about what worked, and what we can do to improve our success. We talk with participants, leaders like teachers, and parents to discuss how our efforts created success in our participants. Monitoring Federal and State Road crashes, injuries, and fatalities.

3735.description: Funded by a direct grant through the Department of Children and Families, the Center will develop and deploy an evidenced based website, which will serve as a long-term, dynamic, and reliable resource, delivering critical help, resources, and support for Florida families as they work with both public and private institutions to learn how to best protect their children in a rapidly evolving online environment.
3735.purpose: Funds from the appropriation will be used for research, development, and curation of tools, resources, and tailored recommendations to be hosted on the website, for the implementation of a statewide marketing campaign to educate parents about the harms posed to adolescents by social media.
3735.activities: A research and review process, deployment and development of a website, and a statewide outreach campaign.
3735.direct_services: The website will provide family-focused and accessible resources, recommendations, and educational information designed to empower parents, and provide them with the tools to make the best choice for their family. The Center will also engage in a statewide outreach campaign, to raise awareness of the risk factors and preventative measures associated with them.
3735.population: K-12 students, parents, and educators over 800 are expected to be served.
3735.outcome: Research has shown that social media negatively impacts youth on many dimensions. Efforts to reduce this impact will improve youth health, and protect children from developmental, physical, and mental harm. Comparison of data prior to, and in in the years following the establishment of the website, and feedback from users and partners.

3729.organization: The Washington Center for Internships and
3729.description: The proposed project calls for The Washington Center to come to FIU's main campus in Miami to run a three day program called "Career Launch Bootcamp." We propose to serve approximately 110 college students from FIU and other public universities by running interactive seminars that will equip students with the requisite skills to enter the workforce. The skills include lessons on navigating the workplace dynamics, adapting to hybrid environments, maintaining career visibility, effective public speaking and communication, professional networking, resume design, cover letter writing, leveraging AI in the workplace, job searching, interview preparation, and negotiating salary/benefits. TWC did its first regional program at University of North Carolina Greensboro in October 2025 and has three (3) regional programs planned for FY2026. TWC would propose working together with FIU on calendaring
3729.purpose: Teach college students at FIU and other public universities to develop skills needed to thrive in today’s workforce and contribute to Florida’s economy. The 3 day program provides practical lessons on navigating workplace dynamics, problem solving/critical thinking, maintaining career visibility, effective public speaking and communication, networking, resume design, cover letter writing, leveraging AI in the workplace, job searching, interview preparation, and negotiating salary/benefits.
3729.activities: University students throughout Florida will participate in interactive seminars at FIU which enable them to learn career readiness skills. Instructors will include staff from The Washington Center, faculty and administrators from FIU, and career services professionals from the South Florida area. Educational services will be provided directly to students.
3729.direct_services: As explained above, students will learn skills in up to ten different interactive seminars. The different interactive seminars listed in question 13.a. identify the direct services to be provided to students, including writing, speaking, researching, and negotiating skills related to obtaining jobs.
3729.population: College students chiefly at FIU but also at the seven other public universities in the Florida System. The number of individuals expected to be served is approximately 110.
3729.outcome: The entire program is designed to equip students with the requisite skills to obtain good jobs in Florida, skills which will also help them be successful in their jobs and strengthen the economy of Florida. The short-term benefit of the program is the acquisition of the skills. Long-term benefits to the economy of Florida cannot be measured immediately following the four day seminar. The Washington Center will measure the success of the program in instilling the require career readiness skills with surveys have quantitative and qualitative dimensions.

3713.description: The Northwest Florida Workforce & Military Rental Housing Initiative tackles a clear threat: military and essential workforce families are being priced out of the communities that power Florida's defense edge. With a targeted $900,000 investment, the Northwest Florida Community Housing Development Corporation will create and manage up to 25 affordable rental homes through new construction and acquisition/rehabilitation—half reserved for active-duty families, half for essential workers up to 120% AMI. This program directly supports readiness at NAS Pensacola, Hurlburt Field, NAS Whiting Field, Corry Station, and Eglin AFB. When service members and essential workers can't afford local housing, Florida risks losing missions to competing states. This investment creates permanent, affordable assets that protect billions in defense spending and keep Florida the premier destination for military
3713.purpose: The funds will deliver up to 25 new affordable rental homes across Northwest Florida—created through a mix of new construction and high-quality renovations—with a target of up to 50% reserved for active-duty military families. This targeted investment keeps mission-critical families housed near duty stations, stabilizes the essential workforce, and locks in long-term affordability that strengthens base readiness, community resilience, and Florida’s defense economy.
3713.activities: Funds will deliver affordable rental housing in Northwest Florida through new home construction and purchase/renovation of existing homes. Eligible activities include property acquisition, site development and utilities/infrastructure connections, rehabilitation, code-compliant new construction, and required planning/engineering (design, environmental review, permitting). The project will produce up to 25 safe, high-quality rental units, all professionally owned and managed to ensure long-term a
3713.direct_services: The appropriation will directly provide affordable rental housing to citizens of Northwest Florida by building new homes and purchasing/renovating existing homes to full code compliance before anyone moves in. Residents will lease safe, stable, high-quality homes at below-market rents protected by long-term affordability covenants. Each property will be professionally owned and managed by the Nort
3713.population: The project will primarily serve active-duty military families in Northwest Florida (up to 50% of units reserved) and essential workforce households—including teachers, nurses, and law enforcement—earning up to 120% of AMI. By creating up to 25 affordable rental units, the project is expected to serve approximately 50–100 individuals, based on average household size.
3713.outcome: The project will increase the supply of affordable rental housing in Northwest Florida by delivering up to 25 safe, high- quality units. Up to 50% of units will support active-duty military families, with the remainder serving essential workforce households, reducing housing cost burdens and improving community stability. Outcomes will be measured through the number of units constructed or rehabilitated, certificates of occupancy, executed leases, and tenant income certifications (=120% AMI). Additional tracking will include unit occupancy rates, length of tenancy, and property management records confirming ongoing maintenance and affordability standards.

3743.description: Establish a pilot program to determine the benefits of integrating creative approaches into the workforce development of healthcare professionals. The pilot uses creative modalities to positively impact skill level, communication ability, & mental health of healthcare workers. Results and data suggest it improves patient care, staff unit cohesion, and that integrated practices attract and retain high-achieving healthcare professionals, providing competitive advantages for health institutions.
3743.purpose: Florida Agency for Healthcare Administration reports a projected physician shortfall of 17,000 and a nurse shortage of 59,000. Permanente Journal (June 2023), burnout & poor performance in the medical workforce may successfully be addressed by creative-approach integration in workforce development. This retains healthcare professionals who then service patients better. Staricoff & Loppert, 2003, the integration of arts programs into clinical environments reduces staff stress and is a significant
3743.activities: The program trains area health professionals in workshop settings of tactile art-making. Sessions require participants to learn and rely on precise communication skills to ensure quality group output. Adopting artistic, collaborative environments leads to positive workplace mental health orientation of professionals and better staff satisfaction and retention. Sessions result in the ability to provide better patient care (per a May 2024 American Heart Association/ASA Journals report).
3743.direct_services: Each workshop includes a series of trainings for medical staff and is led by a trained workshop facilitator who utilizes hands-on curriculum designed to teach new skills and integration of new practices into healthcare. Patients benefit because healthcare workers will have new practices, better communication with each other and patients, and better positive outlook on their work. The artistic acti
3743.population: Staff in clinical environments. 51-100 persons. The project has written support from St. Petersburg College, Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, The Hive Community Clay studio, and Foundation for a Healthy St. Pete.
3743.outcome: Participants will create a more holistic approach to patient care, so they enhance their employability in an evolving medical field. In addition to the completion of continuing education, the workshop will conclude with a review of participants' plans to integrate new skills or approaches; and review by supervisors of workshop relevancy to retention and opportunities. Workshop project review will occur after a workshop series and will include pre- and post-surveys.

3723.agency: Department of Legal Affairs and Attorney General
3723.description: The specific purpose of the requested funding is to provide 18 individual adults and/or emancipated minors who are survivors of human (sex and/or labor) trafficking with emergency housing (in the form of hotels), transitional housing up to 12 months, and access to wrap around services, such as legal aid, dental care, internal medical care, behavioral healthcare, childcare, and job training.
3723.purpose: The purpose of obtaining funds provided by this grant is for United Way of Pasco County to be able to continue to provide survivors of human trafficking throughout the state of Florida services without interruption to current program clients and expand the program reach to keep up with the demand. The funds requested would be used to continue to provide housing and wrap around services such as intensive behavioral health therapy, legal assistance, childcare, healthcare, and dental care.
3723.activities: To execute this statewide initiative, our Case Work team will accept request for emergency hotel stays for no more than 7 nights, from law enforcement agencies and or anti-trafficking agencies throughout the state. Our agency will lease 1-3 bedroom housing units in the United Way of Pasco County name. There will be at least one housing unit located in each of the following counties: Pasco, Pinellas, Hernando, and Hillsborough. These housing units will serve as safe and healthy living environment
3723.direct_services: Survivors of human trafficking require a variety of wrap around services in order to regain a healthy and self sufficient life. To assist our clients in our program, we will offer our clients access to many kinds of wrap around services. Our agency has a well established relationship with a dental clinic, legal aid, mental health therapist, and health clinics. We also partner with agencies that pr
3723.population: The target population served by this project are adult men, adult women, and emancipated minors in the State of Florida. The estimated number of individuals to receive housing assistance is 18 plus, to include dependents if applicable. Full wrap-around services will be provided for survivors (not dependents), with the potential of another 100 plus wrap-around services and a minimum of 75 emergency hotels.
3723.outcome: The goal of this project is to help survivors of human trafficking achieve long term stability through access to employment, healthcare, sobriety support, legal advocacy, mental health therapy, and safe transitional housing. While in the program, clients meet with a Case Worker at least once a month. After exiting transitional housing, they continue to receive monthly check ins and wraparound services for at least 3 months and up to 12 months. Our mental health therapist works closely with our case management team and shares updates that are reflected in each client’s care plan. Since April 2021, the program has delivered over 3,000 services to more than 280 survivors. We have provided long

3754.description: The Allied Health Center initiative is a core component of St. Petersburg College's college-wide space efficiency strategy to modernize aging infrastructure, align facilities with workforce demand, and reduce long-term operating costs. Nearly 60 percent of SPC's buildings are more than 25 years old and 34 percent of buildings are 50 years old, including the existing Health Education Center constructed in 1971, which carries approximately $20 million in deferred maintenance and no longer supports modern healthcare education or scalable workforce training. Rather than reinvest in obsolete space, SPC proposes to dispose of the existing facility and construct a new, purpose-built Allied Health Workforce Center that maximizes space efficiency, program synergy, and economic return. SPC has secured $8.9MM towards the project costs.
3754.purpose: The new facility will consolidate nursing and high-demand allied health programs, centralized student success services, and employer partnerships into a single, integrated workforce hub.
3754.activities: The Allied Health Workforce Center is designed to accelerate job placement through employer-embedded training, shared clinical and simulation environments, and direct-to-hire pipelines aligned with regional healthcare needs. Programs will support rapid entry, upskilling, and career advancement in critical areas such as patient care, behavioral health, sterile processing, care navigation, and outpatient services.
3754.direct_services: This integrated ecosystem delivers measurable economic impact by expanding workforce capacity, improving clinical readiness, and increasing job placement outcomes for students and incumbent workers. Through strategic facility modernization, SPC strengthens fiscal stewardship while advancing workforce alignment, regional economic mobility, and employer-responsive healthcare training.
3754.outcome: 18% improvement in space efficiency. $24MM cost savings in operating expenses over 10 years.

3768.organization: Cypress Chapter of the Izaak Walton League
3768.description: This project will work to restore Lake Okeechobee's aquatic ecosystem by removing nutrient-rich lake-bottom muck and mechanically removing invasive aquatic vegetation including tussocks. These efforts will improve navigation on the Lake as well as improve habitat for waterfowl and wildlife. Cypress IWLA will work with partners to maximize the waterfowl and wildlife benefits. Rather than disposing of the removed materials as waste, the collected material will be processed into a natural soil amendment and applied on nearby agricultural lands.
3768.purpose: To restore Lake Okeechobee's aquatic ecosystem by removing nutrient-rich lake-bottom muck and mechanically removing invasive aquatic vegetation including tussocks. These efforts will improve habitat for wildlife and waterfowl as well as navigation and recreational access on the Lake.
3768.activities: Removal of nutrient-rich muck and invasive vegetation. The collected material will be processed into a natural soil amendment and applied on nearby agricultural lands.
3768.direct_services: The funds will improve the use and enjoyment of Lake Okeechobee by improving recreational access and wildlife habitat on Lake Okeechobee. Fishing and hunting on the Lake draws more than 6 million people on an annual basis.

Additionally, rehabilitation of these two lift stations is a requirement of an existing FDEP issued Consent Order.

Additionally, the rehabilitation of the two stations will lower the Town's operation and maintenance costs at these stations and allow the Town to better allocate their limited staff. Lastly, the Town of Century's Consent Order requires improvements to all of the lift stations within the Town's collection system.
3766.activities: The project will be bid and constructed.

3777.description: Flow Equalization in a wastewater treatment plant is a pre-treatment process using a tank to buffer and blend fluctuating wastewater flows and pollutant concentrations (like BOD, pH, solids) into a steady, uniform stream, improving the efficiency, reliability, and control of downstream treatment processes by preventing shock loads, reducing chemical costs, and allowing biological and chemical treatments to function optimally. It works by temporarily storing incoming sewage and releasing it gradually, with mixing/aeration/odor control systems to prevent settling and odors. Installation of this process as part of the WWTP project will reduce the potential of sanitary sewer overflows,odor complaints from areas adjacent to the WWTP and the possibility of insufficiently treated wastewater being discharged from the facility during heavy rainfall events.

3792.description: Urinary Incontinence is a leading cause of health problems including falls, UTI's, skin breakdown, and pressure sores for the 70,000 residents in 691 licensed nursing homes in our state. Based on the industry average of 60 - 70% prevalence of urinary incontinence, our state supports the care of more than 40,000 incontinent residents at an cost of $250 - 300 million annually. Further, nursing home staff members spend nearly 60% of their time on incontinence related activity - checking, cleaning, and changing residents, changing bed linen and cleaning furnishings.
3792.purpose: The pilot program would provide the eBrief program to at-risk Skilled Nursing Facilities to reduce incontinence related infections, falls, wounds and re-hospitalization. The goal of the project is to reduce infections and falls related to incontinence by 25-50%, thereby increasing quality scores and reducing Medicaid costs.
3792.activities: Outfitting the nursing home with the eBrief System, which includes: assessment of current incontinence care practices; design, installation, and setup of the eBrief system; and training for the nursing home staff. Following setup, operation of the system for one year, including monitoring of incontinent residents, disposable eBrief inserts, and management and performance reports.
3792.direct_services: The eBrief system will notify nursing home care staff when it is necessary to check or change a resident because they are wet. This reduces the amount of time a resident is exposed to a wet undergarment and the time required by the staff to check and change the resident. The eBrief system may also be used to monitor residents for dehydration through variation in the urination patterns.
3792.population: The primary beneficiaries will be the Medicaid long stay residents of the nursing homes who will experience better health through reduced incidence of falls, infections and other complications of urinary incontinence. The secondary beneficiaries will be the staff providing care to the residents through reduced time required to check and change residents and clean up after events of incontinence. The other beneficiaries include the families of nursing home residents and the State through lower co
3792.outcome: We seek to reduce incontinence related falls, infections and other issues by 25 - 50% as measured by comparing pre- installation quality data against the same data periodically during operation and following one year of operation.

Furthermore, our goal is to bolster the economic self-sufficiency of participants and demonstrate a 50% increase in employment rates among those with co-occurring behavioral health disorders (COD) during their time in the program. 3806.activities: Movies, live performances, concerts and musical theater, children's theater programs, cultural performances, church services, dinner theater, education presentations, and special events. The theater can be rented for private/civic events and will be on a sliding scale to be affordable to all. The theatre will host artist receptions for event such as "Plein Air Paint Out."
3806.direct_services: The Port Theatre will provide a venue for art, music, performance, and education. There exist no similar venues within a 60-mile radius. Education camps will instruct youth on all aspects of theater production. Guest-Speaker series will promote and area and provide tools for business and community development. It will provide a venue for religious services and private or community events.
3806.outcome: The arts have a positive effect on mental health, engage the mind in novel ways, tap into our emotions in healthy way, and simply make us feel good. Art therapy serves to help veterans with PTSD and TBI. Research shows that the arts can be used to create a unique experience.
